title: SmackDown Hits Two-Month High in Viewership
raw_title: WWE Smackdown Viewership & Ratings Report: 10/9/26
summary_src: WWE SmackDown's average viewership hit a two-month high on the October 9 episode, which served as the go-home show for the Money in the Bank PLE.
body: WWE Add Wrestling Inc. on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover The October 9 edition of " WWE SmackDown ," which was the go-home show for the Money in the Bank PLE, witnessed the highest viewership for the show in two months. "SmackDown," which was held a day before Money in the Bank in Louisiana, saw average viewership grow from 1,250,000 for the previous week's show to 1,352,000 viewers for the October 9 show, " Wrestlenomics " reports. This is the highest average viewership for the blue brand since the August 7 show, which drew 1,470,000 viewers. Last week's episode also surpassed the four-week average of 1,249,000 viewers. Viewership among the key 18–49 demographic also grew, with the rating rising from 0.27 for the October 2 show to 0.32 last week. This is the joint-highest rating for the show in the past two months, matching the figure recorded on August 21. The August 7 episode, meanwhile, drew a rating of 0.35. So far, viewership and ratings for the blue brand have been significantly higher this October than during the same period last year, with viewership up 22% and ratings rising by an even larger 25%, according to the report. The upcoming "SmackDown" will take place at the Golden 1 Center in Sacramento, California, with two singles matches confirmed for the show — Nikki Bella vs. former teammate Paige, and former tag team partners R-Truth and Damian Priest facing off. Also on the show, Randy Orton and Cody Rhodes will come face-to-face, continuing their rivalry which has gotten incredibly bitter.
summary: The October 9 episode of WWE SmackDown drew an average of 1.352 million viewers, up from 1.25 million the previous week and marking the highest figure since August 7. The show, which served as the final episode before Money in the Bank, also improved in the key 18-49 demographic with a 0.32 rating that tied the second-highest mark of the past two months. Year-over-year numbers for October are up 22 percent in total viewership and 25 percent in the demo compared to 2024.

llm_long: The October 9 episode of WWE SmackDown achieved the highest viewership for the show in two months. The go-home episode ahead of the Money in the Bank premium live event drew an average of 1,352,000 viewers. This marked an increase from the previous week's 1,250,000 viewers.

The October 9 show represented the highest average viewership for SmackDown since the August 7 episode, which attracted 1,470,000 viewers. Last week's episode also exceeded the four-week average of 1,249,000 viewers.

Viewership in the key 18-49 demographic increased as well. The rating rose from 0.27 for the October 2 episode to 0.32 for the October 9 show. This tied for the highest rating in the past two months, matching the August 21 figure.

The August 7 episode had posted a higher 18-49 rating of 0.35. Overall, SmackDown viewership and ratings in October have shown significant gains compared to the same period last year. Viewership is up 22 percent while ratings have increased by 25 percent.

The next episode of SmackDown is scheduled for the Golden 1 Center in Sacramento, California. Confirmed matches include Nikki Bella facing Paige as well as R-Truth versus Damian Priest. Randy Orton and Cody Rhodes are also set to appear face-to-face.

title: WWE Plans To Proceed With Crown Jewel In Saudi Arabia
raw_title: Latest Update On WWE's Plans For Holding Crown Jewel In Saudi Arabia
summary_src: WWE's Crown Jewel is scheduled to take place in Saudi Arabia on November 7, and a report has revealed the event's current status and the company's backup plans.
body: Tim Nwachukwu/Getty Images Add Wrestling Inc. on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover A new report has addressed whether WWE will host Crown Jewel in Saudi Arabia and whether the company has alternative venues in mind for the PLE. WWE recently announced that Crown Jewel will take place in Saudi Arabia in November, but uncertainty remains over how the event will proceed amid the ongoing bombing in the country. " Fightful Select " is reporting that those backstage in WWE believe the show will go ahead as originally planned in Saudi Arabia on November 7. The report added that WWE has a backup plan if the event cannot take place in Saudi Arabia, with a US venue as the likely option. The outlet noted that the Six Kings Slam tennis tournament, originally scheduled for October 21, 22, and 24, has been postponed until the last week of December. Several events that were scheduled to be held in the Gulf nation have been postponed due to the ongoing clashes between the Saudis and the Houthis. These include the Asian Tour golf tournament, FIFAe Finals 2026, and political meetings. Last week, WWE CCO Triple H confirmed that Crown Jewel would take place on November 7, featuring Champions vs. Champions matches. Reports have said that some WWE personnel and wrestlers aren't too pleased about going to Saudi due to the current situation there. WWE's wrestlers last featured in the country in June for the Night of Champions PLE, just months after the Iran-Israel conflict began.
summary: WWE intends to hold Crown Jewel in Saudi Arabia on November 7 as announced, according to those backstage. The company has prepared a backup plan that would move the event to a venue in the United States if needed. This comes as multiple other major sporting and political events in the country have been postponed amid regional conflict.

title: Jacy Jayne feared release before NXT title win
raw_title: Jacy Jayne Was Worried She'd Be Fired Weeks Ahead Of WWE NXT Title Win
summary_src: According to WWE star Jacy Jayne, in the weeks leading up to her NXT Women's Championship victory, she harbored fears that she would be fired.
body: WWE Add Wrestling Inc. on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Jacy Jayne has emerged as one of the most promising additions to the main roster, with her Fatal Influence stablemates Fallon Henley and Lainey Reid alongside her. All three are currently reigning as champions, but looking back at the height of her "NXT" run, Jayne admitted that she was still battling anxiety in the weeks leading up to her NXT Women's Championship victory . "Before I won the title, I actually thought I was getting released," she admitted during an interview with Denise Salcedo . "I was having panic attacks thinking, like, it's over for me." Winning the title allowed her to get some momentum, but Jayne added that she still felt like she was in a "do-or-die" situation. "Every single time I'm on television, I have to be a 100%, I have to be on my game, I can't have any slip-ups," she said. Jayne then explained that her attitude and consistency eventually impressed the higher-ups, who believed that she could be placed in any position and still handle herself. "I think that's what ultimately brought me to main roster," Jayne said. "If I didn't have that title reign or all those opportunities, I don't think I'd be on main roster. I'd either be still in NXT or not here at all!" Jayne recalled that she'd been in "NXT" for four years before winning the title. Although she "came in hot" with Toxic Attraction, she eventually fell down the card. Even so, she pointed out that she always had TV time as a supporting role before recalling her time with Chase U, where she believes she found herself as a wrestler, as she no longer wanted to play a supporting role. "I wanted to be champion, I wanted to be the main 'It Girl!'" she expressed. WWE Before Fatal Influence, there was Toxic Attraction, the stable in which Jacy Jayne established herself in front of the WWE audience alongside former WWE stars Mandy Rose and Gigi Dolin . However, Rose and Dolin both parted ways with WWE by 2025, after the faction officially disbanded in 2023 when Jayne turned on Dolin. According to Jayne, the entire process left her feeling in over her head, and she was very frustrated with her booking. "Shawn [Michaels] kind of made it really click for me," she explained. Jayne noted that WWE pushed back on her bids for more, and while she steadily improved, she got tired of waiting around and went directly to Shawn Michaels' office personally and asked for a match to prove herself. "Like, what do you need from me? Because clearly, I'm not doing what you need, so what do you need?" Michaels told Jayne to stay consistent, so she kept asking for a match before being booked in a non-title match against then-NXT Women's Champion Stephanie Vaquer. "They were super happy with it, and I think the ball honestly started rolling from there," she said, adding that her stint in TNA also proved her worth. title: TNA Impact 10/15/2026: Loved & Hated Moments
raw_title: TNA Impact 10/15/2026: 3 Things We Hated & 3 Things We Loved
summary_src: Tonight's "TNA Impact" was built around Matt and Jeff Hardy booking the show, and it fittingly featured some extreme stipulations because of that.
body: TNA Wrestling Add Wrestling Inc. on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Coming off the heels of TNA Bound for Glory, tonight's episode of "TNA Impact" was booked by Matt and Jeff Hardy. So did it live up to the hype? In some ways, yes, but in others, it fell short. Thankfully, we have just the column to deal with such a show, with three matches/segments we loved and three that we hated. From the opening promo in which the Hardy brothers laid out their plan for the episode, all the way through the ladder match main event, you'll find we have plenty of opinions on tonight's happenings. If that's not enough for you, feel free to check out our "TNA Impact" results page, then come back to find out our takes on all of it. Without any further ado, here are our thoughts. TNA Wrestling "We're selfless bookers, we're not booking any title matches." Now I can't lie: I found this line from Matt Hardy in the middle of the opening segment of tonight's show to be something of a bit of irony considering that the opening segment from this edition of "TNA Impact" was a pointless 20-minute segment that had The Hardys right at the center of the entire thing. I wouldn't have minded this as much if this was being used as a means of setting up a future storyline for The Hardys, and didn't really accomplish much of anything at all. It was boring to watch, incredibly long, and really dragged on. While I understand that TNA likely wanted to bring the past and the present together into one segment, I don't think that's enough of a justification for this to have been as long as it was. There was already more than enough of Matt and Jeff's presence throughout this show, and this was wasted television time that felt like it could've been dedicated to something else that would've benefitted from it far more instead. TNA Wrestling The Hardy Boyz were granted full creative control of "Impact" tonight, and there were definitely some misses. There were some hits, too — one of them being Ryan Nemeth vs. Nic Nemeth. Naturally, one might assume that the Nemeth brothers might try to weasel their way out of facing each other by intentionally lying down for a cover. They did exactly that, with Ryan delivering a light kick (emphasis on light) and Nic collapsing to the mat. Before Ryan could capture a pinfall on his older brother, though, Matt and Jeff Hardy stormed out to remind them that if they didn't truly wrestle each other, they'd be stripped of the TNA World Tag Team Championships. Ryan tried to surprise Nic with a quick roll-up. Nic returned the favor as the crowd and The Hardys loudly encouraged them to fight. The Nemeths then traded pokes and shoves until Nic blasted Ryan with a superkick. The former TNA World Champion reluctantly followed with a Famouser to secure a pinfall on his younger brother. title: Trey Miguel Wins Ladder Match For TNA Title Shot
raw_title: Trey Miguel Earns World Title Shot (With Nic Nemeth's Help) In TNA Impact Main Event
summary_src: Trey Miguel earned number one contendership to the World Championship in the main event of "TNA Impact."
body: TNA Add Wrestling Inc. on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Trey Miguel emerged victorious in a ladder match for a TNA World Championship opportunity during "TNA Impact." Thursday's show celebrated 35 years of the Hardys and thus saw the brothers booking the show, deciding that Miguel, Moose, Ricky Sosa, Elijah, and International Champion Jason Hotch would all be vying for a shot at Leon Slater's title at Destination X in a ladder match. Slater only won the title from Nic Nemeth at Sunday's Bound For Glory . Much like Hotch, having beaten Mustafa Ali; Ali would enter the ring during the match to cost Hotch the opportunity with the contract within reach. They brawled back up the ramp to effectively remove Hotch from the competition. Nemeth would later invade the match looking to seize the opportunity for himself, costing Elijah as he had the contract in hand. And it was Miguel who stopped Nemeth from stealing the contract, pulling him off the ladder, casting him from the ring and claiming it for himself. Destination X takes place on November 15 in Edmonton, Canada.
summary: Trey Miguel defeated Moose, Ricky Sosa, Elijah and Jason Hotch in a ladder match on TNA Impact to earn a TNA World Championship opportunity against Leon Slater at Destination X. The Hardys booked the episode in celebration of their 35th anniversary. Mustafa Ali eliminated Hotch by attacking him during the bout, while Nic Nemeth tried to grab the contract himself before Miguel pulled him down and secured the win.

title: John Cena Rejects 'Own Terms' Retirement Narrative
raw_title: John Cena Pushes Back On The Idea That His WWE Retirement Came On His 'Own Terms'
summary_src: In a recent interview, John Cena pushed back on the idea that his retirement from WWE came on his "own terms."
body: WWE Add Wrestling Inc. on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover WWE legend John Cena went out on his back, tapping out to GUNTHER's sleeper hold in the middle of the ring, a smile on his face, during his planned retirement match at WWE Saturday Night's Main Event in December 2025 . The loss came after a year-long retirement tour, which saw Cena turn heel for the first time in decades , as well as his 17th run with a world championship. During his recent media tour ahead of the release of "Matchbox: The Movie," Cena sat down on "Happy Sad Confused" with Josh Horowitz and spoke about his acting career. The star compared it to his WWE run, and said he's in "an occupation that's fragile," and he knows it will end. Cena said he also knows that end is beyond his control. "If I have my own story to paint and doing it on my own terms, I'd like to do this forever," Cena said. "When I retired from WWE, everybody's like, 'Man, you're doing it on your own terms.' Bulls***. I want to do it forever. I know that it's time to go. It is within my values. I said, 'I want to do good work and I want to leave doing good work, but my own terms are to do it infinity.' I want to continue to do it. But, I gotta be realistic and look at the math and be like, 'Okay, it's time to step away." Since retiring from WWE, Cena has become the face of the company's exclusive Club WWE brand. He also announced the "John Cena Classic," a tournament where "WWE NXT" stars will face main roster stars, rumored for December. If you use any quotes from this article, please credit "Happy Sad Confused" and provide a h/t to Wrestling Inc. for the transcription.
summary: John Cena discussed his 2025 WWE retirement after losing to Gunther by submission at Saturday Night's Main Event, following a year-long tour that included a heel turn and his 17th world title reign. The WWE legend told Josh Horowitz he knows his career in the fragile occupation must end despite wanting to perform forever. Cena stressed he stepped away realistically to leave after doing good work, even though his ideal terms would be to wrestle infinitely.

llm_long: John Cena lost his final WWE match by tapping out to a sleeper hold from GUNTHER at Saturday Night's Main Event in December 2025. The bout concluded a year-long retirement tour during which Cena turned heel for the first time in decades and captured a world championship for the 17th time.

Cena discussed his transition from wrestling during an interview on the Happy Sad Confused podcast while promoting his film Matchbox: The Movie. He compared his acting career to his time in WWE, describing both as fragile occupations that eventually come to an end.

The retired wrestler stated that he would continue performing indefinitely if he could control the narrative. Cena rejected the idea that he retired on his own terms, explaining that his preference would be to wrestle forever but that the timing required him to step away.

He emphasized the importance of doing good work and leaving on a positive note while acknowledging the need to be realistic about when it is time to move on. Since retiring from in-ring competition, Cena has served as the face of the Club WWE brand.
Cena also announced the John Cena Classic, a tournament featuring WWE NXT stars competing against main roster talent.

title: TNA Impact Results: Hardy Brothers Book 10/15 Show
raw_title: TNA Thursday Night Impact Results 10/15/26 W/ Live Updates
summary_src: This is Wrestling Inc.'s live blog for "TNA Thursday Night Impact" on October 15, with a match pitting brothers Nic Nemeth and Ryan Nemeth against one another!
body: TNA Wrestling Add Wrestling Inc. on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Welcome to Wrestling Inc.'s live coverage for "TNA Thursday Night Impact" on October 15, 2026, coming to you from the Boeing Center at Tech Port in San Antonio, Texas! With Matt Hardy and Jeff Hardy in charge of booking tonight's show in honor of their 35th anniversary in the professional wrestling business, TNA World Champion Nic Nemeth will be squaring off against his brother Ryan Nemeth. If either Nic or Ryan throws the match to the other person by intentionally losing, then they will be stripped of their TNA World Tag Team Championship per the stipulation added to the match by Matt and Jeff. Indi Hartwell dethroned Xia Brookside as Knockouts Champion at TNA Bound for Glory this past Sunday, while Shayna Baszler and Zoey Serrano captured the Knockouts World Tag Team Championship from Kiera Hogan and Allie that same night. Following such, Hartwell will be joining forces with Harley Hudson and Gabby Forza to take on Baszler, Serrano, and Brookside. With both teams having history with the aforementioned Hardys, Joseph Sawyer and Samuel Shaw of Syx will be going head-to-head with The Righteous' Vincent and Dutch in a Tables Match. The Righteous have been working to recruit the aforementioned Hudson to their ranks over the past several weeks, while Sawyer and Shaw scored a win against The Hardys at Bound For Glory in a Falls Count Anywhere Match thanks to some assistance from their ally Erick Redbeard. While nothing else has been announced for tonight's show as of writing, Bound For Glory is now in the history books. Among some of the events that took place on the show, Leon Slater dethroned Nic Nemeth as TNA World Champion to become the youngest titleholder in company history and successfully cash in Option C of his X-Division Championship. A new X-Division Champion was also crowned in Amazing Red, while Jason Hotch became a two time International Champion in an Order 4 Four-Way Match and Frankie Kazarian won the Call Your Shot Gauntlet Match to earn a future championship match at any time and place of his choosing. Welcome back to our weekly Thursday night coverage for "Thursday Night Impact"! Will Ryan Nemeth be able to beat his brother inside the ring, or will TNA World Champion Nic Nemeth be the one who will come out on top? Let us know your thoughts down below! We are live! The show kicks off with a video recapping some of the events from Bound For Glory. Tom Hannifan and Matthew Rehwoldt greet audiences at home as The Hardys make their way to the ring. Matt Hardy says this edition of "Thursday Night Impact" will be a very special show. Jeff Hardy says The Hardys are celebrating 35 years of himself and Matt, then says The Hardys are somehow still kicking it. Matt promises that tonight will be crazy and reminds fans that himself and Jeff are making the matches on this show, then says if The Hardys are booking this show, there will be extreme matches and extreme events
summary: Matt and Jeff Hardy booked TNA Impact from San Antonio to mark their 35th wrestling anniversary. Nic Nemeth defended the TNA World Championship against brother Ryan Nemeth under a no-throw stipulation that risks their tag titles. Indi Hartwell teamed with Harley Hudson and Gabby Forza against Shayna Baszler, Zoey Serrano and Xia Brookside in a six-knockouts tag, while Syx's Joseph Sawyer and Samuel Shaw faced The Righteous in a tables match.

title: Zack Gowen Announces Retirement From Wrestling
raw_title: Former WWE Star Zack Gowen Announces Retirement
summary_src: After 24 years as the most famous one-legged wrestler in the business, Zach Gowen has hung up his boot and retired from wrestling.
body: AEW/Lee South Add Wrestling Inc. on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover After nearly a quarter of a century in the business, former WWE Superstar Zach Gowen has called time on his wrestling career. Gowen took to his Facebook page to formally announce that he is retiring from wrestling, posting his first-ever promo picture alongside his most recent one with a heartfelt message written underneath. "Thank you to every promoter who gave me an opportunity to wrestle. I've had the privilege of performing for every major company over the past 24 years. Special thank you to the fans for not rejecting me. Pro wrestling provided a direction and outlet for a very lost kid. All I ever wanted to be was a professional wrestler and I accomplished that solely because you accepted me not as a sideshow act but as a legitimate pro wrestler. I'm deeply grateful." Gowen stated that the highlight of his wrestling career actually came in his one-off appearance for AEW in 2025 where he wrestled Ricochet . The main reason for this was because his family were at ringside to see him bounce back from a dark period in his life where he battled a serious drug addiction, which was all documented in the "Dark Side of the Ring" episode which aired on VICE TV earlier this year. Gowen called the AEW match the cherry on top of a redemption story for himself that resulted in him changing the course of his own life. He rounded off by saying "My victories are not the result of my talents but ultimately the result of God working through others allowing them to pour into and invest in me. I am the luckiest guy in the world." NJPW commentator Walker Stewart shared the news on his own X (formerly known as Twitter) account as he was able to call Gowen's final match at a recent WrestleRave event in Houston, Texas. Last night on Facebook, Zach Gowen announced his retirement from professional wrestling. A fighter inside and outside of the ring. A man who was determined never to be defined by his demons or his disabilities, but by his work ethic and spirit. Gowen noted his career highlight... pic.twitter.com/AMKMQ9rWft — Walker Stewart (ウォーカー・スチュワート) (@VelvetVoiceWS) October 15, 2026 Considered by many fans as the most famous one-legged wrestler of all time, Gowen wrestled for the likes of TNA, ROH, and of course, WWE, where he had an infamous feud with company Chairman Vince McMahon in the summer of 2003.
summary: After 24 years in the industry, former WWE performer Zack Gowen has officially retired. He shared a heartfelt message on Facebook thanking promoters, fans, and every major company he worked for, noting that pro wrestling gave purpose to a lost young man. Gowen cited his 2025 one-off AEW match against Ricochet, with family at ringside, as the highlight of his career following his battle with drug addiction featured in Dark Side of the Ring.

llm.headline: Zack Gowen Announces Retirement From Wrestling
llm.summary: After 24 years in the industry, former WWE performer Zack Gowen has officially retired. He shared a heartfelt message on Facebook thanking promoters, fans, and every major company he worked for, noting that pro wrestling gave purpose to a lost young man. llm_long: Zach Gowen has announced his retirement from professional wrestling after nearly 25 years in the industry. The former WWE Superstar shared the news on his Facebook page along with his first promo picture and his most recent one.
Gowen thanked every promoter who provided him opportunities throughout his career. He noted that he performed for every major wrestling company over the past 24 years.

He expressed gratitude to the fans for accepting him as a legitimate wrestler rather than a sideshow act. Gowen stated that pro wrestling gave direction to a lost kid and allowed him to accomplish his dream.

Gowen identified his one-off match against Ricochet for AEW in 2025 as the highlight of his career. His family was at ringside for the bout, which came after he overcame a serious drug addiction documented earlier this year.
He described the AEW appearance as the conclusion of a personal redemption story that changed the direction of his life. Gowen credited his victories to the support and investment from others.

NJPW commentator Walker Stewart shared the retirement news on X after calling Gowen's final match at a recent WrestleRave event in Houston, Texas. Gowen is recognized as one of the most famous one-legged wrestlers and previously competed for TNA, ROH, and WWE.

title: Adam Copeland Replaces Injured Jay White In Clockwork Carnage
raw_title: Adam Copeland Reportedly Replaced Injured AEW Star In Clockwork Carnage
summary_src: Adam Copeland's spot in the upcoming Clockwork Carnage match reportedly came about because of an injury to another AEW star.
body: John Lamparski/Getty Images Add Wrestling Inc. on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover The line-up for the first-ever Clockwork Carnage match is officially set , and eight AEW performers will put their bodies to the test at AEW WrestleDream 2026 in order to win the AEW World Championship. Will Ospreay will have to defend his crown against Kazuchika Okada, Konosuke Takeshita, Samoa Joe, "Speedball" Mike Bailey, Ricochet, Darby Allin, and Adam Copeland, but the line-up did have one major change in recent weeks. It was noted during Ricochet's qualifying match against Ace Austin on "AEW Collision" this past Wednesday that "Switchblade" Jay White was supposed to wrestle Ricochet, and in the latest edition of " Wrestling Observer Radio, " Dave Meltzer reported that White was meant to be in the match, and his spot would eventually go to Adam Copeland. "Jay White was originally going to be in it but he got hurt, and Adam Copeland was not going to be in it, but because Christian [Cage] got hurt, they were going to be a tag team, but because Christian got hurt they moved [Copeland] into it. So I guess Jay White would have been in the spot that Adam Copeland took. That's what it looked like to me." Bryan Alvarez confirmed this report by stating that Copeland did in fact step in to replace White because of his injury. However, neither man confirmed whether Ricochet being in the match was change made because of White's injury either. Copeland announced on Wednesday night that Christian Cage suffered three broken ribs and a collapsed lung at AEW All Out 2026, the same show were White suffered his own injury. Because Cage is out for the foreseeable future, Copeland stated that he wants to win the AEW World Championship before he retires, with 2027 being his last year as an in-ring performer. title: Roman Reigns Explains His Limited Live Event Schedule
raw_title: Roman Reigns Comments On WWE Schedule, Says It 'Doesn't Make Sense' To Do Live Events
summary_src: World Heavyweight Champion Roman Reigns explains why it doesn't makes sense for him to work WWE live events anymore.
body: Ethan Miller/Getty Images Add Wrestling Inc. on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover 2024 and 2025 saw a noticeable reduction in WWE live events (also known as house shows). In 2026, however, the schedule has revved up again , with main roster live event tours taking place in the winter, summer, and fall months of 2026. Despite this overall change in pace, the personal schedule of WWE World Heavyweight Champion Roman Reigns' will remain as is. In a recent interview with "Club Shay Shay ," he explained why. "I think we're trying to run more live events. They are good, but we're just at a business model where TV rights are TV rights, and there's just so much money on the line that we got to that point where it's just like, it doesn't make sense for me to do live events anymore," Reigns said. "What if I got hurt? There's so much money that's riding on Mondays and Fridays and our PLEs now that I can't just go out there and wrestle for 4,000, 5,000 only, just for those eyes only. Now, I got to conserve it. But those reps, they're critical. To have a fresh crowd, every single night, you can run the same thing." In his early WWE days, Reigns noted that he consistently worked between 150 to 200 shows a year, which greatly helped him sharpen many of the skills required to be a WWE Superstar. "The OTC" believes that the current landscape of rising WWE stars can achieve the same through their own live event reps . Since 2022, Reigns has operated on a part-time schedule with WWE. Following his world title win at WrestleMania 42, though, he's appeared more frequently on WWE programming. His latest outing resulted in him retaining the World Heavyweight Championship over LA Knight at Money in the Bank. His last live event match took place in October 2023. If you use any of the quotes in this article, please credit "Club Shay Shay" with a h/t to Wrestling Inc. for the transcription.

Reigns added that the reps from live events remain important for honing skills in front of fresh audiences, noting he once wrestled 150-200 times annually early in his career.

llm_long: WWE has reduced the number of live events in 2024 and 2025. The schedule for 2026 includes main roster tours during the winter, summer, and fall months.
WWE World Heavyweight Champion Roman Reigns will maintain his current limited live event schedule despite the increase in overall events. He addressed the decision in a recent interview.

Reigns stated that television rights deals involve substantial financial stakes for Mondays, Fridays, and premium live events. He explained that risking injury at smaller live events no longer makes sense given those amounts.

He noted that he must now conserve his performances rather than wrestle in front of crowds of only a few thousand. Reigns added that live event repetitions remain important for developing skills in front of fresh audiences each night.

During his early years with WWE, Reigns worked between 150 and 200 shows annually, which helped him develop necessary in-ring abilities. He believes current rising stars can gain similar experience through their own live event work.

Reigns has followed a part-time schedule with WWE since 2022. He has appeared more regularly on programming since winning the world title at WrestleMania 42 and retained the championship against LA Knight at Money in the Bank. His most recent live event match occurred in October 2023.

With that said, given everything that has happened recently, it's no surprise that some people within WWE aren't exactly thrilled about going. During a recent episode of " Wrestling Observer Radio ," Dave Meltzer admitted that while he doesn't know what it going to happen with the event, he does know that several WWE employees have made their feelings known about traveling to Saudi Arabia. Though because they don't want to get on the bad side of Turki Al-Sheikh, WWE is trying to bring everyone together on the matter. "I heard that WWE wasn't thrilled that some of the employees, non-wrestlers, did actually talk about not wanting to go because they want that united front," Meltzer said. "Not one wrestler said a word, which doesn't surprise me because if they did, there would be repercussions. It would be stupid to do so, it's not your fight, but I would expect that they can't be thrilled about this." Meltzer noted that UFC 333 will be taking place in Abu Dhabi on October 24, which might not as close to the active warzone as Crown Jewel would be, but that company is not being phased with the conflicts and will travel over regardless. Because of an event like that, as well as the investments into Zuffa Boxing that TKO has agreed upon in Saudi Arabia, the main reason why WWE would want to travel is for monetary reasons. WWE Naturally there has also been the discussion amongst fans about WWE Crown Jewel 2026 being moved to a completely different country, with Meltzer even noting last week that a reason the company may not have announced a replacement arena is that one simply hasn't been found on short notice. That's why no one talks about the idea of a backup plan and they deny it." body: Saquon Shugars/X Add Wrestling Inc. on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Independent wrestler, "Cauliflower" Chase Brown has died at 41. Brown died on October 13. "Truly a one of a kind professional wrestler and a legitimate genuinely good person in this crazy business. For those that didn't know Chase Brown, many of us in the mid 2010s met him through the ROH tryouts and ring crew. He was a guy coming around working his a** off trying to earn a spot. He re-invented himself coming out playing his music with his guitar and bringing out a giant cauliflower he would take a bite from! He got the name Cauliflower from Terry Funk if I recall correctly due to his ear, he was a legit shooter and tough dude! His charm and sense of humor made 12 hour tv crew days for ROH go by much quicker. I remember all of us on ring crew being so insanely hyped when Chase finally got his first ROH match! He would serenade us backstage with songs on his guitar as well." WWE's Saquon Shugars posted a tribute and reflected on Cauliflower letting him set up ROH shows at 13. Yall let me set up ROH shows @ like 13 RIP to my dog thank you Cauliflower https://t.co/qqtAIFZGYm pic.twitter.com/bN0j50BrtY JCW's Caleb Konley also shared his thoughts on the passing of Brown. title: Roman Reigns Wishes He Said No More Early In WWE

body: WWE Add Wrestling Inc. on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Roman Reigns has discussed what he would change from his WWE career, saying that he would've been more assertive in his early years. He recalled an infamous promo he had with Seth Rollins back in 2015, which people still quote to criticize him despite the good work he has done since then. He feels that if he could go back in time and change a few things, there would be two or three promos or segments in which he would have firmly told WWE management that he wasn't willing to say or do what was asked of him. I mean, I've delivered unbelievable work since then, but still, I'll be tied to that. There wasn't that many, but there's probably two or three promos or scenarios, segments or, you know, finishes of a match or something like that that I would probably go back and develop the balls to be like, 'Nah, not today, brother,'" he added.

title: Bully Ray Defends LA Knight's Announce Table Spot
raw_title: Bully Ray Says 'Absolutely Nothing Went Wrong' With Announce Table Spot At WWE MITB
summary_src: WWE legend Bully Ray doesn't think there was anything wrong with LA Knight missing his first attempt at powerbombing Roman Reigns at Money in the Bank.
body: WWE Add Wrestling Inc. on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Bully Ray has hit out at fans who criticized LA Knight for taking two attempts to land a powerbomb on Roman Reigns in their match at WWE Money in the Bank . Knight attempted to lift Reigns and throw him through the announce table in the closing stages of the match . He failed on his first attempt but eventually managed to lift the WWE World Heavyweight Champion and send him crashing through the table. Ray, on " Busted Open ," said that nothing was wrong with that spot and the failed first attempt actually made fans back him even louder. "Nothing went wrong with the announce table spot. Not everything is supposed to be perfect. Not everything is supposed to be smooth. It's supposed to look like a struggle. It's supposed to look like a fight. It shouldn't be easy. That announce table spot went perfectly fine. It worked. How do I know it worked? Because when LA Knight powerbombed Roman Reigns through it, the people went crazy. He threw him back in the ring, he hit the elbow drop, and more people bit on that false finish than any other false finish in the match. It was as great of a false finish in a Roman Reigns match as any false finish in any Roman Reigns match of all time," said Ray. The Hall of Famer went in on critics calling it a botch, and argued that the failed first attempt at the powerbomb made it look more real, as most wouldn't believe it would be easy for Knight to powerbomb Reigns. "If you think there was something wrong with the announce table spot, there's something wrong with you. If you're calling that a botch, you were botched at birth. Why? Because they didn't get it on the first try? Who cares? It made it more realistic. It's a struggle. Roman is heavy. LA Knight shouldn't be able to manhandle Roman Reigns," he added. Ray was so impressed with Knight's performance against Reigns that he wants to see a rematch between the two , even more than a rematch between Reigns and Penta following their recent match.
summary: Bully Ray stated that absolutely nothing went wrong with LA Knight's powerbomb attempt on Roman Reigns through the announce table at WWE Money in the Bank. He explained that the initial struggle made the spot look like a real fight and ultimately drew a massive crowd reaction. Ray added that the subsequent false finish after the table spot received one of the strongest responses in any Reigns match.

title: Michael Cole Welcomes CM Punk Back To WWE
raw_title: Michael Cole Shares Thoughts On CM Punk's WWE Comeback
summary_src: Veteran commentator Michael Cole has detailed his reaction to CM Punk's return to WWE and revealed his relationship with the former world champion.
body: WWE Add Wrestling Inc. on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover CM Punk's return raised many eyebrows, with fans curious about how WWE's old guard would react, and veteran WWE personality Michael Cole has recalled his reaction to Punk's return. Cole revealed in an interview with " OutKick " that he was good friends with Punk before the latter's departure from WWE, but they lost touch afterward. However, Cole welcomed the former AEW star with open arms, saying he was willing to do business with him and was pleased to see him back in WWE. "Punk and I were real close when he was here the first time around. Obviously, he leaves the company. This business is weird because you can be best friends with someone while they're working here and then they leave and you might not talk to them for a few years. That was my situation with Punk," revealed Cole. "Listen, business is business. I learned that a long time ago when I started here. Never say never to anything in WWE. I was excited when Punk was going to come back." Cole admitted he was unsure how Punk would act upon his return to WWE or how the locker room would react. However, he was determined to do business and had no issues with Punk rejoining WWE, adding that he was pleased to have him back in the promotion. The veteran commentator acknowledged that Punk had said a few things about him after leaving WWE but noted that surviving in pro wrestling requires one to let go of past disagreements. "You, you can't hold a grudge. If you take anything personal in our business, you won't survive. There's a reason I've been here for 30 years. You have to just let it slide down your back, move on with a smile on your face, and do business," he added. Punk vowed to never return to WWE after leaving in 2015, but went back on his word, with him saying that Nick Khan and Triple H played a key role in it .

title: Injury Removes AEW Women's Tag Title Match From WrestleDream
raw_title: Injury Forcing Change To AEW WrestleDream 2026 Card
summary_src: The AEW WrestleDream 2026 card has been forced to change due to an injury to a current champion.
body: Cindy Ord/Getty Images Add Wrestling Inc. on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Following the October 14 episodes of "AEW Dynamite" and "AEW Collision," the card for AEW WrestleDream 2026 has taken its final form, but one match that was originally scheduled to take place this Saturday has been postponed due to an injury. AEW President Tony Khan took to X (formerly known as Twitter) to announce that the AEW Women's World Tag Team Championship match between The Brawling Birds and Wrathlander has been taken off the WrestleDream card due to Jamie Hayter not being medically cleared for the show. "I was hoping The Brawling Birds would be able to defend the tag team championships but Jamie Hayter, from that Chicago Street Fight [at AEW All Out 2026] is still out injured. Hopefully Jamie Hayter will be back in a couple of weeks." As Khan mentioned, Hayter picked up an injury during the title defense she and Alex Windsor made at All Out against Divine Dominion, and while she has appeared on television since All Out, including on last night's "Dynamite," Hayter has not been in the ring since. Kris Statlander and Harley Cameron actually defeated Divine Dominion, as well as The Sisters of Sin, in a three-way match to determine the number one contenders , but the bout will now take place at a later date. Hayter wasn't the only one to leave All Out with an injury. "Switchblade" J ay White suffered an injury during the Tailgate Brawl pre-show and will be sidelined for up to two months, and even missed out on qualifying for the Clockwork Carnage match due to that injury as he was replaced by Ace Austin, who failed to qualify after being beaten by Ricochet. Steven Borden hasn't been seen since All Out after suffering a concussion which stopped his and Darby Allin's match against Kyle Fletcher and Kevin Knight, and Adam Copeland announced during last night's "Dynamite" broadcast that Christian Cage suffered three broken ribs and a collapsed lung during their Ladder match for the AEW World Tag Team Championships. title: Deonna Purrazzo Calls For More Women In Backstage Roles
raw_title: Deonna Purrazzo: I'd Like To See More Women In Creative, Talent Relations, And As Agents And Producers
summary_src: Deonna Purrazzo wants to see women step into backstage roles in wrestling more. Compared to the past decade, women’s wrestling has made a lot of progression in several different areas in wrestling.
body: Deonna Purrazzo wants to see women step into backstage roles in wrestling more. Compared to the past decade, women’s wrestling has made a lot of progression in several different areas in wrestling. More and more women are being featured on the main event scene and being given the proper time and investment required to grow their characters. While speaking with The Ledgera magazine , Purrazzo was asked what progress in women’s wrestling she’s most proud of and what the business still needs to work on. Purrazzo explained that she was proud of seeing more women stipulation matches and them closing out more shows. “I’m most proud of how normal it has become to see women in stipulation matches and main-eventing television and pay-per-views. Twenty years ago, women often weren’t given the time, investment or storylines necessary to warrant those opportunities. Now, we’ve proven over and over again that when the work warrants the spotlight, women can deliver in it. I’ve been fortunate enough to experience that progress firsthand. I main-evented three PPVs during my time in TNA/IMPACT and became the first-ever Iron Woman of IMPACT. I main-evented AEW Dynamite while under contract with TNA, defending the ROH Women’s World Championship. In AEW, I was one half of the first-ever televised women’s Texas Bullrope match. Last year, we saw the first women’s Blood & Guts match, and in ROH, Athena has main-evented PPV after PPV. I’ve always believed women shouldn’t be given the spotlight simply because we’re women. We should be given it because the work we’ve done warrants it. What we’re seeing now is evidence that women’s wrestling draws fans’ attention and deserves the same opportunities as the men because, every time we’re given one, we continue to deliver.” While she was proud to see the stuff happening on television, Purrazzo also realizes that there’s still some work left to do behind the scenes. She wants more female wrestlers to get into backstage roles. “Where I think we still have work to do is behind the scenes. Wrestling can still feel like a boys’ club, especially when it comes to positions of influence and decision-making. I’d like to see more women in creative, more women in talent relations, and more women working as agents and producers. We’ve proven that women belong in every position in front of the camera. Now, I’d like to see that same progress reflected in the people helping shape what happens behind it.” Elsewhere in the interview, Purrazzo said that her time in TNA Wrestling shaped her most as a performer. Fans can read her full comments here .
summary: Deonna Purrazzo highlighted the increased presence of women in stipulation matches and main events across major promotions as a key area of progress in women's wrestling. She noted her own achievements including main-eventing multiple TNA pay-per-views, becoming the first Iron Woman of IMPACT, and headlining AEW Dynamite while holding the ROH Women's World Championship. Purrazzo expressed a desire to see greater female representation in creative, talent relations, agent and producer positions.

Purrazzo highlighted the significant progress women's wrestling has made over the past decade. Women are now more frequently featured in main events, stipulation matches, and given adequate time to develop their characters.

She expressed pride in how commonplace it has become for women to compete in stipulation matches and to main event television shows and pay-per-views. This marks a shift from two decades ago when such opportunities were rarely provided.

Purrazzo noted her own experiences with this progress, including main eventing multiple pay-per-views in TNA/IMPACT and becoming the first Iron Woman there. She also main evented AEW Dynamite while contracted to TNA and participated in the first televised women's Texas Bullrope match.

She pointed to additional milestones such as the first women's Blood & Guts match and Athena main eventing several ROH pay-per-views. Purrazzo emphasized that women should earn spotlight based on the quality of their work rather than gender alone.

While acknowledging advancements on screen, Purrazzo stated that wrestling still operates like a boys' club in backstage areas involving influence and decision-making. She advocates for the same level of progress behind the scenes that has been achieved in front of the camera.

body: ‘The Jet’ hasn’t wrestled for the company since May 2025, when he took part in the Best Of The Super Juniors tournament. Since then, Knight has been on an upward trajectory in AEW. Speaking with TMZ Inside The Ring for a new interview , Kevin Knight was asked about Kenny Omega’s upcoming return to NJPW and if he’d be interested in a similar move. “Yeah, you know, me personally, I would love to. I would love to get that chance. If we can make that happen, yes. If the timing is right, yes. Obviously, Kenny Omega had a much longer tenure in New Japan than I did, he reached the mountain top before he came over to AEW. So, the New Japan fans have already gravitated to him, you know what I mean? So, I feel like it would be a different situation for me to go back, but I would love to go back in New Japan and show the audience just how much I’ve grown in my character and my stature, in my work. New Japan has seen me from the very beginning when I was a Young Lion. For them to see me now, I feel like maybe a little more time needs to pass, but I would ultimately love to come back to New Japan and show them this new side.” Kevin Knight will team with Kyle Fletcher to challenge the Young Bucks for the AEW World Tag Team Championships at WrestleDream. title: Killer Kross vs Josh Bishop Last Man Standing for MLW Title
raw_title: Last Man Standing Match For MLW World Heavyweight Title Set For Saturday Night SuperFight
summary_src: Last Man Standing match for the World Title. Major League Wrestling is piecing together the lineup for the Saturday Night SuperFight show on November 7th in Cicero, Illinois. The organization made the announcement that Killer Kross will be defending the MLW World Heavyweight Title at the show.
body: Major League Wrestling is piecing together the lineup for the Saturday Night SuperFight show on November 7th in Cicero, Illinois. The organization made the announcement that Killer Kross will be defending the MLW World Heavyweight Title at the show. He’ll put the belt on the line against Josh Bishop in a Last Man Standing match. “Major League Wrestling today announced MLW World Heavyweight Champion Killer Kross vs. Josh Bishop in a Last Man Standing match at Saturday Night SuperFight on Saturday, November 7, LIVE worldwide on pay-per-view exclusively on VEEPS from sold-out Cicero Stadium in Chicago. Fans can pre-order MLW’s signature pay-per-view now on VEEPS. Their first World Championship fight left Bishop bloodied and the ring stripped to its boards. Kross survived that No Holds Barred encounter by choking the challenger unconscious with the Kross Jacket, but the “Intense Icon” emerged determined to force another fight. Then, in New York City, Bishop did what no one in MLW had done before: he pinned Killer Kross. Competing alongside Donovan Dijak against Kross and Matt Riddle in a New York City Street Fight, Bishop absorbed the champion’s Diamond Cutter, answered with Exit 187 and secured the three-count. Four years of Kross never being pinned in an MLW ring ended at Bishop’s hands. Suddenly, the challenger’s pursuit of the World Heavyweight Championship carried something far more dangerous than ambition: proof. Addressing the defeat on Fusion, Kross acknowledged Bishop’s ability and advocated for another championship opportunity. Even as Dijak attempted to claim credit for the victory and push himself to the front of the line, the champion made clear who had earned the fight. MLW officials agreed. As announced by Rich Bocchini on Fusion, Bishop will get his rematch at Saturday Night SuperFight—with a stipulation that demands a decisive ending. There will be no pinfalls and no submissions. To leave Chicago with the MLW World Heavyweight Championship, one man must render the other unable to answer the referee’s ten-count. For Bishop, this is the opportunity to finish what he started and turn the biggest victory of his career into a championship breakthrough. For Kross, it is a test of his reign against a challenger who has already endured his punishment, pushed him to the limit and put his shoulders on the mat. Their first title fight ended with Bishop unconscious. Their next encounter ended with Kross pinned. In Chicago, the championship belongs to the last man standing. Saturday Night SuperFight is sold out. The only way to watch LIVE worldwide is on VEEPS. Pre-order now and watch November 7 on the VEEPS app, your favorite streaming device or VEEPS.com.” IWGP Heavyweight Champion Yota Tsuji is scheduled to appear at Saturday Night SuperFight.
summary: Major League Wrestling has booked MLW World Heavyweight Champion Killer Kross to defend against Josh Bishop in a Last Man Standing match at Saturday Night SuperFight on November 7 from Cicero Stadium in Cicero, Illinois. The pay-per-view event will stream live worldwide on VEEPS. Bishop previously pinned Kross for the first time in a New York City Street Fight and seeks to capture the title after an earlier No Holds Barred loss.

Killer Kross will defend the MLW World Heavyweight Championship against Josh Bishop in a Last Man Standing match. The bout will be contested at the sold-out Cicero Stadium and air live on pay-per-view.

The two wrestlers previously met in a No Holds Barred match that left Bishop bloodied. Kross retained the title by choking Bishop unconscious with the Kross Jacket. Bishop later earned a pinfall victory over Kross during a New York City Street Fight teaming with Donovan Dijak against Kross and Matt Riddle.

Bishop's pinfall ended a four-year streak of Kross never being pinned in an MLW ring. Following the loss, Kross addressed the defeat on Fusion and supported granting Bishop a championship rematch. MLW officials approved the rematch with the Last Man Standing stipulation to ensure a conclusive result.

The Last Man Standing rules eliminate the possibility of pinfalls or submissions. Victory can only be achieved by rendering the opponent unable to answer a ten-count. The match will determine whether Bishop can convert his prior victory into a title win or if Kross will retain the championship.

body: Jalwa Game Goa Game Raja Game MaanWin DMFirst Veer Game WWE ESPN LAWSUIT UPDATE By Mike Johnson on 2026-10-12 14:00:00 United States District Court of ConnecticutJudge Sarah F. Russell ruled on 10/6 that WWE, ESPN, etc. will have until 10/16 to respond to Michael Diesa and Rebella Toback's motion objecting to ESPN and BAMTech, LLC being added as defendants in the lawsuit alleging that WWE misled customers about how to watch its major PPV/PLE events after it moved them to the ESPN Unlimited streaming platform as of WrestlePalooza 2025. Judge Russell also ruled the Court will hold off on ruling whether the case should be moved to arbitration until Diesa and Toback's objection is ruled on. Obviously, access depended on behind-the-scenes agreements between Disney (ESPN’s parent company) and individual TV providers. At the time, some services (Verizon Fios, DirecTV, Spectrum, and Hulu + Live TV) allowed customers to log into the ESPN app and watch the events. Others (such as Cox, Xfinity and YouTube TV at the time) did not at the time of launch, forcing customers to pay extra. The class action lawsuit is for United States-based customers who paid for the ESPN App between 8/6/25 and 9/20/25 but had already been paying for ESPN through cable or a live TV streaming service. Anyone who had automatic access to the ESPN App through their cable or satellite providers by 9/20/25 would not be included. The lawsuit has been seeking, "An award of actual, compensatory, and/or consequential damages, alternatively, an award of nominal damages (if and as necessary), an award of statutory damages (if and as permitted by law), an award of punitive damages (pursuant to Conn. Gen. Stat. §42-110g(a) and/or as otherwise permitted by law, an award of reasonable attorneys’ fees and expenses incurred in connection with this action (pursuant to Conn. Gen. Stat. §42-110g(d) and/or as otherwise permitted by law, an award of the costs of this action (pursuant to Conn. Gen. Stat. §42-110g(d) and/or as otherwise permitted by law), any injunctive relief necessary to preclude WWE from (a) continuing to violate CUTPA, (b) conspiring with ESPN to violate CUTPA, and/or (c) aiding and/or abetting ESPN in its violation(s) of CUTPA; and/or any other legal or equitable relief as the Court deems appropriate." By Mike Johnson on 2026-10-07 14:14:00 The following was issued to PWInsider.com by Stoked Sports & Entertainment: WWE Legend Thaddeus Bullard Toplines Signing Class in Stoked Sports & Entertainment Expansion Led by Tammy Hunt Elite Athletes Added Include Patrick Patterson, Darius Miller, Norris Cole, and Shannon Briggs LOS ANGELES — Stoked Sports & Entertainment today announced a major expansion of its management division, led by Co-Founder and Head of Sports Tammy Hunt and headlined by the signing of Thaddeus Bullard aka WWE Legend Titus O’Neil. The elite athlete signing class also includes veteran NBA forward Patrick Patterson, former NBA guard Darius Miller, two-time NBA champion Norris Cole, and former heavyweight world champion Shannon Briggs, with Metta World Peace represented through a partnership with Artest Management. Hunt, a cofounder of the company, steps forward as Head of Sports after more than 15 years in talent management and production. She has represented talent recognized with Emmy and Academy Award nominations, and she now leads a management team that includes Jameela Jackson, Joshua Diaz, Qituwra Anderson, Patrick Strom and Lelia-Michelle Walker. “I have spent my career helping talent build careers with staying power and Stoked is the platform I always wanted to build from,” explains Hunt. “Titus and this class are exactly the kind of talent we want to grow with, on the field and well beyond it.” Bullard, known around the world as Titus O’Neil, is one of the most recognizable crossover figures in sports and entertainment. A former University of Florida and professional football player who became a WWE Global Ambassador, he has hosted WrestleMania, earned the WWE Hall of Fame Warrior Award, and been named a two-time finalist for the ESPN Muhammad Ali Sports Humanitarian Award for his community work through the Bullard Family Foundation in Tampa. “Stoked sees athletes and entertainers as whole people with businesses, families and legacies to build,” says Bullard. “Tammy and this team think the way I think, and that is why I am all in.” The signing class gives Stoked representation across multiple sports and generations, from basketball and boxing to sports entertainment. Patterson, Miller, and Norris Cole add veteran NBA pedigree, and Briggs extends the company into professional boxing. Stoked Sports & Entertainment was founded by Jarnell Stokes, Aisha Wynn, Isaiah Stokes, and Tammy Hunt. “Tammy is one of the best in the business, and Titus is a force,” adds Jarnell Stokes. “This is the team and the talent that take us to the next level.” Stoked Sports & Entertainment is a sports and entertainment management company representing talent across professional sports and entertainment. title: Why NFL Stars Transition to Pro Wrestling
raw_title: Why So Many Former NFL Players Go into Wrestling
body: Jalwa Game Goa Game Raja Game MaanWin DMFirst Veer Game Why So Many Former NFL Players Go into Wrestling By Kendall Jenkins on 2026-10-14 10:05:00 Former NFL players have long made the transition to professional wrestling. The two sports share similar physical attributes, skills, and culture, making the crossover a more natural progression for players looking to make the change. Active recruitment of NFL players by promoters has also provided a pathway and encouraged players to take the leap. There are other factors at play here too. NFL careers can be notoriously short; therefore, the chance to become a professional wrestler and pursue another potentially lucrative path is an attractive proposition for many, especially for fringe players and free agents. Some players just want to remain in the spotlight a little bit longer and extend their careers for longer than would ever be possible in football. American football and professional wrestling may look like very different sports, but there’s a surprising number of skills that both disciplines share. Strength and power are the most obvious. Football players use it for blocking, tackling, and breaking tackles, while wrestlers rely on it for takedowns, throws, lifts, and control. Linemen in particular have multiple crossover skills. Their speedy reactions and upper-body coordination, plus experience of fighting for hand position, are similar to wrestlers fighting to establish grips and create openings. A lineman exploding off the line and a wrestler shooting for a takedown also require similar abilities. Mental toughness is often overlooked, but to succeed in football or wrestling, athletes must be able to stay calm and focused under intense physical discomfort and fatigue. For footballers, that means taking the skills required to perform at the top level for Sunday Night Football in front of millions of fans and a packed stadium to the intense spotlight of competing in the ring in front of a sold-out arena on live TV. Staying upright is important in both sports, despite opponents desperately trying to take you down. That’s why agility, footwork, balance, and body control are key skills in wrestling and football. The similarity between tackling and takedowns needs no explanation. There are plenty of NFL players who didn't go on to become full-time wrestlers but made notable WWE appearances, including Lawrence Taylor, four-time Super Bowl champion Rob Gronkowski , and William "The Refrigerator" Perry. But some of the most successful wrestling stars to have ever entered the squared circle are former football players. Sonnenberg is regarded as the first prominent professional football player from the major era to successfully make the leap. He played in the National Football League (NFL) from 1923 until 1930, winning the 1928 NFL championship with the Providence Steam Rollers. Sonnenberg’s wrestling career proved even more successful. Not only did he revolutionise the sport by introducing the "flying t
summary: Former NFL players frequently move into professional wrestling due to overlapping physical demands, shared skills like strength, power, blocking and tackling that translate to takedowns, throws and lifts. The typically brief careers in football push many fringe players and free agents toward the lucrative opportunities in wrestling. Promoters actively recruit these athletes while some simply seek to prolong their time in the public eye.

title: PWInsider Explains Coverage Criteria for Indie Promotions
raw_title: HOW INDEPENDENT PROMOTIONS GET MENTIONED ON PWINSIDER, WHAT CRITERIA LEADS TO THEM BEING COVERED AND MORE QUESTIONS FROM INDY PROMOTERS
body: Jalwa Game Goa Game Raja Game MaanWin DMFirst Veer Game HOW INDEPENDENT PROMOTIONS GET MENTIONED ON PWINSIDER, WHAT CRITERIA LEADS TO THEM BEING COVERED AND MORE QUESTIONS FROM INDY PROMOTERS By Mike Johnson on 2026-10-10 10:00:00 I was wondering how smaller promotions get mentions on PWInsider? I am starting a promotion in Montana and would like to have it mentioned on the site when I do. Thanks. Once a year, I throw some variation of this on social media, but I'll throw it here. It's basically a quick FAQ for independent promoters, based on past inquiries - all of these are legitimate former questions [not sent by the promoter in question above.] Email me a press release. That means a real PR, not a link to your Facebook page, Twitter account or a graphic. An actual press release. We are happy to run them at PWInsiderXTRA.com especially but make sure you they have the date, the venue, the address, how to buy tickets, the card/talents and a weblink for additional information. If not, someone who reads it may not be able to find out more details and actually may not be able to attend. Put ALL the info out there! You would be shocked how many I've seen that don't even explain where to buy tickets or where the show is. I sent you a link to my social media but you didn't run it? Why? See above. We are not going to just mindlessly post links to FB or Twitter or IG accounts. Spend 5 minutes writing the press release and send it out to the world. Why did you book one finish and not the other? Usually, if I am covering an independent, it means I thought the show was interesting and/or I had the downtime to do it. I would love to cover 25 shows a week but I can't sit there watching 25 shows x 3-4 hours a week. I would fall apart, my brain would melt and I would be done and then who would you ask these questions to? No, it does not. I love indy wrestling. It's the purest part of professional wrestling. Why wouldn't I want to spotlight that? But, there's only so much a person can do, especially with the onslaught of content the larger scale companies put out a week. I would love to, but I have other life responsibilities beyond wrestling. If I can and especially if you are local, I'd sure love to. There are a lot of promotions I would love to go see, but there's only so much time in the week. I love AIW in Cleveland for example, but have never been there live because everything is so ridiculously expensive these days. I miss going to Philly as much as I used to, but again, everything is ridiculously expensive. House of Glory is a great promotion in NYC but I haven't been able to get there in some time. It sucks but it's life currently. Nothing really. A table, a few chairs, a place to see the ring and a place to plug in. Easy. No. Call Lenny Leonard or someone who would be good at it. I have zero interest in such a thing, because I know I wouldn't be good and don't want to waste anyone's time. Book Lenny! I am not. I am being a reasonable adult. We are hap

title: Nikki Bella earns Women's Title shot by beating Paige
raw_title: WWE SmackDown preview (Oct. 16, 2026): Nikki Bella’s WWE world title push is finally here
summary_src: SmackDown airs tonight (Oct. 16) with a live show emanating from Golden 1 Center in Sacramento, California. This is the first episode of SmackDown during the four week build to Crown Jewel, which takes place on November 7 in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.
body: Link WWE Cain A. Knight is a hardcore number-cruncher who has analyzed and covered pro wrestling for Cageside Seats since 2014, and followed the sport as a fan going back to the 1980’s. SmackDown airs tonight (Oct. 16) with a live show emanating from Golden 1 Center in Sacramento, California. This is the first episode of SmackDown during the four week build to Crown Jewel, which takes place on November 7 in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. It’s been over two months since the Bella Twins turned on Paige at SummerSlam. Whatever plans WWE originally had for the aftermath of the turn had to be scrapped due to Brie Bella’s broken shoulder blade. Nikki Bella is instead out here on the cusp of another singles world title match. All she has to do tonight is defeat Paige on SmackDown, and it sounds like that will be good enough to put Bella in line for a shot against WWE Women’s Champion Chelsea Green. Bella already beat Paige a month ago in a very quick match on SmackDown. In fact, Paige has wrestled three total matches since the SummerSlam turn, and she’s lost all three of them. There isn’t much reason to expect her to win tonight, unless WWE is already having second thoughts about pushing Bella to a world title match. If that’s the case, the push can be killed dead tonight with some 50/50 booking where Paige goes over in the rematch. Bella feels like a bit of an afterthought given that Tiffany Stratton now holds the Money in the Bank contract, and some of the Bella/Paige segments have seemingly been cut for time on Friday nights. Green isn’t exactly the strongest champion after losing to Roxanne Perez on Raw, so a filler title program where she goes over Bella can perhaps help her out in that regard. Tune in to SmackDown tonight to see if WWE is really pushing Nikki Bella to a future world title match in 2026, or to see if those apparent plans have already been changed. Damian Priest has been repackaged as an asshole heel, and he makes his in-ring debut with this new presentation tonight in a singles match against R-Truth. Will it be a squash match? Does El Malo have a new and improved finishing move? Will he slip on a banana peel and actually lose against Truth? WWE loves to book talking segments featuring Cody Rhodes and Randy Orton, and it looks like another one is headed our way tonight. The American Nightmare has demanded a face-to-face confrontation with The Viper. Are they going to set up a high stakes gimmick match for Crown Jewel that involves bone sawing punting each other’s heads off in Saudi Arabia? - Alexa Bliss and Tatum Paxley are the new WWE women’s tag team champions after beating Fatal Influence last week. Charlotte Flair gave her spot in the match to Alexa after Jade Cargill’s attack took her out. Even so, will a rift finally begin to grow between Alexa and Charlotte now that The Queen has to deal with her best friend having a championship while she does not? Or will Flair try to rectify the situation by targeting Women’s United States Champion
summary: Tonight's SmackDown from Sacramento kicks off the four-week build to Crown Jewel on November 7. Nikki Bella faces Paige with a victory earning her a future WWE Women's Championship match against Chelsea Green. This continues the storyline that began when the Bella Twins turned on Paige at SummerSlam over two months ago.

title: Trey Miguel earns TNA title shot vs Leon Slater
raw_title: Leon Slater’s first TNA world title opponent is set
summary_src: TNA continues to push fresh faces up the roster. At Bound For Glory, five championships had new titleholders. The cream of the crop was Leon Slater dethroning Nic Nemeth in the main event.
body: Link TNA Manolo Has Pizzazz learned all of life’s lessons from decades of professional wrestling. Manolo has been covering the sport for over ten years on Cageside Seats. TNA continues to push fresh faces up the roster. At Bound For Glory , five championships had new titleholders. The cream of the crop was Leon Slater dethroning Nic Nemeth in the main event. The question heading into Impact (Oct. 15, 2026) was what is next for Slater in the world title scene. The Hardys had an answer, and the result is Trey Miguel earning the shot for a PPV main event. In honor of the Hardys’ 35th year in professional wrestling, TNA rewarded them with creative control to book this episode of Impact. In the opening promo session, Slater expressed that he wants to be a fighting champion. The Hardys devised a plan to determine the #1 contender for Destination X. They handpicked five of their favorites wrestlers to compete in a ladder match. Miguel was joined by Elijah, Ricky Sosa, Jason Hotch, and Moose. It was an all-babyface affair. That didn’t stop heels from meddling. The finish knocked wrestlers down one by one for a clean path to climb the ladder. When Hotch had a chance to climb, Mustafa Ali ran in to interfere. Hotch and Ali brawled to the back. Down to four. Moose pulled Sosa off the ladder for a powerbomb outside onto another ladder. Down to three. Elijah leaped for a springboard guitar shot on Moose’s head. Down to two. Elijah was inches away from the contract, then Nic Nemeth ran in to shove the ladder over. Nemeth climbed the ladder as an unofficial participant. Miguel was on the spot to stop that nonsense with a Lightning Spiral. Down to one. Miguel had a clear coast to climb the ladder for victory. TNA made the bout official. Slater defends the world championship against Miguel at Destination X on November 15 from Edmonton, Alberta, Canada. This is an interesting choice to elevate Miguel for the PPV main event, and I support it. Miguel has been in TNA for ten years working hard. It’s time to see if he has what it takes to be the world champion in TNA. I believe that Miguel does for this current roster. I’m not saying I’d pick Miguel to beat Slater, but I do think a strong showing over the next month would be beneficial to his future star power. At the least, Slater has a great opponent to steal the show on PPV. summary_src: Tony D’Angelo debuted in NXT over five years ago, but here we are in 2026 with no WWE main roster call-up in sight. That begs the question, what the heck is going on here? In an interview this week on WWE Radio’s Busted Open After Dark, D’Angelo admitted that it does bother him to see […]
body: Link WWE Cain A. Knight is a hardcore number-cruncher who has analyzed and covered pro wrestling for Cageside Seats since 2014, and followed the sport as a fan going back to the 1980’s. Tony D’Angelo debuted in NXT over five years ago , but here we are in 2026 with no WWE main roster call-up in sight. That begs the question, what the heck is going on here? In an interview this week on WWE Radio’s Busted Open After Dark , D’Angelo admitted that it does bother him to see other NXT wrestlers chosen over him for those spots. “I mean, yeah. I feel like that’s a natural human reaction, to see somebody kind of bypass you. But I also think that it’s out of my control, to an extent. Look, I’m always gonna go out there and give 150%. I’m never gonna half-ass anything. So, that’s all I can do. And I can continue to learn, and progress in an upward motion.” The former NXT champion has been assured by head honcho Shawn Michaels that these call-up decisions are about “timing” rather than being an indictment of his performance in the ring. “But this business [is] unlike any other business, you know? Some people have what they’re looking for right now, and it’s just like a circumstance thing. And, you know, Johnny Russo, Shawn Michaels, Matt Bloom, they’re all assuring me that it’s not because you’re doing bad work, or it’s not because you’re not ready, or any of that. It’s just a timing thing. They’re looking for something that, you know, I didn’t fit that mold of right now. And this person might have came in, maybe doesn’t have as much experience as I do, but it’s exactly what they were looking for. So, I can’t really be upset at that.” My non-existent Spidey-sense immediately went off when I heard the people in charge blamed it on “timing,” because Booker T just used that same shitty excuse for why Travis Scott’s WWE training failed . It sounds like they’re lying to you, Tony. Despite how long it’s taking to reach the WWE main roster, D’Angelo doesn’t plan to give up chasing that goal. “Yes, I’ve been here for a long time, but I am not a quitter. I have never quit anything in my life. And if I did, I would be doing a disservice to my family, my coaches, my parents, my son. That’s just a bad look. I don’t want that reputation. It doesn’t matter how long it’s gonna take. I’m going to keep going. And I’m still here, so I gotta keep moving. That’s all it is.” Do you think Tony D’Angelo is ever getting called up to Raw or SmackDown, or will it always happen to not be the right time for him? Let me know in the comments below, Cagesiders. title: Security guard sues Montez Ford and WWE
raw_title: Security guard is suing Montez Ford and WWE over ‘sexually provocative dance’ on Raw
summary_src: The Street Profits have not wrestled in WWE since the July 6 episode of Raw at Allstate Arena in Rosemont, Illinois. Montez Ford and Angelo Dawkins dropped the world tag team championship to The Vision on that night, one month before Ford became a new father.
body: Link WWE Cain A. Knight is a hardcore number-cruncher who has analyzed and covered pro wrestling for Cageside Seats since 2014, and followed the sport as a fan going back to the 1980’s. The Street Profits have not wrestled in WWE since the July 6 episode of Raw at Allstate Arena in Rosemont, Illinois. Montez Ford and Angelo Dawkins dropped the world tag team championship to The Vision on that night, one month before Ford became a new father . It’s also the the same match where Ford spent part of his entrance dancing next to this security guard for an extended period of time, with his crotch uncomfortably close to the guy’s face. You can hear WWE commentator Corey Graves joke about how the security guard “clearly hates fun,” and encouraging Ford to “get him to crack.” It’s worth noting that this portion of the Street Profits’ entrance has been edited out of the July 6 Raw episode that is currently available to stream on Netflix. The security guard’s name is Noel Lucas, and he is now suing Ford (real name Kenneth Crawford) and WWE as a result of that “lap dance.” Post Wrestling’s Brandon Thurston says Lucas is “alleging 14 counts including assault, battery, intentional infliction of emotional distress, and violations of the Illinois Gender Violence Act.” Per Thurston, Lucas’ complaint says Ford danced toward him without consent, and because WWE spread that video on social media, “members of the public recognized him from the videos of the encounter…and mocked him, thrusting their hips in his direction, imitating the sexual movements.” On top of his own humiliation and embarrassment, Lucas says his children have been “mocked and ridiculed” in school as a result of the incident. Lucas also alleges that Ford’s inner left thigh repeatedly “rubbed against” his leg during the “sexually provocative dance” that involved “thrusting and gyrating his hips and pelvis” towards him. Lucas wants the court to award him “unspecified monetary damages, punitive damages, his legal costs, and to order that WWE and Crawford can’t use his identity.” Thurston says there is a case management hearing scheduled for December 10. title: Zach Gowen retires from pro wrestling
raw_title: Former WWE star Zach Gowen announces retirement, says his best career moment was in AEW
summary_src: During his brief WWE stint in 2003, Zach Gowen wrestled against the likes of Brock Lesnar, John Cena, and Big Show. He saved Hulk Hogan from an attack by Roddy Piper. The famous one-legged star even lost a PPV match against Vince McMahon.
body: Link AEW Cain A. Knight is a hardcore number-cruncher who has analyzed and covered pro wrestling for Cageside Seats since 2014, and followed the sport as a fan going back to the 1980’s. During his brief WWE stint in 2003, Zach Gowen wrestled against the likes of Brock Lesnar, John Cena, and Big Show. He saved Hulk Hogan from an attack by Roddy Piper. The famous one-legged star even lost a PPV match against Vince McMahon. Fast forward over 20 years and his prosthetic leg was ripped off by Ricochet in AEW. Gowen battled drug addiction along the way, but his pro wrestling career now has a happy ending. Here is his retirement announcement on Facebook , where he explains why his favorite career moment happened in AEW. “First promo pic and last promo pic! My in-ring career has come to an end. Special thank you to the fans for not rejecting me. Pro wrestling provided a direction and outlet for a very lost kid.
