title: Tony Khan Teases Hurt Syndicate's Mercenary Future
raw_title: Here is Tony Khan’s rambling answer about what he’s doing with the Hurt Syndicate in AEW
summary_src: During today’s call with the media ahead of this weekend’s WrestleDream pay-per-view, AEW President Tony Khan was asked for an update on Mick Foley and the Hurt Syndicate, and how he plans to utilize them in AEW going forward.
body: Link AEW Cain A. Knight is a hardcore number-cruncher who has analyzed and covered pro wrestling for Cageside Seats since 2014, and followed the sport as a fan going back to the 1980’s. During today’s call with the media ahead of this weekend’s WrestleDream pay-per-view, AEW President Tony Khan was asked for an update on Mick Foley and the Hurt Syndicate, and how he plans to utilize them in AEW going forward. Here is Khan’s response, where he does his best to dance around the topic while saying almost nothing of substance. “Well you know, they’ve both been involved in some of the great AEW events this year. We’ve seen the Hurt Syndicate and Mick Foley were both involved in Double or Nothing, which I thought was one of the best shows of the year, and AEW All In London, one of the best shows of the year. Mick Foley has come in with a fantastic, positive outlook in his first year in AEW, and I’m really excited to have him as part of the team outside of the ring. And in the ring, the Hurt Syndicate have said they are for hire. So, we could see them any place, any time, for the right amount of money. And certainly, one thing they did not want to do was beat up Big Justice and The Rizzler. So, they were happy to work with Big Boom AJ, Big Justice, and The Rizzler, and turn things around. They had kind of a precarious relationship that we saw from when they brawled at the Brawl in the Ballpark, to some of the matches where STP, [who] were bested by the Hurt Syndicate at the Brawl in the Ball park, STP tried to hire the services of the Hurt Syndicate. But you know, the Hurt Syndicate they won’t work with just anybody, but they are for hire under the right circumstances, kind of like the A-Team. I think it’ll be interesting to see as they get involved, and I have a lot of respect for Bobby, and Shelton, and MVP. And they could come in as hired guns for potentially anybody here. I guess Tony thinks the Hurt Syndicate’s current mercenary gimmick is just as cool as the A-Team. Other than that, I learned nothing when it comes to an update on their status (they haven’t wrestled in AEW since the All In pre-show in late August) or how he plans to use them going forward. Instead, Khan answered the question by praising AEW PPVs from earlier this year and recapping Hurt Syndicate’s summer storyline with Shane Taylor Promotions and the Costco Guys. I am simultaneously rolling my eyes at his rambling while also somewhat impressed with his ability to bullshit his way around a question he doesn’t want to answer. title: Security Guard Sues WWE and Montez Ford Over Lap Dance
raw_title: Security guard sues WWE, Montez Ford over “lap dance” on Monday Night Raw
summary_src: Plaintiff alleges emotional distress, humiliation, and other counts, due to moment broadcast live on Netflix and shared on social media
body: A Cook County Sheriff’s officer who was working off-duty security at a July episode of WWE Monday Night Raw has sued WWE and Montez Ford, whose legal name is Kenneth Crawford, alleging that Crawford performed an unwanted sexualized “lap dance” on him during a live Netflix broadcast and that WWE then promoted the footage on social media. The moment was part of the Street Profits’ entrance, as Crawford and tag team partner Angelo Dawkins made their way to the ring for a match that night at the Allstate Arena, in Rosemont, Illinois, just outside of Chicago. The security guard, Noel Lucas, filed a lawsuit on Wednesday in the Circuit Court of Cook County, alleging 14 counts including assault, battery, intentional infliction of emotional distress, and violations of the Illinois Gender Violence Act. The named defendants are WWE, Crawford, and the company’s subsidiary Event Services, LLC. WWE didn’t immediately respond to a request to provide a statement in response to the lawsuit. As of Thursday evening, the current version of the July 6 Raw on Netflix doesn’t include the interaction between Crawford and Lucas. The video appears to go to a break early in the Street Profits’ entrance. But the clip of the moment that’s central to the case is easy to find online. Lucas says Crawford danced toward him without warning and without his consent. The video got hundreds of thousands of views, Lucas says, including on WWE and Crawford’s own social media accounts. As a result of the attention the clip got, the plaintiff says, he became publicly recognizable. The next day, when he reported to work at his full-time job working at a courthouse, he alleges that “members of the public recognized him from the videos of the encounter that had circulated on social media and mocked him, thrusting their hips in his direction, imitating the sexual movements” that Crawford had performed on Raw the previous night. Lucas adds that his children have also been “mocked and ridiculed” at school because of the video. Because of that, Lucas’s lawsuit says he’s “suffered humiliation, embarrassment, and emotional distress,” and that he continues to suffer because the video has been widely shared and remains publicly available online. Lucas’s face is readily visible in the clip, so he also complains that WWE and Crawford used his image for commercial purposes, which he alleges violates the Illinois Right of Publicity Act. “Like so many law enforcement officers, Mr. Lucas works a second job in order to better provide for his children,” Whitney Barr, an attorney for Lucas, said in a press release provided to POST Wrestling. In addition to his job for the Cook County Sheriff’s Department, Lucas also supervises a team of security guards for the private security firm Monterrey Security, which is how he ended up working security at Raw. According to the legal complaint, Lucas was instructed by a WWE employee to take his position near ringside. His suit describes the moment Crawford approached

title: Vince McMahon car crash case dismissed
raw_title: Vince McMahon court case stemming from car crash charges dismissed
summary_src: Vince McMahon's court case stemming from a July 2025 car crash was dismissed in Connecticut court on Thursday.
body: Vince McMahon completed his one-year probation stemming from his July 2025 car crash case. The case was officially closed, according to PWInsider . McMahon faced a reckless driving charge following a traffic accident involving three vehicles. Barbara Doran, 72, gave her account of the incident in a now-unavailable Facebook post . She had stated she was “lucky to have survived.” Authorities released footage of the former WWE Chairman’s crash, and POST Wrestling obtained dashcam and body-worn camera recordings from the Connecticut Department of Emergency Services and Public Protection via a public records request. McMahon was granted a pretrial probationary program on the condition that he make a $1,000 donation to charity and only drive while licensed and insured. POST Wrestling contacted McMahon’s lawyer, Mark Sherman , about the case. He stated, “This was not probation, however, this was a continuous state for a dismissal.” Sherman did not immediately respond to a follow-up question about the details of the probation or pretrial probationary program, nor about the $1,000 donation McMahon was required to make by the judge. POST Wrestling also attempted to contact McMahon’s PR team, but they did not respond to the inquiry. McMahon’s case file in Connecticut court is sealed, but there was a hearing scheduled for Thursday at 9 a.m. ET, and the case was “Awaiting Disposition.”
summary: Vince McMahon has completed his one-year pretrial probationary program related to a July 2022 three-vehicle accident that led to a reckless driving charge. The case has now been officially closed and dismissed in Connecticut court. His attorney clarified that the arrangement was a deferred dismissal program rather than standard probation and required McMahon to make a charitable donation while remaining properly licensed and insured.

title: WWE Unhappy With Saudi Arabia Travel Issues
raw_title: Saudi-led military coalition claims Houthis launched 20 attacks in Riyadh this month
summary_src: A Saudi-led military coalition claimed that the Houthis have launched 20 attacks on Riyadh this month as WWE advertises Crown Jewel.
body: The Saudi-led military coalition claimed that the Houthis launched 20 attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh this month, ​killing 17 people and wounding 333 others. Coalition ​spokesperson Turki al-Maliki spoke at a press conference to address the Houthis’ attacks on dozens of Saudi airports, ports and oil facilities. The coalition added that Houthi attacks on Abha airport, in southwestern Saudi Arabia near ​the Yemeni border, had killed three people and wounded 28. The Houthis’ attacks came in response to Saudi Arabia’s backing of government forces in Yemen, and the coalition’s latest statement continued to highlight the risk to Saudi civilian infrastructure. At least 572 flights from Riyadh King Khalid International Airport were cancelled Tuesday, and the annual Six Kings tennis tournament was postponed to December. Finance firms let workers based in Saudi Arabia, including those in offices in Riyadh, work from home, according to Reuters . However, Saudi official and Zuffa Boxing co-founder Turki Al-Sheikh claimed that Canelo Alvarez still wants to fight in Riyadh in a card billed as “Mexico vs. the World.” That event is still scheduled for Oct. 31. Dave Meltzer on Wrestling Observer Radio said that he heard that WWE was not thrilled that some non-wrestler employees talked about not wanting to go to Saudi Arabia because they wanted to be a united front. No wrestler has publicly stated their intention not to participate in Crown Jewel. Meltzer supported Bryan Alvarez’s report that there is a United States backup location under consideration if Crown Jewel needed to be moved.
summary: WWE expressed dissatisfaction after learning that non-wrestling staff were advised to work from home amid ongoing Houthi attacks on Riyadh. The Saudi-led coalition reported 20 strikes on King Khalid International Airport this month, resulting in multiple deaths, injuries and widespread flight cancellations. Despite the disruptions, a boxing event featuring Canelo Alvarez remains scheduled for October 31 in the city.

She also has been a public advocate for others with ALS, fighting for Congress to extend the Accelerating Access to Critical Therapies for ALS Act, commonly known as “ACT for ALS”. The bill was passed, extending federal programs supporting ALS research and expanding treatment access for five more years. I AM ALS added a statement to Brooks’ inclusion on its board. Since she came on as an I AM ALS Ambassador in June, Rebel has used her platforms to increase ALS visibility, spreading a national message of hope and urgency, and drove action leading to our big recent wins, including reauthorizing ACT for ALS. The AEW Dynamite: Rebel Heart special was held to honor Brooks’ fight and continue to spread awareness about ALS. Fans can continue to support Brooks here .

title: Eight wrestlers set for AEW Clockwork Carnage title match
raw_title: All eight competitors confirmed for Saturday’s AEW Clockwork Carnage title showdown
summary_src: The final five qualifying matches for this weekend's Clockwork Carnage match took place on Wednesday's AEW Dynamite.
body: All eight competitors for this weekend’s Clockwork Carnage match have been confirmed. At AEW WrestleDream this Saturday, the company’s first-ever Clockwork Carnage match will take place, with the winner leaving as AEW World Champion. Stepping into the match will be Samoa Joe, Speedball Bailey, Adam Copeland, Konosuke Takeshita, Kazuchika Okada, Ricochet, Darby Allin, and, of course, defending champ Will Ospreay. The final five spots in the match were confirmed on Wednesday’s episode of Dynamite. In a physical singles match, Konosuke Takeshita tapped out former Don Callis Family teammate Brian Cage with a Dragon Sleeper. Joining Takeshita in the match will be rival Kazuchika Okada, who avoided a 450 Splash from Myron Reed then connected with a Rainmaker to win his qualifier on Wednesday. Adam Copeland took down fellow Canadian Josh Alexander, catching him with a spear for the pinfall win. The win puts Copeland into his third-ever shot at the AEW World Championship. Shortly after his performance, Copeland announced that he plans to retire from wrestling in 2027. Ricochet took down Ace Austin, scoring a Spirit Gun then Vertigo for the pinfall win, securing his long-awaited first-ever AEW title opportunity. In the final match of the night, Darby Allin caught Hechicero with a pair of Coffin Drops for the win. The victory puts Allin on track to potentially regain the AEW World Title, which he carried early in 2026. In a Clockwork Carnage match, wrestlers enter one-by-one, with any wrestler who gets pinned or submitted during this stage of the match eliminated. Once all eight have entered, a 15-minute clock begins. By the end of the timer, the wrestler with the most falls wins. Mike Bailey and Samoa Joe earned their spots in the title match during earlier weeks of TV. Being the champ, Ospreay was automatically qualified for the bout. Following Wednesday’s Dynamite, here’s an updated look at Saturday’s AEW WrestleDream pay-per-view:

The final five qualifiers were decided on Wednesday's Dynamite with Takeshita submitting Brian Cage, Okada pinning Myron Reed, Copeland pinning Josh Alexander, Ricochet pinning Ace Austin and Allin defeating Hechicero.

title: Adam Copeland Sets 2027 Retirement
raw_title: Adam Copeland: ‘2027 will be my last year in professional wrestling’
summary_src: AEW's Adam Copeland announced on Wednesday night that he plans to end his decorated in-ring career in 2027.
body: Copeland, formerly known as Edge, announced on Wednesday night that he plans to end his in-ring career in 2027. Shortly after winning a match against Josh Alexander on Wednesday night’s episode of AEW Dynamite, qualifying him for the Clockwork Carnage championship match this Saturday, Copeland got on the microphone. Copeland first revealed that tag partner Christian Cage suffered a series of injuries two weeks back when they competed in a ladder match at All Out, including numerous broken ribs and a collapsed lung. Copeland described these injuries as something which caused him to “do some soul searching.” “My face isn’t on the posters on teenagers’ walls anymore,” Copeland said. “I’m aging out, and that’s okay. It happens to everybody. But because of that, I just want to let y’all know that 2027 will be my last year in professional wrestling. All that being said, that is why I have to go for the AEW Championship.” Copeland, 52, has been wrestling since the early 90s. His career includes six runs as WWE World Heavyweight Champion, 12 reigns as WWE World Tag Team Champion, and a reign earlier this year as AEW World Tag Team Champion. His aforementioned aspiration to gain the AEW World Championship could emerge as soon as this weekend, when he competes in AEW’s first-ever Clockwork Carnage match. Along with seven others, Copeland will be fighting in a unique ruleset announced just a few weeks back.
summary: Following his victory over Josh Alexander on AEW Dynamite that advanced him toward a title shot, Adam Copeland disclosed that 2027 will mark the final year of his wrestling career. He cited Christian Cage's recent severe injuries from their All Out ladder match, including broken ribs and a collapsed lung, as a catalyst for personal reflection on his own aging and place in the industry. The 52-year-old veteran, who began wrestling in the early 1990s, aims to capture the AEW World Championship before retiring.

title: Roman Reigns Explains Avoiding House Shows
raw_title: Roman Reigns explains not working house shows: ‘What if I got hurt?’
summary_src: Roman Reigns explained his absence from WWE live events recently, explaining that he doesn't want to risk getting hurt on a smaller show.
body: WWE World Heavyweight Champion Roman Reigns isn’t afraid to admit that he doesn’t wrestle often. Reigns has made fewer than 15 in-ring appearances a year since 2023, and hasn’t worked a non-televised match in over three years. But the “OTC” recently explained that his lack of appearances is to protect himself, keeping him safe from getting hurt in low-importance situations. “With my schedule, people will pick on it. But, they don’t remember, from 2012 to 2018 when I was doing 150, 200 shows a year, every single year, just working my ass off … But we’re just at a business model where TV rights are TV rights. There’s just so much money on the line that we got to that point where it’s like, it doesn’t make sense for me to do live events anymore. What if I got hurt? There’s so much money that’s riding on Mondays and Fridays and our PLEs now that I can’t just go out there and wrestle for 4,000, 5,000 [live fans] only, just for those eyes only. Now, I got to conserve it. But those reps, they’re critical.” Reigns has wrestled seven matches thus far in 2026. All appearances have come as part of Premium Live Event (PLE) broadcasts, except for his Monday Night Raw matchup against Penta last month in Mexico City. He most recently appeared as part of last weekend’s Money in the Bank broadcast, defending in a 26-minute showing against LA Knight.
summary: WWE World Heavyweight Champion Roman Reigns has limited his schedule to fewer than 15 matches annually since 2023 and has not competed at non-televised events in over three years. He cited the high stakes of television rights deals and premium live events as the reason, noting the risk of injury at smaller live shows for only a few thousand fans. Reigns referenced his earlier career of working 150 to 200 dates per year from 2012 to 2018 and has wrestled seven times in 2026, all on PLEs except for one Raw match against Penta.

title: Riyadh Six Kings tennis event delayed to December
raw_title: Riyadh’s Six Kings tennis tournament postponed to December due to attacks in region
summary_src: Riyadh, which is scheduled to host boxing and WWE events in the coming weeks, has just postponed a major sporting event.
body: A major sporting event in Riyadh has been postponed, showing that the region is beginning to reconsider upcoming events amid a series of recent attacks. The Six Kings Slam, an annual tennis tournament which brings six of the top men’s players in the world to Saudi Arabia for an exhibition, has been postponed. Saudi General Entertainment Authority Turki Alalshikh announced Wednesday that the tournament, which was scheduled to begin in a week’s time, has been pushed back to December 27. تأجيل بطولة Six Kings Slam لأسباب لوجستية، على أن تقام في موعدها الجديد يوم 27 ديسمبر 🎾 The Six Kings Slam tournament has been postponed due to logistical reasons and will now take place on December 27 🙏🏼🎾 pic.twitter.com/WY4fQVIaNQ The change comes due to a series of attacks in the region which have been claimed by the Iran-backed Houthi militia. Most notably, a missile strike at Riyadh International Airport caused 13 deaths and more than 300 injuries last week. Major events in professional wrestling and boxing are set to take place in the region soon, calling into question whether they’ll follow in the footsteps of tennis organizers and postpone, relocate, or even cancel. A massive boxing showdown between Canelo Alvarez and Christian Mbilli is scheduled for October 31 in Riyadh. Alalshikh recently reinstated their hopes to go forward with the event, saying that he was told Canelo won’t reschedule the event “no matter what.” WWE is scheduled to present Crown Jewel from Riyadh just a week later, on November 7. As of this week, WWE has continued to promote the event in Riyadh, showing graphics listing the location on Monday’s Raw broadcast.
summary: The Six Kings Slam tennis exhibition featuring six of the world's top men's players has been postponed from its original date to December 27. Saudi General Entertainment Authority chairman Turki Alalshikh cited logistical reasons for the move following recent attacks in the region claimed by the Iran-backed Houthi militia, including a deadly missile strike at Riyadh International Airport. summary_src: Shotzi's latest deal with MLW has reportedly come to an end, making her free to sign anywhere else.
body: Shotzi has exited the MLW roster and joined TNA, per a new report. Questions regarding Shotzi’s future with MLW started to come out this week, as local reports showed that she worked a recent set of TNA Wrestling TV tapings. Shortly after that news came out, Fightful Select provided an update on the former WWE talent’s status. Per Fightful, Shotzi recently finished up a six-month deal with MLW and has since signed with TNA. Her exit from MLW was on “good terms,” and Shotzi had agreed to make further appearances with the company through to 2027, although of course this new deal calls into question whether that will still happen. MLW has been one of the main homes for Shotzi ever since she departed the WWE roster last year. She captured the company’s Middleweight Women’s Championship in February. Shotzi lost the title in September as part of an MLW Fusion episode that has yet to air. Shotzi is the second women’s division name to reportedly exit a deal with MLW recently. It was reported last week that former AEW name Lady Frost had wrapped up with the company after a six-month stint.

title: Kevin Knight Grateful for Pillar Status in AEW
raw_title: Former champion reacts to Tony Khan considering him as one of the pillars of AEW
summary_src: Kevin Knight reacted to Tony Khan naming him one of the future pillars of AEW. Speaking with TMZ’s Inside The Ring, Knight expressed gratitude for the recognition by Khan especially when he feels his wrestling career progressed massively since joining the promotion.
body: Kevin Knight reacted to Tony Khan naming him one of the future pillars of AEW. Speaking with TMZ’s Inside The Ring , Knight expressed gratitude for the recognition by Khan especially when he feels his wrestling career progressed massively since joining the promotion. Additionally, being categorized among the likes of Mercedes Mone, Thekla and Kyle Fletcher who had extensive wrestling experience was monumental. “That means a lot honestly because I’ve been in this company what, a little over a year at this point, and I was on the dual contract. When I first got to AEW, I was mainly New Japan and things happened and I looked up and everything has happened, the way it happened. It impacted me, I wasn’t one of his first guys that he first signed right off the box. Mercedes was a big name coming from WWE. Thekla was a big name coming out of Stardom. Kyle has been grinding, the last two, three years on TV and me, I feel like I just got here. So, for him to mention me among those names, it’s like, ‘Wow, he really thinks a lot of me.’ And for me, I just go out there and do what I’m supposed to or I just do what I do to my best abilities. And obviously he gravitates to it. So, I’m just like, I’m doing something right, so let me just keep doing it.” At AEW WrestleDream on October 17, Knight and Fletcher challenge The Young Bucks for the Tag Team Titles. title: Lola Vice Recalls Scary Ladder Spot at Money in the Bank
raw_title: WWE star says dangerous spot in Money in the Bank ladder match ‘could have been very ugly’
summary_src: Lola Vice competed in her first WWE Money in the Bank ladder match on October 10. However, there was a spot with Jacy Jayne which could have ended horribly. In her interaction with WWE Ahora, Vice replayed the segment when she put Jayne, who was nearing the top of the ladder, in a chokehold.
body: Lola Vice competed in her first WWE Money in the Bank ladder match on October 10. However, there was a spot with Jacy Jayne which could have ended horribly. In her interaction with WWE Ahora , Vice replayed the segment when she put Jayne, who was nearing the top of the ladder, in a chokehold. They fell backwards with Vice landing on a ladder before falling to the floor. The former NXT Women’s Champion explained that the moment was scary and could’ve ended in severe injury. “I had Jacy in a choke and when I put her to sleep, she fell back and I fell with her. I thought that was the end of it, but suddenly the ladder went backwards, and literally, it got us out of the ring. Because of that, I didn’t win Money in the Bank. It hurt a lot and was very scary, but looking back, thank God it came out like this because it could have been very ugly. I think an injury in a Ladder match would have been rough. They are not for everyone, but thank God I’m strong and I was able to do it.” (H/T Fightful ) Vice was officially moved to Raw in August after nearly four years on NXT. title: Zelina Vega Recalls Cody Rhodes Extending Her Match Time
raw_title: Former WWE star recalls how Cody Rhodes’ unexpected gesture earned her extra match time
summary_src: Xelina recently recalled an unexpected moment involving Cody Rhodes that gave her and Giulia more time for their WWE United States Championship match on SmackDown.
body: Xelina recently recalled an unexpected moment involving Cody Rhodes that gave her and Giulia more time for their WWE United States Championship match on SmackDown. While Rhodes’ last-minute gesture offered them a rare opportunity to showcase their match, the sudden change also left Vega scrambling to adjust their plans backstage. In her interview with Ring the Belle, Xelina narrated how Rhodes gave her and Giulia 10 minutes extra on their United States Title match which barely had a couple of minutes of TV time. She stated how the first half an hour of that edition of SmackDown was for a segment between Rhodes and John Cena. “I had asked Cody, obviously English is not Giulia’s first language. So I wanted to also help ease her mind. Who, mind you, I love Giulia. She has become one of my very, very close friends. I feel she’s literally my soulmate when it comes to wrestling. I love her. I ask Cody, I’m like, ‘Hey, so how long do you think you and John are gonna go? You’re gonna be probably a little bit longer….Like what are you thinking?’ And he’s like, ‘Why? Do you guys have to base it on us?’ And I’m trying to ease Giulia’s mind as far as how much we actually might have, and he was like, ‘Oh, I think either we’ll probably go right on time.’ I was like, ‘Okay, cool.’ Then I knew, all right, we’ll have exactly a minute maybe, and then I kind of planned it in my head as that. As we’re in Gorilla, Cody comes back and he goes, ‘Hey! Saved you guys an extra 10 minutes. Have fun!’” Despite receiving extra TV time due to Rhodes’ gesture, a last-minute change to the segment led to some confusion backstage, as they scrambled to manage an unexpected situation. Xelina approached Triple H to extend introductions for the match to make the necessary adjustments. “Panic right away. Panic. First of all, amazing for him to do that because he did that. We wouldn’t have had that time if it was for Cody and John. He’s thinking that we’re gonna be excited, and I’m like, ‘No, bro.’ English is not her first language. This is not a normal, we didn’t really plan it that way. And he’s just like, ‘Oh, sorry.’” Xelina held the US Title for two months from April 2025, losing it to Giulia. During the same interview, Xelina expressed that Triple H had not allowed her to defend the title in the manner she had envisioned. body: October 16 2004 was the date of ROH Joe vs Punk II, which saw CM Punk and Samoa Joe go 60 minutes in the main event for a bonafide ***** classic. Here is some of what Dave had to say about CM Punk vs Samoa Joe: “One of the most talked about matches of late was the 10/16 Samoa Joe vs. C.M. Punk 60:00 draw from Chicago Ridge, IL, for the ROH title. It was the rematch of their 60:00 draw on 6/12 in Dayton (****1/4) that many had talked about as a match of the year contender. Mick Foley watched the Chicago Ridge match, seeing the second half in the stands and nobody even noticed he was there because there was so much attention on the match. Foley called it one of the best matches he’d ever seen live. Everyone who saw both matches said the Chicago Ridge match was better, and after seeing it, I think it was considerably better. “The match really exemplified the upside of ROH, which is, to their niche audience, the booking of the championship as the main characters. The story here was as old as wrestling. Samoa Joe played world champion, who is respected but plays very subtle heel, only because the challenger, Punk, is a local product. What made the match was, in 2004, they got the audience to totally buy into the idea that the belt is a meaningful world title. With the exception of NOAH (which books their world champion similarly), no other worked promotion can get that kind of intensity from the crowd in their world title matches now, although there were some early in the year WWE matches like Eddie Guerrero vs. Brock Lesnar at the Cow Palace in San Francisco and the Wrestlemania main event from Madison Square Garden that did as well. “To go 60:00 today, you need everything working for you. You need wrestlers who are over and a title which people take seriously. When HHH and Chris Benoit tried to do it on Raw, realistically, it failed. While the crowd was into the final 10 minutes, they didn’t care much about anything but the finish, and they knew the finish wasn’t coming. Of course, that’s the problem with the Iron Man dynamic, as opposed to a match that simply goes the hour. “The downside is it was 750 people in a city the size of Chicago. ROH delivers the nearly perfect product for its audience, but right now, the audience still is smaller than it needs to be. “But the crowd was buzzing for this match even before it started, which was half the battle. After the Japanese streamers open, the early part of the match was very much superior to the first match. The first match had them playing around with a ringside fan, and they were trying to kill time, knowing they were going so long. This match so them do a lot of mat wrestling, but they never lost focus on the goal of making it appear to be a realistic match for a realistic title. The crowd took to the realism, as every escape and exchange got a reaction, even though it was mainly moves like headlocks, head scissors and hammerlocks. body: October 16 is a much slower day than we’ve seen recently when it comes to pro wrestling title changes. According to wrestlingdata.com , there have been around 236 major/notable title changes on this date historically. body: Having wrestled in Japan just once, and that too under WWE, AEW’s Tommaso Ciampa recently discussed the possibility of wrestling in NJPW. Recently, speaking to James Dator in an interview on SB Nation ahead of AEW WrestleDream 2026, Ciampa addressed the chances of wrestling in NJPW. “ Shingo [Takagi] always jumps out at me as someone I’ve always wanted to share a ring with ,” he said. However, Ciampa also added that he was not sure about his body permitting him to perform in a tour or NJPW’s iconic G1 tournament. “ I don’t know that my body or personal life at this point bodes well for a full-on tour or G1 Tournament, but doing a show here or there, or three shows, I’d be 100% open to that.” Ciampa has previously wrestled in NJPW, but it was at the ROH/NJPW ​War Of The Worlds 2014, where he wrestled twice in a span of 1 week, once in Canada, and later in the USA. Ciampa is now scheduled to face Andrade for his National title at AEW WrestleDream 2026. title: Austin Creed Details Swerve Strickland's AEW Trios Plan
raw_title: Austin Creed reveals Swerve Strickland’s original pitch for New Level in AEW
summary_src: After parting ways with WWE in early 2026, the New Level [Austin Creed & Kofi] made their AEW debut at All In 2026 in London, UK, where they teamed up with Swerve Strickland. Just minutes after their debut, the New Level became the brand-new AEW Trios Champions.
body: After parting ways with WWE in early 2026, the New Level [Austin Creed & Kofi] made their AEW debut at All In 2026 in London, UK, where they teamed up with Swerve Strickland. Just minutes after their debut, the New Level became the brand-new AEW Trios Champions . Recently, Creed spoke with Cameron Hawkins of Uncrowned/Yahoo Sports and revealed what Strickland originally planned for him and Kofi in AEW. “ [Strickland] goes, ‘Look, if we jump in this trios [situation], you get a chance to wrestle, what, six, seven other tag-teams right from the jump at Wembley ,” Creed shared. “ So logically, well, of course we want to put hands on everybody as quick as we can. And now by winning those titles, we beat a bunch of other very credible, very good tag-teams that AEW has to offer. And so it’s about making sure that we are getting the reps with all of these people on the roster, and having the most dangerous man in all of AEW [Strickland] at our side while we’re doing that, with [manager] Prince Nana as well ,” he finished. The New Level made their debut in the Trios Roulette Royale for the AEW World Trios Championship, where they defeated all the other Trios teams to become the new Trios Champions. They later defended their title on Dynamite and then against “Hangman” Adam Page and Brodido at All Out 2026. They are again scheduled to defend their titles against “Hangman” and Brodido at WrestleDream 2026 in a Two out of three falls match. title: Trey Miguel Earns TNA World Title Shot at Destination X
raw_title: World title match to headline TNA Destination X 2026
summary_src: New TNA World Champion Leon Slater has his first challenger set after the events of Thursday’s Bound for Glory fallout edition of Impact.
body: New TNA World Champion Leon Slater has his first challenger set after the events of Thursday’s Bound for Glory fallout edition of Impact . In a ladder match featuring Elijah, Trey Miguel, Jason Hotch, Moose and Ricky Sosa, Miguel ended up with the contract and will challenge Slater at next month’s Destination X, TNA’s final special event of the year. The end came when Sosa was power bombed on a ladder by Moose followed by a top rope guitar shot by Elijah who was then taken out by Nic Nemeth who was upset he wasn’t included in the match. He was about to steal the contract when Miguel pulled him off the ladder, blocked a superkick, and hit his Lightning Spiral to take him out. He then climbed up to grab the contract. The 32-year-old Miguel has never held the World title, but is a former International, X-Division and Tag Team Champion. Slater won the title from Nemeth at last weekend’s Bound for Glory to kick off his first World title run. It will be their third-ever singles match and second in TNA with the first coming in June 2024 (no contest).
summary: Trey Miguel won a multi-man ladder match on the post-Bound for Glory episode of Impact to earn a future title opportunity. He will challenge new TNA World Champion Leon Slater at the promotion's final special event of 2025, Destination X. Since defeating and retiring AJ Styles at WWE Royal Rumble 2026 , Gunther has failed to be a part of any significant WWE storyline. And while he faced off against Seth Rollins at WWE WrestleMania 42, it did not lead to anything. Recently, Gunther was involved in the Money in the Bank qualifying match, where he took a pinfall loss to CM Punk, and has been feuding with Danhausen on SmackDown since. As per the reports, the frustrations have emerged, especially based on his career’s current trajectory after he was retiring several WWE legends before moving to SmackDown. title: Montez Ford and WWE sued by security guard
raw_title: Montez Ford, WWE sued over ‘sexually provocative dance’ during ring entrance
summary_src: Both WWE and Montez Ford have sued by an off-duty security guard over a July 2026 ring entrance on WWE Raw.
body: Both WWE and Montez Ford have sued by an off-duty security guard over a July 2026 ring entrance on WWE Raw. First reported by Wrestlenomics on Thursday , Noel Lucas filed suit Wednesday alleging 14 counts including assault, battery, intentional infliction of emotional distress, and violations of both the Illinois Gender Violence Act and the Illinois Right of Publicity Act. A case management hearing is set for December 10. Lucas is asking for an award of monetary damages, punitive damages, legal fees and that his identity can’t be used by either WWE or Ford. The total damages are unspecified. The incident took place on Monday, July 6 at the Allstate Arena in Rosemont, Illinois. As Ford (Kenneth Crawford) and Angelo Dawkins were heading to the ring, Crawford performed a “sexually provocative dance” in front of Lucas for nearly 30 seconds that Lucas claimed included physical contact. The camera was focused on the scene the entire time — a scene that has since been removed from the version found on Netflix, but can found online. Lucas is a Cook County Sheriff’s officer. He is suing WWE, Crawford and Event Services, LLC, as he claimed the video has been seen hundreds of thousands of times and was promoted by both Crawford and WWE on social media, continuing to circulate. Lucas said he became “publicly recognizable” and that “members of the public (who) recognized him from the videos of the encounter that had circulated on social media and mocked him, thrusting their hips in his direction, imitating the sexual movements.” He claims he “suffered humiliation, embarrassment, and emotional distress” and that his children have also dealt with being “mocked and ridiculed” at school.
summary: An off-duty Cook County Sheriff's officer named Noel Lucas filed a lawsuit Wednesday against Montez Ford, WWE and Event Services LLC. Lucas alleges 14 counts including assault, battery, intentional infliction of emotional distress and violations of the Illinois Gender Violence Act and Illinois Right of Publicity Act stemming from a July 6 ring entrance at Raw in Rosemont, Illinois. Ford performed a sexually provocative dance in front of Lucas for nearly 30 seconds that included physical contact, which was captured on camera, promoted on social media and has been viewed hundreds of thousands of times; Lucas seeks monetary and punitive damages, legal fees and to prevent use of his identity.

title: Drew McIntyre Slams Pre-Planned Matches
raw_title: Drew McIntyre criticizes wrestlers who plan entire matches in advance
summary_src: WWE’s Drew McIntyre says he can’t stand wrestlers who plan entire wrestling matches in advance. Speaking on Bradley Martyn’s Raw Talk, McIntyre opened up about his in-ring match psychology and how he prefers to listen to the crowd and perform.
body: WWE’s Drew McIntyre says he can’t stand wrestlers who plan entire wrestling matches in advance. Speaking on Bradley Martyn’s Raw Talk , McIntyre opened up about his in-ring match psychology and how he prefers to listen to the crowd and perform. While he is in favor of talking about the match with his opponent, he is critical of planning entire matches in advance. “ Unless it’s a stunt, practice stunts. But when it comes to the matches, you should know what you’re doing. We can talk about it a bit. You got 10 minutes, you got 15 minutes, you got 20 minutes. Go out there and listen to the crowd. Wrestle ,” McIntyre shared. “ I can’t stand when people plan stuff from beginning to end because you don’t know how the crowd’s going to react. If you plan out this choreographed match, you walk out there, and the crowd are just sitting on their hands. They’re like, ‘Huh? But they liked it in Chicago last week.’ You’re not Chicago. Different crowds like different things ,” McIntyre emphasized. The former WWE Champion added that wrestlers have not learned how to improvise. And while some people are good at listening , some people panic. McIntyre added that if one’s on live and somebody panics, it’s not fun and looks choppy. “ You’re talking to them like, ‘Hey, this ain’t working. We’re going to go this direction now,’ and they kind of freeze up. That’s when things look choppy. “ Not choppy in the good way. I like if it looks kind of real, if it’s kind of choppy and you get really physical with each other ,” he said. “ But if things start messing up in an obvious way, it is not good. If there’s a miscommunication or somebody trying to tell the other person, let’s go this direction, and they’re not quite ready.” McIntyre finished off by saying that things are different now as WWE does not have many non-televised shows now, which they used to do back in the day. McIntyre shared that it was the non-TV matches where wrestlers practiced their game. “ The talent are finding their feet, especially the younger talent ,” he concluded. McIntyre stressed that panicking during a live broadcast creates an awkward and disjointed feel for everyone involved.

llm_long: WWE wrestler Drew McIntyre has expressed strong dislike for wrestlers who plan their matches from start to finish in advance. He prefers an approach that involves talking briefly with opponents about match length while adapting to the live crowd's reactions during the performance.

McIntyre emphasized that wrestlers should know their craft and go out to listen to the audience rather than follow a fully choreographed script. He noted that crowds in different cities respond differently, making pre-planned matches risky if the audience does not react as expected.

According to McIntyre, many wrestlers have not developed the ability to improvise effectively. Some performers listen and adjust well, while others panic when things deviate from the plan, leading to awkward and choppy action on live television.

He clarified that he enjoys matches that appear real and physical even if they look somewhat choppy in a natural way. However, obvious miscommunications or hesitation when changing direction during a match make the action look poor.

McIntyre pointed out that the current WWE schedule includes fewer non-televised events compared to the past. These untelevised shows previously allowed talent, especially younger wrestlers, to practice and find their footing in front of live crowds.

title: Kit Wilson Embraces Growth in WWE Singles Run

body: Ever since Pretty Deadly member Elton Prince got injured and went on a hiatus, Kit Wilson reinvented himself and emerged as a popular singles wrestler. Currently in a partnership with The Miz, Wilson recently opened up to Denice Salcedo , where he reflected on the challenges of a singles career. “ It really has been that. It’s been finding myself. Sometimes art imitates life and life art, and as I go through this change on TV, going from a tag team wrestler- and I was only ever a tag team guy, and I was so committed to that- into this singles journey, it really grows you as a person and you kind of mature with it ,” Wilson shared. He further claimed that he has now developed as a man and a performer, and is “better than ever.” Kit Wilson claimed that the singles career has made him grow and look at the hard parts of it. “ Being in a tag team, you have each other and it’s so beneficial, but I think also it can cover up some gaps. You can rely on your partner in a somewhat negative way. That can cover up for you. “ So I’ve had to address that and cover those gaps, and I’m better than ever. It’s been a journey, but I feel like it’s only made me grow as a person. That’s what I’m looking for: growth ,” he finished. While there are no updates on Prince’s return, Wilson is regularly active in the ring and last wrestled Kyoki on the Sept. 11, episode of WWE Main Event. summary_src: Zach Gowen has officially retired from wrestling. Gowen posted to Facebook on Wednesday, expressing his gratitude to the fans who supported him. He also called wrestling for AEW in front of his family the “best moment” of his career.
body: Gowen posted to Facebook on Wednesday, expressing his gratitude to the fans who supported him. He also called wrestling for AEW in front of his family the “best moment” of his career. “My in-ring career has come to an end. Thank you to every promoter who gave me an opportunity to wrestle. I’ve had the privilege of performing for every major company over the past 24 years. Special thank you to the fans for not rejecting me. Pro wrestling provided a direction and outlet for a very lost kid. All I ever wanted to be was a professional wrestler and I accomplished that solely because you accepted me not as a sideshow act but as a legitimate pro wrestler. I’m deeply grateful. The best moment of my career was wrestling for AEW in front of my wife, kids, and parents. That was the cherry on top after burning my career to the ground as a result of my crippling drug addiction then having the opportunity to not only rebuild my life but my passion then sharing that with the world while enjoying every second of it. My victories are not the result of my talents but ultimately the result of God working through others allowing them to pour into and invest in me. I am the luckiest guy in the world.” The match Gowen referenced above was his loss to Ricochet at the AEW Dynamite Beach Break special on May 14, 2025, at the NOW Arena in Hoffman Estates, Illinois. Gowen worked in a production role for Maple Leaf Pro Wrestling at the company’s October 3 Northern Rising pay-per-view from the former Maple Leaf Gardens in Toronto. He had previously wrestled for the company at its August 7 tapings in Windsor, defeating Michael Allen Richard Clark. Gowen’s run with WWE in 2003 and 2004 saw him align with Hulk Hogan’s Mr. America character in a rivalry with Roddy Piper and Sean O’Haire. He was later released from the company in February 2004. title: Mike Bailey cherishes emotional Montreal homecoming

body: Mike Bailey recently reflected on his emotional Montreal homecoming during AEW Redemption. Earlier this year, Bailey participated in and won the AEW International Title number one Contender Ladder match at AEW Redemption. Recently speaking to Wrestling Classic , Bailey reflected on that moment and winning the match in his hometown. “ It was absolutely amazing. Not just the fact that I was back home in the arena that I first went to see pro wrestling, but it’s so much closer than that. And I hope that people realize how tight and close the Quebec wrestling community is.” “ Literally, I remember standing on top of that ladder and seeing in the audience my family, my mother and my cousins and my uncles and aunts had come to see me do pro wrestling for the first time in my life ,” he shared. Bailey added that while he has been wrestling for 20 years, that was the first time his mother ever came to a wrestling match. Seeing his family and close friends meant something special to him, because they didn’t tell and were just there. “ Seeing faces of people from the Quebec wrestling community all over the crowd that I knew personally, not just people that I have met in passing, but people that I know literally in every direction, seeing people that I’m close with and then grabbing that contract that guaranteed me a title shot at Grand Slam was definitely a highlight of my career ,” he finished. Bailey is currently scheduled to participate in the Clockwork Carnage match at AEW WrestleDream 2026 for the World Championship. title: Wren Sinclair Wins Suspicious NXT Title Shot
raw_title: Big Vinny V: Wren Sinclair and a particularly stupid episode of NXT
summary_src: Wren Sinclair was awarded an NXT Women’s Championship match this week because she won a battle royal while suspended. That was the stupidest thing on the show, but hardly the only example of nonsensical booking. Sinclair had been suspended since early September for attacking a referee.
body: Wren Sinclair was awarded an NXT Women’s Championship match this week because she won a battle royal while suspended. That was the stupidest thing on the show, but hardly the only example of nonsensical booking. Sinclair had been suspended since early September for attacking a referee. It seems like a half-dozen worse crimes are committed on NXT every week with no repercussions, but let’s put that aside for now. For the next several weeks, she only appeared on the show one time: working the merchandise booth outside the building. Even that was too much for NXT general manager Robert Stone, who had her escorted off the premises. On the October 6 episode of NXT, a battle royal was held to name a new challenger for NXT Women’s Champion Kelani Jordan. It appeared that Lady Shani from AAA had won after hiding outside the ring for most of the match, but then she unmasked herself to reveal Sinclair. Where was Shani? What happened to her? Nobody knows. Early in the October 13 episode, a backstage segment showed Stone saying that Sinclair should not have been in the battle royal. This seemed to set the stage for the finish of the battle royal to be overturned, but that’s not what happened. Instead, Sinclair got premium promo time in the ring in the middle of the show. She proceeded to spend way too much time talking about what she had done without ever explaining why she was getting away with it. She said she wasn’t sorry for what she had done to Lady Shani, whatever that may have been. She said entering the battle royal was a risk and she would have to live with the consequences if she lost, without explaining why there were no consequences after she won. Finally, she said her victory proved that she did not have to back down anymore. Imagine if other sports were run this way. In the NFL this week, San Francisco’s Dre Greenlaw was suspended for headbutting Seattle’s Ernest Jones on the sideline after a play. (To make things worse, Greenlaw was wearing a helmet, but Jones wasn’t.) To follow NXT’s logic, Greenlaw should just put on a teammate’s uniform and play against Washington this weekend anyway. And if he makes an interception or sack to win the game, that will prove he does not have to back down anymore. The whole situation is too silly to comprehend. Jordan interrupted Sinclair’s promo and pointed out Sinclair cheated to win and never should have been in the battle royal in the first place, and she was refusing to give Sinclair a title match. She was right about everything. She was also the heel. Stone then appeared and lifted Sinclair’s suspension, and after a quick fan poll, he made the Sinclair-Jordan match official for Halloween Havoc. That would be enough stupidity for most wrestling shows, but no other wrestling shows are like NXT. In that same two-hour program, we also had: That last point is key. This was a particularly stupid episode of NXT, but that’s saying a ton—most episodes are barely any smarter than this. So go ahead and watch if you
summary: Wren Sinclair earned an NXT Women's Championship match against Kelani Jordan by winning a battle royal while still under suspension for attacking a referee in early September. She had been largely absent from the show except for one appearance working the merchandise table before being removed from the premises by Robert Stone. On the October 6 episode Sinclair disguised herself as Lady Shani from AAA to win the multi-woman match, leading to further nonsensical booking when Stone's objections the following week resulted in her receiving extended in-ring promo time rather than any reversal.

body: The early reviews for the Street Fighter movie are in, and Cody Rhodes is receiving praise from critics, with many saying he is particularly funny in it. The film itself is currently at a 41% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a 6.1 out of 10 on IMDb. However, several outlets have singled out Rhodes for his performance as Guile. The Hollywood News called Rhodes “a scene-stealing stunner ,” writing: “ Wrestler Cody Rhodes is a scene-stealing stunner as high haired Guile. Rhodes proves himself to have a great talent for comedy and his line delivery is on point. “ The Guardian said that Rhodes is “genuinely funny in the way he barks pleasantries and threats in equal measure.” Entertainment journalist Joseph Deckelmeier also praised Rhodes’ performance, writing on X : “Cody Rhodes steals every scene he’s in, & I genuinely had a blast from beginning to end!” ClutchPoints praised both Rhodes and Reigns, saying that Roman “brings ‘OTC’ energy to Akuma.” The outlet also said that Rhodes was the biggest surprise in the film, writing that his “first couple of lines will shock any WWE fans who only know him from his work in the squared circle.” The Associated Press was particularly negative on the film, giving it one star out of four and calling it “a complete mess.” Reviews of Rhodes’ performance posted to social media are available below. body: If Adam Copeland is going to wrestle at the Tokyo Dome before his career is done, AEW head Tony Khan isn’t giving any answers as to whether that is going to happen…but didn’t say it won’t. During Thursday’s pre-WrestleDream media call, Khan was asked about Copeland’s recent comments about wanting to wrestle in the famed stadium before his career ends and Khan said he was definitely aware of that desire but that he would leave those conversations between himself, NJPW booker Gedo and Copeland. In August, Copeland said he had some “great white whales” he was pursuing in terms of venues he had never worked in: Arena Mexico, Wembley Stadium, Maple Leaf Gardens and the Tokyo Dome. He checked off the box for the first three already with the possibility of appearing at January’s Wrestle Kingdom seeming like more of a reality. On Wednesday’s Dynamite, Copeland revealed that 2027 will be his final year in wrestling .
summary: AEW president Tony Khan acknowledged Adam Copeland's desire to wrestle at the Tokyo Dome but declined to give details on any potential plans. Khan stated he would discuss the matter privately with Copeland and NJPW's Gedo. title: Vince McMahon reckless driving charges dismissed
raw_title: Vince McMahon’s reckless driving case reaches its conclusion
summary_src: The reckless driving charges against former WWE chairman Vince McMahon stemming from a July 2025 car accident have reportedly been dismissed. According to Connecticut State Police, McMahon rear-ended a BMW driven by Barbara Doran while driving his Bentley on July 24, 2025.
body: The reckless driving charges against former WWE chairman Vince McMahon stemming from a July 2025 car accident have reportedly been dismissed. According to Connecticut State Police, McMahon rear-ended a BMW driven by Barbara Doran while driving his Bentley on July 24, 2025. A state trooper had been attempting to pull McMahon over for speeding moments before the crash. In October 2025, a judge approved McMahon’s application for a one-year accelerated rehabilitation program , which would lead to the charges being dismissed on October 15, 2026, provided McMahon complied with certain conditions. According to the Stamford Advocate , those conditions required McMahon to make a $1,000 charitable contribution, drive only while properly licensed and insured, and stay out of further legal trouble during the one-year period. A disposition was scheduled for 9 a.m. on Thursday, October 15, 2026. While the court docket is statutorily sealed, PWInsider reports that the charges against McMahon have now been officially dismissed. title: Rebel Named First Honorary Board Member of I AM ALS
raw_title: Rebel named first honorary board member of I AM ALS
summary_src: Rebel (Tanea Brooks) is taking on an additional role as she continues her advocacy work for I AM ALS. The non-profit group issued a press release today announcing that Rebel has been named the very first honorary member of its board of directors.
body: Rebel (Tanea Brooks) is taking on an additional role as she continues her advocacy work for I AM ALS. The non-profit group issued a press release today announcing that Rebel has been named the very first honorary member of its board of directors. She first joined I AM ALS this summer, and AEW has donated money to the organization through its Rebel Heart fundraising efforts. I AM ALS is a patient-led group that is “accelerating a cure for ALS by mobilizing collective power to drive urgent policy and systems change.” In her honorary board member role, Rebel will “continue to elevate her story, lived experience, and platform to I AM ALS’s mission and activate fans nationwide to take action on behalf of people living with ALS.” “Advocacy for ALS is a major priority in my battle,” Rebel said. “And I plan to continue to fight the good fight with I AM ALS to find a cure and help others get access to treatment.” Rebel announced her ALS (amyotrophic lateral sclerosis) diagnosis this May following a long health battle where doctors could not fully figure out what was causing her issues. The terminal neurodegenerative disease does not currently have a cure, but organizations like I AM ALS are fighting for a future where lifespans will be extended and a cure will eventually be found. Rebel and I AM ALS successfully advocated for a congressional act that would expand access to investigational therapies. “Tanea turned a devastating moment into immediate action, calling us soon after her diagnosis to join the movement,” I AM ALS CEO Andrea Goodman said. “She uses her platform, humor, vulnerability and unwavering honesty to make people pay attention, and take action. Welcoming ‘Rebel’ to our Board as Congress reauthorizes ACT for ALS is a powerful reflection of what she has helped us achieve and what this movement is built on: collective power and visibility of the very people living with the disease.” Last month, AEW celebrated Rebel with a special “Rebel Heart” Dynamite episode where she appeared and took part in the event. One silver lining in such an awful situation is that Rebel has been able to see how much people love her and care about her. “The greatest thing ALS has given me is to be able to see how much people care and love and support me before I am gone,” she told WDRB News this summer . Dave Meltzer and Bryan Alvarez discussed the latest on the situation on Thursday’s edition of Wrestling Observer Radio. “They will not even publicly say that there’s a backup plan, there is, but they can’t publicly say it because if they publicly say it, it sounds like they’re wavering on going. And they can’t have that out because then the Saudis and Turki will be very upset at them for having that out. That’s why no one talks about the idea of a backup plan, and they deny it. But to not have a backup plan, you would have to be incompetent, and if there is anything that the people that run WWE are, incompetent is not one of those things.” Ian Carey Ian Carey is the Managing Editor at F4WOnline and is based in Toronto, Ontario, Canada. title: Kojima can earn NJPW Junior Title Shot with Weight Stipulation
raw_title: Satoshi Kojima could earn NJPW Junior Heavyweight title shot in unique stipulation
summary_src: Satoshi Kojima has been a very successful heavyweight throughout his NJPW career, and he now has the chance to earn a shot at his first junior heavyweight gold.
body: Satoshi Kojima has been a very successful heavyweight throughout his NJPW career, and he now has the chance to earn a shot at his first junior heavyweight gold. NJPW has announced that Kojima will face off against IWGP Junior Heavyweight Champion YOH at Taichi’s Old School Pro-Wrestling 2 this Saturday (October 17). It’s a non-title match but comes with the unique stipulation where, if Kojima makes weight for the bout and then goes on to defeat YOH, he’ll earn a future shot at the Junior Heavyweight Championship. This is the second consecutive year that NJPW has held the Taichi-produced Old School event. It’s taking place from Taichi’s former junior high school in Ishikari City Hokkaido and will air live on NJPW World as a pay-per-view ($22.99 price). There will be live Japanese commentary for the PPV, with English commentary being added later on-demand. After a back and forth with Taichi over whether he’d actually be able to lose the weight, Kojima joked that, while trying to go without snacks is tough, he’s doing exercises at 10 times the usual intensity . YOH won this year’s Best of the Super Juniors tournament and went on to defeat DOUKI for the IWGP Junior Heavyweight Championship. His most recent title defense was a victory over Robbie Eagles at King of Pro Wrestling. title: Indie Wrestler Cauliflower Chase Brown Dies at 41
raw_title: Indie wrestler ‘Cauliflower’ Chase Brown passes away at 41
summary_src: The wrestling world is mourning another tragic loss with indie wrestler “Cauliflower” Chase Brown passing away at 41. Brown’s passing was announced on Wednesday, though the circumstances of his death have not been reported.
body: The wrestling world is mourning another tragic loss with indie wrestler “Cauliflower” Chase Brown passing away at 41. Brown’s passing was announced on Wednesday, though the circumstances of his death have not been reported. He was based out of the Carolina region and had past experience for ROH (both in the ring and working on ring crew). Aside from wrestling, Brown was passionate about music and philosophy. He is survived by his wife and their young daughter. The “Aria of Babyface Cauliflower Brown” mini-documentary mentioned by Carolina Wrestling Channel was uploaded by the New York Times in 2017, with Brown detailing how storytelling in pro wrestling is just like any other medium. “There’s very real things that are going on in professional wrestling,” Brown said. “A lot of people want to be like, ‘Oh, well that’s just a fake sport.’ It’s not a fake sport. It’s a form of storytelling, no better or worse than any other form of storytelling.” Cheeseburger, who spent some time working with Brown at ROH shows in the 2010s, posted a tribute on Instagram and shared how happy everyone on ring crew was when Brown finally got to have his first match for the promotion. He noted that Brown’s “Cauliflower” nickname was given to him by Terry Funk due to his cauliflower ear: Willow Nightingale remembered Brown as a “sweet, sweet human” but said she only got to meet him a small handful of times. “It’s a story about how things ought to be,” Brown said about pro wrestling in the New York Times doc. “I’m speaking to what wrestling can be, not necessarily what it always is. But I think that’s true of pretty much any art form. It’s as good or as bad as we make it.” Joseph Currier Joseph Currier is a graduate of the University of Massachusetts, obtaining a journalism degree in 2016. Joseph joined F4W during his time at UMass and has now been writing about the industry for nearly a decade. In addition to his work with F4W, Joseph has previously contributed to Sports Illustrated's wrestling coverage. He lives in Massachusetts and is a diehard fan of the Boston sports teams and Liverpool Football Club.

title: Kaitlyn Recalls Unhappy 2014 WWE Exit
raw_title: Kaitlyn discusses WWE exit in 2014 : ‘I just wanted to be done’
summary_src: Former WWE star Kaitlyn opened up about the circumstances that led to her decision to part ways with the company in 2014. Kaitlyn recalled informing Mark Carano, the former VP of Talent Relations, about requesting for her WWE release.
body: Former WWE star Kaitlyn opened up about the circumstances that led to her decision to part ways with the company in 2014. “It was in Baltimore, and funny enough, Baltimore was where I debuted. Now, being in Baltimore, the day that I asked for my release, it was like this horrible travel day. I didn’t even get travel that week. Someone knew in Talent Relations, they weren’t going to bring me to TV, and I’m like, ‘Oh my God!’ I had reached out to Tom, that writer, and I was like, ‘I’m not booked for TV this weekend.’ You always want to just be at TV because you never know if they’re going to write you in. I didn’t get travel, and so he pulled some strings, and I got travel literally last minute, and it was January in Baltimore, and so it was a snowstorm, and it was the most horrific time getting there.” “Finally got there, and I obviously wasn’t on the show, wasn’t booked. I looked around and I was like, ‘Oh my god, I debuted here, and it was this full circle moment’. And kind of gave me this permission, because I had been thinking about it, asking for my release, because I was so unhappy. They told me. I went to Talent Relations, and Mark Carano was sitting there, and I told him. He’s like, ‘Okay, can you sleep on it?’ I was like, okay. I think SmackDown was in Philly or somewhere, and they were like, sleep on it. I think he had gone to talk to Hunter, and that was the kind of feedback. I did, and I felt horrible and awful the next day. But still, I was standing by my decision, and I didn’t tell anybody. I didn’t even tell AJ, and I was really close with Big E then too. We were very, very good friends.” “I didn’t tell anybody because I didn’t want it to be a big deal. I just wanted to leave. I just wanted to be done, and that is one of the things I kind of regretted because I cared about a lot of people there, but I needed to remove myself. I just needed space, so I didn’t tell anybody. Then of course, a lot of people knew the next day, the writers knew, and everybody essentially knew.” Kaitlyn recalls being ‘sick to her stomach’ on day of final WWE match- In the same interaction, Kaitlyn revealed that she had not even informed her friends AJ Lee and Big E of her plans to leave WWE. She recalled feeling sick to her stomach during her Main Event match against Lee in 2014. “They gave me one last match, it was on Main Event, and it was against AJ. I don’t even remember the match, but I was so sick to my stomach all day, and AJ of course was very upset, and she was trying to be supportive and her and Tamina were kind of paired up at that time. So we had the match and then I just took a really brutal super kick to the face from Tamina and that was it. I hated it because I felt so sick, and I just wanted to leave, and I was sad. It was just this amalgamation; it wasn’t good.” Rosanne Raphael Rosanne Raphael is a wrestling writer with over three and a half years of experience covering all things related to the industry. title: WWE upset over staff voicing Saudi travel fears
raw_title: WWE unhappy some employees voiced concerns about going to Crown Jewel in Saudi Arabia | Exclusive
summary_src: WWE is said to be unhappy that some of its non-wrestling employees have expressed concerns about traveling to Saudi Arabia for Crown Jewel amid the ongoing security situation in the region.
body: WWE is said to be unhappy that some of its non-wrestling employees have expressed concerns about traveling to Saudi Arabia for Crown Jewel amid the ongoing security situation in the region. Online reports suggest some WWE employees have expressed reluctance to travel to Saudi Arabia on social media, although the original posts have not been independently verified. Speaking on Thursday’s Wrestling Observer Radio , Dave Meltzer discussed WWE’s reaction to employees making their concerns known. “I heard that WWE wasn’t thrilled that some of the employees, non-wrestlers, did actually talk about not wanting to go because they want that united front. And not one wrestler said a word, which doesn’t surprise me because if they did, there would be repercussions. It’d be stupid to do so. It’s not your fight. But I would expect that they can’t be thrilled about this.” Meltzer also addressed Bryan Alvarez’s report from earlier this week that WWE has a backup U.S. location under consideration should Crown Jewel need to be moved. “They will not even publicly say that there’s a backup plan, there is, but they can’t publicly say it because if they publicly say it, it sounds like they’re wavering on going. And they can’t have that out because then the Saudis and Turki will be very upset at them for having that out. That’s why no one talks about the idea of a backup plan, and they deny it. But to not have a backup plan, you would have to be incompetent, and if there is anything that the people that run WWE are, incompetent is not one of those things.” WWE has not announced any changes to its plans for Crown Jewel, which remains scheduled for November 7 in Riyadh. However, the Six Kings Slam 2026 tennis tournament, which was scheduled to take place in Riyadh from October 21 to 24, has been postponed until December 27-30. Saudi official Turki Alalshikh stated that the postponement was due to “organizational and logistical challenges,” but did not mention the ongoing conflict in the region. However, Alalshikh has said that the scheduled boxing match between Canelo Alvarez and Christian Mbilli will take place on Saturday, October 31 in Riyadh as planned. He joined the F4WOnline team in 2019 and was named Managing Editor in the summer of 2026. Born in Calgary, Alberta, Ian has covered professional wrestling for more than 15 years.
summary: WWE is unhappy that several non-wrestling employees have publicly expressed reluctance to travel to Saudi Arabia for Crown Jewel due to the current regional security situation. No wrestlers have commented on the matter, which the company views as maintaining a united front. WWE has an internal backup U.S. venue prepared if the event must be relocated but refuses to acknowledge it publicly to avoid upsetting Saudi officials.

title: ESPN Leaves Roman Reigns Off College Football-Wrestling Graphic Despite Georgia Tech Career
raw_title: ESPN Leaves Roman Reigns Off College Football-Wrestling Graphic Despite Georgia Tech Career
summary_src: ESPN decided to mix college football and pro wrestling over the weekend, but one massive WWE name was nowhere to be found — Roman Reigns. During its college football coverage, ESPN aired a graphic spotlighting notable professional wrestlers who also played college football.
body: 蝶 Connect with us on Bluesky → ESPN decided to mix college football and pro wrestling over the weekend, but one massive WWE name was nowhere to be found — Roman Reigns. During its college football coverage, ESPN aired a graphic spotlighting notable professional wrestlers who also played college football. The list included Ron Simmons, “Stone Cold” Steve Austin, Dwayne “The Rock” Johnson, Bill Goldberg and Bron Breakker. Reigns, who played defensive tackle at Georgia Tech before becoming one of WWE’s biggest stars, somehow didn’t make the cut. That omission didn’t exactly go unnoticed. Wrestling fans quickly started questioning how ESPN could put together a list like that and leave out the current WWE World Heavyweight Champion, especially considering Reigns had a much more accomplished college football career than some of the names who actually appeared on the graphic. One fan summed up the reaction pretty clearly. “I am not even going to ask why ESPN could not make room for WWE’s current World Champion Roman Reigns (Georgia Tech) on the list.” The reaction makes sense when you look at Reigns’ history. Before WWE ever called him The Tribal Chief, Leati Joseph Anoa’i was a three-year starter at Georgia Tech and earned First Team All-ACC honors during his senior season. His football career eventually took him through brief stops with the Minnesota Vikings and Jacksonville Jaguars before he played in the Canadian Football League and ultimately moved on from the sport. Reigns has never treated that chapter of his life like some throwaway footnote either. He previously admitted that he probably would have chosen football over professional wrestling if his career on the field had gone differently . While discussing what he originally wanted out of his athletic career, Reigns explained just how seriously he viewed football at the time. “I wanted to have an impact on young men. I wanted to be the way Emmitt Smith and Michael Jordan and Joe Montana and the stars of when I was a child, the way they made me feel. I wanted to make other young athletes feel that way. But no matter what, it was either you’re going to be a wrestler, or you’re going to be a football player. A superstar of some sort.” WWE has also leaned directly into Reigns’ Georgia Tech history before. In 2024, the company filmed Roman Reigns and Cody Rhodes at Georgia Tech ahead of WWE Bad Blood , turning Reigns’ old football stomping grounds into part of one of WWE’s biggest storylines at the time. That makes ESPN’s omission even stranger considering the network’s growing WWE connection. ESPN is now part of WWE’s Premium Live Event ecosystem, and Reigns was just featured prominently at Money in the Bank, where he defeated LA Knight to retain the World Heavyweight Championship . title: Injury Update: Rey Fénix Still Dealing With Effects of Serious Hip Injury
raw_title: Rey Fénix Still Dealing With Effects of Serious Hip Injury
summary_src: Rey Fénix has put his body through plenty over the years, but there’s one injury that still forces him to take extra care of himself every single day.
body: 蝶 Connect with us on Bluesky → Rey Fénix has put his body through plenty over the years, but there’s one injury that still forces him to take extra care of himself every single day. The WWE star revealed that a serious right hip injury was the worst he’s ever suffered, and if he doesn’t constantly stretch and warm it up, things can get painful enough that even walking becomes uncomfortable. Speaking on his YouTube channel , Fénix opened up about the damage he’s accumulated throughout his wrestling career. His list includes fractures, ligament issues and multiple dislocations, but none of them compared to what happened to his hip. “I’ve had some injuries — to me, they’re many, right? Because I would love to tell you, ‘Oh, no, I’ve never been injured.’ I think there are very few lucky wrestlers who can say they haven’t been hurt or haven’t suffered an accident. But the first one that comes to mind quickly from the beginning of my career is that I fractured the instep of my right leg. That’s, more or less, the first one. Later, I fractured the tibia of my left leg. I took a very hard hit to my right knee. It didn’t become a huge problem, but basically the ligaments were overextended, so to speak.” That wasn’t the end of the list either. Fénix also dealt with a dislocated elbow and shoulder before getting to the injury he considers the worst of them all. “So, to regain that strength in the ligaments and muscles of my knee again, it took quite a while. I dislocated my left elbow, I dislocated my right shoulder, and the most painful and strongest one I can tell you about was in my hip — my right hip.” The hip injury happened during one of the high-risk dives Fénix has become known for. He landed completely on the right side of his body, causing serious problems with the cartilage where his hip and leg meet. “I had a very bad fall. I did a dive to the outside and landed completely on the entire right side of my body, specifically the hip. That led me to have very serious problems with the cartilage that is in the junction of my hip and leg. And it was very hard for me to recover from that injury.” Fénix says he doesn’t consider the hip actively injured anymore, but that doesn’t mean the problem has completely disappeared. He now has to stretch as soon as he wakes up and again before going to bed because the muscles around the area remain extremely sensitive. “That is why today the first thing I do when I wake up is stretch, and before sleeping is to stretch, because the muscles in my hip were left so sensitive that, if I don’t warm them up, if I don’t stretch them, two or three days can pass and my muscles start to atrophy, and then this flexibility problem arrives.” And if Rey Fénix gets lazy about that routine for even a couple of days, he definitely notices it. body: 蝶 Connect with us on Bluesky → Kamille is still under AEW contract, but you wouldn’t know it by watching the company’s television lately. Pasted text Kamille made her AEW return at Dynasty on April 12, 2026, attacking Willow Nightingale backstage before defeating Big Anne on the Zero Hour pre-show. Ringside News covered her return at the time after she had been missing from AEW television since November 2024. That comeback didn’t last long. Her most recent AEW match took place just three days later on the April 15 episode of Dynamite, where Willow Nightingale defeated Kamille in an AEW TBS Championship match. Kamille has wrestled only once since then. Her latest match anywhere took place for Diamond Championship Wrestling, where Bobbi Thunder defeated her on DCW Synergy 2026 #17. The match aired on August 25 from the Bullet Bob Armstrong Memorial Arena in Theodore, Alabama. Cagematch notes that the exact taping date is unknown, but August 25 was the broadcast date. Kamille returned with a ready-made feud against Willow Nightingale, but that was never designed to launch her into another lengthy run on television. “There was never a long term plan for her after she was taken off TV for the Mercedes angle ever.
