title: Tatum Paxley Defends WWE Signing Athletes Without Indie Experience
raw_title: Tatum Paxley Defends WWE Signing Athletes Without Indie Experience
summary_src: Tatum Paxley knows there are wrestling fans who aren’t exactly thrilled about WWE signing athletes who never spent years grinding on the independent scene. But if anyone expects that criticism to bother her, Paxley says they’re wasting their time.
body: 蝶 Connect with us on Bluesky → Tatum Paxley knows there are wrestling fans who aren’t exactly thrilled about WWE signing athletes who never spent years grinding on the independent scene. But if anyone expects that criticism to bother her, Paxley says they’re wasting their time. Speaking to Complex Graps , Paxley was asked about her unusual path into WWE. She didn’t arrive after years of wrestling on the indies or even as someone who had spent her entire life dreaming about becoming a wrestler, instead coming from a competitive powerlifting background. That’s become increasingly common in NXT, where WWE has recruited athletes from a variety of sports and trained them from scratch. It has also led to criticism from some fans who believe those recruits haven’t “paid their dues” in the same way wrestlers who spent years on the independent circuit did. Paxley understands that conversation exists, but she doesn’t walk around feeling like she has something to prove because of it. She believes anyone who doesn’t genuinely fall in love with professional wrestling probably isn’t going to make it very far anyway. “Yeah. I wouldn’t say I have a chip on my shoulder. I understand why people—I don’t understand why they have it out for me, you know? Because, to me, you really only get far if you have a genuine love for the business, you know? Because you can tell if somebody’s not happy here, you know? And if you’re not happy here, then, you know, you’re welcome to go elsewhere.” As far as Paxley is concerned, the success of WWE’s athlete recruits speaks for itself. She believes the people who stick around and start succeeding are doing so because they’ve developed a real passion for wrestling, regardless of what brought them through the door in the first place. “So, when you see, you know, these Superstars getting the success that they’re getting, it’s because they found the love for the business. And I think if you love something, you want to share that love with other people.” And when it comes to fans who are still angry that people like her didn’t come through the indies, Paxley isn’t losing any sleep over it. She’s happy with where she is and loves what she’s doing, which is ultimately all she cares about. “So, I mean, people, you know, can get mad. It doesn’t really bother me that much. I’m happy. I love what I do, and that’s all that matters.” Paxley isn’t arguing that everyone has to take the same road into wrestling. Her point is that how someone gets through the door matters a lot less than whether they actually fall in love with the business once they’re there. There have been many incidents when a match finish has not gone to plan, leading to some unexpected moments. Something similar happened during an episode of WWE RAW in 2012. A Divas battle royal was held to determine the number one contender for the Divas Championship, held by Layla. Eva Torres was supposed to win the match, but a botched ending saw Kaitlyn win the battle royal. During a recent appearance on INSIGHT with Chris Van Vliet , Kaitlyn detailed what happened and the aftermath of the situation. She revealed how she was supposed to last till the end, but Eve would eliminate her. However, the ending didn't go as planned. Kaitlyn was supposed to clothesline Eve and send her over the top rope. But the plan was for Eve to hang on and eliminate her opponent. However, things didn't go to plan. Kaitlyn said this left everyone surprised, and the referee was asked to raise her hand. However, the former WWE Divas Champion was left fearing the botch could get her fired. Kaitlyn said when she headed backstage, she saw Eve was upset, but Vince was laughing. Kaitlyn joined WWE in 2010 and started her run on NXT. Her early run on the brand saw her be a part of an infamous match. She faced fellow NXT talent Maxine, and both of them had their respective mentors in their corner. Kaitlyn was mentored by Vickie Guerrero, and Maxine had Alicia Fox accompany her. The match was widely panned by the fans and saw many botches with a clear lack of chemistry between the two stars. During the contest, Michael Cole repeatedly criticized the match on commentary and even took a phone call on air. Speaking on INSIGHT about the segment, Kaitlyn said both she and her opponent were not experienced but said Michael Cole took things really far with his actions . The star returned to the Stamford-based promotion in 2024 and has been competing on the NXT brand. Shawn Spears recently returned to action during NXT house shows, and his recent outing saw him compete in an eight-man tag team match in a live event. He teamed up with Shiloh Hill, Tavon Heights, and Tony D'Angelo to beat Birthright in the main event. The show was held in Kitchener, Ontario. Following the match, Spears talked about his time in the business, thanked the crowd and acknowledged that it could be his last time competing in Canada. Spears initially joined WWE in 2013 and began competing under the name Tye Dillinger. After a run as a tag team wrestler, he branched into singles competition and began his "Perfect 10" gimmick. He was soon called up to the main roster and joined SmackDown. On the blue brand, he feuded with Aiden English and also challenged AJ Styles for the US championship. Spears was released in 2019 and joined AEW in the same year. Spears was part of MJF's The Pinnacle faction and feuded with some top names. He eventually left the promotion in 2023. Shawn Spears' last televised match in WWE came on the July 21 episode of NXT. He faced The Culling's Niko Vance and won the match after a disqualification. Since then, he has been absent from programming with no update on his status. Earlier this month, Mike Johnson of PWInsider shared what Spears has been up to amid his absence. During a Q&A, Johnson was asked why Spears' story with The Culling was dropped abruptly. Johnson said that Shawn Spears is still with NXT and assists with coaching. Before the eight-man tag team match in Ontario, Spears also teamed up with Saquon Shugars to beat Niko Vance and Tristan Angels at a NXT house show in Jacksonville, Florida.

Ex-WWE star gets major honor Discuss Now Former WWE star Tanea Brooks has been given another major platform in her ongoing battle against ALS. On October 15, patient advocacy organization I AM ALS announced that Brooks had been named the first Honorary Member of its Board of Directors, according to a press release from PR Newswire . Tanea Brooks' ring name is Rebel. This comes after she joined the group as an ambassador in June, following her terminal diagnosis in May. In her new leadership role, Rebel will continue leveraging her wrestling platform to drive public awareness, fight for treatment accessibility, and push for a cure. The ex-WWE star emphasizes that this remains a priority in her journey and commitment to fight the good fight alongside the organization. I AM ALS CEO Andrea Goodman praised Brooks for transforming a devastating personal experience into immediate, impactful action that has inspired others to get involved. Rebel's time in WWE was brief, and she was not signed to a contract. She teamed up with Amber Nova in a tag team match against Io Shirai (now Iyo Sky) and Kairi Sane during an NXT television taping, and that was her only match there. This was during the time Triple H was in charge of the developmental brand. The wrestling community has come together to raise funds through AEW's Rebel Heart merchandise line, which benefits I AM ALS and Team Gleason, an organization founded by former NFL star Steve Gleason, who was also diagnosed with ALS. After her stint in WWE, she joined AEW in a backstage role as the hair-and-makeup stylist. Then she appeared on screen as Britt Baker's assistant and began wrestling, too. AEW dedicated the September 9 edition of AEW Dynamite in Rebel's honor. The show, which took place at Akins Ford Arena in Athens, Georgia, opened with Britt Baker hosting The Waiting Room alongside Rebel, commending her co-host's strength and resilience. AEW also presented a tribute video celebrating Rebel's career and honoring her work in the fight against ALS.

title: Cook County sheriff's officer sues WWE, wrestler over alleged unwanted lap dance during Raw
raw_title: Cook County sheriff's officer sues WWE, wrestler over alleged unwanted lap dance during Raw
body: CHICAGO - A Cook County sheriff’s officer is suing WWE, wrestler Montez Ford and an event production company, alleging he was subjected to unwanted sexualized contact while working security at a live wrestling event. Noel Lucas filed the lawsuit Wednesday in Cook County Circuit Court. The complaint says he was working an off-duty security job at WWE Monday Night Raw on July 6 at Allstate Arena in Rosemont. According to the lawsuit, Lucas was seated at his assigned post outside the ring when Ford, whose legal name is Kenneth Crawford, approached him, straddled him and began moving his hips in a sexually suggestive way. Lucas’ attorneys say he was not told he would be part of the performance and did not consent. Live announcers on the Netflix broadcast allegedly mocked Lucas in real time, telling viewers, "That guy clearly hates fun," and comparing him to Paul Blart, the fictional security guard from "Paul Blart: Mall Cop." "Mr. Lucas was there to do his job, not to be made a part of WWE’s entertainment," attorney Whitney Barr said in a statement. The incident aired live on Netflix. The lawsuit says WWE later shared video of it on TikTok and Instagram, where it received more than 300,000 views. Ford also shared footage, according to the lawsuit. The complaint says Lucas, who has roughly 24 years of law enforcement experience, was later mocked at work, while his children were ridiculed at school because of the videos. The complaint includes 14 counts, including battery, assault, intentional infliction of emotional distress and claims under Illinois’ Gender Violence Act and Right of Publicity Act. "Entertainment is not a defense to unwanted sexual contact," Barr said. "We intend to hold WWE and those responsible accountable for what happened to Mr. Lucas and for the harm caused by the subsequent publication of the footage." FOX Chicago has reached out to WWE for comment, but the company had not responded as of publication. The Source: The information in this story came from Chicago-based law firm Caffarelli & Martin Ltd. and Cook County court documents.
summary: CHICAGO - A Cook County sheriff’s officer is suing WWE, wrestler Montez Ford and an event production company. He was working an off-duty security job at WWE Monday Night Raw on July 6 at Allstate Arena in Rosemont, The complaint says.

title: WWE Reportedly Cooling Off Gunther Push
raw_title: Internal WWE Fears Growing About Gunther? Major Report Emerges
body: Last year was another big one for the Austrian star. After 2023 and 2024 were spent turning him into a main event player in the company, last year was used to turn him into one of the most fearsome and hated men on the roster. The company did that by having Gunther send some of WWE's most beloved stars home forever. In July, he was the man who put Goldberg to sleep in his final match in front of friends and family in his adopted home of Atlanta, GA. The company then took things to another level in December when Gunther made John Cena quit in his retirement match. Yet that wasn't where his reign of retirement terror ended. In January at the Royal Rumble in Saudi Arabia, AJ Styles put his career on the line in a match against the two-time World Heavyweight champion. That was a bad decision, as the "Phenomenal One" was the latest legend who was put to sleep and sent into retirement. The expectation was that after such a strong push in the second half of 2025, this year would be another big one for Gunther. However, it hasn't been, as he has suffered some surprising losses and has had trouble securing an opportunity at the WWE Championship on SmackDown. The company has randomly pulled back on his push as a top star, and it has confused some fans. Well, it seems they aren't the only ones. According to a new report from Wrestle Votes, via Fightful Select, " there's been a mild sense of frustration and confusion surrounding the recent use of Gunther on SmackDown." A source told the industry insider that Gunther's current direction has raised questions among those in creative, especially considering the trajectory he was on following his string of retirements. Per Emmanuel Morgan of the New York Times , Rhodes' extension is a five-year contract. It's unclear how much time Rhodes had left on his previous deal, but the five-year timeline ensures he will remain with WWE at least into 2031. Rhodes specifically mentioning not falling down for a living when his daughter is 11 would seem to indicate this new contract will be his last one as an in-ring competitor. The 41-year-old Rhodes returned to WWE in 2022 after helping establish AEW when it launched in 2019. He has won the undisputed WWE title three times since making his comeback and has been featured in the WrestleMania main event every year since 2023.

title: WWE Stands By Crown Jewel Plans Despite Saudi Conflict
raw_title: Backstage Update On WWE Promoting Crown Jewel For Saudi Arabia Amid Armed Conflict
body: Frazer Harrison/Getty Images Add Wrestling Inc. on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover After some uncertainty thanks to the ongoing armed conflict in Saudi Arabia, WWE made clear on Monday that they were still planning on holding Crown Jewel in Riyadh next month. It's a decision that has raised eyebrows, and one that Dave Meltzer believes may have been made thanks to some outside pressure. On Monday's "Wrestling Observer Radio," Meltzer and co-host Garrett Gonzalez were discussing a tweet sent by Saudi's General Entertainment Authority director Turki Al-Sheikh , which was seemingly directed just at Canelo Alvarez coming to the country for a boxing match, but one Meltzer thinks was directed towards WWE as well. "In WWE, when that tweet came out, they knew it was a message for them too," Meltzer said. "I mean...it's a real tough thing. And this is obviously going to be Ari Emanuel's decision. This is way over Nick Khan's head...I'm sure it won't be without Nick Khan's input. But that's...it's a really tough decision, because they shouldn't go. We all know that. It's too dangerous." Meltzer pointed out that the United States State Department and Travel Advisory had also advised against anyone traveling to Saudi Arabia for the time. Even still, Meltzer believes that the money WWE is being paid and Al-Sheikh's desire for them to put on the show would ultimately be prioritized over anything else, pointing out that WWE's parent company, TKO, was beholden to Al-Sheikh due to his funding of TKO's Zuffa Boxing . As a result, Meltzer thinks WWE will exhaust any option to get there, even if many people within the company are against the idea. "If there is anyway they can go, they're going to go," Meltzer said. "And it's going to be very interesting because the families of the talents, I'm sure, are not going to be happy. The talent probably isn't going to be happy. The backstage people, I know, aren't happy." If you use any of the quotes in this article, please credit "Wrestling Observer Radio" and provide a h/t to Wrestling Inc. for the transcription

title: WWE's Montez Ford Sued for Alleged Lap Dance on Security Guard
raw_title: WWE star Montez Ford sued over alleged ‘sexualized lap dance’ on Illinois security guard during live broadcast
body: An Illinois security guard alleged that WWE star Montez Ford performed a “sexualized lap dance” on him during a live Netflix broadcast of “Monday Night Raw.” Noel Lucas accused Ford, whose real name is Kenneth Crawford, and the WWE of assault, battery, intentional infliction of emotional distress and other claims, according to the lawsuit filed on Wednesday, which was obtained by Post Wrestling and confirmed by The Post. Lucas alleged the incident unfolded as Ford and his Street Profits tag team partner, Angelo Dawkins , made their entrance before their televised match at Allstate Arena in Rosemont, Ill. on July 6. Lucas, an officer with the Cook County Sheriff’s Department who was working off-duty security at the event, claimed Ford approached him without warning or consent and began dancing in a “sexually provocative” manner. “Defendant Crawford then began performing a sexually provocative dance immediately in front of and over Plaintiff [Lucas], repeatedly thrusting and gyrating his hips and pelvis towards Plaintiff, performing a sexualized ‘lap dance,’” the lawsuit, filed in the Circuit Court of Cook County, stated. Lucas alleges Ford moved increasingly closer to Lucas as the dance continued and that his “left inner thigh repeatedly rubbed against Plaintiff’s leg.” The lawsuit alleges 14 counts, including violations of the Illinois Gender Violence Act. Ford is seen intently thrusting his hips and dancing over Lucas, who appears uncomfortable and initially looks away before eventually cracking a smile, according to fan footage. The July 6 episode of “Raw” drew an estimated 12,500 fans at Allstate Arena and recorded 2.5 million global views on Netflix over seven days, according to Wrestlenomics data reported by “Wrestling Inc.” The episode currently available on Netflix appears to cut away early during the Street Profits’ entrance, leaving out the interaction described in the lawsuit. Lucas claimed footage of the encounter spread across social media, drawing hundreds of thousands of views, including on WWE’s and Ford’s own accounts. The alleged fallout continued the following day when Lucas returned to his full-time job at a courthouse. “Members of the public recognized him from the videos of the encounter that had circulated on social media and mocked him, thrusting their hips in his direction, imitating the sexual movements” allegedly performed during the broadcast, the lawsuit stated. title: Will Riyadh Airport Attacks Force a Change? — WWE Crown Jewel
raw_title: WWE Crown Jewel: Will Riyadh Airport Attacks Force a Change?
body: WWE Crown Jewel remains scheduled for Riyadh on November 7, but a series of attacks on the Saudi capital’s King Khalid International Airport has raised serious questions about whether the event will go ahead as planned. WWE has not announced a cancellation or a change of location, although recent reports suggest the situation is being discussed internally. The attacks have intensified concerns just weeks before WWE is due to stage one of its major international premium live events in Saudi Arabia. With the airport struck repeatedly and new threats issued against the country’s aviation infrastructure, the question is no longer simply whether Crown Jewel will proceed, but whether WWE can safely maintain its plans. WWE and Saudi Arabia’s General Entertainment Authority announced on September 1 that Crown Jewel would take place at Riyadh Season Stadium at KAFD on Saturday, November 7. The event is expected to feature champion-versus-champion matches in both the men’s and women’s divisions. WWE’s official announcement continues to list Riyadh as the host city. As of October 12, however, neither WWE nor its parent company, TKO Group Holdings, has publicly announced a change to the date or venue. That means Crown Jewel remains on the calendar, even as the security situation creates uncertainty around the event. The distinction matters. Reports of internal concern do not amount to an official postponement, and there is no confirmed replacement venue or revised date at this stage. The immediate concern is the repeated targeting of King Khalid International Airport. Saudi authorities reported that an attack on October 10 killed at least 12 people and injured hundreds. A further strike on Sunday, October 11, killed one person and injured 11 others, according to reporting published by Al Jazeera on Monday. Airport operations were disrupted as authorities assessed damage and safety conditions. The Iran-backed Houthi group in Yemen has claimed responsibility for earlier attacks and issued a new warning against using Saudi airports and airspace, according to Wrestling Observer reporting. The warning adds another layer of concern for an international event that would require wrestlers, staff, production crews and travelling fans to reach Riyadh. The airport attacks do not establish that the Crown Jewel venue itself has been targeted. However, the safety of travel routes and the ability to move international personnel into the country are significant considerations for WWE and its partners. A recent report of Wrestling Observer by Dave Meltzer, described Crown Jewel as being in jeopardy amid the escalating situation. Meltzer also suggested that a contingency plan would need to be available if WWE could not hold the event in Riyadh as scheduled. That does not confirm WWE has decided to move the show, nor does it establish that a backup location has been selected. title: New WrestleMania 42 Rumor May Point To a Major Heel Turn From a Top Star
raw_title: New WrestleMania 42 Rumor May Point To a Major Heel Turn From a Top Star
body: While we are still six months from the 2027 edition of the "showcase of the immortals," the WWE has long tried to plan its top matches for the event well in advance. That tradition returned to being the norm once company legend Triple H officially took over the creative direction a few years ago. While injuries and fan reactions can always change plans, now would be a good time to start plotting out a rough draft for the Night 1 and Night 2 headliners for the first WrestleMania ever on foreign soil. According to Wrestle Votes, WWE decision-makers already have two specific matches in mind. In a new report from the industry insider , Oba Femi vs. Roman Reigns is still penciled in as one of the main events. That claim would align with reports in recent months that the brand was eyeing a showdown between its biggest and hottest stars. However, the other match may be a letdown for fans, and that allegedly will be a rematch between Cody Rhodes and CM Punk . Finding out that WWE is thinking about going back to the Rhodes and Punk well will probably get a sigh from a good number of fans. While the build-up to their match at SummerSlam was solid, the bout itself underwhelmed. Especially when compared to the other headliner of the two-night event, Reigns vs. Seth Rollins. Yes, both men are two of the most popular stars on the roster, but why would the company want to rehash a rivalry that did not deliver epic moments? Well, that may be because they are planning something major to come before or during the rematch. It is possible that WWE is considering a heel turn for either man. For a few months, the company has been trying to tell a story of Rhodes tapping into a darker side because being a true blue hero is not working for him anymore. It makes sense if this is all a build to his long-rumored turn before or at WrestleMania 42. Punk can sometimes act like a heel and still get cheers from fans. Turning him would be trickier, but it is not impossible. Furthermore, there may be a belief that a heel version of Punk can be extremely helpful in lifting up younger stars they are trying to turn into main event players. title: Drew McIntyre Calls CM Punk a Piece of Crap
raw_title: Drew McIntyre Blasts Former WWE Champion: 'I Can't Stand Him'
body: McIntyre has been absent from WWE programming since losing to Jacob Fatu at WrestleMania 42 weekend six months ago. The 41-year-old took time off to film The Last Druid (a historical action movie starring Russell Crowe) and Highlander (a fantasy action film also starring Crowe and Henry Cavill). While there's no clear timeline on McIntyre's return to the squared circle, he certainly appears ready to rekindle a feud with another former WWE Champion. "He's a piece of crap. I avoid him whenever I can avoid him," McIntyre said. "I can tell everybody, he's a genuine piece of crap. I can't stand him. I got writers telling me, 'You're working with that guy' and I'm like, 'Alright, I can't stand him but I know he's very good at his job.' I can't stand him. "You put us together, it's magic for the audience but also, we have to be professional and not pound each other because if we pound each other's heads, I would murder him. Did you see him in UFC? It would look like that if it got real in there." McIntyre and Punk had a lengthy 10-month feud in 2024, starting after the latter tore his triceps in the men's Royal Rumble Match. Following McIntyre's successful World Heavyweight Championship defense against Seth Rollins at WrestleMania 40, Punk viciously attacked his rival. Damian Priest then showed up to cash in his Money in the Bank contract, easily defeating McIntyre to become the new champion. Punk and McIntyre concluded their program at the Bad Blood 2024 pay-per-view, with the former emerging victorious. McIntyre is a four-time world champion in WWE (one World Heavyweight title and three WWE Championships). Punk is an eight-time world champion in WWE, with three of those reigns occurring over the last 14 months. Sami Zayn, who ended Punk's last WWE Championship reign, is the current title holder. Roman Reigns has held the World Heavyweight title since WrestleMania 42, defeating Punk in the main event. title: Maria Kanellis Leaves Door Open For WWE Return

body: Maria Kanellis last competed in WWE on the July 1, 2019, episode of RAW. She teamed up with her husband, Mike Bennett, losing to Seth Rollins and Becky Lynch in a mixed tag team match. She and Bennett left the promotion the following year and signed with AEW in 2022. While her husband is still signed to the promotion and working in ROH, she announced her exit in January 2025. "I don't know. In wrestling, you never know. I haven't closed the door, but it's not always up to the person." "Wrestling probably not, unless it's like the Royal Rumble or another Evolution pay-per-view or something like that. But consistently wrestling? Probably not. I think it's so much fun, and those girls took care of me so well the last time I was there, so that's great. I got to look awesome in the ring, much better than I am. It was so much fun. But wrestling consistently, probably not. When I got into wrestling, it wasn't for wrestling," the former WWE star said. Maria Kanellis said she was initially interested in working as a backstage interviewer in WWE before growing interested in an on-screen manager role. "I'm sure you remember this, but Jonathan Coachman and The Rock used to have the banter backstage, and I really wanted to be an interviewer. I loved it. I loved the banter. I loved the way of moving the conversation from one topic to the other. I loved that Jonathan Coachman could do one little thing, and it meant everything in the interview. So that's what I wanted to do, and then somehow I ended up wrestling. But the interviewing part, the managing part, all of that, I really love," the former WWE star said. The post Ex-WWE Star Isn't Ruling Out a Wrestling Comeback Seven Years After the Last Match appeared first on Wrestlezone .
summary: Maria Kanellis last wrestled in WWE on the July 1 2019 episode of Raw in a mixed tag team match alongside husband Mike Bennett against Seth Rollins and Becky Lynch. The couple departed WWE the next year before signing with AEW in 2022 where Bennett remains active in ROH while she exited the company in January 2025. Kanellis stated she has not fully closed the door on wrestling but is unlikely to compete consistently again although she would consider appearances like the Royal Rumble or an Evolution pay-per-view.

title: Austin Creed Names Key New Day Match Before Kofi's WrestleMania Push
raw_title: Austin Creed Feels Most Important Match That New Day Had As A Team Was Securing Kofi's WWE Title Match At WrestleMania 35
body: Austin Creed discusses the past and looks ahead to the future. As of this writing, it is coming up on a full month since The New Level (Kofi & Austin Creed) arrived at All Elite Wrestling. Alongside Swerve Strickland, they are in the midst of a reign as the AEW World Trios Champions. A new interview with Creed and Kofi was conducted by Cameron Hawkins of Uncrowned. Looking back on their time as The New Day with Big E, Creed feels the most important match they had was in the lead-up to WrestleMania 35 when they secured Kofi’s shot at the WWE Championship. “I think with my definition (of important),” he says, “the most important match that we’ve had as a team was when me and (Big) E won that match to get Kofi a title shot.” As for the present, Creed talked about venturing into All Elite Wrestling. “(Swerve Strickland) goes, ‘Look, if we jump in this trios, you get a chance to wrestle, what, six, seven other tag teams right from the jump at Wembley,” says Creed. “So logically, well, of course we want to put hands on everybody as quick as we can, and now by winning those titles, we beat a bunch of other very credible, very good tag teams that AEW has to offer, and so it’s about making sure that we are getting the reps with all of these people on the roster, and having the most dangerous man in all of AEW at our side while we’re doing that, with Prince Nana as well.” On October 17th at AEW WrestleDream, Creed, Kofi, and Strickland will defend the Trios Titles against Hangman Adam Page, Bandido, and Brody King in a two-out-of-three falls match.
summary: Austin Creed believes the most significant match in The New Day's history came when he and Big E earned Kofi Kingston a WWE Championship opportunity at WrestleMania 35. Now competing in AEW as The New Level with Kofi, Creed discussed how teaming with Swerve Strickland allowed them immediate access to multiple top tag teams. The trio are currently reigning as AEW World Trios Champions after defeating several credible opponents.

title: Sheriff's Officer Sues WWE and Montez Ford
raw_title: Cook County Sherriff’s Officer Files Lawsuit Against WWE & Montez Ford
body: A Cook County Sheriff’s officer named Noel Lucas filed a lawsuit on October 14th in the Circuit Court of Cook County against WWE and Montez Ford, real name Kenneth Crawford. WWE’s subsidiary, Event Services, LLC, is also included in the suit. Lucas was working as an off-duty security guard for a July 2026 edition of Monday Night Raw in Rosemont, Illinois. Crawford is from the city of Chicago. Lucas is suing because Crawford performed a ‘lap dance’ on him during Netflix’s live broadcast of Raw, and WWE then pushed the clip out onto their social media pages. Lucas alleges 14 counts, including assault, battery, intentional infliction of emotional distress, and violations of the Illinois Gender Violence Act. POST Wrestling reached out to WWE for a statement, but as of this writing, they have not responded. The site notes that the interaction between Crawford and Lucas is no longer on the July 6th Raw on Netflix feed. Lucas states that Crawford danced toward him without consent. He added that because of the attention it got, he became publicly recognizable. He said the next day, people saw him and started mocking him by imitating what Crawford had done. Lucas added that his children have been ‘mocked and ridiculed’ at school because of what happened. He said he’s suffered humiliation, embarrassment, and emotional distress. He brought up that WWE and Crawford used his image for commercial purposes, which he alleges violates the Illinois Right of Publicity Act. Lucas’ attorney, Whitney Barr, issued the following statement to POST: “Like so many law enforcement officers, Mr. Lucas works a second job in order to better provide for his children.” “Defendant Crawford then began performing a sexually provocative dance immediately in front of and over Plaintiff [Lucas], repeatedly thrusting and gyrating his hips and pelvis towards Plaintiff, performing a sexualized ‘lap dance.'” It continues, “[Crawford] moved his body increasingly closer to [Lucas]; continued the lap dance. [Crawford’s] left inner thigh repeatedly rubbed against Plaintiff’s leg.” Lucas is asking the court to award him an unspecified amount of monetary damages, punitive damages, his legal costs, and to order that WWE and Crawford can’t use his identity.
summary: Cook County Sheriff's officer Noel Lucas filed a lawsuit October 14 in Cook County Circuit Court against WWE, its subsidiary Event Services LLC, and Montez Ford over an unwanted lap dance performed during the July 6 Monday Night Raw broadcast in Rosemont, Illinois. Lucas claims the incident, which aired live on Netflix and was shared on WWE social media, led to public mockery, recognition on the street, and ridicule of his children at school. The suit alleges 14 counts including assault, battery, intentional infliction of emotional distress, and violations of the Illinois Gender Violence Act.

title: On the Record: Roman Reigns Explains Why He No Longer Works WWE Live Events
raw_title: Roman Reigns Explains Why He No Longer Works WWE Live Events
body: In the past few years, Roman Reigns has become more of a star attraction for WWE. He doesn’t wrestle as often as he used to, but his involvement still brings a lot of eyeballs to the product. During his early days in WWE, Reigns was consistently featured on WWE programming, including its live events. With Reigns now working a part-time schedule with WWE, he rarely works on such events anymore. Also read: Roman Reigns On Whether Being Called ‘Overrated’ By Conrad Thompson Bothers Him Reigns explained that WWE’s current business model is television rights, so it doesn’t make sense for him to work house shows for a smaller audience. “Now with my schedule, people will pick on it but they don’t remember from 2012 to 2018 when I was doing 150-200 shows a year, every single year, just working my a** off but staying in the lab, continually getting the reps, conquering my 10,000 hours, putting my time in, that’s where I learned how to do everything, and we’re trying to get that back,” Reigns said. “I think we’re trying to run more live events and they are good, but we’re just at a business model where TV rights are TV rights and there’s just so much money on the line that we’ve got to that point where it’s just like it doesn’t make sense for me to do live events anymore. What if I got hurt? There’s so much money that’s riding on Mondays and Fridays and our PLEs now that I can’t just go out there and wrestle for 4,000-5,000 only, just for those eyes only. Now, I’ve got to conserve it.”

body: WWE superstar Montez Ford (born Kenneth Crawford) has found himself in hot water. Per a Thursday (October 15) report from the Post Wrestling, legal action was recently brought against the high-flyer by an Illinois security guard. Per the report, the security guard, named Noel Lucas, is suing the former WWE tag team champ over an unwanted "sexualized lap dance "that occurred during a live Netflix broadcast of WWE Raw over the summer. title: Drew McIntyre Prioritizes Acting While Staying Ring-Ready
raw_title: Former WWE Champion Says He’s Ready To Wrestle but Is Focused on ‘Hollywood Drew’
body: During a new interview with OutKick Dropkick , the former WWE World Heavyweight Champion made it clear that he's mainly concentrated on his acting gigs. In case WWE calls him for his return, though, he's keeping himself physically ready. "I'm as big as I've ever been. I'm 285, right? And I'm 10 pounds bigger than I was for 'Agent of Shadows.' I'm in the best shape of my life," McIntyre said when asked about his return to a WWE ring. "I posted myself running the ropes the other day, keeping myself in ring shape. I'm always ready to go. I think it got like over 8 million views, just bouncing off the ropes a few times, across my social media platforms. But right now, I'm focused on Hollywood Drew. So, we'll see. We will see." Amidst his hiatus from WWE TV, McIntyre took on roles in The Last Druid and Highlander , action movies in which he starred alongside Academy Award-winning actor Russell Crowe. A press release also revealed him as a voice actor in Disney's upcoming fantasy film Hexed , starring Hailee Steinfeld. Next week, fans will see him in a new ReelShort microdrama, titled Agent of Shadows , too. The timeframe for McIntyre's long-awaited return to a WWE ring is unclear. WrestleVotes on Fightful Select recently reported that WWE officials have discussed the possibility of him landing on the WWE Raw brand whenever he does make it. His last WWE appearances saw him feuding with The Bloodline's Jacob Fatu on SmackDown in the lead-up to WrestleMania 42 in Las Vegas. McIntyre is currently focused on his Hollywood career, which includes starring roles in The Last Druid and Highlander alongside Russell Crowe, a voice part in Disney's Hexed with Hailee Steinfeld, and an upcoming appearance in the ReelShort microdrama Agent of Shadows. The timing of his WWE comeback remains unknown after officials reportedly discussed bringing him back during his hiatus.

body: Fightful Select is reporting that members of the creative team are asking questions about Gunther's recent direction on episodes of SmackDown. The 'Ring General' has gone from retiring top names like Goldberg, John Cena and AJ Styles to hamming it up in backstage skits and matches against comedy characters like Danhausen. However, Gunther is still technically involved in the WWE Title mix. He's currently warring with fellow title hopeful Finn Bálor, but the Danhausen stuff has some behind the curtain concerned about where things are going. The current plan has "raised questions" from some on the creative squad to their higher ups. A few are wondering out loud if WWE even had a solid plan in place for Gunther once he'd shut down Cena at Saturday Night's Main Event on 13 December 2025 . Recent evidence since moving to SmackDown from Raw would suggest that people are right to query that. Gunther mopped the floor with Danhausen on last week's show , and he'll surely now move on completely from the walking sideshow. Most wrestling fans would agree that Dan has his place on the product, but it probably isn't opposite a more serious wrestling machine like the acclaimed Austrian brute. As Fightful reports, "There appears to be some uncertainty regarding how WWE intends to capitalise on the momentum Gunther had built in recent months". There's surely no denying that he could be doing more on SmackDown than he has been. Way more. title: Randy Orton Pays For Wrestling Impersonator's Tuition
raw_title: WWE’s Randy Orton gives amazing $2.4K gift to wrestling impersonator
body: While he has been relatively quiet over the last couple of weeks, WWE Superstar Randy Orton made a big move in support of a viral wrestling impersonator. T'Ziah Hanks, better known as Zy, is known for impersonating professional wrestlers. He revealed (via Zaibi on X, formerly Twitter) that the "Viper" covered his tuition to go to wrestling school, donating $2,400 to his fund. "The 'Legend Killer' just paid for my wrestling school tuition," Hanks wrote on his Instagram Stories post. "Was literally just wondering how I was gonna pay for it." Maybe someday, the training will pay off, and Hanks and Orton meet in the ring. It would be a really cool full-circle moment for the social media content creator and WWE legend. Orton has not been super active over the last couple of weeks in WWE. His last notable match was against his former protege, Cody Rhodes, at Sunday Night's Main Event on Sep. 6. He beat the "American Nightmare" in the latest chapter in their feud. A couple of weeks later, the "Viper" lost a Money in the Bank-qualifying match to Trick Williams. The match also featured Rey Fénix. Meanwhile, his rival, Rhodes, is still in the Undisputed WWE Championship scene. He recently lost a Money in the Bank-qualifying match against Kevin Owens and Johnny Gargano. He is also promoting his latest movie role, Street Fighter . Rhodes plays Guile in the upcoming adaptation of the video game. His longtime rival, Roman Reigns, is also in the movie as Akuma. Earlier in the year, Orton and Rhodes faced at WrestleMania 42. The "American Nightmare" was able to beat the "Legend Killer," who attacked him afterward. Orton then went on an extended hiatus until SummerSlam 2026, when he cost Rhodes his match against CM Punk. title: Roman Reigns Names His Wrestling Mount Rushmore

body: superstar Roman Reigns revealed which pro wrestlers he has on his own personal Mount Rushmore list. The Mount Rushmore list has been an ongoing debate within the pro wrestling community. Pro wrestling has a very rich history. Given the success of companies outside of WWE, there are several wrestlers who can make strong arguments. As a result, many fans and wrestlers themselves have their own criteria that they prioritize most. Reigns is no different, as he shared the metric he strongly considers when putting together a Mount Rushmore list. That metric is money that the talent drew during their career, particularly when they were top stars in the industry. revealed which WWE legends he has on his personal Mount Rushmore list. 'The Tribal Chief' took into account the money each star drew, as well as their popularity. "Only one metric matters, the money. It's show business. The first day I went around the ring, my dad told me, 'Don't ever be confused, this ring is only about money. It's a business. Don't treat it any other way,'" Reigns told Club Shay Shay . "I would probably have to say Hulk [Hogan], Steve [Austin], Dwayne [ The Rock ], and John [Cena]. I mean, you could definitely throw some other guys in there for sure, but we only got so many slots. And those guys, when it came to the money and shifting the business, and changing the view of it, the optics of it, they all had their way of doing that, and they were all critical." He added: "We wouldn't be here today without those four for sure." Reigns also revealed that he considers Hulk Hogan to be the greatest of all time. During his appearance on Club Shay Shay , host Shannon Sharpe asked Reigns who he considers to the greatest of all time. Like the Mount Rushmore debate, the GOAT conversation has become an ongoing debate among fans. Although Reigns noted that while his cousin, The Rock, makes a strong argument, Hogan revolutionized the industry. "Dwayne, I really respect how he did it. It was just lightning in a bottle. You never seen it like that. Nobody picked it up so quickly and at such a jump," he said. "Early on, Rock trying to figure out that character to boom, superstardom in a matter of 18 months and then was able to just go like, 'I don't need the machine anymore.' So in a way, there's a GOAT factor to that." "Hulk had a crazy amount of merch. Every little thing you could think of. Hulk took us from a carnival to a global product, you know what I mean? So that's a tough one." The post WWE Superstar Roman Reigns Reveals His Mount Rushmore appeared first on HEAVY .

body: San Antonio pro wrestlers Brock Ali and Casey Blackrose got a major publicity boost when they appeared in a recent WWE Monday Night Raw brawl in Milwaukee. The pair were invited to appear as extra talent on the Sept. 28 card and took a leap of faith, unsure how — or even if — they’d be included. “We waited all day to be told what we were going to do,” Ali said. “After the security guards got picked, we were picked as fans, still not knowing what we were going to do. They finally told us and we were like ‘Wow, hopefully this goes through,’ and it did! It was a lot of fun.” But after they arrived at the Fiserv Forum, they found themselves in the center of the action. Ali and Blackrose were incorporated into a throwdown between the Bloodline faction (Jacob Fatu and the Usos) and the heel stable the 946 (Royce Keys, Bronco Nima and Lucien Price). Tensions couldn’t have been higher between the rival groups, and their six-way brawl escaped the confines of the ring. After Bloodline’s Jimmy Uso jumped from the barricade, the 946’s Price grabbed him and hurled him into the audience, straight into Ali. Blackrose, who narrowly avoided being toppled by Uso, opted for a more direct altercation. He confronted Nima and, despite his best efforts, went down after a swift hit to the jaw. The segment ended shortly after with the two factions taking their feud backstage. The Alamo City wrestlers’ appearance was brief, but it gave them a chance to perform at one of professional wrestling’s highest-profile events. Like their Greyhound bus journey to last month’s Raw, Blackrose and Ali’s wrestling careers began in San Antonio. Both are graduates of the Hybrid School of Wrestling, where they train under the guidance of head coaches Sho Funaki, a WWE legend, and independent wrestler Chris Marval. San Antonio-born Blackrose got the wrestling bug early. He attended his first WWE show at the age of 9 and saw legendary El Paso-born wrestler Eddie Guerrero in action three weeks before his untimely death. “Years later, I attended a [River City Wrestling] show, and that’s when I discovered independent wrestling,” Blackrose said. “I asked RCW promoter Brandon Oliver about joining the business, and he gave me the information for Hybrid, where I’ve trained since 2019. I have also evolved into a coach and help train the next generation of wrestlers, like Brock Ali.” Months after graduating from Hybrid in 2021, Blackrose faced San Antonio grappler Keith Lee in a dark match at the AT&T Center — now the Frost Bank Center — before a separate WWE Raw. title: Kaitlyn Rules Out In-Ring Return
raw_title: Former WWE champion definitively rules out return and confirms retirement: ‘I don’t have this burning desire’
body: Former WWE Divas Champion Kaitlyn, aka Celeste Bonin, has shared a major update on her wrestling career. A part of the WWE roster from 2010 to 2014, Kaitlyn was known for her powerhouse move set and impressive physique. A former WWE Divas Champion, Kaitlyn parted ways with WWE in 2014 and wrestled for a few years in the indies. She later returned for a brief run in 2018. However, her second run did not last long, and she was eliminated in the Mae Young Classic 2018 Second Round by Michin, aka Mia Yim. Recently, speaking to Chris Van Vliet, Bonin opened up about her wrestling future and completely ruled out the chances of an in-ring return . "I hope no one hates me for this, but I don't really want to get back in the ring. I respect wrestling a lot, and I find it very entertaining. "I love the artistry of it. I don't think I could ever have the appreciation that I have now if I had never been a professional wrestler. Because there are so many aspects to the performance," said Kaitlyn. "There's so many things to think about. The psychology of the match, connecting with people, telling a story with your face and your body, protecting your face and your body, protecting the person that you're in the ring with, helping them perform to their best," she further added. The 40-year-old currently works as a model and has no "burning desire," for a wrestling return. "Knowing where the cameras are, knowing how much time you have, being able to change it up if the people in the audience aren't buying it, if they don't care about it, so there's so much to it. "It's such a beautiful art form, so I will always love it and deeply respect it. I don't really watch it, but occasionally I will if there's someone that I'm still friends with or that I love. Occasionally I'll watch a match, but I don't know. I don't think I am gonna get back in the ring because I don't have this burning desire to do that." She last wrestled in 2019 at the GWA 3rd Annual Toy Drive and is vividly remembered for her feud against AJ Lee in WWE.

Cody Rhodes has been gearing up to play the popular Street Fighter character “Guile” in the highly anticipated movie reboot, and recently explained why being a proficient pro wrestler has helped to inform the U.S. Air Force pilot’s presentation on the big screen. In a recent Q&A to promote the upcoming movie, Cody Rhodes says that his love of Street Fighter II began when he got the top-selling game for his Nintendo console as a kid. “I loved me some Street Fighter II, ” he reflected. “And I was shockingly better at it as a child than I am as a full-grown adult male.” Still, as an adult, Rhodes has certainly been no slouch. He’s held the WWE Championship multiple times and as such, is a playable character in many of the pro wrestling promotion’s own video game offerings. The grappler shared some of the inspirations behind bringing the U.S. Air Force pilot into the upcoming film. “So much of what we’ve done with Guile is very funny,” he commented. “I have a buddy who’s in the Air Force, and I asked him about a few things, you know, whether it be posture, or is there a phrase that they like to hear? But the part that I connected the most, is the dog tags.” Rhodes also shared how coming from the larger-than-life WWE Universe helped with Guile’s presentation. “Being a wrestler and coming to do Street Fighter informs the character, but probably in different ways than people think,” said The American Nightmare. “I can get on the wire, and I can actually pull this Flash Kick off, and I can land. (Photo by Meg Oliphant/WWE via Getty Images) Roman Reigns is one of the most heralded WWE superstars in history. A former Royal Rumble winner, WrestleMania main eventer, and multi-time World Champion, there are few things Reigns has not accomplished in the squared circle. Although he descends from a lineage of wrestling legends , Reigns initially did not intend to pursue wrestling. In an interview with Pro Football Hall of Famer Shannon Sharpe, Reigns explained how his leukemia diagnosis spurred his career pivot from football to WWE . Play Reigns (real name Joe Anoa’i) played defensive tackle at Georgia Tech for four seasons from 2003 to 2006. During his senior season, the standout defensive tackle earned First Team All-ACC honors. He was also named Lifter of the Year in 2006, an award he shared with Detroit Lions legend and Georgia Tech alum Calvin Johnson . Shortly after college, Reigns signed with the Minnesota Vikings as an undrafted free agent, and believed he would carve out a lengthy NFL career. However, a leukemia diagnosis all but dashed his football dream. Reigns recalled that lab work revealed he had “way more” white blood cells than usual, putting his budding NFL career in jeopardy. “I think I had about 70,000 white blood cells . Typically, you’re somewhere between 5,000 and 10,000 if anything is running normally.” He added, “Back then, there was nobody like me. There was nobody that had come out at 21 years old, collegiate athlete with leukemia. So, I thought it was pretty much a sports death sentence. There was a gonna be a giant asterisk attached to my name. Nobody was gonna [sign] me.” Reigns said of his leukemia diagnosis: “ That was the day that changed my life .” Reigns briefly signed with the Jacksonville Jaguars in 2007, when his leukemia was in remission, but was cut during training camp. The reigning World Heavyweight Champion retired from football in 2008 after his lone season in the CFL. Although he didn’t have the NFL career he envisioned, Reigns is grateful that he ultimately pursued pro wrestling. It's a blessing to just kind of be able to be in the ring with somebody that I used to study, and now that we kind of built like a brotherhood. ... But I think we both also know that when it comes to wrestling and when it comes to goals and stuff, we both want to achieve them." Though both men took to the skies together and won their tag team match against The Vision's Austin Theory and Bron Breakker last Monday on "WWE Raw" , they stood in opposition at this year's Money in the Bank days later. Taking a critical mid-air spear from Breakker, Evans tried with all his might to bounce back from that devastating move. However, he wasn't able to secure the briefcase. Instead, his partner Penta won the briefcase for the first time in his WWE career. title: Did Street Fighter Actor And WWE Wrestler Cody Rhodes Accidentally Let Slip He’s In The X-Men Reboot?
raw_title: Did Street Fighter Actor And WWE Wrestler Cody Rhodes Accidentally Let Slip He’s In The X-Men Reboot?
body: We already know a handful of the actors who will be joining the Marvel Cinematic Universe when Marvel finally fully reboots the X-Men in 2028 . Sadie Sink has already made her debut as Jean Grey in Spider-Man: Brand New Day , and others set to join the mutant crew in the new film include Inde Navarrette as Rogue, Maya Boyd as Storm, Christopher Abbot as Professor X, Kit Connor as Cyclops, and Samara Weaving as Emma Frost. Adam Driver will round out the cast as villain Mr. Sinister, but there are plenty of other X-Men who aren’t accounted for. Enter Cody Rhodes, a WWE wrestler turned actor who is playing Guile in the new Street Fighter movie that’s out tonight. With his new movie in theaters, he and the rest of the cast have been on a promotional tour, and in a new interview with Nerdist , Rhodes may have accidentally let it slip that he’s in the X-Men movie. At the 1:29 mark, Rhodes is talking about his various nerd interests, and says what sure sounds like “I’m in X-Men .” . His co-star, anti-woke personality Andrew Schulz , reacts immediately, saying “Wait, you are?”, and then, as Rhodes carries on as if all is normal, says he thought Rhodes had just “made an announcement” of some kind. If Rhodes realized what he’d said, he maintained a great poker face and managed to carry on the interview without missing a beat. Now, fans are speculating about who Rhodes could be playing in the movie. There’s no shortage of big buff mutants in the X-Men universe, so could he be Colossus, Cable, Havok, Iceman, or someone less obvious and prominent? If he’s locked down the role, maybe an official announcement is imminent. For now, the MCU is focused pretty squarely on December’s Avengers: Doomsday , though VisionQuest premiered this week on Disney+ and is pretty good so far. body: By Josh Coulson Published Oct 16, 2026, 5:37 AM EDT Josh studied Journalism and Media and Cultural Studies at the University of the West of England, graduating in the summer of 2014.. Josh is a writer at TheSportster and a lifelong wrestling fan who has been doing news coverage of WWE and AEW for many years. An off-duty security guard has filed a lawsuit against both parties for the unwilling part he played during a Street Profits entrance earlier this year, with emotional distress listed among the many counts being brought against the defendants. Details about the lawsuit have been shared by POST Wrestling . The plaintiff, Cook County Sheriff’s officer Noel Lucas, was working his second job as a security guard during an episode of Raw this past July, which aired live on Netflix. Lucas was one of the many people working security who spend the majority of the show sitting just inside the barrier with their back to the ring. The clip that aired live and was subsequently shared on social media, including by Ford himself, shows the WWE Superstar approaching Lucas and then dancing in front of him for an extended period. Ford gyrates and thrusts his hips towards Lucas in a moment the plaintiff's attorney claims was unplanned and describes as a "lap dance". The suit also claims Ford's leg repeatedly rubbed against Lucas's. The lawsuit includes 14 counts being brought against Ford and WWE, including assault, battery, intentional infliction of emotional distress, and violations of the Illinois Gender Violence Act. Lucas also claims that since his face is visible in the clip, meaning that he can be easily identified, WWE has violated the Illinois Right of Publicity Act by using his likeness for commercial purposes without permission. title: AEW Teases Ilja Dragunov Debut Before WrestleDream

body: Is "The Mad Dragon" on his way to AEW? After weeks of reports and speculation about Ilja Dragunov 's much-awaited AEW debut, it now seems that the time has finally come. Dragunov parted ways with WWE a couple of months ago when he decided to not renew his contract. Soon after rejecting a contract extension, Dragunov immediately became a free agent upon its expiry. Rumors soon emerged about him signing an AEW deal and joining the promotion. While fans waited weeks for signs of his arrival, AEW decided to keep silent. Now, after months of speculation, AEW has finally dropped Dragunov's first television tease . On the recent Oct. 14, 2026, episode of AEW Dynamite and Collision, before AEW WrestleDream 2026, a mysterious vignette aired. Running for about 25 seconds, the vignette features multiple shots of a metronome as well as a person conducting music with their hands. The video package also shows a person walking down a set of steps and running across a training ring. The video teased the arrival of a new AEW star. While it did not confirm or specify Ilja Dragunov's name, fans were certain of his arrival on the internet. Once the signing is made official, Dragunov will join The New Level and Motor City Machine Guns as former WWE talents joining AEW in the last few months. Dragunov is a former WWE United States Champion, NXT Champion, and NXT UK Champion. He was with WWE since 2019 before not renewing his contract in 2026. The 33-year-old's last match dates back to the 2026 Andre the Giant Memorial Battle Royal before WWE WrestleMania 42.

Fans immediately connected the package to Dragunov, who has been the subject of signing speculation for weeks and would become the latest ex-WWE talent in AEW alongside recent additions like The New Level and Motor City Machine Guns.

body: Vice TV Add Wrestling Inc. on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Deathmatch legend Necro Butcher recently announced that he had signed a WWE Legends deal , and a new report has revealed the possible reason the promotion offered him a contract. The 53-year-old Butcher continues to wrestle in his hardcore style on the independent circuit, and his story was recently told in an episode of "Dark Side of the Ring," which chronicled his infamous match against AEW's Samoa Joe in 2005.

title: Adam Copeland Sets 2027 Retirement
raw_title: Adam Copeland, Edge in WWE, Announces His Retirement Plans
body: Copeland announced Wednesday on AEW Dynamite that 2027 will be his final year in professional wrestling. The 52-year-old made the announcement after defeating Josh Alexander to qualify for the Clockwork Carnage match at WrestleDream, where the AEW World Championship will be at stake. Copeland acknowledged that he is "aging out" and isn't the wrestler whose face is on posters on teenagers' walls anymore. He then made it clear that becoming AEW World Champion is one of the goals he wants to accomplish before walking away. Copeland is one of the greatest wrestlers of all time and one of my personal favorites, so I wish him nothing but the best. His comments about aging out of the business are true, but this time there is something satisfying about it. Copeland gets to decide when it's time. That wasn't the case in 2011, when Edge was forced to retire because of his neck. His return at the 2020 Royal Rumble was something most fans never expected to see. Now, assuming he wrestles into 2027, Copeland will have effectively gotten a seven-year second act to a career that once ended far too soon. I'd love to see Edge wrestle one more WWE match before it's over. At the same time, I don't feel like I need it. His WWE return already gave us more than we ever thought we'd get after 2011. Everything since 2020 has been bonus time. Now Copeland gets something even better: the chance to finish on his own terms. body: The creator, T'Ziah Hanks, better known online as Zy, shared the news on his Instagram Stories. He posted screenshots showing Orton's contribution and explained how much the gesture meant to him. "The Legend Killer just paid for my wrestling school tuition! Was literally wondering how I was gonna pay for it." Zy is best known for his viral "Be Like" videos, in which he imitates the movements, expressions, and signature mannerisms of professional wrestlers. His recreations have featured Orton, Kurt Angle, Booker T, Triple H, Batista, Rob Van Dam, and Roman Reigns, among others. He has also parodied wrestling match types, including ladder matches, bringing his own comedic spin to familiar WWE moments. Although his online impersonations helped him gain attention, Zy has been working toward a career in the ring. He has shared footage of himself training, including sessions at Test Of Strength Wrestling, showing that his interest in wrestling extends beyond making videos for social media. Before his wrestling impressions took off, Zy also made viral basketball videos by mimicking popular players. His content has since expanded to wrestling, where his attention to the small details of each performer's style has helped him connect with fans. Randy Orton's contribution arrives while the veteran remains involved in a heated WWE storyline with Cody Rhodes on SmackDown. Their rivalry has intensified since "The Viper" cost Rhodes his Money in the Bank qualifying match on October 2, attacking his longtime associate's chances of earning another opportunity at the Undisputed WWE Championship. On the October 9 episode, SmackDown General Manager Nick Aldis turned Orton away from the arena to prevent the situation from escalating ahead of Money in the Bank. Orton insisted that Rhodes was the real problem and left, but that did little to calm his rival. "The American Nightmare" later confronted Aldis and demanded that he arrange a face-to-face meeting with Orton. He made it clear that he was finished waiting and threatened to travel to St. Louis himself if necessary. WWE subsequently announced that the two would meet face-to-face on the October 16 episode of SmackDown. While Orton's on-screen rivalry with Rhodes continues to build, his contribution to Zy offers a glimpse of his support for someone trying to break into the wrestling business. body: Chelsea Green has stated that she wanted Zoey Stark in her group. There’s an extensive interview with the former Zelina Vega, now going by Xelina, on the Ring The Belle YouTube channel . You would win it back, but have Zoey come in, beat the everliving sh*t out of me. Make it disgusting. Make it really bad so that people will feel for me. title: Shotzi Blackheart Withdraws From CMLL Tour
raw_title: Former WWE Star Shotzi Blackheart Withdraws From CMLL Tour Following Family Tragedy
body: WWE/Getty Images Add Wrestling Inc. on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover It's been a week of change for Shotzi Blackheart's career, as she's made the move from MLW to TNA after appearing on the latter's TV tapings on Tuesday. Unfortunately, it has also been a trying week for Blackheart in her personal life, one that will be affecting a booking she had next week. Taking to X on Wednesday morning, Blackheart revealed that her brother, Dean, had passed away last Sunday night. Blackheart further stated that now that her booking obligations for this week had been fulfilled, she would be taking time off to be with family and "honor my brother's memory," announcing that she would be pulling out of the CMLL Women's Gran Prix as a result. "It was a huge honor to be selected for the CMLL Grand Prix, and I don't take that opportunity lightly," Blackheart said. "Thank you to everyone at CMLL and the fans for understanding how hard all this is for me." It was just seven months ago that Blackheart's brother was in the news after the former MLW Women's Featherweight Champion revealed that he had gone missing in California after stumbling away from a car accident. He was found shortly after and hospitalized . Blackheart has credited her brother with helping her become a wrestling fan as a child, as she would watch matches and play wrestling video games with him. It's the second family loss Blackheart has suffered in the last five years, having lost her father in 2021 . At the moment, it is unclear who will replace Blackheart in CMLL Gran Prix next week. It will be the second time CMLL has had to make a change to the lineup after Lady Frost was removed from the match and replaced by Masha Slamovich last week after Frost departed MLW. Wrestling Inc. would like to offer its condolences to Blackheart during this difficult time.

title: Lola Vice Recalls Scary Ladder Fall At MITB
raw_title: Lola Vice Comments On Ladder Incident At WWE Money In The Bank: “It Hurt A Lot & Was Very Scary”
body: One of the marquee bouts at the 2026 WWE Money in the Bank Premium Live Event was the women’s Money in the Bank Ladder match. Among the participants were Lola Vice and WWE Women’s United States Champion Jacy Jayne. There was a point in the bout when the two talents were trading blows on the same side of a ladder. Vice put Jayne in a chokehold, and then they fell onto a ladder that was propped up by the middle ring rope and the ladder they were standing on. Vice and Jayne bounced off the ladder, but it shifted and then sent them both out of the ring and onto the floor. Vice commented on the incident during her appearance on WWE Ahora (translation by Fightful’s Luis Pulido ). “I had Jacy (Jayne) in a choke and when I put her to sleep, she fell back and I fell with her. I thought that was the end of it, but suddenly the ladder went backwards, and literally, it got us out of the ring. Because of that, I didn’t win Money in the Bank. It hurt a lot and was very scary, but looking back, thank God it came out like this because it could have been very ugly. I think an injury in a Ladder match would have been rough. They are not for everyone, but thank God I’m strong and I was able to do it.” If the quote in this article is used, please credit WWE Ahora with an H/T to Fightful’s Luis Pulido for the transcription.
summary: During the women's Money in the Bank ladder match at the 2025 premium live event, Lola Vice and Jacy Jayne fell from a ladder that shifted unexpectedly after Vice applied a chokehold. The incident sent both competitors out of the ring to the floor, preventing Vice from winning the briefcase. Vice later described the moment as painful and frightening but expressed relief that neither wrestler was injured in what could have been a serious accident.

title: Cody Rhodes Says Ari Emanuel Didn't Know Him Before WrestleMania 40
raw_title: Cody Rhodes Claims TKO CEO Ari Emanuel Didn’t Know Who He Was Until WWE WrestleMania 40
body: Among the cast members of the Street Fighter movie are WWE’s Cody Rhodes and Roman Reigns. They’ve been touring with fellow cast members for a media run, and one of the outlets they spoke to was the New York Times . Rhodes told the outlet that TKO CEO Ari Emanuel was unaware of who he was until WrestleMania 40 in 2024, where Rhodes headlined nights one and two. A month after WrestleMania 40, Rhodes signed with W.M.E. (Williams Morris Endeavor), which is the talent and media agency that Emanuel is the Executive Chairman of. In 2023, a deal made W.W.E. part of a new company, TKO Group Holdings, led by the Hollywood power broker Ari Emanuel. After a high-profile match in Philadelphia in 2024, Rhodes signed with WME, the talent agency Emanuel helped found, which also represents Johnson and Cena. Rhodes said Emanuel did not know who the wrestler was before that night, but WME set up the meeting at Legendary and Rhodes was cast in “Street Fighter.” Rhodes said he wanted to “do right” by Emanuel and Khan, a former television agent at Creative Artists Agency, a rival of WME. “They’ve told the town, ‘You’re a serious person,’ and that’s really helpful,” Rhodes said. A TKO spokeswoman declined to make Emanuel available for comment. Rhodes is a three-time Undisputed WWE Champion. His latest reign came to an end in June 2026 when he dropped the belt to Sami Zayn.

A month after the event Rhodes signed with WME, the agency Emanuel serves as Executive Chairman of, which helped lead to his casting in the upcoming Street Fighter movie alongside Roman Reigns. Rhodes noted he wanted to do right by both Emanuel and his former CAA agent Ari Greenwald, crediting them for establishing him as a serious talent in Hollywood.

title: Roman Reigns Says Wrestling Is His Craft
raw_title: Roman Reigns: Wrestling Is My Craft, I Own That Shit - Fightful | WWE News, AEW News, Pro Wrestling Backstage News
body: The upcoming ‘Street Fighter’ film features a big cast that includes egos from the world of wrestling and from Hollywood. According to most accounts, it sounds like the cast had a blast during the film’s shoot in Australia. Speaking with Sam Roberts for a new interview , Reigns said that he wasn’t running around the set acting like he was Noah Centineo. But in wrestling, a bunch of people walk around acting like their on Roman’s level. “There’s a great camaraderie in wrestling. I mean, being one of the boys, I can’t even explain it because I’m in the small fraternity, I’m in that 1%. Honestly, that should just be for us. But, the difference is I wasn’t running around thinking I’m Noah [Centineo], you know what I mean? There’s plenty of dudes in the locker room that are running around thinking they’re Roman Reigns, thinking they’re of my level. It’s crazy. It’s just ridiculous. Look in the mirror and look at all your stuff, everything that comes with your life. Look at your bank account, all the stuff. We’re not the same. I didn’t run around thinking I’m Noah [Centineo] or Andrew [Koji]. No, I’m here to work with them, compliment them, make the very best combination or collaboration to create the best film. There’s no confusion here, we all understand who we are and what we’re trying to do and we all came together that way in a perfect way. But in wrestling, it just can’t be had that way.” Despite coming from a football background, Reigns isn’t vibing with the teamwork aspect of wrestling. He insists that he owns “that shit”. “Look, I come from football, so I’m always going to look at a teamwork aspect but wrestling is different. That’s my craft, I own that shit. That is mine, you know what I mean? Like mine. I don’t give a shit about any of them, it’s mine.” Sam Roberts proceeded by asking Reigns when he adopted this mindset. “Probably when I was born, but it doesn’t click until — honestly, before COVID hit and I left, I had dog food all on me, it was just one of those situations where I just wasn’t creatively — I just wasn’t in line. I didn’t like what I was doing. I didn’t like the way I was portrayed. It was just time to take complete ownership and the proof is in the pudding.” Elsewhere in the interview, Roman Reigns talked about the importance of analytics in wrestling. title: Bully Ray Questions WWE Booking Of Chelsea Green's Raw Loss
raw_title: Bully Ray Is Baffled By WWE's Decision To Have Current World Champion Lose On Raw
body: Bryan Steffy/Getty Images Add Wrestling Inc. on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover It was a rare appearance for WWE Women's Champion Chelsea Green this past Monday on "Raw," and not one she'll want to remember, as she not only lost to Roxanne Perez, but was beaten up by Perez, Liv Morgan, and Raquel Rodriguez in the post-match . While all of this was done to build to Green vs. Morgan at Crown Jewel , Bully Ray was left cold to it, questioning co-host Dave LaGreca on "Busted Open Radio" about why Green had to be the one who lost this match. "Can you help me make sense of it?" Bully said. "I'm legitimately asking you this question. This is not for radio entertainment. I don't know why they brought Chelsea over last night. I don't know why Chelsea had to lose in the middle to Roxanne last night." While LaGreca presented plenty of arguments, and did note that Green's loss wasn't a clean loss, Bully still wasn't buying it. "For the most part, I got that there was a pretty definitive victory for Roxanne, and then the beat down afterwards," Bully said. "I just didn't know why they had to beat Chelsea Green last night. It just seems like every time there's a step forward for Chelsea Green, there's some kind of a step back. And then Chelsea finds a way to step forward again." Bully then argued that Green should've gone over, and if the idea was for WWE to keep Perez strong, they should've had her win the Women's Money in the Bank match days before . Furthermore, Bully was bothered by WWE presenting Green as a serious wrestler, only for her to come up short at her best. "They went out of their way last night to have Chelsea Green really wrestle a match, didn't they, to show her wrestling ability, which we see a lot more of Chelsea's entertainment side then we see her wrestling side, right?" Bully said. "Well, in Chelsea bringing her best wrestling game to the table last night, in a wrestling match, not climbing a ladder, in a wrestling match, she lost." In celebration of all things that go bump in the night, make the hairs on your arms stand up and send shivers down your spine, relive these moments from the last four decades of WWE television—each worthy of a horror movie in its own right. Imagine if the giant snake in Anaconda had feasted on Jennifer Lopez's character, or the titular serpent had gotten the best of Jessica Rothe's character in Beware Boiúna . That was the situation in 1991, when Jake "The Snake" Roberts produced a live cobra and taunted "Macho Man" Randy Savage as the reptile bit into the Hall of Famer's biceps. Miss Elizabeth and fans in attendance and watching at home looked on in horror, fearing for the former WWE champion's safety. Savage would recover and get revenge on Roberts, but the attack remains unsettling to watch today—especially for viewers afraid of snakes. He didn't carry red balloons or ask young fans in the front row if they could float too, but the original incarnation of Doink the Clown was evil nonetheless. Taking great delight in tormenting fans and wrestlers alike, the evil jester would chuckle one moment, then stare menacingly into the camera the next, his expression suddenly turning deadly serious. It wasn't one particular moment that made the original Doink terrifying—it was the entire experience. He laughed and joked like an innocent circus clown but behaved like a vile, deceitful horror villain. Much of that could be credited to Matt Borne and his understanding of how to bring Doink to life. His performance gave the character a sinister depth and helped establish a legacy that endures today. As long as you stop watching before his ill-fated babyface turn. Still, Doink evoked Tim Curry's portrayal of Pennywise in 1990's It . Beneath the seemingly harmless clown exterior lurked a sinister edge—a reminder that appearances could be deceiving. Former WWE star Xelina has opened up about her run as Women’s United States Champion, revealing that she wanted to take the championship beyond WWE and establish it as a true workhorse title. During an interview with D.S. Shin of Ring The Belle , she reflected on what she hoped to accomplish and why she wished WWE’s creative direction had allowed her more freedom. Xelina became the second holder of the Women’s United States Championship and held the title for 63 days. However, her reign featured just one successful title defense before she lost the championship to Giulia. Speaking about her championship run, Xelina said she wanted to defend the belt in different promotions rather than keep it confined to WWE programming. “I wish that he (Triple H) would have loved it on me enough to let me defend it the way I wanted to defend it,” Xelina said. She then explained the bigger ambition behind her idea, naming two promotions where she hoped to bring the championship. “But it’s fine, because I wanted to go and bring it to AAA and f*cking STARDOM. Let me bring it to different places and really make this the workhorse title if that’s what we were gonna do.” The comments suggest Xelina wanted the championship to become a regular feature across multiple wrestling promotions, giving it a more active presence through frequent defenses. Her proposed approach would have taken the title beyond WWE’s own shows and introduced it to audiences elsewhere. The Women’s United States Championship was Xelina’s first singles title in WWE. She had previously won the Women’s Tag Team Championship, but her singles reign offered a unique opportunity to establish herself as a champion. Her remarks also reflect a broader frustration with the creative freedom she believes was limited during her WWE tenure. In the same interview, she discussed wanting more room to express her personality through promos and pursue matches she felt suited her abilities. For Xelina, the title could have been more than another championship to hold — she wanted it to be defended regularly and travel with her. Her vision for a workhorse belt never fully materialized during her reign, but she has now made clear what she hoped it could become.
