title: Who Is Necro Butcher? Hardcore Wrestling Legend Signs WWE Deal at 53
raw_title: Who Is Necro Butcher? Hardcore Wrestling Legend Signs WWE Deal at 53
body: Butcher announced Tuesday that he signed what he described as a "basic legends deal" with WWE. PWInsider subsequently confirmed with WWE sources that the deal is "100% accurate" and reported that WWE President Nick Khan spearheaded the agreement. The signing is unusual because Butcher built his reputation almost entirely outside wrestling's biggest companies. For WWE fans who only became familiar with him this year through Dark Side of the Ring , here's what to know about one of independent wrestling's most notorious performers. Necro Butcher's real name is Dylan Keith Summers. Born July 13, 1973, in West Virginia, Summers made his professional wrestling debut in 1998 and eventually became known for an exceptionally violent style of wrestling. His matches frequently included the weapons and violence associated with "deathmatch" wrestling, but Butcher also worked with some of the biggest names to emerge from the 2000s independent scene. His list of opponents included Bryan Danielson, Kevin Steen, Eddie Kingston, Chris Hero, Claudio Castagnoli and Samoa Joe. Butcher even reached Hollywood. He appeared in the acclaimed 2008 film The Wrestler , starring Mickey Rourke. If there is one match that defines Butcher's career, it's his 2005 encounter with Samoa Joe. The two met at IWA Mid-South's Something to Prove at the former ECW Arena in Philadelphia. The match developed a reputation over the next two decades for its brutality, including a memorable moment in which Joe kicked Butcher off the arena bleachers and onto the concrete floor. More than 20 years later, that match put Butcher back into the wrestling conversation. VICE's Dark Side of the Ring dedicated an episode of its seventh season to the story behind Samoa Joe vs. Necro Butcher. The episode explored not only the match but Butcher's life, career and the circumstances that brought the two wrestlers together. VICE later released the full episode on YouTube in July, where it has since generated more than 700,000 views. The timing is noteworthy. Butcher went from being the subject of a nationally televised wrestling documentary in 2026 to signing a WWE Legends deal months later. While neither WWE nor Butcher has publicly said Dark Side of the Ring led to the agreement, the episode undoubtedly brought renewed attention to his career and likely helped put him back on the radar. A WWE Legends deal generally allows WWE to license a wrestler's name and likeness for merchandise, video games and other projects, while also opening the door for appearances. It will be interesting to see whether that eventually includes an on-screen WWE appearance for Butcher. Given the unusual nature of the signing and the renewed attention surrounding his career, a future WWE Hall of Fame induction no longer feels completely out of the question, either. title: Dave Meltzer Explains Short Vaquer Title Run
raw_title: Backstage Report On Recent WWE Women's World Title Changes
body: WWE Add Wrestling Inc. on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover At WWE Money in the Bank , Liv Morgan defeated Stephanie Vaquer and Becky Lynch to become the Women's World Champion for the fourth time . She landed the Ob-LIV-ion on Vaquer after Vaquer sent Lynch through a table with a running knee to regain the title. Vaquer defeated Morgan at a live event in her home country of Chile with Lynch as the special guest referee. On last week's "Raw" , the match between Lynch and Vaquer to determine the Number One contender ended in a disqualification, leading to the triple threat match. The match on Saturday was Vaquer's first title defense in her 28-day title reign. On Wrestling Observer Radio , Dave Meltzer provided more information on why Vaquer's title reign was so short. "Essentially the story is that the Chile thing was a one night thing for Chile and as soon as they had the chance, they got it back on Liv. Which doesn't surprise me at all because you know, they want Liv as champion and they think she's the Superstar on that brand. Her and Rhea Ripley are the two Superstars right now in the women's division, so that was the deal." If you use any quotes from this article, please credit Wrestling Observer Radio and provide a h/t to Wrestling Inc. for the transcription.
summary: Liv Morgan won the Women's World Championship for the fourth time at Money in the Bank by defeating both Stephanie Vaquer and Becky Lynch. Vaquer had previously beaten Morgan at a live event in Chile with Lynch serving as special guest referee, but lost the title back after a 28-day reign. According to Dave Meltzer the Chile victory was planned as a one-off for the local market with plans already in place to return the title to Morgan, who along with Rhea Ripley is viewed as the top star in the women's division.

title: Tommy End and Xelina Have Personal Issues, Pulled from PROGRESS, OTT - TWNP-Wrestling News

body: The post-WWE runs for Aleister Black and Zelina Vega have been a roller coaster. This married duo made quite the splash in the UK wrestling scene over the past month. First, the ex-Malakai Black headed to Progress Wrestling in September and quickly won the PROGRESS Men’s World Championship as Tommy End. By October, his wife, Xelina, also made her PROGRESS debut . Just as the couple was about to be featured regularly, they were pulled from the upcoming PROGRESS and OTT Wrestling shows. According to the UK-based companies, Tommy End and Xelina have personal issues that they must tend to. Ever since Xelina joined Tommy End in the United Kingdom, the former WWE Superstars were set to take the European wrestling scene by storm. Unfortunately, it looks like the power couple’s plans are getting sidetracked. This morning, Big Damo announced that Tommy End and Xelina wouldn’t make it for their scheduled appearance at PROGRESS Chapter 199: Bonestorm in London, England. Big Damo and Nikki Storm are co-owners of PROGRESS Wrestling. Xelina was set to team with Nikki Storm to wrestle Alexxis Falcon and Myla Grace. Meanwhile, Tommy End was scheduled to face Luke Jacobs. It’s now been confirmed that Eddie Kingston will take the former AEW Superstar’s place in the match on October 25th. The wrestling community is concerned about Tommy and Xelina’s sudden departure from the wrestling scene. They made the decision ten days before their scheduled appearance, so it wasn’t a last-minute call for the former WWE Superstars. That said, all posts allude to family being first. One fan showed concern for the couple’s health, hoping that they are okay. We won’t speculate on the health of wrestlers. However, we do offer our thoughts to the Trinidad-Büdgen family.

title: Kofi and Austin Creed chase tag team greatness in AEW
raw_title: The New Day is gone, but the brotherhood lives on: Kofi and Austin Creed on finding a New Level in AEW
body: But while the location may change, and the names might be tweaked, and the music may get a new mix, the brothers who make up AEW's New Level have come this far together, and that reliance on one another has them looking at a run as pro-wrestling's definitive tag-team. "I'm funny with the word legacy, because honestly, I don't care if people remember me or not," Kofi, sans his former Kingston surname, explains ahead of Saturday's AEW WrestleDream 2026 pay-per-view , with a giant mural of Falor from "The NeverEnding Story" painted on the wall behind him. The man who won virtually every title during his WWE tenure, including becoming the company's second Black and first African-born WWE Champion ever, doesn't live in the past. He's always looking at what he can do, right now, to make people feel something in the moment. "The reason that we do community service, the reason that we help people, it's not for us. Like, I'm not doing it so that you remember me. I want everybody to have the greatest experience when I interact with them. And whether you remember me or not, is not important." There are too many moments in the group's career to count, but outside of KofiMania's climax , it's hard to think of a more electric, more feel-good moment than A$AP Ferg's "New Level" blaring through Wembley Stadium's speakers this past August at All In , the graphics that were once pink unicorns giving way to fire-breathing dragons on a wireframe grid, and Kofi and Austin Creed emerging to flank Swerve Strickland to challenge for the AEW Trios Championship. "I believe in myself and I believe in [Kofi]," Creed chimes in, leaning back on his "Rocky"-inspired roots for the next chapter of his career. "So regardless of where we are, we're going to be able to adapt. We're going to be able to create change. We are always going to be able to create success. So I don't necessarily think that we focus on legacy, because we're focused on the now. Like, what can we do now?" That "now" came about as quickly as possible under AEW's roof, with the pair capturing the trios titles alongside Strickland that night in the inaugural "Trios Roulette Royale." Now they're set to defend them against the former champions — "Hangman" Adam Page, Brody King and Bandido — at WrestleDream in a two-out-of-three falls match. But between bursting onto the new scene and giving the former champs their rematch, The New Level had to address the question that was top of everyone's minds: Did they have what it takes to hang with the no-frills, no-fear athletes of All Elite Wrestling? Their answer came right away, in a week-one title defense against The Rascalz, the free-spirited cruiserweight crew known for their quick tags, intricate team maneuvers and outlandish out-of-the-ring dives. We'd know right away if Creed and Kofi were up to snuff. body: 00:22 Featured Video Epic Bat Flip in Guardians Win 😱 Previous Next AEW Dynamite Results, Winners, Live Grades, Reaction, Highlights Before WrestleDream 2026 Chris Mueller Oct 14, 2026 Welcome to Bleacher Report's coverage of the final Dynamite before WrestleDream this weekend. Let's take a look at what happened on this week's supersized Dynamite. The first match of the night saw Jon Moxley, Daniel Garcia and Gabe Kidd take on Wardlow, Mark Davis and Jake Doyle in a trios bout. While not explicitly babyfaces, The Death Riders were the default fan favorites in this bout due to facing the always villainous DCF. Mox spent more time than usual in the crowd during his entrance to get everyone riled up. The major exception was Wardlow, who got a pop from his hometown crowd. Garcia kicked things off against Davis, so it was the smallest guy from one team against the biggest guy from the other. Dunkzilla almost laughed at Garcia's attempt to push him at one point. The most surprising thing about this match was how structured most of it felt. Trios bouts in AEW can often be chaotic, but this one took its time building up to the more exciting stuff. This might not end up being the match of the night, but it certainly had the crowd invested, especially with AEW being in Wardlow's home of Cleveland, Ohio. It felt like all six guys contributed, but it also felt like it was teasing a possible singles feud between Wardlow and Mox. Davis ended up pinning Moxley to get the win, which definitely caught a lot of people by surprise. Another Clockwork Carnage qualifying match was up next with Adam Copeland taking on Josh Alexander, making this the second match in a row with DCF representation. They started with a simple exchange of headlocks and takedowns. Cope took control for a moment, but Alexander started going after his leg to soften him up. The Walking Weapon has rarely had a chance to show off in singles competition in AEW, so it was great to see him get the opportunity to remind everyone that he is an accomplished technical wrestler who brings a lot to the table. This was a decent match, but it felt like it lacked energy in some spots. It wasn't until well after the mid-match break that it started to pick up. Alexander sent Copeland into an exposed turnbuckle and used his own Spear against him, but it wasn't enough to get the win. Once he recovered, the Rated-R Superstar hit the Spear to get the win. While Copeland was still in the ring, Don Callis came out with Brian Cage. He told Cope he might not make it to 2027, which led to a few DCF members attacking him from behind. Konosuke Takeshita and the Conglomeration came out to make the save. Cage and Takeshita were already in the ring after the last segment, so their match got started right away after a quick video explaining Clockwork Carnage. Cage had an obvious power advantage, but Takeshita is no slouch. He is a big, strong wrestler who is also quick on his feet, so it felt like this was an even matchup. T

Staff sat through all three and a half hours of the show, and have many thoughts to share. They will laud things like the "Dynamite" closing tag match or the blistering TNT Title Match/Clockwork Carnage Qualifier that closed "Collision. There was also plenty that didn't work, and they will tell you all about it. The comments section will also be open, should you feel the need to keep the conversation going. Without further ado, here's what the staff loved and what they hated, starting with what they hated. AEW/Speedy Ruiz There's a limit to how many qualifier or tournament matches for any given special-stipulation match or prize you can feature on a single show. Five qualifier matches in three hours got really tiring and old after the second one, and I wasn't super excited about it. I also found the winners of all the qualifiers to be very predictable, which was exacerbated in the two that unnecessarily had the International and TNT Championships on the line. title: Tommaso Ciampa is living his WrestleDream in AEW
raw_title: Tommaso Ciampa is living his WrestleDream in AEW
body: Link Tommaso Ciampa is living the dream. Since arriving in AEW in January of 2026, the former WWE and NXT star has been having phenomenal matches and traveling the world with his family. His dream year culminates in Ciampa’s “own backyard,” as he takes on a very familiar face from his time in NXT: Andrade El Idolo, for the AEW National Championship at WrestleDream . Ciampa teamed up with Samoa Joe to face Will Ospreay and Andrade on AEW Dynamite , Wednesday — and I had the opportunity to sit down and talk to him about the upcoming match, his history in wrestling, and what the switch to AEW has meant to him. One thing that sticks with you in talking to Tommaso Ciampa is the complete understanding he has of the wrestling business, and his current place in it. Profoundly complimentary of other wrestlers, Ciampa speaks candidly about how glad he is to have come up in a different era. “If I came up in today’s era with such heavy social media influence, I don’t know if I’d even know how to navigate it,” Ciampa says. “I’m very lucky I came up during a time where you just went to class, put in the work, and put in the reps to get where you needed to go. If it relied on social media presence alone, I don’t think I would have done very well.” There aren’t many active wrestlers who can say they had the opportunity to train with titans like Killer Kowalski and Harley Race, but Ciampa did just that coming up in the New England indies, working for promotions like Chaotic Wrestling and Top Rope Promotions, where he cut his teeth in the business. “Killer would always invite us out to lunch after class and chat with us for as long as we wanted to answer questions. He was a huge influence on my style and approach. ‘Make the people believe’ was his main quote that he would repeat, so I’ve taken that to heart.” It’s what’s come to differentiate this era of Ciampa’s “Psycho Killer” persona, and he sees his WrestleDream fight against Andrade being very different to the standout matches the two faced off in while in NXT. “Right now we’re seeing the very best Andrade we’ve ever seen,” Ciampa says, pointing out that not only is his opponent having phenomenal matches, but has been making a mammoth impact with his new persona, and “How you know?” catchphrase, which has quickly become one of the most popular in AEW. “I was in a three-way with him in Mexico at Arena Mexico, him and Komander, and the response when his music hit was just insane.” There’s no question that Andrade enters this weekend as the fan-favorite, something Ciampa knows — but he believes the biggest pressure on both wrestlers comes from within. “It’s a fun mesh of two guys who are just hungry, have chips on their shoulders, and have a lot to prove to themselves — probably even more so than to others. But our paths have kind of been parallel at times, and right now it’s a fun place for them to intertwine.” Those crossing paths are something that’s impossible to overlook when reflecting on Tommaso Ciampa jo

title: Kenny Omega Targets Wrestle Kingdom Title Shot
raw_title: AEW's Kenny Omega Eyeing NJPW Wrestle Kingdom Return: 'I'm Aiming For The Dome'
body: AEW/Ricky Havlik Add Wrestling Inc. on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Former AEW World Champion Kenny Omega has his eyes back on a piece of gold he has a lot of history with, the IWGP Heavyweight Championship. He recently attacked current champion Yota Tsuji at NJPW King of Pro Wrestling 2026 , who Omega believes isn't doing his job by being the world champion of New Japan Pro Wrestling. This has led to Omega getting a three-way match against Tsuji and Boltin Oleg at NJPW Power Struggle 2026 to earn his shot at the champion, but Omega is already thinking to where he wants his title shot. In a translated interview with Tokyo Sports , Omega revealed that winning the title isn't the only thing he wants to achieve, as he actually wants to win the title at one of wrestling's most famous venues. "Japan is my second home, so I want to win the belt in front of New Japan's fans, and that's the biggest stage I deserve. So, of course, I'm aiming for the [Tokyo] dome. In my time, Okada was too strong, and to win the belt, I had no choice but to become a very strong all-rounder. But the current IWGP champions have almost obvious weaknesses. Tsuji is also very strong, but he lacks experience. To me, it seems like he's scared of failing on the world stage, so maybe that's why he's running away from my challenge. The Tokyo Dome will once again host NJPW's biggest show of the year, Wrestle Kingdom 21, on January 4, a venue Omega has wrestled at multiple times and even defended the IWGP Heavyweight Championship at Wrestle Kingdom 13. However, Omega wants to win the title at the iconic venue not just for his own achievements, but because he wants to show the NJPW roster what a real champion looks like. "There may be many fighters who want to beat Tsuji, but when I look at Ryogoku, I feel that few truly admire or respect him. Everyone seems to be just waiting for their turn. But if I become champion, everyone will understand that winning won't be easy, so my motivation will rise and I can practice even harder. Right now, Tsuji is just one step ahead of everyone. I want to become a champion who can't even see my back." Please credit "Tokyo Sports" when using quotes from this article, and give a H/T to Figure Four Online for the transcription.

title: AEW’s Kyle Fletcher hits the big time but keeps it all in perspective
raw_title: AEW’s Kyle Fletcher hits the big time but keeps it all in perspective
body: As a professional wrestler, Kyle Fletcher lives for the big moment, the big move, the big pop from the crowd. But when he goes outdoors, he’d rather feel small, dwarfed by the vast expanse of nature. Fletcher is one of the top stars of All Elite Wrestling, which will bring its WrestleDream pay-per-view to Addition Financial Arena on Saturday night. Fletcher, who is Australian, has wrestled on four continents. He said he tries to see much more than just the airport, the hotel and the gym when he travels, instead visiting national parks or communing with animals. His dream vacation, he said, would be an African safari. “I just love anytime I can get lost in nature,” said Fletcher, 27. “Anytime there’s a massive view, like the Grand Canyon especially, I felt so small, and I felt so in awe of the world around me. Anytime you can feel small in this world, and realize that you are insignificant, and your problems are even more insignificant, that’s a beautiful feeling. So that’s what I try to chase.” During four-plus years with AEW, Fletcher has gained a reputation as a spectacular and versatile wrestler, equally comfortable in brawls and technical masterpieces. This weekend, he teams with Kevin Knight to face the Young Bucks for the world tag-team championship. All are used to working at a fast pace with high-flying moves. Fletcher has wrestled the Bucks — considered one of the best tag teams ever — before, but he’s still studying to see what ideas he can bring to the performance of the match. “I know everybody’s moves, and how they wrestle, religiously. Everybody I’m in the ring with on any given night kind of dictates how I’m going to wrestle a little bit differently,” Fletcher said. “That’s not to say that I try to match someone else’s style, but I like to blend styles together. … I pride myself on having the physical capability to match with any style. I can do pretty much everything to bring the best out of other people and also myself.” Darby Allin: From homeless in Orlando to the top of All Elite Wrestling Fletcher said even after more than 10 years in the ring, the pressure of the spotlight can make him nervous. He said his worst tendency as a wrestler is over-analyzing himself, working up into what he calls an “internal panic” and losing the emotion of a moment in his performance. But he thrives on that pressure, a trait he remembers going all the way back to high school drama class. “Any kind of monologue I had to do, just feeling that immense pressure that if I mess up here, everyone’s looking at me … I loved it,” Fletcher said. “I loved that feeling of, ‘I can’t mess up. I physically cannot.’ And it’s something that definitely has carried over into wrestling, I think.” All Elite Wrestling brings WrestleDream to Orlando this October No matter what might be going on inside his head, Fletcher knows his most important job is making viewers suspend their disbelief and go on the emotional ride with the performers. title: Tony Khan Welcomes Skydance Merger for AEW
raw_title: Tony Khan Doubles Down on AEW's Outlook After Skydance News
body: That merger and transaction potentially created some rocky waters for the pro wrestling industry, though AEW President Tony Khan has maintained his positivity about the move . Why does the merger create questions? Paramount and its streaming service are currently in the middle of a major content distribution partnership with TKO Group, which owns WWE and UFC. All UFC events are streamed on Paramount Plus, and TKO Group is a direct competitor to Tony Khan's AEW. In addition, as with any major media merger, AEW could face an uncertain future as Skydance re-evaluates content priorities. AEW's television programming currently runs on Warner Bros. Discovery platforms, and if things stay as is, Skydance will have two competing pro-wrestling promotions on its platforms. During Khan's media press conference ahead of AEW WrestleDream on Saturday , Khan was asked about the proposed merger and doubled down on how much he thought it would be a positive for AEW. "This (the merger) is great for AEW and the wrestling fans who like AEW and watch AEW shows," Khan said. "I think AEW is going to become a stronger company and I've been very positive and said a lot of things that I was really looking forward to with this merger because I've had so many great conversations with David Ellison. I really respect him and like him a lot and I think he's going to be a fantastic leader. "So, definitely David Ellison's very positive and excited about AEW. I've had a lot of really good conversations with him as far as what's going to be the strategy of the company. I can't speak to all those things, but I think it's going to be great and I think it's great for AEW and our fans, and for the company - for Skydance and Warner Brothers." During the media appearance, Khan also revealed that two key AEW advocates at Warner Brothers Discovery were staying on board with the new Skydance company after the merger. Channing Dungy and J.B. Perrette are two high-level Warner executives who have been stewards of AEW inside the company walls. According to Khan, they will remain at Skydance. This weekend, AEW continues its 2026 PPV year with WrestleDream . Announced matches for the show include Mercedes Mone vs. Thekla for the AEW Women's World Championship, Jon Moxley vs. Mark Davis for the AEW Continental Championship, and the brand-new Clockwork Carnage match for the AEW Men's World Championship in the main event. title: Kevin Knight Previews Young Bucks Title Match

body: 02:07 Featured Video Biggest Surprise Fantasy Players 😯 Previous Next AEW's Kevin Knight on Wrestling Origin Story, Young Bucks Match at WrestleDream and More Chris Mueller Oct 15, 2026 This weekend, Kevin Knight will attempt to win his first AEW World Tag Team Championship alongside Kyle Fletcher when they battle The Young Bucks at WrestleDream. Knight has had an interesting career so far. Since beginning his journey in 2019, he has wrestled worldwide, trained at the NJPW LA Dojo, signed with AEW, and already won multiple titles in the company. He came into AEW as a babyface, winning gold in the trios division alongside the likes of Mike Bailey, Adam Page and Mistico. He also won the TNT Championship before turning heel and joining The Don Callis Family. B/R spoke with Knight this week ahead of the PPV on a variety of topics. Bleacher Report: You're about to challenge The Young Bucks at WrestleDream for the tag titles. What is the difference for you when preparing for a singles match and a tag or trios match? Kevin Knight: Truthfully, it's all the same. The preparation is hard day in and day out. With a tag team partner as good as Kyle Fletcher is, as good as he is individually, we kind of go in knowing the game plan. raw_title: AEW WrestleDream 2026 preview and predictions: 5 big questions before Will Ospreay's Clockwork Carnage
body: AEW's third pay-per-view in as many months is littered with title matches, including a brand-new concept called Clockwork Carnage, in which Will Ospreay will defend his AEW World Championship against seven other men. The Uncrowned Horsemen — Kel Dansby, Robert Jackman, Drake Riggs and Anthony Sulla-Heffinger — are here to preview WrestleDream, answer key questions and make their picks for the show. Let's ride! Dansby: I've tried reading the rules for Clockwork Carnage several times, but somehow I get more confused every time I go over them. I'm all for creativity and introducing new match concepts, but I genuinely don't know how AEW is going to pull this off in a way that makes sense to the audience. Sometimes the best gimmick matches are the simplest ones. Give fans a concept they can easily understand and let the wrestlers do the rest. I enjoy almost everything AEW puts together on pay-per-view, and I'm sure the talent involved will find a way to make this entertaining. That said, there's a difference between producing one memorable match and creating a stipulation fans want to see year after year. I'm not convinced Clockwork Carnage has what it takes to become a staple of the company moving forward. Sulla-Heffinger: Two things I'm going to need for Saturday's main event: Will Ospreay to come out in all-white gear and a black bowler, and at least one commentary reference to ultra-violence. "A Clockwork Orange" homage aside, I think it's an interesting concept, but I am skeptical to see how it plays out with eight wrestlers in the fray at once — assuming there are no eliminations before the scoring period begins. I think it will be a bit difficult to keep track of as a fan, either in the arena or watching at home. Logistics aside, there is the possibility for high drama, as you can tease Ospreay needing to come back to win or surviving with a pinfall or submission that comes right as time expires. There are plenty of compelling narrative angles to take. Ultimately, I am always a fan of innovation in wrestling — it's how we've gotten some matches that have now become iconic. I'm sure this will stick around in some fashion, perhaps with a cap of four to six wrestlers. Riggs: Whether AEW sticks with Clockwork Carnage long-term depends entirely on how cohesive the match is. In a way, AEW is at its best when finding beauty in chaos, rather than highly restrictive rulesets like this match appears to be. But that's what makes it all the more interesting. It could be one big cluster or a smashing success, like NXT's Iron Survivor Challenge. Realistically, the Iron Survivor concept should be used in a WWE main-roster situation too, so if AEW pulls off anything remotely similar, it'd be nice to see it at least once a year. It's one of those rare match types that fits the calendar well, like Elimination Chamber or Royal Rumble, and doesn't feel forced for the sake of a gimmick show, like Blood & Guts and WarGames. title: Kyle Fletcher Feels Ready For AEW World Title
raw_title: Kyle Fletcher Can’t Put A Timeline On His Potential AEW World Title Win
body: Kyle Fletcher doesn’t want to put a timeline on a potential AEW World Championship win. Fletcher is at the top of the list when it comes to wrestlers that are expected to be a world champion in the near future. With his TNT Championship and International Championship reigns, the ‘Protostar’ has already proven that he can carry a singles title. Speaking with Forbes for a new interview, Kyle Fletcher was asked to talk about how close he is to the AEW World Championship. “I feel like this is going to be a very hard question to answer. I think I feel ready. I feel ready for it. I want the pressure that comes with it. I want to be the guy that is the face of the company, and I think the guy who has that championship, by proxy, becomes the face of the company.” Continuing on, Fletcher admitted that he does feel closer than ever to the world title. “I want to be the man who’s taking that title anywhere and everywhere, getting it on TV shows in front of people. And I want to be that guy, and I feel like I’m ready to be that guy. It’s just not up to me, so I need to keep doing what I’m doing. I need to keep putting my best foot forward. I need to keep being the best version of myself, and when other people realize that I’m ready for that spot, then it will happen. I can’t put a timeline on it, really. It’s pretty hard to put a timeline on it. But I feel closer than ever, and I hope that it’s not too far off.” Kyle Fletcher will team with Kyle Fletcher to challenge the Young Bucks for the AEW World Tag Team Championships at WrestleDream. title: Seth Rollins Pays Tribute To Late AEW Star Pac
raw_title: Seth Rollins Comments On The Death Of AEW Star & Former WWE Opponent Pac
body: Rollins said it was the first time he's spoken on camera about Pac, real name Benjamin Satterley. He said it was hard to put his thoughts about who Satterley was as a person into one concise statement. "He was just an awesome dude. He was so funny and so unique," Rollins said. "He was also super loyal and he was down to earth. He was just one of those people that... We looked up to Ben. We admired him, I think, because he was so incredible at what he did in the ring but he was also so humble about that part of his life. And the way he treated people with kindness and love and there was a warmth about him." Rollins said he first met Satterley when he was 21-years-old during his first trip to Europe. He was blown away by the late star's in-ring ability. Rollins said he always thought he was athletic, but joked he thought he was going to have to find a new profession after seeing Satterley. "I hope his legacy in the wrestling world will be one thing, but his legacy amongst the people who loved him and knew him was just that he was an awesome, awesome human being," Rollins said. If you use any quotes from this article, please credit "No Contest Wrestling" and provide a h/t to Wrestling Inc. for the transcription.

Rollins recalled first meeting him at age 21 during an early trip to Europe and being awestruck by his in-ring talent, later describing him as funny, unique, loyal, humble and incredibly kind. He emphasized that while Pac's wrestling legacy is significant, those closest to him will remember him most as a genuinely warm and admirable human being.

body: This was a special three-hour edition of AEW programming, with the first two hours for Dynamite featuring multiple Clockwork Carnage qualifying matches and an AEW International Championship match between Kazuchika Okada and Myron Reed. Clockwork Carnage Qualifying Match After the match, Copeland says the last few weeks have been difficult, revealing that Christian Cage broke three ribs and suffered a collapsed lung during their TLC match at All Out. He praises Cage for powering through the match because of his work ethic and dedication to the fans. Copeland says he's done some soul-searching and recognizes that his face is no longer on teenagers' bedroom walls. He's getting older, and because of that, 2027 will be his final year in professional wrestling. He says that's why he wants to pursue the AEW World Championship. Don Callis interrupts alongside Brian Cage and says it's been a great night for the Don Callis Family. Callis says people like Copeland don't get to decide when they retire, and he'll dictate how things play out. He warns that he doesn't like Copeland's chances of making it to 2027 before Kevin Knight, Kyle Fletcher and Lance Archer attack Copeland from behind. The Conglomeration runs out to make the save. title: Christyan XO Recalls AEW/ROH Debut Path

body: The faction Shane Taylor Promotions consists of Shane Taylor, ROH Men’s Pure Champion Lee Moriarty, Trish Adora, Cpt. Shawn Dawn, Carlie Bravo, and Christyan XO. Out of the group members, Christyan is the newest. She participated in a virtual signing with Captain’s Corner and detailed how she got started with AEW/ROH. “Last December, I did some extra work with them… So, they offered me a few times after I did extra work and yeah, it was pretty awesome.” She was asked where she did extra work for AEW, and she said, “The first one was — I wanna say in Virginia — but where I got offered was in New York.” She spoke about her connection with Carlie Bravo and added that the entire group has been helpful. She is happy to be with them. “Amazing person,” she said about Carlie Bravo. “I love the opportunity to be able to work beside him. I wouldn’t wanna be standing beside anybody else… The whole group, all amazing people, and they make everything super fun, and they help guide me and help me these past couple of months so, amazing people. Very happy I’m with them.” “I love Trish (Adora) as well. She always helps me out if I’m feeling nervous and stuff. Again, she’s like a sister to me. She’s amazing.” Christyan continued, “I learn a lot from her and (to) be able to go out there with her, I’m very grateful. Amazing wrestler. I love Trish.” Christyan began her in-ring career in 2024. She reguarly competes for the Maryland Championship Wrestling promotion. She last wrestled for Ring of Honor at a taping in April 2026. body: Share Facebook X WhatsApp Linkedin Reddit Copy AEW Watch AEW WrestleDream live on DAZN Adam Copeland has announced that he will retire from professional wrestling in 2027 , bringing one of the most celebrated careers in WWE and AEW history towards its conclusion. The 52-year-old, formerly known as Edge in WWE , made the emotional revelation during AEW Dynamite on Wednesday, October 14 , shortly after defeating Josh Alexander to secure his place in the Clockwork Carnage match at WrestleDream. Copeland admitted that a serious injury suffered by his longtime friend and tag team partner Christian Cage had forced him to reflect on his own future in wrestling. However, the WWE Hall of Famer made clear that he has one major ambition remaining before hanging up his boots: winning the AEW World Championship . He will have an opportunity to achieve that goal at AEW WrestleDream on Saturday, October 17 , when he competes in an eight-man championship match against Will Ospreay and six other stars. Copeland made the announcement following his victory over Josh Alexander in a Clockwork Carnage qualifying match on Wednesday night. After securing the win with a Spear, the veteran wrestler addressed the crowd and spoke openly about the physical demands of professional wrestling and the reality that his career is approaching its conclusion. The former WWE champion acknowledged that his place in the industry has changed as he has grown older, before delivering the news that 2027 will be his final year competing. "My face isn't on the posters on teenagers' walls anymore. I'm aging out, and that's okay. It happens to everybody," Copeland told the audience. The announcement represents a major moment for AEW, with Copeland having established himself as one of the promotion's most recognisable stars since joining in 2023. However, he made clear that he does not intend to spend his remaining time simply reflecting on his achievements. "It's time. But all of that being said, that is why I have to go for the AEW Championship," he declared. His comments confirmed that the pursuit of the AEW World Championship will be central to the final chapter of his wrestling career. Although Copeland has confirmed that 2027 will be his final year, he has not announced the exact date or event at which he intends to wrestle his final match . title: Adam Copeland Announces 2027 Retirement
raw_title: Adam Copeland to retire in 2027 after Christian Cage sustains collapsed lung at AEW All Out
body: On Wednesday's "AEW Dynamite," Copeland defeated Josh Alexander in a Clockwork Carnage qualifier match to advance to Saturday's AEW World title match at AEW WrestleDream 2026 . The match saw Copeland return to singles action following his recent tag-team championship run alongside longtime friend and rival Christian Cage. The biggest surprise of the night came after the match, when the 52-year-old Copeland revealed that 2027 will be his last year as a professional wrestler. "My face isn't on the posters on teenagers' walls anymore. I'm aging out, and that's OK. It happens to everybody. But because of that, I just want to let y'all know that 2027 will be my last year in professional wrestling. "I get it. It's time, but all of that being said, that is why I have to go for the AEW Championship." Copeland has been wrestling on borrowed time since he initially retired from WWE in 2011 due to serious neck injuries. In 2020, he miraculously returned for that year's WWE Royal Rumble match in what many consider the greatest pro-wrestling comeback of all time. His final stint with WWE ended in 2023 before he joined AEW. His longtime best friend and teammate Cage also previously had to his career put on hold because of injuries — and unfortunately, it's happened again. Before his announcement, Copeland shared that Cage suffered serious injuries in their three-way ladder match at All Out 2026 , which will sideline Cage indefinitely, if not permanently. "What a lot of people don't know is that at the tables, ladders, and chair match at All Out in Chicago two weeks ago, Christian Cage was thrown into a ladder five minutes into the match. What we didn't know is that he ended up breaking three ribs. One rib broken in three places, and suffered a collapsed lung — five minutes into the match. Yet, at the end, he was standing on top of those ladders reaching for our tag-team championships. He did that because of his work ethic, and he did it for all of you. The duo of Cage & Cope are wrestling royalty with nothing more to prove after their great final stretch teaming together. For Copeland, though, he'll try to add one more world title to his mantle this Saturday in the promotion's first-ever Clockwork Carnage match. However, after defeating Alexander — a member of the Don Callis Family — the rest of the stable won't make it easy for Copeland, as they attacked him afterward on Wednesday's show. "I hate to tell ya, buddy, but I'm usually right on these little predictions of mine," said Callis. "I don't like your chances of seeing 2027. In fact, I don't like your chances of seeing Clockwork Carnage this Saturday."
summary: Adam Copeland defeated Josh Alexander in a qualifier on AEW Dynamite to earn a shot at the AEW World Championship at WrestleDream 2026. Following the victory, the 52-year-old revealed that 2027 will be his final year in professional wrestling as he feels he is aging out of the spotlight. Copeland's announcement came after his recent tag team run with Christian Cage, whose career has once again been sidelined by injury.

title: AEW Sets ROH Final Battle 2026 For San Antonio
raw_title: AEW Reveals Date And Location For ROH Final Battle 2026
body: AEW/Ricky Havlik Add Wrestling Inc. on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover As the end of the calendar year approaches, so is Ring of Honor's biggest event of the year, Final Battle. ROH's signature December event has become a staple of the wrestling calendar since 2002, and this year, it will be taking place in San Antonio, Texas. Typically with AEW's schedule, the venue that hosts Final Battle will often host an episode of "AEW Collision" the following day, which in this case is Saturday, December 5, a date that has not yet been listed on AEW's official website. AEW will already be in Texas that week as the December 2 episode of "AEW Dynamite" will take place in Laredo, before the entire roster heads south of the border to Mexico for the Winter is Coming TV specials in Monterrey. Since Tony Khan purchased Ring of Honor back in 2022, Final Battle has played host to some very memorable moments. In that same year, FTR and The Briscoes rounded out their trilogy of ROH World Tag Team Championship matches with a brutal Double Dog Collar match, while Athena dethroned Mercedes Martinez to become the ROH Women's World Champion. Athena has since headlined every Final Battle event, defending her title against her protégé Billie Starkz on two occasions, while also defeating Persephone at last year's event. If Athena keeps hold of her title through Final Battle until the end of the year, she will become the first champion in ROH history to hold any title for four consecutive years.

title: Mike Bailey Excited For AEW Clockwork Carnage Main Event
raw_title: Mike Bailey: Clockwork Carnage Is The Kind Of Match That I’ve Worked So Hard To Be Perfectly Prepared For
body: The pay-per-view is set to feature the company’s first Clockwork Carnage match . With the intrigue of a new stipulation and the stacked lineup of competitors, the bout will likely bring in some new eyeballs. Speaking with Fightful’s Sean Ross Sapp, Mike Bailey spoke about his excitement for the match. “It feels absolutely fantastic and the great thing about AEW pay-per-views is that this is All Elite Wrestling This is where the best wrestle. Any match could be the main event. But this will be my first time main eventing an AEW pay-per-view for the AEW World Championship, and where I would like to be is I would like to be defending the AEW World Championship as the main event of a pay-per-view. But I am getting there and this is the first step.” Bailey also recalled hearing about the idea from Ospreay before it was announced. “So since joining United Empire, I’ve gotten a lot closer to Will Ospreay. This is a concept that he had mentioned in the past and I saw it on TV when they announced it and, honestly, I love ridiculous match ideas more than anyone on earth quite possibly. The more complex the better and when I saw it announced on TV, I was like, ‘We are doing this for real.,’ and I was excited to watch it. My first thought was, ‘Wow, this is going to be incredible. I can’t wait to see this.’ It wasn’t in my mind yet. I thought Will Ospreay’s in this, he’s the head of United Empire. I would like to qualify, obviously, but it wasn’t until I was able to actually bring that up and make that happen.” Rounding out the topic, Bailey described the Clockwork Carnage match as “the kind of match” that he wants to be in. “But now that I’m gonna be in it, it feels all the more surreal. But this is exactly the kind of match that I’ve worked so hard for my career to be perfectly prepared for, having been in DDT, in some of the most ridiculous matches in professional wrestling history. Also, throughout my independent career, I did hour-long, 45-minute-long, 30-minute matches, sometimes—very often—several times a week. So this is exactly the kind of match that I want to be in.” Elsewhere in the interview, Mike Bailey talked about joining United Empire. Check out his full comments by clicking here. title: Adam Copeland to Retire in 2027
raw_title: AEW Star and Former WWE Champion Will Retire in 2027
body: Since 2025, the wrestling world has watched WWE legends Goldberg, John Cena, AJ Styles and Brock Lesnar retire. Now, a top AEW star and former WWE Champion is gearing up for one last rodeo. During Wednesday night's episode of AEW Dynamite , Adam Copeland (formerly known as Edge in WWE) announced that he'll retire from in-ring competition in 2027. "I am ageing out, and that's okay; it happens to everybody," Copeland told a stunned crowd at the Wolstein Center in Cleveland, Ohio. "But because of that, I just wanted to let y'all know that 2027 will be my last year in professional wrestling." Copeland announced the news after defeating Josh Alexander to qualify for the Clockwork Carnage match for the AEW World Championship at Saturday's WrestleDream pay-per-view. Copeland has yet to win the AEW World Championship, currently held by Will Ospreay. However, the former has won the AEW TNT Championship twice and previously held the AEW World Tag Team Championship with Christian Cage, his longtime wrestling partner. In 2011, Edge announced he had to retire prematurely at age 37 due to spinal stenosis. However, the WWE Hall of Famer never gave up on a return to the ring, and he made his thrilling return at the 2020 Royal Rumble. After a three-year second stint in AEW, Copeland signed with All Elite Wrestling. An 11-time world champion in WWE (seven World Heavyweight titles and four WWE Championships), Copeland has had a remarkable career that will hopefully end on a high note in 2027. This story was originally published by Men's Journal on Oct 15, 2026, where it first appeared in the News section. Add Men's Journal as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
summary: Adam Copeland announced on this week's AEW Dynamite that 2027 will be his final year as an active wrestler. The former WWE Champion made the statement in Cleveland after defeating Josh Alexander to qualify for the Clockwork Carnage match at WrestleDream, where he will challenge for the AEW World Championship held by Will Ospreay. Copeland previously retired in 2011 due to spinal stenosis before returning in 2020 and joining AEW for a three-year run that included two TNT Championship reigns and one AEW World Tag Team Championship with Christian Cage.

title: Zach Gowen Announces In-Ring Retirement
raw_title: Zach Gowen Retires From In-Ring Competition
body: Taking to his Facebook page, Zach Gowen shared the news that he has officially retired from in-ring competition. “First promo pic and last promo pic! My in-ring career has come to an end. Thank you to every promoter who gave me an opportunity to wrestle. I’ve had the privilege of performing for every major company over the past 24 years. Special thank you to the fans for not rejecting me. Pro wrestling provided a direction and outlet for a very lost kid. All I ever wanted to be was a professional wrestler and I accomplished that solely because you accepted me not as a sideshow act but as a legitimate pro wrestler. I’m deeply grateful. The best moment of my career was wrestling for AEW in front of my wife, kids, and parents. That was the cherry on top after burning my career to the ground as a result of my crippling drug addiction then having the opportunity to not only rebuild my life but my passion then sharing that with the world while enjoying every second of it. My victories are not the result of my talents but ultimately the result of God working through others allowing them to pour into and invest in me. I am the luckiest guy in the world.” Gowen began his in-ring career in 2002. He had a run in WWE in 2003. He’s competed for a multitude of different independent promotions, and towards the later years of his career, he made his way to IMPACT Wrestling, AEW, and Maple Leaf Pro Wrestling. Gowen was a producer at Maple Leaf Pro’s Northern Rising show.
summary: Zach Gowen revealed on social media that he has retired from professional wrestling after a 24-year career. The one-legged wrestler began in 2002, had a notable run in WWE during 2003, and worked for numerous independent promotions along with a recent appearance for AEW that he called the highlight of his career. He credited fans, promoters and his faith for his journey from personal struggles with addiction to rebuilding his life and passion for the business.

Tony Khan is feeling positive about AEW’s future under its new corporate structure. His conversations with Skydance CEO David Ellison have given him a lot of reasons to be optimistic. The AEW President has shared how Ellison feels about the wrestling promotion following Skydance’s acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery. Speaking during the WrestleDream 2026 media call , Khan discussed his talks with Skydance executives and explained why he believes the change in ownership could benefit AEW. According to Khan, Ellison has been “very excited and positive about AEW” and believes in what the promotion is building. “I think AEW is going to become a stronger company and I’ve been very positive and said a lot of things that I was really looking forward to this merger because I’ve had so many great conversations with David Ellison, and I really respect him and like him a lot. I think he’s going to be a fantastic leader,” Khan revealed. Having a good relationship with Ellison could prove crucial for AEW. Skydance’s acquisition of WBD gives the company influence over AEW’s TV partner. As a result, the new leadership’s attitude toward wrestling could play a big role in the future. Khan’s comments suggest that his early conversations with Ellison have gone well. However, the long-term impact of the corporate changes remains yet to play out. title: Speedball Mike Bailey says shared wrestling passion strengthens marriage
raw_title: EXCLUSIVE: Speedball Mike Bailey says their marriage with Veda Scott works well because they both love wrestling
body: Speedball Mike Bailey says their marriage to pro wrestling commentator Veda Scott works well despite them having different schedules because they both love wrestling. “I think the reason Veda is so good at commentary is because just like myself, we are both, and always have been, obsessed with professional wrestling,” said Bailey during an interview on Radican Worldwide available now for PWTorch VIP members. “You hear of some people who are like, ‘Oh, uh, this is very common in, uh, couples in professional wrestling,’ right? But we keep our work and our personal life separate. We don’t talk about pro wrestling at home. And we are the complete opposite. We love it. We love to talk about it. We love to dissect it.” Bailey said that although they are often on different shows in different places, they love to get on the phone after the show and talk about the shows they participated in that night. “So often we are gonna be doing separate shows,” said Bailey. “I’ll be doing a Dynamite, and Veda will be doing a CMLL show, and then as soon as the show is done, we’ll get on the phone, and we will break down our shows match by match, moment by moment, and dissect every little piece of it, because we absolutely love pro wrestling. “And I don’t know how our relationship would work if we didn’t share the thing that we are both the most passionate about. So I mean, I’m so grateful for Veda.” NOTE: You can GO VIP and listen to the entire interview with Mike Bailey talking about transitioning from TNA to AEW, joining United Empire, and the Clockwork Carnage match for the AEW World Hvt. Championship at WrestleDream on Oct. 17 HERE Speedball Bailey will challenge for the AEW World Hvt. Championship on Oct. 17 in the Clockwork Carnage match at the WrestleDream PPV against seven other wrestlers including Samoa Joe, Adam Copeland, Konosuke Takeshita, Kazuchika Okada, Ricochet, Darby Allin, and AEW World Hvt. Champion Will Ospreay. You can purchase the WrestleDream on HBO Max, traditional PPV providers, and PPV.com .
summary: Speedball Mike Bailey explained that his marriage to commentator Veda Scott thrives because both are deeply obsessed with professional wrestling. The couple deliberately keeps work and personal life separate at home yet eagerly discusses and analyzes each other's shows over the phone after events, including when Bailey works a Dynamite and Scott calls a CMLL show. Bailey noted they love breaking down matches and moments in detail, contrasting with many wrestling couples who avoid the topic outside of work.

title: On the Record: AEW's Samoa Joe Discusses 'WrestleDream' & 'Twisted Metal' Season 3
raw_title: AEW's Samoa Joe Talks 'WrestleDream' & 'Twisted Metal' Season 3
body: Samoa Joe brings a certain level of intimidation whenever he appears on All Elite Wrestling . This largely stems from respect and a reputation earned over the former world champion’s two decades in the business. The combination of his body of work and overall imposing aura made him the perfect vessel for the Sweet Tooth killer clown character on Twisted Metal . The real-life adaptation of the video game is set to return for Season 3 on Peacock . While Joe plays the actual iconic figure onscreen, Will Arnett voices the role. Joe, real name Joe Seanoa, returned to AEW in September after filming and didn’t lose a step by defeating Jack Perry during the special Dynamite : Grand Slam France on TBS from Paris. The win qualified him for the Clockwork Carnage match at the WrestleDream pay-per-view from Orlando on October 17. Will Ospreay puts the AEW World Championship on the line in a unique environment involving seven contenders with Joe among them. The bout begins with two randomly selected wrestles before the others join the fray every three minutes. Those eliminated by pinfall or submission during the opening round will not move on to the final phase. It’s then the remaining participants will have 15 minutes to earn as many points as possible with the most total falls leaving with the gold. Here Joe tells us how he is preparing for the big main event. The star also chats about what it was like on the Twisted Metal set with the addition of his onscreen dad Mark Hamill . You came back to AEW at a time of mourning as the company lost Pac (Benjamin Satterley) and The Butcher (Andy Williams) in a matter of weeks. There seems to be such camaraderie in the locker room, but especially when these tragedies occur. The company really had a moving tribute. What has it been like to move forward, which I know isn’t easy? Samoa Joe: You know, the truth of it is there is no real established protocol beyond how anybody grieves amongst friends and loved ones. I think in times like this we try to be there for each other and available for that late-night call if you need to talk about it or something like that. I think we’re just more sensitive to that around these times. Obviously, the loss of Ben and Andy was felt far and beyond even AEW. Almost every locker room in the world felt it because they made an impact in the many places that they worked. With the show must go on mentality, I think if anything, we’re grateful that we even have the opportunity to have the show go on. I think we’re just more cognizant of that, I think we’re a bit more grateful of that. I think the endeavor that kind of starts with gratitude usually ends up being pretty spectacular in the end. Tony [Khan] is very admirable in that he’s very sensitive to these types of situations and how much we as performers mean to each other, especially over the breadth of our career and the journey that is what we do. However, I think that is across the board. I think it’d be selfish to say it is just AEW. I
summary: Samoa Joe brings a certain level of intimidation whenever he appears on All Elite Wrestling . This largely stems from respect and a reputation earned over the former world champion’s two decades in the business.

title: Christian Cage sidelined with broken ribs and collapsed lung
raw_title: AEW star Christian Cage out injured with broken ribs, collapsed lung
body: Last seen wrestling at AEW All Out 2026 in a ladder match, Christian Cage has not wrestled since. On the latest Oct. 14, 2026 episode of AEW Dynamite, Cage's best friend and tag team partner, Adam Copeland , shared the latest update on him. Following his match against Josh Alexander, Copeland revealed that Cage had suffered a few serious injuries during their match at AEW All Out. Copeland defeated Alexander and qualified for the Clockwork Carnage match at WrestleDream. After the match, Copeland took a microphone and discussed the unfortunate incident that happened during the three-way ladder match for the AEW World Tag Team Championships at All Out. According to Copeland, Cage suffered three broken ribs and a collapsed lung after being thrown into a ladder within the first five minutes of the match. Despite the serious injuries, Cage continued the match and remained involved even in the closing stages of the bout. He further praised his longtime tag team partner's determination and love for the sport. Copeland explained that Cage pushed through the injury and the pain due to his commitment to the AEW fans. However, the injuries were serious, and he was ruled out of action. Cage, 52, is one of the most successful and popular wrestlers in the industry. A wrestling veteran, Cage has performed all over the world under multiple promotions. A former AEW Tag Team Champion, Cage is also a former two-time AEW TNT Champion as well as a Trios Champion. As of now, there have been no confirmed updates regarding Cage's return.
summary: Adam Copeland revealed on the October 14 episode of AEW Dynamite that Christian Cage suffered three broken ribs and a collapsed lung during the three-way ladder match for the AEW World Tag Team Championships at All Out. Despite the injuries occurring in the opening minutes, Cage continued wrestling through the pain and stayed involved until the end of the bout. Copeland praised his longtime partner's dedication to the fans before confirming that the 52-year-old veteran is now ruled out of action.

title: Zayda Steel Reflects On Dream Match With Mercedes Mone
raw_title: AEW's Zayda Steel Plans To 'Run It Back' With Mercedes Mone
body: AEW/Ricky Havlik Add Wrestling Inc. on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover It's not often in professional wrestling that a performer gets to lock up with one of their idols, let alone getting that chance so early in their career. However, Zayda Steel got that chance on the August 15 episode of "AEW Collision" when she went one-on-one with the current AEW Women's World Champion Mercedes Mone. On the night, it was "The CEO" who picked up a routine victory as she was building momentum ahead of the match where she would win the world title from Willow Nightingale, but for Steel, it was a night she will never forget. Steel opened up about the moment she wrestled Mone during a recent interview with MuscleManMalcolm on "Muscle Memory," admitting that she almost burst into tears just walking down the ramp. "My music hit and instantly I tried to hold back tears on my entrance," Steel said. "Like I've never blanked out that quick in a match. That was like my comfort wrestler you know? You know when you deal with a lot in life and you have your like comfort people? Mercedes was always that for me, and to get that early on year one, I haven't even been in AEW for a year and I got my dream match already. So I already know after year one, I'm only going to get better and better. So Mercedes, we're going to run it back." Mone wasn't the only idol of Steel's that the 22-year old has had the privilege of facing in AEW throughout 2026 as she was also involved in a mixed trios match that saw her go up against Jon Moxley. Steel admitted that she used to edit videos of Moxley, and her first piece of wrestling merchandise was Moxley's when he wrestled in WWE as Dean Ambrose so she was extremely nervous, so nervous in fact that she believes she actually hurt Moxley's groin during the bout, but Steel is glad that she survived such a stressful ordeal. Please credit "Muscle Memory" when using quotes from this article, and give a H/T to Wrestling Inc. for the transcription.

title: Copeland, Takeshita Qualify For AEW WrestleDream Clockwork Carnage
raw_title: Adam Copeland And More Fill Out AEW WrestleDream Clockwork Carnage
body: AEW/Ricky Havlik Add Wrestling Inc. on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover The AEW World Championship will be on the line in the first-ever Clockwork Carnage match at AEW WrestleDream 2026 on October 17, and on the special three-hour broadcast of "AEW Dynamite" and "AEW Collision" on October 14 , the rest of the field was determined in a series of qualifiers. In the first of the qualifiers without any championships on the line, Adam Copeland made his first appearance in the ring since AEW All Out 2026 by defeating Josh Alexander. "The Walking Weapon" spent the majority of the match targeting the leg of the "Rated-R Superstar," the same leg that Copeland broke back in 2024. However, the one variable that Alexander didn't take into account was one he brought into the match himself, the exposed turnbuckle. In the closing moments, Alexander went head-first into the turnbuckle to stun him, allowing Copeland to muster enough momentum to hit a Spear to book his spot in the match. Immediately after, Konosuke Takeshita also made his return to action in AEW back outlasting Brian Cage. "The Machine" dug deep into his bag of tricks, even hitting an Avalanche Hurricanrana and a Tope Con Hilo to throw "The Alpha" off his game. Takeshita tried to stick to his game plan but Cage kept firing back to keep the match even, resulting in Takeshita being forced to change strategy. This would ultimately prove fruitful for Takeshita as he managed to hit the Power Drive Knee and then locked in a Dragon Sleeper to get the submission victory. Rounding out the non-title qualifiers was Ricochet getting the win over Ace Austin of The Bang Bang Gang. Austin was stepping in to replace the injured "Switchblade" Jay White, and had kept himself in the fight by using his speed and his leg strength, kicking Ricochet at every opportunity. Ricochet would also use his speed to maintain the momentum and almost went to the well on time too often by missing a Shooting Star Press, but he caught Austin off guard with a Headbutt, and landed a Spirit Gun and a Vertigo to get the win. Copeland, Takeshita, and Ricochet join the current AEW World Champion Will Ospreay, Samoa Joe, "Speedball" Mike Bailey, and Kazuchika Okada in the Clockwork Carnage match, with the final spot belonging to either Darby Allin or Hechicero.

title: Adam Copeland Sets 2027 Retirement
raw_title: Adam Copeland Announces 2027 Retirement, Provides Injury Update On Christian Cage
body: AEW/Ricky Havlik Add Wrestling Inc. on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Adam Copeland defeated Josh Alexander on " AEW Dynamite " to qualify for the Clockwork Carnage match at AEW WrestleDream on Saturday, and following the match on Wednesday, he had some major news, as well as an update on his tag team partner, for fans. The qualifier was Copeland's first AEW bout since the three-way ladder match for the AEW World Tag Team Championships at All Out . During that match, Copeland revealed that Christian Cage suffered a collapsed lung, as well as multiple broken ribs, after being thrown into a ladder just five minutes into the bout. Copeland said Cage finished the match due to his work ethic, and he did it all for the fans. He said because that happened to his best friend, he realized he needed to sit down and do some soul-searching. Copeland revealed that 2027 will be his final year competing in the ring, and he wants to go for the AEW World Championship. The soon-to-be 53-year-old said that he realized he's no longer the guy on posters on teenager's walls, and he's okay aging out. The speech then brought out Don Callis, who said he was sorry to interrupt Copeland "pity party," but it was going to be a good "Dynamite" for the Don Callis Family. He said that he didn't like Copeland's chances of seeing 2027, and Copeland might not even see Clockwork Carnage on Saturday. That's when other members of the DCF, including Kevin Knight and Lance Archer, took Copeland out from behind.

title: Adam Copeland Sets 2027 Retirement
raw_title: AEW’s Adam Copeland announces retirement with a catch
body: Pretty soon, legendary professional wrestler and AEW star Adam Copeland will retire, and this time, the former WWE star known as Edge will really hang it up. During the Oct. 14, 2026, edition of AEW Dynamite, Copeland, who turns 53 on Oct. 30, revealed his plans to retire next year. He said that 2027 would be his final year of in-ring competition. The announcement came after he defeated Josh Alexander in a Clockwork Carnage-qualifying match. That said, he will not go down without a fight. During his announcement, he said that he would be going after the AEW World Championship. Since joining AEW three years ago, Copeland has won the TNT Championship twice. However, he has never won the company's top prize. We'll see if he's successful, though. During his final WWE run, he chased the Universal Championship, which was held by Roman Reigns, for a while. He never won it, though. Father Time is undefeated, and Copeland, who is in his fifties, has been wrestling for the better part of over 30 years. He is a legend, but nothing lasts forever. So, fans will have to take it in while they can. He has given fans a second run that seemed impossible years ago. In 2011, he retired from professional wrestling after WrestleMania 27 after being diagnosed with cervical spinal stenosis. He would stay retired for almost nine years until the 2020 Royal Rumble, making his surprise return in the battle royal. This kickstarted the second part of his career. Copeland, then going by Edge , remained in WWE until 2023. During that stretch, he had matches against old foes like Randy Orton as well as new faces like Reigns, Finn Bálor, and Seth Rollins. His last WWE match was against Sheamus during the Aug. 18, 2023, edition of Friday Night SmackDown.

The 52-year-old revealed his plans immediately after defeating Josh Alexander in a Clockwork Carnage qualifier and stated he intends to pursue the AEW World Championship before retiring. body: AEW Add Wrestling Inc. on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover The Motor City Machine Guns challenged FTR to a best of five series during "AEW Dynamite." title: Okada Retains Title and Advances to Clockwork Carnage
raw_title: Kazuchika Okada Retains AEW International Title In Clockwork Carnage Qualifier
body: AEW/Ricky Havlik Add Wrestling Inc. on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Kazuchika Okada is not only still AEW International Champion, he also qualified for the Clockwork Carnage match at AEW WrestleDream on Saturday with a victory over Myron Reed on "AEW Dynamite" on Wednesday . After a back-and-forth beginning to the match, Reed attempted a backslide, but Okada slipped out of it. Reed hit an enziguri to Okada and knocked him out of the ring, but "The Rainmaker" was back inside quickly, where he avoided a boot from the challenger. Okada sent Reed face-first into the mat to gain control of the match. Okada went to the top rope, but saw Reed get his knees up and avoided disaster. Reed then went to the top to look for a 450 splash, but Okada rolled out of the ring. Reed took him down on the outside with a big dive. Okada rolled out of the way of another 450 attempt and hit a dropkick. Reed dodged the Rainmaker, and Okada dodged a cutter and hit Reed with a piledriver, but Reed rolled out of the ring, where he hit a back body drop to Okada, sending him to the floor. Reed hit a 450 from the steps to Okada on the outside, then attempted another in the ring. Okada rolled out of the way once again and hit the Rainmaker for the victory.

body: AEW Add Wrestling Inc. on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Darby Allin beat Hechicero to retain the TNT Championship and qualify for WrestleDream's Clockwork Carnage during the "AEW Collision" portion of Wednesday's show. title: David Finlay Adapting To AEW Style And Schedule
raw_title: David Finlay Details Aspects Of AEW He's Still Adjusting To
body: AEW Add Wrestling Inc. on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover AEW's David Finlay has detailed the various things that he has had to adapt to since making the switch from NJPW. Finlay joined AEW earlier this year after spending over a decade in NJPW, where he was a two-time IWGP Global Heavyweight Champion . Despite being a supremely experienced wrestler, Finlay has had to get accustomed to his new surroundings, particularly the wrestling style. "I feel like work-wise, I'm still trying to figure it out because it's just a completely different style. But the schedule is so much nicer. I went from, like, a short tour would be like 10 days, which is easy, but then we'd have the G1, which is 6 weeks long, and it's the G1, it's the toughest tournament in the world," he said when speaking to Chris Jericho on " Talk is Jericho ." Finlay also noted that he has had to adjust to the way AEW films its TV shows compared to NJPW, particularly the cameras, as well as sticking to the time allotted for each match. "Yeah, I'm still adjusting [to the cameras]. I had a little bit of experience working for companies in the States, like just a tiny bit, so it wasn't completely foreign to me. But, like, in New Japan, it's like, do the match and they'll catch you. Also, if you're in the main event in New Japan, it's like, yeah, however long you want to go. If you get told time, it's usually, like, a range, like from here to here, whatever," he said. He explained that AEW has stricter time limits for matches and segments, and he believes that working within those limits requires a certain level of skill. However, he said he enjoys working in such environments, where he has to constantly adapt during a match. Since debuting in AEW, Finlay has joined forces with fellow former NJPW stars Clark Connors and Gabe Kidd. The trio even won the AEW World Trios Championship, although their reign lasted just a few days.

title: Samoa Joe Says AEW Locker Room Bands Together After Losses
raw_title: AEW's Samoa Joe On Losing Pac & Andy Williams: 'In These Times We Band Together'
body: AEW/Lee South Add Wrestling Inc. on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Last month, the world lost both Andy "The Butcher" Williams and Pac, only weeks apart from each other. Speaking to TVInsider, AEW star Samoa Joe was asked about the atmosphere backstage following his recent return and he shared how the locker room has dealt with losing both men so close together. "There's no real established protocol beyond how anybody grieves amongst friends and loved ones," Joe said. "I think in times like this, we try to be there for each other and available for that late-night call if you need to talk about it or something like that." Joe feels the loss of Williams and Pac has resonated throughout the wrestling world, beyond just AEW, which reflects the impacts that both men made during their careers. He also believes that continuing to work has helped the locker room process the loss. "I think, if anything, we're grateful that we even have the opportunity to have the show go on," he continued. AEW honored both wrestlers with their own tribute shows, including 10-bell salutes. Williams' tribute was capped off with a 12-man battle royal on "AEW Collision," while the "AEW Dynamite" in honor of Pac featured a main event pitting his former Death Riders stablemates against The Don Callis Family in a 10-man tag team match. Joe also praised AEW President Tony Khan for his sensitivity toward the talent, along with emphasizing the solidarity shown in the locker room. "I think in these times we band together. We definitely cherish and have a better understanding that our time on this earth is precious," Joe said, honing in on what the loss has meant to him. "We should tell the people that we care about them, and we love them when we get the opportunity."

title: Match Made: Ricochet qualifies for Clockwork Carnage, Moxley shows rare emotion, Wayne and Jericho interact, Darby vs. Hechicero — AEW COLLISION HITS & MISSES (10/14)

body: To help add context, my “Hits” are ordered from best to worst. With that said, let’s move into the high points of this week’s episode. The entire Nick Wayne segment was excellent. From the pyro throughout his entrance to Wayne reminding everyone that he defeated Chris Jericho, AEW went out of its way to make him feel like a big deal. Wayne interrupting Jericho’s entrance music and controlling the video presentation himself was another nice touch. Coming off arguably the biggest victory of his career, Wayne needed a presentation that matched the significance of that win. The video package highlighting Wayne was incredible, and Jericho delivering a low blow was a great way to close the segment and continue their rivalry heading into their WrestleDream rematch. Wayne and Jericho have shown great chemistry together, and this was another example of why their pairing works so well. Jon Moxley showed a level of raw emotion during his backstage interview with Renee Paquette. Whatmade this segment particularly effective was Renee’s position as both a professional interviewer and Moxley’s wife. When she asked what was wrong and what was happening, there was genuine concern behind those questions. Moxley admitted he was in a great deal of pain. When Renee asked what kind of pain he was experiencing, Moxley said he couldn’t tell the difference anymore. This was a rare moment of vulnerability from someone who typically presents himself as nearly indestructible. Marina Shafir then stepped in, telling Moxley to keep his eyes up and lock in, reminding him that “the only way out is through.” It was a strong closing moment that showed a different side of Moxley while reinforcing Marina’s role alongside him. Styles make fights, and Darby Allin and Hechicero worked extremely well together in the main event. Rather than simply overpowering Darby or playing the role of a monster, Hechicero relied on his technical ability to ground Darby throughout the match. What made this match work was the contrast in styles. Hechicero used his skill and technique to control the pace, forcing Darby to find another way to fight back. Eventually, Darby turned his entire body into a weapon, punishing Hechicero with multiple Coffin Drops to secure the victory, retain the TNT Championship, and earn his spot in Clockwork Carnage. Tony Khan has a tendency to give fans a lot of credit for knowing wrestlers from the international and independent scenes. While I understand that approach, I don’t think it’s doing Dani Luna any favors. Luna made a cold debut on pay-per-view and has quickly become another face in the background. That’s disappointing because I know how talented she is. Rather than continuing down this path, AEW might need to take a couple of steps backward to take one forward. Give Luna some vignettes and video packages that highlight who she is and what makes her different. She’s talented enough to get over, but the audience needs a reason to invest in her. title: WWE Hall Of Famer Confirms He Will End His Career In AEW In 2027
raw_title: WWE Hall Of Famer Confirms He Will End His Career In AEW In 2027
body: By Josh Coulson Published Oct 15, 2026, 4:53 AM EDT Josh studied Journalism and Media and Cultural Studies at the University of the West of England, graduating in the summer of 2014.. Josh is a writer at TheSportster and a lifelong wrestling fan who has been doing news coverage of WWE and AEW for many years. Pro wrestling got its hooks in him at the age of ten and he's been watching ever since. His favorite wrestlers are The Rock and CM Punk, despite the latter doing his level best to make us all dislike him. Sign in to your TheSportster account Adam Copeland , formerly known as Edge in WWE, revealed on Wednesday's Dynamite that his career is coming to an end, technically for the second time. Copeland confirmed that 2027 will be his final year competing as a pro wrestler, but he wants to do something before he leaves the ring for good. Copeland, along with his long-time tag partner and best friend Christian Cage, rolled back the clock at All Out by competing in a three-way tag team ladder match, a match type they created almost 30 years ago. Copeland and Cage lost the AEW Tag Titles in that match, and the latter suffered serious injuries that will take a while to heal. Copeland revealed as much before confirming his retirement plans, revealing Cage broke some ribs and punctured a lung a few minutes into the match. It's those injuries that have led Copeland to decide it's probably time he retired. The WWE Hall of Famer didn't say when exactly - just that he wants to be a World Champion one last time before he heads off into the sunset. That might happen as soon as this weekend, as Copeland has secured his spot in the Clockwork Carnage match at WrestleDream. A new match type to AEW, and with seven other wrestlers in there, the odds will very much be stacked against him, but it's an opportunity to become AEW World Champion nonetheless. Should Copeland not win the title this weekend, then it seems his entire gimmick heading into his final year as a wrestler will be about him trying to become World Champion one more time. Copeland is one of the most decorated performers in pro wrestling history, having won 11 World Championships over the course of his career. However, not only were all of those wins in WWE, but they all came before his initial retirement in 2011. Copeland actually had to relinquish the last World Championship he won due to that first retirement after having successfully defended it at WrestleMania 27. Copeland was told by doctors that he could no longer wrestle due to a cervical spinal stenosis diagnosis. Time to heal, paired with advances in medicine, meant that in 2020, he was able to return from that retirement and continue wrestling. Another seven years later, Copeland is ready to retire again, this time on his own terms. But can he become AEW Champion before it's too late?

title: Kofi Calls New Level AEW Debut Worst Kept Secret
