llm.summary: MJF sent a video message to open NJPW's Road to King of Pro Wrestling tour, calling out G1 Climax winner Ryohei Oiwa and labeling the promotion as second rate. He offered to defend his self-proclaimed real AEW World Championship belt known as the Triple B in the bout and vowed to beat Oiwa with a Headlock Takeover to prove he is the superior wrestler. The challenge stems from a social media exchange that began after Oiwa's G1 Climax victory in August.

title: On the Record: Dave Meltzer Says This AEW Star Was Responsible For Relationship With NJPW
raw_title: Dave Meltzer Says This AEW Star Was Responsible For Relationship With NJPW
body: Netflix Add Wrestling Inc. on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover AEW and New Japan Pro Wrestling have had a strong working relationship for over five years at the time of writing, to the point where the AEW x NJPW Forbidden Door pay-per-view has become a staple of the wrestling calendar and has been held in the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom. However, things didn't start out that way. Initially, there was no relationship between the two companies as NJPW management wasn't happy with The Elite leaving in 2019, as well as former NJPW President Harold Meij not seeing any upside in working with AEW since the company was already partnered with CMLL and ROH. However, according to Dave Meltzer on " Wrestling Observer Radio ," one man was pivotal to the AEW and NJPW relationship becoming a reality, and that man was Jon Moxley. "Jon's the one responsible for the New Japan and AEW relationship back during the pandemic," Meltzer said. "Jon had the [IWGP] US title and he was an AEW guy...there was no relationship at all. it opened up the relationship. That's when KENTA came to AEW and it opened the door. They basically built a relationship after that point." Moxley actually won the IWGP United States Championship in his debut match for NJPW , a match that took place less than two weeks after his AEW debut. However, while he was initially stripped of the title due to travel complications that forced him out of a title defense in October 2019, he wasn't stripped of the title when he won it back in January 2020 and couldn't make it back over to Japan throughout that year due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Chris Jericho also competed in NJPW as the AEW World Champion no less, though that would be Jericho's final official match for NJPW and hasn't returned to the company since. Please credit "Wrestling Observer Radio" when using quotes from this article, and give a H/T to Wrestling Inc. for the transcription.

llm_long: AEW and New Japan Pro Wrestling have maintained a strong working relationship for more than five years. The partnership has led to the annual AEW x NJPW Forbidden Door pay-per-view event, which has taken place in the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom.

The relationship did not exist at first. New Japan Pro Wrestling management was unhappy with The Elite's departure in 2019, and the company's former president saw no benefit in partnering with AEW because of existing ties with CMLL and ROH.

According to Dave Meltzer on Wrestling Observer Radio, Jon Moxley played a key role in establishing the connection between the two promotions. Moxley held the IWGP United States Championship while signed to AEW at a time when no formal relationship existed between the companies.

Meltzer stated that Moxley's possession of the title during the pandemic period opened the door for cooperation. This led to KENTA appearing in AEW and the two promotions building an ongoing relationship afterward.

Moxley captured the IWGP United States Championship in his first match with New Japan Pro Wrestling, which occurred shortly after his AEW debut. He was stripped of the title once due to travel issues preventing a defense but regained it in January 2020 and retained it despite being unable to travel to Japan during the COVID-19 pandemic.
Chris Jericho also appeared in New Japan Pro Wrestling while holding the AEW World Championship. That appearance marked his last official match for the Japanese promotion.

title: WWE legend Brock Lesnar looks unrecognizable at Minnesota Hall of Fame event
raw_title: WWE legend Brock Lesnar looks unrecognizable at Minnesota Hall of Fame event
body: On Saturday, Oct. 3, 2026, WWE legend Brock Lesnar was inducted into the University of Minnesota's M Club Hall of Fame following his professional wrestling retirement at SummerSlam . The "Beast Incarnate" was one of 10 inductees into the Hall of Fame. He wore glasses and a suit to the induction event, a far cry from his MMA gloves and shorts from his WWE days. Fellow former WWE Superstar and Lesnar's college roommate, Shelton Benjamin, was at the festivities to celebrate his friend. He posed for a picture with the "Beast" and his family. Born in South Dakota, Lesnar attended Bismarck State College before transferring to the University of Minnesota on a wrestling scholarship. He was a decorated wrestler, winning the 2000 NCAA Division I heavyweight championship a year after finishing as the runner-up. Lesnar went 106-5 in his collegiate career. After his collegiate amateur wrestling days, Lesnar transitioned to professional wrestling. He joined WWE's former developmental program, Ohio Valley Wrestling (OVW), in 2000. In March 2002, he made his main roster debut. Almost immediately, the "Beast Incarnate" was treated as the "Next Big Thing" and won a world championship five months into his main roster career. He beat The Rock at SummerSlam 2002 to win his first of 10 world championships. He left WWE in 2004, wrestling in other promotions like New Japan Pro-Wrestling (NJPW) before trying his hand at professional football and MMA. Lesnar became a decorated UFC fighter before rejoining WWE in 2012. His return marked a shift in his persona. Lesnar began infusing more MMA moves in his arsenal and wearing MMA gloves to the ring. Lesnar retired from WWE at SummerSlam 2026 after losing to Oba Femi in a "Hell in a Cell" match. Their feud had been going on for months, and the "Ruler" finally slayed the "Beast Incarnate" for the final time at SummerSlam.

title: End of an Era: 5 Ways Adam Copeland Can Retire From AEW

summary_src: Adam Copeland shocked the AEW universe by revealing that 2027 will be his final year in professional wrestling.
body: This Wednesday, AEW held a three-hour Dynamite+Collision special , the go-home show for tomorrow night's WrestleDream 2026 pay-per-view. Adam Copeland competed on the show, facing Josh Alexander in a Clockwork Carnage Qualifying Match. After his victory, Cope made two shocking revelations: his tag partner, Christian Cage, was severely hurt in their 3-way ladder match at All Out, and 2027 will be his last year in wrestling. Adam Copeland revealed that his decision stemmed from Cage's injury and the fact that he's getting older. He also noted that he now has to go all in for the AEW World Championship. With that in mind, here are five ways the Jacksonville-based promotion can book Cope's retirement match. By winning his Clockwork Carnage qualifier, Adam Copeland has joined seven other challengers for Will Ospreay's AEW World Title. The eight participants are Ospreay, Cope, Darby Allin, Konosuke Takeshita, Samoa Joe, Ricochet, Kazuchika Okada, and Mike Bailey, who will battle for the championship at WrestleDream this Saturday. It seems unlikely the Aerial Assassin will lose his title at this event Adam Copeland's desire to win the AEW World Title before retiring almost certainly means the promotion will put the belt on him. We just don't know when. The pro-wrestling world is structured to create tomorrow's stars, and right now the company's next big star, likely to become its flag bearer, is none other than Kyle Fletcher . In early 2027, Tony Khan could put the World Title on Adam Copeland, who would then serve as a fighting champion. During this time, the Rated-R Superstar would face many challengers and defeat them all except his final opponent, Kyle Fletcher. Many would argue that the Protostar is a mirror image of a young Cope (fka Edge), which makes narrative sense. This could be a true passing-of-the-torch moment if booked right. Adam Copeland's retirement run will be one to watch, and he will most likely compete against everyone on the roster he wants to lock up with. That said, choosing the right superstar as the Rated-R Superstar's final opponent becomes increasingly important. Interestingly, AEW could go the John Cena route and let the locker room fight for the chance. A month before Cope's final match at Worlds End 2027 or Dynamite: New Year's Smash, Tony Khan and Cope could announce a Rated-R Invitational tournament. The tournament would feature superstars such as Kenny Omega , MJF, Darby Allin, Will Ospreay, Swerve Strickland, Hangman Page, Kyle Fletcher, and Konosuke Takeshita. Cope could tell a compelling story with each of these stars, making the match one to watch, even beyond the Canadian legend's final. The legendary tag team of Adam Copeland and Christian Cage finally reunited earlier this year and even went on an impressive 125-day run with the titles before losing them to the Young Bucks at All Out 2026 in a chaotic 3-way ladder match. Unfortunately, Cage suffered multiple injuries in the bout and has been out of action since.

title: On the Record: John Cena Opens Up On Why Staying in WWE Longer Would Have Been Unfair to His Wife
raw_title: John Cena Reveals Why Staying in WWE Longer Would Have Been Unfair to His Wife
summary_src: John Cena may miss wrestling every single day, but he has a pretty personal reason for refusing to push his body beyond its expiration date. During his appearance on TODAY’s Making Space with Hoda Kotb, Cena opened up about knowing when it was time to end his in-ring career.
body: During his appearance on TODAY’s Making Space with Hoda Kotb , Cena opened up about knowing when it was time to end his in-ring career. Hoda Kotb asked how he could be so certain when plenty of people were still telling him he had more left in the tank. Cena explained that the answer came down to the amount of preparation and recovery required to continue performing at WWE’s level. At 49, Cena said he knew he could technically keep wrestling, but doing so would demand more and more of him physically and personally. “Simply because of the preparation and recovery it takes to participate at that level and speed. And I’m not near as fast as, like, younger, more athletically refined, elite-level performers. It wasn’t like I, I’m, I’m at peace with what I had to do and have a lot of gratitude for being able to do it for 23 years. That’s amazing. The normal lifespan is way less than that.” Cena said the numbers ultimately made the decision for him. He had already enjoyed a wrestling career far longer than most, and continuing would have meant putting even more of his life into staying physically capable of performing. “So I’ve already kind of beat the system by not only making it, but by having a nice long tenure. The data was the closure for me. Like, I’m just, I just can’t keep up, and I can’t, I could continue to do this. It’s already very consuming. It will be exponentially more consuming.” That led Cena into the bigger reason why walking away made sense. WWE was once the center of his entire life, but that changed as he got older and his relationship with wife Shay Shariatzadeh became his priority. “So when I was 20, WWE was it. When I was 30, WWE was also it. Started to fragment as I turned 40. I have love and partnership in my life, and that’s like, that’s the bull’s-eye. So, hey, is taking all this time and putting it away from the bull’s-eye really walking the talk about saying I want to try to be a good husband and a good partner? Not really.” Cena then explained that the issue went beyond simply spending too much time away from home. He also had to think about what another serious wrestling injury could mean for his wife later in their lives. “And physically, am I being fair to my partner by, hey, I’m gonna put my health at risk so people, when I’m 52, can cheer as they might bring me out on a stretcher, but then I put an unnecessary burden on you if I make it to 80? You know what I’m saying? So I guess my priorities shifted.” Even after laying out all of those reasons, Cena made it clear that retirement did not happen because his love for wrestling disappeared. “Yeah, clear. But I still, I love it and I miss it every day.” Cena spent more than two decades putting WWE ahead of nearly everything else, but his explanation makes it clear that retirement became less about whether he could squeeze out another match and more about what that match might cost him years later. title: WWE Eyes Reigns vs Femi For WrestleMania 43 Main Event
raw_title: Backstage Report On WWE's Early Plans For WrestleMania 43 Card
summary_src: WrestleMania 43 will be held in Saudi Arabia next year, and WWE appears to have begun planning the show, including a potential main event.
body: Next year's WrestleMania will be held in Saudi Arabia, and according to " Fightful Select ," WWE has earmarked a clash between WWE World Heavyweight Champion Roman Reigns and 2026 King of the Ring winner Oba Femi for the show. The report added that some sources they spoke to believe that the match could main event the show. As expected, former world champions Cody Rhodes and CM Punk will play important roles at the show, according to the report. A source also suggested that the two could face off again in a rematch of their SummerSlam match . Rhea Ripley — currently out with an injury — is also expected to play a part in it. Reports from earlier in the year had claimed that the Saudi Arabia organizers want to see The Rock at the event, who last wrestled in WWE back in 2024 at WrestleMania 40. WWE is keen to host the show in Saudi Arabia , marking the first time its biggest PLE will take place in the country, despite the ongoing conflict involving the Houthis. Reports have highlighted WWE's firm stance on holding both WrestleMania, which is still several months away, and Crown Jewel, scheduled for November, in Saudi Arabia. At the time of publication, WWE has yet to announce a date for WrestleMania 43, which is reportedly not a priority for the promotion at the moment.

title: On the Record: John Cena Opens Up On What WWE Fans Chanting “You Suck” Taught Him About His Critics
raw_title: John Cena Reveals What WWE Fans Chanting “You Suck” Taught Him About His Critics
summary_src: John Cena spent years walking into WWE arenas where half the crowd treated him like Superman and the other half couldn’t wait to tell him he sucked. It turns out those hostile reactions taught him a lesson he still carries with him today.
body: Cena explained that he had already experienced hostile crowds long before he became WWE’s top star. In fact, he believes wrestling in front of tiny audiences prepared him even better than being booed by thousands of people. “Having the anonymity to be in a crowd of 10,000 yelling, ‘You suck,’ when you know you’re, you can’t be noticed, that, that doesn’t take a lot of courage. When you’re at, um, Saint Teresa’s Gym and you’re in a crowd of 10 and you’re one of those 10 who stand up and say, ‘Prototype, you suck,’ and I can look you in the eye and be like, ‘What?’ That takes courage and bravery.” Cena said he dealt with that kind of direct reaction while wrestling as The Prototype in Ultimate Pro Wrestling and later during his developmental run in Ohio Valley Wrestling. “And I dealt, I got to deal with that wrestling in the LA for Ultimate Pro and I got to deal with that wrestling for, uh, Ohio Valley Wrestling.” Those early experiences helped Cena understand what professional wrestling really was and gave him an important lesson before he was ever standing in packed WWE arenas. “So I guess, I guess I just kinda, again, good teachers around me to tell me, like, this is the business, you know, and, um, and what a great lesson to learn of, like, you can’t please everybody.” Cena then connected those divided WWE reactions to the rebellious personality he had as a kid. He recalled wearing clothes that made him stand out when he was younger and said he could have changed himself then just as easily as he could have changed his WWE character later. “And I think the reason I was so polarizing is just like at 12 years old wearing those MC Hammer pants. When I could have easily took them off, that’d been an easy route. Or I could have remained myself.” That same mentality became a major part of how Cena approached his WWE character. Instead of trying to eliminate the boos by becoming whatever critics wanted him to be, Cena said he stayed committed to a character that reflected his actual values. “I was very authentic to character, and character mirrored a lot of the things that I value in real life. And either you’re watching that channel or you’re not. You know what I’m saying? And that’s, you know, we all have our favorite things to do and things we also criticize, and I’m, I am who I am.” Cena said trying to create a version of himself capable of winning everybody over would have been impossible anyway. “I’m not trying to amalgamate to get to, to, to spread this impossible blanket that includes everybody. I can’t please everybody.” His message to the fans who supported him, and especially those who didn’t, was simple. Cena spent years hearing “Let’s Go Cena” and “Cena Sucks” battle each other inside the same building, but he never saw winning every critic over as the endgame. He learned early that some people were never going to ride with him, so his answer was to stay himself and make sure they had plenty to react to anyway. H Jenkins H Jenkins has bee
summary: He had already experienced hostile crowds long before he became WWE’s top star, Cena explained. He believes wrestling in front of tiny audiences prepared him even better than being booed by thousands of people. Having the anonymity to be in a crowd of 10,000 yelling.

body: Hope has been a thorn in India's flesh on the tour. The West Indies skipper has scored four centuries across three ODIs and four T20Is. body: Bron Breakker and Austin Theory won the tag team titles from The Street Profits on the July 6 episode of RAW, thanks to Maxxine Dupri . The Alpha Queen hit a low blow to Angelo Dawkins, helping Theory and Breakker win. WWE receives plenty of criticism for how they book the tag team division. The Vision regularly appears on WWE TV, but not to represent the tag team division. The heel group is more focused on its members' individual feuds. Recently, The Vision was involved in a feud with Oba Femi . First, Bron Breakker feuded with The Ruler, leading to a match at Sunday Night's Main Event. However, the bout did not produce a clear winner due to Bronson Reed attacking Femi. Reed then began feuding with Femi. At WWE Money in the Bank, The Ruler defeated the Australian powerhouse despite The Vision trying to help Reed. The lack of title defenses could eventually force Adam Pearce to take action. The RAW General Manager has a responsibility to keep the tag team division moving, and it would be difficult to justify The Vision holding the championships indefinitely without putting them on the line. Adam Pearce could confront The Vision and remind them they have a responsibility to defend the World Tag Team Titles as the reigning champions. The heel faction's members aren't known to be team players, so they might not take the RAW General Manager seriously. However, Pearce could make it clear that there would be consequences if they refuse to cooperate. Such a decision would give the tag team division an opportunity to move forward. WWE could use this situation to make the World Tag Team Championship feel important again. If Adam Pearce believes the champions are neglecting the titles, he could be forced to take action. That said, this scenario is only based on speculation, and nothing has been confirmed.

title: WWE superstars AJ Styles and Nattie bring smiles to Perth Children’s Hospital ahead of weekend — Telethon 2026
raw_title: Telethon 2026: WWE superstars AJ Styles and Nattie bring smiles to Perth Children’s Hospital ahead of weekend
body: Styles and fellow global wrestling heavyweight Natalya made a surprise heart-warming visit at Perth Children’s Hospital yesterday, sharing hugs and snapping selfies with patients — and WWE devotees — ahead of the Telethon weekend. For 13-year-old patient Blade Dyson, meeting his WWE idol was an unforgettable moment. “I have been waiting for hours to meet him, as soon as Mum told me I couldn’t believe it,” he said, shaking in disbelief. “I’m so starstruck right now, he (AJ Styles) is like my hero. I love wrestling so this has just been the best day ever.” Five-year-old Elijah Green was equally captivated as the stars walked into his ward. “Dad loves AJ and I do, too,” he said. “It’s cool that he is here.” For the two-time WWE world champion, meeting patients at PCH put everything into perspective before the frantic fundraising frenzy kicks off on the weekend. “I think that it’s great being able to be a superstar in wrestling, but it’s even better when you’re able to share special moments with kids who really sometimes need to, you know, get a smile on their face,” Styles, 49, said. “It’s the best, I love being able to be a star in wrestling, but it’s even better when you’re able to make kids smile. It marks his first time visiting Perth’s iconic charity marathon and the father of four immediately felt the cause’s magnitude. “I don’t know much about Telethon, but From what I’m seeing, it’s a pretty big deal. So I’m expecting something big,” Styles said. “I think the opportunity to just obviously meet the kids and then meet other celebrities that are able to do this as well is what I’m looking forward to most. Third-generation wrestler and former SmackDown women’s champion Natalya — affectionately known as Nattie — was equally moved by the warm WA welcome a decade after last visiting Perth. “And almost all the kids that we’ve met today, they are big fans of WWE, so it’s even more rewarding to know that they know who we are and they’re excited that we came. Looking ahead to the weekend, Nattie promised WWE fans plenty of enthusiasm, photo opportunities, and high energy. “I’m so excited to meet everyone that’s coming,” she said. “We’ve been getting tagged in posts, and people are so excited and it’s just going to be so nice to meet everybody, say hi, give hugs, take selfies. We’re coming for the people . body: Share on Twitter --> Major League Wrestling has landed on Amazon Prime Video. body: Shotzi Blackheart has officially signed with TNA Wrestling, according to Fightful Select. Shotzi appeared at the promotion’s television tapings on Tuesday, October 13 at the Dothan Civic Center in Dothan, Alabama. Her final match with MLW took place at the company’s September 12 taping in Charleston, South Carolina, where she dropped the MLW Women’s World Championship to Masha Slamovich. Shotzi posted to social media earlier in the day on Wednesday that her brother Dean passed away on Sunday night. She said that while she was able to fulfill her commitments this week with her family’s support, she is withdrawing from her scheduled CMLL tour next week to be with her family. Shotzi had been scheduled to compete in the 2026 International Women’s Grand Prix on October 23 at Arena Mexico. Shotzi made her MLW debut at Summer of the Beasts on June 26, 2025. That appearance came shortly after her departure from WWE when her contract expired, ending a six-year run with the company. Since leaving WWE, Shotzi has also wrestled for GCW, House of Glory, World Series Wrestling in Australia, PROGRESS, and several CMLL shows in Mexico in April. title: Shotzi Blackheart Signs With TNA
raw_title: Former WWE Star Signs With TNA Wrestling — Report
body: Skip to content Wrestling News Home » Former WWE Star Signs With TNA Wrestling — Report Shotzi Blackheart has reportedly secured her next wrestling destination following her recent departure from MLW, appearing at TNA Wrestling’s television tapings in Alabama this week. However, the career development comes during a difficult period for the former WWE star, who has also announced a change to her upcoming schedule following a family tragedy. According to Fightful Select , Blackheart has signed a deal with TNA after appearing at the Dothan Civic Center in Dothan, Alabama, on Tuesday, Oct. 13. Her MLW contract reportedly expired on Oct. 5, opening the door for the move. Blackheart is no stranger to TNA, having competed for the promotion in 2019 when it operated under the IMPACT Wrestling name. She also built experience across several independent promotions after her WWE contract expired, ending a six-year run with the company. Her most recent MLW run began in June 2025, and she previously held the MLW Women’s World Featherweight Championship before losing the title to Masha Slamovich at a September taping. While Blackheart’s next professional chapter appears to be taking shape, she has also shared heartbreaking news with fans. On Wednesday, she revealed that her brother, Dean, had passed away on Sunday night. Blackheart announced she would withdraw from the CMLL Women’s Grand Prix, which is scheduled for Oct. 23 at Arena México, so she could spend time with her family and honor her brother’s memory. “It was a huge honor to be selected for the CMLL Grand Prix, and I don’t take that opportunity lightly,” Blackheart wrote. “Thank you to everyone at CMLL and the fans for understanding how hard all this is for me.” Blackheart has previously credited her brother with helping spark an interest in wrestling during childhood, making the loss particularly personal. The details of her future role with TNA have not been provided, but her appearance at the tapings signals a fresh start when she is ready to return to the ring. summary_src: Drew McIntyre has been wrestling for 26 years, but somehow he says his body feels better now than it has in more than a decade.

Like so many of us as kids, young men, just idolized Arnold. He was like, ‘I’m going to be like Arnold.’” McIntyre explained that Black spent years learning how to strengthen his own body and eventually started passing some of those techniques along to him. That’s led to Drew doing a ton of preventative work that he simply wasn’t thinking about earlier in his career. “And he started reading books about how to strengthen your bones, strengthen your tendons, learned a lot of tricks. And inevitably — I mean, he’s the angriest, littlest man I’ve ever met in my life. Tall as he is wide, but he’s jacked out of his mind. He could have walked on the outside of his feet, but he’s built up his body where he gets around great. He trains like crazy.” That work has apparently paid off in a big way. McIntyre is currently sitting at 285 pounds, the heaviest he’s ever been, but says he physically feels better than he has in around 12 years. The biggest surprise for Drew was discovering just how much of his problem started with his feet. He’d noticed himself feeling strangely off-balance both in everyday life and inside the ring, something his wife apparently had plenty of fun roasting him about. “They’re very, very important. My feet were — I roll them out. You really don’t think about it. I didn’t realize how bad they were either. Like, I felt off-balance at times in real life, in the ring. My wife says, ‘You’re the most unathletic professional athlete in the world. You go inside a wrestling ring and it’s like magic. Then you walk around, you’re falling over and stuff.’” Once Drew started working on his feet, things began changing. His routine now includes rolling them out along with toe raises and calf raises, all with the goal of giving him a stronger base. “And I was like, ‘Yeah, I always feel off-balance at times.’ And he told me it starts from the ground up, and we’ve got to start rolling those feet out, start doing toe raises, calf raises — just start building from the ground up.” McIntyre really noticed the difference when he recently stepped back into a wrestling ring and filmed a clip of himself running the ropes. title: Adam Copeland Sets 2027 Retirement, Eyes AEW World Title
raw_title: Adam Copeland Announces Retirement Timeline in New Video, Plans to Claim AEW World Title
body: Copeland announced that 2027 marks his final year as a wrestler on Wednesday's edition of AEW Dynamite while also confirming that he's looking to capture the AEW World Title. "I'm aging out, and that's okay," Copeland said (0:20 mark). "It happens to everybody. But because of that, I just want to let you all know that 2027 will be my last year in professional wrestling." But all of that being said, that is why I have to go for the AEW Championship." Copeland also revealed that tag-team partner Christian Cage suffered a collapsed lung and three broken ribs after he was thrown into a ladder at AEW All Out on Sept. 26. Copeland's 2027 retirement will mark the end of a legendary professional wrestling career that began in 1992, as he started by competing in singles and tag team competitions with several independent promotions. He finally made his televised debut with the WWF, which was later renamed to WWE, in 1998 as Edge. During his WWE career, he won 31 total titles. This included 11 world championships. Copeland also had memorable feuds with rivals such as John Cena, Jeff Hardy, Matt Hardy and The Undertaker. Copeland eventually returned to WWE from 2020-23 before making his AEW debut in Oct. 2023. He quickly established himself as a threat upon joining AEW, winning the TNT Championship by defeating Cage at Worlds End in Dec. 2023. It represented the first of two TNT Championship reigns by Copeland. Copeland and Cage ultimately joined forces, capturing the AEW World Tag Team Championship at Double or Nothing on May 24. The 52-year-old will be stepping away from wrestling at the end of 2027, but will attempt to secure the title before doing so.

He explained that he wants to capture the AEW World Championship before retiring due to his age. Copeland also updated fans on tag team partner Christian Cage, who sustained a collapsed lung and three broken ribs from a ladder spot at All Out.

title: Tony Khan Updates On Jay White And Jamie Hayter Injuries

summary_src: Ahead of WrestleDream, AEW CEO Tony Khan addresses the recent injuries sustained by Jay White and Jamie Hayter.
body: The Bang Bang Gang's Jay White and AEW Women's Tag Team Champion Jamie Hayter are also on the shelf after sustaining undisclosed injuries of their own. Hayter's forced AEW to pivot away from its original women's tag team plans for WrestleDream. On the WrestleDream media call, AEW CEO Tony Khan suggested that White also would have been involved in the October 17 PPV had it not been for his respective injury. White reportedly got hurt in the midst of an eight-man tag bout on the Tailgate Brawl, which aired ahead of All Out's main show on September 26. He's expected to be out of action for up to two months. Lee South/AEW Hayter sustained her injury during a Chicago Street Fight in which she and Alex Windsor also defended the AEW Women's Tag Team Championships against Megan Bayne and Lena Kross. According to Khan, Hayter's injury is minor, with doctors advising her to wait an additional two weeks before returning to the ring. Following their successful outing at All Out, Hayter and Windsor, together known as The Brawling Birds, were slated to defend their tag team titles against Kris Statlander and Harley Cameron at WrestleDream. Due to Hayter's sideline stint, that title match has since been pushed back to a time and date yet to be announced. In its place, AEW has confirmed that Bayne and Kross, the former AEW Women's Tag Team Champions, will take on The Sisters of Sin (Julia Hart and Skye Blue) on the WrestleDream pre-show. AEW Women's Champion Mercedes Mone will put her title on the line against The Sisters of Sin's ally, Thekla.

title: Sheamus Recalls Nervous WWE ECW Debut
raw_title: Sheamus Looks Back On WWE Debut, Says He Never Had A 'Great Story' In The Company
summary_src: "The Celtic Warrior" Sheamus opens up about his main roster WWE debut and the years of storylines, or lack thereof, that followed.
body: For former WWE Champion Sheamus, his main roster journey traces back to that now-defunct brand, with his official debut pitting him in a match against Oliver John on the June 30, 2009 edition of "ECW." "The Celtic Warrior" ultimately walked away with a win, but not without a sense of nervousness behind it. In his early years with WWE, Sheamus noted that he got "extremely" nervous out of fear of making mistakes. Fortunately, he spent time in WWE's developmental system and competed in dark matches to make him more comfortable, and in turn, prepare him for his eventual ascent. Sheamus defeated John in quick fashion on "ECW," courtesy of a Brogue Kick and a backbreaker. Less than six months later, he bested the company's top star, John Cena, to become the WWE Champion. Multiple current and former WWE stars have gone on record citing Sheamus as the hardest in-ring hitter they've ever encountered . Sheamus himself confirmed that he never stopped them from dishing the physicality right back to him, however. In fact, he encouraged it, both for the sake of his opponent and the audience watching along. "People love to see a fight," Sheamus said. "They want to see a person give something, a character, wrestler, whatever it is you want to call it, they want to see something different. An internal hunger and fight in them. I prided myself in getting that out of them. That was my forte. Would I have loved a lot more storylines and stuff like that? Of course, I would have. I never really got a really great story that I could sink my teeth into." The multi-time world champion departed from WWE after reportedly turning down a restructured contract extension offer. He officially hit the free agency market earlier this month.

The Celtic Warrior admitted feeling extremely nervous early in his WWE run and credited time in developmental plus dark matches for helping him gain confidence before winning the WWE Championship from John Cena less than six months later. He also discussed his reputation as one of the hardest hitters in the business and how he always encouraged opponents to return the physicality because fans want to see a real fight.

body: Some have argued that GUNTHER's booking has been underwhelming since he retired several WWE legends, and a new report by " Wrestlevotes on Fightful Select " has revealed that some members of the company's creative team are unhappy with it. Curiously, he has also been feuding with Danhausen, an unusual pairing given that Danhausen is a comedy character while GUNTHER has a more serious gimmick. On last week's " SmackDown ," GUNTHER attacked Danhausen before the bell rang to signal the start of their match, but Finn Balor came to Danhausen's rescue, who is another star currently feuding with GUNTHER.

body: "I think Queen Aminata. There is a ton of potential that is kind of unrealized there. I would say the same thing with Trish Adora. I think those are two talents that I consistently see where maybe their best is still kind of in front of them. On the men's side, there are also a lot. I'd say [Action] Andretti. I think, him being given more opportunity and given more spots could be quite the force to be reckoned with." In the case of Action Andretti, Joe could potentially play a role in getting him those opportunities as Andretti became the latest member of The Opps back at ROH Death Before Dishonor 2026 in August. Now that Joe is back in AEW after filming the next season of "Twisted Metal" over the summer, he will once again look to lead The Opps to championship gold heading into the new year.
summary: Samoa Joe singled out Queen Aminata and Trish Adora as two women whose best performances are still ahead of them. On the men's side he highlighted Action Andretti as someone who could become a major force with increased opportunities. Joe recently welcomed Andretti into The Opps at ROH Death Before Dishonor and plans to lead the group toward titles in AEW upon his return from filming.

On the men's side, Joe singled out Action Andretti as someone who could become a major force. He suggested that additional opportunities and ring time would allow Andretti to excel.

title: WWE and Montez Ford Sued by Security Guard
raw_title: WWE & Montez Ford Reportedly Being Sued By Security Guard
summary_src: WWE & Montez Ford (Kenneth Crawford) are reportedly being sued by a security guard that was working at the Allstate Arena in Rosemont, Illinois.
body: According to POST Wrestling , Lucas filed a lawsuit in the Circuit Court of Cook County. The suit alleges 14 counts, including assault, battery, intentional infliction of emotional distress, along with violating the Illinois Gender Violence Act. POST also notes that Event Services, LLC, a WWE subsidiary is also named in the lawsuit. Since the clip of the interaction between Crawford and Lucas is widely available online, Lucas alleges that both he and his kids have been "mocked and ridiculed". Due to these actions, Lucas believes he has "suffered humiliation, embarrassment and emotional distress". Because his face is easily seen in the clip, Lucas also claims his image has been used for commercial purposes and therefore violates the Illinois Right of Publicity Act. The clip is not currently on the Netflix replay as the show cuts to commercial. Lucas maintains that a WWE employee had him seated against the ringside barricade, positioning him in Street Profits path. The filing states that "Defendant Crawford then began performing a sexually provocative dance immediately in front of and over Plaintiff [Lucas], repeatedly thrusting and gyrating his hips and pelvis towards Plaintiff, performing a sexualized 'lap dance.'" As Crawford moved closer to Lucas, the suit alleges that his "left inner thigh repeatedly rubbed against Plaintiff's leg." A case management hearing is scheduled for December 10. Lucas is seeking punitive damages along with unspecified monetary damages, and coverage of his legal costs. He also wants an order that WWE and Crawford cannot use his identity.
summary: A security guard named Lucas has filed a 14-count lawsuit in Cook County Circuit Court against Montez Ford, WWE and its subsidiary Event Services LLC. The suit alleges assault, battery, intentional infliction of emotional distress and violations of the Illinois Gender Violence Act and Right of Publicity Act after Ford performed a sexually provocative dance in front of him at ringside. Lucas claims the widely circulated clip has caused him and his children to be mocked, resulting in humiliation, embarrassment and emotional distress.

title: Bully Ray Praises Je'Von Evans' Intense Ambulance Return
raw_title: Bully Ray Talks Je'Von Evans Spot That Stood Out To Him In WWE MITB Men's Ladder Match
summary_src: Bully Ray highlighted a spot that made Je'Von Evans stand out in the men's WWE Money in the Bank ladder match, and it wasn't his ambulance bump.
body: Evans competed in the men's Money in the Bank match alongside eventual winner Penta , CM Punk, Trick Williams, Bron Breakker, and Kevin Owens. During the match, Evans was wheeled away but returned to the ring in an ambulance and got his revenge on Breakker by landing punches, which greatly impressed Ray. "There was a moment in time in that match that meant more to me, for Je'Von Evans and his future, than that spot. When he pulls up to the ring, and Bron Breakker looks inside the driver's side, and Je'Von opens that door with such force, Bron Breakker goes flying, did you see Je'Von Evans when he jumped out of that ambulance and started beating the sh*t out of Bron Breakker?" asked Ray on " Busted Open ." "There was so much intent behind those fists flying. We talk about the art of the run-in, or we talk about, you know, making everything mean something. I felt Je'Von Evans in that moment, more than I felt him in the entire match." "A babyface can only rely on his fists. That's all a babyface needs at the end of the day is his fists. And the way Je'Von's fists were flying made me believe in him more than any other spot in that match. And that's why less is more," he added. The Hall of Famer praised Evans for looking determined and making his punches seem convincing. Evans' night ended on a brutal note, as Breakker threw him from the top of the ladder onto the ambulance just minutes after he landed multiple punches on him. Breakker continued the assault on the following episode of "WWE Raw," spearing an already injured Evans.
summary: Bully Ray highlighted a specific moment from the men's Money in the Bank ladder match that stood out more than Je'Von Evans' other spots. After being wheeled away, Evans returned in an ambulance, forcefully opened the door to knock Bron Breakker down, and unloaded with purposeful punches that Ray felt conveyed real intent and made him believe in Evans as a babyface. The WWE Hall of Famer emphasized that the convincing fist strikes and determination shown were more impactful than any other part of the match, proving less is more.

kind.quote: There was so much intent behind those fists flying.

Upon his return Evans opened the ambulance door with force, sending Breakker flying. He then jumped out and delivered a series of punches to Breakker.

title: Samoa Joe Remembers PAC's Meteoric Rise
raw_title: Samoa Joe Pays Tribute To PAC, 'It's Tough Going Back To Work And Not Seeing Him There'
summary_src: Samoa Joe comments on the passing of PAC. The wrestling world has continued to grieve the recent loss of Benjamin Satterley, who unexpectedly passed away at the end of September. In a new interview with Sports Illustrated, Samoa Joe took a moment to remember everyone's favorite "bastard".
body: The wrestling world has continued to grieve the recent loss of Benjamin Satterley, who unexpectedly passed away at the end of September. In a new interview with Sports Illustrated , Samoa Joe took a moment to remember everyone’s favorite “bastard”. “Ben was a guy that came up with a lot of us in that who we watched just have this meteoric rise internationally, probably from one of the most improbable places at the time when you think about the scene where there was actually people were getting exposure. But he was that good.” Continuing on, Joe praised Satterley for being a wonderful human being. “He was that good where, going from his work to Japan, even back in the States, everybody knew he was something special. Then you get the pleasure of meeting a guy like him and being his friend and kind of understanding the wonderful human being that he is.” Samoa Joe will compete in the Clockwork Carnage match at AEW WrestleDream. Check out the current card for the show by clicking here.
summary: Samoa Joe paid tribute to the late Benjamin Satterley, known as PAC, in a new interview. Joe highlighted how PAC achieved international success from an unlikely background and was recognized as special everywhere he wrestled. Joe also described him as a wonderful human being and friend while preparing to wrestle at AEW WrestleDream.

kind.quote: It's tough going back to work and not seeing him there

title: Bandido Surpasses Jay Lethal For Most Combined ROH World Title Days
raw_title: Bandido Breaks Jay Lethal's Record For Most Overall Days As ROH World Champion
summary_src: Bandido breaks a major record. History was made on October 14, as Bandido officially passed Jay Lethal for the most overall days (710+) as the ROH World Champion. This number is spread over two separate reigns, one from 2021 and his current reign, which started at AEW Dynasty in April 2025.
body: History was made on October 14, a s Bandido officially passed Jay Lethal for the most overall days (710+) as the ROH World Champion. This number is spread over two separate reigns, one from 2021 and his current reign, which started at AEW Dynasty in April 2025. Lethal previously held the record with 707 total days as champ across two separate title reigns. One reign spanned from June 2015 to August 2016, while the other ran from June 2018 to April 2019. Congratulations to #ROH World Champion @bandidowrestler , who now holds the record for the most combined days as champion at an incredible 709 DAYS! Watch #ROH TV on #HonorClub at https://t.co/l79CE3grm1 pic.twitter.com/Qpo39Jx0ZQ — ROH – Ring of Honor Wrestling (@ringofhonor) October 16, 2026 Bandido will now aim to unseat Samoa Joe, who holds the record for the longest ROH World Championship reign of all time at 645 days. As of publish time, Bandido’s current reign with the title sits at the 558 day mark. If you missed anything from Thursday’s episode of ROH TV, catch up on the show by clicking here.
summary: Bandido broke Jay Lethal's record for the most overall days as ROH World Champion on October 14. His two reigns now total more than 710 days combined, passing Lethal's previous mark of 707 days across his 2015-2016 and 2018-2019 title runs. Bandido's current reign, which began at AEW Dynasty in April 2025, stands at 558 days as he targets Samoa Joe's all-time single-reign record of 645 days.

llm.summary: Bandido broke Jay Lethal's record for the most overall days as ROH World Champion on October 14. His two reigns now total more than 710 days combined, passing Lethal's previous mark of 707 days across his 2015-2016 and 2018-2019 title runs. Bandido's current reign, which began at AEW Dynasty in April 2025, stands at 558 days as he targets Samoa Joe's all-time single-reign record of 645 days.

llm_long: Bandido has surpassed Jay Lethal for the most combined days as ROH World Champion. He reached the milestone on October 14 with more than 710 total days across two reigns.
Bandido's first reign occurred in 2021. His second and current reign began at AEW Dynasty in April 2025.
Lethal previously held the record with 707 combined days as champion. Those days came from two separate reigns, one from June 2015 to August 2016 and the other from June 2018 to April 2019.
Bandido now holds the record for most combined days as ROH World Champion at 709 days. He will next aim to surpass Samoa Joe's record for the longest single ROH World Championship reign at 645 days.
Bandido's current reign stands at 558 days as of the latest update.

title: Roman Reigns regrets 'Sufferin Succotash' promo
raw_title: Roman Reigns wishes he’d said ‘Nah’ to that ‘Sufferin’ Succotash’ promo
summary_src: As the three former members of The Shield began their runs as singles stars, Seth Rollins and Jon Moxley/Dean Ambrose seemed to be favored by many wrestling fans because of their time on the independents, and because they were CM Punk’s first choices for the group.
body: There was much more skepticism of Roman Reigns, and it wasn’t long until that turned into hostility. A key moment that led to the outright rejection of Reigns happened in early 2015, when he interrupted Rollins on SmackDown and said ( emphasis mine): “… look at you, you’re just so full of yourself now. Actually, you’re full of something else. You are a sniveling little suck up sellout full of sufferin’ succotash, son ! Yeah, yeah, yeah, I know, that was not easy to say!” Talking about that stretch of his career on Club Shay Shay earlier this week, Roman told Shannon Sharpe: The example that came to mind for the Big Dog-turned-Tribal Chief? He was fuzzy on the dates, but… you guessed it… ”This was like 14 years ago, and they’ll still quote me for saying ‘sufferin succotash.’ This was so long ago. It was 12 years ago, you know? ”I mean, I’ve delivered unbelievable work since then, but still, I’ll be tied to that. There wasn’t that many, but there’s probably two or three promos or scenarios, segments or, you know, finishes of a match or something like that that I would probably go back and develop the balls to be like, ‘Nah, not today, brother,’” That’s a sentiment our own Geno Mrosko expressed on the moment’s third anniversary : Watching it back now, it’s still mind blowing that he was given such horrific copy to recite from a script that should have been burned before it ever reached his fingertips. It is, however, worth watching because I’ll be damned if it doesn’t show just how much Roman Reigns has grown as a performer. I’m not saying he could make that copy work today — I don’t even think John Cena at his cheesiest could make that work — but he’s far more comfortable in his own skin, the kind of change you hardly notice because it’s drawn out over time. And that was back when The Bloodline was just a glimmer in Reigns’ eye! For me, while I’m sure it wasn’t fun for him, I’m glad we had that awkward stretch of Roman’s WWE career. It informs his current character so much, adding layers we wouldn’t have if The OTC had arrived fully formed before our eyes. body: AEW is honoring the late Benjamin Satterley, ‘PAC’, in its artwork for next month’s Full Gear pay-per-view. Full Gear became a term in relation to PAC’s appearance at the inaugural AEW press conference in January 2019 to confront Hangman Page in his trunks. The term was used on an edition of ‘Being the Elite’ and led to the name being adopted for the promotion’s annual pay-per-view in November. AEW has updated the logo for this year’s event, scheduled for November 14 in Arizona. The logo features two black arrows coming out of the logo, a ‘Black Arrow Warning’ sign with a sketch of PAC performing the maneuver, and an image of Pac’s chair and towel, which have become a staple of the Death Riders’ entrances. The performer died suddenly on September 27, one day after competing at the All Out show in Illinois.

title: Netflix Ousts Chief Content Officer Bela Bajaria

body: Netflix’s chief content officer Bela Bajaria is out as the streamer made a bold decision to let the executive go. Bajaria helped oversee Netflix’s programming strategy with a $20 billion budget and was pivotal in WWE coming to Netflix in 2025. When the deal was announced in early 2024, Bajaria was quoted , “(WWE) has been very under-distributed outside the US. I think there’s really great opportunity to still grow it outside the U.S.” The exit comes one day after Netflix cut approximately 1,000 jobs with an underperforming stock and stalled engagement on the platform. Co-CEO Ted Sarandos acknowledged the disappointing performance in a recent chat, saying the service was “Not growing as fast as I want us to.” Former Fox and Disney executive Peter Rice will replace Bajaria.

body: PAC helped inspire the name of AEW Full Gear — and the logo for this year’s edition has been updated to pay tribute to him. The new Full Gear logo includes multiple nods to PAC . A “Black Arrow Warning” sign has been added to the Arizona desert backdrop, and a pair of black arrows are now part of one of the Full Gear cogs. PAC’s Death Riders chair and his towel have also been included. Full Gear has been one of AEW’s pay-per-views since the promotion’s inaugural year of 2019. The name derives from PAC showing up in full wrestling gear at AEW’s February 2019 launch rally in Jacksonville. While pretty much everyone else was dressed formally in business attire, PAC, without a shirt on, confronted Hangman Page while wearing wrestling trunks and boots. That became a bit on Being the Elite during PAC and Page’s feud. At Full Gear 2019, Page defeated PAC in a singles match. The 2025 edition of Full Gear saw PAC defeat Darby Allin. AEW, and the entire wrestling world, has been in mourning since PAC unexpectedly passed away at 40 years old on September 27. His cause of death is still pending additional testing after an initial autopsy was performed. Mortgage Matchup Center in Phoenix, Arizona is hosting Full Gear 2026 on Saturday, November 14. The PPV is already less than a month away, and the build will pick up after WrestleDream concludes this weekend. title: JBL Named President of Tragos/Thesz Professional Wrestling Hall of Fame
raw_title: JBL Named President of Tragos/Thesz Professional Wrestling Hall of Fame
summary_src: John Bradshaw Layfield is taking on a major new role in professional wrestling, while Gerry Brisco is stepping away from the position he has held for more than two decades.
body: The National Wrestling Hall of Fame Dan Gable Museum announced that Brisco is stepping down as president of the George Tragos/Lou Thesz Professional Wrestling Hall of Fame board of directors and moving into an advisory role. Layfield will replace him as president effective immediately. Brisco has served as president since the Hall of Fame was established in 1999 and helped guide its growth into one of the most respected institutions honoring professional wrestling history. Brisco said he feels comfortable handing things over to JBL and believes the Hall of Fame will continue moving in the right direction. “I’m happy to be leaving the board in the capable hands of JBL, and I am confident that he and his support team will ensure that the Tragos/Thesz Hall of Fame continues to grow and remain the best.” Brisco brings plenty of history to the role he is leaving behind. He won multiple championships during his career in the NWA and WWE and has been inducted into several halls of fame, including the Tragos/Thesz Hall of Fame itself. Layfield also has a long connection to the organization. He received the Lou Thesz Award from the Tragos/Thesz Hall of Fame in 2012 after a career that included three WWE Tag Team Championship reigns alongside Ron Simmons. “I’m honored that Mr. Brisco has chosen me to help continue the incredible success he has worked so hard to achieve.” He also made it clear that he and the team already have plans to expand the Hall of Fame’s reach. “The team and I look forward to growing the Tragos/Thesz Hall of Fame and moving forward in building the Global Hall of Fame brand.” That Global Hall of Fame brand is tied to the newly created Global Pro Wrestling Hall of Fame, LLC, which is expected to work closely with the Tragos/Thesz Hall of Fame. The new organization was created to expand opportunities involving the Hall of Fame, the Dan Gable Museum, professional wrestlers and the wrestling business as a whole. Layfield addressed any concern that the new organization could change how the Tragos/Thesz Hall of Fame operates for fans or inductees. He added that more information is coming and believes the arrangement will benefit both groups. “The GPW Hall of Fame will not affect fans or the enshrinement of members of the Tragos/Thesz Hall of Fame.” “We will announce more details in the future, but we view this as a win-win situation for both the GPW Hall of Fame and the Tragos/Thesz Hall of Fame.” Brisco helped lead the Tragos/Thesz Hall of Fame for more than 25 years, and now JBL is being handed the keys as the organization looks toward its next phase. With Brisco remaining involved in an advisory capacity and Layfield already talking expansion, this is less of a clean break and more of a major changing of the guard. What do you think about JBL taking over as president of the Tragos/Thesz Professional Wrestling Hall of Fame? Leave your feedback and let us know what you think. raw_title: Why John Cena Tries to Follow So Many People on Twitter
summary_src: John Cena doesn’t just want millions of people following him on social media — he wants to follow millions of them right back. In fact, the WWE legend says the only thing stopping him from following way more people on X is the platform itself.
body: Speaking to BuzzFeed UK , Cena was asked about the massive number of accounts he follows. He explained that the whole thing actually started while he was in Kensington filming Fast 9 , when he noticed how obsessed people had become with bragging about their follower counts. “They cut me off. I want to follow everybody. You used to only be able to — before it transformed names into X — follow a thousand people a day. And I actually started doing that here in Kensington. I was shooting Fast 9, and I’m like, ‘You know what? People are bragging about their followers. I get that — like, so many people are paying attention to me.’” Cena had already taken a completely different approach with Instagram. He deliberately follows nobody there because his account is basically a collection of unexplained images, and he doesn’t want who he follows influencing how people interpret whatever he posts. But when it came to Twitter, now X, Cena decided to go completely in the opposite direction. Instead of bragging about how many people wanted to hear from him, he liked the idea of bragging about how many people were willing to let him listen. “Because I didn’t follow anybody on Instagram and I was following a bunch of folks on Twitter, I’m like, ‘No. Follow everybody.’ Like, I want to brag about the people who allow me in their conversation.” There’s also a practical reason behind it. Cena follows all kinds of different people because he wants to see opinions and conversations that might be completely different from his own. “It can be a pretty gamey environment. And I follow a wide range of folks because if I want to learn and if I want to see how people think, you’ve got to be open to listening to their conversation.” “Now with X, you can only follow, like, eight people a day. That’s why I’m stuck at a million. I wish I was at, like, 12 million right now. Every day you get on there and chip away and chip away, and hopefully that number will go up. But, like, I’m still working.” Cena also knows that getting a random follow from John Cena can be a pretty cool moment for somebody. If clicking one button can make a fan smile or give them something to brag about, he figures there’s no reason not to do it. “There’s a lot of nuance there. People want to be heard. If they’ve got a message to send, they’ve got a voice that they believe in. A follow from me — it feels good, it makes them smile.” For Cena, it’s a ridiculously easy way to give a little something back to people who have spent years supporting him. It doesn’t cost him anything, but he knows that tiny notification could mean a lot more to the person receiving it. Cena’s social-media strategy might look completely random from the outside, but there’s clearly a method behind it. While Instagram is deliberately kept disconnected and mysterious, X is basically the opposite — Cena wants to hear from as many people as the platform will allow. title: Injury Update: Mercedes Martinez Undergoes ACL Surgery After GoFundMe Covers Procedure in Full
raw_title: Mercedes Martinez Undergoes ACL Surgery After GoFundMe Covers Procedure in Full
summary_src: Mercedes Martinez has officially undergone the ACL surgery she needed after turning to the wrestling community for financial help. The veteran wrestler had launched a GoFundMe after tearing the ACL in her right knee during her August 15 match against Allie Katch.
body: The veteran wrestler had launched a GoFundMe after tearing the ACL in her right knee during her August 15 match against Allie Katch. Martinez previously explained that she did not have health insurance and would have to pay for the surgery herself before doctors would schedule the procedure. Now that surgery is done. In a new video posted to Twitter, Martinez gave fans an update from the early stages of recovery and revealed that the GoFundMe covered the operation in full. Martinez said she was already moving into the next phase of recovery, which includes removing the dressing, cleaning the incision and starting rehab exercises from home. “Today we are taking the dressing off and cleaning up the incision and starting our first rehab session. Basically, it’s at home. Just me doing my own exercises is at home for today and taking the pain meds if we need them.” She also said she has barely been using pain medication and prefers to avoid it unless she absolutely needs it. “But me, I don’t take pain meds. Doctor says with me not taking my pain meds means I’m way ahead of the game, which just means I have a high tolerance of pain. And I prefer to do this as much as possible without any meds. And just if I need them, I’ll take them. If not, I can deal with it.” Martinez then showed fans part of the immediate post-surgery process, explaining that the larger bandage had been removed and she was preparing to clean the area, put on a smaller dressing and get back into her brace. “We took the big bandage off. Right now it’s now the gauze. We gotta clean this up. I’m gonna clean all this up and then put the big brace back on. Our big trusty brace right here. I’ll put that back on once I clean this out and put a different bandage on, smaller one, so we can start icing it.” The biggest news came when Martinez confirmed that the fundraiser had accomplished exactly what she needed it to do. “I just wanted to do a quick shout out and just say thank you all for the GoFundMe. The GoFundMe paid for the surgery in full. Thank you, thank you, thank you. That is a blessing for me where it’s one less stress and now it’s just dealing with the expenses of the recovery.” Martinez had previously said the surgery could not be scheduled until it was paid for because she was considered a self-pay patient. The GoFundMe changed that situation, allowing her to move forward with the procedure and begin the long road back. She said the next concern is covering the costs that come with rehabilitation and recovery. “I have done an Amazon ACL recovery wish list for some of the things that I’m figuring out now what I need to help get this recovery faster and heal faster. I didn’t realize how much I need. I’ll probably still be adding to it as the days go along and once I figure out everything, but one day at a time.” “Thank you all for everything. title: WWE Had Nothing to Do With Max Caster’s Firing After TNA Bound for Glory
raw_title: WWE Had Nothing to Do With Max Caster’s Firing After TNA Bound for Glory
summary_src: WWE is apparently making one thing very clear about Max Caster’s TNA exit — don’t blame them. Despite WWE and TNA’s working relationship, people within WWE insist they had absolutely nothing to do with Caster getting dropped after his controversial Bound For Glory rap.
body: That shuts down any idea that WWE stepped in behind the scenes and pressured its partner promotion to do something about Caster. Based on the report, TNA made the call on its own before the situation even reached most of WWE’s decision-makers. The controversy started at Bound For Glory, where Caster made his TNA debut against Moose. As usual, he performed an entrance rap before the match, but a line referencing Riyadh quickly became the bigger story coming out of his appearance . Caster’s run didn’t survive the fallout. We had also previously reported that TNA President Carlos Silva made the decision to cut ties with him , ending Caster’s stint with the company after just one match. Caster wasn’t believed to have a long-term contract either. He was working under a per-appearance arrangement, which made it much easier for TNA to simply end the relationship once the controversy erupted. Another major detail was that TNA didn’t know what Caster was going to say beforehand. He had creative control over his entrance rap, and the Riyadh line was neither scripted nor approved by the company. TNA ultimately removed Caster-related content and issued a public apology before cutting ties with him altogether . Some people within AEW felt TNA should have anticipated the possibility of Caster pushing things too far considering controversial freestyle raps have always been part of his act. With WWE and TNA working together, it was always possible that questions would come up about whether WWE had any influence over how the situation was handled. This report paints a much simpler picture — TNA had apparently already made its move before most important people in WWE even knew there was a controversy. summary: That shuts down any idea that WWE stepped in behind the scenes and pressured its partner promotion to do something about Caster. Based on the report, TNA made the call on its own before the situation even reached most of WWE’s decision-makers.

title: Key Executive Who Helped Put Together WWE’s Netflix Deal Leaving Streaming Giant
raw_title: Key Executive Who Helped Put Together WWE’s Netflix Deal Leaving Streaming Giant
summary_src: WWE’s relationship with Netflix just got a pretty interesting shakeup behind the scenes. One of the executives who helped bring WWE to the streaming giant is leaving, and the man replacing her happens to be very familiar with WWE himself.
body: Netflix chief content officer Bela Bajaria is leaving the company after holding the position since 2023. Bajaria was instrumental in the negotiations that helped land WWE on Netflix , making her departure especially notable just a couple of years after WWE made its massive move to the platform. Her exit comes during a bigger shakeup at Netflix. The company is laying off around six percent of its workforce amid stock declines and concerns over stagnant business without signs of substantial growth. But here’s where things get interesting for WWE. Former Disney and Fox executive Peter Rice is taking Bajaria’s position, and Rice isn’t exactly a stranger to the wrestling business. Rice was one of the major players behind SmackDown moving to Fox. Back in 2018, when he was Chairman and CEO of Fox Networks Group, he was directly involved in trying to land WWE as soon as NBCUniversal’s exclusive negotiating window ended. The morning after that window expired on May 16, 2018, Rice hosted a meeting on the 44th floor of Fox’s Manhattan headquarters. Paul “Triple H” Levesque, Stephanie McMahon, Rupert Murdoch, Eric Shanks and Larry Jones were all involved, with Fox making a serious pitch to WWE. There’s another reason this situation is worth watching. Raw and WWE’s premium live events have been doing good numbers on Netflix, even if they may not have reached some of the expectations people had when the deal was first announced. Netflix’s behavior since landing WWE has also raised questions about how much weekly sports programming it actually wants. The company has shown more interest in major events than adding a bunch of regular weekly sports properties, and it didn’t outbid ESPN when the U.S. rights to WWE’s premium live events became available. None of that means WWE is suddenly in trouble at Netflix, and there’s no indication right now that Rice plans to change anything involving the company. But the executive who helped bring WWE to Netflix walking out while one of the people who helped bring SmackDown to Fox walks in certainly gives WWE another situation to keep an eye on. summary_src: A major AEW star recently dropped an interesting post on her social media. This post caught the attention of professional wrestling fans, and many considered it to be a statement related to her future.
body: The star is none other than Deonna Purrazzo. She was signed with AEW in 2023. Her last match in the Jacksonville-based promotion was on an episode of Collision in January 2025. She has not made any All Elite Wrestling appearances since then. But she has been working in Ring of Honor as the ROH Women's Pure Champion. But the fans can see her wrestle at Ring of Honor. Many people are under the impression that, with this message, the ROH Women's Pure Champion is expressing her frustration with her absence from All Elite Wrestling . Only time will tell when Purrazzo will make her next appearance for AEW from here on out. Deonna Purrazzo has been having a dominant run in the world of professional wrestling. In April 2025, Purrazzo made her return to Ring of Honor. She competed in a tournament to crown the inaugural ROH Women's Pure Champion. The Virtuosa defeated Billie Starkz to capture the title, and she has been undefeated in the promotion since then. Taking to X, the 32-year-old star highlighted that she is undefeated in Ring of Honor for more than a year. She asked her fans to put some respect on her name moving forward as a sign of respect for her dominant reign. In her reign as the ROH Women's Pure Champion, Deonna has defeated names like Trish Adora, Diamante, Viva Van, and Steph De Lander. It will be interesting to see who will be the next star to challenge Deonna Purrazzo for the championship from here on.

title: Massive championship match Set for WWE SmackDown
raw_title: Massive championship match announced for WWE SmackDown
summary_src: A massive championship match has been announced for WWE SmackDown.
body: A few segments and matches have already been announced for the show. Nikki Bella and Paige will continue their feud with another match on the blue brand, while Cody Rhodes will confront Randy Orton after The Viper cost him a chance to qualify for the Money in the Bank ladder match. The show will also see R-Truth go head-to-head against his former tag team partner, Damian Priest, after the Archer of Infamy turned on him a few weeks ago. Now, the show has added a title match to the card as well. On WWE.com , it was announced that Rey Fenix will defend his AAA Cruiserweight championship against Ricky Saints. This comes after Saints pinned Fenix in a six-man tag team match on the October 2 episode of SmackDown. Saints teamed up with The War Raiders to beat Rey Fenix and Fraxiom, and now the "Absolute" superstar has earned himself a title match. The two stars did meet in a title match on the September 11 episode of SmackDown, where Fenix beat Saints to retain the Cruiserweight championship. It will be interesting to see if the outcome will be similar this time or whether the former NXT champion will finally win his first championship on the main roster. This week on WWE RAW, Chad Gable put the Intercontinental championship on the line against Rey Fenix. It was a highly competitive bout with the luchador's high-flying style offering a perfect foil for Gable's technical wrestling. Later, Fenix took to social media to post some pictures from the match and mentioned that Gable was the better wrestler on the night. He said that he won't give up and that he would love to face Gable one more time. He pitched the idea of a Champion vs. Champion match for their next encounter.
summary: Officially, Rey Fenix will defend his AAA Cruiserweight championship against Ricky Saints. The two stars did meet in a title match on the September 11 episode of SmackDown, where Fenix got past Saints to retain the Cruiserweight championship.

title: There Is Only One Way Cody Rhodes and Randy Orton Can End Their Feud in WWE
raw_title: There Is Only One Way Cody Rhodes and Randy Orton Can End Their Feud in WWE
summary_src: Cody Rhodes and Randy Orton may have reached the point of no return.
body: The latest chapter of this rivalry began when Randy Orton returned at SummerSlam and hit Cody Rhodes with an RKO, preventing him from defeating CM Punk for the Undisputed WWE Championship. Orton later made it clear that he wanted to stop his former friend from winning another championship, giving The American Nightmare another reason to go after him. Since then, the two WWE Superstars have struggled to keep their emotions under control. Their showdown at Sunday Night's Main Event ended with The Viper bagging the W after playing mind games with Cody Rhodes. Rhodes’ hesitation when Orton appeared vulnerable also showed that their complicated history could still affect him inside the ring. And that is why the unforgiving structure of Hell in a Cell makes so much sense. The so-called devil’s playground will keep both men inside, making it harder for either superstar to escape when the action gets brutal. It would also allow WWE to pursue a different angle in the rivalry, with Rhodes forced to show how far he is willing to go to finally defeat his former mentor. The match should also come with one clear stipulation: the rivalry ends when the bell rings, regardless of who wins. That would give the result real meaning and prevent WWE from dragging the conflict into another premium live event.
summary: The latest chapter of this rivalry began when Randy Orton made a comeback at SummerSlam and hit Cody Rhodes with an RKO. Orton later made it clear that he wanted to stop his former friend from winning another championship, giving The American Nightmare another reason to go after him.

title: Chicago-area officer sues WWE, Montez Ford over alleged unwanted lap dance during Raw
raw_title: Chicago-area officer sues WWE, Montez Ford over alleged unwanted lap dance during Raw
body: A Cook County sheriff’s officer is suing WWE over an alleged incident during a live broadcast. CHICAGO - A Cook County sheriff’s officer is suing WWE, wrestler Montez Ford and an event production company, alleging he was subjected to unwanted sexualized contact while working security at a live wrestling event. Noel Lucas filed the lawsuit Wednesday in Cook County Circuit Court. The complaint says he was working an off-duty security job at WWE Monday Night Raw on July 6 at Allstate Arena in Rosemont. According to the lawsuit, Lucas was seated at his assigned post outside the ring when Ford, whose legal name is Kenneth Crawford, approached him, straddled him and began moving his hips in a sexually suggestive way. Lucas’ attorneys say he was not told he would be part of the performance and did not consent. Live announcers on the Netflix broadcast allegedly mocked Lucas in real time, telling viewers, "That guy clearly hates fun," and comparing him to Paul Blart, the fictional security guard from "Paul Blart: Mall Cop." "Mr. Lucas was there to do his job, not to be made a part of WWE’s entertainment," attorney Whitney Barr said in a statement. The incident aired live on Netflix. The lawsuit says WWE later shared video of it on TikTok and Instagram, where it received more than 300,000 views. Ford also shared footage, according to the lawsuit. The complaint includes 14 counts, including battery, assault, intentional infliction of emotional distress and claims under Illinois’ Gender Violence Act and Right of Publicity Act. "Entertainment is not a defense to unwanted sexual contact," Barr said. "We intend to hold WWE and those responsible accountable for what happened to Mr. Lucas and for the harm caused by the subsequent publication of the footage." title: On the Record: Ex-WWE Referee Opens Up On How Valuable The Miz Truly is

body: The former WWE referee was with the company when Miz first debuted. It is well-documented that the two-time WWE champion was not very popular in the locker room. Miz came from the world of reality TV, so he was already labeled an outsider before he debuted. He has opened up about being kicked out of the locker room for months before The Undertaker allowed him return. Despite his rocky start, Miz turned things around and has since become one of the longest-tenured superstars on the roster. Miz, 46, has main evented WrestleMania opposite John Cena and had memorable feuds with the likes of Daniel Bryan. He has also transitioned into film and television, while returning to his reality TV roots. Former WWE referee Jimmy Korderas says The Miz ‘s versatility as a performer makes him a valuable asset to the company. “People concentrate on the in-ring stuff and the moves, it’s not about the moves, it’s how you engage your audience and get them invested in you. Miz was able to, whether he was a babyface or a heel, because he was a babyface a few times, but his main deal is being a heel, that’s where he really excels. That’s his strength. That’s where I think people buy him more as a heel,” Korderas exclusively told Heavy Sports via T he Game Plan . “You need a guy to plug in anywhere. In a spot where you need comedy, he’s there because he can do it. You need a guy who can help get someone over, a young talent over, he’s the guy to put him in there with, because it’s still to this day, for a young talent, a big deal to beat The Miz.” The former WWE referee pointed to Miz’s track record and praised him for excelling wherever he is needed. “Eventually we saw it in The Miz. At first, he did generate a lot of heat from the locker room, and I hate to say it, it was pretty much deserved, because he did alienate some people in the wrong way. But he stayed the course, he learned, he developed. And he became not only a good hand, but one of the best ever utility players in wrestling, ever,” Korderas exclusively told Heavy Sports via The Game Plan . title: 7 Wrestlers Who Got Fired RIDICULOUSLY Fast

body: To work for the majors in North America is to c hase job security in an industry with almost none . At the very top, there are guaranteed contracts, reduced schedules, generous travel and accommodation offerings and a wealth of opportunities to earn money outside of wrestling to improve your negotiations to simply stay in it. In an era where television rights deals have replaced house show, merchandise and pay-per-view numbers as primary revenue drivers, wrestlers have theoretically never had less individual value, but the motivation to get to the very top is made clear by the cushy lives of those that occupy the best spots. The slope is slippery, and never is that clearer than when a wrestler has lost their spot before audiences have gotten used to them even getting it. Season Two's finale on August 31st 2010 very briefly profiled the women that would be competing the first all-female edition of the show, and very literally standing out amongst the newest chasing pack was new rookie "diva" Lindsay Kay Hayward. Known previously as "Isis The Amazon", she'd worked around 20 matches over two years en route to the market leader, so it wasn't as if the company were just taking a total punt on somebody with physical gifts. Nor would that be a new phenomenon for pro wrestling anyway - plenty of behemoths broke in simply because other wrestlers were taken with their size upon spotting them out and about somewhere or other. It was effectively "airport test" stuff, and the rebranded Aloisia had passed with flying colours just by standing there in the line-up . Why, then, was she nowhere to be found when the show started for real a week later? In storylines, her "pro" Vickie Guerrero had fired her due to supposed unhappiness with her efforts, but the reality was far harsher.

On the Raw after Money in the Bank , Femi's future became clear during an exchange with a WWE Hall of Famer. The next face of WWE will not have a mouthpiece speaking for him. He will rule alone. Oba Femi was an NXT call-up with a ton of potential until the moment he showed up on Raw this spring to answer Brock Lesnar's WrestleMania 42 challenge. From the moment his music hit, and he destroyed the Beast, fans erupted and began chanting his name. Just like that, Femi became the next big thing. Over his three-match feud with Lesnar, which Femi eventually won at SummerSlam to send Lesnar into retirement, there was Paul Heyman by Brock's side. He understood exactly how much of a threat Oba was, and even as he tore him down on the mic, he respected his abilities.
