Lucas was working off-duty security when, according to the lawsuit, Ford approached him during the Street Profits’ entrance and performed a sexually suggestive dance (embedded above) involving hip thrusts and gyrating without his consent. Lucas alleges that footage of the incident spread widely across social media, including on WWE’s and Ford’s accounts, making him recognizable to the public. He also alleges that when he returned to his full-time courthouse job the next day, people recognized and mocked him by imitating the dance. He also alleges that his children were ridiculed at school because of the video, causing him significant humiliation, embarrassment, and emotional distress. The lawsuit includes 14 counts, including assault, battery, intentional infliction of emotional distress, alleged violations of the Illinois Gender Violence Act, and unlawful use of his image under the Illinois Right of Publicity Act. Lucas is seeking monetary and punitive damages, legal costs, and an order preventing WWE and Ford from using his identity. Neither WWE nor Ford have responded to the lawsuit as of yesterday. Santi Rivera, aged 24, began his wrestling career in 2021. He has appeared for promotions including Create A Pro, Beyond Wrestling, and Reality of Wrestling.

body: Jalwa Game Goa Game Raja Game MaanWin DMFirst Veer Game ROMAN REIGNS AND MORE TALK 'STREET FIGHTER' ON SIRIUSXM SPECIAL By Mike Johnson on 2026-10-16 07:30:00 SiriusXM issued the following: SiriusXM Front Row special w/ Roman Reigns and the Cast of "Street Fighter" The cast of the upcoming “Street Fighter” movie recently joined Sam Roberts for a special SiriusXM Front Row event on the WWE Radio channel, where stars 50 Cent, Roman Reigns, Noah Centineo, Andrew Koji, and Callina Liang discussed their experiences filming the movie, behind-the-scenes moments, and the camaraderie among the cast. Roman Reigns spoke about making the transition from WWE to acting, and the difference in dynamics between being on a movie set and working with actors, versus working/competing in the world of pro wrestling. Noah Centineo talks about Marky Mark and Jake Paul being inspirations he drew from for his character in the film, Ken Masters. The cast also shares fun behind-the-scenes stories about 50 Cent buying out Luna Park for the entire cast and crew to build camaraderie, and more. Sam Roberts: How do you wrap your head around commanding that attention when you’re shooting scenes, it’s a movie, it’s not like getting into a wrestling ring and feeling 20,000 people around you. And, number two, making it different than Roman Reigns. Akuma is very different, even in the way you use your body, very different than what Roman Reigns does. Roman Reigns: The main parallel for me, especially in this movie, my main contributions were in the third act. So it’s in the main event of the movie is what I was telling myself. And that’s what I practice, is main event performance. That’s my bag. That’s what I do when it’s my time to go out there and wrestle. So I just try to keep that type of weight on it. The stakes are as high as can be so you need to be able to come in and match what everybody’s done. … These guys know what they’re doing. I'm not a real actor. I go out and I wrestle. It really helped me to see what they have done and the way they led the film. It set the tone for what needed to be matched. It wasn't easy, but there were a bunch of things I was able to rely on from wrestling to help me take this on. Sam Roberts: You've also evolved your performance as a wrestler, I think, further than a lot of traditional wrestlers and WWE Superstars do, in terms of the stories that you actively tell with your face. Bringing the audience on that ride, is that something that translates into film? Is that something you bring over here and maybe then bring something from here back to how Roman Reigns is portrayed? A post about the business of independent wrestling might fit a publication that covers sports media or event promotion. A generic article with no connection to wrestling, entertainment or the site's readership is much harder to justify. Before arranging a placement, look at the website as a reader would. Is it publishing current material? Does it have a clear subject and a consistent editorial voice? Are its recent stories relevant to the audience you hope to reach? A site that has a wrestling section but rarely updates it may not be as useful as a smaller publication with an active readership and a clear focus. Check the quality of the articles around the proposed placement, too. A page surrounded by unrelated posts or a long list of paid-looking contributions can make even a well-written article feel out of place. Ask what the editor expects, whether the article will be reviewed, and whether it will remain published. Those details affect the reader's experience as much as the link itself. There are different ways to handle outreach and publishing. FATJOE is positioned as a managed service, while iCopify operates as a marketplace where users can select publishing websites themselves. The comparison of FATJOE and iCopify is useful for understanding that difference before deciding which process suits a campaign. A managed service may appeal to a buyer who wants more of the process handled for them. A marketplace can offer more direct choice, but that choice also means doing the evaluation: reviewing available sites, checking their subject matter and deciding whether the proposed placement is appropriate. Neither approach removes the need to read the final article carefully or consider how it will look to the site's audience. For a wrestling-related campaign, make a short list of acceptable publications before ordering anything. Set practical standards for relevance, quality and audience. If the goal is to introduce a new training school, for example, a local sports or community publication may be more relevant than a broad marketing site. If the article concerns wrestling collectibles, an entertainment or hobby publication could make more sense. The strongest guest articles answer a question or provide context that the host site's audience can use. A piece about how smaller promotions build a live-event audience could cover venue selection, local promotion and the challenge of creating repeat attendance. An article about wrestling media might explain how a promotion can share timely information without overwhelming fans with promotional posts. title: Why So Many Former NFL Players Go into Wrestling
raw_title: Why So Many Former NFL Players Go into Wrestling - PWInsider
body: Jalwa Game Goa Game Raja Game MaanWin DMFirst Veer Game Why So Many Former NFL Players Go into Wrestling By Kendall Jenkins on 2026-10-14 10:05:00 Former NFL players have long made the transition to professional wrestling. The two sports share similar physical attributes, skills, and culture, making the crossover a more natural progression for players looking to make the change. Active recruitment of NFL players by promoters has also provided a pathway and encouraged players to take the leap. There are other factors at play here too. NFL careers can be notoriously short; therefore, the chance to become a professional wrestler and pursue another potentially lucrative path is an attractive proposition for many, especially for fringe players and free agents. Some players just want to remain in the spotlight a little bit longer and extend their careers for longer than would ever be possible in football. American football and professional wrestling may look like very different sports, but there’s a surprising number of skills that both disciplines share. Strength and power are the most obvious. Football players use it for blocking, tackling, and breaking tackles, while wrestlers rely on it for takedowns, throws, lifts, and control. Linemen in particular have multiple crossover skills. Their speedy reactions and upper-body coordination, plus experience of fighting for hand position, are similar to wrestlers fighting to establish grips and create openings. A lineman exploding off the line and a wrestler shooting for a takedown also require similar abilities. Staying upright is important in both sports, despite opponents desperately trying to take you down. That’s why agility, footwork, balance, and body control are key skills in wrestling and football. The similarity between tackling and takedowns needs no explanation. There are plenty of NFL players who didn't go on to become full-time wrestlers but made notable WWE appearances, including Lawrence Taylor, four-time Super Bowl champion Rob Gronkowski , and William "The Refrigerator" Perry. But some of the most successful wrestling stars to have ever entered the squared circle are former football players. Sonnenberg is regarded as the first prominent professional football player from the major era to successfully make the leap. He played in the National Football League (NFL) from 1923 until 1930, winning the 1928 NFL championship with the Providence Steam Rollers. Sonnenberg’s wrestling career proved even more successful. Not only did he revolutionise the sport by introducing the "flying tackle" , but he won the National Wrestling Association (NWA) World Heavyweight Championship in 1929 and held the title for two years. In 1939, Sonnenberg became the American Wrestling Association champion after defeating and unmasking Marvin Westenberg (“The Shadow”). body: Jalwa Game Goa Game Raja Game MaanWin DMFirst Veer Game ALEX GRACIA VS. HEATHER BY ELEGANCE & MORE: 10/16 TNA XPLOSION REPORT By Mike Johnson on 2026-10-16 13:02:00 Welcome to this week's TNA Xplosion report. Red charges in to start fast, but Styles repeatedly shoves him away, taking a shot to the face for his trouble. A 619 rocks Styles and sends him outside, where he catches Red’s dive and turns it into a powerbomb backbreaker. Back inside, Red unloads with strikes, only for a discus clothesline to bring him crashing back down. A middle-rope sunset flip goes nowhere, but Red backflips over Styles (which looks great) and lands right into a failed Styles Clash attempt. Red counters with a tornado DDT, only for Styles to turn it into a Northern Lights suplex and regain control. Styles' manager Mortimer Plumtree even sneaks in a few shots, earning himself an anklescissors for his efforts. Styles retaliates by dropping him face-first onto the steps, but Red still manages to snap off a hurrancanrana. A reverse DDT earns Styles a two count before he locks in a Muta Lock, even rolling onto his stomach to crank back harder. When that fails to finish things, Styles plants Red with a hard sitout powerbomb, and they head to the top rope. The super Styles Clash is blocked, however, and Red counters with a super hurricanrana to score the pin. TNA ODB Hall of Fame induction speech - Cory Strode reporting Amazing Red Hall of Fame induction speech - Cory Strode reporting Red starts by saying he was just a Spanish kid from Brooklyn, and everyone made this a reality for him. He thanks Frankie. He then thanks Don West for helping him with promos. He says when he started, he didn’t know why he was here, but when people showed up, he knew why he was here. He thanks Chris DeVine, who got him to shows when he started. Brian XL, the man he made House of Glory with. He thanks his family. He then thanks the fans for making the X Division big. He then says he is in the X Division match later tonight. Cruz Montana (Mike Santana in TNA) is out next to induct Konnan and says he will be showing something the people here worked hard on, and it’s the video package for Konnan highlights. He says he didn’t write anything because it will come straight from his heart. He says without Konnan, there are no Latino wrestlers and no cruiserweight division of Lucha Libre in the US. Sitting under his learning tree was the most important part of his life. Kash keeps the pressure on with a clothesline that nearly ends the match, followed by a Boston Crab. He abandons the hold to powerbomb Red for another two-count. Red answers with a spinning kick, but Kash counters with a German suplex and a facebuster before locking in a camel clutch in the middle of the ring. The two trade a series of pinning attempts until Red catches Kash with a kick to the head. The Code Red follows, but Kash kicks out at two! Red connects with a springboard dropkick and the 718, then adds a springboard elbow drop, on

title: Max Caster Issues Statement Following TNA Firing
raw_title: MAX CASTER ISSUES STATEMENT FOLLOWING TNA FIRING - PWInsider
body: Jalwa Game Goa Game Raja Game MaanWin DMFirst Veer Game MAX CASTER ISSUES STATEMENT FOLLOWING TNA FIRING By Mike Johnson on 2026-10-13 08:37:00 Max Caster released the following statement this morning via his Twitter account: "Just to address all the TNA stuff, I want to say thank you to Carlos Silva. I talked to him in person. He was very generous, very professional, even after all this stuff happened. And I, I understand why he did what he did. It's his show. He's got to protect TNA, and I went too far for him. So, I want to apologize to him and everybody else in the office. I want to apologize to anyone who vouched for me to get that spot. I feel like I let those people down. Thank you to Moose for sharing your platform with me, and I wish things didn't turn out the way they did, but I'm proud of that match and I'm sorry for how things have ended up, and then for anybody who's offended, I just want everybody to know that when I do these wraps, it's never to offend people. It's only to entertain. So in my mind, it's entertainment value first. And then if you're offended by it, that's your right. So I can't apologize for anyone being offended, but just know that it's not my intention to make people upset. If it gets a reaction, I think I did my job. It was a very relevant part of the show and highly talked about, so I feel good about that. But the consequences of everything, I'm accepting that. I can accept the facts of that. And then to anybody who is asking if I'm good, I'm good. I'm just embarrassed how all this happened. It's, you know, you don't want it to be one match and then that's it, you get fired. But again, that's the reality of the situation. I'm accepting it, and that's life. And in life, sometimes you got to man up and just accept it and move on. So whatever's next, I don't know, but we'll see. Thank you, everybody who's reaching out and supporting." Veer Game DM First Raxi Win 6 Club BDG Play Game BDG BET Game Ok win

title: Meltzer: Saudi Government Pressuring WWE Over Crown Jewel
raw_title: Dave Meltzer Believes WWE Crown Jewel Decision Comes Down To Saudi Arabian Government
summary_src: Dave Meltzer has broken down the situation regarding WWE Crown Jewel, and believes the Saudi government have the final say on if the event takes place.
body: Meltzer mentioned the recent post on X (formerly known as Twitter) by Al-Sheikh that read "Thank you to everyone who checked in and showed support. Hard times reveal true friends," was a post that has put pressure on TKO to not cancel Crown Jewel, or any of the boxing and MMA events that are on the horizon. Al-Sheikh did announce that the Six Kings Slam tennis tournament has been moved from October to December, and events like the Red Sea International Film Festival, the FIFAe Finals, The Joy Awards, and the Soundstorm EDM festival have all been postponed. However, because WWE Superstars are independent contractors in name only, they wouldn't have a choice about going. Many people in the company, particularly the non-wrestlers, aren't thrilled about going over , and as for the wrestlers, it is largely expected everyone travels over to Riyadh to avoid pressure from above. These backups might need to be put into play due to the high risk of terrorist attacks in Saudi Arabia, with entertainment venues, hotels and locations where U.S. citizens gather, and places visited by U.S citizens and other foreigners all be at risk of being potential targets. Transportation hubs such as airports are also targets, as proven by the recent bombing at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh. Meltzer stated that the the Iran-backed Houthi have threatened to attack Saudi Arabia again, and even if missile strikes are intercepted, falling debris could also be a risk to citizens in certain areas. With all that said, the amount of money at stake is too much to risk according to Meltzer. While WWE will not lose any money on their current deal by postponing an event due to their current deal with the Saudi's, the long-term relationship between the two parties could be hindered when it comes to negotiating a new deal when the current one expires in 2028. Al-Sheikh is also the sole investor in Zuffa Boxing, another TKO entity, and much like WWE's deal, a pull out wouldn't be the end of the world at this time but it could hamper the relationship between TKO and the Saudi government in the future.
summary: Dave Meltzer reported that Turki Al-Sheikh's recent social media post has increased pressure on TKO Group to proceed with Crown Jewel in Riyadh despite regional instability. Several major Saudi entertainment events have been postponed or rescheduled following the recent airport bombing and heightened terrorist threats targeting foreigners and public venues. WWE talent classified as independent contractors would have little say in attending the show, though many non-wrestling staff members are reportedly unhappy about the trip.

title: AEW's Pac Died From Bronchial Asthma
raw_title: Late AEW Star Pac's Cause Of Death Reportedly Revealed
summary_src: The cause of death for late AEW star Pac, real name Benjamin Satterley, was reportedly revealed.
body: The outlet, citing a spokesperson from the Cook County Medical Examiner's Office, reported that Satterley, age 40, died of bronchial asthma. Officials, who found Satterley dead when they arrived on scene, noted at the time that while his death did not appear suspicious , he was found with saliva on the front of his shirt. Reports indicated undisclosed medication was found in the vehicle. Satterley was headed to O'Hare Airport and had stopped at a CAVA restaurant on the way. That's where he was discovered slumped over in the vehicle by witnesses, who alerted authorities. Officials arrived on scene and pronounced the star dead around 4 p.m. AEW revealed his passing later that night via social media. Pac competed the night before his death at All Out, where he faced off against Andrade El Idolo for the AEW National Championship. At the end of the night, Satterley appeared once again on the show, coming to the aid of Death Riders leader Jon Moxley in his match against AEW World Champion Will Ospreay. In the days following his passing, AEW held an emotional tribute show in his honor , where the Death Riders, including Moxley, Marina Shafir, Claudio Castagnoli, Wheeler Yuta, Daniel Garcia, and even Bryan Danielson, all competed in matches to honor their friend. Various WWE stars who knew Satterley as Neville during his time in WWE, including in "WWE NXT," also shared their memories of the star in an emotional tribute video posted to the company's YouTube channel.
summary: Pac, whose real name was Benjamin Satterley, was 40 when he passed away. The Cook County Medical Examiner's Office determined the cause to be bronchial asthma after he was found unresponsive in his vehicle outside a Chicago-area CAVA restaurant while en route to O'Hare Airport. The night before, he had wrestled Andrade El Idolo for the AEW Continental Championship at All Out and later aided Jon Moxley in the main event; AEW paid tribute with an emotional show featuring the Death Riders stable in the following days.

summary_src: A new report revealed more on former WWE star Sheamus, now going by S. Farrelly, booking a convention date the same day as AEW Full Gear.
body: Farrelly was announced for The Big Event EXS, a wrestling fan convention at the Suffolk Credit Union Arena in Brentwood, New York, on November 17. The star recorded a video, posted to the convention's Facebook page , confirming he'd be in attendance to sign autographs and take photos with fans. The date, notably, lines up with AEW Full Gear. As of this writing, Farrelly has not been teased for any upcoming AEW event, including AEW WrestleDream on Saturday. Alongside the news of Farrelly's free agency, Fightful Select also reported there are many within AEW, both from a talent standpoint, as well as executives, who would like to see the former "Celtic Warrior" in the company. As of the report on October 2, no discussions had been had between the sides. TNA reportedly wanted the star at Bound for Glory 2026 , but the appearance was never locked on, or even considered, on Farrelly's side. Max Caster ended up filling the spot the company reportedly wanted for Sheamus, in a match against Moose.
summary: Stephen Farrelly, formerly known as Sheamus, has been announced for The Big Event EXS fan convention at Suffolk Credit Union Arena in Brentwood, New York on November 17. That date coincides with AEW's Full Gear pay-per-view. Multiple people within AEW are interested in bringing in the free agent, though no talks have taken place between the sides as of early October.

title: Royce Keys Welcomes Carmelo Hayes To 946
raw_title: WWE's Royce Keys Discusses Adding Carmelo Hayes To 946, Future Of Faction
summary_src: Royce Keys, the leader of 946 on "WWE Raw," spoke about the future of the faction, as well as adding Carmelo Hayes to the stable.
body: Keys, the leader of 946, sat down on " Busted Open Radio " to talk more about the dangerous faction and his friend, Hayes, getting involved. After months of not appearing on "WWE SmackDown," Hayes joined in the beatdown of the Usos and Solo Sikoa on Monday. "That my dog, you know, way, way before I even set foot in the door," Keys said of "'Melo." "He's a great addition. He's got a chip on his shoulder like we all do. There's more to come... More to come with the destruction and chaos. People are genuinely afraid of us, so we like that." Keys started his beatdown of the Bloodline alongside Sikoa, in addition to LA Knight, at SummerSlam, where the trio defeated Jacob Fatu and the Usos during night one. Keys was off WWE TV for a few weeks before returning to cause chaos alongside OTM as a surprise on the August 24 edition of "Raw." He said going from the undercard to multiple main event segments of the red brand has been a dream. He's keeping his head down, however, and continuing the work. "You know, you gotta always stay ready," he said. "When they call the play for you, you may only get one shot at it. I'm ready to run any play they throw at me."
summary: Royce Keys appeared on Busted Open Radio to discuss Carmelo Hayes joining his faction 946 after Hayes helped attack the Usos and Solo Sikoa on SmackDown. Keys noted that Hayes has long been a close friend with the same drive as the group and that more destruction is planned. Keys also reflected on his rapid rise from undercard matches to multiple Raw main events since returning alongside OTM.

title: Medical Examiner Rules PAC Died of Bronchial Asthma
raw_title: Medical examiner determines Ben Satterley’s cause of death as bronchial asthma
summary_src: The cause of death of Benjamin Satterley, known professionally as PAC, has been determined as bronchial asthma.
body: The cause of death of Benjamin Satterley, known professionally as PAC, has been determined as bronchial asthma. Edward Lewis, senior sports reporter for the California Post, first reported the determination on Friday. The Cook County Medical Examiner’s Office ruled Satterley’s death as natural following its investigation. No additional medical details surrounding the determination have been made public. Satterley died on September 27, less than 24 hours after wrestling Andrade El Idolo for the AEW National Championship at All Out in Hoffman Estates, Illinois. As detailed in John Pollock’s obituary , Satterley was found unresponsive in a vehicle outside a restaurant in Des Plaines, Illinois. Emergency services responded and he was pronounced dead at 4.08 pm local time. Authorities said shortly afterward that there were no indications of trauma or foul play and that his death did not appear suspicious. An autopsy was performed, with the cause and manner of death remaining pending while additional testing was completed. Born in Newcastle upon Tyne, Satterley began wrestling in 2004 and became closely associated with Dragon Gate, where he held multiple championships and established a record 447-day reign as Open the Brave Gate Champion. He signed with WWE in 2012 and performed as Adrian Neville and later Neville. His accomplishments included the NXT Championship, two NXT Tag Team Championship reigns and two runs as WWE Cruiserweight Champion. After returning to Dragon Gate and winning the Open the Dream Gate Championship, Satterley joined AEW in 2019. He became the inaugural AEW All-Atlantic Champion, later renamed the International Championship, and also held the AEW World Trios Championship as part of Death Triangle. His final match was the September 26 loss to Andrade at All Out. Satterley also appeared later that night during the AEW World Championship main event between Will Ospreay and Jon Moxley.

He passed away on September 27 in Illinois, less than a day after competing against Andrade El Idolo for the AEW National Championship at All Out. No signs of trauma or foul play were found, and authorities confirmed the death was not suspicious.

body: Netflix’s chief content officer Bela Bajaria is out as the streamer made a bold decision to let the executive go. Bajaria helped oversee Netflix’s programming strategy with a $20 billion budget and was pivotal in WWE coming to Netflix in 2025. When the deal was announced in early 2024, Bajaria was quoted , “(WWE) has been very under-distributed outside the US. I think there’s really great opportunity to still grow it outside the U.S.” The exit comes one day after Netflix cut approximately 1,000 jobs with an underperforming stock and stalled engagement on the platform. Co-CEO Ted Sarandos acknowledged the disappointing performance in a recent chat, saying the service was “Not growing as fast as I want us to.” Former Fox and Disney executive Peter Rice will replace Bajaria.
summary: Netflix has parted ways with chief content officer Bela Bajaria, who played a key role in bringing WWE programming to the platform beginning in 2025. The move follows a round of layoffs impacting around 1,000 employees amid disappointing stock performance and slowing subscriber growth. Peter Rice, formerly of Fox and Disney, has been named as her replacement.

title: Backstage Buzz: WWE’s Crown Jewel plans put money and power ahead of safety
raw_title: WWE’s Crown Jewel plans put money and power ahead of safety | Opinion
summary_src: Saudi Arabia right now isn’t the safest place in the world. But that likely won’t stop WWE. The country has been rocked by several attacks over the last few weeks by Iranian-backed forces from Yemen.
body: Saudi Arabia right now isn’t the safest place in the world. But that likely won’t stop WWE. The country has been rocked by several attacks over the last few weeks by Iranian-backed forces from Yemen. Between October 7 and October 11, 17 people have died dead and 333 people injured in attacks that have taken place at Riyadh’s airport. In a fair world filled with common sense, WWE would naturally find an alternative for their event in Riyadh next month, prioritizing safety concerns over money. And recent reports do indicate there is a backup plan. Unfortunately, that is not exactly how the world operates currently. There is money to be made, after all, and relationships to keep. So as of right now, WWE will be sending their talent and production team to what will essentially be an active warzone. There was also an incident the following year that saw Vince McMahon reportedly clash with the Saudi Arabian government over the airing of one of their shows locally following a pay dispute. Coincidentally, the plane meant to take the talent home suddenly developed engine trouble, leaving a majority of the roster stranded in Saudi Arabia for an extra six hours. Now, the two incidents have never been fully linked to one another, and it’s never been fully established that the Saudi Arabian government deliberately held WWE talent hostage. But it is easy to see how some could see the two incidents being connected. This time around, the situation seems more unstable than controversial. The country is in the middle of a war with Iranian-backed Houthis in Yemen. King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh has been attacked 20 times this month alone. The US State Department has issued a level 3 advisory urging Americans to reconsider travel to the country, and the Australian government is specifically advising citizens to not travel there. At this point, that makes sense and is a good call. There is no reason for anyone to travel to Saudi Arabia right now, let alone for a pro wrestling show that could be held anywhere else. While Canelo Alvarez still plans to head there for his next fight at the end of this month, other events are backing out . “Hard times reveal true friends,” Turki Alalshikh, the Chairman of Saudi Arabia’s General Entertainment Authority, wrote on social media after confirming Canelo would continue on. But there are two things that will make WWE go. One is relatively simple – there’s way too much money on the table. WWE staying away will not only prevent them from getting a big payday, it also poses many risks with their relationship with Saudi Arabia. And the second stretches beyond WWE. TKO’s Zuffa Boxing, which is heavily promoted across WWE television, is financially backed by the Saudi Arabian government. The last thing TKO would want to do is imperil that relationship by backing away from their contractual deals, even if they are risking lives by doing so. title: In Memoriam: PAC’s Cause of Death Revealed After Sudden Passing at 40
raw_title: PAC’s Cause of Death Revealed After Sudden Passing at 40
summary_src: PAC’s cause of death has finally been revealed weeks after the AEW star was found unresponsive inside a rental car near Chicago O’Hare International Airport.
body: The New York Post reported on October 16 that the Cook County Medical Examiner’s Office determined Benjamin Satterley, better known to wrestling fans as PAC, died from bronchial asthma. His manner of death was officially ruled natural. A spokesperson for the medical examiner’s office confirmed the finding following the investigation into Satterley’s sudden September 27 death . The ruling brings an answer to a case that had remained open while officials waited on additional testing following the initial autopsy. Satterley was discovered unconscious inside a rental vehicle outside a CAVA restaurant in Des Plaines, Illinois, at around 4 p.m. on September 27. First responders rushed to the scene and attempted life-saving measures, but the 40-year-old wrestler was pronounced dead at approximately 4:08 p.m. The circumstances surrounding his death immediately raised questions because there were no obvious signs of trauma or foul play. Police noted that Satterley had saliva on the front of his shirt, while medication was also found inside the vehicle. The specific medication was redacted from the publicly released incident report. His phone provided another look at what he had been doing before his death. Google Maps was still open with directions to Chicago O’Hare International Airport, where Satterley was preparing to catch a flight back to the United Kingdom. A woman who spoke with police said Satterley had planned to stop at CAVA for lunch before heading to the airport after his flight had been delayed. The 911 call later revealed just how suddenly the situation unfolded. The woman who found Satterley said his vehicle was still running while he remained completely unresponsive inside. “We’ve been banging on the window for I want to say, like, five minutes now. His face is, like, straight down. Apparently their eyes are open, too. I don’t see his chest moving at all.” The Cook County Medical Examiner’s Office performed an autopsy shortly after Satterley’s death but did not immediately announce a cause. Officials said additional testing was needed before a final determination could be made. That delay led to plenty of questions about what examiners were looking for, but the final ruling now makes clear that Satterley died from bronchial asthma and that his death was natural. Satterley had been in the Chicago area for AEW All Out and wrestled Andrade the night before his death. His sudden passing stunned the wrestling world, with AEW, WWE and numerous wrestlers paying tribute to him in the days that followed. PAC’s death remained one of wrestling’s biggest unanswered stories for nearly three weeks, but the medical examiner has now closed the biggest question surrounding what happened. The official ruling is bronchial asthma, with the manner of death listed as natural. Steve Carrier Steve Carrier is the founder of Ringside News and has been reporting on pro wrestling since 1997. His stories have been featured on TMZ, Forbes, Bleacher Report, and more.

A spokesperson for the medical examiner’s office made official the finding after the investigation into Satterley’s sudden September 27 death .

summary_src: Becky Lynch says Triple H went out of his way to make sure she could step away from WWE without immediately losing her paycheck when she hit a point of burnout. Lynch revealed that when she told Paul “Triple H” Levesque she needed time away, his response was to offer a way for her existing ...
body: Lynch opened up about the situation during the 2026 espnW: Women + Sports Summit while discussing how WWE has supported her as both a performer and a mother. The conversation started with Lynch recalling how supportive WWE had been when she first became pregnant while she was champion. Vince McMahon congratulated her immediately, and Lynch said the company placed no pressure on her to rush back after giving birth. She then revealed that WWE showed her the same kind of flexibility years later when she reached another difficult point in her career. Instead of trying to convince Lynch to stay on the road, Levesque offered to extend the arrangement she already had so she could continue getting paid while taking the time she needed. “And he was like, ‘Well, let’s just, whatever you’re on, let’s just prolong it so that at least you can get paid until you feel like you’re ready to come back.’” The larger issue, according to Lynch, is that professional wrestling can still be a brutal business to navigate as a parent. WWE operates year-round, and performers have historically spent several nights every week traveling from city to city. “But the thing about wrestling is that it’s 52 weeks a year. You’re in a different city, right? Sometimes four, five nights a week and you’re on the road.” “WWE has been very good at facilitating like, ‘Okay, you’re a mom. Okay, we’re not going to put you on live events. You’ll be at TV.’” “I’ll put her to bed on a Sunday night, get on a red eye, do Monday Night Raw, and then fly back as early as I can. So really, I only miss one sleep.” Derek Holloway Derek Holloway is a writer at Ringside News specializing in professional wrestling news, rumors, and results. title: On the Record: Becky Lynch Says Becoming a Mom at Height of WWE Run Was About Proving Women Don’t Have to Choose
raw_title: Becky Lynch Says Becoming a Mom at Height of WWE Run Was About Proving Women Don’t Have to Choose
summary_src: Becky Lynch was sitting on top of WWE when she decided to start a family, and she now says part of that decision was about proving women shouldn’t have to sacrifice one dream to have another.
body: Speaking during the 2026 espnW: Women + Sports Summit , Lynch revealed that the same event actually played a role in changing how she viewed motherhood years earlier. “I will say this panel has a lot to answer for because in 2019 I was sitting on this panel and I was with this sprinter Shelly-Ann Fraser, and she was talking about how she had a two-year-old and she came back, and I was like, ‘Oh, it can be done. You can do that. You can go have a kid and come back and be at the top of your game.’ Six months later…” That realization came while Lynch was experiencing the biggest run of her WWE career. She had already main-evented WrestleMania and was in the middle of a 399-day championship reign when she eventually stepped away from WWE after becoming pregnant. Lynch said she had always wanted a family and felt she had found the right person to build one with in Seth Rollins. What she didn’t accept was the idea that motherhood automatically meant surrendering everything she had worked for professionally. “Well, you know, for me, I always wanted to have a family. I met the perfect partner. And, you know, for me, it didn’t feel like I was giving up my top spot. It felt like I was doing something with my top spot because before it was, if you go off and you have a kid, well then that’s it. Goodbye.” Lynch’s goal was bigger than simply proving that she personally could make a comeback. She looked at the biggest male wrestlers and saw that they were never expected to choose between becoming fathers and remaining at the top of WWE. “I wanted to show that I could have everything, you know, like the top men, they don’t have to choose whether they have a family or they’re on top of the game. And I was like, ‘Huh, well, if they don’t have to choose, why would I have to choose?’ And it was the best decision I’ve ever made.” Years later, Lynch believes that mindset has become much more common inside WWE. She pointed to the growing number of mothers in the locker room and said women now understand that having children doesn’t automatically mean walking away from their careers. For Lynch, becoming a mother wasn’t the end of her run as one of WWE’s biggest stars. She came back, won more championships and helped prove the exact point she wanted to make when she first stepped away. title: John Bradshaw Layfield named new president of Tragos/Thesz Hall of Fame
raw_title: Former WWE Champion named new president of the Tragos/Thesz Pro Wrestling Hall of Fame
body: By Jason Powell , ProWrestling.net Editor ( @prowrestlingnet ) The following press release was issued on Friday to announce the new president of the George Tragos/Lous Thesz Pro Wrestling Hall of Fame. WATERLOO, Iowa – The National Wrestling Hall of Fame Dan Gable Museum ‘s George Tragos/Lou Thesz Professional Wrestling Hall of Fame announced Wednesday that Gerry Brisco is stepping down as president of its board of directors and moving into an advisory role. John Bradshaw Layfield will replace Brisco as president, effective immediately. “I’m happy to be leaving the board in the capable hands of JBL, and I am confident that he and his support team will ensure that the Tragos/Thesz Hall of Fame continues to grow and remain the best,” said Brisco, who won multiple championships in the NWA and WWE and is a member of multiple halls of fame, including the Tragos/Thesz Hall of Fame. “I’m honored that Mr. Brisco has chosen me to help continue the incredible success he has worked so hard to achieve,” said Layfield. “The team and I look forward to growing the Tragos/Thesz Hall of Fame and moving forward in building the Global Hall of Fame brand.” Global Pro Wrestling Hall of Fame, LLC, which will work closely with the Tragos/Thesz Hall of Fame, was created to expand opportunities to serve the Hall of Fame, the Dan Gable Museum, professional wrestlers and the sport of professional wrestling. “The GPW Hall of Fame will not affect fans or the enshrinement of members of the Tragos/Thesz Hall of Fame,” said Layfield, who serves as president of the organization. “We will announce more details in the future, but we view this as a win-win situation for both the GPW Hall of Fame and the Tragos/Thesz Hall of Fame.” Powell’s POV: Briscoe did a terrific job as president, and hopefully JBL will do the same. It’s been a few years since I last attended the annual Hall of Fame weekend in Waterloo, Iowa, but I had a great time and highly recommend it.
summary: Gerry Brisco has stepped down as president of the George Tragos/Lou Thesz Professional Wrestling Hall of Fame and transitioned to an advisory role. John Bradshaw Layfield immediately assumes the presidency and expressed his commitment to building on Brisco's success while expanding the Global Hall of Fame brand. The announcement was made by the National Wrestling Hall of Fame Dan Gable Museum.

Knowing where the cameras are, knowing how much time you have, being able to change it up if the people in the audience aren’t buying it, if they don’t care about it, so there’s so much to it. It’s such a beautiful art form, so I will always love it and deeply respect it. I don’t really watch it, but occasionally I will if there’s someone that I’m still friends with or that I love. Occasionally I’ll watch a match, but I don’t know. I don’t think I am gonna get back in the ring because I don’t have this burning desire to do that.” Not everybody gets to be the Divas Champion, and you were only there for four years, but you got to be the person there. title: Former MITB Winner Says Edge’s Original Cash-In Changed WWE Forever
raw_title: Former MITB Winner Says Edge’s Original Cash-In Changed WWE Forever
body: Containing a contract that guarantees a championship match of choice at any time, any place (within a calendar year), the Money in the Bank briefcase is one of the most coveted possessions in pro wrestling. Few people admire its career-altering ability more than Nic Nemeth , known as Dolph Ziggler in WWE , who won the prized Money in the Bank briefcase in 2012. Ever the underdog, Ziggler used the briefcase to capture the World Heavyweight Championship and establish himself as a main event talent . In an exclusive interview shared with Heavy, Nemeth praised Edge for being the first Money in the Bank winner to showcase the briefcase’s game-changing power. Nemeth believes that Edge’s inaugural cash-in forever changed the WWE landscape, saying, “The first one, we didn’t know what it was. Edge comes out and he’s standing there with Vince, and he hands him the briefcase. I’m asking, is this how it works? Is this the thing? “What a great introduction and loophole for people like myself. Because that was the way some people could only ever kick in that door and make it to that real gold circle in Vince’s eyes ,” Nemeth told Casino.org . Play Nemeth also said he believes the Money in the Bank should be reserved for rising stars trying to claw their way to the top, not established megastars. “ When you’re already in the gold circle, get the hell out of here . You can show up on a Monday or Friday and go, I’m fighting for that title, and everyone goes, yay! Save that other stuff for us,” Nemeth told Casino.org . Money in the Bank has largely been a tool to fast-track midcard wrestlers into the WWE elite. Edge, CM Punk and Nemeth (formerly Dolph Ziggler) all experienced a meteoric rise after successfully cashing in the Money in the Bank briefcase. Penta, the winner of this year’s Men’s Money in the Bank Ladder match, is determined to experience a similar ascension. During the Oct. 12 episode of RAW , Penta sent a strong warning to reigning champions, and declared that he will cash in to become a World Champion . He added , “This briefcase means everything to me. Because now I have the power in my hands. So champs, watch your back. Because you don’t know when, you don’t know where, but when Penta decides to cash in, I will become a World Champion!” Penta didn’t just declare his championship goal; he did it in style. Over the years, WWE superstars have begun customizing the generic green-and-yellow MITB briefcase with designs that match their own flair and persona. Naomi had the warning tape briefcase. Edge flashed a Rated-R briefcase. Tiffany Stratton debuted a Barbie-themed briefcase. Perhaps no design is better than Penta’s “Dinero Del Banco” briefcase, which comes equipped with pyro(!). title: AEW wrestler Pac died from bronchial asthma

body: Officials have determined what killed wrestling star Benjamin Satterley . A spokesperson for the Cook County Medical Examiner’s Office told the California Post on Friday that following a probe into his sudden death , investigators concluded Satterley — who performed in AEW rings as “Pac” — passed away from bronchial asthma. The manner of his death was officially ruled natural, the rep added. Satterley was discovered unconscious in a rental car outside of a CAVA in Des Plaines, Ill. at around 4 p.m. on Sept. 27. A 911 caller stated she had found Satterley “passed out” in his ride, and authorities formally pronounced him deceased just minutes after getting to the scene. First responders wrote in an incident report that there were no injuries or “suspicious markings” on Satterley when they located his body. They did note, however, that he had saliva on the front of his shirt and medication in his vehicle. The incident report also stated that one officer on the scene was able to make contact with a woman who knew Satterley, and she told them that the wrestler had stopped for lunch before heading to the airport. Satterley’s phone had Google Maps open and a route to O’Hare Airport was on display, according to the report. Satterley had been in the area for his gig with AEW. On Sept. 26, he wrestled against Andrade at the NOW Arena in Chicago. He ended up losing in the All Out pay-per-view contest, but he later showed up in during the main event matchup between Jon Moxley and Will Ospreay.
summary: Officials ruled Benjamin Satterley, known in AEW as Pac, died of natural causes from bronchial asthma. The 37-year-old was found unconscious in a rental car outside a Des Plaines, Illinois restaurant on September 27 while heading to the airport after an AEW event. title: Mike Bailey grateful for shared wrestling passion with wife Veda Scott

body: By Jason Powell , ProWrestling.net Editor ( @prowrestlingnet ) Radican Worldwide with guest Mike Bailey Host: Sean Radican Available via PWTorch VIP “So often we are gonna be doing separate shows. I’ll be doing a Dynamite, and Veda will be doing a CMLL show, and then as soon as the show is done, we’ll get on the phone, and we will break down our shows match by match, moment by moment, and dissect every little piece of it, because we absolutely love pro wrestling. And I don’t know how our relationship would work if we didn’t share the thing that we are both the most passionate about. I am being put in these opportunities for a reason. And I mean, All Elite Wrestling is where the best wrestle, and that’s a tagline, but it’s true. There is a roster full of absolute killers. There are so many wrestlers in AEW who would be right at home winning the AEW World Championship and defending that on pay-per-view. “And I mean, I think if you look at my record, right, I have not been able to win a singles title in AEW, but I am a two-time Trios Champion, and none of those losses have been easy. I have given every champion that I have faced some of their biggest challenges. Again, as you mentioned, I took Jon Moxley very, very close to that 20-minute time limit, which is no easy feat… “And I think that at WrestleDream I will get the chance to win the AEW World Championship, and that is exactly where I want to be. That is exactly where I should be. And if, God forbid, I don’t win the championship at WrestleDream, I will keep trying. And I think that my joining United Empire was a big part of that plan.”

body: AEW star Benjamin Satterley, known to fans as "Pac," died of bronchial asthma, the California Post reported, citing a spokesperson for the Cook County Medical Examiner's Office. The manner of his death was ruled natural. Satterley was 40. Benjamin Satterley was found unresponsive in a rental car parked outside a CAVA restaurant on Mannheim Road in Des Plaines , Illinois, at around 4 p.m. local time on September 27. He was pronounced dead at the scene. His death came less than a day after he competed at AEW All Out 2026 on September 26. He challenged Andrade El Ídolo for the AEW National Championship but lost, and later appeared in the main event. AEW announced his death and paid tribute to the wrestler, remembering his career and contributions to the sport. "All Elite Wrestling is saddened to announce the passing of Benjamin Satterley, aka Pac. A native of Newcastle upon Tyne, England, Satterley began his wrestling career in 2004 and went on to perform for wrestling organizations all over the world, captivating fans with innovative high-flying moves and incredible in-ring ability. Pac signed with All Elite Wrestling in 2019 and held multiple AEW Championships and competed in some of the most memorable matches in AEW history. Our condolences go out to Satterley’s family, friends and fans," AEW said. He soon earned nicknames such as “The Super Superman” and “The Man That Gravity Forgot” for his athleticism and high-flying style. He began wrestling internationally in 2007 and performed as Adrian Neville in WWE from 2012 to 2018. After joining AEW in 2019, he became the inaugural AEW International Champion and a two-time AEW World Trios Champion. News of Satterley’s death prompted tributes from wrestlers and wrestling executives. Fellow wrestler Will Ospreay remembered him as both an exceptional performer and a close friend. “The greatest export from our country. Also the greatest human being,” Ospreay wrote on X. “Honored to have shared the ring with you so many times. You truly are such a hero to myself and many others.” AEW president Tony Khan also paid tribute to Satterley, writing, "Benjamin Satterley defined excellence, as a beloved husband & friend to his many loved ones, + in his wrestling knowledge, skill, unprecedented athleticism, professionalism, consistency + dedication to the sport that he loved & traveled the world to pursue. May Ben rest in peace." WWE chief content officer Triple H , who worked with Satterley during his time in WWE, also mourned his death.

raw_title: JOHN LAYFIELD NAMED PRESIDENT OF GEORGE TRAGOS/LOU THESZ PROFESSIONAL WRESTLING HALL OF FAME IN IOWA - PWInsider
body: Jalwa Game Goa Game Raja Game MaanWin DMFirst Veer Game JOHN LAYFIELD NAMED PRESIDENT OF GEORGE TRAGOS/LOU THESZ PROFESSIONAL WRESTLING HALL OF FAME IN IOWA By Mike Johnson on 2026-10-16 13:29:00 The following was announced: Brisco Moves Into Advisory Role, Layfield Named President of Tragos/Thesz Hall of Fame WATERLOO, Iowa - The National Wrestling Hall of Fame Dan Gable Museum's George Tragos/Lou Thesz Professional Wrestling Hall of Fame announced Wednesday that Gerry Brisco is stepping down as president of its board of directors and moving into an advisory role. John Bradshaw Layfield will replace Brisco as president, effective immediately. "I'm happy to be leaving the board in the capable hands of JBL, and I am confident that he and his support team will ensure that the Tragos/Thesz Hall of Fame continues to grow and remain the best," said Brisco, who won multiple championships in the NWA and WWE and is a member of multiple halls of fame, including the Tragos/Thesz Hall of Fame. "I'm honored that Mr. Brisco has chosen me to help continue the incredible success he has worked so hard to achieve," said Layfield. "The team and I look forward to growing the Tragos/Thesz Hall of Fame and moving forward in building the Global Hall of Fame brand." Global Pro Wrestling Hall of Fame, LLC, which will work closely with the Tragos/Thesz Hall of Fame, was created to expand opportunities to serve the Hall of Fame, the Dan Gable Museum, professional wrestlers and the sport of professional wrestling. "The GPW Hall of Fame will not affect fans or the enshrinement of members of the Tragos/Thesz Hall of Fame," said Layfield, who serves as president of the organization. "We will announce more details in the future, but we view this as a win-win situation for both the GPW Hall of Fame and the Tragos/Thesz Hall of Fame." When Tony Khan introduced the AEW WrestleDream pay-per-view, he named it after New Japan Pro-Wrestling founder Antonio Inoki, whom he dubbed “wrestling’s greatest dreamer.” Inoki passed away in October 2022. Now in its fourth year, the 2026 edition of WrestleDream will take place on Saturday, Oct. 17 at Addition Financial Arena in Orlando, Florida. title: Cop claims WWE wrestler 'grinded' on him at ringside in 'sexualised lap dance'
raw_title: Cop claims WWE wrestler 'grinded' on him at ringside in 'sexualised lap dance'
body: An off-duty sheriff’s deputy has launched a lawsuit against WWE and one of its stars. This comes after he claimed he was subjected to a “sexualised lap dance” while working security at a televised event in Chicago, Illinois, USA. Noel Lucas, a Cook County Sheriff’s officer doing private in Illinois, off-duty security work, has filed a 14-count claim against World Wrestling Entertainment (WWE), its subsidiary Event Services LLC, and wrestler Kenneth Crawford, known to fans as Montez Ford of tag team The Street Profits. The incident is alleged to have happened during Monday Night Raw at the Allstate Arena in Rosemont, Illinois, on July 6, during a show broadcast live on Netflix . According to the lawsuit, obtained by the Daily Mail, Lucas was directed by a WWE employee to take up a position near ringside and was instructed to remain at his post. But as The Street Profits made their entrance, the filing claims Ford approached Lucas “without warning or consent” and performed an explicit routine over him. “Defendant Crawford then began performing a sexually provocative dance immediately in front of and over Plaintiff [Lucas], repeatedly thrusting and gyrating his hips and pelvis towards Plaintiff, performing a sexualized [sic] ‘lap dance,’” the lawsuit reads. Lucas also reportedly alleges the wrestler moved increasingly closer during the routine, with physical contact escalating. He claims Crawford’s left inner thigh was “repeatedly” rubbing against his leg. The deputy says the moment exploded online after airing and being shared in a promotional clip. Consequently, the fallout has reportedly followed him back into daily life. When Lucas returned to his full-time job at a local courthouse the next day, he says members of the public recognised him from viral clips and mocked him. “Members of the public recognized [sic] him from the videos of the encounter that had circulated on social media and mocked him, thrusting their hips in his direction, imitating the sexual movements [allegedly performed during the broadcast],” the lawsuit states. Lucas claims the situation also hit his family. Moreover, he alleged his children were “mocked and ridiculed” at school because of the viral footage, while he has suffered “substantial humiliation, embarrassment, and emotional distress”. The suit reportedly includes claims of assault, battery, intentional infliction of emotional distress, and alleged violations of the Illinois Gender Violence Act. It also alleges a breach of the Illinois Right of Publicity Act, arguing WWE and Ford used Lucas’ clearly visible image for commercial promotion without authorisation. Lucas is seeking unspecified damages, punitive damages, legal fees, and a court order stopping WWE from continuing to use his identity. A case management hearing is set for December 10. summary_src: Indian veteran pacer Bhuvneshwar Kumar could be set for a spectacular comeback to international cricket after being drafted into the T20I squad for the last T20I against the West Indies.
body: Bhuvneshwar Kumar's comeback was confirmed recently when the selectors included him in the squad for the upcoming five-match T20I series in New Zealand. However, recent circumstances mean that he has a chance of donning the international colors earlier than expected. If Bhuvneshwar Kumar does feature in the playing XI for the fifth T20I at the M Chinnaswamy Stadium in Bengaluru, it will end a lengthy wait. His last appearance in international cricket came during the tour of New Zealand in late 2022. Bhuvneshwar Kumar played the third T20I of the series on November 22, 2022, at McLean Park in Napier. He ended with figures of 0-35 in four overs as New Zealand were bowled for 160 in the first innings. His fellow pace bowling partners, Arshdeep Singh and Mohammed Siraj, picked up four wickets each to bundle out New Zealand for 160 from 130-2. India scored 75-4 in nine overs, before rain had the final say. With the visitors managing to hit the DLS par score just in time before rain interrupted, the match was declared a tie. The veteran pacer's last international appearance on home soil was during the three-match T20I series against Australia during the build-up to the T20 World Cup 2022. On September 25, 2022, the pacer recorded figures of 1-39 in three overs in the high-scoring series finale in Hyderabad. Bhuvneshwar Kumar dismissed Cameron Green in the first innings, but was the most expensive bowler on show as Australia posted 186-7. India managed to chase down the score with a ball to spare and complete a turnaround in the series from a 0-1 deficit. 34 of Bhuvneshwar Kumar's 87 T20I appearances have come on home soil, which does not include his years of experience in the Indian Premier League (IPL). With the series on the line against West Indies, he comes across as a massive boost to the bowling unit that has largely struggled so far. The fifth T20I between India and West Indies is scheduled to be held on Saturday, October 17.

title: In Memoriam: All Elite Wrestling Star Pac’s Cause of Death Revealed After Investigation Into His Sudden Passing
raw_title: All Elite Wrestling Star Pac’s Cause of Death Revealed After Investigation Into His Sudden Passing
body: All Elite Wrestling star Benjamin Satterley ’s (a.k.a. Pac) cause of death has been revealed. A Cook County Medical Examiner’s Office spokesperson told the California Post on Friday, October 16 that after an investigation, it was determined that Benjamin died from bronchial asthma. Benjamin was pronounced dead on September 27 after his body was found behind the wheel of a rental car in a Des Plaines, Illinois, parking lot. He was 40. When authorities arrived on the scene of Benjamin’s death , they “did not find any injuries or suspicious markings on him besides what appeared to be saliva on the front of his shirt,” according to a report from the Des Plaines Police Department obtained by Us on October 5. Benjamin’s family broke their silence about his death with a statement read by AEW on-air personality Renee Paquette during an episode of Dynamite on September 30. The statement added, “Thank you to all of Ben’s fans for their support over the years. We send you our love and have been so moved to see so many people saying so many wonderful things about his impact on their lives, whether great or small. We will love you forever, Ben, and our lives will never be the same without you. Thank you, the Satterley family.” Benjamin’s widow, Natalie Satterley, later shared her devastation over the loss. “The cruelty of having all of our future hopes and dreams snatched away will never feel real,” Natalie wrote via Instagram on Monday, October 12. “You were so excited to get home to us, you were going to shoot hoops all week with your best mates, we were going to set up your new home gym and take [dog Wolfie] for some autumnal walks, have pizza at Rudy’s on your cheat day, go to the match, see [comedian] Sam Campbell live.” Continue with Google --> --> --> --> Continue with Facebook --> --> Continue with Amazon --> Continue with Apple We won't post to any of your accounts Continue with Google --> --> --> --> Continue with Facebook --> --> Continue with Amazon --> Continue with Apple We won't post to any of your accounts

title: On the Record: Brian Cage Explodes Over AEW WrestleDream Snub: “What Is Going On Here?”
raw_title: Brian Cage Explodes Over AEW WrestleDream Snub: “What Is Going On Here?”
summary_src: Brian Cage is fed up with watching AEW pay-per-views come and go without his name on the card, and WrestleDream appears to have pushed him over the edge.
body: Cage took to Twitter on October 16 and posted another video from his car, where he unloaded over being left off AEW WrestleDream despite what he believes has been some of his strongest work lately. Cage made it clear that he has heard the criticism about both his promos and his matches, and he thinks he has already answered all of it. He started by admitting he never planned on making another one of these car rants, but here he was anyway. “I told myself I wouldn’t do this again. I wouldn’t be doing this again in the car. Yet here we are.” Cage then pointed to his recent promo work and in-ring performances, saying he has already shown that he can talk and deliver when the bell rings. He also made sure to call out the people who had doubted him before those performances. According to Cage, plenty of those same fans are now changing their tune. “Earlier this week, I showed all of you. Oh, you damn right I can talk. Then I showed you all a couple days later. Well, I’ve already showed you multiple times that I can work, having match of the night.” Cage said he has no problem welcoming anyone who has recently started backing him, even if they were late to the party. “I know there’s been a lot of followers, a lot of believers, a lot of people backing Cage. A lot of people part of the Cage brigade. And I’ll tell you what. I welcome everyone there with open arms. Better late than never.” “Every time I go out there, you damn right I own the spotlight. Have the match of the night. I get all of my stuff in. The athletic anomaly, the physical phenomenon. You just saw it all in person. You saw it there live on TV. And who’s there this weekend at WrestleDream? That’s right, not me.” He then took the WrestleDream name and turned it into a shot at the fact that he is sitting this one out. title: Legal Watch: Montez Ford, WWE Sued Over Alleged Unwanted Contact
raw_title: Montez Ford, WWE Sued Over Alleged Unwanted Contact
body: Posted in: Sports , TV , WWE | Tagged: montez ford , wrestling , WWE Raw Report: A Cook County Sheriff's officer has filed a lawsuit against Montez Ford and the WWE over an alleged incident during WWE Raw. A Cook County Sheriff's officer has reportedly filed a civil lawsuit against World Wrestling Entertainment (WWE), performer Montez Ford , and a company subsidiary. The suit stems from an interaction at the July 6, 2026 episode of Monday Night Raw at Allstate Arena in Rosemont, Illinois. The complaint was reportedly filed Wednesday, October 14, 2026, in the Circuit Court of Cook County, according to POST Wrestling's report on the complaint . The alleged incident took place during the entrance of The Street Profits at the live Netflix broadcast of Raw . The officer alleges that a WWE employee directed him to his ringside position, that he was never told he would be part of the performance, and that he did not consent to the contact he describes. "Defendant Crawford then began performing a sexually provocative dance immediately in front of and over Plaintiff, repeatedly thrusting and gyrating his hips and pelvis towards Plaintiff, performing a sexualized 'lap dance.'" POST Wrestling's account of the filing adds that Ford allegedly "moved his body increasingly closer to" and that his "left inner thigh repeatedly rubbed against Plaintiff's leg." These passages represent the plaintiff's version of events as presented in the court filing. Neither outlet reports a response from the defendants disputing or confirming the reports, and the incident no longer appears in the version of the show streaming on Netflix at this time, nor can it be found in the company's social media posts from the event. The complaint reportedly contains 14 counts. POST Wrestling lists assault, battery, and intentional infliction of emotional distress among them, along with claims under the Illinois Gender Violence Act and the Illinois Right of Publicity Act. The publicity claim relates to the footage itself. FOX 32 Chicago reports that the complaint alleges WWE shared video of the interaction on TikTok and Instagram, and that Ford also shared footage on his own social media. POST Wrestling reports that the officer alleges the clip's circulation led to public ridicule and emotional distress. As for remedies, POST Wrestling reports that the officer seeks unspecified monetary damages, punitive damages, and court costs. He also seeks an order barring further use of his identity. A case-management hearing is reportedly set for December 10, 2026. FOX 32 Chicago quotes Lucas's attorney, Whitney Barr , as saying, "[The Plaintiff] was there to do his job, not to be made a part of WWE's entertainment." Barr also stated, per the same outlet, that "Entertainment is not a defense to unwanted sexual contact." As the matter proceeds toward its scheduled December 10 case-management hearing, any formal answer from the defendants or any change to the docket would clarify the competing positions.
summary: Posted in: Sports , TV , WWE | Tagged: montez ford , wrestling , WWE Raw Report: A Cook County Sheriff's officer has filed a lawsuit against Montez Ford and. A Cook County Sheriff's officer has by most accounts filed a civil lawsuit against World Wrestling Entertainment, performer Montez Ford , and a company subsidiary.

title: WWE strikes intriguing content partnership as pro wrestling's popularity continues to soar
raw_title: WWE strikes intriguing content partnership as pro wrestling's popularity continues to soar
body: WWE announced a strategic content partnership with Bleacher Report on Monday. Bleacher Report will have the global rights to highlights across WWE’s programming, including "Monday Night Raw," "Friday Night SmackDown," NXT and premium live events, the company said in a news release. Bleacher Report will also have a presence at certain WWE premium live events. "Bleacher Report has long been at the intersection of sports and culture," WWE executive vice president Alex Varga said in a statement. "Our partnership with B/R reinforces WWE’s commitment to bringing our content to a global audience." Bleacher Report general manager Bennett Spector added, "WWE fans don’t just watch. They are highly engaged, analyze every detail and debate the sport all week long. That’s exactly the kind of passionate fandom B/R and House of Highlights were built for. "This partnership gives us the opportunity to bring fans closer to the biggest moments happening today while also tapping into the incredible history and personalities that have made WWE part of sports culture for generations." On the surface, the partnership appeared to be just another way for WWE to further its global reach across social media. WWE boasts more than 102 million followers on Facebook, 40.1 million followers on TikTok, 35 million followers on Instagram and 13 million followers on X. But the deal comes days after Paramount reached a settlement with states that sued to block the Warner Bros. Discovery takeover. Warner Bros. Discovery announced in June 2025 it planned to keep TNT Sports and Bleacher Report under Global Networks, separating it form its TV and film endeavors. Sportico reported in December that was still the plan for the end of 2026. Bleacher Report previously hosted AEW pay-per-views on its streaming platform before discontinuing it in 2024. Khan has repeatedly welcomed the merger and reiterated his happiness after All Out over the weekend. "Now, we enter something that I consider more of a known quantity and I’m very excited about it. I think we’ve proven that AEW is a feather in the cap of a media company that we are a great partner, and for me, I’ll work to make sure that AEW fits in any corporate structure. I’ll work very hard, and I think I’ve proven time after time that I am the ultimate corporate soldier, and that is why AEW continues to grow and expand as the media landscape changes and I think that’s why Warner Bros., even as the company has evolved and changed, AEW has always been a very important part of the portfolio for years and years and I expect that’s gonna continue with AEW and Warner Bros. for many years to come."

title: In Memoriam: Cause of death revealed for All Elite Wrestling star Pac
raw_title: Cause of death revealed for All Elite Wrestling star Pac
body: 0 Benjamin Satterley, known as Pac, died of natural causes, the Cook County (Illinois) Medical Examiner’s Office ruled. A cause of death has been determined in the death of wrestler Benjamin Satterley , also known as Pac in All Elite Wrestling. Satterly died of bronchial asthma, according to the Cook County (Illinois) Medical Examiner’s Office. The death was ruled natural. The 40-year-old wrestler died on Sunday, Sept. 27 after he was found inside a vehicle at a Cava parking lot in the city of Des Plaines, Illinois, just outside of Chicago O’Hare International Airport. According to a police report , Pac was found "unconscious and unresponsive, slumped over, in a vehicle." Responding authorities attempted life saving measures, but hewas later pronounced dead at the scene. Officials noted they "did not find any injuries or suspicious markings on him besides what appeared to be saliva on the front of his shirt." An autopsy was perfomed the following day. Pac became a prominent wrestler after joining WWE in 2012 as Neville, becoming one of the best Cruiserweight stars with the company until he departed in 2017. He then joined upstart All Elite Wrestling in January 2019, where he worked for the remainder of his career. He held multiple AEW Championships while being part of major factions like the Death Triangle and Death Riders. AEW held a tribute show in honor of Pac on Wednesday, Sept. 30.

title: Austin Creed Hints at New UpUpDownDown Successor in AEW Era
raw_title: Austin Creed Hints at New UpUpDownDown Successor in AEW Era
body: Speaking with Phid McAwesome at PAX Australia , Creed discussed leaving the gaming channel behind and hinted at the possibility of working with his former Da Party teammates again. Creed spent years building UpUpDownDown into a popular channel for wrestling fans. It gave them a chance to see their favorite WWE superstars outside the ring. The channel featured wrestlers playing video games, taking part in challenges, and showing their personalities away from their regular TV appearances. However, Creed’s departure from WWE in May meant he had to leave the project behind. Despite losing access to the channel, the AEW star seems confident that he can create something new. When asked about how it felt leaving UpUpDownDown, Creed said, One big question is whether Creed could reunite with Da Party for another gaming project. The group includes Creed, Tyler Breeze, Adam Cole, and Claudio Castagnoli. All four share a love for video games, and their chemistry made their gaming sessions popular with wrestling fans. Cole, Castagnoli, and Creed are now signed to AEW, while Breeze is a free agent. Since none of the four are currently under WWE contract, working together on a new project may be easier than it was when they were part of WWE. Creed addressed the possibility but also admitted he wouldn’t confirm any plans. “None of the Da Party members are currently signed with WWE. And that would lead me to believe that there is at least the chance that something will happen. The chance of something to be created is available. I will not confirm or deny if anyone has been filming anything or if anyone has been creating assets for a new YouTube channel. I will not confirm or deny that,” Creed said. Creed then explained that his friendships with WWE Superstars helped make UpUpDownDown successful. He wants to build similar connections with the AEW locker room before starting a similar project. “I would hope that maybe there would be a chance to do something with video games, I don’t know. I cannot say. But that rapport with the locker room is first and foremost the most important thing,” Creed said. body: Benjamin Satterley, an English-born wrestler known for high-flying moves that delighted fans worldwide, has died. He was 40. WLS CHICAGO (WLS) -- Benjamin Satterley, the professional wrestler known to fans as "Pac," died Sunday, less than 24 hours after competing at an All Elite Wrestling event in Hoffman Estates, a northern suburb of Chicago, according to the Cook County Medical Examiner. Satterley, 40, wrestled Saturday night at NOW Arena before his death was reported Sunday in nearby Des Plaines. The medical examiner has not yet determined a cause of death and said it may be several weeks before autopsy results are available. The news shocked fans who watched the English-born wrestler perform the night before, including Jayson Weidman, who attended the event. Inside NOW Arena on Saturday, Satterley competed for All Elite Wrestling under the ring name Pac. The English wrestler, who previously performed in WWE as Adrian Neville, was known for high-flying moves that delighted fans worldwide. "There are wrestlers that can do incredible things, and then there's wrestlers who can do things that you question how it's even humanly possible that they can do what they're doing. Pac was one of those wrestlers," Weidman said. Satterley, who was from Newcastle upon Tyne, began his wrestling career in 2004 and signed in 2019 with All Elite Wrestling, where he held multiple championships. He competed and lost to Andrade El Ídolo on Saturday in Chicago in the AEW National Championship. Weidman said he purchased his seat specifically in hopes of being close to Pac and his group, the Death Riders. "It was such a special moment for me to be able to see him wrestle," Weidman said. After signing with AEW, he became the inaugural AEW International Champion and a two-time AEW World Trios Champion. According to Weidman, Pac wrestled in Saturday's opening match and later returned during the main event. "He looked healthy as can be, and it's unbelievable how less than 24 hours, he could possibly be gone," Weidman said. title: In Memoriam: AEW star Pac's death leaves pro wrestling world in disbelief
raw_title: AEW star Pac's death leaves pro wrestling world in disbelief
body: The death of pro wrestling star Pac left the pro wrestling world in utter disbelief on Sunday night. All Elite Wrestling (AEW) announced Pac’s death just one day after he wrestled against Andrade El Idolo for the national championship at All Out in Hoffman Estates, Illinois. He was 40. Many pro wrestlers posted heartfelt tributes to Pac, whose real name is Benjamin Satterley, on social media with many in shock because most had just seen him wrestle on the pay-per-view. Pac was one of the first wrestlers to sign with All Elite Wrestling in 2019. He was a two-time trios champion and the inaugural all-Atlantic champion. He was a member of The Death Riders faction who supported their leader, Jon Moxley. He also competed for WWE before joining AEW under the name Adrian Neville. He was a two-time cruiserweight champion, an NXT champion and two-time NXT tag team champion. Pac got his start on the independent circuit in 2004 and quickly became a fixture at Pro Wrestling Guerrilla. He also performed at Dragon Gate USA, Wrestle Zone Wrestling, One Pro Wrestling, Frontier Wrestling Alliance and elsewhere. Pro Wrestling Illustrated named him the 11th best wrestler in the world in 2017.

title: Benjamin Satterley, globetrotting wrestler known as Pac, dies at 40
raw_title: Benjamin Satterley, globetrotting wrestler known as Pac, dies at 40
body: Share Add NBC News to Google Sept. 27, 2026, 10:22 PM EDT / Updated Sept. 29, 2026, 8:31 PM EDT By Rudy Chinchilla Benjamin Satterley, the hard-hitting and high-flying professional wrestler known to fans worldwide simply as Pac, has died, All Elite Wrestling announced Sunday night. He was 40. News of his death came the day after he’d wrestled during AEW’s “All Out” pay-per-view Saturday night at the NOW Arena in Hoffman Estates, Illinois, outside Chicago. A cause of death was not immediately provided. In a statement Tuesday, the Cook County Medical Examiner’s Office said Satterley was found in Des Plaines, around 2 miles north of the Chicago O’Hare International Airport. An autopsy was performed Monday, it said, and a cause and manner of death will be determined after additional testing, which could take several weeks. Des Plaines police said in a statement Monday that there were no immediate indications of foul play and that the circumstances surrounding Satterley’s death were not considered suspicious. In announcing his death, AEW highlighted Satterley’s “incredible in-ring ability.” “A native of Newcastle upon Tyne, England, Satterley began his wrestling career in 2004 and went on to perform for wrestling organizations all over the world, captivating fans with innovative high-flying moves and incredible in-ring ability,” it said. Satterley first began training at 18 and made a name for himself on the British independent scene before embarking on a globetrotting career in which he performed in some of the biggest promotions on the planet, including AEW, World Wrestling Entertainment (where he went by Adrian Neville), New Japan Pro-Wrestling and Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre. His high-flying offense, made all the more impressive by the brawny physique on his stocky frame, earned him the nickname “The Man That Gravity Forgot.” When he started training and had to choose a name, Satterley couldn’t think of anything else. “It was only meant to be kind of a temporary thing, but then it kind of — it’s one of those names that kind of, it just stuck,” he said. Satterley debuted on All Elite Wrestling in 2019, where he’d eventually earn the moniker “The Bastard.” In AEW, he won the All-Atlantic Championship in 2022 and became one of the company’s more prominent wrestlers as part of the Death Riders faction, with whom he’d earn the AEW World Trios Championship alongside fellow members Claudio Castagnoli and Wheeler Yuta in 2025. It followed another Trios title in 2022 alongside Penta El Zero Miedo and Rey Fénix as part of the “Death Triangle.” Between the ropes, few wrestlers could combine speed, agility, technique and raw power quite like Satterley. He could twist and wind his body off the top turnbuckle with his signature “Black Arrow,” or he could use his “Brutalizer” to tie up an opponent’s arms and neck on the canvas. On the microphone, his promos conveyed no-nonsense intensity that relayed an ultimately simple message to opponents: I’m here to hurt

Leon Slater interrupted the celebration. He confirmed that he had exercised Option C earlier in the day to challenge Nic Nemeth for the TNA World Championship at Bound for Glory and expressed confidence in becoming the youngest world champion.
