body: Max Caster debuted for TNA at Bound For Glory 2026. Max Caster was released by TNA the day after Bound For Glory 2026. Keeping his Acclaimed rapper gimmick going, Caster entered for his loss to Moose verbally cutting down the TNA lifer with his usual topical shtick, going as far as to reference "bombs" and "Riyadh" during a weekend in which Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport experienced missile attacks. It got everybody's attention, drew the requisite oohs and ahhs in the building, and Caster got in the ring and had the match. All was well...ish, until TNA had their take on it the next day. They went one further and let him go, just 24 hours on from him walking down the aisle for the first time. The Acclaimed were at one point arguably the most over act in the industry , but any sort of rebirth for the team might now have to go on hold until this newest strain of heat dies down.

title: Cody Rhodes edges toward darker instincts on SmackDown
raw_title: WWE SmackDown recap & reactions (Oct. 16, 2026): Cody Rhodes turns to the Dark Side
summary_src: SmackDown promised a face-to-face between Cody Rhodes and Randy Orton as the night’s key event, and we nearly got swerved by Baron Freakin’ Corbin. Fortunately, the show ended with a satisfactory conclusion that introduced a whole new direction.
body: Link WWE WWE SmackDown promised a face-to-face between Cody Rhodes and Randy Orton as the night’s key event, and we nearly got swerved by Baron Freakin’ Corbin. Fortunately, the show ended with a satisfactory conclusion that introduced a whole new direction. The first image we saw of Rhodes was The American Nightmare entering the arena in Sacramento while wearing eyeglasses, so you know he was in a serious mood. While he looked pensive, he must’ve been happy later in the show after spotting a few people in the crowd wearing Street Fighter merchandise in the form of plastic wigs to look like his character Guile’s exaggerated flattop. Since Rhodes was in workout clothes instead of a robber baron suit, viewers were understandably expecting a fight with Orton. What we got instead was Baron Corbin. Rhodes managed to avoid a Punt from Orton, and he seemed on the way to dishing out the move himself before Baron resurfaced to end the fun. Orton retreated to the aisle, but at least we got to see Rhodes Punt Baron. The crowd chanted “one more time,” as Orton looked perturbed and retreated to the back. While it still didn’t feel like a complete sea change, Cody moved closer tonight to embracing some buried, darker instincts. I wouldn’t expect an actual heel turn yet, but this edge could certainly inject a new energy in this feud. Before delving deeper into the show, I recommend checking out a full rundown of all the action on SmackDown from the always-excellent Claire Elizabeth’s live blog . Before we got the Cody and Randy Show, Sami Zayn kicked off the night with Johnny Gargano and Candice LeRae to remind us he’s The Last Real Good Guy. He was quickly interrupted by Trick Williams, and the audience really wanted to see these two go at it, but we got Gargano cutting off the tense standoff. Of course, WWE is not going to give away Trick versus Sami on a SmackDown, so Johnny Wrestling will instead get whooped. Williams (mostly) landed a Trick Shot knee on a slingshotting Gargano but oddly opted to execute a manhandle slam before pinning his opponent clean. The ending was exactly what should have happened, but I found myself slightly relieved given WWE’s pension for having messy interferences leading to non-finishes. Zayn getting back-up from Gargano/LaRae still feels a little random, but I feel like it works, mostly because the trio are veterans/pros. And getting Trick on the card is always a bonus…so,pretty decent opener. Considering how half-hearted WWE has dealt with this rivalry, I was somewhat surprised Paige and Bella faced off tonight after Nikki cheated to beat the English star last month. I kind of assumed the feud was being sidelined until Brie returns from her injury, but maybe WWE wanted Nikki to clear her plate to challenge Chelsea Green for the Women’s Championship (more on that later). title: Results Recap: AEW WrestleDream 2026 preview and predictions: 5 big questions as Will Ospreay braces for Clockwork Carnage
raw_title: AEW WrestleDream 2026 preview and predictions: 5 big questions as Will Ospreay braces for Clockwork Carnage
body: AEW's third pay-per-view in as many months is littered with title matches, including a brand-new concept called Clockwork Carnage, in which Will Ospreay will defend his AEW World Championship against seven other men. The Uncrowned Horsemen — Kel Dansby, Robert Jackman, Drake Riggs and Anthony Sulla-Heffinger — are here to preview WrestleDream, answer key questions and make their picks for the show. Let's ride! Dansby: I've tried reading the rules for Clockwork Carnage several times, but somehow I get more confused every time I go over them. I'm all for creativity and introducing new match concepts, but I genuinely don't know how AEW is going to pull this off in a way that makes sense to the audience. Sometimes the best gimmick matches are the simplest ones. Give fans a concept they can easily understand and let the wrestlers do the rest. I enjoy almost everything AEW puts together on pay-per-view, and I'm sure the talent involved will find a way to make this entertaining. That said, there's a difference between producing one memorable match and creating a stipulation fans want to see year after year. I'm not convinced Clockwork Carnage has what it takes to become a staple of the company moving forward. "A Clockwork Orange" homage aside, I think it's an interesting concept, but I am skeptical to see how it plays out with eight wrestlers in the fray at once — assuming there are no eliminations before the scoring period begins. I think it will be a bit difficult to keep track of as a fan, either in the arena or watching at home. Logistics aside, there is the possibility for high drama, as you can tease Ospreay needing to come back to win or surviving with a pinfall or submission that comes right as time expires. There are plenty of compelling narrative angles to take. Ultimately, I am always a fan of innovation in wrestling — it's how we've gotten some matches that have now become iconic. I'm sure this will stick around in some fashion, perhaps with a cap of four to six wrestlers. Riggs: Whether AEW sticks with Clockwork Carnage long-term depends entirely on how cohesive the match is. In a way, AEW is at its best when finding beauty in chaos, rather than highly restrictive rulesets like this match appears to be. But that's what makes it all the more interesting. It could be one big cluster or a smashing success, like NXT's Iron Survivor Challenge. Realistically, the Iron Survivor concept should be used in a WWE main-roster situation too, so if AEW pulls off anything remotely similar, it'd be nice to see it at least once a year. It's one of those rare match types that fits the calendar well, like Elimination Chamber or Royal Rumble, and doesn't feel forced for the sake of a gimmick show, like Blood & Guts and WarGames. This match kind of served as a preview for that, as well as an opportunity for Matsumoto to press his case for going on excursion soon. Goto and Shingo did what they always do. I don’t remember seeing them against each other very often but they both have a very high floor on their match quality. Matsumoto would have done no harm to his case with this performance, but it would not be accurate to say he stood out. He did hit a rarely-seen waterwheel suplex on Shingo but it was not clean. There didn’t seem to be much to this match beyond reigniting the Sanada-Just Five Guys feud. And filling a slot on the card I suppose. Early offence for HoT focused on Desperado’s knee. Desperado made the tag, and attempted HoT Shenanigans (TM) backfired when Taichi superkicked a pimp-cane-wielding Takahashi. One Black Mephisto later we had our (largely predictable and inconsequential) result. WINNERS: Taichi, Uemura, and Desperado via pinfall at 8:21 (*½). They are the stars of All Elite Wrestling (AEW), and they are invading Central Florida this weekend. For the first time ever, AEW is bringing its monumental WrestleDream pay-per-view event to the Sunshine State. The high-octane action takes over UCF’s Addition Financial Arena tomorrow, Saturday, October 17th. Sitting at the absolute peak of the mountain is the reigning, defending AEW World Champion, Will Ospreay. The charismatic 33-year-old Englishman has taken the wrestling world by storm, and tomorrow night, he puts his coveted title on the line in a brutal, one-of-a-kind “Clockwork Carnage” match against seven other world-class competitors. For tickets, go to AEWTix.com. llm_long: During a GCW event, promoter Brett Lauderdale appeared ready to strip Joseph Sawyer of the GCW World Championship. Sawyer then appeared via video screen to respond directly to the situation.

Sawyer acknowledged that some of the criticism directed at him had elements of truth but dismissed much of it as nonsense. He explained that after suffering an injury he was booed by fans and faced online attacks, which left him unwilling to return to GCW.

Sawyer stated he had already paid his dues in the promotion and had no interest in dealing with the ungrateful fanbase or stepping into the locker room. He accused Atticus Cogar of wasting time in GCW while seeking cheap reactions from the crowd.

Despite holding the title, Sawyer declared that he had GCW in a vulnerable position but was not going to avoid a fight. He agreed to defend the GCW World Title against Cogar on November 7 in a no-rules match.
Sawyer added that if he defeats Cogar, he will take the championship with him and depart.

Creed went on to add that he and Kofi are revitalized in AEW. “It’s been awesome,” Creed said about the transition. “It’s been awesome. I’ve known Swerve (Strickland) for a long time, and so to see where he was and what he’s turned into has been amazing to see.” Creed added, “Seeing how much him and Hangman (Adam Page) hate each other… and every time that they’re on screen together, the crowd knows that it’s about to go down. So it’s really cool, like I said, knowing him from the past and seeing him now is really great. For me and Kof, we’re just revitalized. AEW is a place where everybody there just wants to have the best show possible. The fans that come to the show are there to see wrestling. It’s not just a random night out for them. They come because they wanna cheer, they wanna boo, they wanna chant, they wanna clap, and that energy is infectious, and as a performer, if you’re putting everything you have into your performance and you’re getting that energy back from the crowd, it allows you to go to another level.” Creed continued, “So it’s been really refreshing to feel that again because it’s something that for me, I felt, you know, when I was on the independents, and I was sleeping in my car and I’m just trying to work shows and I’m going everywhere that’ll have me to do a match. That type of hustle and grind, it fuels you creatively. You have a certain fulfillment that you get from it and that’s kind of what AEW has felt like to me. It feels that everybody is just grinding to get better. I’m gonna get better and you’re gonna get better and the show’s gonna get better. So it’s really cool to be part of that.” The New Level is getting into singles action in All Elite Wrestling as well. Kofi challenged Bandido for the ROH World Championship at Dynamite: Grand Slam France.

It also kind of came out of nowhere, and there wasn't any build heading into the closing moments of this. body: Jalwa Game Goa Game Raja Game MaanWin DMFirst Veer Game MOVING WRESTLEMANIA, ORTON GETTING NUMBER 15, PAY RAISES AND MORE By Dave Scherer on 2026-09-29 10:00:00 You can send us questions for the PWInsider.com Q and A at pwinsider@gmail.com . The public reason for TKO asking multiple WWE talents taking a pay cut was due to the elimination of house shows, which means most talents only appearing on their weekly TV and likely wrestling only once or twice per month. Since TKO has decided to bring a few domestic House Show tours back per month, have you heard anything about them going back to these talents with improved deals or excluding them from the house show tours? Or like most businesses in the modern market, are they expecting their "independent contractors" to do more work for less money? I don’t see any world where TKO goes back to the talents with improved deals. Their modus operandi is usually the opposite of that. A Dude Wipes fan? Beats me because I am not one. With that said, the shirts worn on TV are part of the show. You can buy a Dom shirt that doesn’t also have an ad proclaiming love for a product that cleans the old hole. Do you think they are going to prolong Randy winning 15 till WM43 since he is so loved there, or will he win it before? And if he does win it prior, who do you think he would Main Event and defend against at Night 1? Cody or Punk? Man, that is way too far in the future for me to guess at. I think he will get number 15 at some point, and he should. When that will be, I have no idea but if I was booking I would let it simmer for a while. What the point of the stupid spot that injured Steve Borden besides trying to recreate the Ricochet-Logan Paul spot from a few years ago? With the situation in the Middle East being very fluid and the possibility of some scheduled PLEs like Wrestlemania taking place there having to be moved, does WWE/TKO have a window that they would use to activate plan B, C or D ? Say, 60-90-120 days prior? Whenever I have asked I have been told that they are closely monitoring the situation there and they have back up plans in place. Now, are they GOOD plans? Probably not because it’s hard to fill a football stadium for two nights on short notice. But, that’s the world that we live in now. WWE has announced several matches for the next two episodes of SmackDown. Giulia and Blake Monroe will look to settle their differences, while Nikki Bella will face Chelsea Green for the first time one-on-one. The October 16 episode of SmackDown featured several developments that shaped the upcoming shows. The biggest match announced for the October 23 episode will see Giulia take on Blake Monroe in a Street Fight. SmackDown GM Nick Aldis made the match official after Monroe approached him and demanded action over her ongoing issues with Giulia. The two women have been feuding for months, with Monroe repeatedly targeting Giulia before making her SmackDown debut three weeks ago. Their first official match ended with Monroe getting the win after sending Giulia into the ring post and knocking her out. Giulia will now have a chance to get revenge. The Street Fight rules will also allow both women to use weapons and take their fight beyond the usual limits of a regular match. The October 23 episode will also see Alexa Bliss and Tatum Paxley defend their WWE Women’s Tag Team Championship against Michin and B-Fab after the heated confrontation on this week’s SmackDown. This will be Bliss and Paxley’s first title defense since they defeated Fatal Influence to win the championships. Meanwhile, WWE Tag Team Champions MFT, represented by Tama Tonga and Talla Tonga, will face Bakusai’s Shinsuke Nakamura and Kyoki in a non-title match. WWE Women’s Tag Team Championship: Alexa Bliss and Tatum Paxley (c) vs. Michin and B-Fab Non-title tag team match: MFT (Tama Tonga and Talla Tonga) vs. Bakusai (Shinsuke Nakamura and Kyoki) The October 16 episode also confirmed a match for October 30’s SmackDown. This week, Chelsea Green approached Nick Aldis to discuss Tiffany Stratton’s Money in the Bank victory, but Nikki Bella interrupted their conversation. Bella took another shot at Green and made it clear that she wanted to become the next WWE Women’s Champion. After their latest confrontation, Aldis agreed to book a title match between the two women for October 30 at the Charleston Coliseum in Charleston, West Virginia. title: In Memoriam:
raw_title: Exclusive | AEW star Pac discovered slumped over in vehicle outside CAVA restaurant before death
body: All Elite Wrestling star Benjamin Satterley , who performed in the ring under the stage name Pac, was found “passed out” in a vehicle in a CAVA parking lot just before he was pronounced dead in Illinois on Sunday, the California Post can exclusively report. Medics raced to Satterley at the Mediterranean-themed restaurant in Des Plaines at around 4 p.m., according to dispatch audio obtained by The Post on Monday. “This is going to be a slumper,” authorities said in the audio. “We can’t confirm breathing at this time.” “This is going to be a slumper in a car. We cannot confirm breathing yet. At this point, we’re still on the phone getting further,” they later added. An official could be heard in the audio a short time later appearing to relay that Satterley was discovered dead when they arrived. Some of the restaurant’s customers had seen Satterley “passed out” in his vehicle and called for 911, a witness told The Post. The patrons looked for any sort of medical equipment inside the CAVA to try to help the wrestler before emergency personnel arrived. “There was an ambulance, police and a fire truck, all outside,” the witness said. A spokesperson for the Cook County Medical Examiner’s office told The Post on Monday Satterley was pronounced dead at 4:08 p.m. and a rep for the Des Plaines Police Department stated there are currently “no indications of foul play and the circumstances surrounding the death are not considered suspicious.” A cause of death is pending “additional testing” following an initial autopsy, the Cook County Medical Examiner’s office spokesperson added. Satterley had been in Illinois for an AEW match against Andrade, which occurred on Saturday night at the NOW Arena in Chicago. He lost the All Out pay-per-view contest, but later showed up in the ring during the main event matchup between Jon Moxley and Will Ospreay. AEW announced Satterley’s passing in an emotional post on X Sunday evening. “A native of Newcastle upon Tyne, England, Satterley began his wrestling career in 2004 and went on to perform for wrestling organizations all over the world, captivating fans with innovative high-flying moves and incredible in-ring ability,” the wrestling promotion said. “Pac signed with All Elite Wrestling in 2019 and held multiple AEW Championships and competed in some of the most memorable matches in AEW history. “Our condolences go out to Satterley’s family, friends and fans.”

body: Impact Zone! It’s Thursday Night, which means are in for a brand-new edition of the delight known as Impact! Taking place from the Dothan Civic Center in Dothan, Alabama, tonight Matt and Jeff Hardy are going to have creative control over the show in honor of their 35th anniversary in the wrestling business. From the backyards of wrestling to OMEGA to superstardom in WWE, TNA, and ROH, the Hardy’s have done it all, except run the show. And that changes tonight. The Hardys are going to focus on getting their recent rivals to go against one another. In that vein, there will be a Tables Match between syX and the Righteous, while Ryan and Nic Nemeth will face one another. llm_long: The Nemeths faced off in a tag team match but showed little interest in competing against each other. They started slowly with minimal action until a gentle kick sent one competitor down. The referee appeared unimpressed as a cover attempt followed.

The Hardys then appeared on the stage and sat down, insisting the competitors fight or risk being stripped of their titles. The Nemeths traded rollups using tights for near falls. The Hardys continued to pressure them to engage more seriously.

One Nemeth delivered a superkick and shouted at the Hardys, who encouraged him to repeat the move. A Fameasser then ended the bout in five minutes. The segment focused on the Hardys exerting control over the Nemeths rather than a competitive match.

After the match, one Nemeth complained about his exclusion from the number one contenders match. The Hardys encountered AJ Francis and the Expressions, leading to a challenge for a tag team match later that night. The Expressions reacted strongly to the proposal.

The Hardys also crossed paths with Frankie Kazarian and Avery Styles, who sought a tag team title opportunity. Matt Hardy agreed to a future title shot without requiring the trophy to be cashed in once the Hardys regain the championships. Closeups showed Allie and a smiling Rosemary.

In the main tag match, Jeff Hardy avoided a charge from Francis and targeted the arm, with Matt doing the same. A double suplex took Francis down before the Expressions provided a distraction. The Hardys used moves including a Tree of Woe and multiple Twist of Fates before a Swanton Bomb secured the victory in just over five minutes.

title: WWE hosts tryouts for local athletes
raw_title: WWE hosts tryouts for local athletes
body: 0 HONOLULU (KHON2) -- WWE is in Hawaii for the first time in years, and ahead of Friday's live event, it began the search for some local talent. "We're out here doing a WWE tryout, trying to find the next big WWE Superstar," said Raquel Rodriguez, WWE Women's Intercontinental Champion. "I think the best thing about doing this out in Hawaii is that we're getting a really big mix of cultures, which is really beautiful to see." Download the free KHON2 app for iOS or Android to stay informed on the latest news Athletes were given the chance to do promos, hear feedback from current superstars, and even do some in-ring workouts. "Like anything else, we want whatever we try and do, whether it's football, NFL, all professional aspects, you want people from here," said Makoa Chapa, a try-out participant from Kailua-Kona, a native and strongman competitor. "You want people from Hawaii to be inspired by it, sometimes it takes somebody to just set the tone, like so if one of us makes it or a bunch of us make it." Unfortunately, try-outs are not open to the general public, but the WWE said getting the chance to connect with the local talent in Hawaii, a place they aren't often at, is very special. "Getting to see these athletes come out here and showcase what they do and their cultures, and getting to get a little taste of that, it makes me hungrier for more," said Rodriguez. "I just want to explore more of Hawaii, I want to know more about these athletes, and I think they're doing a great job representing their culture." Ahead of Friday's event, the City declared Oct. 16 as WWE Day, making it official with WWE Superstar and Hall of Famer Rey Mysterio. "(Fans) are about to enjoy two of the greatest nights in the history of WWE, not only because of our performance, but because today is a very special day. Today is WWE day here," said Mysterio.
summary: 0 HONOLULU -- WWE is in Hawaii for the first time in years, and ahead of Friday's live event, it began the search for some local talent. We're out here doing a WWE tryout, trying to find the next big WWE Superstar, explained Raquel Rodriguez, WWE Women's Intercontinental Champion.

title: WWE stars Roman Reigns and Cody Rhodes lead a roster built from the ring — Street Fighter cast

body: The wrestling contingent sits at the top of the villain chart. WWE star Roman Reigns plays Akuma, one of the series’ most powerful villains and a frequent final boss, while Cody Rhodes takes Guile, the Air Force pilot with the flat-top, in what Variety calls his largest film role to date. Alexander Volkanovski, a two-time UFC champion, turns up as Joe, a background fighter from the very first game. Japanese pro wrestler Hirooki Goto makes his American feature debut as the sumo E. Honda, and towering bodybuilder Olivier Richters, already seen in Reacher and Black Widow, plays the Soviet grappler Zangief. The actors carry the story around them. Andrew Koji, the martial artist who played Storm Shadow in Snake Eyes, is Ryu, and Noah Centineo is Ken, here a loudmouth, washed-up celebrity trying to claw his way back after his childhood training partner became world champion. Callina Liang, of Presence and Bad Genius, bulked up to play Chun-Li. David Dastmalchian is M. Bison, and Mel Jarnson, who played Nitara in Mortal Kombat, is his agent Cammy. The rest of the casting leans toward celebrity and comedy. Jason Momoa plays the electric green brawler Blanka, and Curtis “50 Cent” Jackson is the boxer Balrog. Country singer Orville Peck makes his film debut behind Vega’s mask, a role that suits a performer who almost never appears without one. Comedians Andrew Schulz and Eric Andre play the hapless Dan Hibiki and the announcer Don Sauvage. Indian actor and martial artist Vidyut Jammwal makes his American feature debut as Dhalsim, Rayna Vallandingham of Cobra Kai plays Juli, and Don Lee voices the mentor Gouken. That register matches the director. Kitao Sakurai comes from Beef, Dave and The Eric Andre Show, and he took over a project that previously had Danny and Michael Philippou, the brothers behind Talk to Me and Bring Her Back, attached. In 1994, Guile’s flat-top belonged to a martial-arts movie star. In 2026, it sits on a WWE star, and the game’s most powerful villain is played by another. body: Share Add NBC News to Google Oct. 17, 2026, 12:00 AM EDT / Updated Oct. 17, 2026, 12:01 AM EDT By Rudy Chinchilla Benjamin Satterley, known to wrestling fans around the world as Pac, died last month of bronchial asthma , the medical examiner’s office in Cook County, Illinois, confirmed Friday. Satterley, 40, died Sept. 27, just one day after having wrestled on All Elite Wrestling’s “All Out” pay-per-view. His death sent waves of shock and grief across the world of professional wrestling. He was found in Des Plaines, around 2 miles north of the Chicago O’Hare International Airport, the medical examiner’s office said at the time. He went on to earn global acclaim, wrestling for some of the top promotions in the world, including AEW, World Wrestling Entertainment (where he went by Adrian Neville), New Japan Pro-Wrestling and Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre. At a time when the fourth wall between fan and wrestler had long collapsed, Satterley rarely broke character. Yet, his death highlighted the humility and kindness behind “The Bastard” persona. “I wouldn’t be here today if I didn’t share time and space with this man,” she said. Days after his death, AEW turned its weekly “Dynamite” show into an emotional tribute to its fallen star, nicknamed “The Man That Gravity Forgot.” “Whilst he will always have a legacy as one of the greatest wrestlers the U.K. has ever produced, we have been so glad to see so many wonderful tributes that acknowledged who Ben was as a person,” the Satterley family said in a statement read during the show. “He exemplified what it meant to be a decent human being, an honorable man with principles, who adored his family and his sausage dog son, Wolfie.” On Instagram, his wife, Natalie, thanked Satterley “for our beautiful life.” Share Add NBC News to Google Rudy Chinchilla Rudy Chinchilla is a breaking news editor for NBC News Digital.

Hailing from Minnesota, a state known for its wrestling legacy, Gable was a state champion in high school before reaching the pinnacle of amateur wrestling in 2012, earning a spot on Team USA at the London Olympics. After the Games, Gable transitioned to WWE, signing on to train at the Performance Center. After the duo’s split, Gable tagged with Shelton Benjamin and Bobby Roode and ventured into singles competition, even making it to the finals of the 2019 King of the Ring tournament. Eventually, Gable’s pursuit of the Intercontinental Championship was marred by frustration, culminating in a shocking confrontation with Sami Zayn. His behavior became more manipulative, leading to a dramatic fallout with Alpha Academy and his former allies, Otis and Maxxine Dupri, in June 2024. In a shocking twist, Gable was revealed as the man behind The Original El Grande Americano, but undertaking the appearance of a luchador had unintended consequences. title: In Memoriam: Pac's Cause Of Death Has Been Revealed
raw_title: Pac's Cause Of Death Has Been Revealed
body: By Josh Coulson Published Oct 17, 2026, 4:14 AM EDT Josh studied Journalism and Media and Cultural Studies at the University of the West of England, graduating in the summer of 2014.. Josh is a writer at TheSportster and a lifelong wrestling fan who has been doing news coverage of WWE and AEW for many years. Pro wrestling got its hooks in him at the age of ten and he's been watching ever since. His favorite wrestlers are The Rock and CM Punk, despite the latter doing his level best to make us all dislike him. Sign in to your TheSportster account It's been almost three weeks since Benjamin Satterley, better known to wrestling fans as Pac in AEW and Neville when he wrestled in WWE, suddenly and tragically passed away at the age of just 40. What caused the pro wrestler's unexpected death has now been revealed. As reported by the New York Post , the Cook County Medical Office relayed to the California Post that Pac passed away from bronchial asthma. The final ruling on Pac's death, therefore, is that he died from natural causes and, as suspected, there was no foul play involved in his passing. As for whether Pac had an inhaler of some kind, or if he was even officially diagnosed with bronchial asthma before his passing, is still unclear. The wrestler presumably suffered from an asthma attack while in his car and passed away shortly after. Pac was discovered slumped in his car by a passerby on the afternoon of Sunday, September 27, 2026. He had wrestled Andrade El Idolo at All Out less than 24 hours prior. Further details revealed that Pac was seemingly on his way to the nearby airport where he was supposed to board a flight back to the UK. He had spoken to a woman on the phone hours earlier when he discussed where he was going to eat, presumably before flying home.
summary: Per TheSportster: what caused the pro wrestler's unexpected death has now been disclosed. The final ruling on Pac's death, therefore, is that he died from natural causes and, as suspected, there was no foul play involved in his passing.

title: Mike Bailey Explains His Realistic In-Ring Style

body: AEW wrestler Mike Bailey, who is a high-flyer, has shown that they are capable of wrestling that style while also appearing to be in a real fight when they are in the ring. Not only is Bailey a capable high-flyer, but their offense and movement in the ring is crisp and tight. Everything they do appears to have momentum behind it whether they are whipping someone off the ropes or bouncing off of them. Bailey said the key to their wrestling looking so crisp and their matches looking like they are in a real fight is that they have cultivated a narrow set of moves they are comfortable with. “But I think that this is a general thing about professional wrestling, but also a good piece of advice for professional wrestlers,” said Bailey during an exclusive interview on Radican Worldwide available now for PWTorch VIP members ahead of AEW’s WrestleDream PPV on Oct. 17. “But nothing looks as good as what you’re comfortable doing, right? I’ve been doing pro wrestling for 20 years, and I have actively cultivated a very narrow skill set, right? title: The Strange History of Wrestling Games Built Around Luck
raw_title: The Strange History of Wrestling Games Built Around Luck - PWInsider
body: Jalwa Game Goa Game Raja Game MaanWin DMFirst Veer Game The Strange History of Wrestling Games Built Around Luck By Kendall Jenkins on 2026-10-14 10:08:00 Professional wrestling has always had a funny relationship with chance. The finishes are planned, the champions are chosen, and nothing in the ring is supposed to be left to fortune. Yet for about seventy years, the games fans took home to play with the same stars have leaned on dice, spinners, charts and sealed card packs. A sport built on careful booking produced a whole shelf of games where a lucky roll could topple the biggest name on the card. The earliest known example came out in 1956, when Gardner Games released Verne Gagne Wrestling. It was sold as one of six sports games in a single package, next to football, golf, basketball, stock car racing and baseball, and Gagne was one of only two pro athletes whose name went on a box in that set. The other was Mickey Mantle. That tells you how big a television wrestler could be in the mid-fifties. Like most sports board games of the era, it turned a contest of skill into something a roll could settle. Nobody expected it to simulate a real match. The point was to put a famous face on the kitchen table and let two kids argue about who won. The format got more ambitious in 1970 with The Original Superstar Wrestling, designed by John Harwood. It used a pair of dice plus wrestler cards and result cards, handled up to four players, and a full match took about fifteen minutes. In chart-driven games of this kind, the cards do the job a referee would, turning a number into something that happened in the ring: a clean takedown, a missed charge, a sudden pin. That chart-driven chance never really went away. It simply moved onto screens. The same fans who once rolled for pinfalls on a card table now fill quiet evenings with quick digital games that run on a random outcome and a bright reveal, from mobile card battlers to Playfame free slots online . The mechanics are a long way from a cardboard ring, but the pleasure of not knowing what the next result will be is the same one that sold those early boxes. Collectible cards added a different kind of luck. The 1985 Topps WWF Pro Wrestling Stars set had 66 base cards and 22 stickers, and every sealed pack was a small lottery of its own. Some kids pulled Hogan twice. Others spent a whole summer hunting for one missing wrestler. The reason for all that randomness is simple. A real promotion has a booker who decides the finish. A board game has no booker, so the dice take the job. Two dice are especially useful for this, because their totals are not equally likely. A seven comes up about one roll in six, while a two or a twelve appears only one time in thirty-six. A designer can put ordinary strikes in the crowded middle of the chart and save the rare comebacks and finishing moves for the edges, which produces something that feels a lot like a well-paced match. It also explains why the star on the box mattered so

title: In Memoriam: Cause of death revealed for AEW star Pac after tragic death at just 40
raw_title: Cause of death revealed for AEW star Pac after tragic death at just 40
body: A spokesperson for the Cook County Medical Examiner’s Office told the California Post that the 40-year-old passed away from bronchial asthma. It is a chronic inflammatory condition that makes the airways in your lungs swell, narrow, and produce extra mucus, making it harder to breathe than normal. Satterley was discovered unconscious in a rental car in Illinois at around 4 pm on September 27. A 911 caller stated she had found Satterley “passed out”. Authorities formally pronounced him deceased just minutes after arriving on the scene. First responders wrote in an incident report that there were no injuries or “suspicious markings” on Satterley when they found him PAC is England's GOAT wrestler - he proved it in AEW before tragic death However, it was noted that he had saliva on the front of his shirt and medication in his vehicle. Satterley’s phone had Google Maps open and a route to O’Hare Airport was on display, according to the report. He had been performing in Chicago just one night before against Andrade, a fellow former WWE star. Known as Neville in WWE and PAC everywhere else, Satterley is arguably the greatest wrestling talent to ever emerge from England . He was one of AEW’s first signings when they launched in 2019 and stayed with the company until his dying day. But he won the respect of fans and wrestlers all over the world with his work, especially in Japan , America and the UK. He was seemingly in his professional prime, but becomes one in a long list of wrestlers to leave the world too soon. Just in the past five years, the wrestling world has lost Bray Wyatt and Brodie Lee to sudden, health-related deaths. ﻿

That incident later became part of a segment on Being the Elite and helped inspire the name of AEW’s annual Full Gear pay-per-view. The first edition took place in November 2019, making PAC’s connection to the event part of the promotion’s history from its earliest year. This year’s show will take place at the Mortgage Matchup Center in Phoenix on November 14. The updated artwork brings together references to PAC’s in-ring identity and the moment that helped give the event its name. The tribute also gives the Full Gear branding a personal connection beyond the event itself. The Black Arrow imagery and familiar ringside items ensure that PAC remains part of the show’s identity, even as AEW prepares for its next chapter. summary_src: Will Ospreay has already borrowed plenty from the Assassin’s Creed world for his wrestling career, but now he’d like to take that relationship somewhere completely different.
body: Speaking to Orlando Tourism Report , Ospreay was initially asked whether playing newer Assassin’s Creed games ever gives him ideas for new wrestling moves. At this point, he’s not really looking to reinvent himself because he feels the presentation he already has is working just fine. “I don’t know about that. I’m more trying to just, like, feel the storylines and the characters and stuff. Like, because what’s worked for me for so long has worked, and I don’t really need to change that much about my presentation as much now.” Ospreay is still very much into the games themselves. He’s played Shadows , recently started the new Black Flag , and remains a massive fan of the franchise that helped shape his wrestling character. “And, like, I’ve played Shadows. I’ve just started playing the new Black Flag as well, and I think that’s, like — honestly, the picture quality is just beautiful on that. And I just implore everyone to go and play those games because they were such a huge hit for me. I always enjoyed playing them.” Assassin’s Creed gave Ospreay an easy way to communicate exactly what his character was supposed to be. Fans could look at the way he moved and immediately understand the inspiration behind it. “It was just kind of like everyone knew what I was going for in my production-wise, in my presentation, and people just understood, like, I’m moving like the Assassin’s Creed characters. So that was kind of the main reason behind it.” Then came the Hidden Blade. Once Ospreay developed the elbow strike, naming it after something from the franchise that had already influenced so much of his career felt like an obvious move. “Once I developed the elbow strike, the Hidden Blade, it was just kind of like, how can I not attach that to the game that’s given me so much?” That relationship eventually became a real partnership with Ubisoft and Assassin’s Creed . summary_src: AEW’s WrestleDream pay-per-view is one of the most hyped events in a long time. With a strong lineup of matches from start to finish, AEW has made sure fans will be entertained all night. Clockwork Carnage Match for the AEW World Championship: Will Ospreay (c) vs.
body: Will Ospreay isn’t getting one challenger at WrestleDream. He’s getting seven. Ospreay puts the AEW World Championship on the line against Samoa Joe, Mike Bailey, Darby Allin, Kazuchika Okada, Ricochet, Adam Copeland and Konosuke Takeshita in the Clockwork Carnage match. The rules make this even crazier. Two wrestlers start before the remaining six enter at three-minute intervals. Anyone pinned or submitted before the eighth entrant arrives is eliminated from advancing to the next phase. Once everybody has entered, the remaining wrestlers move into a 15-minute scoring period. Every pinfall or submission earns one point, and whoever has the most points when time expires leaves as AEW World Champion. Thekla finally gets Mercedes Moné one-on-one with the AEW Women’s World Championship on the line. Thekla has already been champion before, losing the title to Willow Nightingale at Redemption in July. The championship eventually moved from Nightingale to Moné at All-In London, putting Mercedes at the top of AEW’s women’s division. Now Thekla gets the opportunity to become a two-time champion. Mercedes has continued competing despite dealing with a nose injury, but WrestleDream gives her another serious test. Thekla has been trying to get back to the championship she lost for months, and now there isn’t anybody standing between her and Moné. The Young Bucks haven’t had much time to enjoy being champions again. Matt and Nick Jackson won the AEW World Tag Team Championship at All Out, becoming four-time champions by defeating Christian Cage and Adam Copeland in a match that also included FTR. Now Kyle Fletcher and Kevin Knight are coming for them. Fletcher and Knight might be an unusual pairing, but they’ve already shown they can work together. That chemistry will have to hold up against two brothers who have spent years wrestling beside each other. title: In Memoriam: Pac cause of death revealed after tragic passing of AEW and former WWE star
raw_title: Pac cause of death revealed after tragic passing of AEW and former WWE star
body: British wrestling star Benjamin Satterley, also known as Pac, died of natural causes, it has been revealed. The All Elite Wrestling (AEW) star was discovered unconscious in a rental car on 27 September just one night after wrestling on a show for the promotion in Chicago, Illinois. A 911 caller told authorities she found the 40-year-old ‘passed out’. Police pronounced him deceased shortly after arriving on the scene. No cause of death was announced at the time but a spokesperson for the Cook County Medical Examiner’s Office has now told the California Post that ‘Pac’ passed away from bronchial asthma. Born in Newcastle, Satterley is regarded as one of the greatest wrestling talents to emerge from these shores. After wrestling on various independent circuits in the UK, US, Mexico and Japan, he joined WWE in 2012 under the name Aaron Neville where he reigned a cruiserweight champion. He joined AEW in 2019, appearing at the promotion’s first ever press conference and their first All Out event the same year, remaining with them for the rest of his career. He wrestled Andrade El Idolo for the AEW National Championship at All Out the day before his tragic death. AEW held ‘A Tribute to Pac’ on 30 September to honour Satterley with WWE also running a special tribute package featuring a number of superstars paying their respects. title: On the Record: Andrade Wants to Become ‘Andrade Two Belts’
raw_title: Andrade Wants to Become ‘Andrade Two Belts’
summary_src: Andrade already has gold around his waist, but he is nowhere near satisfied. The AEW National Champion has his sights set on the biggest prize in the company too, and he made it crystal clear that his endgame is walking around with two belts.
body: During an appearance on Close Up with Renee Paquette , Andrade was discussing his National Championship defense against Tommaso Ciampa when the conversation shifted to what comes next. Andrade did not dance around it. He wants the AEW World Championship too. “But this is my title. This is my title. I want this title. I want the world title. So I want Andrade two belts.” That opened the door for Renee to ask the obvious question. Andrade already has a future shot at the World Championship, so when exactly is he planning to pull the trigger? He is keeping that part close to the vest. Andrade said he knows there is a move to make, but he is not going to force it just because the opportunity is sitting there. “Oh, I know. It’s difficult. I want to wait for the right time.” For Andrade, this is bigger than just adding another championship to the collection. He said everyone wants to be the top guy, and part of the reason he came back to AEW was to prove that he can be trusted to represent the company at the highest level. “This is a business. Everyone, everybody want to do the best and the number one in the company, and this is why I am back to AEW, because I want to show that I can represent the company.” The interesting part is that Andrade does not even know who will be standing across from him when he finally decides the time is right. Will Ospreay’s name came up, but Andrade said he is willing to wait and see who has the belt when he is ready to make his move. “I don’t know if it’s with Ospreay or I don’t know who is the champion in this moment, but I need to make a decision. I want to wait a little, little while. When I’m ready, I need to change.” So Andrade is not in any rush here. He has one championship, a future World Title shot waiting in the wings, and a very simple goal when the dust settles: become “Andrade Two Belts.” The clock is now ticking on when Andrade finally decides to make that move, and when he does, whoever is holding the AEW World Championship is going to have a serious problem on their hands. body: These WWE SmackDown results cover the fallout episode following Saturday’s Money in the Bank premium live event. WWE United States Champion Trick Williams and Undisputed WWE Champion Sami Zayn continued their heated rivalry. “Absolute” Ricky Saints and AAA World Cruiserweight Champion Rey Fenix stole the show, while R-Truth may have suffered an injury during the broadcast. Zayn, Gargano, and Candice LeRae opened with a promo, suggesting that Mr. Money in the Bank Penta should challenge WWE World Heavyweight Champion “The OTC” Roman Reigns instead. This promo was interrupted by Williams, who has an ongoing rivalry with the champ and was a Money in the Bank participant. Zayn and Williams traded digs before Gargano stepped in and warned the US champ that he’s all sizzle, no steak. A match started then and there, and it was a relatively physical affair. It’s nice to see Johnny putting on entertaining matches again, even if he took the loss in this case. The finish was equally boring. Bella attempted a roll-up, but Paige reversed it into her own pinfall attempt. The referee counted to three, ending the match. In another former tag-team-turned-enemies storyline, Truth and Priest went one-on-one. The segment ended in unfortunate fashion when the referee threw up an X to signal an apparent injury. Priest won by referee stoppage, and his concerned expression was noticeable as he left the ring. Bliss and Paxley took the ring for their first promo as champs, but were quickly interrupted by Fatal Influence. The champs welcomed the challenge as Henley and Reid tried to rush them. After a short brawl, the new champs ended up on top. Few matches get any better than this. Saints and Fenix combined high-flying offense with believable physicality, creating a fast-paced contest filled with impressive reversals. Saints pushed the referee into the ropes as Fenix prepared to finish the match, but the move backfired. The official disqualified the challenger after the confrontation. Orton beat Rhodes around the outside of the ring before throwing him back. The Viper set up for a punt, but it was reversed into a Cody Cutter. Corbin rushed The American Nightmare from there, but actually ended up on the worse end of that exchange. After being accused of being too hesitant over recent weeks, Rhodes tried to buck the moniker. With Corbin set up for a punt, he immediately pulled the trigger. Orton and The American Nightmare locked eyes to end the show. Orton and Rhodes are destined for a payoff match; Saints were disqualified during their match against Fenix, and the new WWE Women’s Tag Team Champions held their ground. title: On the Record: Will Ospreay Says Women’s Wrestling Is Still Undersold and Opens Up On How Alex Windsor Got Signed by AEW

summary_src: Will Ospreay wants women’s wrestling to get a much bigger spotlight, and he says he is doing more than just talking about it.
body: That led to a discussion about whether Ospreay could continue using EVE as a place to experiment with new wrestling ideas. Ospreay said he enjoys trying things that haven’t been done before, but made it clear there is also a bigger reason he wants to stay involved. Ospreay then explained that one of his biggest goals is helping women’s wrestling grow. “For me personally, like, my whole thing is just, like, I really want to push women’s wrestling as far as it physically can go because it’s undersold and it’s one of these things that have been underappreciated for so long.” Ospreay said he enjoys being part of EVE because of the wrestlers involved and the opportunity it gives them to get noticed. He then revealed that AEW has been supportive of what the promotion is doing, to the point where he personally sends matches to Tony Khan. “I just generally enjoy being a part of something that, like, the girls are super grateful for, for, like, the team and everything. And then it always is good that AEW is, like, fully supportive of it. Like, I mean, the amount of times I’ll send Tony, like, an EVE match.” “I mean, that’s how my wife Alex got signed, is because Tony saw the match with Jamie Hayter that they done, first time they ever met one another, let alone wrestle one another, and he saw that and was just kind of like, ‘All right, I’ll bring her in.’” Ospreay said he is grateful that EVE can now serve as another doorway for women who have spent years grinding for opportunities. “And I think she’s great and, like, I’m so grateful for that because it’s one of these things where now we can sell to all of these girls who have been busting their ass off for so long and it’s like now time for them to be like, look, this is how the doorway can open. Like, if the door opens, like, kick it down, bro.” Ospreay is clearly using his position in AEW to do more than worry about his own matches. title: Tony Khan Claims AEW’s Biggest Pay-Per-View Numbers Ever Have Come in 2026
raw_title: Tony Khan Claims AEW’s Biggest Pay-Per-View Numbers Ever Have Come in 2026
summary_src: Tony Khan says AEW is having its biggest year yet on pay-per-view, and he isn’t being shy about the numbers. The AEW President says the company’s PPV business has continued climbing in 2026, with its biggest numbers to date all coming this year.
body: Khan discussed AEW’s business during an interview with WPRK 91.5 FM ahead of WrestleDream. The conversation turned to AEW’s media situation, including Skydance, Warner Bros. and Paramount, and Khan used the opportunity to lay out how he believes the company is performing across television and pay-per-view. Khan first said AEW’s television audience is up year-over-year and claimed the company is having the strongest year for viewership growth among wrestling promotions. “We’re having great results on pay-per-view. So, it’s a very exciting time for this all to happen as AEW’s viewership is up year-over-year. And of wrestling companies year-over-year, AEW’s having the best year on TV in terms of viewership growth.” “And on pay-per-view, we’ve had a great year with AEW pay-per-views significantly up since we launched on HBO Max last year. Our first pay-per-view last year on HBO Max was All Out 2025. All Out 2026 was significantly up.” Khan then dropped the bigger claim, saying AEW’s Wembley Stadium event produced the company’s largest pay-per-view number yet. “And our biggest pay-per-view yet by far was AEW All In Wembley Stadium in London, which was a huge success for us.” He followed that by saying AEW has now produced all of its biggest numbers during 2026. “And all of our biggest numbers to this date have been in 2026. So the numbers keep going up on pay-per-view, which is great news. And I think it shows that the AEW fans really love the AEW pay-per-view product. We put on very strong shows that our fans love to watch. And we continue to get great viewership for Dynamite and Collision.” Khan tied that growth back into AEW’s media future, saying he believes the company is entering an even stronger position with its partners. “And this is all happening at a great time because this is a media partnership that I think will make AEW even stronger. And I think AEW brings a lot of positives to Skydance and we have a great relationship with David Ellison.” AEW has taken plenty of heat over ratings and business chatter over the years, but Khan clearly believes the company has serious momentum where it matters most. If his numbers are any indication, 2026 isn’t just another strong year for AEW. In his eyes, it is the company’s biggest pay-per-view year yet. Felix Upton Felix Upton has over 15 years of experience in media and wrestling journalism. His work at Ringside News blends speed, accuracy, and industry insight.
summary: The conversation turned to AEW’s media situation, including Skydance, Warner Bros. and Paramount. AEW’s television audience is up year-over-year and claimed the company is having the strongest year for viewership growth among wrestling promotions. We’re having great results on pay-per-view, Khan first explained.

title: Alternative Footage Shows Security Guard Visibly Upset After Montez Ford RAW Incident
raw_title: Alternative Footage Shows Security Guard Visibly Upset After Montez Ford RAW Incident
summary_src: Alternative footage of the Montez Ford interaction at the center of the lawsuit against WWE has now surfaced online, and the new angle puts the security guard’s reaction front and center.
body: The incident happened during The Street Profits’ entrance on the July 6 episode of Monday Night RAW at the Allstate Arena in Rosemont, Illinois. Lucas, an off-duty Cook County Sheriff’s officer working security near ringside, is now suing WWE, Ford, whose legal name is Kenneth Crawford, and WWE subsidiary Event Services, LLC over what happened. The alternate angle gives a much clearer look at the interaction itself. Ford can be seen getting directly in front of Lucas and grinding on him before he and Angelo Dawkins jump the barricade and continue toward ringside. What stands out most in the footage is Lucas’ reaction immediately afterward. Lucas remains seated with a blank look on his face before slowly shaking his head, visibly appearing upset and confused by what had just happened. The reaction comes across like he is trying to process the moment while the entrance continues around him. Ford and Dawkins then keep the act going after clearing the barricade, dancing on the announce table before moving on to the match that was ahead. That footage now adds to allegations made in Lucas’ lawsuit. The complaint claims Ford performed what it described as a sexualized “lap dance” without Lucas’ consent. The lawsuit also claims Ford kept moving closer during the interaction. “Defendant Crawford then began performing a sexually provocative dance immediately in front of and over Plaintiff [Lucas], repeatedly thrusting and gyrating his hips and pelvis towards Plaintiff, performing a sexualized ‘lap dance.’” “[Crawford] moved his body increasingly closer to [Lucas]; continued the lap dance.” Lucas is accusing the defendants of 14 counts, including assault, battery, intentional infliction of emotional distress and violations of the Illinois Gender Violence Act. The newly surfaced footage does not settle the legal case, but it does show the moment from a different angle and, more importantly, captures Lucas’ immediate reaction after Ford moved away. Instead of playing along with the entrance, Lucas can be seen sitting there stone-faced and shaking his head while The Street Profits continue the show. title: Bron Breakker Needs to Become WWE's Monster Heel
raw_title: It's Time For Bron Breakker to Turn Into WWE's Monster Heel
body: This feels cliche on first pass, no doubt. "Just go heel" is a really common solution onlookers come up with while trying to suggest changes for lagging wrestlers. Grading SmackDown 🔠 Bleacher Report 8h Backstage WWE Rumors 🍿 Bleacher Report 14h Recasting Street Fighter with WWE Stars 🎬 Bleacher Report 18h But with Breakker, it's different. There's storyline and character justification in droves. Everyone knows how Breakker got passed up by Oba Femi, who is now on the fast path to a WrestleMania date with Roman Reigns. Breaker got hurt, but even if he hadn't, Femi probably would've lapped him. That's a wrestler who stands out. And the lowlights just keep coming from Breakker. At least one outlet, False Finish , has reported that Breakker was originally scheduled to win the Money in the Bank briefcase in the men's match before WWE gave it to Penta instead. So, two distinct, super-hot-with-crowd stars have leapfrogged Breakker in a small amount of time. It's made worse by a new report, too. According to Self Made Pro (h/t Cain A. Knight of Cageside Seats), CM Punk likes Breakker and will eventually put him over in a match. There's the rub: This isn't going to stop happening. In his current state, Breakker will just keep getting passed up. He tried to shake the weird nepo-accusations via his family name. He became something of a community project where fans were cheering on his promo improvement by the week while just waiting for him to become that preordained next big thing. He's had Paul Heyman, Seth Rollins and others working with him. Slap a small railing against "the man" gimmick on it in the process. Forget the nepo accusations, he's clearly being held back by the corporate suits who don't want him as the face of the company. He's not supposed to win, so he's going to break free of the shackles by force. Nobody's saying slap on some jorts and start downing beers, but make Breakker more relatable. Anyway, shifting Breakker from the obvious next-big-thing to an underdog would have plenty of character justification at this point. The roster lacks those mega-heels right now. Gunther is nowhere to be found and Drew McIntyre has become a tad stagnant. Femi is going to need that long-term foil, and over the years, they can swap good and bad guy roles when needed. But right now? Breakker feels like he's stuck in neutral. But he's very painfully got the potential to break free of the pack and really grab that brass ring everyone thinks is hanging above him. It helps that WWE feels willing to take some risks right now. We've seen some really creative presentation decisions over the last few years, even with new camera angles and backstage shots of stuff. The faction war with the Bloodline and 946 is a good example right now. Bringing some innovation that's unique to Breakker's chaos he spreads across all brands while lashing out could be really fun and get fans invested. It just, frankly, doesn't need to be this difficult. Breakker in his current state
summary: Bron Breakker has been repeatedly passed over in recent months, first by Oba Femi who is headed for a WrestleMania match with Roman Reigns and then by Penta who took the Money in the Bank briefcase that Breakker had been planned to win. A new report indicates CM Punk is a fan and plans to put him over in a future match, but the pattern shows Breakker will continue to be leapfrogged by hotter acts unless he changes course. Turning heel as an unstoppable monster offers clear storyline justification given his frustrations and the mounting lowlights in his current babyface run.

Williams called himself a real superstar and a bundle of bad memories for Zayn. He added that Zayn had disrespected him weeks earlier and that he would now beat him as a result.
Zayn reminded Williams that he is the WWE Champion and recounted their previous interaction. He claimed that Williams cannot feel the moment or survive chaos while he himself thrives in it.

Williams challenged Zayn to take a swing if he meant what he said. Johnny Gargano then took the microphone and criticized Williams for receiving opportunities based on his presentation rather than substance, declaring that he would prove his own worth in the ring.
Williams accepted the challenge from Gargano. A referee was called as the segment led into their match later that night.

summary_src: In the span of a few weeks, AEW lost two of its own. Andy Williams, The Butcher, and Benjamin Satterley, PAC. Two active wrestlers, two people who were still working, doing the thing they love.
body: In the span of a few weeks, AEW lost two of its own. Andy Williams, The Butcher, and Benjamin Satterley, PAC. Two active wrestlers, two people who were still working, doing the thing they love. Just because the calendar has moved forward and routines become closer to normal does not mean the anguish diminishes. We are constantly reminded of their absence. AEW has run three tribute shows since September. They did not have to; they chose to, because that is what you do when the people you lost were more than colleagues. The roster and audience needed somewhere to try and put the grief, but grief does not have a natural container. Expecting a proper build to a pay-per-view in the middle of all of that is an unreasonable expectation. In fact, it is a failure of basic human empathy. Any criticism of this card’s construction that does not begin with an acknowledgement of what this roster has been carrying is criticism that should be set aside, derided, and then ignored. The fact that they have assembled anything at all under these circumstances is, frankly, remarkable. PAC was one of my guys, one of my favorites. I wrote about him in these digital pages, and I won’t pretend that writing this column felt normal this week. It did not. Imagine how his loved ones still feel. But the show goes on, as it always does. Hopefully that’s what he would have wanted. The best thing anyone can do now is watch. I do think Nick Wayne (call him Nick Wayne) has something, and clearly AEW does too. They’re giving him time to put things together, make mistakes, and grow. That’s the right way to invest in talent. Whether that investment can reach its ceiling in a program with Chris Jericho is, generously, open to interpretation (it can’t). At this stage of his career, and when he’s on his best behavior, Jericho is still a validator based on his name. Sharing the ring with a legend, even one most people are a bit fatigued by, still means something. This has been lowercase-f fine, provided this wraps up at WrestleDream. Wayne got ring time on the important shows, got to show more of his personality, and got to prove that at some point down the road, he belongs in important conversations. None of that requires anything more than a third act, which wraps up here. Persephone is extraordinarily talented. The kind of talent that pierces your TV the moment she steps on screen. The Kill Bill sirens blare, she steps out from behind the curtain, and is instantly and viscerally exciting. She carries her titles, plural, with a credibility that betrays her 25 years. Whatever she does next, and wherever she goes after this title reign, should be as big as her ceiling is. Queen Aminata is another name to watch here. I’ve been a believer for some time, and AEW appears to have arrived at the same conclusion. Her in-ring style is exactly what this division needs more of – purposeful, direct, and hard-hitting. You do not get a world title showcase against Mercedes Moné at Grand Slam Paris and
summary: The latest: AEW lost two of its own. AEW has run three tribute shows since September.

summary_src: Will Ospreay isn’t treating the AEW World Championship like just another belt on the résumé. He says carrying the company’s top title comes with a responsibility he takes very seriously.
body: For Ospreay, that makes his current spot at the top of AEW mean even more. title: On the Record: Tony Khan Says Some AEW Talent Couldn’t Wrestle After PAC’s Death
raw_title: Tony Khan Says Some AEW Talent Couldn’t Wrestle After PAC’s Death
summary_src: PAC’s death hit AEW hard, and Tony Khan says some wrestlers simply weren’t in any condition to perform the next day. During an interview with WPRK 91.5 FM, Khan opened up about the Ring of Honor taping that took place shortly after Benjamin Satterley’s death.
body: During an interview with WPRK 91.5 FM , Khan opened up about the Ring of Honor taping that took place shortly after Benjamin Satterley’s death. Instead of forcing the show to go on like nothing happened, Khan made the taping optional for talent. He said some wrestlers were just too shaken up to work. “Well, it was voluntary and there were some people that definitely were not feeling well and understandably could not wrestle that day. So, I changed my plans around and I do think there were some great matches and moments on that taping and the shows coming out of the Ring of Honor taping I think have been strong, but it was a hard show to put on.” Khan also admitted he had to completely rework parts of the card because several people couldn’t make it. “I did have an outline for the card and I had to make a lot of changes to the outline because there were a handful of people who couldn’t make it. And I understood that because it’s very challenging and I think I expected there would be some people where the emotional toll was just too much to wrestle the next day.” That doesn’t mean everybody stayed home. Khan said a number of wrestlers still wanted to go out there and perform, and Bandido ended up delivering one of the most emotional moments of the night. After defending the ROH World Championship against AR Fox, Bandido placed a PAC armband on the title. “Having said that, there were a lot of people that did want to go out and wrestle. And we saw Bandido put the PAC armband on the Ring of Honor World Championship after he defended it against AR Fox in Jacksonville at the taping.” Khan said the entire situation was brutal, especially with PAC’s death coming so close to the show and AEW also dealing with the loss of Andy Williams. “It was a great tribute in the main event for Bandido to put the PAC wristband on the world championship and very emotional day of tapings. So, thank you for saying that. And with Andy Williams and now with Ben, it’s been very hard. And I had a lot of respect for both of them. And with Ben, it happened so suddenly, so close to the taping.” AEW still held the taping, but this was clearly not a normal day at work. Khan gave talent the option to stay home, changed the card on the fly, and let those who did wrestle honor PAC in their own way. title: AEW WrestleDream predictions — Murphy's Blog
raw_title: Murphy's Blog: AEW WrestleDream predictions - Who will leave Clockwork Collision with the AEW World Championship? Will other titles change hands?
body: By Don Murphy , ProWrestling.net Contributor ( @DonThePredictor ) Will Ospreay vs. Samoa Joe vs. Mike Bailey vs. Adam Copeland vs. Konosuke Takeshita vs. Kazuchika Okada vs. Ricochet vs. Darby Allin in a Clockwork Carnage match for the AEW World Championship. For context, the Clockwork Carnage rules are listed as follows: “Two wrestlers will start with two wrestlers selected at random. Every three minutes, another randomly selected wrestler enters. Until all eight wrestlers have entered, any wrestler who is pinned or submits is eliminated. Once the final wrestler enters, all remaining wrestlers enter a 15-minute scoring period. During those 15 minutes, every pinfall or submission scores one fall. When the time expires, the wrestler with the most falls wins.” My pet peeve is here in all its glory. I understand the desire to try a new match concept. Heck, I encourage it. Without innovation, we don’t have WarGames, Hell in a Cell, Elimination Chamber, etc. And I may feel different after I see how it plays out and is received, but to me, this seems more complicated than it should be. More importantly, it accentuates my biggest issue – not building anyone to be a credible singles challenger to Will Ospreay. Instead, we incorporate lazy booking by throwing everyone into a multi-person match. Yes, they all qualified to be there, so that part was good. But unless there’s a big shakeup planned, there’s no reason to believe any of the seven challengers has a shot at winning the title. I also have a smaller issue with Okada being granted a qualifying match. Yes, he’s the International Champion, but he was just on the losing end of a title match against Ospreay. Despite all of this, the match should delight the fanbase. Don Predicts: Will Ospreay defeats Samoa Joe, Mike Bailey, Adam Copeland, Konosuke Takeshita, Kazuchika Okada, Ricochet, and Darby Allin in a Clockwork Carnage match to retain the AEW World Championship. Mercedes Mone vs. Thekla for the AEW Women’s Championship. Thekla and Willow Nightingale are the two talents in the women’s division that I am most high on. Thekla has potential to be the breakout babyface star of the division, but I think it would be too soon to put the title on her. I think this will be a highly competitive match, with Mone retaining. With the right booking and story, it’s a match you can rebuild and go back to when you’ve fully baked Thekla’s presentation and are ready to give her a big moment. Don Predicts: Mercedes Mone defeats Thekla to retain the AEW Women’s Championship. “The Young Bucks” Matt Jackson and Nick Jackson vs. Kyle Fletcher and Kevin Knight for the AEW Tag Team Titles. I’m going to give this one a bit of a pass because we don’t know for sure if this was the plan before Steven Borden’s injury at All Out. The match will be fine, as Fletcher and Knight have shown some decent chemistry. title: Tommaso Ciampa Ready To Be AEW's Fighting Champion (Exclusive)
raw_title: Tommaso Ciampa Ready To Be AEW's Fighting Champion (Exclusive)
body: "I'm really proud of it," Ciampa tells me. "I'm a big Halloween enthusiast. I love carving pumpkins." Ciampa's excitement about pumpkin carving is as enthusiastic and contagious as his excitement about being in AEW. Haivng joined the company in January, he's had an impressive run of matches and wins, including a TNT Championship win and a violently wild match with Chris Jericho that ended with a drill to the head. Ciampa's called the experience a great one since joining, telling me the extra time he's had with his family has been the best part of it all. "I like to journal, and I find myself oftentimes [when] I finish writing and I'm like, 'Oh, I wrote 95% about out-of-the-ring family experiences and 5% of it was 'and then I wrestled and I had this match.' So in that sense, it's been just a really, really wonderful experience." Ciampa's ready for his next challenge, facing off against Andrade El Idolo for the AEW National Championship at this weekend's AEW WrestleDream . With Andrade accepting his challenge on this past week's AEW Dynamite , Ciampa tells me he's the right challenge at this moment because Andrade is hotter than he's ever been. He mentions their match at AEW Grand Slam Mexico with Kommander, and that the crowd went crazy for him during his entrance. Andrade wants to be a fighting champion, and should he defeat him tonight, Ciampa says he's ready to continue with the fighting champion spirit and thinks those things are fun for the fans to see, as well as helping newer performers to elevate their platforms. But he also loves the idea of performers earning their spots. He calls himself a "run the plays" guy, and will plug in whenever, and wherever, he needs to. "I don't know that I live in one camp over the other. I just appreciate both, so I think in that scenario, it's kind of like what's best for the National title, what's best for the program, what's best for AEW as a whole. Like, what's the programming need? Does Dynamite or Collision need open challenges weekly, or do we need to tell stories that are three weeks long, six weeks long, 12 weeks long that build up challengers as we go? Because either scenario, to me, is wonderful. You either build up an opponent every three to four weeks and have pay-per-view title matches, or you maybe don't build up opponents and you give people these platforms and these opportunities on a week-to-week basis." Ciampa has worked hard to integrate the passion and edge of his trainers, Killer Kowalski and Harley Race, into his in ring work, and while he can't say for sure this is the most authentic he's ever been in the ring, this iteration of the Pscyho Killer is among his favorite career work, and he's ready to continue to show AEW why he's ready to be the next fighting champion. "I'm a unicorn in AEW in the sense that I'm like this chameleon. I can be a bad guy on Monday and a good guy on Friday. It's crazy to me. With Okada, I kind of was more the good guy, and now with Andrade, I'll probably be
summary: I'm really proud of it, Ciampa tells me. Andrade is hoping to be a fighting champion, and should he defeat him tonight, Ciampa says he's ready to continue with the fighting champion spirit and thinks those things are fun for the the audience to see.

title: Kelly Kelly Explains Rejecting Playboy Offer
raw_title: Former WWE Star Kelly Kelly Recalls Turning Down Playboy
summary_src: Former Divas Champion Kelly Kelly explains why she turned down the opportunity to pose for Playboy during her WWE career.
body: "Well, I remember them asking me to do it, and I remember I was like, 'Oh, well, I have to talk to my family,' because I was literally 21, " she said on "LayTalk." "I just remember in the back of my head being like, you know, if I do this, it's going to haunt me for the rest of my life. Like, these pictures are never going to go away...I know I want to have kids. I don't want to have that on the internet."
summary: Former WWE performer Kelly Kelly has shared that she declined an invitation from Playboy while she was only 21 years old. She consulted her family before making the decision, fearing the images would remain online forever and could impact her future plans to have children.

title: Will Ospreay Grateful For Kicking Out Of One Winged Angel
raw_title: Will Ospreay On Kicking Out Of The One Winged Angel At AEW All In: To Have That Was Out Of This World And Mindblowing
summary_src: Will Ospreay reflects on kicking out of Kenny Omega's One Winged Angel at AEW All In 2026 back in August. At AEW's biggest pay-per-view of the year this past August, Will would challenge for the AEW World Championship against Kenny Omega in his home country of England.
body: Will Ospreay reflects on kicking out of Kenny Omega’s One Winged Angel at AEW All In 2026 back in August. At AEW’s biggest pay-per-view of the year this past August, Will would challenge for the AEW World Championship against Kenny Omega in his home country of England. During the bout, Ospreay would emphatically kick out of Omega’s One Winged Angel finish, a move that has been protected over the years, with Kota Ibushi and Omega himself being amongst the few to actually kick out of the move in the past. While speaking to 1010XL in a new interview, Will Ospreay reflected on kicking out of the One Winged Angel and what it meant to him. “That I won Kenny’s trust, because a lot of that comes down to how much he wants to protect it and going forward, like where… Where does that put me? It just elevates me up to like a legendary status that I will never fully be able to express my gratitude for having that type of moment with someone that I do generally look at as like a hero of mine. So to have that was just out of this world, mind blowing. Like I’m just super grateful for it.” If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.

Ospreay kicked out of Omega's protected One Winged Angel finisher during the match, a feat previously accomplished by only a small number of wrestlers including Kota Ibushi and Omega. In a recent interview, Ospreay expressed that earning Omega's trust with the moment elevated him to legendary status and left him extremely grateful.

title: On the Record: Drew McIntyre Calls CM Punk a ‘Guilty Piece of Crap’ After Using Criminology Degree to Judge Him
raw_title: Drew McIntyre Calls CM Punk a ‘Guilty Piece of Crap’ After Using Criminology Degree to Judge Him
summary_src: Drew McIntyre has spent years tearing into CM Punk, but this time he actually brought his college degree into the fight and reached a pretty brutal verdict.
body: During an appearance on Stephanie McMahon’s “What’s Your Story?” podcas t, McIntyre was asked about his degree in criminology and whether he ever applies anything he learned to the people he deals with in wrestling. Drew didn’t have to think very long before Punk’s name entered the conversation. McIntyre joked that Punk would make one hell of a subject to study. Drew then explained that he actually leaned into that criminology background during his feud with Punk. His argument was simple: people should look at the history of both men and decide for themselves who deserves to be trusted. “Now type his name in. He’s a terrible human being. I know he’s Charles Manson-like. I know he just woos you all with his words, but trust the guy that’s always been there for you.” Stephanie played along with Drew’s criminology angle by bringing up the idea of being guilty beyond a reasonable doubt. Drew didn’t hesitate to deliver his verdict. That wasn’t the only controversy tied to Punk at the MGM Grand. Ringside News also covered claims of a second hotel confrontation involving Punk and another fan , while police were also called in connection with the hotel drama . The circumstances surrounding those interactions became a major debate, especially since wrestlers have repeatedly pushed back against fans following or approaching them at hotels. Another situation surfaced in July when a mother spoke out following an encounter involving Punk and her six-year-old son at a WWE hotel. The mother claimed Punk “mad-dogged” the child after he recognized him , while she later denied that her family had stalked or followed Punk to the hotel . Punk had also posted a since-deleted Instagram Story around that time warning fans not to follow him back to his hotel . Those incidents produced plenty of arguments online over where the line should be between fan access and a wrestler’s privacy, so Drew certainly won’t be alone in having strong opinions about Punk, even if his reasons go much deeper than a few hotel encounters. McIntyre and Punk already turned their genuine friction into one of WWE’s most personal rivalries, and Drew clearly hasn’t decided to leave any of that hostility in the past. If anything, giving Punk a criminology-inspired guilty verdict shows he is still finding new ways to keep the rivalry alive even when they aren’t standing across the ring from each other.
