body: One glance at this week says it all. There's buzz about the fabled John Cena classic yet again, rumblings about WrestleMania 43 plans and some budding problems around the booking of a certain major top star. That's just a few highlights, too. To help fans keep up with the hot rumor mill, let's throw must-know rumors on the BS Meter, with 10 being the highest form of unbelievable buzz fans can safely dismiss. More proof Triple H is lurking on the internet? According to WrestleVotes (h/t Geno Mrosko of Cageside Seats), Penta's briefcase win was a late development after his strong match in Mexico City against Roman Reigns. Likewise, from the same note, Tiffany Stratton's win was an effort to keep fans guessing. Remember the John Cena Classic? WWE apparently does. According to Fightful Select (h/t Mrosko ), there are two dates in mind: Dec. 12 after Wrestlepalooza and Dec. 19. That December 19 date would put the Cena creation up against AEW's Worlds End, instantly making it more believable, considering how much WWE loves to counterprogram these days. Forcing the event to happen in 2026 is starting to narrow down the dates they can actually run it, obviously. Does anybody care about the date? What does a date matter when nobody, including Cena himself, can even say what the event is? Maybe WWE scraps together something involving the tournament that includes fan voting or whatever, but this has been a mess from the start, and nailing down a date before what the event actually is seems ill-advised. Here comes the…Oba Femi backlash? According to Self Made Pro's Ibou (h/t Cain A. Knight of Cageside Seats), some wrestlers are hesitant to work with him because it could push them down the card and make them look weak, essentially. Historically, refusing to work with a wrestler for these types of reasons tends to get the unwilling pushed down a card anyway, right? Losing is part of the job or the magic doesn't happen for everyone. Ask LA Knight if he felt like a chump in the main event of Money in the Bank against a modern GOAT while having a classic match and cashing a big paycheck in the process. This is silly. It almost feels like getting worked by the incident where Bronson Reed put his foot on Femi at the end of a segment. Outsiders can wax poetic all they want about no-selling finishers and stuff, but Femi's on an obvious path no matter who gets in his way and the job is the job. Bron Breakker is another one of those guys on the way up. According to Self Made Pro (h/t Knight ), Punk has personally told Breakker he will put him over eventually, apparently because he likes him. Everyone seems to love Breakker, whose untimely injury and the rise of Femi put a slight hold on his next-big-thing push. It would make sense that there are some light long-term plans to get some of the big-name veterans to put him over when the time is right. We'll see when Breakker's moment happens. Femi is still on the warpath for Roman Reigns at WrestleMania next year. Punk fee

title: WrestleDream 2026 features new Clockwork Carnage title match
raw_title: WrestleDream 2026 preview: Tony Khan knows how to make AEW’s bizarre new gimmick a wild success
body: Link If you buy something from a link, Vox Media may earn a commission. See our ethics statement. All Elite Wrestling returns to pay-per-view tonight (Oct. 17) with WrestleDream 202 6. The show comes our way from Addition Financial Arena in Orlando, Florida. The event begins at 7 pm ET with both the Tailgate Brawl special on TNT and the Buy In pre-show on YouTube. That leads right into the PPV main card at 8 pm ET. Fans in the USA can purchase it from PPV.com , HBO Max , Amazon , DAZN , Fubo , and YouTube , or their cable or satellite provider. The show is also available on MyAEW for fans in the UK and many international markets. AEW only had a three week turnaround from All Out to WrestleDream, and some of that TV time was spent ignoring story development in order to pay tribute to PAC. Those time constraints were probably a factor in the creation of a new “ Clockwork Carnage ” gimmick match for the AEW world title that will be featured as the main event of WrestleDream. It takes a while to read and process all the rules for Clockwork Carnage. For the sake of simplicity, AEW has described it as a mashup of a Casino Gauntlet match (phase one) and an Iron Man match (phase two). If there is no funny business with the clock, it should last around 33 minutes, with 18 minutes for the first phase and 15 minutes for the second phase. Let’s see how exactly it works. The match features eight wrestlers competing across two phases. The Entry Phase starts with two men in the ring at random. A new competitor enters the match every three minutes until all eight stars have entered the fray. If anybody is pinned or submitted during this phase, they are eliminated from the match. Whichever wrestlers survive will make it to the Scoring Phase. This part of the match is a 15 minute scramble to see who scores the most pins or submissions. That wrestler will walk out of WrestleDream as the AEW world champion. It can be hard to make a somewhat complicated new gimmick match work in pro wrestling, but Tony Khan picked the right strategy to ensure Clockwork Carnage is a success. That obvious strategy is to take advantage of his very deep roster by loading up this brand new gimmick match with seven tremendous workers and Darby Allin. Will Ospreay is the defending AEW world champion and the best wrestler in the world. The seven challengers are Samoa Joe, Kazuchika Okada, Ricochet, Adam Copeland, Konosuke Takeshita, Speedball Bailey, and Darby. It’s an extremely impressive collection of star power and talent for the debut of Clockwork Carnage. How many competitors will be eliminated during the Entry Phase? How many falls will it take to win the Scoring Phase? Will finishing moves that normally don’t win a PPV match on the first try suddenly be way more effective at scoring pin falls tonight? What happens if there is a tie? Tune into WrestleDream to see how AEW pulls off the debut of Clockwork Carnage, and if the new concept looks like one with staying power to be an annual f

body: Para disfrutar los contenidos de Clarín es necesario que actives JavaScript en tu navegador. Less than a day after performing inside the ring at AEW All Out, 40-year-old wrestler Benjamin Satterley was found dead in a Chicago suburb. Officials have officially confirmed the English star died of bronchial asthma. Photo: JJ Williams/Wrestling Observer NEWSROOM CLARIN English professional wrestler Benjamin Satterley , widely celebrated by wrestling audiences around the globe under the ring name "Pac," died from bronchial asthma , according to official findings released by the Cook County Medical Examiner's Office. The medical examiner determined that the 40-year-old athlete's manner of death was natural , resolving weeks of uncertainty that followed his unexpected passing in suburban Chicago late last month. Satterley was found unresponsive inside a vehicle on the afternoon of Sunday, September 27, 2026 , less than 24 hours after performing on live pay-per-view for All Elite Wrestling (AEW). According to records released by Cook County authorities, emergency personnel were dispatched shortly after 4:00 p.m. on September 27 to a commercial parking lot outside a CAVA restaurant at 2761 Mannheim Road in Des Plaines, Illinois—located approximately two miles north of Chicago O’Hare International Airport. The announcement of Satterley’s death on September 27 shocked fans and colleagues, largely because the wrestler had completed a rigorous, high-impact athletic performance the previous evening. WWE extends its condolences to the family, friends and fans of Benjamin Satterley, known to the WWE Universe as Neville. pic.twitter.com/i1mXLenFUz On Saturday, September 26, Satterley competed at AEW's All Out pay-per-view at the NOW Arena in Hoffman Estates, Illinois: Born in Newcastle upon Tyne, England, Satterley started training at age 18 in 2004, developing a unique hybrid wrestling style that merged explosive martial arts strikes with high-flying maneuvers. Following the news of his death, AEW dedicated an episode of its flagship broadcast Dynamite to Satterley , highlighting both his athletic contributions and his reserved personal character away from the cameras. Fellow English star Will Ospreay wrote on social media: "The greatest export from our country. Also the greatest human being. Honored to have shared the ring with you so many times. You truly are such a hero to myself and many others." Andrade El Ídolo vs PAC - AEW National Championship | AEW All Out 2026 In a statement shared during the tribute broadcast, Satterley's family emphasized his character behind the villainous on-screen persona : "Whilst he will always have a legacy as one of the greatest wrestlers the U.K. has ever produced , we have been so glad to see so many wonderful tributes that acknowledged who Ben was as a person. He exemplified what it meant to be a decent human being , an honorable man with principles, who adored his family and his sausage dog son, Wolfie."

body: Matt Hardy has addressed what went wrong with Tiffany Stratton’s Swanton off a ladder at WWE Money in the Bank 2026. Stratton appeared to land hard outside the ring after attempting to deliver the move onto several wrestlers below during the women’s ladder match on the show. “If you’re on top of a tall ladder that’s eight, 10, 12 feet, you can’t push off because the ladder will topple over even if people are holding on to it. So you just kind of have to drop off. I’ve seen Jeff do that a million times and I’ve done it a couple times in the past. But I usually would prefer to go off a rung because that way you can push a little more. “But if you’re on top of that ladder, it’s typically going to tip out behind you if you try and push off of it real hard. So I just think when it was all said and done, the girls who she was jumping on, in theory, they probably should have been a little closer. They did knock down her legs a little bit, which probably slowed her momentum and made it a little less impactful. Stratton did not appear on Friday’s edition of WWE SmackDown from Sacramento. At the post-Money in the Bank press conference , she mentioned that her neck was still hurting following the move. title: Injury Update: Stephanie Vaquer Explains What Really Happened After WWE Money in the Bank with Injury Scare
raw_title: Stephanie Vaquer Explains What Really Happened After WWE Money in the Bank with Injury Scare
summary_src: Stephanie Vaquer has finally explained what happened after she was seen struggling to walk following WWE Money in the Bank, and the situation sounds much better than it looked. Speaking to TJ Sports: Lucha Wrestling, Vaquer confirmed that she twisted her ankle during the show.
body: “I twisted my ankle. It’s not a big deal — just a couple of days of rest.” Vaquer’s ankle was not the only thing bothering her after Money in the Bank. She also lost the Women’s World Championship to Liv Morgan, and that defeat appears to be weighing on her much more than the injury. “But more than anything, I’m very disappointed about that match. I would have loved to be able to do this interview with you with the championship here on my shoulder, but I wasn’t able to retain it.” There was immediate concern about Vaquer after the show because she was visibly limping and needed referee Jessika Carr to help her. At one point, Vaquer sat down on the steel steps before eventually making her way backstage. “Like I said, every time I lose, I come back stronger, and that’s my goal. You can’t beat someone who never gives up.” Money in the Bank clearly did not go according to plan for Vaquer. She walked into the show as Women’s World Champion and left without the title while also dealing with an injured ankle. Still, Vaquer made it clear that she plans to recover and get right back to work. “So that’s the optimism I have right now, but yes, I’m disappointed. No, I didn’t expect something like that to happen at Money in the Bank, but we’re going to recover, like always.” Considering how bad Vaquer looked while leaving the ring, hearing that she only expects to need a few days of rest is a huge relief. Losing the Women’s World Championship was a major setback, but the ankle injury does not appear likely to keep her away from WWE for long. title: In Memoriam: Wrestler Benjamin Satterley's cause of death revealed
raw_title: Wrestler Benjamin Satterley's cause of death revealed
body: The cause of death for Benjamin Satterley, the wrestler known to fans as "Pac," has been released. Satterley died Sept. 27 at 40 years old, a day after facing Andrade El Idolo in the All Elite Wrestling National Championship in Chicago. The Cook County, Illinois, Medical Examiner’s Office confirmed Satterley died of bronchial asthma, according to The New York Post . The manner of death was natural. Satterley is a native of Newcastle upon Tyne, England. He began his wrestling career in 2004, "and went on to perform for wrestling organizations all over the world, captivating fans with innovative high-flying moves and incredible in-ring ability," AEW said in a statement Sept. 27. Satterley was one of the first wrestlers to sign with AEW in 2019 and was a two-time Trios Champion as well as the inaugural All-Atlantic Champion, Outkick reported . Prior to joining AEW, Satterley had wrestled in the WWE as Adrian Neville. During that time, he held the Cruiserweight Championship twice, was an NXT Champion, and two-time NXT Tag Team Champion. His wife, Natalie, shared an emotional tribute to her late husband on Instagram a few days ago. "Thank you for our beautiful life darling," she wrote. "Twenty one years ago we became friends, nineteen years ago we fell in love and eleven years ago we were married. Two souls entwined in one; my best friend and better half. "You always worked so incredibly hard to ensure we would have a great life together, both now and once you had retired. The cruelty of having all of our future hopes and dreams snatched away will never feel real.

body: The match that has everyone talking is the first-ever Clockwork Carnage match for the AEW World Championship. Eight performers will compete in a match devised by AEW President Tony Khan and AEW World Champion Will Ospreay, all with the goal of leaving Orlando with the gold in hand. Two wrestlers will start, and every three minutes another man will enter the match until all eight wrestlers have arrived. If a wrestler is pinned before the final entrant arrives, they are eliminated and won't advance to the next stage. Once the final entrant has arrived, the remaining participants will have 15 minutes to earn as many falls as possible. The man with the most falls at the end of the match will be declared the winner and the AEW World Champion. Ospreay will have to deal with current AEW International Champion Kazuchika Okada, current AEW TNT Champion Darby Allin, Konosuke Takeshita, Ricochet, "Speedball" Mike Bailey, Samoa Joe, and Adam Copeland , all of whom will be hoping to end the night with the richest prize in All Elite Wrestling around their waists. As for the other world championship, AEW Women's World Champion Mercedes Mone will look make her second defense of her crown when she takes on Thekla. "The Toxic Spider" earned her shot by defeating Willow Nightingale at AEW All Out 2026 , an event that Mone missed due to suffering a broken nose. Now that she's cleared and already back in action, she will be looking to put an end to Thekla once and for all. AEW/Ricky Havlik Elsewhere on the WrestleDream card, the AEW World Trios Championships will be at stake in a Two-out-of-Three Falls match , where Swerve Strickland and The New Level will take on Hangman Page and Brodido. Strickland, Kofi, and Austin Creed defeated Page, Bandido, and Brody King at All Out, but the personal animosity between Strickland and Page has led to a rematch where each team will need two wins rather than one. The key to victory might be getting Strickland and Page composed before anything goes off the rails. The AEW World Tag Team Championships will be on the line as The Young Bucks defend against Kyle Fletcher and Kevin Knight of The Don Callis Family. Fletcher and Knight earned their shot at All Out when their match with Steven Borden and Darby Allin was stopped due to Borden suffering a concussion, but regardless of how they got their opportunity, Fletcher and Knight are looking to bring more gold back to Don Callis at the expense of Matt and Nick Jackson. title: Kawada Surprises Taichi at NJPW School Show

body: NJPW were in Taichi’s old junior high school for a special homecoming event. Ahead of an all-star main event, Taichi was surprised with an appearance by his mentor and one of the four heavenly pillars, Toshiaki Kawada. Taichi made his entrance for the main event, wearing the sash as a special ambassador for his hometown, Ishikari. After that, the ring announcer revealed that Taichi’s teacher was here. Instead of one of Taichi’s old schoolteachers, his trainer, Toshiaki Kawada, made his way to the ring instead. Kawada took the microphone and spoke to his student: Taking the microphone after the match, Taichi addressed his opponents, his partner, his mentor and the hometown crowd: Marufuji, thank you for coming all the way out here for me, even taking time out of your NOAH schedule. Wrestling you here it made me think, how many more years can we still go? Our time is short, so next time, let’s make it a singles match. Some people think we’re done, but we got the loudest chants of the day. So next time, you and me one on one. And Kanemaru, you left? You let me down. But you still came here for the second year in a row, so maybe there’s something of me he’s fond for. So thank you. So maybe sometime we can do it again. Zack, thanks for answering the call. It was great to team with you again. Wouldn’t it be a shame if this was the last one? Let’s tag again sometime. You can see the Ishikari school motto here about making dreams come true. I never became a top wrestler like Kawada did, but I was able to do things he couldn’t. I was able to create something nobody else could and nobody else can, something that’s only mine. summary_src: All Elite Wrestling returns to pay-per-view tonight (Oct. 17) with WrestleDream 2026. The show comes our way from Addition Financial Arena in Orlando, Florida.
body: Link If you buy something from a link, Vox Media may earn a commission. See our ethics statement. All Elite Wrestling returns to pay-per-view tonight (Oct. 17) with WrestleDream 202 6. The show comes our way from Addition Financial Arena in Orlando, Florida. The event begins at 7 pm ET with both the Tailgate Brawl special on TNT and the Buy In pre-show on YouTube. That leads right into the PPV main card at 8 pm ET. Fans in the USA can purchase it from PPV.com , HBO Max , Amazon , DAZN , Fubo , and YouTube , or their cable or satellite provider. The show is also available on MyAEW for fans in the UK and many international markets. AEW only had a three week turnaround from All Out to WrestleDream, and some of that TV time was spent ignoring story development in order to pay tribute to PAC. Those time constraints were probably a factor in the creation of a new “ Clockwork Carnage ” gimmick match for the AEW world title that will be featured as the main event of WrestleDream. It takes a while to read and process all the rules for Clockwork Carnage. For the sake of simplicity, AEW has described it as a mashup of a Casino Gauntlet match (phase one) and an Iron Man match (phase two). If there is no funny business with the clock, it should last around 33 minutes, with 18 minutes for the first phase and 15 minutes for the second phase. Let’s see how exactly it works. The match features eight wrestlers competing across two phases. The Entry Phase starts with two men in the ring at random. A new competitor enters the match every three minutes until all eight stars have entered the fray. If anybody is pinned or submitted during this phase, they are eliminated from the match. Whichever wrestlers survive will make it to the Scoring Phase. This part of the match is a 15 minute scramble to see who scores the most pins or submissions. That wrestler will walk out of WrestleDream as the AEW world champion. It can be hard to make a somewhat complicated new gimmick match work in pro wrestling, but Tony Khan picked the right strategy to ensure Clockwork Carnage is a success. That obvious strategy is to take advantage of his very deep roster by loading up this brand new gimmick match with seven tremendous workers and Darby Allin. Will Ospreay is the defending AEW world champion and the best wrestler in the world. The seven challengers are Samoa Joe, Kazuchika Okada, Ricochet, Adam Copeland, Konosuke Takeshita, Speedball Bailey, and Darby. It’s an extremely impressive collection of star power and talent for the debut of Clockwork Carnage. How many competitors will be eliminated during the Entry Phase? How many falls will it take to win the Scoring Phase? Will finishing moves that normally don’t win a PPV match on the first try suddenly be way more effective at scoring pin falls tonight? What happens if there is a tie? Tune into WrestleDream to see how AEW pulls off the debut of Clockwork Carnage, and if the new concept looks like one with staying power to be an annual f

title: Je'Von Evans Details Promo and Physique Goals
raw_title: WWE Star Je'Von Evans Explains Aspects Of His Game He's Intent On Improving
summary_src: Je'Von Evans understands that making it to the WWE main roster isn't the end of his learning journey.
body: "When it comes to, you know, my mic skills, like I've been trying to work hard on just talking, you feel me," he explained during an interview on " The Rich Eisen Show ." Evans pointed out that he started his career on the indies at 13, and he never liked cutting promos, especially because he was facing adults and was aware that he'd come off as unbelievable. "Being signed to WWE has made me understand and made me, like, lock in when it comes to promos," he added. Evans explained that promos are easy when you break them down and work hard to get better at them. At the same time, he's glad that he's been given the opportunity to practice his promo skills live, and claims he's been working with Paul Heyman lately. "He understands that, like, I just talk so different. He worked with, you know, my unc', New Jack, so like he understands how I talk." Another aspect of his career that he's focused on is his physique, which Evans claims he's constantly working on improving as well. "I feel like it'll just be better and just easier when it comes to, like, longevity," he said. Evans argued that if he were to put on more muscle mass, he should reach a sweet spot where he can still be as explosive in the ring without putting unnecessary strain on his body.
summary: Je'Von Evans has been focusing on improving his microphone skills after beginning his career on the independent scene at age 13. The WWE star admitted he avoided promos early on because he felt inauthentic addressing adults but now treats them seriously since joining the company. He has been practicing live segments and recently working with Paul Heyman, while also consistently building his physique for better longevity and ring explosiveness without excess strain.

title: AEW WrestleDream 2026 Draws 6,695 Tickets
raw_title: AEW WrestleDream 2026 ticket sales update on day of show
summary_src: AEW WrestleDream has just under 6,700 tickets distributed. According to a report from WrestleTix on Saturday morning, 6,695 tickets have been distributed for tonight’s AEW pay-per-view at Addition Financial Arena in Orlando, Florida.
body: According to a report from WrestleTix on Saturday morning, 6,695 tickets have been distributed for tonight’s AEW pay-per-view at Addition Financial Arena in Orlando, Florida. WrestleTix notes that the number is an increase of 71 tickets from the 6,624 reported on Friday. The cheapest ticket available, or “get-in price,” is listed at $36.40. The show is trending to draw a crowd comparable to previous WrestleDream pay-per-views. The inaugural event in Seattle in 2023 drew a reported 6,771 fans. The 2024 edition in Tacoma drew a reported 8,045, while last year’s event at Chaifetz Arena in St. Louis drew a reported 6,293. WrestleDream is also trending to be one of AEW’s lowest-attended pay-per-views of 2026, and potentially the lowest. Revolution in Los Angeles drew a reported 12,577 fans, Dynasty in Vancouver drew 9,136, Double or Nothing in New York drew 14,394, and Forbidden Door in San Jose drew 9,021. Redemption in Montreal drew a reported 7,002 fans, All In in London drew 46,987, and All Out in Hoffman Estates drew 9,456. The figure represents a small increase from Friday's total of 6,624, with the lowest available ticket priced at $36.40. The attendance is expected to fall in line with prior WrestleDream events and rank among AEW's lowest-grossing pay-per-views of the year.

title: Injury Update: R-Truth Injury Causes SmackDown Match Against Damian Priest to Stop - TWNP-Wrestling News
raw_title: R-Truth Injury Causes SmackDown Match Against Damian Priest to Stop - TWNP-Wrestling News
body: After weeks of tension building between Damian Priest and R-Truth, Wepa Up imploded on SmackDown last night. The two traded hard-hitting blows in what was to be a highly personal matchup. Unfortunately, the match came to a screeching halt just four minutes into it. As John Cena’s biggest fan climbed to the top rope, R-Truth launched himself off with a Missile Dropkick. While Damian Priest went flying, R-Truth landed awkwardly. The former WWE Tag Team Champion took a regular flat-back bump, but immediately rolled to his left side. Moments later, the referee called for the bell. The match was stopped due to R-Truth sustaining a legitimate injury. Coming out of SmackDown, backstage reports indicate that R-Truth suffered a shoulder injury. Suffice to say, R-Truth shouldn’t take a shoulder injury lightly. That’s why the official ended the match, and WWE scrambled to finish the segment. Damian Priest defeated R-Truth on last night’s SmackDown due to match stoppage. The match went just over four minutes. Initially, it was slotted to go for about ten minutes. So, R-Truth’s injury was not part of the storyline. Plus, R-Truth was scheduled to be involved in the aftermath. Therefore, WWE had to scramble and figure out a way to progress the story, kill some time, and not injure R-Truth further. Fraxiom still came down to tend to the WWE legend. Instead of beating his former partner down, Damian Priest grabbed a steel chair. The former World Champion threatened to decimate R-Truth with the weapon. However, Axiom and Nathan Frazer ran down to shield the former US Champion. It looks like Damian Priest will feud with the former NXT Tag Team Champions in the coming months.
summary: The latest: after weeks of tension building between Damian Priest and R-Truth, Wepa Up imploded on SmackDown last night. Damian Priest got the win over R-Truth on last night’s SmackDown due to match stoppage.

title: David Finlay Reveals Early WWE Career Plan
raw_title: AEW's David Finlay Recalls WWE Ambitions Prior To NJPW Run
summary_src: AEW star David Finlay recalls having WWE ambitions prior to his New Japan run, and how his plan of six months in NJPW turned into eleven years
body: "When I was fifteen, I sat down with my dad and was like 'No, this [wrestling] is what I want to do with my life,'" Finlay said. "He was like 'Alright. Here's the plan. You should do amateur wrestling, which Nattie Neidhart also told me to do that. And I did. And then from there, it was like 'Alright. You're going to go to England and Germany for a bit. And then go and do the [New Japan] Dojo for six months, And then go to 'NXT' or FCW, whatever it was at the time. And then six months in Japan turned into eleven years, cause I loved it so much."
summary: David Finlay decided at age 15 that he wanted to pursue professional wrestling. His father outlined a path that included amateur wrestling, experience in England and Germany, a six-month stint at the New Japan Pro-Wrestling dojo, and then joining WWE's developmental system. The planned half-year in Japan instead became an 11-year stay because Finlay enjoyed it so much.

title: Samoa Joe Pushes Back on Old-School Wrestling Rule About Protecting Finishers
raw_title: Samoa Joe Pushes Back on Old-School Wrestling Rule About Protecting Finishers
summary_src: Samoa Joe isn’t buying one of professional wrestling’s longest-running unwritten rules as an absolute truth.
body: During an interview with SHAK Wrestling , Joe was given a series of wrestling hot takes and unwritten rules and asked to give his opinion on them. One of those involved protecting a wrestler’s finisher. The old-school philosophy is pretty straightforward: if too many opponents kick out of your finishing move, the move eventually stops feeling like something that can actually finish a match. Joe wasn’t willing to make it that simple. Instead, Joe said the answer depends entirely on the performer because wrestling history gives plenty of examples on both sides. Some stars protected their finishing moves and got everything possible out of them, while others allowed plenty of kickouts and still became major stars. “You know, once again, I feel it is circumstantial on the performer because I’ve seen successful performers who have absolutely protected their finisher and have maximized its utility to the best of their ability. And I’ve seen other ones who’ve been wildly successful and haven’t.” That’s why Joe believes declaring that every wrestler must protect a finishing move is taking an unnecessarily rigid position on something where the evidence isn’t nearly that clear. Joe said he would rather look at the actual results and compare how many performers succeeded using both philosophies. That makes Joe’s position even more interesting. He isn’t arguing that protecting a finishing move has no value. He’s saying there simply isn’t one formula that every wrestler needs to follow, especially when decades of wrestling have produced successful stars using completely different approaches. He believes there has to be genuine belief and repentance behind it. “Will the majority of them go to heaven? Probably not. And I’m going to live forever outside of the kingdom of God, and I don’t want to do that. I want to be inside the kingdom of God.’” For Venis, none of this depends on how ugly someone’s past might be. title: On the Record: Samoa Joe Calls Fear-Based Locker Room Leader Mentality a ‘Ridiculous Ideology’
raw_title: Samoa Joe Calls Fear-Based Locker Room Leader Mentality a ‘Ridiculous Ideology’
summary_src: Samoa Joe has zero problem with someone being considered a locker room leader, but he has a big problem with the idea that leadership should come from fear.
body: “I just, I think, I don’t think it’s, let me rephrase. I think being a locker room leader isn’t, I think, how a lot of people think it as is or is described. You know, the truth of it is the locker room leader is usually somebody that everybody kind of universally respects because, you know, they usually conduct themselves in a professional way. They have a fair and even mindedness about how they approach things and how they see situations and, you know, they make moves in an effort for the betterment of, you know, kind of all them, you know, people around them and for the benefit of the company and, you know, being making money, drawing money, all that kind of good stuff. Best for business, all the buzzwords.” Joe continued by explaining that real leaders aren’t followed because people are scared of them. They’re followed because others respect their knowledge and actually care about what they have to say. “And really that’s kind of, you know, I think what you would base it off of. And really a locker room leader, I, you know, I think no great men is led by fear. They’re usually led by people that they respect and that they find knowledgeable and that they, you know, that they give a [inaudible] about their opinion.” From there, Joe explained that becoming a leader starts with something much simpler: earning basic respect and building relationships with the people around you. “So I think it’s the first thing, just kind of, you know, establish some basic respect and establish a rapport with people and, you know, if they choose to respect you, they choose to like you and you find yourself in that position, then so be it.” “But I think this idea of, you know, this physically domineering presence who will bury your career if you don’t adhere to the unwritten book of laws is a ridiculous ideology. And I mean, I’ve never come up across it and I’ve never felt pressured by that or something like that. So, I just think it’s kind of a weird fallacy, you know.” “I think a lot of people respect the Undertaker because they respect the Undertaker as a person, you know, not out of some type of, you know, career fear.” That distinction is especially interesting considering The Undertaker’s history running Wrestlers Court backstage in WWE. The Undertaker previously explained why he believed Wrestlers Court was necessary , saying it was intended as a way to correct problems without every backstage issue becoming an ugly confrontation. Joe has also been viewed as exactly the type of leader he described. Bobby Fish previously named Samoa Joe as the person he considered AEW’s locker room leader , explaining that if Joe had something to say, he was going to listen. title: Cena retirement triple autograph card surfaces
raw_title: 1-of-1 triple autograph trading card from John Cena’s retirement has been found
body: Cena, who had a record 17 WWE world title reigns during his career, faced off with Gunther and lost at Saturday Night's Main Event on December 13 last year. After the match, many superstars and other personnel came out to the ring to celebrate the wrestler, including Cody Rhodes and CM Punk. Punk and Rhodes held both the main men's titles at the time and handed them to Cena for him to hold one last time, a moment that has since been immortalised in a 1-of-1 Topps trading card. The card in question was autographed by Punk, Rhodes and Cena, no doubt making it a very desirable collector's item. Now, Topps have confirmed that the unique card has been found, writing on X: "The 1-of-1 Cody Rhodes/John Cena/CM Punk triple autograph from Cena's retirement just surfaced on Facebook." The card does not appear to have been graded by whoever found it yet. But if they are able to secure a PSA 10, it could end up being worth a significant amount of money. For some context, a 1-of-1 autographed John Cena WrestleMania 41-used patch card, which was graded a PSA 8, reportedly sold for $329,400 last month, making it the highest public sale for any wrestling card. title: Mike Bailey Explains Benefits Of Wrestling Barefoot
raw_title: Mike Bailey Discusses Pros And Cons Of Wrestling Barefoot
summary_src: Mike Bailey reveals the advantages and disadvantages of wrestling barefoot. Over the years, Bailey has made a name for himself by going to the ring and competing without shoes. Instead, 'Speedball' just wears kickpads that strap to the bottom of his feet.
body: Mike Bailey reveals the advantages and disadvantages of wrestling barefoot. Over the years, Bailey has made a name for himself by going to the ring and competing without shoes. Instead, ‘Speedball’ just wears kickpads that strap to the bottom of his feet. Speaking with Fightful’s Sean Ross Sapp for a new interview, Mike Bailey said that he has very few injury issues when it comes to his feet. “No, I don’t. I have very few feet issues. I mean, I’ve hurt some toes. I think I’ve broken some toes, but I just pop them back in. It’s the kind of thing where it’s not gonna get worse. If you break a toe and you snap it back, you can’t break it more. It’s just gonna heal and be fine. Back in my Taekwondo days, I would have chronic turf toe, just feet constantly bruised from kicking elbows.” Bailey continued by explaining the advantages of wrestling without shoes. “But it is easily outweighed by the advantages of wrestling barefoot for me. The main one that people don’t think of is ropes. When I’m standing on the top rope and I can grab the rope with my toes and when I do a springboard, you can see my feet curl around the rope and I get extra balance that way. I love wrestling barefoot and I’m glad that I get to do it in a place like All Elite Wrestling that actually embraces the individuality of the wrestlers and that’s something that’s very important for me. Again, the emphasis is on letting the wrestlers be the best and that includes being the best versions of themselves, which, in my case, is wrestling without boots or shoes.” “I don’t take off my shoes backstage. I’m usually in flip flops. I try to try to keep my best, and of course, you have to keep them clean. But also it’s funny because I think what I’m doing is a lot more sanitary than the wrestlers who will wear their boots backstage, go to the urinal in boots and then stomp you in the face in the middle of the ring and no one bats an eye. No one disinfects their wrestling boots before a match. I think it’s fair. I don’t think we have to. I’ve not had any facial infections from dirty wrestling boots and I don’t know why my bare feet would be more of a concern, where I think it’s in fact less.” Bailey then revealed that being barefoot actually slows him down in the ring. “This is absolutely correct. However, one issue, I don’t think I can run as fast. I think I can run faster barefoot than the people in the thick boots. But I think people who wrestle in running shoes, some wrestling shoes with very grippy soles, I think that can help, especially depending on the canvas. If you have a brand new canvas or that has a painted logo, sometimes that gets really tricky. If you’ve ever wrestled on one of those vinyl canvases. Those can get terrible. They can get slippery, they can get wet just from it gets cooler as the show goes on, condensation happens and it just becomes a puddle. That can be an issue. Also, one thing that I’ve done before which is wrestle on a vinyl canvas in the blistering summer heat.
summary: Mike Bailey has built his career competing without shoes, opting only for kickpads strapped to his feet. He reports minimal foot injuries, noting that broken toes can simply be reset and heal without worsening. The Speedball star highlighted superior balance and grip on the ropes as the biggest advantage, which he is able to utilize in All Elite Wrestling.

title: John Cena Pushes For WrestleMania In London
raw_title: John Cena Continues To Advocate For WrestleMania In London
summary_src: At WWE Money in the Bank 2023 in London, John Cena made an appearance and stated that WrestleMania should be held in London. Three years later, Cena hasn't backed down from his stance. "I’m still an advocate to try and bring WrestleMania to London.
body: At WWE Money in the Bank 2023 in London, John Cena made an appearance and stated that WrestleMania should be held in London. “I’m still an advocate to try and bring WrestleMania to London. I think London has earned the right to have the event. I am very excited about this year’s WrestleMania because it is the first WrestleMania outside of North America. It’s like proof of concept that it can be done. I am still a strong advocate that this crowd, this city, has earned the right to WrestleMania. What little stroke I have, I try to rile up the crowd a few times to say London has earned WrestleMania, and it did get people talking. I don’t know where those talks are at, but hopefully, maybe I can return to the O2 and stake that claim again,” he said on Off The Menu with Ed Gamble and James Acaster . Asked if anyone knew Cena would advocate for WrestleMania in London at WWE Money in the Bank, Cena said, “That was just me putting it out there. Honestly, it’s just my perspective. I look around and see the energy, passion, and enthusiasm. What a great city for people to come to. WrestleMania is such a travel to event. It’s one of my favorite cities in the world. I think it’d be a nice piece of culture for people to explore and experience WrestleMania. We need to do WrestleMania here.” If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.

title: Channing Lorenzo Hospitalized After NXT Live Event Injury
raw_title: Channing ‘Stacks’ Lorenzo reportedly hospitalized after injury at NXT live event
summary_src: Channing “Stacks” Lorenzo was reportedly taken to hospital after suffering an injury during the main event of Friday’s WWE NXT live event in Sudbury, Ontario.
body: Channing “Stacks” Lorenzo was reportedly taken to hospital after suffering an injury during the main event of Friday’s WWE NXT live event in Sudbury, Ontario. The match pitted BirthRight members Lorenzo, Lexis King, Charlie Dempsey & Uriah Connors against Tony D’Angelo, Tavion Heights, Shiloh Hill & Shawn Spears at Sudbury Community Arena. A fan who attended the event reported on Reddit that Lorenzo was injured while taking a back body drop from the ring to the floor. Another attendee wrote that Lorenzo may have struck his head on the ring post before landing heavily on his back. The referee signaled for medical assistance and the match was stopped. Lorenzo was fitted with a neck brace before being placed on a stretcher and taken from ringside. Bryan Alvarez of the Wrestling Observer subsequently reported that Lorenzo was in hospital following the incident. No details regarding the nature or severity of the injury have been reported. Spears then addressed the audience, acknowledging what had occurred and thanking those in attendance. He said WWE’s wrestlers and fans were “one big family” and apologized that the show had ended under those circumstances. As of publication, neither WWE nor Lorenzo had provided an update on his condition. Lorenzo is currently part of BirthRight alongside Dempsey, King, Connors and Arianna Grace. WWE’s official profile lists him as a former NXT Tag Team Champion and NXT Heritage Cup Champion. He and Connors also recently represented BirthRight in the Dusty Rhodes Tag Team Classic , losing in the opening round to Mini Vikingo & Chazz “Starboy” Hall.
summary: Channing Lorenzo suffered an injury during the main event of a WWE NXT live show in Sudbury, Ontario on Friday. The BirthRight member was taking a back body drop from the ring to the floor when the incident occurred, leading to the match being halted. He was fitted with a neck brace, placed on a stretcher and transported to hospital, with no update yet on the injury's severity.

title: Darby Allin And Steve Borden Praise Sting's AEW Happiness
raw_title: Darby Allin And Steve Borden Say Sting Had 'More Fun In AEW Than Anyone Else'
body: During an interview with " Q101 ," Borden recalled coming to AEW shows while his father still competed in the promotion. "I think he had more fun in AEW than he had anywhere else," Borden said about his father's time there, attributing that happiness in part to his relationships with the talent backstage and AEW President Tony Khan. "That's the happiest that I've seen him with whoever it is that's managing a company. His relationship was so good, and yes, of course, I think he felt extremely respected." Allin then chimed in, describing AEW as a place where he also feels happy and calling it the "greatest thing" to ever happen in his life. "Without a doubt, and I think a lot of it has to deal with Tony actually letting the wrestlers outside of the ring – and inside of the ring – live their best lives," he explained. He then added that wrestlers often see the industry chew people up and spit them back out, leaving them with nothing while they have to juggle staying relevant in wrestling and their personal lives. Unlike other promoters, Khan seems to understand those pressures, according to Allin, and urges the wrestlers to focus on their personal lives. AEW Sting's final match in WWE was at Night of Champions 2015, where he suffered an injury after a Buckle Bomb by Seth Rollins, forcing him to retire . Based on this, Darby Allin felt like Sting needed to step back into the ring and end things on his terms. "It wasn't a lot of convincing; I felt like he, the moment we were rolling around and he took a couple of bumps, he's like, 'I feel pretty good,'" he recalled. "The fact that he came into the company during the Pandemic , because a lot of people, with their egos," he said, "they'd be like, 'Well, if I'm going to debut, I'm gonna have to come in when it's a sold-out, packed house.'"
summary: Steve Borden said his father Sting enjoyed his time in AEW more than anywhere else in his career, crediting strong backstage relationships and respect from Tony Khan. Darby Allin agreed, calling AEW the greatest thing in his life and highlighting how Khan encourages wrestlers to prioritize their personal lives outside the ring instead of burning out. Allin noted that many promoters fail to understand the pressures wrestlers face balancing their careers and well-being.

title: Results Recap: A Dictator's Guide to Tonight's Big PPV — AEW WrestleDream Preview
raw_title: AEW WrestleDream Preview: A Dictator's Guide to Tonight's Big PPV
body: Posted in: AEW , Sports , TV | Tagged: AEW WrestleDream , wrestling Comrades! El Presidente previews AEW WrestleDream's historic Clockwork Carnage match and seven title bouts from his luxury yacht. ¡Viva la revolución! Greetings, comrades! It is I, your beloved El Presidente, reporting to you live from my luxury viewing suite aboard my nuclear-powered yacht currently anchored off the coast of Orlando, where tonight AEW WrestleDream makes its historic first visit to the Sunshine State. My faithful capybara Esteban and I have been preparing all day for what promises to be a magnificent celebration of wrestling excellence, complete with imported caviar, vintage rum, and a satellite uplink the CIA tried three times to disable. Those capitalist fools never learn! Tonight's spectacle features an unprecedented eight matches, seven of which involve championship gold, headlined by the first-ever Clockwork Carnage Match for the AEW World Championship. This diabolical creation reminds me of the time I explained my revolutionary five-year economic plan to Fidel Castro and Kim Jong-un during our annual dictators' poker night in Pyongyang. Dennis Rodman was there too, naturally. The rules were complex, the stakes were high, and by the end, nobody could remember who actually won, but everyone agreed it was spectacular entertainment. Much like Clockwork Carnage, comrades! The main card of AEW WrestleDream begins at 8 p.m. ET/5 p.m. PT on HBO Max PPV, with the AEW Saturday Tailgate Brawl kicking off an hour earlier at 7 p.m. ET/4 p.m. PT, airing live coast-to-coast on TNT and HBO Max. This is the fourth annual AEW WrestleDream, continuing the tradition of honoring NJPW founder Antonio Inoki and his contributions to professional wrestling. Inoki understood what I have always known: true greatness requires vision, courage, and occasionally dropping people on their heads. Tonight, the first-ever Clockwork Carnage Match is Ospreay's own creation. When Tony Khan asked him what he wanted for his WrestleDream title defense, Ospreay called upon his Casino Gauntlet experience, having won the first two gauntlets, and the result is a match unlike anything AEW has presented. Here's how it works: Clockwork Carnage features eight wrestlers, two stages and one winner. Stage 1: Two wrestlers selected at random start the match, and every 3 minutes, another randomly selected wrestler enters until all eight have entered. Anyone who is pinned or submits before all eight have entered is eliminated and does not move on to Stage 2. Stage 2: Once the final wrestler enters, all remaining wrestlers enter a 15-minute scoring period. Every pinfall or submission scores one fall, and when time expires, the wrestler with the most falls wins and leaves as AEW World Champion. That makes Clockwork Carnage a mash-up of a Casino Gauntlet and an Iron Man match with many possibilities. A wrestler could beat the champion and not win the match, and Ospreay could lose the title without ever being pinned

title: Jacy Jayne Describes Out-of-Body Title Win
raw_title: Jacy Jayne Had 'Out Of Body Experience' Beating Stephanie Vaquer For WWE NXT Title
summary_src: Looking back at her WWE NXT Women's Championship victory, Jacy Jayne recalled being in disbelief.
body: During an interview with Denise Salcedo , Jayne looked back at the match and her state of mind when she picked up the win. "It didn't really feel like it was happening," she recalled. "I felt like I was having almost an out-of-body experience that day." Jayne explained that she envisioned the moment happening for so long, but when it finally arrived, she was in disbelief. The online reaction to Jayne's victory was largely negative, as many fans were unhappy to see one of "NXT's" biggest babyfaces, Vaquer, lose her title after being cheated out of it. Vaquer's reign ultimately lasted just 77 days. But according to Jayne, the criticisms didn't bother her in the slightest. "You couldn't write anything better! People were so mad," she recalled. She then pointed out how she was viewed as an "underdog" for a long time, which didn't make sense to her, especially after everything she accomplished in "NXT." "I really don't know what I have to do to show everyone that I am 'That Girl.' I am the 'It Girl!'" While she can't seem to wrap her head around the things fans say online, Jayne claims that she loves the hate she gets and especially loves when people underestimate her or crowds boo her. "It just keeps making me work harder and it makes me want it more, 'cause I love to rub it in your face," she said.
summary: Jacy Jayne captured the NXT Women's Championship from Stephanie Vaquer in a match that felt surreal to her. She described experiencing an out-of-body sensation as the long-envisioned moment finally arrived, leaving her in disbelief. Vaquer's 77-day reign ended amid heavy fan backlash over the finish, but Jayne said the negative reactions only fuel her drive as she embraces her role as the despised 'It Girl.'

title: Perry Saturn Opens Up On Condition After Hospitalization Over Severe Respiratory Issues
raw_title: Perry Saturn Reveals Condition After Hospitalization Over Severe Respiratory Issues
summary_src: Perry Saturn has finally explained just how bad his recent health scare got, and it sounds like he went through a brutal few days.
body: “This is the third f***ing time I’ve had COVID. That seems a bit much to me. And I wasn’t getting better. So, I had to go back to the emergency room. I can’t breathe. I’m hacking up stuff. I had no sound would come out of my voice. Nothing. I couldn’t make a sound.” “And I have a URI, upper respiratory infection, that they just started treating. And two days into treatment, I’m up and moving around.” “The URI is what I think really got me. You know, I was hacking up — because I’ve had COVID three times now. So, the first time I got it was really bad. The second time wasn’t that bad. This time, I’m not sure because I got this infection, too, which maybe I got because of COVID. I don’t know.” “But I was hacking up this yellow, this cream-colored, like rubber almost. It was coming up, you know, and I couldn’t breathe. So I had to go back to the hospital. And I was there for like 48 hours in the emergency room.” The hospital stay wasn’t exactly smooth either. Saturn recalled being there for around 24 hours when a doctor told him they still didn’t know what was wrong, something that obviously wasn’t reassuring when he was having such a hard time breathing. “I’m there now 24 hours, about, I’m in the emergency room, and the doctor tells me, ‘Well, I have no idea what’s wrong with you.’ Okay, well, we got to figure something out because I can’t go home, you know.” Thankfully, Saturn is now doing considerably better. He confirmed that he’s recovering after beginning treatment, even if he’s clearly not back to 100 percent yet. “I’m better. I’m getting there, man. I have like f***ing luck sometimes. I don’t know what the deal is.” Saturn didn’t downplay how hard the upper respiratory infection hit him either. He said there was a point where he could barely get himself up because of how badly it had knocked him around. “This URI was brutal. It just knocked my d*** in the dirt. I couldn’t get up, man. It was f***ing brutal.” Perhaps the most encouraging update came when Saturn described how much easier it had become to breathe and move around. He used a very wrestling-specific comparison to explain just how crushing the pressure on his chest had felt at its worst. “I felt like I had Yokozuna sitting on my chest with Rikishi on his lap. I just felt like I couldn’t expand. And now I’m getting up, moving around better, you know.” H Jenkins H Jenkins has been breaking pro wrestling news on Ringside News for nearly a decade, with his reports featured by TMZ, Forbes, The Sun, and more.
summary: This is the third f***ing time I’ve had COVID. So, I had to go back to the emergency room.

title: Pac's Cause of Death Revealed as Bronchial Asthma
raw_title: Pro Wrestler Benjamin Satterley Cause Of Death Determined
body: Champion professional wrestler Benjamin Satterley died last month at 40 of bronchial asthma, Chicago’s Cook County Medical Examiner’s Office has determined. The death was classified as natural. The cause of death was first reported by The New York Post and has been confirmed by other media outlets. Satterley, who over the years wrestled for AEW and WWE under various names including Pac, Bastard, Adrian Neville and Neville, died September 27, one day after he was featured (as Pac) at AEW’s All Out pay-per-view from Chicago. He had lost the AEW National Championship to Andrade El Idolo. His death was announced by AEW in a statement reading, “A native of Newcastle upon Tyne, England, Satterley began his wrestling career in 2004 and went on to perform for wrestling organizations all over the world, captivating fans with innovative high-flying moves and incredible in-ring ability. Pac signed with All Elite Wrestling in 2019 and held multiple AEW Championships and competed in some of the most memorable matches in AEW history. Our condolences go out to Satterley’s family, friends and fans.” Watch on Deadline

Roman’s got the Street Fighter out right now so he’s doing some big things. But I think I’ll eclipse him in that area. Then I gotta beat Roman because I’ve never beat him. One of the things, I’ve got these swords here so if it comes to–Because Roman’s got 95 family members, I may have to bring the sword back. I can’t say I had the sword in WWE for years, I never used it. Shockingly so, PG product. But Agent of Shadows, I’m telling you right now, I finally used the sword.” If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.

title: Willow Nightingale Shares Imposter Syndrome Coping Strategy
raw_title: AEW's Willow Nightingale Explains How She Deals With Imposter Syndrome
summary_src: Former AEW Women's World Champion Willow Nightingale has revealed how she is able to talk herself out of feeling imposter syndrome leading up to major shows.
body: "So I sometimes kind of deal with imposter syndrome a little bit, where I'm like, 'I don't know how I got in this position. I don't know what I'm doing here. How did I get here?'" she answered. "One of the ways that I counter-act that is, before I ever go out or the day before a big show, ... I'll tell myself, 'You wouldn't be in this position accidentally. Nobody would let that happen by mistake, so clearly you've been doing something right that helped you get here.'" Nightingale acknowledged that she's also had to deal with injuries during matches, including a broken hand heading into that show in particular. However, it's the internal struggles that can often be more difficult to manage, with Nightingale describing an injury as more of a "logistical" problem to deal with. Despite the recent injury, Nightingale has remained active in the ring following her title loss. She wrestled Thekla at AEW All Out in a number-one contender's match but fell short, and then took part in a match at AEW Grand Slam: France.
summary: AEW star Willow Nightingale revealed she battles imposter syndrome by reminding herself that she earned her spot and no one reaches that level by accident. She noted that physical injuries like her broken hand are logistical issues compared to mental hurdles. Nightingale has stayed active since losing her title, competing at All Out in a number-one contender bout against Thekla and later at Grand Slam: France.

title: End of an Era: Drew McIntyre Shuts Down Retirement Talk Despite Growing Hollywood Career

summary_src: Drew McIntyre may be getting some serious opportunities in Hollywood, but anyone thinking that means his WWE career is winding down can forget about it.
body: McIntyre explained that he already has an understanding with WWE President Nick Khan and Paul “Triple H” Levesque when it comes to outside opportunities. If something worthwhile comes along, they will figure out how to make it work without Drew having to walk away from WWE. “This is home. I’m not going anywhere. This is like we have an understanding of talking with Nick and Paul that if something good comes up, we do that. But I’m a full-time wrestler. I just turned 41.” Drew then made his plans for the future even clearer. Despite being 41 and already finding success outside the wrestling business, he doesn’t see himself slowing down anytime soon. “I’m going to be here for years. So don’t expect me to disappear anytime soon.” That declaration comes at an interesting time for McIntyre. He admitted during the same interview that he has been away from wrestling for more than five months, which is longer than any previous absence in his career. Even when he tore his biceps after returning to WWE in 2017, Drew said he was only out for around three months. That arrangement appears to be something McIntyre is comfortable with going forward. Hollywood may be giving him opportunities he never expected, but he clearly doesn’t view acting as an escape route from professional wrestling. title: On the Record: Becky Lynch Opens Up On Vince McMahon’s Reaction When She Told Him She Was Pregnant
raw_title: Becky Lynch Reveals Vince McMahon’s Reaction When She Told Him She Was Pregnant
summary_src: Becky Lynch was one of WWE’s biggest stars when she found out she was pregnant, but telling Vince McMahon she was leaving still had her shaking. Lynch has now revealed exactly how that conversation went down, and McMahon’s reaction wasn’t anything close to what she feared.
body: Lynch said she can only speak from her own experience, but WWE was incredibly supportive when she became pregnant. The stakes were especially high because Lynch wasn’t simply another wrestler on the roster at the time. She was champion and described herself as one of, if not the biggest star in WWE. That’s why walking into the conversation with McMahon was so nerve-racking. “Look, I think wrestling’s particularly tricky. I can only speak for myself and say WWE were amazing to me. Like when I told them, and I was the champion at the time, I was a huge star. I was one of, if not the biggest star in the company at the time. And I had to tell Vince McMahon, ‘Hey, I’m leaving. I’m gonna go have a kid.’ And I was shaking.” Whatever Lynch expected to happen disappeared almost immediately. She said McMahon didn’t hesitate before congratulating her and telling her how happy he was about the news. “He didn’t miss a beat. And he was like, ‘Oh my God, congratulations. That is the best news that I’ve ever heard. I’m so happy for you.’” Lynch was actually the person trying to figure out how she could continue providing something for WWE while she was away. She even started throwing out ideas for projects she could work on during her pregnancy. McMahon wasn’t interested in putting that kind of pressure on her. “And I kept trying to pitch him ideas like, ‘Here’s how I can be useful. I can make a documentary. I don’t know.’ I was just trying to give him something, you know, and he was just like, ‘Oh, no. This is the best. This is amazing.’” That same attitude carried over to Lynch’s eventual WWE comeback. According to her, the company never gave her a deadline or pushed her to return to training before she felt comfortable. “And there was no pressure of, ‘You have to be back. Come on, let’s get back in the gym. Let’s go.’ They were very much like, ‘Whenever you feel ready.’ And I was the one like, ‘I’m ready. I’m ready. Let’s go. Get me back in there, coach.’” Lynch announced her pregnancy on WWE television in May 2020 and relinquished the RAW Women’s Championship before stepping away. She ultimately returned to WWE at SummerSlam in August 2021 and quickly found herself back in the championship picture. Considering how nervous Lynch was before telling McMahon, his immediate reaction clearly stuck with her years later. Instead of being treated like WWE was losing its biggest star, Lynch says she was treated like someone who had just received some of the best news of her life. title: AEW's Pac Died of Natural Causes
raw_title: AEW Star 'Pac' Benjamin Satterley's Cause of Death Confirmed by Medical Examiner
body: A spokesperson for the Cook County Medical Examiner's Office in Chicago shared the findings Friday with Edward Lewis of the California Post . Pac, whose real name was Benjamin Satterley, was found unconscious in a rental car in the parking lot of a Des Plaines, Illinois, restaurant on Sept. 27, and he was later pronounced dead. Copeland To Retire in 2027 ‼️ Bleacher Report 2d Grading SmackDown 🔠 Bleacher Report 14h Dynamite Results & Reaction 🔠 Bleacher Report 2d The Cook County Medical Examiner's Office ruled that Pac's death was natural. One day earlier, Pac wrestled on AEW's All Out card, which took place at Now Arena in Hoffman Estates, Illinois. In the opening match of the show, Pac challenged Andrade El Idolo for the National Championship. Andrade prevailed in what was a highly regarded bout. Originally from Newcastle upon Tyne, England, Pac was part of AEW since its inception in 2019, and he went on to hold the All-Atlantic Championship once and World Trios Championships twice. Prior to joining AEW, Pac wrestled under the names Neville and Adrian Neville in WWE from 2012 to 2018. As part of the NXT roster, Pac was a one-time NXT champion and two-time NXT tag team champion, and he later held the WWE Cruiserweight Championship twice.

title: AEW WrestleDream Feud Tracker Highlights
raw_title: AEW FEUD TRACKER: Barber’s evaluation of the feuds headed into WrestleDream including Clockwork Carnage, Wayne-Jericho, Mercedes-Thekla
body: Another PPV is upon us as WresteDream takes places tonight live from Orlando, Fla. Look, the build to this PPV has been rushed and barely surface-level, but it’s hard for me to be too critical. AEW lost a week due to the sudden death of Pac and it’s likely some things had to be changed as well. They did themselves no favors scheduling this event so soon after All Out while also scheduling Grand Slam France right in the middle. “Speedball” Mike Bailey, Adam Copeland, Kazuchika Okada, Samoa Joe, Ricochet, Konosuke Takeshita, and Darby Allin all qualified to challenge Will Ospreay for the AEW World Heavyweight Title in Clockwork Carnage. As I said in the intro, I like the match concept and the full field of competitors is pretty strong. While I appreciate that Okada, Takeshita et al had to qualify, the qualifying matches themselves were extremely predictable. Maybe the most interesting thing to happen in any of the qualifiers was Takeshita tapping Brian Cage out with a Dragon Sleeper. Adding that move to his repertoire is a nice touch. The rules are clear and the having to score points in a certain amount of time gives it a very sports-like feel. Ospreay is almost certainly winning, but I do wonder if this match helps set up Ospreay’s next one-on-one feud with maybe Ricochet or even Adam Copeland who announced that he is winding down his career. Thekla got the win in a trios match alongside the Sisters of Sin ahead of her title match with Mercedes Moné. The Triangle of Madness teamed up to fight Mercedes Moné and Divine Dominion. The match was fine and Thekla picked up the win on Lena Kross. Her match against Mercedes on Saturday will be very good and Mercedes is winning. That’s all well and good. She’s gotten over as a babyface because her unique energy and irreverent promo style yet she’s still teaming with Julia Hart and Skye Blue. At this point, she’s outgrown them yet they’re tethered together because they are the Artist of Stardom champions. This needs to be rectified soon because I think Thekla could a future as a strong face if she just shed the dead weight. The New Level, with a largely unknown comedian, cut a disappointing go-home promo for their two-out-of-three falls match against The Good, The Bad, and The Ugly. Swerve Strickland was out dealing with family matter according to Prince Nana. In his place, he sent a friend of his, Mojo Brookz. This happened backstage and that’s where things immediately went off the rails. According to Google, Brookz is a “nationally acclaimed stand-up comedian.” The problem is, I’ve never heard of him. The minute he got on TV backstage, it was clear he had no business being there. He was way too performative and silly. The New Level would’ve done better cutting the promo by themselves. They wouldn’t have had to play of Brookz and his goofiness. The feud is built around the long-standing rivalry between “Hangman” Page and Swerve Strickland which is deadly serious. It deserved better than this promo. Thankfu
summary: WrestleDream takes place tonight in Orlando after a rushed build impacted by the sudden death of Pac and tight scheduling around All Out and Grand Slam France. Will Ospreay defends the AEW World Heavyweight Championship against seven qualifiers in the Clockwork Carnage match featuring Speedball Mike Bailey, Adam Copeland, Kazuchika Okada, Samoa Joe, Ricochet, Konosuke Takeshita and Darby Allin. The multi-man bout features a points-based system with a sports-like feel, Takeshita added a Dragon Sleeper submission during qualifiers, and Ospreay is heavily favored to retain while potentially setting up a future singles program.

The post-match action gave us a brief glimpse of Clockwork Carnage when all eight participants brawled to end the night! In addition, Mark Davis pinned AEW Continental Champion Jon Moxley in the opening trios match before they meet at WrestleDream for the Continental Title. Thekla sent a big message to AEW Women’s World Champion Mercedes Moné with a statement victory in a huge trios battle. title: On the Record: Cody Rhodes Says He Wouldn’t Wear Stardust Face Paint Again Even for One Day
raw_title: Cody Rhodes Says He Wouldn’t Wear Stardust Face Paint Again Even for One Day
summary_src: Cody Rhodes has made it crystal clear that Stardust is staying dead. While speaking with Overtime, Cody was asked to choose between wearing the Stardust face paint for 14 days or rocking Guile’s flat-top haircut for an entire year. He did not hesitate.
body: While speaking with Overtime , Cody was asked to choose between wearing the Stardust face paint for 14 days or rocking Guile’s flat-top haircut for an entire year. He did not hesitate. “I would rather always do the Guile haircut. I mean, a year is a long time, so you’re committing. I can’t see a world where I would want the Stardust face paint for one day. So I definitely would go with the Guile flat top.” That is about as blunt as Cody could get without outright burying the gimmick. Stardust was one of the final characters Cody portrayed before leaving WWE in 2016, and he has spent years building a completely different identity since then. Now, even the idea of putting that face paint back on for a single day sounds like a hard no. The Guile look is a different story. Cody plays Guile in Street Fighter , which hit theaters on October 16, while Roman Reigns stars as Akuma. Rhodes has fully leaned into the role, even showing up at UFC 332 dressed as Guile . His involvement in the movie also grew after filming started. Cody’s role was expanded after producers saw his performance , and Andrew Schulz later revealed that hours of Cody Rhodes footage never made the final cut . So if Cody has to pick between looking like Guile for a year or looking like Stardust for two weeks, the choice is apparently not even close. Stardust may still live on in WWE history, but Cody Rhodes clearly does not want that paint anywhere near his face again. body: DaParty was a subgroup within Austin Creed, a.k.a. Xavier Woods’ UpUpDownDown YouTube channel. DaParty consisted of Creed, Adam Cole, Claudio Castagnoli, and Tyler Breeze. Creed went on to state that he would love to do something with video games in AEW, but the main thing would be establishing rapport in the locker room. He said the reason UpUpDownDown worked so well in WWE is because he knew those individuals for years. WWE owns the UpUpDownDown channel. summary_src: Andrade’s first AEW exit was not about some explosive fallout with Tony Khan or a backstage war. The AEW star says his decision came down to choosing between his career and his personal life, and at that point, he felt he had to put the latter first. During an appearance on Close Up with Renee ...
body: “Professionally is a little sad because one, my contract was expired in this moment, so I need to pick a decision. Like I need to go for my personal life because I was married in this moment, or my professional life.” In the end, Andrade said he chose his personal life. He also made it clear there was no ugly breakup with AEW on his way out. Andrade said he went directly to Tony Khan, thanked him for the opportunity and left the door open for them to cross paths again. “So I pick my personal life and need to make a decision, but I went with Tony and say thank you for the opportunity. The contract expire and I hope see you in the future.” That door eventually opened again. Andrade later returned to AEW and quickly started rebuilding his place on the roster. His second AEW run eventually saw him introduce a new finisher as he settled back into the company and started carving out a fresh direction for himself. Andrade also stressed that he always maintained a good relationship with AEW, which makes his eventual return a lot easier to understand. There was no scorched-earth goodbye here. Andrade says he made a personal decision, thanked Tony Khan before leaving and eventually came back when the timing made sense for him. title: WWE Told Richard Holliday to Improve His Social Media Presence After Rejected Tryout
raw_title: WWE Told Richard Holliday to Improve His Social Media Presence After Rejected Tryout
summary_src: Richard Holliday didn’t get a WWE contract after his 2023 tryout, but he did leave with one message that completely changed how he handled his career. WWE told him to step up his social media game.
body: “So when I came back to wrestling in June of ’23, I had a WWE tryout in September of ’23. So I’m like a couple months removed from — I had chemo in February. Now I got a WWE tryout in September, right? That’s not a lot of time in between.” WWE ultimately passed on signing him. Instead of just sending him home empty-handed, Holliday said he was given some advice on the way out: put more effort into social media. “So I’m there, and ultimately they said, ‘We’re not going to offer you anything at this time.’ Okay. And I got a little advice to say, ‘Maybe try putting a little bit more into social media.’ Okay, challenge accepted.” Holliday clearly took that personally. Three years later, he says he has turned himself into one of the strongest social media personalities anywhere on the independent scene. “Now fast forward, I feel like I am the most untouchable on social media in independent wrestling. I don’t think anybody can touch me. But part of that is because I’m relentless in the marketing.” He is not shy about putting himself over either. Holliday praised his own content, plugged his accounts and made it clear that he does not need anybody else helping him sell himself. “Also, I have tremendous ideas. All of my content is great, is hilarious. If you don’t follow me, Most Marketable on Instagram, on Twitter, on TikTok. I told you I’d plug myself. I don’t need the ‘Where do you want — where can we find you?’ I do it all on my own, okay? I am my own machine.” That aggressive approach has apparently paid off. Holliday said other wrestlers now come to him asking how he keeps producing content, and his advice is simple: stop overthinking it and post. “I am relentlessly marketing, and now I have wrestlers of all different — I want to say age brackets, but all different tenures, right? A couple years in to over a decade in — ‘How do you find all this inspiration? How do you do all the social media?’” If something bombs, Holliday just moves on. More importantly, he says the online attention is turning into actual money and bookings. Promoters have straight-up told him they booked him because of how hot he was online. “And I just tell them, if I think an idea is good, I do it. I just do it because what’s the worst that happens? It stinks. Okay, that idea stunk. I’m going to go somewhere else. But if I can pump out a bunch of things, something’s going to stick.” “I’ve had plenty of instances where companies have said to me, ‘Yeah, we booked you because you’re hot online.’ Okay, great.” The timing is interesting because Holliday’s WWE future has come back into question. Sean Ross Sapp recently said that while people inside WWE had previously believed Holliday was headed there, he no longer believes that move is happening right now . WWE may have rejected Richard Holliday in 2023, but the advice they gave him clearly stuck. Instead of disappearing after the tryout, he turned social media into one of his biggest weapons and says it is now directly getting him

title: On the Record: Andrade Says He Wants to Repay Tony Khan for Giving Him Another Shot in AEW
raw_title: Andrade Says He Wants to Repay Tony Khan for Giving Him Another Shot in AEW
summary_src: Andrade is treating his second AEW run like something he has to earn every single week. The National Champion says Tony Khan giving him another opportunity means enough that he feels he owes him something back, and he plans on paying that debt with what he does inside the ring.
body: During an appearance on Close Up with Renee Paquette , Andrade opened up about getting another opportunity in AEW and explained why he is approaching this run differently. For Andrade, coming back was about proving exactly who he is now. Andrade then explained that he feels a responsibility to Tony Khan for giving him another shot with the company. He quickly clarified that when he talks about “paying” Khan back, he is talking about his work and what he delivers in the ring. “I need to pay to Tony, no, like pay with my work in the ring. This is why I want to defend this title. This is why I am here.” That mindset has become a major part of his National Championship run. Andrade has made it clear that he wants to defend the title regularly, and AEW has leaned into that idea by continuing to put the championship on the line. AEW even added another National Championship match to Dynamite as Andrade continued pushing the idea that he wants to be a fighting champion. Andrade also made it clear that his goals go beyond simply keeping gold around his waist. He wants to help people in the locker room, stay close with the rest of the roster and represent AEW the right way. “I am here to help the company. They want the best for this company. They want the best for me. I want to represent this company very well.” That says a lot about how Andrade is viewing this second run. He is not just back to collect a paycheck or hold a belt. He wants to prove Tony Khan made the right call bringing him back and make himself valuable to AEW from top to bottom. Andrade may call it “paying” Tony Khan back, but the message is pretty simple. He wants his work to speak for him, and he is determined to squeeze everything he can out of this second chance.
