title: Zoey Serrano Explains Why She Wants to Wrestle Men in TNA
raw_title: Zoey Serrano Explains Why She Wants to Wrestle Men in TNA
summary_src: Zoey Serrano has no problem throwing hands with the men in TNA, and she says some of the best matches of her entire wrestling career came when she was doing exactly that. During her latest “Zoey’s 10001 Internet Questions” Q&A on YouTube, Serrano was asked how she feels about intergender wrestling.
body: During her latest “Zoey’s 10001 Internet Questions” Q&A on YouTube , Serrano was asked how she feels about intergender wrestling. Turns out, she doesn’t just like it. That style of wrestling was a huge part of her career before WWE. Serrano explained that she actually felt like she could take the gloves off a little more when she was wrestling men. When working with women, she sometimes worried about going too hard and accidentally hurting somebody. Against men, she didn’t have that same hesitation. “I felt like I could just go harder with the guys. I was always a little scared of going, I don’t know, like I just didn’t want to hurt them. With the men, I didn’t have to worry about that. I could just go full throttle and not worry about it. But vice versa, they knew they could bring it back to me.” Serrano wasn’t just doing intergender matches for the spectacle either. Looking back at her career, she believes some of her best work happened when she was standing across the ring from a male opponent. “I’m not going to shy away from that. And I feel like a lot of like a lot of my best matches with with men.” One match immediately came to mind. Serrano singled out her FSW bout against Matt Vandagriff, which took place before she moved to Orlando to continue the next chapter of her wrestling career. Years later, she still considers it one of her personal favorites. “So, if you go back and watch Matt Vandergri versus me at FSW, it was like my sendoff match before I had to move to Orlando to start training over there. Hands down, one of my favorite matches. Love you, Matt Vander. You’re amazing. You deserve a shout out.” Now Serrano finds herself in TNA, and that opens the door to something she clearly wouldn’t mind revisiting. Her TNA run has already given her a fresh environment after her time with WWE, but Serrano isn’t looking at the company’s men’s and women’s divisions as completely separate worlds. TNA has plenty of history when it comes to intergender wrestling, and she knows it. That’s exactly why Serrano didn’t hesitate when asked whether she would wrestle men again. “I would do intergender wrestling today. I mean, I’m in TNA. They have a history of intergender wrestling, so why not? I could freaking put on some bangers with the men over at TNA. Are you kidding me? That would be a lot of fun.” Serrano clearly isn’t talking about intergender wrestling like some one-night gimmick. She did it before WWE, remembers those matches as some of her best, and sounds ready to jump right back into it if TNA gives her the opportunity. At this point, the bigger question might be whether TNA actually pulls the trigger. Serrano is already volunteering for the fight, and judging by the way she talks about her old intergender matches, she wouldn’t exactly be showing up to take it easy on anybody. title: Injury Update: Rusev Makes In-Ring Return at WWE Live Event After Injury Absence

summary_src: Rusev is officially back in the ring. After spending nearly three months on the sidelines with an injury, the former United States Champion finally wrestled his first match back during WWE’s live event in Honolulu on October 16.
body: His quick exit afterwards initially led to speculation that he was upset about losing to Evans. CJ Perry later shut that down , explaining that Rusev was in considerable pain and was simply trying to get backstage so WWE’s medical team could examine him. Things finally started looking up in September when Perry revealed that Rusev had returned to the WWE Performance Center and received medical clearance . She also mentioned that he’d dealt with another health issue during his time away, but confirmed that he was cleared to get back to work. Rusev wasn’t planning on jumping straight back into competition without getting himself ready either. Perry revealed that he intended to train extensively at the Performance Center and Natalya’s Dungeon 2.0 so he’d be prepared whenever WWE finally called his number. “Next week he’ll go to Orlando and train in NXT all week long, going to Nattie’s Dungeon 2.0, because when he gets called, he wants to be as snappy, aggressive, fast, and calculative as possible. He wants to live up to being that super athlete.” Perry also made it clear at the time that getting medically cleared didn’t automatically mean WWE had an immediate television storyline waiting for him. Rusev simply needed to stay ready until the right opportunity came along. “I think that’s what all it is in WWE. Not everyone is on TV every single week, and you just have to wait for your storyline and opportunity, and then blow it out of the water.” H Jenkins H Jenkins has been breaking pro wrestling news on Ringside News for nearly a decade, with his reports featured by TMZ, Forbes, The Sun, and more.

The WWE Hall Of Famer announced on AEW Dynamite that next year will be his final one competing between the ropes , closing a multi-decade career which has seen world title glory, early retirements, major comebacks, and more. In his promo, Copeland declared that the clock ticking on his career was the reason why he was now focused on claiming the AEW World Championship, seeking one more world title reign before he hangs up the boots. This provides a very divisive conversation of whether or not the 52 year-old should win the AEW World Title, or whether booking the aging star with the gold is a bad decision. One of the biggest reasons why some fans are open to an Adam Copeland title reign is just to the “what if” of his WWE return run. Back in 2011 , Copeland (then wrestling as Edge) relinquished the World Heavyweight Champion and entered retirement. Upon his return in 2020, one thing was on both his mind and those of his supporters - reclaiming the world championship that he never lost and having one final, complete reign with a top prize. Unfortunately, Roman Reigns’ dominance over WWE’s main event scene saw Copeland lose in title matches at WrestleMania 37 and at Money In The Bank 2021 , before falling down into the upper midcard and remaining there for the remainder of his run. When WWE introduced a brand new World Heavyweight Championship in 2023, fans were hopeful that a redemption arc was in store… only for Copeland to lose in the tournament to crown the inaugural champion, before exiting the company just a couple months later. title: Richard Holliday Takes Offense to Claims Independent Wrestling Has No Stars
raw_title: Richard Holliday Takes Offense to Claims Independent Wrestling Has No Stars
summary_src: Richard Holliday has heard people say the independent wrestling scene doesn’t have any real stars left, and he’s not buying it for a second. In fact, Holliday takes that claim personally because he believes he’s living proof that it isn’t true.
body: “You know, some of my favorite opponents that stick out would be Killer Kross. Anytime I get in the ring with Killer Kross, it’s magic. Santana, Mike Santana, now Cruz Montana, anytime with him was magic. Matt Riddle. I’ve been able to share the ring with Nick Nemeth, Matt Cardona on several occasions.” “But now I’m the guy. So I’m the guy who other wrestlers are saying, ‘This is a high-profile match for me,’ because on the independent scene, you know, people say that there’s—I always see, you know, discourse of there’s no stars on the independent scene. I take full offense of that. I take full offense of that because I’m a star.” Holliday didn’t stop there. He said the proof comes when opponents get matched against him and immediately start selling the bout as one of the biggest opportunities of their careers. “And there’s a reason that when I get announced for a match, my opponent will make a promo saying, ‘This is one of the biggest matches of my career, if not the biggest match of my career. This is the biggest test of my career going up against Richard Holliday.’ It just is, you know?” He made it clear that he believes his current position has been earned. “But yeah, man, you got to be confident, and I just—I’m in that position right now in the independents.” That confidence hasn’t exactly come out of nowhere. Holliday has spent the past few years aggressively building his name outside the major companies. Earlier in 2026, he said that Richard Holliday had become a business and a brand while acknowledging that WWE and other major promotions were watching him . The WWE conversation around Holliday only got louder as the year went on. Booker T publicly pushed for Holliday to get another WWE opportunity , saying he was pulling for the longtime independent wrestler to finally get his shot. There was also plenty of attention after Holliday left his boots in the ring following a GCW match , which immediately raised questions about whether his time on the independent scene might be nearing its end. Those WWE expectations have since cooled, with his status remaining unsettled. For now, Holliday is still out there proving his point the old-fashioned way: taking bookings, wrestling recognizable names and making sure fans know exactly who he is before he leaves the building. People can argue all they want about whether the independent scene still produces legitimate stars, but Holliday isn’t waiting around for anyone to give him that label. title: Richard Holliday Shuts Down Claims AEW Is Responsible for Independent Wrestling’s Success
raw_title: Richard Holliday Shuts Down Claims AEW Is Responsible for Independent Wrestling’s Success
summary_src: Richard Holliday doesn’t buy the idea that AEW deserves credit for independent wrestling being successful.
body: “No. No. I think that would discredit the work that independent wrestlers and independent wrestling companies have been doing. So, no.” “Is it cool if an AEW wrestler is on the same card? Yeah, it’s nice because, again, it might bring more additional eyeballs. But for that to be the reason that independent wrestling is successful? No. No way.” “I think that independent wrestling is successful. Some people will say it’s not successful. I’ll say it is successful. I just told you I’m going to have 120 matches this year. Not a lot of those are going to be repeat companies.” For Holliday, constantly traveling somewhere new tells him there are still plenty of promoters putting on wrestling shows. He doesn’t believe every company needs to draw thousands of people before anyone can call it successful either. “A lot of them are going to be, you know, I’m going somewhere for the first time. That means a lot of independent wrestling is happening. That means a lot of companies are running.” Holliday argued that success looks different depending on the size and goals of the promotion. If a company draws 250 fans, turns a profit, pays everyone and sends the crowd home happy, he doesn’t see why that should automatically be treated as a failure. “Okay, is everybody filling up 5,000-seat arenas, 1,000-seat arenas? No, not really. But then now we have to have a deeper conversation about what’s the level of success? What does success mean?” He believes those smaller victories matter just as much to the health of the independent scene. Another promotion might regularly draw 600 people, but Holliday sees both situations as potentially successful depending on what each company is trying to accomplish. “If success for an independent company is bringing 250 people, and the company is profitable, and everybody’s being paid, and everybody’s having a good time, who is anybody to say that that’s not successful? But then there might be somebody who says, ‘Well, I get 600 regularly, so that’s success to me.’ Okay, great.” Holliday’s own calendar is another reason he isn’t buying the argument that independent wrestling is struggling. He said he’d start worrying if he couldn’t find work, but right now he has the opposite problem because he’s staying extremely busy. “But all I know is that wrestling is happening, and there’s a lot of it. If I was struggling to find bookings and I was, you know, looking at my calendar and saying, ‘Man, I only have four matches for November,’ then I would say independent wrestling is hurting. But no, I’m booked out. I’m busy.” “Is it like that for everybody? No. Could it be like that for everybody? Yes, if they utilize social media. I’ve had plenty of instances where companies have said to me, ‘Yeah, we booked you because you’re hot online.’ Okay, great.” “I had two fans come up to my merch table and said, ‘Dude, we saw your reels online, and we saw you were going to be in Chicago, so we came to see you.’ I went, ‘Get out of here. body: It's three hours of AEW action tonight, as AEW Dynamite & Collision comes your way with a live 3-hour special at 8 p.m. ET/7 p.m. CT on TBS and HBO Max from the Wolstein Center in Cleveland, Ohio! It’s the final stop before AEW WrestleDream on Saturday in Orlando, Florida, but there’s still much to be decided tonight when five Clockwork Carnage qualifiers, including a pair of title matches, will determine who joins AEW World Champion Will Ospreay and “Speedball” Mike Bailey of United Empire, as well as Samoa Joe, in the 8-man field. Speaking of Ospreay and Joe, they’ll be on opposite sides of a star-studded tag team match that is just one of four multi-person matches with WrestleDream opponents facing off tonight. After Tommaso Ciampa attacked Andrade on Collision to make his AEW National Title aspirations clear, Andrade and Ospreay challenged Ciampa to find a partner, so he’s bringing Joe to the fight. AEW champions who are part of the Clockwork Carnage qualifiers were required to put their titles on the line, so as mentioned above, we’ll see a pair of championship tilts among the five matches. TNT Champion Darby Allin defends against CMLL World Heavyweight Champion Hechicero, and AEW International Champion “The Rainmaker” Kazuchika Okada risks his title against Myron Reed. Plus, Adam Copeland takes on Josh Alexander, Brian Cage meets Konosuke Takeshita, and Ricochet faces Ace Austin in the remaining Clockwork Carnage qualifiers. AEW Women's World Champion Mercedes Moné joins Divine Dominion to fight Triangle of Madness days before facing Thekla at WrestleDream, and the Death Riders face the Don Callis Family in trios action with Mark Davis set to challenge AEW Continental Champion Jon Moxley on Saturday in Orlando. Plus, TBS Champion Persephone and Dr. Britt Baker, D.M.D. battle Dani Luna and Hyan! Check out everything you need to know for this LIVE 3-HOUR SPECIAL! Two current champions face two challengers tonight before their respective matches at WrestleDream. Andrade and Ospreay responded by challenging Ciampa and any partner to a fight, so Ciampa is bringing Samoa Joe, who is already set to meet Ospreay, Speedball Bailey and five other wrestlers in Clockwork Carnage after beating "Jungle" Jack Perry in Paris. title: Kevin Nash Moved By Ospreay Vs Omega At All In
raw_title: Kevin Nash Says He Was 'Moved' By Will Ospreay Vs. Kenny Omega At AEW All In
summary_src: WWE Hall of Famer Kevin Nash admits he was "moved" by the Will Ospreay vs. Kenny Omega AEW Men's World Championship main event match at All In
body: "The last thing I watched that really, really moved me was when I watched Ospreay and Omega in Wembley," Nash said. Nash admitted that he enjoyed the match despite the fact that "it's not my style," even suggesting that it was so far from his preferred style of wrestling that it was comparable to the difference between how Karl Gotch and Lou Thesz wrestled compared to catch wrestlers in France. He found himself so enthused about what Ospreay and Omega did that he found himself wishing he could see the duo team up to take on two WWE stars in what Nash considered a major styles clash.
summary: Kevin Nash revealed that Will Ospreay versus Kenny Omega at AEW All In in Wembley was the last match to truly move him. He admitted the bout was far from his preferred wrestling style, likening the contrast to the differences between Karl Gotch and Lou Thesz versus French catch wrestlers. Nash became so invested that he expressed a desire to see Ospreay and Omega team together against two WWE performers in a major styles clash.

title: David Otunga Skeptical Of Montez Ford Lawsuit
raw_title: David Otunga Gives His Verdict On Montez Ford Lawsuit
summary_src: David Otunga shares his verdict on the Montez Ford lawsuit. On October 14, Noel Lucas, a Cook County Sheriff’s officer, filed a lawsuit against Montez Ford and WWE because of a “lap dance” performed on him by Ford during the July 6 edition of WWE Raw.
body: In the filing, it was alleged that Crawford’s “left inner thigh repeatedly rubbed against Plaintiff’s leg.” David Otunga broke down the clip that circulated on social media in his YouTube video. He couldn’t see any physical contact being made as the filing alleged. The interesting thing is, from this vantage point, I don’t see the physical contact. Now, the screen is cut off a little bit, but remember, it alleges that Montez’s left thigh, his inner thigh, makes unwanted contact. I’m keeping my eye on it there. It’s further away from him. So, if there is contact, it would appear to only be incidental. Like, it doesn’t look like it’s intentional. I haven’t seen any contact yet. Now, there may be other angles where you can see it more clearly, but at least from this angle, I don’t even see that contact, which is going to be a bit of a problem for Mr. Lucas, who’s alleging battery, civil battery.” David Otunga once again said that he couldn’t see any physical contact being made between the two. Later in the video, David Otunga shared his verdict on this suit. “Well, on the public evidence we’ve discussed, I lean towards the defense on the claims about Ford’s conduct. I’m particularly skeptical of the emotional distress claim on the record. I really am. It looks like Lucas knew that this was a joke. Clearly, Montez intended this to be a joke. I just don’t see there being legitimate emotional distress. I could be wrong. He might be able to convince a jury of this. But my take is, I don’t think so. But like I said, surviving an early motion is different from actually convincing a jury. Just like winning one claim is different from winning all of them. Proving liability is different from proving a large amount of damages. If the evidence shows no contact, no reasonable anticipation of unwanted contact, as is needed for assault, and a brief comic interaction without the required severe distress, several essential theories have serious problems. If another angle or credible testimony establishes deliberate repeated contact, then the battery analysis changes substantially. But from the video angles we’ve seen, I don’t see any contact. If there’s any contact, it does not look deliberate to me. So I think battery fails. But again, there’s no visible injury required for battery. But a large damages award still needs support. Now the publicity claim turns on its own evidence and defenses. I can’t responsibly give you a percentage before seeing the complete complaints, seeing the agreements, and seeing both sides’ evidence. A sweeping victory or major trial award for Lucas, I don’t know if I see that by what we’ve seen so far.” If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.
summary: David Otunga reviewed footage from the Montez Ford incident in a YouTube video and stated he could not see the alleged inner thigh contact described in the lawsuit filing. He noted the contact, if any, appeared incidental rather than intentional and expressed doubt it would support a civil battery claim. Otunga ultimately leaned toward the defense on Ford's conduct and voiced particular skepticism about the emotional distress allegations.

summary_src: When WWE made a whole thing about John Cena’s retirement and gave him a full blown tour, it put more of a focus on retirement as a gimmick. We’re already seeing one of his old rivals in WWE, Adam Copeland, follow in his footsteps by announcing 2027 will be his final year. There are quite […]
body: There are quite a few veteran wrestlers who are at the age where retirement is a conversation that is going to come up more frequently. Considering how it’s become such a gimmick, it’s worth asking about future plans to any one of those wrestlers. SHAK Wrestling did just that with Samoa Joe recently, asking what this stage of his career looks like. He’s 47-years-old and the end is much closer than the beginning: “I mean really just putting on meaningful, fun matches for the fans. I think trying to consistently give people something to tune in for and have a good time with. Listen, you know, what my time frame is is kind of still not quite nailed down but I will say this: I want to leave as many good memories as I can while I have the opportunity. I think that’s just kind of the best way to approach things right now.” The next meaningful fun match on his schedule: Clockwork Carnage at tonight’s (Sat., Oct. 17, 2026) AEW WrestleDream pay-per-view in Orlando, Florida. It’s just another first in a long line of them for the near 30-year vet. We should be cherishing those before we get to his one last. title: On the Record: David Otunga Says Montez Ford and WWE Have a Strong Case in Lawsuit
raw_title: David Otunga Says Montez Ford and WWE Have a Strong Case in Lawsuit
summary_src: David Otunga has taken a hard look at the lawsuit filed against Montez Ford and WWE, and based on the footage that’s out there right now, he’s not exactly convinced the case against them is a strong one.
body: Cook County Sheriff’s officer Noel Lucas filed the lawsuit on October 14 over an interaction with Ford during the July 6 episode of WWE Raw. Lucas claims Ford performed an unwanted “lap dance” while he was working security and alleged that Ford’s left inner thigh repeatedly rubbed against his leg. The suit includes 14 counts, including battery, assault, intentional infliction of emotional distress and alleged violations of the Illinois Gender Violence Act. Otunga, who is not only a former WWE wrestler but also a Harvard Law graduate and Illinois attorney, broke down the viral footage on his YouTube channel and immediately zeroed in on one huge issue — he couldn’t actually see the physical contact Lucas described. Watching the clip, Otunga said Lucas looked like he was trying to keep a straight face while Ford was clearly playing up the moment. That was only part of Otunga’s problem with the lawsuit. He said the angle being circulated doesn’t appear to show Ford repeatedly rubbing against Lucas at all. “The interesting thing is, from this vantage point, I don’t see the physical contact. Now, the screen is cut off a little bit, but remember, it alleges that Montez’s left thigh, his inner thigh, makes unwanted contact. I’m keeping my eye on it there. It’s further away from him. So, if there is contact, it would appear to only be incidental. Like, it doesn’t look like it’s intentional.” Otunga kept watching and still didn’t see what Lucas alleges happened. “I haven’t seen any contact yet. Now, there may be other angles where you can see it more clearly, but at least from this angle, I don’t even see that contact, which is going to be a bit of a problem for Mr. Lucas, who’s alleging battery, civil battery.” He admitted the spot could technically be described as a lap dance, but said the context mattered. “All right, it is somewhat of a lap dance. But, hey, Montez Ford is a playful guy, and he’s just having fun. This definitely is a comedic spot and seems like it was harmless to me.” Otunga was careful not to claim Lucas’ facial expressions prove anything by themselves. He made it clear that another camera angle could change the situation completely, especially because parts of their legs are blocked in the footage. “Again, I don’t see clear physical contact being made. Could another angle show something that this one doesn’t? Absolutely. Because parts of their legs are obscured.” However, he said there would still be a major difference between an accidental brush and the repeated, intentional contact described in the lawsuit. When Otunga finally gave his overall verdict, he landed firmly on Ford and WWE’s side based on what has been made public. “Well, on the public evidence we’ve discussed, I lean towards the defense on the claims about Ford’s conduct.” He was especially skeptical of Lucas’ emotional distress claim, saying the footage looked more like a joke that Lucas understood was happening. “I’m particularly skeptical of the emotional distress cl
summary: The latest: the latest: Cook County Sheriff’s officer Noel Lucas filed the lawsuit on October 14 over an interaction with Ford during the July 6 episode of WWE Raw. Lucas claims Ford performed an unwanted lap dance while he was working security and alleged that Ford’s left inner thigh repeatedly rubbed against his leg.

title: Nic Nemeth finds glory in TNA after 20-year pro wrestling career
raw_title: Nic Nemeth finds glory in TNA after 20-year pro wrestling career
body: Nic Nemeth has put in the hard work for more than 20 years as a professional wrestler. And now, finally, he’s getting what he feels he has deserved — a consistent spot in the main event, as the star of the show. In less than three years with TNA Wrestling, he has won two world championships. He’ll defend the belt this Sunday in Tampa at Bound for Glory, TNA’s biggest showcase pay-per-view of the year, facing Leon Slater. Nemeth, 46, was a featured performer as Dolph Ziggler in WWE from 2008 to 2023 and earned a reputation for his work ethic, precision and versatility in the ring. He had two brief runs with the world title there, but was generally regarded as a wrestler who could make anyone else look good — the measuring stick for others, but never the top guy. Since joining TNA in 2024, he’s earned both admiration and gold belts. “I was the guy to figure out if somebody can wrestle a broom or not,” Nemeth said about his WWE career. “But at the same time, I felt like I should be the world effing champion. You’re living your dream, but you’ve got to start getting selfish and looking out for yourself. I love the business too much to be selfish, so it probably cost me … I do have the respect of my peers, and that helped me sleep a little bit at night.” When he’s not wrestling, Nemeth has found a different spotlight as a stand-up comedian, a field he has dabbled in since 2013. His mix of work stories, observational humor and improv has starred at wrestling-related events but also in comedy venues like Los Angeles’ UCB Theater and Comedy Central’s Roast Battle. “From the time I was a kid, I wanted to be the star of the show in whatever I did,” he said. “And a few years ago, I was at a point where I was stealing the show in wrestling, but I needed something else to do with my days off besides reading a book. TNA wrestler Leon Slater is enjoying high-profile week (and his time in Orlando) Most recently, he has toured with his brother Ryan in a comedy show they call “Hunkamania.” They’ve also teamed together extensively in the ring in TNA for the first time, winning the tag-team championship twice since 2024. “Watching my brother get better and better is the coolest thing ever,” Nic Nemeth said. “We have this crazy chemistry in life, but I didn’t know if it would translate inside the ring. I told him, ‘If it doesn’t, I’m pulling the plug on this (tag team) because I’ve set a standard here and if this doesn’t reach that standard, I want out.’ But I’ve watched Ryan instantly take to it like a fish to water. It worked out that our chemistry was there. Damn it, it works, so let’s go.” But this weekend, Nemeth is out to defend his singles gold against Slater, a talented Englishman who, Nemeth noted, is less than half his age. But he’s won several titles in TNA and around the world and has earned plenty of respect. “When I first got to TNA, he’s the first guy I saw in the ring and I said, ‘Who is that, and can we sign him to a 10-year deal?’ ” Nemeth said. “He

title: Cody Rhodes Names His Favorite Dusty Promo
raw_title: WWE's Cody Rhodes Says His Favorite Dusty Rhodes Promo Isn't 'Hard Times'
summary_src: WWE star Cody Rhodes recalled his favorite promo cut by his father, Dusty Rhodes, and said it wasn't his dad's famous "Hard Times" segment.
body: He said that while a lot of people always cite "Hard Times," he had actually heard it before, when his father cut the promo on Ole Anderson in Georgia Champion Wrestling, which wasn't televised. Rhodes said that his favorite Dusty promo came in WCW in 1994. "My favorite promo he ever did was with my brother, Dustin, 'The View Never Changes,' talking about neglecting Dustin and wanting to be his partner," Rhodes said. "Our family has lived out in front of them. As much as it's a performance in WWE, you know, however you want to look at it, the character Cody Rhodes is pretty real, you know? I think the main difference is 'Runnels' and 'Rhodes.' To be able to do that promo with my brother and share that moment was kind of the only way he could apologize and tell him he loved him, so that one really stands out to me a lot."
summary: Cody Rhodes revealed that his favorite Dusty Rhodes promo is not the widely celebrated "Hard Times" but rather a 1994 WCW segment with brother Dustin titled "The View Never Changes." In it Dusty addressed neglecting Dustin and expressed a desire to become his tag team partner. Cody explained that the family has lived much of their story publicly and that the heartfelt promo served as Dusty's way of apologizing and saying he loved his son.

title: AEW wrestler Benjamin Satterley, a.k.a. Pac, dies at 40
raw_title: AEW wrestler Benjamin Satterley, a.k.a. Pac, dies at 40
body: Professional wrestling star Benjamin Satterley, who was known as Pac inside the ring, has died at 40, All Elite Wrestling (AEW) announced in a statement Sunday evening. AEW’s statement did not indicate how Satterley died, and no other information has been confirmed. Satterley had been scheduled to face Andrade El Idolo for the AEW National Championship on Saturday in Chicago. "A native of Newcastle upon Tyne, England, Satterley began his wrestling career in 2004 and went on to perform for wrestling organizations all over the world, captivating fans with innovative high-flying moves and incredible in-ring ability," AEW wrote in the post announcing Satterley’s death. The organization also noted the AEW championships that Satterley had held and offered its condolences to the family. Satterley was one of the first wrestlers to sign with AEW in 2019 and was a two-time Trios Champion as well as the inaugural All-Atlantic Champion, Outkick reported . Prior to joining AEW, Satterley had wrestled in the WWE as Adrian Neville. During that time, he held the Cruiserweight Championship twice, was an NXT Champion, and two-time NXT Tag Team Champion.
summary: Professional wrestling star Benjamin Satterley, who was known as Pac inside the ring, has died at 40, All Elite Wrestling revealed in a statement Sunday evening. AEW’s statement didn't indicate how Satterley died, and no other information has been made official.

title: Mike Bailey Explains Benefits of Wrestling Barefoot
raw_title: Mike Bailey Discusses Wrestling Barefoot, Whether It Slows Him Down
body: During a recent interview with Fightful’s Sean Ross Sapp , Mike Bailey spoke about what it’s like to wrestle barefoot. Below are some highlights from Fightful: “No, I don’t. I have very few feet issues. I mean, I’ve hurt some toes. I think I’ve broken some toes, but I just pop them back in. It’s the kind of thing where it’s not gonna get worse. If you break a toe and you snap it back, you can’t break it more. It’s just gonna heal and be fine. Back in my Taekwondo days, I would have chronic turf toe, just feet constantly bruised from kicking elbows.” “But it is easily outweighed by the advantages of wrestling barefoot for me. The main one that people don’t think of is ropes. When I’m standing on the top rope and I can grab the rope with my toes and when I do a springboard, you can see my feet curl around the rope and I get extra balance that way. I love wrestling barefoot and I’m glad that I get to do it in a place like All Elite Wrestling that actually embraces the individuality of the wrestlers and that’s something that’s very important for me. Again, the emphasis is on letting the wrestlers be the best and that includes being the best versions of themselves, which, in my case, is wrestling without boots or shoes.” “I don’t take off my shoes backstage. I’m usually in flip flops. I try to try to keep my best, and of course, you have to keep them clean. But also it’s funny because I think what I’m doing is a lot more sanitary than the wrestlers who will wear their boots backstage, go to the urinal in boots and then stomp you in the face in the middle of the ring and no one bats an eye. No one disinfects their wrestling boots before a match. I think it’s fair. I don’t think we have to. I’ve not had any facial infections from dirty wrestling boots and I don’t know why my bare feet would be more of a concern, where I think it’s in fact less.” “This is absolutely correct. body: Rusev made his return to the ring on the October 16 WWE live event in Hawaii. It was his first match since July 27, when he suffered an injury against Je’Von Evans. CJ Perry (Lana), Rusev’s wife, said that he got cleared in September. She stated about his injury, “It was the Intuit Dome in LA; he had a match against Je’Von Evans, and in the match, something happened and his arms went completely numb. He had to roll outside of the ring and the refs were thinking about calling the match. He’s like, ‘I can’t feel my hands.’ I didn’t hear this; I was about ten rows back, and I missed it, but someone got on camera and went viral on Twitter. The fans were debating and fighting each other because some were like, ‘He’s really hurt and injured.’ Some were like, ‘He just doesn’t want to lose.’ He took a couple of seconds outside, and when the ref was like, ‘We’re going to call the match. Your hands are going numb.’ Once he had feeling, he was like, ‘No.’ He rolled in and finished the match. Those rumors are not true when people are like, ‘He doesn’t want to put people over.’ That’s not accurate and not true. He’s always there to do business. He always fights for a good story. That’s how people get over. “He finished the match. He was in a lot of pain and tried to get out the ring as quick as possible and get back to medical. That’s when the rumors started. I saw the internet [Fightful] reported the true story, and that was encouraging. It had nothing to do with the loss. He could’ve had WWE stop the match and not lose, but he chose to roll back in the ring and do what’s right for business. He just had to get back to the back as quick as possible because he wasn’t well at the time.”

title: Reigns and Rhodes settle rivalry with rock-paper-scissors
raw_title: Roman Reigns & Cody Rhodes Bring Their Rivalry to a Rock-Paper-Scissors Match
body: The Tribal Chief and The American Nightmare appeared on BuzzFeed Celeb alongside fellow cast members, including Noah Centineo, Andrew Koji, Callina Liang, Andrew Schulz, Eric André, and David Dastmalchian. The group took part in a team trivia challenge, with Reigns representing "Winners" and Rhodes playing for "Ansatsuken." The competition came down to the two former WrestleMania opponents in a final tiebreaker. With both teams waiting for the result, Reigns and Rhodes faced each other and prepared to settle things with a Rock-Paper-Scissors game. The other participants treated the moment as a potential viral highlight. They encouraged the WWE stars to trust their instincts and maintain eye contact before making their choices. The rest of the cast also joined in on the banter. The contest began, and both WWE superstars came up with Scissors at first, which felt like even the universe was hyping up their competitive rivalry from WWE to real life. However, in the second trial, Reigns came up with Stone while Rhodes came up with Paper. The tiebreaker ended with a dramatic finish, and the Ansatsuken team celebrated after securing the win. Their BuzzFeed appearance was also notable because it was the only promotional interview where the two stars appeared together while promoting Street Fighter. It was also reported that Reigns and Rhodes had some tension on the set of the movie. During an appearance on INSIGHT with Chris Van Vliet, Rhodes revealed that the production crew tried to keep the two men apart. According to The American Nightmare, the crew seemed worried that their intense WWE rivalry might lead to a real-life confrontation. Rhodes' Ansatsuken team ultimately won the contest as the rest of the cast watched and cheered the dramatic finish.

title: In Memoriam: Wrestler Benjamin Satterley's cause of death revealed - FOX 4 News Dallas-Fort Worth
raw_title: Wrestler Benjamin Satterley's cause of death revealed - FOX 4 News Dallas-Fort Worth
body: The cause of death for Benjamin Satterley, the wrestler known to fans as "Pac," has been released. Satterley died Sept. 27 at 40 years old, a day after facing Andrade El Idolo in the All Elite Wrestling National Championship in Chicago. The Cook County, Illinois, Medical Examiner’s Office confirmed Satterley died of bronchial asthma, according to The New York Post . The manner of death was natural. Satterley is a native of Newcastle upon Tyne, England. He began his wrestling career in 2004, "and went on to perform for wrestling organizations all over the world, captivating fans with innovative high-flying moves and incredible in-ring ability," AEW said in a statement Sept. 27. Satterley was one of the first wrestlers to sign with AEW in 2019 and was a two-time Trios Champion as well as the inaugural All-Atlantic Champion, Outkick reported . Prior to joining AEW, Satterley had wrestled in the WWE as Adrian Neville. During that time, he held the Cruiserweight Championship twice, was an NXT Champion, and two-time NXT Tag Team Champion. His wife, Natalie, shared an emotional tribute to her late husband on Instagram a few days ago. "Thank you for our beautiful life darling," she wrote. "Twenty one years ago we became friends, nineteen years ago we fell in love and eleven years ago we were married. Two souls entwined in one; my best friend and better half. "You always worked so incredibly hard to ensure we would have a great life together, both now and once you had retired. The cruelty of having all of our future hopes and dreams snatched away will never feel real.

llm_long: Will Ospreay will defend the AEW World Championship against Samoa Joe, Mike Bailey, Adam Copeland, Konosuke Takeshita, Kazuchika Okada, Ricochet, and Darby Allin in a Clockwork Carnage Match at WrestleDream 2026. The match begins with two wrestlers in the ring, with the remaining six entering at three-minute intervals. Eliminations by pinfall or submission cannot occur until all eight competitors have entered the ring.

Once all wrestlers are in the ring, the match advances to a second stage featuring a 15-minute time limit. Competitors score points through pinfalls and submissions during this period. The wrestler with the most points at the end of the time limit will be declared the AEW World Champion.

Mercedes Mone will defend the AEW Women's World Championship against Thekla. Mone comes off a successful title defense against Queen Aminata on the October 6 episode of AEW Dynamite Grand Slam France. Thekla earned her title opportunity by defeating Willow Nightingale in a number one contender's match at All Out on September 26.

Hangman Adam Page, Brody King, and Ring of Honor World Champion Bandido will challenge Swerve Strickland, Kofi Creed, and Austin Creed for the AEW World Trios Championship in a best two-out-of-three-falls match. The trio previously came up short against the champions at All Out last month.

Matt Jackson and Nick Jackson will defend the AEW World Tag Team Championship against Kyle Fletcher and Kevin Knight. The Young Bucks won the titles at All Out on September 26 in a three-way match that also included Christian Cage, Adam Copeland, Dax Harwood, and Cash Wheeler.

Persephone will defend the TBS Championship against Hyan, Queen Aminata, and Dani Luna in a four-way match. Hyan and Dani Luna defeated Persephone and Britt Baker on the recent Dynamite and Collision double feature, leading to a beatdown that was interrupted by Aminata.

title: Legal Watch: Montez Ford and WWE Face 14-Count Lawsuit Over ‘Raw’ Incident That Allegedly Left Guard Humiliated
raw_title: Montez Ford and WWE Face 14-Count Lawsuit Over ‘Raw’ Incident That Allegedly Left Guard Humiliated
body: Return to Homepage Entertainment: TikTok bans 'Musk' film account Halle Berry's son allowed to testify Cannes winner 'Fjord' sparks debate New movies this weekend Busfield's charges dropped Angine de Poitrine 'Fourth Wing' series The 'Digger' discourse 'DWTS' rehearsals Stiles to honor Ledger Security guard Noel Lucas is suing WWE star Montez Ford over an alleged unwanted inappropriate dance during Monday Night Raw , TMZ reported. He filed the civil complaint on Wednesday, October 14, 2026, in the Circuit Court of Cook County, Illinois. It names Ford, whose legal name is Kenneth Crawford, World Wrestling Entertainment, LLC, and the company's subsidiary Event Services, LLC. The encounter occurred on July 6, 2026, at Allstate Arena in Rosemont during Netflix's live broadcast. Ford and Angelo Dawkins, the Street Profits, were entering for a World Tag Team Championship defense against Bron Breakker and Austin Theory, according to WWE . According to the complaint, WWE personnel had instructed Lucas to remain seated at a security post outside the ring. His attorneys say he had not been told that he would be incorporated into the performance. The filing alleges that Ford straddled Lucas and repeatedly moved his hips and pelvis toward him. It further alleges that Ford drew closer and rubbed his left inner thigh against Lucas's leg several times, according to Fightful . The complaint alleges that announcers mocked Lucas during the live broadcast, remarking, "That guy clearly hates fun," and comparing him to the fictional security guard from Paul Blart: Mall Cop , FOX 32 Chicago reported. "Mr. Lucas was there to do his job, not to be made a part of WWE's entertainment," attorney Whitney Barr said in a statement from Caffarelli & Martin . Barr also said Lucas took on the additional security work to help provide for his children. The complaint alleges that WWE posted footage on TikTok and Instagram after the broadcast and that Ford shared it on his own accounts. It attributes more than 300,000 views to WWE's posts. When Lucas returned to his courthouse duties the following day, he says members of the public recognized him and imitated Ford's movements in his direction. He also alleges that his children were ridiculed by their peers at school. Lucas says the exposure caused humiliation, emotional distress and damage to his reputation. According to his law firm, WWE and Ford eventually removed their own posts. Recordings shared by others remained publicly accessible when the lawsuit was filed. POST Wrestling 's Brandon Thurston reported that, as of October 15, the version of the episode available on Netflix omitted the interaction. The program appeared to cut to a break earlier in the team's entrance. The lawsuit contains 14 civil counts, including assault, battery and intentional infliction of emotional distress. It also raises claims under the Illinois Gender Violence Act and the Illinois Right of Publicity Act. Lucas's law firm identifies additional claims
summary: Per the complaint, WWE personnel had instructed Lucas to remain seated at a security post outside the ring. It further alleges that Ford drew closer and rubbed his left inner thigh against Lucas's leg a number of times, per Fightful .

Joe Alonzo: I mean, I think you should ask Carlos Silva, “How does it feel to have Alonzo as part of the TNA roster?” Because that’s a lot. No matter where I go, views are gonna follow, whether I’m signed to TNA or not. So, I mean, it’s cool. It’s good for everyone. Families eat for generations. But I think Joe Alonzo is a lot bigger than the X Division. That, me personally, I think I’m more like TNA World Championship material. Soundsphere: Let’s talk about Leon Slater challenging Nick Nemeth for that at Bound for Glory. You might want to get your lick back on Leon. So, would it be more suitable for you to fight Nick for that, or would you hope Slater wins it so you could potentially take it off him? Joe Alonzo: I think it doesn’t matter who has it. I mean, I just want the title. I don’t care how I get it. I just would like that. I mean, it’d be cool to get in there with someone like Nick, who’s a legend himself. But then Leon, I think I would just feel genuinely better about that, just taking that from him because, I mean, he took my moment away from me. So why not take that away from him? I don’t know. title: Harlem Lewis retains Evolve Title at Succession IV

body: -Wendy Choo, Nikkita Lyons, Harley Riggins, and Harlem Lewis all cut brief promos at the top of the show. Blake Howard and NXT GM Robert Stone introduced Succession IV from ringside before going right into the first title match. (1) HARLEM LEWIS (c) vs. HARLEY RIGGINS – Evolve Championship Match Riggins did some strange gesturing and posing prior to the match that didn’t work for me. Sarah Schreiber handled the official ring introductions. The match started with a slugfest, which Lewis got the best of. He clotheslined Riggins over the top rope a couple of times before Riggins woke up and went into Big RIg mode, dealing some heavy blows to the champ. A tilt-a-whirl slam earned him a two-count before they cut to a quick commercial break. [c] WINNER: Harlem Lewis at 6:23 to retain the Evolve Championship. (Miller’s Take: That was rather anti-climactic and much shorter than I expected it to be, but I’m assuming they’re saving time for the last woman standing match. Riggins is very talented, but I’m not sure how far his Diesel-esque gimmick will take him in WWE. He also needs to slow down when he’s talking. His promos are too fast and choppy. Harlem Lewis has a great backstory and look. He can also get the job done in the ring, which leads me to believe we’ll be seeing him in NXT when the Harlem World Violence Tour comes to an end in Evolve.) -Footage was shown from a recent Reality of Wrestling event in which Booker T presented Josiah Jean with a WWE ID contract. Luck looked slightly apprehensive during her ring entrance. I really don’t blame her, because Vanta scares the bejesus out of me, too. The two women traded headlocks into top wristlocks. Vanta escaped an arm twist in a way that I can’t describe, then used another strange, but smooth way to sidestep Luck as she charged in. Vanta continued to wow the crowd with her extremely unorthodox offense. Vanta locked in an abdominal stretch variation that Luck struggled to fight out of. She finally fired up with some effective offense to slow Vanta down, but that’s all she accomplished. Luck tried to apply a Laynie Lock, but Vanta slipped around and turned it into a DisarmHer on steroids, pulling back until it appeared that she was trying to take home Luck’s arm as a souvenir. Laynie had no choice but to tap out. (Miller’s Take: Vanta looks, acts, and speaks like something I’d have nightmares about after eating too much spicy food before bed. The way she moves in the ring is indescribable and has to be seen to be believed. So far, she’s only had two short matches in Evolve, so we’ll have to see if she can carry a longer match, but so far she’s damn impressive. Luck is talented, and I can see her moving up the WWE food chain with more time and reps.) [c] -Blake Howard ran down next week’s card, including Ball & Rivera vs. Jones & Hall, Jacobs vs. Raye, and Dixon vs. Rourke. -Adriana Rizzo was once again ringside, this time with Elijah Holyfield. title: On the Record: Leon Slater’s “thrill of victory” promo, Hardyz in charge, Baszler and Serrano as certified badasses, Nic Nemeth-Trey Miguel, Eddie Edwards side-eyed by his System cohorts — TNA IMPACT HITS & MISSES (10/15)
raw_title: TNA IMPACT HITS & MISSES (10/15): Leon Slater’s “thrill of victory” promo, Hardyz in charge, Baszler and Serrano as certified badasses, Nic Nemeth-Trey Miguel, Eddie Edwards side-eyed by his System cohorts
body: This promo was very simple, yet very passionate. It came across as motivated, yet humble and gracious as to how he has gotten to this point. I wish the Hardys didn’t selfishly bigfoot this moment, but Slater did and said all the right things. I like that Slater doesn’t try to overcomplicate things. Eddie Edwards showing slight respect for Ricky Sosa and the rest of the System seeing him side-eyed Zoey Serrano and Shayna Baszler do look like certified badasses, as a team, and that is something that I can’t remember in the Knockouts tag team division. I hope TNA has a clear path as to how to establish multiple credible teams for them to decimate. TNA has not successfully done this for quite some time. Nic Nemeth being a heel foil for Trey Miguel’s ladder match win to become Leon Slater’s first title challenger The Hardys Opening the show (again) and booking everything for the night How does one exactly determine if someone loses a match intentionally? Well that was one of the weird stipulations that we got from the Hardys 35th anniversary celebration which apparently gives them the power to book an entire show. I guess the other twelve authority figures were busy tonight. Also, calling the Righteous and the SYX two of the Hardys “greatest rivals” made me roll my eyes so hard that my retinas detached. What a weird show opening promo and beginning to an episode with an already weird supposition. It just always feels like the Hardys have to be looming over everything like Amazing Reds first promo after his feel-good X-Division Title win and Leon Slater’s first promo after becoming the youngest World Champion on relevant American television of all-time. The Hardys coming out and making both Nemeth brothers look like doofuses The fact that the Hardys were able to come out and instantly create tension between the Nemeth brothers was so cartoonish and unbelievable based on no strife between the two prior to tonight. Unceremoniously having the Righteous face the SYX in a big tables match with zero build I say this every week, like a broken record, but these are always bad. They almost never make any sense or advance anything. The one positive is they’re almost always short. The Hardys scheduling a match between themselves and AJ Francis & Expressions The Hardys really should have put themselves in a match against a credible team (like Frankie Kazarian and Avery Styles) to put them over. Instead we get them in what was essentially a comedy match with Francis and a debuting Expressions that felt completely inconsequential. This win did nothing for the Hardys and was an empty way to get them on the show. Xia Brookside having a “contractual rematch” for Indi Hartwell’s Knockout Title

llm_long: Will Ospreay will defend the AEW World Championship against Samoa Joe, Mike Bailey, Adam Copeland, Konosuke Takeshita, Kazuchika Okada, Ricochet, and Darby Allin in a Clockwork Carnage Match at WrestleDream 2026. The match begins with two wrestlers in the ring, with the remaining six entering at three-minute intervals. Eliminations by pinfall or submission cannot occur until all eight competitors have entered the ring.

Once all wrestlers are in the ring, the match advances to a second stage featuring a 15-minute time limit. Competitors score points through pinfalls and submissions during this period. The wrestler with the most points at the end of the time limit will be declared the AEW World Champion.

Mercedes Mone will defend the AEW Women's World Championship against Thekla. Mone comes off a successful title defense against Queen Aminata on the October 6 episode of AEW Dynamite Grand Slam France. Thekla earned her title opportunity by defeating Willow Nightingale in a number one contender's match at All Out on September 26.

Hangman Adam Page, Brody King, and Ring of Honor World Champion Bandido will challenge Swerve Strickland, Kofi Creed, and Austin Creed for the AEW World Trios Championship in a best two-out-of-three-falls match. The trio previously came up short against the champions at All Out last month.

Matt Jackson and Nick Jackson will defend the AEW World Tag Team Championship against Kyle Fletcher and Kevin Knight. The Young Bucks won the titles at All Out on September 26 in a three-way match that also included Christian Cage, Adam Copeland, Dax Harwood, and Cash Wheeler.

Persephone will defend the TBS Championship against Hyan, Queen Aminata, and Dani Luna in a four-way match. Hyan and Dani Luna defeated Persephone and Britt Baker on the recent Dynamite and Collision double feature, leading to a beatdown that was interrupted by Aminata.

title: Max Caster Steps Away From Wrestling For Therapy
raw_title: Max Caster Says He's Stepping Away From Wrestling And Going To Therapy
summary_src: Max Caster speaks on his future. Caster made his debut at TNA Slammiversary, answering Moose's open challenge. During his pre-match rap, Caster referenced the bombing in Riyadh.
body: Caster made his debut at TNA Slammiversary, answering Moose’s open challenge. During his pre-match rap, Caster referenced the bombing in Riyadh. “In the span of one day, I started a contract and ended a contract with TNA Wrestling. I put out a statement, I addressed it and apologized to a lot of people, but the one group I didn’t get the apologize to is all the fans. I really appreciate the support, everybody who has reached out after this happened. A lot of people were excited to watch TNA for the first time or come back to the product, and now a lot of people are disappointed that I’m not on the show. Thank you guys here at ACW for welcoming me. For that, I say, I love you and thank you. I don’t know what my next move is. I don’t know where I’ll be, but I will be stepping away from the ring for an extended period of time. I’m gonna go home, I’m gonna go to therapy, I’m gonna get it right so that the next time I’m in the ring it feels like I’m at home,” he said. Max Caster appeared at tonight’s ACW show and once again addressed what happened with him and TNA. Says he’s headed to therapy and stepping away from wrestling for an extended period of time. pic.twitter.com/XDPZtyWNfV
summary: Max Caster debuted for TNA at Slammiversary by answering Moose's open challenge but drew backlash for a pre-match rap referencing the Riyadh bombing. He issued an apology and later appeared at an ACW event where he thanked fans for their support, expressed regret over disappointing viewers, and announced he would take an extended break from the ring to focus on therapy and personal improvement.

kind.quote: I will be stepping away from the ring for an extended period of time. I’m gonna go home, I’m gonna go to therapy, I’m gonna get it right so that the next time I’m in the ring it feels like I’m at home.

llm_long: Max Caster debuted for TNA at Slammiversary by answering Moose's open challenge. In his pre-match rap, he referenced the bombing in Riyadh, which led to him being released from the company on the same day he signed a contract.

Caster issued a public statement and apologized to many people involved. He noted that he had not yet directly apologized to the fans who were excited about his appearance or returning to the product but ended up disappointed.
At an ACW event, Caster thanked the promotion for welcoming him. He expressed appreciation for the fan support he received after the incident and stated his love and thanks to those in attendance.

Caster announced that he will step away from wrestling for an extended period. He plans to return home and attend therapy to address his issues so that future appearances in the ring feel comfortable again.

The win provided Kross with revenge after previously falling victim to the Black Mist from the opposing team.
Divine Dominion previously held the AEW Women’s Tag Team Championships but lost them to the Brawling Birds at AEW All In.
Both teams had competed earlier in an AEW Women’s Tag Team Championship number one contenders match on AEW Collision Grand Slam France, which was won by Harley Cameron and Kris Statlander.

llm_long: Rusev returned to the ring at the WWE live event in Hawaii on October 16. The appearance marked his first match since sustaining an injury on July 27.
The injury occurred during a match against Je’Von Evans at the Intuit Dome in Los Angeles. Rusev experienced complete numbness in his arms, requiring him to roll out of the ring.
Medical staff considered stopping the match as Rusev reported he could not feel his hands. After regaining sensation, he re-entered the ring and completed the bout despite significant pain.
Rusev's wife CJ Perry noted that he received medical clearance in September. She emphasized that he finished the July match to do what was right for business rather than having the bout stopped.
Perry addressed online rumors suggesting Rusev avoided putting others over. She clarified that he consistently works to create strong stories and support the business.

title: Legal Watch: WWE Star Hit With Shocking Lawsuit Over Alleged Unwanted Lap Dance Caught On Camea During Raw
raw_title: WWE Star Hit With Shocking Lawsuit Over Alleged Unwanted Lap Dance Caught On Camea During Raw
body: An off-duty sheriff’s officer has reportedly sued Montez Ford, a WWE star, after a live event in Chicago. The deputy did off-duty security work for the company during a “Monday Night Raw” show a couple of months ago. The shift came with an unexpected and unwanted performance by Ford, which allegedly caused multiple issues in the officer’s life. He sued the company and the superstar for having a “sexualized lap dance” performed on him during the event. The Daily Mail reported that Noel Lucas filed a lawsuit against World Wrestling Entertainment (WWE), Event Services, LLC, and Kenneth Crawford, who performs as Montez Ford. Lucas claims that he suffered “substantial humiliation, embarrassment, and emotional distress” after the incident. Footage from the July 6 Netflix live stream showed the moment. “Defendant Crawford then began performing a sexually provocative dance immediately in front of and over Plaintiff [Lucas], repeatedly thrusting and gyrating his hips and pelvis towards Plaintiff, performing a sexualized ‘lap dance,” read the lawsuit. Additionally, the lawsuit accuses defendants of violating the Illinois Gender Violence Act. This allows survivors to sue individual perpetrators, anyone involved in the acts and even employers. Lucas’ lawsuit alleges 14 total counts, including assault and battery. He added that classmates “mocked and ridiculed” his children at school after the lap dance moment went viral. title: In Memoriam: Ex-wrestler Pac's sudden death cause revealed by Cook County Medical Examiner's Office
raw_title: Ex-wrestler Pac's sudden death cause revealed by Cook County Medical Examiner's Office | OutKick
body: Former wrestling star Pac, whose real name was Benjamin Satterley , died of bronchial asthma late last month, the California Post said, citing the Cook County Medical Examiner’s Office. Pac was 40 years old when All Elite Wrestling (AEW) announced his death. "All Elite Wrestling is saddened to announce the passing of Benjamin Satterley, aka Pac," the company said. "A native of Newcastle upon Tyne, England, Satterley began his wrestling career in 2004 and went on to perform for wrestling organizations all over the world, captivating fans with innovative high-flying moves and incredible in-ring ability. Awesome Championship Wrestling national champion Zack Clayton was in action at Reckoning on Saturday, May 16, 2026. (Fox News Digital) "Pac signed with All Elite Wrestling in 2019 and held multiple AEW Championships and competed in some of the most memorable matches in AEW history. Our condolences go out to Satterley’s family, friends and fans." He challenged Andrade El Idolo for the AEW National Championship at All Out, which occurred just one day before his death. Pac was found dead in a rental car the next day outside of a CAVA outside of Chicago, where that bout occurred. Officers saw his phone's GPS guiding him to O'Hare airport. Des Plaines, Illinois, police investigate Benjamin Satterley's death on Sept. 27, 2026. His rental car was found near a Cava. (Des Plaines, Illinois, Police Department) PRO WRESTLER TAKING HIS SHOT AT RUNNING HIS OWN INDEPENDENT SHOW: 'LET'S JUST TAKE IT UP A NOTCH' Pac was one of the first wrestlers to sign with All Elite Wrestling in 2019. He was a two-time trios champion and the inaugural all-Atlantic champion. Before wrestling in AEW, he was with WWE and known as Adrian Neville. Satterley was a two-time cruiserweight champion, an NXT champion and two-time NXT tag team champion.

title: MLW Sets Streaming Distribution Deal with Tubi
raw_title: MLW Sets Streaming Distribution Deal with Tubi
body: Flagship Weekly Series to Stream Free on Tubi, Thursdays at 8 PM ET. Major League Wrestling (MLW) today announced a new streaming distribution agreement with Tubi for its weekly flagship series, MLW FUSION . Beginning Sept. 17, new episodes of MLW’s flagship weekly series will stream Thursdays at 8 PM ET free on Tubi. “Wrestling should be easy to find and free to watch,” said MLW Founder and CEO Court Bauer. “We built MLW around that, no paywalls, no subscription barriers, nothing standing between a fan and the show, and Tubi shares that same fan-first philosophy at scale. Starting Sept. 17, Tubi’s 110 million monthly active users have a front row seat on Thursday nights to the hardest hitting hour in pro wrestling, and it won’t cost a dime.” MLW FUSION serves up a distinctive brand of pro wrestling, blending cutting-edge, new-era wrestling with the grit, colorful characters and throwback flavor of ’rasslin. Built around big fights, heated rivalries, championship stakes and an anything-can-happen attitude, FUSION brings a rowdy, hard-hitting edge to the modern wrestling landscape. MLW will also continue to produce live special events alongside the weekly series. MLW is executive produced by Court Bauer, Paul Walter Hauser and Bryan Walsh.
summary: The latest: the latest: Major League Wrestling today revealed a new streaming distribution agreement with Tubi for its weekly flagship series, MLW FUSION . Beginning Sept. 17, new episodes of MLW’s flagship weekly series will stream Thursdays at 8 PM ET free on Tubi. Wrestling should be easy to find and free to watch.

llm.headline: MLW Fusion Heads to Tubi for Free Streaming
llm.summary: Major League Wrestling has signed a distribution deal with Tubi to air its flagship weekly series MLW Fusion. New episodes will stream free every Thursday at 8 PM ET beginning September 17. The partnership aligns with both companies' commitment to making wrestling accessible without paywalls or subscriptions.

llm_long: MLW has reached a television streaming agreement with Tubi. The partnership includes a rights fee along with a revenue share tied to library content integration. The deal was finalized in August.

The agreement arrives nearly five years after MLW filed an antitrust lawsuit against WWE. The suit claimed WWE influenced Tubi to drop existing and potential deals with MLW. Tubi was owned by Fox, which broadcast WWE SmackDown during that period.
The lawsuit named Stephanie McMahon as the WWE executive who applied pressure on Tubi regarding MLW. A settlement between the parties was reached in December 2023.
MLW brought back its program Fusion in May following a three-year break. The show has been available at no cost on YouTube.

MLW owner Court Bauer stated that the promotion was built on a model with no paywalls or subscription barriers between fans and the content. He noted that Tubi follows a similar fan-first approach on a larger scale.

body: Max Caster has announced that he will step away from professional wrestling for an extended period following his departure from TNA Wrestling. Speaking to the crowd, Caster referred to the controversy surrounding his appearance at TNA Bound for Glory the previous weekend, which led to the company cutting ties with him. “I don’t know if everybody here is aware of what happened with me this past week,” he began. “If you don’t know, in the span of one day, I started a contract and ended a contract with TNA Wrestling.” Caster said that while he had already issued a public statement and apologized to several people, he had not yet addressed the fans. A lot of people were excited to watch TNA for the first time. A lot of people were excited to come back to the product, and now a lot of people are disappointed that I’m not on the show. After thanking those who had supported him and the ACW audience for welcoming him, Caster announced his plans to take an extended break. I don’t know what my next move is. I don’t know where I’ll be, but I will be stepping away from the ring for an extended period of time. So I’m gonna go home. I’m gonna go to therapy. I’m gonna get it right, so that next time I’m in the ring, it feels like I’m at home, just like you guys made me feel here tonight. Caster concluded his remarks by telling the audience, “So, finally, for the last time in a long time, you are looking live at the best wrestler alive. Thank you.” The announcement comes six days after Caster made his TNA debut against Moose at Bound for Glory on October 11. During his entrance rap, he referenced deadly attacks in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, drawing criticism for the line, “I drop bombs. You don’t even have to fly to Riyadh.” TNA announced the following day that Caster would no longer wrestle for the promotion. The company apologized for the remarks, acknowledged responsibility for allowing them to air, and removed the segment from replays and social media. The former AEW World Tag Team Champion had entered free agency earlier this month following the expiration of his AEW contract. Max Caster appeared at tonight’s ACW show and once again addressed what happened with him and TNA. Says he’s headed to therapy and stepping away from wrestling for an extended period of time. pic.twitter.com/XDPZtyWNfV

title: Motor City Machine Guns Lead FTR 1-0
raw_title: Motor City Machine Guns beat FTR after Tailgate Brawl main event spills into AEW WrestleDream
summary_src: The Motor City Machine Guns took a 1-0 lead over FTR after the main event of AEW Tailgate Brawl continued well into the WrestleDream pay-per-view.
body: The Motor City Machine Guns took a 1-0 lead over FTR after the main event of AEW Tailgate Brawl continued well into the WrestleDream pay-per-view. The one-hour pre-show aired on TNT and HBO Max immediately before Saturday’s event at Addition Financial Arena in Orlando. Alex Shelley & Chris Sabin began their first match in a best-of-five series against Dax Harwood & Cash Wheeler shortly before the scheduled 8 pm ET conclusion of Tailgate Brawl. Rather than stop at the top of the hour, the match continued as WrestleDream went live on pay-per-view. The PPV opened with its usual introduction and pyro before returning directly to the match, which ultimately occupied approximately the first 17 minutes of the main broadcast. FTR controlled Shelley for an extended period before he eventually reached Sabin. Stokely Hathaway attempted to interfere but accidentally struck Harwood, leading to a series of near falls for the Machine Guns. FTR later hit Sabin with a spike piledriver, but he kicked out. The Guns also came close with Skull and Bones, with Wheeler placing Harwood’s foot on the bottom rope to stop the count. Shelley & Sabin eventually countered an attempted Shatter Machine and hit Wheeler with a double pumphandle slam for the victory, giving them the first win in the five-match series. Another notable development saw Jay White make an unexpectedly early return to the ring. White teamed with Austin & Colten Gunn and The Conglomeration against the Death Riders & The Dogs. AEW had announced on October 3 that White was expected to miss one to two months with an undisclosed injury sustained around All Out. Instead, he returned after two weeks and received a strong reaction before entering the match. The Death Riders & The Dogs ultimately won when Claudio Castagnoli launched Wheeler Yuta from the top rope onto Colten Gunn for the pin. The two sides continued brawling after the bell. Divine Dominion opened the broadcast by defeating Sisters of Sin. Megan Bayne & Lena Kross isolated Skye Blue for much of the match before finishing Julia Hart with their From Heaven to Hell double chokeslam. Josh Alexander, Jake Doyle & Wardlow then made short work of Alex Breeze, Papi D & Rhys Maddox. Wardlow delivered multiple powerbombs before the Don Callis Family recorded the victory.
summary: The Motor City Machine Guns defeated FTR in the opening contest of AEW WrestleDream after their best-of-five series match spilled over from the Tailgate Brawl pre-show. The bout began on the one-hour TNT and HBO Max special before continuing live on pay-per-view for roughly 17 minutes. Stokely Hathaway's interference backfired on Dax Harwood, and the Guns overcame a spike piledriver on Chris Sabin to secure the first fall.

title: Tony Khan's Tribute To Pac — Complete Transcript
raw_title: COMPLETE TRANSCRIPT: TONY KHAN'S TRIBUTE TO PAC
body: Jalwa Game Goa Game Raja Game MaanWin DMFirst Veer Game COMPLETE TRANSCRIPT: TONY KHAN'S TRIBUTE TO PAC By Mike Johnson on 2026-09-28 17:21:00 At tonight's Ring of Honor taping in Jacksonville, AEW President Tony Khan gave the following tribute to the late Ben "Pac" Satterley: "...I'm also here to talk to you about something more important than wrestling. As somebody who epitomized the very best of wrestling and the very best of humanity, one of the best people I've ever known. And, sadly, the world lost PAC. In AEW, he wrestled as Neville for WWE, and he wrestled all over the world. Ben was an absolutely fantastic wrestler, an absolutely fantastic human being. A great person to work with, and a great person to spend time with. Before we begin the wrestling today and for these tapings, I would like to have a 10-bell salute for PAC. Please, if we can have a moment of silence and a 10-bell salute. Thank you." "We started AEW right out back here, in the parking lot over here, and we announced the launch of the company January 8th of 2019, in person out here, in this very parking lot, here in Jacksonville. Some of you were probably even there that day. And I first met PAC before that. From the very beginning, when we talked about launching AEW, he was somebody that I knew would be a big part of the company, and somebody that outside of wrestling also became a big part of my life. Just like for the wrestlers in the back and so many people around wrestling, PAC... Ben has been a huge part of their lives. And you're going to hear a lot about that in the week to come. I wanted to announce here to all of you, ahead of these Ring of Honor tapings—I'm very glad you're all here. For the wrestling today, as you've been to a lot of these tapings, as you know, there will be plenty of wrestling today. But it's important for us to take a moment and talk about somebody that has accomplished so much in life as a wrestler, as a friend, somebody who I think could have been successful in any walk of life that they set their mind to, and he set his mind to being one of the greatest wrestlers of all time. And I believe he succeeded in that. I wanted to announce to all of you Wednesday night Dynamite this week will be a tribute show to PAC. And, very fittingly, the very first Dynamite, as I recall, in Pittsburgh—'cause Dynamite will be in Pittsburgh this Wednesday—and PAC was in the main event of the very first Dynamite in Pittsburgh, as I recall, against Jon Moxley. A man whose career Ben will be linked to for a long time. Ben is a very first-class person, and he left behind a lovely wife and a lot of great friends and a legacy that will last forever. I appreciate you all being here. Thank you very much. And just know that all the wrestlers wrestling here on Ring of Honor tonight and everybody wrestling this Wednesday is doing so voluntarily, and I believe out of love for Ben. Thank you very much."

body: Jalwa Game Goa Game Raja Game MaanWin DMFirst Veer Game TONY KHAN ON WHAT'S NEXT FOR AEW AFTER PARAMOUNT MERGER, WILL OSPREAY WALKOUT, STEVEN BORDEN AND MORE By Mike Johnson on 2026-09-24 15:42:00 AEW President Tony Khan took part in a media call today to discuss Saturday's All Out PPV. Highlights: Mercedes Mone : "Mercedes Moné was originally scheduled to wrestle on AEW All Out, and that's the nature of wrestling. It's a hard-hitting sport, there are injuries, and just like in all sports, you have to have a deep roster and be able to think on your feet and be flexible. That's what's great about AEW: there are so many great wrestlers in this company, and in this case, multiple former world champions looking to step up and fight each other to get in line to fight the champ. In Mercedes' case, it's not a long, long-term injury; it's something where she'll be back. I think she'll be back next month, and I'm almost certain she'll be back next month. That's the plan, is for Mercedes to return in October. That's why we have this match on the pay-per-view to determine who will challenge for the World Title at our next pay-per-view, Wrestledream. So Mercedes' injury did affect plans. She was originally set to wrestle at AEW All Out, and I think she very much wants to wrestle on Saturday, but the doctors have not cleared her. So that's a great question by you. Yes, Mercedes' injury did change things, but Mercedes is a fighting champion. She's going to be, I think, a fighting champion, and she will be fighting next month." World's End 2026 given the Jaguars have a Sunday game towards the end of December: " There will definitely be a World's End pay-per-view this year. That's a really great question and very good observation by you looking at the calendar. There will be a World's End pay-per-view, and we're looking ahead and planning the calendar for later in the year. Of course, World's End will be the culmination of the Continental Classic, which is always one of the highlights of AEW in recent years, and World's End is a tremendous pay-per-view, I believe. I really enjoyed the show last year, and as you said, speaking of the Jags, it was a great memory for me. I didn't get a lot of sleep that day or that night or the next day, but it was a great memory having that World's End pay-per-view, and then taking a red-eye to Indianapolis and arriving at the hotel as the coaches were getting on the bus to go to the stadium, and then going to the stadium and the Jaguars had a great win, and then going back home and watching World's End again! title: Divine Dominion Score WrestleDream Win After Black Mist Incident
raw_title: Divine Dominion Score WrestleDream Win After Black Mist Incident
body: 0 Divine Dominion secured a victory over Sisters of Sin at the AEW WrestleDream Tailgate Brawl, with Lena Kross and Megan Bayne settling their rivalry with Julia Hart and Skye Blue . The women’s tag team clash featured several close calls before a decisive counter turned the tide in Divine Dominion’s favor. The contest carried extra tension after the Sisters of Sin used Black Mist against their opponents. Kross and Bayne entered the match looking to get even, but Hart and Blue made them work for every opening. The Sisters of Sin initially used their speed and teamwork to challenge Divine Dominion’s power. Hart and Blue combined for double-team offense, including a double superkick that left their opponents in trouble, while Hart came close to securing the victory with a series of high-impact moves. Divine Dominion answered with their own power-based offense, including German suplexes against both opponents. Hart and Blue continued fighting back, with Blue even breaking up a pin attempt after Kross and Bayne combined to attack Hart. The decisive sequence came when Hart climbed the ropes and attempted a Tornado DDT on Kross. However, Kross stopped the move before Hart could complete it, leaving the Sisters of Sin unable to capitalize on the opening. Bayne then joined Kross, and the pair delivered a double chokeslam to Hart. Kross covered her opponent to secure the pinfall, giving Divine Dominion the win and a measure of revenge for the earlier Black Mist attack. The result offers Divine Dominion a chance to regain momentum after losing the AEW Women’s World Tag Team Championships to Jamie Hayter and Alex Windsor of the Brawling Birds at All In. The teams had also competed in a number-one contenders match at Collision Grand Slam France, where Kris Statlander and Harley Cameron emerged victorious. The post Divine Dominion Score WrestleDream Win After Black Mist Incident appeared first on Wrestlezone .
