title: Mercedes Moné Retains AEW Title vs Thekla at WrestleDream
raw_title: Mercedes Moné retains AEW Women’s World Championship against Thekla at WrestleDream
summary_src: Mercedes Moné retained the AEW Women’s World Championship against Thekla in the first official match of AEW WrestleDream.
body: Mercedes Moné retained the AEW Women’s World Championship against Thekla in the first official match of AEW WrestleDream. Moné pinned Thekla with the Moné Maker on Saturday at Addition Financial Arena in Orlando, Florida. Thekla began the match by immediately targeting Moné, who was still wearing a protective face mask following the nose injury she suffered at All In. The challenger escaped an early Statement Maker and later sent Moné into the barricade before scoring a near fall with a diving crossbody. Moné took control with a lungblower and Meteora before applying a Romero Special. Thekla recovered and hit a spider suplex from the ropes, followed by a double stomp to Moné’s back and a spear for two. Thekla later trapped Moné in a modified headscissors submission, but the champion reached the ropes. A subsequent curb stomp also produced only a two-count after Moné again got a foot on the bottom rope. The finish came after Moné removed her protective mask while referee Stephon Smith was occupied with Thekla. Moné struck Thekla with the mask and attempted the Moné Maker. Thekla countered into an O’Connor Roll for a close near fall, but Moné avoided another curb stomp and hit the Moné Maker to retain. Thekla earned the title shot by defeating Willow Nightingale at All Out. Moné won the championship from Nightingale at All In: London on August 30. She subsequently missed All Out because of the nose injury suffered at Wembley Stadium before returning to action in late September.
summary: Mercedes Moné successfully defended the AEW Women’s World Championship against Thekla in the opening match of WrestleDream at Addition Financial Arena in Orlando. Thekla targeted Moné’s injured nose early and traded near falls throughout, but Moné removed her protective mask and used it to strike Thekla before finishing with the Moné Maker for the pinfall victory.

raw_title: Mercedes Mone Defeats Thekla, Retains AEW Women's World Title At WrestleDream 2026
summary_src: At AEW WrestleDream 2026, Mercedes Moné retained the Women's World Championship over Thekla in her second title defense.
body: Moné sent Thekla into three corners to start the match. Thekla sent her face first into the last one. Moné put her in the Statement Maker. Moné went to the outside when Thekla moved. Thekla sent her face first into the apron and into the barricade twice. Thekla kicked her in the side of the head as she dangled over the ropes and landed a crossbody. Thekla got in the spider position, but Moné picked her up, kneed her in the face and landed a lungblower. She followed with a meteora. Moné pulled Thekla's arms behind her and wrenched her before putting her knee in her back. She moved into the Romero Special. She sent Thekla face first into the turnbuckle, But Thekla put her in the tarantula hold. Moné landed a lung blower on the apron. She hit her knees on the ringpost when Thekla dodged a meteora. Thekla double stomped her back on the outside. They battled up top before Thekla landed a spider suplex. She followed with a double stomp to the back and a spear. Moné landed a Sunset Flip Bomb and meteora. Thekla locked her in a submission, but Moné got to the ropes. Thekla curbstomped her and covered her, but Moné got her foot on the ropes. Moné removed her face mask and when Thekla grabbed her by the hair, she hit Thekla in the face with it. Thekla reversed Moné Maker and rolled her up for 2.99. Moné landed Moné Maker for the win.
summary: Mercedes Mone successfully defended her AEW Women's World Championship against Thekla in a hard-fought bout at WrestleDream. The match featured intense back-and-forth action with multiple submission attempts, high-flying maneuvers and stiff strikes from both competitors. Mone ultimately overcame Thekla's resilient offense to secure the victory and retain her title.

llm_long: Will Ospreay will defend the AEW World Championship against Samoa Joe, Mike Bailey, Adam Copeland, Konosuke Takeshita, Kazuchika Okada, Ricochet, and Darby Allin in a Clockwork Carnage Match at WrestleDream 2026. The match begins with two wrestlers in the ring, with the remaining six entering at three-minute intervals. Eliminations by pinfall or submission cannot occur until all eight competitors have entered the ring.

Once all wrestlers are in the ring, the match advances to a second stage featuring a 15-minute time limit. Competitors score points through pinfalls and submissions during this period. The wrestler with the most points at the end of the time limit will be declared the AEW World Champion.

Mercedes Mone will defend the AEW Women's World Championship against Thekla. Mone comes off a successful title defense against Queen Aminata on the October 6 episode of AEW Dynamite Grand Slam France. Thekla earned her title opportunity by defeating Willow Nightingale in a number one contender's match at All Out on September 26.

Hangman Adam Page, Brody King, and Ring of Honor World Champion Bandido will challenge Swerve Strickland, Kofi Creed, and Austin Creed for the AEW World Trios Championship in a best two-out-of-three-falls match. The trio previously came up short against the champions at All Out last month.

Matt Jackson and Nick Jackson will defend the AEW World Tag Team Championship against Kyle Fletcher and Kevin Knight. The Young Bucks won the titles at All Out on September 26 in a three-way match that also included Christian Cage, Adam Copeland, Dax Harwood, and Cash Wheeler.

Persephone will defend the TBS Championship against Hyan, Queen Aminata, and Dani Luna in a four-way match. Hyan and Dani Luna defeated Persephone and Britt Baker on the recent Dynamite and Collision double feature, leading to a beatdown that was interrupted by Aminata.

title: Nick Wayne beats Jericho in series finale
raw_title: Nick Wayne defeats Chris Jericho at AEW WrestleDream to take series 2-1
summary_src: Nick Wayne defeated Chris Jericho at AEW WrestleDream on Saturday to win their three-match series 2-1.
body: Nick Wayne defeated Chris Jericho at AEW WrestleDream on Saturday to win their three-match series 2-1. The 21-year-old scored the pin with a small package after a closing sequence in which both wrestlers attempted to outmaneuver one another with low blows. Wayne made his entrance with new music and graphics before Jericho immediately took the fight outside. Jericho sent Wayne into the barricade and later dropped him with a Death Valley Driver onto the steel steps. Wayne responded with a moonsault to the floor and later hit a 450 splash for a near fall. Jericho twice applied the Walls of Jericho, with Wayne reaching the ropes on the first occasion and escaping the second. During the closing minutes, Wayne shoved referee Bryce Remsburg aside and attempted a low blow. Jericho showed that he had anticipated the tactic by revealing an athletic cup beneath his gear. Jericho struck Wayne with the cup until Remsburg confiscated it. With the referee disposing of the object, Jericho then delivered a low blow of his own. Afterward, Wayne took the microphone and emphasized that “Nick Wayne beat Chris Jericho,” with pyro going off as he celebrated up the entrance ramp. The match completed a rivalry that began during the summer after tensions between the two developed following the All In Casino Gauntlet. Jericho won their first match on the September 16 Dynamite with a roll-up. Wayne evened the series by defeating Jericho on Collision: Grand Slam France on October 10, leading AEW to book the rubber match for WrestleDream.
summary: Nick Wayne defeated Chris Jericho at AEW WrestleDream to win their three-match series two matches to one. The 21-year-old scored the victory with a small package pinfall after a frantic closing stretch featuring multiple low blow attempts by both men. Jericho used a protective cup to block one attempt before landing his own low blow once the referee removed the object.

llm_long: Nick Wayne defeated Chris Jericho at AEW WrestleDream on Saturday. The victory allowed Wayne to win their three-match series by a score of 2-1. Wayne secured the pinfall with a small package following a sequence where both competitors tried to gain the advantage with low blows.

Wayne made his entrance using new music and graphics. Jericho quickly took the action outside the ring and sent Wayne into the barricade. Jericho later delivered a Death Valley Driver onto the steel steps.

Wayne countered with a moonsault to the floor and followed up with a 450 splash that resulted in a near fall. Jericho applied the Walls of Jericho twice during the bout. Wayne reached the ropes to break the first submission and escaped the second.

In the closing minutes Wayne shoved the referee aside and attempted a low blow. Jericho revealed he was wearing an athletic cup under his gear to block the move. Jericho then struck Wayne with the cup until the referee took it away.

While the referee disposed of the cup Jericho delivered a low blow of his own. Wayne ultimately scored the pin to conclude the match. After the bout Wayne took the microphone to declare that he had beaten Jericho before celebrating with pyro on the entrance ramp.

The rivalry between the two began during the summer after tensions arose following the All In Casino Gauntlet. Jericho won the first match on the September 16 episode of Dynamite with a roll-up. Wayne tied the series by defeating Jericho on the October 10 episode of Collision: Grand Slam France which set up the decisive match at WrestleDream.

Shelley performed a top rope splash on Harwood for a good near fall. The Guns hit a double-team move on Harwood and had him beat, but Wheeler put his partner’s foot over the bottom rope. An “AEW” chant broke out while the broadcast team noted that they were over 25 minutes into the match. Harwood and Wheeler went for the Shatter Machine on Sabin, but he avoided the move. raw_title: Mercedes Mone Beats Thekla to Retain AEW Women's World Title at WrestleDream 2026
body: Updated 2026 AEW WrestleDream Card and Predictions for Match Order Bleacher Report 1d AEW WrestleDream Live Grades 🔠 Bleacher Report 1h Copeland To Retire in 2027 ‼️ Bleacher Report 2d Near the end of the match, Moné used her mask to attack Thekla. She then tried to land the Mone Maker, but Thekla countered and rolled up Moné for a pin attempt. However, Moné couldn't be held back for long. She evaded Thekla's attempt to hit Blackout and countered with the Moné Maker for the win. After falling short in multiple attempts previously, Moné finally became AEW women's world champion for the first time in August at All In when she beat Willow Nightingale. The CEO suffered a broken nose during that physical bout, which kept her out of action for the next month. With Mercedes not cleared to compete at All Out last month, Thekla and Nightingale faced off in a No. 1 contender's match for the right to challenge for the AEW women's world title at WrestleDream. Thekla was victorious, and she gained retribution in the process, as Willow was the one who ended her 165-day reign as AEW women's champ. Moné returned to action on the Sept. 30 episode of Dynamite, which paid tribute to Pac, losing to Marina Shafir, Thunder Rosa and Hyan in a six-woman tag team match. With that, Moné locked in her spot on the WrestleDream card and cemented a highly anticipated clash with Thekla. Since Thekla had a lengthy title reign with All In approaching, many assumed she would face Mercedes then, but Willow's title win threw a wrench into those plans. Fans had to wait a bit longer than anticipated for Moné vs. Thekla, but they delivered, and The CEO prevailed.

summary_src: The Young Bucks retained the AEW World Tag Team Championship against Kevin Knight & Kyle Fletcher at WrestleDream on Saturday.
body: The Young Bucks retained the AEW World Tag Team Championship against Kevin Knight & Kyle Fletcher at WrestleDream on Saturday. Matt & Nick Jackson pinned Knight after a BTE Trigger at Addition Financial Arena in Orlando, Florida. Knight & Fletcher controlled several stretches of the match and repeatedly matched the Bucks’ pace, including borrowing some of their opponents’ trademark double-team offense early on. The challengers came close after Knight hit a Coast-to-Coast dropkick and Fletcher followed with a sheer-drop brainbuster. Fletcher later delivered a top-rope brainbuster before Knight added a UFO Splash, but Nick broke up the pin. Knight tagged himself in as Fletcher appeared to want to remain legal, prompting an argument between the partners. Moments later, Knight attempted a springboard clothesline intended for the Bucks but struck Fletcher instead. Matt & Nick immediately capitalized, hitting Knight with the BTE Trigger for the three-count. Earlier, the Bucks also survived a series of high-impact sequences that included Fletcher hitting a Michinoku Driver and Knight landing a standing hurricanrana while Matt and Nick were positioned on their opponents’ shoulders. Knight & Fletcher earned their title opportunity at All Out when they defeated Darby Allin & Steven Borden after the match was stopped by the ringside doctor. The Young Bucks became the first four-time AEW World Tag Team Champions later that night, winning a three-way ladder match against then-champions Adam Copeland & Christian Cage and FTR. After Saturday’s defense, Nick Jackson was heard telling the camera, “I don’t know how many of those I have left, Tony,” as the Bucks celebrated up the ramp.
summary: Matt and Nick Jackson defeated Kevin Knight and Kyle Fletcher to keep the AEW World Tag Team Championship at the Addition Financial Arena in Orlando. The challengers matched the champions' pace throughout and came close to victory with multiple high-impact moves including a Coast-to-Coast dropkick, brainbusters and a UFO Splash. Internal disagreement between Knight and Fletcher allowed the Young Bucks to capitalize with a BTE Trigger on Knight for the pinfall.

The match begins with two wrestlers in the ring, with the remaining six entering at three-minute intervals. Eliminations by pinfall or submission cannot occur until all eight competitors have entered the ring.

Once all wrestlers are in the ring, the match advances to a second stage featuring a 15-minute time limit. Competitors score points through pinfalls and submissions during this period. The wrestler with the most points at the end of the time limit will be declared the AEW World Champion.

title: Benjamin Satterley, pro wrestling star known as Pac, dead at 40
raw_title: Benjamin Satterley, pro wrestling star known as Pac, dead at 40 | OutKick
body: Benjamin Satterley, the pro wrestling star known as Pac, has died, All Elite Wrestling (AEW) announced on Sunday night. He was 40. "All Elite Wrestling is saddened to announce the passing of Benjamin Satterley, aka Pac," the company said. "A native of Newcastle upon Tyne, England, Satterley began his wrestling career in 2004 and went on to perform for wrestling organizations all over the world, captivating fans with innovative high-flying moves and incredible in-ring ability. "Pac signed with All Elite Wrestling in 2019 and held multiple AEW Championships and competed in some of the most memorable matches in AEW history. Our condolences go out to Satterley’s family, friends and fans." The circumstances behind Pac’s death were unclear. He challenged Andrade El Idolo for the AEW National Championship at All Out, which occurred on Saturday in Chicago. Pac was one of the first wrestlers to sign with All Elite Wrestling in 2019. He was a two-time trios champion and the inaugural all-Atlantic champion. Before wrestling in AEW, he was with WWE and known as Adrian Neville. Satterley was a two-time cruiserweight champion, an NXT champion and two-time NXT tag team champion.
summary: Benjamin Satterley, the pro wrestling star known as Pac, has died, All Elite Wrestling revealed on Sunday night. All Elite Wrestling is saddened to announce the passing of Benjamin Satterley, aka Pac, the company explained.

title: Max Caster Steps Away From Wrestling

summary_src: Just days after making his TNA debut at Bound for Glory, Max Caster has now decided to step away from wrestling. During his TNA Bound for Glory match against Moose, Caster made his entrance while freestyle rapping his way to the ring.
body: Just days after making his TNA debut at Bound for Glory, Max Caster has now decided to step away from wrestling. During his TNA Bound for Glory match against Moose, Caster made his entrance while freestyle rapping his way to the ring. However, his rap consisted of a few offensive verses about the recent Riyadh airport missile attack in Saudi Arabia. Caster’s words soon became a major controversy as many fans spoke out, and TNA later decided to part ways with him and release an official statement. Caster also later shared an official apology v ideo. Now, days later, Caster recently appeared on ACW , where Caster opened up and addressed the incident. “ In the span of one day, I started a contract and ended a contract with TNA Wrestling. I put out a statement, I addressed it and apologized to a lot of people, but the one group I didn’t get the apologize to is all the fans. I really appreciate the support, everybody who has reached out after this happened. “ A lot of people were excited to watch TNA for the first time or come back to the product, and now a lot of people are disappointed that I’m not on the show. Thank you guys here at ACW for welcoming me ,” he shared. Caster further opened up and announced his decision to visit therapy, step away from wrestling, and take a break. “ For that, I say, I love you and thank you. I don’t know what my next move is. I don’t know where I’ll be, but I will be stepping away from the ring for an extended period of time. I’m gonna go home, I’m gonna go to therapy, I’m gonna get it right so that the next time I’m in the ring it feels like I’m at home.” A former champion in AEW, there are currently no updates on Caster’s in-ring return or next wrestling appearance. body: Persephone retained the TBS Championship against Queen Aminata, Dani Luna and Hyan at AEW WrestleDream on Saturday. The champion pinned Hyan following a moonsault at Addition Financial Arena in Orlando, Florida. The four-way began with Persephone taunting all three challengers before being sent from the ring, leaving Luna, Aminata and Hyan to trade control. Aminata received a strong response from the crowd and came close to winning after hitting Persephone with a rolling neckbreaker followed by the Off with Her Head. Hyan broke up the ensuing cover. Hyan later hit Aminata with a butterfly suplex, running knee and Falcon Arrow for another near fall. Luna used her power against multiple opponents, at one point lifting Hyan and Persephone simultaneously for a Samoan Drop/fallaway slam combination. She later hit Aminata with a slingshot Blue Thunder Bomb before Hyan interrupted the pin. The closing sequence saw Luna and Hyan exchange strikes before Hyan dropped Luna and appeared poised to continue her attack. Persephone returned to take Hyan down and followed with a moonsault from the top rope for the three-count. Dr. Britt Baker DMD joined Persephone on the entrance ramp afterward to celebrate the successful defense. Persephone won the championship from Maya World during the All In: London Buy-In after Baker returned and became involved in the finish. She has since retained the title several times, including a defense against Luna at All Out. Saturday’s four-way was announced on Wednesday as one of the final additions to the WrestleDream card.

title: On the Record: Max Caster Opens Up On He’s Stepping Away From Wrestling to Seek Therapy
raw_title: Max Caster Reveals He’s Stepping Away From Wrestling to Seek Therapy
summary_src: Max Caster is taking a break from wrestling, and he’s making it clear that getting himself right is his biggest priority after his controversial TNA debut ended with the company cutting ties with him.
body: Caster got himself into serious trouble after referencing the bombing in Riyadh during his entrance rap at TNA Bound For Glory. The line sparked immediate backlash, and TNA cut ties with him the very next day. During an appearance at ACW, Caster addressed what happened and apologized to the fans who were excited to see him in TNA. He admitted his time with the company lasted just one day and thanked everyone who supported him after the controversy. “In the span of one day, I started a contract and ended a contract with TNA Wrestling. I put out a statement, I addressed it and apologized to a lot of people, but the one group I didn’t get the apologize to is all the fans. I really appreciate the support, everybody who has reached out after this happened. A lot of people were excited to watch TNA for the first time or come back to the product, and now a lot of people are disappointed that I’m not on the show. Thank you guys here at ACW for welcoming me. For that, I say, I love you and thank you.” Caster then revealed that he has no idea what’s next for his wrestling career. Instead of looking for another opportunity right away, he’s planning to take an extended break from the ring and go to therapy. “I don’t know what my next move is. I don’t know where I’ll be, but I will be stepping away from the ring for an extended period of time. I’m gonna go home, I’m gonna go to therapy, I’m gonna get it right so that the next time I’m in the ring it feels like I’m at home.” The announcement comes after new details emerged about how TNA handled the situation. TNA President Carlos Silva p ersonally made the decision to end Caster’s run after the backlash. Caster was believed to be working on a per-appearance deal rather than a long-term contract. TNA also gave him complete freedom over his entrance rap and had no idea he was going to reference Riyadh before he went out there. After the controversy, the company removed his content and issued a public apology. The report also noted that some people within AEW felt TNA should have known what it was getting into, considering Caster’s history of pushing the limits with his entrance raps. For now, Caster isn’t giving fans a timeline for his return. His TNA run was over almost as soon as it started, and now he’s putting wrestling on hold while he focuses on himself. Whether he returns to AEW, TNA or somewhere else remains to be seen. Steve Carrier Steve Carrier is the founder of Ringside News and has been reporting on pro wrestling since 1997. His stories have been featured on TMZ, Forbes, Bleacher Report, and more.
summary: Caster got himself into serious trouble after referencing the bombing in Riyadh during his entrance rap at TNA Bound For Glory. Caster addressed what happened and apologized to the the audience who were excited to see him in TNA.

Aminata executed a headscissors takedown on Luna followed by Chocolate Kisses, a stomp, and sent her into the barricade.

title: Injury Update: Jay White Makes Surprise AEW Return Weeks Ahead of Injury Timeline at WrestleDream
raw_title: Jay White Makes Surprise AEW Return Weeks Ahead of Injury Timeline at WrestleDream
summary_src: Jay White is already back in an AEW ring, and nobody expected it to happen this soon. The Switchblade made his surprise return during AEW WrestleDream on October 17, 2026, just two weeks after the company announced he was injured and could miss up to two months of action.
body: White returned during the WrestleDream Tailgate Brawl preshow, teaming with The Gunns (Austin and Colten Gunn) and The Conglomeration (Orange Cassidy, Roderick Strong and Kyle O’Reilly) against the Death Riders (Wheeler Yuta, Claudio Castagnoli, Gabe Kidd and Daniel Garcia) and The Dogs (David Finlay and Clark Connors). The Death Riders and The Dogs ultimately picked up the victory, but White’s unexpected return was a major development considering his recent injury history. During the October 3 episode of AEW Collision , AEW announced that White was dealing with another injury and could be sidelined for one to two months. The setback came after his appearance at AEW All Out, where he competed in a Tailgate Brawl match. At the time, AEW didn’t reveal the exact nature of the injury. That announcement was especially concerning because White had already spent much of the previous year dealing with serious physical setbacks. In March 2025, White suffered a broken hand during a match against Kevin Knight, forcing him to undergo surgery and withdraw from the Owen Hart Foundation Tournament. His recovery became even more complicated when doctors discovered a shoulder injury that eventually required another surgery. Those issues kept White out of action for an extended period before he finally returned in 2026. Tony Khan later revealed that White’s clearance came down to the wire ahead of Forbidden Door, making his latest injury announcement another frustrating setback. However, instead of missing another month or two, White managed to get back inside the ring just 14 days after AEW publicly announced his latest injury. While his team didn’t walk away with the victory at WrestleDream, the fact that White was able to compete again so quickly is encouraging news. It remains to be seen whether AEW plans to put him right back into regular competition or ease him into things following his unexpected comeback. title: Injury Update: Maya World Cleared for AEW In-Ring Return After Injury Scare
raw_title: Maya World Cleared for AEW In-Ring Return After Injury Scare
summary_src: Maya World is officially cleared to get back in the ring, and her recovery didn’t take nearly as long as some expected. The former TBS Champion confirmed the news during the AEW WrestleDream on October 17, 2026 Buy-In preshow, putting an end to weeks of uncertainty surrounding her status.
body: World appeared as a guest during the WrestleDream Buy-In, which was hosted by Renee Paquette, Jeff Jarrett and R.J. City. During her appearance, she announced that she has officially been medically cleared to compete, meaning her latest absence is finally over. The news comes after World had been sidelined since September 9, when she last competed on AEW Dynamite. Her absence raised concerns after Dave Meltzer indicated she could potentially miss a couple of months following a medical procedure. Meanwhile, AEW had incorporated her absence into an ongoing storyline involving Britt Baker. The two even exchanged messages on social media, with World appearing to push back on the suggestion that she would be gone for several months. World’s return to action could also have major implications for the TBS Championship picture. She previously held the title for 35 days before losing it at AEW All In, where Britt Baker interfered and aligned herself with Persephone . Persephone currently holds the championship and is scheduled to defend it in a four-way match against Queen Aminata, Dani Luna and Hyan at WrestleDream. Hyan also happens to be World’s tag team partner, giving the former champion a personal connection to the title match. While World hasn’t announced when she’ll wrestle her first match since being cleared, she’s now officially available for AEW to bring back into the mix. Considering her unfinished business with Britt Baker and Persephone, there are plenty of directions the company could take now that she’s ready to compete again. title: On the Record: Kenny Omega Opens Up On NJPW Wrestle Kingdom 21 ambitions
raw_title: Kenny Omega reveals NJPW Wrestle Kingdom 21 ambitions
body: Kenny Omega recently made his return to New Japan Pro Wrestling, appearing during the King of Pro Wrestling event and taking out IWGP Heavyweight Champion Yota Tsuji and Oleg Boltin. Omega will now be in a triple threat match with Tsuji and Boltin at Power Struggle 2026, where if he gets the pinfall, he will be #1 contender to the IWGP Heavyweight Championship. Speaking to Tokyo Sports , Omega revealed that he plans on winning the triple threat match at Power Struggle and then going on to win the belt at Wrestle Kingdom 21 on January 4 2027 from the Tokyo Dome: (Translated from Japanese) “Japan is my second home, so I want to win the belt in front of New Japan’s fans. And that’s the biggest stage I deserve. So, of course, I’m aiming for the dome. In my time, Okada (Kazuchika) was too strong, and to win the belt, I had no choice but to become a very strong all-rounder. But the current IWGP champions have almost obvious weaknesses. Tsuji is also very strong, but he lacks experience. To me, it seems like he’s scared of failing on the world stage, so maybe that’s why he’s running away from my challenge. “There may be many fighters who want to beat Tsuji, but when I look at Ryogoku, I feel that few truly admire or respect him. Everyone seems to be just waiting for their turn. But if I become champion, everyone will understand that winning won’t be easy, so my motivation will rise and I can practice even harder. Right now, Tsuji is just one step ahead of everyone. I want to become a champion who can’t even see my back.” Jake Jeremy Jake Jeremy is the Head of Audience Development at F4WOnline, having previously worked as a Combat Sports, Gaming and Pro Wrestling writer, successful Editor in Chief and Sports Coordinator. body: Will Ospreay and the United Empire (Great-O-Khan and HENARE) defended their NEVER Openweight Six Man Tag Team Title at NJPW King of Pro Wrestling 2026 earlier today. Ospreay and UE would lose the belts to Unbound Co’s Jeff Cobb, OSKAR & Yuto-Ice, with a promo afterwards setting up a match for Ospreay at NJPW Power Struggle. After losing his NEVER Openweight Six-man belt, Ospreay would challenge the Knockout Brothers to put their IWGP Tag Team Championship on the line. The duo would accept, but only after they decided who his tag team partner would be at Power Struggle on November 3. The Knockout Brothers confirmed that they wanted Ospreay’s partner to be Callum Newman, the leader of United Empire in Japan. There has been dissention in the ranks for some time among Ospreay and Newman, with the latter unhappy that the AEW Champion is putting together his won version of United Empire (UE US in All Elite Wrestling). This match at Power Struggle on November 3 will very likely confirm Ospreay vs Newman at the Tokyo Dome on January 4, possibly with the AEW World Championship on the line. This isn’t a confirmation of that, more speculation, but it’s very likely that this is the direction New Japan are going in. title: Three wrestlers pulled from NJPW Destruction in Kobe 2026

body: Three wrestlers are off the NJPW Destruction in Kobe 2026 card due to either injury or illness. Ahead of Sunday’s event, NJPW announced that Yuya Uemura, Yushin Hatazawa, and Kosei Fujita will no longer be competing . Illness was the reason cited for Uemura and Hatazawa, while Fujita is dealing with a right knee injury. No further details on Fujita’s injury, or how long he might be out of action, were provided in NJPW’s announcement. “We apologize to fans who were looking forward to seeing all three wrestle, and appreciate your understanding,” the promotion wrote. Uemura and Fujita were scheduled to be on opposite sides of the same six-man tag match, so NJPW has removed them both and will continue with the bout as two-on-two. It will be Aaron Wolf & Taichi vs. Ryohei Oiwa & Zack Sabre Jr. Taichi himself had missed multiple NJPW events earlier this week due to illness but is now okay to return. A new Young Lion who recently debuted , Hatazawa was set to team with Tatsuya Matsumoto against Masatora Yasuda & Taisei Nakahara in the kickoff match at Destruction at Kobe. That bout has been canceled with the other three wrestlers no longer set to compete. title: Andrade retains AEW National Title over Ciampa
raw_title: Andrade El Idolo retains AEW National Championship against Tommaso Ciampa at WrestleDream
summary_src: Andrade El Idolo retained the AEW National Championship against Tommaso Ciampa at WrestleDream on Saturday.
body: Andrade El Idolo retained the AEW National Championship against Tommaso Ciampa at WrestleDream on Saturday. Andrade pinned Ciampa with The DM at Addition Financial Arena in Orlando, Florida, after turning the challenger’s attempt to repeat a successful tactic from Wednesday against him. The match mixed extended striking exchanges with several near falls. Andrade completed the Three Amigos on the floor before hitting a split-legged moonsault inside the ring. The pair also played into Andrade’s recurring routine of removing his entrance pants during matches. Ciampa stripped off one layer of his own gear to reveal trunks reading “I Just Know,” a reference to Andrade’s “How you know?” catchphrase. After Andrade eventually removed his pants, he hit several running double knees and later Dia de los Muertos for a close near fall. Ciampa responded with a running knee and subsequently sent Andrade into a camera operator at ringside before scoring another two-count. Ciampa initially tried to bring the title into the ring, but referee Aubrey Edwards stopped him. He then introduced a chair, drawing Edwards away as she removed it. That mirrored Wednesday’s Dynamite, when Ciampa used the National title behind the referee’s back to hit Andrade with the Willow’s Bell during a tag match, setting up Samoa Joe to submit Andrade. This time, Andrade was ready. He reversed Ciampa’s attempt and drove him onto the championship belt with a DDT. Ciampa kicked out, but Andrade followed immediately with The DM for the victory.
summary: Andrade El Idolo defeated Tommaso Ciampa at AEW WrestleDream to retain the AEW National Championship. The match featured multiple near falls, striking exchanges, and callbacks to Andrade's signature pants removal routine, ending with a pin after The DM. Ciampa attempted to use weapons late but was thwarted by the referee before Andrade turned the tide.

El Idolo has been champion since July, and the bout against Ciampa was his seventh defense. Ciampa grabbed hold of El Idolo’s pants and started beating up the pants. He then hit ‘Project Ciampa’ onto the pants and told referee Aubrey Edwards to count. The pants ‘kicked out’ at two, and that got a ‘holy sh*t’ chant from the crowd. Andrade swooped in and hit his spinning elbow onto Ciampa. The backend of the bout saw Ciampa trying to cheat and use the National Title belt, but Andrade spiked him onto it. That moment got so much attention that AEW referee Bryce Remsburg later admitted he deliberately delayed ringing the bell to give the audience more time to continue chanting. More recently, the chants returned during the September 16 episode of AEW Dynamite when King teamed with Hangman Page and Bandido. That reaction was relatively brief, but WrestleDream was a different story. Now the chants have followed King onto another major AEW pay-per-view. What started as a crowd reaction in February has become a recurring occurrence whenever he steps into the ring, and WrestleDream showed just how loud that reaction can get when thousands of fans join in. title: In Memoriam: Benjamin Satterley, pro wrestler known as "Pac," cause of death revealed
raw_title: Benjamin Satterley, pro wrestler known as "Pac," cause of death revealed
body: The cause of death for All Elite Wrestling star Benjamin Satterley, known to fans as "Pac," has been revealed. Satterley died last month, just one day after wrestling for AEW's "All Out" event in Hoffman Estates, Illinois, that was held on Saturday, Sept. 26. The Cook County Medical Examiner's Office revealed he died from bronchial asthma — a chronic inflammatory disease of the airways. The office said the manner of his death was natural. The English-born wrestler was known for high-flying moves that delighted fans worldwide. Satterley, who was from Newcastle upon Tyne, began his wrestling career in 2004 and signed in 2019 with All Elite Wrestling, where he held multiple championships. After signing with AEW, he became the inaugural AEW International Champion and a two-time AEW World Trios Champion. He competed and lost to Andrade El Ídolo during the "All Out" event — his last match. Before joining AEW, he wrestled with World Wrestling Entertainment from developmental under the name "Adrian Neville" to the main roster, where it was shortened to "Neville." AEW dedicated the entire Sept. 30 episode of "Dynamite" to Satterley. Wrestlers in both AEW and WWE wore armbands with "PAC" on them in his honor.
summary: The cause of death for All Elite Wrestling star Benjamin Satterley, known to the audience as Pac, has been disclosed. Satterley died last month, just one day after wrestling for AEW's All Out event in Hoffman Estates, Illinois, that was held on Saturday, Sept. 26.

raw_title: Swerve Strickland Refuses to Hand Over AEW Trios Titles After WrestleDream Loss
summary_src: Swerve Strickland wasn’t happy about losing his championship at AEW WrestleDream on October 17, 2026, and he made sure everyone knew it.
body: The incident happened after Strickland and The New Level, consisting of Austin Creed and Kofi, lost their AEW World Trios Championships to Page, Brody King and Bandido in a Two-Out-of-Three Falls Match. The champions got off to a strong start, with Kofi securing the first fall after working together with Creed to put Bandido away. However, the challengers weren’t going down that easily. The finish came when Strickland attempted to put Bandido away with Big Pressure. Bandido managed to counter the move into a pinfall, securing the third and deciding fall to crown Page and Brodido the new AEW World Trios Champions. However, the drama didn’t end when the bell rang. As the new champions celebrated their victory, Strickland wasn’t interested in showing any respect to the men who had just beaten his team. Rather than handing over the championship belt, he dropped it onto the canvas and walked away. It was a clear sign that Strickland wasn’t taking the loss well, especially considering his ongoing issues with Hangman Page. The two have spent years trying to get the better of each other, and losing another championship to Page only adds to their heated history. For Page and Brodido, the victory also marked a return to the top of AEW’s trios division. They previously lost the championships to Strickland and The New Level at All In London, making WrestleDream their opportunity to finally get some payback. Now Page, King and Bandido are champions again, but Strickland’s reaction suggests he isn’t ready to accept how things ended. Whether that frustration leads to another confrontation with Page remains to be seen. Felix Upton Felix Upton has over 15 years of experience in media and wrestling journalism. title: Hangman Page, Bandido & Brody King capture AEW Trios gold

summary_src: Hangman Page, Bandido & Brody King won the AEW World Trios Championship by defeating Swerve Strickland & The New Level in a two-out-of-three falls match at WrestleDream.
body: Hangman Page, Bandido & Brody King won the AEW World Trios Championship by defeating Swerve Strickland & The New Level in a two-out-of-three falls match at WrestleDream. The challengers won the deciding fall when Bandido countered Strickland’s Big Pressure into a victory roll at Addition Financial Arena in Orlando, Florida. The match was a rematch from AEW All Out , where Strickland, Austin Creed & Kofi retained after Strickland pinned Bandido. The champions concentrated on Bandido during the opening stretch, with Creed & Kofi combining on a series of double-team attacks. Kofi ultimately pinned Bandido after Creed held him in position for a top-rope leg drop, putting the champions ahead 1-0. Page and Strickland immediately renewed their rivalry, trading punches before Page hit the Dead Eye. Creed & Kofi pulled Strickland from the ring before Page could make the cover. The challengers later took control as the match broke down among all six wrestlers. Page hit Strickland with a Buckshot Lariat before King positioned Creed for Bandido. King then monkey-flipped Bandido into a 450 Splash onto Creed, allowing Bandido to score the pin and level the match at one fall apiece. The deciding fall included several dives to the floor before the champions isolated Bandido and delivered a double stomp onto Strickland’s knees. King responded with a dive onto all three champions, while Page & Bandido combined for a Buckshot Lariat/German suplex sequence on Creed. Strickland broke up the pin with a Swerve Stomp. Page and Strickland again exchanged strikes, with Page accidentally hitting King during the sequence. Strickland followed with a House Call that sent King from the apron before hitting Page with a Swerve Stomp. Later, Bandido delivered a double fallaway slam from the ropes to Creed & Kofi before turning his attention to Strickland. Strickland landed on his feet out of an attempted 21-Plex and went for Big Pressure, but Bandido countered into a victory roll for the three-count and the championship. Afterward, Strickland took possession of the title belts and initially refused to hand them over. Creed & Kofi disagreed and presented their belts to Bandido & King before shaking hands and embracing the new champions. Strickland eventually held the remaining belt out toward Page, only to drop it to the mat as Page reached for it. Strickland & The New Level had held the titles since winning them in the Trios Roulette Royale at All In: London on August 30.
summary: Hangman Page, Bandido and Brody King defeated Swerve Strickland, Austin Creed and Kofi at AEW WrestleDream in a two-out-of-three-falls match to win the World Trios Championship. The challengers took the deciding fall when Bandido used a victory roll to counter Strickland's Big Pressure. It was a rematch from All Out where Strickland's team had retained the titles after pinning Bandido.

The bout served as a rematch from AEW All Out, where Strickland, Austin Creed and Kofi retained the titles after Strickland pinned Bandido. Early in the WrestleDream contest, the champions focused their attacks on Bandido, using double-team maneuvers that led to Kofi pinning him after a top-rope leg drop assisted by Creed to take the first fall.

Shortly after, a giant metronome appeared before the arena went black and Dragunov’s newest theme song hit, making the crowd go bonkers. As a red hue captured the arena, Dragunov appeared on stage in a full suit and made an entire round of the AEW ring before hopping back to the gorilla position. The AEW announcers’ team also noted Dragunov as All Elite now, before the promotion’s social media team also updated fans about Dragunov’s All Elite status . As of now, AEW has not yet announced a debut match for the former WWE United States Champion. In addition to Dragunov’s signing, AEW has already signed a bunch of other former WWE superstars, including Andrade El Idolo, Tommaso Ciampa, Motor City Machine Guns, and others. body: Ilja Dragunov made his first AEW appearance at WrestleDream on Saturday, with the promotion unveiling him as its latest roster addition. The reveal came immediately after Hangman Page, Bandido & Brody King captured the AEW World Trios Championship at Addition Financial Arena in Orlando, Florida. Renee Paquette appeared on the entrance stage and said AEW was where “the best wrestle” before introducing the company’s newest signing. A metronome then appeared on the screen, continuing the imagery used in AEW’s recent teasers . The lights went out before Dragunov’s music played and the arena was bathed in red light. Dragunov emerged to a large reaction from the crowd and made his way to the ring. He did not speak during the segment, instead posing in the ring and acknowledging the audience before heading backstage. The appearance confirmed weeks of speculation surrounding Dragunov after imagery used in AEW vignettes had heavily pointed toward his arrival. Dragunov parted ways with WWE after his contract expired in August, ending a seven-year run with the company. During that tenure, he held the NXT UK Championship and NXT Championship before moving to the main roster in 2024. Dragunov missed approximately one year after suffering an injury before returning in October 2025 and defeating Sami Zayn for the United States Championship. He lost that title to Carmelo Hayes in December and wrestled only sporadically in WWE during 2026 before his departure.

body: Bandido, Hangman Page, and Brody King regained the AEW Trios titles at WrestleDream , defeating Swerve Strickland, Austin Creed, and Kofi in a two out of three falls match. In the deciding third fall, Bandido pinned Kofi with a cradle after he had avoided a twenty-one plex attempt. After the match, Swerve grabbed the championships and gave them to the New Level, arguing their opponents didn’t deserve the titles. New Level, regardless, handed the titles to Brody King & Bandido as a sign of respect. Swerve and Hangman then had a staredown before Swerve dropped the title in front of Hangman, bailing to end the segment. The New Level made their debut for AEW at All In on August 30, teaming with Strickland to win the Trios Roulette Royal and the belts. At All Out, they successfully retained the titles. Soon after, Kofi unsuccessfully challenged for the ROH World title at Grand Slam France, losing to Bandido. After the match, Swerve & The New Level were upset about the loss and challenged Hangman & Brodido to a Trios title match at WrestleDream, this time in a two out of three falls match. llm_long: Hangman Page, Bandido and Brody King won the AEW World Trios Championship by defeating Swerve Strickland and The New Level in a two-out-of-three-falls match at WrestleDream. The challengers secured the deciding fall when Bandido countered Strickland's Big Pressure into a victory roll at Addition Financial Arena in Orlando, Florida.

The bout served as a rematch from AEW All Out, where Strickland, Austin Creed and Kofi retained the titles after Strickland pinned Bandido. Early in the WrestleDream contest, the champions focused their attacks on Bandido, using double-team maneuvers that led to Kofi pinning him after a top-rope leg drop assisted by Creed to take the first fall.

Page and Strickland then renewed their personal rivalry by trading punches, with Page landing the Dead Eye. Creed and Kofi prevented the pin by pulling Strickland from the ring. The match later broke down into a six-man brawl, allowing the challengers to gain momentum.

Page connected with a Buckshot Lariat on Strickland, and King set up Creed for Bandido to deliver a monkey-flipped 450 splash for the pin that evened the falls at one apiece. In the decisive third fall, multiple dives occurred before the champions isolated Bandido and hit a double stomp onto Strickland's knees.

King answered with a dive onto all three opponents. Page and Bandido then combined for a Buckshot Lariat and German suplex on Creed, but Strickland broke up the pin with a Swerve Stomp. After further exchanges, Bandido hit a double fallaway slam on Creed and Kofi from the ropes.

Strickland escaped an attempted 21-Plex by landing on his feet and attempted Big Pressure, only for Bandido to counter into a victory roll for the winning pinfall. Following the match, Strickland initially refused to surrender the title belts before Creed and Kofi handed theirs over to Bandido and King.

body: In the first championship match of the night at AEW WrestleDream 2026 , Mercedes Mone defended her Women’s World Championship against Thekla. After winning the title back at AEW All In 2026 in London, UK, this marked Mone’s second world championship title defense. After a 15-minute bout between the two, Mone was able to keep Thekla down. In the final moments of the match, Mone took off her faceguard and hit Thekla with it. Mone followed up by attempting a Mone Maker, but Thekla swiftly countered. However, eventually, Mone finally hit the Mone Maker and pinned Thekla to retain her title. With her successful title defense , Mone is now going strong into her first AEW Women’s World title reign at 49 days. As of now, AEW has not yet announced Mone’s next title defense. Thekla a former Women’s Champion herself, lost the title earlier this year to Willow Nightingale at AEW Redemption 2026. title: Moxley Retains Continental Crown At WrestleDream
raw_title: Jon Moxley Outlasts Mark Davis, Retains AEW Continental Title At WrestleDream 2026
summary_src: After a bloody battle with "Dunkzilla" Mark Davis, Jon Moxley retained his AEW Continental Title at AEW WrestleDream 2026.
body: Moxley was thrown off by the strength of Davis at the start of the match, but continued to move forward with a number of punches and chops regardless. Davis wore Moxley down in the corner with a series of sliding elbows, the last one busting the champion open above the left eye. The challenger would take the action to the outside, hanging Moxley upside down letting the blood gush out of his head, and once the action returned to the ring, Davis continued to squeeze Moxley to encourage more blood-flow. Davis went for a Powerbomb but Moxley countered out of it, only for him to hit a Spinning Side Slam and two diving punches for a near fall. However, Davis almost ended the match completely with a Piledriver on the apron where Moxley just about beat the count out. Moxley was sent outside again but was encouraged back into the ring by the Death Riders, and when he returned he fired up with a Stomp. Moxley weathered the storm of Davis' strikes and landed a King Kong Lariat for a double down.
summary: Jon Moxley overcame an early power disadvantage and a nasty cut above his eye to defeat Mark Davis in a hard-hitting AEW Continental Championship match. Davis dominated stretches with heavy strikes, a prolonged hanging spot that increased the bleeding, and a near-fall piledriver on the apron, yet Moxley rallied with a Stomp and King Kong Lariat to secure the victory.

title: Moxley retains Continental Crown in emotional WrestleDream clash
raw_title: Jon Moxley retains AEW Continental title in emotional battle with Mark Davis at WrestleDream
summary_src: Jon Moxley retained the AEW Continental Championship against Mark Davis in an emotional match at WrestleDream, with the memory of PAC woven throughout the presentation.
body: Before Moxley made his entrance Saturday at Addition Financial Arena in Orlando, Renee Paquette spoke about the grief experienced by the Death Riders since Ben Satterley’s death. Paquette said the group had been “grieving in real time” for the past three weeks, adding that Moxley had carried much of that weight. Moxley then gathered with the Death Riders for their customary pre-match huddle. A towel honoring PAC was draped over the railing beside them. Davis controlled much of the early going and opened a wound near Moxley’s eye, leaving the champion bleeding heavily. The challenger later delivered a piledriver on the edge of the ring apron, with Moxley barely beating referee Paul Turner’s count. Davis immediately sent him back to the floor with an enzuigiri. Marina Shafir and Daniel Garcia then appeared behind the barricade and encouraged their teammate as Moxley struggled to continue. Moxley eventually returned to the ring and the crowd rallied behind him as the match developed into an exchange of forearms, headbutts and submission attempts. The connection to PAC continued late in the contest when Moxley trapped Davis in the Brutalizer, a submission closely associated with his late Death Riders teammate. The Death Riders immediately came to ringside. Moxley repeatedly struck a chair against the steel steps before collapsing at the feet of his teammates, then appeared overcome with emotion as he paced around ringside.
summary: Jon Moxley defeated Mark Davis at AEW WrestleDream in Orlando to retain the Continental Championship. The match came three weeks after the passing of PAC, with Renee Paquette noting the Death Riders had been grieving in real time and Moxley carrying much of the emotional weight. Davis dominated early, busting Moxley open and nearly finishing him with a piledriver on the apron, but Moxley fought back amid crowd support and ring exchanges until securing the victory.

title: Legal Watch: Wwe, Montez Ford Sued Over WWE Raw 'lapdance'
raw_title: WWE, MONTEZ FORD SUED OVER WWE RAW 'LAPDANCE' - PWInsider.com
body: Jalwa Game Goa Game Raja Game MaanWin DMFirst Veer Game WWE, MONTEZ FORD SUED OVER WWE RAW 'LAPDANCE' By Mike Johnson on 2026-10-16 08:45:00 ???????? pic.twitter.com/T6pdOoR20q PostWrestling.com in Canada reported yesterday that Cook County Sheriff’s officer Noel Lucas is suing WWE, Montez Ford of the Street Profits tag team and WWE subsidiary Event Services, LLC, over an alleged unwanted sexualized dance during the 7/6 episode of WWE Monday Night Raw, which was broadcast from the Chicago area at the Allstate Arena in Rosemont, Illinois. Lucas was working off-duty security when, according to the lawsuit, Ford approached him during the Street Profits’ entrance and performed a sexually suggestive dance (embedded above) involving hip thrusts and gyrating without his consent. Lucas alleges that footage of the incident spread widely across social media, including on WWE’s and Ford’s accounts, making him recognizable to the public. He also alleges that when he returned to his full-time courthouse job the next day, people recognized and mocked him by imitating the dance. He also alleges that his children were ridiculed at school because of the video, causing him significant humiliation, embarrassment, and emotional distress. The lawsuit includes 14 counts, including assault, battery, intentional infliction of emotional distress, alleged violations of the Illinois Gender Violence Act, and unlawful use of his image under the Illinois Right of Publicity Act. Lucas is seeking monetary and punitive damages, legal costs, and an order preventing WWE and Ford from using his identity. Neither WWE nor Ford have responded to the lawsuit as of yesterday.
summary: Per the lawsuit, lucas was working off-duty security when Ford approached him during the Street Profits’ entrance and performed a sexually suggestive dance involving hip thrusts and gyrating without his. Hayes popped the question during a romantic trip to Maui, Hawaii, and now the couple has finally made it official. There was one interesting twist to the wedding. While Hayes and Jordan were celebrating their big day in Miami, many of their WWE coworkers couldn’t attend because the company was busy running live events in Hawaii. That’s right, the same place where Hayes originally proposed. The wedding also comes during a pretty big week for Hayes. After spending time away from WWE television, he made his return during the October 12 episode of RAW as the newest member of The 946 faction . Jordan has also been busy making a name for herself on NXT, where she currently holds the NXT Women’s Championship. The couple had been planning their wedding for months, with Hayes previously explaining that Jordan was handling most of the arrangements. Now the planning is finally over, and the two can officially call each other husband and wife. With both stars enjoying major moments in their WWE careers, this is another big milestone for Hayes and Jordan, only this time it happened outside the ring. title: On the Record: Adam Copeland Opens Up On 2027 will be his last year in wrestling
raw_title: Adam Copeland reveals 2027 will be his last year in wrestling
body: On AEW Dynamite tonight, Adam Copeland made a big announcement about his in-ring future. The 52-year-old Copeland cut a promo on the episode where he revealed that 2027 will be his last year as an active wrestler. He did not specify exactly when he’ll be retiring but stressed how much he wants to become AEW World Champion before he does step away. Copeland will have the chance to achieve that goal when he is one of Will Ospreay’s challengers in Clockwork Carnage at WrestleDream 2026 this Saturday. Copeland defeated Josh Alexander on Dynamite to qualify for Clockwork Carnage. Even before this announcement, Copeland had made it clear that he did not have all that much time left in his career. He’s been crossing off items on his bucket list like competing at Arena Mexico, Wembley Stadium, and the former Maple Leaf Gardens. Because he had to retire from 2011-2020 due to neck issues, Copeland has viewed the last six years as a gift. He returned to WWE as Edge in January 2020 before debuting for AEW under his real name in October 2023. The promo Copeland gave on Dynamite tonight also included the announcement that his tag team partner Christian Cage suffered broken ribs and a collapsed lung just five minutes into their ladder match at All Out, where Copeland & Cage lost the AEW Tag Team titles to The Young Bucks. Copeland’s segment tonight led to him being interrupted by Don Callis. When the Don Callis Family launched an attack on Copeland, Konosuke Takeshita and The Conglomeration made the save. In addition to winning the AEW World Championship, Copeland still has a few goals left he hopes to accomplish before hanging up his boots. Wrestling at the Tokyo Dome is one of them, and we’ll see if he ends up part of the card for Wrestle Kingdom 21 in January 2027. Kenny Omega, Swerve Strickland, and Kyle Fletcher are three of the opponents Copeland wants to face one-on-one before retirement. Copeland hasn’t decided what he wants to do in post-retirement life yet, but he’d be willing to have a conversation with Tony Khan about a possible backstage role in AEW if Khan wanted him to serve in that capacity. title: Michael Cole Eyes WWE Retirement At 65

summary_src: Veteran WWE commentator Michael Cole recently hinted as his future retirement plans during an interview.
body: "I'm 59, going to be 60 this week, actually. I want to get to retirement age," he said. "I'd like to get to 65, if I can. But, one of the things that I've been very adamant about, and I've talked to Paul Levesque about this. I've talked to my producers, my boss, Lee Fitting, and I've made sure, I want them to know that if they believe that I'm slipping at all I want to know, because I want to get out at the top of my game. I don't want to hang on and do this 'til I'm 75 or 80 years old."
summary: WWE commentator Michael Cole revealed he hopes to continue calling matches until age 65. title: Ex-WWE Star Makes AEW Debut on WrestleDream
raw_title: Ex-WWE Star Makes AEW Debut on WrestleDream
body: 0 AEW WrestleDream 2026 delivered a long-awaited arrival after weeks of cryptic teasers featuring a ticking metronome. The mystery finally unveiled itself on October 17, as Renee Paquette introduced a new face to the promotion following the AEW World Trios Championship match. Ilja Dragunov made his AEW debut at WrestleDream, with the promotion confirming that the former WWE star is officially “All Elite.” Introduced by Paquette, Dragunov walked onto the stage and entered the ring before taking a lap and leaving without speaking. There was no match or confrontation during the appearance, making it a brief introduction rather than an in-ring debut. Still, the announcement confirmed that the man known as “The Mad Dragon” would continue his wrestling career with AEW. The reveal followed a series of mysterious videos featuring orchestral imagery, a metronome, and footage of a wrestler moving around a ring. AEW later tied the clues to Dragunov, including a social media teaser carrying the WrestleDream hashtag. Dragunov became a free agent after his WWE contract expired in August 2026. Reports from Fightful Select and the Wrestling Observer indicated that he had signed a full-time deal with AEW, with visa issues reportedly delaying his arrival. The debut also came after Adam Page and Brodido — Brody King and Bandido — won the AEW World Trios Championships earlier in the show. With Dragunov now officially part of the roster, the metronome’s countdown has ended, but his first AEW chapter is in its infancy. The belt was on the line during the Ricky Steamboat versus Randy Savage match at WrestleMania 3. Current bids stand at $125,000 with the auction closing on October 24.

Reigns noted that Thompson's show may not draw large audiences and suggested that mentioning his name helps generate views. The Street Fighter film arrives in theaters on Friday. It includes WWE performers Cody Rhodes portraying Guile and Roman Reigns portraying Akuma.

title: Max Caster Issues Statement Following TNA Firing
raw_title: MAX CASTER ISSUES STATEMENT FOLLOWING TNA FIRING - PWInsider.com
body: Jalwa Game Goa Game Raja Game MaanWin DMFirst Veer Game MAX CASTER ISSUES STATEMENT FOLLOWING TNA FIRING By Mike Johnson on 2026-10-13 08:37:00 Max Caster released the following statement this morning via his Twitter account: "Just to address all the TNA stuff, I want to say thank you to Carlos Silva. I talked to him in person. He was very generous, very professional, even after all this stuff happened. And I, I understand why he did what he did. It's his show. He's got to protect TNA, and I went too far for him. So, I want to apologize to him and everybody else in the office. I want to apologize to anyone who vouched for me to get that spot. I feel like I let those people down. Thank you to Moose for sharing your platform with me, and I wish things didn't turn out the way they did, but I'm proud of that match and I'm sorry for how things have ended up, and then for anybody who's offended, I just want everybody to know that when I do these wraps, it's never to offend people. It's only to entertain. So in my mind, it's entertainment value first. And then if you're offended by it, that's your right. So I can't apologize for anyone being offended, but just know that it's not my intention to make people upset. If it gets a reaction, I think I did my job. It was a very relevant part of the show and highly talked about, so I feel good about that. But the consequences of everything, I'm accepting that. I can accept the facts of that. And then to anybody who is asking if I'm good, I'm good. I'm just embarrassed how all this happened. It's, you know, you don't want it to be one match and then that's it, you get fired. But again, that's the reality of the situation. I'm accepting it, and that's life. And in life, sometimes you got to man up and just accept it and move on. So whatever's next, I don't know, but we'll see. Thank you, everybody who's reaching out and supporting."

summary_src: Will Ospreay survived seven challengers and a chaotic new match stipulation to keep his AEW World Championship.
body: Ospreay defended his title against Samoa Joe, Mike Bailey, Darby Allin, Kazuchika Okada, Ricochet, Adam Copeland and Konosuke Takeshita in a match featuring eliminations followed by a 15-minute scoring period. Once Samoa Joe entered as the eighth competitor, the match shifted into the Iron Man portion, where every pinfall or submission counted as one point. Joe quickly made his presence felt by hitting Darby Allin with a Muscle Buster to score the first point. Ricochet followed with a pin on Allin, while Okada scored against Copeland. Things only got crazier from there. Ospreay pinned Ricochet with a Styles Clash, Darby scored two falls of his own, and Joe forced Ospreay to tap out to the Coquina Clutch. With time running out, several wrestlers were tied at two points, including Ospreay, Joe, Darby and Copeland. Copeland looked like he might steal the championship after hitting consecutive spears on Joe and Ricochet to get himself into contention. He then went after Ospreay before turning his attention to Okada. With just seconds remaining, Copeland hit Okada with a spear and went for the cover. However, Ospreay broke things up with a Hidden Blade and immediately pinned Copeland to earn his third point. The clock expired moments later, giving Ospreay the victory and allowing him to retain the AEW World Championship. However, there was still some tension after the bell. Copeland confronted Ospreay and shoved him following the loss. Things looked like they might get physical again, but Copeland eventually cooled down and offered the champion a handshake. Ospreay accepted, and Copeland left the ring while the champion celebrated with his title. summary_src: Will Ospreay survived AEW’s first Clockwork Carnage match to retain the World Championship in the main event of WrestleDream.
body: Will Ospreay survived AEW’s first Clockwork Carnage match to retain the World Championship in the main event of WrestleDream. Ospreay scored the decisive fall on Adam Copeland with only seconds remaining in the 15-minute scoring period, finishing with three points at Addition Financial Arena in Orlando, Florida. Copeland, Darby Allin and Samoa Joe finished tied behind him with two points apiece. Kazuchika Okada and Ricochet scored once each. Konosuke Takeshita and Mike Bailey were eliminated before the scoring portion began. AEW announced Clockwork Carnage earlier this month as a two-stage match. Two wrestlers start, with another entering every three minutes. Pins and submissions eliminate wrestlers until the final entrant arrives, at which point a 15-minute period begins and every fall counts as one point. Ospreay and Takeshita start: The draw put Ospreay and Konosuke Takeshita in the number one and two spots. They immediately traded strikes before taking turns diving to the floor. Mike Bailey entered third, briefly joining United Empire stablemate Ospreay in double-teaming Takeshita. Ricochet arrived fourth and initially suggested an alliance with Takeshita before almost immediately trying to roll him up. Kazuchika Okada entered sixth and immediately confronted Ospreay, continuing their rivalry after Ospreay defeated Okada at Grand Slam France. The first elimination came when Takeshita countered Bailey and hit a Blue Thunder Bomb followed by Raging Fire for the pin. Samoa Joe, who had been the first wrestler to qualify, drew the final position. His arrival ended the elimination stage and started the 15-minute clock with six wrestlers remaining. Joe strikes first: Joe immediately hit Allin with a Muscle Buster to record the first point. While Joe turned his attention elsewhere, Ricochet covered the fallen Allin to draw level. Okada then hit Copeland with the Rainmaker for his first point. Ospreay joined the scoreboard by hitting Ricochet with a Styles Clash. Allin answered almost immediately with a Coffin Drop on Ospreay, leaving five wrestlers on one point. Copeland makes a late charge: With approximately three minutes remaining, Joe attempted a Muscle Buster on Ospreay. Copeland intervened with a spear and pinned Joe for his first point. Copeland ducked and speared Okada, but before he could capitalize, Ospreay struck Copeland with the Hidden Blade. Ospreay covered him with only three seconds remaining to score his third point. The clock expired before anyone could answer. Final score: Will Ospreay 3; Adam Copeland 2; Darby Allin 2; Samoa Joe 2; Kazuchika Okada 1; Ricochet 1. Ospreay therefore retained the AEW World Championship in the promotion’s inaugural Clockwork Carnage match. After the bell, Copeland initially shoved Ospreay. He then regained his composure and offered his hand, which the champion accepted. Copeland pointed toward the World Championship before leaving Ospreay alone in the ring to close WrestleDream with the title.
summary: Will Ospreay retained the AEW World Championship in the first-ever Clockwork Carnage match at WrestleDream by scoring the final fall on Adam Copeland in the closing seconds of the 15-minute scoring period. Ospreay finished with three points while Adam Copeland, Darby Allin and Samoa Joe each scored two points. Kazuchika Okada and Ricochet tallied one point apiece, with Konosuke Takeshita and Mike Bailey eliminated prior to the scoring phase.

summary_src: Andrade El Idolo apparently isn’t giving up his new favorite ringside routine anytime soon. During AEW WrestleDream, Andrade once again found a woman in the crowd, stopped for a selfie and even planted a kiss on her cheek before getting back to business.
body: Naturally, it didn’t take long for fans to start wondering who Andrade had found this time. After the pay-per-view, the mystery was solved when independent wrestler Madisyn Maxxwell took to her Instagram Story and uploaded a photo of herself with Andrade, confirming that she was the woman involved in the ringside moment. Maxxwell isn’t just a random fan AEW happened to put in the front row either. She’s an active independent wrestler who has competed for promotions including LPW, WOW, CCW and UFW, along with several other companies on the indie scene. This is becoming quite the habit for Andrade. Just days earlier on the October 14 episode of Dynamite , he stopped in the middle of his tag team match with Will Ospreay to take a selfie with another woman sitting at ringside . Ospreay wasn’t exactly impressed with his partner’s priorities that night. He scolded Andrade and tried to get him focused on their match against Tommaso Ciampa and Samoa Joe, but the ringside selfie ended up getting plenty of attention anyway. That woman was later identified as independent wrestler Kelly Madan, who has previous WWE television experience and has also worked for promotions including Outlaw Wrestling, ACW, NWA Powerrr, NEW and Warrior Pro Wrestling. Andrade was already doing this before the Madan interaction too. At AEW Grand Slam France, he approached a woman in the crowd, took a selfie and received a kiss on the cheek before returning to his match against Michael Oku. She was later identified as Instagram personality bad.oce, who is known around the French wrestling scene. Felix Upton Felix Upton has over 15 years of experience in media and wrestling journalism. body: 00:33 Featured Video AUBURN STUNS GEORGIA 😱 Previous Next Will Ospreay, Mercedes Moné and Real Winners and Losers of AEW WrestleDream Match Card Kevin Berge Oct 17, 2026 The 2026 edition of WrestleDream featured championship and a first-time special match for the AEW Men's World Championship, airing from Addition Financial Arena in Orlando, Florida. Will Ospreay overcame the odds in Clockwork Carnage to retain his AEW Men's World Championship while Mercedes Moné defeated her top rival Thekla to successfully defend her gold. This was only the foundation of a fun night of All Elite Wrestling action. For all the real winners and losers from WrestleDream, keep reading. It has been an odd start for Chris Sabin and Alex Shelley. The Motor City Machine Guns have slowly found their footing in AEW, barely appearing to date. In some ways, their match with FTR was the true introduction to AEW for MCMG, who finally got to show off what they could do. It was a long battle against Dax Harwood and Cash Wheeler that started on the Tailgate Brawl and bled 15 minutes into the main show. While capturing the first win in a Best of 5 series was nice, it was even more important that Sabin and Shelley looked like one of the best tag teams in AEW right now. This was a great start to selling the unfamiliar fans on what they can do. This was a definitive win for The CEO, who stands far and above the rest of the women's roster right now. Anyone could step up to Moné next week, but at least until Toni Storm returns, no one else is a clear candidate to dethrone the Women's world champion. What most matters for The CEO will be the company building strong stories around her. Who is going to be built to step up to The CEO's level? All Elite Wrestling Nick Wayne The biggest winner of WrestleDream was the man in the least anticipated match of the show. title: On the Record: AEW Wrestler PAC Dies at 40 from Bronchial Asthma: What We Know About His Final Days
raw_title: AEW Wrestler PAC Dies at 40 from Bronchial Asthma: Details on His Final Days
body: 0 AEW wrestler PAC, whose real name was Benjamin Satterley, died at 40, and now the medical examiner has revealed the cause of death. The British professional wrestler, Benjamin Satterley, better known to his fans as PAC in All Elite Wrestling (AEW) and as Neville in WWE, died on September 27. He was 40 at the time of his death. According to People Magazine , the wrestler died of bronchial asthma, the Cook County Medical Examiner’s Office has said. The medical examiner’s office stated that Satterley had died from natural causes, a finding which was reported by the New York Post on October 16; this conclusion helps to explain the circumstances surrounding the sudden death of a wrestler who had still been fighting in the ring at the time of his death. Satterley was found to be unconscious in a rental car in a parking lot in Des Plaines, Illinois, an area close to Chicago O’Hare International Airport on September 27. The police went to the spot and took the necessary emergency actions, but Satterley was found to have died. Initially, the authorities stated that there were no obvious signs of injury or foul play and then had the body autopsied the following day. When AEW announced that AEW had died, the cause of death was not stated immediately. The medical examiner concluded that bronchial asthma had caused the death, which was classified as a natural death. No additional medical details have been released since. Satterley was born in Newcastle upon Tyne, in England, and began his career in professional wrestling in 2004. He became well known amongst the fans of different wrestling promotions because of his athletic ability and the way he used aerial moves. He joined WWE in 2012 and wrestled for the company under the name Neville, eventually becoming a prominent wrestler in both the NXT and cruiserweight divisions. While with WWE, he won the Cruiserweight Championship before departing in 2018. In 2019, Satterley joined AEW under the name PAC and presented himself as one of the promotion’s main performers, gaining several titles. He also took part in international competitions, such as those held with New Japan Pro-Wrestling and Mexico’s Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre. People in the wrestling industry paid tribute to him, with AEW and other wrestlers remembering the role he had played in the sport, and his final match against Andrade El Idolo is now seen as his last appearance in the ring. summary_src: Will Ospreay won AEW's first-ever Clockwork Carnage match to retain the World Championship at WrestleDream.
body: Per the stipulation, the first stage of the match was contested like a gauntlet eliminator with staggered entrances. Ospreay drew the first entrance to ensure he would have to battle all seven opponents to defend his title, followed by Konosuke Takeshita as the second entrant. The third entrant to the match was Ospreay's United Empire teammate, "Speedball" Mike Bailey, and the fourth entrant came in the form of Ricochet. Number five was the TNT Champion, Darby Allin, who immediately introduced a table to the affair. International Champion Kazuchika Okada came out as number six. The seventh entrant, Adam Copeland, made his entrance moments after the first elimination came; Takeshita pinned Bailey to ensure he would not progress to the second stage. AEW Joe scored the first fall after a Musclebuster to Allin, followed then by Ricochet clearing Joe from the ring so he could pin Allin. Okada got his first on the board with a Rainmaker and rare pin on Copeland. Ospreay got his first with a Styles Clash to Ricochet, only to then get a Coffin Drop from Allin to tie up the contest for all but Copeland. Copeland only announced on Wednesday that he would be calling it quits on his in-ring career next year.

He drew the first spot and outlasted seven challengers including Konosuke Takeshita, Mike Bailey, Ricochet, Darby Allin, Kazuchika Okada and Adam Copeland. Takeshita eliminated Bailey first, while later falls came from Samoa Joe, Ricochet, Okada and Ospreay himself before the match advanced to its second stage.

llm_long: Will Ospreay defended the AEW World Heavyweight Championship in a Clockwork Carnage match at AEW WrestleDream 2026. The unique format was designed by Pro Wrestling EVE, with whom Ospreay has collaborated. Ospreay entered the bout early in his title reign following an emotional win over Kenny Omega at AEW All In 2026.

In Clockwork Carnage, wrestlers enter every three minutes until all eight participants are in the match. Any wrestler pinned or submitted before the final entrant arrives is eliminated. Once the last wrestler enters, the remaining competitors begin a 15-minute scoring period where each pinfall or submission counts as one fall.

Ospreay and Konosuke Takeshita opened the match at a fast pace. Takeshita executed a gorilla press from the top rope followed by a flying clothesline on Ospreay. The action continued with Takeshita delivering a dive to the outside onto Ospreay.

Mike Bailey entered wearing United Empire colors, though commentary noted that alliances do not apply in Clockwork Carnage. Takeshita eliminated Bailey and focused his attack on Ospreay. Ospreay and Bailey later showed a moment of solidarity with a United Empire high-five before Takeshita interrupted it.

Ricochet attempted to form a temporary alliance with Takeshita against the United Empire members. The partnership broke down when Ricochet tried to roll up Takeshita. Ricochet then hit a dive onto Ospreay on the outside before Takeshita dropped him with a headbutt.

Ospreay and Bailey delivered a double superplex to Takeshita, but Ospreay's attempt to steal the pin failed. Darby Allin entered using a skateboard, performing an ollie on Ricochet's back and setting up a table outside the ring. Kazuchika Okada's music played as the match continued.
