title: Ospreay Wins Inaugural Clockwork Carnage at WrestleDream
raw_title: Will Ospreay Wins 1st-Ever AEW Clockwork Carnage to Retain AEW Title at WrestleDream 2026
body: Ospreay prevailed in a unique, eight-man match that also included Samoa Joe, "Speedball" Mike Bailey, Adam Copeland, Konosuke Takeshita, Kazuchika Okada, Ricochet and Darby Allin. AEW WrestleDream Live Grades 🔠 Bleacher Report 4h Pac's Cause of Death Bleacher Report 11h AEW Winners and Losers 📊 Bleacher Report 21m Takeshita eliminated Bailey with Raging Fire. The scoring period began after Samoa Joe entered the match as the eighth and final competitor. He got the first point after hitting Allin with the Muscle Buster. Ricochet got a point too, hitting Allin with a lateral press. Okada got on the scoreboard when he landed the Rainmaker on Copeland. The champion got his first point when he executed the Styles Clash on Ricochet, but Allin got his point with a Coffin Drop on Ospreay. At this juncture, five of the six remaining wrestlers had a point apiece, with Copeland being the lone exception. Samoa Joe got his second point when he made Ospreay tap with the Coquina Clutch. Copeland then made things awfully interesting with back-to-back points on spears to Samoa Joe and then Ricochet. With a minute left, Copeland, Allin, Samoa Joe and Ospreay had two points each. Okada and Ricochet had one point apiece. Copeland was in position to win the match after hitting a spear on Okada, but Ospreay broke up the pin by hitting Copeland with the Hidden Blade and then pinning him with just a few seconds on the clock. The match type was conceived in Pro-Wrestling: EVE—a promotion in which Ospreay works behind the scenes in the United Kingdom. A series of qualifying matches were held leading up to WrestleDream, starting off with a de facto qualifier when Ospreay beat Okada at the Grand Slam France edition of Dynamite to retain the AEW World Championship. Additionally, Joe defeated Jack Perry, Bailey took down Lee Moriarty, Copeland beat Josh Alexander, Takeshita topped Brian Cage, Okada got the better of Myron Reed, Ricochet outlasted Ace Austin, and Allin triumphed over Hechicero to qualify. With such a stacked field in the Clockwork Carnage match, Ospreay was seemingly in legitimate danger of seeing his title reign end after less than two months. However, Ospreay was clearly motivated to win the match he helped create, especially with it taking place on a big stage for the first time. That is exactly what Ospreay did, as he outlasted seven hungry challengers to conquer Clockwork Carnage and remain AEW world champion.

llm_long: All Elite Wrestling will present WrestleDream 2026 on pay-per-view from Addition Financial Arena in Orlando, Florida. The event begins at 7 pm ET with a Tailgate Brawl special on TNT and the Buy In pre-show on YouTube before the main card starts at 8 pm ET.

The show will be available for purchase in the United States through PPV.com, HBO Max, Amazon, DAZN, Fubo, YouTube, and cable or satellite providers. International fans in the UK and other markets can access it via MyAEW.
AEW scheduled the event only three weeks after All Out. Some television time during that period was used to pay tribute to PAC rather than advancing storylines.
The main event will be a new Clockwork Carnage match for the AEW world championship. The match combines elements of a Casino Gauntlet in its first phase and an Iron Man format in its second phase.

Eight wrestlers will compete across two phases. The Entry Phase begins with two competitors and adds a new entrant every three minutes until all have entered, with any wrestler pinned or submitted during this phase being eliminated.

Surviving wrestlers advance to the 15-minute Scoring Phase, where the competitor with the most pins or submissions is declared the AEW world champion. The defending champion Will Ospreay faces challengers Samoa Joe, Kazuchika Okada, Ricochet, Adam Copeland, Konosuke Takeshita, Speedball Bailey, and Darby Allin.

title: Ospreay Retains AEW World Title in Clockwork Carnage

summary_src: Will Ospreay has survived the Clockwork Carnage match at AEW WrestleDream 2026. In the main event of the Oct.
body: Will Ospreay has survived the Clockwork Carnage match at AEW WrestleDream 2026. In the main event of the Oct. 17, 2026 edition of AEW WrestleDream, Will Ospreay defended his AEW World Championship against Kazuchika Okada, Samoa Joe, ‘Speedball’ Mike Bailey, Adam Copeland, Konosuke Takeshita, Ricochet, and Darby Allin. Ospreay entered the match in the number one spot, followed by Takeshita at number 2 and Bailey as the third entrant. Ricochet and Darby Allin followed them as the fourth and fifth entrants, while Kazuchika Okada was the sixth participant. Takeshita eliminated Bailey from the match. Shortly after, Adam Copeland came in at the seventh position. Okada eliminated Takeshita from the match as Joe entered as the last entrant. In the final moments of the match, Ospreay, Joe and Allin held two points; Ricochet and Okada held one point each, with Copeland not opening his books till the very end of the bout. In the final moments of the match, Copeland scored two quick pinfall victories in the last few minutes of the match. In the last ten seconds, Ospreay landed a Hidden Blade on Copeland while he tried to score a third point. With the successful execution of his move, Ospreay kept Copeland down for the three-count and retained his World Championship. In the aftermath of the match, Copeland and Ospreay shared an intense exchange before Copeland shook hands with the champion and walked out. llm_long: Will Ospreay defended the AEW World Heavyweight Championship in a Clockwork Carnage match at AEW WrestleDream 2026. The unique format was designed by Pro Wrestling EVE, with whom Ospreay has collaborated. Ospreay entered the bout early in his title reign following an emotional win over Kenny Omega at AEW All In 2026.

In Clockwork Carnage, wrestlers enter every three minutes until all eight participants are in the match. Any wrestler pinned or submitted before the final entrant arrives is eliminated. Once the last wrestler enters, the remaining competitors begin a 15-minute scoring period where each pinfall or submission counts as one fall.

Ospreay and Konosuke Takeshita opened the match at a fast pace. Takeshita executed a gorilla press from the top rope followed by a flying clothesline on Ospreay. The action continued with Takeshita delivering a dive to the outside onto Ospreay.

Mike Bailey entered wearing United Empire colors, though commentary noted that alliances do not apply in Clockwork Carnage. Takeshita eliminated Bailey and focused his attack on Ospreay. Ospreay and Bailey later showed a moment of solidarity with a United Empire high-five before Takeshita interrupted it.

Ricochet attempted to form a temporary alliance with Takeshita against the United Empire members. The partnership broke down when Ricochet tried to roll up Takeshita. Ricochet then hit a dive onto Ospreay on the outside before Takeshita dropped him with a headbutt.

Ospreay and Bailey delivered a double superplex to Takeshita, but Ospreay's attempt to steal the pin failed. Darby Allin entered using a skateboard, performing an ollie on Ricochet's back and setting up a table outside the ring. Kazuchika Okada's music played as the match continued.

title: Legal Watch: WWE Espn Lawsuit Update
raw_title: WWE ESPN LAWSUIT UPDATE - PWInsider.com
summary_src: WWE ESPN LAWSUIT UPDATE PWInsider.com
body: Jalwa Game Goa Game Raja Game MaanWin DMFirst Veer Game WWE ESPN LAWSUIT UPDATE By Mike Johnson on 2026-10-12 14:00:00 United States District Court of ConnecticutJudge Sarah F. Russell ruled on 10/6 that WWE, ESPN, etc. will have until 10/16 to respond to Michael Diesa and Rebella Toback's motion objecting to ESPN and BAMTech, LLC being added as defendants in the lawsuit alleging that WWE misled customers about how to watch its major PPV/PLE events after it moved them to the ESPN Unlimited streaming platform as of WrestlePalooza 2025. Judge Russell also ruled the Court will hold off on ruling whether the case should be moved to arbitration until Diesa and Toback's objection is ruled on. Obviously, access depended on behind-the-scenes agreements between Disney (ESPN’s parent company) and individual TV providers. At the time, some services (Verizon Fios, DirecTV, Spectrum, and Hulu + Live TV) allowed customers to log into the ESPN app and watch the events. Others (such as Cox, Xfinity and YouTube TV at the time) did not at the time of launch, forcing customers to pay extra. The lawsuit has been seeking, "An award of actual, compensatory, and/or consequential damages, alternatively, an award of nominal damages (if and as necessary), an award of statutory damages (if and as permitted by law), an award of punitive damages (pursuant to Conn. Gen. Stat. §42-110g(a) and/or as otherwise permitted by law, an award of reasonable attorneys’ fees and expenses incurred in connection with this action (pursuant to Conn. Gen. Stat. §42-110g(d) and/or as otherwise permitted by law, an award of the costs of this action (pursuant to Conn. Gen. Stat. §42-110g(d) and/or as otherwise permitted by law), any injunctive relief necessary to preclude WWE from (a) continuing to violate CUTPA, (b) conspiring with ESPN to violate CUTPA, and/or (c) aiding and/or abetting ESPN in its violation(s) of CUTPA; and/or any other legal or equitable relief as the Court deems appropriate."

llm.summary: Will Ospreay defended his AEW World Championship in the promotion's first Clockwork Carnage match at WrestleDream on October 17. The staggered entry bout featured Konosuke Takeshita, Mike Bailey, Ricochet, Darby Allin, Kazuchika Okada, Adam Copeland and Samoa Joe. Samoa Joe scored the first two points of the point-scoring phase before the match concluded with Ospreay retaining his title.

llm_long: Will Ospreay retained his AEW World title in the Clockwork Carnage match that closed the WrestleDream pay-per-view on October 17. The bout featured a staggered entry format devised by Ospreay himself and began with the champion entering first against Konosuke Takeshita.

Subsequent entrants included Mike Bailey, Ricochet, Darby Allin, and Kazuchika Okada. Any pinfall or submission during the initial phase resulted in elimination, with Takeshita eliminating Bailey before Adam Copeland made his entrance.
Copeland locked up with Takeshita, allowing Okada to eliminate the latter. Samoa Joe entered last, reducing the field to six competitors and beginning the point-scoring portion of the match.

Joe secured the first pinfall and added a second point, positioning himself to challenge for the world title. Ospreay intervened at the final moment to prevent Joe from winning and retained the championship.
Following the match, Copeland shook Ospreay's hand before pulling him in to indicate he remains a future challenger for the title.

llm_long: All Elite Wrestling performer Benjamin Satterley, known in the ring as Pac, was found unresponsive in a vehicle in a restaurant parking lot in Des Plaines, Illinois. Emergency responders arrived at the scene around 4 p.m. after patrons noticed him passed out in his car and called for help. Dispatch audio described the situation as a person slumped in a vehicle with breathing unconfirmed.

Medics and authorities reached Satterley, who was pronounced dead at 4:08 p.m. Customers at the restaurant attempted to locate medical equipment to assist him before first responders arrived. Multiple emergency vehicles including an ambulance, police cars, and a fire truck responded to the location.

Officials stated there were no indications of foul play and that the circumstances surrounding the death were not considered suspicious. The cause of death remains pending additional testing after an initial autopsy. Satterley had competed in an AEW pay-per-view event the previous night in nearby Chicago.

He lost a match against Andrade at the NOW Arena and later appeared during the main event between Jon Moxley and Will Ospreay. Satterley, originally from Newcastle upon Tyne, England, began his professional wrestling career in 2004. He joined All Elite Wrestling in 2019 and won multiple championships during his time with the promotion.

llm_long: At a Ring of Honor taping in Jacksonville, AEW President Tony Khan paid tribute to the late Ben Satterley, known as PAC. Khan described him as someone who represented the best of wrestling and humanity, calling him one of the finest people he had ever known.

Khan highlighted PAC's accomplishments as a wrestler who performed in AEW, as Neville in WWE, and around the world. He emphasized that PAC was an outstanding performer, a great colleague, and a wonderful person to spend time with.

Before the wrestling began, Khan requested a moment of silence followed by a ten-bell salute in PAC's honor. He noted that PAC had been integral to AEW from its early planning stages and had become a significant part of many people's lives in and out of wrestling.

Khan recalled first meeting PAC prior to the company's public launch in January 2019 in the same Jacksonville parking lot. He stated that PAC was always envisioned as a major figure in AEW and had a profound impact on wrestlers and others in the industry.

The tribute included recognition of PAC's broad potential for success in any field and his achievement as one of the greatest wrestlers. Khan shared the announcement with the live audience ahead of the day's Ring of Honor tapings.

body: New Japan Pro-Wrestling’s powerhouse arrives November 7 at sold-out Cicero Stadium in Chicago. Major League Wrestling today announced that New Japan Pro-Wrestling’s Yota Tsuji will make his MLW debut at Saturday Night SuperFight on Saturday, November 7 , LIVE worldwide on pay-per-view exclusively on VEEPS from sold-out Cicero Stadium in Chicago . Fans can pre-order MLW’s signature pay-per-view now on VEEPS. For weeks, cryptic transmissions on Fusion hinted at an arrival from beyond MLW’s borders. Now, the message has a name: Yota Tsuji – the IWGP Heavyweight Champion. Combining heavyweight power, explosive athleticism and a confidence that dares opponents to stand their ground, Tsuji brings one of New Japan’s most formidable arsenals to Chicago. His devastating Gene Blaster can end a fight in an instant, turning a single opening into a collision an opponent never recovers from. Tsuji’s arrival brings a new dimension to Saturday Night SuperFight. A commanding presence in Japan, he now steps into an MLW ring with the opportunity to impose his style on a different league, against different opposition, before a worldwide pay-per-view audience. For MLW, the debut advances its ongoing strategic alliance with New Japan Pro-Wrestling and delivers on a defining challenge: MLW vs. The World. For the MLW locker room, it means another dangerous international force has crossed into their territory. With Cicero Stadium already sold out, Chicago will provide a deafening welcome for a debut built for the scale and stakes of Saturday Night SuperFight. Tsuji’s opponent will be announced soon. Killer Kross and Josh Bishop will fight to be the Last Man Standing. Tessa Blanchard will make her MLW debut. Now, Yota Tsuji joins an international supercard where championship ambitions and bitter grudges collide. Saturday Night SuperFight is sold out. The only way to watch LIVE worldwide is on VEEPS . Pre-order now and witness Yota Tsuji’s MLW debut November 7 on the VEEPS app, your favorite streaming device or VEEPS.com.

body: Bishop has already pinned the champion. On November 7, he must put Kross down for good—LIVE on pay-per-view exclusively on VEEPS. Major League Wrestling today announced MLW World Heavyweight Champion Killer Kross vs. Josh Bishop in a Last Man Standing match at Saturday Night SuperFight on Saturday, November 7 , LIVE worldwide on pay-per-view exclusively on VEEPS from sold-out Cicero Stadium in Chicago . Fans can pre-order MLW’s signature pay-per-view now on VEEPS. Their first World Championship fight left Bishop bloodied and the ring stripped to its boards. Kross survived that No Holds Barred encounter by choking the challenger unconscious with the Kross Jacket, but the “Intense Icon” emerged determined to force another fight. Then, in New York City, Bishop did what no one in MLW had done before: he pinned Killer Kross. Competing alongside Donovan Dijak against Kross and Matt Riddle in a New York City Street Fight, Bishop absorbed the champion’s Diamond Cutter, answered with Exit 187 and secured the three-count. Four years of Kross never being pinned in an MLW ring ended at Bishop’s hands. Suddenly, the challenger’s pursuit of the World Heavyweight Championship carried something far more dangerous than ambition: proof. Addressing the defeat on Fusion, Kross acknowledged Bishop’s ability and advocated for another championship opportunity. Even as Dijak attempted to claim credit for the victory and push himself to the front of the line, the champion made clear who had earned the fight. MLW officials agreed. As announced by Rich Bocchini on Fusion, Bishop will get his rematch at Saturday Night SuperFight—with a stipulation that demands a decisive ending. There will be no pinfalls and no submissions. To leave Chicago with the MLW World Heavyweight Championship, one man must render the other unable to answer the referee’s ten-count. Their first title fight ended with Bishop unconscious. Their next encounter ended with Kross pinned. In Chicago, the championship belongs to the last man standing. Saturday Night SuperFight is sold out. The only way to watch LIVE worldwide is on VEEPS . Pre-order now and watch November 7 on the VEEPS app, your favorite streaming device or VEEPS.com.

The bout will air live on pay-per-view via VEEPS from the sold-out Cicero Stadium in Chicago. Bishop earned the opportunity by becoming the first man to pin Kross inside an MLW ring during a recent New York City Street Fight.

title: Mattel Expands WWE Toy Line With Global Lucha Libre AAA Partnership
raw_title: Mattel Expands WWE Toy Line With Global Lucha Libre AAA Partnership
body: Mattel is bringing the masks, personalities and high-flying action of Lucha Libre AAA Worldwide to toy shelves around the globe. The company announced a multi-year worldwide licensing agreement with WWE during a joint San Diego Comic-Con panel, expanding Mattel’s long-running WWE portfolio to include one of Mexico’s most influential wrestling promotions. An all-new line of AAA action figures is scheduled to launch in fall 2027, featuring the promotion’s colorful costumes, signature masks and larger-than-life stars. The initial collection will include Psycho Clown, El Hijo del Viking, La Parka and Mr. Iguana. To mark the announcement, Mattel Creations will release a made-to-order Mr. Iguana figure during San Diego Comic-Con. The figure, complete with the wrestler’s signature iguana companion, will be the first product from the new collection. “Our partnership with WWE has been an incredible collaboration, and bringing AAA into the fold is the next exciting chapter,” said Nick Karamanos, Mattel’s general manager and head of entertainment partnerships, action figures and preschool entertainment. “For generations, AAA has entertained audiences with its unforgettable characters, signature masks and rich lucha libre tradition.” Founded by Antonio Peña in 1992, AAA has featured some of lucha libre’s biggest names, including Eddie Guerrero, Rey Mysterio and Penta. WWE announced in August 2025 that it had acquired the promotion in partnership with Mexico-based sports and entertainment holding company Fillip. “As a cornerstone of Mexico’s lucha libre culture, AAA has built a highly engaged fanbase across Latin America and beyond,” Abby Esrock, WWE’s vice president of revenue, said in a press release. “This collaboration marks an exciting new chapter as we expand WWE’s collectibles portfolio and bring AAA’s iconic stars into Mattel’s industry-leading action figure line.” The partnership arrives as AAA continues to push beyond its traditional Mexican and Latin American fanbase. Its August 2025 Triplemanía broadcast generated more than 4.3 million views in its first 24 hours and peaked at 614,000 concurrent viewers. Triplemanía 34 is set to expand to a two-day event this September, with shows planned for Mexico City and Las Vegas. Mattel said additional figures, release dates and availability details will be announced later. Stay up-to-date with products here . Disney will host the four-day Banana Ball Open at Walt Disney World in April 2027 and release a music-driven documentary on Disney+ and Hulu later that year. As the Brewers prepare for their first World Series in 44 years, Ticket Club data shows a nearly $2,000 opening-game get-in and sharply different prices for potential Cleveland and Tampa Bay home games.

title: On the Record: Lucha Libre AAA Fallout (10/10/26) – Pagano Explains His Betrayal

body: October 11, 2026 By Jason Jimenez-Garrido AAA , North America , Pro Wrestling , WWE , WWE Universe As we head towards AAA’s next big event, Heroes Inmortales, two weeks from now, one more match has been confirmed for this week’s Lucha Libre AAA. Meanwhile, a feud between two longtime rivals has been renewed. This week’s episode of Lucha Libre AAA took place during the 10/4 set of tapings at Domo de la Feria in Leon, Guanajuato, MX. Here is the fallout from the 10/10 episode. In the first match of the night, Kento and Takuma (Tokyo Bad Boys) faced Rayo and Bravo (Los Americanos). On the cusp of their loss in the first round of the NXT Dusty Rhodes Tag-Team Classic , both teams came into this match looking to get a win. This was an incredibly fun opener. The Tokyo Bad Boys never cease to amaze me in every one of their appearances on AAA. Without a doubt, the fan favorites were Los Americanos, who had the crowd in the palm of their hands with every move (or dance move). You can say what you want about whether Pete Dunne and Tyler Bate are being wasted with this gimmick or not, but you can’t deny that they are putting their all into their characters. In the end, Los Americanos defeated the Tokyo Bad Boys after hitting an Assisted Diving Headbutt. One can assume that this win will bring them one step closer to an opportunity to challenge the Wagner Brothers for the AAA Tag-Team Championship. At Triplemanía 34, it was revealed that Pagano was aligned with El Carnicero all along . On this episode of AAA, Pagano answered the question that, by this point, everyone knew the answer to. Who was behind the attacks on the Psycho Circus? Pagano left no room for questions, declaring: Pagano blamed Psycho for overshadowing him while they were supposed to be a team. He resented the fact that he lost who he truly was in order to appease Psycho, his former Psycho Circus brothers, and the entire AAA audience. He then explained why the partnership with Carnicero came to be: “Psycho, I became your brother, I became your partner. I became everything you all wanted me to be… until one day, I was in the locker room… looked at myself in the mirror… and I didn’t recognize Pagano. But he [El Carnicero] reminded me what it means to say “there’s no party without a clown,'” Pagano credited Carnicero for showing him that he doesn’t need anyone by his side. Not Psycho, the Psycho Circus, nor the support of the fans. He went on to say that Triplemania 34 was the first time in a long time that he felt like himself again. He warned Psycho by telling him to watch out because that was only the beginning. Dave the Clown and Murder Clown then ran out to the ring to confront their former friend. Instead, Pagano ordered Carnicero to make quick work of them. As Carnicero accomplished the task, Psycho’s music began to play. title: 10/14 AEW Dynamite Report — Last Stop Before Wrestledream
raw_title: LAST STOP BEFORE WRESTLEDREAM: 10/14 AEW DYNAMITE REPORT - PWInsider.com
body: The Death Riders (Jon Moxley, Daniel Garcia, and Gabe Kidd) vs. Don Callis Family (Wardlow, Mark Davis, and Josh Doyle) Garcia lays in chops, and Doyle lariats him to the mat and then picks him up. Garcia escapes out the back and tags in Kidd. Doyle tags in Wardlow. Kidd charges into Wardlow and Wardlow doesn’t move, but Kidd is knocked to the mat. Kidd tags in Garcia and the same thing happens. Mox tags in and he charges into Wardlow, who is knocked back a bit, but Wardlow knocks him down with a shoulder tackle. Mox smacks Wardlow, and when Wardlow charges into him, he runs into a chop. Mox gets a series of headbutts, and Wardlow drops Mox with a lariat and then stomps Mox down in the corner. Doyle tags in and avoids a charge from Mox and tags in Kidd, who knocks Wardlow and Davis off the apron. Kidd and Doyle charge into each other, and this sets off the tag team alarm, and everyone is in the ring charging at each other as we go picture-in-picture. On the floor, Mox gives Doyle and Wardlow a double DDT. The Death Riders charge into Davis with Forever Charges in the corner. Shafir joins in when the ref is distracted. Garcia gets a Dragon Tamer on Davis, with Mox getting a curb stomp on him as well for two, which brings everyone into the ring. After Kidd knocks Doyle to the floor, Garcia and Wardlow go back and forth, but Kidd clotheslines Wardlow and himself to the floor. Garcia gets a guillotine choke on Doyle on the floor. Davis clotheslines Mox and hits him with a gutwrench piledriver for the pin and the win. Adam Copeland vs. Josh Alexander - Clockwork Carnage Qualifier They lock up and move to waistlocks and headlocks. They run the ropes, and Cope gets a shoulder tackle and then a hip toss. Cope goes for a baseball slide, but Josh grabs the leg and then runs his leg into the steel steps as we go to picture-in-picture. When we return to full screen, Josh is working on Cope’s leg in the ring. After Cope gets to his feet, Josh gets a chop block to the same leg. Cope gets a one-leg dropkick, and both men are down. They throw hands as they work to their feet. Josh slaps, and then pie-faces Cope, which makes Cope drop him to the mat and then clothesline him to the floor. Cope rolls Josh into the ring and goes to the top. Cope gets a crossbody to Josh’s back for two. Cope grabs a mic and says that the last few weeks have been difficult and Christian Cage was injured five minutes into the match at All Out with broken ribs and a collapsed lung. Cope says he needed to do some soul-searching. He then says he is aging out, and he wants to let people know that 2027 will be his last year in Professional Wrestling. title: On the Record: Ilja Dragunov Opens Up On Why He Chose AEW After WWE Exit
raw_title: Ilja Dragunov Reveals Why He Chose AEW After WWE Exit
summary_src: Ilja Dragunov has finally explained why he chose AEW, and it sounds like he was simply ready to breathe again. After making his debut at WrestleDream, the former WWE star said he needed a new environment where he could feel like a complete version of himself and satisfy his hunger for competition.
body: Dragunov didn’t specifically blame WWE or point to one particular issue that made him leave. Instead, he described the feeling of having fewer opportunities available to him and realizing that he needed a change before he became completely stuck. “If I feel this chance is limited and it gets more limited, I feel like I’m getting stuck somewhere — not because of external factors, but stuck in general.” For Dragunov, that feeling doesn’t work with the way he approaches professional wrestling. He still has the urge to fight, compete and constantly challenge himself, so staying somewhere that no longer gives him room to breathe wasn’t something he wanted to do. “But because I have this urge to fight — I love to fight and step up. If I feel like the air in a certain environment gets thinner for me, I need to breathe.” “That’s what I did today here. If I need a place to breathe new, fresh air, see a new landscape, and see what the world can offer me to satisfy this hunger for competition — that’s the easiest answer I can give to that question.” Dragunov officially arrived earlier in the night at WrestleDream after weeks of speculation about his future. Renee Paquette introduced him during the show before he entered the ring, took a lap and soaked in the reaction without cutting a promo or immediately getting physical with anyone. Tony Khan didn’t wait long to confirm what Dragunov’s appearance meant either. Shortly afterwards, the AEW President posted the familiar “All Elite” graphic and officially welcomed him to the roster . “He has arrived in AEW tonight at #AEWWrestleDream, and now it’s official: @UNBESIEGBAR_ZAR is All Elite!” Dragunov had been available since his WWE contract expired in August, while his eventual AEW arrival was delayed as visa matters were worked out. AEW eventually began airing mysterious vignettes for him before everything finally came together at WrestleDream. Now Dragunov isn’t just officially All Elite — fans finally know what attracted him to the company in the first place. He wanted somewhere he could breathe, find new competition and avoid feeling stuck, and AEW is the fresh landscape he chose for the next chapter of his career. title: Ilja Dragunov’s AEW WrestleDream Debut Came Down to the Wire
raw_title: Ilja Dragunov’s AEW WrestleDream Debut Came Down to the Wire
summary_src: Ilja Dragunov’s AEW debut came down to the wire in a much bigger way than fans realized. Tony Khan says that when AEW aired its first mysterious vignette on Wednesday, he still didn’t know for sure whether Dragunov would even be able to appear at WrestleDream.
body: Speaking during the post- AEW WrestleDream media scrum , Khan explained that Dragunov’s visa process created plenty of uncertainty behind the scenes. In fact, AEW didn’t get the news it needed until Wednesday night while Dynamite and Collision were already being broadcast live. “It’s something I’ve been looking forward to. Thanks to the process — it can be an incredible process of acquiring a visa — and it’s something that I wasn’t sure until this Wednesday night, during a live broadcast, that I was able to bring you.” That makes the timing of AEW’s mysterious vignettes a lot more interesting. Fans saw the first orchestra-themed tease on Wednesday, but Khan revealed that the company didn’t actually know Dragunov would be able to pick up his visa until the show was already underway. “Some people asked about the timing of the vignettes that suggested your arrival at WrestleDream on Wednesday and then having a second vignette on Friday. Well, there’s a lot of uncertainty in wrestling. On Wednesday night, in the middle of the show, at 2 AM your time, we got the message that Ilja was able to pick up the visa the next day, and we found that out during the live broadcast.” Thankfully for AEW, everything came together in time. Khan said Dragunov’s visa situation was resolved a few days ahead of schedule, allowing the company to move forward with the WrestleDream debut. “Thankfully, it happened a few days ahead of schedule. It was a heads-up by you. Welcome to AEW.” Dragunov ultimately made his surprise appearance during WrestleDream on October 17, with Renee Paquette introducing him before he stepped into the ring and soaked in the reaction. He didn’t wrestle or cut a promo, but the announcers made it clear that the former WWE star was officially All Elite. Dragunov had been a free agent since his WWE contract expired in August, but his visa situation kept AEW from knowing exactly when it could finally bring him in. As Khan has now revealed, the company was still waiting for that answer while its live television show was already on the air just three days before WrestleDream. So what looked like a carefully timed series of mysterious vignettes was actually happening with plenty of uncertainty behind the scenes. AEW got the visa news it needed at virtually the last minute, and that finally allowed Dragunov’s WrestleDream arrival to become a reality. title: AEW WrestleDream 2026: 3 Things We Loved and Hated
raw_title: AEW WrestleDream 2026: 3 Things We Hated & 3 Things We Loved
body: If you missed the show, please feel free to catch up on everything that went down in Orlando on Saturday night by checking out our AEW WrestleDream 2026 live blog , which contains all the info you need on every match and happening on the broadcast, not just the ones that stuck out the most to the WINC crew. Those specific matches — the ones we felt strongest about, for better or worse — are the focus of this column, along with the WINC staff's subjective opinions. Here are three things we hated and three things we loved about AEW WrestleDream 2026! AEW AEW WrestleDream featured some instant classics and a variety of middling-to-great matches, but it cannot be understated that enhancement matches do not belong on a major event. Now, technically the Tailgate Brawl isn't a pay-per-view event but rather the free show that feeds into it, but that doesn't change the fact that having an enhancement match at a major event is egregious to anyone that didn't make it onto the card. Jake Doyle, Josh Alexander, and Wardlow came out for a match against Alex Breeze, Papi D, and Rhys Maddox that would have been considered nigh-on pointless on TV. It was less than three minutes of them obliterating their opponents, with Doyle then feeding them one-by-one to Wardlow for a Powerbomb Symphony. That was it. It was a match, if one could call it that, that sat between a nine-minute contest and an 11-minute contest. And realistically the time would have been better allocated to either of those, and Tony Khan, as much as it may have pained him, didn't need to have a six-man tag here. One can perfectly understand wanting to get Wardlow out there to get some wind under his sails. One can perfectly understand wanting to get the crowd warmed up. Where the understanding breaks down is the rationale that either of those things equated to an enhancement match at a major event. No one coming out of that venue was going to be talking about Wardlow. In fact, a lot of people might have popped to the bathroom and returned completely oblivious to the fact there was even a match. So why do it? What value did it add? Wardlow has been powerbombing nigh-on nameless wrestlers for years, he should be beyond it by now. If he isn't, then that is an indictment on either the talent and/or the booking. That's without considering the litany of wrestlers who did not make it onto the event that could have been in the spot instead, working an actual match against Wardlow and company. It just makes the mind boggle honestly. AEW/X It's unfortunately a bit of a rare occurrence to see the women of AEW get the time in the ring to show off the awesome things that they can do between the ropes. It's been one of the bigger criticisms of the company and something that I have definitely said myself before, but luckily that was not a problem at all in the AEW Women's World Championship match between titleholder Mercedes Mone and Thekla. AEW/Ricky Havlik In case you weren't aware, Nick Wayne beat Chris Jericho

The event's pre-show Tailgate Brawl included an enhancement match featuring Jake Doyle, Josh Alexander and Wardlow against Alex Breeze, Papi D and Rhys Maddox, which drew criticism for appearing on a major card. The WINC staff highlighted their subjective top three positives and negatives from the show.

title: On the Record: Tony Khan Explains Why AEW Doesn’t Run Lots of House Shows
raw_title: Tony Khan Explains Why AEW Doesn’t Run Lots of House Shows
summary_src: Tony Khan doesn’t seem interested in turning AEW into a company that runs house shows every other night, and there’s a pretty simple reason why.
body: “We’ve done a few this year. We did House Rules in Australia after Grand Slam back in February. Then we did the Brawl in the Ballpark at the Minnesota Twins this summer.” Rather than putting house shows on the calendar simply for the sake of having them, Khan said AEW tries to pick situations where the events actually serve a purpose. That includes giving wrestlers additional reps, showcasing younger talent and creating content the company could potentially use later. “We had a few of them, and I think we picked out spots to make the most of them — to get reps, to feature young wrestlers, and record content for future use. And also trying to make the most of it, to do events that are economical and logical and that are going to deliver a quality AEW product.” Khan also doesn’t want AEW’s name attached to a stripped-down live event that doesn’t feel up to the company’s usual standards. Whether it’s a house show, Dynamite , Collision or a pay-per-view, he believes fans should still feel like they’re getting a legitimate AEW experience. “So if I put the AEW name on it, I want it to be a really, really good experience. People have high expectations. Whether it’s Dynamite, Collision, or a pay-per-view, I take a lot of pride in it. So when we do house shows, I try to make sure to make them really good and deliver a strong product.” There’s another major reason AEW isn’t filling every open date with house shows, and that’s the physical toll on its roster. Khan pointed to the style of matches AEW wrestlers regularly have on television and said there is value in not asking them to wrestle dozens of additional live events every month. “We’ve done dozens of really good TV shows apart from the house shows — to deliver the best live event experience with big stars and great AEW action that fans expect, and to make sure we protect our wrestlers. I think, given the kind of hard-hitting matches we do on TV, there’s also something to be said for not having dozens of house shows every month so wrestlers can have hard-hitting matches on TV.” That doesn’t mean house shows are disappearing completely. Khan simply wants them used selectively instead of becoming another demanding touring schedule for the roster. “When we do house shows, I don’t want to put too much on the calendar, and that’s in the business plan of AEW. For me, it means having a wrestling company where we do this every week on TV, have a deep roster, but also don’t have dozens of house shows so we keep our wrestlers healthy.” Felix Upton Felix Upton has over 15 years of experience in media and wrestling journalism. His work at Ringside News blends speed, accuracy, and industry insight.

title: Yota Tsuji to Make MLW Debut at Saturday Night SuperFight in Chicago

body: MLW billed Tsuji as the IWGP Heavyweight Champion in its announcement, adding another international attraction to a card that already includes a world championship Last Man Standing match and the MLW debut of Tessa Blanchard. After weeks of cryptic transmissions on MLW Fusion teasing an international arrival, MLW has revealed Tsuji as the wrestler behind the mystery. Known for his imposing power, explosive athleticism and aggressive offense, Tsuji has developed a reputation as a dangerous heavyweight competitor. His Gene Blaster finishing move can quickly change the direction of a match, making his arrival a significant challenge for whoever meets him in Chicago. While MLW has confirmed Tsuji’s participation, his opponent has not yet been announced . That leaves one of the event’s biggest international attractions awaiting a matchup. Tsuji’s appearance highlights the working relationship between Major League Wrestling and New Japan Pro-Wrestling. MLW has positioned the collaboration as part of its broader “MLW vs. The World” concept, bringing international stars into its ring. For the Chicago audience, Tsuji’s debut offers a chance to see one of NJPW’s prominent heavyweight talents against new opposition on an MLW stage. The event’s sold-out status, as announced by the promotion, adds to the anticipation. Saturday Night SuperFight will also feature MLW World Heavyweight Champion Killer Kross defending against Josh Bishop in a Last Man Standing match . The stipulation requires one competitor to leave the other unable to answer the referee’s ten-count, with no pinfall or submission deciding the result. MLW has additionally announced the promotional debut of Tessa Blanchard. Together with Tsuji’s arrival, these attractions give the November 7 pay-per-view a mix of championship stakes, rivalry-driven matches and international talent. FightBook MMA will continue to cover Saturday Night SuperFight as MLW reveals Tsuji’s opponent and further details about the Chicago card.

title: Match Made: Killer Kross vs. Josh Bishop Last Man Standing Title Match Set for MLW SuperFight
raw_title: Killer Kross vs. Josh Bishop Last Man Standing Title Match Set for MLW SuperFight
body: The stipulation raises the stakes of a rivalry that has already seen Bishop survive a brutal title challenge and later accomplish something no MLW competitor had previously done: pin Kross in an MLW ring. The rivalry took a significant turn in New York City. Bishop teamed with Donovan Dijak against Kross and Matt Riddle in a New York City Street Fight. After absorbing Kross’s Diamond Cutter, Bishop responded with Exit 187 and scored the pinfall. According to MLW, the result ended a four-year stretch in which Kross had never been pinned inside an MLW ring. It also gave Bishop a compelling case for another championship opportunity. Following the defeat, Kross acknowledged Bishop’s performance on MLW Fusion and supported giving him another title opportunity. Dijak also attempted to stake his claim to a championship shot, but Kross identified Bishop as the deserving challenger. MLW announcer Rich Bocchini subsequently confirmed the rematch for Saturday Night SuperFight, this time under Last Man Standing rules. There will be no pinfalls or submissions. The winner must leave his opponent unable to answer the referee’s ten-count. The stipulation means that Bishop’s previous pinfall over the champion cannot simply be repeated; he must keep Kross down to capture the championship. Bishop enters the championship rematch with evidence that he can overcome Kross, but the champion has already demonstrated that he can withstand Bishop’s offense and finish their encounters. The Last Man Standing stipulation could make their latest confrontation the most punishing yet. For Bishop, the stakes are a first MLW World Heavyweight Championship triumph. For Kross, the bout offers an opportunity to avenge his pinfall defeat and reinforce his position at the top of MLW. FightBook MMA will continue covering MLW Saturday Night SuperFight and additional match announcements ahead of November 7.

title: On the Record: Tony Khan Speaks On Toni Storm’s AEW Return Status Amid Absence
raw_title: Tony Khan Addresses Toni Storm’s AEW Return Status Amid Absence
summary_src: Tony Khan just gave fans the biggest update yet on Toni Storm’s mysterious AEW absence, and there’s finally some good news. While he still won’t say exactly when she’ll return, Khan confirmed that the former AEW Women’s World Champion will be back and already teased what could be waiting for her.
body: Speaking during the post-AEW WrestleDream media scrum , Khan addressed Storm’s lengthy absence from television . He admitted that she’s been missed but praised the rest of AEW’s women’s division for stepping up while she’s been gone. “The former World Champion, Timeless Toni Storm. I know we’ve been missing her, and just everyone’s been doing fantastic. The division has seen the locker room step up in the absence of the former World Champion.” Khan also pointed to Mercedes Moné’s run as AEW Women’s World Champion while discussing how the division has moved forward without Storm. Still, he made it pretty clear that Storm hasn’t been forgotten behind the scenes. “We have a great World Champion in Mercedes. Toni Storm is on a lot of our minds, and I can’t say when or where, but I know she will be back in AEW and looking to get payback on whoever it was who took her out.” That’s a pretty important confirmation considering how strange Storm’s disappearance has been. She was originally scheduled to face Marina Shafir in a No Holds Barred match on the March 18 episode of Dynamite , only for AEW to suddenly pull her from the match. Instead, Storm was shown laid out backstage in a pool of blood as part of a mystery attacker angle. Mina Shirakawa replaced her against Shafir, while AEW used the attack to explain why Storm was suddenly gone. Dave Meltzer later reported on Wrestling Observer Radio that AEW only learned about Storm’s situation on the day of the show . More importantly, he said whatever caused her extended absence wasn’t an injury. “So on the Toni Storm thing, the — you know, it appears that she’s not going to be wrestling for a long, long time. And this was something that they found out on Wednesday. It was not an injury or anything like that.” The change was apparently so sudden that Storm had still been expected to wrestle until AEW was forced to come up with an emergency angle and put Shirakawa into the match instead. “And you know, like on Wednesday she’s there — she is set up to wrestle in this match — and they had to do this emergency angle to take her out and put Mina Shirakawa in.” Months later, Khan still isn’t revealing what has kept Storm away or putting a date on her comeback. What he is finally confirming is that this isn’t the end of Timeless Toni Storm in AEW, and the mystery attack that wrote her off television is apparently still waiting to be settled. That also gives Storm’s eventual return a ready-made storyline whenever the time comes. AEW still hasn’t revealed who attacked her, and Khan is already promising that Storm will be looking for revenge once she’s finally back. body: Let’s break down WrestleDream from top to bottom. Get full play-by-play from Claire Elizabeth. Clockwork Carnage for the AEW World Championship: Will Ospreay (c) defeated Konosuke Takeshita, “Speedball” Mike Bailey, Ricochet, Darby Allin, Kazuchika Okada, Adam Copeland, and Samoa Joe to retain the title. AEW’s newest concept was a combination of the Casino Gauntlet and the Ironman match. Stage 1 had eliminations. The order of entrance is the same as listed above in the result. The drama was fairly tame with just cool moves and the pop of finding out who enters next. Then, there were two eliminations on the back end. Bailey was victim to Raging Fire from Takeshita. When Takeshita lifted Copeland for Raging Fire, Okada snatched the Alpha to unload the Rainmaker for an elimination. Okada eliminating Takeshita was a nice touch to revisit their feud. That left six wrestlers for the Stage 2 scoring period. A blaze of excitement ignited with several pinfalls. The pace slowed in the middle, then the action exploded again with Copeland scoring two spears for pinfalls. A handful of wrestlers had 2 points heading into the final minutes, in particular Ospreay and Copeland. Cope ducked the Rainmaker from Okada, then he nailed a spear. The victory was within grasp. Cope crawled on top of Okada for the pin, then Ospreay blasted the Hidden Blade to pin Cope. That gave Ospreay the lead with 3 points as two seconds remained on the clock. Ospreay won the match on a proverbial buzzer beater. Afterward, Copeland made his intention known that this isn’t over. Cope is coming for the world title. So, was Clockwork Carnage good? I’d say yes and no. The concept lends itself to popcorn theater with the countdown clock for entrances, the rapid pace of action, the tension building in the scoring period, and the drama in the final minute. The start of the scoring period was a roller coaster. There was a lot of creativity in the moving parts to hit crazy moves. The finish electrified the crowd. The problem is that the booking felt manufactured to a fault. Copeland also looked a little goofy when he hit Impaler DDTs a few times and never went for the pin. He sold his fatigue to the extreme trying to rise up for spears and crawling too slow for pinfalls. I’m guessing part of the issue was trying to time it so Ospreay could get the final pin with a few seconds left. In my eyes, Cope’s struggle came off as hokey. All in all, I’d like to see Clockwork Carnage return as a special attraction. There are a lot of elements to enjoy as long as it doesn’t get overly dramatic. I’m not sure about it being a staple for the world title. With the way AEW built the prestige of the world championship, it doesn’t feel right to have a title change in a fluky gimmick match. For the first Clockwork Carnage, the win fits for Ospreay, and seeds were planted to feud with Copeland. title: Cinta De Oro Compares WWE Leaders on Lucha Libre
raw_title: Cinta De Oro (FKA Sin Cara) Discusses WWE Leadership's Views On Lucha Libre
body: Across his stint with WWE, Cinta de Oro portrayed Sin Cara Negro and later Sin Cara , and worked under both Vince McMahon and Triple H. During an interview with TMZ's "Inside The Ring," de Oro was asked which of his former bosses understood Lucha Libre better. "That's a really hard question, to be honest, because at the end of the day, it became 'entertainment,'" de Oro said. "It wasn't considered professional wrestling, or Lucha Libre. It was more of an entertainment." He further asserted that he never asked for more than an opportunity, and pointed out how the stars in WWE who are succeeding today are getting the screen time he once asked for. "I think, for me, I never got that opportunity to succeed in that sense," de Oro said. "Obviously, times have changed now with the purchase of AAA. ... But, at the end of the day, who's the biggest star right now in AAA? Is it a Latino or is it somebody that's not a Latino or a Mexican guy?" While he seems to be disillusioned with El Grande Americano's position at the top of AAA, de Oro still praised him for using social media to market himself and effectively adjust to the Mexican culture. "At the end of the day, what's happening with him? He got the opportunity to become a star! That's all we've asked all this time!" he exclaimed. "All I ask for the new generation is an opportunity for the Mexican kids, the Latino kids, to showcase their talent. That's all we've asked this time, and hopefully that time has come now."

He explained that WWE treated the style as entertainment rather than professional wrestling or Lucha Libre itself. De Oro noted he only sought screen time opportunities now given to current stars and referenced the AAA purchase while questioning who the top star is in that promotion.

body: 0 Former TNA wrestler Max Caster has revealed a surprising decision he has taken in the aftermath of his firing from the promotion. Caster was one of the most hyped up recruits in the promotion heading into Bound for Glory. He made his debut at the PPV event and received a warm reception from the fans. So, guys, I really appreciate the support.” The ex-AEW star said that people were “disappointed” because he was no longer part of TNA before expressing his thanks to ACW for giving him a platform. He then disclosed his decision to step away from wrestling for “an extended period of time” and get therapy. “I don’t know what my next move is,” he added. “I don’t know where I’ll be, but I will be stepping away from the ring for an extended period of time. So, I’m gonna go home, I’m gonna go to therapy, I’m gonna get it right so that the next time I’m in the ring it feels like I’m at home.” Caster finished the address with his catchphrase and again indicated he will be out for a “long time.” The post Max Caster Makes a Shocking Decision After TNA Firing appeared first on Wrestlezone .

body: 0 Carmelo Hayes and Kelani Jordan have gotten married. The WWE stars held a private ceremony to celebrate their union. Jordan, whose birth name is Lea Mitchell, tied the knot with fellow professional wrestler Christian Brigham (Hayes’ birth name) on October 16, 2025. The pair engaged in a relationship back in 2023. At the time, Jordan shared several photos of the magical moment when Hayes proposed. “I said yesss! And I’d say yes in every lifetime,” she wrote in the caption. Meanwhile, Carmelo Hayes shared in June this year, “Four months until I get to marry the woman of my dreams. When it’s all said and done, my biggest blessing will always be you, Lea. I love you and can’t wait to make you my wife.” Aside from sharing photos of their wedding day, Hayes and Jordan have posted clips of moments leading up to the wedding on their respective Instagram Stories. All this comes after Hayes made his WWE return as a member of the dreaded wrestling stable The 946. title: Backstage Buzz: What's next for the WrenQCC leader after becoming number one contender? — Wren Sinclair WWE NXT future plans
raw_title: Wren Sinclair WWE NXT future plans: What's next for the WrenQCC leader after becoming number one contender?
body: Published: Oct 13, 2026 by SP3 | Last Updated: Oct 13, 2026 by SP3 On the October 6 episode of WWE NXT, Wren Sinclair won the NXT Women’s Championship #1 Contender’s Battle Royal. Sinclair did this while suspended by dressing as Lucha Libre AAA star Lady Shani. Now that she is the number one contender, it should be interesting how the company prepares Sinclair to do battle with NXT Women’s Champion Kelani Jordan. Here are some potential Wren Sinclair WWE NXT future plans after becoming number one contender. After a kendo stick attack on Kelani Jordan, NXT General Manager Robert Stone was forced to suspend Wren Sinclair. Despite being suspended, Sinclair showed up at the NXT merchandise stand just a few weeks later before she was escorted away by security. Now that she has fooled everyone as Lady Shani to win the number one contender’s battle royal, Stone will be forced to go back on his ruling. Reinstating Wren Sinclair should be an immediate top priority for Stone after she earned her NXT Women’s Championship shot at Halloween Havor 2026. As previously mentioned, Wren Sinclair was able to enter the NXT Women’s Championship number one contender’s battle royal as AAA’s Lady Shani . After using her mask and gear, Sinclair should give Shani a chance to become number one contender. With weeks remaining before WWE NXT Halloween Havoc 2026, there is still time for Sinclair to give Lady Shani an opportunity to get the NXT Women’s Championship shot. Shani coming to NXT to face Wren would be interesting that plays off of the ending of the number contender’s battle royal. Thanks to her win in the battle royal, Wren Sinclair is now scheduled to challenge Kelani Jordan for the NXT Women’s Championship at Halloween Havoc 2026. With this potential battle set to take place on October 31, Sinclair has all the momentum to pick up the biggest win of her career. Sinclair will be fighting for not only herself, but also her WrenQCC stablemate Kendal Grey. Considering her technical skills and experience, Wren has everything she needs to get the job done against Jordan and become NXT Women’s Champion sooner rather than later. In 2025, Kendal Grey made her debut on the WWE NXT brand and immediately joined forces with Wren Sinclair. Becoming the WrenQCC, these two ladies became the best of friends and basically inseparable since then. Grey has been out of action in recent weeks after losing the NXT Women’s Championship to Kelani Jordan at Heatwave 2026. Grey coming back for her best friend’s big title bout could see Wren snapping after failing to win the title and turning heel on the former NXT Women’s Champion at Halloween Havoc.
summary: The latest: now that she is the number one contender, it should be interesting how the company prepares Sinclair to do battle with NXT Women’s Champion Kelani Jordan. Here are some potential Wren Sinclair WWE NXT future the plan after becoming number one contender.

title: Tony Khan Confirms Toni Storm Will Return To AEW
raw_title: Tony Khan: "I Can’t Say When Or Where But I Know ‘Timeless’ Toni Storm Will Be Back In AEW"
summary_src: An update on 'Timeless' Toni Storm. The last time 'Timeless' Toni Storm was seen on AEW programming was when she was found unconscious on a March 2026 episode of Dynamite. AEW President Tony Khan was asked about Storm during the WrestleDream post-event media scrum.
body: The last time ‘Timeless’ Toni Storm was seen on AEW programming was when she was found unconscious on a March 2026 episode of Dynamite. AEW President Tony Khan was asked about Storm during the WrestleDream post-event media scrum . He stated that Storm is missed but added that the division has stepped up in her absence. Khan can’t say when or where, but said Storm will be back in AEW to get revenge on whoever attacked her. “You asked about the former World Champion ‘Timeless’ Toni Storm. Well, I know we’ve been missing ‘Timeless’ Toni Storm but everybody’s just been doing absolutely fantastic. The women’s wrestling in AEW has seen the locker room absolutely step up in the absence of the former World Champion, now in Mercedes Moné… The former World Champion ‘Timeless’ Toni Storm is certainly on a lot of our minds and I can’t say when or where but I know ‘Timeless’ Toni Storm will be back in AEW and looking to get payback for whoever it was that took her out.” Fightful Select reported in March that AEW was not expecting Storm to wrestle for the remainder of 2026.
summary: AEW President Tony Khan said that 'Timeless' Toni Storm, last seen unconscious on a March 2026 episode of Dynamite, will be back in the company to seek payback on her attacker. He noted that the women's division has stepped up during her absence and praised their performance. Per Fightful Select, AEW was not expecting Storm to wrestle for the remainder of 2026.

title: Results Recap: AEW WrestleDream 2026 , grades: Will Ospreay survives Clockwork Carnage; Ilja Dragunov debuts
raw_title: AEW WrestleDream 2026 results, grades: Will Ospreay survives Clockwork Carnage; Ilja Dragunov debuts
body: By the time Saturday's finale rolled around, you could've easily forgotten WrestleDream centered on the world title main event with its fancy new stipulation. That's because everything before it was that damn good. But make no mistake, Clockwork Carnage — and Ospreay — are here to stay. It was a multi-layered story that primarily focused on Ospreay entering first and attempting to defend his title in the stipulation match he created. Meanwhile, Adam Copeland is officially making the final push of his career to become a world champion . And boy, did he come close, as a final Spear to Kazuchika Okada would've given him the win until a literal last-second Ospreay Hidden Blade sealed it. This was the most car-crash match possible without a literal car crash match existing. (Don't get any ideas, Tony Khan). It's a double-edged sword — or blade, if you will. But all in all, Clockwork Carnage was arguably the most fun wrestling match of the year. I didn't say it was the best. It was, however, an absolute ripper of a time, and hopefully we see it again. Shortly before the main event, AEW revealed its recently teased new arrival: Ilja Dragunov. Only one championship changed hands at WrestleDream 2026, and that was the trios. Brodido and "Hangman" Adam Page are once again on top of the division after outlasting Swerve Strickland and The New Level in a fantastic 2-out-of-3-falls match. Once again, the match was largely all about Page and Strickland's forever feud, which will surely cause the end of Strickland's alliance with New Level. But everyone played their parts to great effect, and it closes out the current chapter of things between Strickland and Page, while moving New Level in their inevitable tag-focused direction. Speaking of the tag division, it may be better than ever, which is feels stunning to say. It makes no sense that The Young Bucks are still able to go in the way they can, and they defeated the duo of Kyle Fletcher and Kevin Knight tonight to retain their belts. The match the world is waiting for now is the Bucks against New Level, but Knight and Fletcher sold multiple tickets for a potential win in what was a strong contender for tag match of the year. This pairing was destined to deliver, and they went above and beyond. What All Out lacked in pacing , WrestleDream made up for in spades. Only a match or two tonight felt like they took noticeably more time than the others. But collectively, WrestleDream hit you in the face like an unrelenting heatwave. It was just too hot to look away, and a home run on all fronts. AEW WrestleDream 2026 crown score: 👑 10/10 👑 Just think about this: Everyone loves surprises in wrestling. We've seen them executed to perfection numerous times in AEW, specifically. On rare occasions, the surprise isn't much of a surprise, and it still delivers even if it was so expected, like CM Punk's debut. With Dragunov, AEW teased his arrival ahead of Saturday night with vignettes that hid his face. It seemed pretty clear
summary: By the time Saturday's finale rolled around, you could've easily forgotten WrestleDream centered on the world title main event with its fancy new stipulation. But make no mistake, Clockwork Carnage — and Ospreay — are here to stay.

llm_long: All Elite Wrestling will present WrestleDream 2026 on pay-per-view from Addition Financial Arena in Orlando, Florida. The event begins at 7 pm ET with a Tailgate Brawl special on TNT and the Buy In pre-show on YouTube before the main card starts at 8 pm ET.

The show will be available for purchase in the United States through PPV.com, HBO Max, Amazon, DAZN, Fubo, YouTube, and cable or satellite providers. International fans in the UK and other markets can access it via MyAEW.
AEW scheduled the event only three weeks after All Out. Some television time during that period was used to pay tribute to PAC rather than advancing storylines.
The main event will be a new Clockwork Carnage match for the AEW world championship. The match combines elements of a Casino Gauntlet in its first phase and an Iron Man format in its second phase.

Eight wrestlers will compete across two phases. The Entry Phase begins with two competitors and adds a new entrant every three minutes until all have entered, with any wrestler pinned or submitted during this phase being eliminated.

Surviving wrestlers advance to the 15-minute Scoring Phase, where the competitor with the most pins or submissions is declared the AEW world champion. The defending champion Will Ospreay faces challengers Samoa Joe, Kazuchika Okada, Ricochet, Adam Copeland, Konosuke Takeshita, Speedball Bailey, and Darby Allin.

The 2023 WrestleDream in Seattle drew 6,771 fans. The 2024 event in Tacoma attracted 8,045 attendees, and the previous year's show in St. Louis drew 6,293.

The following Wednesday, on 9/30, AEW presented a tribute show in Satterley’s memory. body: During the AEW WrestleDream media scrum , Tony Khan mentioned that Wednesday would be Dragunov’s in-ring debut. Dragunov liked the idea, setting the stage for his first match since April when he competed in the Andre the Giant battle royal prior to WrestleMania 42. Dragunov made his AEW debut earlier in the night , being introduced as the latest signee to the company. Vignettes had been airing for his impending debut since Wednesday, when the first one aired featuring a wrestler training while a metronome played. At the media scrum, Khan noted that Dragunov’s visa issues didn’t come together until Wednesday, and in fact made the decision to air the vignette during the live broadcast. When Dragunov said he would be coming to WrestleDream, the second vignette was posed on social media Friday, with AEW confirming that the mystery person would be making their debut the following day in Orlando. title: AEW WrestleDream Takeaways Include Clockwork Carnage Innovation
raw_title: AEW WrestleDream: 9 big takeaways for Clockwork Carnage, Ilja Dragunov's future, what's next and more
body: As we get ready for AEW Blood and Guts in less than a month, here's eight takeaways from WrestleDream 2026. In a wrestling world where moves, stories, and matches are all ripped from things that have been done in the past, credit to AEW CEO Tony Khan for continuing to innovate with new match concepts. Clockwork Carnage hit all the right notes, with "Speedball" Mike Bailey getting ousted first and Kazuchika Okada surprisingly eliminating Konosuke Takeshita. The second phase of the match saw things kick into high gear, with the lead changing hands numerous times within seconds of the phase starting. Ospreay closed out the match with a literal last-second Hidden Blade on Adam Copeland to retain his Men's World Championship. The direction from here feels quite clear: With Cope announcing this past Wednesday that 2027 will be his last year wrestling , we're surely going to see the WWE Hall of Famer giving everything he has into one last run for the world title. Ospreay and Cope had a contentious handshake following the match, and the camera lingered on Samoa Joe at the top of the stage, so I'd assume that's the angle we're barreling toward. My only hot take on Clockwork Carnage is that if you earned a pin or submission in the first phase, you start the second phase with that amount of falls. In this situation, Okada would've automatically started Phase 2 with one fall, having eliminated Takeshita. But nothing is ever a given in AEW, and the former champ, Thekla, rode a star's entrance into a bar-setting match Saturday that showed she every bit belongs in the main-event scene. Thekla and Moné exchanged mat wrestling, intensity, storytelling, and matched each other every step of the way. Ultimately, Moné used her mask as an advantage before hitting the Moné Maker for the pinfall. Moné will unquestionably face some bumps in the road, but 2026 should see her continue to roll on and build her portfolio as champion. What'll be interesting to watch is who she inevitably drops the belt to, and whether that ends up being a veteran contender or if she continues to pay it forward and help establish rising talent, the likes of Maya World. For Thekla, it's back to the drawing board after falling just short in her pursuit of another world title. She looked like absolute money in the build-up to Saturday and during the match, holding her own against Moné. There was a strange post-match moment after Moné pinned Thekla, where the challenger sold the beating. But once she got to the apron, she gestured toward the camera and appeared to be done selling on her way up the ramp. I'm curious to see if there's any fallout from that moment. That's Jon Moxley's motto as he and AEW navigate the on-screen grief of losing beloved Death Riders member, PAC . title: Karmen Petrovic First Approached For Perros del Mal In November 2025
raw_title: Karmen Petrovic Was First Approached About Being Part Of AAA's Perros del Mal Faction In November 2025
body: Under WWE’s presentation of Lucha Libre AAA, the Perros del Mal faction returned in June 2026. The revamped version started with Daga, Karmen Petrovic, Bronco Nima, Angel, and Berto. Present day, Nima is no longer with the group, as he was kicked out. While speaking to the Toronto Sun , Petrovic shared that she was first approached about being part of Perros del Mal in November 2025. “I was approached, I believe it was sometime last year actually. It was around maybe November time of last year. So they actually had plans to debut us a lot earlier but it was just about understanding when the best timeframe would be to debut, especially this faction that has so much history in Mexico and the legacy and everything around it so they wanted to make sure it was perfect. I guess the anticipation, the waiting was kind of driving me crazy too because I couldn’t wait. Oh my gosh, I don’t even know. I wanna say, like, outside of myself, outside my body with the opportunity, just knowing, especially everything that the faction holds and the amount of weight that would be on our shoulders. But it was more so excitement and I couldn’t wait to just get out there and be in front of the Mexican crowd as well because I never had the opportunity to do that before.” Daga, Angel, and Berto are the reigning AAA World Trios Champions. They are going to be defending the belts on October 24th at AAA Héroes Inmortales.

title: Ilja Dragunov Reveals Reason for AEW Jump
raw_title: Ilja Dragunov Explains Why He Joined AEW
body: Ilja Dragunov opened up about his decision to join All Elite Wrestling during the AEW WrestleDream 2026 post-show. He reflected on his journey as a pro wrestler and added that he decided to breathe “fresh, new air” after realizing that the air in a “certain place” got thinner for him. “I love to fight, and I want to compete, and I want to step up. If I feel that the air in a certain environment gets thinner for me, I need to breathe. That’s what I did today, here. If I need a place to breathe new, fresh air, see a new landscape, and see what the world can offer me to satisfy this hunger for competition.” Ilja Dragunov exited WWE in August 2026, ending a seven-year association with the company. He had been off television since the SmackDown before WrestleMania 42 in mid-April.

title: Lucha Libre AAA Fallout (10/17/26) – La Catalina Causes Friction Between Las Toxicas
raw_title: Lucha Libre AAA Fallout (10/17/26) – La Catalina Causes Friction Between Las Toxicas
body: October 18, 2026 By Jason Jimenez-Garrido AAA , North America , Pro Wrestling , WWE Universe Tensions are high as we head into AAA Heroes Inmortales , which begins next week. On this episode , we received confirmation of what’s in store over the course of the next three episodes of Lucha Libre AAA, including four title matches and a long-awaited match between bitter rivals. This week’s broadcast was the final episode recorded at the 10/4 set of tapings in Leon, Guanajuato, MX. Here is the fallout from the 10/17 go-home episode to AAA Heroes Inmortales. To kick off this episode, La Catalina made her first appearance in AAA as the new Reina de Reinas Champion. She began her celebration by telling the crowd: “Leon, Guanajuato, this isn’t a dream, this is reality! I am your NEW Reina de Reinas Champion!!” Catalina told the audience that 2026 has been a year of ups and downs, both personal and professional, but that it has all been worth it. She thanked Mexico for being the reason she gets to achieve her dream: “At Triplemania, I beat the most untouchable Luchadora in AAA; Flammer. The longest reigning Reina de Reinas Champion in AAA history. And when the moment came to see who’s the best, Catalina did it.” She then sent a message to the entire AAA women’s division, saying that Flammer’s reign of terror is over, and it’s the start of a new era. As the saying goes, “to be the best, you gotta beat the best”, and that is exactly what Catalina plans on doing. Unfortunately for Catalina, Flammer doesn’t seem to be done with the Reina de Reinas Championship yet. As Catalina celebrated with her title in the air, Las Toxicas’ music began to play as they headed to the ring. “You said “a new era?” Don’t get it confused. This is not a new era, this is only a spark of good luck,” “You didn’t end my story. You only interrupted it… and I will make sure to get that title back.” Catalina responded by giving her a sarcastic round of applause for her historic reign, but asked Flammer, “What makes you think you’re deserving of an opportunity for the Reina de Reinas title?” She added that there are many women on the roster much more deserving of an opportunity, such as the only member of Las Tóxicas who still has gold around her waist: La Hiedra. The camera panned to Hiedra, who had a huge smirk on her face as she nodded in agreement. Catalina then asked: “She [Flammer] is your friend right? How many years of friendship- three years as champion, yet she never gave you an opportunity for the championship? … But I want to face the best Luchadoras, so I have a question […] between the two of you, who’s the best?” This led to a stare-down between Hiedra and Flammer, which was quickly broken up by Lady Maravilla. Maravilla told Catalina that she knows exactly what she’s trying to do, and if she thinks she can drive a wedge between Las Toxicas, she’s very mistaken. title: Max Caster Steps Away From Wrestling For Therapy

body: Max Caster made his TNA debut at Slammiversary, but his TNA tenure was short lived. In his pre-match rap before facing Moose, he referenced the recent Riyadh airport missile attack in Saudi Arabia, sparking controversy . TNA ended up parting ways with Caster the next day. “In the span of one day, I started a contract and ended a contract with TNA Wrestling. I put out a statement, I addressed it and apologized to a lot of people, but the one group I didn’t get the apologize to is all the fans. I really appreciate the support, everybody who has reached out after this happened. A lot of people were excited to watch TNA for the first time or come back to the product, and now a lot of people are disappointed that I’m not on the show. Thank you guys here at ACW for welcoming me. For that, I say, I love you and thank you. I don’t know what my next move is. I don’t know where I’ll be, but I will be stepping away from the ring for an extended period of time. I’m gonna go home, I’m gonna go to therapy, I’m gonna get it right so that the next time I’m in the ring it feels like I’m at home,” he said. Max Caster appeared at tonight’s ACW show and once again addressed what happened with him and TNA. Says he’s headed to therapy and stepping away from wrestling for an extended period of time. pic.twitter.com/XDPZtyWNfV

body: Jalwa Game Goa Game Raja Game MaanWin DMFirst Veer Game YOU WILL NEVER GUESS WHO JUST ANNOUNCED HE SIGNED A WWE LEGENDS DEAL - UPDATED By Mike Johnson on 2026-10-06 22:17:00 Dylan Summers aka The Necro Butcher announced this evening on his Facebook page that he has signed a WWE legends deal. Necro Butcher, probably best known for his countless death match appearances in promotions like IWA Mid-South and CZW as well as his role in The Wrestler starring Mickey Rourke, wrote, "I have signed a basic legends deal with the WWE. The offer actually came in the day after I walked out of my job. The timing was ridiculous. Now, the door is open for various projects, which have already been discussed. But I'm taking things slow. What does this say about my career ? A man who never worked there. But he worked hard everywhere he went. And still will. I will NOT miss my scheduled shows and most definitely will NOT be making any apology videos or speeches. I've worked hard, both for myself and for my fans. Nothing was more important to me than credibility and believability. I hope this leads to more opportunities for guys who never got that call to the big time. This is OUR reward. Let's enjoy this together." The announcement was accompanied with what appeared to be a screenshot of a PDF file that read: "All parties finished Dylan Summers - WWE Nostalgia Agreement Attached is the final agreement between: WORLD WRESTLING ENTERTAINMENT, INC. Dylan Keith Summers Nick Khan" Necro Butcher vs. Samoa Joe was spotlighted on the most recent season of ViceTV's Dark Side of the Ring . Update 10:53 PM EST - PWInsider.com has confirmed with WWE sources that they have indeed signed Necro Butcher to a nostalgia deal.

llm.headline: Necro Butcher Signs WWE Legends Deal
llm.summary: Dylan Summers, known as The Necro Butcher, announced on his Facebook page that he has signed a basic legends deal with WWE. The offer arrived the day after he walked out of his regular job. Per the update from PWInsider, the pact opens the door for various projects already discussed while he continues to work his independent dates.

llm_long: Necro Butcher announced that he signed a basic legends deal with WWE. The agreement was confirmed as accurate by sources within the company. WWE President Nick Khan led the effort to secure the deal.

The signing stands out because Necro Butcher built his reputation almost entirely outside of wrestling's largest promotions. He became known for an exceptionally violent style that frequently featured weapons and the elements of deathmatch wrestling.

Necro Butcher's real name is Dylan Keith Summers. Born on July 13, 1973, in West Virginia, he made his professional wrestling debut in 1998. Over time he faced several prominent names from the 2000s independent scene, including Bryan Danielson, Kevin Steen, Eddie Kingston, Chris Hero, Claudio Castagnoli and Samoa Joe.

He also appeared in the 2008 film The Wrestler starring Mickey Rourke. A 2005 match against Samoa Joe at IWA Mid-South's Something to Prove event in Philadelphia gained a reputation for its brutality, highlighted by a moment in which Joe kicked him off arena bleachers onto the concrete floor.

More than two decades later the match received renewed attention when it became the focus of an episode in the seventh season of Dark Side of the Ring. The episode examined the bout along with Butcher's life and career. The full episode was later released on YouTube in July and has accumulated more than 700,000 views.

Butcher moved from being featured in the documentary to signing the WWE Legends deal months afterward. The contract typically permits the use of a wrestler's name and likeness for merchandise, video games and other projects while allowing for possible appearances.

summary_src: Thekla’s wild spider-themed entrance at AEW WrestleDream came with a little extra help from the indie wrestling scene. After the show, the identities of the two men who carried Thekla to the ring on her custom throne were finally revealed.
body: Thekla went all-out for her AEW Women’s World Championship match against Mercedes Moné, making her entrance on a custom-made throne designed around her Toxic Spider character. Two men carried the throne down the entranceway while Thekla sat on top, giving her one of the more elaborate entrances of the night. Those two men weren’t just random extras hired for the entrance either. They were independent wrestlers Dante Casanova and Daniel Lacey, both of whom have been putting in work outside AEW. Casanova confirmed their involvement after WrestleDream when he took to Instagram and uploaded a backstage photo alongside Lacey and Thekla. The picture showed all three together after helping bring the Toxic Spider’s special entrance to life. Lacey has competed for several independent promotions, including CCW, BRCW and FIP. Casanova has also built up experience across the indie scene with appearances for AWE, HAW and 1FW, and he’s even stepped inside the ring for ROH. Thekla may not have left WrestleDream with the championship, but she definitely made sure her arrival felt like a big deal. Now fans know that two working indie wrestlers, Dante Casanova and Daniel Lacey, were the men underneath that massive spider-themed throne helping her make the entrance happen.
