title: Massive Price Tag for WWE WrestleMania in Saudi Arabia Revealed
raw_title: Massive Price Tag for WWE WrestleMania in Saudi Arabia Revealed
summary_src: WWE is getting paid some serious money to bring WrestleMania to Saudi Arabia, and the price tag is absolutely insane. We’re not talking about a normal Saudi Arabia payday, either. According to Dave Meltzer, the company is set to collect a whopping $150 million for the event.
body: During the October 18 edition of Wrestling Observer Radio , Meltzer revealed the figure while discussing WWE’s upcoming business in Saudi Arabia. The conversation turned to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East and whether major sporting events in the region would still take place. That’s when Meltzer dropped the financial details. He explained that sources in Saudi Arabia had previously told him WrestleMania would cost more than $100 million, but new financial information he saw that morning pointed to an even bigger number. “So I saw one of the stock things. Okay, so it looks like, you know, we didn’t know this. I actually just found this out, like this morning. It looks like the WrestleMania price is 150 million. I knew it was over 100 because people in Saudi Arabia told me it’s north of 100 million. You usually. They get 55 to go. It’s 150 million for WrestleMania.” “And that is, you know, you don’t want to put that in jeopardy.” “There’s a UFC show in Saudi Arabia November 28th or December 5th, which I would say that’s in jeopardy. There’s the Canelo fight, which has not been canceled yet, but there’s certainly lots of talk about it.” He also said organizers were already preparing backup plans in case things take a turn for the worse. Meltzer wasn’t exactly thrilled with the idea of companies continuing to run major events in the region under the current circumstances, either. “I mean, we’re in the middle of a war and it’s obviously they shouldn’t go.” Still, that’s one heck of a payday. WWE has been collecting huge checks from Saudi Arabia for years, but this WrestleMania deal is on another level. With $150 million potentially coming WWE’s way, it’s pretty clear why keeping this arrangement intact is such a big deal. Steve Carrier Steve Carrier is the founder of Ringside News and has been reporting on pro wrestling since 1997. His stories have been featured on TMZ, Forbes, Bleacher Report, and more.
summary: Meltzer disclosed the figure while discussing WWE’s forthcoming business in Saudi Arabia. WWE has been collecting massive checks from Saudi Arabia for years, but this WrestleMania deal is on another level.

title: Contract News: WWE Pulled Ilja Dragunov From Television After He Refused New Contract
raw_title: WWE Pulled Ilja Dragunov From Television After He Refused New Contract
summary_src: Ilja Dragunov didn’t just walk away from WWE when his contract expired. WWE apparently stopped putting him on television once it became clear he wasn’t sticking around, and now we know more about what went down behind the scenes.
body: “Ricochet and Ilya, they left on their own. You know, I mean, they wait for their contract to expire. They want, you know, they, you know, Ricochet, I can’t say he wanted out. He was debating it, but they kind of knew that, look, he wouldn’t sign a new deal.” Things got interesting when Meltzer explained what WWE did after Dragunov refused to sign. Instead of continuing to feature him on television until his deal expired, the company decided to keep him off TV altogether. “And Ely is the same way, Eli. They kept off TV because they wanted him to sign a new deal and he would not sign the new deal. And they figured did it like, look, look, he’s not signing the new deal. We’re not gonna put him on TV because it may mean that he can go if he won’t sign the new deal.” Meltzer also pointed out that Dragunov’s exit was different from some of the former WWE stars who ended up in AEW after being released. He claimed several of those wrestlers wanted to return to WWE once Triple H took over creative from Vince McMahon, but their AEW contracts prevented them from making an immediate move. “In the case of some of those guys, it was Vince McMahon’s decision. And then Vince is out and Levesque is in. And Levesque did want them back immediately, you know, Swerve included. And you know, Swerve said no and the rest of them said yes, but they couldn’t get out of their deals.” “They had the vignette ready and they knew it was going to be any day now, but they didn’t want to put it on if he wasn’t going to be at the pay per view. I mean, the plan and the hope absolutely was for him to be on the pay per view.” Dragunov eventually got his visa situation sorted out a nd made his AEW debut as planned. So WWE wanted Dragunov to stay, Dragunov wouldn’t sign, and WWE decided to stop using him on television. Now he’s working for the competition, and the same guy WWE kept off its shows is getting a fresh start in AEW. title: On the Record: AEW’s Television Future Still Not Guaranteed Despite Tony Khan’s Positive Discusses With David Ellison
raw_title: AEW’s Television Future Still Not Guaranteed Despite Tony Khan’s Positive Talks With David Ellison
summary_src: Tony Khan may be feeling pretty good about AEW’s future under Skydance, but that doesn’t mean the company is out of the woods just yet.
body: Following AEW WrestleDream on October 17, 2026 , Khan confirmed that he’s had several conversations with David Ellison about AEW’s future. Khan made those discussions sound very encouraging, saying Ellison was excited about working with AEW and that the Warner Bros.-Paramount merger could open up new opportunities. However, during the October 18 edition of Wrestling Observer Radio , Meltzer wasn’t ready to celebrate just yet. He acknowledged that Khan has good relationships with important executives, including Ellison, but made it clear that friendly conversations don’t guarantee anything once the new company starts making business decisions. Meltzer wasn’t suggesting that AEW is about to lose its television home. In fact, he believes the company is safe for the immediate future and doesn’t expect its programming to suddenly disappear from TBS or TNT. The bigger question is what happens once Ellison and his team start deciding which programming deals they want to keep. “But he’s had the conversations and I have no doubt that the conversations have gone great because they’re still there. They’re still going to be there for, you know, a year and a couple of months at worst. I don’t see them cutting them, you know, or taking them off TBS and TNT.” The problem is that AEW isn’t the only property the new ownership has to consider. Meltzer pointed out that Skydance will eventually have to make difficult financial decisions, and AEW will be competing with major sports properties for a place in the company’s budget. “If the numbers keep going the way they are, it’s a best case scenario for them. It’s still not, nothing’s a guarantee because they’re gonna have to make some, you know, you know, Ellison and, and his crew are going to make some hard decisions to cut something.” “They’re not going to cut, you know, the NCAA basketball tournament. It’s, they’re not going to cut. I don’t think they’re going to be cutting the NHL.” Meltzer then warned against anyone claiming to know exactly how the situation will play out. He suggested that the next few months could provide a much clearer picture once executives begin making decisions about the company’s future. “Eventually someone’s going to make the hard decisions. I don’t know what they are. It’s, it’s up in the air and anything that you hear from anyone, probably for the next, I don’t know, short period of time, I think you should throw out the window in, in three, four months if you start hearing stuff from reliable people, you know, then, then you gotta listen. But right now I just say that anyone who says that they know they’re full of.” This isn’t the first time questions have been raised about AEW’s position under the new corporate structure. llm.headline: This Day In Wrestling History: October 18
llm.summary: On October 18, several notable events took place across wrestling history. In 1954, George Becker and Bobby Becker won the NWA Southern Tag Team titles in Charlotte. In 1963, Bruno Sammartino defended the WWWF World Championship against The Crusher in Pittsburgh. Additional events included a 1962 card in Greensboro and the 2005 TNA Bound for Glory main event featuring AJ Styles versus Sting.

llm_long: On October 18, 1954, a live wrestling event took place in Charlotte, North Carolina. Lou Plummer defeated Tiger Joe Marsh, and Tinker Todd defeated Al Cortez. George Becker and Bobby Becker defeated Mr. Moto and Kinji Shibuya to capture the NWA Southern Tag Team championships in the Mid-Atlantic version.

In 1962, Mid-Atlantic Wrestling held an event at the Greensboro Coliseum in North Carolina before 2,705 fans. Rip Hawk and Rock Hunter defeated George Becker and Billy Two Rivers in a best of three falls match. The Great Bolo defeated Johnny Weaver, while Ray Villmer and Reggie Parks beat John Smith and Ivan Kameroff in another best of three falls bout.

On October 18, 1963, WWWF World Champion Bruno Sammartino defeated The Crusher using a backbreaker in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. Boxing legend Jersey Joe Walcott served as the special referee for the match.

A Mid-Atlantic Wrestling show occurred in Raleigh, North Carolina, in 1966. Boris Malenko and Missouri Mauler defeated Aldo Bogni and Bronco Lubich in a bout called the Battle of the Bullies. The Red Demons beat Abe Jacobs and Jesse James, and Paul DeMarco defeated Tinker Todd.

In 1968, Mid-Atlantic Wrestling presented an event at the State Fairgrounds in Richmond, Virginia. Paul Jones and Nelson Royal defeated Rip Hawk and Swede Hanson in a two out of three falls match. Aldo Bogni and Bronco Lubich beat Billy Hines and Jimmy Hines, while Tinker Todd defeated Bob Burns.

During a 1977 WWWF television taping in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, World Champion Superstar Billy Graham attacked High Chief Peter Miavia ahead of a scheduled match. Graham broke Miavia's ukulele and left him bloodied. In 1978, Abdullah The Butcher defeated Billy Robinson in Utsunomiya, Japan.

summary_src: AEW WrestleDream on October 17, 2026, is officially in the books, and the betting odds were almost dead-on. The oddsmakers correctly picked nearly every winner on the card, but one championship upset gave fans who backed the underdogs a chance to walk away with some serious cash.
body: Before the show, BetOnline.ag released betting odds for 10 matches. Will Ospreay, Jon Moxley, Mercedes Moné and The Young Bucks were all massive favorites, with some of those lines offering almost nothing in return for a $100 wager. Now that AEW WrestleDream is in the books , we can see just how much money someone could have made betting on the winners. And while the bookmakers got most of their predictions right, the biggest payday came from the one match they got wrong. Here’s a look at all 10 winners, their odds going into the show, and how much someone would have made by placing a $100 bet on each one. These payouts are based on the betting odds provided before WrestleDream. Profit represents money won beyond the original $100 wager, while total payout includes the original stake. The biggest winner for bettors wasn’t Ospreay, Moxley or any of the other huge favorites. It was Adam Page and Brodido. Swerve Strickland and The New Level entered their AEW World Trios Championship match as -400 favorites, while Page, Brody King and Bandido were sitting at +250. The underdogs ended up winning the titles, which means a $100 bet on Page and Brodido would have paid out $350, including $250 in pure profit. The Young Bucks were at the complete opposite end of the spectrum. Matt and Nick Jackson entered as massive -5000 favorites against Kyle Fletcher and Kevin Knight, and they retained their AEW World Tag Team Championships. But anyone betting $100 on the Bucks would have made a whopping $2 in profit. That’s right, risk $100 to win two bucks. Jon Moxley wasn’t much better. His -3000 odds against Mark Davis meant a $100 winning bet would have earned just $3.33. Will Ospreay’s -2000 odds in the Clockwork Carnage match would have produced $5 in profit, while Mercedes Moné’s win over Thekla at -1500 would have made bettors $6.67. Those were winning bets, but nobody was getting rich off them. The oddsmakers had a pretty impressive night when it came to predicting the actual winners. Of the 10 matches with betting lines, nine had a clear favorite. Eight of those nine favorites won their matches. That gives the oddsmakers an 88.9% success rate in matches where one wrestler or team was favored to win. The only real upset came when Adam Page and Brodido defeated Swerve Strickland and The New Level to capture the AEW World Trios Championships. title: Chad Gable Says Shoulder Injury Fueled His Drive
raw_title: WWE's Chad Gable Explains How Shoulder Injury Created 'Competitive Fire' Within Him
summary_src: WWE Intercontinental Champion Chad Gable explained how his shoulder injury created da "competitive fire" rather than jealousy within him.
body: Gable spoke more about the injury, which he suffered during his Worlds Collide 2025 match against El Hijo del Vikingo , on " Insight with Chris Van Vliet ." He said the way things worked out that led to the mask vs. mask match and everything that followed are "unfathomable to think about." "It's the kind of stuff you can't write even if you wanted to," Gable said. "It's just happenstance. To me, at the end of the day, it tells me, even more reason, I can stop believing in coincidence. Like, some things were just meant to be. Things were meant to play out a certain way, and that's out of our control. I'm no longer a believer in coincidence." He said that he was having what he would call the peak of his career right before he was injured. He was creatively fulfilled and doing a lot, but then, he said it all came crumbling down. "It was one of those stories you hear about, where it's like, right at the peak, the bottom just fell out," Gable explained. "It doesn't get much more tragic for a guy like me, who values progress and achievement at such a high level.... It just all came to a halt, and I didn't have a choice at that point. I was told, 'This needs to get fixed.'" "I never gave it a chance to really settle in, because it was like, 'We got stuff to do here, man,'" he said. "Then, there was some pretty gnarly bumps in the Money in the Bank match, as well, that took their toll... Woke up the next day and man, I don't think I've ever felt that level of fragility that I felt the next day. Almost like any little thing I did, I was just going to ruin myself." Gable said the time spent at home following the injury was anxiety-inducing, but he had faith in all the people he talked to about what was in store for him. He said that the FOMO was real, watching Kaiser take the character he created and transform it, transcending into a success no one expected. "What it did, fortunately for me, it didn't create any jealousy," he said. "It created just like, this competitive fire that I think, if you're coming up against me, it's one of my strongest assets, is my competitive fire. I'm not a hater. I don't look down on anyone else's success, but I will challenge you and I will try and be better than you."
summary: Chad Gable discussed his shoulder injury from the Worlds Collide 2025 match against El Hijo del Vikingo on Insight with Chris Van Vliet. He described being at the peak of his career creatively before the injury caused everything to collapse, calling the sequence of events leading to the mask vs. mask bout something that could not have been scripted. Gable stated the experience ended his belief in coincidence and instead reinforced that some things are simply meant to be.

title: AEW scrapped Dynamite seventh-anniversary plans after PAC death
raw_title: AEW scrapped Dynamite seventh-anniversary plans for PAC tribute show
summary_src: The September 30 episode of AEW Dynamite was originally planned as a seventh-anniversary show before the company changed course following PAC’s death.
body: The September 30 episode of AEW Dynamite was originally planned as a seventh-anniversary show before the company changed course following PAC’s death. Tony Khan revealed the original plans for the episode, which took place at the Petersen Events Center in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, during the post-AEW WrestleDream media scrum on Saturday. “I didn’t talk about it at all for an important reason, because the show where we were going to talk about this, and it was going to be the seven-year anniversary show, it was far more important to celebrate the life of PAC. What would have been seven years of Wednesday Night Dynamite, where we would have marked this, it wasn’t the most important milestone. “And Ben’s in our hearts every night. As far as a one-night tribute show, that was the best we could do. It was perfect. And I think everybody who participated gave it their very best for him. And so that would have been where we would have talked a lot about the seven-year anniversary.” Dave Meltzer also addressed the original plans on Sunday’s Wrestling Observer Radio. “They were going to talk about the length that they’ve been on the air and the longest prime-time wrestling show in Turner history,” Meltzer said on the show. “And he said that once it became the PAC show, they were never going to mention that at all on the air, and that he made the call: no pushing the pay-per-view on that show. They really lost a lot of time that they could have done building it.” The first edition of AEW Dynamite aired on TNT on October 2, 2019. PAC wrestled on that show, defeating Hangman Page in the third match of the night. Meltzer awarded the match three and a half stars. Following PAC’s death on September 27, Khan announced that the September 30 episode would be dedicated to the late wrestler. The tribute show featured matches and tributes honoring PAC, and also Bryan Danielson’s return to the ring. Following PAC's death, Tony Khan shifted the focus to a tribute show instead. Khan discussed the change during the post-WrestleDream media scrum and noted that the anniversary was no longer the priority.

llm_long: The Cook County Medical Examiner’s Office has ruled that Benjamin Satterley, known professionally as PAC, died of bronchial asthma. The determination classifies his death as natural. The senior sports reporter for the California Post first reported the ruling.
Satterley died on September 27 in Des Plaines, Illinois. He was found unresponsive in a vehicle outside a restaurant. Emergency services responded and pronounced him dead at 4:08 pm local time.
Authorities stated there were no indications of trauma or foul play. His death did not appear suspicious. An autopsy was performed and additional testing completed before the cause was finalized.

Satterley was born in Newcastle upon Tyne and began wrestling in 2004. He became closely associated with Dragon Gate, where he held multiple championships including a record 447-day reign as Open the Brave Gate Champion.

He signed with WWE in 2012 and performed as Adrian Neville and later Neville. His accomplishments there included the NXT Championship, two NXT Tag Team Championship reigns, and two runs as WWE Cruiserweight Champion.

Satterley joined AEW in 2019 after returning to Dragon Gate. He became the inaugural AEW All-Atlantic Champion, later renamed the International Championship, and held the AEW World Trios Championship as part of Death Triangle. His final match was a loss to Andrade El Idolo for the AEW National Championship at All Out on September 26.

title: Austin Creed Was Completely Burned Out Before Leaving WWE
raw_title: Austin Creed Was Completely Burned Out Before Leaving WWE
summary_src: Austin Creed may be enjoying his new life in AEW, but the former Xavier Woods has admitted that his final years in WWE came with some serious exhaustion.
body: During an interview with Fightful at PAX Australia , Creed opened up about the three-month break he took following his WWE departure. For the first time in his 23-year wrestling career, he was able to spend an entire summer at home with his children instead of constantly being on the road. “I’ve never been home for the summer. I’ve been wrestling 23 years. And I’ve been wrestling 23 summers.” Creed explained that finally having that time with his family made him realize just how much he had been missing. More importantly, it gave him a chance to establish a healthier balance between his career and personal life. “For me this was the first time that I got to be home for the summer with my kids so I got to actually, you know, be there and be dad, which was really cool and so it also helped me to figure out how to build a foundation to have a better work life balance than I had previously.” The former New Day member didn’t sugarcoat how exhausted he had become. Between wrestling, running his YouTube channel and making appearances, Creed admitted that his packed schedule had taken a toll. He also explained why he kept pushing himself despite feeling that way. “I was very burnt out. Yeah. Very burnt out. You know, wrestling constantly doing the YouTube channel constantly, doing appearances constantly everywhere, which is important to me because I want to be able to hustle.” Creed said his motivation was always to make the most of his career while his body could still handle the demands of professional wrestling. He knows that eventually there will come a point when he can’t perform at the same level, and he doesn’t want to be financially forced to continue. “I want to be able to build what I can while I can because once my body doesn’t want to do it anymore, I don’t want to have to feel like I have to keep doing it, you know? So, sure there’s sacrifice.” However, the time away from wrestling also helped Creed understand that he doesn’t need to accept every opportunity that comes his way. He said having an entire summer to himself allowed him to reconsider his priorities and become more selective about his commitments. “Being able to have that summer really allowed me to figure out what I want my life to look like and what I will say yes to, what I will say no to, what I’m comfortable doing, what I’m not comfortable doing, what I will get out of bed for and leave my house for, and what I will not.” Creed explained that establishing those boundaries has completely changed how he approaches his career and personal life. “And so having that mindset now has really, really given me a new center. And it feels really good to be able to have that balance.” Creed is now back inside the ring, but it sounds like he has no intention of returning to the exhausting routine that dominated his WWE career. title: AEW May Be Planting Seeds for Kyle Fletcher and Kevin Knight Split
raw_title: AEW May Be Planting Seeds for Kyle Fletcher and Kevin Knight Split
summary_src: Kyle Fletcher and Kevin Knight might be one of AEW’s most exciting tag teams right now, but it looks like the company could already be setting the stage for them to go their separate ways. Some interesting moments during AEW WrestleDream have Dave Meltzer convinced that a breakup could be coming.
body: Fletcher and Knight challenged The Young Bucks at AEW WrestleDream on October 17, 2026 . The match was packed with crazy moves and near falls, but there were also a couple of moments that might end up meaning a whole lot more down the road. During the match, Knight accidentally connected with Fletcher while trying to break up a move. The Young Bucks eventually took advantage and picked up the victory after hitting Knight with the BTE Trigger. On the October 18 edition of Wrestling Observer Radio , Meltzer praised the match but also pointed out that AEW appeared to be deliberately teasing trouble between Fletcher and Knight. He said it wasn’t just something that happened at WrestleDream, either, because the company had already dropped hints during Dynamite. “There are two spots in there where teased the future split, which, you know, you can see it coming, and they teased it on Wednesday as well.” That doesn’t mean a breakup has been officially confirmed, but Meltzer clearly believes AEW is building toward something. Rather than having Fletcher and Knight suddenly turn on each other, the company appears to be using small mistakes and moments of miscommunication to create tension between them. What makes the situation more interesting is how strongly Meltzer praised both men. He believes they’re developing into major stars, especially after their performance against The Young Bucks. “Three years from now, man, you know, they’ll be two of the top guys in this business.” Meltzer also had enormous praise for the match itself, calling it one of the greatest tag team matches he’s ever seen. “That Young Bucks match was legit like one of the greatest tag team matches I’ve ever seen.” AEW hasn’t announced any plans to separate Fletcher and Knight, and neither wrestler has turned on the other. Still, between the accidental contact at WrestleDream and the earlier television hints, there may be more to their recent problems than a couple of mistakes. For now, Fletcher and Knight are still together, but AEW might already be laying the groundwork for a major split. If Meltzer is right, that spectacular match against The Young Bucks could eventually be remembered as one of the first signs that things were about to fall apart. summary_src: Cody Rhodes discusses his visit to Marvel Studios from back in August, noting it was 'a wonderful meeting with wonderful people.' Back in August, Cody would take to social media to share a photo of himself visiting Marvel studios, and has yet to confirm any tidbits from the…
body: Cody Rhodes discusses his visit to Marvel Studios from back in August, noting it was ‘a wonderful meeting with wonderful people.’ Back in August, Cody would take to social media to share a photo of himself visiting Marvel studios, and has yet to confirm any tidbits from the meeting about what potential role he could have in the Marvel Cinematic Universe. While speaking to Brandon Davis in a new interview , Cody Rhodes would be asked if he has been asked much about the meeting while doing media for Street Fighter. “You know, there’s one guy (Andrew Schulz) in particular who was sitting next to me on this couch pretty much all day who is teasing things that aren’t real, and if they were real, I wouldn’t say anything, and guessing characters that are great, great characters because I grew up I mean, I learned every Marvel character you could from the trading cards, and then, of course, I had the animated series, and we have it again now. It’s been heavily discussed, but I never discuss it. That’s the beauty. I’ve said nothing other than that was just a photo at a wonderful office after a wonderful meeting with wonderful people. (It’s a pretty cool office.) Yeah, it is, really, and also the whole history. If they had said to you, hey, this character, something like that, and you go in there, there’s a whole library. You could take 30 minutes and go, got it, know it, you know?” If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.
summary: Cody Rhodes described his August visit to Marvel Studios as a wonderful meeting with wonderful people. While promoting Street Fighter, he told Brandon Davis that the encounter has been heavily discussed in media but he has revealed no details about any potential role in the MCU. title: On the Record: Austin Creed Admits He Wanted to Join AEW While Still Working for WWE
raw_title: Austin Creed Admits He Wanted to Join AEW While Still Working for WWE
summary_src: Austin Creed didn’t just start thinking about AEW after leaving WWE. The former Xavier Woods has confirmed that he was already interested in joining Tony Khan’s company while he was still working for WWE, and his reasoning had a lot to do with wanting to wrestle a different style.
body: During an interview with Fightful at PAX Australia , Creed was asked whether he had ever considered jumping to AEW while watching his friends and former colleagues compete there. He didn’t hesitate to confirm that the idea had crossed his mind. “Yeah, definitely. Just to experience another style. There’s definitely a very specific WWE style and very specific AEW style.” The interviewer pointed out that Creed and Kofi Kingston looked noticeably different during their first match on AEW Dynamite. The two former New Day members were moving at a much faster pace than fans had become accustomed to seeing during their WWE run. Creed agreed with that observation and explained that the faster style wasn’t something new to him. In fact, he reminded fans that he originally made a name for himself working in TNA’s X Division, where athleticism and high-speed wrestling were major parts of his presentation. “Just a different style and I think that for a long time being seen in that way people forget. So like if you’ve been watching wrestling a long time, you know, I came up in the X Division. So like this is what I was born to do.” He also pointed out that Kingston had a similar background. Long before The New Day became one of WWE’s most successful factions, Kingston was known for his high-flying offense and fast-paced matches. Creed said AEW has given both men the chance to revisit that side of their wrestling careers. “And Kofi was always that fast moving high flyer. And so it’s just refreshing to be able to have the chance to move around like that again.” Creed wasn’t interested in turning the conversation into an attack on WWE. Instead, he explained that having two major wrestling companies with different approaches is a good thing for both performers and fans. For him, the biggest benefit of joining AEW has been the opportunity to do something different after spending so many years working in WWE’s system. “I think it’s great that there’s two different styles. I think it’s great that people have options of what they want to watch and what they’re interested in. And for me as a performer, it’s nice to be able to do something different than what I’ve been doing for a while. It’s a different kind of fulfillment, you know what I mean?” Creed also explained that joining AEW has allowed him to face wrestlers he has never worked with before, including younger talent who actually grew up watching him and Kingston compete in WWE. “And so to be able to be at AEW and have these matches with people that yes, we have history with some people, some people we have no history with. We’re meeting them for the first time. And there are some people who watched us when they were growing up and wanting to be wrestlers.” That realization has also made Creed appreciate just how much his career has changed since his early days in the business. “That’s crazy to think like I was always the young guy in the locker room and now I’m definitely not. So it’s been a really cool shift

title: Shingo Takagi Angers Wife Natsupoi Over Favorite Wrestler

body: Shingo Takagi Learns the Hard Way as He Angers Wife Natsupoi by Naming WWE’s Stephanie Vaquer as His Favorite Female Wrestler (Full Video with Subtitles) 29 seconds ago Photo courtesy of meraWRESTLING X account Photo courtesy of meraWRESTLING X account New Japan Pro-Wrestling superstar Shingo Takagi is learning the hard way what the trials and tribulations of marriage is all about. Takagi is married to STARDOM superstar Natsupoi and the two are set to team up on Oct. 29th for the first time to take on Hirooki Goto & Yuna Mizumori. Takagi began to speak when Natsupoi asked him who his favourite women’s wrestler was and Takagi wisely motioned to Natsupoi. Hoping for a bit of help, Takagi reminded Natsupoi that they were in the middle of a interview and motioned to the interviewer. The interviewer didn’t get hint that Takagi was desperately sending and suggested that he talk it out with Natsupoi. The interviewer received a subtle death stare from Takagi but still seemed clueless by suggesting Takagi apologize to his wife. Eventually, Natsupoi got up and told Takagi she wasn’t going home that evening then proceeded to leave. title: Will Ospreay Makes Another Joke About His Wife Alex Windsor After Controversial AEW Promo
raw_title: Will Ospreay Makes Another Joke About His Wife Alex Windsor After Controversial AEW Promo
summary_src: Will Ospreay just can’t resist making jokes about his wife, Alex Windsor, and his latest comment might sound familiar to anyone who remembers his controversial wedding night promo.
body: During a recent interview with WKMG News 6 , Ospreay was asked about the challenge of defending his AEW World Championship in the eight-man Clockwork Carnage Match. Since he would be entering the match first, Ospreay knew he’d need some serious stamina to survive. However, instead of giving a typical answer about his conditioning, Ospreay couldn’t help himself and slipped in a joke about his wife. “I mean, it is, but thankfully, I’m a cardio machine. I’m very good at that. Ask the wife.” “I got a good wife, man. So here’s what I did to treat her—I took her upstairs, I smashed the life out of her, bruv. I said, ‘Babe, clean yourself up, I gotta go to Houston.’” The remark drew criticism online, with some fans accusing Ospreay of being disrespectful toward his wife. He later defended the joke during an interview with 107.7 The Bone, claiming he was actually talking about beating Windsor at Mario Kart. Ospreay also made it clear that he wasn’t interested in apologizing to anyone who took offense, pointing out that his wife, his boss and AEW’s television partners had no problem with what he said. As for his latest cardio joke, Ospreay actually backed up his claims inside the ring at WrestleDream. He entered the Clockwork Carnage Match first and survived all seven challengers before securing the deciding fall with just two seconds remaining. Ospreay hit Adam Copeland with a Hidden Blade and pinned him to finish with three points, retaining the AEW World Championship. title: Results Recap: WWE SmackDown , grades (Aug. 28): Sami Zayn stands tall after chaos reigns in main event
raw_title: WWE SmackDown results, grades (Aug. 28): Sami Zayn stands tall after chaos reigns in main event
body: Despite WWE's planned pre-tapings of "SmackDown" for the next two weeks, it still felt like there had to be a significant follow-up to one of the biggest TV matches of the company's year , right? In one of the absolute stupidest, self-sabotaging booking decisions we've seen in quite some time, WWE booked a triple-threat match — a match type notorious for having a no-DQ element to it — to end via a no-contest . That's right. Make that make sense. All it took for Kevin Owens vs. Gunther vs. Finn Balor to end without a winner was apparently Sami Zayn attacking two referees. (Fun fact: WWE has a quite a few more referees than that working for them.) In what world should that end a match? A match where the winner gets a world title shot , no less. Did "SmackDown" general manager Nick Aldis go home before the main event? Was he still hanging out with Danhausen? Were all the other referees or officials of any kind distracted in catering? And it's a shame the ending was so bad, because the match itself had a high pace and was a great time between the ropes. But clearly, Zayn is dealing with a real hand injury, which has delayed WWE's desired progression of his story beat. He hasn't wrestled since SummerSlam — which was literally this same match but without him in it. Honestly, I shouldn't even have to describe why this was all so dumb. The only good bit of continuity out of all this was Owens' interaction with Randy Orton backstage. Speaking of Orton, he and Cody Rhodes went face-to-face in an intense promo battle. It was good, purely thanks to each man digging deep with the family insults. Other than that, it didn't really add much to their feud. WWE booked itself into somewhat of a corner by adding the "you can't touch each other unless you want to never challenge for a world title again" stipulation to this. It feels wildly familiar in some respects and can be really exploited by Orton in particular. Have him go a step further by actually getting Rhodes' family involved. It's not like we haven't seen that type of personal depth in WWE storylines countless times over the years, after all. Black and blue. I see what WWE is doing with Chelsea Green by having her do nothing but lose since winning the interim world title. I really do. It's going to build to a "big," happy, first successful title defense. (Hopefully.) But it just feels wrong, and it isn't establishing her as the caliber she should be treated as. The woman is wicked over. Pay. It. Off. Boo-la Twins. Paige getting back into singles competition is fun, even if her first match post-tag title run was randomly a U.S. title shot that she anticlimactically lost. Separating her from the Bellas and the tag scene is refreshing — but the saga isn't over, despite Brie Bella's injury. The injury derailed any excitement for this feud, not that it had a ton to begin with. Not worthy to wrestle. title: By the Numbers: AEW All In 2026 records 41,102 turnstile count attendance, according to local government in London
raw_title: AEW All In 2026 records 41,102 turnstile count attendance, according to local government in London
body: AEW All In: London 2026 at Wembley Stadium had a turnstile count of 41,102, according to local government organization Brent Council. The turnstile count, also called the “scan count” or “drop count” represents the number of tickets actually recorded as used for admission. For wrestling events generally, the turnstile count is often lower than the number of tickets sold for the given event, and naturally can’t exceed the number of tickets distributed. WrestleTix , which analyzes ticketing maps, estimated 46,987 tickets distributed for All In 2026. “Tickets distributed” refers to the total number of tickets sold or given away for free. Attendance for All In this year was up from the prior year. All In usually takes place at Wembley Stadium but last year was held at Globe Life Field in Texas. All In 2025 had a turnstile count of 21,973, according to records obtained by Wrestlenomics responsive to a public records request. The final estimate of tickets distributed from WrestleTix was 27,245. The 2025 show was main-evented by Jon Moxley vs. Adam Page. After last year’s event, Khan told media the attendance was “close to 29,000.” The numbers for All In 2026, however, were lower than those of the previous two All In events in London. The 2023 event was headlined by MJF vs. Adam Cole and drew one of the largest crowds in pro wrestling history, with WrestleTix estimating 83,131 tickets out, AEW itself announcing a paid attendance of 81,035, and Brent Council disclosing that 72,265 tickets were used. That event had a $10 million gate, according to Khan at the time. The 2024 event at Wembley, main-evented by Bryan Danielson vs. Swerve Strickland, distributed 53,922 and scanned 46,476. The difference between estimated tickets distributed and turnstile count for each of the AEW events at Wembley Stadium has been consistent, with the turnstile count being 86% or 87% of the tickets distributed estimate in each year. That percentage was lower, 81%, for the event in Texas. Going by WrestleTix estimates of tickets distributed, this year’s All In is among the highest attendances for a pro wrestling event so far this year, behind each night of WWE’s two-night WrestleMania in Las Vegas , which were estimated at 50,081 and 52,011. All In was ahead of the individual nights of SummerSlam, which also took place in August and were estimated at 35,654 and 34,216. New Japan’s Wrestle Kingdom at the Tokyo Dome in January had an attendance of 46,913, according to New Japan’s own announced attendance.
summary: AEW All In: London 2026 at Wembley Stadium had a turnstile count of 41,102, per local government organization Brent Council. All In 2025 had a turnstile count of 21,973, per records obtained by Wrestlenomics responsive to a public records request.

title: Ilja Dragunov Set For AEW Dynamite Debut
raw_title: Ilja Dragunov speaks at WrestleDream presser, will make AEW in-ring debut on October 21 Dynamite
summary_src: Ilja Dragunov will make his AEW in-ring debut on the October 21 episode of Dynamite. Tony Khan made the announcement during the WrestleDream post-show press
body: Ilja Dragunov will make his AEW in-ring debut on the October 21 episode of Dynamite. Tony Khan made the announcement during the WrestleDream post-show press conference on after Dragunov was revealed as AEW’s latest signing earlier in the pay-per-view. Khan asked Dragunov whether he was ready to begin wrestling for the promotion on Wednesday. “How about this Wednesday night? Based on what we said backstage, I think you’ve said you’re ready to start fighting this Wednesday night on Dynamite.” Dragunov later made his enthusiasm for getting started clear. At the press conference, Dragunov described his arrival in AEW as “very, very overwhelming” and “a new breath of fresh air.” “The way I’ve got welcomed here, I know it feels just plainly right,” he said. Asked which members of the AEW roster he wanted to wrestle, Dragunov named Jon Moxley, Samoa Joe and Kyle Fletcher before suggesting that the list extended much further. A better question is who not. Like, for real, if I think about all the competitors here at AEW, it is hard to say who I do not want to wrestle. Dragunov also discussed his decision to sign with AEW after his WWE contract expired in August. He said that after almost 14 years in professional wrestling, he wanted an environment in which he could continue to bet on himself and satisfy his desire to compete. Asked for his early impressions of AEW, Dragunov cited “freedom” and “trust,” describing the promotion as “a landscape of limitless opportunities.” Khan also explained why AEW only began airing vignettes teasing Dragunov’s arrival in the days immediately before WrestleDream. According to Khan, Dragunov informed him during Wednesday’s Dynamite that he would be able to collect his visa the following day. AEW had prepared the vignette in case his arrival needed to be delayed by another week or two, but accelerated the plans once his availability for WrestleDream became certain. Khan said he had not wanted to promote Dragunov for the pay-per-view until the company knew he could attend.
summary: Tony Khan announced that Ilja Dragunov will have his first AEW match on the October 21 episode of Dynamite. The news came at the WrestleDream post-show press conference after Dragunov was revealed as the promotion's newest signing. Dragunov called the opportunity overwhelming and a fresh start while naming Jon Moxley, Samoa Joe and Kyle Fletcher among those he hopes to face.

title: Riyadh Airport Reopens With WWE Crown Jewel Still In Doubt
raw_title: Riyadh airport reopens amid uncertainty over WWE Crown Jewel
summary_src: King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh reportedly reopened on Sunday as questions remain regarding WWE holding Crown Jewel in the city on November 7. The airport had been closed since last Saturday.
body: King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh reportedly reopened on Sunday as questions remain regarding WWE holding Crown Jewel in the city on November 7. The airport had been closed since last Saturday. Saudi coalition officials said Thursday that it had been targeted 20 times this month, leaving 17 people dead and 333 wounded. However, there are conflicting reports about the airport’s status, with some news outlets continuing to describe it as closed. FlightStats listed 113 arrivals scheduled for Sunday, primarily domestic flights, while Flightera showed at least one international passenger flight as having landed. Many international airlines are still suspending flights to Riyadh. Several major sporting events in Saudi Arabia have been canceled or postponed following increased attacks by the Iran-backed Houthi rebel group. The Six Kings Slam tennis tournament, part of Riyadh Season, was originally scheduled for October 21–24 but has been postponed until December 27–30. The UCI Urban Cycling World Championships, scheduled for November 3–7 in Riyadh, have been canceled. However, the Canelo Alvarez vs. Christian Mbilli boxing match scheduled for October 31 is still expected to proceed. “Sources within WWE concurred that tweet put even more pressure on TKO not to cancel its two planned shows. I can’t say everyone of course, but everyone that I have been in contact with after this past week would rather not go there right now. In the past, going to Saudi Arabia was “optional,” in a sense that one would not be punished financially for not going, but at times there have been people told if they voluntarily choose not to go, it’s fine, except they may have to drop championships or have pushes toned down.” As of this writing, WWE has not announced any plans to postpone, reschedule or relocate Crown Jewel. He joined the F4WOnline team in 2019 and was named Managing Editor in the summer of 2026. Born in Calgary, Alberta, Ian has covered professional wrestling for more than 15 years.

The Six Kings Slam tennis event was postponed to December while the UCI Urban Cycling World Championships set for early November were canceled.

llm_long: AEW WrestleDream 2026 has distributed 6,695 tickets for the event at Addition Financial Arena in Orlando, Florida. The figure represents an increase of 71 tickets from the previous day's total of 6,624.
The lowest available ticket price for the pay-per-view stands at $36.40. The attendance is expected to align closely with prior WrestleDream events.
The 2023 WrestleDream in Seattle drew 6,771 fans. The 2024 event in Tacoma attracted 8,045 attendees, and the previous year's show in St. Louis drew 6,293.

WrestleDream 2026 is on track to rank among AEW's lowest attended pay-per-views for the year. Other 2026 events included Revolution in Los Angeles with 12,577 fans, Dynasty in Vancouver with 9,136, Double or Nothing in New York with 14,394, and Forbidden Door in San Jose with 9,021.
Additional 2026 pay-per-view attendances were Redemption in Montreal with 7,002 fans, All In in London with 46,987, and All Out in Hoffman Estates with 9,456.

title: On the Record: Ilja Dragunov explains why he left WWE for AEW
raw_title: Ilja Dragunov explains why he left WWE for AEW
body: At the 2026 AEW WrestleDream PPV event, Ilja Dragunov made his official debut with the company. While speaking to media after the show, Dragunov explained why he left WWE for AEW… I’ve never had the chance where I couldn’t bet on myself. And if I feel that this chance is limited and it gets more limited, and I feel like I’m getting stuck somewhere—not because of external factors, just feeling stuck in general—because I have this urge to fight. I really love to fight, and I want to compete. I want to step up, and if I feel that the air in a certain environment gets thinner for me, I need to breathe. And that’s what I did today here. I need a place to breathe new, fresh air, see a new landscape, and see what the world can offer me to satisfy this hunger for competition.”

body: Categories AAA TV Reviews MUST-READ LIST NEWS TICKER TV REVIEWS By Chris Vetter , ProWrestling.net Contributor ( @chrisvetter73 ) Lucha Libre AAA Worldwide (Episode 38) Taped on October 3, 2026, in Leon, Mexico, at Domo de la Feria Streamed October 17, 2026, on Fox in Latin America and on the WWE YouTube Channel * Like most episodes, it opened with a video package of past weeks’ highlights, and we saw wrestlers arriving at the building. * La Catalina came to the ring; she was not dressed to wrestle. Rey provided translation. She showed off her newly won Reina de Reinas Title and said this year has had its lowest lows, but also its highest highs. Now, she’s living her dream. She discussed her win over Flammer. Right on cue, “Las Toxicas” — Flammer, Lady Maravilla, and La Hiedra — marched to the ring. Flammer told her it was “good luck” that she won and mockingly congratulated Catalina. Flammer vowed she would regain it. Catalina wondered which of the three was the best wrestler. Suddenly, Maravilla was playing peacemaker, keeping Flammer and Hiedra apart! Maravilla said they are the best team. Catalina needled La Hiedra, noting that Flammer never gave her a title shot. Catalina said she will talk to GM Rey Mysterio about determining who will be the No. 1 contender. * Seriously… five minutes of WWE commercials aired. We saw the AAA stars meeting with fans outside to promote the Street Fighter movie. * Backstage, Flammer spoke to Rey Mysterio . Rey said he’ll decide before the show ends. Fiscal got up and hit some forearm strikes. He peeled off his top and hit a top-rope twisting crossbody block for a nearfall. Fiscal applied a Trailer Hitch leg lock, but Taurus reached the ropes at 6:00. Fiscal hit a back-body drop; Taurus immediately clutched his knee upon landing. While the ref was checking on Taurus, Abismo Negro jumped in the ring and hit a Roderick Strong-style gutbuster over his knees on Fiscal! Taurus hopped up — his knee was fine! — and he hit a senton for the tainted pin! * El Fiscal got on the mic and shouted at Abismo Negro. (This time, we had English subtitles. No consistency on that.) * Backstage, it was now La Hiedra’s turn to talk to Rey Mysterio and try to convince him to give her a title shot. * Footage aired of Chazz “Starboy” Hall and Mini Vikingo losing their match in the Dusty Rhodes Tag Team Classic. * After several more commercials, Rey Mysterio sat down for a press conference and announced some of the matches that will take place next week, including Dominik Mysterio vs. Grande Americano. Also, Rey Fenix vs. Mini Vikingo will take place in two weeks. He said Catalina will face both La Hiedra and Flammer in a three-way. In the ring, Mesias stomped on Wagner and kept him grounded. On the floor, Mesias scooped up Wagner and ran him back-first into the ring post, then threw him back into the ring. Mecha Wolf got a nearfall at 4:30. Galeno was pulled off the apron so he wasn’t there for a hot tag. Mesias hit a Flatliner, with Mec
summary: La Catalina appeared on the show to display her Reina de Reinas Championship and reflect on her recent victory over Flammer. llm_long: The latest episode of AAA TV opened with a video package highlighting recent events and showed wrestlers arriving at the venue in Leon, Mexico. La Catalina entered the ring holding her newly won Reina de Reinas Title and spoke about overcoming challenges to achieve her dream.

Las Toxicas consisting of Flammer, Lady Maravilla, and La Hiedra interrupted La Catalina. Flammer mocked her victory and vowed to reclaim the championship while Maravilla attempted to keep peace between her teammates.

La Catalina questioned which member of Las Toxicas was the strongest wrestler and pointed out that Flammer had not granted La Hiedra a title opportunity. She announced plans to speak with GM Rey Mysterio about determining the number one contender.

A match between Fiscal and Taurus featured Fiscal landing forearm strikes, removing his top, and executing a top-rope twisting crossbody. Fiscal applied a leg lock, but Taurus reached the ropes. After a back-body drop, Taurus sold a knee injury.

While the referee checked on Taurus, Abismo Negro entered the ring and delivered a gutbuster on Fiscal. Taurus then recovered and scored the pinfall with a senton in the tainted finish. Fiscal later confronted Abismo Negro on the microphone.
Backstage segments included Flammer and later La Hiedra speaking separately with Rey Mysterio about the title situation as the show continued.

title: Channing Lorenzo Injured At NXT Live Event
raw_title: Channing 'Stacks' Lorenzo Seemingly Injured At WWE NXT Live Event
summary_src: Channing "Stacks" Lorenzo seemingly suffered an injury during Friday's "WWE NXT" live event in Sudbury, Ontario, Canada.
body: According to a fan report on Reddit , paramedics rushed down to the ring and fit him in a neckbrace before stretching him out of the venue. Lorenzo had been teaming with his fellow BirthRight members Lexis King, Charlie Dempsey, and Uriah Connors to take on Tony D'Angelo, Tavion Heights, Shiloh Hill, and Shawn Spears in the show's main event. A fan in attendance noted that he may have sustained an injury while taking a back body drop from the ring to the floor. Another indicated that Lorenzo had either jumped or fell off the top turnbuckle and collided face-first with the ringside barricade; he was said to have then landed "hard" on the floor, appearing unresponsive. Spears, a native of Canada, addressed the crowd after the match , saying that "unfortunately, things happen in this ring." He went on to call WWE a family before thanking the crowd for coming out to the show. Bryan Alvarez of the Wrestling Observer reported that, as of Friday night, Lorenzo was still in the hospital. On Saturday afternoon, Connors provided a further update on Lorenzo's condition, writing on X: "My boys alive and well!! We can't be stopped, last of a dying breed! Thanks for checkin on em, I got his a**." My boys alive and well!! We can't be stopped, last of a dying breed! Thanks for checkin on em, I got his ass🫡 #BIRTHRIGHT Lorenzo is a regular fixture on "NXT," with his most recent in-ring outing resulting in and him and Connors losing to Mini Vikingo and Chazz "Starboy" Hall in the first round of the Dusty Rhodes Tag Team Classic.
summary: Channing Lorenzo was removed from the ring on a stretcher wearing a neck brace after a main event tag match at a WWE NXT live event. He was teaming with Lexis King, Charlie Dempsey and Uriah Connors against Tony D'Angelo, Tavion Heights, Shiloh Hill and Shawn Spears when the incident occurred. Per the Wrestling Observer, Lorenzo remained hospitalized as of Friday night, with Uriah Connors issuing an update on his condition the following day.

llm_long: Rusev returned to the ring at the WWE live event in Hawaii on October 16. The appearance marked his first match since sustaining an injury on July 27.
The injury occurred during a match against Je’Von Evans at the Intuit Dome in Los Angeles. Rusev experienced complete numbness in his arms, requiring him to roll out of the ring.
Medical staff considered stopping the match as Rusev reported he could not feel his hands. After regaining sensation, he re-entered the ring and completed the bout despite significant pain.
Rusev's wife CJ Perry noted that he received medical clearance in September. She emphasized that he finished the July match to do what was right for business rather than having the bout stopped.
Perry addressed online rumors suggesting Rusev avoided putting others over. She clarified that he consistently works to create strong stories and support the business.

title: Riyadh Airport Reopens as WWE Crown Jewel’s Saudi Arabia Status Remains Uncertain
raw_title: Riyadh Airport Reopens as WWE Crown Jewel’s Saudi Arabia Status Remains Uncertain
summary_src: WWE may have just gotten some good news ahead of Crown Jewel, but the company isn’t out of the woods yet.
body: The airport had been closed since last Saturday following a series of attacks in the region. Saudi coalition officials said Thursday that the airport had been targeted 20 times this month, with 17 people killed and 333 wounded. That has raised serious questions about whether WWE can safely get its wrestlers, staff and production crew into Riyadh for Crown Jewel. Now there are signs that things may be improving. According to flight tracking information, FlightStats listed 113 arrivals scheduled for Sunday, with most of those being domestic flights. Flightera also showed at least one international passenger flight had landed at the airport. However, there is a pretty big catch. Some news outlets are still describing the airport as closed, and several major international airlines continue to suspend flights to Riyadh. So while some planes appear to be getting in, that doesn’t mean WWE can start booking everyone on flights and call it a day. Canelo Alvarez’s October 31 fight against Christian Mbilli is still expected to go ahead in Riyadh. Saudi entertainment official Turki Alalshikh recently claimed that Canelo personally reached out to confirm he was still planning to fight. The airport situation is only part of the problem. Riyadh’s recent airport attacks have already raised security concerns about Crown Jewel , while Saudi Arabia has also been considering canceling additional Riyadh Season events . For now, WWE is still operating under the assumption that Crown Jewel will take place in Riyadh on November 7. No location change has been announced, and the company is continuing preparations for the show. WWE now has less than three weeks to figure out whether Riyadh is actually going to be ready for Crown Jewel. The airport may be showing signs of life again, but with other sporting events already getting canceled and international travel still disrupted, this is far from a done deal. body: Chris Sabin thinks that AEW has the greatest tag team division in the history of pro wrestling and that you can’t argue that. Earlier this year, the Motor City Machine Guns (Sabin and Alex Shelley) would sign with AEW after being released by WWE. The pair would share the ring with several other top tag teams in the promotion at AEW All In, and are currently one match into a best of five series with FTR. While speaking to MuscleManMalcolm in a new interview, Chris Sabin would speak about the moment at All In, noting his belief that AEW has the greatest tag team division in wrestling history. “It was a pretty surreal moment, especially, like, being out there with, like, Adam Copeland and Christian Cage. Like, these are two guys that I watched growing up. So then we have them. We have the Young Bucks out there who was, like, if anyone knows the history of the Motor City Machine Guns, were tied with the Young Bucks. You know, we’ve wrestled them so many times. TNA, Independents, PWG, everywhere. You know, we’ve never wrestled FTR before. Never had a match. So that was a cool moment to be out there with them. Yeah, man, I don’t know. I just think AEW has the greatest tag team division in the history of wrestling. I think that you can’t argue that, and we’re just excited to get in the mix with everyone, you know?” If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.

Her answer quickly turned into a much deeper discussion about how much her life has changed since leaving WWE. “I’m so lucky and so blessed and so, so grateful to have done so many things in my life, but I just, you know, within my personal life, I still wanted I wanted to grow more, you know? And I had I’ve resolved so many things with my husband over the last couple years, and I’ve grown so much from leaving WWE till now. Like, I’m a different person.” That’s when Perry admitted that her mental health had been particularly difficult to manage during certain periods of her life. “I’m really, really a different person. I’ve really focused on my mental health. I There were a couple years that I was very manic with my mental health, and I was really struggling.” Perry explained that one of the hardest things about leaving WWE was losing the feeling that came with performing live. She described the rush of appearing in front of enormous crowds as something that was almost impossible to recreate outside professional wrestling. “Uh I feel like as a performer, you know, there’s no greater high that you get, no greater adrenaline rush and dopamine hit that you get than when you’re performing live.” She went further, explaining that WWE provided an experience so intense that she still gets goosebumps just thinking about it. “And I To be able to do it at such a high level in WWE, there’s There’s really no higher level, you know? You’re performing in front of 100,000 people, and they’re either booing you or cheering you, and that’s like Just thinking about I get goosebumps. And it’s just an instant adrenaline rush that really no drug will ever satisfy.” However, Perry eventually realized that constantly chasing that feeling wasn’t necessarily healthy for her. She had to find a way to build a fulfilling life without depending on the excitement of performing inside a WWE ring. “And so, I really had to go on a journey to find happiness without it. title: Comeback Watch: CJ Perry Opens Up On What It Would Take for Her to Return to WWE
raw_title: CJ Perry Reveals What It Would Take for Her to Return to WWE
summary_src: CJ Perry isn’t done with WWE just yet, and the former Lana already knows exactly what she wants to do if the company brings her back. While her husband Rusev has returned to WWE, Perry remains absent from television, but she’s making it clear that she would love another opportunity.
body: Speaking on Nick Club Wrestling Happy Hour , Perry was asked whether she could see herself returning to WWE or getting involved in professional wrestling again. She didn’t hesitate to express interest, but explained that any comeback would need to make sense creatively. “I mean I would love to do something back in wrestling. I’d love to do something back in WWE if the story calls for it and it’s the right fit.” Perry believes WWE already has plenty of women competing for championships. Instead of joining that crowded field, she thinks her greatest value would come from working as a manager or an on-screen character who can help develop storylines and get other talent over. “I believe that my strong suit and where I can help move the needle in storytelling and and on the business side I think is definitely as a manager and as a character and you know, I don’t I don’t think they need any new women fighting for championships out there.” She continued by explaining that WWE’s women’s division already has considerable talent, but she still believes there’s a place for someone with her experience on the microphone and in character-driven storytelling. “I think they have a very very strong roster and a lot of options but I do believe I’m a very good storyteller. I believe I’m very strong on the mic, and I’m I I yeah, I and I would love to do something in the future.” “You know, Paul Heyman’s been around for a long time, so I like to hope and believe that age wouldn’t stop me.” “Uh but, it’s all about story. It’s all about We don’t see all the back ends in WWE. That’s the biggest thing I’ve learned over time is And when you guys asked earlier about stories, like if you pitch something or not, like we don’t know everything on the back end.” Perry finished by pointing out that rejected ideas can eventually become reality in WWE. She recalled how Rusev once pitched working with Kurt Angle before his return, only for the idea to be dismissed at the time. That experience is one reason she refuses to give up on getting another opportunity. “And I think a big part of life is keeping dreams alive, you know? So I keep that dream alive, that’s for sure. I’ll be ready if they call me. I mean, that’s why I’m in acting class.” For now, Perry remains outside WWE’s weekly television product, but she clearly isn’t ready to close that chapter. With Rusev already back in the company and Perry openly campaigning for a character-driven role, the possibility of seeing Lana return to WWE television is still very much on the table. title: Maria Kanellis Details 2017 WWE Return Path
raw_title: Maria Kanellis Recounts How Her WWE Return Came About After TNA Run
body: Maria Kanellis recently spoke about how her and Mike Bennett’s 2017 WWE signing came after their stint in TNA. The duo signed with WWE back in June of 2017, returning at Money in the Bank. It was of course a return for Kanellis, who had last been with the company in 2010. Maria spoke about her return on Insight With Chris Van Vliet , noting that the wedding angle for Laurel Van Ness (aka Chelsea Green) got them on WWE’s radar. You can check out the highlights below: “Okay, I’ll try and cut it short. So we’re in Ring of Honor. We’re doing all this new Japan stuff. It’s incredible, but we’ve kind of met our ceiling. So that would have been in 2015, end of 2015. I get a call from David Lagana, who is writing for TNA at the time, and he goes, ‘Hey, we would love for you to come over, work for TNA. We’ll put you guys in a main storyline. Think it’d be awesome.’ All this stuff. So I’m like, okay, cool. ‘Will I have control? Will I be able to still play a character that I want to play?’ He said, ‘Yeah, we’ll give you a lot of control.’ So I had a lot of control over what we were doing and the direction we were going. Then Mike became The Miracle. “We show up in TNA, and that year, everybody. Bobby Lashley is in, Drew McIntyre, The Hardys were there. There was just a killer roster. The Bullet Club was in and out at the time. So we were in everybody’s storylines at the time. A lot of times are the ones that are getting made a fool of, but you always need the fool in order to make a star. So we do this whole year. We build up this storyline into the wedding of Laurel Van Ness, who is Chelsea Green, The Hot Mess and Braxton. We do that wedding, and I kid you not, the crowd did not shut up once the whole time they are chanting, and everybody is playing their role, Mike is this drunk husband guy, and then we’ve got Allysin Kay, and we’ve got Laura. Even the pastor was incredible. Everybody is spot on. And then I leave the ring looking like Cruella De Vil. I’ve got this big boa on, and I’m screaming. And there’s this photo of me, and then Chelsea Green is in the ring, and she’s just makeup everywhere. Then we get the phone call from WWE, and we were convinced we were going to end up staying in TNA, and then we get the phone call.”
summary: Maria Kanellis explained on Insight With Chris Van Vliet how the Laurel Van Ness wedding storyline in TNA drew WWE's attention to her and Mike Bennett. title: Eric Bischoff Says Hulk Hogan Lived His Character
raw_title: Eric Bischoff Admits WWE HOFer Hulk Hogan 'Lost Sight Sometimes Of Who Terry [Bollea] Was'
summary_src: Eric Bischoff thinks fellow WWE HOFer Hulk Hogan got lost in the character.
body: Hulk Hogan was one of WWE's biggest stars for years, with a persona larger than most of the roster. However, according to Eric Bischoff, he often lost sight of who Terry Bollea was beneath the gimmick. "He was in character all the time," he said during an appearance on " Planet Tyrus ." Bischoff explained that Hogan would go out into public knowing he had to be 'The Hulkster,' and when he'd be approached, he was never Terry Bollea. "He lived it. And, over time, I think he lost sight sometimes of who Terry was and who Hulk was." Recalling the documentary made about Hogan after his passing , Bischoff stated that anyone watching will get glimpses of Terry Bollea, which he believes was important for fans to see. Tyrus then weighed in, recalling the many controversies that Hogan was involved in, while praising the late veteran for always owning the worst parts of himself. "He didn't blame every mistake [on someone else], he told it like it was. He wasn't perfect; he didn't always say the right thing," he said. "Who the f*** does?" Tyrus emphasized that, unlike the average person, Hogan constantly had to contend with the possibility of being recorded, despite being human like everyone else. "He could have made a lot of excuses. No one would've interrupted him if he blamed 'this one' and 'this one,'" Tyrus noted. Tyrus, a Black American wrestler himself, addressed the leaked recording and urged people to show empathy toward Hogan. Additionally, Tyrus emphasized that he doesn't want wrestlers to be measured by their race and instead by whether they're good or not, expressing that someone like Booker T should be considered a great wrestler and not a great Black wrestler.
summary: Eric Bischoff explained on Planet Tyrus that Hulk Hogan stayed in character as The Hulkster at all times in public and over the years sometimes lost sight of who Terry Bollea really was beneath the persona. Bischoff noted that the documentary made about Hogan after his death shows glimpses of the man behind the gimmick. Tyrus added that Hogan owned his mistakes without blaming others and was not perfect.

title: Success Or Failure? — AEW WrestleDream 2026
raw_title: AEW WrestleDream 2026: Success Or Failure?
body: Taking a look across the entirety of AEW WrestleDream 2026 , there are both positives and negatives to take away from the show, whether that be creative booking decisions, match quality, winners & losers, or something more. Ever since returning to AEW programming, Chris Jericho’s work has been some of the most unsung in the company, and he proved once again at WrestleDream how great he is for his age, putting in a strong performance against the rising Nick Wayne. It might not have all been perfect, with a kickout at one from Jericho feeling forced and a slightly awkward finish, but for the most part these two vastly exceeded expectations. This was a fun, hot match in which both showed good personality and talent, and it importantly finished with Nick Wayne going over and standing tall after beating the multi-time world champion. Given that they had only won the gold at All Out 2026, many fans had predicted a Young Bucks title retention far in advance for WrestleDream. However, the sheer quality of their show-stealer against Kyle Fletcher & Kevin Knight had the fans on the edge of their seats, going wild for the match they were seeing. The in-ring work was stunning, the pace of the contest was wild, the near-falls were electric, and all four men looked like a million bucks. This was among the best matches of the whole night and it elevated the entire PPV. Whether it be due to poor placement on the card or a lack of character development for names such as Dani Luna and Hyan, the fans simply didn’t care all too much for the fatal four way match for the TBS Championship at AEW WrestleDream 2026. There was some good in-ring work and a nice showcase for underdeveloped stars in the midcard division, but it was severely lacking a spark to take it to another level. Unfortunately, this ended up being one of the weaker bouts on the PPV. Andrade El Idolo has been impressive as AEW National Champion, but with him now on the periphery of the main event scene, it could be argued that he no longer needs this belt. At WrestleDream 2026, he successfully defended the gold against Tommaso Ciampa, who was in dire need of a big win. Over recent months, Ciampa lost to Darby Allin for the AEW World Title, came up short in his feud with Chris Jericho, and was defeated by International Champion Kazuchika Okada … all the while putting in some of the best work of his career. In another entertaining display, Ciampa lost once again, and it was a huge shame. Ciampa deserves to win a championship, and he should have beaten Andrade. At All Out 2026, Swerve Strickland & New Level vs. Adam Page & Brodido was a match of the year contender, leading to very high expectations for their 2-out-3-falls rematch at WrestleDream 2026. Unfortunately, the stipulation was pretty redundant and the match itself failed to generate the same levels of quality, excitement, structure and storytelling. title: On the Record: Kevin Owens Explains Why He Made NXT In-Ring Return After Seven Years
raw_title: Kevin Owens Explains Why He Made NXT In-Ring Return After Seven Years
summary_src: Kevin Owens finally explained why he returned to NXT after nearly seven years, and it came down to two pretty personal reasons.
body: Following the October 17 NXT live event in Gatineau, Quebec , Owens addressed the crowd and opened up about why he agreed to make the trip. He said getting to work with Tony D’Angelo, Kendal Grey and Shiloh Hill made the appearance especially appealing because he believes they’re already becoming an important part of WWE. “With that said, another thing that helped me say yes when they asked if I wanted to be part of this show was knowing that I’d be able to share the ring with people that are shaping what WWE will be. These three — I just said the future, but quite frankly, I think you’re looking at the present. So, for that, Tony, Kendall, Shiloh, thank you.” There was another reason Owens made the trip, and that one was much more personal. He revealed that veteran wrestler and WWE Performance Center coach Steve Corino was the person who asked him to appear, which pretty much made turning the invitation down impossible. Owens certainly didn’t have an easy travel schedule leading into the show either. He revealed that he’d gone from Winnipeg to Sacramento before making the long trip back to Gatineau, all while dealing with issues involving his knee, neck and shoulder. Owens then revealed that Corino was the man behind the request. The two have a relationship stretching all the way back to 2004, and Owens credited the former ECW star with taking him under his wing early in his wrestling career. “But the guy who asked me is a legend named Steve Corino. Steve, I can genuinely say without a doubt, if you’re not familiar with his career, go back and watch — one of the greatest of all time. I met him in 2004, and he took me under his wing, and without him, I would not be standing here right now.” Owens made sure Corino knew exactly how much that relationship still means to him. He also extended the same offer to the NXT roster, making it clear that he’s willing to help whenever they need him. “So, Steve, I love you. Anytime you need anything, I’m here. Anytime you guys need anything, I’m here. I’m at the Performance Center.” The Gatineau appearance marked Owens’ first time wrestling for NXT since TakeOver: WarGames in November 2019, when he was revealed as the surprise partner for Tommaso Ciampa’s team. Nearly seven years later, his latest return wasn’t about chasing an NXT title or starting another run with the brand. Instead, Owens came back because he wanted to work with the wrestlers helping shape WWE’s next generation and because one of the people who helped shape his own career personally asked him to do it. Judging by his message afterwards, Corino won’t have much trouble getting Owens to answer the phone again. "I'm feeling, honestly, amazing," she said. "If I can share the news, as of today, I am officially cleared to wrestle. So excited to be back." The former TBS Champion had been sidelined since early September, the same month in which she underwent a procedure. It was reportedly not related to any in-ring injury. World most recently competed in a six-woman trios match pitting her, Hyan, and Thunder Rosa against Britt Baker, Persephone, and Hikaru Shida on the special "AEW Dynamite: Rebel Heart" show on September 9. Less than two weeks before that, Persephone dethroned World as TBS Champion with help from a returning Baker on the AEW All In Buy In. At WrestleDream , Persephone successfully defended the TBS Championship against Dani Luna, Queen Aminata, and Hyan, the latter of whom has frequently teamed with World over the last year. Mercedes Mone, another recent opponent of World's, retained the AEW Women's Championship with a victory of "The Toxic Spider" Thekla. "Who watched me on the WrestleDream Buy In? it's giving the IT GIRL is CLEARED TO WRESTLE," World wrote on social media after her pre-show appearance. When and where she will make her official in-ring return next has yet to be seen. Bang Bang Gang member Jay White marked his respective in-ring return on the WrestleDream Buy In by competing in a 12-man tag team match.

title: Tony Khan Holds Multiple Talks With Skydance CEO David Ellison
raw_title: Tony Khan says he has held “a few great conversations” with Skydance CEO David Ellison about AEW
summary_src: AEW President Tony Khan says he has held several conversations with Skydance CEO David Ellison about the future of the promotion.
body: AEW President Tony Khan says he has held several conversations with Skydance CEO David Ellison about the future of the promotion. Khan spoke for approximately 40 minutes at the WrestleDream post-show press conference on Saturday, addressing AEW’s relationship with its newly restructured media partner, injuries, the women’s division, live events and other subjects. Skydance completed its acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery earlier this month, bringing Warner Bros., Paramount and their various television and streaming assets under one corporate umbrella. AEW’s U.S. programming airs on TBS and TNT and streams on HBO Max. Asked whether he had spoken with Ellison since the transaction, Khan said: Yes, I’ve had a conversation with David Ellison about the future of AEW. I’ve had a few great conversations with David Ellison about AEW, and he is very excited to be partner in AEW with us. Khan said he believed the combination of Warner Bros. and Paramount would give AEW access to “more exciting opportunities” and “more resources.” “He’s somebody who’s the same age as me. He’s a wrestling fan. I think that’s really exciting for us,” Khan said. The Skydance transaction closed on October 6, combining assets that include TBS, TNT, HBO Max, Paramount+, CBS and the Warner Bros. and Paramount movie studios. Khan said keeping TBS, TNT, Warner Bros. and HBO Max together was particularly important to AEW. Keeping what we have going with TBS, TNT and HBO Max, it makes a lot of sense. It was a huge step for us to add HBO Max a couple years ago, and keeping the whole company strong together, it’s a fantastic situation for us. He also cited continued relationships with Warner Bros. executives Channing Dungey and JB Perrette as a source of continuity. Khan repeatedly referenced the physical toll on AEW’s roster, saying injuries coming out of All Out forced significant changes to plans for the weeks leading into WrestleDream. He specifically pointed to the ladder match, Chicago Street Fight and other matches on the previous pay-per-view as having affected subsequent booking. That issue also formed part of Khan’s explanation for AEW holding relatively few non-televised live events. The company has staged two such events in 2026: House Rules in Brisbane and Brawl in the Ballpark in Minnesota. Khan said AEW was designed primarily as a television and pay-per-view product and argued that limiting house shows can help wrestlers remain available for the company’s higher-profile events. There’s also something to be said with not having dozens and dozens of house shows every month so that the wrestlers can come in and deliver hard-hitting matches on pay-per-view and TV. Khan said AEW would continue choosing its spots for live events rather than substantially expanding the schedule. Khan also discussed the AEW women’s division, including the absence of former Women’s World Champion Toni Storm. He stopped short of providing a date for her return but said she would be back.
