Well, I know we’ve been missing Timeless Toni Storm, but everybody’s just been doing absolutely fantastic. The women’s wrestling in AEW has seen the locker room absolutely step up in the absence of the former world champion. “We have a great world champion now in Mercedes Moné, who’s had her first successful defense of the world championship tonight. The former world champion, Timeless Toni Storm, is certainly on a lot of our minds, and I can’t say when or where, but I know Timeless Toni Storm will be back in AEW and looking to get payback for whoever it was that took her out.” Storm has been absent from AEW programming since March, when she was shown bloodied in her locker room ahead of a scheduled match against Marina Shafir on Dynamite. Storm had also been involved in a pull-apart angle with Ronda Rousey at AEW Revolution three days earlier on March 15. The non-storyline reason for Storm’s absence has never been revealed. title: AEW's Pac Passes Away at 35
raw_title: Cause Of Death For Former WWE Star Neville Has Been Announced
body: "All Elite Wrestling is saddened to announce the passing of Benjamin Satterley, aka Pac," the company said in a statement. "A native of Newcastle upon Tyne, England, Satterley began his wrestling career in 2004 and went on to perform for wrestling organizations all over the world, captivating fans with innovative high-flying moves and incredible in-ring ability. Pac signed with All Elite Wrestling in 2019 and held multiple AEW Championships and competed in some of the most memorable matches in AEW history. Our condolences go out to Satterley's family, friends and fans." According to the California Post, the Cook County Medical Examiner's Office concluded that "Neville" passed away from bronchial asthma. His death has been officially ruled natural. A few weeks ago, The Rock offered his condolences to the Satterley family. "It hurts my heart to do this," The Rock said. "I wanted to send out into the universe and to the Satterly family my love and my condolences, my support, my light, my mana, as you are enduring the loss of your loved one, Benjamin Satterley. As global as professional wrestling is, as global as WWE is, as much as AEW is growing into this phenomenal wrestling company, and wherever you're wrestling at around the world… we're still a very tight knit unit and a tight knit group because we all share the same DNA. But when we lose one of our own, it hurts. And when they're young and so insanely talented, it really [expletive] hurts." Former champ and WWE chief content officer Triple H also issued a statement online.
summary: All Elite Wrestling announced the death of Benjamin Satterley, known in wrestling as Pac and formerly Neville in WWE. The English high-flyer began his career in 2004, signed with AEW in 2019, won multiple titles there and delivered several memorable matches. Per the California Post, the Cook County Medical Examiner's Office ruled his cause of death as bronchial asthma and the manner natural.

title: Liv Morgan Names Her Favorite WWE Opponents & Dream Matches
raw_title: Liv Morgan Names Her Favorite WWE Opponents & Dream Matches
summary_src: WWE Women's World Champion Liv Morgan identifies her favorite in-ring opponents and those she's still dreaming of facing.
body: On a recent edition of "Six Feet Under," Morgan pointed to another pair of former women's champions: Rhea Ripley and IYO SKY. "My favorite person to work with, I find things about all my opponents that I like, but I guess just off the top of my head, I enjoy working with Rhea. I enjoy working with IYO," Morgan said. "I enjoy all my opponents to different degrees. I get something different out of it, or they get something different out of it. So there's things I like about all my opponents. "Probably Rhea or IYO [brings the best out], just because they're both physically dominating in different ways," she continued. "I like a struggle. I like a battle. I'm full of grit, so I enjoy the physicality that they bring. I feel like it makes me dig a little deeper, it makes me tap into something a little bit different just because I have to kind of match what they're giving me." Morgan's rivalry with Ripley extends back to 2022, when they initially aligned in the lead-up to a WWE Women's Tag Team Championship match at WrestleMania 38. This pairing ultimately proved unsuccessful as they failed to capture the titles on two different occasions, which later prompted "The Eradicator" to turn on Morgan. Their feud has been on and off since then, with one of their most recent encounters positioning them on opposite ends of a tag title bout in January 2026. SKY stood alongside Ripley during that Women's Tag Team Championship match. She later met Morgan one-on-one in the finals of the Queen of the Ring tournament and a Women's World Title bout at SummerSlam. Their first ever televised singles collision traces back to December 2024, when SKY again challenged for the world championship. Stephanie McMahon, also a former WWE Women's Champion, last competed in 2018 as she and husband Paul "Triple H" Levesque took on Ronda Rousey and Kurt Angle at WrestleMania 34. Across two decades, McMahon wrestled in two dozen official matches, all while balancing on-screen and backstage management roles. She received her induction into the WWE Hall of Fame in 2026. CM Punk and AJ Lee both wrestled this year, with the latter on hiatus from in-ring competition following WrestleMania 42. Punk, meanwhile, remains a regular fixture on the "WWE SmackDown" brand. The couple reunited in the ring last year to battle Becky Lynch and Seth Rollins. Regarding Morgan's other dream clash against him and Michelle McCool, The Undertaker noted that he'd be open to making it happen, but only on the AAA stage, where he currently serves as the head of creative.

title: Max Caster Announces Extended Hiatus From Wrestling

summary_src: Former AEW star Max Caster has announced that he'll be taking an indefinite hiatus from pro wrestling one week after his TNA Bound for Glory appearance.
body: Appearing at Awesome Championship Wrestling's (ACW) "Mischief Night II" on Saturday, Caster thanked the fans for their unwavering support during this rather difficult time. That said, the former AEW World Tag Team and Trios Champion then broke the news that he'll be taking an indefinite hiatus from the wrestling business to go to therapy and rebuild his life: "I don't know what my next move is. I don't know where I'll be, but I will be stepping away from the ring for an extended period of time. I'm gonna go home, I'm gonna go to therapy. I'm gonna get it right so that the next time I'm in the ring, it feels like I'm at home." His full statement can be seen below. Max Caster appeared at tonight's ACW show and once again addressed what happened with him and TNA. Says he's headed to therapy and stepping away from wrestling for an extended period of time. pic.twitter.com/XDPZtyWNfV Last Sunday, Caster appeared at Bound for Glory, answering Moose's open challenge contest. During his promo, Caster rapped about the recent missile attacks that occurred at the King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. TNA management, specifically its President Carlos Silva, made the immediate decision to terminate Caster and his pay per appearance deal. Two days later, Caster issued a public apology, which he published across his social media platforms.

llm_long: A match on SmackDown between R-Truth and Damian Priest was halted after Truth appeared to suffer an injury. Truth attempted a missile dropkick from the turnbuckle and stayed on the mat afterward while remaining conscious and moving.

The referee checked on Truth and then stopped the match, signaling the X sign to indicate a legitimate injury. Priest left the ring and retrieved a steel chair, but the referee intervened to prevent further action.
Fraxiom came to the ring to check on Truth as Priest dropped the chair and exited the area. Reports confirmed that the match stoppage was legitimate.

title: MJF Trashes Will Ospreay and Ilja Dragunov While Mocking AEW WrestleDream 2026

summary_src: MJF apparently wasn’t impressed with AEW’s latest pay-per-view, and he made sure everyone knew it.
body: MJF posted what he called his “Wrestledream synopsis” on Twitter, and he didn’t have much positive to say about the show. His biggest target was Ospreay, who successfully defended his AEW World Championship in the eight-man Clockwork Carnage Match. Rather than congratulate Ospreay for surviving seven challengers, MJF dismissed both the champion and his title while accusing him of cheating to win. “Fake world champion defends fake world championship in match with opponents who are way better than him and cheats to win.” Ospreay retained his championship after scoring the deciding fall against Adam Copeland with just seconds remaining in the match. He finished with three points, allowing him to walk away with the title despite being pinned and submitting earlier in the contest. MJF wasn’t finished there. He also took aim at Ilja Dragunov, who made his official AEW debut after weeks of mysterious vignettes featuring a man conducting an orchestra. MJF mocked both Dragunov and the presentation of his arrival. “Russian/german loser debuts by pretending he’s a ‘composer’…cool.” Dragunov was introduced by Renee Paquette during the pay-per-view, where he entered the ring before leaving without cutting a promo or getting physical. Tony Khan later confirmed that Dragunov was officially All Elite. Finally, MJF took a shot at Chris Jericho while referencing Nick Wayne’s victory over the veteran wrestler. title: Tony Khan Comments On Toni Storm Return And Britt Baker Team-Up
raw_title: Tony Khan Weighs In On Toni Storm’s AEW Absence, Britt Baker’s Alliance With Persephone
body: Khan spoke about Storm on the AEW WrestleDream post-show media scrum, as well as Britt Baker’s alliance with Persephone since returning at AEW All In. He noted that he can’t say when Storm will return but knows that it will happen. You can check out the highlights below: “It’s been great having Britt back in AEW. And also, she’s formed a very successful pair with the TBS Champion Persephone, who is also the CMLL World Women’s Champion, and they teamed up in Arena Mexico last night and flew back here. They were teaming up last night, and then Persephone came, defended the title tonight and Britt was here. Persephone won the match without outside interference, because Britt has interfered in some of her matches. Tonight, Persephone did it on her own. She’s a great wrestler and those were great challengers. I would love to see any of them and all of them back at the ring with Persephone and also could be some interesting pairs. “Also, Britt got involved when Persephone won the title from Maya World, the former TBS Champion. Maya World’s been out injured; she’s having a great 2026. Somebody who’s really stepped up and filled in in what’s been an incredible year, and I think the women’s wrestling has been great. So, a lot of exciting possibilities. It’s great to have Britt back as you asked about, but also a lot of great things happening with the TBS Title and her teammate lately, Persephone the champ.” “You asked about the former World Champion, Timeless Toni Storm. Well, I know we’ve been missing Timeless Toni Storm, but everybody’s just been doing absolutely fantastic. The women’s wrestling in AEW has seen the locker room absolutely step up in the absence of the former World Champion; we have a great World Champion now in Mercedes Moné, who’s had her first successful defense of the World Championship tonight. “The former World Champion Timeless Toni Storm is certainly on a lot of our minds. And I can’t say when or where, but I know Timeless Toni Storm will be back in AEW and looking to get payback for whoever it was that took her out.”

title: Dominik Mysterio Skips NXT Training For Main Roster
raw_title: Dominik Mysterio Explains Why He Bypassed Full WWE NXT Run
summary_src: Dominik Mysterio has explained why he skipped NXT when he began his full-time WWE career and how he learned on the job while on the main roster.
body: "But I still never actually did the PC [Performance Center] stuff. Originally, I was supposed to go down to NXT and do the classes while I was doing NXT, but the issue was, I was on Raw, and then I would do NXT Tuesdays, and then I'd be home Wednesdays, and then I'd fly out Thursdays for SmackDown, and then we'd have live events Saturday and Sundays. So there's no time. What class did you want me to go to on Wednesday?" asked Mysterio. The Judgment Day said that he learned on the job while working with several of the talented stars on the WWE main roster, both on live events and WWE television shows. "At that point, I didn't see what I was going to learn when I was learning from everyone on the road doing three different TV shows," he added. Mysterio eventually competed on "NXT," but by the time he joined the brand, he had already racked up several matches on the main roster and began his run with a bang. In just his second match on "NXT," Mysterio won the NXT North American Championship, holding it for more than two months before losing it to Trick Williams. He had his second and final run with the title later in 2023, eventually losing it to Dragon Lee , a wrestler he would face frequently on the main roster.
summary: Dominik Mysterio explained that he never attended WWE Performance Center classes because his schedule with Raw, NXT and SmackDown left no room for them on Wednesdays. He learned on the job instead by working live events and television with main roster talent. Mysterio later joined NXT after already competing on the main roster and captured the NXT North American Championship in his second match there, holding it for over two months.

Truth landed awkwardly after delivering the move, prompting the referee to immediately check on him. The match was supposed to be another chapter in the heated rivalry between the former tag team partners. Priest turned on R-Truth during the September 11 episode of SmackDown after they failed to capture the AAA World Tag Team Championships from the War Raiders. The two had previously enjoyed a 147-day reign as WWE Tag Team Champions before losing the titles to Talla Tonga and Tama Tonga on August 14. Things got even uglier when Priest attacked Truth at the WWE Performance Center on September 24, making it clear that their friendship was finished. For now, WWE fans can at least take some comfort in hearing that R-Truth appears to be doing okay. After watching his match end so suddenly, that’s certainly better news than many were expecting. title: In Memoriam: Wrestling icon PAC cause of death revealed after final AEW appearance and tragic discovery
raw_title: Wrestling icon PAC cause of death revealed after final AEW appearance and tragic discovery
body: Medical examiners have confirmed what caused the former WWE wrestler's sudden death less than a day after his final match The British wrestler died on September 27 at the age of 40, shortly after appearing at All Elite Wrestling 's All Out pay-per-view event the previous evening. Now, the Cook County Medical Examiner's Office has confirmed that Satterley 's death resulted from bronchial asthma, according to the California Post, with officials classifying the manner of death as natural. Satterley was discovered unresponsive in the driver's seat of a rental car outside a CAVA restaurant in Des Plaines, Illinois, at approximately 4pm. Emergency services were contacted after a witness noticed the wrestler apparently unconscious inside the vehicle, with dispatch communications describing someone as "slumped in a car." First responders arrived at the scene but were unable to revive him, and Satterley was pronounced dead shortly afterward. Authorities also noted saliva on the front of his shirt, but the report didn't establish what significance, if any, that observation had. An acquaintance told investigators that Satterley had stopped for lunch before traveling to the airport, where he was expected to leave the Chicago area. His mobile phone was reportedly found on the center console with Google Maps displaying directions to O'Hare International Airport. The timing of Satterley 's passing made the tragedy particularly difficult for wrestling fans, given that he had competed at a major AEW event just hours earlier. Performing at the NOW Arena in the Chicago area, PAC faced Andrade in a singles match, ultimately suffering defeat in what became his final wrestling contest. He also appeared later during the event's main event involving Jon Moxley and Will Ospreay , marking his final televised appearance for the promotion. There's been no confirmed evidence linking his performance that evening to the medical condition subsequently identified as his cause of death. He rose to prominence in WWE under the names Adrian Neville and Neville , becoming NXT Champion before enjoying further success in the company's cruiserweight division. After leaving WWE, he joined AEW in 2019 and became an important figure in the promotion's early development. His achievements included winning the AEW All-Atlantic Championship and two World Trios Championships, strengthening his reputation as one of Britain's most accomplished modern wrestlers.
summary: What caused the former WWE wrestler's sudden death less than a day after his final match The British wrestler died on September 27 at the age of 40. Performing at the NOW Arena in the Chicago area, PAC faced Andrade in a singles match, ultimately suffering defeat in what became his final wrestling contest.

title: Becky Lynch's path to wrestling stardom
raw_title: Before they were stars: Becky Lynch
summary_src: Becky Lynch is widely recognized as one of the biggest female stars in wrestling history, but her life almost went down a completely different path. In fact, it could have gone in a few other directions. Lynch was born Rebecca Quin in Limerick, Ireland, in 1987 before her parents moved to Dublin.
body: Lynch was born Rebecca Quin in Limerick, Ireland, in 1987 before her parents moved to Dublin. She and her brother, Richy, became wrestling fans at a young age. However, her passion for wrestling didn’t translate into athletics at first. Early in her life, Lynch was interested in pursuing acting, which she was able to take up again with some success after becoming a WWE star with roles in Happy Gilmore 2 , Young Rock , and Star Trek: Starfleet Academy . However, the wrestling bug also bit her early, and she entered into a wrestling school run by another future WWE star, Finn Bálor, in 2002 at the tender age of 15. Lynch later dropped out of college at 17 to wrestle in Japan and Canada, but she practically abandoned the endeavor two years later after sustaining a head injury during a match in Germany. She was later diagnosed with possible damage to her eighth cranial nerve, and she turned away from wrestling for several years. “I quit wrestling in 2006, because I just got lost. My mom didn’t want me wrestling, I was wondering if I was going to make it in wrestling, I got injured in a match, I was 19, I was away from home, living in Florida, and I just got lost,” she told ESPN.com in 2016. “I couldn’t face it, so I stepped away. It was like a death for me, and that is not an exaggeration. I struggled for years to find what I wanted to do. I was away for seven years.” Away from the ring, Lynch got a degree in acting and performed in plays. She also worked as a flight attendant for Aer Lingus for more than two years, as well as found employment as a personal trainer, as an English language teacher, and doing stunt work. One of her more colorful side quests was studying the art of clowning while attending Columbia College Chicago. “I studied clown in Columbia,” she told comedian Bert Kreischer on his Something’s Burning show in November 2025. “More just the nose and the embodiment of the clown. Just the mask work.” Lynch continued: “So, I went back to college ,and I did my degree in acting, and I went to Columbia College. And then at the end of the semester, I was in physical theater, and this teacher, this little Italian woman, brings in the clown nose. And everybody just stood up there, and she wouldn’t let you do anything, and you just had to stand there, and like everybody just started crying. And I was like, ‘What is this? What is this thing?’ And so then I became fascinated with it, and I ended up doing my thesis on it — on how clown can bring out a truthful performance. I loved it.” But of course, Lynch eventually found her way back to wrestling, signing a contract with WWE in 2013. Even after finally making it to WWE, Lynch still needed a little time to fine tune her persona. When she debuted for NXT in 2014, her gimmick played up her Irish heritage with all-green ring gear and an entrance that featured her dancing an Irish jig. “I would put that over Shockmaster in terms of shameful debuts,” Lynch said to Chris Van Vliet in 2023 of her first N
summary: Born Rebecca Quin in Limerick, Ireland in 1987, Becky Lynch and her brother Richy grew up as wrestling fans in Dublin. She trained at Finn Bálor's wrestling school at age 15 in 2002, later dropped out of college at 17 to wrestle in Japan and Canada, but stepped away from the business in 2006 after a head injury in Germany that led to a diagnosis of possible damage to her eighth cranial nerve. Lynch pursued acting during her time away from wrestling and later returned to find success in WWE while also taking on roles in Happy Gilmore 2, Young Rock, and Star Trek: Starfleet Academy.

title: Keith Lee Remains Under AEW Contract

body: Keith Lee hasn’t been seen in AEW in almost three years, but he is still reportedly with the company. Lee last competed on AEW TV at the December 23rd, 2023 Holiday Bash episode of AEW Collision. Since then, he has been off of TV and his in-ring status has not been entirely clear. A fan question in the latest Fightful Select Answers Q&A asked about Lee’s contract and injury status. Sean Ross Sapp said that Lee is still under contract with AEW and isn’t currently factored into any future creative plans. As previously noted , a comeback for Lee was discussed at a point in the first half of the year, but obviously it didn’t happen and there was no reason why given. Keith Lee got a bit of controversy online after he posted a pic with Darius Wright in September, a figure who teaches alternative spirituality practices like out of body experiences and more. Sapp noted that the post was a “topic of conversation for about a day” in the company, but there was nothing talked about after that.
summary: Keith Lee has not appeared on AEW television since the December 23, 2023 episode of Collision. The cause was bronchial asthma. CBS Chicago reported on the 18th (Korea time) that the cause of death of Satterley, an All Elite Wrestling (AEW) star known to fans as Pac, has been revealed. He died the day after competing at AEW's "All Out" event in Hoffman Estates, Illinois. According to the outlet, the Cook County medical examiner's office released that the cause of his death was bronchial asthma. Bronchial asthma is a chronic inflammatory disease of the airways. The medical examiner's office ruled his death natural. The exact cause was disclosed about three weeks after news of his sudden death first emerged. Satterley was found unconscious in a rental car parked outside a restaurant in Des Plaines, Illinois, at about 4 p.m. on Sept. 27. He had collapsed alone inside the vehicle, and emergency responders at the scene officially confirmed his death within minutes. According to the New York Post, the 911 caller described Satterley as "unconscious and collapsed" inside the car. The initial incident report found no obvious injuries or suspicious marks on his body. However, saliva was found on the front of Satterley's shirt, and drugs were discovered in the vehicle. The specific type of drugs or any connection to his death has not been confirmed. What made Satterley's death more shocking was that he had been in the ring just one day earlier. He competed at the All Out event at Now Arena in Hoffman Estates, Illinois, on Sept. 26, the day before his death. Satterley faced Andrade El Idolo but lost. That became his final match. He was reportedly scheduled to head to the airport the next day. The New York Post reported that a woman who spoke with police at the scene said Satterley had stopped at a restaurant for lunch before heading to the airport. The report said his phone had Google Maps open showing a route to Chicago O'Hare International Airport. But Satterley never reached his destination and died at the young age of 40. He was a 1986-born professional wrestler from Newcastle upon Tyne, England. Satterley began his career in 2004 and became known worldwide for his spectacular aerial moves and outstanding ring work. He notably also competed in World Wrestling Entertainment (WWE). In its developmental brand he used the ring name Adrian Neville, and on the main roster he performed as Neville. He then signed with All Elite Wrestling in 2019 and enjoyed a new peak. Performing under the name Pac, he became AEW International Champion and was a two-time AEW World Trios Champion.

title: WrestleMania 32 Produced Record $170M Economic Impact
raw_title: WrestleMania 32 generated record $170 million for Dallas/Arlington region
body: More Share Options More Share Options Share close facebook x threads email WWE, Dallas Mayor Mike Rawlings and Arlington Mayor Jeff Williams announced today that WrestleMania 32 generated $170.4 million in economic impact for the Dallas/Arlington region this past April, according to a study conducted by the Enigma Research Corporation. This marks a new record for WrestleMania’s economic impact and the fifth consecutive year that WrestleMania generated more than $100 million in economic impact for its host region. Over the past 10 years, WrestleMania has generated nearly $1 billion in cumulative economic impact for the cities that have hosted the event. WrestleMania 32 also generated approximately $23.8 million in federal, state and local taxes. “We are proud that WWE’s biggest event in history was held here in Arlington,” Arlington Mayor Jeff Williams said. “The event was an incredible success for our city, and we would like to thank the Dallas Cowboys for their tireless efforts in bringing WrestleMania to AT&T Stadium." "We are thrilled that WrestleMania continues to break records for both WWE and our host community,” said John P. Saboor, WWE Executive Vice President, Special Events. "This success would not have been possible without the support of Mayor Rawlings, Mayor Williams, Charlotte Jones and the entire Dallas Cowboys organization as well as all of our public and private sector partners that embraced WWE’s worldwide fan base for this historic celebration. We now look ahead to our return to Orlando for WrestleMania 33." A record crowd of 101,763 fans from all 50 states and 35 countries attended WWE’s pop-culture extravaganza this past April, making it the highest-grossing and best-attended event in WWE history. The story is Young promised Nash $60,000 to take out Hernandez, his enemy, and he’d make sure Nash kept the title. “After Young gave Hernandez an elbow off the top, Nash went for the power bomb. Young then grabbed Hernandez’s head and rammed it into Nash’s sore groin (from when Daffney and Dr. Stevie gave him a taser to the groin) and Nash went down and Young pinned Nash to take the title. title: ACW Mischief Night 2 results
raw_title: Awesome Championship Wrestling "Mischief, Night 2" results (10/17): Vetter's review of Killer Kross vs. Joseph Sawyer for the ACW Title, Max Caster saying he's going to therapy
body: By Chris Vetter , ProWrestling.net Contributor ( @chrisvetter73 ) 1. Real1 vs. Buddy Thomas vs. Liamo. Real1, of course, is best known as Enzo Amore. Two unknown opponents were already in the ring, and they didn’t get on-screen graphics. Real1 cut a typical promo. Liamo, wearing white trunks, attacked Real 1. Buddy wore an ugly blue one-piece. He walked the top rope while holding an umbrella. Real1 hit a running punt kick to Buddy’s ribs. Liamo set up for a dive, but Real1 struck him. Real1 crotched both guys on the guardrail at ringside. Real 1 picked up Liamo and ran him shoulders-first into the ring post. * A woman interviewed J-Rod and Janai Kai in the locker room. J-Rod vowed to win; Janai simply snickered under her breath and walked away. Janai flipped J-Rod to the mat at 3:00 and hit her own stiff kick to the spine. J-Rod hit a brainbuster for a nearfall, then a hard clothesline. She mockingly did some jumping jacks before tying up Kai on the mat. Kai hit a running Helluva Kick at 5:00 and more spin kicks to the back. J-Rod hit a spinebuster, but Janai hit a running knee for a nearfall at 7:00. J-Rod cut her in half with a spear, then hit a Samoan Drop for the pin. I enjoyed that. * A woman interviewed Zack Clayton backstage. He was supposed to face Flip Gordon , but Flip has (legitimately) re-enlisted and is now overseas. Zack said Flip is a coward for running away from him. Zack has issued an open challenge! I’ll point out that Zack has dyed his hair darker and he looks so much younger for it! The last time we saw him in AEW, he was really turning silver at a premature age. He headed to the ring first! He got on the mic and again made fun of Flip for not being there. The crowd chanted, “USA!” in response. He vowed to beat whoever came out. Zack Clayton defeated Max Caster to retain the ACW National Title at 6:26. * Max got on the mic! “Yo! Yo! Yo! Listen.” He asked if everyone was aware of what happened with him last week. “ In the span of one day, I started a contract, and ended a contract, with TNA wrestling ,” he said. He apologized to a lot of people, but he said he didn’t get to apologize to the fans. He appreciates the support. “ I love you, and I thank you. I don’t know what my next move is. But I will be stepping away from the ring for an extended period of time. So I’m going to go home and go to therapy until I get it right. ” He won’t be back until being in the ring feels like being at home. 4. Mance Warner vs. Marcus Mathers in a hardcore match. Cagematch.net shows these two have shared the ring eight times, with Mance 1-0 in singles action. I’ve seen Marcus do hardcore matches, but not during the time he was under WWE ID contract. ( I don’t know if ID prohibited that — just acknowledging it’s been at least two years since he’s done a match like this. ) Mance attacked from behind; Marcus still had his robe on. Mance grabbed the mic and told Mathers never to turn his back on Ol’ Mancer. He stomped on Marcus and hit some chops.

However, behind the battle royale lies a deadly conspiracy that forces them to face off against each other and the demons from their past. The film has a 41% critical rating on Rotten Tomatoes, but a 79% popcorn rating.

title: What Happened to Chris Benoit’s Surviving Son - 19 Years After Double-Murder Incident
raw_title: What Happened to Chris Benoit’s Surviving Son - 19 Years After Double-Murder Incident
body: The news rocked the wrestling world, and it is still yet to fully recover. That a loved and respected professional could do such a thing seemed unfathomable, and many questions will remain unanswered forever. Friends, family and fans all mourned Benoit's wife, Nancy, and his seven-year-old son Daniel, while trying to understand what had snapped in the ex-wrestler's head. The person left in the hardest position imaginable was his other son, David. Over the course of the weekend spanning the 22nd to 24th of June 2007, Benoit murdered Nancy and Daniel before hanging himself from the weight machine in his suburban Atlanta home. The man nicknamed 'The Rabid Wolverine' was scheduled to appear at a WWE event on the Sunday but cancelled, citing an undisclosed 'family emergency'. Authorities were prompted to carry out a wellness check after Benoit sent 'several curious text messages' to friends. His body, along with his wife and son, was found on the Monday. Investigators believe Benoit killed Nancy first, before his son. Both died from asphyxiation. Even 19 years later, a lot of details surrounding Benoit's motivation are unknown and are likely to stay that way. An autopsy revealed his brain showed evidence of chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE). However, there is no way of proving the role it played in his actions. Speaking to Chris Van Vliet in 2020, David opened up on the harrowing reality of what his father did to his stepmother and half-brother. David, who was 14 at the time, is still convinced something went seriously wrong in Chris' head that day. "It wasn’t him, man. It definitely wasn’t. He would never do that, I know he wouldn’t. I think something terribly went wrong. The doctor said he had CTE. That’s what, at the beginning, gave me some closure. It just made my life a little easier, didn’t have to think about it. He had CTE. I don’t think it was him." The now 33-year-old admitted that he struggled to believe it at the time and even punched a police officer. "I didn’t believe it for days, bro. I think the day it really hit me was his funeral. That was a hard day, that was a super hard day," he explained. Eddie Guerrero, Benoit's best friend, had passed away from heart failure in November 2005 , and several people close to him have described how much it impacted him. "That played a role. That took a toll on him, man, when Eddie passed away? That man was his best friend," David claimed. Despite originally hosting a tribute show on the same day the news of his death was reported, WWE haven't mentioned Benoit's name ever since the truly shocking details came to light. But David would like the company to recognise the professional achievements of his father, and even said he wants him in the Hall of Fame. He said: "I would like the WWE to remember him, at least for the good times. I want him in the Hall of Fame." summary: Friends, family and the audience all mourned Benoit's wife, Nancy, and his seven-year-old son Daniel, while trying to understand what had snapped in the ex-wrestler's head. Investigators believe Benoit killed Nancy first, before his son.

title: Roman Reigns Discusses Nepotism and Samoan Wrestling Success
raw_title: Roman Reigns Comments On Nepotism In Wrestling, Why Samoans Make Good Wrestlers
body: Roman Reigns recently weighed in on the nuances of nepotism in wrestling and why Samoans make good pro wrestlers. Reigns is of course a member of the legendary Anoaʻi family, which has been a major part of professional wrestling for decades. Roman Reigns was asked in his interview on Club Shay Shay about people who say he got into WWE easy because of his family, and was asked why Samoans “are so good at wrestling.” You can see the highlights below: “I mean, it’s like anything. Nepotism is funny. It’s a funny case, because the door opens for you. But what are you going to do when you get in the room? Are you going to just be one of those guys in the corner blending in, or you going to take over the room? “So yeah. I mean, we do have the advantage. But nowadays in this — I mean, if you told me 20 years ago to 40 years ago, we definitely have the advantage, because we know about Fight Club. Nobody knew about Fight Club back then, you know? There was a mystique around the business. Not everybody — if you tried to get in, they beat you up for real. That way you’d be like, ‘No, I don’t want to do this.’ Because they don’t want everybody in the business; we don’t want to share our secrets. Now, all you got to do is like go on Instagram, you know what I mean? Like, follow WWE, you can get a try out tomorrow. So it’s just a little bit different nowadays.” “That’s a good [question]. I was about to say, it feels like athletically, I — and I say this too. And I feel like over the years, it’s gotten a little like ridiculous, it’s almost like a lie. But I heard back when I was younger, 40% of Polynesian males make it professionally in athletics, one way or the other. Whether it’s rugby or football. “So I mean, the athletic background and that base is there. I mean, we’re just we’re big humans that can move. If you sprinkle in a little bit of storytelling, a little bit of charisma, a little bit of public speaking, and you have us.”
summary: Roman Reigns addressed criticism that his Anoa'i family ties gave him an easy path into WWE. He explained that while family connections open doors, it is up to the individual to seize the opportunity and excel once inside. Reigns also noted that Samoans benefit from generational knowledge of the wrestling business that was once hidden from outsiders.

title: Cena Ate Hornswoggle's Vomit-Covered Burger After Missed Flight
raw_title: A Missed WWE Flight In Ireland Led To Hornswoggle Vomiting On John Cena's Hamburger
summary_src: Having an incredible WWE career, the "Never Seen 17" star John Cena recalls an unforgettable night that did not end in his favor.
body: "We got stuck in Ireland because there was a volcano and we couldn't get back to the states to perform [on] '[WWE] Raw.' The last thing you want to do is leave us stuck someplace alone idle with nothing to do. Boy, we had a great night," the former "Never Seen 17" World Champion said. "A friend of mine, Dylan, who wrestled under the moniker Hornswoggle, and another friend of mine, Christian Cage, who was Christian in the WWE. Christian took Dylan to bed. Dylan was drunk and he had room service and ended up throwing up on his hamburger. Christian put him to bed and tucked him in. He said, 'Dude, I'm gonna get the tray out,' and put the tray in the hallway. Flash forward to hours later, I am heavily influenced. Food is closed and there are no options available. I look and I'm like, 'That burger is not even touched. I'm just gonna bring that inside.' I ate the thing." Cena then told Noah that the next morning, he was informed by Christian and Hornswoggle that the tasty, much needed late night burger he ate wasn't so tasty after all. It was a riot of a story, and Cena told it in good spirits. December 13 will mark one year since Cena competed in his final in-ring match against "The Ring General" GUNTHER at Saturday Night's Main Event. Since that anniversary is drawing near, it appears there are working plans to execute the already announced "John Cena Classic" tournament. The date WWE is aiming to hold this inaugural tournament on is Saturday, December 12.

After a night of heavy drinking, Hornswoggle vomited on his room service hamburger, which Christian placed in the hallway after putting him to bed. Hours later a hungry Cena found the untouched-looking burger and ate it, only learning the truth from the pair the next morning.

title: Backstage Buzz: Billy Gunn Calls Out Modern Wrestlers for How They Handle Backstage Drama
raw_title: Billy Gunn Calls Out Modern Wrestlers for How They Handle Backstage Drama
summary_src: Billy Gunn thinks wrestlers today could do a much better job handling their problems backstage. While talking about the drama surrounding CM Punk’s time in AEW, Gunn compared it to his WWE days and basically said you don’t have to like somebody to get in the ring and do business with them.
body: Speaking to Inside The Ropes , Gunn said Vince McMahon was pretty good at keeping backstage issues under control. There were obviously people who didn’t get along, but Gunn remembers most wrestlers being able to put that aside when it was time to work. “They do, but nothing like that. Like, Vince had things under control really good. Like, there’s this couple — like, we all — like, I don’t have to like you to wrestle with you or to work with you. I don’t have to like you. I don’t have to do anything. I just have to do business. And mostly, 99.9% of the guys always did that, right?” Of course, there were still times when things got personal. Gunn said the difference was that those problems weren’t supposed to become everybody else’s problem too. If two wrestlers had serious heat, Gunn said they would be pulled into a room, the door would be shut and they’d deal with it privately. That’s also how Gunn says he handles things as a coach when he’s angry about something a wrestler has done. “There’ll be that every speck now and then where you just pull them into a room, you know? You pull them into a room, you shut the door. So, you don’t do it out in public, like — and I don’t do it in front of the boys. It’s just like if I have something bad to say about coaching and I’m about to lose my — I don’t do it in front of people. I take them somewhere where nobody else can hear it because it’s nobody else’s business.” The goal wasn’t to have an argument, walk away and stay mad at each other either. Gunn said if there was a problem, they were supposed to figure it out right there and make sure it was finished before they left the room. “You pull them into a room, you shut the door, and you go, ‘All right, here we go. What are we doing?’ Like, if you got a problem, we need to fix it now. We’ll fix it now so when we walk out the door, we don’t have a problem anymore. Right?” “And that’s how grown-ass people deal with it. But nowadays, we don’t, and that’s sad. But there’s going to be people that are going to do that, you know.” Gunn isn’t saying everybody in a wrestling locker room needs to love each other. His point is much simpler — hate each other if you want, but when there’s business to do, handle the personal stuff privately and get the job done. title: Lyra Valkyria’s X Account Appears Suspended as WWE Star’s Instagram Vanishes
raw_title: Lyra Valkyria’s X Account Appears Suspended as WWE Star’s Instagram Vanishes
summary_src: Something strange is going on with Lyra Valkyria’s social media accounts, and nobody seems to have an answer. The WWE Superstar’s X account now appears to be suspended, while her Instagram has completely vanished.
body: Valkyria’s X account, @Real_Valkyria, is no longer accessible, while her Instagram account, @real_valkyria, has also disappeared. It’s unclear whether Valkyria pulled the plug herself or something else happened, but neither WWE nor Valkyria has offered an explanation. And this isn’t something that just happened overnight. Fans first noticed Valkyria’s accounts were missing in late June. Some people started noticing the disappearance on June 28, 2026. Both accounts had seemingly vanished without warning, leaving fans wondering what was going on. Now, here’s where the timing gets suspicious. Just days earlier, Valkyria had completely snapped on Bayley during the June 22 episode of WWE RAW. After the two failed to capture the WWE Women’s Tag Team Championship from Paige and Brie Bella, Valkyria turned against her former partner and laid her out with the Nightwing. It was a shocking betrayal that officially sent Valkyria down a darker path on WWE television. Then, less than a week later, her social media accounts were gone. Coincidence? Maybe. But the timing certainly raises some questions. Some fans initially believed Valkyria had intentionally deactivated her accounts to match her new villainous WWE character. After all, disappearing from social media immediately after betraying one of the company’s biggest fan favorites would certainly fit the direction of her storyline. But there’s a catch. Nobody has confirmed that explanation, and there’s a pretty big difference between someone voluntarily deactivating an account and having it suspended by the platform. Meanwhile, Valkyria hasn’t disappeared from WWE television. She was still competing as recently as the October 14 edition of WWE Main Event, where she faced Sol Ruca in a match that also involved a reminder of her ongoing issues with Bayley. So while Valkyria is still doing her thing inside the ring, her online presence has been missing for nearly four months. And considering how active WWE Superstars typically are on social media, that’s a pretty noticeable absence. raw_title: Shelley Martinez Admits She Was Wrong About Maria Kanellis After Publicly Dragging Her Into Controversy
summary_src: Shelley Martinez had a LOT to say about Maria Kanellis, but now she’s admitting she got the whole thing wrong! The former WWE Superstar brought up old personal drama, questioned Kanellis’ past behavior, and helped turn a controversy involving Kelly Kelly into a much bigger story.
body: Well, that speculation didn’t exactly age well. Martinez revealed that after the episode went viral, several people within the wrestling business contacted her with information about the situation. And apparently, somebody finally gave her the detail she was missing before she started talking about Maria. “Amongst everyone texting me in the business, I found out who it was that that not Maria that Barbie was talking about and it wasn’t Maria.” That’s right. Maria wasn’t the woman Kelly Kelly had been talking about. After all that discussion about Kanellis and their personal history, Martinez was now walking back the very suspicion that helped kick off the controversy. And she didn’t even try to deny that she’d been wrong. “I was wrong. It wasn’t It wasn’t her. But I never even said for sure it was Maria. So get over it, people.” “So since then, finding out that she has apologized to Barbie, that Barbie helped her find her fertility doctor to help her have another kid And I looked, I did my research. I looked and Barbie does follow Maria.” “Now, if I knew that information before our last show, I wouldn’t have talked about the ex-boyfriend and all of that.” Martinez didn’t have the full picture, went into her personal history with Kanellis anyway, and then admitted that having the actual information would have changed what she said. That’s not exactly a ringing endorsement of how the original controversy was handled. “There were people, highprofile people, I’m not going to name names, highprofile people saying thank you for saying that. Thank you.” Martinez also insisted that she’s not trying to stay relevant or manufacture controversy for attention. She argued that her previous experiences in WWE and elsewhere give her firsthand knowledge about the people she discusses, and that being retired means she no longer has to worry about upsetting anyone who might affect her career. “I stand by what I say because people in the business liter literally thank me for saying what other people won’t cuz they’re scared.” And despite the incorrect speculation, Martinez made it clear she wasn’t backing down from her decision to discuss the controversy. “I don’t regret anything because I got my answers and I didn’t even have to talk to Maria. I got my answers and my closure and I didn’t even have to talk to her.” Martinez explained that she had carried resentment toward Kanellis for years and that the latest developments finally allowed her to move past those feelings. She said Maria had disrupted her peace on numerous occasions, but learning what actually happened helped her find the closure she’d been looking for. “Maria doesn’t affect me anymore. And I’m so glad to break the chains of Maria.” Steve Carrier Steve Carrier is the founder of Ringside News and has been reporting on pro wrestling since 1997. His stories have been featured on TMZ, Forbes, Bleacher Report, and more.

title: Backstage Buzz: Billy Gunn Opens Up On AEW Initially Had Very Different Plans for His In-Ring Career
raw_title: Billy Gunn Reveals AEW Initially Had Very Different Plans for His In-Ring Career
summary_src: Billy Gunn wasn’t supposed to spend nearly as much time wrestling in AEW as he eventually did. In fact, when he first signed with the company, his talent contract only called for 12 wrestling dates for the entire year.
body: Speaking to Inside The Ropes , Gunn explained that his original AEW role was mainly supposed to happen behind the scenes. He had separate talent and employee contracts, with most of his work centered around producing and coaching rather than getting back inside the ring every week. “Yeah. So, my contract, I had 12 dates a year. Like, I really wasn’t going to wrestle, but I told Tony, ‘If you need me to, I’ll do some here and there.’” “So, we put in — like, I still had a talent contract and an employee contract because I was mostly just producing, coaching and whatever else. And then the talent one was little because I was just going to, you know, if I even filled those dates.” That arrangement didn’t exactly go according to plan. Instead of occasionally throwing on his gear for one of those 12 dates, Gunn suddenly found himself being used much more regularly. “And then, lo and behold — oh, they cracked me out, and then I’m working both shows. I’m working all the time, about to fall apart.” Gunn went from somebody AEW expected to use sparingly in the ring to working across both shows while still handling his responsibilities behind the scenes. What started as a dozen potential wrestling dates quickly turned into a much bigger in-ring role than he originally signed up for. Considering how much Gunn eventually became part of AEW television, it’s pretty wild that wrestling was initially supposed to be such a small part of his job. His willingness to step in whenever Tony Khan needed him ended up turning those occasional appearances into a regular part of his AEW run. body: He said he got the ink following his time in New Japan Pro-Wrestling, with the promotion's Bullet Club. Rhodes explained that he wanted to get away from the faction's design with its guns. "I wanted to get away from that, no disrespect, I just wanted my own logo," he said. "I'll say it's a regret because of maybe the logo itself, because of its size and its placement, but it's been nothing but a career on an upwards trajectory ever since," Rhodes said.

summary_src: Wrestling is a genre full of winners and losers, and here are the big ones from AEW WrestleDream 2026.
body: So let's talk winners, let's talk losers. The great thing about AEW running marathon shows is that there's plenty of each. As always winners will not be literal, hell they might not even be people at all, and the same goes for the losers. Winners can lose, losers can win, and match stipulations get their flowers. AEW/Ricky Havlik I was a little skeptical of the Clockwork Carnage Match. It sounded like it would be a mess of nearfalls and eliminations to make up for the fact that all the real drama is in the last 5 minutes or so, but I am happy to be proven wrong. AEW only has so many stipulation matches that they can claim. A lot of their stipulations are modified versions of WWE, TNA, or WCW matches. AEW didn't invent Clockwork Carnage, that bit of trivia belongs to Pro Wrestling EVE, but by being the first to bring it to a global stage, it is now theirs. It's not reinventing the wheel, it's like a gauntlet eliminator match that turns into a multi-man Iron Man Match at the end, but it does feel perfect for the skillset of the AEW roster. Let's be honest, AEW is something of a promotion made entirely out of TNA's X-Division, and Clockwork Carnage is exactly the kind of highly-entertaining, highly-athletic nonsense that the X-Division guys were doing in the mid-2000s. It's just a perfect marriage of match and promotion. A home run for AEW, and a grand slam for Pro Wrestling EVE, who will be able to tout "the original" for as long as they run. AEW/Ricky Havlik I think Persephone is a tremendous in-ring talent. I also think that the AEW TBS Title Four-Way Match was a very solid match. It just lacked drama, and that feels like a crushingly regular thing with Persephone. It's hard to describe, but between the underwhelming nature of her competition, as well as the Britt Baker of it all, it feels like Persephone is in a placeholder situation. Like Thekla's world title reign, she is mainly champion so that AEW can get the proper pieces in place for whatever plans they have for the next champion. But unlike Thekla, she is not interrupting the show with chaotic promos and working with the word "b****" like Dutch Masters worked in oil and pigment. It feels like she is having great matches, while spinning her wheels narratively. The nature of her opponents doesn't provide the drama that could warrant a title reign of "good matches" and not much else. I am waiting for the other shoe to drop, and I am getting bored. AEW/Ricky Havlik The great thing about Clockwork Carnage is that it broke open the edges of the AEW main event scene. Speedball Mike Bailey, specifically, felt like they were elevated by their presence in the match. There were plenty of men in the match who have never been AEW World Champion, but they were the Kazicuka Okadas, Konosuke Takeshitas, and Adam Copelands of the world. Mike Bailey had some proving-themself to do, and prove themself he did. It's something wrestlers, promoters, and pundits talk about all the time, but very hard to pull off

title: Shingo Takagi Irks Wife Natsupoi By Praising Stephanie Vaquer
raw_title: Marital “Young Lion” Shingo Takagi Learns Hell Hath No Fury Like a Natsupoi Scorned by Naming WWE’s Stephanie Vaquer as His Favorite Female Wrestler
body: Marital “Young Lion” Shingo Takagi Learns Hell Hath No Fury Like a Natsupoi Scorned by Naming WWE’s Stephanie Vaquer as His Favorite Female Wrestler 3 hours ago Photo courtesy of meraWRESTLING X account Photo courtesy of meraWRESTLING X account New Japan Pro-Wrestling superstar Shingo Takagi is learning the hard way what the trials and tribulations of marriage is all about. Takagi is married to STARDOM superstar Natsupoi and the two are set to team up on Oct. 29th for the first time to take on Hirooki Goto & Yuna Mizumori. Takagi & Natsupoi announced their marriage earlier this year and recently, Takagi made a crucial mistake that has apparently cost him dearly. Both Takagi & Natsupoi were talking to reporters after a practice session when Takagi was asked about Natsupoi’s ability as a wrestler. Takagi began to speak when Natsupoi asked him who his favourite women’s wrestler was and Takagi wisely motioned to Natsupoi. They continued the heated conversation about Vaquer and a novice Takagi asked if they were done with the topic. Natsupoi assured him that she wasn’t done in the least bit. Takagi, to his credit, tried to make amends by praising Natsupoi’s ability as a wrestler but the damage had already been done and he had reached a point of no return. An angry Natsupoi then began complaining about the practice session they just had by telling Takagi that they only practiced his signature moves and she was the only one getting thrown around. Hoping for a bit of help, Takagi reminded Natsupoi that they were in the middle of a interview and motioned to the interviewer. The interviewer didn’t get hint that Takagi was desperately sending and suggested that he talk it out with Natsupoi. The interviewer received a subtle death stare from Takagi but still seemed clueless by suggesting Takagi apologize to his wife. Eventually, Natsupoi got up and told Takagi she wasn’t going home that evening then proceeded to leave. title: Results Recap: AEW WrestleDream 2026 , grades, awards: Will Ospreay survives Clockwork Carnage; Ilja Dragunov debuts

body: By the time Saturday's finale rolled around, you could've easily forgotten WrestleDream centered on the world title main event with its fancy new stipulation. That's because everything before it was that damn good. But make no mistake, Clockwork Carnage — and Ospreay — are here to stay. It was a multi-layered story that primarily focused on Ospreay entering first and attempting to defend his title in the stipulation match he created. Meanwhile, Adam Copeland is officially making the final push of his career to become a world champion . And boy, did he come close, as a final Spear to Kazuchika Okada would've given him the win until a literal last-second Ospreay Hidden Blade sealed it. This was the most car-crash match possible without a literal car crash match existing. (Don't get any ideas, Tony Khan). It's a double-edged sword — or blade, if you will. But all in all, Clockwork Carnage was arguably the most fun wrestling match of the year. I didn't say it was the best. It was, however, an absolute ripper of a time, and hopefully we see it again. Shortly before the main event, AEW revealed its recently teased new arrival: Ilja Dragunov. Only one championship changed hands at WrestleDream 2026, and that was the trios. Brodido and "Hangman" Adam Page are once again on top of the division after outlasting Swerve Strickland and The New Level in a fantastic best-of-3-falls match. Once again, the match was largely all about Page and Strickland's forever feud, which will surely cause the end of Strickland's alliance with New Level. But everyone played their parts to great effect, and it closes out the current chapter of things between Strickland and Page, while moving New Level in their inevitable tag-focused direction. Speaking of the tag division, it may be better than ever, which is feels stunning to say. It makes no sense that The Young Bucks are still able to go in the way they can, and they defeated the duo of Kyle Fletcher and Kevin Knight tonight to retain their belts. The match the world is waiting for now is the Bucks against New Level, but Knight and Fletcher sold multiple tickets for a potential win in what was a strong contender for tag match of the year. This pairing was destined to deliver, and they went above and beyond. What All Out lacked in pacing , WrestleDream made up for in spades. Only a match or two tonight felt like they took noticeably more time than the others. But collectively, WrestleDream hit you in the face like an unrelenting heatwave. It was just too hot to look away, and a home run on all fronts. AEW WrestleDream 2026 crown score: 👑 10/10 👑 Just think about this: Everyone loves surprises in wrestling. We've seen them executed to perfection numerous times in AEW, specifically. title: William Regal Urges Wrestlers To Sell Pins And Kickouts Better
raw_title: WWE's William Regal: Wrestlers Should Pay More Attention To Pin Attempts & Kick-Outs
summary_src: 42-year industry veteran William Regal offers valuable advice about wrestling pin attempts and kick-outs.
body: Such was the case this weekend as the 42-year industry veteran offered valuable advice about match pin attempts and kick-outs. "We are portraying trained pro fighters with instincts (even comedy bouts)," he wrote on X . "If you don't win you would make less money in the story we're telling. Every TV bout, if there's a pin, the cameras focus in. Please pin and kick out like your life and career depend on it. In story, it does." As an example of the kick-outs and pins he's looking for, Regal referenced a match between in-ring legends AJ Styles and Amazing Red from the early 2000s, in which both competitors aggressively applied every pin, with their opponent's shoulders both covered and stacked. Regal noted that every subsequent kickout was equally as forceful, almost as if "their life depended on it." 20 years later, he believes that art has since been lost. "Let's not insult the intelligence of our audience who are giving us their precious time," Regal continued. "In a fight scene in a movie (which is what wrestling is) we know the punches don't really hit but if we saw that we would eventually stop watching it. Your audience and fans deserve better. If you can't be uncomfortable for a few seconds being stacked up in a pin, maybe this isn't for you." I work for WWE but watch a lot of wrestling worldwide. This goes for all wrestlers in all companies. I have worked in Wrestling for 42 years. An observation. We are portraying trained pro fighters with instincts ( even comedy bouts). If you don't win you would make less money in... Regal himself spent multiple decades competing in the ring, with his official retirement match pitting him against Claudio Castagnoli (formerly WWE's Cesaro) in 2013. The former WWE Intercontinental Champion has remained involved in the business in a non-wrestling capacity since then.
summary: WWE veteran William Regal advised wrestlers to treat every pin attempt and kick-out with maximum intensity as if their career depended on it. He pointed to an early 2000s match between AJ Styles and Amazing Red as the ideal example where both men covered shoulders fully and exploded out with force. Regal stressed that this approach respects the audience's time and maintains the realism of the pro wrestling story.

llm_long: William Regal shared advice for wrestlers on how to better sell pin attempts and kickouts during matches. The longtime industry veteran emphasized that wrestlers are portraying trained professional fighters with instincts.

He stressed that in the story being told, failing to win would result in earning less money. Regal urged performers to treat every pin and kickout in television matches as if their life and career depended on it, especially since cameras focus closely on those moments.

As an example, Regal pointed to an early 2000s match between AJ Styles and Amazing Red. In that bout, both competitors applied pins aggressively by fully covering and stacking their opponent's shoulders.
Regal observed that each subsequent kickout in the match was delivered with equal force. He believes this approach to selling pins and kickouts has been lost over the past 20 years.

He encouraged wrestlers not to insult the intelligence of audiences who invest their time. Regal compared wrestling to fight scenes in movies, noting that visible lack of effort would cause viewers to stop watching.

Regal, who competed for multiple decades before retiring, made the comments after working in the business for 42 years. He has remained involved in wrestling in a non-wrestling role since his 2013 retirement match.

title: Bron Breakker Lands on His Neck During Scary Spot at WWE Live Event
raw_title: Bron Breakker Lands on His Neck During Scary Spot at WWE Live Event
summary_src: Bron Breakker had another really scary landing on his neck during a WWE live event, and the footage is tough to watch. Breakker somehow managed to finish the match afterwards, but right now there’s no word on whether he actually walked away without an injury.
body: The moment happened during WWE’s October 17 live event, where Breakker teamed with Bronson Reed and Austin Theory against Oba Femi, LA Knight and Penta. The babyface trio eventually won the match, but a clip involving Breakker and Knight has since started making the rounds online. Breakker was setting Knight up for his Frankensteiner from the top rope, something fans have seen him pull off plenty of times before. This time, however, Knight slipped out just as Breakker was jumping toward the turnbuckle, and everything went sideways from there. Breakker appeared to lose his footing on the turnbuckle and came crashing down in a really ugly way. He landed around his neck and upper-body area, and the referee immediately rushed over to check on him. Thankfully, Breakker was able to keep going and finish the match. That’s obviously a positive sign, but there’s currently no confirmation from WWE or Breakker about whether he was actually hurt during the spot. The footage is even harder to watch because this isn’t the first time Breakker has had a nasty landing on his neck. Back at Survivor Series: WarGames in November 2025, things went badly wrong during a Doomsday Device spot involving Cody Rhodes and CM Punk. Breakker didn’t get the full rotation and came down directly on his neck. Bryan Alvarez later described just how frightening it looked while discussing the match on Wrestling Observer Radio . Now Breakker has had another frightening close call less than a year later. The fact that he finished the October 17 match is encouraging, but until there’s an actual update on his condition, it’s probably too early to say he came out of this one completely fine. title: Jacy Jayne Cried During Priest's WrestleMania Cash-In
raw_title: Jacy Jayne Says She Cried Watching This WWE MITB Cash-In
body: "When Damian Priest cashed in at WrestleMania, I was in the audience," Jayne said. "Now, I know him and we're friends, and it's like really funny looking back on this. But, I actually cried. Just because I knew his story about being on the indies and how long it took him to get there. He was never like the 'first round draft pick,' so to say. So, for him to get the briefcase, A, was a big deal. And then B, to cash in at WrestleMania, like I could only imagine how he was feeling in that moment. When I heard the crowd erupt, it just made me emotional. There's something about genuine crowd reactions that makes me really, really emotional." While she didn't capture the briefcase in her first MITB attempt, Jayne had an impressive showing at the event in 2026. It would be Tiffany Stratton to ascend the ladder and grab the guaranteed title shot for the second time of her career.

She became emotional watching the moment due to her knowledge of his long journey from the independents and the genuine crowd reaction. Jayne had an impressive showing in the 2026 women's ladder match though she did not win the briefcase, which was retrieved by Tiffany Stratton for the second time in her career.

title: On the Record: Paige Collett Says Medical Marijuana Saved Her Life as She Fires Back at Critics
raw_title: Paige Collett Says Medical Marijuana Saved Her Life as She Fires Back at Critics
summary_src: Paige Collett is fed up with people treating her like some kind of drug addict just because she smokes weed. The JCW wrestler says marijuana is the reason she’s still able to chase her wrestling dreams, and she’s got a message for anyone judging her without knowing what she’s been through.
body: Collett took to Twitter on October 18 and went off on people who see her smoking and immediately assume she’s some kind of party girl. She says the reality couldn’t be further from the truth. She’s battling a chronic illness, and medical marijuana has been a lifesaver. “People see me smoking and judge me & typecast me! I’m a strong advocate for medical marijuana. It has saved my life and it lets me continue to pursue my wrestling dream.” And she’s not stopping there. Collett says she’s made the decision to stay away from ketamine infusions and opioids, but people still lump her in with others who use recreational drugs simply because they’ve seen her smoking around them. And the pain doesn’t just show up when she’s wrestling. Collett has previously opened up about how her condition affects physical intimacy , saying even something most people wouldn’t think twice about can leave her recovering for days. So when strangers see Collett smoking marijuana and decide she’s just out partying, she’s not exactly going to sit there and take it. As far as she’s concerned, weed has helped keep her wrestling career alive while she’s dealing with a condition that once took away her ability to walk. title: Contract News: Gillberg Claims Goldberg Had Contract Clause Blocking His WWE Merchandise
raw_title: Gillberg Claims Goldberg Had Contract Clause Blocking His WWE Merchandise
summary_src: Gillberg thinks WWE left some pretty obvious money on the table when it came to his parody of Goldberg. Not only did he never get the Goldberg vs.
body: Speaking on Developmentally Speaking , Gillberg talked about Goldberg’s apparent dislike of the parody character and wondered why WWE never released a battle pack featuring the two of them. Considering the entire Gillberg gimmick was built around mocking Goldberg, he couldn’t understand why WWE never cashed in on the obvious pairing. “They — I don’t know how they didn’t make a battle pack of Goldberg-Gillberg.” According to Gillberg, WWE eventually produced merchandise based around the Festival of Friendship but somehow left him out. He even claimed that an image featuring those involved in the segment didn’t include him. “I don’t understand. I don’t understand. I was on the Festival of Friends. They did the entire Festival of Friends — everybody on it but me. Even the picture, you know what I mean? But not me.” Gillberg then dropped a much more interesting explanation for why that might have happened. He claimed he’d heard that Goldberg actually had language in his contracts preventing WWE from giving Gillberg certain merchandise opportunities. “Because I heard that Goldberg had in his contracts that Gillberg gets nothing — no action figures, no video games, no nothing.” That’s Gillberg’s claim, and he didn’t say that he’d personally seen Goldberg’s contract or confirmed the language himself. Still, if what he heard was accurate, it would certainly explain why a character so closely connected to Goldberg never received the kind of merchandise treatment Gillberg expected. It’s also why Gillberg still seems confused about WWE never putting the two together in something as simple as a battle pack. More than two decades after the parody became part of WWE history, he still believes Goldberg and Gillberg merchandise practically sold itself. title: On the Record: Max Caster is stepping away from professional wrestling for “an extended period of time”
raw_title: Max Caster is stepping away from professional wrestling for “an extended period of time”
body: At TNA Bound for Glory 2026, former AEW star Max Caster made his TNA Wrestling debut in a losing effort to Moose. Caster stated during his pre-match rap promo, “I drop bombs. You don’t even have to fly to Riyadh.” The line was a reference to the recent Houthi missile/projectile attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. TNA apologized for what Caster said and noted that the company will no longer be working with him . After a match at the ACW event on Saturday, Caster stated the following about his future… “I don’t know if everybody here is aware of what happened with me this past week. If you don’t know, in the span of one day, I started a contract and ended a contract with TNA Wrestling. And I put out a statement. I addressed it. I apologized to a lot of people, but the one group I didn’t get to apologize to was all the fans. So, guys, I really appreciate the support. Everybody who’s reached out after this happened, thank you. A lot of people were excited to watch TNA for the first time. A lot of people were excited to come back to the product, and now a lot of people are disappointed that I’m not on the show. But you know what? Thank you, guys, here tonight at ACW, for welcoming me. And for that, I say I love you, and thank you. I don’t know what my next move is. I don’t know where I’ll be, but I will be stepping away from the ring for an extended period of time. Wow. So, I’m gonna go home, I’m gonna go to therapy, I’m gonna get it right so that the next time I’m in the ring, it feels like I’m at home, just like you guys made me feel here tonight. So finally, for the last time in a long time, you are looking live at the best wrestler alive. Thank you.” Max Caster appeared at tonight’s ACW show and once again addressed what happened with him and TNA. Says he’s headed to therapy and stepping away from wrestling for an extended period of time. pic.twitter.com/XDPZtyWNfV

title: Adriana Rizzo Breaks Silence on Wrestling Future Following WWE Release
raw_title: Adriana Rizzo Breaks Silence on Wrestling Future Following WWE Release
summary_src: Adriana Rizzo isn’t done with wrestling just because WWE decided to let her go. The former NXT star is already thinking about what’s next, but there’s one thing she needs to get through before she can really start shopping around.
body: Speaking with Pario Magazine , Rizzo was asked whether she still planned on pursuing wrestling following her WWE release . She revealed that she’s currently waiting out her 30-day period before she starts seriously looking at other opportunities. “I think, um, right now I’m still within my 30 days, so I haven’t — once I get past the 30 days, I’ll really kind of start looking into options and see what’s out there. So that’s — I’m just kind of waiting until those 30 days are up right now. Yeah.” So Rizzo isn’t announcing her retirement or walking away from wrestling. She’s basically waiting until she’s free to see who’s interested and what kind of opportunities are sitting out there for her. Her WWE exit came after a pretty unlucky run in NXT. Dave Meltzer previously reported on Wrestling Observer Radio that WWE saw something in Rizzo, but two straight knee injuries seriously hurt the momentum she had going . “And then she had two straight knee injuries, and that pretty much killed her.” The timing got even worse when Tony D’Angelo moved away from the gimmick Rizzo had been attached to. Once that happened, Meltzer said there wasn’t really an obvious spot left for her in the act. “And with that gimmick that. That left no room for her. And I guess they just made the decision that they didn’t think that she was going to make it.” Meltzer previously threw AEW and Ring of Honor out there as places that could potentially take a chance on Rizzo, but there’s been no indication that either promotion has actually made a move. Rizzo herself isn’t naming names yet either. For now, she’s simply counting down those 30 days before seeing who might want to talk. WWE may have pulled the plug on her NXT run, but Rizzo clearly isn’t ready to do the same with her wrestling career. title: On the Record: Austin Creed says he thought about joining AEW while still working for WWE
raw_title: Austin Creed says he thought about joining AEW while still working for WWE
body: While speaking with Phid McAwesome at PAX Australia, Austin Creed (formerly known as Xavier Woods) discussed whether he ever considered joining AEW while still working for WWE. Here is what Creed had to say… “Yeah, definitely. Just to experience another style. There’s definitely a very specific WWE style and a very specific AEW style. Just a different style, and I think that for a long time, being seen in that way, people forget. So, if you’ve been watching wrestling a long time, you know I came up in the X Division. So, this is what I was born to do, you know what I mean? It’s just refreshing to have the chance to move around like that again. And I think it’s great that there are two different styles. I think it’s great that people have options for what they want to watch and what they’re interested in. For me as a performer, it’s nice to be able to do something different from what I’ve been doing for a while. It’s a different kind of fulfillment, you know what I mean? And so, to be able to be at AEW and have these matches with people that, yes, we have history with some people, some history with others, or no history with others—we’re meeting them for the first time. And there are some people who watched us when they were growing up and wanted to be wrestlers. That’s great. You know, it’s crazy to think that I was always the young guy in the locker room, and now I’m definitely not. It’s been a really cool shift in just how how I’m able to look at wrestling now, and I’m really enjoying it.”
summary: The latest: while speaking with Phid McAwesome at PAX Australia, Austin Creed discussed whether he ever considered joining AEW while still working for WWE. There’s definitely a very specific WWE style and a very specific AEW style.

body: Many of my long-time readers have been asking “where have you been”, as my column volume has dropped off a bit. Well, for one, I write when I want… There’s no schedule for yours truly, as I just write when I’m feeling it… But, there’s some method to the madness as to why I took a few weeks off. No, it wasn’t for the 9/22/2026 column , as I’ve clearly followed that up with my 10/15/2026 column . I’ve been saying it for YEARS how dangerous putting on big events is within the Middle East. I’m not afraid of that topic. His death was officially ruled as bronchial asthma. If left undiagnosed or untreated, it is indeed lethal as asthma is inflammation of your airways. Now, here’s what I’m curious about… A Wellness Policy isn’t just about drug testing. In fact, it’s often a program offered by most corporation for insurance purposes as a means to help get costs down. WWE implemented one for drug testing specifically, following the death of Eddie Guerrero in late 2005 and then ramped up its seriousness during mid 2006 due to Chris Benoit’s downfall and then the online pharmacy stuff right afterward. To a normal company, it’s usually bloodwork and a physical examination. WWE’s Wellness Policy did both the examination and the drug testing, and in FACT, it saved MVP’s life when he was in the WWE and an examination found an unknown heart condition that he’s treated ever since. THIS is why ALL pro wrestlers in a corporate wrestling setting NEED TO BE INSURED and with that, required to have regular physical examinations. The physical activity of performing, along with maintaining your look, makes it essential to require your performers to be examined for any health reasons. Treat wrestlers like human beings and employees, not bulls going against a matador. They aren’t just “independent contractors”, and often times, you have to save people from themselves. There are MULTIPLE studies out there that show men, in particular, refuse to see a doctor. Just doing various Google searches of various studies shows that 50% of men refuse to do annual examinations, 65% of men will avoid going to the doctor unless they absolutely have to, and men are more unlikely to see a doctor versus women by a big margin of various polls (ranging from 33% to 50%, depending on the survey). I don’t know what happened to PAC. Was he diagnosed previously with asthma or not? Did he just forget to take his treatments? Did he forget his inhaler when an episode came up? I don’t know… BUT, if you have performers putting their bodies on the line, you should require regular examinations of the human beings you’re employing. We don’t have the full facts here, but I strongly implore both WWE and AEW to TAKE CARE OF YOUR WRESTLERS and PROTECT YOUR WRESTLERS FROM THEMSELVES. However, WWE implemented the serious Wellness Policy during 2006 and then later implemented a concussion protocol. That has SAVED LIVES.
