title: On the Record: Max Caster Announces Wrestling Hiatus After TNA Incident, Says He Plans To Seek Therapy
raw_title: Max Caster Announces Wrestling Hiatus After TNA Incident, Says He Plans To Seek Therapy
body: Max Caster announces he is stepping away from pro wrestling after TNA Bound For Glory incident Share on Twitter --> Max Caster has announced that he will be stepping away from professional wrestling for an extended period following his controversial departure from TNA Wrestling. Caster made his TNA debut at Slammiversary, answering an open challenge from Moose. However, his appearance drew controversy after he referenced the bombing in Riyadh during his pre-match rap. During a recent appearance at an ACW event, Caster addressed the situation, apologized to fans and reflected on his brief stint with the promotion. “In the span of one day, I started a contract and ended a contract with TNA Wrestling. I put out a statement , I addressed it and apologized to a lot of people, but the one group I didn’t get the apologize to is all the fans,” he said. “I really appreciate the support, everybody who has reached out after this happened. A lot of people were excited to watch TNA for the first time or come back to the product, and now a lot of people are disappointed that I’m not on the show.” Caster also thanked ACW for welcoming him before revealing that he intends to take an extended break from in-ring competition to focus on his personal well-being. “Thank you guys here at ACW for welcoming me,” he continued. “For that, I say, I love you and thank you. I don’t know what my next move is. I don’t know where I’ll be, but I will be stepping away from the ring for an extended period of time.” Caster concluded by revealing that he plans to seek therapy before eventually returning to wrestling. “I’m gonna go home, I’m gonna go to therapy, I’m gonna get it right so that the next time I’m in the ring it feels like I’m at home.” Caster did not provide a timetable for his return or indicate where he might wrestle next. Max Caster appeared at tonight’s ACW show and once again addressed what happened with him and TNA. llm_long: Will Ospreay defended the AEW World Heavyweight Championship in a Clockwork Carnage match at AEW WrestleDream 2026. The unique format was designed by Pro Wrestling EVE, with whom Ospreay has collaborated. Ospreay entered the bout early in his title reign following an emotional win over Kenny Omega at AEW All In 2026.

In Clockwork Carnage, wrestlers enter every three minutes until all eight participants are in the match. Any wrestler pinned or submitted before the final entrant arrives is eliminated. Once the last wrestler enters, the remaining competitors begin a 15-minute scoring period where each pinfall or submission counts as one fall.

Ospreay and Konosuke Takeshita opened the match at a fast pace. Takeshita executed a gorilla press from the top rope followed by a flying clothesline on Ospreay. The action continued with Takeshita delivering a dive to the outside onto Ospreay.

Mike Bailey entered wearing United Empire colors, though commentary noted that alliances do not apply in Clockwork Carnage. Takeshita eliminated Bailey and focused his attack on Ospreay. Ospreay and Bailey later showed a moment of solidarity with a United Empire high-five before Takeshita interrupted it.

Ricochet attempted to form a temporary alliance with Takeshita against the United Empire members. The partnership broke down when Ricochet tried to roll up Takeshita. Ricochet then hit a dive onto Ospreay on the outside before Takeshita dropped him with a headbutt.

Ospreay and Bailey delivered a double superplex to Takeshita, but Ospreay's attempt to steal the pin failed. Darby Allin entered using a skateboard, performing an ollie on Ricochet's back and setting up a table outside the ring. Kazuchika Okada's music played as the match continued.

title: Johnny Gargano's Inspiring WWE Journey
raw_title: Johnny Gargano
body: Johnny Gargano More Share Options More Share Options Share close facebook x threads email superstar stats Superstar Stats Johnny Gargano NXT Champion; NXT North American Champion; NXT Tag Team Champion; WWE Tag Team Champion Johnny Gargano’s journey is proof that with heart and determination, anything is possible in WWE. Known as Johnny Wrestling, Gargano has faced countless setbacks and heard “no” more times than he can count. Labeled too small to succeed and even rejected after a 2015 WWE tryout, the self-described “chubby kid from Cleveland” refused to give up on his dreams. From play-wrestling on mattresses to aspiring to be the next Shawn Michaels, Gargano’s rise is a testament to grit and passion. He first made waves in NXT as one-half of the iconic tag team #DIY with Tommaso Ciampa. Together, they elevated NXT’s tag division, delivering unforgettable matches and capturing the NXT Tag Team Title. After parting ways with The Blackheart, Gargano formed The Way — a tight-knit group including his wife Candice LeRae, Austin Theory and Indi Hartwell — showcasing his loyalty and leadership. Despite heartache, personal struggles and setbacks, Gargano always bounces back stronger. Gargano was turned away after a 2015 WWE tryout and was told he was too small to succeed. The Cleveland native continued pursuing his goal of becoming a top performer like Shawn Michaels.
In NXT he teamed with Tommaso Ciampa to form the duo known as #DIY. The pair won the NXT Tag Team titles and produced several memorable matches that strengthened the brand's tag division.

Gargano returned to WWE programming on August 22 2022 and immediately made an impact. After recovering from an injury in summer 2023 he reunited with Ciampa, and the revived #DIY went on to win the WWE Tag Team Championship.

title: Rumor Claims TNA Wrestling Planning Wyatt Sicks Reunion Soon?
raw_title: Rumor Claims TNA Wrestling Planning Wyatt Sicks Reunion Soon?
body: All five were let go after WrestleMania 42 in April, part of a round of cuts in which WWE and TKO released or declined to renew more than two dozen names. Kofi Kingston and Austin Creed were among them, as were the Motor City Machine Guns. All four of those wrestlers have since signed with AEW. The Wyatt Sicks went a different way. Their 90-day non-compete periods expired over the summer, and most of the group went straight to the independents rather than to a promotion. Joseph Sawyer, known in WWE as Joe Gacy, is the reigning GCW World Champion and has kept tagging with Samuel Shaw, formerly Dexter Lumis. Sawyer also worked a six-man tag for Maple Leaf Pro Wrestling on September 11 alongside Erick Redbeard, the former Erick Rowan, and AEW's Evil Uno. Sawyer and Shaw were WWE Tag Team Champions for nearly 200 days, taking the titles from Montez Ford and Angelo Dawkins in July 2025 and anchoring a SmackDown division that carried much of that summer. Their defenses included the Six Pack TLC match at SummerSlam 2025 at MetLife Stadium. Taylor Rotunda, who played Uncle Howdy, is the only member of the group who has not returned to the ring. Sawyer and Shaw alone would reshape the TNA tag division overnight. A team that held WWE's tag titles for two-thirds of a year and worked a SummerSlam stadium main card is a bigger signing than anything TNA has made in that division recently, and the two have stayed a team on the independents rather than drifting into singles work. They arrive ready to go. The name is the obstacle nobody can solve with money. WWE owns Wyatt Sicks, Uncle Howdy and everything attached to them, which is why all five are working under their own names or older ones. Whatever TNA builds cannot reference the character it is actually buying. title: Kevin Owens Explains NXT Gatineau Appearance
raw_title: Kevin Owens Explains Why He Said Yes To WWE NXT Live Event In Gatineau, Quebec
summary_src: Kevin Owens talks about his NXT live event return. On October 17, WWE held an NXT live event in Gatineau, Quebec, Canada.
body: This was Owens’ first match in an NXT ring since 2019. Following the match, Owens cut a promo for the fans explaining why he said yes to the show. The clip was posted online by a fan . With that said, another thing that really helped me say ‘yes’ when they asked me if I want to be a part of this show, was knowing that I get to share the ring with people that are shaping the future of what WWE will be. The four idiots we just beat – very talented idiots – but still, not the best attitude. These three, I just said the future; quite frankly, I think you’re really looking at the present. So for that, Tony, thank you. Kendall, thank you. Shiloh, thank you. It was an honor and a pleasure. Thank you guys so much.” Owens says it was Steve Carino who asked him to perform on the show, and he couldn’t say no to him. Steve, I can genuinely say, without a doubt, if you’re not familiar with his career, go back and watch. One of the greatest of all time. I met him in 2004. He took me under his wing, and without him, I am telling you, I would not be standing here right now. Tonight, or ever, I would have never had the career I had without him. So Steve, I’m not going to make you come out here, because I know you won’t want to, but you’re back there. I love you. Thank you. Anytime you need anything, I’m here. Anytime you guys need anything, I’m here. I’m at the Performance Center, you know it. Well, you guys can’t tell me, you don’t have my phone number… just know, if they ask me to be here for you guys, I’ll be here. Thank you.” If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.

summary_src: More TNA deals are coming up soon. According to a Fightful Select report, there are a number of contracts that are set to expire over the “next couple of months,” enough to where TNA President Carlos Silva held a meeting during a recent television taping.
body: “TNA President Carlos Silva spoke to talent and noted that the company would be working on getting a lot of these deals done in the coming weeks, around Bound For Glory,” the report reads. “He also noted that he wanted the company to be able to plan ahead creatively, and effectively held the meeting to let talent know that discussions regarding their contracts would be happening soon.” Fightful also reported that “a lot” of contracts are due in December. Bryan Alvarez notes that TNA holds a talent meeting before every single show, and the contract situatuon was something mentioned during one of those meetings. TNA’s most recent pay-per-view, Bound for Glory, was held last weekend. In the main event, Leon Slater became the youngest TNA Champion in history by defeating Nic Nemeth . Other highlights saw Indi Hartwell defeat Xia Brookside to win the TNA Knockouts title, Jason Hotch winning a four-way match to win back the International title, and Zoey Serrano & Shayna Baszler defeating Allie & Kiera Hogan to win the Knockouts Tag Team titles. title: Will Ospreay proud of trying new Clockwork Carnage at WrestleDream
raw_title: Will Ospreay says he’s proud of ‘daring to try’ Clockwork Carnage match at AEW WrestleDream 2026
summary_src: Will Ospreay comments following the Clockwork Carnage match at WrestleDream. In a social media post, he thanked fans for their response to the match that headlined Saturday’s AEW pay-per-view, saying he was proud of himself for trying something new.
body: In a social media post, he thanked fans for their response to the match that headlined Saturday’s AEW pay-per-view, saying he was proud of himself for trying something new. “Thank you all for watching #AEWWrestleDream & being part of Clockwork Carnage,” he wrote. “The fact a company like @AEW & @TonyKhan put faith in trying something that’s not been done before. Grateful for all the reviews for it, proud of myself for daring to try something new. All love guys.” The first-ever Clockwork Carnage match took place Saturday in Orlando , with Ospreay defending the AEW World Championship against Samoa Joe, Speedball Mike Bailey, Konosuke Takeshita, Darby Allin, Adam Copeland, Ricochet, and Kazuchika Okada. Bailey and Takeshita were eliminated before all eight competitors made it to the ring, eliminating them from the match. Towards the end of the second phase, the remaining six wrestlers all had two points except for Copeland, who had zero. The final few moments suddenly saw Copeland earn two points. He was preparing to go for a third when Ospreay took him out with the hidden blade, pinning him with just seconds to go and earning three points for the win . llm_long: Will Ospreay defended the AEW World Heavyweight Championship in a Clockwork Carnage match at AEW WrestleDream 2026. The unique format was designed by Pro Wrestling EVE, with whom Ospreay has collaborated. Ospreay entered the bout early in his title reign following an emotional win over Kenny Omega at AEW All In 2026.

In Clockwork Carnage, wrestlers enter every three minutes until all eight participants are in the match. Any wrestler pinned or submitted before the final entrant arrives is eliminated. Once the last wrestler enters, the remaining competitors begin a 15-minute scoring period where each pinfall or submission counts as one fall.

Ospreay and Konosuke Takeshita opened the match at a fast pace. Takeshita executed a gorilla press from the top rope followed by a flying clothesline on Ospreay. The action continued with Takeshita delivering a dive to the outside onto Ospreay.

Mike Bailey entered wearing United Empire colors, though commentary noted that alliances do not apply in Clockwork Carnage. Takeshita eliminated Bailey and focused his attack on Ospreay. Ospreay and Bailey later showed a moment of solidarity with a United Empire high-five before Takeshita interrupted it.

Ricochet attempted to form a temporary alliance with Takeshita against the United Empire members. The partnership broke down when Ricochet tried to roll up Takeshita. Ricochet then hit a dive onto Ospreay on the outside before Takeshita dropped him with a headbutt.

Ospreay and Bailey delivered a double superplex to Takeshita, but Ospreay's attempt to steal the pin failed. Darby Allin entered using a skateboard, performing an ollie on Ricochet's back and setting up a table outside the ring. Kazuchika Okada's music played as the match continued.

title: Joe Hendry Names Favorite WWE Entrance Themes
raw_title: Joe Hendry Reveals Favorite WWE Entrances Themes From Past & Present
body: "Okay, so [my] favorite theme of all time is The Rock's Hollywood theme," Hendry said. "That just, like, as a fan, it gave me goosebumps watching that. I think some really iconic ones? Obviously, Steve Austin's glass smash, and 'The Game' by Motorhead is iconic as well." Hendry then segued into a discussion about current WWE themes, a polarizing subject within the WWE fanbase due to the overall negative reception to themes created by WWE's inhouse composer Def Rebel . Hendry was careful to avoid any criticism of modern WWE themes, insisting that there were plenty of strong ones. In terms of ones he thinks that work, Hendry believes they feature a certain quality, with Trick Williams' theme song having that in abundance. "On the current roster, there are some great songs," Hendry said. "I think ultimately songs that are about crowd interaction [work best], so I think they did a really great job with Trick's song. There's so many good ones."

title: On the Record: ‘Toni Storm Tapes’ Found By Content Creator At AEW WrestleDream
raw_title: ‘Toni Storm Tapes’ Found By Content Creator At AEW WrestleDream
body: It looks like the Toni Storm mystery has taken a new direction, with tapes of the AEW star ‘discovered’ at AEW WrestleDream. As noted , Storm was written off TV back in March by way of a backstage attack. She hasn’t been seen on AEW TV since. Flash-forward to Sunday, when content creator Astrid Pizarro posted to Twitter with an image of a cassette tape with lipstick and the message “Play Me.” Pizarro summarized the tapes in a series of posts to Twitter, noting that Renee Paquette narrated the tapes that arrived in Jacksonville at AEW offices last Wednesday with no return address containing five cassettes. The summary of the tapes seem to be Storm giving affirmations and speaking with different people. Paquette responded to the tweet thread, giving it validity. You can see the full text of the posts below: Since March 18,2026 no one has seen or heard from Toni. So last Wednesday, a package arrived at the AEW office in Jacksonville, Florida/ Brown paper package tied up with string, no return address, inside 5 analog cassettes.” “The cassettes are from an indeterminate past, meticulously labeled. It was long rumored had Toni had a recording device inside her purse. She recorded every conversation, meeting and moment and now the rumors are [true]. These are the Toni Storm Tapes” “1st tape is labeled mundanities, inside into the every day of the timeless one. Opening track is named: Morning mantra. Someone is yawning to start, they say ‘there it is.’ Rustling heard and ‘there she is.’ Toni says I look like a dried apple carving” ‘I face the day with resentment and scorn. My mind is a mess, my heart is in shambles and my body is barely holding it together like an overstuff garbage bag but damn it, I am timeless.’ She spits, ‘okay let’s start the day.’ Renee returns, the next track is titled ‘talking to Chauncey? title: On the Record: Nikki Bella Says She’s Single But “Not for Sale”
raw_title: Nikki Bella Says She’s Single But “Not for Sale”
summary_src: Nikki Bella may be single, but that doesn’t mean she’s looking for someone to start shopping around for her next boyfriend. The WWE Hall of Famer made that hilariously clear after Brie Bella announced her relationship status and immediately tried to play matchmaker.
body: Speaking on The Nikki & Brie Show , the sisters were talking with Gillie and Wallo about some of the predictable pickup lines they’ve heard because of their wrestling careers. When the conversation turned to whether either Bella had actually been interested in someone who tried the classic “Do you want to wrestle?” approach, Brie pointed out that Nikki still hasn’t met that person. That was all Brie needed before announcing that her sister was available and asking whether their guests knew anybody. Nikki immediately pumped the brakes on that idea. She might be single, but she definitely wasn’t asking Brie to start taking applications on her behalf. The timing made the exchange even funnier considering what had happened to the sisters the previous night. Nikki and Brie had already revealed that a man repeatedly approached them during dinner at their hotel, despite security stepping in several times. Brie joked that Nikki was the one who could give the guy a chance since she’s the single twin. “That’s why she was on the dumb shit last night. She was like, ‘Go ahead. You got a chance with her.’” Nikki wanted absolutely no part of that suggestion. Being single was one thing, but that particular guy definitely wasn’t making the cut. “Ew. Try — sick. Not that one. And that’s what bothered me about her — is she immediately saw who the single twin was.” Apparently, the man had chosen to sit next to Nikki during the encounter, which made her wonder how he’d figured out which sister was single: “So he sat next to me.” Nikki also admitted that she might initially entertain someone who approaches her, but that doesn’t mean they’re getting unlimited time to make an impression. Once somebody crosses a line, she’s perfectly comfortable shutting the whole thing down. “No, that’s crazy. That’s crazy. And I should’ve been like, ‘Yeah,’ but I’m also the first one to, like, tell someone, like, ‘Bye,’ or, like, be also, like, very confrontational too. Like, I don’t care. Like, I’ll entertain, and then I’ll be like, ‘Go now.’ You know what I mean? Which is so rude. I just wanna, like, just nip it from the beginning.” So yes, Nikki is single, but Brie probably shouldn’t start running a matchmaking service just yet. Nikki’s “not for sale” response made it pretty clear that being available doesn’t mean she’s looking for just anybody. title: Bayley Makes Surprise Appearance at Big Time Wrestling’s 30th Anniversary Show
raw_title: Bayley Makes Surprise Appearance at Big Time Wrestling’s 30th Anniversary Show
summary_src: Bayley went back to where her wrestling journey started, and the moment clearly hit her harder than she expected. The WWE star returned to Big Time Wrestling for its 30th anniversary show on October 18 and ended the night fighting back tears as the crowd welcomed her home.
body: Bayley wasn’t originally there to wrestle, but she still found her way into the action. She became the impromptu special guest referee for Aaron Solo’s match against Starboy Charlie and ended up playing a pretty important role in the finish. Things got messy when Solo tried to use his championship belt against Charlie. Bayley wasn’t having any of it and stopped Solo from using the title, giving Charlie the opening he needed to turn things around. Bayley grabbed the microphone as fans started chanting “Welcome back” at her. The reaction clearly got to her, and she admitted she was trying her best not to start crying in front of everybody. “I get too emotional — I don’t wanna cry in front of you guys. Thank all of you for coming out tonight. This is a very, very special show tonight.” There was a pretty good reason the night meant so much to Bayley. Long before WWE fans knew her by that name, Big Time Wrestling was one of the places where her career first started taking shape. Bayley’s first recorded wrestling appearance came for BTW on September 19, 2008, in Newark, California. Wrestling as Davina Rose, she teamed with Shane Ballard in a losing effort against Melissa Coates and Shannon Ballard. Nearly two decades later, Bayley got to walk back into the promotion as one of WWE’s biggest names and hear the same local crowd welcome her home. She didn’t need a match of her own to make the return special, as getting emotional in the ring showed just how much coming back to BTW still meant to her. raw_title: Mysterious Toni Storm Tapes Surface at AEW WrestleDream With Clues About Her Disappearance
summary_src: Toni Storm has been missing from AEW television since March, but somebody just dropped a pretty bizarre clue about her whereabouts — and it came on a cassette tape handed to a fan at WrestleDream.
body: The mystery started at AEW WrestleDream on October 17, 2026 , when content creator Astrid Pizarro was handed a package by someone she didn’t identify. Inside was a cassette marked “Toni Storm Tapes,” wrapped in paper stamped “confidential” with instructions to “play me.” The really interesting part? It was labeled “one out of five.” Pizarro said she was the only person in her area who received one, and she has no clue where the other four ended up. “I was handed out the tape at WrestleDream by somebody. I opened it, it just said ‘play me.’ Thankfully my dad and my brother have a cassette player, so I was able to play it today. I was the only one in my area that got it, and it says one out of five. I don’t know who the other four people are.” Pizarro eventually uploaded the audio to YouTube, revealing that Renee Paquette narrates the recording. According to the storyline, nobody has seen or heard from Storm since March 18, 2026, but a mysterious package recently arrived at AEW headquarters in Jacksonville containing five cassette tapes with no return address. And apparently, Storm had been secretly recording just about everything. “It was long rumored that Toni had a recording device inside her purse capturing every conversation, every meeting, every moment. Well, now those rumors are true. These are the Toni Storm tapes.” The first cassette, titled “Mundanities,” gives fans a look at Storm’s daily routine, and it’s exactly the kind of insanity you’d expect from the Timeless One. One recording features her delivering a morning motivational speech that sounds more like she’s preparing to ruin somebody’s day. “I am capable, strong, and ready to make the day my mistress. Today, I choose misery, conflict, and hostility in all that I do. I exude fragility, pettiness, and an unfillable void to everyone I see.” “I face the day with resentment and scorn. My mind is a mess. My heart is in shambles. And my body is barely holding it together like an overstuffed garbage bag. But damn it, I am timeless.” Another recording features Storm talking to her 12-year-old cocker spaniel, Chanty. What begins with her calling him a good boy quickly turns into an absolutely unhinged lecture about who’s in charge. “Now, you listen to me. I own you. I created you, and I can end you. You are nothing without me. You worship the ground I walk on, or I will make your life a living hell.” There’s also a recording of Storm giving wrestling students career advice, which apparently includes one very important fashion requirement. “Lesson number four, if you want to make it in this business, you’ve got to get yourself a cool hat.” Another track, titled “Cinema,” features audio from the disastrous production of Storm’s unreleased movie, “Toni, Toni, Toni.” But one detail really sticks out. title: Former WWE EVOLVE Star Veronica West Explains Why She Dropped Fallyn Grey Ring Name
raw_title: Former WWE EVOLVE Star Veronica West Explains Why She Dropped Fallyn Grey Ring Name
summary_src: Veronica West is clearing up why she ditched the Fallyn Grey name after leaving WWE, and it turns out she had no interest in going back to her old identity. The former WWE EVOLVE star says she’s tired of the comparisons, tired of people getting her name wrong, and ready to do things her own ...
body: West took to Twitter on October 19 after fans kept asking why she wasn’t using Fallyn Grey anymore. She explained that Fallyn was the character she created when she first broke into wrestling, and she spent years building that identity on the independent scene. But everything changed when she signed with WWE ID and became Veronica Haven. “Fallyn Grey was who I was when I first started prowrestling. She was the blueprint I crafted, and I spent years building that name on the independent scene. It was a character and an identity I poured so much of myself into. When I signed with WWE ID, I became Veronica Haven and had to conform to what was needed of me creatively. I wasn’t able to continue using that name after I was released.” “However, I didn’t want to go back to Fallyn Grey because of the constant mispronunciations and comparisons to other wrestlers. I needed a fresh start and a name that I could truly make my own.” West also pointed out that there’s something pretty fitting about all this. Her fallen angel character has always been about losing everything and fighting to rebuild, and that’s essentially what she’s doing after her WWE departure. “My character’s backstory has always been that of losing everything and starting from nothing. Loss, uncertainty, and persistence has always been the common theme. And thanks to Fallyn, I don’t have to completely start from nothing this time. 🫀” So that’s the end of Fallyn Grey and Veronica Haven, at least for now. West has already had to reinvent herself more than once, and this time she wants to be the one calling the shots. WWE may have been one chapter of her career, but she’s making it clear that the story isn’t over just because that door closed. title: U.S. State Department Issues New Middle East Travel Warning Ahead of WWE Crown Jewel
raw_title: U.S. State Department Issues New Middle East Travel Warning Ahead of WWE Crown Jewel
summary_src: WWE just got another reason to be nervous about Crown Jewel in Saudi Arabia. The U.S.
body: The warning comes as WWE continues preparing for Crown Jewel on November 7, despite serious concerns about travel into Saudi Arabia. King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh showed signs of resuming operations on October 18 after being shut down for more than a week following deadly attacks . However, getting everyone into the country safely remains a major question. Now the State Department’s official TravelGov account has issued a warning urging Americans in the Middle East to stay on high alert, specifically pointing to attacks by Iranian-backed Houthi forces against Saudi Arabia. The warning goes on to address the attacks that have already caused major problems for Saudi Arabia’s airports and other infrastructure. “Americans currently in the Middle East should exercise heightened vigilance due to the complex security environment. Be aware of potential flight cancellations, airspace closures, and travel disruptions.” “Iranian-supported Houthis have engaged in hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including attacks on civilian airports and other critical infrastructure resulting in civilian casualties and severe travel disruptions. The hostilities have the potential to escalate rapidly beyond that immediate area.” That’s a pretty serious concern for WWE, considering the company needs to transport its wrestlers, production crew and equipment into Riyadh for Crown Jewel. Even if some commercial flights have resumed, that doesn’t mean international travel is anywhere close to normal. The State Department also urged Americans traveling to or from the Middle East to monitor airport operations and prepare backup plans. It warned that Iran and groups supporting the country could target additional American interests overseas, including U.S. businesses and institutions. And this isn’t just a general warning with no connection to Saudi Arabia. The State Department currently has the country under a Level 3 travel advisory , telling Americans to reconsider travel because of armed conflict, terrorism and the threat of drone and missile attacks. As Ringside News previously covered , the repeated attacks on Riyadh’s airport have raised serious concerns about whether WWE can safely run Crown Jewel as scheduled. Saudi Arabia has also considered canceling additional Riyadh Season events . There’s also a major financial issue hanging over the situation. It was recently indicated that WWE’s parent company, TKO, has faced additional pressure to keep its Saudi Arabia events on schedule following public assurances from Saudi entertainment official Turki Alalshikh about Canelo Alvarez’s upcoming fight in Riyadh. WWE also has a backup venue in the United States available if Crown Jewel cannot take place in Saudi Arabia. However, no relocation has been announced, and the company is still moving forward with preparations for November 7. title: Nikki and Brie Bella Harassed By Man Who Tried Getting Into Their Hotel Room

summary_src: Nikki and Brie Bella were just trying to enjoy dinner when some random guy decided to make their night a living hell — and things got downright creepy when they learned he allegedly tried getting into their hotel room.
body: The WWE Hall of Famers spilled the details on The Nikki & Brie Show , revealing that a man repeatedly approached their table while they were eating at their hotel’s restaurant. Security had to step in multiple times, but the guy just kept coming back with a new excuse to talk to them. First, he tried impressing the sisters by bragging about how rich and important he was. When that didn’t work, he switched things up and started talking about identical twins. “But no, the good thing is the restaurant, they were aware. So the security would immediately come up and ask him to leave. And this — I think he might’ve been, like, a regular — and so they were trying to be very calm with him at first. But he would have, like, another story just to sit down. Like, first story was, like, how much money he had and who he was and whatever — ‘I’m a hot shot.’ And then the second one, he’s like, ‘Hey, so, you know, I spoke — was it to a scientist or something?’ And he’s like, ‘You wanna know something crazy about identical twins?’” That’s when dinner took a seriously disgusting turn. The man claimed he had an identical twin brother who had died, then started bragging about the size of his penis compared to his late brother’s. “He knows we’re identical twins. But what he said about it was like, ‘Did you know that one has a big d ** and one has a micro penis?’ He said ‘c k,’ by the way. He told you that. He said, ‘Big ‘c k.’ He goes, ‘So I am the one with the big ‘c**k.’”* “So then he was like, ‘Who do you think has the micro c ** and the big c***?’ And I was like, ‘This is when he needs to go — kicked out.’”* Security escorted the man away, but he STILL wasn’t finished. He eventually returned with another story, this time claiming he was a cancer survivor and inviting the sisters to a cancer event. And when that failed to impress them, he apparently figured a stack of cash might do the trick. “And then he’s, ‘You guys wanna go to a cancer event with me?’ And we’re like — the security guy’s like, ‘Leave them alone, boy.’ And then he went like this — he’s sitting and he pulls out a bunch of cash and he’s got tons of hundreds, trying to show us, flash us. And I’m like… corny, corny, corny.” But the most disturbing part of the encounter didn’t come until later. According to the sisters, they found out the man had allegedly been trying to make his way upstairs to their hotel room. “He was nuts. We found out later he was trying to get up to our room.” That’s a whole different situation from some obnoxious guy interrupting dinner. The sisters were eating at the same hotel where they were staying, and once their guests realized that, one immediately warned them not to do it again because it was dangerous. Nikki also said the man’s behavior reminded her of American Psycho , comparing his unsettling demeanor to a serial killer. “You had to see how he did it too. summary_src: Channing “Stacks” Lorenzo suffered a nasty injury at a WWE NXT live event, but there’s finally some encouraging news after the wrestler was stretchered out of the arena and taken to the hospital.
body: The scary incident happened during the October 16 NXT house show in Sudbury, Ontario, where Stacks teamed with Charlie Dempsey, Lexis King and Uriah Connors against Tony D’Angelo, Tavion Heights, Shiloh Hill and Shawn Spears. Things went wrong when Stacks took a back body drop over the top rope and crashed onto the floor, forcing WWE to stop the match . Medical personnel rushed to check on Lorenzo before placing him on a stretcher and taking him out of the arena. Bryan Alvarez of the Wrestling Observer later confirmed that Stacks had been transported to a nearby hospital , while Dave Meltzer noted that there were concerns he may have suffered a concussion. “Thank you for coming out tonight. Unfortunately things happen in this ring that are unexpected. You’ve heard us say 1000 times we’re one big family in WWE. You all are included and are a part of our family. When something serious such as this takes place it’s not easy. I’m sorry we had to end the night like this. From the bottom of my heart, thank you all for coming out tonight.” “My boys alive and well!! We can’t be stopped, last of a dying breed! Thanks for checkin on em, I got his ass.” Stacks’ injury turned what was supposed to be another routine NXT live event into a frightening situation, but at least fans have gotten some encouraging news since he was taken to the hospital. Whether he needs additional recovery time remains to be seen, and WWE will have to wait until he’s medically cleared before bringing him back into action. title: Paige Collett Drops Steamy Photos to Celebrate 56 Days Without Sugar
raw_title: Paige Collett Drops Steamy Photos to Celebrate 56 Days Without Sugar
summary_src: Paige Collett is showing off a little skin for a cause, and the JCW wrestler has a pretty good reason to celebrate. She’s officially gone 56 days without sugar, and she’s using some revealing new photos to bring attention to her ongoing battle with chronic illness.
body: On October 19, Collett took to Twitter and shared two provocative photos of herself posing in black lace underwear, including one in black and white. But this wasn’t just about getting attention. She used the post to celebrate her progress with cutting sugar from her diet while spreading awareness about Complex Regional Pain Syndrome, or CRPS. The photos come just one day after Collett fired back at people judging her for smoking medical marijuana . She explained that cannabis has played a major role in helping her manage chronic pain and continue pursuing her wrestling career, despite strangers assuming she’s simply out partying. “People see me smoking and judge me & typecast me! I’m a strong advocate for medical marijuana. It has saved my life and it lets me continue to pursue my wrestling dream.” Collett’s health struggles have been anything but easy. As Ringside News previously covered , she says a wrestling bump during training under WWE Hall of Famer Rikishi triggered the condition, eventually leaving her dependent on a wheelchair. She spent years searching for answers before fighting her way back to walking and wrestling. She’s also opened up about how CRPS affects her personal life , explaining that even physical intimacy can leave her dealing with days of pain and recovery. Now Collett is trying another approach to managing her health, and she’s clearly proud of sticking with it for 56 days. Whether cutting sugar will continue helping her symptoms remains to be seen, but she’s using the milestone to get people talking about CRPS while giving her followers something else to look at. Collett has already spent years fighting to get her life and wrestling career back, so she’s not taking the small victories for granted. And if posting a few steamy photos gets more eyes on a condition she’s been battling for years, she apparently has no problem putting that attention to good use. raw_title: Drew McIntyre Admits Going Off Script on WWE TV Has Gotten Him in Trouble With Triple H
summary_src: Drew McIntyre isn’t afraid to throw WWE’s creative plans out the window when he thinks something isn’t working — even if it means getting an earful from Triple H backstage.
body: McIntyre explained that WWE’s creative team works closely with talent to develop storylines, with Triple H overseeing the overall direction. However, he believes wrestlers who understand their characters should have a major say in how those stories are told. “These days, it’s very much a collaboration and has been for a few years now with myself personally anyway and generally across the board. If you know your character, you can work with the writers, etc., and get the character into the story. But it’s very important to me to make sure the creative matches what I’ve got going on in my head. Like the writers, the creative team, Triple H leading the creative team, they kind of set out, here’s the story, here’s what we’re thinking, here’s who we’re thinking you’re going to work with and this is where we’d like to get to.” Drew said that while WWE might have a destination in mind, the process of getting there is something he helps shape every week. He also made it clear that nobody needs to tell him what Drew McIntyre would say because, well, he’s Drew McIntyre. “Then it goes week to week. Like how we get there, that’s kind of a collaboration. Like when I go out there and I’ve got an interview in the microphone, I’m not getting handed a piece of paper that says here’s what you’re saying. Here’s all the words you’re saying because that’s what Drew McIntyre would say. Because my response, which I’ve said in real life, is no, you wouldn’t. What do you mean? I’m Drew McIntyre. I know what I would say.” McIntyre explained that he’ll go back and forth with WWE’s writers to make sure everything sounds believable. If he doesn’t believe what he’s saying, he doesn’t expect the audience to buy it either. “So, we have to go back and forth about what we want in the paper, where we’re going next, and make sure it’s in line with what’s in my head. Because if I don’t believe it, sure as hell, the fans are not going to believe it. They can see in your eyes, even if they don’t know or they can’t articulate it subconsciously, they’re like, you feel it. I don’t believe this and I have to believe it. So, they believe it. So, we very much work together every step of the way to create, you know, the storylines of where we’re going and make sure we’re getting the right emotional reaction.” But here’s where things get interesting. McIntyre admitted that even after WWE’s creative team agrees on a plan, he sometimes changes everything in front of the live audience. Depending on how Triple H feels about those decisions, Drew either gets congratulated backstage or finds himself in trouble. “Then on top of that, you’re in front of a live crowd. Sometimes they don’t react to the stuff on the paper and I’m very much the big ad-libber and sometimes it gets me a big slap on the wrist when I get to the back or a high five like good move out there.” And apparently, dealing with an angry Triple H isn’t exactly a pleasant experience. body: McIntyre claimed he actively avoids Punk backstage and doesn’t particularly enjoy being around him. That’s when he took a pretty wild shot at what would happen if they ever stopped being professional. “But also, we have to be professional and not pan each other’s heads. When I say we pan each other’s heads, I would murder him. You see him in UFC? Would look like that if it got real in there.” “Oh, for real life? I don’t care how many jiu-jitsu guys that tell me like, ‘Yeah, I’m MMA bros.’ Did you fight for the UFC? No, shut up. I said, ‘I will crush you. I’m giant and Scottish and many fights happen.'” McIntyre then joked about how people approach professional wrestlers and ask whether they would use wrestling moves in an actual fight. He made it clear that wouldn’t be his approach. “Guys are like, ‘Hey man, I’m going to — you’re going to chokeslam me? You got a tombstone?’ I was like, ‘No, I’m going to punch [you].’ I say the C word with a thick Scottish accent. Oh, Jesus. He’s a psycho. Yeah, I am. Don’t push me.” Of course, this isn’t the first time McIntyre has made his feelings about Punk known. As Ringside News previously covered, Drew admitted that his issues with Punk were personal , explaining that their genuine frustrations helped make their 2024 rivalry work so well. He admitted there were periods when the wear and tear of his career started catching up with him, but those days appear to be behind him. “As long as I enjoy it, I guess. As long as the fans are enjoying what I do. I can’t imagine slowing down. Like I say, I’ve never felt as physically good. According to Drew, even his trainer was surprised by how much his movement had improved compared to his last stretch in WWE. “And my trainer was there and he’s been watching me and coming to shows the past year, year plus. And he’s like, ‘The way you’re moving in the ring.’ I was wrestling barefoot as well, rolling around all over the place. He was like, ‘You were not moving like this before. title: Drew McIntyre Mocks CM Punk’s Body Transformation With Brutal Physique Insult
raw_title: Drew McIntyre Mocks CM Punk’s Body Transformation With Brutal Physique Insult
summary_src: Drew McIntyre just can’t help himself when it comes to CM Punk. Even when the Scottish Warrior tries to give his longtime rival a compliment, he somehow finds a way to turn it into an insult — and this time, Punk’s physique was the target.
body: That’s when CM Punk’s name came up. McIntyre admitted he’s genuinely surprised Punk is still wrestling at 48 years old and even acknowledged that his rival has improved his physical condition. For a brief moment, it almost sounded like Drew was going to say something nice about Punk. That didn’t last long. “I’ve still got a few more years in the wrestling first and like you know I’m amazed Punk’s still going. There’s one thing I can compliment him on. He’s 48. He’s still going. And he got himself in better shape.” McIntyre immediately made sure nobody confused that compliment with actual praise. He clarified that Punk was only in better shape compared to how he looked previously, before delivering a pretty nasty assessment of his rival’s physique. “I mean, better shape for him. Let’s not go crazy now. He doesn’t look like me. He’s just better shape for him. So skinny, so fat at the same time. Before now, he just got in all right shape.” But Drew wasn’t finished. He then mocked fans who have praised Punk’s body transformation, suggesting people are getting carried away with how much his rival has improved. “Everyone’s like, ‘Have you seen the changes? He looks so good.’ I’m like, remember, we’re WWE. Like he’s not walking to Mr. Olympia. He’s like if he walks on to Mr. Bloody Chicago, the local area that he lives in stage, never mind Mr. Olympia.” “Yeah, I hear that a lot. It’s just not intentionally funny. I just tell the truth.” So while Punk has been getting attention for improving his physique, McIntyre apparently thinks the comparisons should stop right there. Drew might be willing to admit Punk looks better than he used to, but he clearly isn’t about to put his rival in the same category as himself. Their WWE rivalry may have ended inside Hell in a Cell, but McIntyre is still taking every opportunity to get one more shot in — even if it’s about Punk’s body. title: Andrade Recalls Origin Of His Pants-Off Routine In AEW
raw_title: Andrade El Idolo Didn't Realize Fans Were Chanting For Him To Take His Pants Off At First
summary_src: Andrade El Idolo has become one of the most popular stars in AEW, and it all started when he began to take his pants off. Andrade removing his bottoms has become commonplace in AEW, but even he was confused by the chant at first. Speaking to Renee Paquette on Close Up, Andrade gave the origin…
body: Andrade El Idolo has become one of the most popular stars in AEW, and it all started when he began to take his pants off. Andrade removing his bottoms has become commonplace in AEW, but even he was confused by the chant at first. Speaking to Renee Paquette on Close Up , Andrade gave the origin story of taking his pants off. “I love wrestling and I respect the ring. In the ring, I like to show who I am. I know I’m a good wrestler. One moment, I was beating some wrestler, and the people started saying something, but I didn’t understand it. I asked the ref, ‘What are the people saying?’ ‘The people are saying to take your pants off.’ ‘What?’ It was weird because it’s usually ‘Tables! This is awesome!’ But people saying ‘take your pants,’ I don’t understand. I’m in there, I’m beating him, I’m heel. ‘Maybe they want more punches,’ but they continued (to chant for me to take my pants off). I go over to ref Aubrey, ‘What did they finally say?’ ‘Take your pants off.’ ‘What? No.’ ‘Yeah, they want your pants off.’ Okay, you want the pants off. I take my belt off, my zipper down, and the people go crazy. Okay, I’ll take my pants off. I always have trunks to cover me because something can happen with the pants; they can rip. This is why I always wear trunks, not because I was prepared. One time I didn’t have trunks; I had boxers. People started that chant, so I took my pants off, and people [cheers]. ‘I am the heel.’ The people chant, ‘Take your pants off,’ So, I took my pants off,” he recalled. Andrade successfully defended the AEW National Championship against Tommaso Ciampa at AEW WrestleDream. He initially did not understand the crowd's reaction and had to ask the referee what they were saying. Once he realized the chant, Andrade obliged by taking off his belt and unzipping, which has since become a regular part of his act and helped boost his popularity in AEW.

title: Results Recap: WWE SmackDown , grades (Sept. 4): CM Punk retains; is Johnny Gargano leaving WWE?
raw_title: WWE SmackDown results, grades (Sept. 4): CM Punk retains; is Johnny Gargano leaving WWE?
body: OK, some ranting needs to be done off the top here because WWE has created an insane mess in its world title scene, and the overbooking is atrocious. With Sami Zayn, Gunther, Kevin Owens and Finn Balor all emerging to play a part in the finish of tonight's match, that's how we got to Gargano taking the loss. On a positive note, I like what's being created here with Punk continuously defending his title with interference or shenanigans. That can lead to something good, whether for a heel turn or in his immediate future feuds. Will it? I don't have faith, but the potential is there. The absolute worst part of all this is that Zayn is getting a handout title shot next week despite ruining both the most recent title match and No. 1 contender match. You know, the exact same booking that led to his title win against Cody Rhodes and Gunther in June — the last time Zayn won a match . Booking doesn't get any lazier than this. How are we supposed to care? And why should we, when Zayn has immediate enemies in Gunther, Owens and Balor who will surely ruin his match? Or at least, they should . WWE has created a scenario where the Punk vs. Zayn rematch would be booked improperly if none of those three plays a role in the finish. That's where we're at. I like that all three went after Zayn to start the night, but that has to continue if there's even a shred of logic or continuity to be had anywhere here. The easy solution for WWE to make it clear before next week's match that suspensions or some kind of punishment would be dealt in the case of interference. That doesn't make Zayn's title shot any more excusable, but it's a fix for the rest of the issues around this. Anyway, as for the Gargano match itself, it was very good. What would you expect out of a pairing between him and Punk in Gargano's hometown of Cleveland? Johnny Wrestling's literal rise to his feet was overdue and arguably should've happened when Zayn briefly held gold. But this was a nice spot for it. In the end, we may have seen the last of the former NXT staple in WWE, as he addressed the crowd in what felt like a goodbye after the show went off the air. It's amazing what Randy Orton and Cody Rhodes can do without a completely random celebrity interjection, isn't it? (No. No, it's not at all. It's what we knew these two were capable of — and should have delivered — ahead of the biggest event of the year.) At least we're getting it at all, but this feud simply can't end on Sunday in Atlanta. It's too good. Running joke. What's going on with Blake Monroe has become a literal joke. Two weeks in a row, she and Giulia fight — while geared up this time — only not to wrestle. At least they're getting some airtime, I guess. But this is just silly now. Celebrity Night's Main Event. Lil Yachty made a music video for his Baron Corbin match this weekend. I would ask who this is for, but the answer is obviously the TKO overlords. Poor Trick Williams is being kept from audiences for this. (Please don't) fight

title: Cody Rhodes Picks Favorite Dusty Promo, Bans AI Voice
raw_title: Cody Rhodes Names His Favorite Dusty Rhodes Promo, Vows ‘No AI Dusty’ In WWE
body: Cody Rhodes recently named his favorite Dusty Rhodes promo and said that there will never be an AI Dusty Rhodes voice in WWE. Dusty Rhodes is one of the most influential promo guy in wrestling history and has a number of famous, top-tier promos. His most famous is the “Hard Times” promo, which has crossed into mainstream culture and was recently used in a Zach Bryan song. Rhodes spoke on Last Mean about his father’s promos and why “Hard Times” isn’t in fact his favorite. He also said that there is a rule in WWE: no Dusty Rhodes AI voice. You can see the highlights below: “Well, he loved Billy Graham. Not the wrestler Billy Graham. Pastor Billy Graham. He loved Martin Luther King Jr. He grew up in the Southern Baptist church. The church he went to majority was all Black. And Thunderbolt Patterson, a famous, famous wrestler who — later in life, I think they’ve seen how great he was and what a [trendsetter] — Dad stole a great deal from Thunderbolt, stole a great deal from Bob Dylan. Michael Hayes is very similar. They’d find these things that they liked and weave them into the promo.” “I can tell you that a lot of people always want to quote ‘Hard Times.’ And I just — ‘Hard Times’ to me was cool, but I’d actually seen it before. Because he cut a similar one on Oie Anderson in the Georgia Championship Wrestling situation pre — again, they were playing without cable at the time. summary_src: October 19 2003 was the date of WWE No Mercy that year, and the main event was Brock Lesnar vs The Undertaker in a Biker Chain WWE Championship match. body: October 19 2003 was the date of WWE No Mercy that year, and the main event was Brock Lesnar vs The Undertaker in a Biker Chain WWE Championship match. Our own Dave Meltzer would describe it as a match that “dragged,” with one of the bigger being that the chain gimmick didn’t even really come into play until nearer the end. Here is what Dave had to say about Brock Lesnar vs The Undertaker at WWE No Mercy 2003: “Lesnar power bombed his way out of a triangle. Lesnar hit an F-5, but Undertaker got his foot on the ropes. Lesnar went to the top, but Undertaker choke slammed him off the top. Undertaker finally went for the chain, but Nunzio climbed up to stop him. Nunzio managed to get the chain and take a bump to the floor. At this point, Chuck Palumbo and Johnny Stamboli hit the ring, but Undertaker laid them out and cleaned house on them fast. Undertaker gave Lesnar the last ride, and then did pretty spectacular running dive over the top onto Palumbo & Stamboli. Undertaker came into the ring and got the chain, but Vince came out and shoved Undertaker, who crotched himself on the ropes. This gave Lesnar time to get the chain and he KO’d Undertaker with one punch and got the pin. **” Jake Jeremy Jake Jeremy is the Head of Audience Development at F4WOnline, having previously worked as a Combat Sports, Gaming and Pro Wrestling writer, successful Editor in Chief and Sports Coordinator. He has more than ten years of experience covering mixed martial arts, pro wrestling, football and gaming across a number of publications, starting at SEScoops in 2012. He previously also worked for PROGRESS Wrestling as Head of Media as well as working on the social channels of the company.

title: Drew McIntyre Calls Out WWE Wrestlers Who Can’t Improvise During Matches
raw_title: Drew McIntyre Calls Out WWE Wrestlers Who Can’t Improvise During Matches
summary_src: Drew McIntyre has a problem with wrestlers who need every second of their matches planned out — and he’s not keeping quiet about it.
body: McIntyre believes experienced wrestlers should already know how to work a match without needing every move planned in advance. He explained that the live crowd should dictate how a match unfolds, not some predetermined sequence that might have worked in another city. “Unless it’s a stunt practice stunts, but when it comes to the matches like you should know what you’re doing. We could talk about it a bit. You got 10 minutes, you got 15 minutes, you got 20 minutes. Go out there and listen to the crowd wrestle. Like I can’t stand when people plan stuff from beginning to end because you don’t know how the crowd’s going to react.” Drew then explained why that approach drives him crazy. Just because something worked in one city doesn’t mean another audience will react the same way, and wrestlers who refuse to adjust are setting themselves up for a disaster. “If you plan out this choreographed match, you walk out there and the crowd are just sitting on their hands. They’re like, ‘Huh?’ But they liked it in Chicago last week. You’re not Chicago. Different crowds like different things.” Things got even more interesting when the host asked what happens when wrestlers don’t get the reaction they expected. According to McIntyre, that’s where some talent expose themselves because they haven’t learned how to improvise. Drew said he’s experienced situations where he tries to change direction in the middle of a match, only for the other wrestler to freeze because they weren’t prepared for anything outside the original plan. “Yeah. I mean, they’ve not learned how to improvise in the moment. And sometimes, like, a lot of people are good at listening, but some people panic and it’s not fun if you’re in live TV and somebody panics and you’re talking to them like, ‘Hey, this ain’t working. We’re going to go this direction now.’ And they kind of freeze up and that’s when things look choppy.” “Not choppy in the good way. I like if it looks kind of makes it look real. If it’s kind of choppy and you get really physical with each other, but if things start messing up in an obvious way, it is not good. If there’s a miscommunication or somebody trying to tell the other person, let’s go this direction and they’re not quite ready.” But Drew also pointed to a bigger issue within WWE. The company doesn’t run nearly as many non-televised live events as it used to, which means younger wrestlers have fewer opportunities to practice their craft in front of actual audiences. “And I mean, things are different now. We don’t have as many non-televised shows now as we used to where people kind of practice game. And there is more now. People are getting their reps in. Um, and the talent are finding their feet, especially the younger talent.” That issue is something WWE management has already been addressing. As Ringside News previously covered, Triple H and Nick Khan explained why WWE was bringing back more house shows , with younger wrestlers needing additional in-ring experience being
summary: McIntyre believes experienced wrestlers should already know how to work a match without needing every move planned in advance. Just because something worked in one city doesn’t mean another audience will react the same way.

title: Solo Sikoa parties with rival Carmelo Hayes at wedding
raw_title: WWE’s Solo Sikoa breaks character as life of party at Carmelo Hayes’ wedding
body: While they are on-screen rivals, WWE star Solo Sikoa was going hard at Carmelo Hayes and Kelani Jordan's wedding over the weekend. A video from the reception has gone viral from the reception. Hayes appears to have his arm around him as they're dancing in the middle of a circle. The Bloodline member appeared to be the life of the party. Of course, this is iconic, considering that Sikoa and Hayes' last interaction in WWE programming was violent. During the Oct. 12, 2026, edition of Monday Night RAW, Hayes joined Royce Keys' 946 faction, attacking Bloodline members Sikoa, Jey Uso, and Jimmy Uso. Hayes and Jordan tied the knot on Saturday, Oct. 17, 2026. They got engaged on Tuesday, July 1, 2025, before getting married the following October. They are both two of WWE's top rising stars. Hayes just joined 946, and he is a former United States Champion. During his time in NXT, he won the North American Championship and was the final Cruiserweight Champion. Additionally, he won the NXT Championship in April 2023 at Stand & Deliver, beating Bron Breakker to win the title. Hayes held the title for 182 days before losing it to Ilja Dragunov. His wife, meanwhile, joined WWE a year after him in 2022. She made her NXT debut in October 2022 before making her on-screen debut in June 2023 at Gold Rush. She became the inaugural Women's North American Champion in a six-woman ladder match at NXT Battleground in June 2024. She beat Kendal Grey at Heatwave on Aug. 30 to win the NXT Women's Championship for the first time. She has also worked in Total Nonstop Action (TNA), winning the Knockouts World Championship in September 2025, before losing it to Léi Yǐng Lee. While she hasn't made her main roster debut yet, Jordan competed in the 2026 Royal Rumble.

The pair had just been involved in a violent brawl on the October 12 edition of Monday Night Raw when Hayes joined the 946 faction and attacked Sikoa along with Jey and Jimmy Uso.

raw_title: AJ Styles Explains Why Avery Styles Signed With TNA Wrestling
body: Avery Styles, the son of AJ Styles, is barely two months into his wrestling career, and he’s already signed with TNA Wrestling. Avery has competed for various independent promotions, including GCW, during his brief career. Speaking on the AJ Styles Show , AJ explained why Avery has now joined TNA. “He’s going to do independents. He’s definitely doing TNA. TNA gets him the reps he needs on television. You need these reps on television because you have to hit times. You have a certain time limit before the break and after. I’m a stickler of ‘hit your time. You’re a professional. Do your job.’ Being at TNA will help him hit his times,” he said. Avery has yet to compete in a televised match for TNA Wrestling. body: AEW WrestleDream took an unexpected turn as mysterious cassette tapes attributed to Toni Storm surfaced at the pay-per-view, offering a bizarre and unsettling glimpse into the former AEW Women’s World Champion’s world. Paquette proceeded to highlight each track with the next one being about Storm’s 12-year-old cocker spaniel, Chanty. “Oh, Chanty. That’s a good boy, Chanty. Who’s a good Chanty? Take a chance. Take a chance, Chanty. Oh, what a beautiful boy. Now, you listen to me. I own you. I created you, and I can end you. You are nothing without me. You worship the ground I walk on, or I will make your life a living hell. When company comes over, they’re here to see me, not you.It’s not a time for your little tricks or performances. It’s not amateur hour with Chantsy. It’s my time. You will greet them. You will wait till I make one witty remark, and then Luther will escort you down to the basement to eat your rubbish. Otherwise, you have one job and one job only. To f*ck. You are a hunting machine and I want you to scour this damn neighborhood making onto anything that moves because mama is in the mood to sell and I can make a pretty good penny off of whatever half freak hamster you manage to knock up. Call it something exotic like a ham dog. You hear me? You worthless wanted beast. Okay, Chanty, let’s go for a walk.” The tape features a couple more tracks titled ‘Seminar’, where Storm shares her wisdom with wrestling students. “Lesson number four, if you want to make it in this business, you’ve got to get yourself a cool hat.” Paquette introduced Track 4, titled “Cinema,” describing it as “chronicling the failed production of her self-funded, unreleased major motion picture.” The final track was labelled “Death,” with Paquette concluding the recording by stating, “These are the Toni Storm Tapes.” Storm’s last AEW appearance was on March 18 when she was found bloodied on the floor backstage . body: Kyle Fletcher shares that he tries to watch every single matches he participates in back to take feedback and apply it to himself. Fletcher has been one of the top rising talents in AEW over the past couple of years, and has developed into one of the top in ring competitors not only in AEW but in the world of pro wrestling. title: WWE Should Break Up Judgment Day Now
raw_title: Why Now is The Time For WWE to End The Judgment Day Faction Once and For All
body: A case can even be made that the mere existence of the faction is doing more to hinder than help everyone still in it. That's a strange statement to make when two of the members currently hold gold and the group gets more screen time than almost anyone on Raw most weeks, but that's exactly why it's time for WWE to call it quits with them. They're overexposed, uninteresting and stuck in the same stories. Liv Morgan and Stephanie Vaquer have been at odds over the Women's World Championship since February, Dominik Mysterio has been feuding with his father Rey Mysterio on and off for four years, and the rest of Judgment Day are treading water. Raw could use a significant shakeup in the worst way, and breaking up Judgment Day once and for all could be what benefits both the brand and everyone associated with the stable. The incarnation of the stable with Ripley, Damian Priest, Dominik Mysterio, Finn Bálor and JD McDonagh was peak Judgment Day, but it had also run its course. Ripley and Priest had already begun to embrace the audience as babyfaces, so removing them from their ranks gave the group a fresh coat of paint. It also put Morgan in a prominent position on Raw for the first time in her career, a spot she has shined in ever since. Her stock skyrocketed, and within a matter of months, she was one of the most popular performers—male or female—in the entire company. As such, it made sense for her to win the Women's World Championship at WrestleMania 42. Unfortunately, the fallout left a lot to be desired, and she went until SummerSlam four months later without defending her title. Stephanie Vaquer regaining the gold in her native Chile was a fun moment, but all it ended up being was just that: a moment. She won back the belt at Money in the Bank not long after, and currently, there aren't any obvious challengers waiting in the wings. She's stuck doing the same shtick and being bogged down by Judgment Day isn't doing her or the title any favors. That would have allowed Perez to subtly tease tension with Morgan and plant the seeds for an eventual (successful) cash-in on her. Perez and Morgan weren't exactly on the same page in the wake of WrestleMania 42, but their dissension was quickly forgotten about and never acknowledged again. Perez was the perfect addition to Judgment Day in 2025. She had just been called up to the main roster from NXT and the group served as a vehicle to introduce her to the audience in an organic way, not to mention she instantly had chemistry with everyone already in the faction. Morgan vs. Perez being the ultimate endgame is acceptable, but it shouldn't be taking this long to get there. The Bloodline have obviously been a focal point of the flagship show this year, along with The 946 as part of their ongoing rivalry with the Roman Reigns-led group. The Vision, for some reason, still have a presence on the program as well and remain relevant largely thanks to Bron Breakker and Bronson Reed. That has automatically made The J

Breaking up the group could provide a much-needed shakeup for the brand and fresh opportunities for everyone involved.

llm.headline: This Day in Wrestling History: October 19
llm.summary: On October 19, multiple title changes took place across several promotions including Fred Blassie winning the NWA Southern Heavyweight Title, Johnny Valentine capturing the NWF World Heavyweight Title, Bobby Shane taking the NWA Florida Television Title, Carlos Colon regaining the WWC Universal Heavyweight Title, and Hector Guerrero & Dr. D claiming the AWA World Tag Team Titles. The date also marks the passing of Mike Graham, the on-screen Vince McMahon versus Stephanie McMahon match, Kurt Angle's induction into the TNA Hall of Fame, and the debut of Celebrity Championship Wrestling. Keiji Mutoh & Masahiro Chono defeated Kensuke Sasaki & Kazuo Yamazaki to win the IWGP Tag Team Titles.

llm_long: On October 19 in wrestling history, several title changes took place across various promotions. Fred Blassie defeated Wild Bull Curry to capture the NWA Southern Heavyweight Title for the fourth time in 1956.

In 1972, Johnny Valentine beat Abdullah The Butcher to win the National Wrestling Federation World Heavyweight Title in Cleveland, Ohio. On the same date that year, Bobby Shane defeated Tim Woods in Tampa, Florida, to claim the NWA Florida Television Title for the second time.

Carlos Colon defeated Abdullah The Butcher in San Juan, Puerto Rico, in 1985 to win the WWC Universal Heavyweight Title for the fourth time after the belt had been held up from a prior match between them. In 1987, Hector Guerrero and Dr. D defeated Jerry Lawler and Bill Dundee to take the AWA World Tag Team Title in Memphis, Tennessee.

Keiji Mutoh and Masahiro Chono defeated Kensuke Sasaki and Kazuo Yamazaki to win the IWGP Tag Team Title in Kobe, Japan, in 1997. That same day, Atsushi Onita and Kintaro Kanemura beat Hisakatsu Oya and Mr. Gannosuke for the FMW World Brass Knuckles Tag Team Title in Sendai, Japan.

In 2001, Vader and 2 Cold Scorpio became the inaugural Pro Wrestling Noah Global Honored Crown Tag Team Champions by defeating Jun Akiyama and Akitoshi Saito in a tournament final in Yokohama, Japan. On the same card, Tatsuhito Takaiwa defeated Yoshinobu Kanemaru to win the Pro Wrestling Noah Global Honored Crown Junior Heavyweight Title.

Also in 2001, Road Dogg defeated Jeff Jarrett to become the first World Wrestling All-Stars World Heavyweight Champion in Perth, Australia. Black Warrior defeated Negro Casas to win CMLL's Legend Of The Silver Mask tournament that year as well.

title: Billy Gunn Calls Triple H's 2019 AEW Jab A Dick Move
raw_title: Billy Gunn Says Triple H's Shot At AEW At 2019 WWE Hall Of Fame Was 'A Dick Move' That Only Hurt Him
summary_src: D-Generation X was inducted into the WWE Hall of Fame in 2019, with Triple H, Road Dogg, Sean Waltman, Billy Gunn, Shawn Michaels, and Chyna all going into the Hall. Gunn was already working for AEW at the time of their induction, though AEW had yet to run a show when the ceremony took place.…
body: D-Generation X was inducted into the WWE Hall of Fame in 2019, with Triple H, Road Dogg, Sean Waltman, Billy Gunn, Shawn Michaels, and Chyna all going into the Hall. During the ceremony, fans chanted “AEW” while Gunn and DX were on stage. Triple H responded that Vince McMahon would buy that “pissant company” just to fire Gunn again. Speaking to Kenny McIntosh on Inside The Ropes , Gunn reflected on the incident, saying, “I knew it was coming. I kind of knew they were going to do something AEW because it was hot at the time and I was there and they were all wondering how I got to go there, and that’s because Tony Khan was super cool. I went, asked, and he said ‘100%. Of course you can. I would never hold you back from that.’ I didn’t know what they were gonna do, but I knew they were going to do something. I also knew that if they were, Hunter was going to have something to say. Once I set myself up for that, I just let it go. The only one that got hurt out of that whole deal was him. I don’t want to say it, but it was a dick move. It was kind of trying to save face, and you didn’t need to because it’s going to happen. It’s the wrestling business. It’s what we do. They like to stir up shit. When you have somebody in another company, which was me, they can’t believe it, and then you see me, they have to do it. It’s like an unwritten thing in a book. ‘If another guy is in another company, we have to say or do something.’ They started chanting it, and you get a response from the guy leading the company.” Vince McMahon has not purchased AEW and is no longer involved with WWE after a lawsuit was filed against him by former employee Janel Grant, who accused Vince of sexual assault and sex trafficking. body: Kyle Fletcher doesn’t think that his current character is too far off what he imagined it would be as a kid dreaming of being a wrestler. Fletcher is one of the top wrestlers under the age of 30 in the world of professional wrestling, and continues to grow as a performer in All Elite Wrestling. Now, he has spoken about his current character. While speaking to Westwood One Sports Night in a new interview, Kyle Fletcher was asked if his wrestling character is what he imagined it would be as a kid. “That’s actually a very interesting question. I don’t think it’s too far… off what I pictured when I was a kid, just because, I think the person that I am, and I think about this quite a lot, I think the person that I am today, not just in wrestling, but in general, is an accumulation of all the things that I loved as a kid growing up, an accumulation of- I looked at just people and wrestlers in whatever I loved, tattoos. I loved collecting Pokemon cards. I loved, music. I loved wrestling and I look at myself and I go, ‘oh, that’s pretty much everything that I am.’ I loved dressing nice. I loved pink, and it’s like, everything is, everything makes sense. You know, I’m just the same, the same person, just a larger version, I guess. So yeah, I can’t say it’s too far away from what I pictured because if you gave 10-year-old Kyle SmackDown vs. Raw 2009 or whatever, I’d probably create exactly what you see in front of me in Create-A-Wrestler.” If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.

Fenix and Gable share a mutual respect after their superb title match last week. Page vs. Fenix or Gable seems likely. MJF who is one of biggest names and his absence from major shows often attracts attention. After WrestleDream 2026, he took to X, formerly known as Twitter, to criticize several stars. MJF called Will Ospreay a fake champion and accused him of cheating. He also mocked Ilja Dragunov’s debut and mentioned Nick Wayne’s victories over Chris Jericho. He wrote , “Wrestledream synopsis. Fake world champion defends fake world championship in match with opponents who are way better than him and cheats to win. Russian/german loser debuts by pretending he’s a “composer”…cool. Nick Wayne beat Jericho twice ? MJF has continued questioning the legitimacy of Kenny Omega’s AEW World Championship reign. He previously claimed he had Omega defeated and remains the company’s real champion. MJF blames Will Ospreay for interfering in their match. He believes that interference allowed Omega to win the title. MJF also claims Ospreay cost him his AEW All In main event spot. body: Kyle Fletcher recalls a bump that made him feel like he was pissing blood and made his ‘insides fall out of his butthole.’ Fletcher has been a wrestler on the AEW roster who has never been afraid of taking bumps that cause the normal person to wince, including bumps from tops of cages and to the outside of the ring in ugly landings. Now, he has named one that rests at the top of the list. While speaking to Westwood One Sports Night in a recent interview, Kyle Fletcher was asked about the nastiest bump he has taken in pro wrestling, recalling a bump he took while facing Mark Briscoe. “The one that comes to mind when I’ve been asked this question before is I took a suplex… from the top of the guard rail to the floor from Mark Briscoe, and you can see, you can, people have like put up the clip and you can see in my face, it literally- I landed directly on my tailbone and it felt like my insides exploded. It felt like… I don’t know how graphic I want to get. It felt like I was pissing blood and my insides fell out my butthole at the same time it was it was the weirdest feeling ever, and I literally just had to go, give me a minute, and I had to make sure that I was okay. I lay there for probably like 30 seconds going, ‘can I keep wrestling?’ Then I went, yeah, I think I can keep wrestling, and then I got up and kept wrestling.” If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.

Fletcher landed directly on his tailbone, causing an intense sensation that he described as his insides exploding.

The impact left Fletcher feeling as though he was pissing blood while his insides fell out of his butthole simultaneously. He required about 30 seconds lying on the mat to assess whether he could continue wrestling. After determining he was able to proceed, Fletcher got up and finished the match.

title: Match Made: What is the Crown Jewel Championship? How the champion-vs-champion match works and every past winner
raw_title: What is the Crown Jewel Championship? How the champion-vs-champion match works and every past winner
summary_src: The WWE men’s and women’s Crown Jewel Championships were introduced in 2024 and, at least in storyline, should be the most prestigious titles in the company. For anyone who skipped the last two Crown Jewel PLEs, the championships are only awarded once a year and are never defended.
body: The WWE men’s and women’s Crown Jewel Championships were introduced in 2024 and, at least in storyline, should be the most prestigious titles in the company. For anyone who skipped the last two Crown Jewel PLEs, the championships are only awarded once a year and are never defended. WWE’s men’s and women’s world champions from Raw and SmackDown face each other with neither of their regular titles on the line. Instead, the winner receives an enormous Crown Jewel Championship belt, carries it around for a few hours, and then it goes back on display at the WWE Experience in Riyadh. Many fans have not warmed to the idea of the Crown Jewel titles, but if professional wrestling were a real sport where winners and losers weren’t predetermined, these would arguably be the most important championships in the industry. In theory, the matches determine who the ultimate champion in WWE actually is. The Crown Jewel Championship at least kicks that concept up a notch. The first Crown Jewel champions were determined on November 2, 2024 in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Cody Rhodes won the inaugural men’s Crown Jewel Championship by defeating World Heavyweight Champion Gunther. Liv Morgan became the inaugural women’s Crown Jewel Champion that same night, defeating WWE Women’s Champion Nia Jax. World Heavyweight Champion Seth Rollins won the men’s Crown Jewel Championship by defeating WWE Champion and 2024 Crown Jewel winner Rhodes. On the women’s side, Stephanie Vaquer defeated Tiffany Stratton to win the Crown Jewel Championship. The two Crown Jewel Championship matches are already set. Women’s World Champion Liv Morgan will face WWE Women’s Champion Chelsea Green, while World Heavyweight Champion Roman Reigns will face WWE Champion Sami Zayn. Morgan has an opportunity to become the first wrestler to win the Crown Jewel Championship twice after capturing the inaugural women’s title in 2024. Neither Reigns nor Zayn has previously competed in a Crown Jewel Championship match. Zayn would also figure to have plenty of his ride-or-die fans in attendance should the event ultimately take place in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. There are still plenty of questions surrounding this year’s Crown Jewel event , including where exactly it will take place. One thing that does appear set to continue, however, is the tradition introduced in 2024: WWE’s top men’s and women’s champions facing each other to determine who leaves as that year’s Crown Jewel Champion.
