llm.headline: WWE Crown Jewel Championship explained
llm.summary: WWE introduced men's and women's Crown Jewel Championships in 2024 as annual awards determined at the Crown Jewel PLE. The Raw and SmackDown world champions from each gender compete in a champion-versus-champion match with their regular titles not at stake, and the victor receives a large belt to carry briefly before it returns to display at the WWE Experience in Riyadh. The concept is presented in storyline as crowning the ultimate champion in the company, with the first winners decided on November 2, 2024 in Saudi Arabia when Cody Rhodes captured the inaugural men's title.

llm_long: The WWE men's and women's Crown Jewel Championships were introduced in 2024. In storyline, they are presented as the most prestigious titles in the company.
The championships are awarded once a year and are never defended. Men's and women's world champions from Raw and SmackDown compete against each other with their regular titles not on the line.
The winner of each match receives a large Crown Jewel Championship belt. The belt is carried for a few hours before being placed on display at the WWE Experience in Riyadh.

The first Crown Jewel champions were crowned on November 2, 2024 in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Cody Rhodes defeated Gunther to become the inaugural men's champion, while Liv Morgan defeated Nia Jax to become the inaugural women's champion.
Seth Rollins later won the men's Crown Jewel Championship by defeating Cody Rhodes. Stephanie Vaquer won the women's Crown Jewel Championship by defeating Tiffany Stratton.

This year's Crown Jewel Championship matches are set with Women's World Champion Liv Morgan facing WWE Women's Champion Chelsea Green. World Heavyweight Champion Roman Reigns will face WWE Champion Sami Zayn.

title: Bron Breakker falls awkwardly at Hawaii live event
raw_title: Bron Breakker takes nasty fall at WWE live event
summary_src: Bron Breakker took a nasty fall at a WWE live event. During WWE’s tour in Honolulu, Hawaii, Breakker and The Vision teamed up against LA Knight, Penta and Oba Femi.
body: During WWE’s tour in Honolulu, Hawaii, Breakker and The Vision teamed up against LA Knight, Penta and Oba Femi. In the bout, Breakker attempted his signature Frankensteiner on Knight who dodged the move, causing Breakker to lose his balance and fall backwards, seemingly striking his head on the mat. The referee immediately checked on Breakker, who continued the match and proceeded to finish it. title: Injury Update: Jade Cargill Opens Up On Past Neck Injury Left Her Struggling to Lift Opponents
raw_title: Jade Cargill Reveals Past Neck Injury Left Her Struggling to Lift Opponents
summary_src: Jade Cargill has built her WWE career around her incredible strength, but there was a point when a neck injury made even lifting another wrestler a serious challenge.
body: Speaking in a workout video published on the Women’s Health YouTube channel , Cargill revealed that she dealt with a neck injury approximately two years ago. She explained that a pinched muscle affected her ability to hold people up, which was especially difficult considering how much her wrestling style depends on strength. “A move in the gym that I do that makes me feel strong is actually pull-ups. I had an injury about 2 years ago with my neck. I had a pinched muscle. I could barely hold people up. So, me being able to do that and continue at least to get to 10, to get to 20, it means the world to me these days.” For someone whose signature offense involves lifting opponents into the air, that kind of physical limitation is a big deal. Cargill didn’t specify exactly when the injury happened or how long it affected her, but she made it clear that being able to perform those exercises again is something she doesn’t take for granted. This also isn’t the first time Cargill has addressed problems with her neck. Back in April, Cargill shut down accusations that she used performance-enhancing drugs and mentioned that neck issues had affected her lifting. Cargill also explained that she’s become more careful with her body as she gets older. Between WWE’s demanding schedule and the physical punishment that comes with wrestling, she now places greater importance on stretching and recovery. “How I go about bulletproofing my body is stretching. It’s something that I really put an emphasis on and I really take my time in doing now as I’m getting older, especially in the sport that we do and we’re taking all these bumps.” The WWE Superstar also admitted that maintaining her physique is currently more important than constantly pushing for heavier weights. She knows there isn’t a traditional offseason in WWE, and she’s not interested in risking an injury just to prove how much she can lift. title: On the Record: Jade Cargill Opens Up On How WWE Legend Chyna Inspired Her Muscular Physique
raw_title: Jade Cargill Reveals How WWE Legend Chyna Inspired Her Muscular Physique
summary_src: Jade Cargill didn’t develop her muscular physique by accident, and it turns out a WWE legend played a major role in inspiring the look she’s known for today.
body: “All my life, I’ve been muscular, and it’s something that I just wanted to put the pedal to the metal. I looked up to the great China. I seen her. She was a woman that walked in, owned the room, and I wanted to do the exact same thing.” That inspiration eventually followed Cargill into college, where she began taking strength training more seriously. After discovering that her school had a strength and conditioning coach, she decided to pursue the powerful look she had admired for years. “So, I got in college, seen we had a strength and conditioning coach, and I just said, ‘That’s what I want to do, and I want to look strong as ever.'” Interestingly, Cargill’s connection to Chyna isn’t something that only she has noticed. Back in 2022, Tommy Dreamer compared Jade Cargill to Chyna while discussing her athletic ability and potential as a professional wrestler. At the time, Dreamer praised Cargill’s natural gifts and saw similarities between the two performers. Cargill went on to explain that while Chyna remains her biggest fitness inspiration, the women she currently shares the ring with in WWE also motivate her to keep improving. Seeing other female wrestlers in tremendous shape reminds her that she can’t afford to slack off. “My biggest gym motivation or inspiration, I would say, was China. Just seeing her embody and go out there and just shine so bright, I was like, that’s exactly what I want to do. but also all the women athletes that we have in our company really motivate me.” She admitted that being surrounded by other impressive athletes sometimes makes her feel like she needs to work even harder. “And when I feel like I’m slacking and I’m in the ring with these women and they look just as phenomenal, I’m like, ‘Okay, I got to get back in the gym and go a little harder.'” Chyna helped change how muscular women were presented in WWE, and Cargill is now carrying some of that same inspiration into her own career. For Cargill, the goal was never simply to have big muscles. She wanted the kind of presence that made people pay attention the moment she walked into a room, just like Chyna did. title: On the Record: Jade Cargill Says Looking Good Naked Is a Bonus of Her Intense Workout Routine
raw_title: Jade Cargill Says Looking Good Naked Is a Bonus of Her Intense Workout Routine
summary_src: Jade Cargill spends plenty of time in the gym maintaining one of the most recognizable physiques in WWE, and she’s not pretending that it’s all about getting stronger for the ring.
body: “I get my best ideas when I work out. I get really hyped when I work out. Working out is my therapy, but looking good when you’re naked is a bonus as well.” Cargill certainly puts in the work to maintain that physique. She explained that she trains her core five days a week and demonstrated several exercises, including Russian twists, bicycles, in-and-outs, and planks. According to Cargill, those exercises aren’t just about having visible abs, either. They’re also essential to performing her power moves inside the ring. “If you ever see me pick somebody up for a stalling suplex, just know it is all core.” “I actually did this for 3 minutes one time and I was very proud of myself at 34 years old that I could do a three-minute plank. And you never know how strong you are until you push yourself to that limit.” Of course, Cargill has never been shy about showing off the results of her hard work. She’s previously fired back at accusations about how she maintains her muscular physique , insisting that her appearance comes down to genetics and dedication in the gym. She’s also been outspoken about her confidence outside the gym. Earlier this year, Cargill explained why she prefers playing a heel in WWE , acknowledging that feeling good about how she looks is part of her natural personality. At the end of the day, Cargill isn’t making any apologies for enjoying the results of her training. Her workouts help her perform in WWE, give her a mental escape, and keep her looking exactly how she wants. And as she pointed out herself, looking good naked doesn’t hurt, either. title: Debating Triple H's Focus on Survivor Series WarGames
raw_title: Debating Triple H's Obsession With WWE's Survivor Series WarGames Match
body: The two-ring, steel cage war of attrition has become a staple of the pro wrestling calendar, but should it be, or has its yearly usage at the big-four premium live event watered down its effectiveness? Let's debate each side of the argument, including Triple H's seeming obsession with keeping it on the schedule, and come to a conclusion. Yes, the creative team may introduce story threads that will ultimately culminate at WrestleMania, but there has always been a sense of the mundane and lackluster when it comes to the post-SummerSlam months in WWE. There was the Deadly Game tournament and brand warfare before Triple H introduced War Games as a main event marketing tool. Since then, the match has helped Survivor Series regain prestige as one of WWE's elite shows of the year, while also paying off long-running rivalries that have dominated airwaves for months. It worked well for The Bloodline story in 2022 and again a year later, when Cody Rhodes and Co. faced The Judgment Day. It has also emphasized the importance of factions in WWE, and if history teaches us anything, it is that factions, groups, trios, and the like allow for more creative opportunities and, as a result, better TV. Look no further than the aforementioned Bloodline and Judgment Day, both of whom, at their peaks, were central and driving forces on Raw and SmackDown. Every year, without fail, WWE would trot out the event, headlined by matches that lacked the hate or longevity around them to justify taking place in the namesake steel structure. The result was diminishing returns and the long-overdue elimination of the event from the WWE schedule in 2022. The show had so watered down the Hell in a Cell concept that it took a legitimate, long-running rivalry with legitimate dislike between the competitors to justify bringing it back, which Triple H and his creative team did in October of 2024 when CM Punk and Drew McIntyre delivered an instant classic at Bad Blood. While this year's event is an exception, thanks to the excellently crafted Bloodline vs. 946 feud, the War Games match risks the same overexposure. Just like it did in NXT, when its introduction meant the conclusion of a long-running or intensely personal, faction-based rivalry, it became a staple of the Survivor Series amid the height of the Bloodline story. It served a purpose involving The Judgment Day, too. Over the years, in both the developmental and main roster brands, the continued promotion of the War Games match has spoiled the creative direction of some of the top feuds in WWE. There is no question about where programs are heading, and as a result, the excitement that once existed is in danger of wearing off. The moment The Bloodline and 946 began feuding, it was abundantly clear that the creative team was booking toward Survivor Series. While it is absolutely a positive for the writers to have an endgame in mind and a direction to take stories, there is a certain level of predictability that can settle in. That p
summary: The two-ring steel cage match has turned into an annual Survivor Series highlight under Triple H, helping restore the event's status after the post-SummerSlam lull that once featured Deadly Games and brand warfare. It has successfully paid off extended storylines such as The Bloodline in 2022 and Cody Rhodes versus The Judgment Day in 2023 while stressing the role of factions in WWE programming. The discussion weighs whether yearly repetition at the premium live event has reduced the match's impact or remains a needed creative anchor.

body: In today's surveillance era, where smartphone cameras are ubiquitous, many fans took notice of Thekla's post-match actions, which drew a wide range of reactions on social media from amusement to some suggesting the Toxic Spider was being disrespectful. "LMAOOOO Thekla not selling the finish of the match. I love her. [sic]," read one post. "What happened here? Anyway, Thekla should have sold the damage from Mercedes Moné's finisher," said another Twitter account. Further fanning the flames of the Thekla vs. Mercedes feud, Mercedes Mone seemed to dismiss her otherwise strong match against Thekla during the WrestleDream 2026 media scrum. "Uh, I mean, it's not one of my favorite matches," said Mercedes before seeming to deliver an in-character response to her rival. "I told you guys that I'm not scared of a little spider. She's more like a chihuahua that doesn't stop talking and just (makes chihuahua noises.)" "She's not toxic ," Mercedes continued. "I'm sick of toxic people." "Mercedes Mone flat out buried Thekla. I'm crying son," read a tweet in response to Mercedes' apparent jab. Whether or not Mercedes Mone and Thekla have any real-life animosity remains to be seen, but it doesn't matter if that's how fans perceive it. One of the oldest phrases in professional wrestling is "personal issues draw money." Typically that quote speaks to the spirit of simulated drama, but if real-life issues can be safely incorporated into wrestling storylines, all the better. Charlotte Flair and Becky Lynch famously went off script during a belt exchange ceremony on SmackDown in 2021. In what was supposed to be an innocuous exchange of championship belts with both stars switching brands, tensions ensued when Charlotte Flair dropped the WWE Raw Women's Championship on the ring mat. While the moment soured their once-tight bond, it led to increased interest in their ensuing Survivor Series match. "We were supposed to exchange the titles. I grab it out of her hand unknowingly, I'm 'Becky Two Belts' for a second then I toss her the title, then she tells Sonya (Deville) to pick it up. Then she challenges me to a fight, and I back out of it and I go. So everybody was supposed to get their moment there," said Lynch of how the segment was supposed to go before it went left. "The title dropped," explained Charlotte. "I didn't drop it on purpose." "If anyone knows how important the [WWE Raw women's title] is to me—I would never be dismissive of the title in the way that it was presented that I did." AEW is no stranger to backstage drama. CM Punk's Brawl Out / Brawl In saga remains the subject of some of AEW's most notorious lore. Punk's yearlong crashout on his ex-employer continues to be the subject of heated discussions within the wrestling community. Punk returned to WWE for an unlikely and successful run that continues to this day. llm_long: Will Ospreay defended the AEW World Heavyweight Championship in a Clockwork Carnage match at AEW WrestleDream 2026. The unique format was designed by Pro Wrestling EVE, with whom Ospreay has collaborated. Ospreay entered the bout early in his title reign following an emotional win over Kenny Omega at AEW All In 2026.

In Clockwork Carnage, wrestlers enter every three minutes until all eight participants are in the match. Any wrestler pinned or submitted before the final entrant arrives is eliminated. Once the last wrestler enters, the remaining competitors begin a 15-minute scoring period where each pinfall or submission counts as one fall.

Ospreay and Konosuke Takeshita opened the match at a fast pace. Takeshita executed a gorilla press from the top rope followed by a flying clothesline on Ospreay. The action continued with Takeshita delivering a dive to the outside onto Ospreay.

Mike Bailey entered wearing United Empire colors, though commentary noted that alliances do not apply in Clockwork Carnage. Takeshita eliminated Bailey and focused his attack on Ospreay. Ospreay and Bailey later showed a moment of solidarity with a United Empire high-five before Takeshita interrupted it.

Ricochet attempted to form a temporary alliance with Takeshita against the United Empire members. The partnership broke down when Ricochet tried to roll up Takeshita. Ricochet then hit a dive onto Ospreay on the outside before Takeshita dropped him with a headbutt.

Ospreay and Bailey delivered a double superplex to Takeshita, but Ospreay's attempt to steal the pin failed. Darby Allin entered using a skateboard, performing an ollie on Ricochet's back and setting up a table outside the ring. Kazuchika Okada's music played as the match continued.

title: Crown Jewel status, Street Fighter, more — Psyko’s random thoughts on wrestling
raw_title: Psyko’s random thoughts on wrestling: Crown Jewel status, Street Fighter, more
body: Not a lot can be written about this situation that hasn’t already been covered, but while I do feel like WWE should seriously consider moving the show outside of Saudi Arabia, I don’t think it’s as simple as having every wrestler and employee boycott the show. We have to remember that we’re not in the Vince McMahon era of WWE anymore, where wrestlers could just skip the show if they wanted to. We’re in the TKO era, and from everything that’s been reported, the only people who can make the call are Ari Emanuel and his partners. Nick Khan and HHH have no power over this decision. In fact, from what’s been reported, they’re actually against going to Saudi Arabia for this show, just like many of the wrestlers and crew members, but it’s out of their hands at this point. The biggest roadblock right now isn’t the money because TKO isn’t going to lose any money if it moves the show elsewhere. The biggest problem is that TKO is scared of being on bad terms with the Saudi government if it doesn’t hold the show in a few weeks. Since the Saudi government already has money invested in TKO boxing and the next big event is still happening, it has put TKO in a very awkward position. The other thing to consider is this: Do you see wrestlers risking their jobs over this? While it’s great that wrestlers have options outside of WWE, nobody outside of WWE is going to pay them the amount of money they’re making in WWE, with the exception of AEW. However, AEW’s roster is already more than full, so for most wrestlers, the only option is to do their jobs, even if they really don’t want to. The only reason I could see TKO moving this show out of Saudi Arabia is if the Saudi government cancels the whole thing, which I doubt will happen. I get that modern wrestlers, especially those who come from the indie circuit, have the mindset that everybody knows wrestling is scripted and fake. However, that doesn’t mean you can’t make an effort to make it believable for those who buy tickets or watch on television. In any other combat sport, if a smaller guy fights a bigger guy, the smaller guy would have to fight from underneath for the entire match and would probably get killed before the end of it. So why, in wrestling, is that same smaller guy able to go move for move with a heavyweight? That makes no sense. The same goes for heavyweight wrestlers. I get that you’re able to do flips and dives, but that’s not why we buy a ticket to see you wrestle. We want to see you beat the living shit out of your opponent, not hit a 450 splash from the top rope and perform suicide dives. Wrestlers really need to learn how to work to their size because, if they don’t, they’re just hurting themselves and the matches they’re in. When you fail to make a match feel believable, all you’re doing is performing moves for the sake of doing moves, and that has become forgettable. I wanted to end on a lighter note with a short review of the new *Street Fighter* movie, which stars Roman Reigns and Cody Rhod

title: On the Record: WWE's Joe Hendry Details His 'Unconventional' Amateur Wrestling Background
raw_title: WWE's Joe Hendry Details His 'Unconventional' Amateur Wrestling Background
body: "I think the thing about my amateur wrestling days is — it's very me, it's very unconventional," Hendry said. "It all started because I'd just started professional wrestling ... and I found that people weren't taking me seriously." While he's perfectly okay with using comedy in his wrestling, Hendry also wanted to be respected as a threat in the ring as well. He already had some history with judo, but Hendry decided to train as a grappler, too. It was something he felt came naturally to him. "MMA has progressed massively, but back when this was happening — this was, like, 12 years ago, when MMA wasn't as big in the U.K., and I would just go to MMA gyms and roast everyone in grappling," Hendry continued. That only lasted for a short while, however, as he eventually progressed to training in a more serious gym in Scotland and found himself facing more talented competition. That included former UFC fighter Paul Craig. "I don't know if I ever took him down, to be honest," Hendry stated. After defeating a wrestler who was slated to participate in the Commonwealth Games, Hendry decided to take a chance on entering himself. He continued training and, before participating in the Commonwealth Games, he won the British Championship in freestyle wrestling for his weight class. "That was one of the greatest days of my life," he said. "To be able to call my dad on the phone and say, 'I'm British Champion.' ... It's not often that I get emotional. ... I'll never forget that phone call." In 2018, Hendry joined Team Scotland for the Commonwealth Games, which were taking place in Australia. He was initially set to face Australian UFC fighter Robert Whittaker. "I was like, 'I must be living in a simulation, because don't tell me that the pro wrestler is about to face the UFC Middleweight Champion at the Commonwealth Games," Hendry said. Hendry reached out to UFC veteran and noted pro wrestling fan Chael Sonnen ahead of the fight, looking for advice. According to Hendry, he knew that he was heavily outmatched, but Sonnen encouraged him to talk some trash regardless. Sonnen wrote a promo for Hendry to deliver, but the fight never took place, as Whittaker learned he would have to vacate his UFC title if he decided to participate in the Commonwealth Games.

body: Billy Gunn addressed Triple H’s dig towards him and AEW at the 2019 Hall of Fame ceremony. In an interview with Inside The Ropes , Gunn recalled Triple H taking a dig at AEW during the 2019 WWE Hall of Fame ceremony on April 6, citing that Vince McMahon would buy the “p*ss-ant company” just to fire him again. Gunn revealed that he had approached Tony Khan about attending the ceremony, adding that he knew Triple H would have something to say about AEW. He described the remark as a “d*ck move” on Triple H’s part. “I knew it was coming. I kind of knew they were going to do something AEW because it was hot at the time and I was there and they were all wondering how I got to go there, and that’s because Tony Khan was super cool. I went, asked, and he said ‘100%. Of course you can,” said Gunn. “I would never hold you back from that.’ I didn’t know what they were gonna do, but I knew they were going to do something. I also knew that if they were, Hunter was going to have something to say. Once I set myself up for that, I just let it go. The only one that got hurt out of that whole deal was him. I don’t want to say it, but it was a d*ck move. It was kind of trying to save face, and you didn’t need to because it’s going to happen.” “It’s the wrestling business. It’s what we do. They like to stir up shit. When you have somebody in another company, which was me, they can’t believe it, and then you see me, they have to do it. It’s like an unwritten thing in a book. ‘If another guy is in another company, we have to say or do something.’ They started chanting it, and you get a response from the guy leading the company.” Gunn initially joined AEW as coach in 2019 and sporadically made in-ring appearances for matches. body: During an interview on Game On ahead of AEW WrestleDream, Ospreay was asked whether he gets tired of people constantly bringing up WWE and questioning when he might eventually make the jump to the company. Ospreay acknowledged that those questions are part of being a professional wrestler, but insisted that his focus remains on AEW. He also explained why he believes AEW is changing the wrestling business and why he doesn’t concern himself with other promotions. “I know it’s a part of the gig. People always ask, and I can only give my opinion. I don’t really care about it. I’d rather focus on AEW, and I’d rather focus on what we’re able to do here and what I believe AEW is doing, which is changing the face of professional wrestling. I love what we present. I love what we do. I love our wrestling. I love everything that we’re all about. So I couldn’t really care less about any other promotion.” The interviewer then shifted the conversation toward the ongoing AEW vs. WWE debate among wrestling fans, asking whether constantly comparing the two companies does more harm than good to professional wrestling. Ospreay didn’t seem particularly concerned about the comparisons and suggested that wrestlers simply need to accept them. “It’s just part of the game, boss. You just got to learn to take it.” Of course, there’s nothing wrong with Ospreay having an opinion about another wrestling company. AEW and WWE are constantly compared by fans, and it’s only natural that prominent wrestlers from both promotions get asked about the competition. However, saying he couldn’t care less about other promotions is a little harder to reconcile with how often he’s been willing to discuss WWE in the past. For now, Ospreay insists that his attention is on AEW and helping the company continue growing. Whether that means he’ll stop weighing in on WWE remains to be seen, but given his history, it wouldn’t be surprising if the subject comes up again before long. title: How AEW Reacted To Keith Lee Endorsing A Man Who Believes The Pyramids Were Built With 'Laser Technology'
raw_title: How AEW Reacted To Keith Lee Endorsing A Man Who Believes The Pyramids Were Built With 'Laser Technology'
body: AEW backstage reaction to Keith Lee endorsing Darius J. Wright Keith Lee had been inactive on social media for almost a year when he suddenly resurfaced on September 10 to endorse Darius J. Wright , a self-proclaimed "consciousness explorer" who has stated on multiple occasions that he believes the Egyptian pyramids were constructed using "laser technology." Reports then noted that Lee was "all in" on Wright's school and teachings. Lee's endorsement of Wright caused a stir within pro wrestling circles on social media but it seemingly didn't have much of a lasting impact in All Elite Wrestling. Sean Ross Sapp noted in a Fightful Select Answers Q&A that Lee's post was a topic of conversation within AEW for about a day, but they haven't heard anything else about the tweet beyond that. Keith Lee has not appeared for AEW since December 2023 when he took time off due to requiring a double surgery, which he underwent in early 2024, and Lee suggested in the summer of 2025 that he was cleared to wrestle once again. Lee was discussed for a return earlier this year, but the return never happened, with reports noting in July that the belief within pro wrestling was that Keith Lee has actually retired from in-ring competition . llm_long: Necro Butcher announced that he signed a basic legends deal with WWE. The agreement was confirmed as accurate by sources within the company. WWE President Nick Khan led the effort to secure the deal.

The signing stands out because Necro Butcher built his reputation almost entirely outside of wrestling's largest promotions. He became known for an exceptionally violent style that frequently featured weapons and the elements of deathmatch wrestling.

Necro Butcher's real name is Dylan Keith Summers. Born on July 13, 1973, in West Virginia, he made his professional wrestling debut in 1998. Over time he faced several prominent names from the 2000s independent scene, including Bryan Danielson, Kevin Steen, Eddie Kingston, Chris Hero, Claudio Castagnoli and Samoa Joe.

He also appeared in the 2008 film The Wrestler starring Mickey Rourke. A 2005 match against Samoa Joe at IWA Mid-South's Something to Prove event in Philadelphia gained a reputation for its brutality, highlighted by a moment in which Joe kicked him off arena bleachers onto the concrete floor.

More than two decades later the match received renewed attention when it became the focus of an episode in the seventh season of Dark Side of the Ring. The episode examined the bout along with Butcher's life and career. The full episode was later released on YouTube in July and has accumulated more than 700,000 views.

Butcher moved from being featured in the documentary to signing the WWE Legends deal months afterward. The contract typically permits the use of a wrestler's name and likeness for merchandise, video games and other projects while allowing for possible appearances.

title: WWE Trades Ruthless Aggression For PG
raw_title: WWE Trades Ruthless Aggression For PG | Wrestling Timelines
body: The 2000s was a turbulent time for WWE . It started wonderfully, if you only watched the TV product. Stone Cold Steve Austin was written out of storylines in November 1999, but no matter; as early as January 2000, Triple H had evolved into a main event-level heel. The Rock replaced Austin as the top babyface, more than adequately, by setting a record of consecutive attendances in excess of 10,000 fans. Underneath, powered by Chris Kreski’s overlapping, brilliant creative direction, Kurt Angle, Edge and Cstohristian, the Hardy Boyz, and countless more acts connected with the people. 2000 was arguably the best year in WWE history; while it was not as fascinating nor as futuristic as 1997 , the top-to-bottom match quality had never been better. A greying cloud hovered overhead the entire time. In December 1999, the media went after the WWF. Wrestling was over, and outrage is timeless. Various hit-pieces were penned by various outlets, generating so much attention that Coca-Cola pulled its sponsorship. WWE’s TV carriers got spooked by the pressure applied by the Parents Television and Media Council; Vince McMahon, in turn, made halfhearted, on-off attempts to tone down the product. With the Rock and a returning Steve Austin drawing so much money, a lack of sponsors was not an issue. And then, in 2003, with the Attitude Era fad dead, the Rock and Austin left. Stars were made eventually, John Cena and Batista most notably, but business wasn’t great. In order to ensure maximum profits, WWE had to behave.

title: Billy Gunn Comments On Brawl Out Incident
raw_title: Billy Gunn Weighs In On Brawl Out, 'Certain Veterans Aren't Going To Put Up With That Shit'
summary_src: What started as one of the greatest returns in wrestling history ended in wrestling tragedy as the relationship between CM Punk and AEW flamed out in two years.
body: What started as one of the greatest returns in wrestling history ended in wrestling tragedy as the relationship between CM Punk and AEW flamed out in two years. Speaking to Kenny McIntosh on Inside The Ropes , Billy Gunn, who works as a coach in AEW, reflected on the incident. “I wasn’t around for that. I knew the incident that happened, and it was what it was. They just have to realize that sometimes, there are certain veterans that aren’t going to put up with that shit, no matter what. If you’re a young buckaroo and you want to poke the bear, get ready to get bit. I think that’s what happened. I don’t know the whole details; that’s between them,” he said. Gunn said he didn’t pay attention to the media stuff surrounding the incident. Asked about how things like that were handled during his time, Gunn replied, “Vince (McMahon) had things under control really good. I don’t have to like you to work with you. I just have to do business. 99.9% of the guys always do that. There will be a spat every now and then where you just pull them into a room, shut the door, and you don’t do it in public or in front of the boys. If you have a problem, we fix it now, so that when you walk out the door, we don’t have a problem anymore. That’s how grown-ass people deal with shit. Nowadays, we don’t, and that’s sad.” Punk was suspended by AEW for his role in the incident. He returned a year later, but was fired after another incident at AEW All In 2023. title: Mike Bailey Jokes That He Might've Disrespected Michael Oku By Putting French TV Host In A Half Crab

summary_src: Mike Bailey had a great time in France. AEW visited the country for the Grand Slam France event on Tuesday, October 6. If you ask Mike Bailey, this was a huge step towards pushing wrestling into mainstream culture in France.
body: AEW visited the country for the Grand Slam France event on Tuesday, October 6. If you ask Mike Bailey, this was a huge step towards pushing wrestling into mainstream culture in France. “I think it’s very fascinating to see how pro wrestling is captured by the media lens all over the world, right? Pro wrestling is ingrained in American culture as it is for many, many other countries, but France is still a few years behind. Pro Wrestling is evolving, I think bringing AEW and Grand Slam to the Adidas Arena is a huge step in pushing pro wrestling to the mainstream in France, but sometimes they just feel like, ‘Our audience, if we just talk about it, they might not know what it is, so we kind of have to show them.'” Bailey told Fightful’s Sean Ross Sapp in a new interview. Continuing on, B ailey talked about putting a submission hold on a television host during his media tour before the show. “I think just asking a pro wrestler to put the host in a hold might not be the best idea. But I have been doing this for 20 years. I have been put in similar situations many, many times and I think that the half crab— which might be disrespectful to Michael Oku because he is the master of the half crab and I was kind of relatively on his turf, right? He’s English but still, Europe. But I think it was a much smarter hold than a high elbow guillotine or an open hand slap to do to a news presenter. This is the thing, he’s not gonna fight his way out of it. Not only do I have a fantastic half crab, but I have an even better straight ankle lock. So once that locked in, I have full control of him. Also when I’m sitting on his lower back, he’s not going to be able to wriggle himself out. So I can sit there comfortably as long as I want which was a big part of my plan.”

title: Riyadh Airport Stays Closed After Houthi Strikes
raw_title: Report: Riyadh International Airport remains highly restricted following Houthi attacks
summary_src: Saudi Arabia, which is scheduled to host WWE next month, has reported 20 attacks on the country as of late.
body: King Khalid International Airport, the main travel hub in Saudi Arabia, remains incredibly restricted after suffering attacks earlier in the month. The airport has been closed since last week due to a deadly bombing by the Iran-backed Houthis earlier this month. Despite plans to reopen by Sunday, the airport was “still shut as of Monday,” per Bloomberg. The airport is currently operating under a Notice to Airmen Advisory (NOA), which says that departures and landings can only occur if they’ve been given prior permission. The airport is reportedly not available for emergency landings currently. Riyadh has been under attack as of late, just weeks before WWE and a high-profile boxing match remain scheduled to take place in the Saudi capital. WWE’s November 7 trip to Riyadh for Crown Jewel remains on despite Saudi Arabia reporting that it suffered 20 attacks from the Houthis so far this month. Just a week before then, Riyadh is expected to welcome high-profile boxer Canelo Alvarez for a match against Christian Mbilli. The U.S. Department of State Consular Affairs provided a security alert on Monday morning, warning Americans to “exercise heightened vigilance” while visiting the Middle East. The Canadian government, which is currently recommending a full avoidance of all non-essential travel to Saudi Arabia, is suggesting citizens who wish to leave the country by air “should consider using airports in neighbouring countries.” Instability in the region has caused many international sports, entertainment and business events in the area to be postponed. The annual Six Kings Slam, a tennis exhibition featuring a half-dozen of the top men’s players in the world, was moved from October to late December. The Saudi International golf tournament, typically a final event on the European and Asian tour, was postponed indefinitely. The Asian Football Confederation is reportedly considering delaying the 2027 Asian Cup, which is scheduled to begin in January, by a year. Yet to follow in the footsteps of these major events are combat sports or professional wrestling, with the Canelo fight and Crown Jewel still on the schedule. With less than a month to go until either event, a rescheduling or postponement, if it were to happen, would be a last-minute call.
summary: King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh remains shut down and highly restricted following deadly attacks by Iran-backed Houthis earlier this month. The facility is operating under a Notice to Airmen that requires prior permission for any departures or landings and is unavailable for emergency use. WWE's Crown Jewel event on November 7 and a Canelo Alvarez boxing match the week prior are both still scheduled to proceed in the Saudi capital despite the ongoing security issues.

body: Kevin Owens addressed fans after his NXT appearance at their live event in Gatineau, Quebec. Owens teamed up with Kendal Grey and Shiloh Hill to face Tony D’Angelo and BirthRight in the main event. He also highlighted Hill, Grey, and D’Angelo as the present stars of the brand. “With that said, another thing that really helped me say ‘yes’ when they asked me if I want to be a part of this show was knowing that I get to share the ring with people that are shaping the future of what WWE will be. The four idiots we just beat, very talented idiots, but still, not the best attitude. And these three, I just said the future; quite frankly, I think you’re really looking at the present,” said Owens. “So for that, Tony, thank you. Kendal, thank you. Shiloh, thank you. It was an honor and a pleasure. Thank you guys so much.” Owens added that Steve Corino, a coach at the Performance Center reached out to him for making the special appearance at the live event. “And Steve, I can genuinely say, without a doubt, if you’re not familiar with his career, go back and watch. One of the greatest of all time. I met him in 2004. He took me under his wing, and without him, I am telling you, I would not be standing here right now. Tonight, or ever, I would have never had the career I had without him. So Steve, I’m not going to make you come out here, because I know you won’t want to, but you’re back there. I love you. Thank you. Anytime you need anything, I’m here. Anytime you guys need anything, I’m here. I’m at the Performance Center, you know it. Well, you guys can’t tell me, you don’t have my phone number just know, if they ask me to be here for you guys, I’ll be here. Thank you.” Rosanne Raphael Rosanne Raphael is a wrestling writer with over three and a half years of experience covering all things related to the industry. title: WWE Trades Ruthless Aggression For PG
raw_title: WWE Trades Ruthless Aggression For PG | Wrestling Timelines – Page 3
body: After failing to renew the deal on the cheap, the CW Network makes the decision to drop WWE SmackDown from its airwaves. This is embarrassing, and significantly affects WWE’s bottom line. While nowhere near close to fatal - SmackDown finds a new home on MyNetworkTV in October - it’s an echo of WCW’s demise. But really, it’s a tale as old as time. SmackDown is among the highest-viewed shows on the station. In June 2008 , it draws strongly with teenagers and young adult males - elusive demographics that every television executive dreams of capturing - and yet, it does not matter. This is something of an exaggeration, but to understand this disconnect, think of it like a maths question: what is 3 million multiplied by 0? It doesn't matter if SmackDown on the CW Network draws, say, 3 million viewers. Ad execs believe that wrestling fans have 0 money. Blue-chip companies hold the opinion that wrestling fans are uneducated - how dumb must they be, if they believe in this fake crap?! - and thus poor. They can’t afford fancy things, so why waste money targeting them? By June 2008, WWE earns a meagre $1,154,000 from TV rights fees - and this factors in Raw, SmackDown, and ECW . WWE makes more money doing house shows, which is why the calendar is so brutal. Vince knows that there is a safe containing a vast fortune that WWE is yet to crack, and sets about transforming his company in order to open it up.

title: ICW: NHB Loses Default Judgment in Rachel Price Lawsuit
raw_title: Update On Lawsuit Against Independent Promotion Icw: Nhb
body: Jalwa Game Goa Game Raja Game MaanWin DMFirst Veer Game UPDATE ON LAWSUIT AGAINST INDEPENDENT PROMOTION ICW: NHB By Mike Johnson on 2026-10-19 10:39:00 There was a "proof hearing to determine the amount and extent of damage" won by plaintfiff Rachel Price in her lawsuit against independent promotion ICW: No Holds Barred on 9/24 in Newark, New Jersey. Price was officially given a default judgment on 7/21. During the hearing. Price was ordered to submit "a supplemental certification with any additional medical bills and the amount of the outstanding lien" within 30 days, which should be sometime in the next week. After that, the court should issue a ruling about what would be owed to Price. As previously noted, the promotion stopped responding and appearing before the United States District Court of New Jersey after their initial attorney removed himself from the case. In her lawsuit, Price alleged she was working for the venue at a 6/25/22 ICW: NHB event when there was an announcement made that those with vehicles in a lot adjacent to the move their vehicles. Price claims she exited the venue via a side door to move her vehicle, but poor lighting, a lack of railing, no signage and a lack of employees stationed at the door caused her to fall from the landing to the floor below, at least three feet, where she was injured. Price has alleged she has permanent personal injuries and is suing for over $75,000. Court records indicate that the parent company of the Heart Ballroom never responded and a summary judgment was ruled against them. Whether Price recovered any damages from them is unknown. ICW: NHB did iitially respond to the lawsuit, basically stating that any issues that happened were the responsibility of the venue, not them, as they had merely rented the space for the evening. On 1/29, ICW: NHB's attorney withdrew from the case as he had relocated. Since then, the court has not heard from anyone new representing the promotion and have not heard from its owner Danny "Demanto" Purdue either. There had been a settlement conference set for 3/10 but no one representing ICW: NHB appeared to take part. The court advised on 4/30 that Price could request a summary judgment against ICW: NHB. Price did that and on 6/2, the Court informed Price she could file a motion of final judgment against ICW. She did just that on 7/2, while also alleging the promotion had shifted its assets under a new LLC, NHB Merch and is seeking to amend her lawsuit to include the new LLC as well as the company's owner Danny Purdue (aka Danny Demanto) in order to prevent them from being able to be held liable for anything she may be awared in the lawsuit she filed back in 2024. In that filing, Price claimed the promotion has shifted everything under the new LLC and is now running under the company name No Holds Barred - The Chains. As of this writing, the court has not ruled on that request. ICW: NHB owner Purdue previously made reference to the lawsuit on the mic at an ICW: NHB

title: Eva Marie Opens Up On Marriage to Jonathan Coyle Became a Transactional Business Relationship Before Divorce
raw_title: Eva Marie Reveals Marriage to Jonathan Coyle Became a Transactional Business Relationship Before Divorce
summary_src: Eva Marie is opening up about what really went wrong in her marriage to Jonathan Coyle, and according to the former WWE Superstar, their relationship had reached a point where they were more like business partners than husband and wife.
body: The former Total Divas star filed for divorce in December 2024 after 10 years of marriage, bringing an end to a relationship that WWE fans watched unfold on reality television. As Ringside News previously covered , the couple had separated before the divorce filing, with irreconcilable differences cited in the paperwork. During a recent interview with Page Six , Eva explained that there wasn’t one explosive incident that destroyed the marriage. Instead, she began questioning her future after turning 40 and realizing that the relationship wasn’t giving either of them what they deserved. She recalled how spending more time in California while working on her treatment and recovery centers helped set things in motion. However, the real turning point came when she took a serious look at what her marriage had become. Eva then explained how turning 40 changed her perspective. She compared her own marriage to her parents’ relationship, which has lasted more than five decades, and admitted that what she had with Jonathan simply wasn’t the same. “But when I turned 40, I had like kind of this aha moment of you only have one life and you know, with my marriage, there is nothing like I we were like business partners. So like I look at my parents and my parents have been married for 53 years and to me it like they have true blue like ride or die love till death do you part type of a marriage and I really felt like Jonathan and I were doing a disservice to one another because we just had a very transactional business relationship.” “We got along, we were totally, you know, best of buddies, but that’s not really what a marriage is, nor should it be, nor is that what I wanted it to be. So I was like, you know what? I’m 40 years old like I always I want to live my life to the fullest and I want to be as honest and as happiest as I possibly can be and I want that for him as well.” The interviewer pointed out that leaving a relationship can be especially difficult when things aren’t necessarily terrible. Eva agreed, explaining that there wasn’t some dramatic moment where either person had done something that made the marriage impossible to continue. “For sure and I think that as individuals, you know, a lot of times because there wasn’t this like massive turning point of like you know, this turmoil of oh my goodness, either he should leave me or I should leave him type situation, which I thank God for cuz I’m sure that is like really traumatic all as well for individuals.” Eva went on to explain that staying in a familiar situation can sometimes prevent people from finding what actually makes them happy. “But I think a lot of us in our life, we stay in situations, whether it’s business or even you know, your personal relationships because it is comfortable, because it is easy. And and having to like make a change or all of a sudden do something completely different is scary because you have to make all of these different types of moves, but I think that if we live i

llm_long: Andrade El Idolo retained the AEW National Championship by defeating Tommaso Ciampa at WrestleDream. The match took place on Saturday at Addition Financial Arena in Orlando, Florida. Andrade secured the pinfall using The DM.

The contest featured extended striking exchanges along with multiple near falls. Andrade executed the Three Amigos on the floor and followed with a split-legged moonsault inside the ring. Both wrestlers incorporated elements of Andrade's routine of removing his entrance pants during the bout.

Ciampa removed a layer of his gear to reveal trunks with the phrase "I Just Know," referencing Andrade's catchphrase "How you know?" After Andrade removed his pants, he delivered several running double knees and hit Dia de los Muertos for a near fall.

Ciampa answered with a running knee and sent Andrade into a camera operator at ringside before earning another two-count. Ciampa first attempted to bring the title belt into the ring but was stopped by referee Aubrey Edwards. He then introduced a chair, which drew the referee's attention away.

The sequence mirrored events from Wednesday's Dynamite, where Ciampa had used the National title behind the referee's back. This time Andrade reversed the attempt and drove Ciampa onto the championship belt with a DDT. Ciampa kicked out, but Andrade immediately followed with The DM to retain the title.

Khan also made it clear that when his four-time Women’s World champion returned, she’d be looking for the person who took her out back in March of this year. What TK didn’t mention? The build for the Timeless One’s comeback seems to have started at WrestleDream . Small packages appear to have been strategically placed around Addition Financial Arena in Orlando, Florida on Saturday night. At least one was found by its intended target, an internet content creator named Astrid Pizarro. They did what the folks behind viral marketing campaigns hoped she would do… created content about it. Pizarro found something wrapped in brown paper with the word “Confidential” stamped on it, and and“Play Me” scribbled in marker. It’s also marked with a kiss in red lipstick. The cassette tape within is labeled “Mundanities”, and its narrated by Renee Paquette. The next track Paquette intros is about Toni’s 12-year-old cocker spaniel: “Oh, Chanty. That’s a good boy, Chanty. Who’s a good Chanty? Take a chance. Take a chance, Chanty. Oh, what a beautiful boy. Now, you listen to me. I own you. I created you, and I can end you. You are nothing without me. You worship the ground I walk on, or I will make your life a living hell. When company comes over, they’re here to see me, not you.It’s not a time for your little tricks or performances. It’s not amateur hour with Chantsy. It’s my time. You will greet them. You will wait till I make one witty remark, and then Luther will escort you down to the basement to eat your rubbish. Otherwise, you have one job and one job only. To f*ck. You are a hunting machine and I want you to scour this damn neighborhood making onto anything that moves because mama is in the mood to sell and I can make a pretty good penny off of whatever half freak hamster you manage to knock up. Call it something exotic like a ham dog. You hear me? You worthless wanted beast. Okay, Chanty, let’s go for a walk.” Over the rest of the tape, Storm gives wrestling advice to students like, “if you want to make it in this business, you’ve got to get yourself a cool hat.”* “Fantastical. Mysterious. Timeless. These are the Toni Storm Tapes.” Will these provide meaningful information about Toni’s absence, the kayfabe reason for it, and maybe even clues about what she’ll do when she returns? Does it further distract from the (generally believed to be happy) reason she’s been out? WWE used these sorts of marketing campaigns in the past for Wyatt-related acts, even incorporating augmented reality game elements in them. Those were interesting and really excited a portion of the audience, but ultimately didn’t lead to much. Are these just awareness raising tactics? Or will the return of Timeless Toni Storm be the next evolution of this kind of pro wrestling story? * A properly-sized one , as we all know that tiny hat was holding the

body: TNA Wrestling made the announcement on October 19, 2026, confirming that Shotzi Blackheart has joined its roster. The company credited Busted Open on SiriusXM with first breaking the news, making her signing official just days after she appeared at TNA’s mid-October live events. The signing comes after Shotzi returned to TNA earlier this month, wasting little time getting herself involved in the Knockouts Division. Her appearance immediately got fans talking about whether she was simply making a one-off appearance or had something more permanent lined up. Now we have our answer. Shotzi is no stranger to the wrestling business. The California native made her professional wrestling debut in 2014 before eventually making her way to WWE, where she became an NXT Women’s Tag Team Champion alongside Ember Moon. She also spent time on WWE’s main roster, becoming known for her distinctive personality, bright green hair, and willingness to take some pretty wild risks in the ring. Following her WWE departure, Shotzi continued wrestling outside the company, and her recent TNA appearances made it clear that she wasn’t planning to disappear from the spotlight anytime soon. TNA didn’t just announce her signing either. The company also released 10 fun facts about its newest addition, giving fans a look at what Shotzi gets up to when she isn’t throwing herself around a wrestling ring. Apparently, she’s been riding motorcycles since she was 18, has traveled across America hunting ghosts for her YouTube series Chamber of Horrors , and even studied musical theatre at AMDA in Hollywood. She’s also a massive horror movie fan who dreams of directing her own horror film someday. And that’s just the beginning. TNA revealed that Shotzi is obsessed with Elvis Presley, owns her own chicken farm, and once managed to ride every attraction across all four Walt Disney World theme parks in one day. The company also noted that she was named PWI’s 2025 Independent Wrestler of the Year and appeared on the magazine’s cover. Shotzi also made a point of celebrating her heritage. Then there’s the detail about her wedding, which sounds like something straight out of a wrestling storyline. Shotzi revealed that she didn’t just get married and call it a day. She actually wrestled while still wearing her wedding dress. “I got married and wrestled in my wedding dress all on the same day.” As Ringside News previously covered, Shotzi’s future became a major topic of discussion following her departure from WWE and subsequent appearances outside the company. Her return to TNA gave fans another reason to wonder what she had planned next, but the company’s latest announcement makes it clear that she’s officially part of the roster. Now Shotzi has a fresh opportunity to establish herself in TNA’s Knockouts Division, and there are plenty of potential opponents waiting for her. She’s already proven that she isn’t afraid to take chances, and with a new contract in place, it looks like the next chapter
summary: TNA Wrestling made the announcement on October 19, 2026, confirming that Shotzi Blackheart has joined its roster. The signing comes after Shotzi made a comeback to TNA earlier this month, wasting little time getting herself involved in the Knockouts Division.

summary_src: Eva Marie isn’t shutting the door on WWE just yet. The former Superstar has made it clear that she would absolutely consider stepping back into the ring, and she still has plenty of love for the company that helped launch her career.
body: Eva hasn’t wrestled for WWE since her second run with the company ended in 2021. That comeback saw her return to Monday Night RAW with the Eva-Lution character, eventually becoming involved in a storyline with Piper Niven, who was introduced on WWE television as Doudrop. During a recent interview with Page Six, Eva was directly asked whether she would ever return to the wrestling ring. She didn’t hesitate with her answer, making it clear that WWE remains an important part of her life. “Of course, yes and yes. So, WWE will always hold a special place in my heart because, like I said, they took a chance on a no-name kid who never wrestled a day in her life.” Eva then reflected on how different her background was before entering professional wrestling. While she grew up watching WWE during its WWF days thanks to her three older brothers, she wasn’t someone who had spent years training to become a wrestler. Instead, soccer was her sport before WWE came calling. “Soccer was my sport, so like when it came to the wrestling ring, and I was a fan, of course, of WWE back in the day when it was WWF because I have three older brothers.” Despite getting her start without wrestling experience, Eva eventually developed an appreciation for portraying a villain on television. She specifically pointed to her 2021 return as a time when she felt particularly comfortable embracing the character. “I think like I played a bad guy on So, I was a heel in WWE, and there’s nothing nothing better to play. Like when I went back in 2021, I had the best time ever because I really embraced that character.” As Ringside News previously covered , Eva later revealed that WWE originally had different plans for her final run, including a longer storyline involving her partnership with Piper Niven. She has also discussed the challenges of balancing WWE training with filming Total Divas , which played a role in her decision to seek additional development during her first stint with the company. While Eva clearly remains interested in wrestling again, she didn’t reveal any current discussions with WWE or suggest that a comeback is already being planned. For now, it’s simply an open invitation from someone who still has a soft spot for the business. Still, Eva Marie’s willingness to return is bound to get a reaction. She was never exactly the most universally loved performer during her WWE career, but that was also part of what made her heel character work. Whether WWE would ever bring back the Eva-Lution is another question entirely, but Eva herself is clearly game for another round. title: Eva Marie Left Speechless When Asked About Current Relationship With Ex-Husband Jonathan Coyle
raw_title: Eva Marie Left Speechless When Asked About Current Relationship With Ex-Husband Jonathan Coyle
summary_src: Eva Marie had plenty to say about her divorce from Jonathan Coyle, but one question about where things stand between them today actually managed to leave the former WWE Superstar struggling for words.
body: Eva and Jonathan’s marriage ended after a decade together, with the former Total Divas star filing for divorce in December 2024. Their relationship had been featured extensively on WWE’s reality series, making the split particularly interesting for longtime fans who watched their romance play out on television. During a recent interview with Page Six , Eva discussed moving forward with her life following the divorce. However, things got a little awkward when the interviewer asked whether she and Jonathan were currently on good terms, bad terms, or somewhere in between. Eva admitted that she hadn’t really prepared herself for that question, especially since she hasn’t publicly discussed the divorce very much. “You know, that’s a Wow. Out of all the things that I would think like to prepare myself because, you know, I’m not really that public with and I nor have I been talking about my divorce.” After struggling to come up with an answer, Eva kept things pretty simple. The interviewer suggested that perhaps Eva simply wished him well from a distance, and the former WWE star agreed. She didn’t exactly sound interested in maintaining a close friendship with her ex-husband. “Yeah, I wish him well over there, and that’s about it, you know?” “Yeah. I don’t know. I’m stumped. I’m like, ‘Damn, girl, I am not lost for words.’ And you have just stumped me because that one is like you know now that I you have my wheels turning it’s it’s more so I’m trying to find the word where it’s like there’s no real bad blood in in me but I also have it’s not like we’re best friends or I’m calling them up you know.” That response says quite a bit about where things stand. Eva wasn’t accusing Jonathan of doing anything wrong, and she made it clear that she doesn’t harbor serious resentment toward him. At the same time, she wasn’t pretending they’re still close friends who regularly check in on each other. As Ringside News previously covered , Eva filed for divorce after 10 years of marriage. The couple originally met at a CrossFit gym and tied the knot in 2014, with their relationship becoming part of the storylines featured on Total Divas. Eva has also spoken about why she chose to keep the divorce private rather than turn the situation into a public spectacle. Now that the marriage is officially behind her, Eva seems perfectly comfortable wishing Jonathan the best without keeping him involved in her everyday life. She may not have found the perfect words immediately, but she eventually made her position pretty clear: there’s no major bad blood, but they’re not exactly buddies either. title: Eva Marie Opens Up On She Gave Up More Than Fans Realize in Divorce Settlement
raw_title: Eva Marie Reveals She Gave Up More Than Fans Realize in Divorce Settlement
summary_src: Eva Marie’s divorce is behind her, but getting to that point apparently cost her more than most people realize. The former WWE star says she gave up quite a bit during the split, but there was one thing she absolutely refused to lose — her name.
body: Speaking to Page Six , Eva revealed that her divorce from Jonathan Coyle was legally finalized around August 22, 2025. Even then, she still had some loose ends to clean up before she could really feel like that chapter was closed. One of the biggest remaining pieces was the Texas home she previously shared with Jonathan. Once the house was sold and the remaining assets were sorted out, Eva said she finally had everything in place to move forward. “It was finalized August 22nd, but then I was able to sell the house in Texas and get all those assets kind of dialed in.” Apparently, keeping the name wasn’t completely uncontested either. When asked whether Jonathan pushed back on it during the divorce, Eva admitted there was at least some resistance. “Um, a little bit, you know, which I understand to a certain degree because Natalie Eva Marie is a brand, you know.” “God gave me the platform, gave me the opportunity with WWE, gave me the platform that I have today, which I’m so grateful for, that if God gave it to me, He’s the only one that can take it away, and nobody else can do that.” “I go by Natalie Eva Marie. That is, like, my legal name. I got rid of my married name.” Eva may have walked away from the marriage giving up more than she expected, but her name was apparently the one thing that wasn’t negotiable. Natalie Eva Marie is now legally hers, and she made sure the identity behind her WWE career stayed with her as she moved into the next chapter. He focuses on delivering reliable coverage across WWE, AEW, and major wrestling promotions.

title: Raquel Rodriguez reflects on her WWE journey, special bond w/ Liv Morgan and father's influence

body: SAN DIEGO -- As Money in the Bank came to an end on October 10th, Raquel Rodriguez's Saturday night was far from over. She still had to make the five-hour drive from New Orleans to Bossier City, Louisiana. The two jumped into a car, and what started as another trip between WWE events turned into something resembling a ride in a DeLorean, transporting Rodriguez back to her childhood. “It almost feels like you know those road trips that we have going from New Orleans to Bossier City are the same road trips that we had going from Harlingen, Texas, to Corpus Christi to watch my dad wrestle, and that's something so beautiful,” Rodriguez said. González competed on the South Texas wrestling circuit during the 1980s and 1990s under the names Ricky "Desperado" González and Speedy González. Sometimes, his wrestling schedule kept him away from home. Other times, he would load up the family and bring them along to watch him compete. “It’s an amazing connection that I have with my dad, and I'm so grateful that I get to experience that with him,” Rodriguez said. After Rodriguez graduated from college and her basketball career came to an end, González encouraged her to follow in his footsteps and step inside the wrestling ring. Before her WWE tryout, her father took her to Laredo, Texas, for a practice match to help prepare her for the next chapter of her life. A decade later, Rodriguez has established herself as one of WWE's top female wrestlers, with her father supporting her every step of the way. “That's another reason that I'm able to wake up grateful,” Rodriguez said. “Because I can take my dad slash my driver slash my security with me on a lot of trips.” Rodriguez has held the championship for 84 days after defeating Sol Ruca on Monday Night Raw on July 27. She was struck in the nose earlier in the match but continued competing despite blood dripping from her face, knowing that a little spilled blood was nothing compared to the opportunity to capture her first singles championship in WWE. She is grateful to be the first Mexican woman to hold the championship, to travel around the world and to be part of The Judgment Day, one of WWE's longest-running factions. The Judgment Day has undergone several transformations since its original lineup featured Edge, Damian Priest and Rhea Ripley. The faction now consists of Rodriguez, Dominik Mysterio, Liv Morgan, JD McDonagh and Roxanne Perez. Rodriguez's connection to The Judgment Day began with Morgan, the current WWE Women's World Champion. Their partnership dates back to WrestleMania 39, when they competed against Becky Lynch and Trish Stratus. The two later captured the WWE Women's Tag Team Championship for the first time and have since enjoyed four championship reigns together. What began as a tag team partnership eventually blossomed into a friendship that Rodriguez considers a sisterhood. Speaking to ExtraTV on the red carpet for Street Fighter , the former Undisputed WWE Champion said gaming has become a major part of life on the road for WWE talent, replacing some activities that used to fill time after the cameras stopped rolling. "I'm not very good at it nowadays," Reigns admitted when asked about gaming. "But yes, that has been a positive replacement for some of the other extracurricular activities wrestlers would do." And with so many professional wrestlers now livestreaming their gaming sessions, it has also become another way for performers to connect with audiences when they're not competing in the ring. For Reigns, the relationship with video games started long before he became the Tribal Chief. "It was one of the ways that me and my cousins bonded," he recalled. "Back in the day, everybody was outside all the time, but that was one of the few things that could get us to stay inside." body: On the October 16 episode of WWE SmackDown, R-Truth battled Damian Priest in singles competition. During the match, Truth came off the top rope with a front dropkick, but failed to get to his feet. The referee checked on Truth and ended up stopping the match. On social media , Truth wrote, “I AM OK, Thank you ALL for your support, concerns and get well wishes , Wow, It truly feels amazing to feel and be loved I’m grateful for you all….On 10/16/2026 I almost passed away… Damien Priest tried to kill me,, I didn’t think he was ThAt serious…But ok, l’ll be back” I AM OK, Thank you ALL for your support, concerns and get well wishes , Wow, It truly feels amazing to feel and be loved I'm grateful for you all. …On 10/16/2026 I almost passed away… Damien Priest tried to kill me,, I didn't think he was ThAt serious… But ok, l'll be… pic.twitter.com/Q4nLOzBYEL
summary: During his singles match against Damian Priest on the October 16 episode of WWE SmackDown, R-Truth came off the top rope with a front dropkick and was unable to get back to his feet. The referee checked on him and stopped the bout. R-Truth later posted on social media that he is okay and expressed gratitude for the support and well wishes he received.

llm.summary: During his singles match against Damian Priest on the October 16 episode of WWE SmackDown, R-Truth came off the top rope with a front dropkick and was unable to get back to his feet. The referee checked on him and stopped the bout. R-Truth later posted on social media that he is okay and expressed gratitude for the support and well wishes he received.

llm_long: A match on SmackDown between R-Truth and Damian Priest was halted after Truth appeared to suffer an injury. Truth attempted a missile dropkick from the turnbuckle and stayed on the mat afterward while remaining conscious and moving.

The referee checked on Truth and then stopped the match, signaling the X sign to indicate a legitimate injury. Priest left the ring and retrieved a steel chair, but the referee intervened to prevent further action.
Fraxiom came to the ring to check on Truth as Priest dropped the chair and exited the area. Reports confirmed that the match stoppage was legitimate.

The original plan for the match had Priest winning followed by a post-match attack that Fraxiom would interrupt to make the save. Truth previously suffered a torn quad during an NXT match in November 2022 that required surgery and kept him sidelined for more than a year.

summary_src: Charles Crowley speaks about potentially signing with a major wrestling promotion to have the platform to show what he's capable of.
body: Charles Crowley speaks about potentially signing with a major wrestling promotion to have the platform to show what he’s capable of. Crowley is currently a staple of the independent scene not only in the UK but across the world, and is also a talented actor and voice actor, recently joining the Star Wars franchise, playing Biddy Blass in their recent racing video game. While speaking to Soundsphere Magazine in a recent interview, Charles Crowley spoke about wanting to be signed by a major promotion. “Of course I would absolutely love to get signed. We all want to be on WrestleMania. TNA has such a cool aesthetic, and the vibe of AEW is unmatched. I’ve spent a lot of time, effort, energy, and money on my promos as and when I can, and I can’t always do that because I’m a struggling artist, but it’s more just the platform to be able to show what I’m capable of… And I believe it will happen. Just got to keep grinding away, keep getting better every day, and just do my best. When I got into wrestling, someone said to me, ‘It’s all been done before, so don’t try and like recreate the wheel’. And I hated that. I’ve never fucking forgotten it, ever since then, I’ve tried to prove it wrong.”

Crowley expressed belief it will happen if he continues grinding and improving every day.

title: Billy Gunn calls Triple H's AEW joke a dick move
raw_title: Billy Gunn: Triple H’s AEW jab at D-X’s WWE Hall of Fame induction was a ‘d*ck move’
summary_src: In April of 2019, Billy Gunn was inducted into the WWE Hall of Fame as a member of D-Generation X. Gunn had just taken a job with Tony Khan’s All Elite Wrestling, which launched as a WWE “challenger brand” a few months earlier.
body: Link WWE.com In April of 2019, Billy Gunn was inducted into the WWE Hall of Fame as a member of D-Generation X. Gunn had just taken a job with Tony Khan’s All Elite Wrestling, which launched as a WWE “challenger brand” a few months earlier. Billy was given permission to take part in the ceremony, during which D-X star and WWE executive Shawn Michaels made a joke about the ROH/independent show ALL IN that served as proof of concept for AEW, and fellow D-Generate and higher-ranking exec Paul “Triple H” Levesque called it a “pissant company” . Gunn looked back on that moment in an interview he did last month with Inside The Ropes : “I knew it was coming. I kind of knew they were going to do something AEW because it was hot at the time and I was there and they were all wondering how I got to go there, and that’s because Tony Khan was super cool. I went, asked, and he said ‘100%. Of course you can. I would never hold you back from that.’ “I didn’t know what they were gonna do, but I knew they were going to do something. I also knew that if they were, Hunter was going to have something to say. Once I set myself up for that, I just let it go. The only one that got hurt out of that whole deal was him. I don’t want to say it, but it was a dick move. It was kind of trying to save face, and you didn’t need to because it’s going to happen. “It’s the wrestling business. It’s what we do. She wants actual stories to sink her teeth into, and that’s always been her favorite part of professional wrestling. Fans already got a taste of where things could be heading when Shotzi crossed paths with Rosemary and Allie. She’s not giving away exactly what’s coming, but she’s clearly excited about getting weird with those two on television. “Yes, that’s what really excites me because that’s my favorite part of pro wrestling — the storytelling and, you know, like how wild the stories get. title: R-Truth Breaks Silence on Scary WWE SmackDown Injury With Hospital Update
raw_title: R-Truth Breaks Silence on Scary WWE SmackDown Injury With Hospital Update
summary_src: R-Truth is finally speaking out after his scary injury on WWE SmackDown, and while the veteran Superstar says he’s doing okay, he’s also sharing a hospital photo that has fans concerned about what happened during his match against Damian Priest.
body: On October 19, 2026, R-Truth took to Twitter to address his condition following the October 16 episode of SmackDown. Truth thanked fans for their support and shared a photo of himself wearing a hospital gown while sitting in front of an MRI machine, smiling and giving a thumbs-up. Truth started by reassuring everyone that he’s doing okay and appreciating the overwhelming support he’s received since the incident. “I AM OK, Thank you ALL for your support, concerns and get well wishes , Wow, It truly feels amazing to feel and be loved I’m grateful for you all.” Of course, Truth couldn’t resist throwing in a little humor at Damian Priest’s expense. He joked that his former tag team partner nearly killed him during their match before making it clear that he intends to return. “…On 10/16/2026 I almost passed away… Damien Priest tried to kill me,, I didn’t think he was ThAt serious… But ok, I’ll be back” The update comes after R-Truth was legitimately injured during his match against Damian Priest on October 16. Truth landed awkwardly after delivering a missile dropkick from the top rope, prompting the referee to check on him and stop the match before its planned conclusion. The injury came during an already heated rivalry between Truth and Priest, who had been feuding since their tag team partnership fell apart. What was supposed to be another chapter in their storyline ended with a legitimate medical concern instead. Now Truth is giving fans some much-needed reassurance while making it clear that he isn’t finished with WWE just yet. The hospital photo might look concerning, but his message was positive, and he’s already talking about getting back into the ring. There’s still no official timetable for his return, but at least Truth hasn’t lost his sense of humor. title: "Sensational" Sherri passes away
raw_title: "Sensational" Sherri passes away - WWE
body: More Share Options More Share Options Share close facebook x threads email WWE is saddened to learn of the death of WWE Hall of Famer "Sensational" Sherri. She was 49. She passed away at her mother's home in Birmingham, Ala. Friday morning, according to her husband of 10 years, Robert Schrull. "It's a great loss to the wrestling world," he told WWE.com. The couple resided in St. Petersburg, Fla. In the early 1980s, Sherri began her career in the AWA. In 1985, she defeated Candi Devine to become the AWA Women's Champion. Their rivalry lasted more than a year, with the championship trading hands on several occasions. It was during this time that she began perfecting her skills as a manager, leading "Playboy" Buddy Rose and "Pretty Boy" Doug Somers to the AWA Tag Team Championship. On June 28, 1986, Martel would win the AWA Women's Championship for a third and final time from Candi Devine. On July 24, 1987, "Sensational" Sherri debuted in WWE, pinning her trainer and mentor the Fabulous Moolah to become Women's Champion. Sherri defended the gold against Debbie Combs, Velvet McIntyre, and Desiree Peterson. She quickly earned the reputation as someone who would do anything to win, even if it meant using unsavory tactics. Her rivalry with Moolah continued as they became the captains for the first-ever female Survivor Series teams in 1989. Sherri held the championship for 15 months before losing to Rockin' Robin. In the early ‘90s WWE phased out the Women's Division, leaving Sherri to focus on managing the male wrestlers. Her first client was "Macho Man" Randy Savage. It was during this time that she became "Sensation Queen." The couple had rivals with Miss Elizabeth, Hulk Hogan, Dusty Rhodes and Sapphire. In 1991, "The Million Dollar Man" Ted DiBiase enlisted her services. After that relationship dissolved, she took on the managerial duties of Shawn Michaels. In 1994, Sherri appeared in WCW as "Sensuous" Sherri managing Ric Flair during his rivalries with Sting and Hulk Hogan. After separating from Flair, she became "Sister" Sherri guiding Harlem Heat to seven WCW Tag Team Championships. Sherri was enshrined in the WWE Hall of Fame in 2006. "Million Dollar Man" Ted DiBiase was her presenter.
