title: NJPW adds two title matches to King of Pro Wrestling 2026
raw_title: NJPW adds two title matches to King of Pro Wrestling 2026
body: With the Destruction tour now over, NJPW is gearing up for its biggest event of the fall . Two new title bouts have been confirmed for NJPW King of Pro Wrestling 2026, which takes place from Sumo Hall in Tokyo on October 12. The event will see Gabe Kidd defend his IWGP Global Heavyweight Championship against Shota Umino. Plus, the NEVER Openweight Six-Man Tag Team titles will be on the line with United Empire (Will Ospreay, HENARE & Great-O-Khan) defending against Unbound Company (Yuto-Ice, OSKAR, and a partner to be announced). Umino is finally getting his rematch against Kidd after Kidd won the Global title in controversial fashion this July . In that bout, there was a pre-match angle where Kidd bloodied Umino and disrespected NJPW. Umino still chose to go forward with the defense and ended up losing his title. We were originally supposed to get a Kidd vs. Umino matchup in the G1 this summer, but Umino suffered a concussion that led to him forfeiting all but of one his matches in the tournament. Ospreay is heading back to Japan for the first time since winning the NEVER titles with HENARE & O-Khan in May. As tension between Ospreay and United Empire leader Callum Newman persists, we’ll see how that impacts the road to Wrestle Kingdom. Before King of Pro Wrestling, HENARE & O-Khan will put their IWGP Tag Team titles on the line against Yuto-Ice & OSKAR on October 6. title: IYO SKY Tapped For Women's Intercontinental Title Run
raw_title: IYO SKY Needs a Change: Four New WWE Directions
body: This is the direction WWE has already started to set up. Raquel Rodriguez has held the Women's Intercontinental Championship since beating Sol Ruca on the July 27 episode of Raw, and SKY challenged her in four-way title matches on WWE's South America tour in September. Rodriguez came out on top in each of those matches. SKY has never held the Women's Intercontinental Championship. She has already won the NXT Women's Championship, the WWE Women's Championship, the Women's World Championship and the WWE Women's Tag Team Championship. Rodriguez is part of The Judgment Day, which has targeted SKY on Raw for months, so a program between the two would build on a story that is already in place. It would also give the title a challenger who is a former Women's World Champion. SKY and Rhea Ripley , who teamed as Rhiyo, won the WWE Women's Tag Team Championship from The Kabuki Warriors on the January 5 episode of Raw. They held the titles for 53 days before losing them to Nia Jax and Lash Legend on the February 27 episode of SmackDown. Alexa Bliss and Tatum Paxley won the titles by beating Fatal Influence on the October 9 episode of SmackDown. Ripley is recovering from surgery for a torn meniscus and does not have a return date, so a Rhiyo reunion would have to wait. SKY teamed with Sol Ruca to beat Rodriguez and Perez on the August 10 episode of Raw. A run with Ruca would give both women something to do while Ripley is out, and the tag titles can be defended on either brand. SKY spent close to two years as a heel in Damage CTRL after debuting on the main roster with Bayley and Dakota Kai at SummerSlam in 2022. That run included her Money in the Bank win in 2023 and her cash-in on Bianca Belair at SummerSlam later that year to become WWE Women's Champion. She turned face in July 2024. A heel turn would change how she is presented after a string of near misses since SummerSlam. Losing to Morgan and falling short in a Money in the Bank qualifier give her reasons to be frustrated, and her run as a heel included her biggest singles win in WWE. On the other hand, she has become one of the more popular women on the roster as a face, and a turn would mean dropping her story against The Judgment Day. A brand switch would give SKY a new set of opponents. Chelsea Green holds the WWE Women's Championship and is set to face Morgan for the Women's Crown Jewel Championship at Crown Jewel . SmackDown also has Jade Cargill and Charlotte Flair, who are in the middle of their own issues after Cargill attacked Flair before the October 9 tag title match. The Women's Intercontinental Championship is the best option. WWE has already put her in title matches with Rodriguez on the road and had her name herself as the next challenger on Raw. Winning a title she has never held in WWE would give her a clear accomplishment after losing at SummerSlam, and she would be a champion who can work with almost anyone on the Raw roster. The referee checked on Truth and then stopped the match, signaling the X sign to indicate a legitimate injury. Priest left the ring and retrieved a steel chair, but the referee intervened to prevent further action.
Fraxiom came to the ring to check on Truth as Priest dropped the chair and exited the area. Reports confirmed that the match stoppage was legitimate.

The original plan for the match had Priest winning followed by a post-match attack that Fraxiom would interrupt to make the save. Truth previously suffered a torn quad during an NXT match in November 2022 that required surgery and kept him sidelined for more than a year.

title: WWE Stars Make Surprise Appearance at NASCAR Phoenix Race
raw_title: WWE Stars Make Surprise Appearance at NASCAR Phoenix Race
body: The Miz, whose real name is Mike Mizanin, is a longtime WWE wrestler who signed with the company in 2004. The 46-year-old out of Cleveland, Ohio is a two-time WWE champion and a former headliner of WWE’s largest show of the year, WrestleMania, in 2011. Paul Heyman is a longtime wrestling manager. In WWE, the 61-year-old wrestling legend has worked alongside some of the company’s biggest stars in history, including Brock Lesnar, CM Punk, and Roman Reigns. The two WWE stars were seen at the driver’s meeting prior to the Freeway Insurance 500 at Phoenix. “WWE’s Paul Heyman and The Miz are here in Phoenix,” wrote motorsports insider Bryan Nolen via X. The Miz and Paul Heyman were also spotted on pit road talking it up with Jeff Dickerson, owner of Spire Motorsports. “Spire owner Jeff Dickerson talking (& recruiting?) WWE’s Paul Heyman and the Miz,” via Braking Bob on X . Standing atop the spotter’s stand high above the 1.0-mile track, The Miz posted a “Miz Method” video to his Instagram. Noting how loud it is at a NASCAR race, Mizanin added the caption, “Yelling a Miz Method lesson at the top of my lungs and NASCAR still has me on mute.” “Team work makes the dream work. Everybody sees the driver but watch what happens around him when everybody does their job perfectly. Surround yourself with people who make you a better version of yourself,” Miz said in the video . The Miz and Paul Heyman are not the first WWE stars to make appearances at NASCAR races in the past, let alone this season. Last year at Las Vegas Motor Speedway, WWE women’s star Chelsea Green served as the honorary pace car driver. Tyler Reddick captured his sixth win of the 2026 NASCAR Cup Series season on Sunday at Phoenix. After overtaking Chase Briscoe following a late-race restart, the driver of the No. 45 drove to victory in the Freeway Insurance 500. Reddick, who has the most Cup wins of any driver this season, made up tremendous ground in the championship battle. While there are only three races left in the season, Reddick is 56 points behind points leader Kyle Larson in the seventh position. Larson finished a disappointing 34th after exiting the race early due to a right-front tire failure that sent him into the wall. Meanwhile, Christopher Bell went on to finish fourth and is now only five points behind Larson in the second position. Denny Hamlin wound up finishing 28th on Sunday after tire problems of his own. Despite the difficult finish, the driver of the No. 11 managed to gain points on Larson as he is now 31 points behind with three races left. John Breeden John Breeden is a NASCAR contributor at Heavy Sports. He has five years of sports journalism experience. He graduated from James Madison University in May of 2022 with a degree in media arts and design. John is also a sports reporter for the Daily News-Record in Harrisonburg, Virginia. Previously, John was a sports writer for JMU's The Breeze and a NASCAR content writer for Sportskeeda. More about John Breeden

title: How AEW Can Improve This New Concept — Clockwork Carnage
raw_title: Clockwork Carnage: How AEW Can Improve This New Concept
body: By Andrew Kelly Published Oct 19, 2026, 1:00 PM EDT Andrew Kelly is a pro wrestling writer from The Wirral, England. With bylines on many pro wrestling websites, Andrew has proven himself to be very knowledgeable in the realms of WWE, AEW and more. Andrew is one of TheSportster's Match Reviewers and has covered the best matches of superstars like Cody Rhodes, MJF, Bianca Belair and more. He's also written hundreds of lists and features covering wrestling current events and history. He is also an MA Graduate from the University of Manchester, and a BA Graduate from Liverpool John Moores University, both in Creative Writing. Sign in to your TheSportster account AEW hosted its first ever Clockwork Carnage match at the WrestleDream 2026 PPV, which saw Will Ospreay defend the AEW World Championship against a sea of talented opponents in Samoa Joe, Kazuchika Okada, Konosuke Takeshita, Mike Bailey, Ricochet, Adam Copeland and Darby Allin. The match itself was pretty fun, with non-stop action, brilliant in-ring work, and interweaving storylines, but it wasn’t perfect in execution. The Clockwork Carnage matchup is one that can stay on AEW programming, but there are improvements that must be implemented to make it better the next time around, in terms of booking, match structure, and rules. One of the biggest issues of AEW’s first Clockwork Carnage match was the predictability of the outcome. Will Ospreay won the AEW World Title as recently at All In: London 2026 and was the brains behind the creation of the bout, so there is no way he was losing, especially when you consider the rest of the field wherein there was no obvious alternative for AEW to book. In the future, AEW shouldn’t book such an obvious outcome - for instance it would have been harder to call had Ospreay been in the ring with bigger names like MJF, Kenny Omega, Jon Moxley and others. AEW booking any other championship across any division would provide more unpredictability than AEW’s top prize, or else they could have number one contenders determined in Clockwork Carnage showdowns. After Konosuke Takeshita & Mike Bailey got eliminated from Clockwork Carnage, the remaining six wrestlers battled it out for 15 minutes to score as many points as possible. This led to 11 falls in 15 minutes, which felt like a little overkill. Sure, it made sense for wrestlers to not exert energy in kickouts or tap out quicker than usual to avoid passing out, but there were still definitely way too many. It soon became clear that any finisher was going to score a point, whereas if it were harder to get a point on the board, then the whole match would have felt more intense, hard-to-call, and dramatic. Next time around, AEW should consider perhaps half the number of pinfalls and submissions for a more effective production. summary: The Clockwork Carnage matchup is one that can stay on AEW programming, but there are improvements that must be implemented to make it better the next time around. One of the biggest issues of AEW’s first Clockwork Carnage match was the predictability of the outcome.

body: Speedball Mike Bailey speaks on the events of AEW WrestleDream, noting that they are ‘seriously doubting themselves’ after the event. At WrestleDream, Speedball would compete in their first pay-per-view main event, competing in the Clockwork Carnage bout. Speedball would come up short, being eliminated before the second phase of the bout. While speaking on their AEW WrestleDream vlog , Speedball Mike Bailey noted that they are seriously doubting themselves following the events of the pay-per-view. “After last night, right, this is one of those moments where I’m seriously doubting myself. Because obviously what I want to be is the best professional wrestler in the world. I want to be the AEW world champion, and that’s not happening yet however yet however I fucking love pro wrestling. I love all of you. I’m going to keep doing what I do. I’m going to keep working hard. I’m going to keep trying. I’m going to keep living my passion, and it’s not going to be easy. But it’s going to be much better being surrounded and supported by people who love me than if I were on my own.” If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.

title: R-Truth updates fans after SmackDown injury scare
raw_title: WWE’s R-Truth breaks silence after match was stopped after he ‘almost passed away’
body: During the Oct. 16, 2026, edition of Friday Night SmackDown, WWE Superstar R-Truth's match against his former tag team partner Damian Priest was abruptly stopped, causing concern that he suffered a legitimate injury. According to the former 24/7 Champion, he "almost passed away" on Friday night, blaming Priest. He took to X, formerly Twitter, to share an update from the hospital . He smiled and had his thumb up while sitting on a CT scan machine. "I AM OK, Thank you ALL for your support, concerns and get well wishes," he wrote. "Wow, It truly feels amazing to feel and be loved I'm grateful for you all. "…On 10/16/2026 I almost passed away… [Damian] Priest tried to kill me,, I didn't think he was ThAt serious… But ok, l'll be back," R-Truth added. On Oct. 16, Truth and Priest faced in a singles match. Truth went for a top-rope dropkick, hitting the move but injuring himself in the process. The referee stopped the match, and WWE medical personnel came out to check on him. This didn't stop Priest from attacking him before Fraxiom (Axiom and Nathan Frazer) came out to stop him. It was later reported that Truth was "all right" and was going to be evaluated the following week. Luckily, it appears he is "OK," as he put it in his post. This is unlikely to be the final chapter in their feud. The tensions between Truth and Priest were boiling for months, and it came to a head in September 2026. Priest turned on Truth after they failed to win the AAA World Tag Team Championship from the War Raiders (Ivar and Erik). Truth and Priest have crossed paths several times over the last couple of years, dating back to the former trying to get into the Judgment Day stable in 2023. They later began teaming up and won the Tag Team Championship in March 2026, holding the titles for 147 days.
summary: During his October 16 match against Damian Priest on SmackDown, R-Truth injured himself on a top-rope dropkick, prompting the referee to halt the bout and bring out medical staff. Priest continued the attack until Fraxiom intervened. From the hospital, R-Truth posted a photo of himself on a CT scan machine giving a thumbs-up and stated he is okay while thanking fans for their support.

title: Ex-WWE Referee Shares Honest Take on WWE Championship Changing Hands So Quickly
raw_title: Ex-WWE Referee Shares Honest Take on WWE Championship Changing Hands So Quickly
body: Zayn is already in his second title reign in a matter of months. He first won the title at Night of Champions in June. That reign was short-lived, as CM Punk defeated him to become champion nine days later. Zayn’s second reign has lasted longer, approaching the 40-day mark. However, given that the WWE Championship has changed hands so quickly already, the title scene has become more unpredictable. “I don’t mind it under the right circumstances. When you have [superstars] like Sami Zayn, you’ve got [CM] Punk, you’ve got [Kevin Owens], you can even throw in Johnny Gargano, who’s finally got off the road cases. In the situation, if it’s presented correctly, I don’t mind it,” Korderas told The Game Plan . Despite the current circumstances on SmackDown, Korderas also believes that Roman Reigns’ lengthy reign makes sense on Raw. “On the other side, you look on the Raw side and Roman Reigns having basically a stranglehold on the championship over there, that works for that title in that situation. So again, it’s all situational.” Korderas explained why Roman Reigns ‘ World Championship reign makes sense as part of WWE’s long-term plans for Raw. The former WWE referee pointed to Reigns’ booking, as well as Oba Femi’s emergence, to explain why ‘The Tribal Chief’ should hold the title for longer. “Each story is different. Going back to Money in the Bank, when people talk about LA Knight, who had a great match against Roman Reigns. But if LA Knight wins the championship, if he beats Roman Reigns, then what? The long-term plan here is Oba Femi and Roman Reigns,” Korderas told The Game Plan . Korderas feels that once Oba Femi becomes champion, the moment will be more significant. “Let’s not get that confused. So people say, ‘Well, it’s okay if he loses it and then wins it back.’ No, it’s not okay. Because in that case, Oba Femi now has beaten someone who has already beaten Roman Reigns, as opposed to having two guys meet who look seemingly unbeatable.” Giancarlo Aulino Giancarlo Aulino is sports writer who covers UFC for Heavy.com. title: On the Record: Grayson Waller Calls Out WWE Stars Who “Complain and Moan” Online and to Dirt Sheets
raw_title: Grayson Waller Calls Out WWE Stars Who “Complain and Moan” Online and to Dirt Sheets
summary_src: Grayson Waller has a message for WWE stars who disappear from television and then start complaining about their booking online — do something about it. The current NXT Champion says he could have easily gone down that road himself, but instead, he went back to NXT and changed his own situation.
body: Speaking on NotSam Wrestling , Waller opened up about why returning to NXT became so important after things weren’t going the way he wanted on WWE’s main roster. For Waller, the first step was reminding himself just how good he could be when given the opportunity. That confidence certainly isn’t lacking anymore. Now that he’s sitting on top of NXT as champion, Waller believes RAW and SmackDown will eventually realize they dropped the ball with him. “Part of the reason that I wanted to go back to NXT was because I needed to remind myself first — that took the first few weeks. Now that I’m the NXT Champion, I know how good I am. Now my job is to remind the guys on RAW and SmackDown — hey, you fumbled the ball back, and you’re gonna regret it.” Waller then turned his attention toward wrestlers who handle their own frustrations very differently. He said some talent disappear from WWE television and immediately start complaining on social media or taking their grievances to wrestling dirt sheets. Waller made it clear that’s not how he wanted to handle his own situation. In his mind, wrestlers basically have two lanes when things aren’t working out, and he chose to actually make something happen rather than publicly complain about it. “You’ve got two lanes. Some wrestlers will disappear — they will go on Twitter and complain and moan and go to the dirt sheets and say certain things. But that’s not me.” Instead of waiting around for WWE to suddenly change its mind about him, Waller decided he needed to take control of what he could. Going back to NXT became his way of forcing the issue and rebuilding the momentum he felt he’d lost. “I sat there and went, ‘Things aren’t going the way I need them to go, so I’m gonna do something about it. I’m gonna make that happen for myself.’ And that’s exactly what I’ve done for myself.” Now Waller has the NXT Championship around his waist and a pretty big chip on his shoulder about proving WWE’s main roster wrong. If his plan was to make people pay attention again instead of complaining about being overlooked, he’s clearly convinced that returning to NXT did exactly that. title: Judge Upholds Maryland Child Victims Act in WWE Ring Boy Case
raw_title: Judge denies WWE and McMahons’ effort to throw out ring boy lawsuit on U.S. constitutional challenge to Maryland Child Victims Act
summary_src: A federal judge on Monday rejected an effort by WWE, its parent company TKO, Vince McMahon, and current U.S. Secretary of Education Linda McMahon, to
body: U.S. District Judge James K. Bredar ruled that the law is constitutional as applied to the case. The lawsuit may now move forward toward the discovery phase, where depositions are conducted, and evidence is exchanged. A teleconference is set for November 17 to set future deadlines. The case would still be at least several months away from a potential trial. Monday’s ruling does not address whether the alleged abuse happened or whether the defendants are responsible for it. The ring boys also overcame an earlier motion to dismiss in May , which narrowed the number of plaintiffs from eight to seven. Claims by two of the plaintiffs remain against Linda McMahon, while all seven proceed against Vince McMahon, WWE, and TKO. In 2023, Maryland passed the Child Victims Act, which eliminated any time limits for filing civil lawsuits related to child sexual abuse. If not for the new law, the statute of limitations on the plaintiffs’ claims would have expired years ago. The former ring boys allege they were abused in a variety of states but, importantly, they all claim that some of the abuse they were subjected to happened in Maryland. Maryland’s state-level Supreme Court upheld the Act in 2025, ruling that the law was valid under the state’s constitution, allowing this and other cases to move forward. But the defendants’ recent challenge was based on arguments related to the U.S. Constitution, which the Maryland Supreme Court decision couldn’t address, but which Monday’s ruling by Judge Bredar did. Bredar, however, is a federal judge at the district level. The defendants could eventually try to appeal his ruling to the higher appellate court, the Fourth Circuit Court of Appeals. In this context, a right to due process refers to a guarantee that people have under the Fourteenth Amendment, to not have their rights violated by unfair or arbitrary laws. WWE and the McMahons argued that Maryland did that by taking away their protection from these lawsuits by removing the time limit for bringing such cases to court. In his ruling, Bredar said the U.S. Constitution gives states broad power over lawsuit deadlines. A deadline to sue is a rule set by lawmakers, in this instance, the Maryland state legislature. And lawmakers can change those deadlines, Bredar ruled, even for very old claims. A court can strike down a change like this only if the change serves no purpose. The defendants did not “show how their particular hardships make the [Maryland Child Victims Act] arbitrary or irrational,” Bredar wrote. Instead, the defendants were trying to “hold the [Maryland] legislature to a stricter standard than is required under the Due Process Clause” of the Fourteenth Amendment. summary: A U.S. District Judge ruled the Maryland Child Victims Act is constitutional, allowing the ring boy lawsuit against Vince McMahon, Linda McMahon, WWE and TKO to proceed to the discovery phase. The case had already survived an earlier motion to dismiss that reduced the number of plaintiffs from eight to seven. Claims by two plaintiffs continue against Linda McMahon while all seven proceed against the remaining defendants; the ruling does not address the validity of the abuse allegations themselves.

title: Undefeated Farid Basharat Weighs In On UFC release: They don’t like the way I fight
raw_title: Undefeated Farid Basharat comments on UFC release: They don’t like the way I fight
summary_src: Farid Basharat believes his technical style isn't what UFC wants: "I think they're trying to go for brawlers."
body: 29-year-old Basharat confirmed his departure from the UFC roster recently, stating that the company “did not want to give me a new contract.” After a UFC campaign which saw him earn all but one of his wins via decision, Basharat believes his departure from the company comes due to his fighting style and what the UFC is hoping to receive from performers nowadays. “I don’t think I fit the direction they’re trying to move in,” Basharat said. “I think they’re trying to go for brawlers, spill your blood whether you win or lose type of stuff. Me, the way I fight, it’s just high IQ, intelligent, defeat the opponent where they’re weak and don’t fight them where they’re strong. And I just don’t think that’s where they’re going for.” Basharat later explained that he believes UFC is cultivating an audience which values finishes that end via finish, and doesn’t care as much about the actual level of skill being displayed. This goes against his fighting style, and he believes this type of company isn’t sustainable, he stated. “A lot of the fanbase are equating entertainment to finishes, and that’s just not the case … It’s sad that a lot of the fanbase is being brainwashed into believing that. I think the company, the UFC, is manufacturing a fanbase that doesn’t appreciate good quality fighting. They just appreciate these rock’em type fights where, even if it’s a mismatch, even if it’s a low-level fight, as long as there’s blood, as long as it’s a first-round finish, we’re happy. And in my opinion, you can’t build a sport off that. Because you might do well for a couple of years ratings-wise, but sooner or later it’s going to delegitimize the sport and the fans are going to be left wanting high-quality fights.” Basharat said he wasn’t sure where he would go next in his career, but assured fans he’s not done fighting. A potential avenue for him could be joining his brother, Javid, on the PFL/MVP MMA roster sometime down the line.

title: Legal Watch: Judge Rejects WWE and McMahons’ Attempt to Dismiss Ring Boy Lawsuit
raw_title: Judge Rejects WWE and McMahons’ Attempt to Dismiss Ring Boy Lawsuit
summary_src: WWE, TKO, Vince McMahon and Linda McMahon just took another loss in their attempt to shut down the “ring boy” lawsuit before it gets much further. A federal judge rejected their latest argument for dismissal, meaning the seven former ring boys can keep pushing their case toward discovery.
body: WWE and the McMahons argued that having to defend themselves after so much time has passed creates serious problems. Several people connected to the allegations are dead, including former WWF ring announcer Mel Phillips and former executives Pat Patterson and Terry Garvin, while other potential witnesses have also passed away. The judge found that states have broad authority when it comes to setting and changing deadlines for lawsuits. In his view, the defendants hadn’t shown that Maryland acted irrationally by reopening the door for childhood sexual abuse claims. “Defendants do not show how their particular hardships make the [Maryland Child Victims Act] arbitrary or irrational.” “Instead, Defendants attempt to hold the [Maryland] legislature to a stricter standard than is required under the Due Process Clause.” The judge didn’t completely brush aside the problems that come with litigating allegations from the 1980s and 1990s. He simply made it clear that his job at this stage wasn’t to decide whether those problems make the lawsuit harder to defend, but whether Maryland had the constitutional authority to change its law. In the end, Bredar found that Maryland lawmakers had a legitimate reason for removing the old time limit. “But the Court’s role here is to interpret the United States Constitution and to resolve disputes that arise under it. The Maryland General Assembly created its statute of limitations for child sexual abuse claims and, in response to a legitimate and pressing issue, decided to alter it in a rational way.” This ruling absolutely does not mean the seven plaintiffs have proven their allegations. Bredar wasn’t deciding whether the alleged abuse happened or whether WWE, TKO or either McMahon was responsible, and the defendants have denied the central claims in the lawsuit. The seven men say they were minors when they were sexually abused while working around WWF events in the 1980s and 1990s . All seven accuse Phillips of abuse, while one also alleges abuse by Patterson and another alleges sexual harassment involving Garvin. Their lawsuit claims WWE and the McMahons were negligent in allowing the alleged conduct to happen. This also isn’t the first time the plaintiffs have survived an attempt to stop the case . An earlier ruling left seven plaintiffs moving forward, with all seven pursuing claims against Vince McMahon, WWE and TKO, while two still have claims against Linda McMahon. There’s also still a chance this latest ruling gets challenged. Bredar is a federal district judge, meaning the defendants could eventually try taking the issue to the Fourth Circuit Court of Appeals, but POST Wrestling reported that they hadn’t immediately responded when asked whether an appeal was coming. So this isn’t a verdict against WWE or the McMahons, but it is another attempt to stop the case that didn’t work. This week, I’m looking at the best ring technicians in WWE’s men’s divisionn and the performers whose in-ring limitations are becoming increasingly difficult to ignore. In his years in NXT, Carmelo Hayes rose to the top based on his ability to put on captivating matches. His remarkable athleticism, fluid transitions, creative offense, and convincing selling allowed him to deliver exciting, fast-paced matches with a variety of opponents. He shined as the NXT Champion and seemed destined for greatness on the main roster. As the newest member of the 946, Hayes finally finds himself as an important player in a top program. Positioned alongside WWE’s hottest new faction in its battle against the Bloodline, Hayes has the spotlight like never before. His affiliation with the group gives him an identity and a purpose beyond simply being a great wrestler, and allows him to share mic time in a way that can help mask any weaknesses in his promo game. One thing’s for sure: He will elevate the quality of any match he’s involved in. For the first time, Hayes has a legitimate shot at becoming a major player on Raw. The suit notes that the State Attorney’s Office ultimately dropped all charges. Montalvo is demanding a trial by jury and requesting compensatory and punitive damages, as well as declaratory relief against all named parties. In August 2015, Montalvo was arrested for trespassing after being warned to leave WWE property, leading to WWE seeking and receiving an injunction against him in an attempt to keep him from trespassing on the WWE Performance Center property in Orlando, Florida as there had been multiple incidents of Montalvo showing up demanding a job, threatening talent and even throwing and smearing feces on the Performance Center building. Undeterred, Montalvo returned to the PC on 8/31/15. Montalvo plead not guilty to all charges. During a Sheriff's media conference following the 2015 incident, Montalvo was described as being "fixated" on a female WWE performer. llm.headline: Man Shot Outside WWE Performance Center Files Lawsuit
llm.summary: Armando Alejandro Montalvo, who was shot and arrested outside the WWE Performance Center in August 2015, has filed a civil lawsuit. The suit names WWE, Performance Center Manager David Bailey, the Orange County Sheriff’s Office, two deputies, Aspire Health Partners and Walmart as defendants. Per PWInsider, Montalvo also claims he was targeted and falsely charged with trespassing at a Walmart location in June 2020.

llm_long: A man shot outside the WWE Performance Center in 2015 has filed a civil lawsuit. Armando Alejandro Montalvo named World Wrestling Entertainment Inc. and several other parties as defendants in the case filed in federal court in Florida.

The lawsuit was submitted in May with an amended complaint filed last month. It names WWE Performance Center Manager David Bailey, the Orange County Sheriff’s Office, two individual deputies, Aspire Health Partners Inc., and Walmart Inc. as co-defendants.

Montalvo claims he was targeted in a separate incident at a Walmart store in June 2020. He alleges store management and deputies worked together to bring false criminal trespass charges against him, which were later dropped by the State Attorney’s Office.

In 2015 Montalvo was arrested for trespassing at the Performance Center after being warned to leave the property. He had previously shown up multiple times demanding a job, threatening talent, and smearing feces on the building.

Montalvo returned to the facility on August 31, 2015, and acted out as a wrestler while banging on the doors. When police arrived he engaged with them and was shot, then hospitalized and charged with aggravated assault on a law enforcement officer, resisting arrest, and trespassing.

The suit seeks a jury trial along with compensatory damages, punitive damages, and declaratory relief against all named parties. WWE had previously obtained an order of protection against Montalvo following the earlier incidents.

title: US Issues Security Alert Before WWE Crown Jewel
raw_title: New Middle East security alert issued ahead of WWE Crown Jewel
summary_src: The situation in the Middle East remains volatile with WWE Crown Jewel 2026 now less than three weeks away.
body: The situation in the Middle East remains volatile with WWE Crown Jewel 2026 now less than three weeks away. On October 18, the US State Department Bureau of Consular Affairs i ssued a new security alert advising that Americans in the region should “exercise heightened vigilance” due to the ongoing complex security environment. The alert urged Americans traveling to or from the Middle East to monitor information about airport and airline operations and to have a contingency plan in place if their original travel plans get disrupted. The alert applies to 12 countries, including Saudi Arabia. The State Department’s travel advisory for Saudi Arabia remains at a level three, which means Americans citizens are advised to reconsider traveling there amid the strikes that have been carried out by the Iranian-supported Houthis group. WWE Crown Jewel is still being promoted for Saturday, November 7 in Riyadh as part of the annual Riyadh Season festival. A backup location in the United States is on the table if WWE does end up needing to change its plans. A star-studded tennis tournament was supposed to be held in Riyadh this week but has been postponed to December . The Future Investment Initiative, a major investment conference nicknamed “Davos in the desert” has also been postponed . The conference was scheduled to begin next week but has been moved to 2027, with the new dates to be announced. Roman Reigns vs. Sami Zayn and Liv Morgan vs. Chelsea Green to determine the ceremonial Crown Jewel Champions for 2026 are official for the November 7 PLE. title: WWE Shut Down Grayson Waller’s Plan to Wear Stephanie Vaquer’s NSFW Championship Photo on NXT
raw_title: WWE Shut Down Grayson Waller’s Plan to Wear Stephanie Vaquer’s NSFW Championship Photo on NXT
summary_src: Grayson Waller tried to bring Stephanie Vaquer’s nearly naked championship photo to WWE television, but somebody backstage clearly wasn’t having it.
body: The WWE Superstar revealed that he had a T-shirt made featuring Vaquer’s viral Instagram photo, where she posed wearing nothing but the Women’s World Championship. His plan was to wear the shirt on NXT, but WWE put the brakes on that idea before it ever made it in front of the cameras. During an appearance on NotSam Wrestling , Waller was talking about his habit of wearing shirts designed to get under other wrestlers’ skin. He’s gotten away with plenty over the years, but apparently putting Vaquer’s barely covered body across his chest was a little too much for WWE. Waller explained that he had the shirt made after seeing the photo Vaquer posted to Instagram , which paid tribute to Shawn Michaels’ famous championship pose. The shirt was ready to go, but WWE never allowed him to wear it on NXT. “There’s some that haven’t ended up on TV. I don’t know if you remember that Stephanie Vaquer broke the internet recently. She did an Instagram story like Shawn Michaels — there was a T-shirt with that on it. That didn’t end up on TV.” “If anyone wants it, you can buy it. There’s some fan who will pay some crazy money for it.” Waller also admitted that even he has some boundaries when it comes to trolling other WWE stars. He loves stirring the pot, but he’d prefer to pick on somebody who can actually step into the ring with him afterward. That’s where the Vaquer shirt became a bit of a problem, since the two aren’t exactly going to settle their differences in a singles match. “I love to cause chaos, but I think if I can’t fight you, if we can’t fight after this, then that’s the line. Stephanie Vaquer doesn’t feel like we won’t have a match — that’s where my line is.” Vaquer originally shared the revealing photo after the October 5 episode of RAW, using the Women’s World Championship to cover herself in a pose that immediately drew comparisons to Shawn Michaels. The image took off online, and apparently Waller figured it would look even better on a shirt during NXT. Vaquer has since lost the Women’s World Championship to Liv Morgan at Money in the Bank , but her viral photo nearly got another moment on WWE television thanks to Waller’s latest attempt at stirring up trouble. Instead, WWE shut it down, and Waller is now sitting on a shirt he thinks some fan will pay ridiculous money to own. Considering his track record of trolling just about everybody, it’s probably only a matter of time before he finds another way to get himself in trouble. title: Ospreay Retains AEW World Title at WrestleDream
raw_title: Ospreay Retains AEW Title in Clockwork Carnage Thriller
body: DMFirst Veer Game Ospreay Retains AEW Title in Clockwork Carnage Thriller By Kendall Jenkins on 2026-10-19 12:02:00 Ospreay Survives Eight-Man Gauntlet War to Keep AEW Gold at WrestleDream Will Ospreay walked out of WrestleDream on Sunday, October 18, 2026, still holding the AEW World Championship after beating seven opponents in the promotion's first-ever Clockwork Carnage match. The stipulation forced Ospreay into a brutal two-stage format, starting as a gauntlet with staggered entrances before shifting into a 15-minute scored-fall period once eight men had entered. It was a chaotic, physically demanding structure that tested every competitor in the field. Ospreay drew the first entrance, meaning he would have to face all seven challengers to keep his title. Konosuke Takeshita came in second, followed by Ospreay's United Empire teammate 'Speedball' Mike Bailey as the third entrant. Bailey, a Canadian wrestler, was among the group chasing the title before Takeshita pinned him to eliminate him from advancing to the second stage. Ricochet entered fourth, and Darby Allin, the TNT Champion, came in fifth carrying a table that would factor into the match later. International Champion Kazuchika Okada arrived sixth, and Adam Copeland made his entrance as the seventh competitor shortly after Bailey's elimination. Joe pulled level with Allin and Ospreay by locking in the Coquina Clutch on Ospreay, then went for another Musclebuster before Copeland speared him out of it to claim his first fall of the match. Copeland then equalized again with a spear on Ricochet with just over a minute remaining, and a follow-up spear on Okada briefly put him in position to walk away as champion. With Copeland's retirement plans looming and Ospreay now having survived one of AEW's most grueling title defenses yet, the promotion heads into its next chapter with its World Championship picture wide open for fresh challengers.
summary: Will Ospreay retained the AEW World Championship in the promotion's first Clockwork Carnage match at WrestleDream on October 18 2026. The two-stage bout began as an eight-man gauntlet with staggered entrances before transitioning into a 15-minute scored-fall period once all competitors were in the ring. Ospreay started first and outlasted Konosuke Takeshita, Mike Bailey, Ricochet, Darby Allin and three other opponents to keep his title.

The show will be available for purchase in the United States through PPV.com, HBO Max, Amazon, DAZN, Fubo, YouTube, and cable or satellite providers. International fans in the UK and other markets can access it via MyAEW.
AEW scheduled the event only three weeks after All Out. Some television time during that period was used to pay tribute to PAC rather than advancing storylines.
The main event will be a new Clockwork Carnage match for the AEW world championship. The match combines elements of a Casino Gauntlet in its first phase and an Iron Man format in its second phase.

Eight wrestlers will compete across two phases. The Entry Phase begins with two competitors and adds a new entrant every three minutes until all have entered, with any wrestler pinned or submitted during this phase being eliminated.

Surviving wrestlers advance to the 15-minute Scoring Phase, where the competitor with the most pins or submissions is declared the AEW world champion. The defending champion Will Ospreay faces challengers Samoa Joe, Kazuchika Okada, Ricochet, Adam Copeland, Konosuke Takeshita, Speedball Bailey, and Darby Allin.

llm_long: Billy Gunn commented on the incident involving CM Punk that led to his departure from AEW. The event occurred after what had been viewed as one of the biggest returns in wrestling history, ultimately resulting in the end of Punk's relationship with the promotion after two years.

Gunn, who serves as a coach in AEW, stated that he was not present for the incident. He noted that some veterans will not tolerate certain behavior and suggested that attempting to challenge them can lead to consequences.

He indicated that he was not familiar with all the details of the situation and chose not to follow the related media coverage. Gunn emphasized that the specifics remain between those directly involved.

When asked about handling similar issues during his earlier career, Gunn pointed to the approach taken under Vince McMahon. He explained that wrestlers were expected to conduct business professionally regardless of personal feelings.

Gunn described a method of addressing conflicts privately by pulling individuals into a room to resolve problems immediately. He contrasted this with current practices, calling the shift away from such discretion unfortunate.
Following the incident, Punk received a suspension from AEW. He made a return one year later before being fired after a separate event at All In 2023.

body: After competing on WWE’s house show tour in Hawaii, Bayley flew home to help Kirk Whit’s Big Time Wrestling celebrate its 30th anniversary. Bayley started attending Big Time Wrestling shows as a teenager and then began her career there at 18 years old. The indie promotion held its 30th anniversary show in San Jose, California on Sunday (October 18). The card included names like Rob Van Dam, Andrade El Idolo, Mustafa Ali, Bandido, Mike Bailey, and Zoey Serrano — and Bayley also stopped by to be part of the festivities. At the show, Bayley gave a speech in the ring thanking the fans. She then showed up as the impromptu special guest referee during a match between Aaron Solo (her ex-fiance) and Chazz “Starboy” Hall. Bayley went to stop Solo from using a title belt as a weapon, which led to her accidentally striking him in the face with the belt. She then counted the pin after Hall hit a reverse rana, a dive to the outside, and a Shooting Star Press. During the speech she gave, Bayley pointed out that her mother and some of her friends were in the crowd at the show. Bayley was in action at both of WWE’s house shows in Honolulu, Hawaii this weekend. Sol Ruca defeated IYO SKY, Bayley, and Lyra Valkyria in a four-way match on Friday night’s card . title: Jonathan Coachman Questions WWE’s Decision to Drag John Cena Into Nikki Bella-Paige Feud
raw_title: Jonathan Coachman Questions WWE’s Decision to Drag John Cena Into Nikki Bella-Paige Feud
summary_src: Jonathan Coachman isn’t a fan of WWE dragging John Cena into Nikki Bella’s current storyline with Paige. In fact, the former WWE commentator thinks the company is outright disrespecting Cena by repeatedly using his history with Nikki as part of the rivalry.
body: Speaking on The Coach & Bro Show , Coachman questioned why WWE is still leaning so heavily on a relationship that ended years ago. Nikki and Cena were together for several years and were engaged before splitting in 2018, but both have long since moved on with their lives. Coachman pointed out that Cena is now married, making WWE’s decision to keep bringing up his past relationship with Nikki even stranger to him. “How long ago did Nikki Bella date and do that reality show with John Cena? Probably more than five years ago. Cena is either married or in a long-term relationship with a beautiful young lady that resembles Nikki Bella.” Paige teased the Five Knuckle Shuffle before Nikki stopped her, while Nikki later put Paige in Cena’s STF. Paige then went even further by hitting Nikki with an Attitude Adjustment for a near fall. For Coachman, that wasn’t just a couple of harmless wrestling callbacks. He felt WWE was deliberately making Cena’s old relationship with Nikki part of the story and questioned why the company would want to do that to one of its biggest stars. “So you put Nikki and Paige in a rivalry, and in the match, they do the ‘AAA,’ and the announcers say, ‘Clearly, that’s disrespecting because she dated Cena.’ Then Nikki did an STFU because that’s one of Cena’s moves.” Coachman then directly questioned WWE’s creative thinking behind the whole thing. From his perspective, repeatedly connecting Nikki to Cena this many years later doesn’t do Cena any favors, especially when he’s moved on from that part of his life. “Vince, as a creative, if you’re doing that, why are we doing storylines that completely disrespect John Cena at this point?” Coachman also sees another problem with the angle: newer WWE fans might not even understand what they’re supposed to be watching. Nikki and Cena’s relationship was once a huge part of WWE’s reality television world, but that doesn’t necessarily mean every current viewer knows the history behind Paige using an Attitude Adjustment against her. “And the new people probably don’t even know what they’re watching.” Whether WWE keeps leaning into the Cena references remains to be seen, but Coachman has made his position pretty clear. He thinks the company is digging up old history at Cena’s expense when Nikki and Paige should be able to make their feud personal without him. summary_src: Cody Rhodes and Charlotte Flair are getting some Hollywood company for their upcoming interview, and the mystery guest has finally been revealed. Ice Cube’s son, O’Shea Jackson Jr., is joining the two WWE stars for a special sit-down with Paul Heyman’s son, Jacob Heyman.
body: Jackson confirmed the news on Monday, October 19, revealing that he’ll be part of The Roundtable , which premieres Wednesday, October 21, on Heyman Hustle TV. The actor made the announcement in an Instagram post shared with the platform, joking that fans probably weren’t expecting him to be the surprise guest. And naturally, he couldn’t resist calling himself the heel of the group. “I know what you’re thinking. ‘There’s no way…’ That’s right folks Wednesday October 21st you will be able to catch the roundtable convo between @americannightmarecody @charlottewwe @jacob.heyman. And the heel that you love to hate. Me.” Jackson, who portrayed his father Ice Cube in the 2015 movie Straight Outta Compton , then dropped the jokes and explained how much the opportunity meant to him. He described the conversation as surprisingly personal and even therapeutic. “All fun aside, this was truly an honor to even be able to sit with Charlotte, Cody, and Jacob. An amazing conversation and look into things from their perspective. And honestly very therapeutic. I’m so grateful to everyone involved and my friends over at @heymanhustletv for even thinking of ya guy. You will not wanna miss this.” The announcement ends the mystery that started Friday when Charlotte Flair revealed that she and Cody Rhodes would be sitting down with Jacob Heyman alongside an unnamed special guest. Heyman Hustle TV had already started teasing the project on October 8, asking why The Roundtable would show a side of Cody Rhodes that fans had never seen before. The interview also comes as Cody has been opening up about his life outside the ring. title: Ospreay Retains AEW Title in Clockwork Carnage Thriller

body: DMFirst Veer Game odds uden om ROFUS Ospreay Retains AEW Title in Clockwork Carnage Thriller By Kendall Jenkins on 2026-10-19 12:02:00 Ospreay Survives Eight-Man Gauntlet War to Keep AEW Gold at WrestleDream Will Ospreay walked out of WrestleDream on Sunday, October 18, 2026, still holding the AEW World Championship after beating seven opponents in the promotion's first-ever Clockwork Carnage match. The stipulation forced Ospreay into a brutal two-stage format, starting as a gauntlet with staggered entrances before shifting into a 15-minute scored-fall period once eight men had entered. It was a chaotic, physically demanding structure that tested every competitor in the field. Ospreay drew the first entrance, meaning he would have to face all seven challengers to keep his title. Konosuke Takeshita came in second, followed by Ospreay's United Empire teammate 'Speedball' Mike Bailey as the third entrant. Bailey, a Canadian wrestler, was among the group chasing the title before Takeshita pinned him to eliminate him from advancing to the second stage. Ricochet entered fourth, and Darby Allin, the TNT Champion, came in fifth carrying a table that would factor into the match later. International Champion Kazuchika Okada arrived sixth, and Adam Copeland made his entrance as the seventh competitor shortly after Bailey's elimination. Joe pulled level with Allin and Ospreay by locking in the Coquina Clutch on Ospreay, then went for another Musclebuster before Copeland speared him out of it to claim his first fall of the match. Copeland then equalized again with a spear on Ricochet with just over a minute remaining, and a follow-up spear on Okada briefly put him in position to walk away as champion. With Copeland's retirement plans looming and Ospreay now having survived one of AEW's most grueling title defenses yet, the promotion heads into its next chapter with its World Championship picture wide open for fresh challengers.

title: On the Record: Vince Russo Blasts WWE Agents Over Bron Breakker’s Scary Neck Landing at Live Event
raw_title: Vince Russo Blasts WWE Agents Over Bron Breakker’s Scary Neck Landing at Live Event
summary_src: Bron Breakker’s nasty neck landing at a recent WWE live event has Jonathan Coachman wondering why the spot was happening in the first place.
body: Speaking on The Coach & Bro Show , Coachman reacted to footage of Breakker crashing down around his neck and upper body during WWE’s October 17 live event. Breakker was attempting his top-rope Frankensteiner on Knight when things went wrong, leading to the frightening landing. Coachman admitted he couldn’t tell exactly what was supposed to happen. However, if Knight made the mistake that caused Breakker’s fall, he believes nearly injuring somebody WWE views as a major star is exactly the kind of thing that can create backstage heat. “Not quite sure if he was supposed to land there or whatever was supposed to happen. Someone’s getting heat for that, and I’m guessing it’s LA Knight. That’s the kind of stuff, if indeed it was his fault and you almost hurt one of the cash cows, that’s a way to get heat. I’m not saying he has it.” Coachman was careful not to claim Knight actually has backstage heat, since he doesn’t know who was responsible for the spot going wrong. His bigger problem was Breakker attempting the move at all during a live event. Breakker regularly uses the Frankensteiner, but Coachman already considers it dangerous. With Breakker working late on the card and the ring potentially getting slick as the show went on, he couldn’t understand why the risk was necessary at a non-televised event. “If you’re Breakker, and I know you do that move — that move, which I think is dangerous — and he’s doing it, he’s always on at the end of the show, and everything is slick, why are we doing that move in front of 6,000 people in Hawaii at a house show?” Vince Russo took the conversation in a different direction and put more of the responsibility on WWE’s producers and agents. Russo argued that the mentality backstage has changed from the days when protecting important talent was treated as protecting the company’s ability to make money. According to Russo, agents also don’t necessarily know everything wrestlers plan on doing during their matches anymore. Even when they do, he doesn’t believe most producers today approach risky spots with the same business-first mentality he remembers from previous generations. “Number one, this isn’t the way it used to be, where the talent was in on the entire match. Bredar of the District of Maryland rejected the defendants’ latest attempt to dismiss the survivors’ claims. At issue was the constitutionality of Maryland’s Child Victims Act of 2023, which eliminated time limits for filing civil lawsuits involving childhood sexual abuse. The law recognizes that survivors often delay disclosing abuse due to the lasting effects of trauma, giving them an opportunity to pursue justice when they are ready to come forward. DiCello Levitt, together with Murphy, Falcon & Murphy, represents the survivors in John Doe 1 et al. v. World Wrestling Entertainment, LLC et al. “This ruling is a significant victory for our clients and for other survivors of childhood sexual abuse who have waited years for the opportunity to seek justice,” said Greg Gutzler, a partner at DiCello Levitt who leads the litigation. “Trauma does not follow a legal deadline, and Maryland’s Child Victims Act recognizes that reality. Our clients have waited years to hold those responsible accountable. We will not stop fighting until their voices are heard and they have their day in court.” The ruling follows the court’s December 2025 decision largely denying the defendants’ earlier motions to dismiss. The WWE Ring Boys sexual abuse lawsuit alleges that WWE employees, including ringside announcer and ring crew chief Melvin Phillips Jr., recruited underage boys to assist with wrestling events and used their positions to groom, exploit, and sexually abuse them. The plaintiffs further allege that WWE leadership, including Vince and Linda McMahon, knew or should have known about the abuse but failed to take reasonable steps to prevent it. However, those discussions did not lead to a return, and no timeline was provided for his comeback. llm_long: A U.S. District Judge ruled that Maryland's Child Victims Act is constitutional as applied to the lawsuit filed by former WWE ring boys. The decision allows the case to proceed to the discovery phase, where depositions will be conducted and evidence exchanged. A teleconference is scheduled for November 17 to establish future deadlines.

The ruling does not determine whether the alleged abuse occurred or if the defendants bear responsibility. The case remains several months away from any potential trial. The ring boys had previously overcome a motion to dismiss in May that reduced the number of plaintiffs from eight to seven.

Claims by two plaintiffs continue against Linda McMahon, while all seven plaintiffs proceed with claims against Vince McMahon, WWE, and TKO. The former ring boys allege abuse in multiple states but claim some of the incidents took place in Maryland.

Maryland enacted the Child Victims Act in 2023, removing time limits for filing civil lawsuits involving child sexual abuse. Without the law, the statute of limitations on the plaintiffs' claims would have expired years earlier. Maryland's state Supreme Court upheld the Act in 2025 under the state constitution.

The defendants challenged the law on U.S. Constitutional grounds, specifically arguing it violated due process rights under the Fourteenth Amendment by eliminating protections from old lawsuits. The federal judge determined that the U.S. Constitution grants states broad authority over lawsuit deadlines.

summary_src: Ludwig Kaiser just took a loss in court. The WWE Superstar’s attempt to get his misdemeanor battery charge thrown out was denied on October 19, and newly updated court records reveal that Kaiser personally took the stand during the hearing.
body: According to court records obtained by Ringside News , the judge denied Kaiser’s motion to dismiss following Monday’s hearing in Orlando, Florida. The ruling means the battery case against Kaiser, whose real name is Marcel Barthel, will continue, with a pretrial conference now scheduled for December 17, 2026. And the hearing wasn’t just a quick appearance before the judge. The court docket confirms that Kaiser was sworn in and testified as a defense witness, while Richard Reap, the man accusing him of battery, also took the stand for the prosecution. The state also introduced evidence during the proceedings, including a CD admitted as State’s Exhibit 1 and four photographs entered as a composite exhibit marked State’s Exhibit 2. The docket doesn’t explain what the CD contains or what the photographs depict. The court also invoked the rule of sequestration, a procedure generally used to keep witnesses from hearing each other’s testimony before taking the stand. As Ringside News previously covered , Kaiser was arrested in May following an April 23 confrontation with Reap at an Orlando apartment complex. Reap accused Kaiser of punching and pushing him during an argument, while Kaiser’s legal team maintained that he was acting in self-defense. Kaiser’s attorneys had filed a motion seeking dismissal under Florida’s Stand Your Ground law , arguing that Reap was the aggressor and that Kaiser acted to protect himself and Bazarte. The defense also accused Reap of making threats involving Immigration and Customs Enforcement. For now, Kaiser is still facing the misdemeanor battery case, and his next scheduled court date is December 17. With both Kaiser and his accuser already having testified and the judge refusing to toss the charge, this legal battle is far from finished. title: Evolution of Triple Threat Matches in Pro Wrestling
raw_title: THEN, NOW, FOREVER – Triple Threat Matches: The Rock vs. Undertaker vs. Kurt Angle, Brock Lesnar vs. John Cena vs. Seth Rollins, more
body: Because of their frequency in contemporary pro wrestling, it’s hard to imagine that once upon a time, a triple threat match, triangle match, or three-way dance was a special attraction that happened very rarely. I remember when I started watching ECW in 1997. They talked about a mythical match dubbed The Night the Line Was Crossed. The match was special and talked about as something extraordinary, which intrigued me as a fan for several reasons. First, because of the three wrestlers involved: Sabu, Shane Douglas, and Terry Funk. Second, the match went to a 60-minute draw. Third, it was a three-way dance, something that was still very rare at the time. Over the last 20 years, the triple threat match has increased in frequency to the point that it is no longer a special attraction. It has become increasingly commonplace, frequently appearing on WWE television every week. Many fans complain that the triple threat match has become too common and is often used as a crutch to ensure a protected wrestler doesn’t have to take the fall. However, a well-designed and well-executed three-way match can still be a work of art. In fact, I would argue that some of the best matches in WWE history have been triple threat matches. What makes a triple threat different, and what makes one special? With three wrestlers involved, the pacing is often faster, and the action can remain nearly nonstop while still allowing sufficient time for selling. Adding another competitor also increases the chances of an upset or a surprise finish. Near falls can become more dramatic, further emphasizing the unpredictability of the contest. As with any match stipulation, there are good versions of triple threat matches that are booked for the right reasons and executed well, and there are bad versions that feel like little more than a watered-down singles match. Sometimes, a triple threat match diminishes a feud that would have been more important and substantial as a one-on-one contest. In other words, the whole can become less than the sum of its individual parts. In this week’s article, I’ll look at three triple threat matches that exemplify the stipulation done right. Chaos is the one word that could describe the WWF Championship picture during the first eight months of 2002. By the time Brock Lesnar won the championship at SummerSlam, he had become the sixth WWE Champion of the calendar year. Some chaos is good because it creates unpredictability and a sense that anything can happen. However, too much chaos can be detrimental. When the boat is constantly rocking, it’s hard to stay on your feet and pay attention. None of the competitors is able to maintain control for long, and the match never settles into a predictable rhythm. One of the things that made this match stand out at the time was the relatively rare sight of wrestlers stealing one another’s finishers. While that has become commonplace in contemporary wrestling, this was one of the earliest examples I can remember seeing
summary: Triple threat matches were once rare special attractions as seen in ECW's 1997 Night the Line Was Crossed bout featuring Sabu, Shane Douglas and Terry Funk that ended in a 60-minute draw. Over the past two decades the format has become commonplace on WWE television and is frequently criticized for being overused as a booking device to protect certain wrestlers from taking a loss. The piece examines multiple notable examples from wrestling history.

title: Judge Denies Ludwig Kaiser's Motion To Dismiss Battery Case
raw_title: Judge denies Ludwig Kaiser’s motion to dismiss battery case
summary_src: The battery case against WWE star Ludwig Kaiser is moving forward after a judge denied his motion to dismiss.
body: The battery case against WWE star Ludwig Kaiser is moving forward after a judge denied his motion to dismiss. A hearing regarding the motion was scheduled for today (October 19), and court records list the motion as being “denied.” A pre-trial conference is scheduled for December 17, 2026, where the two sides will attempt to figure out a resolution or decide if the case is going to trial. Kaiser’s defense was attempting to get the misdemeanor battery charge against him dismissed under Florida’s “Stand Your Ground” law. The argument was that Kaiser was justified in using the amount of force he used against the alleged victim (Richard Reap) because he reasonably believed it was necessary to protect himself and his girlfriend Andre Bazarte from “imminent use of unlawful force.” The case stems from an April incident between Kaiser and Reap at the Orlando, Florida apartment complex they lived at. Both sides agree that Kaiser and Bazarte were being affectionate toward each other in an elevator, but their stories differ from there. Reap claims he told the couple to “please have some manners,” which led to Kaiser attacking him. Kaiser says Reap swore at him and Bazarte, along with making a racist remark about calling ICE on Bazarte. A pre-trial conference is set for December 17 2026 to determine whether the case will proceed to trial or reach a resolution.

Kaiser's defense sought dismissal under Florida's Stand Your Ground law. The argument claimed he used necessary force to protect himself and his girlfriend from imminent unlawful force by the alleged victim Richard Reap. The incident occurred in April at an Orlando apartment complex where both men lived.

Both parties agree that Kaiser and his girlfriend were being affectionate in an elevator. Their accounts diverge afterward with Reap stating he asked the couple to have manners before Kaiser attacked him. Kaiser claims Reap swore at them and made a racist remark about calling ICE on his girlfriend.

Kaiser acknowledges pushing Reap after Reap moved toward him aggressively. According to Kaiser he did not retaliate when Reap threw a soft drink bottle at him and instead left the area with his girlfriend. Police reports indicate surveillance video showed Kaiser punching and pushing Reap and that Reap had a visible scratch on his head.

The state entered a CD and four photos into evidence believed to be elevator surveillance footage and images of Reap's injuries. Reap has retained a personal injury attorney which may signal plans for a civil suit against Kaiser.

title: WWE Not in Discusses to Extend Saudi Arabia Deal Beyond WrestleMania 43
raw_title: WWE Not in Talks to Extend Saudi Arabia Deal Beyond WrestleMania 43
summary_src: WWE may be getting ready to hit the brakes on making any new long-term commitments to Saudi Arabia.
body: “#WWECrownJewel is happening because @TKOGrp and @WWE still have money to collect on prior site-fee commitments and need to secure the deposit tied to #WrestleMania43.” So Crown Jewel going ahead doesn’t necessarily mean WWE is already planning the next round of Saudi shows. In fact, Avignon claims the opposite is happening behind the scenes right now. “I’m told there haven’t been meaningful talks about renewing or extending the Riyadh Season relationship beyond the current commitments.” That’s where things get especially interesting considering everything happening in the region. Political and security tensions have been escalating, and Avignon believes TKO executives Ari Emanuel and Mark Shapiro are more interested in finishing the business they already have than signing WWE up for anything else right now. “With political tensions in the region escalating, it looks like Ari Emanuel and Mark Shapiro are trying to finish the existing business, collect what’s owed, and avoid locking WWE into anything new for now.” Basically, the claim is that WWE isn’t walking away from a pile of money that’s already on the table, but TKO also doesn’t appear eager to immediately put more WWE events on that table. Once WrestleMania 43 is finished, the company could have a much bigger decision to make. That doesn’t mean TKO itself is done doing business in Saudi Arabia. Avignon noted that Zuffa Boxing still has a relationship there, so this isn’t being framed as the company completely packing its bags and leaving the market. “Saudi Arabia still has the @Zuffa_Boxing relationship, so TKO isn’t exactly walking away from the market.” “This looks more like WWE finishing the chapter already on the books before deciding what comes next.” The timing certainly isn’t great for WWE’s Saudi relationship. Crown Jewel is scheduled for November 7 in Riyadh, while recent attacks and travel disruptions have already created questions about how WWE will safely get its wrestlers, staff and production operation into and out of the country. The U.S. State Department has also warned Americans in the Middle East about potential flight cancellations , airspace closures and further travel disruptions. King Khalid International Airport has shown signs of returning to operation following a lengthy shutdown, but the situation remains anything but normal. None of this means WWE has decided to pull out of Saudi Arabia once WrestleMania 43 is over. The key part of Avignon’s report is simply that meaningful extension talks apparently aren’t happening right now, which is pretty notable considering how important Saudi events have become to WWE’s business over the years. For now, WWE appears to still have money to collect and shows to run before it can close the book on anything. Once those obligations are handled, however, what happens next between WWE and Riyadh Season suddenly looks a lot less certain.htt H Jenkins H Jenkins has been breaking pro wrestling news on Ringside News for nearly a decade

title: Backstage Buzz: WWE’s Backstage Reaction to Bron Breakker’s Scary Neck Landing
raw_title: WWE’s Backstage Reaction to Bron Breakker’s Scary Neck Landing
summary_src: Bron Breakker’s scary neck landing looked like the kind of thing that could get somebody in serious trouble backstage, but apparently WWE isn’t playing the blame game here. In fact, the word backstage is basically to no-sell the whole thing, hope Breakker is fine and move on.
body: During a recent Q&A, JoeyVotes and TC of WrestleVotes were asked what WWE’s reaction was after Breakker’s nasty fall at the October 17 live event. According to WrestleVotes, people backstage don’t seem interested in turning the accident into a bigger story than it already is. “People backstage are like, ‘Let’s no-sell this a little bit and hope he’s done.’” Breakker was teaming with Bronson Reed and Austin Theory against Oba Femi, LA Knight and Penta when everything went wrong. He tried going for his usual top-rope Frankensteiner on Knight, but Knight slipped out and Breakker came crashing down around his neck and upper body. It looked brutal, and the referee immediately went over to check on him. Breakker somehow kept going and finished the match, but there still hasn’t been an official announcement from WWE about whether he suffered an injury. WrestleVotes believes Breakker was almost certainly checked out after the match. At the same time, WWE apparently wants to get past the whole thing pretty quickly rather than keep drawing attention to it. “I’m sure there were medical personnel checking on him. But at the same time, they want to get over this quickly.” “It was a house show — it was probably a simple sort of mistake. There’s no heat on anybody.” For now, WWE apparently wants this to be nothing more than one very scary house show mistake. Nobody’s getting blamed, nobody’s catching heat, and if Breakker is okay, it sounds like the company would be more than happy to put the whole thing behind them. llm_long: A judge denied a motion to dismiss the battery case against WWE performer Ludwig Kaiser. The hearing on the motion took place on October 19 and court records show it was denied. A pre-trial conference is set for December 17 2026 to determine whether the case will proceed to trial or reach a resolution.

Kaiser's defense sought dismissal under Florida's Stand Your Ground law. The argument claimed he used necessary force to protect himself and his girlfriend from imminent unlawful force by the alleged victim Richard Reap. The incident occurred in April at an Orlando apartment complex where both men lived.

Both parties agree that Kaiser and his girlfriend were being affectionate in an elevator. Their accounts diverge afterward with Reap stating he asked the couple to have manners before Kaiser attacked him. Kaiser claims Reap swore at them and made a racist remark about calling ICE on his girlfriend.

Kaiser acknowledges pushing Reap after Reap moved toward him aggressively. According to Kaiser he did not retaliate when Reap threw a soft drink bottle at him and instead left the area with his girlfriend. Police reports indicate surveillance video showed Kaiser punching and pushing Reap and that Reap had a visible scratch on his head.

The state entered a CD and four photos into evidence believed to be elevator surveillance footage and images of Reap's injuries. Reap has retained a personal injury attorney which may signal plans for a civil suit against Kaiser.

title: Legal Watch: Reason Behind Montez Ford’s WWE Absence Amid Lawsuit
raw_title: Reason Behind Montez Ford’s WWE Absence Amid Lawsuit
summary_src: Montez Ford’s WWE absence suddenly looks a lot less mysterious. With Ford now facing a lawsuit over his viral RAW interaction with a security guard, some fans naturally wondered if that’s why he’s disappeared from television, but apparently the two have nothing to do with each other.
body: During a recent Q&A, WrestleVotes was asked straight up whether Ford’s time away was connected to the lawsuit. According to the backstage word they’ve received, Ford is actually off television because he and Bianca Belair recently welcomed a new addition to their family. “Montez Ford and Bianca Belair recently welcomed an addition to their family. So, according to people we speak to, that’s the reason he’s off TV.” WrestleVotes then addressed the lawsuit itself and noted that WWE managed to keep the situation pretty tightly under wraps before it eventually became public. “This lawsuit was kept as quiet as it could be before it broke.” The lawsuit was filed by Noel Lucas, an off-duty Cook County Sheriff’s officer who was working security during the July 6 episode of Monday Night RAW . Lucas is suing Ford, WWE and WWE subsidiary Event Services, LLC over Ford’s interaction with him during The Street Profits’ entrance. Lucas alleges Ford performed an unwanted sexualized “lap dance” directly in front of him. The lawsuit includes 14 counts, including assault, battery, intentional infliction of emotional distress and alleged violations of the Illinois Gender Violence Act. Things got even more attention after another camera angle of the incident surfaced . That footage puts Lucas’ reaction in clearer view, showing him sitting almost completely still during the interaction before giving a blank stare and shaking his head once Ford moved away. Apparently, that’s not the case. WrestleVotes’ backstage word is that Ford’s absence is about his family, while the lawsuit is an entirely separate situation that happened to become public while he was already away. That doesn’t make the lawsuit itself disappear, but it does clear up one big question surrounding Ford right now. As things stand, there’s no reported punishment keeping him off WWE television, and his absence isn’t being blamed on the legal drama. title: On the Record: Billy Gunn says Triple H calling AEW a “pissant company” was a “dick move”
raw_title: Billy Gunn says Triple H calling AEW a “pissant company” was a “dick move”
body: WWE Hall of Famer Billy Gunn spoke with Kenny McIntosh in an interview published to the Inside The Ropes YouTube channel. Here is an excerpt… McIntosh: “In January 2019, you signed with AEW, the new company that was starting up. Then, that April, you went into the WWE Hall of Fame with D-Generation X. Of course, the crowd started chanting for AEW, and Hunter [Triple H] had to get on the microphone and say Vince [McMahon] would buy that ‘pissant company’ just to fire you again. I know you’ve said you’ve let it go, but in the moment, or when you went backstage afterward, was there a conversation about what that was all about, or did you just accept it for what it was?” Gunn: “No, because I knew it was coming. I kind of knew they were going to do something about AEW because it was hot at the time, and I was there. They were all wondering how I got to go there, and that was because Tony Khan was super cool. They were going to stick us in, so I went and asked him, and he said, ‘100%.’ He said, ‘Of course you can. I would never hold you back from that.’ I didn’t know what they were going to do, but I knew they were going to do something. I also knew that Hunter was going to have something to say about it. Once I prepared myself for that, I just let it go. The only one who got hurt out of that whole deal was him. I don’t want to say it, but it was a dick move. It was kind of an attempt to save face, and you didn’t need to because it was going to happen. That’s the wrestling business. That’s what we do, and that’s what they like to stir up. When you have somebody in another company, and I’m not trying to be egotistical, but I’m sure a lot of people didn’t think I was going to make it because I worked for another company. Then, when you see me, they have to do something. It’s like an unwritten rule in a book: if another guy is in another company, we have to say something and do something.”

title: Ring Boy Lawsuit Advances Against WWE
raw_title: Ring boy plaintiffs get ‘significant victory’ as lawsuit against WWE, McMahons moves forward
summary_src: The “ring boy” plaintiffs suing WWE, TKO, and Vince & Linda McMahon got a “significant victory” in court today as their lawsuit was allowed to continue. Post Wrestling reports that federal judge James K.
body: The “ring boy” plaintiffs suing WWE, TKO, and Vince & Linda McMahon got a “significant victory” in court today as their lawsuit was allowed to continue. Post Wrestling reports that federal judge James K. Bredar ruled on October 19 that the Maryland Child Victims Act is constitutional as applied to the case . The suit from the seven anonymous plaintiffs will now move into the discovery phase ahead of a potential trial, which Post Wrestling says would still be at least several months away. The lawsuit concerns WWE’s ring boy scandal of the 1980s and 1990s, where former ring announcer Mel Phillips is accused of having recruited teenagers to the ring crew for the purpose of sexually abusing them. All of the plaintiffs have alleged abuse by Phillips. One also alleges that he was abused by Pat Patterson, while another says they were sexually harassed by Terry Garvin. In 2023, the Maryland Child Victims Act was passed and allowed for victims of childhood sexual abuse to bring civil lawsuits no matter how long ago the alleged abuse happened. WWE, TKO, and the McMahons, in their attempt to get the lawsuit dismissed, argued that their constitutional rights relating to due process were being violated. With the alleged abuse having happened decades ago and with key figures like Phillips, Patterson, and Garvin being deceased, WWE, TKO, and the McMahons said it would be too difficult to litigate the case. Judge Bredar admitted that the timeframe could make it difficult to gather evidence but said the Maryland Child Victims Act was a rational way to address the statute of limitations concerning childhood sexual abuse claims. Greg Gutzler, the lead attorney for the plaintiffs, said after today’s ruling: Post Wrestling says WWE, TKO, and the McMahons did not immediately respond to a question from the outlet regarding whether they plan to appeal Bredar’s decision. The case, centered on alleged sexual abuse of teenagers working as ring crew in the 1980s and 1990s by Mel Phillips with additional claims against Pat Patterson and Terry Garvin, will now enter the discovery phase. Per the Wrestling Observer, the development represents a significant victory for the plaintiffs with a potential trial still months away.
