llm_long: A U.S. District Judge ruled that Maryland's Child Victims Act is constitutional as applied to the lawsuit filed by former WWE ring boys. The decision allows the case to proceed to the discovery phase, where depositions will be conducted and evidence exchanged. A teleconference is scheduled for November 17 to establish future deadlines.

The ruling does not determine whether the alleged abuse occurred or if the defendants bear responsibility. The case remains several months away from any potential trial. The ring boys had previously overcome a motion to dismiss in May that reduced the number of plaintiffs from eight to seven.

Claims by two plaintiffs continue against Linda McMahon, while all seven plaintiffs proceed with claims against Vince McMahon, WWE, and TKO. The former ring boys allege abuse in multiple states but claim some of the incidents took place in Maryland.

Maryland enacted the Child Victims Act in 2023, removing time limits for filing civil lawsuits involving child sexual abuse. Without the law, the statute of limitations on the plaintiffs' claims would have expired years earlier. Maryland's state Supreme Court upheld the Act in 2025 under the state constitution.

The defendants challenged the law on U.S. Constitutional grounds, specifically arguing it violated due process rights under the Fourteenth Amendment by eliminating protections from old lawsuits. The federal judge determined that the U.S. Constitution grants states broad authority over lawsuit deadlines.

summary_src: Jordynne Grace has been missing from WWE television for months, but apparently fans shouldn’t read that as a sign she’s heading out the door. The latest backstage word is much simpler — WWE just doesn’t have a creative spot for her right now.
body: During a recent WrestleVotes Q&A, JoeyVotes and TC were asked what’s actually going on with Grace and when fans might see her again. Joey said the specific thing he’s heard recently is that Grace simply isn’t included in WWE’s current creative plans. “The thing that I’ve heard recently is she’s not in the creative plans. That doesn’t mean they don’t want plans for her.” Joey pointed to just how crowded the women’s side of SmackDown has become. WWE already has several ongoing stories eating up television time, and with the show back to two hours, somebody inevitably gets squeezed out. “But when you look at where she is on the women’s roster, they’ve got full-blown stories. They’ve got Fatal Influence, Charlotte’s group, Jade Cargill’s group — that’s one story. They’ve got Tiffany with the briefcase. They’ve got Nikki and Paige and Chelsea Green — that’s another story.” For Joey, Grace’s disappearance isn’t some huge mystery or indication that WWE has suddenly soured on her. He believes it’s basically a numbers problem when WWE only has so much television time to spread around. “Numbers thing. How many different female stars can you feature on a two-hour SmackDown? Someone can’t always be featured, and she unfortunately falls under that category.” TC then pushed back on any idea that Grace could be on her way out of WWE. Based on the people he’s spoken with, that’s not the impression he’s getting at all. “She isn’t on her way out — that’s not the sense based on the people I have spoken to.” Grace hasn’t exactly been sitting around waiting for the phone to ring, either. She recently spent several weeks secretly preparing for a bodybuilding competition , something TC believes WWE may simply be allowing her to finish before figuring out where she fits next. “It’s one of those things, like, when you’re done with the bodybuilding, we’ll see where we can plug you in where we might not need you.” TC also used Johnny Gargano as an example of how quickly things can change in WWE. Gargano went months without much happening before suddenly finding himself right back in the mix once WWE had something for him. “Look at Johnny Gargano — did nothing for months and then now finds himself in a number one contender’s match, Money in the Bank qualifying match. title: C4 Wrestling Holds Final Ottawa Show November 27
raw_title: C4 Wrestling Running Final Event At Preston Event Center On November 27
summary_src: C4 Wrestling is set to leave the Preston Event Center. On Monday, C4 announced that they will hold their final event at the Preston Event Center in Ottawa on November 27. The event will be their 19th anniversary show.
body: On Monday, C4 announced that they will hold their final event at the Preston Event Center in Ottawa on November 27. The event will be their 19th anniversary show. At the time, Ottawa wasn’t exactly known as a hotbed for independent professional wrestling. Over the years, the region has seen its share of promotions come and go. Some found success, but very few managed to sustain it. Many were one-off events, short-lived organizations, or groups that simply burned themselves out. When I launched C*4, my goal was simple: to bring Ottawa the best independent professional wrestling possible. It wasn’t about perceived star power. It wasn’t about superficial appearances, outdated beliefs, or an old boys club deciding what professional wrestling in this city should look like. It was about giving talented people opportunities. Allowing wrestlers to face opponents they might never otherwise have the chance to work with. Building relationships with the larger independent wrestling world. Giving local talent a platform where their work could be seen beyond Ottawa, rather than having their opportunities begin and end here. There were people who doubted us. There were people who wanted us to fail. But here we are. We made our own path. And if it all ended tomorrow, I think most would agree that C*4 has left a lasting mark, not just on professional wrestling in Ottawa, but on Canadian independent wrestling as a whole. Over the years, we’ve faced countless challenges. Some bigger than others. But we’ve always found a way forward. And now, as we prepare to enter our twentieth year, we’re facing another massive challenge. For a long time, we’ve been looking ahead to 2027 as a year of celebration. Twenty years of C*4 is something I never could have imagined when we started, and we ve been working toward making it something truly special. Unfortunately, a few months ago, we received news that completely changed those plans. Almost overnight, we went from planning how to celebrate our twentieth year to figuring out how to survive it. On November 27th, C*4 Wrestling will celebrate our 19th anniversary. It will also be our final event at the Preston Event Centre. After nine years, we will be saying goodbye to a building that has become synonymous with C*4 Wrestling. This wasn’t our decision. Due to circumstances beyond our control, continuing at Preston is simply no longer possible. That said, we understand the circumstances surrounding the situation, and we have nothing but appreciation for the years we’ve spent there. Some of the greatest nights in C*4 history happened inside those walls, and we’ll always look back on our time there fondly. Not an announcement we were looking forward to making, but here we are. You can find results from around the wrestling world at Fightful’s results section .
summary: C4 Wrestling will present its 19th anniversary event as the final show at the Preston Event Center in Ottawa on November 27. The promotion launched with the goal of delivering the best independent wrestling to the area by providing opportunities for talent, creating unique matchups and building connections with the wider independent scene. Over the years Ottawa has seen many short-lived promotions come and go while C4 sustained operations.

title: WWE’s Internal Reaction to Ilja Dragunov Joining AEW
raw_title: WWE’s Internal Reaction to Ilja Dragunov Joining AEW
summary_src: Ilja Dragunov’s jump to AEW apparently isn’t causing any hard feelings inside WWE. In fact, the latest backstage word is that people who worked with Dragunov are happy for him and WWE management isn’t holding his decision against him either.
body: During a recent WrestleVotes Q&A, JoeyVotes and TC were asked how WWE reacted to Dragunov showing up at WrestleDream and officially becoming All Elite . According to WrestleVotes, the people who know Dragunov personally were happy to see him land somewhere else. That attitude apparently goes beyond just Dragunov’s friends. WrestleVotes said there isn’t some automatic resentment backstage whenever somebody leaves WWE and decides they can make better money somewhere else. “There is no animosity when it comes to talent leaving and going to get their bag.” “We talked about how people in WWE were suggesting Sheamus go to AEW and not be disrespected by the offer he was getting from AEW. Go out there and get your money.” When it comes specifically to Dragunov, WrestleVotes said the feeling is basically the same from both sides of the curtain. His friends are happy for him, and even management apparently isn’t bitter about seeing him become part of AEW. “From that side of things, they wish him well. From the management side of things, they wish him well.” That makes Dragunov’s departure a little more interesting than simply WWE deciding it was finished with him. The latest report suggests the company would have preferred things to work out differently, but once Dragunov made his move, there wasn’t any backstage grudge over it. Dragunov officially debuted for AEW at WrestleDream after his WWE contract expired in August and visa issues delayed his arrival. Tony Khan quickly made things official afterwards, confirming that the former WWE star had signed with the company. Dragunov has since explained that he wanted a fresh environment where he could “breathe ,” find new competition and avoid feeling stuck. He didn’t specifically blame WWE for that feeling, instead framing AEW as the new landscape he needed at this stage of his career. So while Triple H apparently didn’t want to lose Dragunov, WWE isn’t treating his AEW move like some kind of betrayal. The backstage reaction sounds much more like wishing him well, letting him chase what he wants and moving on without any bad blood. title: Where Things Stand With WWE Running Another Evolution Event
raw_title: Where Things Stand With WWE Running Another Evolution Event
summary_src: WWE fans hoping Evolution would finally become an annual event probably shouldn’t get too excited. Despite the positive reaction to last year’s all-women’s PLE, the latest word is that another Evolution isn’t expected anytime soon.
body: “The only thing I can say about Evolution, going back to the first Evolution in 2018 — the running tale within WWE is the show drew lesser numbers on the WWE Network viewership, both live and replay, than most of the TakeOvers around that time, which they were not happy about.” “They seemed to get over that last year, but now it is nowhere to be found. I don’t think it’s coming soon.” TC doesn’t necessarily think that’s a bad thing either. Instead of WWE forcing Evolution onto the calendar every year, he believes spacing the shows out could actually help keep the concept feeling special. “It’s better off every couple of years, where you’re not shoehorning it, since it feels special when it pops up on the calendar. All-women’s wrestling is not everyone’s cup of tea.” Joey then got to what may be the biggest issue from WWE’s perspective — the numbers. According to him, an all-women’s event simply doesn’t attract the same level of audience as WWE’s regular major programming, making the company less interested in pouring the same resources into it. “It doesn’t draw as many eyeballs as a RAW or SmackDown or PLE does. WWE doesn’t want to put the resources in for something that isn’t going to return the same type of numbers that a standard PLE would.” That’s a pretty different picture from the optimism coming out of last year’s Evolution. Rhea Ripley openly pushed for the event to become annual , saying the women had proven what they could do and hoping fans would come away believing WWE needed to run the show every year. For now, that doesn’t appear to be happening. WWE hasn’t announced Evolution 3, and if the latest word is accurate, fans could be waiting a while before the all-women’s PLE makes another comeback. The door doesn’t sound permanently closed on Evolution, but yearly shows apparently aren’t part of the plan. WWE may instead treat the event as something that comes around every few years when the timing and business make sense. title: Ex-WWE Official Shares Honest Take on Behind-the-Scenes Content
raw_title: Ex-WWE Official Shares Honest Take on Behind-the-Scenes Content
body: The former WWE referee spent 22 years with the company and witnessed several changes. However, the company’s content, including Unreal on Netflix and LFG on A&E, has given fans a behind-the-scenes look. Fans now have a better idea of what goes into the creative aspects of WWE’s programming. Additionally, they can learn more about what the training is like for WWE superstars as they put matches together. WWE sharing behind-the-scenes content can be viewed as a sign that the company is adapting to the times. However, former referee Jimmy Korderas feels that some areas should still be protected. “I think putting it out there the way they do on shows like Unreal , it makes me question, too, because this industry is predicated on making your audience believe something that isn’t real. So is Unreal just that? It’s not real, but we’re going to make people believe it is? So maybe the greatest work of all, where they’re making people think, ‘See, I told you so,’ and ‘No, that wasn’t what it was,’ but they’re going to make you believe it.” “I’m not entirely convinced that all of what you see on that show is in fact legit, and nothing more than just another television show.” YouTube has been a platform for WWE to post vignettes and retrospectives of certain feuds. Superstars have also used X to generate additional interest. “It’s one of those things in today’s wrestling in 2026, now going into 2027, it’s completely different how you run angles. We’ve seen a lot of times on WWE where they’ll run angles on their social media, as opposed to running them on TV,” Korderas told The Game Plan . “And people would say, ‘Why wouldn’t you run it on TV? That’s where the biggest audience is.’ But now we’re finding out that some of the stuff that [WWE streams] online is getting more views than what people would have seen on television, on Netflix, or wherever.” “It makes you think, especially me, like the old head me going, ‘That should have been on TV.’ Yeah, but it’s on social media, and it got 12 million views. Maybe that was the right decision.” Giancarlo Aulino Giancarlo Aulino is sports writer who covers UFC for Heavy.com. He began writing for Heavy in 2025 after providing MMA coverage for Sportskeeda. Giancarlo is an experienced journalist and interviewer, having covered soccer clubs Toronto FC and Inter Toronto FC as a full-season reporter, and also producing sports coverage for Toronto radio station VIBE 105.5FM. title: El Grande Americano Motion To Dismiss Denied
raw_title: Latest On Criminal Case Against El Grande Americano, Wwe's Marcel Barthel
body: DMFirst Veer Game odds uden om ROFUS LATEST ON CRIMINAL CASE AGAINST EL GRANDE AMERICANO, WWE'S MARCEL BARTHEL By Mike Johnson on 2026-10-19 18:04:00 There was a hearing earlier today in Orlando, Florida related to the misdemeanor battery charge against WWE star Marcel Barthel aka Ludwig Kaiser aka El Grande Americano before the County Court of the Ninth Judicial Circuit, in and for Orange County, Florida. The hearing was regarding Barthel's motion to dismiss, where Barthel argued for a dismissal on the grounds that Barthel's use of force was legally justified and that he was immune from criminal prosecution under Florida law. Both Barthel and Richard Reap, who filed the charges against him testified at the hearing. At the end of the hearing, Barthel's motion to dismiss was denied with a new pre-trial hearing set for 12/17. Barthel was arrested in May on charges of battery, pleading not guilty after learning of a warrant for his arrest on charges of battery and traveling from Mexico to Florida to turn himself in to authorities. A arrest affidavit stated that Orlando Police responded to an apartment complex (we are not publishing the address) at approximately 6:37 PM on 4/23 following reports of a physical altercation on the 12th floor of the building. The complainant, identified as Richard Reap, told officers that he entered an elevator around 6:30 PM and encountered Barthel alongside an unidentified woman. Reap alleged that the pair were acting in what he described as an “uncontrollably intimate” manner while inside the elevator. Reap stated that after exiting onto the 12th floor, he told the couple to “please have some manners.” According to the affidavit, Reap alleged that Barthel immediately responded by punching him multiple times, pushing him to the ground, and threatening additional violence. Barthel's attorney, in the motion to dismiss, argued that he used only non-deadly force, was lawfully present in the common area of his apartment complex, and reasonably believed his actions were necessary to protect both himself and his girlfriend from imminent unlawful force. The motion emphasizes that Florida law does not require a person in those circumstances to retreat before defending themselves. The filing cites Florida's Stand Your Ground statutes, arguing that Barthel has established a "prima facie" claim of self-defense. Under the cited law, the defense contends the burden now shifts to the State to prove by clear and convincing evidence that Barthel was not entitled to statutory immunity. Since his arrest, Barthel's attorneys filed a motion to secure the video footage from the elevator, which one would think would prove what took place during the incident.

The judge denied the motion to dismiss per PWInsider, scheduling the next pre-trial hearing for December 17.

Kaiser's defense sought dismissal under Florida's Stand Your Ground law. The argument claimed he used necessary force to protect himself and his girlfriend from imminent unlawful force by the alleged victim Richard Reap. The incident occurred in April at an Orlando apartment complex where both men lived.

Both parties agree that Kaiser and his girlfriend were being affectionate in an elevator. Their accounts diverge afterward with Reap stating he asked the couple to have manners before Kaiser attacked him. Kaiser claims Reap swore at them and made a racist remark about calling ICE on his girlfriend.

Kaiser acknowledges pushing Reap after Reap moved toward him aggressively. According to Kaiser he did not retaliate when Reap threw a soft drink bottle at him and instead left the area with his girlfriend. Police reports indicate surveillance video showed Kaiser punching and pushing Reap and that Reap had a visible scratch on his head.

The state entered a CD and four photos into evidence believed to be elevator surveillance footage and images of Reap's injuries. Reap has retained a personal injury attorney which may signal plans for a civil suit against Kaiser.

The Attitude Era had "Stone Cold" Steve Austin, quickly followed by The Rock after a neck injury took the Texas Rattlesnake down. The Ruthless Aggression Era was ruled by John Cena . And whatever this new era is called has seen Roman Reigns sit at the head of the table since the awful babyface days of the "Big Dog." Roman Reigns has been a near-constant champion as the Tribal Chief for over half a decade. His non-stop run at the top is comparable to Triple H 's "Reign of Terror" on Raw from the early 2000s, but this time there's one difference which makes Roman's reign so much worse than what The Game did. Roman Reigns has been the face of WWE ever since the Shield came to an end. With Cena's time at the top winding down, Vince McMahon needed a new big dog to lead the company into a new decade. Enter Reigns as a babyface so generic that the boos outweighed the cheers. For years, Reigns' character never changed as he continuously main evented WrestleMania. Reigns' legacy was stuck in the mud until one of the most brilliant heel turns in history. As the Tribal Chief and the head of the Bloodline, Reigns created a character so compelling that it became must-see TV. Who will ever forget Sami Zayn's hilarious turn in the group or Cody Rhodes' two-year finishing of his story? When the American Nightmare finally took down the Head of the Table at WrestleMania 40, it could have been a transitional moment. Instead, after a short time away from the title scene, Reigns is back on top, his hold on the gold worse than ever. Roman Reigns' own reign of terror isn't stopping anytime soon. At Crown Jewel, WWE Champion Sami Zayn will surely be defeated and the 946 only exist to lose to the Bloodline at Survivor Series: WarGames . title: Billy Gunn on AEW’s “Brawl Out” incident: “If you’re a young little buckaroo and you want to poke the bear, get ready to get bit”

body: WWE Hall of Famer Billy Gunn spoke with Kenny McIntosh in an interview published to the Inside The Ropes YouTube channel. Here is an excerpt… McIntosh: “[CM] Punk debuted in 2021, and then there were these nights in wrestling that people talk about, like Montreal and All Out 2022, where Punk did the press conference and then there was an incident backstage. You were in AEW at that point. Were you seeing this stuff going on? Were you thinking, ‘What are we going to do?’ How were you looking at it as someone in AEW?” Gunn: “So, I wasn’t around for that, and I don’t watch any of that media stuff. It’s got nothing to do with me. It’s just whatever. It’s for them to talk or whatever. I knew about the incident that happened back then, which was what it was. They just have to realize that sometimes there are certain veterans who just aren’t going to put up with that sh*t, no matter what. If you’re a young little buckaroo and you want to poke the bear, get ready to get bit. So, I think that’s what happened. I don’t know all the details. That’s between them. And, of course, the media stuff—I don’t watch that because it’s got nothing to do with me either.” McIntosh: “Back in the day, if something happened for real backstage, it would be like, ‘Let’s make an angle out of it.’ You’d work together and do something.” Gunn: “They do, but nothing like that. Vince [McMahon] had things under control really well. There’s this couple of things: I don’t have to like you to wrestle with you or work with you. I don’t have to like you. I don’t have to do anything. I just have to do business. There’d be that every speck now and then where you’d pull someone into a room. You pull them into a room, shut the door. You don’t do it out in public, and I don’t do it in front of the boys. If I have something bad to say about coaching and I’m about to lose my sh*t, I don’t do it in front of people. I take them somewhere where nobody else can hear it because it’s nobody else’s business. You pull them into a room, shut the door, and go, ‘All right, here we go. What are we doing? If you’ve got a problem, we need to fix it now.’ We’ll fix it now so when we walk out the door, we don’t have a problem anymore.”

title: On the Record: Billy Gunn Discusses About Triple H’s AEW Comments at 2019 WWE Hall of Fame Ceremony
raw_title: Billy Gunn Talks About Triple H’s AEW Comments at 2019 WWE Hall of Fame Ceremony
body: Billy Gunn recently did an interview with Inside the Ropes where he discussed a number of topics pertaining to his involvement with WWE & AEW. As you may recall, Gunn was involved in the WWE Hall of Fame Induction ceremony in 2019 as part of De-Generation X. There was some intrigue around this due to Gunn having recently signed with AEW to be a coach. Triple H responded to some fans chanting “AEW” by saying that Vince McMahon would buy that “pissant company”, which generated some online hubbub at the time. People still do ask about it, and Gunn had the following to say: I knew it was coming. I kind of knew that they were going to do something AEW because it was hot at the time, and I was there, and they’re all wondering how I got to go there and that’s because Tony Khan was super cool, because they were going to stick us (DX) in and I went and asked and he said 100%. He said ‘Of course you can, I would never hold you back from that.’ I didn’t know what they were going to do, but I knew they were going to do something. And I also knew that if they were, that Hunter was going to have something to say about it. So once I set myself up to let all that, I just let it go, you know, and the only one that got hurt out of that whole deal was him (Triple H). Like, and I don’t want to say it, but it was just a dick move, right? It was it was kind of trying to save face and you didn’t need to because it’s going to happen. It’s the wrestling business. That’s what we do. That’s what they like to stir up. So they’re when you have somebody in another company…it’s one, they can’t believe it because I’m sure a lot of the people didn’t think I was going to make it because I did work for another company. And then when you see me and then they have to do it, it’s like an unwritten thing in a book. If another guy is in another company, we have to say something and do something. And they started chanting it (AEW) and they would…and then you get a response from the guy that’s leading the company.” If using any of the above quotes, please credit Inside the Ropes, with a h/t to 411mania.com for the transcription.

title: Legal Watch: Federal Court Rejects Wwe, Mcmahons' Constitutional Challenge In Ring Boys Lawsuit
raw_title: FEDERAL COURT REJECTS WWE, MCMAHONS' CONSTITUTIONAL CHALLENGE IN RING BOYS LAWSUIT - PWInsider
body: DMFirst Veer Game odds uden om ROFUS FEDERAL COURT REJECTS WWE, MCMAHONS' CONSTITUTIONAL CHALLENGE IN RING BOYS LAWSUIT By Mike Johnson on 2026-10-19 15:22:00 The following press release was issued: DiCello Levitt Represents Survivors as Federal Court Upholds Application of Maryland’s Child Victims Act, Allowing Claims Against WWE and the McMahons to Proceed In a 26-page opinion issued today, U.S. District Judge James K. Bredar of the District of Maryland rejected the defendants’ latest attempt to dismiss the survivors’ claims. At issue was the constitutionality of Maryland’s Child Victims Act of 2023, which eliminated time limits for filing civil lawsuits involving childhood sexual abuse. The law recognizes that survivors often delay disclosing abuse due to the lasting effects of trauma, giving them an opportunity to pursue justice when they are ready to come forward. DiCello Levitt, together with Murphy, Falcon & Murphy, represents the survivors in John Doe 1 et al. v. World Wrestling Entertainment, LLC et al. “This ruling is a significant victory for our clients and for other survivors of childhood sexual abuse who have waited years for the opportunity to seek justice,” said Greg Gutzler, a partner at DiCello Levitt who leads the litigation. “Trauma does not follow a legal deadline, and Maryland’s Child Victims Act recognizes that reality. Our clients have waited years to hold those responsible accountable. We will not stop fighting until their voices are heard and they have their day in court.” The ruling follows the court’s December 2025 decision largely denying the defendants’ earlier motions to dismiss. body: The same day the news of Hulk Hogan's death broke , McMahon was involved in an accident in Westport, Connecticut that involved two other vehicles. title: R-Truth Shares Positive Injury Update
raw_title: R-Truth Provides Injury Update After Concerning WWE SmackDown Scene
body: Skip to content Wrestling News Home » R-Truth Provides Injury Update After Concerning WWE SmackDown Scene R-Truth has shared an update on his condition following his injury on WWE SmackDown. R-Truth faced his former tag team partner Damian Priest in a singles match on last week’s WWE SmackDown. However, the bout was stopped early after he appeared to injure himself after delivering a top-rope dropkick to Priest. He stayed down on the mat after the impact, and the referee held up the X sign after checking on him. WWE star R-Truth, whose birth name is Ron Killings, took to social media to share an update on his health. He posted a photo of himself in a hospital and wrote, “I am OK. Thank you all for your support, concerns, and get well wishes. Wow, it truly feels amazing to feel and be loved. I’m grateful for you all.” The 52-year-old wrestler then seemingly joked, “On 10/16/2026, I almost passed away… Damien Priest tried to kill me; I didn’t think he was that serious… But ok, I’ll be back.” Last week’s SmackDown featured R-Truth’s first match. This was since Damian Priest turned on him on the September 11 episode in Mexico City. It was also the former 24/7 Champion’s first singles match since December 2025 . Truth and Damian Priest enjoyed a 147-day WWE Tag Team Championship run before dropping it to MFT’s Tama and Talla Tonga on the August 14, 2026, episode of SmackDown. Priest ended their partnership after failing to defeat the War Raiders for the AAA World Tag Team Championship on the September 11 episode of the blue brand. A passionate fan of the business for over two decades, he applies a deep understanding of the sport's history to his daily coverage.

The bout was stopped early as he remained down and the referee signaled for medical attention. The 52-year-old later posted from the hospital on social media confirming he is okay and plans to return soon.

title: Lexis King Drops Brutal Zilla Fatu Diss Track Mocking His Dead Father and Prison Past
raw_title: Lexis King Drops Brutal Zilla Fatu Diss Track Mocking His Dead Father and Prison Past
summary_src: Lexis King just took his beef with Zilla Fatu to a whole new level, and apparently nothing is off-limits. The WWE NXT star dropped a diss track targeting Fatu on October 19, 2026, taking shots at everything from his tattoos and prison past to his late father, Umaga.
body: King released the music video for a track titled “Zilla Vanilla” on Twitter, complete with an ice cream truck and a catchy chorus mocking his NXT rival. But once you get past the jokes about vanilla ice cream, some of the lyrics get pretty nasty. “Zilla vanilla? You soft as a pillar. Your pops was a G, but my dad had the trigger?” King didn’t stop there. He also went after Fatu’s criminal history, making a particularly nasty joke about the six years Fatu spent behind bars. “But who were we kidding? This kid got him in prison? Six years in the pen and the soap kept on slipping?” “Your tattoos are tripping? You got no self respect? It looks like some children drew it on at your sketch?” King then followed that up with another jab about Fatu’s interactions with women. “You stay missing with women like you running in place. Last time you touched a girl, you got smacked by Grace.” The song also references Fatu’s injured hand, which ties directly into their ongoing WWE NXT storyline. King and the rest of BirthRight have been making Fatu’s life miserable ever since he refused to join their faction. “And I know why? Cause we busted your hand. And speaking of busting, that won’t be in your plans.” The music video itself takes a much lighter approach than some of the lyrics, with King performing in front of an ice cream truck while people dance around him. He even renamed his rival “Zilla Vanilla” and repeatedly mocked him for being soft. What’s pretty wild is how personal King decided to make this. Their feud started because Fatu wouldn’t join BirthRight, but now King is dragging dead relatives, prison time, and sexual jokes into a wrestling rivalry. He clearly isn’t interested in keeping things strictly about what happens inside the ring. For now, Fatu hasn’t responded to the track, but considering he already beat King once and got jumped by BirthRight afterward, he has plenty of reasons to want another shot at him. King might be having fun making music videos, but he’s also giving Fatu a whole lot more ammunition for their next confrontation. body: According to Fightful , citing court records, Kaiser's motion to dismiss the case under Florida's "Stand Your Ground" law, which he filed back in July, was denied during a hearing on Monday. The outlet reported a pre-trial conference is set for December 17. With "Stand Your Ground," Florida law states that individuals can use force in self-defense, or in defense of another, if they reasonably believe it necessary to avoid the other person's "imminent use of unlawful force." In Kaiser's case, he was accompanied by girlfriend, fellow AAA star Andrea Bazarte. The alleged victim in the battery case, Richard Reap, reportedly told police that Kaiser and Bazarte were "aggressively kissing" in an elevator, and he asked them to "please have some manners." According to Kaiser, they were hugging when Reap began cursing at them and told them to have some respect "before he called ICE on that b****," referring to Bazarte. In both parties' account of the events, an altercation did take place. The incident took place in April, but Kaiser, the current AAA Mega Champion known as El Grande Americano, was not arrested until May, ahead of his mask-vs-mask match against the original El Grande Americano, Chad Gable. When Kaiser was made aware of the charges, he reportedly traveled from Mexico back to Florida to turn himself in.
summary: Per Fightful Select citing court records, a judge denied Ludwig Kaiser's July motion to dismiss his battery charge under Florida's Stand Your Ground law during a Monday hearing. A pre-trial conference is scheduled for December 17. The April incident involved Kaiser and his girlfriend AAA wrestler Andrea Bazarte in an elevator with the alleged victim Richard Reap, where both sides agree an altercation occurred after words were exchanged.

llm_long: A judge denied a motion to dismiss the battery case against WWE performer Ludwig Kaiser. The hearing on the motion took place on October 19 and court records show it was denied. A pre-trial conference is set for December 17 2026 to determine whether the case will proceed to trial or reach a resolution.

Kaiser's defense sought dismissal under Florida's Stand Your Ground law. The argument claimed he used necessary force to protect himself and his girlfriend from imminent unlawful force by the alleged victim Richard Reap. The incident occurred in April at an Orlando apartment complex where both men lived.

Both parties agree that Kaiser and his girlfriend were being affectionate in an elevator. Their accounts diverge afterward with Reap stating he asked the couple to have manners before Kaiser attacked him. Kaiser claims Reap swore at them and made a racist remark about calling ICE on his girlfriend.

Kaiser acknowledges pushing Reap after Reap moved toward him aggressively. According to Kaiser he did not retaliate when Reap threw a soft drink bottle at him and instead left the area with his girlfriend. Police reports indicate surveillance video showed Kaiser punching and pushing Reap and that Reap had a visible scratch on his head.

The state entered a CD and four photos into evidence believed to be elevator surveillance footage and images of Reap's injuries. Reap has retained a personal injury attorney which may signal plans for a civil suit against Kaiser.

title: Judge lets WWE Ring Boys lawsuit proceed
raw_title: Federal judge allows the "Ring Boys" child sexual abuse case filed against Vince McMahon, Linda McMahon, WWE, and TKO to move forward
body: By Jason Powell , ProWrestling.net Editor ( @prowrestlingnet ) The DiCello Levitt law firm issued the following press release on Monday regarding a federal court allowing the “WWE Ring Boys” child sexual abuse litigation to move forward. In a 26-page opinion issued today, U.S. District Judge James K. Bredar of the District of Maryland rejected the defendants’ latest attempt to dismiss the survivors’ claims. At issue was the constitutionality of Maryland’s Child Victims Act of 2023 , which eliminated time limits for filing civil lawsuits involving childhood sexual abuse. The law recognizes that survivors often delay disclosing abuse due to the lasting effects of trauma, giving them an opportunity to pursue justice when they are ready to come forward. DiCello Levitt, together with Murphy, Falcon & Murphy, represents the survivors in John Doe 1 et al. v. World Wrestling Entertainment, LLC et al. “This ruling is a significant victory for our clients and for other survivors of childhood sexual abuse who have waited years for the opportunity to seek justice,” said Greg Gutzler , a partner at DiCello Levitt who leads the litigation. “Trauma does not follow a legal deadline, and Maryland’s Child Victims Act recognizes that reality. Our clients have waited years to hold those responsible accountable. We will not stop fighting until their voices are heard and they have their day in court.” The ruling follows the court’s December 2025 decision largely denying the defendants’ earlier motions to dismiss. The WWE Ring Boys sexual abuse lawsuit alleges that WWE employees, including ringside announcer and ring crew chief Melvin Phillips Jr., recruited underage boys to assist with wrestling events and used their positions to groom, exploit, and sexually abuse them. The plaintiffs further allege that WWE leadership, including Vince and Linda McMahon, knew or should have known about the abuse but failed to take reasonable steps to prevent it. The litigation is led by DiCello Levitt’s Greg Gutzler and Adam Prom and includes Scott Gilmore , Mark A. DiCello , Bobby DiCello , and Emma Bruder , with local counsel Murphy, Falcon & Murphy. The case is John Doe 1 et al. v. World Wrestling Entertainment, LLC et al. , Case No. 1:24-cv-03487, in the U.S. District Court for the District of Maryland. DiCello Levitt LLP is one of the leading plaintiffs’ law firms in the United States. Nationally recognized for our work in high-stakes class actions, mass torts, and complex litigation, we have recovered more than $25 billion for clients, including individuals, businesses, and communities. We take on some of the world’s most powerful interests, pursuing justice that reshapes industries and improves lives. Built for trial, DiCello Levitt is among the few plaintiffs’ firms with a dedicated trial center, where our acclaimed trial lawyers bring both art and science to courtroom preparation and trial strategy. We are frequently appointed to lead major multidistrict litigation (MDLs) and

title: On the Record: TNA Officially Announces Signing Of Shotzi Blackheart
raw_title: TNA Officially Announces Signing Of Shotzi Blackheart
body: TNA Wrestling has officially confirmed the signing of former WWE Superstar Shotzi Blackheart, adding another established name to its women’s division. The company announced the news in a press release, noting that the signing was first reported by Busted Open on SiriusXM. Blackheart, a California native who began her professional wrestling career in 2014, previously competed in WWE, where she held the NXT Women’s Tag Team Championship alongside Ember Moon. Her arrival follows appearances at TNA’s live events in Dothan, Alabama, in mid-October. In addition to confirming her signing, TNA shared 10 personal facts about Blackheart, offering fans a closer look at her interests and accomplishments outside the wrestling ring. Blackheart also studied musical theatre at the American Musical and Dramatic Academy (AMDA) in Hollywood. A passionate horror movie fan, she hopes to direct her own horror film someday. Among her wrestling accomplishments, TNA highlighted that Blackheart was named Pro Wrestling Illustrated’s 2025 Independent Wrestler of the Year and appeared on the magazine’s cover. The company also revealed several lesser-known details about her personal life, including her obsession with Elvis Presley and the fact that she owns a chicken farm. Another unusual accomplishment involved visiting Walt Disney World, where she managed to ride every attraction across all four theme parks in a single day. Blackheart also spoke about her heritage, stating, “I’m proudly Filipino.” One of the more memorable facts involved her wedding day, which featured both a marriage ceremony and a wrestling match. “I got married and wrestled in my wedding dress all on the same day,” Blackheart revealed. The announcement officially confirms Blackheart’s status with TNA following her recent appearances for the promotion. TNA has not yet disclosed additional details regarding the length or terms of her contract.
summary: The latest: the signing of former WWE Superstar Shotzi Blackheart, adding another established name to its women’s division, TNA Wrestling has officially made official. TNA shared 10 personal facts about Blackheart, offering the audience a closer look at her interests and accomplishments outside the wrestling ring.

title: On the Record: TNA Officially Confirms Shotzi Blackheart Signing
raw_title: TNA Officially Confirms Shotzi Blackheart Signing
body: Shotzi Blackheart has officially joined TNA Wrestling, adding another familiar name to the Knockouts division. TNA confirmed her signing on Monday after she appeared at last week’s television tapings in Dothan, Alabama. News of the deal was first reported by Busted Open on SiriusXM. Blackheart arrives with experience across several major promotions. She began wrestling in 2014 and held the NXT Women’s Tag Team Championship alongside Ember Moon during her WWE career. She also became MLW Women’s Champion before her contract with that company expired earlier this month. MLW hopes to continue booking Blackheart for as long as her contractual arrangements allow. To introduce its newest signing, TNA shared 10 facts about Blackheart, offering fans a glimpse at her interests and achievements outside the ring: She investigates the paranormal and has travelled across America hunting ghosts for her YouTube series, CHAMBER OF HORRORS. PWI named her its 2025 Independent Wrestler of the Year and featured her on its cover. She rode every ride across all four Walt Disney World theme parks in a single day. Speaking about her heritage, she said: “I’m proudly Filipino.” Recalling her wedding day, she revealed: “I got married and wrestled in my wedding dress all on the same day.” Blackheart joins a division currently led by Knockouts World Champion Indi Hartwell. M By Elegance, also known as Maggie Lee, holds the Knockouts TV Championship, while Zoey Serrano and Shayna Baszler are the Knockouts Tag Team Champions. The signing comes during a difficult time for Blackheart, whose real name is Ashley Urbanski. Following the death of her brother Dean, she withdrew from CMLL’s Women’s International Grand Prix, which takes place this Friday. Marina Shafir has replaced her on Team International.
summary: Shotzi Blackheart has officially joined TNA Wrestling, adding another familiar name to the Knockouts division. Her signing on Monday after she appeared at last week’s television tapings in Dothan, Alabama, TNA made official.

title: Tony Khan Discusses AEW Talks With Skydance CEO David Ellison

summary_src: AEW President Tony Khan said he's had conversations with Skydance CEO David Ellison about AEW and its future.
body: "I've had a conversation with David Ellison about the future of AEW," Khan said. "I've had a few great conversations with David Ellison about AEW and he is very excited to be a partner of AEW and with us. To be now Skydance, means Warner Bros. and Paramount under the same roof and this means more exciting opportunities. More resources. Warner Bros. is going to be stronger... I think he's been fantastic for Paramount and he's a great partner for us with the NFL. He's going to be a great partner for AEW with Warner Bros. He's somebody who's the same age as me. He's a wrestling fan. I think that's really exciting for us." AEW's current media rights deal will see the company air "AEW Dynamite" and "AEW Collision" on TBS and TNT until at least 2028, with an option year available. At the time the deal was announced, Variety reported it was valued at up to $150 million per year.

title: On the Record: Billy Gunn Recalls CM Punk & The Elite’s Backstage Clash at AEW All Out 2022
raw_title: Billy Gunn Recalls CM Punk & The Elite’s Backstage Clash at AEW All Out 2022
body: Billy Gunn, who has been with AEW since its early days, discussed the situation during an interview with Inside The Ropes . He explained that he wasn’t directly involved in the incident. Gunn said, “So I knew the incident that happened back in the thing, which was what it was, and they just have to realize that sometimes there’s certain veterans that just aren’t going to put up with that, no matter what. Right?” “And if you’re a young little buckaroo and you want to poke the bear, get ready to get bit. So, I think that’s what happened. And I don’t know the whole details. That’s between them and then, you know, of course, the media thing that I don’t watch, ’cause it’s got nothing to do with me either.” Gunn was also asked whether real backstage disagreements could become wrestling storylines. He compared the situation to how conflicts were handled during WWE’s earlier years. Gunn explained, “They do, but nothing like that. Like, Vince had things under control really good. I don’t have to like you to wrestle with you or to work with you. Don’t have to like you. I don’t have to do anything. I just have to do business. And mostly 99.9% of the guys always did that. Right?” Gunn then described how disagreements should be resolved behind closed doors. He continued, “There’ll be that every speck now and then where you just pull them into a room, you know? You pull them into a room, you shut the door. So you don’t do it out in public, like, and I don’t do it in front of the boys. It’s just like, if I have something bad to say about coaching and I’m about to lose my I don’t do it in front of people. I take them somewhere where nobody else can hear it because it’s nobody else’s business.” He believes private conversations help prevent unnecessary tension. Gunn explained that people should resolve problems before returning to work. He added, “You pull them into a room, you shut the door, and you go, ‘All right, here we go. What are we doing?’ Like, if you got a problem, we need to fix it now. We’ll fix it now, so when we walk out the door, we don’t have a problem anymore. Right? And that’s how grown-ass people deal with sh*t. But nowadays, we don’t, and that’s sad. But there’s going to be people that are going to do that.” The post Billy Gunn Recalls CM Punk & The Elite’s Backstage Clash at AEW All Out 2022 appeared first on Wrestlezone .

title: GCW And JCW To Bring Jersey J-Cup To Ridgefield Park In 2027
raw_title: GCW And JCW To Bring Jersey J-Cup To Ridgefield Park In 2027
body: For the first time since it was first run back in 2000, the Jersey J-Cup will take place at “The Mecca” in Ridgefield Park, New Jersey from February 20 and 21, 2027. The news was announced during JCW (Jersey Championship Wrestling) Nightmare in Bergen County event, also taking place at legendary north Jersey arena. This tournament has sported some incredible lineups. During the initial run with the original JCW, winners included Low Ki (2001), Reckless Youth (2002), Jay Lethal (2003) and Super Dragon (2004). During the NWS era, winners included Rhett Titus (2008) and R.J. Brewer (2010). After the tournament came back in 2014, notable northeast indie wrestler Chris Dickinson won the first tournament. And since its full time return in 2023, Jordan Oliver (2023), Masha Slamovich (2024 & 2025), and Charles Mason have etched their names into the winner’s ledger. As yet, the lineup for the 2027 tournament isn’t available, but that’s something to keep an eye on in the coming weeks and months. As always, we’ll aim to provide any further updates on the 2027 Jersey J-Cup as soon as we hear more.

title: Match Made: Why AEW is Winning the Pro Wrestling War vs. WWE in 2026
raw_title: Why AEW is Winning the Pro Wrestling War vs. WWE in 2026
body: 45:07 Featured Video CBB AP POLL REACTION Previous Next Why AEW is Winning the Pro Wrestling War vs. WWE in 2026 Erik Beaston Sep 2, 2026 All Elite Wrestling presented its biggest event of the year, All In, at Wembley Stadium in London ont Sunday. The show delivered surprises, long-awaited storyline payoffs, strong in-ring action and the crowning of a new champion in an extraordinary main event. As that pay-per-view went off the air, it became clear that AEW is winning the pro wrestling war against WWE in 2026. Sure, WWE remains the industry leader financially, but AEW has surpassed it in several other areas, supporting the argument that it delivered the stronger overall product in 2026. All In culminated with Will Ospreay paying off his long journey to the top of the pro wrestling mountain by defeating Kenny Omega to win the AEW World Championship. Tony Khan and his creative team did not overthink the situation, book a shocking outcome for the sake of it, or worry too much about whether the audience would sniff out the finish. They produced the finish everyone inside Wembley Stadium wanted to see, with Ospreay capturing the title in his hometown, resulting in one of the most memorable and emotional moments in company history. AEW has done this consistently in 2026, putting the right exclamation point on storylines up and down the card. Look no further than Darby Allin vs. Kevin Knight from the same show. Allin avenged Knight's betrayal, took him out in a similar fashion to the attacks he suffered, and won the TNT title. A simple story, with a simple outcome, that fans ate up. Even the Brawling Birds' Jamie Hayter and Alex Windsor arriving back to the UK and doing the seemingly impossible by knocking off Divine Dominion for the women's tag titles was the appropriate conclusion to that rivalry. Dating back to last summer, WWE has adopted a creative strategy to try and stay ahead of the audience. Most famously, it had Seth Rollins feign a knee injury to surprise fans with a Money in the Bank cash-in at the conclusion of the 2025 SummerSlam event. That works in the moment and creates buzz, but it is gimmicky and does not encourage long-term buy-in to the stories and rivalries that play out each week. Then there is the potential for TKO interference, as we saw at this past WrestleMania, with the shoehorning of Pat McAfee into a Cody Rhodes-Randy Orton story that didn't need him. The possibility that something like that could happen on a whim makes it very difficult for the company to deliver the kind of long-term storytelling and payoff it delivered at WrestleMania 40 in 2024, when Cody Rhodes finished his story. title: Injury Update: WWE banned these 5 dangerous wrestling moves after seeing talent seriously injured
raw_title: WWE banned these 5 dangerous wrestling moves after seeing talent seriously injured
body: From the likes of Triple H tearing his quads, Mick Foley ticking off almost every injury possible, and retirement inducing neck injuries to the likes of Edge and Kurt Angle, it's safe to say things can and do go wrong in WWE. While we might see more high flyers in the modern era, there's also a limitation when it comes to certain moves that, frankly, have cost people their careers. Here, then, are FIVE dangerous wrestling moves WWE has banned over the years. Some will argue we might be set to see a return of this being used in the Randy Orton and Cody Rhodes feud but that is only because they are two of the very best around. The reason? Multiple concussions and head injuries suffered as a result of poor timing or the move simply not going as planned. One of the best things about growing up watching the Attitude Era was some of the brutal and downright dangerous steel chair shots we got to see. WWE moved to ban the head shot during the PG-era and it has remained largely the same since. Ultimately, head injuries and concussions are too costly and in the end, outside pressures have forced WWE's hand really. Anyone who saw Brock Lesnar try and fail this move against Kurt Angle at WrestleMania 20 will know exactly why this was banned. On another day, Lesnar would have broken his neck and in reality, could have died. While many of us are accustomed to seeing Triple H or Seth Rollins hit a pedigree, the early inception of the move was quite scary. Instead of the move involving falling to the mat with your chest and body breaking the fall, Triple H instead planned on lifting the arms up fully behind the back and simply planting his opponent on his head. Obviously, this move never made it to TV and WWE quickly adapted it for The Game to keep on using over his career. Another move that on rare occasions we do see. But in essence, the original piledriver has been banned ever since Stone Cold Steve Austin broke his neck and spinal cord against Owen Hart. Anyone who has watched WWE for a long time will have seen the footage and when you look back, it's amazing Stone Cold went on to wrestle again, never mind have the success he did. We still see the piledriver on the odd occasion but much like the punt, it seems reserved for only the highest level of performer. raw_title: Latest update on visa status of former WWE wrestler Kairi Sane
summary_src: It has been six months nearly to the day since Kairi Sane last wrestled on US soil. And it could be a while before she wrestles in America again. According to a report on Fightful Select, Sane needs to reach a deal with a US-based promotion before she can begin the process of applying for […]
body: It has been six months nearly to the day since Kairi Sane last wrestled on US soil. And it could be a while before she wrestles in America again. According to a report on Fightful Select , Sane needs to reach a deal with a US-based promotion before she can begin the process of applying for a work visa. “Kairi remains a free agent after her WWE deal expired when they released her earlier in the year,” the report reads. “Fightful Select has reported that ongoing conversations have ensued since free agency, and that she also has multiple standing offers in Japan.” “There were reports recently that the belief is that visa issues are holding up a deal, but it’s actually the opposite,” the Fightful report explains. “Kairi’s US visa has expired, and would need to either be sponsored by a wrestling company or agency for renewal. As she’s not signed by AEW yet, that hasn’t happened. Once she signs, an expedited visa can be approved in as little as 15 business days. But this isn’t a situation of waiting on the visa right now for her debut, she isn’t signed and no deal is finalized.” Sane does have one future appearance booked for American audiences. She will be taking part of Chris Jericho’s Rock N’ Wrestling Rager at Sea in November. Because the event takes place in international waters, Sane does not need a US visa to participate. Sane’s last match was a tag team match on the April 20 episode of Monday Night Raw. She teamed with Asuka in a losing effort to Iyo Sky & Rhea Ripley. Sane was signed with WWE from 2016 to 2021, and then again from 2023 until this year. She is otherwise best known for wrestling as KAIRI in Stardom.
summary: Per Fightful Select, Kairi Sane has been a free agent since her WWE release earlier this year. She requires a contract with a US-based promotion to sponsor and renew her expired work visa before she can wrestle in America again. The report notes she has multiple standing offers in Japan and that ongoing talks continue, but no deal with AEW or anyone else has been finalized.

body: The October 19th broadcast of WWE Monday Night Raw on Netflix started with World Heavyweight Champion Roman Reigns pulling up in a truck, and pulling up behind him in another truck was his opponent at Crown Jewel, Undisputed WWE Champion Sami Zayn. Zayn briefly acknowledged Reigns and then started making his way to the ring. Reigns would then join Zayn for their in-ring segment. Reigns stated that it was good to see Zayn, and they hugged. The two champions started bonding because Zayn said he finally understood what Reigns was talking about when he was The Tribal Chief, specifically referring to the disrespect that champions receive and the burden that comes with being champion. Reigns went on to state that the most important title Zayn has ever held is the title of ‘Honorary Uce.’ He asked Zayn if he was there to talk about the 946 and to serve The Bloodline. Zayn responded by saying he appreciates his time in The Bloodline, but he’s the head of his own table now. Roman stated that Zayn’s belt is A title, but the belt he has is THE title. They got into a back-and-forth, and then Reigns said maybe the Undisputed WWE Title hasn’t meant anything since he lost it at WrestleMania 40. As Reigns was leaving, Mr. Money in the Bank Penta showed up and went face-to-face with Reigns. Penta then faced off with Zayn in the ring.

The two champions hugged in the ring, bonded over the burdens of holding a world title and the disrespect they receive, with Reigns reminding Zayn that his most important title remains Honorary Uce and asking if he was there to serve The Bloodline. Zayn replied that he values his Bloodline history but now leads his own table, prompting Reigns to call his own World Heavyweight Championship THE title while labeling Zayn's Undisputed WWE Championship merely A title before their verbal exchange continued.

"I can't believe I'm saying this, and I might be the only one in here saying it, but it's good to see you," Reigns said. The former Bloodline teammates engaged in a mid-ring embrace before Zayn admitted to getting everything the Tribal Chief preached. The pleasantries came to an end when Reigns questioned Zayn's motivation for being there and a potential allegiance to 946. Then they verbally battled over which championship was more important. Then, the Last Real Good Guy took exception to the disrespect Reigns has shown him by not even sweating him. "Knowing your track record, you might not even have that championship come Crown Jewel," Reigns said to close out the segment. As he exited the arena, Penta arrived, a not-so-subtle reminder that the luchador has the Money in the Bank briefcase and, one day, will come for the world championship.

title: Interviews with Kiera Hogan and McKenzie Mitchell — RAF in Miami, TNA Wrestling in Tampa
raw_title: RAF in Miami, TNA Wrestling in Tampa: Interviews with Kiera Hogan and McKenzie Mitchell
body: RAF13, under the Real American Freestyle banner, is Friday, Sept. 18 at the Watsco Center at the University of Miami in Coral Gables. The Bound for Glory PPV, under the TNA Wrestling banner, is Sunday, Oct. 11 at the Yuengling Center in Tampa. RAF, a new company, is the unscripted version of professional wrestling, featuring freestyle wrestling from some of the best wrestlers in the world. TNA Wrestling, in its 24th year, is one of the top scripted type pro wrestling companies in the world. Below are some video interviews I conducted to hype the companies, shows and talent. After a five-year hiatus, Kiera Hogan made her triumphant return to TNA Wrestling at TNA Lockdown in August in Chicago. Hogan was the mystery partner of Allie at TNA Lockdown in August in Chicago. She replaced an injured Rosemary to help Allie retain the TNA Wrestling Knockouts tag team titles in a steel cage by defeating The Elegance Brand (Heather by Elegance and M by Elegance) (with Mr. Elegance and The Personal Concierge). Hogan is now a 3-time TNA Wrestling Knockouts tag team champion. She also won gold twice with Tasha Steelz. As Fire, she teamed with her life partner Adrenaline (ROH's Diamante) to win the tag team titles in WOW - Women Of Wrestling, the women's pro wrestling group. TNA Wrestling is in San Antonio, Texas with back-to-back nights of action at the Boeing Center at Tech Port on Thursday and Friday, September 24-25. TNA Wrestling and Real American Freestyle interviewer and ring announcer McKenzie Mitchell is a WWE alum. Fashion meets wrestling in a first-of-its-kind book by Mitchell, which is titled "THREADS OF TRIUMPH: Professional Wrestling's Most Iconic Looks." "THREADS OF TRIUMPH" features wrestling's most intriguing costumes from the 1940s to today, including the looks of big names like "Macho Man" Randy Savage, Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson, The Undertaker, Shawn Michaels, Ric Flair, Rey Mysterio, Becky Lynch, Bianca Belair, and many more. A foreword by one of wrestling's best, Mercedes Moné, completes the all-star package. Mitchell, 32, is a glamorous third-generation jewelry entrepreneur from Dexter, Missouri. She marries the stunning imagery in her book with the wrestlers' thematic choices behind their outfits, including how they select every button, every swatch, to mold their persona and story. The dive into this artistry is something that hasn't been published before and will appeal to the most die-hard wrestling fans and the wrestling curious alike. Chris Jericho, a multi-time world champion in pro wrestling, dubs McKenzie's idea to write an entire book on pro wrestling fashion "a brilliant one, and this book shines brighter than the sequins on the boots I'm wearing right now!" iMPACT also airs on Sportsnet 360 in Canada and TNA+ worldwide.

llm_long: Kiera Hogan returned to TNA Wrestling after a five-year absence at the Lockdown event in Chicago in August. She appeared as the mystery partner for Allie and replaced an injured Rosemary in a steel cage match.

Hogan helped Allie retain the TNA Knockouts tag team titles by defeating The Elegance Brand consisting of Heather by Elegance and M by Elegance along with Mr. Elegance and The Personal Concierge. This victory marked her third reign as a TNA Knockouts tag team champion.

Hogan previously won the TNA Knockouts tag team titles twice alongside Tasha Steelz. She also captured tag team gold in Women Of Wrestling as Fire teaming with her life partner Adrenaline who is known as Diamante in Ring of Honor.

TNA Wrestling will hold back-to-back events at the Boeing Center at Tech Port in San Antonio, Texas on September 24 and 25. Separately Real American Freestyle will present an unscripted freestyle wrestling show on September 18 at the Watsco Center in Coral Gables, Florida.

title: Cody Rhodes Praises WWE's Top Pay Scale
raw_title: Cody Rhodes On WWE Pay Structure: 'That Next Level Pay Is Now Comparable With Sports'
body: During a recent interview with "Flagrant," Rhodes offered a glimpse into how WWE's pay structure has evolved by citing company President Nick Khan. "Nick Khan had a great quote about 'These guys are going to do well. These guys are going to do really well and then these couple guys, they're going to do next level.' And that next level pay is now comparable with sports," Rhodes said. "That's the part that I'm so proud of being a wrestler because when you'd hear baseball contracts and NBA contracts, and you know as a wrestler that you could go all over the world and be known and be seen, but you weren't on that level. You were on the level of penetration but not that level of income. Now, modern TKO and Nick have made it that you are." Rhodes described the money being made in the pro wrestling business as "very good," with amounts cited in WWE contracts now being guaranteed. "The American Nightmare" believes his late father, Dusty Rhodes, would have been particularly "shocked" by today's payouts. Upon returning to WWE in 2022, Rhodes propelled to the main event scene, where he went on to win the Undisputed WWE Championship on three separate occasions. He currently finds himself in a feud with Randy Orton, his former mentor in the stable known as Legacy and a 14-time world champion.

Rhodes noted that the highest level of compensation in WWE is now comparable to contracts in major sports leagues and that modern deals under TKO feature guaranteed money. title: Drew McIntyre Maintains Ring Shape During WWE Hiatus
raw_title: Drew McIntyre details how he has stayed in ring shape during WWE absence
summary_src: Former WWE Champion Drew McIntyre has spent more time on the movie set than between the ropes this year, but that doesn’t mean he’s not staying in shape for his inevitable in-ring return. McIntyre talked about his busy filming schedule in an appearance on Busted Open Radio.
body: Former WWE Champion Drew McIntyre has spent more time on the movie set than between the ropes this year, but that doesn’t mean he’s not staying in shape for his inevitable in-ring return. McIntyre talked about his busy filming schedule in an appearance on Busted Open Radio . “I had an itch so bad that I’ve been getting back in the ring and just moving around,” McIntyre said. “Even when I was in Barcelona, I spent three months in Barcelona filming The Last Druid with Russell Crowe after I finished Highlander . I literally lived there for three months and I said, ‘I can’t do this. I gotta get in a ring.’” “One of the extras, one of the stuntmen was a local indie guy and he told me they have a ring there,” McIntyre said. “So I went down and I started just rolling around in the ring and beating up some of his guys just to get my fix.” “I feel bad for those guys,” he said. “The way I wrestle, I practice the way I play. I was beating the crap out of them with no cameras there.” McIntyre said he had also been training at Rusev’s wrestling school in Nashville. “I put a little video out hitting the ropes,” he said. “I think Bron Breakker is the only man that hits the ropes faster than me on planet Earth. And it got over eight million views on my own socials , so people are excited to see Drew come back. I miss the live fans. I miss the buzz, the adrenaline, but I am enjoying what I’m doing right now.” McIntyre won the Undisputed WWE Championship from Cody Rhodes in Germany in January of this year, but lost it back to Rhodes in March in Portland, Oregon. He then lost an unsanctioned match to Jacob Fatu at WrestleMania 42 in Las Vegas in April and has not wrestled since.
summary: Drew McIntyre has been filming movies including Highlander and The Last Druid with Russell Crowe but continues to train for his WWE return. While in Barcelona for three months he sought out a local ring through an indie wrestler and stuntman to roll around and spar with local talent. McIntyre has also trained at Rusev's wrestling school in Nashville per the Wrestling Observer.

llm_long: Drew McIntyre has been focusing on film work this year but continues to maintain his in-ring conditioning during the hiatus. He described an intense desire to return to wrestling and began seeking opportunities to train in rings while on location.

While filming The Last Druid in Barcelona for three months following Highlander, McIntyre located a local wrestling ring through a stuntman who worked on the indie scene. He used the ring to roll around and spar with the stuntman's associates to satisfy his need for wrestling activity.

McIntyre admitted feeling remorse for the intensity of his sessions, noting that he trains as he competes and delivered heavy impacts even without cameras present. He has also been training at Rusev's wrestling school in Nashville.
A video McIntyre posted of himself hitting the ropes received over eight million views on his social media. He believes only Bron Breakker hits the ropes at a faster pace.

McIntyre expressed missing the energy from live audiences and the adrenaline of performing but stated he is currently enjoying his ongoing projects. His most recent matches were a title win over Cody Rhodes in Germany in January, a title loss to Rhodes in Portland in March, and an unsanctioned loss to Jacob Fatu at WrestleMania 42 in Las Vegas in April.

title: Former WWE EVOLVE Star Anya Rune Announces Wrestling Hiatus
raw_title: Former WWE EVOLVE Star Anya Rune Announces Wrestling Hiatus
summary_src: Former WWE EVOLVE star Anya Rune is stepping away from professional wrestling, and she’s not even sure when she’ll be back.
body: Rune broke the news on social media Monday nigh t, October 19, admitting that she never imagined she’d be making an announcement like this. She also acknowledged that some fans would be disappointed, but made it clear that taking a break is something she needs to do. Rune then explained that she’s putting wrestling on hold indefinitely, hoping that spending time away might help her rediscover the passion she once had for it. “I need to take a step back from wrestling. Both for my physical and mental health. I don’t know how long this is going to last but I’m hoping to find a new love for it in the time I will be spending away. I will be keeping my social media somewhat active, it’ll just be less wrestling related content.” She didn’t sugarcoat how she’s feeling about wrestling either. While she still appreciates the opportunities and experiences the business has given her, the love she once had for it simply isn’t there right now. “I have unfortunately fallen out of love with wrestling but that doesn’t mean I don’t love everything its given me.” The announcement comes just weeks after Ringside News covered Rune’s WWE release on September 4 . She was among several talents let go from WWE’s developmental system after competing on WWE EVOLVE as part of the WWE ID program. Before signing with WWE, Rune wrestled on the independent scene under the Airica Demia name and earned a WWE ID contract in March 2026. She eventually adopted the Anya Rune character for EVOLVE, but her time with the company was cut short before she could move into a regular NXT role. Rune had also reacted to her WWE departure , thanking fans who continued to support her after she was let go. Now, barely six weeks later, she’s announcing a break from wrestling altogether. The timing is particularly unfortunate considering how recently she earned her WWE opportunity. Rune went from getting her foot in the door with the company to losing that opportunity and now stepping away from the ring in a matter of months. She hasn’t specified whether her WWE release contributed to her decision, and she hasn’t offered a timetable for returning. For now, Rune is putting herself ahead of wrestling, and she’s not making any promises about when she’ll be back. Whether this turns into a short break or something much longer remains to be seen, but she’s clearly reached a point where forcing herself to keep wrestling isn’t what she wants to do. However, Korderas explained why WWE may have more difficulty finding the right moment for Penta to cash in. Jimmy Korderas also explained what the coming months could look like for Tiffany Stratton and Penta. The former WWE referee believes that Stratton already has an ongoing story that could end similarly to her previous cash-in. “As for Penta, they have a year to cash in. But I wouldn’t want them carrying around the briefcase for an entire year. That’s the other thing too,” he said. “I think Penta is the one that’s going to be a challenge.” Korderas also reacted to the Money in the Bank ladder matches and felt that both matches delivered. The former WWE referee believed that Roxanne and Bron Breakker would emerge as the winners. Korderas also explained that the men’s match made it clear that WWE is very high on Penta. He noted that the company went against the norm, particularly with how it tends to book future cash-ins. “As for the men, I think a lot of people expected Bron Breakker. I did too, because usually the Money in the Bank briefcase lends itself as a heel kind of prop, kind of sneak a cash in somewhere,” he said. “But, it goes to show you how much faith they have in Penta.” Giancarlo Aulino Giancarlo Aulino is sports writer who covers UFC for Heavy.com. summary_src: Chad Gable may have retained his Intercontinental Championship, but his celebration didn’t last long. The October 19, 2026 episode of WWE RAW took a nasty turn when Ethan Page and Big Cass showed up after Gable’s title defense and unleashed a brutal attack on everyone involved.
body: Gable had just survived a wild Triple Threat Match against Rey Mysterio and Dragon Lee, with all three men pulling out everything they had to walk away with the gold. Mysterio connected with a 619 and a frog splash, while Lee nearly stole the championship with a Styles Clash. Gable ultimately found a way to retain, catching Mysterio with a sunset flip for the three-count. Cass absolutely demolished Lee with a chokeslam onto the ringside barricade before delivering a massive boot to Mysterio. Meanwhile, Page turned his attention to the Intercontinental Champion, planting Gable with a fisherman’s buster. Page wasn’t finished, either. He grabbed Gable’s Intercontinental Championship and held it up, making his intentions pretty clear. To drive the point home, Page delivered another fisherman’s buster to Gable, leaving the champion laid out after an already exhausting title defense. The attack was especially interesting considering Gable had just successfully defended his championship against two of WWE’s most accomplished high-flyers. Instead of getting a moment to enjoy his victory, he found himself on the receiving end of a beating, with Page standing tall and holding his title. Ethan Page certainly made a statement on RAW, and having Big Cass involved made the attack even more dangerous. Gable is still the Intercontinental Champion, but Page has now put himself directly in the championship picture without having to wrestle a match. title: Latest On Criminal Case Against El Grande Americano, Wwe's Marcel Barthel
raw_title: LATEST ON CRIMINAL CASE AGAINST EL GRANDE AMERICANO, WWE'S MARCEL BARTHEL - PWInsider
body: DMFirst Veer Game odds uden om ROFUS LATEST ON CRIMINAL CASE AGAINST EL GRANDE AMERICANO, WWE'S MARCEL BARTHEL By Mike Johnson on 2026-10-19 18:04:00 There was a hearing earlier today in Orlando, Florida related to the misdemeanor battery charge against WWE star Marcel Barthel aka Ludwig Kaiser aka El Grande Americano before the County Court of the Ninth Judicial Circuit, in and for Orange County, Florida. The hearing was regarding Barthel's motion to dismiss, where Barthel argued for a dismissal on the grounds that Barthel's use of force was legally justified and that he was immune from criminal prosecution under Florida law. Both Barthel and Richard Reap, who filed the charges against him testified at the hearing. At the end of the hearing, Barthel's motion to dismiss was denied with a new pre-trial hearing set for 12/17. Barthel was arrested in May on charges of battery, pleading not guilty after learning of a warrant for his arrest on charges of battery and traveling from Mexico to Florida to turn himself in to authorities. A arrest affidavit stated that Orlando Police responded to an apartment complex (we are not publishing the address) at approximately 6:37 PM on 4/23 following reports of a physical altercation on the 12th floor of the building. The complainant, identified as Richard Reap, told officers that he entered an elevator around 6:30 PM and encountered Barthel alongside an unidentified woman. Reap alleged that the pair were acting in what he described as an “uncontrollably intimate” manner while inside the elevator. Reap stated that after exiting onto the 12th floor, he told the couple to “please have some manners.” According to the affidavit, Reap alleged that Barthel immediately responded by punching him multiple times, pushing him to the ground, and threatening additional violence. Barthel's attorney, in the motion to dismiss, argued that he used only non-deadly force, was lawfully present in the common area of his apartment complex, and reasonably believed his actions were necessary to protect both himself and his girlfriend from imminent unlawful force. The motion emphasizes that Florida law does not require a person in those circumstances to retreat before defending themselves. The filing cites Florida's Stand Your Ground statutes, arguing that Barthel has established a "prima facie" claim of self-defense. Under the cited law, the defense contends the burden now shifts to the State to prove by clear and convincing evidence that Barthel was not entitled to statutory immunity. Since his arrest, Barthel's attorneys filed a motion to secure the video footage from the elevator, which one would think would prove what took place during the incident.
summary: The latest: the hearing was regarding Barthel's motion to dismiss, where Barthel argued for a dismissal on the grounds that Barthel's use of force was legally justified and that he was immune. Both Barthel and Richard Reap, who filed the charges against him testified at the hearing.

summary_src: Chad Gable retained the IC title over Rey Mysterio and Dragon Lee on "WWE Raw". All three men were jumped following the match.
body: Lee put Mysterio in a sideheadlock. Lee tossed Gable out of the ring and he exchanged blows with Mysterio. Lee landed a dropkick to both men in the corners. Gable suplexed both men simultaneously. After the break, Gable laid in multiple forearms on Lee. They reversed each other's moves before Lee set up the Styles Clash, but Mysterio landed a crossbody and sent Lee to the outside. Gable locked in the Ankle Lock. Lee kicked Gable to make him let go, only to get put in the same move. Mysterio jumped on Gable's shoulders and punched him before dumping him to the floor. Lee bounced Mysterio's face off the turnbuckle and sent him to the floor. With Mysterio against the announce desk, Lee charged, but Gable blocked him. Lee suplexed Gable and followed with a Superkick. He then landed a hurricanrana over the top rope. Mysterio landed a West Coast Pop on Lee from the top rope. Lee double stomped Mysterio and Gable tossed him into the turnbuckles. Mysterio hurricanrana. He put Lee against the ropes and went for a 619, but Gable grabbed him and put him in an ankle lock. Lee landed a Styles Clash on Mysterio, but he kicked out. Lee landed a Dragon Bomb on Gable, but Mysterio broke up the pin. Lee sent Gable out. Mysterio blocked an Alabama Slam. He landed a 619 on Gable and then Lee. He followed with a Frog Splash on Lee, but Gable broke up the pin. Gable suplexed Mysteiro and then Lee. Gable suplexed Mysterio into Lee and Mysterio reversed a DDT onto Lee. Gable rolled up Mysterio for the win. After the match, Mysterio celebrated with Gable when they were attacked by Ethan Page. Lee was still on the outside when he was attacked by Big Cass.
summary: Chad Gable defeated Bron Breakker and Dominik Mysterio in a triple threat match on WWE Raw. Gable used an ankle lock on Mysterio to secure the victory and keep his Men's Intercontinental Championship.
