The competitors traded holds early with Lee applying a side headlock to Mysterio before tossing Gable from the ring. Lee then exchanged strikes with Mysterio and delivered a dropkick to both opponents in the corners.
Gable responded by suplexing both men at the same time. After a commercial break, Gable landed multiple forearms on Lee as the action continued with frequent reversals.

Lee attempted a Styles Clash but was interrupted by Mysterio's crossbody. Gable applied the Ankle Lock on Lee, who escaped only to be caught in the hold again while Mysterio targeted Gable from the top.

The match featured several high-impact moves including a hurricanrana over the top rope, a West Coast Pop, a double stomp, and multiple suplexes. Mysterio hit a 619 on both opponents followed by a Frog Splash on Lee that was broken up by Gable.
Gable ultimately secured the victory by rolling up Mysterio. Following the match, Mysterio and Gable were attacked by Ethan Page while Lee was assaulted by Big Cass on the outside.

summary_src: The Bloodline versus 946. The conclusion of the October 19th WWE Monday Night Raw from San Diego, California saw The Usos (Jimmy Uso & Jey Uso) storm to the ring with weapons in hand to call out 946 (Royce Keys, Carmelo Hayes, Jaida Parker, Bronco Nima & Lucien Price). body: The conclusion of the October 19th WWE Monday Night Raw from San Diego, California saw The Usos (Jimmy Uso & Jey Uso) storm to the ring with weapons in hand to call out 946 (Royce Keys, Carmelo Hayes, Jaida Parker, Bronco Nima & Lucien Price). Solo Sikoa showed up and took the fight to 946 at ringside, and then The Usos began to fight with the group. 946 ended up gaining control because of the numbers game. Making his way out to the ring to even the odds was WWE World Heavyweight Champion Roman Reigns. The two groups stood across the ring from one another, and then a brawl ensued. The Bloodline got the best of 946.
summary: The October 19 episode of WWE Raw in San Diego ended with The Usos calling out 946 with weapons in hand. Solo Sikoa joined the fight at ringside but 946 gained the advantage through numbers until Roman Reigns came out to even the odds. The Bloodline ultimately stood tall after a full brawl with the group.

body: The match will take place during the first installment of Heroes Inmortales, which AAA will film in Mexico City on Saturday, October 24. According to the event details published by Cageside Seats, the special will be divided into three episodes over the following weeks, with the opening installment airing live. La Catalina captured the AAA Reina de Reinas Championship from Flammer at Triplemania 34. Her upcoming defense will feature both the former champion and La Hiedra, creating a three-woman contest rather than a singles match for the title. The October 17 broadcast opened with Catalina discussing her journey to becoming champion. Las Toxicas interrupted the segment, prompting Catalina to question which member of the group deserved the next opportunity to challenge for her championship. Flammer and La Hiedra subsequently presented their respective cases to Mysterio, each seeking recognition as the leading contender. The general manager ultimately chose to include both wrestlers in the championship match at Heroes Inmortales. The format means Catalina must defend her title against two opponents simultaneously. Flammer and La Hiedra will also compete against each other, with the championship at stake for all three participants. Beyond the Reina de Reinas title, the first episode of Heroes Inmortales will feature two additional championship bouts. El Grande Americano will defend the AAA Mega Championship against Dominik Mysterio, while Los Perros del Mal will put the AAA World Trios Championship on the line against La Parka, Mr. Iguana and Niño Hamburguesa. The second episode is scheduled to feature Fenix defending the AAA World Cruiserweight Championship against Mini Vikingo. The third installment will include a match between El Fiscal and Abimso Negro Jr., alongside the induction of Marisela Peña into the AAA Hall of Fame. The three-part presentation will spread the announced matches and Hall of Fame ceremony across the weeks following the October 24 filming in Mexico City. The La Catalina, Flammer and La Hiedra championship bout is scheduled for the first episode.

body: Elsewhere on the show, World Heavyweight Champion Roman Reigns is back after his absence on last week's show. Reigns already has his next match set after defending against LA Knight at Money in the Bank. He'll be in a champion vs. champion match with Sami Zayn at Crown Jewel, with the latter expected to call him out tonight. Joe Hendry and JD McDonagh will also continue their never-ending feud with a singles match. Check out the full "WWE Raw" lineup below, which starts at 8 p.m. ET on Netflix: Intercontinental Championship: Chad Gable (c.) def. Dragon Lee, Rey Mysterio Chelsea Green and Iyo Sky def. The Judgment Day (Raquel Rodriguez and Roxanne Perez) Bronco takes a Spear from Reigns, and the Bloodline stands tall. It's good to see Reigns finally give a damn about his family after all this turmoil. He walks to the center of the ring, and the Bloodline all stand. All four stare down, and the big brawl ensues. The Usos each hit suicide dives on opposite ends of the ring. Solo takes Keys into the ring to try to land the Samoan Spike, but Hayes hits him with a crowbar, just like last week. 846 begins to completely beat down the Bloodline, as Jaida shows off some handcuffs. Keys threatens Solo with them, and Reigns' music hits. Keys gets on the announce desk and calls them idiots, asking when they're going to learn. Then Solo appears out of nowhere to trip Keys on the desk and send Hayes into him. OTM get in the ring to go at it with the Usos. The Usos pull up backstage with a bat and a chair before heading to the ring. Well, here's your main event segment. Somewhat anticlimactic sequence at the end there, but a fantastic match, as expected. And surprisingly, no interference from Big Cass or Ethan Page, who have been around these guys lately. Well, I spoke somewhat too soon, as both guys have emerged for the post-match attack. Lee hits the Dragonbomb on Gable. Rey breaks up the pin, then Lee throws Gable to the outside. Rey springs up over Lee to avoid an Alabama Slam and Hurricanrana Lee into the ropes! Gable returns to take a 619! Lee takes one! The Frog Splash from Rey! Gable returns to break up the pin! Back in the ring, Rey nails a floatover splash on Gable for a near-fall. Gable crawls to the corner, where Rey attacks with a shoulder check and punches. Gable sneaks out underneath Rey, ripping his feet out from under Rey to ram him face-first into the top turnbuckle. Lee launches Gable off the apron with a Hurricanrana, and Rey hits him with a top-rope West Coast Pop. Gable starts to work over Lee's leg, cranking and twisting until he bounces off the ropes to take a German Suplex and super kick. Lee baseball slide kicks Rey into the announce desk. Uh-oh. He has the dive set up. He hits the ropes, and Gable enters for a big belly-to-belly Suplex for the near-fall.

llm_long: Stardom is holding a meet-and-greet event with the NEW BLOOD tag team challengers known as Meni☆Mani at Korakuen Hall. The event is scheduled for Tuesday, October 20, 2026, and is set to begin at 17:35. It will take place at a special booth located in the lobby of the venue.

Participation requires the purchase of a specific portrait designated for the meet-and-greet at the special booth. Regular portraits and individual wrestler merchandise available at the Stardom merchandise booth do not qualify for the event. The special portraits include a handwritten message from the wrestler along with a printed signature.
The portraits for the October 20, 2026 event are priced at 3,000 yen including tax. This price differs from that of regular meet-and-greet portraits. Payment is accepted in cash only.

Several precautions are in place for the handover event. Any acts of violence, abusive language, slander, or remarks violating public order and morals toward wrestlers or staff may result in the customer being asked to leave without a refund. Customers failing to follow rules may also be removed if deemed malicious.
The event concludes once the line ends. Due to time and stock limits, new queues will be refused after capacity is reached. Each person is limited to purchasing one portrait per session.

After payment, participants must join the event without holding any items. The use of smartphones or other devices to show or hand to wrestlers is not allowed. Gifts such as fan letters or presents cannot be accepted, and physical contact including handshakes is prohibited. Photography and videography are also not permitted.

summary_src: WWE veteran Kevin Nash has a theory about why Roman Reigns defeated LA Knight. A few days ago at the WWE Money in the Bank PLE, Reigns defeated Knight to retain his World Heavyweight Championship. While Knight was seen as a favorite to win the title from Reigns, that did not happen.
body: WWE veteran Kevin Nash has a theory about why Roman Reigns defeated LA Knight. A few days ago at the WWE Money in the Bank PLE, Reigns defeated Knight to retain his World Heavyweight Championship. While Knight was seen as a favorite to win the title from Reigns, that did not happen. The Hall of Famer believed that with Street Fighter coming up, WWE needed to protect Reigns and his championship. “ Do you want the water cooler jargon to be, ‘Hey, that guy in the movie, he used to be the WWE champion up until Saturday when he got beat,’ or do you just say, ‘Hey, man, that’s the WWE champion’?” Street Fighter, also starring WWE’s Cody Rhodes, was released on Oct. 16, 2026, and is currently at 40% on Rotten Tomatoes. title: Ex-WWE Referee Raves About Maple Leaf Pro Wrestling’s Potential
raw_title: Ex-WWE Referee Raves About Maple Leaf Pro Wrestling’s Potential
body: TSN is one of Canada’s biggest and most historic networks, giving the company a platform to succeed. MLP’s show Mayhem aired on TSN, and MyAEW, thanks to the company’s working relationship with Tony Khan’s AEW. Korderas praised MLP’s production value and in-ring talent. He feels that the company can establish itself as the premier destination for pro wrestling in Canada. Jimmy Korderas raved about MLP’s potential as a pro wrestling company. The roster consists of a mix of independent wrestlers, local Canadian talent, and AEW stars. At MLP Northern Rising earlier this month, AEW stars Adam Copeland and Andrade El Idolo were among the wrestlers featured. The event took place at Mattamy Athletic Centre, formerly known as Maple Leaf Gardens, an iconic venue. Mattamy Athletic Centre could become a regular venue for MLP’s biggest events, further helping to establish the company. While the partnership with AEW is positive, Korderas believes the best is still yet to come for MLP. “[MLP], who are a growing company, I think they have something there. They have a product that I think can grow into something much bigger, at least in Canada, if not further on, because they are on the MyAEW platform now too. So [fans] can see it everywhere. And it is a good product,” Korderas told The Game Plan . He added: “It is different. I think it’s a different presentation from what everybody else is doing because they have a nice mix of talent.” “They have a nice mix of how they present their wrestling on television. It’s not as produced as WWE, nobody is. I mean, they’re different from everybody else. AEW is more wrestling focused, like in-ring focused than anything else,” Korderas told The Game Plan . “That’s where MLP is different, where they do a little bit of everything. Because back when Vince McMahon used to say – and I know people hated this – was, ‘We’re a variety show. We have a little bit of everything for everyone'” “If you concentrate on one single niche audience, then you’re missing out on a whole bunch of people watching your product and enjoying it,” he said. “You can do comedy? There’s a place for comedy. There’s a place for hardcore, a place for straight up wrestling.” “I think that’s what MLP’s bread and butter is right now, is they’re a nice mix. And using social media and having a collaboration with AEW definitely helps.” Giancarlo Aulino Giancarlo Aulino is sports writer who covers UFC for Heavy.com. He began writing for Heavy in 2025 after providing MMA coverage for Sportskeeda. Giancarlo is an experienced journalist and interviewer, having covered soccer clubs Toronto FC and Inter Toronto FC as a full-season reporter, and also producing sports coverage for Toronto radio station VIBE 105.5FM. More about Giancarlo Aulino
summary: He feels that the company can establish itself as the premier destination for pro wrestling in Canada. Jimmy Korderas raved about MLP’s potential as a pro wrestling company.

Roman Reigns addressed Thompson's criticism during an appearance on Club Shay Shay with Shannon Sharpe. Reigns noted that Thompson's show may not draw large audiences and suggested that mentioning his name helps generate views. He added that scrolling through Thompson's content reveals his connections and fan preferences.

Thompson responded in an exclusive interview with The Takedown on SI. He questioned whether Shannon Sharpe referenced his opinion for clicks and expressed hope that the upcoming Street Fighter movie achieves major success.
The Street Fighter film arrives in theaters on Friday. It includes WWE performers Cody Rhodes portraying Guile and Roman Reigns portraying Akuma.

title: Roman Reigns and Sami Zayn build toward Crown Jewel
raw_title: Raw recap & reactions (Oct. 19, 2026): Roman Reigns’ very busy night
summary_src: Stranded on Death Row Roman Reigns was a busy man this week. That has nothing to do with the song reference above this sentence, but I’ll get to it I promise. Let’s talk about Roman and Sami Zayn first.
body: Let’s talk about Roman and Sami Zayn first. They started the build for their Crown Jewel match with some nice visual storytelling. Peep what happened when Raw started: Sami “big dogged” Roman, which set the stage for their verbal back and forth. Now, to his credit, Roman reached out to Sami for help in this 946 situation. He reminded the Undisputed Champion about his honorary Uce status after the two bonded on the burden that comes with holding a championship. The problem came when they argued over which one of those titles is the championship. This is a basic story that wouldn’t do much for me if not for the history between these two. Sami pointed out Roman’s arrogance since the Tribal Chief once called the Undisputed Championship the championship but now it’s secondary since it’s not on his shoulders. Roman said it’s not about arrogance; it’s about the man holding the title. The World Heavyweight Champion also told the world the Undisputed Championship hasn’t “meant shit” since WrestleMania XL . Reasonable people can disagree on that, but I mean, yeah. This isn’t just about which title is more important now; it’s a battle for supremacy between two guys who consider themselves family. Ish. And about Sami finally earning Roman’s respect. That is, of course, if Sami makes it to Crown Jewel as champion, a possibility Roman happily mentioned. That led to a brief showdown between Roman and Penta during the latter’s entrance for his match, and then a backstage interview that showed Roman on his way out of the arena. That’s how this usually works these days: Roman shows up early, talks his trash, then leaves to let his cousins handle the dirty work. For once, The Bloodline outsmarted 946. Jimmy & Jey Uso lured 946 to come out and play, Solo Sikoa surprised them, with Roman being the very big surprise. That led to a visual I’m sure WWE will put on a loop from now until Survivor Series . Now, back to the song. There’s a real Death Row Records vibe to 946 right now that I love. Royce Keys is Suge Knight. Carmelo Hayes is Tupac. OTM is Tha Dogg Pound, and Jaida Parker is Lady of Rage. They have a ‘90s Hip Hop aesthetic that speaks to my heart. That said, I still need a bit more from them on the verbal front. Like I said last week, an explanation or two would be cool. They don’t need to be very deep or long explanations either. I just don’t know how many times they can show up on grainy footage, look menacing, and tell us ain’t nobody safe. Even when they got to the ring, Royce picked up the mic to emphasize the few people safe from their wrath. If you’ve ever seen the Prince of Space episode of Mystery Science Theater 3000 , it’s a lot like the insane amount of times the titular hero reminds the bad guys how ineffective their weapons are against him. It’s a cool catchphrase I just want a bit more from Suge, Pac, and crew. All that aside, War Games can happen tomorrow and it would be extra hot. We’re already at the tipping point and we’re not even a month a

title: WWE Raw 10/19/26: 3 Things We Hated & 3 Things We Loved
raw_title: WWE RAW 10/19/2026: 3 Things We Hated & 3 Things We Loved
summary_src: On a night that saw Roman Reigns join the war against the 946, here are three things we hated and three things we loved about the 10/19/26 episode of "WWE Raw!"
body: If you missed the show, as always, you can check out our "WWE Raw" 10/19/26 live blog to catch up on everything that went down Monday night. We keep things factual and objective over there, not to mention comprehensive, which is not something that happens in this space. Here, you get the WINC crew's subjective opinions, and only about the matches and segments that stood out to us the most. So please join us as we present three things we hated and three things we loved about the 10/19/26 episode of "WWE Raw!" WWE Now that it's officially Crown Jewel season, it made sense for this edition of "Raw" to open up with a verbal confrontation between World Heavyweight Champion Roman Reigns and Undisputed WWE Champion Sami Zayn ahead of their Men's Crown Jewel Championship match. With that said, I really struggled to understand the point of what they were saying to each other and the connection between things that they were bringing up. I had a hard time digesting why Reigns was bringing up The 946 to Zayn in the first place, and it wasn't made any easier by the fact it had no relevance to anything else going on in this segment, was incredibly unnecessary to throw into there in the first place, and had the video about Carmelo Hayes joining The 946 to kick off the show when it had nothing to do with this opener. It had no relation to Reigns and Zayn's subsequent debate about who the better champion was or their preceding conversation about Zayn now learning firsthand what Reigns tried teaching him in The Bloodline in terms of what being a champion entailed, making everything feel like it was kind of all over the place. I know that there will be those who did enjoy seeing this because it's Reigns and Zayn, but it just didn't click for me at all and was not my cup of tea. WWE After Roman Reigns and Sami Zayn went from talking about whether or not Zayn's title was important to talking about 946, Penta reminded them that he has El Dinero en el Banco briefcase. As Reigns was making his way up the ramp, Penta appeared. He did his Penta walk and then fist bumped some fans before standing directly in front of Reigns, forcing him to look him in the eye. Penta made his way to the ring and stared down Zayn. Without saying a word, Penta conveyed so much. He put both men on notice that he could come for them at any time and cash in his shot at one of their titles. Following the staredowns, he wrestled Bron Breakker. They were evenly matched until Breakker speared Penta. Penta was able to kick out, but Austin Theory attempted to interfere. Luckily for Penta, Je'Von Evans was there to hit Theory and Breakker with the briefcase. Penta landed the Destroyer to defeat Breakker relatively clean. That's a big deal for a match involving The Vision, let alone a match in WWE. Penta looked like a big deal from the moment his music and pyro hit to him standing tall in victory. title: Shotzi Blackheart plans to continue indie bookings after TNA signing
raw_title: Shotzi Blackheart explains what her TNA signing means for future bookings
summary_src: Despite signing for TNA Wrestling, Shotzi Blackheart is still ready to perform in the indies. A few days ago, Blackheart appeared on a TNA taping and was later announced as TNA’s newest roster addition.
body: Despite signing for TNA Wrestling, Shotzi Blackheart is still ready to perform in the indies. A few days ago, Blackheart appeared on a TNA taping and was later announced as TNA’s newest roster addition. Recently, speaking on Busted Open , Blackheart opened up in detail about joining TNA and what the new signing means for her future indie bookings. “I’m still gonna be busting my butt on the indies, taking as many bookings as possible and just having a good time. But yeah, TNA is where I’m at, and I’m hoping to do some really fun things at TNA. I’m really excited to work with all the girls there ,” the former WWE Superstar said. She also shared the reason behind joining TNA. “ It has been a long time coming. I had a couple matches back in like 2019, maybe 2018, with TNA, hoping I would become a Knockout then. And I’m finally here, and it feels good.” “ I’ve definitely had my ups and downs. Definitely had my doubts. But I feel like consistency is key, and eventually you get your day if you just stay consistent. So that’s just what I kept telling myself, even when I felt like my career was going into the gutter. I just was like, if I just stick with it, I will get my moment ,” she added. A former WWE Superstar for several years, Shotzi has past experience wrestling for TNA, specifically for the Impact Wrestling banner. She wrestled a couple of matches in 2018 and 2019. A few days after the news of her TNA taping appearance came out, Blackheart also wrestled on ACW Mischief Night ​2 in a three-way Casket match for the ACW Women’s Title and won it. title: Sami Zayn Retains WWE Title vs Cody Rhodes on Raw

body: Monday's bout was significant in terms of the impact it could have had on what may be the main event of the Crown Jewel premium live event on Nov. 7. title: Drew McIntyre Details Triple H's Hollywood Shift
raw_title: Drew McIntyre explains how Triple H changed WWE’s approach to Hollywood
summary_src: Comparing leadership between Vince McMahon and Triple H, Drew McIntyre recently shared how the latter changed the promotion’s approach to Hollywood.
body: Comparing leadership between Vince McMahon and Triple H, Drew McIntyre recently shared how the latter changed the promotion’s approach to Hollywood. After recently completing filming a few roles in some upcoming projects with top Hollywood names, McIntyre sat down with Busted Open , where he discussed Triple H’s role in changing WWE’s approach to the industry. “ These days, both the lads see it as, ‘Hey, if this is good for you and your brand, you want to do it, that’s awesome.’ And if it works for our brand, if it helps everybody, if it gets more eyes on the product, they’re all about it, ” McIntyre discussed. The former World Champion further opened up on Vince McMahon’s leadership and compared it with the current one. “Vince [McMahon] was very much like, ‘I need you here.’ McIntyre, being fair, added that with the live events schedule back in the day, McMahon needed his wrestlers. He claimed that his entire life consisted of wrestling every single week until the past few years. “ But as I say, Nick [Khan] and Paul [Levesque] are very much of the mindset, if it makes sense, if it helps everybody and helps your brand, which in turn helps our brand, because I’m not going anywhere anytime soon ,” he finished. McIntyre, 41, is set to be a part of The Last Druid with Russell Crowe and The Highlander with Henry Cavill, Crowe, and other big names. llm_long: Drew McIntyre compared the leadership styles of Vince McMahon and Triple H regarding WWE talent pursuing opportunities in Hollywood. McIntyre recently completed filming for multiple upcoming projects alongside major names in the industry.

During an interview, McIntyre explained that the current approach under Triple H and Nick Khan supports wrestlers taking on external projects. The mindset is that such opportunities benefit both the individual and the overall brand when they make sense.

McIntyre noted that Vince McMahon previously required wrestlers to remain available due to the demanding live event schedule. Under that leadership, McIntyre's career focused entirely on weekly wrestling commitments for years.
The former world champion stated that the shift allows for projects that help everyone involved. He emphasized his long-term commitment to WWE while pursuing these outside endeavors.
McIntyre, who is 41 years old, is involved in the films The Last Druid alongside Russell Crowe and The Highlander with Henry Cavill and Crowe.

Speaking on the latest edition of the Kliq This podcast, WWE veteran Kevin Nash heaped praise on Femi’s current run and how certain things have helped his character. “Am I the only one that realizes that the guy […]
body: Kevin Nash believes Oba Femi has a ‘rocket up his a**’ and is WWE’s next big star. “ Am I the only one that realizes that the guy with the rocket up his a** is Oba Femi? ” Nash said. “ When he came down, it was very exaggerated, kind of cartoony, Bushwhacker-y kind of a thing. Now he does that for maybe six to eight steps and then he just drops out of that and goes into kind of a cool jazz version of the original ,” Nash further addressed the presentation changes Femi underwent and how it helped him. Nash also believes Femi’s exchange with Paul Heyman a few weeks ago also potentially made Heyman join forces with Femi. “ When he was leaving the ring after he told Heyman to go [expletive] off because Heyman wanted to pull him in and be his next guy, he was basically dumping Bron Breakker and saying, ‘You’re my boy.’ And he said, ‘I’m not a Paul Heyman guy.'” “From just how well things are going, and he feels it, you could just see … he’s just a nice guy. You see it in his eyes. You can see it in his face, his smirk. He’s just going to get better and better and better and better ,” Nash said, before comparing Femi to Disney’s Lion King. “ It’s more like a Disney-type thing where he’s the Lion King. The Lion King’s not necessarily bad. He’s just … the hyenas aren’t going to [expletive] with him ,” he finished. Femi made his main roster jump earlier this year and faced off against Brock Lesnar in his main roster rookie year itself, before retiring him at WWE SummerSlam 2026. A former WWE NXT Champion, Femi is also the 2026 WWE Men’s King of the Ring winner. He is also expected to take on Roman Reigns next year at WWE WrestleMania 43. To learn more about how we rank wrestling matches on TheSportster, please check out our match ranking criteria guide here Joe Hendry has been a thorn in the side of The Judgment Day for several weeks, taking every opportunity to make fun of JD McDonagh’s head. In a rematch from early last month , these two competitors faced off once again on Monday Night RAW. A frustrated McDonagh attacked Hendry during his entrance, before taking aim at a guy in a Funko Pop mask at ringside. The match eventually began with Hendry taking it to his opponent, at one point selling how hard and big McDonagh’s head was after punching him. A Funko Pop figure was thrown into the ring to play some mind games, as the giant Funko Pop issued a headbut to Dominik Mysterio. McDonagh slowed things down and exerted some control over the contest before Hendry began fighting back, until more shenanigans ensued between those at ringside, with McDonagh hitting the giant Funko Pop guy with a guitar. One final piece of interference helped McDonagh to score the win with a running headbutt . The whole match was a complete misfire, with awful comedy, an overbooked presentation, and a lack of anything redeemable. Hendry & McDonagh did their best given the scenario, but it was still pretty terrible. Ahead of her match at Crown Jewel against Women’s World Champion Liv Morgan, WWE Women’s Champion Chelsea Green appeared on Monday Night RAW to team with Iyo Sky to take on the Judgment Day pairing of Roxanne Perez & Raquel Rodriguez. The match opened with some decent exchanges between Sky & Perez, with the babyfaces running wild for a few minutes, but it wasn’t long before the Judgment Day slowed the match down by slamming Sky into the barricade. body: While speaking with Brandon Kravitz, AEW World Champion Will Ospreay was asked whether he gets tired of being questioned about WWE. Here is what Ospreay had to say… “I know it’s a part of the gig. People always ask, and I can only give my opinion. I don’t really care about it. I’d rather focus on AEW, and I’d rather focus on what we’re able to do here and what I believe AEW is doing to change the face of professional wrestling. I love what we present. I love what we do. I love our wrestling. I love everything that we’re all about. So, I couldn’t really care less about any other promotion.”
summary: While speaking with Brandon Kravitz, AEW World Champion Will Ospreay was asked whether he gets tired of being questioned about WWE. So, I couldn’t really care less about any other promotion.

title: Lizard Music Starring The Rock Gets Release Date
raw_title: Lizard Music Starring The Rock Gets Release Date
body: The newest film from Benny Safdie featuring The Rock is Lizard Music , and it now has an official release date. Deadline reports that Amazon MGM Studios has set a December 25th, 2027 premiere date for the film, which Safdie is writing and directing. The film reunited Safdie with his Smashing Machine lead in Dwayne “The Rock” Johnson. Johnson was reported in October of last year to be starring in the film. Lizard Music follows a boy (Theo Clark Leber) left to his own devices who stumbles upon a secret late-night broadcast of lizards playing otherworldly music, and a hidden door to the extraordinary swings open. His search for answers leads him to an eccentric and whimsical old man nicknamed The Chicken Man (Dwayne Johnson) and his beloved companion, an 85-year-old chicken named Claudia – the boy and the old man become kindred spirits who find each other at just the right time. title: Tommaso Ciampa Open To NJPW Appearances And Shingo Takagi Match
raw_title: Tommaso Ciampa Open To NJPW Appearances And Shingo Takagi Match
body: Tommaso Ciampa is open to stepping into a New Japan Pro Wrestling ring, with Shingo Takagi high on his list of dream opponents. Speaking to SB Nation’s James Dator ahead of AEW WrestleDream 2026, Ciampa discussed the possibility of making appearances for NJPW and named the wrestler he would love to face. “Shingo [Takagi] always jumps out at me as someone I’ve always wanted to share a ring with,” he said. While the prospect interests him, Ciampa explained that a lengthy tour or a place in the G1 Climax might be difficult to fit around his physical needs and personal life. A shorter run, however, is something he would welcome. “I don’t know that my body or personal life at this point bodes well for a full-on tour or G1 Tournament, but doing a show here or there, or three shows, I’d be 100% open to that.” Ciampa has wrestled in Japan just once, during his time with WWE. He also appeared on ROH and NJPW crossover events in North America in 2014, competing in Canada and the United States. For now, his attention turns to AEW WrestleDream 2026, where he is scheduled to challenge Andrade for the National Championship.

Fantasy Book Adam Copeland’s Opponent For NJPW Wrestle Kingdom 21 | Question Of The Day by Anthony Mango October 16, 2026 0 244 views ReddIt Facebook Twitter Email Copy URL TRENDING (*UPDATED*) – Late-Breaking WWE RAW **SPOILERS** (10/19/26) – Everything Going Down! 0 Keith Lee-AEW Update 0 Adam Copeland / New Japan Pro-Wrestling (Image credit: AEW, NJPW) Welcome to another eWrestlingNews Question of the Day ! My question for you today is “Who do you think would be the best opponent or your favored option to step in the ring with Adam Copeland at Wrestle Kingdom?” My immediate response for any situation like this regarding someone’s retirement is to say that it isn’t up to me or anyone else to make that decision for the person who is bowing out. Who should Copeland face? Ideally, whoever he wants to face, full-stop, end of the conversation. Naturally, he might not have a preference, or his choice could be already booked in some other angle or otherwise unavailable. For instance, I highly doubt the plan is for MJF to face Copeland considering the setup for MJF to face Ryohei Oiwa with the “Real AEW World Championship” on the line. In general, it would make more sense (in my mind, at least) for Copeland to face someone who is more of a New Japan guy than to just step in the ring with another person from AEW. Will Ospreay versus Callum Newman makes more sense than for Copeland to be inserted into that story, or for Copeland to face Kenny Omega, who I’d guess could be up against Yota Tsuji, and it would be very odd if Copeland was just up against Jon Moxley. If he’s going to face someone effectively at random, it should be someone from New Japan’s roster, instead of fighting Gabe Kidd for the global title. My eyes go straight to Zack Sabre Jr. as a potential option. I would think that might kill two birds with one stone, as I know if I were a wrestler, I’d want to step in the ring with Sabre just based on his wrestling skills. He’s a skill-based “let’s put on a great wrestling match” type of opponent in a general sense, and to do that in front of that crowd would be quite the achievement to check off. If Christian Cage is out for several months, we can also count out the idea of a tag team match, unfortunately. It just wouldn’t be the same if Cope is teaming with someone else against The Knock Out Brothers, would it? The one other person who would be my backup idea, if we rule out just having Copeland against someone like Kazuchika Okada or my Zack Sabre Jr. idea, would be Shota Umino, who could always appear on Dynamite and Collision and do something with The Death Riders to help set up something with Copeland so that they aren’t just fighting each other blindly. title: On the Record: Drew McIntyre Takes Shot at WWE Stars for Being ‘Catchphrase Merchants’
raw_title: Drew McIntyre Takes Shot at WWE Stars for Being ‘Catchphrase Merchants’
summary_src: Drew McIntyre doesn’t need a catchphrase to get a WWE crowd eating out of the palm of his hand, and he plans to prove it when he’s back.
body: Speaking to Chris Van Vliet , McIntyre explained how acting has changed the way he looks at delivering promos. One thing he’s still trying to master is dialing down his intensity, because once a live crowd gets going, his plan to stay calm usually goes straight out the window. “It’s hard for me to take it down because I get so excited. My adrenaline gets so high, and I love it so much when I’ve got that audience that, when I’m in a real serious, deep promo, I try so hard to keep myself at a two.” McIntyre admitted that “two” doesn’t usually last very long. Once the adrenaline hits, he can quickly find himself yelling and getting so fired up that even his Scottish accent becomes thicker. “I’m like, ‘I’m going to be at a two, I’m going to be at a two.’ Then I get out there and it’s clearly an eight or a nine, then I go to like a 12 and I start ranting and my Scottish accent gets so thick.” Roman Reigns is someone McIntyre believes has already mastered the opposite approach. Drew praised Reigns for being able to stay restrained and make the audience lean in to hear what he has to say. “Roman and a few of the guys are real good at living around two and just keeping things — you’re going to have to lean in, Jake-style, to listen. And I’m working on that, and maybe with the lessons I’ve learned, I’ll be able to apply that when I get back.” Still, Drew doesn’t want to get so focused on the camera that he forgets about the thousands of people sitting in the building. He wants the live audience involved because he knows they’re desperate to feel like they’re part of the show. “But at the same time, I think you’re doing the crowd a disservice — the live crowd — if you’re kind of doing your thing just for the camera when you’ve got 20,000 people around you. It’s fun to bring them in, make them part of the show, because they want to be part of the show desperately.” “I don’t mean I’m going to start doing catchphrases because everybody does catchphrases. Everyone and their mother does catchphrases. I just want them to pay attention to the material and feel involved.” When Van Vliet pointed out that Drew doesn’t really have a catchphrase of his own, McIntyre said that’s completely intentional. He believes he could create one and get the audience chanting along if he wanted to. “I don’t want a catchphrase. I know I could say something and get them to chant along.” Apparently, Drew is going to put that claim to the test whenever “Hollywood Drew” finally returns to WWE. He already has an idea for a future promo where he’ll deliberately manipulate the crowd into responding exactly how he wants before pointing everyone back to this interview. “In fact, I will say it now — when I go back, whenever that may be, again, Hollywood Drew busy — I will do a test, because I know, like, I’ve learned how to be the puppet master for the fans, and I’m going to get you. He barely got the question out before Meltzer interrupted. “I mean, if this is. If this is, like, their War Games idea, I mean.” Alvarez went on to say that the match could do extremely well considering how strongly the crowd reacted to the confrontation. Meltzer then made it clear once again that WarGames is WWE’s planned direction for the feud, saying, “It is their WarGames. Yeah.” That would make plenty of sense considering WWE has been building this fight for weeks. The feud took another major turn on October 12 when Carmelo Hayes revealed himself as an ally of 946 and helped destroy The Usos and Solo Sikoa. Roman getting involved now gives the family some serious backup. The timing also lines up with Survivor Series: WarGames on November 28. WWE hasn’t officially announced the match, and there are still questions about how the teams will be put together. Roman, Jimmy, Jey and Solo are currently united against a group that includes Keys, Nima, Price, Hayes and Jaida Parker, but the final WarGames lineup remains to be seen. title: Match Made: Speculation on Will Ospreay vs. Adam Copeland World Title Match After WrestleDream
raw_title: Speculation on Will Ospreay vs. Adam Copeland World Title Match After WrestleDream
summary_src: Adam Copeland isn’t retiring without getting his hands on Will Ospreay first. AEW has already started teasing a match between the two, and the current belief is a World Championship showdown is coming. In fact, he thinks the company could pull the trigger as soon as Full Gear.
body: Speaking on the October 19, 2026 episode of Wrestling Observer Radio, Dave Meltzer addressed what happened between Ospreay and Copeland at AEW WrestleDream and the backstage interaction that followed. According to Meltzer, AEW is making it pretty clear that these two are eventually going to fight over the company’s biggest championship. The situation started at AEW WrestleDream on October 17 , where Ospreay successfully defended the AEW World Championship in the eight-man Clockwork Carnage Match. Copeland came incredibly close to winning the title, but Ospreay pinned him in the closing seconds to retain. Copeland wasn’t happy afterward and shoved Ospreay, but things eventually cooled down and the two shook hands. Meltzer believes that moment was no accident. “Yeah. So, you know, at the end of the pay per view, they did the thing where Osprey and Copeland shook hands. It was pretty clear that they’re going to do that match.” “So it would not shock me if that was the full gear main event.” While he isn’t certain about the timing, Meltzer sounded convinced that AEW is building toward Ospreay defending his championship against the former WWE Champion. “Ospreay and Adam Copeland are going to be doing a championship match at some point.” “Will Ospreay is one of the best wrestlers in the world, if not the best. Adam Copeland is very smart. He works his ass off. He’s very good.” Meltzer also pointed to Copeland’s recent matches as proof that he can still deliver when it matters. He specifically praised Copeland’s ability to structure matches and said he has no concerns about the two working together. AEW hasn’t officially announced Ospreay vs. Copeland, and there’s no confirmation that it’ll happen at Full Gear. But between their confrontation at WrestleDream, the handshake afterward and the backstage tease, the company certainly isn’t hiding the possibility. Copeland has a limited amount of time left before retirement, and Ospreay is sitting at the top of AEW with the World Championship. If the company wants to give Copeland another major title match before he walks away, this looks like the fight they’re setting up. title: Match Made: Roman Reigns vs. Penta’s Huge WWE RAW Ratings May Have Changed Company’s Plans for Mexican Stars
raw_title: Roman Reigns vs. Penta’s Huge WWE RAW Ratings May Have Changed Company’s Plans for Mexican Stars
summary_src: WWE may have found a new formula for pulling in viewers, and Penta is a big reason why. His match against Roman Reigns in Mexico City delivered some of RAW’s biggest numbers of the year. Now the belief is that WWE has taken notice, and it could mean a lot more opportunities for Mexican wrestlers ...
body: “Penta showed. He drew, you know, him and Roman drew the second biggest rating of this entire year for, for Raw. And that’s a worldwide number, not a Mexico number, and that is big in the United States.” And WWE already knows how successful that match was. As Ringside News previously covered , the September 14 episode drew more than three million global Netflix views, with both WWE and Netflix extremely pleased with the numbers. Netflix was so impressed that it wanted WWE to start putting bigger names and matches on RAW more often. But Meltzer says there’s another part of the equation. With Nielsen placing greater emphasis on Hispanic households, having Mexican wrestlers in major television roles is becoming increasingly valuable for WWE. “So having Mexican stars in higher positions and more is more valuable right now to WWE than it was two months ago. And they know it. You know, this is their business.” He made it clear that the wrestlers need to be involved in meaningful programs, including championship matches, rather than simply filling spots on the card. “But having them in key spots as top guys as at the championship level, that’ll make a difference if, if they’re, you know, as long as they have some charisma to them.” There’s already evidence that Penta’s performance changed his own standing in WWE. Ringside News previously covered how Penta wasn’t originally supposed to win Money in the Bank , but his match against Reigns helped change those plans. He eventually walked away with the briefcase, putting him in position for another major championship opportunity. title: On the Record: Ric Flair Calls Out WWE’s Developmental System for Making Young Talent “Practice Wrestle” Each Other
raw_title: Ric Flair Calls Out WWE’s Developmental System for Making Young Talent “Practice Wrestle” Each Other
summary_src: Ric Flair doesn’t think WWE has an athleticism problem when it comes to developing its next generation of stars. His issue is that he believes too many young wrestlers are learning by “practice wrestling” each other instead of getting the kind of real-world experience he had coming up.
body: Flair doesn’t believe there’s some massive talent gap between the two companies either. In his eyes, the biggest difference is that WWE has decades of history behind it while AEW is still relatively young. “The only distance — the only thing in between, in my opinion, WWE and AEW is the length of all the time the business has been open. You’re talking about 50 or 70 years as opposed to five years.” When it comes to the wrestlers themselves, Flair believes both companies have plenty of athletic talent. He sees a bigger difference in how WWE and AEW allow those wrestlers to perform. “But there’s equal athleticism on both. Um, Tony’s a daredevil and he lets the guys go wide open. The WWE is like, you know, trying to stay in that G-rated for commercials.” That’s when Flair turned his attention to WWE’s developmental system, and he wasn’t exactly sold on how things are being done. Flair estimated WWE has close to 120 wrestlers in developmental at the moment. “The problem is the WWE is — their developmental program has got 120 people in it, close to that.” “And they’re trying to bring these kids up, and all they’ve done is practice wrestle each other with no real opportunity to go out and learn how to work, and they’re on TV one time and, man, you don’t — make it, impress somebody, you’re not there next week.” The host then asked how things worked when Flair was learning the business, and his answer was pretty simple. Instead of spending most of his time inside one developmental system, Flair was constantly traveling and wrestling wherever he could. “And there’s nobody I didn’t wrestle. I mean, I wrestled — I mean, from Bruiser Brody to Stan Hansen to Lou Thesz, Harley Race, Pat O’Connor. I mean, I wrestled all of them.” That’s really Flair’s problem with WWE’s system — not that today’s wrestlers aren’t talented, but that he believes talent can only learn so much by repeatedly working with the same developmental group. For someone who learned by traveling everywhere and wrestling just about everybody, Flair clearly thinks today’s prospects need more chances to learn the hard way before the television cameras start rolling. What do you think about Ric Flair’s criticism of WWE’s developmental system? Do younger wrestlers need more experience outside the Performance Center before being put on television? title: IYO SKY Could Be Getting WWE Women’s Intercontinental Title Match Soon
raw_title: IYO SKY Could Be Getting WWE Women’s Intercontinental Title Match Soon
summary_src: IYO SKY might be next in line for a shot at the WWE Women’s Intercontinental Championship. She pinned Raquel Rodriguez on the October 19, 2026 episode of WWE RAW, and that victory may have earned her a much bigger opportunity.
body: Speaking on the October 19 episode of Wrestling Observer Radio, Meltzer discussed SKY teaming with Chelsea Green against Raquel Rodriguez and Roxanne Perez on RAW. The match ended with SKY catching Rodriguez in a cradle for the pinfall, giving her a victory over the reigning Women’s Intercontinental Champion. Meltzer believes WWE didn’t book that finish for no reason. He expects the result to lead directly into a championship match between SKY and Rodriguez. “Sets up intercontinental championship match relatively soon. Probably within the next few weeks.” That would be a pretty quick turnaround, but WWE has already been building tension between the two. As Ringside News covered during the October 12 episode of RAW , Rodriguez confronted SKY backstage while Roxanne Perez was arguing with Adam Pearce. Rodriguez accused WWE of forgetting about SKY, which led to an argument between the two women. Now SKY has pinned Rodriguez in the middle of the ring, giving WWE an obvious reason to put them together again with the championship on the line. Meltzer also had plenty of praise for SKY’s performance on RAW, particularly her exchanges with Perez. He felt the match was one of the stronger parts of the show and made it clear that SKY stood out. WWE hasn’t officially announced SKY as the next challenger, and there’s no date set for a title match. But Meltzer clearly believes that’s where things are going, especially after WWE had SKY pin the champion rather than Roxanne Perez. For now, Rodriguez still has the gold, but SKY has already beaten her. If WWE follows up on Monday’s finish, Rodriguez could find herself defending the Women’s Intercontinental Championship against someone who just proved she can put her shoulders on the mat. title: Ludwig Kaiser Stand Your Ground motion denied
raw_title: WWE star Ludwig Kaiser’s battery case dismissal motion denied
body: Earlier this year, WWE Superstar Ludwig Kaiser, aka Marcel Barthel, was arrested in Florida . Kaiser, currently performing as El Grande Americano in WWE's Mexican wrestling promotion AAA, was arrested on battery charges in Orange County, Florida. Kaiser's legal team aimed to have the misdemeanor battery charge dropped by invoking Florida's "Stand Your Ground" law. The claim was that Kaiser was justified in applying the level of force he did against the alleged victim because he reasonably believed it was needed to defend himself and his girlfriend, Andre Bazarte, from the "imminent use of unlawful force." A pre-trial conference is scheduled to take place on Dec. 17, 2026. Earlier this year, Sean Ross Sapp of Fightful and trusted media personality Raj Giri had opened up and shared details about Kaiser's arrest and charges. Previously, the charges were suspected to be domestic charges, but they were later dismissed by Sean Ross Sapp. "This is what I heard regarding the Ludwig Kaiser situation. He was in the apartment elevator with Andrea Bazarte and they were being affectionate, but nothing crazy or out of the ordinary. [Richard] Reap allegedly didn't say anything in the elevator but once he got out on the 12th floor, he allegedly said something to Kaiser to the effect of 'you need to show some f'n respect before I call ICE on that b**ch.' Kaiser got out of the elevator and they had a little scuffle, but no punches were apparently thrown," Giri wrote.
summary: WWE performer Ludwig Kaiser, also known as Marcel Barthel and currently wrestling as El Grande Americano in AAA, had his motion to dismiss a misdemeanor battery charge denied in Orange County, Florida. Kaiser's legal team argued he acted in self-defense under the state's Stand Your Ground law to protect himself and his girlfriend Andre Bazarte from imminent unlawful force. A pre-trial conference is set for December 17, 2026, per details first reported earlier this year by Fightful Select's Sean Ross Sapp and Raj Giri.

title: A&E and WWE to debut new in-ring competition series “WWE LFG” in early 2025
raw_title: A&E and WWE to debut new in-ring competition series “WWE LFG” in early 2025 - WWE
body: More Share Options More Share Options Share close facebook x threads email New York, NY – December 6, 2024 – A&E and WWE today announced an expansion of its programming partnership which will include the debut of “WWE LFG ( Legends & Future Greats ),” a new competition series that features in-ring matches along with a behind-the-scenes look at rising talent vying for a coveted WWE contract while being mentored by WWE Legends such as Paul “Triple H” Levesque, Undertaker, Shawn Michaels and Booker T. Additionally, WWE & A&E will launch “WWE’s Greatest Moments,” a series that will provide fans a front-row seat to relive the iconic events that have shaped WWE history. A new season of the hit-series “WWE Rivals” will also complement this winter’s WWE programming slate on A&E, which will add more than 180 hours of original content over the next three years. "Literally filled with blood, sweat, and tears, there's never been a series that combines in-ring action, behind-the-scenes reality, high-stakes drama, and some of WWE's greatest icons all in one package. From total unknowns to legends, ‘LFG’ will give viewers a raw, ground-up, 360-degree view of what it truly takes to make it in the WWE," said Rob Sharenow, President of Programming, A+E Networks. "Our collaboration with WWE has clearly struck a chord with audiences, and we’re excited to continue producing premium content that resonates with a diverse viewership." “A&E has proved to be an excellent home for WWE content, and we’re excited to partner with their fantastic team on these new show concepts and the latest season of WWE Rivals,” said WWE Chief Content Officer Paul “Triple H” Levesque. “WWE LFG” will offer viewers an inside look at the rigorous training process, featuring iconic WWE Legends such as Paul “Triple H” Levesque and Shawn Michaels and weekly regular coaches Undertaker, Booker T, Mickie James and Bubba Ray Dudley as they mentor a new generation in weekly matches on their quest to become the next WWE Superstars. Executive producers for WWE are Paul “Triple H” Levesque, Lee Fitting, Ben Houser, Shawn Michaels and Jeremy Borash. Elaine Frontain Bryant and Brad Abramson serve as Executive producers for A&E. "WWE’s Greatest Moments" will feature legendary play-by-play announcer Michael Cole hosting half-hour episodes with various WWE Superstars & Legends, including “Stone Cold” Steve Austin, Hulk Hogan, Kevin Owens and others, to share vivid recollections and perspectives on the most remarkable moments in wrestling history. “WWE Rivals” will return with an all-new season this winter celebrating some of the most iconic and beloved rivalries from the WWE including a never-before-seen look at Hulk Hogan vs. Ultimate Warrior and Roman Reigns vs. Seth Rollins . Executive Producers for WWE are Paul “Triple H” Levesque, Lee Fitting, Ben Houser and Marc Pomarico. Gable retained the title in the bout, after which Ethan Page and Big Cass attacked all three participants. llm_long: Chad Gable retained the Intercontinental Championship in a triple threat match on Raw against Bron Breakker and Dominik Mysterio.

The competitors traded holds early with Lee applying a side headlock to Mysterio before tossing Gable from the ring. Lee then exchanged strikes with Mysterio and delivered a dropkick to both opponents in the corners.
Gable responded by suplexing both men at the same time. After a commercial break, Gable landed multiple forearms on Lee as the action continued with frequent reversals.

Lee attempted a Styles Clash but was interrupted by Mysterio's crossbody. Gable applied the Ankle Lock on Lee, who escaped only to be caught in the hold again while Mysterio targeted Gable from the top.

The match featured several high-impact moves including a hurricanrana over the top rope, a West Coast Pop, a double stomp, and multiple suplexes. Mysterio hit a 619 on both opponents followed by a Frog Splash on Lee that was broken up by Gable.
Gable ultimately secured the victory by rolling up Mysterio. Following the match, Mysterio and Gable were attacked by Ethan Page while Lee was assaulted by Big Cass on the outside.

title: Multiple-weight world champion granted release from ZUFFA Boxing without fighting once
raw_title: Multiple-weight world champion granted release from ZUFFA Boxing without fighting once
summary_src: Shakur Stevenson has been granted his release from ZUFFA Boxing without ever stepping into the ring for the promotion. Stevenson confirmed on his YouTube channel that he was no longer with the Saudi Arabian-backed boxing promotion, which is of course headed by UFC and WWE owners TKO/Dana White.
body: Shakur Stevenson has been granted his release from ZUFFA Boxing without ever stepping into the ring for the promotion. Stevenson confirmed on his YouTube channel that he was no longer with the Saudi Arabian-backed boxing promotion, which is of course headed by UFC and WWE owners TKO/Dana White. “I requested to be released from Zuffa Boxing,” Stevenson revealed on his YouTube channel. “Now, over the weekend, my request has been granted. I’ve been in camp for like eight weeks, preparing for fights that I was told was going to happen and have not happened. It is what it is. This is the business of boxing. I’m not mad at anyone, I’m not pointing fingers. I am taking my career in my own hands and starting my own promotional company and I’m willing to work with other promoters and anybody else that’s willing to be as serious about my career as I am.” As of writing, ZUFFA Boxing has not responded publicly to the news. Stevenson was in talks to fight WBO welterweight champion Devin Haney, but those appeared to have stalled to a point that Stevenson wanted to get out of his contract with TKO Group. body: Roman Reigns and Sami Zayn faced off for the first time since both captured world championships, and The OTC followed up by taking the fight to The 946 with The Usos and Solo Sikoa. Penta took down Bron Breakker with the help of Je'Von Evans. Chad Gable again defended his Intercontinental Championship successfully. Lola Vice defeated Lyra Valkyria thanks to a timely Bayley intervention. This was the foundation of an important show as WWE heads toward Crown Jewel on November 7. Check out all the fallout from Raw below. Penta is Mr. Money in the Bank, and he looks extremely confident carrying around the briefcase. In some ways, he is already carrying himself as a world champion, which makes the luchador a big deal every time he appears. With this in mind, WWE should not rush the cash-in. Penta could continue to taunt the world champions while he chooses the perfect time to strike. The luchador could wait until the next major WWE show in Mexico or at least call his shot at a major premium live event, whether it be the Royal Rumble or WrestleMania. A quick cash-in disrupts the stories of both world champions and would take longer-term story builds off the table. Especially if Penta is going to have a lengthy run as champion, WWE should establish a clear direction for his reign before giving him the title rather than hot-shotting the change for immediate buzz. While The Genius of the Sky would be a great titleholder, she does not need the belt right now, especially with multiple younger, less proven stars waiting for their shot. In particular, WWE has set up Lola Vice as an immediately credible threat coming off an NXT Women's Championship reign. She even holds her own pinfall over Rodriguez. While Rodriguez is a veteran who deserved a singles accolade, it is time to move on to a younger star such as the 28-year-old Vice. WWE needs to keep building fresh names, and Sky losing to Rodriguez only for Vice to pull off the win would solidify the former MMA fighter as a real threat on Raw. Is there a bigger story on Raw that WWE has fallen short on building than the rivalry between Lyra Valkyria and Bayley? Since Valkyria's initial heel turn, WWE has been noticeably inconsistent in its presentation of her. Despite Valkyria's two wins over Bayley, The Role Model still feels more important to the weekly product. The Valkyrie's frequent absences from television have not helped. Next week, the two will collide in a No Disqualification match that may end this story. The match needs more than strong action; it needs a memorable moment that gives this rivalry lasting significance. This could mean Bayley and Valkyria pulling off the best spot of the night in the ring or a brawl outside of the ring that leads to a memorable fall in the backstage area. The goal should be to convince fans that these two matter, and whatever comes of this rivalry, both should be moving into the title picture afterward. title: On the Record: Ric Flair Admits He Does Nothing for AEW Despite Still Working for Tony Khan
raw_title: Ric Flair Admits He Does Nothing for AEW Despite Still Working for Tony Khan
summary_src: Ric Flair has a pretty sweet deal with AEW, and he’s not even trying to hide it. The WWE Hall of Famer openly admitted that he still works for Tony Khan despite doing absolutely nothing for the company.
body: Speaking during an October 15, 2026 interview on NewsNation’s BIFF , Flair discussed his relationship with the AEW President and had nothing but good things to say about him. He praised Khan for his generosity and his ability to juggle multiple responsibilities, including running AEW and his involvement with the Jacksonville Jaguars. That’s when Flair casually admitted that his own arrangement with Khan doesn’t involve much work. “He’s got that Learjet. He’s got a beautiful girlfriend. He’s a nice guy. He’s generous. I work for him. I work for him and I don’t do anything.” “You know, I think he takes care of me out of respect for me, you know?” Flair made it clear that his relationship with Khan goes beyond business, once again pointing to the personal respect between them. “He He He grew up on me and um He’s it it’s just a wonderful guy.” As Ringside News previously covered , Flair signed a multi-year agreement with AEW in November 2023. The deal was announced shortly after he appeared on AEW Dynamite as Tony Khan’s special gift to Sting. It also included a promotional partnership involving Flair’s Wooooo! Energy drink. Flair played a role in Sting’s retirement storyline leading up to AEW Revolution 2024, but he hasn’t been a regular presence on AEW television since then. That apparently hasn’t changed his relationship with Khan. In fact, Flair shut down rumors about returning to WWE in September 2026, making it clear that he remains loyal to AEW because Khan allows him to pursue outside business opportunities. Flair also stressed that the two are personal friends. Flair didn’t reveal how much money he receives under his AEW arrangement or whether his current agreement still includes guaranteed payments. However, he certainly made it sound like Khan is happy to keep him connected to the company whether he’s appearing on television or not. title: On the Record: Ric Flair Says Tony Khan Could Be the Greatest Wrestling Promoter of All Time
raw_title: Ric Flair Says Tony Khan Could Be the Greatest Wrestling Promoter of All Time
summary_src: Ric Flair has a pretty massive opinion of Tony Khan, and he’s putting him in some serious company. The WWE Hall of Famer believes the AEW President could go down as the greatest promoter in professional wrestling history.
body: Speaking during an October 15, 2026 interview on NewsNation’s BIFF , Flair discussed how much backstage politics influence professional wrestling. He explained that creative decisions aren’t always made by one person and suggested both WWE and AEW have groups of people involved in determining what happens on television. That’s when he made a huge prediction about Khan’s place in wrestling history. “I mean with Tony Khan who runs runs AEW who is really one of the most wonderful people I’ve ever known. Uh Tony has a group of people which I’m sure they do at WWE that um he circles up with and Tony Tony does it right there. So Tony Khan may be the greatest promoter of all time.” Flair went on to praise Khan for handling AEW while also maintaining responsibilities with the Jacksonville Jaguars. He seemed particularly impressed by Khan’s schedule and his ability to keep multiple major operations running at the same time. This isn’t the first time Flair has suggested Khan could accomplish something huge in professional wrestling. As Ringside News previously covered , Flair claimed in April 2026 that he wouldn’t be surprised if Khan eventually purchased WWE. He pointed to the Khan family’s financial resources as one reason such a deal wouldn’t shock him. Flair also believes AEW deserves more credit when compared to WWE. During the same interview, he argued that the biggest difference between the companies comes down to how long each has been in business. He also insisted that the quality of the wrestlers isn’t what separates the two promotions. “The The only distance The only thing in between, in my opinion, and WWE and AEW is the length of all the time the business been open.” “But there’s equal athletic athleticism on both. Um Tony’s a daredevil and he lets the guys go wide open.” Flair’s praise shouldn’t come as a complete surprise considering his relationship with Khan. The Nature Boy has been connected to AEW since 2023 and reaffirmed his loyalty to the company in September 2026. He’s made it clear that he considers Khan a personal friend and appreciates the freedom he has while working with AEW. Still, calling Khan a potential greatest-of-all-time promoter is a different level of praise. Vince McMahon spent decades building WWE into a global powerhouse, while Khan launched AEW in 2019 and has spent the years since trying to establish a serious alternative. Flair clearly believes Khan has the ability to take things much further. Whether Khan ever reaches that level is another story. title: Ric Flair Claims WWE Doesn’t Want Him in the Building Because of His AEW Ties
raw_title: Ric Flair Claims WWE Doesn’t Want Him in the Building Because of His AEW Ties
summary_src: Ric Flair says WWE doesn’t want him in the building anymore, and he believes his relationship with AEW is the reason. The WWE Hall of Famer claims his connection to Tony Khan’s company has made it difficult for him to attend events where his own daughter, Charlotte Flair, is wrestling.
body: Speaking during an October 15, 2026 interview on NewsNation’s BIFF , Flair was asked about Charlotte’s wrestling career and whether he still follows her matches. He made it clear that he watches everything she does, but attending those matches in person has become another story. Flair then explained that his AEW relationship has created problems when it comes to being welcomed at WWE events. According to the Nature Boy, WWE isn’t exactly interested in having someone connected to its biggest competitor walking around backstage. “If I’m not If I’m not there Well, I can’t go to a lot of them now cuz I work with AEW and they and they They don’t They don’t like to bring me into the building.” Flair was quick to clarify that this isn’t about personal problems with WWE talent or management. He believes it’s simply a matter of the two companies being competitors. “Um not because I don’t get along with the guys. It’s just that, you know, the competition” This isn’t the first time Flair has pointed to AEW as the reason he can’t attend certain WWE events. As Ringside News previously covered , Flair made a similar claim ahead of WrestleMania 41, explaining that his relationship with Tony Khan was keeping him from attending the event. Flair also shut down WWE return rumors in September 2026 , making it clear that he remains loyal to Tony Khan. He explained that he and Triple H are still friends, but he has no intention of disrespecting Khan by creating the impression that he’s returning to WWE. Now Flair is once again saying his AEW connection is keeping him from being welcomed at WWE events. WWE hasn’t publicly confirmed that it doesn’t want Flair inside its buildings, so for now, that’s his side of the story. title: Royce Keys Discusses Leading The 946 On Raw

summary_src: Royce Keys opens up about his position as the "face of" the 946, a group that's calling shots and wreaking havoc on the "WWE Raw" locker room.
body: During a recent interview with "Busted Open Radio," Keys opened up about his position as the "face of" 946, a group that's calling shots and wreaking havoc on the "WWE Raw" locker room. "I'm a natural born leader," Key said. "And so collectively, I wanted these four with me. You look at the great leaders of every faction in this business. The stuff you see with us, like arriving together, working out together, that's all us. We do that in every town. So it is my responsibility, the big brother role, to look after everybody, scold everybody, make sure we're all learning. They can teach me some things, and I'm going to teach them some things. So we're one unified unit." Last week, the 946 lineup was elevated to five members: Keys, Bronco Nima, Lucien Price, Jaida Parker, and Carmelo Hayes. The latter made his presence known in the "Raw" main event , which pitted 946 against The Bloodline's Jimmy Uso, Jey Uso, and Solo Sikoa. Hayes unmasked himself, then helped beatdown The Bloodline members with a crowbar. Jaida Parker marked her arrival by running over Jacob Fatu with a car and proclaiming "Ain't nobody safe." Nima and Price emerged alongside Keys in the stable's original reveal, which again targeted The Bloodline, in August. Parker, Nima, and Price's 946 onboarding coincided with their official call ups to WWE's main roster.

In 2019, Exterminador won the Occidente Heavyweight Title and Ace Austin won the IW X-Division Title. title: In Memoriam: PAC Had Blood Clot Issues and Lung Problems Before His Death at 40
raw_title: PAC Had Blood Clot Issues and Lung Problems Before His Death at 40
summary_src: PAC’s sudden death at 40 shocked the wrestling world, but it turns out he had been dealing with health problems years before his passing. The former AEW star experienced blood clot issues in 2023 and had a history of problems with his lungs.
body: Speaking on the October 19, 2026 episode of Wrestling Observer Radio, Dave Meltzer revealed that one of PAC’s friends had told him about the wrestler’s previous medical issues around the time of his death. Meltzer explained that while the full extent of those problems wasn’t widely known, PAC’s lung issues were something people close to him were aware of. “He did have lung issues. This is not something that came out of nowhere that nobody knew.” Meltzer then revealed that PAC had also dealt with blood clot issues back in 2023, something that adds another piece to his medical history before his death on September 27. “I don’t know how well that was known but one of his friends had told me like, you know, really like the week of his death, you know about the, he had the blood clot issues when in 2023. And he said that he had had some, some lung issues. And so this is. The lung issues are consistent with, with what happened.” Meltzer also shared information from Canadian physician Dr. Alex Patel, who explained how severe asthma attacks can become deadly when the airways become inflamed and restricted. While most cases can be managed with inhalers and medication, some attacks can get out of control very quickly. “Unfortunately you know, usually, you know, you would have the inhaler with you, and I don’t know, you know, you know, it may have happened so quick. There was stuff in his car, in the rental car, but he may not have been able to. It may have happened so quick. He wasn’t able to get it.” As Ringside News previously covered , PAC was discovered inside his running rental car outside a CAVA restaurant on September 27. The woman who called 911 said people had been trying to get his attention for several minutes without any response. Emergency crews arrived and attempted to save him, but he was pronounced dead at 4:08 p.m. The situation was especially shocking because PAC had wrestled Andrade at AEW All Out just one night earlier. By the following afternoon, he was dead at just 40 years old. Meltzer admitted that the more he learned about the situation, the harder it became to process. “And just a. It’s a horrible situation. The more you learn about it, it’s. It doesn’t get better. It gets. It gets worse.” For now, there’s no established connection between PAC’s blood clot problems in 2023 and the bronchial asthma that ultimately took his life. But learning that he had been dealing with previous lung issues makes his sudden passing even more heartbreaking, especially considering he was still competing inside the ring just hours before his death. title: 82-Year-Old Wrestling Legend Tiger Jeet Singh Sends Fan to Hospital With Sword, Then Blames Him for Getting Hit
raw_title: 82-Year-Old Wrestling Legend Tiger Jeet Singh Sends Fan to Hospital With Sword, Then Blames Him for Getting Hit
summary_src: Wrestling legend Tiger Jeet Singh returned to Japan after 14 years away, and things got completely out of hand when he struck a fan in the head with his sword. The 82-year-old wrestling veteran left the man bleeding and needing an ambulance during a live event in Tokyo.
body: The incident happened on October 17, 2026, during Megumi Kudo’s 40th anniversary wrestling show at Yoyogi National Stadium in Tokyo. Singh, who became one of Japan’s most notorious villains during his wrestling career, was serving as a special observer for a tag team match featuring Tatsumi Fujinami and Masakatsu Funaki against Mitsuya Nagai and Shiro Koshinaka. Singh made his entrance alongside his son, former WWE wrestler Tiger Ali Singh, and his grandson. Everything seemed to be going as planned until Singh charged toward the crowd with his trademark saber and started swinging it around. According to Sports Hochi , he struck a male spectator in the forehead, leaving him bleeding. The injured fan was taken backstage for emergency treatment before being transported to a nearby hospital by ambulance. Fortunately, the wound wasn’t deep, and the man suffered only minor injuries. He received treatment to prevent infection and was eventually able to return to the arena, pick up his car and drive himself home. But Singh wasn’t exactly losing sleep over what happened. Speaking to Tokyo Sports after the incident, the wrestling legend made it clear that he believed the fan was responsible for getting hit. “It was a mistake for him to be in front of me. It’s his fault. You know that, right? All he had to do was get out of my way.” His son, Tiger Ali Singh, didn’t exactly disagree. The former WWE star pointed out that announcements had been made warning spectators to be careful, arguing that the injured man should have moved when his father approached with the sword. “The announcer was saying, ‘Please be careful!’ They were warning him it was dangerous, but he didn’t move out of the way. I’m sure he won’t make the same mistake again. Just like my father said, this was an accident.” The show’s organizer, Megumi Kudo, took a different approach and apologized for the incident. The event was supposed to celebrate her 40 years in professional wrestling, but Singh’s entrance ended up becoming one of the biggest stories coming out of the show. Singh has a long history of terrorizing crowds in Japan, particularly during his famous rivalry with Antonio Inoki. Charging toward spectators with his saber was part of what made him one of the country’s most feared wrestling villains during the 1970s and 1980s. Apparently, turning 82 hasn’t changed his approach. The good news is that the fan escaped without serious injuries. The bad news is that Singh doesn’t seem particularly interested in taking responsibility for what happened. His first appearance in Japan in 14 years ended with someone being rushed to the hospital, and he’s still insisting the guy should have known better than to stand in his way. title: TOD by beIN Adds AEW Programming Across MENA
raw_title: TOD by beIN Brings All Elite Wrestling (AEW) to Fans Across the Middle East and North Africa
body: Doha, Qatar – TOD by beIN is expanding its world-class sports offering with the addition of All Elite Wrestling (AEW) , giving fans across the Middle East and North Africa access to one of the fastest-growing wrestling promotions in the world. Known for its high-octane action, compelling storytelling and globally recognised roster, AEW has rapidly built a passionate international fanbase since its launch in 2019 by AEW CEO, GM and Head of Creative Tony Khan. Featuring some of the sport's biggest names, including Will Ospreay, Kenny Omega, MJF, Chris Jericho, Jon Moxley, Adam Copeland, Christian, Mercedes Moné, Darby Allin, Kyle Fletcher, Thekla, Orange Cassidy, Willow Nightingale, Hikaru Shida, Kofi, Austin Creed and many more, AEW has become one of the world's premier wrestling organizations, attracting sold-out arenas, record-breaking pay-per-view events and millions of viewers each week. As wrestling continues to grow in popularity across MENA, TOD by beIN will bring fans weekly episodes of AEW Dynamite and AEW Collision , alongside major live premium events, allowing both long-time followers and newcomers to experience the excitement of the promotion. The upcoming calendar features blockbuster moments, including the highly anticipated AEW All Out event from Chicago on 26 September. For viewers discovering AEW for the first time, the promotion offers a unique blend of world-class athleticism, unforgettable rivalries and larger-than-life personalities, making it one of the most exciting entertainment experiences in global sport today. AEW programming will be available on TOD by beIN across MENA, with weekly episodes and major live events joining the platform's growing catalogue of premium sports and entertainment content.

Fans in the Middle East and North Africa will now get weekly episodes of AEW Dynamite and AEW Collision plus major live premium live events. title: Kairi Sane AEW Signing Delayed By Expired Visa
raw_title: Backstage Update On Visa Status Of Former WWE Star Kairi Sane
summary_src: Former WWE star Kairi Sane has been linked to a move to AEW, and a recent report has revealed that visa issues could be holding up the move.
body: " Fightful Select " reports that Sane has had a number of options, both in Japan and elsewhere, and the outlet highlighted what could be holding up her signing with AEW. The report stated that her US visa has expired and that she would need to be signed by a promotion willing to sponsor a visa for her to wrestle in the country. It further noted that she hasn't signed with AEW yet and that the visa process will begin once she has signed on the dotted line with Tony Khan's promotion. A report from a few weeks ago had revealed that AEW and Sane had talks about her joining the promotion, but it pointed out that she hadn't signed with them. Another former WWE star, Ilja Dragunov, was in a similar situation to Sane, as he also faced visa issues that were resolved ahead of his debut at WrestleDream this past weekend. Khan has acknowledged that Sane is someone that he would be interested in signing , speaking highly about her wrestling ability. Sane hasn't wrestled since her WWE exit but is set to feature in Chris Jericho's Rock 'N' Wrestling Rager at Sea, which will take place from November 7 to November 11, 2026.
summary: Per Fightful Select, Kairi Sane has several options available in Japan and other countries while her expired US visa prevents her from working stateside without a sponsoring promotion. The report adds that she has not yet signed with AEW and that the visa sponsorship process will begin only after she officially joins Tony Khan's company. Khan has previously expressed interest in bringing her in and praised her in-ring skills.
