summary_src: Tyler Breeze was on the chopping block early in his NXT tenure when he had his evaluation with Bill DeMott, who was the head trainer at NXT at the time. Speaking to Certified Mark Show, Breeze recalled the evaluation and how it went so poorly that he definitely thought he was getting fired. "If I’m…
body: Tyler Breeze was on the chopping block early in his NXT tenure when he had his evaluation with Bill DeMott, who was the head trainer at NXT at the time. “If I’m going down, I’m going down swinging. He said, ‘You don’t make any pitches.’ That was where I went, ‘Actually, we did make a pitch. You never got back to me on it.’ He goes, ‘What pitch?’ I said, ‘Me and Woods as a tag team.’ He goes, ‘We got back to you guys.’ I said, ‘No, you didn’t. We pitched it. We showed you the gear. We showed you everything. Why did nothing come from it?’ He goes, ‘We told Woods about it.’ I said, ‘Is that right?’ ‘Yeah.’ It was a tiny room, I opened up the door, and I go, ‘Woods, did they ever tell you anything about our tag team?’ He goes, ‘No.’ ‘Okay.’ I look right back at Bill, and I go ‘oof.’ I see what’s happening here and it’s a bunch of bullshit. From there, I got fired up and I started going [pitching multiple things]. As I’m swinging, Canyon (Ceman) goes, ‘Lets end it here before it goes down this path.’ At the time, right before I went and did the evaluation, I had a staph infection that I saw the trainer for. ‘What does this mean?’ ‘You have to go get it drained. You’ll be out for probably two weeks.’ We had this thing; it went horribly. I said, ‘You know what, I have a staph infection; I’ll be back in two weeks.’ I walk out and Woods is like, ‘What is that?’ I said, ‘By far the worst evaluation that anyone could ever get I’m definitely fired. Good knowing you, I guess,'” he said. Woods and Breeze had a short-lived tag team called the Hollywood Express during their time in FCW. The two would reunite as partners on the gaming channel UpUpDownDown. Woods is currently signed to AEW, wrestling as Austin Creed. Breeze is a free agent. If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.
summary: During an early NXT evaluation with head trainer Bill DeMott, Tyler Breeze brought up a tag team idea he and Xavier Woods had pitched that included showing gear. DeMott claimed the team had been informed of the outcome but Woods confirmed from the next room that he had never been told anything. The discussion energized Breeze to continue pitching other concepts until a producer ended the meeting.

llm_long: Tyler Breeze faced an evaluation with Bill DeMott early in his NXT tenure. During the meeting Breeze referenced a previous tag team pitch with Xavier Woods that had received no response.
Breeze stated that he and Woods had presented the tag team idea along with their gear. DeMott claimed the company had followed up with Woods, but Breeze disputed this.
Breeze then opened the door and asked Woods directly if anyone had informed him about the tag team pitch. Woods replied that he had not been told anything.
The exchange led Breeze to become more animated and begin pitching additional ideas. Canyon Ceman intervened to end the evaluation before it continued further.

Prior to the evaluation Breeze had been treated for a staph infection that was expected to sideline him for two weeks. After the meeting he told Woods it was the worst evaluation possible and that he expected to be released.
Breeze and Woods had previously teamed together briefly as the Hollywood Express in FCW. They later reunited as partners on the gaming channel UpUpDownDown.

title: Vince McMahon Allegedly Couldn’t Stand the Success of Triple H’s NXT
raw_title: Vince McMahon Allegedly Couldn’t Stand the Success of Triple H’s NXT
summary_src: Jaxson Ryker says WWE’s old black-and-gold NXT was so good that Vince McMahon couldn’t stand it. According to the former WWE star, the freedom Triple H and Shawn Michaels gave talent helped create a product that felt completely different from what McMahon was doing on the main roster.
body: “And you knew that. We would go in and sell out arenas, sell out, you know, live events. And from what I heard, Vince could not stand it because the quality — because what Hunter did, and I loved it, is Hunter and Shawn, those two and some others behind the scenes were putting together the shows.” Ryker believes one reason NXT worked so well was that wrestlers actually had a voice. He recalled Triple H, Shawn Michaels and others asking talent what they wanted for everything from entrance music to specific moments inside their matches. “They would have our — they would listen to our input. Even me and the Forgotten Sons, they would go, ‘Okay, well, what kind of music do you like for your theme song?’ Or, ‘What do you think about — what would you want to do in this match, in this circumstance?’” That was noticeably different from Ryker’s experience after reaching Raw and SmackDown . He said there were times on the main roster when matches were far more tightly controlled. “Instead of, you know, at times on the main roster, Raw and SmackDown, there was a lot of, like, man, micromanaging your matches. And, you know, not all the time, but there was a lot of micromanaging.” Triple H still had the final call in NXT, but Ryker didn’t have a problem with that. In fact, he admitted that when Triple H stepped in and suggested changing something, his idea was usually better anyway. “And it was, you know, Hunter still had the ultimate say-so. If he’d go, ‘Eh, maybe you should try this,’ and if he did that, dude, half of the time what he wanted you to do was going to be better.” For Ryker, the important part was that Triple H was willing to listen before making that call. He believes that freedom helped NXT develop its own identity instead of simply feeling like a smaller version of WWE’s main-roster shows. “But he’s very open for your character, for you putting a match together, and, like, the product was just different. And I think that’s why Vince was irritated, because it was just different. People loved it.” The interviewer also remembered NXT TakeOver events sometimes selling out before the main-roster pay-per-view happening the following night. It was the kind of run that made NXT feel like WWE’s legitimate third brand rather than simply the place wrestlers went before Raw or SmackDown . Ryker also remembers the locker room itself being completely different from the cutthroat environment people sometimes associate with wrestling. He said talent weren’t trying to stab each other in the back because everyone felt like they had an opportunity. “Yep. One hundred percent. Yeah, man. Everybody had an opportunity. And that was the beautiful part about it. It’s just — it was, like I said, it was a family, too.” That atmosphere apparently carried over outside the building as well. title: End of an Era: Ex-WWE Star Jaxson Ryker Explains Why He Retired From Wrestling After 23 Years
raw_title: Ex-WWE Star Jaxson Ryker Explains Why He Retired From Wrestling After 23 Years
summary_src: Jaxson Ryker has been offered chances to wrestle again since calling it a career, but don’t expect another comeback match. The former WWE star says he’s perfectly happy staying retired, especially now that his body feels “100 times better” without wrestling.
body: Speaking on Developmentally Speaking , Ryker was asked whether he immediately planned to continue wrestling after WWE released him or if he was already thinking about doing something else. By that point, retirement had already started creeping into his mind because his neck and lower back were giving him serious problems. “No, I think I had in the back of my mind that it was time to start maybe pursuing other things. My body, when I got released from WWE, my body was hurting real bad. I’d had a neck injury and a lower-back injury that was causing some — causing some numbness in my arm and my hand. Just really, really excruciating pain for the most part.” “I always told myself years ago, if I got to where I didn’t enjoy it anymore or my body hurt really bad, I’d walk away on my own. I didn’t want to be 50 and crippled. And so when it happened, man, I was like, ‘Okay, well, what do we do?’” “So, I was like, ‘Let’s just do kind of an independent run. I could go all over these places. I’ve worked for NWA and just do an independent run.’ And that’s basically what I did for the — well, I took three, four months off after they released me because I had a 90-day no-compete clause.” That became what Ryker personally considered his retirement run beginning in 2022. He only worked a handful of matches before finally deciding his body had given him the answer he needed. “And then after that, I started — this was the beginning of 2022 — I started kind of what I called my retirement run. I had a series of six or eight matches and ended in August of 2023. That’s when I had my last match, man. So, I knew it was time to kind of walk away. My body was just not feeling good.” Ryker did get the traditional emotional goodbye when the time came. After his final match, he untied his boots and left them sitting in the ring before heading backstage and realizing that chapter of his life was really over. “No, man. I get asked that quite often. And, you know, of course, when I had that last match and I did the old untie my boots and put them in the ring, and I get to the back and I’m like, ‘This is it.’” That could have easily turned into one of those wrestling retirements that lasts until somebody calls with the right offer. Ryker says those calls have actually come, including from friends and promoters asking if he’d consider getting back in the ring one more time. “But I’ve gotten, even since then, three years ago, I’ve had people call me, buddies of mine, promoters, ‘Hey, man, would you consider one more match?’” So far, none of those offers have tempted him. Ryker says retirement has been good to him physically, and that’s a feeling he’s not interested in giving up just to squeeze another match out of his career. “And I am so content in my retirement life. ’Cause my body feels 100 times better, you know. I don’t ache and moan and groan anymore as much as I used to.” His priorities have changed as well. After 23 years in wrestling, Ryker can look back at the punishment

title: Jeff Jarrett Calls For Max Caster Accountability
raw_title: AEW's Jeff Jarrett Names Most 'Disheartening' Part Of Max Caster-TNA Situation
summary_src: Jeff Jarrett has given his take on the Max Caster-TNA situation and how his former AEW colleague could have better handled the controversial incident.
body: "We're at least 24 hours in, and you know what the biggest thing that is disheartening to me as it stands today, and look, I don't know, Conrad, I am so far on the outside looking in, but obviously Max said it, and I saw the TNA statement. But Max, buddy, we need to hear from you. You have to at least, like, I mean, how can you not go, you know, I probably should, like, get out and talk about it. You scre*ed up. Own it. I mean, take accountability for it," he added. "We go out of our way [to not talk about], and rightly so, because politics and religion are a very personal matter that alienate your audience. There's no upside. None. I hate it, man. I hate it for TNA. I hate it for Max. I hate it for the business because people are talking about that out of an event as opposed to, god, I don't even know matches." Caster ultimately apologized to fans and TNA for the controversial rap, and a few days later announced he would be stepping away from pro wrestling for a little while . Many believed Caster's departure from TNA was due to WWE's partnership with Saudi Arabia, given the strong ties between WWE and TNA, but reports indicate that WWE has distanced itself from the matter , claiming it had no say in his exit.
summary: Jeff Jarrett expressed frustration over the controversy surrounding Max Caster's rap at a TNA event. Jarrett said the most disheartening aspect is that fans are discussing the incident instead of the matches and urged Caster to own his mistake and take accountability. Caster later apologized to fans and TNA before announcing he would step away from pro wrestling for a while.

title: Drew McIntyre praises Elijah Holyfield's potential
raw_title: Drew McIntyre sees ‘big things in the future’ for WWE NXT prospect
summary_src: Drew McIntyre has never actually seen Elijah Holyfield wrestle, but he still believes the WWE NXT prospect has big things in his future.
body: Drew McIntyre has never actually seen Elijah Holyfield wrestle, but he still believes the WWE NXT prospect has big things in his future. The son of boxing legend Evander Holyfield, Elijah signed with WWE in 2024 after playing college football at the University of Georgia and having a brief career in the NFL. Holyfield has competed on WWE LFG, WWE Evolve, and is being given an opportunity in Lucha Libre AAA. It was announced this summer that WWE and ReelShort are partnering together for microdramas , with “Agent of Shadows” being the first project in the collaboration. McIntyre, Jacob Fatu, Royce Keys, Joe Hendry, Ethan Page, and Michael Hayes are among the WWE personalities in the cast. The scripted microdramas are produced like TikTok-style vertical videos. McIntyre described himself as the “right-hand man” of the James Bond-esque main character, who is played by actor Chase Mattson. “It’s fun, It’s a really fun watch,” McIntyre told Van Vliet. “Hopefully everyone goes into it with that idea. Like, I’m about to have a little fun watch. You might be surprised about the romantic elements, the comedic elements, and at the center there is heart. And it is a very fun watch.” McIntyre should be returning to WWE programming soon after taking several months away as his Hollywood profile continues to grow. Joseph joined F4W during his time at UMass and has now been writing about the industry for nearly a decade. In addition to his work with F4W, Joseph has previously contributed to Sports Illustrated's wrestling coverage. He lives in Massachusetts and is a diehard fan of the Boston sports teams and Liverpool Football Club.

He has appeared on WWE LFG, WWE Evolve and is set for an opportunity in Lucha Libre AAA, while McIntyre is among the WWE talents involved in the ReelShort microdrama series Agent of Shadows.

title: Legal Watch: Keanu Carver’s Protection Order Extended as Court Pushes Arianna Grace Hearing Back
raw_title: Keanu Carver’s Protection Order Extended as Court Pushes Arianna Grace Hearing Back
summary_src: Keanu Carver’s legal problems aren’t going away anytime soon. The former WWE NXT star was supposed to be back in court on October 20 over the protection-order case involving Arianna Grace, but that hearing has now been pushed back another month.
body: According to court records obtained by Ringside News , new filings entered on October 19 show that Carver, whose real name is Kevin Robertson, will now have his next injunction review on November 17, 2026, at 9:00 AM before Judge Bryanna Bynum at the Criminal Justice Center in Sanford, Florida. The docket shows that Robertson’s attorney filed an unopposed motion to continue the hearing on October 19. A notice of appearance was also filed on behalf of Robertson that same day. The court subsequently issued an order continuing the temporary injunction and scheduling the November hearing. The October 19 order is listed in the court docket as follows: “ORDER CONTINUING TEMPORARY INJUNCTION SET FOR 11/17/2026 AT 9AM @ CJC CR-4A; JUDGE BYNUM” That means the existing temporary protection order remains in place while both sides wait for their next day in court. Under the previously issued injunction, Robertson is prohibited from contacting Grace, whose real name is Bianca Carelli, and must remain at least 500 feet away from her. As Ringside News previously covered , Carelli filed her petition on September 14, accusing Robertson of stalking, harassment and domestic violence. A judge granted a temporary injunction that same day before continuing it following a September 22 hearing. The October 20 date was supposed to be the next opportunity for the court to review the matter. The case has already produced some troubling allegations. Text messages previously covered by Ringside News showed Carelli repeatedly telling Robertson to stop contacting her, stay away from her home and respect her boundaries. The latest court documents confirm that the civil case remains open. The temporary injunction has not been dissolved, and the October 19 continuance does not amount to a final ruling on Carelli’s allegations. The records provided also do not establish that Robertson has been criminally charged. So while Carver’s WWE run appears to be over, the legal battle is far from finished. Another hearing has been pushed back, the temporary restrictions remain in place, and Robertson now has until November 17 before the case is scheduled to return to Judge Bynum’s courtroom. title: On the Record: Drew McIntyre Opens Up On Who Really Came Up With His Viral “I Prayed for This” CM Punk Line
raw_title: Drew McIntyre Reveals Who Really Came Up With His Viral “I Prayed for This” CM Punk Line
summary_src: Drew McIntyre’s “I prayed for this, and it happened” line about CM Punk is still all over the internet, but there’s a secret behind that infamous insult. It turns out Drew wasn’t even the one who came up with it.
body: “I mean, I knew talking to Triple H during the day that this is going to be so good. Like, I had an idea and it was too much. It would have offended a lot of people, which I’m very good at.” Drew explained that Triple H helped him pull back from his original idea before personally coming up with the line that would eventually become one of the most memorable insults of their entire feud. “He helped me reel it back, and then Hunter himself came out with the line which I ended up using, cuz I had such an extreme version and he dialed it back.” And Triple H wasn’t finished there. According to McIntyre, Hunter actually demonstrated how he should say it. Drew was so impressed that he decided to copy the delivery exactly. “I knew in that moment when Hunter delivered the line by toning me down a little bit, I went, ‘Wow, that is genius.’ Cuz I’m going to use that exact tone.” That’s where things got particularly nasty. Instead of coming out screaming about how much he hated Punk, McIntyre wanted to sound like he actually felt bad for him. He started the promo by talking about how devastating injuries can be, only to reveal that he was thrilled Punk had gotten hurt. The result was the infamous “I prayed for this, and it happened” moment. What started as a vicious shot at an injured CM Punk became an internet meme, with people using Drew’s face and those words for everything from sports victories to everyday situations. McIntyre admitted he knew the line would work when Triple H first suggested it, but he never imagined it would still be everywhere years later. “I didn’t think I’d be seeing it to this day for everything, no matter like what, if it’s sports or it’s well outside of wrestling, outside of wrestling. It’s constantly, it’s me pointing, ‘I prayed for this and it happened.’” Of course, the line was only one part of Drew’s bitter rivalry with Punk. The two spent months attacking each other on WWE television, social media and in interviews before settling things inside Hell in a Cell at WWE Bad Blood 2024. Even after their feud ended, McIntyre has continued taking personal shots at Punk . Drew also made it clear that the reason their rivalry worked so well was because neither man needed to pretend they liked the other. “There was a lot of, you know, programs, rivalries that were very big and spectacular and had their moments. Ours was just consistent. And to this day, it was consistent hatred. And people can feel that. You get two guys that are good at their job. They don’t have to like each other, but they understand when they’re in there, they’ll be professional.” So Triple H gave Drew McIntyre the line that turned into one of WWE’s biggest memes, and Drew made sure nobody would forget it. The crazy part is that McIntyre apparently had something even more offensive ready to go before Hunter talked him out of it. Now that might be the one promo idea Drew should explain next. body: DMFirst Veer Game odds uden om ROFUS IS WAR GAMES BECOMING A TROPE, MOVES THAT SHOULDN’T BE DONE FROM A LADDER, AAA IS FUN AND MORE By Dave Scherer on 2026-10-20 10:00:00 You can send us questions for the PWInsider.com Q and A at pwinsider@gmail.com . Did the WWF ever give serious consideration to main eventing a PPV with a one-on-one match between Hulk Hogan and Ted DiBiase? Not that I am aware of. Hell, they never even put the Title on him so I doubt they were looking to do him vs. Hogan on PPV back then. AAA has great action and solid storytelling. Anyone looking to product a wrestling show could learn from that. It’s the backbone of what makes a company successful. If the wrestlers are going to do dives off the top of a ladder, wouldn't it be safer to have them stand with their feet perpendicular to the top step, rather than parallel? Ability level aside, the way Tiffany Stratton was balancing on the top of that ladder looked awkward and she didn't appear completely comfortable. They should do dives in a way where the ladder is as stable as possible. In Stratton’s case, it was not even close as the ladder was moving as she was launching. Also, rather that do any flip move that requires torque off of a ladder, splashes make much more sense to me. You leave the ladder and immediately go downward, rather than trying to get height off of it. Personally I agree with the reader that feels War Games has had its day. If it happens every year in November without fail then we know it's a crutch for the booking to go down the route of two groups feuding for months and needing War Games to settle it. The best Survivor Series event I ever saw was 2002 which also didn't have the traditional survivor matches. It had an amazing card and was capped off with the first elimination chamber. Would we not be better off with a less is more approach with all these matches? The fact that it’s done because it’s November is an issue when the creative leading up to it isn’t great, for sure. We don’t seem to notice that when the booking is strong and the fans want to see the talents in the cage. But I agree, right now it’s more of a trope and that should never be the case with a match like that. That’s all on creative. Sure, there are politics involved as well, but it comes down to whether Creative wants to pull the trigger or not. You can send us questions for the PWInsider.com Q and A at pwinsider@gmail.com .

He also questioned whether WarGames is turning into a trope and suggested safer positioning for wrestlers performing dives from the top of ladders after observing Tiffany Stratton's balance on the structure.

title: Comeback Watch: Drew McIntyre Teases New Moves and More Violence for His WWE Return
raw_title: Drew McIntyre Teases New Moves and More Violence for His WWE Return
summary_src: Drew McIntyre hasn’t wrestled in WWE since WrestleMania 42, but he’s already planning some surprises for when he gets back. The former WWE Champion has spent months working on his body, and he’s now moving better than he did in his 20s.
body: Speaking during an interview with Chris Van Vliet on INSIGHT , McIntyre explained that his time away from WWE has allowed him to completely change how he trains. Instead of simply focusing on getting bigger, he’s been putting serious work into his footwork, balance, flexibility and conditioning. “I’ve been working out a lot. Like I’ve been building my body from the ground up, like improving my, you know, foundation. I didn’t realize how important it was till the past year and I’ve got like a great base now.” McIntyre said he’s been training barefoot and working with his trainer to improve his stability. That’s made a huge difference in how he moves, especially considering he’s now heavier than he’s ever been. “I’ve been working real hard in a way that my cardio and agility is, I’d say my whole life, but really for sure the past 12 years, is right now the best I’ve been. Like I feel great agility-wise. Bigger than I’ve ever been. I’m moving better than I have.” And Drew isn’t kidding about getting bigger. He revealed that he now weighs 285 pounds after gaining another 10 pounds of muscle. Despite the added size, he believes he’s in better physical condition than he was before stepping away from WWE. The improvements have also given McIntyre some ideas about what he wants to do when he starts wrestling again. He explained that people have been sending him old clips of his matches, and some of the moves he used to perform actually surprised him. “I’ve got a feeling some of my offense is going to be unique. I saw some videos of myself people had sent me, were highlight videos, and I was like, I didn’t realize I did that. Guess I’m going to start stealing for myself.” That doesn’t mean Drew is simply going to repeat everything he used to do. He believes his improved conditioning will allow him to perform some of those moves even better than he did when he was younger. “Forgot I did half the moves, and I physically can do them easily now and probably better than I did them when I was in my 20s.” McIntyre has already given people a glimpse of his progress. As Ringside News previously covered , he shared footage of himself running the ropes in September, showing that he was back inside a wrestling ring despite his extended absence from television. That video picked up millions of views, and Drew said people have been asking when he’s coming back ever since. But while he’s clearly preparing for an eventual return, he isn’t letting anyone rush him. “I know the audience, our fans are wanting me back. I see the messages every day and I appreciate it. I appreciate it. Just give me a little second and I’ll be back. Just a little second. When I decide.” McIntyre has been keeping busy with acting projects during his WWE absence, and he made it clear that Hollywood Drew isn’t finished yet. title: On the Record: Drew McIntyre Opens Up On Insane Sword Attack He Pitched to Vince McMahon for WWE
raw_title: Drew McIntyre Reveals Insane Sword Attack He Pitched to Vince McMahon for WWE
summary_src: Drew McIntyre carried a massive sword to the ring for years in WWE, but he never got to do the one thing he really wanted with it. He actually pitched Vince McMahon an idea that involved chopping someone’s arm off on television.
body: Speaking during an interview with Chris Van Vliet on INSIGHT , McIntyre revealed that he wanted to pull off a brutal sword attack using the same kind of practical effects seen in Saving Private Ryan . The idea was to make it look like he had actually severed someone’s arm, and he took the pitch directly to McMahon. “I also pitched, you know, to the big man himself. I was like, hey, you know, in Saving Private Ryan, and he, Vince, had never seen Saving Private Ryan.” That made things a little awkward because Drew was counting on Vince understanding the reference. McIntyre explained that the movie used performers with amputations to create realistic-looking injuries, and he wanted WWE to try something similar. His plan was to have a fight break out, possibly at WrestleMania, before moving the action backstage. WWE would then switch to a pre-recorded segment where Drew would finally use his sword on another person. “I think Mania or something. We should have a fight sequence. We end up backstage. Then we hit the pretape where I swing the sword at somebody.” “And finally, all those years later, Agent of Shadows, Drew McIntyre is going to go shanking. I’m stabbing some people. Finally.” McIntyre also explained that working on Highlander made him realize he should have taken sword-fighting lessons back when he carried the weapon on WWE television. After learning from professional stunt teams, he was amazed at how much he could actually do with one. As for his WWE entrance, McIntyre hasn’t completely ruled out bringing the sword back . He still has a personal attachment to the weapon, which was named Angela after his late mother, but felt it no longer fit the darker direction his character had taken. So Vince McMahon never gave Drew McIntyre the green light to chop someone’s arm off on WWE television, but Drew eventually got to swing a sword at people in Hollywood instead. Considering how far he wanted to take the original angle, it’s probably one of the more outrageous pitches that never made it onto WWE television. He focuses on delivering reliable coverage across WWE, AEW, and major wrestling promotions.

STAMFORD, Conn. & INDIANAPOLIS, Ind., June 24, 2024 – WWE and Indiana Sports Corp today announced a first-of-its-kind partnership that will bring WWE’s three largest stadium events – WrestleMania , SummerSlam and Royal Rumble – to Indianapolis. Kicking off with Royal Rumble on February 1, 2025, Lucas Oil Stadium will host all three Premium Live Events including a two-night SummerSlam and two-night WrestleMania in future years. “Indianapolis is a fantastic city for major events and we’re excited to invite the WWE Universe to Lucas Oil Stadium for Royal Rumble in 2025, and a future SummerSlam and WrestleMania,” said Chris Legentil, WWE EVP, Talent Relations & Head of Communications at WWE. “Patrick and the team at Indiana Sports Corp have done a phenomenal job bolstering local economics and tourism, and we’re proud to partner with them to shine a light on the great state of Indiana.” WWE and Indiana Sports Corp will also work with community partners across the state to create a legacy program that will leave an impact well beyond the three Premium Live Events. More details will be announced at a later date. Since its inception in 1979, Indiana Sports Corp has hosted more than 500 national and international sporting events, including Super Bowl XLVI, the College Football Playoff National Championship, Men’s & Women’s NCAA Final Fours and 11 Big Ten Football Championship Games. In total, these events have led to more than $4 billion in direct spending in the community. Ahead of the general on-sale date for Royal Rumble 2025, which will be announced at a later date, fans can register now to receive an exclusive presale offer by visiting https://www.wwe.com/royalrumble-2025-presale .

title: Top 50 good guys in wrestling history
raw_title: Top 50 good guys in wrestling history - WWE
body: More Share Options More Share Options Share close facebook x threads email Some folks might try to tell you it’s the villains that make sports-entertainment fun. And why not? It’s the baddies in the black hats who get to throw fireballs, electrocute millionaires and run people over with monster trucks. But it’s the good guys who give the fans something to believe in, a hero to look up to and a reminder that, more often than not, good does triumph over evil. Here, we present the 50 Superstars that wrestling fans grew up admiring — and still do today. ( PHOTOS ) Agree? Disagree? Let us hear about on the WWE Classics Facebook page . Diamond Dallas Page’s career in sports-entertainment is well-documented — from the moment he drove the Pink Cadillac carrying Rhythm & Blues to the ring at WrestleMania VI, to his legendary rivalry with “Macho Man” Randy Savage. Beloved by WCW fans and the WWE Universe, the New Jersey native represented a working class hero — a tireless competitor who earned every accolade. Following the formation of The New World Order, DDP was one of the first WCW competitors to stand up to the notorious faction, becoming an “everyman hero” as he outright refused to join their ranks. During his heated rivalry with “Macho Man,” Page defended both his honor and that of his wife, Kimberly, against Savage’s brutish, nWo-inspired tactics. No matter the odds, DDP never backed down from a fight, earning the moniker of “WCW’s People’s Champion.” ( WATCH ) Quick and agile despite being one of the most muscular grapplers of his era, Johnson’s smooth moves helped him become a popular attraction in areas of the country that were still struggling with segregation. The racial barriers Johnson broke are remembered today, but “Soul Man” wasn’t motivated by politics — he just wanted to entertain. “What set my dad apart from a lot of guys wasn’t the fact that he was this incredible black wrestler,” Dwayne “The Rock” Johnson once said of his WWE Hall of Fame father. “It was just that he was a great wrestler.” — RYAN MURPHY “My dad was a local hero,” The Road Dogg said of his legendary father, Bob Armstrong. A major star in Alabama and Georgia during the ’60s and ’70s, the WWE Hall of Famer’s “salt of the earth” appeal endeared him to Southern fans who favored substance over style. “He was one of them,” WWE official Scott Armstrong added. “He came from very humble beginnings and never hid that. He got up in the morning and had fried eggs and grits and gravy and did his thing.” A champion not only to folks in Dixie, but to his four sons — Brian, Brad, Scott, and Steve — the blue collar "Bullet” had his boys behind him when he took on rivals like Roddy Piper ( WATCH ) and Bobby Duncum, who he battled in a 1973 gorefest in The Omni Coliseum. “My father had a white singlet on and it was stained red,” Road Dogg vividly remembered. “He had to go the hospital and have a blood transfusion, but my father won and we won a 1974 Cadillac.” — R.M. title: In Memoriam: Famed wrestler ‘Pac’ died at 40 of an asthma attack in Des Plaines, officials say
raw_title: Famed wrestler ‘Pac’ died at 40 of an asthma attack in Des Plaines, officials say
body: A famed professional wrestler who died last month after a match in the Chicago suburbs suffered a fatal asthma attack, authorities confirmed Monday. Benjamin Satterley, 40, who performed under the name “Pac,” was found dead Sept. 27 in Des Plaines. An autopsy revealed the respiratory condition caused his death, the Cook County medical examiner’s office said. Satterley’s body was spotted in a rental car on the 2700 block of Mannheim Road, less than one mile from O’Hare International Airport. Satterley was alone and in the driver’s seat when he was found, authorities said, and there were no signs of foul play. A respiratory inhaler was found in a backpack in the car’s trunk, a Des Plaines police spokesperson said Monday. Satterley was part of Florida-based All Elite Wrestling. He was in the Chicago area that weekend for the company’s All Out promotion at the Now Arena in Hoffman Estates. Satterley previously had wrestled in other organizations, including in WWE under the ring names “Adrian Neville” and then “Neville.” Over 28 million people in the U.S. have asthma, according to the Asthma and Allergy Foundation of America. It can be triggered by pollution, allergens, stress and other factors. On average, between 9 and 11 people in the U.S. die from asthma daily, the foundation reports. Avoiding triggers, taking medications to prevent symptoms and being prepared to treat asthma episodes if they occur are the best ways to manage asthma, the foundation said.
summary: Per Chicago Tribune: a famed professional wrestler who died last month after a match in the Chicago suburbs suffered a fatal asthma attack, authorities made official Monday. Benjamin Satterley, 40, who performed under the name Pac, was found dead Sept. 27 in Des Plaines.

title: Tiger Jeet Singh accidentally injures fan with sword
raw_title: 82-year-old wrestling legend injures ringside fan with sword
summary_src: Tiger Jeet Singh recently returned to Japan in what was said to be his first wrestling-related appearance in the country in 14 years. However, the moment will likely not be remembered by most in attendance as a triumphant return.
body: Link Image from the Tiger Jeet Singh Foundation’s Facebook page Tiger Jeet Singh recently returned to Japan in what was said to be his first wrestling-related appearance in the country in 14 years. However, the moment will likely not be remembered by most in attendance as a triumphant return. While seeing the 82-year-old icon was surely a highlight for fans, the October 17th appearance at the Yoyogi National Stadium Gymnasium No. 2 in Shibuya, Japan, was marred by Singh accidentally injuring a fan with his sword. Japanese media reported that as Singh made his way to the ring while wildly swinging his trademark saber, the blade made contact with a fan’s forehead, and medical personnel at the venue attended to the man before an ambulance was called. According to Sports Hochi , the man was treated at a nearby hospital, but fortunately his injury was said to be minor. “It was a mistake for him to be in front of me. It’s his fault. You know that, right?” Singh said to Tokyo Sports . “All he had to do was get out of my way.” The Indian star’s son, former WWE star Tiger Ali Singh , backed up his father. “The announcer was saying, ‘Please be careful!’ They were warning him it was dangerous, but he didn’t move out of the way,” Tiger said. “I’m sure he won’t make the same mistake again. Just like my father said, this was an accident.” “I believe there were shortcomings in our corner team setup,” the Japanese star said at a post-show press conference. “I deeply apologize for injuring the fans who came to enjoy the show. I’m truly sorry. I think you were able to see the Shin you all wanted to see. However, I’m truly sorry that he [the fan] got injured. Speaking with Sam Roberts on Not Sam Roberts , 50 Cent and Noah Centineo explained how Cody was on set. “[Cody’s performance as Guile] is incredible. He’s so funny. He came up with lines off the cuff every day. All of his hilarious moments are pretty much from his brain. title: On the Record: Drew McIntyre Opens Up On His Wife Keeps Adopting Cats While He’s Away Filming
raw_title: Drew McIntyre Reveals His Wife Keeps Adopting Cats While He’s Away Filming
summary_src: Drew McIntyre might be busy building a Hollywood career, but his wife has apparently been building something of her own back home — a small army of cats. The former WWE Champion revealed that his wife, Kaitlyn Galloway, has adopted two rescue cats while he’s been away working on movies.
body: “Big cat, fat, fat black cat, massive. And I was just like, how is this cat living on the street and so massive, but the whole neighborhood was feeding him. He was in the HOA page. His name was Stormy because he lived in the storm drain.” Kaitlyn had already been letting the cat into their garage and feeding him, but Drew didn’t realize she had bigger plans. While he was on a flight, he happened to notice a message on the neighborhood page announcing that Stormy was getting adopted. The name of the person taking him in looked awfully familiar. “Oh, cool. That’s weird. It’s the same name as my wife. I started communicating with her and she’s like, ‘Yeah, I’ve got some news.’ I said, ‘What news would that be?’ ‘Yeah, we’re taking him in and it’s happening, so deal with it.’” That idea didn’t survive negotiations with his wife. Drew also suggested Donatello and considered Boomer because the cat was so big and constantly made noise running around the house. They eventually settled on something much simpler. “But we somehow we landed on Jasper. So he’s Jasper now. And he’s so large, maybe even larger. Just eats everything in sight.” “Then I found out later, okay, we got some news. We got another cat. She was outside in the cold. What was I supposed to do? And I was like, okay, we find another home or something. No, no, she lives with us now. But you get to pick the name.” Drew wasn’t exactly buying that naming arrangement anymore, considering how things went with Jasper. This time, however, the couple agreed on Penny Lane. McIntyre admitted that the newest addition doesn’t always treat him as nicely as she treats his wife. “We collaborated and we came to Penny Lane. Like she’s kind of copper color and occasionally she’s nasty to me and loves her, so I call her Penny Dreadful. But yeah, we’re building an army of cats.” The new additions come after McIntyre suffered the loss of his beloved cat Chaz earlier this year . Drew explained that Chaz’s memory is still part of their home, and Jasper has already picked up some of his old habits, including hanging around the dinner table looking for food. McIntyre confirmed that the household now has three cats, but he’s not convinced the number will stay there. In fact, he joked that if Kaitlyn keeps this up, his retirement plans might have less to do with wrestling and more to do with running a cat sanctuary. “These cat cafes and we’re going to end up owning one 100% or cat farm. That’s life after wrestling. Cat cafe maybe. It won’t be my choice. But yes, but I enjoy it. I reap the rewards. I complain about it, but then I’m just all like, ‘Yeah, these terrible cats. Come here. Be my friend.’ And Jasper has ended up being my buddy.” Of course, this isn’t the first time the McIntyre household has taken in a rescue cat . Back in 2020, Drew revealed that they had welcomed a stray named Piper into their family. For now, McIntyre is still focused on his acting career and an eventual return to WWE . But at this rate, e
summary: His name was Stormy because he lived in the storm drain. Kaitlyn had already been letting the cat into their garage and feeding him. While he was on a flight, he happened to notice a message on the neighborhood page announcing that Stormy was getting adopted.

title: Grayson Waller prevented from wearing Stephanie Vaquer shirt on TV
raw_title: WWE Champion was denied wearing NSFW Stephanie Vaquer Tshirt on TV
body: A few days ago, former WWE Women's World Champion Stephanie Vaquer celebrated her title win by sharing an NSFW photograph on her social media. However, just days after that, Vaquer lost the title to Liv Morgan at WWE Money in the Bank 2026. Recently, speaking to Sam Roberts on Not Sam Wrestling, WWE NXT Champion Grayson Waller opened up about how he had planned to use that photograph on his T-shirt to generate heat and mentally challenge Vaquer's boyfriend, Myles Borne. "There are some that haven't ended up on TV," Waller said when asked if a T-shirt he's made couldn't be worn on TV . "Stephanie Vaquer kind of broke the internet recently. She did an Instagram story posing like Shawn Michaels. "There was a t-shirt with that on it. That didn't end up on television. If anyone wants it, bribe me with some money. There is some fan who would pay some crazy money for it. I love to cause chaos, but if we can't fight about this, there is the line. Stephanie Vaquer doesn't feel like I should be doing that, are we going to have a match? That's not going to happen. That's where my line is," he finished. Wearing a Vaquer T-shirt would not have been new for Waller, who has in the past worn T-shirts referencing his opponents Zilla Fatu, Cruz Montana, and others. However, despite the perfect opportunity to amp up his level as a heel, WWE did not allow Waller to go ahead with the idea. Waller is now scheduled to defend his WWE NXT Championship against Tony D'Angelo at NXT Halloween Havoc.

body: Speedball Mike Bailey says that there are absolutely no half measures when it comes to Will Ospreay, noting he does not hesitate. Ospreay is currently the AEW World Champion and the leader of the US branch of the United Empire faction, which Speedball is a part of alongside Andrade El Idolo, the Brawling Birds and Francisco Akira. While speaking to The Wrestling Classic in a new interview , Speedball Mike Bailey spoke about Will Ospreay, noting that the AEW World Champion does not hesitate in the ring. “There are absolutely no half measures with Will Ospreay. There is nothing that he does, not a single movement, not a decision that he hesitates on. Everything is 100%, and I mean, that gets him in trouble sometimes. You see him overcommit, make decisions a bit too fast, and that might be his one flaw. But I mean, watching him go is absolutely impressive. The commitment and force with which he moves forwards, and that’s something that the first time we wrestled, which was at PWG in 2015, I could feel about Will Ospreay, and it’s something that he has maintained to this day. That has taken him to where he is now, which is AEW World Champion, the best wrestler in the world.” If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.

Khan highlighted PAC's accomplishments as a wrestler who performed in AEW, as Neville in WWE, and around the world. He emphasized that PAC was an outstanding performer, a great colleague, and a wonderful person to spend time with.

Before the wrestling began, Khan requested a moment of silence followed by a ten-bell salute in PAC's honor. He noted that PAC had been integral to AEW from its early planning stages and had become a significant part of many people's lives in and out of wrestling.

Khan recalled first meeting PAC prior to the company's public launch in January 2019 in the same Jacksonville parking lot. He stated that PAC was always envisioned as a major figure in AEW and had a profound impact on wrestlers and others in the industry.

The tribute included recognition of PAC's broad potential for success in any field and his achievement as one of the greatest wrestlers. Khan shared the announcement with the live audience ahead of the day's Ring of Honor tapings.

title: On the Record: Booker T Says WWE Wrestlers Were Afraid of Getting Backstage Heat for Taking Naps
raw_title: Booker T Says WWE Wrestlers Were Afraid of Getting Backstage Heat for Taking Naps
summary_src: Booker T was warned pretty early into his WWE run that taking a nap backstage could get him heat, but he wasn’t about to lose any sleep over it. Instead of following the unwritten rule, Booker deliberately tested it by telling Jim Ross exactly where he was going to sleep. Speaking on the Hall of ...
body: “I would just find a corner and go to sleep, you know. But I remember — I always think about the first time when I got to WWE, and I was in the locker room and I was nodding off, you know, and I was catching a nap.” “And this guy came in. He was so scared, and he goes, ‘Hey, Book, you know, hey man, I wouldn’t do that around here if I was you.’ And I go, ‘What?’ He goes, ‘Taking a nap. That’s not cool. You can get a lot of heat.’ And I go, ‘Taking a nap?’ He goes, ‘Yeah.’” Booker wasn’t exactly terrified by the warning. If anything, hearing how serious the other wrestler was about it made him want to find out whether this supposed rule was actually real. “Okay. And he was scared. He was really frightened, to the point where I go, ‘Let me test this theory, because I’m going to take a nap or they’re going to have to fire me.’ Right?” Booker didn’t quietly sneak away to see if anybody would notice either. Since Jim Ross was the person who signed his WWE contract, Booker decided to go straight to him and basically announce that he was about to break this supposed backstage rule. “So, the person that signed my contract was JR — Jim Ross. I remember walking after this guy told me that. I left, I was walking out, and I passed Jim Ross and I said, ‘Hey, Jim.’ He goes, ‘Yeah, Book.’ I said, ‘If anybody’s looking for me, I’ll be in my car taking a nap.’” Ross’ reaction wasn’t exactly the dressing-down Booker had been warned about. He simply acknowledged him and let Booker carry on. “He goes, ‘All right.’ I kept walking. And he didn’t say nothing.” That was pretty much all Booker needed to hear. As far as he was concerned, if one of the top people involved in bringing him to WWE didn’t care, he wasn’t going to worry about some mysterious backstage heat. “So, I said, ‘I’m going to go to the top guy and test this theory, because if I can’t take a nap, somebody’s going to come and tell me why I can’t take a nap.’” Booker also didn’t see sleeping as him being lazy backstage. He viewed it as part of getting himself physically ready to perform later that night. “Because me taking a nap is me preparing for tonight. I’m getting ready.” If WWE actually had a problem with that, Booker wanted somebody with authority to explain the logic to him. Apparently, that conversation never happened. “And when someone could, you know, tell me why I can’t prepare and get ready for tonight — because I don’t practice. I don’t do a lot of stuff like that like a lot of those guys did — somebody got to tell me. Somebody got to explain it.” In the end, Booker’s little experiment apparently settled the issue for good. He kept taking his naps, nobody came looking to punish him for it, and the supposed backstage rule never became a problem again. “And no one ever explained it to me. And no one ever said anything to me about taking naps, you know, my whole career.” Booker basically called WWE’s backstage bluff on day one and never heard another word about it. title: Injury Update: WWE Rumors on Scary Bron Breakker Fall, R-Truth's Injury vs. Damian Priest and Ilja Dragunov in AEW
raw_title: WWE Rumors on Scary Bron Breakker Fall, R-Truth's Injury vs. Damian Priest and Ilja Dragunov in AEW
body: 01:00 Featured Video Usos Call Out 946 📢 WWE Rumors on Scary Bron Breakker Fall, R-Truth's Injury vs. Damian Priest and Ilja Dragunov in AEW Mike Chiari Oct 20, 2026 Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe and All Elite Wrestling. R-Truth Speaks After Injury Bleacher Report 21h Breakker Should Be WWE's Monster Heel Bleacher Report 2d Full Grades from Latest Raw Bleacher Report 10m Bron Breakker avoided injury despite a scary fall from the top rope during a match at a WWE live event on Saturday night. Teaming with fellow Vision members Bronson Reed and Austin Theory against Oba Femi, LA Knight and Penta in the main event, Breakker lost his footing on the top rope during a spot with Knight and appeared to land awkwardly on his neck: Breakker was fortunately fine after the spot, as evidenced by the fact that he competed in a hard-hitting singles match against Penta on Monday night's episode of Raw. According to WrestleVotes on Fightful Select (h/t H Jenkins of Ringside News), there was "no heat" on anyone for the spot that went awry, as it was considered "a simple sort of mistake." WrestleVotes added that people backstage in WWE decided to "no-sell" the situation rather than making it a major talking point within the company. Given his high-impact style, Breakker does have a penchant for putting himself in harm's way at times during his matches. At the same time, his speed, explosiveness and athleticism are what set him apart from most other Superstars, so it makes sense for him to lean into it. Breakker was lucky to walk away from the fall with nothing significantly wrong with him, and the fact that he is already back in the ring and performing at a high level is a good sign that he should be OK moving forward. Damian Priest was reportedly the one who made the decision to end his match against R-Truth early on SmackDown last week. According to Bryan Alvarez of Wrestling Observer Radio (h/t WrestlePurists ), Priest "made the call" to quickly move to the finish once he realized that Truth had gotten injured. When Truth was unable to get up after executing a missile dropkick, Priest calmly spoke to the referee and went outside the ring to grab a steel chair. That allowed Fraxiom time to run down and protect Truth from Priest, prompting Priest to leave the ring without inflicting further damage. On Monday, Truth posted a photo of himself on X, seemingly preparing to undergo an MRI: Truth noted in the post that he is "OK," while joking that Priest "tried to kill" him. Priest and Truth held the WWE Tag Team Championships together from March until dropping them to The MFTs in August. Despite that run of success, Priest turned on Truth shortly after they lost the championships, noting within the storyline that he felt Truth was holding him back. A former world heavyweight champion, Priest is now able to portray a more serious character once again, and it could help him move back up the card in the singles ranks on SmackDown.

title: AJ Francis Claims AJ Styles Has Been Ducking Him for Years

summary_src: AJ Francis isn’t backing down from his claim that he’s the greatest AJ in TNA history, and now he’s calling out AJ Styles for supposedly avoiding him.
body: “I think AJ Styles agrees with me that I’m the greatest AJ that ever stepped in TNA because if he didn’t agree with me, he’d actually do something about it and he’s been ducking me for years. So I don’t think that he actually disagrees. I think he agrees I’m the greatest AJ to ever step foot in TNA. And you know, AJ Styles been ducking me for years.” “You know, Avery’s apparently ducking me because Frankie Kazarian’s telling him to. You know, maybe, just maybe, ducking is what runs in the Styles family. Maybe, you know, if it’s blood deep, blood in, blood out. Maybe they scared of AJ Francis on that family tree because they know I chopped that shit down.” The conversation then turned to Avery getting opportunities because of his famous father. Francis actually defended Avery’s position in TNA, explaining that he has no problem with second-generation wrestlers benefiting from their family connections. However, that doesn’t mean he’s planning to go easy on him if they ever meet inside the ring. When the interviewer pointed out that Francis still wanted to beat up Avery, he made his intentions clear. “Oh, I beat the shit out of Avery Styles for sure. I beat him. I give him the ass whooping his daddy fucking gave him a long time ago.” Francis was then told that facing Avery would be an opportunity to see whether the young wrestler could handle the pressure. He wasn’t interested in giving Avery much of a chance. “No, he gonna sink. He going to sink. Put belt to ass. I’m from the 90s. In the 90s, we used to beat children. You know what I’m saying? I was one of them children that used to get beat.” For now, these are Francis’ claims, and there’s nothing establishing that AJ Styles has actually been avoiding him. Still, Francis seems determined to get a confrontation with someone in the Styles family, whether that’s the father or the son. title: Keanu Carver Released By WWE
raw_title: KEANU CARVER RELEASED BY WWE
body: DMFirst Veer Game odds uden om ROFUS KEANU CARVER RELEASED BY WWE By Mike Johnson on 2026-10-05 11:34:00 WWE NXT star Keanu Carver was removed from WWE's internal roster and is gone from the company, PWInsider.com has learned. Carver (real name Kevin Robertson) was served with an order of protection preventing him from contacting a contracted WWE NXT talent (who PWInsider.com is not naming) after she filed for the order against him, alleging Carver, who she was formerly involved with, had stalked her and engaged in domestic violence. The talent filed for the order on 9/14 and it was ruled on 9/22 during a court hearing that the order would continue. PostWrestling.com was the first to report on the matter. Their report noted: "The petition alleges that the petitioner and Robertson dated and that the relationship recently ended. In the days that followed the breakup, Robertson allegedly made a series of unwanted visits to the petitioner’s home and made unwanted calls to the petitioner, as many as 44 times in one day. The 49-page filing includes many screenshots showing calls to the petitioner and stills from a security camera outside the petitioner’s home depicting Robertson’s alleged repeated unwelcome visits." The petition details multiple alleged incidents of unwanted visits and calls after their break-up. The petitioner says that Robertson came to the petitioner’s home on September 4 at 7 a.m., “intoxicated and under the influence of drugs and alcohol.” The petition does not specify what “drugs” Robertson was allegedly using. On September 8, the filing claims that Robertson again returned to the petitioner’s residence when the petitioner was not there. Robertson allegedly waited at the door. When he found the petitioner in their car, the petitioner tried to put the vehicle in reverse to drive away. He allegedly grabbed the vehicle, said he needed help, and “said he had drugs on him and he saw cops and his phone was 1% and he had no way to get home.” The petition claims Robertson returned to the petitioner’s home later in the night, knocked on the door, and circled the residence “all night long, finally leaving around 8 am or so.” The next day, on September 9, the petitioner claims Robertson called “a total of 25 times” and came to the petitioner’s residence when no one was home. Robertson allegedly returned again early the next morning at 2:01 a.m. The petition states Robertson proceeded to knock on the door “[a]ll night long” again, and “called my phone from a blocked number, called me on x (FKA twitter), made incoherent sounds, circled my apartment building.” Carver took to his Twitter account on 9/29, writing, "yall gone sound dumb ash in a month" and "Fake ass virtue signaling mfs everything done inna dark come to light" before later deleting the tweets and writing, "Keep god first" before deleting that and his Twitter account. There is a court hearing on 10/20 in regard to the issue in Seminole County, Florida.

title: Backstage Buzz: AJ Francis Claims He Got Backstage Heat in WWE Because a Celebrity Wanted to Meet Him Instead of Brock Lesnar
raw_title: AJ Francis Claims He Got Backstage Heat in WWE Because a Celebrity Wanted to Meet Him Instead of Brock Lesnar
summary_src: AJ Francis says he actually got himself into trouble backstage in WWE because someone wanted to meet him instead of Brock Lesnar or Randy Orton. That’s right, according to the former Top Dolla, simply having a celebrity guest request him was enough to upset people behind the scenes.
body: Speaking on The Wrestling Classic , Francis discussed why he’s much happier working for TNA than he was during his time in WWE. He explained that TNA recognizes his contributions and gives him opportunities to show what he can do. That wasn’t always his experience in WWE, where he believes his own popularity sometimes worked against him. “You know, when I was, you know, in WWE, sometimes you become a victim of your own success. Like, Expressions, who’s with me now in TNA. I remember one time I got a little bit of heat in WWE because when Expressions was backstage as like a celebrity fan before Money in the Bank in London, they asked him who did he want to see and he could have saw Brock Lesnar, he could have saw Randy Orton and he said Top Dolla and they’re like why do you want to see Top Dolla? Like what is, what is, what do you want to see him for?” Francis believes the entire situation showed how differently he was viewed in WWE compared to TNA. Instead of being pleased that a guest wanted to meet him, he claims people were questioning why anyone would make that choice. “So, it’s like I was a victim of success back then that I had fans. You know what I’m saying? And then now that narrative’s completely changed. Now, when I’m in TNA, I get an opportunity to show exactly how good I am. And now people are starting to realize how good I am.” The situation also marked the beginning of Francis’ friendship with Expressions. Francis explained that Expressions had already been following his career since Hit Row’s time in NXT, but their relationship became much closer after that initial meeting. “So he booked his own travel to Slammiversary. We teed it up and then he did my entrance at Slammiversary and that got like 5 million views across all social media. And you know, from that point on, the rest is history.” Francis now has Expressions working alongside him in TNA, and he believes the partnership has been a success. More importantly, he feels the company values the connections and creativity he brings instead of questioning why someone would want to work with him. Francis didn’t identify which WWE personnel allegedly gave him heat over the Money in the Bank incident, so his account remains his side of what happened. Either way, he’s making it clear that he hasn’t forgotten how he was treated during his WWE run, especially when he compares it to the opportunities he’s getting in TNA. title: Meltzer Shares Details On Pac's Lung Problems
raw_title: Dave Meltzer Details Past Health Issues Faced By Late AEW Star Pac
summary_src: Benjamin "PAC" Satterly died unexpectedly in September at age 40. Dave Meltzer provided more info on Satterly's past health issues.
body: During an episode of Wrestling Observer Radio , Dave Meltzer provided more information regarding Satterly's health. Meltzer stated that in the U.S., only about 3,000 to 4,000 deaths per year are due to bronchial asthma. He pointed out that most are over the age of 65. "We don't know if he had an inhaler in his car. He did have lung issues. This isn't something that came out of nowhere that nobody knew. I don't know how well it was known, but one of his friends had told me that really the week of his death — he had the blood clot issues in 2023 — and said that he had some lung issues. And so the lung issues are consistent with what happened unfortunately. Usually, you'd have the inhaler with you and I don't know, it may have happened so quick. There was stuff in his rental car, but it may have happened so quick that he wasn't able to get it. It's a horrible situation the more you learn about it. It doesn't get better, it gets worse," he said.
summary: Dave Meltzer discussed the health background of the late AEW wrestler Pac on Wrestling Observer Radio. He noted that Pac had known lung issues consistent with the reported cause of death and had also dealt with blood clot problems in 2023. Meltzer added that the situation becomes sadder with more information, as Pac may not have had time to use an inhaler that was possibly in his rental car.

Meltzer indicated that Satterly had known lung problems. These issues were consistent with the circumstances of his passing.
A friend had informed Meltzer that Satterly experienced lung issues in the week leading up to his death. Satterly had also dealt with blood clot problems in 2023.
It remained unclear whether Satterly had an inhaler available in his rental car at the time. The situation may have developed too rapidly for him to retrieve it.
Meltzer described the situation as horrible. He added that learning more details makes it worse rather than better.

title: Ludwig Kaiser battery case hits defense snag
raw_title: Ludwig Kaiser’s defense suffers a setback in Florida battery case
summary_src: Ludwig Kaiser’s defense team lost a key decision on Monday (Oct. 19) when a judge denied its motion to dismiss his ongoing battery case under Florida’s “Stand Your Ground” law. Kaiser (real name Marcel Barthel) was arrested on May 20, 2026, in Orange County, Florida, on a battery charge.
body: Kaiser (real name Marcel Barthel) was arrested on May 20, 2026, in Orange County, Florida, on a battery charge. The German wrestler was later released after making bail. TMZ reported it had obtained a police report on the incident, which occurred on April 23 in the building where Kaiser was living. According to TMZ , the report said Kaiser was in an elevator with a female companion (later revealed to be his girlfriend, AAA talent Andrea Bazarte), and the two started kissing and became “uncontrollably intimate.” After the elevator stopped at the 12th floor, a neighbor told the couple to “please have some manners,” which led to Kaiser allegedly punching the man repeatedly, pushing him to the ground, and threatening him. Kaiser flew back to Florida and turned himself in after learning about an arrest warrant while in Mexico on May 19. He was placed in custody and released on $1,000 bond. His attorney entered a “not guilty” plea on his behalf. Legal documents later filed by Kaiser’s defense team described a much different scene of what allegedly occurred during the April elevator ride. In Kaiser’s account, he pushed the neighbor in order to protect Bazarte, and the man threw a soft drink bottle at the wrestler. According to the defense, there were no physical blows during the incident. But on Monday, records show that Judge Andrew L. Cameron shot down the attempt by Kaiser’s legal team to dismiss under “Stand Your Ground”. The next step in the case will be a pre-trial conference scheduled for December 17, where the two sides can attempt to reach a resolution or decide if the case is going to trial. Meanwhile, Kaiser has been able to actively compete in AAA as Grande Americano after the court cleared him for international travel, even winning the promotion’s AAA Mega Championship from Dominik Mysterio last month at Triplemania 34 . title: Santino Marella Re-Signs With TNA Wrestling
raw_title: Santino Marella Re-Signs With TNA Wrestling
summary_src: Santino Marella isn’t going anywhere when his current TNA deal runs out. The Director of Authority has revealed that he’s officially re-signed with the company for another year, saying TNA’s current momentum made staying an easy decision.
body: Speaking on The Johnny I Pro Show , Marella addressed all the recent talk surrounding TNA contracts coming up at the end of the year. According to Santino, TNA President Carlos Silva got ahead of the situation and approached him about sticking around. “Okay, yeah, I mean, there’s a lot of talk about TNA contracts expiring at the end of the year. Carlos is very proactive, and he talked to me last week and said, ‘Of course, we’d love you back.’ So, I signed for another year with TNA.” Marella didn’t sound like he needed much convincing either. He pointed to where TNA is heading right now and the momentum surrounding the company since Impact moved to AMC as major reasons why another year felt right. “It feels like the right thing to do. It’s the right time — the direction we’re going, the momentum we have. Ever since we started with AMC, it’s been incredible. The locker room continues to shine.” Interestingly, Santino is even enjoying some of the negativity TNA has been getting online. He sees the increased criticism as a sign that more people are paying attention, especially after he felt the company proved doubters wrong heading into Bound for Glory. “I notice there’s more hate online this year, which is a good thing. They were doubting us going into Bound for Glory — we showed it to everyone, threw it in their faces.” Things got considerably more personal by the end of that year. After Santino teamed with Mike Santana, Steve Maclin and The Hardys against Team NXT in a Steel Cage match, Grace turned on her father and sided with Stacks, giving Santino a low blow after locking herself inside the cage with him. His authority role has continued to evolve in 2026 as well. TNA’s AMC debut introduced another wrinkle when Daria Rae arrived as Director of Operations, immediately clashing with Santino and claiming she could do his job better than him. That power struggle is something Marella expects to keep playing with now that he’s sticking around. He sees himself as someone making decisions with the audience in mind, while Daria approaches things from a much more business-focused perspective. “Being an authority figure, of course, we have an issue with Daria Rae, who’s imposing her authority. She’s business-oriented, but I think I come from the perspective of fans more, and we butt heads a little bit. It makes for entertaining TV.” H Jenkins H Jenkins has been breaking pro wrestling news on Ringside News for nearly a decade, with his reports featured by TMZ, Forbes, The Sun, and more.

title: AJ Francis Claims He Helped TNA Land Its AMC Television Deal
raw_title: AJ Francis Claims He Helped TNA Land Its AMC Television Deal
summary_src: AJ Francis believes he deserves some serious credit for helping TNA land its television deal with AMC.
body: Speaking on The Wrestling Classic , Francis was asked why he decided to sign another deal with TNA instead of looking elsewhere. His answer was pretty simple. He believes TNA recognizes what he brings to the company, and he feels his work has helped the promotion grow. Francis specifically pointed to the company’s AMC television deal as an example. While he acknowledged that names like The Hardys, Nic Nemeth and Moose have all contributed to TNA’s success, he believes his role has been just as important. Francis then made an even bigger claim about what he’s accomplished during his time with the promotion. According to him, nobody in TNA has done a better job of helping babyface wrestlers become more popular. “But nobody did a better job of building babyfaces over the last two years than me. Um, you know Joe Hendry, Mike Santana, you know even KC Navarro and Rich Swann, now BDE, you know Elijah, you know I could go on forever.” Those names include several wrestlers Francis has worked with during his current TNA run. His rivalry with Joe Hendry helped establish their on-screen relationship, while his more recent program with Elijah allowed him to combine his music career with professional wrestling. Francis believes that ability to help opponents become bigger attractions is something TNA understands and appreciates. “You know, and so like I felt like I have a home in TNA because they recognize what I bring to the table.” He also explained that his time in TNA has allowed him to take on a bigger creative role. Francis previously compared his position in WWE to being an offensive lineman, while describing his position in TNA as being the quarterback. When asked whether that comparison still applies, he didn’t hesitate. “Absolutely. I’m calling the plays. You know what I’m saying? And they sending me out there first to set the tone. And I’m doing it, you know, I’m doing it every time. And I’m making the most out of my opportunities. Whether I get 40 seconds backstage or eight minutes in the ring, you know, it doesn’t matter. I’m going to make the most of my opportunities. I always have, always will.” Francis also pointed to his rivalry with Elijah as an example of what happens when he’s given creative freedom. He described the storyline involving music, identity rights, their matches and Expressions getting hit with a guitar as some of the best work of his career. “That was probably the most, I think if you start from the beginning of me and Elijah’s storyline to the end of it at Lockdown. I mean, that’s probably the best storyline in wrestling this year. It’s the best, it’s the best creative, most creative storyline in wrestling this year. And I stand on that.” Francis isn’t claiming he single-handedly secured TNA’s television deal, but he certainly believes he played an important role in helping the company reach that point. His argument is that building popular wrestlers and delivering memorable storylines contributed to the promotion’s growth. W
summary: Speaking on The Wrestling Classic , Francis was asked why he decided to sign another deal with TNA instead of looking elsewhere. Francis specifically pointed to the company’s AMC television deal as an example.

body: Liv Morgan reflects on filming for ‘Bad Lieutenant: Tokyo’ was a completely different beast to what it is like to act in WWE. Last year, Liv would film for a role in ‘Bad Lieutenant: Tokyo’, and would miss some time with WWE as a result. Despite this gap in her time competing in WWE, Morgan has remained a staple of WWE programming and is currently the WWE Women’s World Champion. While speaking in a new promotional Q and A around her role in the movie, Liv Morgan explained that filming for the role was ‘a different beast’ to her work in WWE. “You know, a lot of WWE is acting, and so I feel like there were a lot of the same tools between WWE and acting. It’s like all the same tools, but maybe just used differently, and so it was cool to use my WWE experience and see how that translated to film. I feel like I was actually more comfortable and more prepared because of prior experience, but filming is like a completely different beast than what WWE is. So I feel like I learned a lot as well. title: AJ Francis Calls Out TNA’s Old Management for Giving Titles to the Wrong People
raw_title: AJ Francis Calls Out TNA’s Old Management for Giving Titles to the Wrong People
summary_src: AJ Francis has some complaints about how TNA used to be run, and he’s not keeping them to himself. The former WWE Superstar believes the company’s previous leadership had an outdated way of deciding who deserved opportunities, especially when it came to championships.
body: Speaking on The Wrestling Classic , Francis was asked how TNA has changed since he joined the company and how its move to AMC has affected the promotion. He immediately pointed to the difference in leadership, explaining that he prefers Silva’s approach over the way the company operated in the past. Francis believes the previous administration relied too heavily on traditional professional wrestling thinking. He praised Silva for bringing a different approach to managing the company and credited him with securing TNA’s television deal. “Uh, you know, I think just the leadership style has changed. I think the old leadership style was much more like oldtimey pro wrestling and I love how Carlos runs TNA.” Francis then defended Silva against people who have criticized his leadership, arguing that outsiders don’t understand everything he’s done for the promotion. Francis didn’t stop there. He explained that he’s able to communicate directly with Silva and appreciates the way he runs TNA. “Like that’s huge, right? And so like to have someone like that at the helm that I can, I mean I talked to him today, like he’s my favorite boss I ever worked for and I think that having him at the helm has been such a big help, such an improvement.” One of the biggest differences, according to Francis, is that Silva approaches wrestling more like a legitimate sports organization instead of relying on the same philosophy that’s been used in the business for decades. Francis believes that approach could finally benefit him, especially considering how long it’s been since he last held championship gold in TNA. “And his leadership style is more so of like real sports, right? Um, he doesn’t ignore what’s right in front of his face, right? Like it’s a damn shame that it’s been two years since I’ve been a champion in TNA. And Carlos recognizes that, right?” That’s when Francis took his biggest shot at the company’s previous approach to handing out championships. He suggested that wrestlers who had already put in the work were sometimes passed over in favor of newer talent who hadn’t accomplished nearly as much. “The old wrestling leadership style would be like, ‘Well, he’s still got a lot to prove, but let’s put a title on this guy who’s been here six months who nobody gives a shit about.’ Like that’s the, that’s the old wrestling style, right? And Carlos, Carlos recognizes what’s in front of his face.” “I do it because I’m trying to steal the show. I do it because I want to prove that I’m the best big man in the business and that I should be TNA World Heavyweight Champion. Um, I think that there’s only a matter of time before these things come to fruition because of the work that I’m putting in.” Francis clearly believes TNA is in better hands with Silva running the show, and he’s hoping that change eventually leads to a world championship run. He hasn’t accused any specific former executive of holding him back, but he certainly doesn’t miss the old way of making decisions

body: More Share Options More Share Options Share close facebook x threads email WWE has officially signed three former Olympic athletes to developmental contracts. The three decorated champions will report to the Performance Center to begin their journeys as WWE Superstars. From Worcester, South Africa, and then the University of South Alabama, Francois Prinsloo is a decorated track and field star with a background in the discus throw. Prinsloo won the Division I title in discus with a throw of 63.51 meters before competing at the 2024 Olympics later that same year. Hailing from Austria, the same country as “The Ring General” Gunther, Aaron Fara is a globally renowned star in the world of judo. A former world champion, Fara won the gold medal at the 2023 IJF Grand Slam and represented his country at the 2024 Olympic Games in Paris.
