title: Legal Watch: Maryland Federal Judge Allows Child Sexual Abuse Lawsuit Against WWE and McMahons to Move Forward - The MoCo Show -
raw_title: Maryland Federal Judge Allows Child Sexual Abuse Lawsuit Against WWE and McMahons to Move Forward - The MoCo Show -
body: In a 26-page opinion issued Monday, October 19, U.S. District Judge James K. Bredar upheld the application of Maryland’s Child Victims Act of 2023, which eliminated the statute of limitations for civil lawsuits involving childhood sexual abuse. The defendants argued that applying the law to allegations dating back approximately 40 years violated their constitutional right to due process, particularly because several individuals connected to the allegations have since died. However, Bredar rejected that argument, finding that Maryland lawmakers had a legitimate reason to eliminate the filing deadlines for childhood sexual abuse claims. The lawsuit, known as the “Ring Boys” case, involves seven men who allege they were sexually abused as minors while helping set up wrestling rings and performing other duties for WWE, then known as the World Wrestling Federation (WWF), during the 1980s and 1990s. According to reporting by Brandon Thurston of POST Wrestling , all seven plaintiffs allege abuse by former ring announcer and ring crew chief Mel Phillips Jr. One plaintiff also alleges abuse by former WWE executive Pat Patterson, while another alleges sexual harassment by former executive Terry Garvin. All three men died before the lawsuit was filed. The plaintiffs allege that WWE leadership, including Vince and Linda McMahon, knew or should have known about the alleged abuse but failed to take reasonable steps to prevent it. The defendants have denied the central allegations. Maryland’s Supreme Court upheld the Child Victims Act under the state constitution in 2025. The defendants subsequently challenged its application under the U.S. Constitution, arguing that allowing decades-old claims to proceed would make it difficult to mount an effective defense because witnesses have died, memories have faded and evidence may no longer be available. In Monday’s ruling, Bredar acknowledged those difficulties but determined that they did not make the law unconstitutional. “The Maryland General Assembly created its statute of limitations for child sexual abuse claims and, in response to a legitimate and pressing issue, decided to alter it in a rational way,” Bredar wrote. The decision follows a December 2025 ruling in which the court largely denied earlier motions to dismiss, reducing the number of plaintiffs from eight to seven. According to Thurston, claims by two plaintiffs remain against Linda McMahon, while all seven plaintiffs’ cases continue against Vince McMahon, WWE and TKO. “This ruling is a significant victory for our clients and for other survivors of childhood sexual abuse who have waited years for the opportunity to seek justice,” said Greg Gutzler, a partner at DiCello Levitt, one of the law firms representing the plaintiffs. “Trauma does not follow a legal deadline, and Maryland’s Child Victims Act recognizes that reality,” Gutzler added. As reported by Thurston, the case can now move toward discovery, during which evidence is exchanged and witnesses

title: Drew McIntyre discusses his physique and WWE future
raw_title: Drew McIntyre looks back on the "I prayed for this" line, being in the best shape of his life, says he's following in the footsteps of Michael Hayes
body: By Jason Powell , ProWrestling.net Editor ( @prowrestlingnet ) I feel like you’ve gotten bigger since the last time I saw you! “I have gotten bigger since the last time you saw me. I believe I was around 275 prior to Mania.” So, are you doing all this because you’re getting ready to return to WWE? “No, I just like to look good. Obviously, I’m in the best shape of my life. I feel physically great. I’m sure you saw the clip that was out there when I was running the ropes. I was just rolling around the ring at Miro’s school, Rusev; you’re very welcome. It’s here in Nashville, and my buddy was like, I’ve never seen anybody hit the ropes so fast because he’s not seen Bron Breaker, the only other man that’s faster than me. He got a little clip, a 15-second clip, and it blew up online. I think over 8 million views, so people seem to be excited about the idea that I’m coming back to wrestling, but I’m just seeing what happens right now. I’m enjoying myself. Hollywood Drew is jumping from project to project, and when the time is right, WWE is home.” When you look at the poster, it is filled with stars! Joe Hendry, Jacob Fatu, Booker T… “How on Earth could you leave out Michael Hayes? Nobody’s more excited about anybody being in that movie. Backstage, a curtain sell-out. Everyone’s very excited to see Michael in action. He killed it. He’s exactly what was needed for that role. I’m kind of following in his footsteps in a way. He was a wrestler, and I became a wrestler. Then he was in Highlander , and then he’s going into Agent of Shadows . So in a way, I’m following in Michael’s footsteps.”
summary: Drew McIntyre stated he has increased in size since WrestleMania and is currently in the best shape of his life. He noted that a clip of him running the ropes at Miro's school in Nashville received over 8 million views online. McIntyre said he is enjoying his Hollywood projects for now and will return to WWE when the time is right, adding that he is following in the footsteps of Michael Hayes.

title: Word On Visa Status Of Kairi Amid Free Agency
raw_title: Note On Visa Status Of Kairi Amid Free Agency
body: A new report has a bit of context on the visa status of Kairi as she remains a free agent. As noted , Kairi remains a free agent after her WWE deal expired following her release from the company. There were some reports recently suggesting that visa problems are preventing a deal from being done, but Fightful Select reports that it’s actually her free agency causing visa issues. Kairi’s US visa has expired and she needs to be sponsored by an employer or agency to get renewed. Kairi is not yet signed by AEW and thus her visa is not approved. Should she sign on with AEW or another promotion, an expedited visa is said to be able to be approved in as little as 15 business days.

llm_long: Chad Gable retained the Intercontinental Championship in a triple threat match on Raw against Bron Breakker and Dominik Mysterio.

The competitors traded holds early with Lee applying a side headlock to Mysterio before tossing Gable from the ring. Lee then exchanged strikes with Mysterio and delivered a dropkick to both opponents in the corners.
Gable responded by suplexing both men at the same time. After a commercial break, Gable landed multiple forearms on Lee as the action continued with frequent reversals.

Lee attempted a Styles Clash but was interrupted by Mysterio's crossbody. Gable applied the Ankle Lock on Lee, who escaped only to be caught in the hold again while Mysterio targeted Gable from the top.

The match featured several high-impact moves including a hurricanrana over the top rope, a West Coast Pop, a double stomp, and multiple suplexes. Mysterio hit a 619 on both opponents followed by a Frog Splash on Lee that was broken up by Gable.
Gable ultimately secured the victory by rolling up Mysterio. Following the match, Mysterio and Gable were attacked by Ethan Page while Lee was assaulted by Big Cass on the outside.

title: Will Ospreay Says Wrestling Has Evolved Past Full Kayfabe
raw_title: Will Ospreay Feels Wrestling As 'Evolved' Past Needing Full Kayfabe Protection
summary_src: Will Ospreay feels that wrestling has 'evolved' past needing to have full kayfabe protection on wrestling shows in 2026.
body: Will Ospreay feels that wrestling has ‘evolved’ past needing to have full kayfabe protection on wrestling shows in 2026. In 2026, kayfabe is not protected near as much as in decades past in professional wrestling, with programs such as WWE: Unreal and AEW: All Access delving into the backstage aspects of pro wrestling companies. While speaking to Real Radio Monsters in a recent interview, Will Ospreay spoke about kayfabe in modern pro wrestling, noting that while some things do need to be protected, wrestling has evolved past needing full kayfabe protection. “I mean it can still be done to this day and age for sure. It can be, but just like, I think, you don’t go into like a cinema. I like the Avengers and like Spider-Man and I love Batman. I don’t go into those things and instantly just go, well, ‘they’re not protecting the business.’ Do you know what I mean? I go into there knowing that I’m going to be sucked into a story and sucked into that universe. So like, it’s the same thing with wrestling. Whenever you walk into any arena that we do, we’re all characters and we’re all there to perform a show. Sometimes it gets dictated onto like social media where people act as their characters from there and they can cut promos there and it can promote over over to like different sources and different places but just like- I feel like wrestling has kind of evolved from that standpoint, like once upon a time it needed to be protected and I still feel like aspects of it do need to be protected, that’s why I’m not the biggest fan of the the backstage like stuff that’s being shown. I just think there are some things that fans need to see and some things that fans don’t need to see, and I don’t think fans need to know what time cues are. I don’t think they need to know when the commercial break’s coming up. I don’t think they need to be… Like, it just seems like one big ego fest. Look how amazing we are, the guys behind the camera. It’s like, shut up.” If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.
summary: Will Ospreay believes professional wrestling in 2026 has moved beyond the need for complete kayfabe protection. He pointed to shows like WWE: Unreal and AEW: All Access that explore backstage elements while noting some aspects still require safeguarding. Ospreay compared the experience to watching superhero films where audiences accept the story without demanding protection of the business.

llm.quote: I mean it can still be done to this day and age for sure. It can be, but just like, I think, you don’t go into like a cinema. I like the Avengers and like Spider-Man and I love Batman. I don’t go into those things and instantly just go, well, ‘they’re not protecting the business.’

llm_long: Will Ospreay believes professional wrestling has evolved beyond the need for full kayfabe protection in 2026. He noted that while certain elements should still remain protected, the industry no longer requires the strict maintenance of character that was once standard.

Ospreay compared modern wrestling to films such as those featuring Avengers, Spider-Man, and Batman. He explained that audiences enter those stories knowing they are fictional yet allow themselves to become immersed without questioning the protection of the craft.

According to Ospreay, wrestlers perform as characters when entering an arena to present a show. Social media sometimes extends this performance, with wrestlers staying in character to cut promos and promote events across platforms.

He expressed reservations about programs that reveal backstage aspects of wrestling companies. Ospreay stated that some information, including time cues and commercial break details, should not be shared with fans as it detracts from the experience.
Ospreay described excessive backstage exposure as resembling an ego-driven display focused on those working behind the camera rather than enhancing the product for viewers.

summary_src: Tiger Jeet Singh made a rare appearance in Japan on October 17 at Yoyogi National Stadium Gymnasium No. 2 in Shibuya, Japan. During his entrance, he swung his trademark saber and ended up cutting a fan on the forehand.
body: Tiger Jeet Singh made a rare appearance in Japan on October 17 at Yoyogi National Stadium Gymnasium No. 2 in Shibuya, Japan. During his entrance, he swung his trademark saber and ended up cutting a fan on the forehand. According to Sports Hochi , medical personnel at the venue attended to the man before an ambulance was called. He was treated at a nearby hospital, but this injury was said to be minor. Speaking to Tokyo Sports , Singh said, “It was a mistake for him to be in front of me. It’s his fault. You know that, right? All he had to do was get out of my way.” Tiger Ali Singh, Jeet’s son, said, “The announcer was saying, ‘Please be careful!’ They were warning him it was dangerous, but he didn’t move out of the way. I’m sure he won’t make the same mistake again. Just like my father said, this was an accident.” Megumi Kudo, who was celebrating her 40th Anniversary, apologizing for the fan being injured.
summary: Tiger Jeet Singh appeared at a show in Tokyo on October 17 and accidentally cut a fan on the forehead with his saber during his entrance. The spectator received treatment at a hospital for a minor injury after being attended by medical staff. Singh told Tokyo Sports the fan should have moved out of his way and that it was the fan's fault, while his son Tiger Ali Singh noted warnings were given beforehand. Megumi Kudo, who was celebrating her 40th anniversary, apologized for the incident.

The former WWE star has now made it clear that she won’t be wrestling at all during the trip, even as questions continue to swirl about her AEW future. ...
body: Speaking with Weekly Pro Wrestling magazine , KAIRI revealed that she’s already getting herself ready for an eventual return to the ring. She’s been training, working on her conditioning and even has some fresh gear almost ready to go. “I’m continuing to train and work on my physical conditioning in preparation for my return. I’ve also started working on a new costume, and it’s almost finished.” Then Chris Jericho’s Rock ‘N’ Wrestling Rager at Sea came calling . For someone who spent years sailing into WWE as the “Pirate Princess,” KAIRI couldn’t resist the chance to take that character onto an actual ship. KAIRI also wanted whatever she did first after WWE to actually mean something to her. The cruise checked that box immediately. “After leaving WWE, I wanted my first wrestling-related activity to be something I genuinely wanted to do, and this was it.” Here’s where things get interesting, especially with all the AEW talk surrounding her. KAIRI isn’t getting into the ring on the cruise, period. “I won’t be wrestling in matches this time. We’re planning merchandise sales, autograph sessions, and things like that.” So instead of throwing elbows and dropping Insane Elbows, KAIRI will be spending her time meeting fans. That’s actually a big part of why she wanted to do the cruise in the first place. “More than anything, I want to cherish the opportunity to meet the overseas fans in person — the people who have continued supporting me since my WWE days. Being able to meet them directly is very important to me.” There has also been plenty of talk about KAIRI eventually landing in AEW, but nothing has been signed publicly. Sean Ross Sapp recently made that part clear when discussing where things stood. The more interesting tease might actually be that new costume sitting somewhere almost finished. KAIRI is clearly preparing to wrestle again, but she’s keeping everyone waiting when it comes to where — and when — the Pirate Princess will actually make that return. title: Natalya Praises Rhea Ripley's Generosity
raw_title: Nattie: Rhea Ripley Is So Giving And Very Unselfish
summary_src: Nattie has high praise for Rhea Ripley. Counting only televised matches, Ripley and Nattie have shared the ring almost 20 times since 2019. This includes their extended feud throughout the back half of 2021.
body: Speaking with The West Sport for a new interview , Nattie said that Rhea Ripley will be in the best shape of her life when she comes back. “I feel like when Rhea comes back, she’s going to show everybody that she’s not only physically in the best shape of her life but she’s also mentally feeling rested, rejuvenated.” As it turns out, ‘The Eradicator’ might be turning Nattie into a dog person. “I went to her house and her dogs — I said to Rhea, ‘I’m a big cat person’ but then after seeing her dogs, all of the sudden I was just like a dog person. Her dogs are like her babies with her husband. They love their dogs but their dogs, you could tell they were so loved. These dogs were the sweetest animals and I was like, that’s because they have parents that love them. You know when you meet good kids, you know that they have good parents. Rhea is turning me into a dog person and I told her when I was at her birthday.” Nattie took her praise a step farther, saying that Ripley is giving and very unselfish. “She’s really one of my favorite people to wrestle because she’s so giving. People don’t realize that about her. When you’re in the ring with her, she’s very very very unselfish. We just had this really magical chemistry, I think she’s one of my top three in the world that I’ve ever wrestled. I just love locking up with her. I’d love a big juicy feud with her when she’s back.” Ripley has out of action since June. While her in-ring return date is currently unknown, she was recently announced for the Wrestlepalooza Perth Pre-Show event. Learn more here . title: Drew McIntyre says Triple H shaped his famous promo line
raw_title: Drew McIntyre credits Triple H for memorable WWE promo line
summary_src: Without Paul “Triple H” Levesque’s input, Drew McIntyre’s “I prayed for this and it happened” promo line never would have happened. McIntyre uttered the remark during a January 2024 promo directed at CM Punk, mocking him for his triceps injury.
body: Without Paul “Triple H” Levesque’s input, Drew McIntyre’s “I prayed for this and it happened” promo line never would have happened. McIntyre uttered the remark during a January 2024 promo directed at CM Punk, mocking him for his triceps injury. It’s proven to have staying power, with McIntyre telling Insight with Chris Van Vliet that he still sees himself pop up in memes more than two years later. He discussed the process of creating the promo and said his original intention was to say something more extreme. Paul “Triple H” Levesque helped McIntyre come up with a toned down version and the right cadence to deliver the line. “I mean, I knew talking to Triple H during the day that this is going to be so good. I had an idea, and it was too much. It would have offended a lot of people, which I’m very good at,” McIntyre said. “He helped me reel it back, and then Hunter himself came out with the line, which I ended up using because I had such an extreme version. And he dialed it back in the way he said it and the cadence of how it’s to be said, he said it like that. And I just went — I got so excited. McIntyre and Punk had a heated feud that included Punk defeating McIntyre in a Hell in a Cell match in October 2024. They still keep up kayfabe to this day, insisting that the hate they have for each other is legitimate. “I’ve been very, very fortunate how things have kind of organically fell in my lap. And WWE has been amazing the whole time, allowing me to do these things,” McIntyre said. “Historically, we weren’t allowed to do outside projects. It was very much, ‘You wrestle for WWE, that’s it.’ “But Nick Khan, Triple H, and the whole team have been very open to, ‘Hey, if it makes sense for the company, if it makes sense for your brand, which in turn makes sense for our brand. We’re going to protect you from things we don’t think are worth it.’ But ‘The Killer’s Game,’ the ‘Highlander’ which led to ‘Last Druid’ and now ‘Agent of Shadows,’ they have all just kind of organically came my way. And I feel very fortunate, and it’s been fun to see how I fare in that world.” Joseph Currier Joseph Currier is a graduate of the University of Massachusetts, obtaining a journalism degree in 2016. Joseph joined F4W during his time at UMass and has now been writing about the industry for nearly a decade. In addition to his work with F4W, Joseph has previously contributed to Sports Illustrated's wrestling coverage. He lives in Massachusetts and is a diehard fan of the Boston sports teams and Liverpool Football Club.

McIntyre originally planned a more extreme version that would have offended many people but Triple H helped tone it down and suggested the exact wording and delivery cadence. title: Where Things Stand With Dralistico and RUSH in AEW After Cryptic Tweets
raw_title: Where Things Stand With Dralistico and RUSH in AEW After Cryptic Tweets
summary_src: Dralistico’s cryptic “Maybe not for long?” post suddenly makes a lot more sense, and RUSH’s own mysterious message apparently has nothing to do with leaving AEW.
body: Bryan Alvarez of the Wrestling Observer addressed both posts after they sparked plenty of questions about the future of La Facción Ingobernable. When it comes to Dralistico, Alvarez believes the message behind that handcuffed photo was pretty easy to read. “Regarding the Dralistico and RUSH tweets we talked about last night: Dralistico’s AEW deal expires in December, and based on that tweet one would presume he wants out.” That’s a much more specific timeline than what had previously been reported. Alvarez had earlier said Dralistico’s contract was expiring “fairly soon,” but now December appears to be the month to watch. Dralistico certainly hasn’t been subtle with the imagery either. He recently posted a photo of himself behind bars with his hands cuffed and added one very short message. Dralistico hasn’t wrestled for AEW since the June 6 Collision taping, where he teamed with RUSH and Sammy Guevara in an unsuccessful challenge for the AEW World Trios Championship. Between that lengthy absence, his December contract expiration and the handcuffed photo, Alvarez believes it’s reasonable to read the post as Dralistico wanting out. The situation with RUSH is apparently completely different. He got fans talking on the same day when he tweeted another cryptic message: “See you 2027.” That immediately raised questions about whether RUSH might also be disappearing from AEW, but Alvarez says there’s a much simpler explanation. According to him, RUSH’s visa has expired, and he isn’t expected to have the situation resolved until the new year. More importantly, Alvarez says there isn’t any indication that RUSH is unhappy with AEW or looking for an exit. His absence is reportedly a legal work issue rather than anything involving his relationship with the company. “From all accounts it appears RUSH is happy in AEW, he just can’t legally work right now.” That clears up what initially looked like two LFI members possibly sending exit teases at almost exactly the same time. Instead, Dralistico is the one with a contract reportedly running out in December and a post that Alvarez believes could signal he wants out, while RUSH apparently just has to wait for his visa situation to get sorted. Dralistico still hasn’t outright announced that he’s leaving AEW, so his December expiration doesn’t guarantee an exit. However, with only a couple of months left on his deal and that “Maybe not for long?” message hanging out there, his future suddenly looks a lot more interesting than RUSH’s. Outside of the “Broke” Corbin gimmick, he has forever been amongst WWE’s least interesting acts. Ever since returning to WWE in 2026, it is hard to pin down what his personality is exactly supposed to be outside of “generic heel”. He comes to the ring with a drawling voice, acts unlikable, and cheats his way to victories, and while it can sometimes be an effective way of drawing heat, fans are starting to get bored. There have been glimpses over the years of Corbin’s quality at portraying an effective character, most notably during his brief run as “Broke” Corbin and during a babyface spell in NXT that invigorated his entire career (until a second main roster call-up where he was completely wasted and misused), but time and time again he has been left with dead-end booking. title: AEW's Pac Dies at 40 in Illinois Parking Lot
raw_title: Exclusive | Heartbreaking call AEW star Pac received as paramedics worked to save his life
body: The wife of AEW star Benjamin Satterley, known as Pac, called his cellphone as police investigated the wrestler’s death after finding him slumped over in his vehicle, a newly released report revealed. Natalie Taylor, Satterley’s spouse, called her husband’s phone on Sept. 27 as law enforcement was on scene after his passing in the parking lot of a CAVA restaurant in Des Plaines, Ill , according to a Cook County Medical Examiner report released to the California Post Monday. When police answered her call, she “reported that she last spoke with Satterley” less than three hours before he was pronounced dead at just 40 years old . “Satterley told his wife that he was stopping at the restaurant CAVA before heading to O’Hare Airport,” officials wrote in the report. They added that Taylor informed them that Satterley had been diagnosed with a redacted medical condition and he had been prescribed medication. They also noted she told them he had “no history of illicit drug or alcohol abuse.” Satterley was discovered passed out in his car just before 4 p.m. by a 911 caller who stated she could not see any signs of life from the wrestler as he was slumped over in the driver’s seat of his rental car. “I don’t see his chest moving at all,” she told police dispatch during the call. After toxicology reports found nothing extraordinary, officials determined Satterley died of bronchial asthma and deemed his passing natural, the medical examiner report stated. Satterley had been in the area for his role with AEW, as he wrestled against Andrade at the NOW Arena in Chicago on Sept. 26. Taylor wrote in an emotional Instagram post on Oct. 12 that she and Sattereley had been looking forward to his return home from Illinois. “You were so excited to get home to us,” Taylor said, “you were going to shoot hoops all week with your best mates, we were going to set up your new home gym and take Wilfie for some autumnal walks, have pizza at Rudy’s on your cheat day, go to the match, see Sam Campbell live.
summary: AEW wrestler Benjamin Satterley, who performed as Pac, was found unresponsive in his vehicle in a Des Plaines, Illinois restaurant parking lot on September 27. He was pronounced dead at age 40. His wife Natalie Taylor called his phone while authorities were on scene and told them she had spoken to him less than three hours earlier as he planned to stop at the CAVA eatery before heading to O'Hare Airport.

Satterley, 40, was found unresponsive inside a vehicle outside a Des Plaines restaurant Sept. 27, a day after competing at an All Elite Wrestling event in Hoffman Estates. The medical examiner’s record lists his death at 2761 Mannheim Road. No secondary cause of death was listed. As Patch previously reported , a passerby alerted police after noticing an unresponsive man in a vehicle around 4 p.m. Satterley was alone in the rental vehicle, and authorities reported no signs of trauma or foul play. His cause and manner of death were initially pending. Satterley had been in the Chicago area for AEW's All Out event at NOW Arena, where he competed against Andrade El Ídolo the previous evening. A native of Newcastle upon Tyne, England, Satterley began wrestling in 2004 and became known internationally for his high-flying style. He joined AEW in 2019 and held multiple championships with the organization. AEW announced his death the evening of Sept. 27, recognizing his contributions and memorable matches.

Satterley died on September 27 in Des Plaines, Illinois. He was found unresponsive in a vehicle outside a restaurant. Emergency services responded and pronounced him dead at 4:08 pm local time.
Authorities stated there were no indications of trauma or foul play. His death did not appear suspicious. An autopsy was performed and additional testing completed before the cause was finalized.

Satterley was born in Newcastle upon Tyne and began wrestling in 2004. He became closely associated with Dragon Gate, where he held multiple championships including a record 447-day reign as Open the Brave Gate Champion.

He signed with WWE in 2012 and performed as Adrian Neville and later Neville. His accomplishments there included the NXT Championship, two NXT Tag Team Championship reigns, and two runs as WWE Cruiserweight Champion.

Satterley joined AEW in 2019 after returning to Dragon Gate. He became the inaugural AEW All-Atlantic Champion, later renamed the International Championship, and held the AEW World Trios Championship as part of Death Triangle. His final match was a loss to Andrade El Idolo for the AEW National Championship at All Out on September 26.

CM Punk took the title nine days later in Zayn’s first defense on the July sixth episode of Raw. Zayn regained the championship on the Sept. 11 episode of SmackDown. title: 7 Greatest Champions of the WWE Renaissance Era
raw_title: 7 Greatest Champions of the WWE Renaissance Era
body: WWE’s push into the mainstream has been successful, but it wouldn’t have happened without the incredible work of the men and women who have held championship gold. These champions are stars from previous eras and ones who have recently made names for themselves. They have been the highlights of WWE’s Renaissance Era and will be listed below. The Tribal Chief stood atop WWE for most of the Renaissance Era. As the era began, Reigns was two years into his record-breaking four-year world-champion reign. He carried the Universal Championship on his waist, but after a winner-take-all match at WrestleMania 38, he became the Undisputed World Heavyweight Champion. He held the championship for two more years before losing it at WrestleMania 40. It was an iconic reign that included multiple high-profile defenses, where he always came out the victor. Roman Reigns took time off from WWE after his defeat, but the championship gold wouldn’t stay hidden for long. At WrestleMania 42, Reigns toppled CM Punk to become the World Heavyweight Champion once again. A championship that he still holds today, competing in high-profile matches at every event. Reigns was a star before this era, but during this time, he became a god in WWE. Cody Rhodes returning to WWE at WrestleMania 38 was a watershed moment for the American Nightmare. He finally returned to the company where he got his start, and it started his path to becoming the biggest babyface champion of the Renaissance Era. The fans rallied behind Cody Rhodes as he tried to finish his story and win the one championship that had eluded him. After a few heartbreaking defeats, Rhodes finally captured the WWE Championship in an emotional WrestleMania 40 finish. Rhodes became a fantastic babyface champion, taking on all comers and becoming the face of World Wrestling Entertainment. His reign lasted an impressive 378 days and included amazing title defenses against the best competitors WWE had to offer. Cody Rhodes added 2 more WWE Championship victories to his resume during this time, becoming the man everyone chased. title: The Strange WWE Program Between Gunther and Danhausen, Analyzed
raw_title: The Strange WWE Program Between Gunther and Danhausen, Analyzed
body: October 20, 2026 By Josh Prost WWE , Pro Wrestling , SmackDown , WWE Universe Gunther started 2026 on an extremely high note. He ended 2025 by defeating John Cena in his final match. Then he defeated AJ Styles to end his career at the Royal Rumble. He followed that up by beating Seth Rollins on night one of WrestleMania: Vegas. But since then, things haven’t been going well for him. He had repeated opportunities to capture the Undisputed WWE Championship, but for one reason or another, couldn’t capture it. That has made him extremely mad, demanding answers over the past few months. But instead of answers, he’s gotten Danhausen. WWE’s breakout hit of this year has repeatedly bothered him, causing him to get angry and yell. That’s why he’s been yelling at Danhausen and trying to beat him up. Any other wrestler would’ve just ignored him and gone back to their business. But Gunther wants to take him out once and for all. Instead of getting back in the Undisputed WWE Championship picture, he’s forced himself to feud with someone many wrestlers don’t take seriously. That seems like a waste of time, as Danhausen probably knows he’ll get beat up. Gunther is taking the bait from a comedy wrestler instead of focusing on title pursuits. I t’s clear that mention wasn’t random. At some point, this feud has to be over between them. Halloween Havoc is the perfect time to do that. Danhausen is the host of the PLE, and a Gunther return to NXT would make the fans very happy. It doesn’t have to be an actual match. Gunther could just beat him up like he did last Friday to stop the constant interruptions he’s been having to deal with. Doing that could definitely end their feud enjoyably. But Gunther takes wrestling seriously, which is why he’s taken so much offense at Danhausen. He’s taking his eyes off the Undisputed WWE Championship picture, which is a huge mistake. Gunther started off the year extremely happy, but over the course of the past few months has gotten very angry. Some of the blame has been directed towards SmackDown General Manager Nick Aldis and his decisions on the Undisputed WWE Championship title matches, but most of it has been directed towards Danhausen. He’s clearly not walking away from feuding with him, forcing him to step away from title ambitions due to his serious view of wrestling. That has caused many fans to be mad about his direction. However, it seems he is determined to beat up Danhausen, which could prove to be advantageous if it motivates him to get back to winning championships. title: Legal Watch: Federal Court Rejects Defendants’ Constitutional Challenge in WWE ‘Ring Boys’ Sexual Abuse Case
raw_title: Federal Court Rejects Defendants’ Constitutional Challenge in WWE ‘Ring Boys’ Sexual Abuse Case
body: Back Federal Court Rejects Defendants’ Constitutional Challenge in WWE ‘Ring Boys’ Sexual Abuse Case Oct 19, 2026 DiCello Levitt Represents Survivors as Federal Court Upholds Application of Maryland’s Child Victims Act, Allowing Claims Against WWE and the McMahons to Proceed In a 26-page opinion issued today, U.S. District Judge James K. Bredar of the District of Maryland rejected the defendants’ latest attempt to dismiss the survivors’ claims. At issue was the constitutionality of Maryland’s Child Victims Act of 2023 , which eliminated time limits for filing civil lawsuits involving childhood sexual abuse. The law recognizes that survivors often delay disclosing abuse due to the lasting effects of trauma, giving them an opportunity to pursue justice when they are ready to come forward. DiCello Levitt, together with Murphy, Falcon & Murphy, represents the survivors in John Doe 1 et al. v. World Wrestling Entertainment, LLC et al. “This ruling is a significant victory for our clients and for other survivors of childhood sexual abuse who have waited years for the opportunity to seek justice,” said Greg Gutzler , a partner at DiCello Levitt who leads the litigation. “Trauma does not follow a legal deadline, and Maryland’s Child Victims Act recognizes that reality. Our clients have waited years to hold those responsible accountable. We will not stop fighting until their voices are heard and they have their day in court.” The ruling follows the court’s December 2025 decision largely denying the defendants’ earlier motions to dismiss. The WWE Ring Boys sexual abuse lawsuit alleges that WWE employees, including ringside announcer and ring crew chief Melvin Phillips Jr., recruited underage boys to assist with wrestling events and used their positions to groom, exploit, and sexually abuse them. The plaintiffs further allege that WWE leadership, including Vince and Linda McMahon, knew or should have known about the abuse but failed to take reasonable steps to prevent it. The litigation is led by DiCello Levitt’s Greg Gutzler and Adam Prom and includes Scott Gilmore , Mark A. DiCello , Bobby DiCello , and Emma Bruder , with local counsel Murphy, Falcon & Murphy. The case is John Doe 1 et al. v. World Wrestling Entertainment, LLC et al. , Case No. 1:24-cv-03487, in the U.S. District Court for the District of Maryland. title: Ospreay Retains AEW Title in Clockwork Carnage Thriller
raw_title: Ospreay Retains AEW Title in Clockwork Carnage Thriller - PWInsider.com
body: DMFirst Veer Game odds uden om ROFUS Jalwa Game Goa Game Raja Game MaanWin Ospreay Retains AEW Title in Clockwork Carnage Thriller By Kendall Jenkins on 2026-10-19 12:02:00 Ospreay Survives Eight-Man Gauntlet War to Keep AEW Gold at WrestleDream Will Ospreay walked out of WrestleDream on Sunday, October 18, 2026, still holding the AEW World Championship after beating seven opponents in the promotion's first-ever Clockwork Carnage match. The stipulation forced Ospreay into a brutal two-stage format, starting as a gauntlet with staggered entrances before shifting into a 15-minute scored-fall period once eight men had entered. It was a chaotic, physically demanding structure that tested every competitor in the field. Ospreay drew the first entrance, meaning he would have to face all seven challengers to keep his title. Konosuke Takeshita came in second, followed by Ospreay's United Empire teammate 'Speedball' Mike Bailey as the third entrant. Bailey, a Canadian wrestler, was among the group chasing the title before Takeshita pinned him to eliminate him from advancing to the second stage. Ricochet entered fourth, and Darby Allin, the TNT Champion, came in fifth carrying a table that would factor into the match later. International Champion Kazuchika Okada arrived sixth, and Adam Copeland made his entrance as the seventh competitor shortly after Bailey's elimination. Joe pulled level with Allin and Ospreay by locking in the Coquina Clutch on Ospreay, then went for another Musclebuster before Copeland speared him out of it to claim his first fall of the match. Copeland then equalized again with a spear on Ricochet with just over a minute remaining, and a follow-up spear on Okada briefly put him in position to walk away as champion. With Copeland's retirement plans looming and Ospreay now having survived one of AEW's most grueling title defenses yet, the promotion heads into its next chapter with its World Championship picture wide open for fresh challengers.

The show will be available for purchase in the United States through PPV.com, HBO Max, Amazon, DAZN, Fubo, YouTube, and cable or satellite providers. International fans in the UK and other markets can access it via MyAEW.
AEW scheduled the event only three weeks after All Out. Some television time during that period was used to pay tribute to PAC rather than advancing storylines.
The main event will be a new Clockwork Carnage match for the AEW world championship. The match combines elements of a Casino Gauntlet in its first phase and an Iron Man format in its second phase.

Eight wrestlers will compete across two phases. The Entry Phase begins with two competitors and adds a new entrant every three minutes until all have entered, with any wrestler pinned or submitted during this phase being eliminated.

Surviving wrestlers advance to the 15-minute Scoring Phase, where the competitor with the most pins or submissions is declared the AEW world champion. The defending champion Will Ospreay faces challengers Samoa Joe, Kazuchika Okada, Ricochet, Adam Copeland, Konosuke Takeshita, Speedball Bailey, and Darby Allin.

title: Edge
raw_title: Edge
body: Edge More Share Options More Share Options Share close facebook x threads email superstar stats Superstar Stats Edge Buy the Song Career Highlights WWE Champion; World Heavyweight Champion; World Tag Team Champion; WWE Tag Team Champion; Intercontinental Champion; WCW U.S. Champion; 2001 King of the Ring; Money in the Bank Ladder Match winner; Royal Rumble Match winner (2010, 2021); 2012 WWE Hall of Fame Inductee In another life, Edge could have been a rock star. From his voluminous hair to his long leather jackets and double-horns signature pose, every detail of his WWE image screamed it. As the pyro blasted into the air behind him on the entranceway before he stepped into the ring, he injected arenas with the energy of a packed concert – without the dangers of crowd-surfing and mosh pits. There was even a legion of groupies – Edgeheads – who tracked his every move. It's no surprise, then, that Edge is a guitar collector and grew up listening to KISS, a band famous for their flamboyant outfits and outrageous stage antics. What is a surprise is how a shy high schooler from the little town of Orangeville, Ontario, evolved into The Rated-R Superstar. Edge had some fine company as he worked his way up the independent scene in the '90s: his childhood friend and partner for countless five-second poses, Christian. When Edge was signed to a WWE contract in 1997, it was only a matter of time before Christian would also climb the ladder, following his best bud into uncharted territory. "E&C" made sweet music as a tag team, using a lot more than just Con-Chair-Tos to claim seven championships together. A Triple Threat Ladder Match victory at WrestleMania 2000 over The Hardy Boyz and The Dudley Boyz laid the foundation for a series of landmark Tables, Ladders & Chairs (TLC) contests, and some of the greatest tag team action of all time. Of course, tag teaming wasn't Edge's only specialty, as he masterfully crafted a singles career and captured a whopping 31 total titles – many of them the WWE Universe didn't even see coming. Beyond his ability to capitalize on opportunities, Edge became known as The Master Manipulator because he wasn't afraid to cross the line in order to rattle the competition. After he made history in 2006 as the first man to ever cash in the Money in the Bank contract, he rubbed his WWE Championship triumph in the face of all challengers with an R-rated celebration on Raw; more explicitly, a frolicking good time with Lita on a bed placed right in the middle of the squared circle. Mind games were taken to a whole new level by the self-proclaimed "most-watched champion." A debilitating injury forced Edge to retire in 2011 but, in the 2020 Royal Rumble Match, The Ultimate Opportunist made an incredible return to the squared circle and immediately set out to add numerous epic matches to hs already storied career. 24:16 Karl Anderson More Share Options More Share Options Share close facebook x threads email Faction reveals that shook WWE: WWE

title: Roman Reigns Treated Street Fighter Role Like WWE Main Event
raw_title: Roman Reigns Says He Viewed Street Fighter Role Like Main Event In WWE
summary_src: For his performance as Akuma in "Street Fighter," Roman Reigns was able to draw from his WWE experience, specifically as a main eventer.
body: During an interview with Sam Robert's " Notsam " radio show, Reigns explained that his character only makes an impact during the third act of the film, and as such, he treated it like competing in the main event of a WWE show. "I just try to keep that type of weight on it, you know what I mean? ... The stakes are as high as can be, so you need to be able to come in and match what everybody's done," the Tribal Chief explained. While he found his feet on set, Reigns is still well aware that he's not a full-time professional actor, and admitted that it wasn't exactly easy for him to step into Akuma's shoes. "It really helped me to be able to see what [my castmates] had done and the way they had led the film, and it kind of set the tone for what needed to be matched," he admitted. "It wasn't easy, but there were a bunch of things that I was able to rely on from wrestling to kind of help me to take this on." Reigns also explained that working in front of an audience was definitely something that helped him portray Akuma. Still, while there might be similarities between his "Street Fighter" character and the Tribal Chief, he considers character work as "a dial" which he can tune, allowing him to adjust the amount of influence he draws from his WWE persona.

He said he studied his co-stars' work to match the established tone and relied on skills from wrestling to help portray Akuma. Reigns noted that performing in front of an audience also aided his transition into the role.

title: On the Record: Ilja Dragunov Details Frantic Visa Process Before Last-Minute AEW Debut
raw_title: Ilja Dragunov Details Frantic Visa Process Before Last-Minute AEW Debut
summary_src: Ilja Dragunov’s AEW debut wasn’t just a stressful waiting game for Tony Khan — Dragunov was losing patience with the visa process himself.
body: Speaking on The Ariel Helwani Show , Dragunov explained that applying for a U.S. visa wasn’t exactly new territory for him. The frustrating part was simply waiting when all he wanted to do was get back to wrestling. “I mean, it’s not the first time that I needed to apply for a visa in the US, so that was familiar. But of course, since everything I wanna do is work and fight and perform, I just couldn’t wait for things to happen quicker.” “And from the company’s side, they were helping me in that process in every way possible, so it was smooth. It took around, I guess, around a month, which was still too long for me. But putting it into perspective, it was very fast, and after the appointment, everything was so quick.” Then came the middle-of-the-night email that changed everything. Dragunov was awake around 2 AM in Germany because his girlfriend was touring Japan with Sendai Girls, and he decided to check his inbox. “So, on that day when I realized I could travel back to the States, it was 2 AM in the morning. I was awake anyway around that time since my girlfriend is touring with Sendai Girls in Japan.” That’s when Dragunov realized his passport was ready to be picked up. Instead of waiting around another day, his mind immediately went to whether he could grab it and get on a plane that same day. Dragunov immediately contacted AEW, and that’s when everything went into overdrive. Flights were arranged almost immediately, and only seven hours later he was on a plane heading back to the United States. “So I reached out to AEW — to the company — and everything went extremely quickly. Everything got booked, and I was, in seven hours, on my flight back to the States. I didn’t want to wait another single second anymore.” That frantic timeline lines up with what Tony Khan revealed following WrestleDream. Khan said AEW was still uncertain about Dragunov’s availability while Dynamite and Collision were airing live, with confirmation finally arriving that Dragunov would be able to pick up his visa the following day. “Some people asked about the timing of the vignettes that suggested your arrival at WrestleDream on Wednesday and then having a second vignette on Friday. Well, there’s a lot of uncertainty in wrestling. On Wednesday night, in the middle of the show, at 2 AM your time, we got the message that Ilja was able to pick up the visa the next day, and we found that out during the live broadcast.” Everything ultimately fell into place just in time. Dragunov made his official AEW debut at WrestleDream on October 17, bringing an end to the uncertainty that had followed him since his WWE contract expired in August. What looked like a carefully planned surprise on television was much more chaotic behind the scenes. Dragunov went from checking an email at 2 AM in Germany to sitting on a flight back to the United States just hours later, and he clearly wasn’t interested in wasting another second once that passport was ready. Subhojeet Mukherjee Subhojeet Mukh

title: On the Record: Ilja Dragunov Opens Up On WWE Tried to Keep Him Before AEW Move

summary_src: Ilja Dragunov says leaving WWE wasn’t something he had already decided months before his contract expired. In fact, when he wrestled his final WWE match in April, Dragunov says he had absolutely no idea that it would end up being the last time fans saw him compete for the company.
body: Speaking on The Ariel Helwani Show , Dragunov was asked whether he already knew his WWE run was coming to an end when he competed in the Andre the Giant Memorial Battle Royal ahead of WrestleMania 42. According to Dragunov, that wasn’t the case at all. “No, absolutely not. Everything that I can talk about — that is not exciting. I didn’t know at the time that I was leaving. I was just waiting.” Dragunov wasn’t sitting at home with one foot already out the door either. He still wanted to wrestle and compete, but things simply reached a point where his WWE career wasn’t moving forward. “Again, I love what I do. I wanna compete and work and do this and that, and it just got a little stuck. But it’s nothing new to anybody. It was obvious. Time just passed by, and then I reached the expiration of my contract.” By the time his contract expired in August, however, Dragunov’s feelings had changed. As the months passed and he looked at where his career was heading, he began realizing that a change might be exactly what he needed. “And like I already said after the show at the press conference at WrestleDream, I felt over time that, with how things are working out and how I’m feeling — because I make a lot of things depending on how I feel about it, always have the courage to do — I felt it was time to breathe some new, fresh air.” Helwani then asked the obvious question: did WWE actually try to keep him? Dragunov confirmed that the company had no intention of simply letting him walk away. “Did they try to re-sign me? I mean, a lot of things were written over the internet. Yeah, there was no intention of the company to let me go.” That makes his departure a little more interesting than simply reaching the end of a contract and being allowed to leave. Dragunov said there were several things he had to weigh, including the offers on the table and what he wanted creatively. “It was an accumulation of a lot of things. It was an accumulation of the offers, because we know it’s a business, but it was also based on my feeling — how do I want to work creatively? Do I need a scenery change? Where can I see myself staying forever?” Dragunov also had to consider just how much of his adult life he’d already spent under the WWE umbrella. I spent most of my 20s in WWE. That’s a long time.” That’s where AEW and the opportunity to experience something completely different entered the picture. Dragunov didn’t frame his WWE departure as some ugly breakup, but rather as a chance to find out whether another environment might fit him better. “The beautiful thing is we have a lot of opportunities, and for me personally, after being so long with another company, to not seek out new opportunities — maybe even a place where I see myself more fitting — who wouldn’t

title: Rush's AEW Return Delayed Until 2027 By Visa Issues
raw_title: Latest Backstage Update On AEW Contract Situations Of Rush And Dralistico
summary_src: A backstage update on the AEW contract situations of Rush and Dralistico reveals two different stories regarding this pair of lucha libre brothers
body: When it comes to Rush, however, the situation appears to be a bit different. Despite the appearance of Rush's previous tweets, Alvarez says they are entirely visa related, as Rush's visa has expired some time in the recent past. Furthermore, Rush's new visa isn't expected to come in until the start of 2027, all but confirming that the new year would be the soonest that AEW fans would see Rush again. It was further noted that, despite the speculation, Rush "is happy in AEW" by all familiar with the situation. If that is the case, it would be yet another occurrence of visa issues affecting AEW plans, as Alvarez' "Wrestling Observer Radio" co-host Dave Meltzer had previously reported that Ilja Dragunov's arrival in the promotion had been delayed due to him waiting for a new visa. Rush himself has dealt with this problem in the past, revealing in early 2024 that his absence from TV during the first part of the year had been due to a combination of recovering from an injury and visa issues . AEW/Lee South Having watched and followed the careers of Rush and Dralistico dating back to when I started following CMLL in 2015, I find this whole situation annoying, exhausting, and probably just the first part of a situation that's going to get even more annoying. But assuming there are no twists and turns coming, it does appear that Dralistico is going to be departing AEW sooner rather than later, while Rush will be sticking around. If that is the case then all I can do is sit here and say praise be! Dralistico leaving AEW is not only the best move for him, but it's the best move for AEW and it's quite frankly the best move for his older brother if he has any hope of becoming a more consistent presence on AEW TV. Now to be clear; I am not a big fan of Dralistico, and haven't been going back to his days where he was the replacement Mistico in CMLL. There's some talent there, but he's always been wildly inconsistent, even at his best, he's doing stuff at a level that other luchadors do far better, and I think he's been an anchor of sorts to Rush, because Dralistico without being paired with Rush doesn't work. So him leaving doesn't hurt AEW, and Dralistico going to AAA or the Mexican indies could be what breathes him new life. It also frees Rush to go off and be Rush, which, when motivated, is one of the most dynamic and exciting luchadors in the world. Of course, there's no guarantee Rush doesn't combust anyway (he's volatile in his own right), nor no guarantee that he gets the sustained AEW push he's looking for. But ultimately, if the idea is Dralistico leaves and Rush stays, it strikes me as a positive for both, and for AEW, who now no longer has to worry about keeping Rush paired with a guy they've seemingly never had much interest in.
summary: Dave Meltzer reported on Wrestling Observer Radio that Rush's absence from AEW stems from an expired visa with his new one not expected until the start of 2027. Sources close to the situation indicated that Rush remains happy in AEW despite the setback. This marks another instance of visa problems impacting AEW talent plans following a similar delay for Ilja Dragunov.

title: On the Record: Ilja Dragunov Explains Why His WWE Contract Negotiations Went Nowhere
raw_title: Ilja Dragunov Explains Why His WWE Contract Negotiations Went Nowhere
summary_src: Ilja Dragunov has finally explained why he completely disappeared from WWE television during the final four months of his contract.
body: Speaking on The Ariel Helwani Show , Dragunov was specifically asked why fans didn’t see him on WWE television between his final match in April and his contract expiring in August . Dragunov admitted the real explanation probably isn’t nearly as exciting as some of the theories that popped up while he was gone. “Again, everything I can say is not as exciting as people made it. Of course, at some point in time, you don’t have creative — you’re just waiting for the next opportunities to come.” Dragunov believes part of the problem was simply how crowded WWE had become. New wrestlers were coming into the picture, existing storylines were already packed, and there was only so much television time available to go around. “Because a lot of new people came up, a lot of stories were full. We all know there is only a certain amount of time for certain people.” So Dragunov waited. There wasn’t some dramatic backstage incident that he pointed to or a secret plan to leave WWE months ahead of time — another creative opportunity just never materialized before his deal reached the finish line. “Everything I know is that the expiration of my contract came and that the negotiations did not lead anywhere.” Helwani then asked Dragunov directly about one of the bigger questions surrounding those negotiations: did WWE ask him to take a pay cut? That’s where Dragunov decided there were some details he wasn’t willing to make public. “Did they offer me a pay cut? To be honest, I am too much of a discreet businessman to talk about these kinds of things.” “Everything I can say is there was nothing I felt was satisfying and nothing that gave me the perspective of, like, ‘Okay, I MUST stick with here.’” That adds another piece to Dragunov’s explanation of how his WWE exit actually happened. He previously revealed that he had no idea his appearance in the Andre the Giant Memorial Battle Royal in April would become his final WWE match, because he hadn’t decided at that point that he was leaving. Dragunov also confirmed that WWE didn’t simply want to get rid of him. He said there was “no intention of the company to let me go,” but as his contract ran down, the two sides ultimately couldn’t reach terms that made staying feel like the right choice for him. “It was an accumulation of a lot of things. It was an accumulation of the offers, because we know it’s a business, but it was also based on my feeling — how do I want to work creatively? Do I need a scenery change? Where can I see myself staying forever?” Dragunov still isn’t revealing the private details of those WWE negotiations, especially when it comes to money. What he is making clear is that months without creative followed by an offer he didn’t find satisfying ultimately made the decision to find that “fresh air” somewhere else a whole lot easier. title: Results Recap: How to Assess Digital PR Campaign for Wrestling Brands
raw_title: How to Assess Digital PR Campaign Results for Wrestling Brands - PWInsider
body: DMFirst Veer Game odds uden om ROFUS Jalwa Game Goa Game Raja Game MaanWin How to Assess Digital PR Campaign Results for Wrestling Brands By Kendall Jenkins on 2026-10-20 10:39:00 For a wrestling promotion, a busy news cycle can make a campaign look successful before anyone checks what it achieved. A press release may be picked up, a new show may trend locally, or a talent announcement may circulate across social media. Those signals matter, but how to assess digital PR campaign results depends on connecting attention to a goal: selling tickets, growing an audience, strengthening a brand, or making a new venture credible. Before a campaign begins, decide what it is meant to change. Promoting a live event calls for different measures than announcing a streaming partnership or introducing a new wrestling brand. If the objective is ticket sales, track visits to the event page, ticket referrals and purchases during the campaign period. If the aim is awareness, look at relevant audience reach, branded searches and meaningful coverage in outlets that wrestling fans actually read. Set a baseline as well. Compare results with a similar period, a previous event or the normal level of traffic and engagement. Without that context, a rise in mentions may simply reflect a major show, a viral moment or a news story unrelated to the PR work. Where possible, use tagged campaign links and dedicated landing pages so that referral activity can be distinguished from general traffic. Coverage volume is easy to report, but it is not the same as influence. A list of placements can include duplicate syndication, brief mentions and stories that reach audiences with little interest in the promotion. Review the quality of coverage: Was the key announcement accurately described? Did the story include the information fans need? Was the outlet relevant to the intended audience? Did coverage lead readers to take a next step? A useful report combines a few types of evidence instead of treating one metric as proof of success: Reach: relevant outlets, estimated audience, social sharing and search visibility. Action: ticket purchases, registrations, merchandise activity or inquiries, when these can be attributed responsibly. Reputation: accuracy of coverage, message inclusion, sentiment and the quality of conversations around the announcement. Keep the measurement proportional. A smaller independent promotion may not have access to sophisticated attribution tools, and that does not make its results unmeasurable. A consistent spreadsheet of placements, links, dates and outcomes can reveal useful patterns. Avoid claiming that PR caused every sale or follower increase; other marketing, talent activity and the event itself may also contribute. title: Why Ilja Dragunov Only Negotiated With AEW After His WWE Exit
raw_title: Why Ilja Dragunov Only Negotiated With AEW After His WWE Exit
summary_src: Ilja Dragunov apparently didn’t spend his free agency shopping himself around the wrestling world before landing in AEW. The former WWE star says AEW was the only promotion he spoke to, and everything came together pretty quickly once he was ready to figure out his next move.
body: Speaking on The Ariel Helwani Show , Dragunov was asked whether he had conversations with any other wrestling companies after his WWE contract expired in August. According to Dragunov, there really wasn’t some huge bidding process happening behind the scenes. “If I gotta be honest, everything went down so fast. Everything I did was just giving myself a rest — that’s pretty much what I did for the most part.” After spending years under the WWE umbrella, Dragunov’s first priority wasn’t immediately finding another contract. He took some time for himself, but once things started moving with AEW, they moved very quickly. “When things clicked, they clicked very fast. Yes, I only spoke to AEW.” That also clears up any questions about whether Dragunov entertained offers from several promotions before ultimately choosing Tony Khan’s company. At least according to Dragunov, AEW was the only conversation he had. Helwani then asked when Dragunov actually signed his AEW contract. Dragunov didn’t give an exact date, but indicated it happened fairly soon after his WWE deal reached its expiration. “I think it was possibly just a minor time after my contract expired. It was a very easygoing expiration.” That’s particularly interesting considering Dragunov previously revealed WWE had no intention of simply letting him go. He said there were negotiations before his contract expired, but ultimately nothing about the situation gave him the feeling that he absolutely needed to remain with the company. “Everything I can say is there was nothing I felt was satisfying and nothing that gave me the perspective of, like, ‘Okay, I MUST stick with here.’” Dragunov had also spent the final months of his WWE contract without a television storyline. His last match came during WrestleMania 42 weekend in April, and he previously explained that he spent the months afterwards waiting for another creative opportunity while WWE’s television time and existing storylines remained crowded. Once his contract expired in August, Dragunov eventually found the change he was looking for in AEW. He previously described wanting “new, fresh air” and a different landscape where he could satisfy his hunger for competition. There was still one thing holding up his actual arrival — his visa. Dragunov revealed that after finally learning his passport was ready , he contacted AEW and was on a flight back to the United States just seven hours later, allowing everything to come together for his WrestleDream debut. So despite all the speculation that surrounded Dragunov’s future after WWE, his version of events is actually pretty straightforward. He took some time to rest, only talked to AEW, and once the two sides clicked, it apparently didn’t take long to make him All Elite. title: Dralistico Reportedly Closing in on AEW Exit: Where Could the Mexican Star End Up?
raw_title: Dralistico Reportedly Closing in on AEW Exit: Where Could the Mexican Star End Up?
body: Bryan Alvarez of F4WOnline addressed Dralistico’s status after the La Faccion Ingobernable member and his brother Rush drew attention with a pair of social media posts. On October 19, Dralistico shared an edited photo of himself in handcuffs and behind bars in a post on X , with the caption “Maybe not for long?” Fans took the post as a sign that he wants to leave AEW. “Regarding the Dralistico and Rush tweets we talked about last night: Dralistico’s AEW deal expires in December, and based on that tweet one would presume he wants out,” Alvarez wrote. Dralistico, whose real name is Carlos Munoz Gonzalez, is the son of La Bestia del Ring and the brother of Rush and WWE’s Dragon Lee. He began his career in CMLL in 2010 under the name Dragon Lee before becoming the second Mistico in 2012. During his time in CMLL, he won the CMLL World Tag Team Championship, the CMLL World Trios Championship and the CMLL World Welterweight Championship. He left the promotion in 2021 and joined his father and brother Rush in La Faccion Ingobernable, also known as LFI. He has worked on AEW and ROH programming for several years. His notable matches include an AEW International Championship challenge against Orange Cassidy in 2023 and an ROH World Championship match against Bandido in 2025. He missed time late in 2025 with an ear injury that required surgery and returned on the March 7 episode of Collision. Dralistico leaving would not be a surprise. He has barely been used since his return from surgery, and a wrestler who is healthy and not on television is usually a wrestler who is looking at his options. The post on X was about as clear a message as he could send without saying it directly, and Alvarez’s read on it matches what most fans took away from it. For AEW, losing Dralistico would be a small loss on paper, but it would further thin out La Faccion Ingobernable at a time when Rush cannot work. The group has not been a priority for months, and with one brother likely leaving and the other unavailable until 2027, AEW has little reason to keep it going in its current form.

title: On the Record: Ilja Dragunov Speaks On Brock Lesnar No-Selling His Offense at WWE Royal Rumble
raw_title: Ilja Dragunov Addresses Brock Lesnar No-Selling His Offense at WWE Royal Rumble
summary_src: Ilja Dragunov isn’t exactly haunted by the way Brock Lesnar steamrolled him at the Royal Rumble. Months after that quick elimination left fans frustrated and even got some eye-rolls backstage, Dragunov says he barely gave the whole thing another thought.
body: Speaking on The Ariel Helwani Show , Dragunov was asked about his brief showdown with Lesnar at the 2026 Men’s Royal Rumble. For Dragunov, getting in the face of someone like Lesnar was exactly what his character was supposed to do. “I said it before, honestly, if you really understand the persona that I have been in the ring for the most part of the time, I’ve been facing monsters. And at the end of the day, you can’t change certain things.” The moment itself was pretty brutal. Dragunov stepped up to Lesnar and started throwing his trademark chops, only for Brock to basically brush them off, scream in his face and dump him over the top rope. Dragunov knows most people probably wouldn’t be lining up to pick a fight with Lesnar. That’s also exactly why he believes backing down would’ve made no sense for him. “I can’t change anything about it, but my best career moments were made by my vulnerability. I wasn’t becoming a name by being the person who dominates at all times.” That’s really the whole Dragunov formula. He gets absolutely destroyed, somehow keeps coming and makes people care about whether he can fight his way back. Dragunov also isn’t mad that people were upset for him. He admitted the whole thing possibly could’ve been handled differently, but he’s definitely not sitting around replaying that Lesnar elimination in his head. So while plenty of people saw the Royal Rumble spot as Dragunov getting completely brushed aside, he clearly doesn’t look at it that way. If anything, fans getting angry on his behalf fits perfectly with a career that’s largely been built around watching Dragunov take a beating and desperately wanting to see him fight back. title: Top Takeaways from Lucha Underground Binge
raw_title: TOP FIVE LIST: Takeaways from binging four season of Lucha Underground including Penta, Rey Fenix, Ricochet, Inter-gender wrestling
body: Working in my own store that carries a lot of pro wrestling merchandise, I spend all day on Mondays with wrestling on the TV in-store. I will watch something until the start of Raw, then pick it back up the next week. In doing so, I was finally able to complete the entire series, and what a wild series it was. On the first episode, you saw Pentagon Jr. and Rey Fénix. They were never announced as brothers on this show, but there was a unique focus on these two characters. They were both incredible in the ring. The first time I watched years ago, I felt a little bit like I did when first watch Rey Mysterio Jr. arrive in WCW. The way Fénix worked the ropes was so unique. Pentagon had this unique charisma that you could not ignore. They were set up to be key characters, and the people running this show, including Konnan’s eye for talent, knew they had something special in these two. Mil Muertes was a reskinned Judas Masias, who came in as a possessed killer, paired with Catrina who controlled him to do her will. Santos Escobar was under a mask as King Cuerno. A hunter who came in to stalk his prey. I could not believe how mishandled this talent was in WWE after watching him perform in “The Temple.” Ricochet, again under a mask, was Puma, Konnan’s new protege, who was trying his talent against top tier opponents for the first time. My favorite character was Sexy Star. It was very unfortunate that she made the decisions she made to blackball her from a career she was very good at. A woman in an abusive relationship finally decided to stand up for herself, and become a fighter. She was able to fight off her abuser, and in doing so, realized she had everything it took to defeat men in a competitive fight. She even worked her way to being the promotion’s champion for a brief moment. Well-defined background, very good in the ring, and beautiful to attract viewers and look great on posters. Perhaps one of wrestling’s biggest losses, but that was a decision of the performer to deserve her fate of no longer being accepted. I was hesitant to accept this when I first viewed Lucha Underground, but came to not only accept it, but enjoy it. I have previously stated my appreciation for the character of Sexy Star, but I also liked seeing competent women mix it up with men, who were confident in selling offense and even taking clean losses to the women on the roster. In a world where we go to theaters and accept Wonder Woman, Harley Quinn, or Atomic Blonde as viable cinema, why can’t this extend to wrestling? I have often said that Asuka would make me more nervous to fight than many of the men on the roster. That said, I completely understand that corporate WWE will not be entertaining this again any time soon. We had Chyna as the Intercontinental Champion, but that was the exception that won’t be happening again any time soon. title: Contract News: 'A Lot of TNA Wrestling Contracts Coming Up' Soon: 6 Stars We Want to See Jump to WWE, Including Matt & Jeff Hardy

body: According to FightFul, “ a lot of contracts are coming up in December ” for some on the TNA roster. It means that quite a few talented wrestlers could be on the free agent market to begin 2027. With that in mind, we take a look at six TNA stars we would love to see make the jump to WWE early next year. Reports in the summer claimed that WWE is trying to make an effort to improve their tag division. However, they decided to do so after cutting The New Day and The Motor City Machine Guns. They could certainly use some veteran teams with charisma, and TNA has a few that might be available in a couple of months. One that WWE should check in on if they hit the open market is The Righteous. The duo of Dutch and Vincent are a well-traveled team that has also competed in AEW. They have a very unique gimmick and presentation that could appeal to the WWE audience. Moose has done everything possible in TNA, so it just seems like a matter of time before he eventually takes his talents elsewhere. He has been open about his desire to one day compete in WWE. If the multi-time world champion is open to first working in NXT, he would be a great veteran for the black and gold brand before he makes the jump to the main roster. Moose could also be a potential candidate to be a member of 946 in the future. The Hardys are not just one of the greatest tag teams in WWE and TNA history. They are one of the greatest ever in any promotion. However, everything ends, and with Matt being 52 years old and Jeff three years behind, they are very close to the end of their careers.

title: Judge denies WWE dismissal in ring boy lawsuit
raw_title: Judge rejects WWE and McMahons’ motion to have ‘ring boy’ lawsuit dismissed
summary_src: A federal judge on Monday (October 19) rejected a motion to dismiss the “ring boy” lawsuit against WWE/TKO, Vince McMahon, and U.S. Secretary of Education Linda McMahon.
body: Link Photo by Jim Spellman/WireImage A federal judge on Monday (October 19) rejected a motion to dismiss the “ring boy” lawsuit against WWE/TKO, Vince McMahon, and U.S. Secretary of Education Linda McMahon. In 2024, a lawsuit was filed against former WWE boss Vince, his wife Linda, and WWE/TKO on behalf of five survivors of what’s dubbed the “Ring Boy Scandal.” The seven plaintiffs who filed the suit claim they were sexually abused when they were minors in the 1980s and 1990s and setting up rings and running errands for WWE. All of the seven men allege abuse by former WWE ring announcer Mel Phillips, while one alleges sexual abuse by former WWE executive Pat Patterson, and one alleges sexual harassment against former WWE Vice President of Operations Terry Garvin. Phillips, Patterson, and Garvin have all passed away. However, the suit claims negligence by the McMahons and WWE/TKO for allegedly allowing the abuse to take place and continue. Brandon Thurston of POST Wrestling on Monday reported U.S. District Judge James K. Bredar rejected an effort by WWE/TKO and the McMahons to have the lawsuit dismissed on grounds that the Maryland Child Victims Act, which the plaintiffs used to file the case, violates the U.S. Constitution. In their motion for dismissal, WWE/TKO and the McMahons cited difficulties in litigating a case based on alleged abuse from decades ago where the accused abusers are no longer living. The defendants contended the 14th Amendment of the Constitution protects people’s rights against unfair or arbitrary laws, which they argued that using the Child Victims Act would do. (The Maryland law eliminates time limits for filing lawsuits related to child sexual abuse.) According to Thurston, Bredar wrote in his ruling that the defendants did not “show how their particular hardships make the [Maryland Child Victims Act] arbitrary or irrational.” Since Bredar ruled the law is constitutional for use in the case, the lawsuit will now go to discovery phase, and a teleconference is scheduled for November 17 to set additional deadlines. The plaintiffs claim abuse by former WWE ring announcer Mel Phillips. One plaintiff also alleges sexual abuse by former executive Pat Patterson, and another alleges sexual harassment by former Vice President of Operations Terry Garvin. All three accused individuals have since passed away.

The suit accuses the McMahons and WWE of negligence for allegedly allowing the abuse to occur and continue. The case was filed under the Maryland Child Victims Act, which removes time limits for lawsuits related to child sexual abuse.

WWE, TKO, and the McMahons argued that the Maryland law violates the 14th Amendment by being unfair or arbitrary, especially given the decades-old allegations and the deaths of the accused. The judge ruled that the defendants failed to demonstrate how the law is arbitrary or irrational in this case.
With the motion to dismiss denied, the lawsuit will proceed to the discovery phase. A teleconference is scheduled for November 17 to establish additional deadlines.

title: What worked and didn’t work with Roman and Sami, Funko Pop hijinks, The 946-Bloodline build to WarGames, more — WWE RAW HITS & MISSES (10/19)
raw_title: WWE RAW HITS & MISSES (10/19): What worked and didn’t work with Roman and Sami, Funko Pop hijinks, The 946-Bloodline build to WarGames, more
body: Roman – Sami – HIT: This was a fun moment to start the show with a reunion between Roman Reigns and Sami Zayn. There was a lot to like about it. Their interplay was strong, as were their performances. I’m okay with Reigns trying to recruit Zayn to help The Bloodline against The 946, as well as Zayn refusing to help. My problem with the segment was when they were arguing over which of their titles is the more important. That stuff is stupid and unproductive. I already don’t care about the Crown Jewel concept (beyond the Saudi Arabia of it all), and this doesn’t do anything to make me care more about their match. So while I liked parts of this opening segment, it is a marginal Hit because it didn’t end as strong as it started. Sky & Green vs. Judgment Day – HIT: This was a good tag team match to continue the build between Chelsea Green and Liv Morgan for their meaningless Crown Jewel match, as well as setting up Iyo Sky as the next challenger for Raquel Rodriguez’s Intercontinental Title. I was glad that Green didn’t take another loss. Sky getting the pin for their team gets her into that IC Title picture while getting Green some needed momentum after her loss to Roxanne Perez last week. Funko Pop – MISS: Making fun of JD McDonagh for having a big head is okay in general, but the Funko Pop figure bit has been lame. Overall, I like Joe Tessitore, but he was way too much like Michale Cole in his over-the-top geeky responses to all of these jokes. The match quality between McDonagh and Joe Hendry was fine, but the backdrop was far too silly. Maybe the destruction of Hendry’s guitar over the head of the mascot will be the end of the silliness. That’s probably too much to hope for. Valkyria vs. Vice – HIT: Lyra Valkyria’s obsession with Bayley is costing her. Not only did it set up this match against Lola Vice, which she didn’t want, but it also helped lead to her losing it. The match itself was good. WWE is doing a nice job of establishing Vice, particularly her spinning backfist finisher, which looked very strong here. The no-disqualification match next week between Valkyria and Bayley should be very good and blow off their feud. Gable vs. Mysterio vs. Lee – HIT: This was a great IC Title match with a predictable finish. I know some people were buying into Rey Mysterio possibly wining to become the new WWE Champion, but there was no way that Chad Gable was going to lose the title before defending it against Ethan Page. But Gable, Mysterio and Dragon Lee put on such a great match that the predicability of it didn’t take away from my enjoyment of it. It made sense to have this match given the storyline between Gable and the luchadores. The attack from Ethan afterwards should finally get him his IC Title match. Big Cass also being involved attacking Mysterio and Lee was interesting. He didn’t seem to be working with Ethan, but with Rusev healthy again after his recent injury, a budding faction is a possibility.
