title: Ilja Dragunov Explains WWE Exit
raw_title: Ilja Dragunov Opens Up About Decision To Leave WWE, 'Nothing Felt Satisfying'
summary_src: Ilja Dragunov made his AEW debut at AEW WrestleDream, where he was announced as the company's newest signing. Dragunov departed WWE in August after not wrestling since April. His contract expired, and he made the decision not to renew.
body: Ilja Dragunov made his AEW debut at AEW WrestleDream, where he was announced as the company’s newest signing. Dragunov departed WWE in August after not wrestling since April. His contract expired, and he made the decision not to renew. Speaking to Ariel Helwani on the Ariel Helwani Show , Dragunov detailed his decision to leave WWE. Asked if he knew his last match would be in April, Dragunov replied, “No, absolutely not. Every tale I have to tell about that is not very exciting. I didn’t know I was leaving at the time. I was just waiting. I love what I do. I want to compete and work. It’s nothing new to anybody. It was pretty obvious. Time just passed by, and I reached the expiration of my contract. I felt that, over time, with how things were working out and how I’m feeling, it was time to breathe new and fresh air.” “Yeah, there was no intention of the company to let me go,” he said. Asked if he was unhappy with the offer, he replied, “It was an accumulation of a lot of things. The offer, as we all know, is a business, but it’s also based on my feelings. How do I want to work creatively? Do I need a scenery change? You have to consider all the factors. I spent most of my 20s in WWE. That’s a very long time. The landscape changed. Now, we have other opportunities. After such a long time being in the company, not seeking out new opportunities at a place where I see myself more fitting- who wouldn’t do that?” Asked if he was asked to take a pay cut or was given a raise, he said, “I’m too discreet and too much of a businessman and a gentleman to talk about these kinds of things. Everything I can say is that there was nothing that I felt satisfied with and nothing that gave me the perspective of, ‘I must stick with this.'” Dragunov was still under contract until August, but kept off TV from April until his deal expired. Asked if they knew he wouldn’t be coming back, he replied, “Anything I can say is not as exciting as people made it. At some point in time, you don’t have creativity, and you’re waiting for the next opportunity to come. A lot of new people came up. A lot of stories were full. There is only a certain amount of time for certain people. I’m not going to go too deep into that. Everything I knew was that the expiration of my contract came, and negotiations didn’t lead anywhere.” Dragunov is set to make his in-ring debut in AEW on Wednesday’s Dynamite. If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.

He had not wrestled since April and chose not to renew with WWE. Speaking on The Ariel Helwani Show, Dragunov said he did not know his last match would be in April, that nothing felt satisfying as time passed, and it was an accumulation of factors including how things were working out and his desire for fresh air.

title: Rush Confirms AEW Happiness Amid Expired Visa
raw_title: Rush Confirms His Visa Has Expired, Addresses Whether He's Happy In AEW
summary_src: AEW star Rush took to social media on Tuesday to confirm his visa has expired, and he addressed whether or not he's happy in the company.
body: Rush shared a photo of himself in a pool, looking out toward the ocean. He started the post by saying, "Everyone loves gossip!" "But they actually got two things right," Rush continued. "I'm happy at my home, #AEW, and my visa has expired." Earlier on Tuesday, it was reported by F4WOnline's Bryan Alvarez that Rush's visa has been expired for some time. According to Alvarez, the star's new visa isn't expected to come in until the start of next year. Rush has previously posted, in regards to his AEW absence, that fans would see him "maybe next year," leading many to believe he was unhappy with his status in the company. I'm happy at my home, #AEW , and my visa has expired. pic.twitter.com/dMc8Pwz8nw Dave Meltzer said on " Wrestling Observer Radio " that he's not sure when Rush's contract is up. In addition to Rush's own words in his most recent post, it was noted in previous reports that he is happy in AEW, despite the visa issues that have been plaguing him and other stars, including the recently-debuted Ilja Dragunov . Rush is reportedly healthy while waiting out his visa issues. His last match took place on the July 1 edition of "AEW Collision," where he defeated Jordan Cruz. Rush also notably faced off against then-AEW World Champion MJF in a no count out match at the beginning of June on an episode of "AEW Dynamite." Alvarez confirmed that Rush's brother, Dralistico's contract is soon coming to an end. After his post on Monday, it appears likely Dralistico will not remain with AEW.

title: Ilja Dragunov details reasons for WWE exit
raw_title: Ilja Dragunov explains WWE departure: ‘The landscape in this beautiful business changed’
summary_src: Ilja Dragunov had a gut feeling that leaving WWE would work out for him. During a Tuesday appearance on The Ariel Helwani Show, Dragunov described leaving WWE as a decision he made to bet om himself.
body: Ilja Dragunov had a gut feeling that leaving WWE would work out for him. “It was an accumulation of a lot of things,” Dragunov said. “An accumulation of, of course, the offering, because we all know, at the end of the day, it’s the business. But it’s also definitely based on my feeling of, like, how do I want to work creatively? Do I need a scenery change? Is the scenery change something where I can see myself staying forever? Because you’ve got to consider a lot of factors. Like, I spent the most of my 20s in WWE. That’s a very, very long time. And the landscape in this beautiful business changed. So the beautiful thing is nowadays we have other opportunities. And for me personally, after such a long time being with a company, to not seek out new opportunities, maybe a place where I see myself more fitting — who wouldn’t do that?” When asked if WWE’s offer included a raise or pay cut, Dragunov didn’t want to go into detail about what was being offered. “To be honest, I’m too much discreet and too much of a businessman and a gentleman myself to talk about these kinds of things,” he said. “Everything I can say is that it was nothing that I felt satisfying and nothing that gave me the perspective of, ‘Okay, I must stick with what I hear.’” Dragunov said he did not know the 2026 Andre the Giant Memorial Battle Royal in April would end up being his last match for the company. The first time he started to feel like WWE maybe wasn’t the right place for him was around March-April 2026. After dropping the United States Championship at the end of 2025, Dragunov thinks there could have been more time to go into a story that was “outside of just holding a championship.” Returning from ACL surgery and winning the US title in October 2025 was an amazing moment for Dragunov, and he’s grateful for all of the beautiful people he got to spend time with in WWE. He has no regrets about his tenure there. Dragunov described his AEW WrestleDream arrival as a “fairytale.” He appreciates the warm welcome the fans gave him and all the work AEW put into making his debut special. Everything has been collaborative so far between Dragunov and AEW. Dragunov will make his AEW in-ring debut on Dynamite this Wednesday night. He told Helwani that he does not know the identity of his opponent yet. Joseph Currier Joseph Currier is a graduate of the University of Massachusetts, obtaining a journalism degree in 2016. Joseph joined F4W during his time at UMass and has now been writing about the industry for nearly a decade. In addition to his work with F4W, Joseph has previously contributed to Sports Illustrated's wrestling coverage. He lives in Massachusetts and is a diehard fan of the Boston sports teams and Liverpool Football Club.
summary: Ilja Dragunov said his decision to leave WWE came from multiple factors including the financial offer, his desire for a creative change of scenery after spending most of his 20s with the company, and the evolving opportunities in the wrestling business. He expressed that after such a long tenure it made sense to explore places where he might fit better long term. Dragunov declined to discuss specifics of WWE's contract offer, citing his discretion as a businessman.

title: Roman Reigns Explains His Part-Time WWE Schedule
raw_title: Roman Reigns On His WWE Schedule: 'Quality Over Quantity'
summary_src: Commenting on his part-time WWE schedule, Roman Reigns emphasized that the quality of his in-ring performances is more important than their frequency.
body: "Quality over quantity, every single day of the week," Reigns stated during an interview with Sam Roberts on his " notsam " radio show. "I don't like to fall down at all, and I — for some reason — chose to do that for a living, but that's a part of the deal. But yeah, it's got to be on a Saturday or a very important Sunday. It's got to check off one of my dates, you know what I mean?" Reigns' response was partially in jest, but in the past, he gave a more serious answer about his part-time schedule. Assessing the business side of pro wrestling, Reigns said he doesn't believe he should be doing live events based on his value as a main eventer. title: Tatum Paxley reflects on path to WWE Women's Tag Team title
raw_title: 'I was so lost': How Tatum Paxley went from college dropout to WWE champion
body: Not long ago, the new WWE Women's Tag Team Champion had no idea what her future held. But fast forward to today, and just over two months have passed since Paxley's main-roster debut on "WWE SmackDown" in August . "Oh man, I don't know if I've had a better week in my life," Paxley told Uncrowned. "It's one of those moments that is very 'pinch me, I'm dreaming.' I can remember it so well, standing in the ring, holding my title up, hearing the pyro. I just remember slowly looking over, and there's Alexa Bliss. "It's just so unbelievable. It's truly a dream come true for me, because she was such an inspiration for me getting here, and to be able to do this with her, and then to have Charlotte [Flair] in the back supporting us — it's just a dream come true." That shiny gold title hasn't left Paxley's side since she and Bliss beat the former champions, Fatal Influence — Fallon Henley and Lainey Reid. For Paxley, it's her third title under the WWE umbrella overall — she also won the top Women's Championship and North American Championship of the promotion's developmental brand, NXT. The drive to adapt came fast for Paxley, and she quickly learned that the performative nature of an endeavor like wrestling was perfect for her personality and athleticism. Normally, the jump from NXT to a WWE main-roster show like "SmackDown" can be jarring, but the change has fit Paxley like a glove, and she knew it was inevitable. "It has been super seamless for me. Personally, the transition from NXT to 'SmackDown' has been super calm," Paxley said. "I feel like it's just because I knew how ready I was. That's not to say that I was rushing by any means, but I just knew for a long time, when I get that call, I know who I am, I know how to connect with the audience, I know how to go in the ring. Like, I'm going to be ready. Then I get the call, I have like some of the best people that have taken me under their wing [with] Charlotte Flair, Alexa Bliss. It has just been super seamless. It just feels right. Paxley likes not having a plan; she's built her career with blinders on, to an extent. That may almost seem counterproductive in a business as calculated as professional wrestling, but Paxley took it so far as even insisting on staying in the dark ahead of her WWE debut in August. She recalled thinking that producer Michael Hayes was ribbing her when told she'd premiere in the long-awaited Charlotte Flair vs. Jade Cargill match. "I'm someone who doesn't really like to know the plan. I don't like to know the direction. I like to really live in the moment," Paxley said. "I have the quality to really overthink something. So I find the less I know, the better. "So when I originally got word that main roster was looking at me, I was like, 'Cool. Don't tell me nothing,' and just kind of just went about my life. People would slowly start kind of telling me what they knew and who I would be [working] with, so I had a little bit of an idea of what was happening. But I tried not to

body: Ilja Dragunov says he has no regrets about his encounter with Brock Lesnar at the 2026 WWE Royal Rumble, despite some fans feeling Lesnar’s response to his chops was disrespectful. During the match in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, on January 31, Dragunov chopped Lesnar several times in the corner. Lesnar no-sold the chops, screamed at Dragunov, and then eliminated him from the Rumble. The new AEW signing addressed his interaction with Lesnar in the Rumble during Tuesday’s edition of The Ariel Helwani Show , with Helwani asking how he felt about fans who believed Lesnar had disrespected him. “First of all, that’s a shout-out to all the fans that are feeling with me and are passionate with me and get angry for me in that sense. I love all of you guys, and you’ve been sticking around with me forever. So I appreciate your concern. “But I said it before, honestly, if you really understand the persona that I have been in the ring for the most part of the time, I’ve been facing monsters. And at the end of the day, you can’t change certain things. You have a person like Brock Lesnar standing in front of you. Most people would run away as soon as that happens. That’s simply what would happen. Dragunov made his AEW debut on Saturday at WrestleDream 2026 in Orlando, Florida. On " Busted Open Radio ," Bully Ray and Dave LaGreca pondered what's next for Cass, and if that involves his former tag team partner. "The first thing that comes to mind if you bring Enzo in now is Big Cass is a failed experiment," Bully Ray said. "If they were to bring in Enzo now, it would be like, 'We need to salvage this guy, and the only way we can salvage him is putting him back with this other guy,'" he said. The hosts agreed that it may not be possible to capture the "lightning in a bottle" that the team once had. LaGreca said it's a different audience now, and some fans will remember the team, but as Bully Ray said, the rest of the WWE universe "would need a reprogramming."

title: Ilja Dragunov Isn’t Worried About Getting Lost on AEW’s Stacked Roster
raw_title: Ilja Dragunov Isn’t Worried About Getting Lost on AEW’s Stacked Roster
summary_src: Ilja Dragunov isn’t worried about becoming just another name on AEW’s ridiculously stacked roster. The former WWE star says getting lost in the shuffle isn’t a fear he has at all, because he’s spent his entire career betting on himself.
body: Speaking to TMZ’s Inside the Ring , Dragunov was asked whether AEW’s loaded roster made him think about how he would stand out from everyone else. For Dragunov, that’s apparently not something he spent much time worrying about. “I mean, we basically talked about this right now. I didn’t consider how stacked the roster is because, like, that’s a fear I don’t have.” That confidence also played a pretty big role in Dragunov walking away from WWE. He believes in trusting his instincts, and leaving the company was another example of him being willing to take that gamble on himself. “I was always betting on myself. I bet on myself when I left WWE. I’m betting on myself still, and I’m betting on what my gut is telling me.” Dragunov also thinks AEW has already shown that it sees something different in him. He pointed directly to the way the company presented his arrival at WrestleDream, where his debut was treated like a major deal before Tony Khan officially confirmed that he was All Elite. “And the way the people — the company — introduced me, I think it speaks for itself that I stick out from all the rest in that roster.” For Dragunov, standing out isn’t about trying to manufacture something just because the roster is crowded. He believes wrestlers who are genuinely different naturally pull people’s attention toward them. “And, you know, people who stick out and are not like anybody else, you kind of, like, put the objective on them.” That’s also where Dragunov slipped in an interesting observation about wrestling today. He suggested that too many wrestlers are trying to look or act like everyone else, and that’s when getting overlooked becomes a real problem. “And only if you are like everybody else or try to be like everybody else — which is also, like, an unfortunate thing happening nowadays, unfortunately — then you get overlooked.” Dragunov doesn’t believe he falls into that category, and he’s got 14 years of experience to back up that confidence. As far as he’s concerned, standing out has never been the problem. “But I haven’t been overlooked once in my 14 years of career.” AEW certainly isn’t short on talent, so Dragunov will have plenty of competition for television time as his run gets going. He just doesn’t sound interested in worrying about any of that, especially when being different has worked out pretty well for him for the last 14 years. Subhojeet Mukherjee Subhojeet Mukherjee has covered pro wrestling for over 20 years, delivering trusted news and backstage updates to fans around the world.

I didn’t consider how stacked the roster is because, like, that’s a fear I don’t have. That confidence additionally played a pretty big role in Dragunov walking away from WWE.

title: Ilja Dragunov details WWE exit and AEW arrival
raw_title: Ilja Dragunov on his AEW fairy tale, WWE regrets, Lesnar’s no-selling, and Gunther’s booking
summary_src: Fresh off a Saturday night debut at AEW’s WrestleDream PPV, and with his first AEW match tomorrow night on Dynamite to promote, Ilja Dragunov stopped by The Ariel Helwani Show this afternoon (Oct. 20).
body: Link Ricky Havlik for All Elite Wrestling Fresh off a Saturday night debut at AEW’s WrestleDream PPV, and with his first AEW match tomorrow night on Dynamite to promote, Ilja Dragunov stopped by The Ariel Helwani Show this afternoon (Oct. 20). Dragunov left WWE when his last contract expired, and spoke a little bit about that decision and the one to join AEW at the post-PPV media scrum, but he went a little more in depth with Helwani. The lack of creative for his character after dropping the United States title last December was a red flag for the Mad Dragon: ”After I dropped the belt, things kind of went in directions where I felt like, ok, it could have been better. There could have been more time to go into a story, into something that is outside of just holding a championship, captivating for the people… It never changed anything about my work mentality, because I love what I do, and I make every minute count for myself. But we all have feelings, and… especially if we’re in a business like this, we want to devote ourselves to this…” “There was no intention of the company to let me go… It was an accumulation of a lot of things. Of course, the offering, because we all know at the end of the day, it’s a business. But also, it’s definitely based on my feeling of how I want to work creatively. I spent most of my twenties in WWE. That’s a very, very long time, and the landscape in this beautiful business changed… the expiration of my contract came and the negotiations didn’t lead anywhere. There was nothing that I felt satisfying. Nothing that gave me the perspective of, ‘Oo, I must stick with what I have here.’ I had a gut feeling. I think things will work out for me, that I can bet on myself… Change always requires guts. It requires courage. It requires dealing with the possibility that things could not work out your way. It all came down to betting on myself and believing it’s going to be all right.” That also sets up a great line from Ilja about the polarizing reaction he gets from wrestling fandom: “I don’t see it as a defeat. I’m glad that people are upset for me, and maybe it could have worked out a different way… “I have two categories of people watching my work. Either people who are extremely behind me, really get me, really get emotionally invested in me, or it’s the polar opposite, the people who think I’m the cringiest person in the world. But I love it that way because people care.” This clip also includes Helwani asked if Dragunov leaves with any regrets, which he dismisses with, “No, why should I?” before talking about what he got out of his seven years there, and expressing gratitude for the opportunities he got during that time. Asking about his old friend and epic rival Gunther’s booking this year got Dragunov to be slightly critical of his old company: “I guess my feelings the same feeling as a lot of other people share — if you are the person to retire John Cena, it’s kind of like a standard that you should keep a certain level

He cited a lack of creative direction after losing the United States title last December as a key factor in his decision to leave when his contract expired. Dragunov also touched on his excitement for his new chapter in AEW, where he is set to wrestle on Dynamite.

title: WWE Covered Hip Surgery For Psicosis
raw_title: WWE Reportedly Covered Hip Surgery Costs For Former AAA Star Psicosis
summary_src: WWE has reportedly covered the hip replacement surgery costs for AAA Hall of Famer Psicosis, at the request of Psicosis' long-time rival Rey Mysterio
body: The decision to pay for the surgery, which is believed to have cost $44K, came from WWE President Nick Khan, and helped by Psicosis being under a WWE Legend's Contract. However, Meltzer describes the operation as being "spearheaded" by WWE luchador Rey Mysterio. Along with Juventud Guerrera, Psicosis is considered to be a key rival for Mysterio during the early portion of his career. Their rivalry spanned promotions such as AAA, the Japanese promotion WAR, ECW, and WCW, where the two notably competed in the acclaimed opening match at Bash at the Beach 1996, the site of the formation of the nWo. Even separate from his matches with Mysterio, Psicosis has had a memorable career, winning the WCW World Cruiserweight Championship twice, the AAA World Tag Team Championships with Joe Lider, and the Mexican National Welterweight Championship twice. He would briefly compete for WWE from 2005 to 2006 as part of the controversial Mexicools stable alongside Guerrera and Super Crazy. He had continued to compete in Mexico up until two years ago, when he was forced to have emergency surgery on his hip following an injury . He was inducted into the AAA Hall of Fame later that year.
summary: WWE paid for former AAA and WCW star Psicosis's hip surgery that reportedly cost $44,000. The decision came from President Nick Khan with the help of Psicosis being under a WWE Legends Contract. title: MJF Replaces Billy Gunn At Create-A-Pro Event
raw_title: Billy Gunn off indie show due to ‘contractual obligations,’ top AEW name added
summary_src: Billy Gunn won’t be making his scheduled appearance for Create-A-Pro Wrestling this weekend, but the Long Island fans are getting a significant makegood.
body: Billy Gunn won’t be making his scheduled appearance for Create-A-Pro Wrestling this weekend, but the Long Island fans are getting a significant makegood. Create-A-Pro announced today that, due to contractual obligations, Gunn will not be at their Base Brawl event in North Merrick, New York this Saturday (October 24). However, former AEW World Champion MJF and AEW broadcaster Alicia Atout will now be doing meet and greets at the event. Those who purchased meet and greet packages for Gunn will have their money refunded, as will anyone who purchased a New Age Outlaws meet and greet. Road Dogg will still be at the show. which is a fundraiser for Merrick Bellmore Little League. MJF, who got his start in wrestling by training at Create-A-Pro, responded to the announcement of him replacing Gunn: “Perfect replacement. I [too] am an ass man.” Create-A-Pro is owned by Brian Myers and Pat Buck. MJF remains close with the school/promotion and returned this May for a victory over Max Caster. Originally, it was supposed to be MJF vs. Nic Nemeth at that event before TNA Wrestling changed its policy to not allow its wrestlers to face AEW names on the indies. On the same night as Saturday’s Create-A-Pro show, AEW will be in Winston-Salem, North Carolina for Collision. Joseph joined F4W during his time at UMass and has now been writing about the industry for nearly a decade. In addition to his work with F4W, Joseph has previously contributed to Sports Illustrated's wrestling coverage. He lives in Massachusetts and is a diehard fan of the Boston sports teams and Liverpool Football Club.

title: Ilja Dragunov explains decision to leave WWE for AEW
raw_title: Ilja Dragunov reveals why he rejected WWE's offer to stay, frustrations that led to AEW move
body: Speaking Tuesday on "The Ariel Helwani Show" , Dragunov said he didn't know he was leaving the company when he competed in his final WWE match in April. "I didn't know at the time I was leaving. I was just waiting," Dragunov told Uncrowned. "I'm a person who loves what they do. I want to compete, I want to work, I want to do this and that. I just got a little stuck. But it's nothing new to anybody. It was pretty obvious. "So, the time just passed by and then I reached the expiration of my contract, and I felt, over time, that OK, how everything is working out, and how I'm feeling — because I do a lot of things depending on how I feel about it. I've always had the courage to do so. I felt it was time to breathe some new fresh air." WWE letting Dragunov go was somewhat of a stunning decision to hear. After recovering from an ACL tear, Dragunov returned last year and made his "SmackDown" debut, winning the aforementioned U.S. title in his first appearance on the program. That alone showed the faith the company appeared to have in someone with his in-ring talent. "It was an accumulation of a lot of things," Dragunov said. "The [deal WWE was] offering — as we all know, at the end of the day, it's a business. But also, it's definitely based off my feeling of, do I want to work creatively? Do I need a scenery change? Is the scenery change something where I can see myself stay forever? "You have to consider a lot of factors. I spent most of my 20s in WWE. That's a very, very long time, and the landscape in this beautiful business changed. The beautiful thing is, nowadays we have a lot of other opportunities, and for me personally, after such a long time being with a company, to not seek out new opportunities, maybe at a place where I see myself more fitting, who wouldn't do that?" "There was nothing that I felt [was] satisfying," Dragunov added of WWE's offer, "and nothing that gave me the perspective of like, 'OK, I must stick with what [I have] here.'" The U.S. title run was refreshing and well-deserved for Dragunov, whose initial main-roster run was cut extremely short on "Raw" by a knee injury. Dragunov, 33, still looks back very fondly at his final year in WWE and how it started. But once the title left his possession, he admits his mind started to wander. "After I tore my ACL, I had been fortunate to win a championship straight on my comeback, which was an amazing moment for me that I still cherish," Dragunov said. "I think that after I dropped the belt, things kind of went two directions where I feel like, 'OK, it could have been better. It could have been more time to go into a story, something that is outside of just holding a championship, captivating for the people.' So, around April, maybe even a month before that, I was just thinking about it. "It never changed anything about my work mentality, because I love what I do and I make every minute count for myself, but we all have feelings, and we all want to — especially in a business like this.
summary: Ilja Dragunov appeared on The Ariel Helwani Show and said he did not know he would be departing WWE during his final match in April. He explained that he grew frustrated feeling stuck in the company despite his desire to compete regularly and decided to let his contract expire before seeking a new environment. After recovering from an ACL tear, he had returned and captured the United States Championship on his SmackDown debut last year.

title: Ilja Dragunov says he needs to wrestle in Japan

summary_src: Ilja Dragunov says he “needs to wrestle in Japan,” believing his in-ring style would connect with the people. During an interview with TMZ on Tuesday, the new AEW signing was asked who he would still like to work with in his career.
body: Ilja Dragunov says he “needs to wrestle in Japan,” believing his in-ring style would connect with the people. During an interview with TMZ on Tuesday, the new AEW signing was asked who he would still like to work with in his career. Dragunov instead said it wasn’t a matter of who he wanted to work with, but rather where. “I wouldn’t say it’s necessarily who I want to work with, but where I want to work. “Back in the day when I started with wXw, they had a working relationship with Big Japan Pro Wrestling. And when I joined wXw, it’s kind of like this time was passed. “And the one thing that I didn’t do in my career so far, multiple things that I didn’t do in my career so far, but specifically something that I need to do is to wrestle in Japan. I need to wrestle in Japan. Because that’s the place where I think my style belongs, and I think I would connect with the people, with this culture for professional wrestling in a whole different way.” Dragunov wrestled on three wXw shows co-promoted with Combat Zone Wrestling and Big Japan Pro Wrestling in 2013. However, all three events took place in Germany. During his time with wXw, Dragunov became a one-time wXw Unified World Wrestling Champion, a three-time wXw World Tag Team Champion and a two-time wXw Shotgun Champion. Dragunov made his AEW debut at WrestleDream 2026 in Orlando on Saturday, where Renee Paquette introduced him as the company’s newest signing. title: Billy Gunn Sides With CM Punk In AEW Fight
raw_title: Billy Gunn On CM Punk & Young Bucks AEW Brawl: 'Poke The Bear, Get Ready To Get Bit'
summary_src: AEW coach Billy Gunn commented on the 2022 backstage brawl between CM Punk and Young Bucks during an interview with "Inside the Ropes."
body: "They just have to realize that sometimes there's certain veterans that just aren't going to put up with that s*** no matter what," Gunn said. "If you're a young little buckaroo and you want to poke the bear, get ready to get bit. So, I think that's what happened. I don't know the whole details, that's between them." Gunn said that during his time in WWE, things like that usually didn't happen. He said then-chairman Vince McMahon had things under control backstage, and most guys knew they didn't have to like one another in order to do business together. He said there'd be a confrontation every now and then, but wrestlers worked it out all behind-the-scenes. "That's how grown a** people deal with s***," he said. "Nowadays, we don't, and that's sad, but there's going to be people that are going to do that."
summary: Billy Gunn commented on the backstage brawl involving CM Punk and The Young Bucks. He said certain veterans won't tolerate certain behavior and that if someone pokes the bear they should expect to get bit. Gunn added that such incidents were rare in WWE because Vince McMahon kept things under control and wrestlers handled issues privately like grown adults.

Gunn, who serves as a coach in AEW, stated that he was not present for the incident. He noted that some veterans will not tolerate certain behavior and suggested that attempting to challenge them can lead to consequences.

He indicated that he was not familiar with all the details of the situation and chose not to follow the related media coverage. Gunn emphasized that the specifics remain between those directly involved.

When asked about handling similar issues during his earlier career, Gunn pointed to the approach taken under Vince McMahon. He explained that wrestlers were expected to conduct business professionally regardless of personal feelings.

Gunn described a method of addressing conflicts privately by pulling individuals into a room to resolve problems immediately. He contrasted this with current practices, calling the shift away from such discretion unfortunate.
Following the incident, Punk received a suspension from AEW. He made a return one year later before being fired after a separate event at All In 2023.

title: Ilja Dragunov explains exit from WWE for AEW

body: By Jason Powell , ProWrestling.net Editor ( @prowrestlingnet ) New AEW signee Ilja Dragunov has addressed his decision to leave WWE. “It was an accumulation of a lot of things,” Dragunov said on The Ariel Helwani Show. “An accumulation of, of course, the offering, because we all know, at the end of the day, it’s the business. title: On the Record: Ilja Dragunov Responds to MJF Trashing His AEW Debut at WrestleDream 2026
raw_title: Ilja Dragunov Responds to MJF Trashing His AEW Debut at WrestleDream 2026
summary_src: Ilja Dragunov has heard MJF’s shot at his AEW debut, and he’s not exactly rushing to fire back. After MJF mocked his elaborate WrestleDream entrance and called him a “Russian/German loser,” Dragunov made it pretty clear he doesn’t consider MJF’s words important enough to worry about.
body: The interviewer tried to get a little more out of him, but Dragunov wasn’t interested in turning it into some big war of words. As far as he’s concerned, there are more important problems to worry about. “Come on. Like, please. I’m Russian-German. We handle problems of relevance.” MJF started the whole thing after WrestleDream, when he posted his not-so-glowing review of AEW’s latest pay-per-view. Along with ripping AEW World Champion Will Ospreay, MJF took aim at Dragunov’s orchestra-themed presentation. “Russian/german loser debuts by pretending he’s a ‘composer’…cool.” “No — chops and elbows and boots and throws and… come on. Like, I handle problems of relevance.” “And especially in Russian culture, we talk about things with depth, but we do not get hurt by words. If I got hurt more by words, I wouldn’t be sitting here nowadays. So, please, come on.” MJF may have been looking for a reaction when he mocked Dragunov’s WrestleDream debut, but he definitely didn’t get much of one here. Dragunov seems far more interested in throwing chops, elbows, boots and bodies than getting dragged into a social media argument. title: Key Moments Building Roman Reigns and Sami Zayn Story

Jey tore the shirt off, and Reigns presented Zayn with a new one reading "Honorary Uce." Zayn put it on, acknowledged Reigns as the Tribal Chief, and the two embraced in the ring. Jey did not look happy with the decision. The Bloodline headlined Survivor Series: WarGames on Nov. 26, 2022, at TD Garden in Boston. Reigns, Jey, Jimmy, Sikoa, and Zayn faced Kevin Owens, Drew McIntyre, Sheamus, Ridge Holland, and Butch. Jey entered the event suspicious, having overheard Owens urge Zayn to turn on the group. Late in the match , Owens hit Reigns with a Stunner, and Zayn grabbed the referee's arm to stop the count. Zayn followed with a low blow and a Helluva Kick to Owens, a longtime friend. Jey hit a splash and pinned Owens for the win. After the bell, Jey accepted Zayn as a member of The Bloodline. Reigns retained the Undisputed WWE Universal Championship against Owens at the Royal Rumble on Jan. 28, 2023, at the Alamodome in San Antonio. Jimmy, Jey, and Sikoa attacked Owens after the match . Reigns handed a steel chair to Zayn and demanded a shot on Owens. A moment of hesitation drew several slaps. Zayn swung the chair into Reigns instead. Jimmy, Sikoa, and Reigns beat Zayn down. Jey did not take part, left the ring, and walked up the ramp. Zayn's time in The Bloodline was over. Zayn attacked Reigns from behind on the following SmackDown and demanded a title match. Reigns accepted and promised to hurt Zayn in front of family and a home crowd. The bout went to Elimination Chamber on Feb. 18, 2023, at the Bell Centre in Montreal. Jimmy interfered during the match and attacked Zayn. Paul Heyman later produced a steel chair for Reigns, and Jey came to the ring but did not strike Zayn. Zayn charged for a Spear, Reigns moved, and Jey took the hit instead. Reigns struck Zayn with the chair and scored the pin after a Spear to retain. Zayn ran in during the post-match attack and helped fight off Sikoa's group. Reigns went for a Superman Punch on Sikoa, as Zayn threw a Helluva Kick. Sikoa moved, and the kick hit Reigns. On the Nov. 8 SmackDown, Zayn told Reigns the kick was an accident. Later that night, Sikoa attacked Reigns and waved Zayn into the ring, only to take a kick to the face. Reigns, Zayn, Jey, and Jimmy stood together to close the show. The reunited group added Punk as the fifth member for Survivor Series: WarGames on Nov. 30, 2024, at Rogers Arena in Vancouver. title: Andrade explains leaving AEW for WWE
raw_title: Andrade opens up about his decision to leave AEW for WWE
summary_src: A few years ago, Andrade El Idolo parted ways with AEW and joined WWE; He has now opened up about that decision. After spending a couple of years in AEW from 2021 to 2023, Andrade parted ways with the promotion and joined WWE.
body: A few years ago, Andrade El Idolo parted ways with AEW and joined WWE; He has now opened up about that decision. After spending a couple of years in AEW from 2021 to 2023, Andrade parted ways with the promotion and joined WWE. The current AEW National Champion recently sat down for an interview with Renee Paquette on AEW’s Close Up , where he explained the decision. The 36-year-old explained that while personally the decision felt good, professionally he was a little sad. “Personally was good, but professionally is a little sad because my contract was expired in this moment. So I need to pick a decision, like I need to go for my personal life because I was married in this moment, or my professional life ,” he shared. “ So I pick my personal life and need to make a decision. But I went with Tony [Khan] and say thank you for the opportunity, the contract expire, and I hope see you in the future. And I need to move for my personal life, or for myself, for a better relation ,” he added. Andrade further claimed that he always had a good relationship with AEW, and after he was done with WWE in 2025, Tony Khan gave him this opportunity. Hoping to pay back Khan with his in-ring work, El Idolo wants to help the promotion. “ I am here to help the company. They want the best for this company. They want the best for me. I want to represent this company very well. This is how I need to pay Tony for this second chance or second opportunity ,” he finished. After returning to AEW in Oct. 2025, El Idolo was soon removed from television after WWE had sent a cease-and-desist letter to AEW, claiming Andrade had violated terms of his contract. Following a lengthy legal battle , the Mexican wrestler officially came back in Jan. 2026. He has been a regular part of the promotion since. title: Drew McIntyre Shares 2006 Talk With PAC
raw_title: Drew McIntyre recalls early-career conversation with PAC
summary_src: Long before PAC and Drew McIntyre became two of the top names in the modern wrestling industry, they had their humble beginnings in the UK’s indie circuit. On Sept. 27, 2026, PAC passed away after he was found dead in his car after AEW All Out 2026.
body: Long before PAC and Drew McIntyre became two of the top names in the modern wrestling industry, they had their humble beginnings in the UK’s indie circuit. On Sept. 27, 2026, PAC passed away after he was found dead in his car after AEW All Out 2026. Recently, speaking on What’s Your Story? With Steph McMahon , McIntyre opened up about an early-career conversation he had with PAC. Reflecting on a conversation he had with the late AEW star in 2006, McIntyre recalled, “ I remember, we mentioned Ben [Benjamin Satterley] PAC. I remember in 2006, 2007 we were doing shows in London, and he was just incredible. Most insane high flyer I’d ever seen, the precision. “ And I’d tell him, ‘You’re going to be the one that makes it big from the UK.’ And he said, ‘No, you’re going to do it.’ And then to watch his journey and how far he came and how much he achieved, it was awesome ,” McIntyre added. The former WWE Champion also opened up about how proud he is of the representation of the British and Scottish people in WWE and the wrestling world. “ And he was complimentary to myself and it was so cool that so many people now from the UK have done so much for the world. Generally it was Americans and Canadians with a couple of Brits sprinkled in maybe here and there, but to see just the worldwide representation of WWE, specifically from the UK and even Scotland, there’s only five million people in Scotland ,” McIntyre added. “ And we’ve had more people than I can count, about eight or nine different superstars, and most of them were girls. Which really, really blew my mind. “ Two decades ago, in 2006, the two faced off against each other at RQW Not Just For Christmas 2006 in London, where PAC defeated Drew McIntyre, aka Drew Galloway, via count-out. title: Ilja Dragunov Explains WWE Exit
raw_title: Ilja Dragunov Talks WWE Departure, Says Their Offer To Retain Him Wasn't 'Satisfying'
summary_src: AEW's newest signee Ilja Dragunov spoke about his WWE departure back in August and said the company's offer to retain him wasn't "satisfying."
body: Ahead of stepping back in the ring on TV for the first time since April, Dragunov appeared on " The Ariel Helwani Show " to discuss his WWE departure. It was revealed that Dragunov's contract expired in August , and the star told Helwani that the story of his departure isn't very exciting. "I love what I do. I want to compete. I want to work," Dragunov said. "It just got a little stuck. But, it's nothing new to anybody. It was pretty obvious. So, the time just passed by and then I reached the expiration of my contract... I felt over time that, 'Okay, with how everything is working out and how I'm feeling, because I make a lot of [decisions] depending on how I feel about it, I've always had the courage to do so, I feel it is time to breathe some new, fresh air.'" The star said that despite things written online at the time, WWE had no intention of letting him go. He said his departure was the accumulation of many things, including what he wanted creatively. Dragunov said he pondered the scenery change, and if it was somewhere if he could see himself staying "forever." "I spent most of my 20s in WWE," he explained. "That's a very, very long time. The landscape in this beautiful business changed... For me, personally, after such a long time being with a company, to not seek out new opportunities, maybe another place more fitting, who wouldn't do that?" AEW/Ricky Havlik Dragunov reiterated that his departure story isn't as exciting as it was made out to be. He said at some points in WWE, you just don't have creative and are waiting for the opportunities to come. He explained that a lot of new people came up toward the end of his time in WWE, and there is only so much time for so many people. When Helwani inquired as to whether or not Dragunov was asked to take a pay cut, like New Level's Kofi and Austin Creed , AEW's newest star stayed mum on the topic. "To be honest, I'm much too discrete and too much of a businessman and a gentleman myself to talk about these kind of things," Dragunov said. "Everything I can say, is there was nothing I felt satisfying, and nothing that gave me the perspective of, 'Okay, I must stick with it [here.]'" "The Mad Dragon" said he's always had faith in himself and he's never been one to question his beliefs. He explained he always follows his gut feelings in life, and it's always worked out for him. The star said that many people want to change, but that change requires courage. "It also requires [dealing] with the possibility that things could not work out your way. I was aware of all these things," he said. "April was the last point in time I was in the ring. The feeling that maybe, 'I'm not right where I am.' I already had it before... It all came down to bet on myself and believe it's going to be alright. That's what I did my entire 14-year-long professional wrestling career."
summary: Ilja Dragunov's WWE contract expired in August. He appeared on The Ariel Helwani Show ahead of his first TV match since April and said the promotion made an offer to keep him that was not satisfying. Dragunov cited creative desires and a need for fresh air after feeling things had gotten stuck.

title: Bully Ray Suggests Alternate Finish To Raw Bloodline Brawl
raw_title: Bully Ray Would Have Changed One Thing About WWE Raw Angle With 946 & The Bloodline
summary_src: WWE Hall of Famer Bully Ray explains how would have kept everything about the latest Bloodline-946 segment the same, except for its finish.
body: On "Busted Open Radio," Ray explained that he would have kept everything about the latest Bloodline-946 segment the same, except for its finish. "946 beats down The Bloodline. Roman's entrance, the John Wayne walk, the four-on-four in the middle, the big schmoz, everything," Ray said, "and just when you think The Bloodline are going to get the upper hand, everybody has spilled out of the ring, Roman Reigns just hit a big Superman Punch on whoever, Carmelo Hayes in the back door with that tire iron he was carrying to the ring. Crack Roman right in the back of the head ... and he goes down." Carmelo Hayes, a former WWE United States Champion, is the newest addition to 946, having just debuted among the terrorizing group last week. In that case, Hayes struck down Jimmy Uso, Jey Uso, and Solo Sikoa with a crowbar. This week, he found himself on the receiving end of a Samoan Spike from Sikoa before rolling out of the ring. In Ray's preferred scenario, Hayes would have nailed "The OTC" Roman Reigns with a crowbar instead this week, with his new allies then helping him continue the attack until they felt satisfied with themselves. "When the rest of The Bloodline run in to check on him, because it's freaking Roman, that's when 946 pours it on again," Ray added. "And you don't have to have 946 standing over The Bloodline like we saw last week, but they give them their shots, and then they get out of dodge."
summary: Bully Ray praised the latest segment pitting 946 against The Bloodline on Raw but would have altered only the conclusion. In his vision, after the brawl spilled outside the ring and Roman Reigns delivered a Superman Punch, Carmelo Hayes would have struck Reigns in the back of the head with a tire iron instead of taking a Samoan Spike from Solo Sikoa. Hayes had previously used a crowbar on Jimmy Uso, Jey Uso and Sikoa in his debut with the group the previous week.

title: Edge
raw_title: Edge - WWE
summary_src: Edge WWE
body: Edge More Share Options More Share Options Share close facebook x threads email superstar stats Superstar Stats Edge Buy the Song Career Highlights WWE Champion; World Heavyweight Champion; World Tag Team Champion; WWE Tag Team Champion; Intercontinental Champion; WCW U.S. Champion; 2001 King of the Ring; Money in the Bank Ladder Match winner; Royal Rumble Match winner (2010, 2021); 2012 WWE Hall of Fame Inductee In another life, Edge could have been a rock star. From his voluminous hair to his long leather jackets and double-horns signature pose, every detail of his WWE image screamed it. As the pyro blasted into the air behind him on the entranceway before he stepped into the ring, he injected arenas with the energy of a packed concert – without the dangers of crowd-surfing and mosh pits. There was even a legion of groupies – Edgeheads – who tracked his every move. It's no surprise, then, that Edge is a guitar collector and grew up listening to KISS, a band famous for their flamboyant outfits and outrageous stage antics. What is a surprise is how a shy high schooler from the little town of Orangeville, Ontario, evolved into The Rated-R Superstar. Edge had some fine company as he worked his way up the independent scene in the '90s: his childhood friend and partner for countless five-second poses, Christian. When Edge was signed to a WWE contract in 1997, it was only a matter of time before Christian would also climb the ladder, following his best bud into uncharted territory. "E&C" made sweet music as a tag team, using a lot more than just Con-Chair-Tos to claim seven championships together. A Triple Threat Ladder Match victory at WrestleMania 2000 over The Hardy Boyz and The Dudley Boyz laid the foundation for a series of landmark Tables, Ladders & Chairs (TLC) contests, and some of the greatest tag team action of all time. Of course, tag teaming wasn't Edge's only specialty, as he masterfully crafted a singles career and captured a whopping 31 total titles – many of them the WWE Universe didn't even see coming. Beyond his ability to capitalize on opportunities, Edge became known as The Master Manipulator because he wasn't afraid to cross the line in order to rattle the competition. After he made history in 2006 as the first man to ever cash in the Money in the Bank contract, he rubbed his WWE Championship triumph in the face of all challengers with an R-rated celebration on Raw; more explicitly, a frolicking good time with Lita on a bed placed right in the middle of the squared circle. Mind games were taken to a whole new level by the self-proclaimed "most-watched champion." A debilitating injury forced Edge to retire in 2011 but, in the 2020 Royal Rumble Match, The Ultimate Opportunist made an incredible return to the squared circle and immediately set out to add numerous epic matches to hs already storied career. 24:16 Karl Anderson More Share Options More Share Options Share close facebook x threads email Faction reveals that shook WWE: WWE

title: On the Record: Dave Meltzer Breaks Down Past Health Issues Faced By Late AEW Star PAC
raw_title: Dave Meltzer Discusses Past Health Issues Faced By Late AEW Star PAC
body: Dave Meltzer has discussed the health issues previously experienced by late AEW star PAC, whose real name was Benjamin Satterley, following the official determination of his cause of death. The Cook County Medical Examiner’s Office ruled that Satterley died from bronchial asthma and classified his death as natural. He was 40. Speaking on Wrestling Observer Radio, Meltzer said the wrestler had experienced health problems before his death, including blood-clot issues in 2023 and problems affecting his lungs. Meltzer said a friend had informed him about PAC’s medical history. Meltzer also discussed the uncertainty surrounding whether Satterley had access to an inhaler during the fatal episode. (via WrestlingInc) “We don’t know if he had an inhaler in his car. He did have lung issues. This isn’t something that came out of nowhere that nobody knew. I don’t know how well it was known, but one of his friends had told me that … he had the blood clot issues in 2023, and said that he had some lung issues. And so the lung issues are consistent with what happened unfortunately. Usually, you’d have the inhaler with you and I don’t know, it may have happened so quick. There was stuff in his rental car, but it may have happened so quick that he wasn’t able to get it. It’s a horrible situation the more you learn about it. It doesn’t get better, it gets worse,” he said. Satterley competed as PAC in AEW and Neville in WWE. He was found unresponsive behind the wheel of a rental car in a parking lot in Des Plaines, Illinois, on September 27, hours after he competed at All Out. AEW dedicated its September 30 episode of Dynamite to Satterley’s life and career.

Speaking on Wrestling Observer Radio, Meltzer explained the wrestler had experienced health problems before his death, including blood-clot issues in 2023 and problems affecting his lungs.

title: Ilja Dragunov explains WWE exit and AEW arrival
raw_title: Ilja Dragunov talks his AEW fairy tale & WWE regrets, Gunther’s booking
body: Link Ricky Havlik for All Elite Wrestling Fresh off a Saturday night debut at AEW’s WrestleDream PPV, and with his first AEW match tomorrow night on Dynamite to promote, Ilja Dragunov stopped by The Ariel Helwani Show this afternoon (Oct. 20). Dragunov left WWE when his last contract expired, and spoke a little bit about that decision and the one to join AEW at the post-PPV media scrum, but he went a little more in depth with Helwani. The lack of creative for his character after dropping the United States title last December was a red flag for the Mad Dragon: ”After I dropped the belt, things kind of went in directions where I felt like, ok, it could have been better. There could have been more time to go into a story, into something that is outside of just holding a championship, captivating for the people… It never changed anything about my work mentality, because I love what I do, and I make every minute count for myself. But we all have feelings, and… especially if we’re in a business like this, we want to devote ourselves to this…” “There was no intention of the company to let me go… It was an accumulation of a lot of things. Of course, the offering, because we all know at the end of the day, it’s a business. But also, it’s definitely based on my feeling of how I want to work creatively. I spent most of my twenties in WWE. That’s a very, very long time, and the landscape in this beautiful business changed… the expiration of my contract came and the negotiations didn’t lead anywhere. There was nothing that I felt satisfying. Nothing that gave me the perspective of, ‘Oo, I must stick with what I have here.’ I had a gut feeling. I think things will work out for me, that I can bet on myself… Change always requires guts. It requires courage. It requires dealing with the possibility that things could not work out your way. It all came down to betting on myself and believing it’s going to be all right.” That also sets up a great line from Ilja about the polarizing reaction he gets from wrestling fandom: “I don’t see it as a defeat. I’m glad that people are upset for me, and maybe it could have worked out a different way… “I have two categories of people watching my work. Either people who are extremely behind me, really get me, really get emotionally invested in me, or it’s the polar opposite, the people who think I’m the cringiest person in the world. But I love it that way because people care.” This clip also includes Helwani asked if Dragunov leaves with any regrets, which he dismisses with, “No, why should I?” before talking about what he got out of his seven years there, and expressing gratitude for the opportunities he got during that time. Asking about his old friend and epic rival Gunther’s booking this year got Dragunov to be slightly critical of his old company: “I guess my feelings the same feeling as a lot of other people share — if you are the person to retire John Cena, it’s kind of like a standard that you should keep a certain level
summary: Ilja Dragunov discussed his decision to depart WWE after his contract expired, citing a lack of creative direction for his character following the loss of the United States title last December. The performer expressed that he desired more storytelling opportunities beyond championship reigns to better connect with audiences while maintaining his strong work ethic. He made his AEW debut at WrestleDream on Saturday and is set for his first match on Dynamite this week.

title: Prime Video Adds More Wrestling as MLW Expands Streaming Reach
raw_title: Prime Video Adds More Wrestling as MLW Expands Streaming Reach
body: Wrestling fans have another place to watch Major League Wrestling (MLW), but the latest streaming deal comes with a catch. MLW has announced that its flagship weekly series, MLW Fusion , is now available to purchase on Amazon Prime Video, giving fans another way to watch matches, follow rivalries, and revisit past episodes. This is not a new show included at no extra cost with a Prime membership, as the latest deal lets viewers purchase full seasons for $26.99 or individual episodes for $1.99. “MLW belongs on the biggest platforms, and Amazon Prime Video is another significant step in that direction,” said MLW Founder and CEO Court Bauer in a statement. For fans who prefer buying individual episodes or seasons rather than relying on a rotating streaming catalog, the new option provides another way to access the show. Still, viewers looking to avoid another expense have other choices. “We’re making it easier for fans to discover and experience Fusion, follow the rivalries and revisit the fights that get everyone talking. This gives our fans another way to watch and opens the door for a new audience to experience MLW,” Bauer said The Prime Video announcement doesn’t replace MLW’s existing free streaming options. Instead, the deal is the latest in a series of moves by MLW to get its programming in front of more viewers. Then, in September, MLW added Tubi as a home for new weekly episodes . The promotion’s flagship series airs on Tubi every Thursday at 8:00 PM ET, giving fans a way to follow without paying for an additional subscription. Now, Prime Video joins YouTube, VEEPS, Tubi, and NJPW WORLD as streaming destinations for MLW programming; however, with Amazon, the promotion is taking a different approach. Rather than relying exclusively on a free, ad-supported service, the promotion can also sell individual episodes and full seasons to viewers who prefer to purchase their content.

title: In Memoriam: Pac’s (Ben Satterley) cause of death determined
raw_title: Pac’s (Ben Satterley) cause of death determined
body: Pac’s cause of death has been determined to have been from bronchial asthma by the Cook County Medical Examiner’s Office in Illinois. His death was ruled as being the result of natural causes. Pac died on Sept. 27 one day after wrestling on AEW’s All Out PPV. Satterley’s body was spotted by a witness in a rental car about on a street about a mile from O’Hare International Airport in Chicago and that person called 911, according to information made available by the Cook County medical examiner’s office. “Benjamin Satterley, who performed under the name ‘Pac,’ was found dead about 4 p.m. Sunday in Des Plaines, according to the Cook County medical examiner’s office.” There were no signs of foul play or trauma when Pac’s body was discovered according to the report. The Cook County Medical Examiner’s Office report on Pac’s cause of death was first reported by The New York Post.

body: 0 Jordynne Grace has been absent from WWE TV for several months, and the latest backstage reports suggest the company has no current plans for her return. The former TNA Knockouts World Champion is reportedly healthy and has been around the WWE roster despite her absence from TV. WWE had previously considered pairing her with Ivy Nile in a new tag team, but those plans appear to have stalled. The team could have given both wrestlers a fresh direction. Reports also suggested that the pairing might have been linked to the trademarked name “Iron Built.” However, WWE has yet to officially announce the team or reveal when Grace might return. It’s also unclear whether the previously filmed segments will eventually air or if WWE has decided to take things in a different direction. For now, no confirmed return date for Grace has come to light. The latest WrestleVotes report also suggests that fans shouldn’t expect her to return to television anytime soon. During a recent WrestleVotes Q&A, JoeyVotes and TC were asked about Grace’s status and when fans might see her return to WWE TV. “The thing that I’ve heard recently is she’s not in the creative plans. That doesn’t mean they don’t want plans for her,” JoeyVotes said (H/T: Ringside News ). He also pointed to the crowded women’s division on SmackDown as a possible reason for her absence. Many superstars are already involved in ongoing storylines, leaving less time for others to appear on TV. “They’ve got full-blown stories. They’ve got Fatal Influence, Charlotte’s group, Jade Cargill’s group. That’s one story. They’ve got Tiffany with the briefcase. They’ve got Nikki and Paige and Chelsea Green. That’s another story,” he explained. As a result, Grace may have to wait for the right opportunity to make her reentry into television. title: Looking At Flaws Pro Wrestling Needs To Correct That Are Lost In The Sea Of Endless Programming
raw_title: LOOKING AT FLAWS PRO WRESTLING NEEDS TO CORRECT THAT ARE LOST IN THE SEA OF ENDLESS PROGRAMMING - PWInsider
body: DMFirst Veer Game odds uden om ROFUS Jalwa Game Goa Game Raja Game MaanWin LOOKING AT FLAWS PRO WRESTLING NEEDS TO CORRECT THAT ARE LOST IN THE SEA OF ENDLESS PROGRAMMING By Mike Johnson on 2026-10-20 11:27:00 For anyone who loves professional wrestling, being a fan requires putting up with a lot of things that can make your brain implode. Whether it’s an absurd spot that brings time to a standstill, a sequence where communication breaks down, a cartoonish storyline that crosses the line into self-parody, or simply talent on screen you don't enjoy, these frustrations are inherent to the business. Yet, there are concrete steps that promoters and talent can take today to improve the presentation of professional wrestling and restore its physical credibility and narrative integrity, especially as it appears everyone is trapped under the weight and responsibility of producing a ludicrious amount of content per week. Think about this the next time you watch weekly pro wrestling TV: "Does Anybody Really Try to Win a Match Anymore?" There are too many matches today that exist purely to be performative, where a rush of things happening in the ring happen and then we move on to the next match. That isn't to say the athleticism isn't impressive, but the performers are not attempting to actually defeat each other within the context of the show, so the audience waits and reacts to the big spots or the run-in, treating what should be perceived as the meat and potatoes of the show as the parsley on the plate. This isn't news to anyone, but ninety-nine percent of the adult audience knows pro wrestling is a scripted work, but they do not want to be reminded of it. Just like going to a movie where you accept the internal logic of superheroes against supervillains once the lights dim in the theater and the Marvel logo appears, wrestling fans want to immerse themselves in the internal logic of the show once the first bell rings and that's something that needs to be worked on, because everything seems so haphazard in presentation up and down the board. Something as simple as punches need to mean something again. The punch was literally the hallmark for Hulk Hogan and Jerry Lawler in the height of their fame. Instead today, so many matches have that back-and-forth "yay/boo" strike exchange that exists solely to elicit a canned audience response rather than reflecting the logic of a real fight. If punching someone back-and-forth isn't working, a believable fighter would try something else, right? One of the reasons current day WWE's version of AAA works is that when punches are thrown, in most instances, they are meaningful and they are presented like they are weapons being used in battle. It takes time to get those little things back over and I understand in the crunch of production, time is a commodity that isn't offered when your back is against the wall, but at some point, the scales needs to be adjusted or else pro wrestling will one day evolve into looking like
summary: The latest: think about this the next time you watch weekly pro wrestling TV: Does Anybody Really Try to Win a Match Anymore? There are too many matches today that exist purely to be performative. It takes time to get those little things back over and I understand in the crunch of production.

The post-WrestleDream edition of Dynamite on Wednesday is set to feature a first-time team-up involving Will Ospreay and Adam Copeland against Kyle Fletcher and Kevin Knight. The match was teased at the post-show press conference this past Saturday and comes after Ospreay and Copeland were featured in the Clockwork Carnage match. In the final seconds, Ospreay hit Copeland with the Hidden Blade and pinned him to win the match with his third fall. Last week, Copeland announced he would be retiring in 2027, and it was made clear that Ospreay and Copeland are expected to have a match for the title eventually. Ilja Dragunov will be taking on Speedball Mike Bailey in his first match with AEW. Dragunov debuted at WrestleDream, and it was announced he would wrestle on Dynamite. It will be Dragunov’s first match since April, after allowing his WWE contract to expire this past April and awaiting a visa to be processed before his arrival in the new company. Finally, Maya World will return to the ring on Wednesday and is scheduled for a #1 contender’s match against Queen Aminata for a shot at the TBS Championship. Maya World was injured last month after wrestling on the Rebel Heart edition of Dynamite on September 9. Dynamite is scheduled for the Watsco Center in Coral Gables, Florida, with WrestleTix reporting that approximately 3,000 tickets have been distributed .

title: Top Takeaways From Lucha Underground Binge
raw_title: TOP FIVE LIST: Takeaways from bingeing four seasons of Lucha Underground including Penta, Rey Fenix, Ricochet, Inter-gender wrestling
body: Working in my own store that carries a lot of pro wrestling merchandise, I spend all day on Mondays with wrestling on the TV in-store. I will watch something until the start of Raw, then pick it back up the next week. In doing so, I was finally able to complete the entire series, and what a wild series it was. On the first episode, you saw Pentagon Jr. and Rey Fénix. They were never announced as brothers on this show, but there was a unique focus on these two characters. They were both incredible in the ring. The first time I watched years ago, I felt a little bit like I did when first watch Rey Mysterio Jr. arrive in WCW. The way Fénix worked the ropes was so unique. Pentagon had this unique charisma that you could not ignore. They were set up to be key characters, and the people running this show, including Konnan’s eye for talent, knew they had something special in these two. Mil Muertes was a reskinned Judas Masias, who came in as a possessed killer, paired with Catrina who controlled him to do her will. Santos Escobar was under a mask as King Cuerno. A hunter who came in to stalk his prey. I could not believe how mishandled this talent was in WWE after watching him perform in “The Temple.” Ricochet, again under a mask, was Puma, Konnan’s new protege, who was trying his talent against top tier opponents for the first time. My favorite character was Sexy Star. It was very unfortunate that she made the decisions she made to blackball her from a career she was very good at. A woman in an abusive relationship finally decided to stand up for herself, and become a fighter. She was able to fight off her abuser, and in doing so, realized she had everything it took to defeat men in a competitive fight. She even worked her way to being the promotion’s champion for a brief moment. Well-defined background, very good in the ring, and beautiful to attract viewers and look great on posters. Perhaps one of wrestling’s biggest losses, but that was a decision of the performer to deserve her fate of no longer being accepted. I was hesitant to accept this when I first viewed Lucha Underground, but came to not only accept it, but enjoy it. I have previously stated my appreciation for the character of Sexy Star, but I also liked seeing competent women mix it up with men, who were confident in selling offense and even taking clean losses to the women on the roster. In a world where we go to theaters and accept Wonder Woman, Harley Quinn, or Atomic Blonde as viable cinema, why can’t this extend to wrestling? I have often said that Asuka would make me more nervous to fight than many of the men on the roster. That said, I completely understand that corporate WWE will not be entertaining this again any time soon. We had Chyna as the Intercontinental Champion, but that was the exception that won’t be happening again any time soon. I do appreciate seeing AEW dip their toe into that water, and like that it happens in TNA in occasion. I think Lucha Underground should be st
summary: A wrestling merchandise store owner completed all four seasons of Lucha Underground while watching in-store on Mondays ahead of Raw. title: Backstage Buzz: WWE’s Backstage Reaction to Bron Breakker’s Scary Neck Landing Revealed — Report
raw_title: WWE’s Backstage Reaction to Bron Breakker’s Scary Neck Landing Revealed — Report
body: 0 Bron Breakker suffered a scary neck landing during a live event on October 17 in Honolulu, Hawaii. Despite how dangerous the moment looked, the company reportedly wants to move on rather than extend the spotlight on the moment. The incident happened during a six-man tag team match. Breakker teamed up with Bronson Reed and Austin Theory to face Oba Femi, LA Knight, and Penta. During the match, Breakker attempted his usual top-rope Frankensteiner on Knight. However, Knight managed to escape the move, causing Breakker to land awkwardly on his neck . The landing immediately raised concerns, and the referee checked on Breakker. But despite the fall, the former NXT Champion continued wrestling and finished the match. While that was encouraging, the incident still raised questions about his condition. WWE has yet to confirm whether Breakker suffered an injury during the match. During a recent Q&A session, JoeyVotes and TC of WrestleVotes were asked about WWE’s reaction to Breakker’s frightening fall. According to WrestleVotes, officials don’t seem interested in making the incident a major talking point. “People backstage are like, ‘Let’s no-sell this a little bit and hope he’s done,’” WrestleVotes said (H/T: Ringside News ). “I’m sure there were medical personnel checking on him. But at the same time, they want to get over this quickly,” WrestleVotes added. One of the biggest takeaways from the WrestleVotes report is that nobody backstage is reportedly being blamed for what happened. Rather than treating the incident as a major mistake, WrestleVotes described it as an unfortunate accident during a non-televised event. “It was a house show — it was probably a simple sort of mistake. There’s no heat on anybody,” WrestleVotes explained. However, that doesn’t mean the company is ignoring how serious the landing could have been. Breakker’s health remains the main concern. The lack of a public injury announcement also doesn’t confirm he escaped the incident unscathed. For now, there is no clear update on his condition beyond the fact that he finished the match. title: Billy Gunn Calls Triple H's 2019 AEW Jab A Bad Move
raw_title: ‘A D— Move’: Billy Gunn Says Triple H’s 2019 AEW Jab Backfired
body: Skip to content Wrestling News Home » ‘A D— Move’: Billy Gunn Says Triple H’s 2019 AEW Jab Backfired Triple H’s response became one of the most memorable moments of the ceremony. However, Gunn is now offering his perspective on the exchange several years later. Speaking with Kenny McIntosh of Inside The Ropes , Gunn recalled anticipating a remark about AEW during the ceremony. He explained that the promotion was generating considerable interest at the time and that he expected Triple H to address his decision to join the company. “I knew it was coming. I kind of knew they were going to do something AEW because it was hot at the time and I was there and they were all wondering how I got to go there, and that’s because Tony Khan was super cool,” Gunn said. He also explained that AEW owner Tony Khan had supported his decision to attend the Hall of Fame ceremony despite working for a rival promotion. “I went, asked, and he said ‘100%. Of course you can. I would never hold you back from that,’” Gunn recalled. “I didn’t know what they were gonna do, but I knew they were going to do something. I also knew that if they were, Hunter was going to have something to say. Once I set myself up for that, I just let it go,” he explained. Gunn then offered his blunt assessment of the incident, arguing that Triple H was the one who suffered from the exchange. “The only one that got hurt out of that whole deal was him. I don’t want to say it, but it was a d*ck move,” Gunn said. He added that he believed the remark was an attempt to save face, despite there being little need for such a response. “It was kind of trying to save face, and you didn’t need to because it’s going to happen. It’s the wrestling business. It’s what we do. They like to stir up sh*t,” Gunn continued. [H/T Fightful ] During the 2019 WWE Hall of Fame ceremony, fans began chanting “AEW” while D-Generation X delivered its induction speech. Gunn had joked that Vince McMahon could not fire him because he worked for AEW. Triple H responded by saying McMahon would buy the company just to fire Gunn again, referring to AEW as a “pissant company.” The remark drew widespread attention as AEW prepared to launch its weekly television programme, Dynamite, later that year. The promotion subsequently established itself as WWE’s most prominent rival in the North American wrestling market. Gunn joined AEW in 2019, initially working as a coach before becoming a regular on-screen personality. He later teamed with his sons, Austin and Colten Gunn, before joining forces with The Acclaimed. Triple H, meanwhile, eventually took charge of WWE’s creative direction and became the company’s Chief Content Officer in 2022. title: AEW in September 2026 – Which Wrestler Had the Best Month?

body: October 20, 2026 By Corey Michaels AEW , North America , Pro Wrestling School is in session, and the leaves have lost their green. September has come and gone, with the autumnal breeze in full force. For All Elite Wrestling, the month has had many changes. Some amazing, some heartbreaking. AEW had a few special episodes and an incredible AEW All Out 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. September certainly was heavy for the company. That is why I’ve moved the Honorable Mentions from before the list to right after for this month. Grab a slice of Chicago-style deep dish pizza and join me as I recap which wrestlers stood out this month. Over half a month late, here’s who made my list! It’s still Swerve’s House, and his new roommates have made AEW their home remarkably quickly. Perhaps moreso with Kofi, as he acclimates to the AEW territory. Since New Level joined Strickland at AEW All In 2026 at the tail end of August, they’ve showcased an entirely different side to their wrestling style. Their moveset is quicker, and their agility more acrobatic; they’ve adjusted so well that you’d be forgiven for thinking they’d been in AEW for years. Leaving WWE may have been a heavy choice, but Austin and Kofi are making the most of their fresh digs. The triumvirate put their titles on the line at All Out 2026 against the previous holders, Hangman Adam Page and BroDido, in a near-25-minute clash that rivaled the other high-caliber matches at the pay-per-view. Fans were left in complete awe, both in the NOW Arena in Chicago and behind screens. Returning to Kofi, he hasn’t slouched one bit. No resting on laurels here. Having spent most of his life wrestling for WWE, he’s gotten cozy with a different way of performing. For Dragon Ball Z fans, Kofi wrestling under fewer limitations is the equivalent of Goku taking off his weighted clothing. This man stayed getting his reps in, facing Lee Moriarty and Bandido in early October. But that’s a story for another time, perhaps when I review October. Nevertheless, it’s safe to say New Level has found the grass was greener on the other side of the fence. Previously, wrestlers who’ve left WWE either used it as a stepping stone to return or leverage their star power. Thankfully, New Level appears to be in the league of those who believe in the company and want to see it grow. Their chemistry with Swerve is also notable. They’re hilarious together, with Strickland the straight man to New Level’s hilarity. In the same vein, they play the same role juxtaposed to Swerve’s sadistic, vitriolic side. body: The situation is also interesting because Blanchard recently spoke about MLW as if she were preparing for a bigger run with the promotion instead of a one-night appearance. During an interview with TMZ's Inside the Ring , Blanchard stated that she had big plans for the MLW Women's World Championship. MLW initially published an article announcing that Blanchard was joining the promotion and also added her to the company's official roster page. Both listings have since disappeared, leaving her status for this weekend's event unclear. The sudden changes have led to speculation that her MLW debut may no longer be happening. The timing is interesting because CMLL had already caused some confusion about Blanchard's MLW plans. Shortly after MLW announced her debut, the promotion said that September 12 was expected to be her only appearance for the company. According to PWInsider , Blanchard's name has now been removed from the MLW roster page . The announcement saying she was joining the promotion is also no longer available. Mike Johnson of PWInsider wrote that "all signs are that won't be happening." However, MLW has not officially confirmed that the booking is canceled.
