title: On the Record: New Details Emerge About Ex-WWE, AEW Star — PAC Cause of Death
raw_title: PAC Cause of Death: New Details Emerge About Ex-WWE, AEW Star
body: According to California Post's Edward Lewis, Satterley was found "passed out" in a vehicle in a CAVA restaurant parking lot at 4 p.m. on Sunday before being pronounced dead in Des Plaines, IL. When a medical dispatch team arrived at the Mediterranean-themed restaurant, they couldn't confirm if he was breathing, the report added. "This is going to be a slumper," authorities said in the audio. "We can't confirm breathing at this time." "This is going to be a slumper in a car. We cannot confirm breathing yet. At this point, we're still on the phone getting further," added the authorities. Witnesses at CAVA called 911 when they noticed PAC unconscious, even searching for medical equipment to help the wrestler until medics arrived. "There was an ambulance, police and a fire truck, all outside," a witness told The Post. A spokesperson for the Des Plaines Police Department ruled out foul play in the veteran wrestler's death, telling The Post that there were "no indications of foul play and the circumstances surrounding the death are not considered suspicious." A cause of death is pending "additional testing" following an initial autopsy, according to the Cook County Medical Examiner's office. Notably, the CAVA restaurant is located near Chicago O'Hare International Airport, suggesting PAC was preparing for a flight later in the evening. He and his fellow wrestlers had competed the previous night at AEW's All Out pay-per-view at the NOW Arena in Hoffman Estates, Illinois. AEW Stars Pay Tribute to PAC as Fans Speculate on Cause of Death AEW will honor the life and legacy of PAC during Wednesday's "AEW Dynamite," the company's CEO Tony Khan announced on Monday. "I've never met a person who was more beloved by his peers and his friends," Khan said during an ROH taping after a 10-bell salute was held in honor of PAC. "And it was such a pleasure to spend time with Ben outside of wrestling as well, whether it was just having dinner or watching the football match or traveling. "Ben is a very first-class person, and he left behind a lovely wife and a lot of great friends and a legacy that will last forever," added Khan, via F4WOnline. Khan highlighted that the tribute show will be held at the Petersen Events Center in Pittsburgh, the same venue where PAC wrestled in the main event of the fourth-ever episode of "Dynamite" in 2019 against Jon Moxley. "He's somebody I knew would be a big part of the company and somebody that outside of wrestling also became a big part of my life, just like for the wrestlers in the back and so many people around wrestling — Ben has been a huge part of their lives," Khan said. PAC was a part of the original AEW roster in 2019 after spending seven years in WWE. Wrestlers from both promotions have poured in their tributes since his tragic passing. title: The Bloodline Will Destroy 946 at Survivor Series
raw_title: Don't Be Fooled, The Bloodline Will Destroy 946 at WWE Survivor Series
body: NXT Results & Grades 🔠 Bleacher Report 10h Breakker, Dragunov, More Rumors 👂 Bleacher Report 20h Full Grades from Latest Raw Bleacher Report 21h Keys and Co. have been spectacular. They have grabbed the ball and run with it, oftentimes resulting in the best segment of any WWE Raw episode. They have been menacing, physical, and violent when necessary, and have presented a front against The Bloodline that fans can buy into as being legitimate. Keys looks the part of a dominant big man who can stand across the ring from Roman Reigns and throw fists. Nima and Prince may be inexperienced, but they have held up their end of the bargain. Hayes is almost too good to be involved as just another face in a faction, but it has helped lift him out of the creative abyss he found himself in and relocated him to the main event. Then there is Parker, whose on-screen aura is that of a star. She may be the biggest name of the bunch when all is said and done. No, the 946 will be destroyed at Survivor Series because that is the nature of things in WWE. The group has been heated up and introduced to the masses with the sole purpose of ultimately putting the Bloodline over in a high-profile match. No match is more significant to feuding factions than War Games. As if there were not already a perceived hierarchy difference between the two groups, the Bloodline is led by the biggest star in the company, Reigns. The same Reigns who has dominated WWE as the Tribal Chief for the last five years. He rarely loses big matches and is in the midst of his greatest run to date, one that has seen him deliver consistent Match of the Year candidates in his World Heavyweight Championship defenses. With him on what appears to be a collision course with Oba Femi for WrestleMania 43, upper management in the company is going to look to keep Reigns as strong as possible, and that is unlikely to include a War Games loss to a 946 faction that does not currently have clear direction even beyond its feud with Reigns and Co. Add to that a storyline that sets up for at least one big return in the form of former Women's World Champion Naomi, who can confront and take out Parker, and you have a scenario that sets up for the Bloodline to stand tall. The only saving grace for the 946 could be the role of Jacob Fatu. body: Speaking on the latest episode of Talk’n Shop , Anderson and Luke Gallows were discussing one of the biggest differences they noticed between working in WWE and promotions such as NJPW. Anderson said that in Japan, the booker’s decision was generally the decision, since everyone understood they were performing a show with predetermined winners and losers. “And also, you know, in Japan, at least with New Japan Pro Wrestling, and we’ve seen it with Pro Wrestling NOAH again, why it shocked me so much when we went to WWE — the direction from the booker, because this is all a work, right? And who writes the f****** show tells you who’s going to win. It shouldn’t be a f******— it wasn’t like the time when we were supposed to pin Seth Rollins.” Gallows jumped in with a comparison to an actor objecting to something written into a movie. That opened the door for Anderson to explain exactly what he remembered happening with Rollins. “It’s like if Tom Cruise doesn’t want to get hurt in the movie.” Before getting into the story, Anderson made sure there was no confusion about his relationship with Rollins. Both he and Gallows stressed that they’re friends with the former World Heavyweight Champion and weren’t trying to bury him. According to Anderson, WWE’s original direction was pretty straightforward: The Good Brothers were supposed to pin Rollins despite him being World Heavyweight Champion at the time. Even Anderson and Gallows were somewhat surprised by the call, but they were prepared to go along with it. “The direction was Good Brothers pin Rollins. He was the World Heavyweight Champion. Even we were like, ‘All right, whatever.’ And Rollins goes, ‘Really?’ And then he talked to the guy a little bit. He goes, ‘I don’t know. Let me just go talk to Vince. Maybe they’ll figure it out.’” That’s apparently when everything changed. Anderson claimed Rollins went to speak with Vince McMahon and returned with a different finish, one that instead had Rollins pinning Anderson before The Good Brothers attacked him afterwards. “He comes back, and it changed where Rollins rolled me up, and then we beat him down after.” Anderson isn’t pretending that one finish would have completely changed The Good Brothers’ WWE careers. Still, he admitted that pinning the reigning World Heavyweight Champion certainly could have helped them at the time. “It doesn’t matter. It does. title: Latest On Criminal Case Against El Grande Americano, Wwe's Marcel Barthel
raw_title: LATEST ON CRIMINAL CASE AGAINST EL GRANDE AMERICANO, WWE'S MARCEL BARTHEL - PWInsider.com
body: DMFirst Veer Game odds uden om ROFUS Jalwa Game Goa Game Raja Game MaanWin LATEST ON CRIMINAL CASE AGAINST EL GRANDE AMERICANO, WWE'S MARCEL BARTHEL By Mike Johnson on 2026-10-19 18:04:00 There was a hearing earlier today in Orlando, Florida related to the misdemeanor battery charge against WWE star Marcel Barthel aka Ludwig Kaiser aka El Grande Americano before the County Court of the Ninth Judicial Circuit, in and for Orange County, Florida. The hearing was regarding Barthel's motion to dismiss, where Barthel argued for a dismissal on the grounds that Barthel's use of force was legally justified and that he was immune from criminal prosecution under Florida law. Both Barthel and Richard Reap, who filed the charges against him testified at the hearing. At the end of the hearing, Barthel's motion to dismiss was denied with a new pre-trial hearing set for 12/17. Barthel was arrested in May on charges of battery, pleading not guilty after learning of a warrant for his arrest on charges of battery and traveling from Mexico to Florida to turn himself in to authorities. A arrest affidavit stated that Orlando Police responded to an apartment complex (we are not publishing the address) at approximately 6:37 PM on 4/23 following reports of a physical altercation on the 12th floor of the building. The complainant, identified as Richard Reap, told officers that he entered an elevator around 6:30 PM and encountered Barthel alongside an unidentified woman. Reap alleged that the pair were acting in what he described as an “uncontrollably intimate” manner while inside the elevator. Reap stated that after exiting onto the 12th floor, he told the couple to “please have some manners.” According to the affidavit, Reap alleged that Barthel immediately responded by punching him multiple times, pushing him to the ground, and threatening additional violence. Barthel's attorney, in the motion to dismiss, argued that he used only non-deadly force, was lawfully present in the common area of his apartment complex, and reasonably believed his actions were necessary to protect both himself and his girlfriend from imminent unlawful force. The motion emphasizes that Florida law does not require a person in those circumstances to retreat before defending themselves. The filing cites Florida's Stand Your Ground statutes, arguing that Barthel has established a "prima facie" claim of self-defense. Under the cited law, the defense contends the burden now shifts to the State to prove by clear and convincing evidence that Barthel was not entitled to statutory immunity. Since his arrest, Barthel's attorneys filed a motion to secure the video footage from the elevator, which one would think would prove what took place during the incident.
summary: The hearing was regarding Barthel's motion to dismiss, where Barthel argued for a dismissal on the grounds that Barthel's use of force was legally justified and that he was immune. Both Barthel and Richard Reap, who filed the charges against him testified at the hearing.

body: Christopher Daniels discusses tribalism in professional wrestling, noting that he thinks fans should support all pro wrestling. Tribalism in professional wrestling has grown over the last few years, as many fans have taken sides of the ‘AEW vs WWE war’, with heavy criticism being levied by both sides at the other company. While speaking to Going Ringside in a new interview , Christopher Daniels was asked about tribalism, noting his belief that professional wrestling fans should support all pro wrestling. “If you’re a professional wrestler, professional wrestling fan, I think you should support all professional wrestling, and, WWE is, they’re the the oldest game in the in the game, they’re the oldest group in the game. But AEW is coming along strong. AEW is great, and hopefully if you like professional wrestling, AEW presents tremendous professional wrestling week in and week out. So if you’re against that, I don’t know what to tell you. Go watch something else. That’s fine. But we’ve got plenty of fans, and we’re making more fans along the way. And I look forward to showing them professional wrestling each and every week.” If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.

title: The Dogs Opens Up On NSFW Name They Originally Wanted to Use in AEW
raw_title: The Dogs Reveal NSFW Name They Originally Wanted to Use in AEW
summary_src: David Finlay and Clark Connors almost had a very different name when they arrived in AEW. Before settling on simply “The Dogs,” the former War Dogs members wanted to call themselves the “Raw Dogs” — but WWE’s Monday Night Raw apparently made that a little difficult.
body: “Yeah. Too many. Too many. I was the, like, the fifth leader, which is like four too many. So, you know, but the merch was good. So, we were like, ‘Yeah, let’s run with it.’” Finlay described what they eventually did as something of a hostile takeover. They got what they could out of the Bullet Club name before eventually moving on. Things changed once Finlay and Connors made their way to AEW. That’s when they revealed that “The Dogs” actually wasn’t their first choice for a team name. “Well, when we came over here, we just became The Dogs, but we really wanted to pitch the name Raw Dogs. But I think there’s an issue with that whole Monday Night thing.” The obvious reference was WWE’s Monday Night Raw , and Finlay and Connors didn’t suggest they were particularly heartbroken about having to find another option. Still, they definitely liked the way “Raw Dogs” sounded. “But it sounds cool because we’re raw f****** dogs, you know?” That’s how they ultimately landed on the much simpler “The Dogs.” They also like the fact that, despite how obvious the name might sound, it hasn’t really been associated with another major wrestling team before them. “But The Dogs also is a sick name. It’s just no one’s ever done it before. No one’s been The Dogs.” Schiavone agreed that the name could work, especially once AEW keeps using it and viewers become accustomed to hearing Finlay and Connors referred to that way. For him, it’s the kind of name that should become more natural over time. “Yeah. You know, I mean, the more you say it, the more you use it, the more everybody gets used to it, and the more it becomes part of the vernacular of AEW.” Connors couldn’t really argue with that logic. Now that “The Dogs” is what they’re going with, he agreed that repetition should help make the name stick. So “The Dogs” may not have been Finlay and Connors’ original plan, but it looks like it’s here to stay. “Raw Dogs” apparently ran into a pretty obvious wrestling problem before it ever had the chance to make it onto AEW television. TNA Wrestling announced a very special night at the Dothan Civic Center on Tuesday, October 13, to mark the start of the 35 th year of Jeff and Matt Hardy as professional wrestlers. The wrestling legends, aka, The GOATs, have been given full creative control of that night’s show, which will air October 15, as Thursday Night iMPACT! on AMC, per TNA Director of Authority Santino Marella. Every element of the October 13 th show in Dothan will be orchestrated from the minds of Jeff & Matt. They are the matchmakers, will set the surprises and match stipulations, and of course play a huge role themselves in-ring during the evening. The October 13 th TNA show in Dothan will air Thursday, October 15 on AMC. To celebrate this special anniversary night, every fan in attendance is encouraged to dress like Jeff or Matt from any era of their historic careers. The two best-dressed fans – one as Matt, one as Jeff – will be crowned the winners and be the first in line for the post-show meet and greet with the real Hardys. A special commemorative photo – of The Hardys and The Hardy Look-Alikes – will be taken and featured on TNA’s social media outlets and the TNA website. Special Hardy merchandise will be available exclusively at the Dothan shows to honor the Hardys’ 35 th year. The Hardys have held countless championships during their illustrious careers, which began on October 15, 1992, in North Carolina. They are recognised by fans, peers and media as the greatest tag team in professional wrestling history and are the only duo to have held the WWE/World, WCW, TNA, ROH, Raw and SmackDown Tag Team Championships. TNA will be hosting live events at the Dothan Civic Center on back-to-back nights – Tuesday & Wednesday, October 13–14 – to be broadcast as episodes of Thursday Night iMPACT! on AMC and AMC+ in the U.S., Sportsnet 360 in Canada and TNA+ worldwide. This is TNA’s first live events in Dothan, Alabama in more than a decade and the first-ever TNA television tapings there. Other TNA stars confirmed to appear in Dothan include Cedric Alexander, Moose, Brian Myers, Eddie Edwards, KC Navarro, Joe Alonzo, Fabian Aichner, Avery Styles, Ricky Sosa, Elijah, Frankie Kazarian, Mila Moore, Harley Hudson and Zoey Serrano, among others.

title: Comeback Watch: Taylor Wilde Was Supposed To Win Knockouts World Title During TNA/IMPACT Comeback Run
raw_title: Taylor Wilde Was Supposed To Win Knockouts World Title During TNA/IMPACT Comeback Run
body: It was in 2021 that former TNA Knockouts Champion Taylor Wilde returned to then-IMPACT Wrestling. She had been away from wrestling since 2011. Purrazzo shared that without Scott D’Amore being aware, Lucha Libre AAA threw her into a title-versus-title bout that she would be winning and went on to become Reina de Reinas Champion. Purrazzo said the match against Wilde was supposed to happen at Slammiversary that year. At the 2021 Slammiversary, Purrazzo had a mystery opponent, and it was revealed to be Thunder Rosa. Wilde had no clue about any of these plans. Purrazzo: “I remember — I don’t even know if we’ve talked about this beforehand. You were coming back and you were challenging me and I was also going to Mexico for AAA, and Mexico had sprung on me that it was gonna be the Reina de Reinas Title versus the Knockouts Championship and winner-take-all, and Scott (D’Amore) didn’t know that. So we’re working towards a program, me and you at Slammiversary, where you are going to become the Knockouts Champion and now AAA has put this stipulation on a match that no one agreed to, and I remember being like — to the writers — ‘Hey, I’m so happy to go to AAA and do this match but if you want Shantelle to win, by all means. She can go to Mexico and have that match.’ I don’t want to say I have to be the champion for this, because it threw a wrench in everyone’s plans and so, not to say that about myself as like, I’m such a good person but I think it was a really great example of the time and the space that the locker room had and the respect we had for each other, and respect for you coming in as a veteran in our locker room.” Wilde has not wrestled since 2023. During her last run, she captured the Knockouts World Tag Team Titles with KiLynn King.

Purrazzo said AAA unexpectedly booked her into a title-versus-title bout for the Reina de Reinas Championship without Scott D’Amore's knowledge, which altered the plans. Wilde had no idea about the original program or the AAA stipulation.

llm_long: Taylor Wilde returned to IMPACT Wrestling in 2021 after being away from the ring since 2011. During this period, she was set to challenge for the Knockouts Championship.

Deonna Purrazzo revealed that Lucha Libre AAA had scheduled a title-versus-title match for her without the knowledge of TNA's Scott D'Amore. The plan called for Purrazzo to win the bout and become the Reina de Reinas Champion.
The scheduled match between Purrazzo and Wilde was planned for Slammiversary in 2021. Instead, Purrazzo faced a mystery opponent at the event, who turned out to be Thunder Rosa.

Wilde was unaware of the AAA stipulation that had been added to the planned program. Purrazzo expressed willingness to let Wilde win the match and travel to Mexico for the Reina de Reinas Championship bout if that was preferred.
The situation highlighted the respect within the locker room at the time. Purrazzo noted it showed consideration for Wilde as a veteran returning to the promotion.
Wilde has not wrestled since 2023. In her final run with the company, she held the Knockouts World Tag Team Titles alongside KiLynn King.

body: Upon Ilja Dragunov’s in-ring debut for All Elite Wrestling, he spoke to TMZ’s Inside The Ring podcas t. During the chat, he stated that he thinks he sticks out on the AEW roster and that he’s always betting on himself. “I didn’t consider how stacked the roster is because it’s a fear I don’t have. I was always betting on myself. I bet on myself when I left WWE. I’m betting on myself still, and I’m betting on what my gut is telling me and the way the people, the company introduced me, I think it speaks for itself that I stick out from all the rest on that roster. People who stick out and are not like anybody else, you kind of put the objective on them and only if you are like everybody else or try to be like everybody else — which is also like an unfortunate thing happening nowadays, unfortunately — then you get overlooked. But, I haven’t been overlooked once in my 14 years of career.” Dragunov’s first match will be against ‘Speedball’ Mike Bailey on the 10/21 Dynamite.

title: Fans Urged to Support Ilja Dragunov

Every time Ilja Dragonuv wasn't utilized by World Wrestling Entertainment, the online discourse was the same - where is he? Why isn't he being utilized? Why isn't be on TV? Why isn't he getting pushed? The Russian-born German star has been beloved for his unhinged intensity, stiff striking, and emotionally charged physical storytelling. The "Unbesiegbar" (Unbeatable) Mad Dragon, Dragunov gained international acclaim before signing with WWE, where captured the WWE NXT UK Championship by ending GUNTHER's insane 870-day reign with an instant classic. He moved to the United States, where he held the WWE NXT title and eventually, the main roster, where he won the WWE United States Championship. Recognized for his intense in-ring style, marked by his signature Torpedo Moskva flying headbutt and H-Bomb forearm strike, Dragonuv excels at believable, hard-hitting encounters and dramatic, resilient selling that position him as one of the most physical performers in modern professional wrestling. He was the exact style of performer that Paul Levesque's NXT popularized themselves utilizing, so it was was unthinkable that under Levesque's creative direction that Dragonuv wouldn't be a massive part of WWE, yet it didn't truly happen. An ACL tear hobbed his momentum for sure, but his return was well received, as was his U.S. title run. However, once 2026 began, other than being unceremoniously tossed from The Royal Rumble by Brock Lesnar, there was nothing truly memorable for Ilja creatively and then, he chose to exit the company. The outpouring of shock and anger over the exit was palapable, to the point I even received emailed accusing me of lying when PWInsider.com broke the news of his exit. No matter how you feel about Dragonuv's run in WWE, the one constant was that die-hard wrestling fans loved his work and loudly complained online when he wasn't utilized in a stronger manner. If they truly believe WWE whiffed the ball on Dragnonuv, those same fans will get the chance to see him step up to bat tonight for All Elite Wrestling on Dynamite. As famously stated in Field of Dreams, "If you build it, they will come." Well, Tony Khan built his ballfield and now Dragonuv has been invited to join the team...but will the fans who championed him and blamed WWE for Dragonuv's main roster run falling flat actually take that negative feedback, flip the hourglass and go cheer on Ilja in his new environment? If they don't, every single person who lamented that the main roster machine was sanding down Dragonuv's violent edges should be ashamed of themselves. This is the first episode of Dynamite during the four week build to Full Gear, which takes place on November 14. One of the big stories at WrestleDream was the reveal that former WWE star Ilja Dragunov is officially All Elite. In the post-show media scrum, the Mad Dragon uttered these words: “Now I am here, and this is gonna be a serious problem for so many people.” Every wrestler on the AEW roster has good reason to be nervous after hearing those words, because Dragunov has a unique intensity and violence to the way he wrestles that ensures physical torture for anyone he steps in the ring with. “Speedball” Mike Bailey gets to experience it first, because he is the unlucky star who is fighting Dragunov tonight in his debut match for AEW. Meanwhile, Ospreay is eager to team with Cope here, but the retiring Copeland wants to take that AEW world title away from the Aerial Assassin. title: Jaxson Ryker details severe injuries after WWE exit
raw_title: Former WWE star reveals ‘excruciating pain’ after release and lower back injury that caused arm numbness
summary_src: Former WWE star Jaxson Ryker opened up about his decision to step away from wrestling, revealing the persistent injuries and body aches that contributed to it. Ryker emphasized the toll of wrestling on his body following his WWE release in 2021.
body: Former WWE star Jaxson Ryker opened up about his decision to step away from wrestling, revealing the persistent injuries and body aches that contributed to it. Ryker emphasized the toll of wrestling on his body following his WWE release in 2021. In his interview with Developmentally Speaking, the former WWE star revisited his decision to retire in 2023, reflecting on his brief return to the independent wrestling scene before ultimately calling it quits for good. “No, I think I had in the back of my mind that it was time to start maybe pursuing other things. My body, when I got released from WWE, my body was hurting real bad. I’d had a neck injury and a lower-back injury that was causing some numbness in my arm and my hand,” said Ryker. “Just really, really excruciating pain for the most part. I always told myself years ago if I got to where I didn’t enjoy it anymore or my body hurt really bad, I would walk away on my own. I didn’t want to be 50 and crippled. And so when that happened I was like, ‘Okay, well, let’s just do an independent run. I could go all over these places. I’ve worked for NWA and that’s basically what I did for the, I took three, four months off after they released me.” He expressed no interest in stepping foot in the ring again despite being approached to do so. “I’ve had people call me, buddies of mine, promoters, ‘Hey, man, would you consider one more match?’” And I am so content in my retirement life. ’Cause my body feels 100 times better, you know. I don’t ache and moan and groan anymore as much as I used to. The wrestling business changed for me. And I think my views in life changed. What was important to me changed. And so it was, no. I sat back and I was like, ‘Dude, I’ve given 23 years of my life to pro wrestling. I’ve escaped with, I mean, I’ve had broken fingers and nose and stuff, but never broken a neck or anything crazy.’ And I was like, ‘I’ve had a blessed career, and I’ve got to do a lot, a lot of stuff that a lot of guys never get to or never will get to do.’” Ryker signed with WWE in 2021 and made his main roster debut in 2020 as part of The Forgotten Sons. After the stable disbanded, Ryker was briefly paired with Elias until their alliance imploded and ultimately led to a singles rivalry before his WWE release. body: Dave Meltzer seemed to confirm during a recent Wrestling Observer Radio that he's had word from inside WWE on The Bloodline vs. The 946 at Survivor Series. What's more, both groups will do battle inside the iconic WarGames double cage and double ring structure on 28 November. This is one of wrestling's worst kept secrets heading into the final few months of 2026. The Bloodline has been warring with the newer 946 faction for a while now, and things have been steadily building towards WarGames . Initially, Roman Reigns looked like he was staying out of the rivalry whilst the Royce Keys-led 946 battled family like The Usos and Jacob Fatu, but he's since been sucked into the story. That was expected, and so was Solo Sikoa rejoining the faction ahead of Survivor Series. At time of writing, both sides only have 4 members each. Well, The Bloodline technically also boasts Fatu, but he's on the bench selling Jaida Parker running him down with her car recently . On The 946 side, they have Keys, Bronco Nima, Lucien Price and Carmelo Hayes, so the heels will need to find another member if this is going to be 5v5. That is, of course, unless Parker is going to be involved. She might stick her nose in at some point during the match, but is unlikely to be an official participant. Reigns has been part of all but one of the WarGames set pieces since Triple H debuted the iconic gimmick on the main roster in 2022 . The 'OTC' didn't work inside the double cage in 2023, but has been a staple of the match type since. body: Billy Gunn was one of the first signings in AEW, originally signed to work as a coach and producer, but he did end up in the ring. Speaking to Kenny McIntosh of Inside The Ropes , Gunn revealed his original AEW talent contract. “My contract, I had 12 dates a year. I really wasn’t going to wrestle, but I told Tony, ‘If you need me to, I’ll do it here and there.’ I still had a talent contract and employee contract. I was mostly producing and coaching. The talent one was little because (I wasn’t sure) if I would even fill those dates. Lo and behold. They cracked me out and I’m working both shows and working all the time, about to fall apart,” he said. Gunn had 23 matches for AEW in 2020 and 34 matches in 2021. He has not wrestled for AEW since January 2026. If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.

llm_long: Billy Gunn has been part of All Elite Wrestling since 2020. He insisted that his sons Austin and Colten complete their college education before pursuing careers in the promotion.
Gunn stated that he refused to help get his sons hired by AEW until they graduated. He emphasized that his own success in wrestling did not guarantee they would succeed in the same field.

On the day Austin Gunn graduated, he handed his diploma to his father and immediately asked when they could start in wrestling. Gunn had required college graduation as the first condition before any discussion of entering the business.
Colten Gunn also decided to pursue wrestling after having a different career path mapped out until age 60. The choice surprised both Gunn and his wife, given the demanding nature of the profession.

Gunn explained that his frequent absences from home, including 300 days on the road each year early in his career, made him hesitant for his sons to follow the same path. He wanted them to have more stable family lives than he experienced.
Although Gunn trained his sons to a certain point, he required them to seek and complete AEW tryouts on their own. He did not ask for them to be hired simply because they were his children.

title: Ilja Dragunov Calls Emotional Expression Wrestling's Toughest Element
raw_title: Ilja Dragunov Says That The Expressive Part Of Wrestling Is 'The Real Exhausting Part'
summary_src: Ilja Dragunov says that the expressive part of wrestling is 'the real exhausting part' of the industry noting that it is harder than moves.
body: Ilja Dragunov says that the expressive part of wrestling is ‘the real exhausting part’ of the industry noting that it is harder than moves. Dragunov is a performer who has never shied away from being expressive in his pro wrestling career, and it is a part of his all round package that fans commonly point to when discussing his abilities in the wrestling industry. “It is definitely the part of expressing yourself. It is the vocality. It is the expressions. This part of portraying what you’re doing is at times much harder than any move that you can do. Like this pressure that your body handles. You’re screaming out when you punch, when you get hit. You constantly focus to include the audience, to have this roundabout vision at all times, it is extremely exhausting, and also, it’s not just comes down to what’s the next cool looking thing that I can do. It’s like, how do I handle what happened right now to me? How does it change me as a person during this beautiful fight that I’m expressing, during this play with my opponent? That’s the real exhausting part, and it’s physically exhausting.” If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.

body: Ric Flair appreciates the generosity Tony Khan has shown him during their friendship. Since 2023, Flair has been under contract with AEW despite only making very rare appearances for the company. He originally debuted as part of Sting’s retirement tour and with a sponsorship deal for his “Wooooo! Energy” drink. That sponsorship is no longer in place, but Flair remains with AEW. He praised Khan in an interview with Biff Poggi of NewsNation, saying he believes Khan still takes care of him out of respect. “He’s a nice guy, he’s generous. I work for him, and I don’t do anything,” Flair said about Khan. “I think he takes care of me out of respect for me. He grew up on me. He’s just a wonderful guy. It’s not that the guys at the WWE — I just think they’re all kind of hanging onto their job, because you never know. [WWE has] fired so many people that were an intricate part of my career when I was there. I don’t understand the rhyme or reason for it. Some of the people — the guys that did my documentary on Peacock, two of the guys that did it have been fired.” “I think Nick Khan is pretty much the boss over there, but at the same time, I don’t know how much power Nick Khan has. He used to be the man,” Flair said. “But, you know, Hunter is the booker now, or the head of creative they call it.” Flair, 77, believes the only thing separating WWE and AEW at this point is the fact that WWE has existed for so much longer. He is impressed by Khan’s ability as a promoter and thinks Khan could be the greatest promoter of all time. “It’s internal. I don’t know who makes the final decision,” Flair responded when asked generally about who makes the political decisions in wrestling. “With Tony Khan, who runs AEW, who is really one of the most wonderful people I’ve ever known, Tony has a group of people, which I’m sure they do at WWE, that he circles up with. And Tony does it right there. Tony Khan may be the greatest promoter of all time.” Poggi asked if Flair meant Khan could be the greatest wrestling promoter or the greatest promoter in any industry. title: RVD Claims WWE Wrestlers Feared for Their Jobs Unlike in AEW
raw_title: RVD Claims WWE Wrestlers Feared for Their Jobs Unlike in AEW
summary_src: RVD believes AEW gives its wrestlers something he didn’t always see during his years in WWE — the freedom to speak up and express themselves.
body: “Yeah. They’ve definitely proven themselves. You know, like, it was so easy when they first came out to be like, ‘Yeah, well, let’s see how long they stick around.’ And I don’t think there’s anything wrong with any of us that felt that way because promotions over the years come up all the time.” RVD admitted he’d seen plenty of companies arrive with serious financial backing and promises of becoming the next big thing, only for them to eventually disappear. AEW has managed to get past that stage, and he believes the company has established itself as a legitimate alternative. “‘Oh, they got Major League Baseball money. This shit’s for real,’ and they got this and that, and it never lasts. And those guys, you know, really fill the void, and so it’s cool. Congrats to AEW, and they’re just going to keep growing.” Van Dam also pays attention to what wrestling fans tell him they’re actually watching. From those conversations, he’s noticed plenty of people aren’t exclusively choosing WWE or AEW and instead follow both companies. “You know, I always check with the fans and ask what they watch, and a lot of people are watching both products. I don’t know how much international distribution they have, but obviously they must be on in the places that they’re going to, at least.” That’s when RVD got into what he believes separates the two promotions. To him, AEW still comes across as a company where the wrestlers themselves have a bigger hand in what they’re doing. “But yeah, pretty cool. And it still — and I think always will — be coming across as, and I think for valid reasons, the boys being the ones that are kind of running the show more.” His description of WWE was much different. RVD claimed there were wrestlers who feared losing their jobs, which could make them reluctant to question directions or push back against something they were being told to do. “You know, whereas WWE was like a lot of people afraid for their job and doing whatever they’re told, and sometimes afraid to go against it or say the wrong thing or whatever.” By comparison, RVD believes AEW gives its wrestlers more room to show what they can do on their own terms. That’s a big part of why the promotion feels more wrestler-driven to him. “And this seems more like guys that want to be out there expressing themselves with their talent and doing it their way.” RVD isn’t claiming every wrestler’s experience in either company is the same, but his own impression of the two environments is pretty clear. After watching AEW survive the early skepticism, he sees its wrestler-driven approach as one of the things that continues to separate it from the WWE environment he remembers. body: Mysterio is one of five WWE Superstars who will be included in the WWE 2K26 x Street Fighter Elite DLC Pack, which features wrestlers playing the roles of Street Fighter characters. Dom is cast as Ken, and he's joined by Rey Mysterio as Ryu, Bianca Belair as Cammy, The Rock as M. Bison and Ultimate Warrior as Blanka. "I've been in a couple of 2K games with WWE the past couple years now, but this is special," Mysterio said. "It's Street Fighter, it's not only a DLC pack that you have to pre-order and get separately, but also they made it an action figure. I have a couple at the house, and it's in, like, an old arcade-style box, and they're super cool. I have a couple in my game room, and it's just cool to be a part of the whole Street Fighter franchise." Dirty Dom revealed that he wasn't told about the Ken action figure ahead of time and didn't know about it until he saw photos. At that point, he instantly wanted to get one in his possession. "I didn't know until I started getting tagged in the pictures of me as Ken, and I was like, 'What is going on? Did someone make this custom, or like, what is it,'" Mysterio said. "And then the company ended up telling me, like, 'Oh no, you're part of this DLC pack in 2K26.' And I was like, 'What? This is so sick.' I found out kind of like the old-fashioned way where I just kept getting tagged. And then as soon as I saw it, I was like, 'How do I get my hands on this action figure?'" Ken has long been among the most popular characters in the Street Fighter video game franchise, which first launched in 1987 and truly rose to prominence with the release of Street Fighter II in 1991. Dominik feels he and Ken have some similarities, noting that Ken's bio describes him as a fighter who comes to the United States to "get humbled because he's too cocky." Dom also acknowledged that both he and Ken have luscious heads of hair, quipping that he may have to "golden up the tips of the good old mullet" at some point in order to match Ken. Fittingly, Mysterio likes to play the Street Fighter video game series with some of his fellow WWE Superstars, and Ken is his character of choice when his back is against the wall in a "glass break in case of emergency" situation since he knows how to do all of his combos. Upon discovering the figure, Dominik immediately wanted to obtain one for himself. He found out about the project in an old-fashioned way through social media tags before official notification.

Ken is one of the most popular characters in the Street Fighter franchise, which began in 1987 and gained major popularity with Street Fighter II in 1991. Dominik noted similarities between himself and Ken, including a bio that describes the character as a cocky fighter who travels to the United States to be humbled.

title: On the Record: Ilja Dragunov Says He Needs To Wrestle In Japan: 'That’s The Place Where I Think My Style Belongs'
raw_title: Ilja Dragunov Says He Needs To Wrestle In Japan: 'That’s The Place Where I Think My Style Belongs'
body: There’s a slight chance that we’ll see Ilja Dragunov wrestle in Japan in the future. At AEW WrestleDream, Ilja Dragunov made his highly anticipated debut in All Elite Wrestling. Dragunov previously worked for WWE, where he had many incredible matches. Despite being popular with fans, WWE didn’t seem to have much planned for him on television. In the end, Dragunov declined WWE’s offer for a new contract and became a free agent. He later signed with AEW and is currently scheduled to make his in-ring debut for the company on the October 21 edition of AEW Dynamite. TMZ’s Inside the Ring recently spoke with Dragunov, where the wrestler was asked about wrestlers he’d like to work with outside AEW. Dragunov didn’t have an answer for that, but he did mention one of the places he’d like to have a match: Japan. Dragunov believes his style of wrestling belongs there. “I wouldn’t say it’s necessarily who I want to work with, but where I want to work. Back in the day when I started with wXw, they had a working relationship with Big Japan Pro Wrestling. And when I joined wXw, it’s kind of like this time was passed. And the one thing that I didn’t do in my career so far, multiple things that I didn’t do in my career so far, but specifically something that I need to do is to wrestle in Japan. I need to wrestle in Japan. Because that’s the place where I think my style belongs, and I think I would connect with the people, with this culture for professional wrestling in a whole different way.” Dragunov has never worked for a Japanese promotion before, but with AEW’s partnership with New Japan Pro Wrestling, this could change in the future. AEW wrestlers frequently work New Japan’s shows, and seeing Dragunov wrestle someone like Zack Sabre Jr. or compete in the G1 Climax would be an incredible experience for the fans. title: On the Record: WWE Accused of “Dropping the Ball” on Ilja Dragunov After AEW Debut
raw_title: WWE Accused of “Dropping the Ball” on Ilja Dragunov After AEW Debut
summary_src: Ilja Dragunov has barely gotten started in AEW, and Jonathan Coachman is already wondering how WWE let this one get away. After watching Dragunov’s WrestleDream debut, Coachman and JD both came away believing WWE could have done a whole lot more with him.
body: Speaking on 2 Count Tuesday , JD said Dragunov’s AEW presentation was even better than he expected. Everything from the music to his look screamed top star to him, and he thinks Dragunov could eventually follow the same path Swerve Strickland did. “If they take Dragunov, I look at it more like a Swerve Strickland. When Swerve came in, it took him a little bit of time to find his footing, and he eventually became a world champion.” JD doesn’t just see Dragunov as someone who could have a nice run in AEW either. He thinks there’s legitimate World Champion potential there, and possibly even someone who could eventually become one of the faces of the company. “I think if they let Dragunov be Dragunov, I think he could be a world champion just like Swerve was, and he can be an ace for that company. That’s how high I think of Dragunov.” “I don’t know why WWE would let him go. I don’t know why WWE dropped the ball on him. I don’t know why they didn’t give him the resources to be a top guy. He’s got top-guy potential, and he’s top-guy shit.” Coachman jumped right on that point, and he put a lot of the responsibility on WWE creative. He wants to know what was actually being written for someone like Dragunov before his run with the company came to an end. “Yeah, it’s that last question — you’ve got to give creative. And this is why I’ve been calling for creative to be called on the carpet, is walk in and show me what you have written. Show me what you have done, because a guy like that, you’ve got to give him creative.” “I’m so tired of hearing people — whether it’s Tony… Oh, they got to — well, Tony doesn’t say it, but Triple H does — ‘He’s got to get himself over. He’s got to get herself over.’” For Coachman, WrestleDream was a pretty good example of what he’s talking about. Dragunov already looks and sounds like a star, so he doesn’t think AEW needs to make every appearance another 15- or 20-minute match just to prove how good he is. “And last night, you talked about the presentation — or at WrestleDream — when you look like a star, sound like a star, and then you go out there and have not 15- or 20-minute matches every time. Make it — change it up just a little bit.” Instead, Coachman wants AEW to keep finding different ways to showcase him. That’s where he believes creative needs to earn its money instead of expecting Dragunov to figure everything out by himself. “Present him differently all the way. But this is where creative’s got to step up, and they’ve got to step up for him.” It’s way too early to know whether Dragunov actually becomes the kind of AEW star JD thinks he can be. But after one presentation, they’re already asking the question WWE probably doesn’t want to hear — did the company let a future top guy walk right out the door? title: Double Champ Bandido Headlines AEW Dynamite At Coral Gables' Watsco Center
raw_title: Double Champ Bandido Headlines AEW Dynamite At Coral Gables' Watsco Center
body: Source: Photos N Effect / Wikimedia Commons A masked luchador carrying two championships into the building will headline AEW Dynamite live from the Watsco Center at the University of Miami on Wednesday, with the show airing on TBS and streaming on HBO Max. Bandido, the current Ring of Honor World Champion, arrives in Coral Gables as one of the promotion's most decorated active stars, known for blending high-flying lucha libre with hard-hitting power moves. According to the Miami Herald , Bandido also recently teamed with Brody King and Adam “Hangman” Page to capture the AEW Trios Titles, defeating Swerve Strickland and New Level, Austin Creed and Kofi, in a best-two-of-three-falls match. That victory makes him a double champion heading into Wednesday's taping, pairing his individual Ring of Honor reign with group gold won alongside two of AEW's biggest names. Bandido's path back to the top of Ring of Honor has been anything but simple. He first won the ROH World Championship on July 11, 2021, defeating Rush at Best in the World, only to vacate the title five months later in December 2021 after testing positive for COVID-19, according to Fightful . He recaptured the title in April 2025 by defeating veteran Chris Jericho in a Title vs. Mask match at AEW Dynasty, a notable reversal since Jericho had beaten Bandido during the luchador's AEW debut back in September 2022. That current reign has now stretched more than 560 days, the second longest in the title's history, and the Herald notes that Bandido has held the ROH World Championship across his two reigns for more combined days than anyone else. Outside of Ring of Honor and AEW, Bandido has also wrestled for CMLL and New Japan Pro Wrestling, and he has been recognized by ESPN as one of the 30 best pro wrestlers under 30 and ranked No. 11 among the top 500 wrestlers in the world by Pro Wrestling Illustrated. In accordance with Mexican lucha libre tradition, Bandido's real identity has never been revealed; he is a fourth-generation luchador whose younger brother competes professionally under the ring name Gravity, according to Wikipedia . Bandido's run with Brody King didn't start with trios. The pair formed the tag team Brodido in the summer of 2025 and won the AEW World Tag Team Championship before losing the titles that November. The trio expanded over the summer of 2026, when Bandido, King and Page won the AEW World Trios Championship at Arena Mexico in Mexico City, only to drop the titles to Swerve Strickland and the New Level at AEW All In: London, held at Wembley Stadium. Wednesday's Coral Gables taping comes just four days after AEW's 2026 WrestleDream pay-per-view at the Addition Financial Arena at the University of Central Florida in Orlando, underscoring how aggressively the promotion has toured Florida this autumn. The Coral Gables show functions as much as a television production as a live event. AEW produces four hours of programming across two weekly shows, with Dynamite airing on TBS

Bandido, the current Ring of Honor World Champion, arrives in Coral Gables as one of the promotion's most decorated active stars.

title: On the Record: Cody Rhodes Explains Why He Doesn’t Get Defensive When Wrestling Is Called “Fake”
raw_title: Cody Rhodes Explains Why He Doesn’t Get Defensive When Wrestling Is Called “Fake”
summary_src: Cody Rhodes has seen plenty of wrestlers get fired up when someone calls professional wrestling “fake,” but that’s not a fight he’s interested in having.
body: The topic came up as Cody was explaining kayfabe to Andrew Schulz and how difficult it can sometimes be for people outside the wrestling world to understand where the performance ends and reality begins. He’s seen interviews take a turn pretty quickly once someone drops what he jokingly called the “F-word.” “I’ve seen several times when you can tell a wrestler instantly — especially when it’s a split-screen interview — when somebody drops the F-word in there, and then a wrestler will be like, ‘Well, I broke my neck.’” Cody understands why wrestlers react that way, especially considering the very real physical toll that comes with the job. It’s just not the approach he personally likes to take when someone questions wrestling’s legitimacy. Instead, Cody takes what he described as a softer approach. He doesn’t need to argue about whether the match itself is “real” when the emotions fans experience watching it absolutely are. “I typically take a softer approach to the feeling you have when you come to an event is a real feeling. It’s a real feeling, man. And that’s usually why I don’t ever use the F-word in that regard.” There’s another reason Cody doesn’t like getting defensive about it. Once a wrestler gets hung up on proving wrestling isn’t fake, he thinks the actual interview can quickly grind to a halt. “But also, that’s where wrestling interviews sometimes can go to die.” When the host suggested that wrestlers sometimes just need to let the subject go, Cody agreed. Getting dragged into an argument isn’t going to accomplish much if it kills the rest of the conversation: “You got to let it go.” “Yeah. Like, you remember when Tyson got interviewed and all of a sudden called that guy a rat? Do you remember that?” After watching the Tyson clip, Cody came back to his own philosophy. He’d rather keep his cool and, if the opportunity presents itself, drop a good wrestling sound bite without letting the entire interview turn into an argument. “Yeah. But it did — that’s again where a lot of wrestling interviews can go to die. I always just, you know, try and keep the composure. If there’s an opening to put my little sound bite in there, great.” Cody isn’t trying to convince every skeptic that wrestling is something it isn’t. For him, the better argument is what fans actually feel when they’re watching it, and he’d rather let that speak for itself than turn an interview into a debate over the word “fake.” Subhojeet Mukherjee Subhojeet Mukherjee has covered pro wrestling for over 20 years, delivering trusted news and backstage updates to fans around the world.

title: Cody Rhodes Claims 99.9% of Wrestlers Don’t Want to Give Up Their Spot
raw_title: Cody Rhodes Claims 99.9% of Wrestlers Don’t Want to Give Up Their Spot
summary_src: Cody Rhodes believes John Cena’s final WWE run could end up being remembered for something much bigger than wins, losses or championships. In Cody’s eyes, Cena spent an entire year doing everything he could to elevate other wrestlers instead of choosing just one person to pass the torch to.
body: Speaking to Andrew Schulz , Cody discussed the difference between simply losing to another wrestler and truly putting that person over. Cody described it as the difference between “doing the job” and “doing the honors,” with the latter involving an established star doing everything possible to make the moment belong to the wrestler they’re elevating. “I think John probably will go down because he spent an entire year doing the honors. He didn’t just pick one.” Schulz pointed out that Cena essentially took a bet on several different wrestlers during that run. Cody agreed, stressing that Cena did much more than simply agree to take a loss and move on. “Yeah, he took a bet on a few, you know. He definitely did more than just doing the favor.” For Cody, that’s the big difference between simply “doing the job” and actually giving someone the full spotlight. He believes Cena understood exactly how to make those moments matter for the wrestlers he was working with. “It was — he did the honors, and that’s the way you want to do it.” Cena wasn’t the only veteran Cody gave credit to. When Schulz asked for other examples of wrestlers who knew how to give back, Cody quickly pointed toward Triple H and The Undertaker. “Oh man, I mean, you mentioned Triple H. Triple H is a great example. Gosh, all — probably all your faves. The Undertaker.” Cody also admitted there’s naturally some selfishness involved when it comes to eventually giving up a spot. Wrestlers can spend years fighting to reach a certain level, so he understands why they might not exactly be eager to let it go. “Yeah. Great. You know, like, you know, and sometimes there’s a selfishness to it as well because you go so long until it’s time.” “I’d say 99.9% of wrestlers perhaps don’t want to let go. And it’s when you have—” “I am not going to get into Wrestling with Shadows with you, but you know what?” Cody’s larger point was that truly putting someone over involves a lot more than simply losing a match. That’s why Cena stands out so much to him — Cody believes his final run was an extended effort to give several wrestlers something meaningful rather than making his farewell all about himself. title: WWE's Worst Storyline Has Ruined The Judgment Day
raw_title: WWE's Worst Storyline Has Ruined The Judgment Day
body: The size of JD McDonagh’s head has been a minor joke in WWE for many years, being used as an easy jibe here and there. In 2026, it was made the subject of an entire storyline. Babyfaces such as Joe Hendry and JD McDonagh have taken aim at both McDonagh and Dominik Mysterio of The Judgment Day, resulting in a truly awful attempt at a “comedic” storyline from WWE. For several weeks, babyfaces have been bringing out people dressed as giant Funko Pops, with it being asserted that McDonagh is the offspring of one of these figures. WWE’s handling of The Judgment Day in 2026 has killed the group forever, especially for those in the men’s division. Dominik Mysterio began the year as both Intercontinental & AAA Mega Champion, but has since lost both championships, come up short in his feud with Finn Balor, feuded with Danhausen for six months in a feud that ended in a remarkably bad “Human Monies On A Pole” match at SummerSlam , and then began teaming with McDonagh in their various battles against Funko Pop-obsessed babyfaces. It hasn’t just been a poor year for Mysterio & McDonagh. Liv Morgan might’ve spent much of 2026 as Women’s World Champion , but her reign with the belt was one of the worst in recent memory. She has hardly any defenses, served mostly as a manager and cheerleader for her stablemates, and had no memorable feuds to shout about. Additionally, Judgment Day’s bad luck continued as Money In The Bank favorite, Roxanne Perez, had plans for her to win changed ahead of the show , leading to a frustrating defeat. Triple H has done far too much damage to this once great group. Fans have been begging for some time for members of The Judgment Day to go their separate ways, especially with how badly 2026 has gone. Triple H needs to end the faction in order to save the individual careers of everyone involved. Mysterio & Morgan no longer generate the same level of heat they once did, the slow-burn breakup of the women’s division members of the group has gone beyond the point of fans caring about it, and overall there is a lack of interest in anything the faction does. The Judgment Day has been on the ropes for a while, but this recent Funko Pop travesty is the ultimate nail in the coffin.

title: Legal Watch: WWE, Vince and Linda McMahon Lose Bid To Dismiss Sexual Abuse Lawsuit
raw_title: WWE, Vince and Linda McMahon Lose Bid To Dismiss Sexual Abuse Lawsuit
body: 0 A federal judge on Monday rejected WWE, TKO, Vince , and Linda McMahon’s effort to have the ring boy sexual assault lawsuit dismissed. Eight anonymous plaintiffs filed the lawsuit in 2024. They claim they were sexually abused in the 1980s and 1990s. This was when they were setting up rings or running other errands in WWE (then known as WWF). They alleged abuse by former ring announcer Mel Phillips. One also accused inaugural Intercontinental Champion Pat Patterson, and another named former executive Terry Garvin. Phillips, Patterson, and Garvin passed away years before the lawsuit was filed. The plaintiffs claim former WWE owners Vince and Linda McMahon were negligent in allowing the abuse to happen. The former ring boys overcame an earlier motion to dismiss in December 2025, which narrowed the number of plaintiffs from eight to seven. All plaintiffs remain anonymous under “John Doe” aliases. The defendants have denied the primary allegations. However, U.S. District Judge James K. Bredar ruled that the Maryland law is constitutional as applied to the case. The case will now proceed to discovery, during which both sides will gather evidence and take sworn depositions. A teleconference to schedule future deadlines will take place on November 17. However, any potential trial remains at least several months off. Maryland passed the Child Victims Act in 2023, which eliminated any time limit for filing civil lawsuits related to child sexual abuse. Had the new law not come into effect, the statute of limitations on the plaintiffs’ claims would have lapsed years ago. The plaintiffs claim the named WWE executives assaulted them in different states, but, importantly, said some of them happened in Maryland. title: On the Record: Ilja Dragunov Speaks On Whether He Blames WWE for His Departure
raw_title: Ilja Dragunov Addresses Whether He Blames WWE for His Departure
summary_src: Ilja Dragunov says he could feel something changing in WWE well before his contract actually expired.
body: Speaking to The TakeDown on SI , Dragunov looked back at what he described as a “very complicated” period of his career. A huge part of that was recovering from the ACL tear that kept him out of action and putting everything he had into getting himself back into the ring. All that work initially seemed to pay off in a huge way. Dragunov said he essentially won the United States Championship as soon as he returned, and he still looks back on that moment as something special. “I came back, and I won the United States Championship basically on my return, which was an awesome, memorable moment.” Things didn’t stay that way forever. Once Dragunov dropped the championship and moved into whatever came next, he started getting a feeling that his situation inside WWE had changed. Dragunov isn’t pointing fingers at WWE or blaming any particular person for that feeling. In fact, he went out of his way to stress how much respect he still has for the company after spending seven years there and giving WWE most of his twenties. “And I don’t blame anybody. I’m a gentleman and I have way too much respect for the last seven years that I — the most of my 20s — that I spent with the company.” “But I felt like it is fine for me and reasonable to ask myself, ‘Is there more? Is there a new air I can breathe?’” “Again, everything I can say is not as exciting as people made it. Of course, at some point in time, you don’t have creative — you’re just waiting for the next opportunities to come.” Dragunov said WWE’s crowded roster and already-full storylines were part of the situation. Eventually his contract expired in August, and negotiations between the two sides didn’t produce anything that convinced him he absolutely needed to stay. “Everything I can say is there was nothing I felt was satisfying and nothing that gave me the perspective of, like, ‘Okay, I MUST stick with here.’” Subhojeet Mukherjee Subhojeet Mukherjee has covered pro wrestling for over 20 years, delivering trusted news and backstage updates to fans around the world.

body: In a latest tweet posted via his X account , Big Daddy Cool revealed that he had been travelling a lot lately. However, until two years ago, that was not possible for him due to major injuries. He said that he had herniated discs in his back and problems in his left quad, with the muscle atrophying at an alarming rate. The WWE legend underwent stem cell procedures for his issues and was able to regain the quality of life while not undergoing surgery. You can read Nash’s tweet below: “I sent my MRI’s to the specialist @BioXcelleratorand they felt the stem cell treatment could prevent a surgical procedure. I don’t thank the medical advances that saved my quality of life and allowed me to return 100% surgery free. If you are in a position that mimics mine please consider @BioXcellerator . I don’t know anyone that has just one back surgery.” Kevin Nash made his professional wrestling debut in 1990 and got signed by the global juggernaut, WWE, in 1993. He debuted under the name Diesel as Shawn Michaels’ bodyguard and then went on to become a top singles star, winning multiple titles including the WWE Championship. He and Scott Hall left WWE to join rival promotion, WCW, in 1996, where they formed the infamous faction, nWo, alongside Hulk Hogan.

title: Amazing Red Signs With TNA After X-Division Title Win
raw_title: Amazing Red Signs With TNA After X-Division Title Win
summary_src: Amazing Red’s wild TNA comeback isn’t stopping with the X-Division Championship. Just 10 days after walking into Bound For Glory as a Hall of Famer and walking out with the title, Red has reportedly signed with the company for another run.
body: According to PWInsider , Amazing Red has officially signed with TNA Wrestling and committed to the promotion. TNA hasn’t announced the deal publicly yet, but the report states that everything is done. “TNA Hall of Famer The Amazing Red, who won the X-Division Championship at Bound for Glory earlier this month, has officially signed with the promotion, PWInsiderElite.com can confirm. The promotion has yet to officially announce the deal, but we can confirm it is done and Red has committed to the promotion.” That’s a pretty big development considering Red’s Bound For Glory appearance initially looked like it could be a special one-night deal. He was there to be inducted into the TNA Hall of Fame, but during his speech, Red suddenly announced that he was entering the vacant X-Division Championship match later that night. Red didn’t just show up for the nostalgia pop either. He hit KC Navarro with the Code Red, got the three-count and became X-Division Champion for the fourth time in his career . The belt had been left vacant after Leon Slater exercised Option C to challenge Nic Nemeth for the TNA World Championship. Red’s surprise entry turned the originally planned six-man match into a seven-man scramble, and he ended up leaving with the championship. The whole thing was already a crazy full-circle moment for Red. Before Bound For Glory, he hadn’t held the X-Division Championship since September 25, 2010, putting more than 16 years between his previous reign and his latest one. Red has remained busy outside TNA as well, running House of Glory Wrestling in New York City alongside Brian XL. The 44-year-old has been part of the wrestling scene since the independent boom of the early 2000s, including the early days of Ring of Honor, while his TNA history also includes an NWA Tag Team Championship run with Jerry Lynn. So much for Bound For Glory being a nostalgia appearance. Amazing Red went from Hall of Fame inductee to champion in a matter of hours, and now he’s reportedly sticking around to see where this comeback goes next. body: Bandido reflects on his final conversation that he had with PAC and the fact they exchanged their respective football clubs shirts. It has been almost a month since the tragic passing of PAC, who was a staple of the AEW roster in recent years, as well as an important member of the Death Riders faction. PAC’s passing would come less than 24 hours after he would compete at AEW All Out and for one AEW roster member, he is hoping to keep PAC with him for as long as he can. While speaking to Jimmy V3 in a new interview , Bandido would be asked about PAC, recalling their final conversation and how they exchanged shirts of their football clubs. “Yeah, you know, PAC, he always was a very good person with me. I met him in Japan. We spent time together in Dragongate and he was a good person with me. The day before he passed away, we spent time (together). He gave me a Newcastle shirt. I gave him my home team shirt, which is Santos Laguna’s shirt, and he said, ‘thank you.’ The last thing that I can remember from him is, ‘I love you, brother,’ and I will have that words in my heart forever, forever. So I want to have him with me for as much time as is possible, you know?” If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.
summary: Bandido recalled his last conversation with PAC the day before the AEW star's passing. In a recent interview, McIntyre recalled a conversation from 2006 or 2007 in which he told PAC he would be the one to achieve major success from the UK. PAC responded by saying McIntyre would be the one to make it big.
McIntyre described PAC as an incredible high flyer with unmatched precision during that period. He expressed pride in watching PAC's career journey and the accomplishments he achieved over time.

McIntyre also discussed the increased representation of British and Scottish wrestlers in the industry. He noted that wrestling was once dominated by Americans and Canadians with only occasional British talent, but the landscape has since expanded to include far more performers from the UK.

McIntyre highlighted the impact from Scotland, a country of five million people, which has produced around eight or nine WWE superstars, most of them women. He said this development particularly stood out to him.
In 2006, PAC and McIntyre, then known as Drew Galloway, competed against each other at an event in London called RQW Not Just For Christmas. PAC defeated McIntyre by count-out in that match.

title: Gurv Sihra Updates Collapsed Lung Recovery

body: It sounds like Gurv Sihra should be back in the ring soon after suffering a scary injury last month. Formerly known as Sunil Singh in WWE, Sihra suffered a collapsed lung while competing at an indie show in Canada on September 19. It was a frightening experience that left Sihra feeling lucky to be alive. He did not immediately grasp the severity of the situation and finished the tag match he and his brother Harv were competing in. But when they got backstage, Gurv couldn’t get to his feet and was still struggling to breathe. He was taken to the hospital and treated for a collapsed lung. Gurv posted a new update last night saying his lungs are now back to normal. He still isn’t able to fly but expects to be cleared soon. “The road to recovery continues,” Gurv wrote. “X-Rays show my lungs are back to normal & there is very little air bubbles left in my chest-cavity from the collapsed lung. I still can’t fly at the moment, however, I should be cleared soon. Thank you all for your continued love & support.” Gurv and his brother Harv team together as The Bollywood Boyz on the indies and are best known for the time they spent in WWE as allies of Jinder Mahal. They debuted for WWE in the Cruiserweight Classic in 2016 and appeared on NXT, 205 Live, and the main roster before being released in 2021. The match where Gurv suffered this collapsed lung took place for Pure Power Wrestling in Lethbridge, Alberta, Canada. The Bollywood Boyz defeated Shaun Martens & Sydney Steele to win Pure Power’s Tag Team titles. Joseph joined F4W during his time at UMass and has now been writing about the industry for nearly a decade. In addition to his work with F4W, Joseph has previously contributed to Sports Illustrated's wrestling coverage. He lives in Massachusetts and is a diehard fan of the Boston sports teams and Liverpool Football Club.

title: In Memoriam: AEW wrestler Pac’s death exposes pro wrestling’s labor problem
raw_title: AEW wrestler Pac’s death exposes pro wrestling’s labor problem
body: Save Few things are more difficult to get down in immutable ink than the history of professional wrestling . Born on the carnival circuit, the pseudo-sport maintained a here today-gone tomorrow feeling until relatively recently. Promoters scraped out regional fiefdoms where transient performers would fight for a spell before jumping ship in search of better deals. Sometimes they took their name with them; other times they molded themselves to whatever gimmick their new promoter needed on the roster. It makes a mess of any timeline, and that’s before you get to the kayfabe — the illusion — of it all, the fact that all these real men and women are deadly serious about keeping up their fake characters. Gorgeous George, one of the most famous faces of wrestling’s Golden Age, didn’t make it to his 50th birthday. “Macho Man” Randy Savage and his ex-wife/manager Miss Elizabeth both died before reaching Social Security eligibility. High-flying technical wrestler Eddie Guerrero died at 38. Windham Rotunda, who freaked out the WWE for years as a swamp-dwelling cultist named Bray Wyatt, passed away at the age of 36. And earlier this week, All Elite Wrestling star Pac died in the parking lot of an Illinois chain restaurant, just a day after his most recent match. HIs cause of death is still unknown. Born Benjamin Satterley in a blue-collar community in Newcastle upon Tyne, England, he first came to national attention stateside in the WWE, where he wrestled under the decidedly English name Neville. He took the cruiserweight title twice before jumping for AEW in 2018. His star rose exponentially as a regular heel for the young promotion. At the time of his passing, he was only 40 years old. Playing a fake brute who’s willing to take a folding chair to the face to settle a disagreement is hell on a body. Learning how to fall and pretending you have superpowers can’t cancel out physics. If a 240-pound man turns you upside down and drives your head into a padded floor, you’re going to feel it the next day (and probably several days after). The wear and tear is cumulative, adding up over time like it does for all contact sports. Just take a boxer’s blown-out ears and a running back’s trick knee and expand it to account for the fact that, in wrestling, shots to the back of the skull are frequently necessary to move the story along. Recruiting almost exclusively among the huge and jacked — it’s easier to appear larger-than-life on camera if you’re real-world large — makes the list of heart conditions start to pile up. It’s all a recipe for a brief career, and a correspondingly short life. The average star of WWE or AEW signs on as an independent contractor, meaning they are responsible for their own health insurance and are subject to being fired for nearly any cause. The situation is exacerbated by wrestling’s employer-employee relationship. Staying true to its seasonal carny roots, almost all professional wrestlers are gig workers. title: Syko Stu Details Year-Long Recovery From Raja Jackson Assault
raw_title: Syko Stu opens up on recovery after Raja Jackson attack: ‘I was off work for an entire year’
summary_src: Syko Stu opened up on his recovery process after suffering an attack from Raja Jackson at a 2025 independent show.
body: Many in the wrestling world and beyond watched with disgust in 2025 after footage surfaced of streamer Raja Jackson, son of ex-UFC star Rampage Jackson, brutally attacking independent professional wrestler Syko Stu. The attack, live-streamed on Kick from a KnokX Pro event in California last year, landed Jackson a 90-day prison sentence over a felony battery charge. The 26-year-old, who paid $81,000 in restitution to Stu and is serving a two-year probationary period, finished his prison sentence over the summer. A year removed from the disturbing incident, Stu continues to battle with the effects of the attack. Among the injuries due to the flurry of punches he took were a shattered maxilla, numerous broken teeth and a severe traumatic brain injury. Stu believes his short-term memory has been significantly affected by the head injury: “My wife, she’ll tell me something, then five minutes later I’ll forget it,” he said. After the incident, Stu recalled being in the hospital for five days. He was only released once he was able to pass a series of tests, including showing that he could walk. Stu hasn’t wrestled since suffering his injuries in 2025. He said that one of his bigger concerns with performing again is less about his physical state, and more about whether his changed mental state could make it harder to put together matches. “It’s all psychology,” Stu said about wrestling. “You’re telling the story, but you’re telling it with your body. You still need the same psychology to put it together to make the match make sense.” When asked if he plans to wrestle again, Stu seemed inclined to eventually return. “My doctors tell me I shouldn’t,” he said. “But, you know, it’s one of those things. You have a love for something so much you really want to find any way that you can make it happen. Whether it’s gonna happen or not still remains to be seen.”

Stu was hospitalized for five days, has seen his short-term memory impacted and was off work for a full year as he continues to deal with the aftermath.

llm_long: At a KnokX Pro event on August 23 2025, Raja Jackson knocked independent wrestler Syko Stu unconscious during a planned spot that escalated beyond the script.
Raja slammed Stu and then delivered more than 20 unanswered legitimate strikes to his head until independent wrestler Doug Malo intervened and pulled him away.
Syko Stu has limited memory of the incident itself. He recalled Raja filming backstage, which is unusual, and remembered calling a finish that involved one wrestling punch after a beer can spot.

Stu stated he was unconscious from the initial slam and has no recollection of the following events. He woke up in the hospital on Tuesday after being admitted on Saturday and remained in and out of consciousness until then.
During his hospital stay, medical staff would not show him video of the incident or discuss it. Wrestler Rikishi visited him there as he began to recover.

Stu was discharged from the hospital on Thursday. He now participates in word exercises during rehabilitation but continues to experience short-term memory issues such as forgetting things within minutes, repeating actions, and failing to recall names and faces.

title: Dave Meltzer: WWE Gets $150M For Riyadh WrestleMania
raw_title: Dave Meltzer Reveals Compensation WWE Will Receive For Holding WrestleMania In Riyadh
summary_src: Dave Meltzer has learned the amount WWE is set to be paid by the Saudi Arabian government for holding WrestleMania 43 in Riyadh next year.
body: "It looks like the WrestleMania price is $150 million," he said. "I knew it was over $100 [million] because people in Saudi Arabia told me it's north of $100 million. Usually, they get $55 [million] to go. ... [They] don't want to put that in jeopardy." Meltzer reaffirmed his understanding that there are "contingency plans" in place, just in case WWE is not able to make the date in Riyadh. Currently, the United States government has issued a Level 3 travel advisory, encouraging U.S. citizens against traveling to the country. If the government were to raise that advisory to Level 4, it would prevent WWE from holding Crown Jewel in Riyadh. Meltzer believes that would act as a "bail-out" for the company, as the decision would be out of WWE's hands and there'd be no risk of insulting Turki Al-Sheikh, the chairman of the country's General Entertainment Authority. In recent weeks, Al-Sheikh made a post on X regarding the upcoming Canelo Alvarez vs. Christian Mbilli boxing match, stating that the fight was still on and the current situation in Saudi Arabia would reveal the country's "true friends." Meltzer interpreted the post as a message to WWE along with other companies, with the subtext being that they would not respond kindly to any organization canceling planned events in Saudi Arabia.

He noted the promotion normally receives $55 million for Saudi Arabia events and does not want to risk that relationship. Meltzer added that contingency plans exist if WWE cannot make the date, with a potential U.S. government Level 4 travel advisory serving as a way out that would not offend Turki Al-Sheikh.

body: Ilja Dragunov makes his AEW debut against “Speedball” Mike Bailey.
