You can catch AEW Dynamite LIVE at 8pm ET/5pm PT on TSN2, TSN.ca and the TSN App. “The Mad Dragon” has arrived in All Elite Wrestling. Ilja Dragunov was the man behind the metronome vignettes and made his first appearance in the company this past Saturday night’s WrestleDream pay-per-view. On Wednesday night, the Moscow native makes his in-ring debut against a man he’s met once before in the United Empire’s “Speedball” Mike Bailey. For the uninitiated, Dragunov is one of the most intense competitors currently in the industry. Born in Russia and raised in Germany, Dragunov first made his name in one of Europe’s top promotions, Westside Xtreme Wrestling (wXw). Among those he did battle with were WALTER (now WWE’s Gunther), the late John “Bad Bones” Klinger and Tommy End (former AEW performer Malakai Black). He became the company’s first Triple Crown champion, winning wXW’s Unified World Wrestling Championship, Shotgun Championship and World Tag Team Championships. Dragunov left Germany for England and WWE NXT UK where he restarted his rivalry with WALTER, who he defeated for the NXT UK Championship, and took on the likes of Chris Hero and Pete Dunne. Relocating to the United States, Dragunov took NXT by storm, facing off with Donovan Dijak and Trick Williams before defeating Carmelo Hayes for the NXT Championship. Moving to the WWE main roster, Dragunov made an early splash with wins over former IWGP World Champion Shinsuke Nakamura and Ricochet before defeating current WWE Champion Sami Zayn for the United States Championship last October. He kept the title for two months, defending it against Johnny Gargano and Tommaso Ciampa among others, before dropping it to old rival Hayes. Choosing to depart WWE at the expiration of his contract, Dragunov immediately jumped into the deep end in AEW with a debut match against Bailey. It will be the first time the two have met in a decade. Much has changed since then. One of wXw’s calling cards is its annual 16 Carat Gold Tournament, a single-elimination tournament normally held over three days in the spring. A yearly tradition since 2006, the tournament counts Shingo Takagi, Zack Sabre Jr., Zayn (as El Generico) and Dragunov himself in 2017 among its winners. Some of the biggest stars in the industry have participated in the event, including the late PAC and current and former world champions Will Ospreay, Seth Rollins (as Tyler Black), Eddie Kingston, Adam Cole, Drew McIntyre (as Drew Galloway) and Cody Rhodes. The 2016 edition was won by ZSJ, but it’s the first round of that tournament that is of particular interest. On March 11 in Oberhausen, Dragunov went one-on-one with Bailey. title: Comeback Watch: Drew McIntyre Busts Out New Move While Training for WWE Return
raw_title: Drew McIntyre Busts Out New Move While Training for WWE Return
summary_src: Drew McIntyre wasn’t kidding when he said his WWE return would come with some new moves. The former WWE Champion just climbed to the top rope during training and busted out a flying arm drag while continuing to prepare for his eventual in-ring comeback.
body: McIntyre showed off the unexpected move in an Instagram post on October 21 . The 285-pounder went up top before launching himself into the flying arm drag, then popped back up and yelled “Olé!” to celebrate pulling it off. Drew clearly enjoyed proving he still has a few tricks hiding in his moveset. He joked about suddenly going full lucha while tagging Chivas in the post. The timing makes the clip even more interesting because McIntyre recently teased that his moveset could look noticeably different whenever he finally wrestles again. During an interview with Chris Van Vliet on INSIGHT , Drew revealed that his time away from WWE has allowed him to rebuild his body and work heavily on his balance, agility and conditioning . “I’ve been working real hard in a way that my cardio and agility is, I’d say my whole life, but really for sure the past 12 years, is right now the best I’ve been. Like I feel great agility-wise. Bigger than I’ve ever been. I’m moving better than I have.” McIntyre currently weighs around 285 pounds, but the extra size apparently hasn’t slowed him down. He previously said old highlight videos had reminded him of moves he’d completely forgotten he used to perform, and that got him thinking about bringing some of them back. “I’ve got a feeling some of my offense is going to be unique. I saw some videos of myself people had sent me, were highlight videos, and I was like, I didn’t realize I did that. Guess I’m going to start stealing for myself.” Drew went even further by claiming he can now perform some of those old moves more easily than he could during his 20s. Considering what he just pulled off from the top rope, he appears pretty serious about testing that theory. “Forgot I did half the moves, and I physically can do them easily now and probably better than I did them when I was in my 20s.” Of course, nobody should expect McIntyre to suddenly turn into a full-time high-flyer. When Van Vliet previously asked whether fans should expect some new additions to his offense, Drew gave a pretty simple description of what he has planned. McIntyre hasn’t wrestled for WWE since WrestleMania 42, and he’s been taking his time before getting back into the ring. He previously told fans asking about his return to give him “a little second,” making it clear that he’ll come back when he decides the time is right. The latest training footage doesn’t give fans a return date, but it does show exactly what McIntyre has been talking about. If a 285-pound Drew is now climbing to the top rope and throwing flying arm drags while promising new offense, his eventual WWE comeback could look a little different from the version fans last saw. title: Results Recap: WWE enters the online casino market but has no intention of becoming an operatorWWE, the world's largest wrestling promotion, continues to convert its intellectual property into revenue streams beyond the ring. Online casino games have emerged as a new avenue, one the company is pursuing exclusively through brand and content licensing to third-party developers. WWE itself takes on no gambling operator functions, keeping its focus on what it does best: creating characters, storylines, and spectacular shows. The strategy revolves around the promotion's most recognizable assets. WWE Superstars, marquee events, and weekly programs serve as the raw material that partners transform into gaming products for the US market. WWE, in turn, collects licensing fees without investing in technology development or taking on the regulatory risks of the gambling business. Who WWE is launching gaming projects with and on what terms The timeline of partnerships shows that WWE is building an entire network of licensing agreements covering different segments of the gaming market. In July 2025, the company signed an exclusive multi-year agreement with Fanatics Betting and Gaming. Under the terms of the deal, Fanatics takes full responsibility for the production and distribution of WWE-themed online casino games in the United States. In January 2026, VGW joined the list of partners, receiving rights to use the brand across its portfolio of online social games. The agreement with VGW includes access to WWE Superstars' likenesses, the promotion's digital channels, and its flagship programs, including SmackDown, WrestleMania, and SummerSlam. In parallel, the WWE and Fanatics partnership has expanded well beyond the casino segment. As early as 2025, the companies extended their collaboration to merchandising, digital content, and fan engagement activities. A telling example was the inclusion of Logan Paul's IMPAULSIVE in a joint digital content network. In essence, WWE is building an ecosystem in which the brand meets audiences at a wide variety of touchpoints — from podcasts and merchandise to slots. From a logo on a slot to full-scale storytelling within the game The first set of products released under the Fanatics deal already included several titles with distinctive names: WWE Blackjack Raw Multiplier Melee SmackDown Big Money Entrance other branded games from the launch portfolio The most ambitious release, however, was the slot WrestleMania: Road to Gold, launched in March 2026 through Fanatics Casino in partnership with White Hat Studios. The game features 20 WWE Superstars, and the promotion's key events are embedded directly into the mechanics and progression structure: SummerSlam Survivor Series Royal Rumble Elimination Chamber Money in the Bank This is the key distinction between basic branding and what WWE brings to the table. In a typical licensed slot, the brand serves as a visual wrapper: a familiar logo, thematic colors, a couple of recognizable symbols on the reels. In WrestleMania: Road to Gold, the promotion's narrative logic is transplanted into the game itself. Major events define the stages of progression, and WWE Superstars function not as decoration but as the substantive core of the gameplay experience. This approach gives partners significantly more material to work with and turns each product into something greater than just another licensed slot. Why WWE does not need its own casino or sportsbook The logic of the business model is entirely transparent. For WWE, the primary value lies in monetizing intellectual property and expanding its digital ecosystem, not in managing gambling infrastructure. Both sides benefit: WWE maintains its focus on characters, storylines, and audience engagement while generating additional licensing revenue with no operational costs related to development or distribution Partners gain a recognizable brand backed by decades of accumulated loyalty — a critical advantage for standing out in the crowded online casino market The promotion's rights and recognizable properties remain the central asset in this arrangement. WWE Superstars such as Cody Rhodes and Rhea Ripley already possess well-established identities in the eyes of audiences. WrestleMania and SummerSlam have long since become globally recognized entertainment brands. And the weekly shows provide a continuous stream of new stories, rivalries, and characters that shows no sign of running dry year after year. WWE's deals fit into a broader trend. Online casino operators are looking for ways to reach audiences that previously had no interest in gambling. The standard toolkit is well known: welcome deposit bonuses, free spins, cashback, loyalty programs, and no deposit bonuses at online casinos, which allow players to try games without risking their own money. These mechanics still reliably attract new players, but competing on them alone is becoming increasingly difficult, as nearly every platform offers similar promotions. As a result, operators are increasingly betting on emotional brand connections, and a partnership with a wrestling promotion delivers exactly that kind of tool. A WWE fan comes not for the bonus, but for the beloved characters and storylines that have long been part of their leisure time. The bottom line comes down to three elements. WWE monetizes its intellectual property through licensing. Development, the technology platform, and distribution are handled entirely by partners. And the gaming products use the promotion's characters and events not as a visual layer, but as the substantive foundation on which the entire user experience is built.

The similarities become less obvious once the action begins. WWE performers train for physically demanding, choreographed contests, while boxers must respond to opponents genuinely trying to defeat them. Strength, timing, and confidence can help in both disciplines, but success in one doesn't guarantee success in the other. Their heavily publicized encounter ended in the sixth round when Danis was disqualified following illegal grappling attempts. title: Nile Remains Active on WWE Roster
raw_title: Another Star May Have Re-Signed With WWE
body: According to Fightful Select , Nile's contract was due to expire at the beginning of October. However, she is still listed as an active talent on WWE's roster page, and she appeared on the October 6 episode of NXT in a battle royal to determine the number one contender for the NXT Women's Championship. That match was won by Wren Sinclair, who was impersonating Lady Shani. Her NXT appearance came after a long stretch away from WWE's main shows. Nile has been off Raw since March, and she has wrestled only two matches on the show this year. Most of her work in 2026 has come on WWE Main Event, where she has wrestled 12 times, including matches against NXT talent such as Thea Hail, Wendy Choo and Lizzy Rain. Fightful Select reported in early September that Nile's contract was set to expire soon and that it had not heard whether she had negotiated a new deal. The same report said WWE had plans for her and that creative had a "big change" in store. Fightful Select later reported that the change was a tag team with Jordynne Grace. According to Fightful, vignettes pairing the two were filmed over the summer, with the hope that they would air in September, and its sources linked the team to the WWE trademark "Iron Built." The vignettes never aired. In May 2025, she won the tournament to become number one contender for the WWE Women's Speed Championship but lost to Sol Ruca in the title match. Grace has also been off television, and a WrestleVotes report said WWE does not have her in its creative plans at the moment, while adding that she is not on her way out. Nile still being on the roster is a good sign that the company sees value in her, even after a year in which she was barely used on Raw. Her name staying on the roster page and her appearance on NXT television right after her contract was due to expire both point to her still being under contract, and they suggest the company wants her visible again. The Grace team is still the best path for her. Both women have strength-based styles and are competing in bodybuilding, the vignettes are already filmed, and the women's tag team division needs new challengers. Tatum Paxley holding the tag titles with Alexa Bliss also gives Nile a built-in story against her former partner. The concern is that WWE has had this plan ready since the summer and still has not pulled the trigger. If Nile did sign a new deal, the company should use it as a reason to finally air those vignettes and give both women something to do on television. They will face the trio of Hartley Jackson, Ryohei Oiwa and Pro Wrestling NOAH’s Kaito Kiyomiya. title: Chad Gable Builds Strong Intercontinental Title Run
raw_title: Chad Gable Is Quietly Having a Huge Title Run
body: Gable won the title from Penta on night two of SummerSlam on August 2 at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis. Wrestling in front of his home state crowd, Gable reversed a second Mexican Destroyer attempt into the Ankle Lock and made Penta tap out. It was the first Intercontinental Championship win of his career. He earned that title shot the hard way. On the July 13 episode of Raw in Dallas, Gable won a number one contender's gauntlet match that lasted more than 38 minutes, getting past Dominik Mysterio, Dragon Lee, Ethan Page, Je'Von Evans, Joe Hendry and Rusev. Since winning the title, Gable has defended it four times on Raw, which works out to a televised title match every 20 days. He beat Rey Mysterio on the August 17 episode in Buffalo, Dragon Lee on the September 14 episode in Mexico City and Rey Fenix on the October 12 episode in Bossier City, Louisiana. Most recently, he retained in a triple threat against Dragon Lee and Rey Mysterio on the October 19 episode in San Diego. Those were not short matches either. According to Cagematch , the Fenix match ran 18 minutes and 35 seconds, the first Dragon Lee match went 15 minutes and 39 seconds, and the triple threat lasted 15 minutes and 35 seconds. The Mysterio match on August 17 went just over 13 minutes. The televised defenses are only part of the picture. Cagematch lists 13 more successful defenses at live events since SummerSlam, bringing his total to 17 without a loss. He defended against Ethan Page several times on WWE's summer tour, beat Dominik Mysterio in both a singles match and a triple threat in Canada, and won four straight fatal four-way matches against Dragon Lee, Ethan Page and Penta on the South America tour in September. He also defended the title at two NXT live events in the Carolinas against Saquon Shugars and Uriah Connors, and won a three-way against Ethan Page and Je'Von Evans in Honolulu on October 16. The run is also the payoff to a long chase. Gable came up short against Sami Zayn in multiple Intercontinental Championship matches in 2024, including a match at Clash at the Castle in June that year that lasted more than 22 minutes. Two years later, he finally got the title in his home state. Gable's reign is a throwback to the way a midcard title is supposed to be booked. He is defending the championship on television on a regular basis, he is doing it against a mix of veterans and younger stars, and the matches are getting real time on Raw. Four televised defenses in 80 days is a steady pace for a secondary title, and the live event defenses show he is putting the belt on the line nearly every time he works. It also matters who he is beating. Rey Mysterio, Dragon Lee and Rey Fenix are some of the best workers on Raw, and Gable's style matches up well with each of them. Those matches have made the Intercontinental Championship feel like one of the more important parts of the show, which is what a strong champion should do. title: On the Record: Swerve Strickland Explains Why WWE and AEW Will Never Hold a Crossover Event
raw_title: Swerve Strickland Explains Why WWE and AEW Will Never Hold a Crossover Event
summary_src: Swerve Strickland doesn’t see WWE and AEW ever putting their differences aside for a massive crossover show. In fact, he doesn’t believe it’ll happen in his lifetime because there are simply too many top stars both companies would want to protect.
body: Speaking to Billboard , Swerve was directly asked whether he could ever see WWE and AEW working together for a cross-promotional event. He didn’t dance around the question and immediately shut down the idea. For Swerve Strickland, the biggest obstacle isn’t whether the wrestlers would want to do it. He believes it all comes down to control, marketing and WWE protecting the stars it has spent years building. “It’s control. It’s all about marketing. It’s like the NFL, WWE has to protect their shield. There’s no way they’d allow any of our wrestlers to look better and be better [than them].” Swerve pointed to Oba Femi as a perfect example. WWE has positioned him as a dominant force, so Swerve doesn’t believe the company would suddenly put him into a crossover situation where that presentation could be compromised. “Obi Femi is a world beater. You gotta protect that and make sure he keeps looking good. Gunther, have to protect that. Roman [Reigns], have to protect that. Cody [Rhodes], have to protect, even more so because of AEW. There’s a lot of that happening.” Cody’s situation would obviously bring another wrinkle considering his history with AEW before returning to WWE. Swerve believes those kinds of factors would make figuring out winners and losers a political headache before the wrestlers even got into the ring. “You wanna see Seth [Rollins] and Ospreay. That’s the generational thing, but who do you protect? Who has the leverage?” The funny part is that Swerve says the wrestlers themselves aren’t nearly as concerned about any of that. He revealed that he’s good friends with Carmelo Hayes, Je’Von Evans and Oba Femi and would happily work with them without caring who actually got their hand raised. “Us in the locker room, we just wanna have these matches. I’m good friends with Carmelo [Hayes], Jevon [Evans] and Oba. Those are my boys. I love those guys. I don’t care who wins. Double DQs. I don’t care.” So while the locker rooms might be willing to make something happen, Swerve believes the business side makes a WWE-AEW supershow nearly impossible. There are plenty of dream matches waiting on paper, but getting two competing promotions to agree on who gets protected could be a much bigger fight than anything happening inside the ring. title: By the Numbers: Swerve Strickland Questions the Credibility of Five-Star Wrestling Match Ratings
raw_title: Swerve Strickland Questions the Credibility of Five-Star Wrestling Match Ratings
summary_src: Swerve Strickland isn’t losing any sleep over those Wrestling Observer five-star ratings. In fact, the AEW star thinks some of those supposed five-star classics might be closer to four stars once you step outside the Observer bubble.
body: Speaking to Billboard , Swerve was talking about balancing wrestling with his career in hip-hop when he got an interesting question. What’s harder — putting on a five-star wrestling match or creating a five-mic album? Swerve didn’t even hesitate. He knows both ratings are completely subjective. What sounds like a perfect album to one person might only be a four or four-and-a-half to somebody else, and Swerve thinks wrestling ratings work exactly the same way. “Both parts are subjective, ’cause five mics for one person might be four-and-a-half or four to other people.” Then came the Wrestling Observer shot. Swerve casually joked that some of those five-star matches might lose a star once you ask somebody outside the publication. “Five-star match to Wrestling Observer were more like four [star] to anybody else.” Swerve wasn’t just trying to get a cheap shot in either. His bigger point was that creating an album capable of winning over hardcore fans, casual listeners, critics and people who weren’t already interested in you is incredibly difficult. That’s also why Swerve puts so much weight behind the five-mic label. For him, a real classic can’t just be hot when it drops — people still need to be talking about it years later. “To me, a five-mic album stands the test of time. There’s all-time great lyricists that haven’t been able to pull that off and I’m not even at that level as a pure lyricist.” Swerve knows that puts the bar ridiculously high, and he’s not pretending he’s already reached it himself. He believes genuine classics are rare for a reason. So Swerve isn’t exactly buying the idea that every five-star wrestling match should automatically be treated like an untouchable classic. Ratings are subjective, but when it comes to creating something that can survive years of changing tastes, he’s putting a five-mic album above anything the Wrestling Observer can hand out. body: Amazing Red is officially back in the fold with TNA Wrestling. After being inducted into the TNA Hall of Fame and winning the X-Division Championship at Bound for Glory 2026, PWInsider reports that Red has signed a contract with TNA . A pioneer of the early X-Division, Red is now on his fourth reign as champion. It’s his first time holding the X-Division belt since 2010. Red was inducted into the TNA Hall of Fame during the Bound for Glory 2026 pre-show and then entered the Ultimate X match for the vacant title later that night. Leon Slater, who is now the TNA World Champion, chose to give up the X-Division title as he exercised “Option C” for a shot at the World Championship. This run is Red’s first time back in TNA since 2011. He is a founder of indie promotion House of Glory, where he competes in the ring and operates the HOG training school. Earlier this week, TNA confirmed the signing of Shotzi Blackheart and re-signing of Director of Authority Santino Marella . There is expected to be more contract news coming over the next several weeks as TNA addresses its wrestlers who have deals coming up before the end of the year. title: Ex-UFC fighter Michael ‘Venom’ Page says MMA fighters need to form union: ‘We have to move as one’
raw_title: Ex-UFC fighter Michael ‘Venom’ Page says MMA fighters need to form union: ‘We have to move as one’
summary_src: Former UFC fighter Michael "Venom" Page believes fighters should form a union to help get better treatment.
body: Michael “Venom” Page believes a fighters’ union might be needed to help improve treatment for competitors in MMA. MVP signed to the UFC roster in 2024, joining after a lengthy Bellator run which saw him put together an impressive compilation of knockout wins. Now out of the UFC, Page told BBC Sport he wants to encourage fighters to form an alliance in MMA for better benefits. “It’s less about speaking out now, it’s more about forming a union and coming together,” he told BBC. “We have to move as one … If all fighters said ‘we’re not gonna do it’, then UFC doesn’t exist. That’s the important thing for fighters to remember. It’s not just the machine of UFC, you guys are the nuts and bolts that help the machine move.” Page said that frustration around fighter pay is an issue you often don’t hear from the competitors themselves, as they fear backlash from promoters. UFC, which is currently in the first year of a seven-year, $7.7 billion deal to stream on Paramount+ in America, has long been accused of underpaying athletes. The company agreed to a settlement worth $375 million in 2024 for a class action lawsuit alleging that the company had engaged in antitrust behavior to keep the pay of its fighters low. Former UFC Middleweight Champion Sean Strickland recently expressed frustration over the company’s pay structure, teasing that he might even want to leave the brand soon. “[Conor] McGregor makes 30 million to fight for 30 second and they don’t want to pay us a fraction of it,” he wrote on X. “Contemplating just going to 205 [pounds] knocking out my contract then scrapping with Jake Paul. That sounds fun.” UFC CEO Dana White downplayed Strickland’s complaints, denying the claims that Strickland had made about pay. “When isn’t Sean upset about something?” he said at a press conference.

title: WWE Faces Pressure Over Saudi Crown Jewel Amid Attacks
raw_title: As missiles rain down on Riyadh, WWE's Crown Jewel dilemma is becoming unavoidable
body: That the Saudi security situation has deteriorated in the weeks after this year's Crown Jewel was first announced on Sept. 1 is an understatement. Since then, we've seen the Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen launch a barrage of missile attacks on Riyadh airport , claiming the lives of at least 20 people and injuring at least 370 in what is already the deadliest attack on Saudi soil in more than a decade. Right now, WWE is insisting that the show will go ahead — a decision that flies in the face of what other businesses and sports events are doing. Just this week, we've seen a bunch of major events in Riyadh postponed, including Saudi Arabia's annual Davos in the Desert, as well as the Six Kings Slam tennis tournament and Saudi International golf tournament. Why is WWE plowing ahead with Crown Jewel when others are playing it safe? As ever, money talks. Anyone who has spent five minutes following TKO's financials knows how important the Saudis are for WWE — in recent years, they've contributed around one quarter of the company's live-event revenues. The average Saudi show brings in more money than this year's WrestleMania. All of which brings us to Turki Alashikh, the man who controls the Saudi purse strings. Perhaps the most intriguing twist in this whole Crown Jewel saga is the reports that WWE insiders are worried that Alashikh's glazing of Saul "Canelo" Alvarez — who is set to fight in Riyadh on Oct. 31 – on social media is a preemptive dig at those in TKO towers. Would the country really pull the plug on SaudiMania if WWE canceled Crown Jewel? All common sense would suggest not. But that's the problem with relying on one source for such a hefty chunk of your revenue — you can't really afford to call their bluff. On the other hand, it's not like the other course of action is safe either, with the risk of missiles raining down on Riyadh airport. So what's a TKO executive to do? If it's so dangerous, you might ask, why is "Canelo" fighting there on Halloween? Well, you'd probably have to ask him. Which is sort of the point: "Canelo" is one man who can make his own decision whether to go to Riyadh to collect his purse or not. (He's also a man who gets punched for a living, so he probably has a different outlook on risk than your typical Wall Street suit.) More seriously, "Canelo" isn't a corporate entity like TKO. He doesn't have to take a whole production crew, or send dozens of supporting talent on commercial jets into Riyadh airport. He doesn't have to justify the fallout to shareholders should the proverbial mess really hit the fan. He's never going to be dragged in front of Congress like the bosses of Enron and Facebook when they faced scandals. In that situation, I don't doubt they could weather the storm in the long run. But the more pertinent question would be, why they didn't see the dark clouds on the horizon beforehand? If you're going to jump into bed with an absolute monarchy in one of the world's most unstable regions, can you real
summary: Missile strikes by Houthi rebels on Riyadh have killed at least 20 people and injured over 370 since WWE announced this year's Crown Jewel event. Multiple major business and sports gatherings in the city have been postponed for safety reasons while WWE maintains the show will proceed. The promotion's decision is driven by the significant financial contribution from Saudi events which account for roughly one quarter of its live event revenue per TKO financials.

title: Vince Russo Goes Nuclear on Fans for Bastardizing the Term “Pop” in Wrestling
raw_title: Vince Russo Goes Nuclear on Fans for Bastardizing the Term “Pop” in Wrestling
summary_src: Vince Russo has had enough of wrestling fans calling every loud crowd reaction a “pop.” The former WWE writer went off on fans for what he believes is the completely wrong use of the term, and he gave a pretty wild explanation for where “pop” supposedly came from in the first place.
body: “Me talking about the damn use of the word ‘pop’ by the marks. So let me educate you guys to make you understand what a pop is. Because when Roman Reigns comes out, bro, that’s not a pop — it’s a reaction.” Russo said the way wrestlers traditionally used the term was completely different. In his telling, the entire idea was about deliberately building a match or storyline toward one huge reaction. “The origin of ‘pop’ and how that word was used within the boys — because the boys would say, ‘We build to the pop.’” That’s where Russo’s explanation took a very NSFW turn. He claimed the wrestling term came from the phrase “pop a nut,” comparing the structure of building toward a major wrestling reaction to building toward a sexual climax. “Okay, here’s where that came from. There’s a term that we use as men called ‘pop a nut.’ And ladies and gentlemen, what ‘pop a nut’ means is when you are having sex with a woman, okay? And you are saying, ‘I’m coming, I’m coming,’ and then you pop the nut — then you come.” Russo wasn’t finished with the comparison either. He argued that the key part is the buildup, because that’s what separates what he considers a real wrestling pop from an instantaneous crowd reaction. “So you’re building and building towards that moment of ejaculation, and then you pop the nut. That’s where the term ‘pop’ came from. You build towards the pop.” To give a wrestling example, Russo pointed toward the classic hot-tag formula. The babyface gets beaten down, repeatedly comes close to reaching their partner and finally makes the tag after several failed attempts, giving the crowd the payoff it has been waiting for. “You build — think about a hot tag. Think about back in the day, the babyface is in trouble, he’s getting his ass kicked, he goes to the corner, they pull him back. Finally, after three attempts — the hot tag, the house pops!” That’s Russo’s problem with fans using the same word for somebody simply receiving a huge entrance reaction. He insists a traditional “pop” needs to have something building toward it rather than happening the second someone’s music hits. “That is where it comes from, guys. That’s where the pop in wrestling comes from. You build towards the pop.” Russo then directly called out fans for what he sees as the term being thrown around incorrectly. As far as he’s concerned, entrances can get enormous reactions, but that still doesn’t make them pops under his definition. “What you guys are talking about are instantaneous reactions. That is not the definition of a pop in wrestling. An entrance is not a pop! That is a reaction.” He wrapped things up by asking fans to stop “bastardizing” the word. Russo also admitted he doesn’t know exactly when wrestling fans started using “pop” to describe entrance reactions in the first place. “A pop, like a climax, is built to — for the pop. So can we stop bastardizing that word and using a word that we have no freaking idea what the hell that word means? I don’t know when ‘pop
summary: Because when Roman Reigns comes out, bro, that’s not a pop — it’s a reaction. Russo explained the way wrestlers traditionally used the term was completely different. The similarities become less obvious once the action begins. WWE performers train for physically demanding, choreographed contests, while boxers must respond to opponents genuinely trying to defeat them. Strength, timing, and confidence can help in both disciplines, but success in one doesn't guarantee success in the other. Several familiar WWE personalities have tested themselves in boxing or related combat sports. Their experiences range from impressive victories to painful reminders that fighting experience matters more than reputation. John Morrison built his wrestling reputation around remarkable athleticism. His acrobatic moves, agility, and impressive physical conditioning helped distinguish him during several WWE runs. His debut demonstrated that athleticism can transfer successfully when accompanied by appropriate preparation. One victory, however, doesn't establish how someone would perform against an experienced professional boxer. Logan Paul's relationship with boxing began before his WWE career. His fights against fellow internet personality KSI introduced him to competitive combat sports, while a 2021 exhibition against Floyd Mayweather attracted considerable attention. Paul subsequently became a recognizable WWE performer, combining his athletic ability with a talent for attracting audiences. Their heavily publicized encounter ended in the sixth round when Danis was disqualified following illegal grappling attempts. Paul had controlled much of the contest with his jab, but the chaotic ending overshadowed his performance. Security personnel entered the ring as tensions escalated between the fighters and their teams. Paul's unusual career reflects the growing overlap between sports entertainment and combat sports. Earlier in his career, he had a recurring role in the Stephen Amell Arrow series for The CW. Reigns has had roles in blockbusters, such as Fast & Furious Presents: Hobbs & Shaw. However, Street Fighter is his biggest role to date. He did voice one of the Zebros in Zootopia 2 last year. The other Zebro was voiced by his former rival, CM Punk. While they are riding the high of Street Fighter's success, Reigns and Rhodes are back in WWE. The "Tribal Chief" appears bound for a WarGames match next month. Copeland said he and Cage would sometimes “stage ambushes” of wrestlers in the parking lot. On this occasion, Cage jumped into the car of Crush (Brian Adams). “This street and this entrance is where Jay and I used to come and annoy and accost all of the wrestlers coming in. We found out that they would park back here and come into the building. So we would always just kind of stage ambushes. “And I’ll never forget the one in particular, and I think it was the last show I came to here. It was Demolition versus Legion of Doom and the Ultimate Warrior. “Jay and I were both big Demolition guys, so we came running out here and Demolition was packing their car and Brian Adams, Crush, was in the front seat. And Jay hopped in the front seat with Brian Adams and just started telling him all of his career highlights and everything like that. “And I was back at the trunk with Ax and Smash annoying them. Years later, Jay’s on a flight. Who sits down beside him? Brian Adams, Crush. And Jay told him the story and he actually still remembered it. And that all happened right here. Copeland defeated Steve Maclin in the main event of MLP Northern Rising at the former Maple Leaf Gardens, now known as the Mattamy Athletic Centre. After the show, Copeland said during the post-event press conference that he believes wrestling at Maple Leaf Gardens is likely a “white whale” for Christian as well. Copeland also revealed on the October 14 episode of AEW Dynamite that Cage suffered three broken ribs and a collapsed lung during the ladder match at AEW All Out. Up next for Copeland, he is scheduled to team with Will Ospreay in a match against Kyle Fletcher and Kevin Knight on tonight’s episode of AEW Dynamite. title: Ric Flair Praises Tony Khan's Generosity
raw_title: Ric Flair Speaks About Tony Khan: "He’s A Nice Guy... I Work For Him & I Don’t Do Anything"
summary_src: Ric Flair heaps praise onto Tony Khan. Biff Poggi of NewsNation conducted an interview with two-time WWE Hall of Famer Ric Flair. As the conversation moved along, Flair opened up about his relationship with AEW President Tony Khan.
body: Biff Poggi of NewsNation conducted an interview with two-time WWE Hall of Famer Ric Flair. As the conversation moved along, Flair opened up about his relationship with AEW President Tony Khan. “He’s a nice guy; he’s generous. I work for him and I don’t do anything. I think he takes care of me out of respect for me. He grew up on me. He’s just a wonderful guy. It’s not that the guys at the WWE — I just think they’re all kind of hanging onto their job because you never know. They’ve fired so many people that were an intricate part of my career when I was there. I don’t understand the rhyme or reason for it. The guys that did my documentary on Peacock, two of the guys that did it have been fired.” Flair went on to state that Tony Khan may be the greatest wrestling promoter of all time. In early 2026, Fightful Select reported that it was believed that Flair was still under contract to AEW.
summary: In an interview with NewsNation, Ric Flair described AEW President Tony Khan as a nice, generous and wonderful person who pays him out of respect despite Flair not having set duties. Flair contrasted the situation with WWE, noting that the company has fired people who played key roles in his career including two involved in his Peacock documentary. Per Fightful Select, Flair remains under contract with AEW into early 2026.

llm_long: Ric Flair has spoken about the generosity shown to him by Tony Khan. Flair has remained under contract with AEW since 2023 while making only rare appearances for the promotion.
Flair first joined AEW as part of Sting’s retirement tour and with a sponsorship for his “Wooooo! Energy” drink. Although that sponsorship deal has ended, he continues to be part of the company.
In an interview, Flair described Khan as a nice and generous person who continues to take care of him out of respect. He noted that Khan grew up watching him and called Khan a wonderful guy.
Flair contrasted his experience with AEW to the situation at WWE. He observed that many longtime WWE employees have been let go and expressed uncertainty about the decision-making process there.

At 77 years old, Flair stated that the main difference between WWE and AEW is WWE’s much longer history. He praised Khan’s skills as a promoter and suggested that Khan could be the greatest promoter of all time.
When asked about decision-making in wrestling, Flair said he believes Khan consults with a group of people before making choices, similar to practices at other companies.

body: Link @AEWonTV Ilja Dragunov’s AEW debut remains the biggest story to come out of the promotion’s WrestleDream PPV this past Sunday. But I bet the second most talked about thing that happened in Orlando, Florida’s Addition Financial Arena on Oct. 18… Tommaso Ciampa “wrestling” Andrade El Ídolo pants, and the pants kicking out . Denise Salcedo’s reaction to the spot pretty much mirrors my own. It was an amusing moment, made more so by the crowd’s enthusiastic buy in (no pun intended). Too much of the match focused on pants-related gags for my liking, but I acknowledge that Ciampa mocking and/or being frustrated with Andrade’s current Latin Lover schtick has been a part of their feud over the International title. And “psycho” is right there in Tommaso’s nickname, which makes snapping like this seem in character. “I felt like it was a little bit of him trying to have fun and play mind games like Orange Cassidy might do. In this case, we see Andrade play mind games with his opponent a lot and he’s always having fun, taking selfies during the match. I felt like Tommaso was trying to reverse the mind games on him. In this case, it’s not a legal fall, but I think he’s having fun. It’s fun within the context of the sport, but on the other hand, it’s important to remember that it is a spot and they’re both great wrestlers and I’m glad they got back to the wrestling after that… At least that’s how it seems, even after you account for the percentage of noise coming from those who just stoke tribalism around anything from either AEW or WWE that sparks debate among the wider community. The chatter’s continued since Sunday, and Jeff Jarrett’s sort-of defense of Ciampa vs. Pantalones has been generating another round of discussion. “I mean, ‘funny don’t draw money’ is such a situational [concept]. I just don’t think you can paint it as… look, creative is subjective. Did you hear the reaction? They loved it. So I just think — and I get it, to each his own. It’s [that sort of spot] not for everybody.” Double-J is on Tony Khan’s payroll, but he makes a good point about the crowd reaction. title: Identity of Person Who Told Paul Heyman to Cut His Ponytail
raw_title: Identity of Person Who Told Paul Heyman to Cut His Ponytail
summary_src: Paul Heyman’s son Jacob Heyman just took credit for one of the biggest changes to his father’s iconic look. According to Jacob, he’s the reason Paul finally said goodbye to the signature ponytail that wrestling fans had associated with him for years.
body: Speaking during HeymanHustleTV Presents: The Roundtable , Jacob was sitting alongside Cody Rhodes, Charlotte Flair and O’Shea Jackson Jr. as the group swapped stories about growing up with famous fathers. When the conversation turned to things about their parents that fans might not know, Jacob decided to drop some “breaking news.” “This is breaking news. I’ve never revealed this to the world, but, uh — I told him to cut the ponytail. That was my idea.” Jacob wasn’t backing away from the claim either. He doubled down and made it clear that getting rid of the ponytail was his suggestion. That prompted another surprised reaction from the table: “You’re the one.” Cody Rhodes then decided to have a little fun at Paul’s expense, joking that Jacob might actually deserve some gratitude for making it happen. “My dad’s played a heel on TV for — what was it? — 40 years. And he’s the biggest babyface of my life. He’s my hero. He’s my best friend. And I couldn’t ask for a better dad.” Paul may have originally imagined CM Punk taking the ponytail as a wrestling trophy, but Jacob is now taking some of the credit for its eventual disappearance. More than a decade later, fans finally have another piece of the story behind one of Heyman’s biggest changes in appearance. Andrew is one of TheSportster's Match Reviewers and has covered the best matches of superstars like Cody Rhodes, MJF, Bianca Belair and more. Sign in to your TheSportster account Jordynne Grace earned herself the reputation for being one of the best women’s wrestlers on the planet during her time outside of WWE , so there was a lot of anticipation for her arrival in the company back in 2025. Since then, she’s had a less than impressive NXT run and a main roster call-up that has led to pretty much nothing - she’s had just six matches on Friday Night SmackDown and hasn’t been seen in any capacity for four months. With reports emerging of WWE’s lack of creative plans for Grace, it spells potential disaster for her future in the promotion, and it may very well spell the end of time in WWE; and it is all down to Triple H 's creative. One thing is for sure - wasting the talents of Jordynne Grace is a major creative blunder from Triple H . Unfortunately for Grace, it appears plans may have changed and are no longer happening, as a new report from WrestleVotes via Fightful Select has revealed that the latest coming out of WWE is that she is not currently involved in creative plans. For someone as talented as Grace to not be involved in WWE’s creative plans for over six months, it is a very real problem. When it comes to creative plans in WWE, blame must fall on Triple H. Jordynne Grace is among the most talented and impressive in-ring workers in the company, and while she hasn’t quite yet shown serious qualities as a character, much of this comes from the fact that WWE didn’t give her much to go on when she arrived on SmackDown. She has still displayed a lot of potential since coming to WWE, having standout showdowns with the likes of Stephanie Vaquer & Giulia in NXT, impressing in her appearance at the 2025 Evolution PLE, and having highly regarded feuds against names in Roxanne Perez & Blake Monroe. title: Injury Update: Damian Priest Responds to R-Truth Blaming Him for Scary WWE SmackDown Injury
raw_title: Damian Priest Responds to R-Truth Blaming Him for Scary WWE SmackDown Injury
summary_src: Damian Priest has officially responded to R-Truth blaming him for the scary injury that stopped their WWE SmackDown match early. Priest isn’t accepting any responsibility either, joking that Truth nearly ended his own life just because he was so desperate to beat him.
body: Speaking on Off the Ropes , Priest was asked about Truth’s recent update following their October 16 match. Truth had shared a photo from a medical facility and joked that Priest “tried to kill” him, and apparently that accusation made its way back to Priest. “You know that guy tried to blame me? I’ve been told he posted some stupid thing that he’s good, but I tried to, like, end his life.” Damian Priest immediately turned the accusation back around on Truth. As far as he’s concerned, Truth was the one who took the risk that led to the match being stopped, all because he wanted the victory. “He tried to end his own just to win a match against me. And guys, it explains who he is.” The exchange comes after Truth was legitimately hurt during their October 16 SmackDown match. Truth landed awkwardly after delivering a missile dropkick from the top rope, leading the referee to check on him before stopping the match ahead of its planned finish. Truth finally addressed the situation on October 19 and thankfully had some reassuring news. He shared a photo of himself in a hospital gown in front of an MRI machine while thanking fans for all the messages he’d received . “I AM OK, Thank you ALL for your support, concerns and get well wishes , Wow, It truly feels amazing to feel and be loved I’m grateful for you all.” Naturally, Truth couldn’t give everyone a completely serious injury update. He decided to keep his storyline with Priest going by accusing his former tag team partner of nearly killing him before promising that he’ll eventually be back. “…On 10/16/2026 I almost passed away… Damien Priest tried to kill me,, I didn’t think he was ThAt serious… But ok, I’ll be back” Subhojeet Mukherjee Subhojeet Mukherjee has covered pro wrestling for over 20 years, delivering trusted news and backstage updates to fans around the world.

llm_long: A match on SmackDown between R-Truth and Damian Priest was halted after Truth appeared to suffer an injury. Truth attempted a missile dropkick from the turnbuckle and stayed on the mat afterward while remaining conscious and moving.

The referee checked on Truth and then stopped the match, signaling the X sign to indicate a legitimate injury. Priest left the ring and retrieved a steel chair, but the referee intervened to prevent further action.
Fraxiom came to the ring to check on Truth as Priest dropped the chair and exited the area. Reports confirmed that the match stoppage was legitimate.

The original plan for the match had Priest winning followed by a post-match attack that Fraxiom would interrupt to make the save. Truth previously suffered a torn quad during an NXT match in November 2022 that required surgery and kept him sidelined for more than a year.

title: New Data Shows Chad Gable is WWE’s Iron Man Champion
raw_title: New Data Shows Chad Gable is WWE’s Iron Man Champion
body: Gable won the title from Penta on night two of SummerSlam on August 2 at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis. Wrestling in front of his home state crowd, Gable reversed a second Mexican Destroyer attempt into the Ankle Lock and made Penta tap out. It was the first Intercontinental Championship win of his career. He earned that title shot the hard way. On the July 13 episode of Raw in Dallas, Gable won a number one contender’s gauntlet match that lasted more than 38 minutes, getting past Dominik Mysterio, Dragon Lee, Ethan Page, Je’Von Evans, Joe Hendry and Rusev. Since winning the title, Gable has defended it four times on Raw, which works out to a televised title match every 20 days. He beat Rey Mysterio on the August 17 episode in Buffalo, Dragon Lee on the September 14 episode in Mexico City, and Rey Fenix on the October 12 episode in Bossier City, Louisiana. Most recently, he retained in a triple threat against Dragon Lee and Rey Mysterio on the October 19 episode in San Diego. Those were not short matches either. According to Cagematch , the Fenix match ran 18 minutes and 35 seconds, the first Dragon Lee match went 15 minutes and 39 seconds, and the triple threat lasted 15 minutes and 35 seconds. The Mysterio match on August 17 went just over 13 minutes. The televised defenses are only part of the picture. Cagematch lists 13 more successful defenses at live events since SummerSlam, bringing his total to 17 without a loss. He defended against Ethan Page several times on WWE’s summer tour, beat Dominik Mysterio in both a singles match and a triple threat in Canada, and won four straight fatal four-way matches against Dragon Lee, Ethan Page and Penta on the South America tour in September. He also defended the title at two NXT live events in the Carolinas against Saquon Shugars and Uriah Connors, and won a three-way against Ethan Page and Je’Von Evans in Honolulu on October 16. The run is also the payoff to a long chase. Gable came up short against Sami Zayn in multiple Intercontinental Championship matches in 2024, including a match at Clash at the Castle in June that year that lasted more than 22 minutes. Two years later, he finally got the title in his home state. Gable’s reign is a throwback to the way a midcard title is supposed to be booked. He is defending the championship on television on a regular basis, he is doing it against a mix of veterans and younger stars, and the matches are getting real time on Raw. Four televised defenses in 80 days is a steady pace for a secondary title, and the live event defenses show he is putting the belt on the line nearly every time he works. It also matters who he is beating. Rey Mysterio, Dragon Lee and Rey Fenix are some of the best workers on Raw, and Gable’s style matches up well with each of them. Those matches have made the Intercontinental Championship feel like one of the more important parts of the show, which is what a strong champion should do.
summary: Gable won the title from Penta on night two of SummerSlam on August 2 at U.S. Wrestling in front of his home state crowd, Gable reversed a second Mexican Destroyer attempt into the Ankle Lock and made Penta tap out.

title: Is War Games Becoming A Trope, Moves That Shouldn’t Be Done From A Ladder, Aaa Is Fun And More
raw_title: IS WAR GAMES BECOMING A TROPE, MOVES THAT SHOULDN’T BE DONE FROM A LADDER, AAA IS FUN AND MORE - PWInsider.com
body: DMFirst Veer Game odds uden om ROFUS Jalwa Game Goa Game Raja Game MaanWin IS WAR GAMES BECOMING A TROPE, MOVES THAT SHOULDN’T BE DONE FROM A LADDER, AAA IS FUN AND MORE By Dave Scherer on 2026-10-20 10:00:00 You can send us questions for the PWInsider.com Q and A at pwinsider@gmail.com . Did the WWF ever give serious consideration to main eventing a PPV with a one-on-one match between Hulk Hogan and Ted DiBiase? Not that I am aware of. Hell, they never even put the Title on him so I doubt they were looking to do him vs. Hogan on PPV back then. AAA has great action and solid storytelling. Anyone looking to product a wrestling show could learn from that. It’s the backbone of what makes a company successful. If the wrestlers are going to do dives off the top of a ladder, wouldn't it be safer to have them stand with their feet perpendicular to the top step, rather than parallel? Ability level aside, the way Tiffany Stratton was balancing on the top of that ladder looked awkward and she didn't appear completely comfortable. They should do dives in a way where the ladder is as stable as possible. In Stratton’s case, it was not even close as the ladder was moving as she was launching. Also, rather that do any flip move that requires torque off of a ladder, splashes make much more sense to me. You leave the ladder and immediately go downward, rather than trying to get height off of it. Personally I agree with the reader that feels War Games has had its day. If it happens every year in November without fail then we know it's a crutch for the booking to go down the route of two groups feuding for months and needing War Games to settle it. The best Survivor Series event I ever saw was 2002 which also didn't have the traditional survivor matches. It had an amazing card and was capped off with the first elimination chamber. Would we not be better off with a less is more approach with all these matches? The fact that it’s done because it’s November is an issue when the creative leading up to it isn’t great, for sure. We don’t seem to notice that when the booking is strong and the fans want to see the talents in the cage. But I agree, right now it’s more of a trope and that should never be the case with a match like that. That’s all on creative. Sure, there are politics involved as well, but it comes down to whether Creative wants to pull the trigger or not. You can send us questions for the PWInsider.com Q and A at pwinsider@gmail.com .

body: Clark Connors says The Dogs originally had a different name in mind when the former Bullet Club War Dogs arrived in AEW. “When we came over here, we just became The Dogs, but we really wanted to pitch the name Raw Dogs, but I think there’s an issue with that whole Monday Night thing, but it sounds cool because we’re raw f—ing dogs, you know?” “But The Dogs also is a sick name. Prior to that, Connors and Finlay lost an AEW World Tag Team Championship match to Matt and Nick Jackson, the Young Bucks, at AEW Collision Grand Slam France on October 6. title: Injury Update: Damian Priest Underwent Medical Procedures After Dealing With Multiple Injuries
raw_title: Damian Priest Underwent Medical Procedures After Dealing With Multiple Injuries
summary_src: Damian Priest has been wrestling with a beat-up body for a long time, but things are finally starting to turn around. The WWE star says he’s feeling “a lot better” after quietly undergoing procedures to ease his pain — and he somehow never took a day off while doing it.
body: Speaking on Off the Ropes , Priest was asked how his body is holding up these days. His immediate answer was basically what you’d expect from someone who has spent years getting slammed into a wrestling ring for a living. “Well, we’re never okay — that’s what we do. No bitching and moaning. I don’t like talking about how my body is. I’m not the only one banged up — my opponent is banged up too.” “But I’m feeling a lot better. I got some procedures done and never took a day off. I got some stuff done to ease the pain, and I feel a lot better.” Priest didn’t get into exactly what those procedures were, so he’s keeping those details to himself for now. What he did say is that fans should already be able to notice a difference in how he’s looking and moving. “I think people can see it visually, and I’m training daily and getting back to the shape I used to be in.” It’s not just his body that’s feeling different either. Priest admitted he’s in a much better headspace now and actually had to check himself after realizing he wasn’t approaching his career with the same positive mentality he normally prides himself on. “I’m training better and in a better headspace too. For someone who thinks positively about my career, I did the opposite and had to check myself a bit.” That’s a pretty big turnaround from what Priest revealed back in December 2025. At the time, he admitted his body was taking a beating, with multiple shoulder tears along with problems involving his knees and back . Priest was so determined to keep going that WWE actually had to make him slow things down. Even then, he made it clear that surgery would always be his last resort because he’d rather rehab, get treatment and stay in the game. “If I don’t need surgery, I won’t do it. I’ll figure it out — rehab, treatment, whatever it takes — just keep me in the game.” Almost a year later, that approach seems to have Priest feeling much closer to himself again. He’s still not pretending his body is magically 100%, but after procedures, daily training and a mental reset, things sound a whole lot better than they did last December. summary_src: AEW star MJF will be donning a referee shirt when he appears for Create-A-Pro Wrestling this weekend. The indie promotion has announced that MJF will serve as the special guest referee for a 10-man tag match at its Saturday, October 24 show in Long Island, New York.
body: AEW star MJF will be donning a referee shirt when he appears for Create-A-Pro Wrestling this weekend. The indie promotion has announced that MJF will serve as the special guest referee for a 10-man tag match at its Saturday, October 24 show in Long Island, New York. It will pit teams managed by Road Dogg and (indie manager) Sidney Bakabella against each other. Team Road Dogg has Create-A-Pro co-owner Brian Myers on the team, along with Anthony Greene, Aaron Rourke, Bobby Orlando & Nick Robles. Bakabella’s team has Leo Sparrow, Dante Drago, Bryce Donovan, Vinny Scalice & TJ Crawford. Create-A-Pro is MJF’s original home promotion and where he trained to become a wrestler. He was added to this event as a make-good after Billy Gunn had to cancel his bookings due to “contractual obligations.” Along with refereeing, MJF will be available for a meet and greet. “Unfortunately due to contractual obligations, Billy Gunn will no longer be appearing at #CAPBaseBrawl this Saturday in North Merrick, NY,” Create-A-Pro announced on Tuesday . “Road Dogg will still be in attendance. Any pre purchased Meet & Greet package for Billy Gunn or the New Age Outlaws will be refunded “As a replacement we will present a special Meet & Greet with the real AEW World Champion @The_MJF! We will also be adding a Meet & Greet with AEW announcer Alicia Atout! A show ticket must be purchased to attend all Meet & Greets.” Brookside Educational Center is hosting the show, which is a fundraiser for Merrick Bellmore Little League. title: Carlie Bravo Claims ROH Has More Hungry Talent Than AEW

summary_src: Carlie Bravo sticks up for Ring Of Honor. Competing alongside Shane Taylor Promotions, Carlie Bravo has been a essential part of the promotion since 2023. Pushing back against the online criticism, Bravo recently spoke with Wrestling Republic and said that ROH has more killers than AEW does.
body: Competing alongside Shane Taylor Promotions, Carlie Bravo has been a essential part of the promotion since 2023. Pushing back against the online criticism, Bravo recently spoke with Wrestling Republic and said that ROH has more killers than AEW does. “I love Ring Of Honor. I love Ring Of Honor. We all see the bullshit sometimes, the negative bullshit that gets spoken about it. But, I think Ring Of Honor got more killers than AEW does and in a sense of hungry. People are hungry. You can’t tell me Red Velvet not hungry, you know what I’m saying? You can’t tell me Dalton Castle & The Outrunners not fucking hungry. Swirl, Infantry, STP, we got people on there that are freaking monsters that are waiting at the gym to go freaking crazy. Adam Priest, you got people that are just waiting to get a moment to go. I think that hunger pushes a lot. We take a lot of pride in Ring Of Honor, you know what I’m saying? We went from one Death Before Dishonor, we had the titles the whole time, then we the lost the belts at the next one. I love that, you know what I’m saying? I love that we can give back to that company like that and make it not just what it was but what it could possibly be.” Bravo continued by putting over more names on the ROH roster. “At the last ROH taping, it was AR Fox versus Bandido. Like, what are we talking about? That’s a main event anywhere. I saw Hechicero and Bandido and it blew my freaking mind. Konosuke Takeshita and Bandido blew my mind. We had the last couple television champions, Nick Wayne, Lio Rush, Action Andretti, we got killers. I mentioned the tag team belts, we got Mistico and Mascara Dorada as the tag champs. Before that, me, Cap, and Shane was the Trios Champions. Then, Dalton and The Outrunners was doing it. Now, Lethal and Swirl got it. Deonna Purrazzo, women’s pure champion. Longest reigning men’s pure wrestling champion of all time, Lee Moriarty talking that wave. Who is fucking with that roster?” ROH Final Battle was recently announced for December. title: Cody Rhodes Calls Out People Who Credit Dusty Rhodes for His Work Ethic
raw_title: Cody Rhodes Calls Out People Who Credit Dusty Rhodes for His Work Ethic
summary_src: Cody Rhodes is tired of people assuming his work ethic comes from being Dusty Rhodes’ son. The WWE star says he’s spent years hearing about the massive shadow his father left behind, but the person who actually deserves credit for teaching him to work hard is his mother.
body: Speaking during HeymanHustleTV Presents: The Roundtable , Cody discussed growing up as the child of a wrestling legend alongside Charlotte Flair, Jacob Heyman and O’Shea Jackson Jr. That’s when he pushed back on the idea that he’s constantly working because he feels some responsibility to live up to Dusty’s legacy. “I’m not working hard because Dusty Rhodes told me to work hard. And I’m not even working hard — it’s unrelated to him now. It’s put out there as like, ‘Oh, you got that big, you know, you got the boots to fill, the shadow,’ like all that.” “It’s like, ‘Oh, you know, you’re Dusty’s kid. You know, you’re Cube’s kid. You know, you’re Ric’s kid. You got — you know, you’re Paul’s kid. You got to do more than everybody else.’ Fuck, I was already going to do more than everybody else.” “My work ethic doesn’t come from my father. It comes from my mom. She don’t get no credit.” Cody also made it clear that Dusty himself wasn’t the person putting all that pressure on him. According to Cody, his father never sat him down and demanded that he surpass what he had accomplished in wrestling. “My dad never told me that. People on the outside told me that, you know. I was never told to like, ‘All right, you got to, you know, top me,’ or like, ‘You got to be better than this.’” Cody isn’t distancing himself from Dusty’s legacy, but he clearly wants people to separate that legacy from his own drive to succeed. For him, constantly turning everything he accomplishes into another comparison with his father can eventually make an incredible family connection feel more like a burden. body: 0 WWE ‘s Drew McIntyre details how Triple H helped him with the “I prayed for this, and it happened” promo. McIntyre said he had something more extreme on his mind for the promo, something he said would’ve offended a lot of people. However, WWE Chief Content Officer Triple H helped to tone it down a bit. “I knew, talking to Triple H during the day, that this was going to be so good. I had an idea, and it was too much. It would have offended a lot of people, which I’m very good at. He helped me reel it back, and then Hunter himself came out with the line, which I ended up using. I had such an extreme version, and he dialed it back, and the way he said it and the cadence of how it’s to be said. He said it like that, and I got so excited,” Drew McIntyre began. Drew McIntyre said Triple H toned down the promo and showed him how to deliver it. He then used the same tone while cutting it in the ring. “He’s obviously a savant when it comes to this business. The things sometimes he comes up with, I went, ‘How do you think of that, Triple H?’ That is genius. That is going to be so good. And I know as a fan I would lose my mind. Didn’t think I’d be seeing it to this day for everything, no matter if it’s sports or outside of wrestling. It’s constantly me pointing, ‘I prayed for this, and it happened,'” McIntyre continued. The post Drew McIntyre Reveals Triple H Was Behind His Infamous CM Punk WWE Promo appeared first on Wrestlezone .

title: Bully Ray Wants Naomi In Bloodline Storyline
raw_title: Bully Ray Comments On Potential Naomi WWE Return, Pairing With The Bloodline
summary_src: WWE Hall of Famer Bully Ray commented on Naomi's potential return to "WWE Raw" to join the Bloodline in their feud against 946.
body: On " Busted Open Radio ," Bully Ray said he believes Naomi's return is imminent. Despite the star being on the run of her career before announcing her pregnancy last summer , the Hall of Famer doesn't believe she should jump right back into the women's division, not while 946 is terrorizing the Bloodline. "To me, that's very flat. You can always go back to that one day," Bully Ray said. "We know that Naomi and Jimmy are married. This entire Bloodline thing is about family. She is a part of the family. I want her involved, but when is the right day to bring her back?" Bully Ray and co-host Dave LaGreca pondered that question, with LaGreca wondering if she makes her big return at WarGames itself. Bully Ray said he thinks it needs to be before the event, and it needs to be a dramatic moment. "I want to see a moment in time where Jaida Parker is going to do something really bad to one of the Bloodline members," he said. "Technically, it should be Jimmy. The whole blowtorch idea, I know it's preposterous and they'll never do it, but can you imagine if the 946 is holding down Jimmy. He's on his knees. They got his arms. He can't move, and here comes Jaida Parker with a blowtorch or whatever [and out comes Naomi.]"

body: "The road to recovery continues," Sihra said. "X-Rays show my lungs are back to normal and there is very little air bubbles left in my chest-cavity from the collapsed lung. I still can't fly at the moment, however, I should be cleared soon. Thank you all for your continued love and support." Sihra was transported to a hospital for treatment of the collapsed lung. The incident occurred while competing for Pure Power Wrestling in Lethbridge, Alberta, where the duo known as The Bollywood Boyz won the promotion's tag team championships.
In a recent social media update, Sihra reported that his lungs have returned to normal according to X-rays. He noted minimal air bubbles remain in his chest cavity from the injury.

The Bollywood Boyz previously performed in WWE under the names Sunil Singh and Samir Singh. They debuted in the 2016 Cruiserweight Classic, appeared across NXT, 205 Live, and the main roster as allies of Jinder Mahal, and were released in 2021.

title: U.S. Orders Diplomatic Personnel Out of Saudi Arabia Ahead of WWE Crown Jewel 2026
raw_title: U.S. Orders Diplomatic Personnel Out of Saudi Arabia Ahead of WWE Crown Jewel 2026
summary_src: WWE’s Crown Jewel situation in Saudi Arabia just got a whole lot more uncomfortable. With the company supposed to bring its roster to Riyadh on November 7, the U.S.
body: The move came on October 21, and the timing couldn’t be much worse for WWE. Reuters reported that the State Department ordered the departures because of increased security threats connected to the Iran-aligned Houthis in Yemen. There were initially even more alarming reports about how far the order went. AFP cited a diplomatic source claiming all American embassy staff and their families had been ordered to leave Saudi Arabia, while families of embassy personnel were also being ordered out of several other Gulf countries. “All American staff and their families have been ordered to depart from the US embassy in Saudi Arabia.” Reuters described the confirmed U.S. action more narrowly, reporting an ordered departure involving non-emergency personnel and family members in Saudi Arabia. Either way, the U.S. government is now actively moving people out of the country while WWE is preparing to move an entire wrestling production into it. None of this means WWE has canceled Crown Jewel. The November 7 show remains on the schedule, and there hasn’t been an announcement from WWE saying the event is being relocated or called off. Still, the clock is ticking pretty fast now. WWE has a little over two weeks before Crown Jewel, and with the U.S. pulling diplomatic personnel and families out while attacks continue, the question of whether WWE can safely get everyone into Riyadh and back home is only getting bigger. Subhojeet Mukherjee Subhojeet Mukherjee has covered pro wrestling for over 20 years, delivering trusted news and backstage updates to fans around the world.
summary: The latest: none of this means WWE has canceled Crown Jewel. WWE has a little over two weeks before Crown Jewel, and with the U.S. pulling diplomatic personnel and families out while attacks continue.
llm_long: King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh reopened on Sunday after being closed since the previous Saturday. Questions continue about whether WWE will proceed with Crown Jewel scheduled for November 7 in the city.

Saudi coalition officials reported the airport had been targeted 20 times during the month, resulting in 17 deaths and 333 injuries. Conflicting reports persist, with some outlets still listing the airport as closed.
Flight data showed 113 arrivals scheduled for Sunday, mostly domestic, and at least one international passenger flight landed. Many international airlines continue to suspend service to Riyadh.

Several major sporting events in Saudi Arabia have been canceled or postponed amid increased attacks by the Iran-backed Houthi rebel group. The Six Kings Slam tennis tournament was delayed from October to December, and the UCI Urban Cycling World Championships set for November were canceled.
The Canelo Alvarez versus Christian Mbilli boxing match planned for October 31 is still expected to take place. WWE has not announced any changes to Crown Jewel as of the latest reports.

The second reign started on Nov. 23, 2014, when Bella beat AJ Lee at Survivor Series. Flair ended it at Night of Champions on Sept. 20, 2015. No reign in the Divas Championship's history lasted longer. The Bella Twins attacked partner Paige after Fatal Influence beat the trio in a six-woman tag match at SummerSlam on Aug. first. body: With WWE Crown Jewel scheduled to take place in Riyadh on November 7, the U.S. State Department has ordered nonessential diplomatic personnel and their family members to leave Saudi Arabia The news comes amid escalating attacks by the Iran-backed Houthi rebel group in the region. Multiple upcoming events in Riyadh have been canceled or postponed. The U.S. Embassy in Riyadh also issued a new security alert Wednesday warning of further attacks. The alert also states that King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh remains suspended. Security Alert: U.S. Mission Saudi Arabia (October 21, 2026) Iranian-supported Houthis have engaged in hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including attacks on civilian airports and other critical infrastructure resulting in civilian casualties and severe travel disruptions. The hostilities have the potential to escalate rapidly beyond that immediate area. U.S. citizens are reminded to follow the guidance of national alerts released by Saudi Arabia’s Civil Defense via cellular broadcast. U.S. government employees working in Saudi Arabia require special authorization from Chief of Mission to use any airport in Saudi Arabia following recent missile and UAV attacks on airports in the Kingdom. Operations at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh remain suspended. King Abdulaziz International Airport in Jeddah and King Fahd International Airport in Dammam are operational with some delays and cancellations. U.S. citizens should be aware of potential attacks on airports, airspace closures, flight cancellations, and travel disruptions. Please take extreme caution if you choose to use airports in Saudi Arabia. We recommend checking your flight departure status directly with the airline and with the airport. Reuters reported on Wednesday that the US State Department was preparing to issue an order to nonessential diplomatic personnel and their families to leave Saudi Arabia. State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott later clarified the news on X writing that the order applied for non-essential employees and their families in Saudi Arabia only. “The U.S. Department of State issued an ordered departure for non-emergency U.S. government employees and their family members in Saudi Arabia only. Iranian-supported Houthis have increasingly engaged in hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including attacks on civilian airports and other critical infrastructure resulting in civilian casualties and severe travel disruptions. The safety and security of Department personnel and their families remain our highest priority, and we will continue to take all necessary steps to protect and support them.” As of this writing, WWE has not announced any plans to postpone, reschedule or relocate Crown Jewel. body: With AEW WrestleDream now in the history books this past Saturday, Ilja Dragunov made his AEW debut when AEW broadcaster Renee Paquette introduced him and he took a lap around the ring. Following his debut, Dragunov will be wrestling his first AEW match against "Speedball" Mike Bailey. While nothing else has been announced for tonight's show as of writing, WrestleDream also saw Will Ospreay retain his AEW World Championship in the inaugural Clockwork Carnage Match. Mercedes Mone also retained her AEW Women's World Championship against Thekla, The Young Bucks retained their AEW World Tag Team Championship against The Don Callis Family's Kyle Fletcher and Kevin Knight, and Persephone successfully defended her TBS Championship in a Four-Way Match. Andrade and Jon Moxley also successfully defended their respective National Championship and Continental Championship against Tommaso Ciampa and Mark Davis, while "Hangman" Adam Page, Brody King, and Bandido dethroned New Level and Swerve Strickland as AEW World Trios Champions and Nick Wayne defeated Jericho.

title: Damian Priest Dismisses R-Truth's Injury Post
raw_title: Damian Priest Responds To R-Truth's Social Media Post After WWE SmackDown Injury Scare
summary_src: Damian Priest fires back at R-Truth. On the October 16 episode of WWE SmackDown, Priest faced off with R-Truth in a singles bout. The match was called off by the referee after R-Truth landed awkwardly while hitting Priest with a missile dropkick.
body: On the October 16 episode of WWE SmackDown, Priest faced off with R-Truth in a singles bout. The match was called off by the referee after R-Truth landed awkwardly while hitting Priest with a missile dropkick. A few days later, Truth took to social media to let fans know that he is fine. In the same post, he jokingly accused Priest of trying to kill him during the match. In a new interview with WWE Radio’s Off The Ropes , Damian Priest scoffed at the post. “Can you believe this guy is trying to blame me? I’ve been told that he posted some stupid thing about that, he’s good but that I tried to end his life. He tried to end his own just trying to win a match against me. The guy is — it explains who he is.” Fightful will update fans when more is known about R-Truth and his return to TV. Check out the current lineup for the October 23 episode of SmackDown by clicking here. If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.
summary: R-Truth suffered an awkward landing on a missile dropkick during his SmackDown singles match with Damian Priest on October 16, prompting the referee to stop the bout. Truth later posted on social media that he is fine while jokingly claiming Priest tried to kill him. In an interview with WWE Radio’s Off The Ropes, Priest laughed off the accusation and said Truth was the one who risked his own well-being trying to win.

Truth later posted on social media that he is fine while jokingly claiming Priest tried to kill him. In an interview with WWE Radio’s Off The Ropes, Priest laughed off the accusation and said Truth was the one who risked his own well-being trying to win.

llm_long: A match on SmackDown between R-Truth and Damian Priest was halted after Truth appeared to suffer an injury. Truth attempted a missile dropkick from the turnbuckle and stayed on the mat afterward while remaining conscious and moving.

The referee checked on Truth and then stopped the match, signaling the X sign to indicate a legitimate injury. Priest left the ring and retrieved a steel chair, but the referee intervened to prevent further action.
Fraxiom came to the ring to check on Truth as Priest dropped the chair and exited the area. Reports confirmed that the match stoppage was legitimate.

The original plan for the match had Priest winning followed by a post-match attack that Fraxiom would interrupt to make the save. Truth previously suffered a torn quad during an NXT match in November 2022 that required surgery and kept him sidelined for more than a year.
