body: 0 AEW star Ilja Dragunov has explained why he rejected WWE’s offer. He also confirmed that WWE wanted to keep him. The Russian wrestler recently made his AEW debut at WrestleDream. Dragunov’s arrival followed weeks of mysterious AEW teaser videos. Following his debut, AEW has now booked him against Speedball Mike Bailey. Their match is scheduled for this week’s Dynamite. Speaking on The Ariel Helwani Show , Dragunov discussed his WWE departure. He revealed that his decision came after careful consideration. WWE wanted him to stay, but he wanted change. When asked whether he knew his April match was his last, Dragunov said, “No, absolutely not. And everything I’ve got to tell about that is also not very hot or very exciting. I didn’t know at that time that I was leaving. I was just waiting.” “Again, I’m a person — I love what I do. I want to compete; I want to work. I want to do this and this and that. And it just got a got a little stuck as it was, but it’s nothing new to anybody. It was pretty obvious. And the time just passed by, and then I reached the expiration of my contract.” He also discussed wanting to explore different creative opportunities. “And like I already said after the show at the press conference at WrestleDream, I felt over time that, ‘Okay with how everything is working out and how I’m feeling.’ Because I do, I make a lot of things depending on how I feel about it. I always had the courage to do so. I feel it is time to breathe some new fresh air.” Dragunov confirmed WWE had no intention of releasing him. He said, “Yeah, there that was definitely — there was no intention of the company to let me go.” However, Dragunov explained that several factors influenced his decision. He explained, “It was accumulation of a lot of things. It was an accumulation of — of course the offering, because we all at the end of the day it’s a business. But also, it’s definitely based also on my feeling of like, ‘How do I want to work creatively? Do I need a scenery change? Is the scenery change something where I can see myself stay for like forever?'” Dragunov believes wrestling has changed significantly over time. He now sees more opportunities outside the company. He continued, “Because you’ve got to consider all the factors. Like, I spent the most of my twenties in WWE. That’s a very, very long time. And the landscape in this beautiful business changed. title: On the Record: Swerve Strickland Speaks On Possibility of WWE-AEW Crossover Event
raw_title: Swerve Strickland Addresses Possibility of WWE-AEW Crossover Event
body: 0 Swerve Strickland has explained why he believes a WWE-AEW crossover event is unlikely to happen during his lifetime. In an interview with Billboard , the AEW star discussed the dream matches such a show could deliver but pointed to a major obstacle that goes beyond what wrestlers want inside the ring. Strickland was direct when asked whether the two rival promotions could ever work together on a joint event. According to Strickland, the biggest issue would be protecting each promotion’s top stars and deciding who comes out looking stronger. He compared WWE’s approach to the NFL protecting its identity, arguing that control and marketing would make a crossover difficult to arrange. “It’s control. It’s all about marketing. It’s like the NFL, WWE has to protect their shield,” Strickland explained. He added that WWE would be unlikely to let AEW wrestlers “look better and be better” than its own talent. Strickland named Oba Femi, Gunther, Roman Reigns, and Cody Rhodes as examples of WWE stars whose presentations would need protecting. He also believes a joint event involving the women would create similar complications, mentioning Rhea Ripley, Liv Morgan, and Chelsea Green. One potential matchup he highlighted was Seth Rollins against Will Ospreay. Strickland called it a generational contest, but questioned how the companies could agree on a winner without worrying about who would benefit more. “You wanna see Seth [Rollins] and Ospreay. That’s the generational thing, but who do you protect? Who has the leverage?” he asked. The situation looks different from the wrestlers’ perspective, according to Strickland. He said he is friends with WWE stars Carmelo Hayes, Je’Von Evans, and Oba Femi, and would welcome the chance to compete against them without being concerned about the result. “Us in the locker room, we just wanna have these matches,” he said. “I don’t care who wins. Double DQs. I don’t care.” The post Swerve Strickland Addresses Possibility of WWE-AEW Crossover Event appeared first on Wrestlezone .

body: The first Blood and Guts match of 2026 has been made official. After scoring a tag win over Copeland and Ospreay, Knight and Fletcher looked to inflict more damage alongside their Callis Family teammates. In for the save were the Bucks, Allin, and, appearing for the first time since suffering an injury at All Out, Borden. After clearing the Family from the ring, Borden got on the mic and called out the faction for Blood and Guts. Last year’s Blood and Guts event featured the first-ever women’s match, taking place alongside the annual men’s bout. It’s unclear at the moment if the women’s match will return next month.

title: Pro wrestlers mourn the passing of AEW star PAC
raw_title: Pro wrestlers mourn the passing of AEW star PAC
body: Professional wrestler Benjamin Satterley, who went by the ring name PAC, passed away at the age of 40 over the weekend, according to All Elite Wrestling . News of Satterley's death was quite sudden, as he had previously wrestled the opening match of AEW's All Out pay-per-view on Sept. 26, and AEW announced his passing the following day. Satterley's passing also coincided with the celebration of life ceremony for fellow AEW wrestler "The Butcher" Andy Williams, who tragically passed on Sept. 5, 2026 . Satterley, born in Newcastle upon Tyne, England, started his wrestling career in 2004, traveling across the world and making his name in promotions such as Ring of Honor, CHIKARA, and Dragongate. Known for his high-flying style, raw athleticism, and technical in-ring ability, Satterley was often called "the man that gravity forgot." He was one of the best to ever do it. Before signing with AEW in 2019, Satterley joined WWE's developmental program NXT in 2012 under the ring name Adrian Neville, where he would become one-half of the company's inaugural NXT Tag Team Champions and a one-time NXT Champion. In 2015, he was called up to WWE's main roster, shortening his name to Neville and becoming a two-time Cruiserweight Champion. After leaving WWE, Satterley would join AEW under his original ring name, PAC. Nicknamed "The Bastard," Satterley became the company's inaugural International Champion (originally called the All-Atlantic Championship), a two-time World Trios Champion, and at one point held both titles to become AEW's first double champion. Outside of his achievements in WWE, AEW, and beyond, Satterley was a beloved figure in pro wrestling, both by fans and his fellow wrestlers. His Death Riders stablemate Marina Shafir shared an emotional, heartbreaking tribute to Satterley at an indie event. "Listen. He was our bastard. I was just holding this man yesterday," she said. "He was the best. He was the fucking best. You know why? Because he knew himself. He was just so modest about how fascinating he was." title: A History-Making One-Off? — AEW Grand Slam France
raw_title: AEW Grand Slam France: A History-Making One-Off? | Column
body: For over fifteen years, no non-European pro-wrestling promotions other than WWE had ever staged a show in France. Until now. On Tuesday, October 6, 2026, All Elite Wrestling held AEW Grand Slam France, a double TV taping of Dynamite and Collision, at the Adidas Arena in Paris. It marked AEW’s first venture in continental Europe – excluding its presence at Gamescom 2022 in Germany. France in particular has always been underserved by American promotions. Now, almost twenty years later, after two RAWs, two Smackdowns and two PLEs held by WWE in the country with great success in only two years, AEW seems willing to get in the market. But will Grand Slam France end up just being a one-night-only affair? Shown on Warner TV Next, a small cable TV channel airing reruns of anime and comic-book superheroes, and now on the MyAEW platform, AEW doesn’t have much of a presence or reach in the French market compared to WWE. Available on Netflix since January 1, 2026, the TKO company surely has the advantage, built on a monopoly dating back to the late 1980s on the paid-network TV channel Canal+ and then on the major cable TV channel, AB1. But AEW Grand Slam France was about testing the waters. AEW went a notch above what WWE typically does to promote its first entry in the market. The previous Saturday, several AEW stars – including Jeff Jarrett returning to France – were booked by the upstart KHAO promotion just outside Paris, with flyers given to spectators to promote AEW Grand Slam France. And on Tuesday, ‘Speedball’ Mike Bailey was given a spot to teach a show-host the Boston Crab on the morning-show Télématin, an institution of public network TV – which came back to the Québécois’ ears during its match taped for Collision against Lee Moriarty. WWE never did that, especially on a news day marked by a massive strike by high-school students. Closing the generous 15-match double-taping (including the first-ever showings in France by international stars like Kazuchika Okada, Darby Allin, and Hangman Page), Jon Moxley and Claudio Castagnioli tried to rally up the crowd one last time in an effort to keep the enthusiasm going and convince AEW’s boss, Tony Khan, seated backstage to try and bring its roster back someday (maybe as a stopover for future All In London weeks or European tours). The crowd seemed hopeful. Some even rejoiced with the Death Riders in their usual huddle at ringside while others in the bleachers flashed their smartphone lights in tribute to their fallen comrade, the late PAC. But even with Tony Khan’s generosity and excitement, business remains business. And with only the next AEW Dynasty and its following Dynamite scheduled in Liverpool in February 2027, there’s no indication for the AEW Grand Slam international brand to grace France – or even continental Europe – once again. body: Swerve Strickland has opened up in detail and compared his in-ring ability to WWE legends. In a recent interview with Billboard’s Carl Lamarre , Strickland reflected on his career and compared himself to several WWE legends. “ Not me being a caricature of hip-hop, and not me being a caricature of a Black wrestler. I’m being me. My success in pro-wrestling is genuinely because of my ability in the ring ,” Strickland said when asked what he would like to be remembered as. “ It’s not because they’re trying to push an agenda, it’s because I perform at a really, really high level — probably the highest level you could see of a Black wrestler in the history of the game. “ You have a lot of guys that truly became household names, like the Mark Henrys, Booker Ts, Ron Simmons, and Dwayne [Johnsons] — but you can rarely ever say they were the best wrestler on that show. They had to compete with Eddie Guerrero, Owen Hart, Bret [Hart], Shawn [Michaels]. Great in-ring technical wrestlers ,” Strickland further added. The former World Champion further continued and claimed that, similar to them, he competes at the highest level with everybody. “ Me and Okada. Me and Kenny [Omega]. Me and [Will] Ospreay. Me and Hangman [Adam Page]. The very, very best I hang with every last one of them. That’s why I’ve always approached hip-hop the same way. I have to be pure and genuinely me as possible and get there because of actual ability rather than just co-signs. ” Strickland, a former AEW Trios Champion with The New Level, recently lost his title at AEW WrestleDream 2026. title: On the Record: AEW's Jeff Jarrett Explains How RevPro Match Came Together At The Last Minute
raw_title: AEW's Jeff Jarrett Explains How RevPro Match Came Together At The Last Minute
body: "When I got off the elevator up where we were doing it, Will Ospreay was walking out of an office with a box of something, and I said, 'Hey, Will, you got a second?' He said, 'Yeah.' And I said, 'I've got this show and this show, blah, blah, blah.' And I said, but tonight, RevPro, it's right there because our hotel literally next door is Wembley Arena, and right around the corner is Wembley Stadium. RevPro's there. I said, 'Do you think you can kind of give them a heads up or ask them? I'd like to walk in the back door and I want to kind of check this out.'" "Will texts me. I didn't respond back because I'm doing the [event]. Then he calls in the middle of it. I'm like, 'Oh man, something must be going on.' He said, 'I got a question for you. Do you have your gear?' And I said, 'Well, you know the old-timer saying, 'Does a carpenter leave work without his hammer and nails and tools?' And he said, 'Well, I just talked to Andy [Quildan] and he wants to know, would you be interested?' It literally all came down around the two or three or four o'clock hour on Saturday." Jarrett was added to the Undisputed British Heavyweight title #1 Contendership Gauntlet match and said that he had a lot of fun doing it.

title: Masatora Yasuda Replaces Injured El Desperado in NJPW Super Jr. Tag League
raw_title: El Desperado out of NJPW Jr. Tag League due to injury, Masatora Yasuda to replace him and team with Mistico
summary_src: El Desperado has withdrawn from this year's NJPW Super Jr. Tag League, which is scheduled to begin this Saturday.
body: Just days before NJPW is scheduled to begin their 2026 Super Jr. Tag League, a change has been made to the lineup. El Desperado has withdrawn from the tour, NJPW confirmed on Thursday morning. The promotional vet was recently diagnosed with spinal canal stenosis and a hernia. In a statement to NJPW, Desperado described beginning to feel a “pins and needles” tingling sensation around his left glute around March. The discomfort turned into pain by June, causing him to wake up in the middle of the night. While he planned to finish up his 2026 schedule before taking time away, Desperado says he struggles to “stand, walk or even sit upright for long periods of time,” and thus has decided to step away from action. Desperado was scheduled to kick off tournament action this weekend alongside CMLL’s Mistico. Taking his place will be Young Lion Masatora Yasuda. The short-notice spot is a huge opportunity for the 27-year-old NJPW trainee. Appearing in his first-ever NJPW tournament (excluding the Young Lion Cup), Yasuda will spend weeks working alongside Mexico’s biggest star currently. Assuming the matchup schedule doesn’t change due to the substitution, Yasuda and Mistico are expected to face Kuukai and Master Wato as part of Saturday’s card in Saitama.
summary: El Desperado has withdrawn from the 2026 NJPW Super Jr. Tag League after being diagnosed with spinal canal stenosis and a hernia. The veteran began experiencing tingling and pain in his left glute in March that worsened by June, ultimately forcing him to step away as he struggles with basic movements. Masatora Yasuda will now team with Mistico in the tournament, marking the 27-year-old Young Lion's first NJPW tournament appearance outside of the Young Lion Cup.

title: First Matches Set For AEW Full Gear
raw_title: First Matches Official For AEW Full Gear
body: AEW has announced the first few matches for AEW Full Gear, making them official on this week’s AEW Dynamite. It was announced on Wednesday night’s show that Wrathlander will get their AEW Women’s World Tag Team Championship match against The Brawling Birds at Full Gear. Harley Cameron and Willow Nightingale beat the Sisters of Sin and Divine Dominion to secure the title shot that they were originally supposed to get at AEW WrestleDream before Jamie Hayter was pulled due to not being cleared. In addition, it was announced that Mark Davis and Jake Doyle will get their shot at The Young Bucks at Full Gear. The two crushed the Bucks in a title eliminator on Dynamite. Among the not-yet-confirmed matches, Swerve Strickland asked for a rematch for him and The New Level against Hangman Page and Brodido for the AEW World Trios Championships they lost at WrestleDream. Page agreed, but turned down Strickland’s proposal to make it a Texas Deathmatch. The Trios Title match has yet to be officially announced as set. And finally, Mercedes Mone cut a promo in the ring asking who was next for her. Marina Shafir came out to the ring and stepped up, challenging Mone to a title match. That match has not been made official, and it was not specifically noted to be for Full Gear as of yet. AEW Full Gear takes place on November 14th from the Mortgage Matchup Center in Phoenix, Arizona and airs live on PPV. The official card thus far is: * AEW Women’s World Tag Team Championship Match: The Brawling Birds vs. Wrathlander. * AEW World Tag Team Championship Match: The Young Bucks vs. Jake Doyle & Mark Davis. * AEW World Trios Championship Match: Hangman Page & Brodido vs. Swerve Strickland & The New Level. * AEW Women’s World Championship Match: Mercedes Mone vs. Marina Shafir.

title: Ric Flair Praises Tony Khan's Generosity at AEW

body: The “Nature Boy” Ric Flair signed a multi-year deal with All Elite Wrestling in late 2023. Flair has appeared numerous times on AEW programming, most notably was his inclusion in Sting’s Retirement Match at AEW Revolution 2024. His last official appearance on AEW Television came on the May 17th, 2025 episode of AEW Collision when he participated in the company’s tribute to Steve “Mongo” McMichael, who had recently passed away after a long battle with ALS. Ric Flair was recently interviewed by Biff Poggi for News Nation , and discussed AEW President/Owner Tony Khan and working for All Elite Wrestling. Flair says that Tony Khan may be the greatest promoter of all time and generous to a fault. He added that Tony is a nice guy, has a learjet and a beautiful girlfriend. He then reminds us again that Tony is generous, while pointing out that he works for him and doesn’t do anything. “ He’s got that Learjet. He’s got a beautiful girlfriend. He’s a nice guy. He’s generous. I work for him. I work for him and I don’t do anything. I think he takes care of me out of respect for me. He grew up on me. raw_title: Ilja Dragunov Wins AEW In-Ring Debut in Dynamite Main Event
body: 0 Ilja Dragunov made an immediate impact in AEW by defeating Mike Bailey in his in-ring debut on the October 21 episode of AEW Dynamite . Both men started the match by testing each other with grappling moves. Dragunov took Bailey down with a waistlock, but Bailey countered with a wristlock before locking in a waistlock of his own. Dragunov backed Bailey into the corner but broke clean. He then tried to hit a powerful chop, but Bailey dodged and hit back with several kicks. Bailey then hit a Frankensteiner after avoiding Dragunov’s attempt to stop his handspring. The action then moved to the outside, where Mike Bailey hit an Orihara moonsault. Dragunov avoided another kick and sent Bailey’s foot crashing into the steel steps. He followed up with a German suplex on the floor. Bailey tried to regain control on the apron, but his next moonsault attempt ended badly. His knees crashed into the hard surface, leaving both men in pain. Bailey was struggling to put weight on his injured leg. Dragunov then started focusing more on his injured knee. He hit a superplex to Bailey from the top of the turnbuckle. Bailey nearly stole the win with an inside cradle as Dragunov prepared to hit the D-Bomb. He continued fighting back, but his injured knee made it difficult to follow up. Dragunov took advantage and went after the leg again. He knocked Bailey off the second turnbuckle with a chop to the knee before hitting a powerbomb. The Mad Dragon then delivered the D-Bomb. title: WWE Crown Jewel in Saudi Arabia unchanged amid embassy evacuation
raw_title: U.S. Saudi Embassy partially evacuated, no changes to Crown Jewel PLE announced by WWE at this time
body: The U.S. State Department has ordered nonessential diplomatic personnel and their family members to leave Saudi Arabia. The order comes after a string of escalating attacks by the Iran-backed Houthi rebel group. Several scheduled events in Riyadh have either been canceled or postponed. WWE is currently scheduled to run the Crown Jewel PLE in Riyadh on Nov. 7. The company has not announced any plans publicly to postpone, relocate or reschedule Crown Jewel as of this writing. The U.S. Embassy in Riyadh issued a new security alert today stating that more attacks were expected. The alert mentioned that the operations at the King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh are still suspended. Iranian-supported Houthis have engaged in hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including attacks on civilian airports and other critical infrastructure resulting in civilian casualties and severe travel disruptions. The hostilities have the potential to escalate rapidly beyond that immediate area. U.S. citizens are reminded to follow the guidance of natioonal alerts released by Saudi Arabia’s Civil Defense via cellular broadcast. U.S. government employees working in Saudi Arabia require special authorization from Chief of Mission to use any airport in Saudi Arabia following recent missile and UAV attacks on airports in the Kingdom. Operations at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh remain suspended. King Abdulaziz International Airport in Jeddah and King Fahd International Airport in Dammam are operational with some delays and cancellations. U.S. citizens should be aware of potential attacks on airports, airspace closures, flight cancellations, and travel disruptions. Please take extreme caution if you choose to use airports in Saudi Arabia. We recommend checking your flight departure status directly with the airline and with the airport. The initial alert led to reports circulating that the Embassy had been ordered to be evacuated, but State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott issued a correction on Twitter/X stating that it was only meant for nonessential personel and their families. The U.S. Department of State issued an ordered departure for non-emergency U.S. government employees and their family members in Saudi Arabia only. Iranian-supported Houthis have increasingly engaged in hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including attacks on civilian airports and other critical infrastructure resulting in civilian casualties and severe travel disruptions. The safety and security of Department personnel and their families remain our highest priority, and we will continue to take all necessary steps to protect and support them.
summary: The U.S. State Department ordered nonessential diplomatic personnel and families to depart Saudi Arabia following attacks by Iran-backed Houthi rebels. Multiple events in Riyadh have been canceled or postponed while the U.S. Embassy issued a new security alert noting expected further attacks and suspended operations at King Khalid International Airport. WWE has made no announcement to alter, postpone or relocate its scheduled Crown Jewel premium live event set for November 7 in Riyadh.

body: AEW Dynamite was live on TBS and HBO Max from the Watsco Center in Coral Gables, Florida, with all the WrestleDream fallout! We were treated to Ilja Dragunov's in-ring debut against “Speedball” Mike Bailey in the main event and a dominant night from the Don Callis Family to set up the first match announced for this year’s Blood and Guts, coming to Jacksonville in two weeks! Plus, AEW Full Gear is fast approaching from Phoenix on November 14! The night began with Don Callis gleefully watching Mark Davis and Jake Doyle absolutely wipe out the Young Bucks in an AEW World Tag Team Championship eliminator in less than three minutes, which earned them a future shot at the titles! In the very next match, “The Protostar” Kyle Fletcher and “The Jet” Kevin Knight beat AEW World Champion Will Ospreay and Adam Copeland when Fletcher pinned Copeland following a brainbuster when AEW International Champion “The Rainmaker” Kazuchika Okada hit Copeland with his title. A post-match brawl saw the return of Steven Borden, who laid out the Blood and Guts challenge to Callis, which was later accepted! In a shocking turn of events, The Dogs and Bang Bang Gang went from bitter rivals to a cohesive unit when they laid waste to the Death Riders and The Conglomeration following AEW Continental Champion Jon Moxley’s Eliminator match win over Roderick Strong! Plus, Queen Aminata became the new #1 contender to Persephone’s TBS Title by beating the returning Maya World and will get her shot at the TBS Championship next week on Fright Night Dynamite! AEW Women’s World Champion Mercedes Moné was confronted by Marina Shafir! And Swerve Strickland wants Texas Death for the AEW World Trios Titles against Hangman and Brodido! Back in the ring, Davis and Doyle sandwiched Matt with lariats in the middle of the ring, followed by a double powerslam. Davis hit Matt with Close Your Eyes and Count to Three while Doyle dragged Nick back into the ring. Davis hit Matt with Close Your Eyes and Count to Three two more times while Doyle bearhugged the air out of Nick. Davis and Doyle pinned the Bucks at the same time for the win in less than three minutes! Callis couldn’t have been cackling any louder at the blowout win for his dominant duo. The Bucks didn’t get an ounce of offense and now Davis and Doyle own a future shot at the AEW World Tag Team Championship! After the match, we took a look back on the fantastic night in Orlando that was WrestleDream, including Will Ospreay winning AEW’s first Clockwork Carnage to retain his AEW World Title. Cope and Knight opened the match, but the crowd chanted, “HOLY SHIT!” before they even touched. Cope stayed a step ahead of Knight in the early going by deking him into a lariat. Knight worked Cope into the corner and choked him with his boot, using the ropes for extra leverage. Knight sent Cope to the opposite side, so he slid under the ropes to the floor and flipped off Knight! Knight chased after, so Cope returned to the ring and Knight dove right back

title: El Desperado Out Of NJPW Super Jr. Tag League
raw_title: El Desperado Withdraws From NJPW Super Jr. Tag League Due To Spinal Stenosis & Hernia
summary_src: El Desperado is out of action. New Japan Pro-Wrestling made the announcement that El Desperado is going to be out of action due to spinal stenosis and a hernia in his leg. He will miss the Super Jr.
body: New Japan Pro-Wrestling made the announcement t hat El Desperado is going to be out of action due to spinal stenosis and a hernia in his leg. He will miss the Super Jr. Tag League tournament and CMLL x NJPW Lucha Kingdom. Below is NJPW’s full write-up along with Desperado’s statement: We apologise to fans who were looking forward to seeing Desperado compete, and appreciate your understanding. In a video released on YouTube, Desperado stated: “My sincerest apologies, but I will not be appearing at Super Jr. Tag League. I’m currently dealing with spinal canal stenosis and a hernia. My left leg has no strength, and with the pain and pins and needles I’m currently unable to stand, walk or even sit upright for long periods of time. From the start of this year I’d noticed some strange sensations in my left glute, and there was some tingling in my legs from around March. At that point I expressed to the company that I was having some symptoms, but that I had no issues with strength or anything like that, and asked to continue wrestling, while staying in contact with the medical and training staff. For this Super Jr. Tag League, Mistico was scheduled to wrestle with me, and we can’t just send him back with nothing to say for it, so I have chosen (Masatora) Yasuda to replace me. Some of you might think ‘with your connections you can come up with a bigger name than a Young Lion,’ but I’d like for you to think of this as a key step to the future of NJPW. And don’t worry about Mistico. Even with his partner like this, he’ll show up for the fans like Mistico always does. I have complete trust in him. So that’s it. I’m off Super Jr. Tag League, and Yasuda is in. Ah, and as for (November 9 Shin Kiba 1st Ring produce event) ‘Gaspe’ Invitational. I can’t move, but my desire to see something truly horrific trumps all that, so we’ll be going ahead as planned. Show up.” New Japan Pro-Wrestling joins fans in wishing Desperado a speedy, full recovery.” As more information about Desperado’s recovery becomes available, we’ll update you here on Fightful.
summary: New Japan Pro-Wrestling announced that El Desperado will miss the Super Jr. Tag League and CMLL x NJPW Lucha Kingdom due to spinal stenosis and a hernia in his leg. The wrestler has been experiencing no strength in his left leg along with pain, pins and needles, preventing him from standing, walking or sitting for extended periods. El Desperado first noticed symptoms in his left glute at the beginning of the year and tingling in his legs from March but continued wrestling after informing the company.

title: Booker T Details Business-Only Bond With Triple H
raw_title: Booker T explains why he and Triple H have never been close friends
summary_src: Booker T has explained his relationship and friendship with Triple H. Always suspected by fans to have a tense relationship with Triple H, Booker T has now cleared the air regarding it.
body: Booker T has explained his relationship and friendship with Triple H. “ When you’re talent, when you know you’re selling tickets, you’re equal. When you’re selling tickets, you might be looked at a little bit different ,” he shared before adding that he never got any heat because he made the boss know that he was selling tickets, and not make friends . “ I don’t have a lot of friends in the wrestling business. I got a few, but I don’t have a lot of friends because I wasn’t there to make friends. I had a lot of cool associates. Even now, people talk about Hunter [Triple H] and I, and our relationship. Hunter and I, we’ve always had a strong relationship, but it’s always been business ,” Booker T said. However, he also made it clear that while they share a strong professional relationship and haven’t gone out eating or hung out together. Despite not sharing a close relationship, he has nothing but respect for him. “ I’ve never looked at this like it was, ‘Hey, we’re buddies. We’re friends,’ or anything like that. Because this thing comes and goes. It’s here, and it’s gone tomorrow. And if you don’t understand that and treat it that way, you can really be upset at the end of the day. I never want to be one of those guys ,” T added. Shounak Chakrabarti Shounak Chakrabarti is an experienced sports journalist with a lifelong passion for athletics and storytelling. llm_long: Booker T described his relationship with Triple H as a strong professional bond focused entirely on business matters. He noted that the two have never socialized outside of work, such as going out for meals or hanging out together.

Booker T emphasized that he approached his wrestling career with the mindset of selling tickets rather than forming friendships. This approach helped him avoid any backstage issues by making his value clear to management.

He stated that he maintains only a limited number of friends in the wrestling industry and views most connections as professional associations. His interactions with Triple H have always remained strictly business-oriented despite their positive working relationship.

Booker T expressed respect for Triple H while making it clear that he never considered them to be personal buddies or close friends. He explained that treating the business as temporary helps prevent disappointment when opportunities change.

title: MLW Fusion available for purchase on Amazon Prime
raw_title: MLW Fusion available for purchase on Amazon Prime
body: By Jason Powell , ProWrestling.net Editor ( @prowrestlingnet ) MLW issued the following press release on Tuesday to announce that its Fusion show is available for purchase via Amazon Prime. CHARLESTON, S.C. – Oct. 13, 2026 — Major League Wrestling (MLW) today announced that MLW Fusion is now available on Amazon Prime Video , expanding the league’s reach and giving fans another way to experience and collect its championship fights, epic rivalries and hard-hitting action. Fans can purchase full seasons for $26.99 or individual episodes for $1.99 . Explore MLW Fusion on Prime Video here. The launch of MLW Fusion on Amazon Prime Video further expands MLW’s distribution across leading streaming platforms, bringing the league’s flagship series to a broader audience and strengthening its global media footprint. “MLW belongs on the biggest platforms, and Amazon Prime Video is another significant step in that direction,” said MLW Founder and CEO Court Bauer. “We’re making it easier for fans to discover and experience Fusion, follow the rivalries and revisit the fights that get everyone talking. This gives our fans another way to watch and opens the door for a new audience to experience MLW.” MLW Fusion premieres Thursdays at 8 PM ET, streaming free on Tubi , with replays available on YouTube, VEEPS and NJPW WORLD. Powell’s POV: Just to make it clear, the weekly Fusion series that premieres Thursdays on Tubi will not be free on Amazon Prime. Rather, it appears that all MLW content on Amazon Prime must be purchased.

title: AEW's Claudio Castagnoli Names Favorite Wrestling Venue: 'As Perfect As It Comes'
raw_title: AEW's Claudio Castagnoli Names Favorite Wrestling Venue: 'As Perfect As It Comes'
body: "I think Arena Mexico," Castagnoli said. "The cathedral. That's pretty much as perfect as it comes." Having received lucha libre training from the luchador Skayde in the early days of his wrestling career, Castagnoli had long desired to wrestle in Arena Mexico before finally debuting there in March 2024. Since then, Castagnoli has become a regular at major CMLL events, including winning the 2024 CMLL International Gran Prix and the CMLL World Heavyweight Championship in late 2025 . The title reign led to Castagnoli signing a dual contract with AEW and CMLL in March , and he defended it successfully six times before dropping it to fellow AEW/CMLL star Hechicero. Castagnoli most recently competed in Arena Mexico for the 2026 International Gran Prix, making it all the way to the final two before once again being defeated by Hechicero. Since his last Arena Mexico appearance, Castagnoli has kept busy by making his third appearance in London's Wembley Stadium, as part of AEW All In this past weekend. Alongside Death Riders stablemates PAC and Wheeler Yuta, Castagnoli was part of the Trios Roulette Royale for the AEW World Trios Championships, once again making it to the end before he and PAC were eliminated by the debuting Austin Creed and Kofi, who captured the Trios Titles with partner Swerve Strickland .

title: WrestleMania III Intercontinental Title Belt Up For Auction
raw_title: 48 Hours Left In Auction For Wrestlemania Iii WWF Intercontinental Championship Belt From Savage Vs. Steamboat
body: The following press release was previously issued about the auction: LEGENDARY WRESTLEMANIA III INTERCONTINENTAL CHAMPIONSHIP BELT HEADS TO HERITAGE AUCTIONS As the high-end wrestling memorabilia market shatters records, a premier multi-champion artifact from the Golden Era hits the auction block Most notably, the belt serves as the central centerpiece of WrestleMania III on March 29, 1987. It was captured by Ricky Steamboat during his legendary, show-stealing masterpiece against "Macho Man" Randy Savage—a bout widely celebrated by historians, peers, and fans as one of the greatest and most influential matches of all time. "Between 1985 and 1989, the Intercontinental Championship belonged to the definitive personalities of WWE's golden era," said Thompson. "No match captures that reputation better than Savage and Steamboat at WrestleMania III. We are approaching the 40th anniversary of that match, and still, to this day, it is referenced by wrestlers and fans alike as one of the best WrestleMania matches of all time.” This marquee offering arrives amidst a historic explosion in the high-end wrestling memorabilia market. Heritage Auctions previously revolutionized the hobby by realizing $1,037,000 for Hulk Hogan’s photo-matched WrestleMania I boots, followed by the $414,800 sale of Hogan’s WrestleMania II WWF World Heavyweight Championship belt. With museum-grade sports entertainment artifacts rapidly transitioning into blue-chip investments, this multi-champion Intercontinental title is expected to command fierce competitive bidding. For more information on this historic championship belt, visit: www.WrestleManiaBelt.com .
summary: The Intercontinental Championship belt from WrestleMania III, central to Ricky Steamboat's match against Randy Savage, is currently in an ongoing auction via Heritage Auctions. The item is highlighted as a key artifact from WWE's Golden Era, with the Savage-Steamboat bout still regarded as one of the greatest matches in WrestleMania history. Per the PWInsider report, less than 48 hours remain in the bidding process as the high-end wrestling memorabilia market continues to set records.

Between 1985 and 1989 the Intercontinental Championship was held by several defining figures from WWE's golden era. The Savage versus Steamboat match at WrestleMania III is frequently cited as one of the best WrestleMania matches even as the event approaches its 40th anniversary.

The auction takes place during a period of strong growth in the high-end wrestling memorabilia market. Heritage Auctions previously sold Hulk Hogan's photo-matched WrestleMania I boots for over one million dollars and his WrestleMania II world heavyweight championship belt for more than four hundred thousand dollars.
The multi-champion Intercontinental title is viewed as a museum-grade artifact and is anticipated to attract significant bidding interest.

title: Two AEW Factions Turn on Their Allies, Form Shocking Alliance on Dynamite
raw_title: Two AEW Factions Turn on Their Allies, Form Shocking Alliance on Dynamite
body: 0 AEW Dynamite delivered a major faction shake-up on October 21 when the Dogs and Bang Bang Gang betrayed their respective allies and joined forces. What began with Jon Moxley defending himself against an attack quickly turned into a chaotic scene that left the Death Riders and Conglomeration outnumbered. The shocking developments followed Moxley’s match against Roderick Strong, with the fallout reshaping several relationships across AEW’s roster. Jon Moxley defeated Strong by submission with a sleeper hold in their Continental Championship eliminator match. Afterward, the Dogs attacked Moxley, forcing him to return to the ring and confront them. When Gabe Kidd tried to intervene, the situation took another turn as his fellow Dogs turned against him and beat him down. The Conglomeration then arrived alongside Jay White, seemingly to help even the odds. Instead, White hit Orange Cassidy with a Blade Runner, while members of the Bang Bang Gang attacked other members of the Conglomeration. The apparent rescue quickly became another betrayal, as the Bang Bang Gang aligned itself with the Dogs. David Finlay struck Castagnoli in the neck with a shillelagh, leaving him vulnerable to further punishment. White then turned his attention back to Moxley, who refused to back down and spat in his face. White responded with another Blade Runner, leaving Moxley down as the new alliance stood tall. With former allies now standing across the battlefield, AEW’s faction landscape has changed dramatically. The new alliance has made its intentions clear, and the next chapter of this rivalry could prove difficult for the groups left picking up the pieces. title: Contract News: Amazing Red Reportedly Signs TNA Contract Following Title Victory
raw_title: Amazing Red Reportedly Signs TNA Contract Following Title Victory
body: TNA Wrestling Hall of Famer Amazing Red has reportedly signed a contract with the promotion following his successful return at Bound For Glory 2026. According to PWInsider, the veteran high-flyer has finalized a deal to remain with TNA after capturing the X-Division Championship and receiving his Hall of Fame induction at the company’s recent pay-per-view. The championship had previously been relinquished by Leon Slater, who exercised TNA’s “Option C” provision to exchange the X-Division Title for an opportunity at the TNA World Championship. Slater subsequently won the TNA World Championship, leaving the X-Division Title available for a new champion. For Amazing Red, the victory marked his fourth reign as X-Division Champion and his first since 2010. Red was one of the defining performers of TNA’s original X-Division, helping establish the fast-paced, high-flying wrestling style that became a signature part of the promotion’s identity. His latest run also marks his first stint with TNA since 2011, bringing him back to the company where he achieved some of his greatest success. The reported signing comes as TNA continues making moves to secure talent for its roster. Earlier this week, the promotion officially confirmed the signing of Shotzi Blackheart, while Director of Authority Santino Marella also agreed to a new contract. Additional contract developments are expected in the coming weeks, with several TNA talents reportedly approaching the expiration of their current agreements before the end of 2026. While fans await official confirmation of Red’s new deal, the reported agreement suggests that his Bound For Glory appearance was more than a one-night return. With the X-Division Championship back around his waist, Amazing Red appears set to begin another chapter with the promotion he helped establish more than two decades ago.

title: Drew McIntyre Details Six-Month WWE Hiatus for Acting
raw_title: Drew McIntyre Discusses Taking Time Away From WWE To Pursue Acting Work, Putting on More Muscle
body: During a recent interview with Insight with Chris Van Vliet , former WWE Champion Drew McIntyre spoke about his career, taking over six months off from WWE to pursue acting work, and whether he’s put on muscle to prep for his WWE return. Below are some highlights from Insight: “Ever, by far since I started wrestling at 15 years old. I have not had six months off. I started doing shows and wrestling basically every weekend or every second weekend when I was 16. My summer job was wrestling at the Butlins holiday camp since I was about 17, and when I tore my bicep, I was out for three months in NXT. I was going stir crazy, so I’d drive down to the PC just to work with Shawn and watch tapes and stuff because you’ve got Shawn Michaels; use him if you’re at the PC. I’ve heard somebody literally say, ‘Who’s the Rockers?’ One time while Shawn was standing there, learn your history for the love of God. When I broke my neck, I was out for eight weeks physicality-wise, but I was doing promos in the second or third week for Evolve and a few other independent companies locally, where I’d take off the brace, cut the promo, head to the back. So this is by far the most amount of time I’ve ever had off.” “Yeah, very, very busy. It has not felt like time off until the past couple of weeks, few weeks, where I’ve actually been at the house with the missus and the cats. It’s been nice, but I’ve been working a lot. It’s been very different. I’ve spent my whole life on the road from town to town, from country to country, 52 weeks a year, no reruns, no offseason in WWE, or the time I was away from WWE, I was even busier than the WWE schedule. So to spend time in the same place was very bizarre. To live in a different country, to live in Spain, was insane. I can tell you now, I’ve learned exactly no extra Spanish words that I knew when I got there.” “No, I just like to look good. Obviously, I’m in the best shape of my life. I feel physically great. It’s here in Nashville, and my buddy was like, I’ve never seen anybody hit the ropes so fast because he’s not seen Bron Breaker, the only other man that’s faster than me. llm_long: Former WWE Champion Drew McIntyre discussed his career during an interview. He revealed that he took more than six months away from WWE to focus on acting opportunities.

McIntyre noted that this period marked the longest break he has experienced since beginning his wrestling career at age 15. He previously wrestled on weekends from age 16 and worked summers at a holiday camp starting at age 17.

His prior injuries included a three-month absence in NXT due to a torn bicep and an eight-week physical layoff after breaking his neck. During the neck injury recovery he continued cutting promos for independent promotions.
The time away from WWE proved busy rather than restful for most of its duration. McIntyre spent part of the hiatus living in Spain before recently settling at home with his wife and cats.

He described the experience of remaining in one location as unusual after a lifetime spent traveling town to town and country to country for 52 weeks each year. McIntyre stated that he added no new Spanish vocabulary during his stay in Spain.

McIntyre confirmed he has maintained strong physical condition throughout the break simply because he enjoys looking fit. He feels he is in the best shape of his life and was recently seen running ropes at a training facility in Nashville.

body: Here's the very good and the very bad from this week's "AEW Dynamite." AEW/Speedy Ruiz Nick Wayne has beaten Chris Jericho twice. Why is this feud still going? I'm sure they're building to some kind of point about maturity, and Jericho seeing himself in Wayne, but it's all moving too slowly. This week was a lot of yelling and a lot of stalling. I'm terrified the next step could be a Jericho win, or worse, a Jericho tag team. I feel like, by beating him twice, Wayne has sucked all the juice he can out of this rivalry, and should be moving on to bigger, better things, and yet here he is, stuck in the Jericho vortex, likely being taken out to sea on a cruise. It just feels like this feud either needs to end or escalate, and since it was neither, this segment was a little underwhelming, even if I do like where Wayne's character seems to be going. AEW/Speedy Ruiz Normally, it wouldn't be a great thing for AEW to have their AEW World Tag Team Champions The Young Bucks be beaten in such a dominant and quick manner by another team because you want to keep your champions looking strong. In the case of Mark Davis and Jake Doyle dominating Matt Jackson and Nick Jackson in what was essentially a squash Eliminator Match, I actually think it was the perfect call. The Don Callis Family has been positioned as major players on the AEW roster, but their overall win-loss record as a stable doesn't always reflect that and can be inconsistent depending on what the situation of specific storylines they're involved in calls for. For that reason, I think it was genius for The Young Bucks to get in, no offense of any kind against Davis and Doyle, because it instantly makes them feel like a serious threat to the AEW World Tag Team Championship and is an effective way to establish them as a dominant tag team without having to do too much work to position them as such. Something about it just worked really well, and it was a shocking and great way to kick off this "Dynamite" in a manner that was attention-grabbing and engaging. AEW/Speedy Ruiz Last year was the first women's Blood & Guts match, and it was absolutely fantastic, so I guess I just assumed we'd be getting another one this year, to go alongside the men's bout set for two weeks in Jacksonville. If there's going to be a women's version of the hardcore bout, however, it wasn't officially or clearly set up tonight. It kind of sucks either way, because if the women are getting a match, they'll barely have any build. Last year's match was six-on-six, and right now, the heels only have five women, with the babyfaces clocking in at just four. Next week's episode would be making the teams official, and then boom, Blood & Guts the next week. Which, I suppose I shouldn't complain about, because getting a thrown-together women's Blood & Guts match is better than none at all. title: AEW Sets Blood & Guts Match For November 4
raw_title: AEW Dynamite recap, reactions (Oct. 21, 2026): Blood, guts, & heel turns
summary_src: When I thought AEW was going to zig for AEW Dynamite (Oct. 21, 2026), they zagged in a major way. I assumed the biggest story would be the in-ring debut for Ilja Dragunov in the main event.
body: AEW built teams for Blood & Guts with an unexpected crew of babyfaces, a heel turn from Jay White unfolded on the Death Riders, and several more directions were established for upcoming TV specials and the Full Gear PPV. All that and more on the WrestleDream fallout episode came from Watsco Center in Miami, Florida. After Okada cheated with his title belt to help Kyle Fletcher & Kevin Knight defeat Will Ospreay & Adam Copeland in tag team action (match details further down below), the Callis Family goons went to work pounding their foes. Darby Allin ushered in the surprise return of Steven Borden from injury, and the Young Bucks also joined the fracas. The Callis Family’s mission is to beat down the champions and take their gold soon after. AEW made Blood & Guts official for November 4. It will be Ospreay, Copeland, the Bucks, Allin, & Borden against Fletcher, Okada, Knight, Wardlow, Davis, & Doyle. The story came together quickly in a manner that feels natural. That is an appealing list of all-stars for Ospreay’s team. This matchup feels fresh with a lot of first-timers for Blood & Guts. As for a potential women’s Blood & Guts, there was a backstage scene with Divine Dominion and the Triangle of Madness beating up the Brawling Birds and Wrathlander backstage. It seems the unifying goal would be to beat up the tag champs and challengers so bad that both heel teams would step into their spots at Full Gear. Add in Willow Nightingale opposite rival Thekla, and we have five versus five. Sounds good to me. On the surface, Divine Dominion with the Sisters of Sin doesn’t make sense, so I like the idea of a common goal to buy into them as a team for Blood & Guts. After Jon Moxley defeated Roderick Strong in an eliminator match (more detail down below), the Continental champion exited the ring. The Dogs duo of David Finlay and Clark Connors swooped in like vultures to pick the bones of Strong. Once Mox noticed, he put a stop to that beatdown. Boom! The Dogs attacked Moxley. Gabe Kidd ran in to corral his pals, boom again. Connors speared Kidd. The Bang Bang Gang are instantly relevant again. I enjoyed their babyface schtick, but they were going upward. Every single member knows how to be heel, so there is no learning curve there. The Bang Bang Gang came run wild with guns blazing. The addition of the Dogs makes sense as former Bullet Club members, and their tension with Moxley has been brewing for weeks. Kidd with the Death Riders is an interesting development. Most of what I’ve seen from Kidd is from AEW, so I’m curious how he does in a babyface role. With the death of PAC, fans wanted the Death Riders to be fan favorites. This does the trick to give them a feud against fresh heels. Also, Claudio Castagnoli was awesome in that scene as a one-man army. AEW made the in-ring debut for Ilja Dragunov feel like a big deal. Could it live up to the hype? I have a mixed reaction about his victory over Mike Bailey. On the positive, the two wrestlers put on a show
summary: Following the WrestleDream fallout, AEW announced a Blood & Guts match for the November 4 episode featuring Will Ospreay, Adam Copeland, The Young Bucks, Darby Allin and Steven Borden against Kyle Fletcher, Kazuchika Okada, Kevin Knight, Wardlow, Davis and Doyle. The teams formed after Okada used his title belt to assist Fletcher and Knight in defeating Ospreay and Copeland in a tag bout, leading to a post-match beatdown that brought out the babyface side including a returning Steven Borden from injury. body: AEW built teams for Blood & Guts with an unexpected crew of babyfaces, a heel turn from Jay White unfolded on the Death Riders, and several more directions were established for upcoming TV specials and the Full Gear PPV. All that and more on the WrestleDream fallout episode came from Watsco Center in Miami, Florida. After Okada cheated with his title belt to help Kyle Fletcher & Kevin Knight defeat Will Ospreay & Adam Copeland in tag team action (match details further down below), the Callis Family goons went to work pounding their foes. Darby Allin ushered in the surprise return of Steven Borden from injury, and the Young Bucks also joined the fracas. The Callis Family’s mission is to beat down the champions and take their gold soon after. AEW made Blood & Guts official for November 4. It will be Ospreay, Copeland, the Bucks, Allin, & Borden against Fletcher, Okada, Knight, Wardlow, Davis, & Doyle. The story came together quickly in a manner that feels natural. That is an appealing list of all-stars for Ospreay’s team. This matchup feels fresh with a lot of first-timers for Blood & Guts. As for a potential women’s Blood & Guts, there was a backstage scene with Divine Dominion and the Triangle of Madness beating up the Brawling Birds and Wrathlander backstage. It seems the unifying goal would be to beat up the tag champs and challengers so bad that both heel teams would step into their spots at Full Gear. Add in Willow Nightingale opposite rival Thekla, and we have five versus five. Sounds good to me. On the surface, Divine Dominion with the Sisters of Sin doesn’t make sense, so I like the idea of a common goal to buy into them as a team for Blood & Guts. After Jon Moxley defeated Roderick Strong in an eliminator match (more detail down below), the Continental champion exited the ring. The Dogs duo of David Finlay and Clark Connors swooped in like vultures to pick the bones of Strong. Once Mox noticed, he put a stop to that beatdown. Boom! The Dogs attacked Moxley. Gabe Kidd ran in to corral his pals, boom again. Connors speared Kidd. The Bang Bang Gang are instantly relevant again. I enjoyed their babyface schtick, but they were going upward. Every single member knows how to be heel, so there is no learning curve there. The Bang Bang Gang came run wild with guns blazing. The addition of the Dogs makes sense as former Bullet Club members, and their tension with Moxley has been brewing for weeks. Kidd with the Death Riders is an interesting development. Most of what I’ve seen from Kidd is from AEW, so I’m curious how he does in a babyface role. With the death of PAC, fans wanted the Death Riders to be fan favorites. This does the trick to give them a feud against fresh heels. Also, Claudio Castagnoli was awesome in that scene as a one-man army. AEW made the in-ring debut for Ilja Dragunov feel like a big deal. Could it live up to the hype? I have a mixed reaction about his victory over Mike Bailey. On the positive, the two wrestlers put on a show

title: After AEW All In, British wrestling dares to dream big again
raw_title: After AEW All In, British wrestling dares to dream big again
body: "I think we did 5,000 in the end," says Andy Quildan, the owner of British independent outfit Revolution Pro Wrestling. That's 500 more than the number that was going around on social media earlier in the night, when Connor Mills was battling Michael Oku for perhaps the most important title in British wrestling, and 1,000 more than RevPro's previous record house. Given the much-vaunted history of the original All In wager , that's a staggering number for an independent show, whether in London or anywhere else. Admittedly, RevPro did have some help in drawing that house. For years, Quildan's promotion has enjoyed what you might call a working relationship (i.e. one short of a formal partnership) with AEW, the massive American promotion that annually descends on London this time of year for one of its marquee shows. It's something that Quildan attributes to AEW founder Tony Khan's longstanding interest in British independent wrestling. "He used to come to some of our shows back in the days before he set up AEW," emphasizes Quildan when we speak on Monday, using his hands-free phone kit on his drive back to Portsmouth in southern England. Back then, he tells me, Khan was the junior owner of Fulham, a London-based Premier League football club, and would visit indie wrestling shows during his time in our capital city, including RevPro. In 2023, that budding friendship between Khan and Quildan would give rise to one of the most iconic sights in independent British wrestling: when a certain Chris Jericho made a surprise run-in during RevPro's 11th anniversary show in a sweaty London venue in order to launch a preemptive attack on Will Ospreay (himself signed to AEW at the time). What had begun as a provincial pipe dream was suddenly part of AEW canon. Three years later and the AEW/RevPro crossovers have only gathered pace. At this year's RevPro anniversary show, it was Ospreay himself who was the surprise entrant , being unveiled as the fifth member of the CPF in a multi-man tag match. That's right: less than 24 hours out from the biggest match of his life , "The Aerial Assassin" was helping some old comrades on the British independent scene. Arguably, it wasn't even the most surreal sight of the weekend when it comes to AEW wrestlers at indie shows. That honor goes to EVE, the British-run all-women's promotion which organized its own independent show on the day before All In. The card featured such AEW luminaries as Kris Statlander, Marina Shafir and Maya World, as well as a spectacularly bloody appearance from Skye Blue — all watched approvingly in an east London taproom by a former indie aficionado going by the name of Jon Moxley. "That was our first ever sell-out crowd," says Dann Read, the veteran promoter and co-founder of EVE Wrestling. The room had a small capacity of 600, he says, but there were just as many names on the waiting list as there were people who managed to get tickets. Like other promoters, Read speaks positively of Khan, not to me

title: Former TNA Champ Tessa Blanchard Joins MLW
raw_title: Former TNA Champ Tessa Blanchard Joins MLW
body: “I’m going to be starting with MLW here soon, and I’m super, super excited for everything to come,” she said. Blanchard is a former TNA Knockouts Champion who also made history by becoming the first woman to win the promotion’s men’s world championship. TNA Tessa says her goal is to make the MLW Women’s World Championship “the number one women’s title in wrestling” ... and she already has her sights set on current champion Shotzi Blackheart . “I think what’s been missing from MLW is a franchise, a name that the division’s built around,” she added. “This division was built and now the franchise ... well, I’m here.” Blanchard is currently based in Mexico City ... where she'll continue to live and to wrestle for Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre, in a joint partnership. The third-generation wrestler ... whose father is WWE Hall of Famer Tully Blanchard ... will make her MLW debut September 12 at FIGHTLAND in Charleston, South Carolina ... the same city where her dad previously wrestled. The full Tessa Blanchard interview drops Thursday on “Inside the Ring.”

title: On the Record: Eric Bischoff Weighs In On Pac Tribute Show, Says Recent AEW Deaths Are 'Concerning'
raw_title: Eric Bischoff Comments On Pac Tribute Show, Says Recent AEW Deaths Are 'Concerning'
body: "You still feel the emotion everybody else is feeling," Bischoff said. "To have to go out and perform as a character and focus on what you're doing in the ring for your own safety as well as the person you're in there with, has got to be challenging." Co-host Conrad Thompson said that while he wasn't saying there was any foul play, sometimes "life just throws you a curveball," and said the recent passings reminded him of an era in the 1990s and early 2000s where it felt as if a lot of guys in their early 40s were dying. Bischoff wasn't as convinced. "Every once in a while, someone will get struck by lightning, but you've got two guys at 40 years old — something's going on," he said. "It is not natural. It's not something that you can just go, 'Sometimes, something happens.' It's concerning and hopefully we're not seeing a pattern like we experienced back in the '90s when it was common, I guess. Relatively speaking. It happened too often, let's put it that way. Let's hope we're not revisiting that. But, you know, somebody might want to take a look at that." Causes of death for Williams and Satterley have yet to be released by officials. Initial reports indicated Satterley's death did not appear suspicious .

Satterley also competed in WWE as Neville, winning multiple championships across both companies. Danielson, who competed in WWE for years before joining AEW in 2021, was a founding member of Blackpool Combat Club alongside Pac and Jon Moxley. The BCC eventually turned on Danielson and formed the Death Riders. Danielson and Pac met in the ring in July 2024, when Danielson beat him in a singles match in the Owen Hart Foundation tournament semifinals. Whether Danielson plans to make any other appearances remains to be seen, but it wouldn't be surprising if he made a one-match return to honor the late Satterly. title: Wrestler Benjamin Satterley, known as 'Pac', dies aged 40
raw_title: Wrestler Benjamin Satterley, known as 'Pac', dies aged 40
body: All Elite Wrestling (AEW) said it was "saddened to announce the passing" of Satterley, 40, who they said had signed with them in 2019. The wrestler's death was confirmed just a day after he participated in AEW's "All Out" event at an arena in Chicago on Saturday evening. "A native of Newcastle upon Tyne, England, Satterley began his wrestling career in 2004 and went on to perform for wrestling organizations all over the world, captivating fans with innovative high-flying moves and incredible in-ring ability," AEW said in a statement. Satterley held multiple AEW Championships, and the organisation said he had competed in "some of the most memorable matches in AEW history". Prior to his partnership with AEW, he also performed in World Wrestling Entertainment (WWE), New Japan Pro-Wrestling and Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre in Mexico. He had a number of different personas during his career including Pac, Adrian Neville and "The Man that Gravity Forgot". The latter was in reference to a signature finishing move which saw him spin 360 degrees from the top rope of the wrestling ring and land on his opponent. Many of the tributes paid to Satterley have expressed shock at his death. WWE Hall of Famer Paul Heyman described it as a "truly terrible loss" and said he was a "tremendous talent and even finer human being". AEW President Tony Khan said he "defined excellence" as a husband, friend and in his wrestling knowledge, skill and "unprecedented athleticism". "The greatest export from our country. Also the greatest human being," fellow British wrestler Will Ospreay wrote on X, sharing a photo of the pair in the ring together. "I am in shock. This is heartbreaking," AEW wrestler Evil Uno said. "We have lost another great person, a great soul, a true professional." "To be able to work with him and watch how incredible he is was something else. "He was a Geordie lad that took on the entire wrestling world and has left a mark that will not be forgotten, and will not be taken away very soon," he told BBC Radio Newcastle.
summary: The latest: the latest: All Elite Wrestling explained it was saddened to announce the passing of Satterley, 40, who they said had inked a deal with them in 2019. A native of Newcastle upon Tyne, England, Satterley began his wrestling career in 2004 and went on to perform for wrestling organizations all over the world.

I think if you’re undashing Cody Rhodes on TV and you’re at Axxess, you’re technically supposed to be in character, so I’d say full gear.” “You know, now I say it, and it’s not so much haunting. I should frame it differently. You asked me the question on one of our talks, and I think I should frame it more as, what’s a good way? The question’s a good question, and the question’s an important question, and I kind of give it a dramatic answer. That’s something you should ask yourself, like me, before I do anything. Because there are probably times, the best prime example is Undashing Cody Rhodes to be in some sort of character, and then there’s times when that’s not a good call at all, also not to waste anyone’s time, right? Not to waste your time, not to waste someone else’s time, or you don’t want to look back at these interviews and think, man, I was just completely full of it, or I was trying to sell a ticket versus actually having a conversation.” “So here’s what I wanted to tell them, and I don’t know them, and I almost contacted you and said, Oh, I want them to know this. They’re telling this funny story about Dusty promoing Ric off the line, and Ric kind of going back and forth. body: When asked about leaning into her unapologetic heel persona - including a viral moment where she refused to count a pinfall as a special guest referee because she was checking her nails - Moore admitted she is having the time of her life. "I've never heard a crowd. When I didn't count, I remember genuinely in that moment being like, oh my gosh," Moore said. "It was that was the most fun I've ever had in a match being out there. They hated me. But it was a lot of fun that match was. It was a lot of pressure too because I didn't realize how much the refs, I don't think people realize how much the refs do." She added: "That was great. I think it's helped me come out of my shell completely also. Even backstage too, it just I feel so much more comfortable and like I'm able to have fun which is the goal I feel like at the end of the day there." Moore’s rise has been heavily tied to her alliance with the faction Order Four, taking on the intentionally convoluted title of Secretary of Strategic Affairs. She credited wrestling veteran Ali for masterminding the group's success. "Honestly, I feel like this whole thing was Ali's idea. He is just a genius in every aspect of wrestling," she revealed. "And he came up to me with the idea, I think somebody in creative came up with the title, Secretary of Strategic Affairs, which no one can say or remember or it's like the worst title. It's just the longest title ever. "And even the first time he introduced me before he was like, I hope I say it right... But yeah, this whole thing was Ali's idea. He's such a creative genius really when it comes to wrestling." Before causing chaos at the recent Bound for Glory pay-per-view, Moore made her UK debut performing for Pro-Wrestling: EVE, an experience she won't soon forget. "I actually, so, Eve, I did Eve, that was my first show in the UK ever. So that was amazing," she recalled. "But my sister lives in London, so I was able to visit her, visit my nephews, and wrestle. And she came to watch. It was awesome. It was honestly one of the best shows I've ever been at." Looking ahead to TNA's upcoming Destination X pay-per-view on November 15 in Canada, Moore already has her sights set on championship gold. Asked who she would like to step into the ring with next, the star didn't hesitate to target the top of the women's division. "Oh, that's a good one. For a future match, oh, maybe I would say Masha Slamovich right now because she has the TV title," Moore stated. "Maybe Indi Hartwell. Actually I've trained with Indi a few times. She's our our new knockouts champ, so maybe I mean that would be the first to go after, right?" TNA Wrestling is heading toward Destination X which is on Sunday, November 15, in Edmonton, Alberta. Tickets for TNA Destination X and all TNA live events can be found at www.tnawrestling.com/events . Fans in the USA can watch Thursday Night iMPACT! in its home of AMC and AMC+. iMPACT also airs on Sportsnet 360 in Canada and TNA+ worldwide.

title: On the Record: WWE’s Tama Tonga Responds To Claims He Took a Shot at Ilja Dragunov After AEW Debut
raw_title: WWE’s Tama Tonga Responds To Claims He Took a Shot at Ilja Dragunov After AEW Debut
body: 0 Tama Tonga has responded after his social media post featuring Ilja Dragunov sparked speculation about a possible dig at the former WWE star following his AEW debut. The WWE wrestler has now addressed the conversation. He made it clear that his intentions may have been far less calculated than some observers suggested. The controversy began […] The post WWE’s Tama Tonga Responds To Claims He Took a Shot at Ilja Dragunov After AEW Debut appeared first on Wrestlezone . Tama Tonga has responded after his social media post featuring Ilja Dragunov sparked speculation about a possible dig at the former WWE star following his AEW debut. The WWE wrestler has now addressed the conversation. He made it clear that his intentions may have been far less calculated than some observers suggested. The controversy began when Tonga shared footage from SmackDown showing him absorbing Dragunov’s chops without selling their impact. The timing attracted attention because Dragunov had recently appeared in AEW. On Wrestling Observer Radio , Dave Meltzer discussed Tonga’s post and questioned whether it was intended as a message to Dragunov. However, Meltzer acknowledged he did not know the reasoning behind the upload. “I don’t know if he was trying to get brownie points or someone told him to do it — I couldn’t tell you,” Meltzer said. He also compared the move to promotional tactics used by Bill Watts and Ole Anderson during the 1980s, when footage of wrestlers being beaten were used to promote competing promotions. “It’s like out of the Bill Watts, Ole Anderson playbook of the ’80s,” Meltzer explained. Tonga subsequently addressed the discussion on social media. He suggested that people were reading too much into a clip he simply considered worth sharing. He then rejected the suggestion that he had borrowed an old promotional strategy. “Great Uncle Dave over here said I took it from a playbook. I don’t even read a playbook, bruh,” Tonga said. "I put a post out about Dragunov and it started some sh*t" – Tama Tonga On Twitter by u/PrinceJohn_ in SquaredCircle Tonga also pushed back against wrestling reporters who contacted him seeking confirmation about the post, telling them to “get the f*ck outta here.” He accused Meltzer of making things up, while insisting nobody inside WWE instructed him to publish the footage. Neither the timing of the post nor Meltzer’s comparison establishes that Tonga intended to take a shot at Dragunov. For now, Tonga has dismissed the theory, leaving the online speculation without confirmation. summary_src: October 22 2000 was the date of the WWF No Mercy PPV that year, which included the bizarre match between Rikishi and Steve Austin. body: October 22 2000 was the date of the WWF No Mercy PPV that year, which included the bizarre match between Rikishi and Steve Austin. It had been revealed that Rikishi “did it for The Rock” and ran over Stone Cold at Survivor Series back in 1999, and this was meant to be Austin’s revenge. Here is some of what Dave had to say about Rikishi vs Steve Austin from WWF No Mercy 2000: “But the biggest story as far as selling PPV buys was the return of Austin, and the competition of the first ever New York Mets vs. New York Yankees world series. Austin’s match left more questions than answers about his physical condition. He went out fast, and did a total gimmick oriented performance with Rikishi that had some brawling, no wrestling and only one or two bumps, and ended without any kind of a finish, even a stunner, leading one to believe they’re actually trying for long-term business. It seemed one more suited for a Raw episode or a bad movie than a PPV main event, but that’s probably why it was put early on the show, and they ended the show with long matches that on paper, and for that matter in the ring, figured to be excellent wrestling matches. “After bloodying Rikishi up, he put him in the bed of his truck, drove him outside the arena, deposited him on the ground, and went to run him over. A police car made the save, but in the process, Austin, who was drinking while driving, perhaps as another way to subtly get him over for an eventual heel turn, crashed into the police car twice, with the idea he had seriously injured an innocent officer, and was swarmed by officers, arrested and taken out. While most seem to think his close television alliance with Jim Ross is being pushed as a way for him to eventually turn on Ross to go heel, it is going to be interesting to watch the crowd manipulation involved in this one, being that Austin’s face turn was precipitated by the hoards of fans who cheered him while he was portrayed as such a strong heel.” Jake Jeremy Jake Jeremy is the Head of Audience Development at F4WOnline, having previously worked as a Combat Sports, Gaming and Pro Wrestling writer, successful Editor in Chief and Sports Coordinator. Kurt Angle won the WWF Title, and Conquistador #1 and Conquistador #2 won the WWF Tag Team Titles. Seven title changes were recorded on October 22nd, 2001. Keiji Muto and Taiyo Kea won the AJPW World Tag Team Titles. Kurt Angle won the WCW United States Title. Tajiri won both the WWF Cruiserweight Title and the WCW Cruiserweight Title. Chris Jericho and The Rock won the WWF Tag Team Titles. Bradshaw won the WWF European Title. Jeff Jarrett won the NWA World Heavyweight Title in 2003. In 2006, Chris Sabin won the TNAW X-Division Title and Sting won the NWA World Heavyweight Title. Joe Doering and Suwama won the AJPW World Tag Team Titles in 2013. Dash Wilder and Scott Dawson won the NXT Tag Team Titles in 2015. Enzo Amore won the WWE Cruiserweight Title in 2017. In 2018, the WWE Universal Title was vacated and Dean Ambrose and Seth Rollins won the WWE RAW Tag Team Titles. In 2021, Becky Lynch won the WWE RAW Women’s Title and Charlotte Flair won the WWE SmackDown Women’s Title. In 2022, Wes Lee won the NXT North American Title and Joe Hendry won the IW Digital Media Title. Seigo Tachibana won the GAORA Television Title in 2024. title: AEW Group Changed Name Due To WWE RAW Concerns
raw_title: AEW Faction Dropped Original Name Over Potential WWE Conflict
body: Skip to content Wrestling News Home » AEW Faction Dropped Original Name Over Potential WWE Conflict David Finlay and Clark Connors had a different name in mind for their AEW faction before settling on The Dogs. However, a potential conflict with WWE reportedly got in the way. The duo originally wanted to call themselves the Raw Dogs, but the name was difficult to use because of its connection to RAW. Finlay and Connors currently compete in AEW alongside Gabe Kidd as The Dogs. The trio previously established themselves as members of the War Dogs faction in NJPW. During a recent appearance on What Happened When with Tony Schiavone , the wrestlers discussed how they came up with their current name. Connors revealed that The Dogs wasn’t their first choice when they arrived in AEW. The duo had another name in mind, but it came with a potential problem. “Well, when we came over here, we just became The Dogs, but we really wanted to pitch the name Raw Dogs. But I think there’s an issue with that whole Monday Night thing,” Connors said. “But it sounds cool because we’re raw f*cking dogs, you know?” he said. Despite having to go with another name, the duo seems happy with the result. Connors explained that The Dogs also has a strong identity and pointed out that no other major wrestling team had used the name the same way. “But The Dogs also is a sick name. It’s just no one’s ever done it before. No one’s been The Dogs,” Connors stated. Schiavone agreed that the name could become more recognizable as AEW continues featuring the faction on TV. He suggested that fans would get used to hearing it as the group appeared more often. Connors agreed. title: Results Recap: A Tribute to PAC Review: Wrestling at Its Finest — AEW Dynamite
raw_title: AEW Dynamite: A Tribute to PAC Review: Wrestling at Its Finest
body: Posted in: AEW , Sports , TV | Tagged: AEW Dynamite , pac , recaps , wrestling El Presidente reviews AEW Dynamite's emotional tribute to PAC, comrades, featuring Jon Moxley, Bryan Danielson's return, and wrestling at its finest. The show opened in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, with Excalibur and Tony Schiavone addressing the tragic loss of Benjamin Satterley , the man the world knew as PAC , "The Bastard." Excalibur spoke about Benjamin as a person, while Schiavone delivered remarks from the ring on behalf of All Elite Wrestling. Comrades, even my pet capybara Esteban, who typically only cries when his truffle supply runs low, shed a tear during this opening tribute. The broadcast then shifted to PAC's final on-camera appearance following All Out , where Jon Moxley addressed the Death Riders after his loss to AEW World Champion Will Ospreay . In that moment, Moxley spoke about getting back up after defeat—a lesson I myself learned after the CIA sabotaged my attempt to corner the international market on commemorative wrestling action figures. PAC was shown as the last member of the Death Riders to leave the frame, a haunting final image that will stay with me longer than the time I got stuck in an elevator with Steven Seagal for six hours. The AEW roster gathered on stage for a solemn 10-bell salute. The Death Riders' music played as a spotlight illuminated PAC's empty chair, draped with his towel—a simple but powerful symbol. Moxley received final words from his stablemates and walked past that chair on his way to the opening contest, carrying the weight of loss into battle like a true warrior. This reminded me of the time Kim Jong-un and I had to eulogize our favorite sushi chef—we honored him by eating seventeen courses in his memory. Moxley defended his AEW Continental Championship against Orange Cassidy , and in a moment that will live forever in wrestling history, Moxley applied PAC's signature Brutalizer submission hold during the closing stretch before finishing Cassidy with the Death Rider for the pinfall victory. But the true shock came in the aftermath, comrades, when Bryan Danielson made a surprise appearance. The two former rivals stood face to face, then embraced—a powerful moment of unity in grief that even moved the hardened capitalist pig executives at Warner Brothers Discovery. Page then teamed with Kenny Omega and the AEW World Tag Team Champions The Young Bucks in an 8-man tag match against the Don Callis Family 's Kevin Knight , Kyle Fletcher , and RPG Vice . The Elite secured victory when Page hit a Buckshot Lariat on Trent Beretta , Omega delivered a V-Trigger, the Bucks followed with a BTE Trigger, and Omega pinned Beretta after a One-Winged Angel. The four men embraced emotionally in the ring afterward, reminding us all that even in the cutthroat world of professional wrestling, solidarity among workers—I mean, wrestlers—is paramount. Cash Wheeler and Jay White shared their own tribute messages, followed by a deeply moving mom

Rhodes expressed frustration with himself for proceeding with the injury. He noted that the fracture has since slowed down his work significantly.
