The rivalry between Rhodes and Orton continues. Rhodes has now taken on the role of delivering punts in their ongoing feud.

title: Cody Rhodes Expects Six or Seven More Years in WWE
raw_title: Cody Rhodes Thinks He'll Wrestle Six Or Seven More Years, Doesn't Want To Wrestle Until He's 50
summary_src: Cody Rhodes gives the latest update on his wrestling future. Cody recently revealed that he signed a new contract with WWE, which he says will be his last, though he didn't give a contract length. Speaking to Chris Van Vliet on Insight, Cody gave further color on his future wrestling plans.
body: Speaking to Chris Van Vliet on Insight , Cody gave further color on his future wrestling plans. “I just signed my last contract. I say last contract, but that’s going to go for a while, and if I’m able to do what I’ve been able to do, because I would love this year not to be just one movie, but perhaps two movies, and I’d love to kind of be able to share that at some point, get that going, and be in that. With all that said, my time with WWE could go. I mean, just to give you a real answer here, and not politic around you, probably seven years. Six, seven? I didn’t mean it like that, but yeah, you know that’s a kids’ thing, right? Had to have Carmelo Hayes explain to me what that was, and I still didn’t get it. Yeah, six, seven years. I’d say so. Yeah, and I don’t want to say that in a final sense. I just know that I don’t want to overstay my welcome,” he said. Asked if he plans on wrestling until he’s 50, he replied, “Well, I definitely don’t want to wrestle into my 50s. No shame to anyone who wrestles in their 50s. I don’t want to overstay my welcome in a sense of this, right? So, I have been given so much from wrestling, and you have to think about my career in its totality. The things that we don’t talk about, the things that I don’t get asked about anymore. You have to think about all that. I have shed so much of my skin for the industry, but I have also been given so, so, so much. I think there’s a point where you have to stop taking. I’m not there, but there’s a point, and I think that’s in that time frame, a point where you just have to stop taking. It’s giving me everything. I am talking to you today, the first time I talked to you, I was a mid-card talent at WWE, and no shame to anything in the mid-card. Mid-card’s beautiful. I heard Triple H explain mid-card in a way that changed my perception of it forever. But I was a mid-card talent with a ceiling that was right above my head, and I’m talking to you today as someone who got to play Guile from Street Fighter, created by Capcom, a game that I played growing up as a little kid. Again, be careful what you wish for, but also I don’t know how many moments like this I can take, and I can get hopefully more, hopefully a lot more. But I’ve been so lucky so far and so blessed so far that I think wrestling. I mean, Cody fatigue is already pretty set in.”

title: Cody Rhodes Recalls Early Hollywood Acting Pursuit
raw_title: Cody Rhodes looks back on moving to Hollywood at 19 to study acting
summary_src: While Cody Rhodes has Street Fighter on his résumé this year, his 19-year-old self once moved to Hollywood to pursue an acting career. Rhodes told Chris Van Vliet on the Insight Podcast that he did not audition or book any roles then.
body: While Cody Rhodes has Street Fighter on his résumé this year, his 19-year-old self once moved to Hollywood to pursue an acting career. “I didn’t book any roles. I didn’t go on an audition. I got my Challenge for the Actor by Uta Hagen book, and I attended Comprehensive Technique with Howard Fine, and then instead of moving on to scene study, I became a stage manager at the Howard Fine Studio just to do Comprehensive Technique again, because I needed the kindergarten level, the first grade level,” said Rhodes. “I needed to completely build up, which was something I was saying on the carpet the other day for the premiere. I hope there’s so many more things for me to do in this world because I need to flex the muscle. “Wrestling can do so much for you as a storyteller, but the transition is different. You’ve seen it with John, you’ve seen it with Dwayne, you’ve seen it with Batista. My gosh, and some of the material he’s taking on. This isn’t a walk in the park. This is challenging. I was very challenged by Street Fighter, and you need those reps, and you need that time.” Despite moving to Hollywood at a young age, Rhodes maintains that wrestling has always been his first choice and top priority. Following in his late father Dusty Rhodes’ footsteps, Cody began his wrestling career in 2006 before making his WWE Raw debut a year later against Randy Orton. “I’m usually really quick to say no, because I grew up loving wrestling so much, and that was all I ever wanted to do. The story about seeing the picture at eight years old and wanting to win the WWE title, it’s a real story. But there’s a couple quotes from a 19-year-old where I might have said acting was the first dream, and even my brother has gone on to you know, Dustin’s good for a hot moment on social media, as you know. I think he’s gone on to say, oh, he always wanted to be an actor. I always wanted to be in entertainment, and the first love I had in the whole world, other than my mom, my sister, and my dad, was wrestling. So I think wrestling was always the thing.” Rosanne Raphael Rosanne Raphael is a wrestling writer with over three and a half years of experience covering all things related to the industry. Rhodes stated that he typically declines other opportunities because of his lifelong passion for wrestling. He recalled a childhood desire to win the WWE title. While some past comments from age 19 suggested acting as an initial dream, he affirmed that wrestling was always his first love in entertainment.

title: Triple H's Key Changes for WrestleMania 43
raw_title: Changes Triple H Must Make to Excite Fans for WWE WrestleMania 43
body: 01:09 Featured Video 1 Match We Want to See at Crown Jewel 👑 Changes Triple H Must Make to Excite Fans for WWE WrestleMania 43 Donald Wood Oct 22, 2026 WrestleMania is supposed to be the biggest event on the calendar, delivering unforgettable matches, career-defining moments, and surprises that keep the WWE Universe talking long after the two-day showcase ends. With WrestleMania 43 on the horizon, Triple H and WWE Creative have a chance to make the event feel special with a few key storytelling and character-development changes. From elevating new stars to making every championship match count, here are changes that could help make next year's WrestleMania an event fans won't want to miss. Why The Bloodline Will Destroy 946 💀 Bleacher Report 18h Dragon Lee, Jordynne Grace, More 🤫 Bleacher Report 18h Breakker, Dragunov, More Rumors 👂 Bleacher Report 1d Create New WrestleMania Main Eventers WrestleMania needs fresh faces in its biggest matches, and Triple H should use the months leading up to the event to establish new main-event contenders. WrestleMania 43 should feature stars who are ready to take the next step, giving audiences a reason to be excited about the company's future as well as its present. Let Established Stars Put Over the Next Generation Creating new main-eventers means very little if WWE refuses to let them win the matches that matter most. Triple H needs to be willing to book rising stars to defeat established names cleanly on the WrestleMania stage, giving them a career-defining moment that can change their standing overnight. Established Superstars can still play important roles without winning every major match, and passing the torch can benefit everyone involved. A young wrestler defeating a respected veteran at WrestleMania gives fans a memorable moment while creating new possibilities for the months ahead. WWE should use WrestleMania 43 to establish who belongs at the top of the card, rather than simply reinforcing the existing pecking order. Stop Overloading WrestleMania WrestleMania has grown into a massive two-night spectacle, but adding more matches does not automatically make the event better. Both nights should have a distinct identity, with a carefully paced lineup that builds toward the biggest matches and strongest moments. body: We’ve been following the sluggish ticket sales of Bound for Glory. Just a week ago, the flagship TNA event had distributed just over 700 tickets, leaving the Tampa Yuengling Center over 70% empty. This past week, WWE and TNA’s partnership came under question. Coincidentally (or not), WWE booked a few TNA Knockouts to participate in a Battle Royal on NXT next week. Then, AJ Styles’ son, Avery Styles, announced he would make his TNA debut at Bound for Glory. Now, Bound for Glory ticket distribution is almost at capacity! What’s the deal with TNA Bound for Glory ticket sales? Let’s take a closer look! TNA returns to Tampa, Florida, for the first time in almost two decades to present its biggest event of the year. With Bound for Glory just over a week away, the card is beginning to take shape. In addition, TNA is promoting Mickie James to be live in Tampa. Yet, TNA Bound for Glory ticket distribution has seen a 200% increase in the past week. WWE has a history of comping tickets to make an event look full and add to the gate in terms of merchandise. title: El Desperado Pulled From NJPW Super Junior Tag League 2026 & CMLL x NJPW Lucha Kingdom Due To Spinal Stenosis And Hernia
raw_title: El Desperado Pulled From NJPW Super Junior Tag League 2026 & CMLL x NJPW Lucha Kingdom Due To Spinal Stenosis And Hernia
body: You are using an outdated, unsupported browser. Please upgrade your browser to experience this site properly. New Japan Pro Wrestling announced that they have pulled El Desperado from their upcoming Super Junior Tag League 2026 tournament due to spinal stenosis and a hernia in his leg. It was also announced that Masatora Yasuda will be replacing El Desperado as Mistico’s tag team partner for the tournament. It was also announced that El Desperado has also been pulled from their upcoming co-promoted CMLL x NJPW Lucha Kingdom event on November 15 at the Arena Mexico in Mexico City, Mexico as well. We apologise to fans who were looking forward to seeing Desperado compete, and appreciate your understanding. In a video released on YouTube, Desperado stated: “My sincerest apologies, but I will not be appearing at Super Jr. Tag League. I’m currently dealing with spinal canal stenosis and a hernia. My left leg has no strength, and with the pain and pins and needles I’m currently unable to stand, walk or even sit upright for long periods of time. From the start of this year I’d noticed some strange sensations in my left glute, and there was some tingling in my legs from around March. At that point I expressed to the company that I was having some symptoms, but that I had no issues with strength or anything like that, and asked to continue wrestling, while staying in contact with the medical and training staff. For this Super Jr. Tag League, Mistico was scheduled to wrestle with me, and we can’t just send him back with nothing to say for it, so I have chosen (Masatora) Yasuda to replace me. Some of you might think ‘with your connections you can come up with a bigger name than a Young Lion,’ but I’d like for you to think of this as a key step to the future of NJPW. And don’t worry about Mistico. Even with his partner like this, he’ll show up for the fans like Mistico always does. I have complete trust in him. So that’s it. I’m off Super Jr. Tag League, and Yasuda is in. Ah, and as for (November 9 Shin Kiba 1st Ring produce event) ‘Gaspe’ Invitational. I can’t move, but my desire to see something truly horrific trumps all that, so we’ll be going ahead as planned. Show up.” New Japan Pro-Wrestling joins fans in wishing Desperado a speedy, full recovery.

summary_src: Cody Rhodes addressed possibly wanting a singles match against The Rock given their storied WWE history. When Chris Van Vliet asked Rhodes about a potential match against The Rock on the Insight Podcast, Rhodes said the decision ultimately rests with him.
body: Cody Rhodes addressed possibly wanting a singles match against The Rock given their storied WWE history. “It’s not that I’m evading that answer. It’s that I don’t really know how to answer because I think personally he has a couple of matches probably left to do. I think that personally, but I also know looking at WrestleMania 40 and another guy who he’s given all, continues to give all as part of the Board. He could easily say that was a great final piece as a performer in a wrestling ring. That’ll be up to him,” stated Rhodes. “That’ll certainly be up to him if there’s more and what those matches might be. I don’t think any wrestler would ever look you in the eye and tell you they wouldn’t want a match like that.” Following WrestleMania 40, it seemed the chapter had closed on Rhodes’ rivalry with The Rock. However, last year, The Rock confronted the then Undisputed WWE Champion with a pitch to join forces. Rhodes’ refusal led to John Cena’s heel turn at Elimination Chamber. Since then, The Rock has remained absent from WWE television and with his Hollywood commitments keeping him busy, the possibility of an in-ring return remains uncertain. title: Contract News: Kofi and Austin Creed’s AEW Contract Lengths Revealed
raw_title: Kofi and Austin Creed’s AEW Contract Lengths Revealed
summary_src: Kofi and Austin Creed aren’t just sticking around AEW for a short run. The New Level have reportedly signed five-year contracts with the company, and Swerve Strickland apparently played a major role in helping bring the two longtime WWE stars through the door.
body: According to Fightful Select on October 22, both Kofi and Creed agreed to five-year AEW deals. That gives AEW a pretty serious long-term commitment from the duo after their arrival at All In. There’s also an interesting story behind how the relationship came together. Fightful reported that The New Level were pitched for AEW with the idea of working with Swerve Strickland, who ended up becoming an important link between the two sides. Strickland played a big part in bridging that relationship while Kofi and Creed were still unavailable for direct negotiations. Tony Khan wouldn’t speak with them until they were contractually free, meaning Swerve was apparently helping lay the groundwork before AEW could actually get involved. That makes the timing of their eventual contracts even more interesting. Kofi previously revealed that he and Creed weren’t officially signed to AEW until less than 24 hours before All In , so things apparently moved pretty quickly once they were legally free to negotiate. Since arriving, Kofi and Creed have also made it clear that AEW offered them more than another place to wrestle. Speaking on Inside the Ring , Creed said the freedom to continue building his presence in gaming was a major benefit of the move . “The ability to do stuff in that space in the way that I want to do it, knowing that I will be the one reaping the fruits of my labor as that tree grows, and possibly being able to bring other people in the locker room into that to bear that fruit as well.” Kofi revealed that those outside opportunities were actually discussed while their contracts were being negotiated. He described their AEW deals as particularly wrestler-friendly when it comes to pursuing projects away from the ring. “There’s a lot of things in there that are very, I guess, player-friendly, right? Like wrestler-friendly, you know, in terms of being able to go out and do what it is that you want to do.” The New Level may have gotten their AEW contracts done at the last possible minute before All In, but these clearly aren’t short-term deals thrown together for one big appearance. With five-year contracts in place and Swerve helping open the door in the first place, AEW appears to have had much bigger plans for Kofi and Creed from the start. title: On the Record: Cody Rhodes Admits “Cody Fatigue” Has Already Set In Among WWE Fans
raw_title: Cody Rhodes Admits “Cody Fatigue” Has Already Set In Among WWE Fans
summary_src: Cody Rhodes knows his wrestling career isn’t going to last forever, and he’s already thinking about when it’ll be time to walk away.
body: Cody jokingly admitted that his old retirement promise didn’t exactly hold up. With his 40th birthday already behind him, he called it another one of his old “Cody lies.” “I just think the — I just signed my last contract. I say last contract — that’s gonna go for a while. And if I’m able to do what I’ve been able to do, because I would love this year not to be just one movie, but perhaps two movies.” “With all that said, my time with WWE could go — I mean, just to give you a real answer here and not politic around you — probably, probably seven. Seven years.” “Six, seven. Yeah. I didn’t mean it like that, but yeah. You know, that’s the kids’ thing, right? To have Carmelo Hayes explain to me what that was and I still didn’t get it. Yeah, six, seven years, I’d say.” The bigger issue for Cody isn’t hitting one specific age. He simply doesn’t want to reach a point where fans are ready for him to leave and he’s still hanging around. “And I don’t want to say that in a final, like a final sense. I just know that I don’t want to overstay my welcome.” One thing Cody does seem pretty certain about is wrestling into his 50s. While he made it clear there’s nothing wrong with other wrestlers doing it, that’s not how he sees his own career playing out. “Well, I definitely don’t want to wrestle into my 50s. No shame to anyone who wrestles in their 50s.” “I have shed so much of my skin for the industry, but I have also been given so, so, so much. I think there’s a point where you have to stop taking. I’m not there, but there’s a point.” Cody believes that moment probably falls somewhere inside the six-to-seven-year window he’s imagining now. He’s not ready to leave yet, but he already understands that he doesn’t want to keep taking opportunities forever. “And I think that’s in that timeframe — a point where you just have to stop taking.” It’s especially striking for Cody when he looks at how dramatically his career has changed. title: On the Record: Cody Rhodes Speaks On Whether WWE Planned a Singles Match With The Rock
raw_title: Cody Rhodes Addresses Whether WWE Planned a Singles Match With The Rock
summary_src: Cody Rhodes still isn’t saying whether WWE ever actually planned to put him in the ring with The Rock. What he will say is that he personally believes The Rock might still have a couple of matches left in him — and Cody isn’t ruling out being involved in one of them. Speaking to Chris ...
body: Speaking to Chris Van Vliet , Cody was taken back to Elimination Chamber in Perth, where he publicly called out The Rock for a one-on-one match. Van Vliet wanted to know whether that challenge was actually supposed to lead somewhere. “Oof. It’s not that I’m evading that answer. It’s that I don’t really know how to answer because I think, personally, he has a couple of matches probably left to do. I think that personally.” Cody never confirmed that WWE had a match between them booked or even formally planned. Instead, he explained that he can also see a scenario where The Rock decides his WrestleMania 40 appearance was the perfect way to finish his in-ring career. “But I also know, looking at WrestleMania 40 — and another guy who has given all, continues to give all as part of the board — he could easily say that was a great final piece as a performer in a wrestling ring.” Ultimately, Cody Rhodes believes that decision belongs entirely to The Rock. If he wants to wrestle again, Cody thinks there are still matches on the table, but nobody else can make that call for him. “That’ll be up to him. That’ll certainly be up to him, if there’s more and what those matches might be.” As for whether Cody himself would want one of those matches, there wasn’t much mystery there. He made it clear that practically any wrestler would jump at the opportunity to share the ring with The Rock. “I don’t think any wrestler would ever look you in the eye and tell you they wouldn’t want a match like that.” Cody also believes WWE is currently in such an unpredictable period that it’s difficult to completely dismiss almost any major match. He pointed to the company’s continued momentum and argued that wrestling fans are watching an era where unexpected things can still happen. “This isn’t me trying to justify anything, but, yeah, no, you are part of an era that’s the most unpredictable time in wrestling, really. It’s unpredictable.” That’s where Cody finally left the door open for the match everyone has been wondering about. He still wouldn’t say that Cody Rhodes vs. The Rock was ever officially the plan, but he isn’t ready to say it’ll never happen either. title: Vince McMahon Accused of Being a “Psychopath” and “Abuser”
raw_title: Vince McMahon Accused of Being a “Psychopath” and “Abuser”
summary_src: Jimmy Jacobs isn’t holding back when it comes to what it was like working for Vince McMahon in WWE. The former WWE writer called McMahon a “psychopath,” a “bully” and an “abuser” while explaining why he found working under him so difficult.
body: “There is no pleasing the mad king. I had a challenging time working for Vince. Yeah.” When the interviewer suggested that people who genuinely loved wrestling sometimes had a particularly difficult time working with McMahon, Jacobs took things much further. He said he viewed McMahon as a “crazy person” before repeatedly describing him as a psychopath. “Vince is a—he was a crazy person. Vince McMahon was like a psychopath. Like a psychopath. Vince McMahon was a psychopath.” Jacobs made it clear he wasn’t simply throwing the word around for dramatic effect. In his personal assessment of McMahon, he believed that was genuinely the type of personality he was dealing with. “That’s the sort of personality type he is, right? He’s like an overt malignant narcissist. Not to use catchphrase words, because I’m not using that hyperbolically. I’m using that like that’s his personality type.” “I was around Vince McMahon not very long before I saw, ‘Oh, I wouldn’t trade places with this guy for one second.’ Not for one second.” Jacobs then offered an even harsher assessment of McMahon’s character. These were Jacobs’ personal claims and descriptions of his former boss, but he didn’t leave much room for interpretation about how he felt. “Because for everything he has, he has nothing because he’s a psychopath. And when you’re a psychopath, you’re incapable of love. And so Vince McMahon’s a bully. He’s a maniac. He’s an abuser.” Jacobs also addressed the negative stories that have emerged about McMahon over the years. From his own experience around him, Jacobs claimed those stories fit with the person he knew. “He’s all of the things that, you know, ‘Oh, this has come out. Is this like Vince?’ Every story you’ve heard about him, it’s something like true. Like, that’s who he is.” “So yeah, it’s hard. It’s hard to work for bullies and psychopaths. That’s challenging, and I had a challenging time with that, and other people did too.” Subhojeet Mukherjee Subhojeet Mukherjee has covered pro wrestling for over 20 years, delivering trusted news and backstage updates to fans around the world.

title: Cody Rhodes Calls Out Wrestling Social Media for Creating Fake Controversies
raw_title: Cody Rhodes Calls Out Wrestling Social Media for Creating Fake Controversies
summary_src: Cody Rhodes has a problem with the way wrestling controversies are being created on social media these days.
body: Speaking to Chris Van Vliet , Cody admitted wrestling media is much harder to navigate now than it used to be. He joked that he was about to get on his “boomer high horse” before explaining exactly what bothers him. “Dude, media is hard these days. I bet you just did your Mount Rushmore. They’re already coming for you. They’re already — it’s hard. Like, it’s not what it used to be. And this is specific to the wrestling media.” Cody believes there are certain wrestling conversations that can appear much bigger online than they actually are. From his perspective, something being discussed heavily on social media doesn’t automatically mean it was already a genuine issue elsewhere. “I’m gonna get on my little boomer high horse here, right? I’m not a boomer, but I want to be. Okay, so there are conversations that take place online in the wrestling community. Here’s what I just wish that people would know: they only take place online.” He then gave an example of how quickly that can snowball. Somebody might claim a wrestler is getting heat over something, and suddenly dozens of people are responding to a controversy that Cody says wasn’t actually happening in the first place. “And I’ll give you a prime example — and this is gonna sound… I feel so bad that I’ve now gone into this rant. Somebody will say something like, ‘I can’t believe she’s getting so much heat for this.’ And then 50 people will reply.” That’s where Cody thinks social media can actually create the very controversy people believe they’re simply discussing. Once the wrestler involved responds or signal-boosts it, the online chatter becomes something much more real. When Van Vliet asked what he meant, Cody immediately became reluctant to even repeat the subject because that would risk starting the conversation all over again. Once Chris mentioned the “best friends” topic, Cody made it clear he’d rather leave it alone. Van Vliet then asked the bigger question: with so much noise surrounding Cody at this stage of his career, how does he decide which opinions actually deserve his attention? Cody admitted his earlier claim that these conversations “only” happen online was too absolute. “I think probably the most important thing is don’t be absolute. So I just gave you an absolute. I said those conversations are only taking place there. That’s not true. That conversation might be happening, right? But then there might be a conversation over here that’s important, and a mentor or a voice.” For Cody, the voices that ultimately need to carry the most weight are the fans actually showing up to WWE events. Those are the people giving their time and energy to the product, and he believes their reactions have to be prioritized over all the other noise surrounding him. “And then there’s, of course, the most important voices — the ones in the arena with us. The ones who are there giving their time and their energy to you to be entertained and to take an escape. I think it’s prioritizing that. That’s wh
summary: Speaking to Chris Van Vliet , Cody admitted wrestling media is much harder to navigate now than it used to be. And this is specific to the wrestling media. Cody believes there are certain wrestling conversations that can appear much bigger online than they actually are.

title: Reason Behind Dralistico’s Cryptic Jail Tweet Amid AEW Exit Speculation
raw_title: Reason Behind Dralistico’s Cryptic Jail Tweet Amid AEW Exit Speculation
summary_src: Dralistico’s AEW future might not be heading toward an exit after all. Despite his contract reportedly running out in December and that bizarre “behind bars” post getting everyone talking, AEW apparently wants to keep him around.
body: Dave Meltzer revealed on Wrestling Observer Radio that AEW plans to make Dralistico a new contract offer. There’s no word yet on whether he’ll accept it, but the company apparently isn’t planning to just let his deal expire without trying to keep him. “From the AEW standpoint, they are going to make him an offer.” That’s a pretty big change from how things looked just a few days ago. Dralistico recently posted an AI-generated image of himself behind bars with his hands cuffed and wrote, “Maybe not for long?” “I was told from people close to him that the thing with the bars and everything, that’s because of the visa issue.” Meltzer also specifically pushed back on the idea that Dralistico is counting down the days until he can leave. He compared the situation to Rey Fenix and said this apparently isn’t another case of a luchador desperately wanting out of AEW. “It’s not because he can’t wait to leave like Fenix. His contract is up soon.” The visa explanation also makes Dralistico’s lengthy absence a little more interesting. He hasn’t wrestled for AEW since the June 6 episode of Collision , when he teamed with RUSH and Sammy Guevara in a losing effort against The Conglomeration for the AEW World Trios Championship. Dralistico originally debuted for AEW in December 2022 before officially signing in October 2023. He’s only wrestled 51 matches across AEW and Ring of Honor since arriving, so his run hasn’t exactly been packed with television time. Of course, AEW wanting Dralistico back doesn’t mean he’s staying. His current contract is still expiring in December, and there’s no indication yet that he’s agreed to whatever the company plans to put in front of him. title: Cody Rhodes Still Feeling Effects of Orton Punt Kick
raw_title: Cody Rhodes says he still feels the effects of Randy Orton’s punt kick from WWE WrestleMania
summary_src: Cody Rhodes claims he still feels the effects of Randy Orton’s punt kick to the face at WWE WrestleMania. Rhodes believes the orbital fracture significantly slowed him down and affected his work. He disclosed his peripheral vision being impacted on the Insight Podcast.
body: Cody Rhodes claims he still feels the effects of Randy Orton’s punt kick to the face at WWE WrestleMania. “I think we skated by with a little bit of an orbital fracture, and that’s not on anyone’s fault but my own…It was bad….I think we skated by a little bit of an orbital fracture, and I think I am mad at myself for doing so because it’s affected my work since, super slowed down.” Rhodes briefly recalled his pectoral muscle injury in 2022 , and cited his passion for wrestling preventing him from staying away from the ring. “I’m letting you know that’s not good. If you’re a young wrestler, don’t do it. Don’t! Live to fight another day. Something about me can’t not want to go. I don’t know what it is. I love it too much. Maybe it’s ego. I don’t know, but I just can’t not. Yeah, that was a nasty one.” After his WrestleMania appearance, Orton returned at SummerSlam to cost Rhodes the Undisputed WWE Title in his bout against CM Punk. The two have since continued their rivalry on SmackDown. summary_src: Though he remains discreet on if there are plans in motion for him to star in any upcoming films or shows, Cody Rhodes describes his summer visit to Marvel Studios.
body: "There's one guy [Andrew Schulz] in particular, who was sitting next to me on this couch pretty much all day, who is teasing things that aren't real, and if they were real, I wouldn't say anything, and guessing characters that are great, great characters, because I grew up... title: Injury Update: Cody Rhodes’s WrestleMania 42 Injury Was Worse Than Initially Believed
raw_title: Cody Rhodes’s WrestleMania 42 Injury Was Worse Than Initially Believed
summary_src: Cody Rhodes came back from his nasty WrestleMania 42 eye injury almost immediately, but apparently he was dealing with more than everyone realized. Cody now says he suffered a minor orbital fracture that affected his peripheral vision and “super slowed down” his work after WrestleMania.
body: Speaking to Chris Van Vliet on October 22, Cody looked back at the injury he suffered during his match against Randy Orton. While he managed to avoid a more serious fracture, he admitted there was still some orbital damage. “I think we skated by with a little bit of an orbital fracture, and that’s not on anyone’s fault but my own… It was bad.” “I think we skated by a little bit of an orbital fracture, and I think I am mad at myself for doing so because it’s affected my work since, super slowed down.” The injury didn’t just leave Cody with a nasty-looking swollen eye either. When Van Vliet asked whether his peripheral vision had been affected, Cody confirmed that it had been impacted to some degree. “Yeah, just to a degree, to a little bit, and I feel like that’s—you can’t go out there QB1 and saying you’re in your prime, and you’re the best you’ve ever been if you’re dealing with something that’s a bit of a hindrance like that.” The good news is Cody says he’s finally past it. Whatever issues he was dealing with following WrestleMania aren’t something he considers an ongoing problem anymore. “I showed up the next night. I am toxic as can be when it comes to physical stuff. Toxic as can be. I can go. Tape it up. I can go.” It’s hardly the first time Cody has done that. His torn pectoral muscle in 2022 became one of the most memorable examples when he still wrestled Seth Rollins inside Hell in a Cell despite the gruesome injury. Cody knows that kind of mentality isn’t something younger wrestlers should be copying. In fact, he went out of his way to warn them against following his example when they’re legitimately hurt. “I’m letting you know that’s not good. If you’re a young wrestler, don’t do it. Don’t! Live to fight another day.” The problem is Cody doesn’t seem entirely sure how to follow his own advice. Whether it’s his love of wrestling or simply his ego, he admitted there’s something inside him that makes sitting on the sidelines incredibly difficult. “Something about me can’t not want to go. I don’t know what it is. I love it too much. Maybe it’s ego. I don’t know, but I just can’t not. Yeah, that was a nasty one.” Cody previously explained that returning so quickly after WrestleMania was about consistency and proving he could continue being WWE’s “QB1 .” Now he’s admitting that decision came with a price, as the injury continued affecting his work and vision even after he was back on television. title: WWE SmackDown Viewership Dips Slightly
raw_title: WWE Smackdown Viewership & Ratings Report, 10/16/2026
summary_src: WWE SmackDown viewership dipped slightly from the previous week, while its ratings remained steady at a high level.
body: Viewership for the show from the Golden 1 Center in Sacramento fell by 2% from the previous week's show , as per " Wrestlenomics ," dropping from 1,352,000 to 1,327,000 viewers. That number is still marginally higher than the four-week average, which is currently standing at 1,282,000. The ratings, meanwhile, have remained unchanged at 0.32, which is also higher than the monthly average of 0.29. The show, which was the first "SmackDown" event since Money in the Bank, saw the Sami Zayn-Trick Williams rivalry continue, with the latter facing Zayn's ally, Johnny Gargano. Paige got the better of her former tag team partner, Nikki Bella, while Rey Fenix retained his AAA Cruiserweight Championship against Ricky Saints. "SmackDown" ended with a match between Cody Rhodes and Baron Corbin, during which Rhodes finally delivered the punt after Randy Orton appeared near the ring. However, the punt was aimed at Corbin, leaving Orton watching in shock from the ramp. The show also had an unfortunate moment when veteran star R-Truth suffered an injury during his match against his former tag team partner, Damian Priest, which ended in a no contest.
summary: The October 16 episode of WWE SmackDown from Sacramento drew 1,327,000 viewers, a 2% decline from the prior week but still above the four-week average of 1,282,000. The rating held steady at 0.32, topping the monthly average of 0.29. The show featured continued Sami Zayn-Trick Williams tension with Trick facing Johnny Gargano, Paige defeating Nikki Bella, Rey Fenix retaining his AAA Cruiserweight Championship over Ricky Saints, and Cody Rhodes punting Baron Corbin after Randy Orton appeared at ringside, plus an injury to R-Truth.

title: AEW Star Will Ospreay Dealt With Body Dysmorphia During NJPW Run
raw_title: AEW Star Will Ospreay Dealt With Body Dysmorphia During NJPW Run
body: During a recent interview with "Muscle & Fitness," Ospreay opened up about his battle with body dysmorphia when he was competing for New Japan Pro Wrestling at the age of 24, explaining that he faced many insecurities in the gym along with online criticism about his in-ring shape. "I first discovered my body dysmorphia, and I won the IWGP Junior Heavyweight Championship, in October of 2017," Ospreay revealed. "And I remember one tweet was saying 'he is in the worst shape,' and they were right ... I didn't understand working out, why you do sets, and why you focus on one body part, and macro counting. I would go to the gym, but I really didn't know what I was doing, I'll be honest, and I was so embarrassed to ask the boys, they're all jacked, I felt like such an idiot, to try and (ask) 'could I workout with you?' so I never went to the gym." During his struggles with body dysmorphia, Ospreay would discover MusclePharm's weekly workouts while he was wrestling in New Zealand and partnered with a personal trainer in order to achieve the physical appearance he was looking for in a healthy way. "I just said, alright, I'm gonna do these for the next six weeks," he said. "Within four weeks, I packed on so much muscle mass, and I started to understand how it worked. And then I invested in a personal trainer, his name is Iestyn Ress, and he really broke down macro counting, and how to count my calories, and why I do a push day and a pull day. It was so simple, but I just never had the courage to ask for help. And I always tell people now, the people in the gym, they're fighting the same demons that you're probably fighting." Nearly a decade later, Ospreay is arguably in the best shape of his entire career and is now the face of the men's division in AEW after defeating Kenny Omega at All In: London last weekend to become world champion. In addition to Ospreay's win, six other title changes occurred at All In, including Mercedes Mone becoming the AEW Women's World Champion, and Darby Allin defeating Kevin Knight for the TNT Title with the help with his former tag team partner, Sting.

Now, those dreams have led me to my next chapter: Ra-Ra Stories (http://RaRaStories.com) , a Louisiana-based production company combining decades of experience, creativity, and passion to develop original film, television, digital, and live entertainment projects. body: The U.S. Embassy in Riyadh issued the new security alert on October 22 as attacks by the Iran-backed Houthis continue. The warning specifically points to civilian airports and critical infrastructure as targets and says the situation could escalate quickly. “Iranian-supported Houthis have engaged in hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including attacks on civilian airports and other critical infrastructure resulting in civilian casualties and severe travel disruptions. The hostilities have the potential to escalate rapidly beyond that immediate area.” That’s obviously a pretty serious problem for WWE considering Crown Jewel is supposed to take place in Riyadh in just over two weeks. Getting the roster into the country is one thing, but the U.S. government is now putting additional restrictions on its own personnel when it comes to using Saudi airports. “U.S. government employees working in Saudi Arabia require special authorization from Chief of Mission to use any airport in Saudi Arabia following recent missile and UAV attacks on airports in the Kingdom.” The biggest concern for WWE is King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh. Despite previously beginning limited operations following earlier attacks, the latest Embassy alert says operations at the airport are once again suspended. “Operations at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh remain suspended. King Abdulaziz International Airport in Jeddah and King Fahd International Airport in Dammam are operational with some delays and cancellations.” That leaves Jeddah and Dammam as operational options, but even those airports aren’t exactly running normally. The Embassy says both are dealing with delays and cancellations as the security situation continues. title: Cody Rhodes plans WWE run of six to seven years

summary_src: Cody Rhodes discussed his current WWE contract and addressed previous statements on plans to wrestle until the age of 40. The WWE star told Chris Van Vliet on the Insight Podcast that he estimates his current contract to run for another six or seven years.
body: Cody Rhodes discussed his current WWE contract and addressed previous statements on plans to wrestle until the age of 40. “I just signed my last contract. I say last contract, but that’s going to go for a while, and if I’m able to do what I’ve been able to do, because I would love this year not to be just one movie, but perhaps two movies, and I’d love to kind of be able to share that at some point, get that going, and be in that. With all that said, my time with WWE could go,” said Rhodes. “I mean, just to give you a real answer here, and not politic around you, probably seven years……Yeah, six, seven years. I’d say so. Yeah, and I don’t want to say that in a final sense. I just know that I don’t want to overstay my welcome.” In the same interview, Vliet referenced AJ Styles’ statement of not wanting to wrestle into his 50s, and questioned whether Rhodes felt the same sentiments. “Well, I definitely don’t want to wrestle into my 50s. No shame to anyone who wrestles in their 50s. I don’t want to overstay my welcome in a sense of this, right? So, I have been given so much from wrestling, and you have to think about my career in its totality. The things that we don’t talk about, the things that I don’t get asked about anymore. You have to think about all that. I have shed so much of my skin for the industry, but I have also been given so, so, so much. I think there’s a point where you have to stop taking. I’m not there, but there’s a point, and I think that’s in that time frame, a point where you just have to stop taking. It’s giving me everything.” “I am talking to you today, the first time I talked to you, I was a mid-card talent at WWE, and no shame to anything in the mid-card. Mid-card’s beautiful. I heard Triple H explain mid-card in a way that changed my perception of it forever. But I was a mid-card talent with a ceiling that was right above my head, and I’m talking to you today as someone who got to play Guile from Street Fighter, created by Capcom, a game that I played growing up as a little kid. Again, be careful what you wish for, but also I don’t know how many moments like this I can take, and I can get hopefully more, hopefully a lot more. But I’ve been so lucky so far and so blessed so far that I think wrestling. I mean, Cody fatigue is already pretty set in.” Rosanne Raphael Rosanne Raphael is a wrestling writer with over three and a half years of experience covering all things related to the industry. Rosanne previously contributed to Sportskeeda as an Assistant Content Manager. When not consumed by wrestling, Rosanne is a musician and an aspiring artist.

body: The field for NJPW Super Junior Tag League 2026 has been shaken up because of an injury to El Desperado. NJPW has announced that Desperado is out of the tournament , where he was supposed to team with Mistico. It will now be Mistico partnering with NJPW Young Lion Masatora Yasuda. The tournament begins this Saturday (October 24) and runs until the finals are held at Power Struggle on November 3. Desperado & Mistico are the current IWGP Junior Heavyweight Tag Team Champions. They were set to be one of the six teams in A Block, but Desperado is out due to the diagnosis of spinal canal stenosis and a hernia. Desperado apologized to fans and, while a timeline for when he’ll be back in action has not been announced, said the Despe Invitacional show he’s producing on November 9 is still happening. Young Lions usually do not fare well record-wise in NJPW tournaments, so it seems unlikely that Mistico & Yasuda will prevail as the Super Junior Tag League winners. The winning team will earn the Super Junior Tag League trophy as well as a shot at the IWGP Tag Team titles. title: On the Record: Cody Rhodes Praises Vidyut Jammwal After Street Fighter Movie
raw_title: Cody Rhodes Praises Vidyut Jammwal After Street Fighter Movie
body: WWE Undisputed Champion Cody Rhodes has plenty of experience sharing the spotlight with larger-than-life personalities, but Indian actor and martial artist Vidyut Jammwal apparently left a lasting impression on him. Rhodes recently opened up about his experience working with Jammwal on the live-action Street Fighter movie, praising his physique, martial arts background, and generosity toward his co-stars. The conversation offered fans a glimpse into the chemistry behind the scenes of the upcoming video game adaptation, which brings together performers from professional wrestling, comedy, and Hollywood action cinema. Cody Rhodes did not hold back when discussing his first impression of Jammwal. “I think I’ve met the most handsome man that’s ever been seen,” Rhodes recalled telling his wife after meeting the Indian actor. He also praised Jammwal’s physical conditioning, describing him as exceptionally muscular and someone whose appearance immediately stood out. Andrew Schulz, who also stars in Street Fighter , shared the enthusiasm. The comedian described Jammwal as a fascinating personality and highlighted his fitness, looks, and unusual approach to life. For Rhodes, however, the admiration went beyond appearances. He described Jammwal as a quiet individual who became increasingly interesting once people got to know him. That impression appears to have made the actor memorable to several members of the production, with Rhodes suggesting that people who met Jammwal often left talking about the encounter. title: On the Record: RevPro’s Andy Quildan on pulling Leon Slater match from MyAEW feed: ‘Maybe we did the wrong thing’
raw_title: RevPro’s Andy Quildan on pulling Leon Slater match from MyAEW feed: ‘Maybe we did the wrong thing’
body: Among the numerous headlines from RevPro’s massive 14th anniversary show last month, one was, unfortunately, tied to industry drama. Those who watched the prominent BritWres brand’s London event via MyAEW PPV noticed that one match didn’t air on the feed: TNA Wrestling’s Leon Slater facing fellow UK star Liam Slater. Initially, many wondered whether the match not airing on MyAEW was a decision made by TNA, who has pulled their talent from matchups involving AEW wrestlers in the past. But, in the days that followed, it came out that RevPro owner Andy Quildan was actually the one who made the move not to put the match on the service. Quildan initially explained to F4WOnline’s Dave Meltzer that he wanted to avoid any issues that could come from putting a TNA talent on an AEW service. He also stressed that the decision came without any influence from either company. In a recent interview with POST Wrestling, RevPro’s Quildan was asked if he will continue to black out appearances from TNA stars when they present shows on MyAEW going forward. Still reflecting on the decision, Quildan was undecided. “I’m not sure, to be honest,” he said. “I was trying to make everyone’s life as easy as possible. My role, as an independent wrestling promoter, has always been to get the match in the ring to try and have foresight. You try to envision every single problem that could occur before it becomes a problem. And the last thing we want is for anything to become an issue on the day, or post-show, or anything like that. And it’s crazy; with the benefit of hindsight, maybe we did the wrong thing, because that almost created more attention on the situation. I think, as we do with everything, we have to learn, we have to evolve, we have to adapt and move forward.” “I don’t want to be involved in any wrestling politics. I always say, we are open to do good business with anyone. I know in business it’s almost impossible, especially when there’s so much tribalism that goes around, but I want to be on the good side of everyone. And I want everyone to know that when they do business with us, we will do good business and we will try and do best by the company, and I don’t want anything to be received as, we’re trying to sneak people into places.” As a way to make up for the blackout, RevPro has uploaded Slater’s match onto Youtube for free. In regard to RevPro’s future on MyAEW, Quildan noted that he plans to be selective about which shows could be sold as PPVs on the service. He explained that some of the venues they run don’t have a reliable internet connection, and that he wouldn’t want to sell PPVs for shows where a feed might struggle to stay on air. POST’s full hour-long discussion with Quildan can be watched here.

title: WWE NXT Expected to Go Head-to-Head With AEW Blood & Guts on November 4
raw_title: WWE NXT Expected to Go Head-to-Head With AEW Blood & Guts on November 4
summary_src: WWE NXT is about to find itself in a pretty unusual Wednesday night fight. The November 4 episode is expected to move away from its normal Tuesday slot, putting NXT directly against AEW’s annual Blood & Guts edition of Dynamite.
body: Upcoming listings for NXT, including Netflix and Futon Critic , currently have the show airing Wednesday, November 4. The move comes because The CW will have coverage tied to the U.S. midterm elections on Tuesday, November 3. “I don’t know this 100%. I was told by people who know that CW wants to move NXT to that Wednesday. It probably will be moved because if it’s on Tuesday, it’ll be preempted on far too many stations.” The problem for WWE is that Wednesday isn’t exactly an empty night. AEW already has Blood & Guts lined up for November 4, with two Blood & Guts matches set for what is traditionally one of Dynamite’s biggest special episodes of the year. “That’s the night of Blood and Guts. AEW has the two Blood and Guts matches they set up tonight that are going to be pretty wild.” Things get even stranger because NXT wouldn’t be WWE’s only programming running that night. WWE EVOLVE airs Wednesdays at 8 PM ET on Tubi, while Main Event recently moved to the same time slot on Rumble. That means WWE could have three different shows airing against AEW Dynamite at the same time. As Meltzer pointed out, WWE wouldn’t just be competing with Blood & Guts — its own shows would also be competing with each other for wrestling fans. “WWE will actually have three shows going against Blood and Guts. They’re going to have NXT, which isn’t 100% but is probable, the Evolve show, and the Main Event show, all at the same time.” For AEW, the timing means Blood & Guts suddenly has a lot more wrestling competition than expected. Meltzer described the situation as WWE going up against one of AEW’s signature shows while simultaneously splitting its own Wednesday night audience across three programs. “They’re competing with themselves on three levels, and they’re competing with one of AEW’s signature shows of the year on their own night.” This doesn’t appear to be WWE deliberately moving NXT to Wednesday just to counter AEW, since the midterm election coverage is driving the expected schedule change. Still, the end result is another NXT versus Dynamite showdown, only this time WWE could have three different shows fighting for viewers on the exact same night. title: On the Record: Ilja Dragunov Speaks On Wrestling Tribalism After Joining AEW
raw_title: Ilja Dragunov Addresses Wrestling Tribalism After Joining AEW
summary_src: Ilja Dragunov isn’t interested in picking sides when it comes to the tribalism between wrestling fans.
body: Speaking to Jon Alba of The TakeDown on SI , Dragunov was asked about the divided wrestling fanbase and all the different styles currently being shown on national television. For Dragunov, the tribalism ultimately comes from the same place that makes wrestling work in the first place — emotion. “I mean, this is a good question. I mean, there are multiple questions layered into this about tribalism. I believe this is an emotionally driven business because, at the end of the day, wherever you watch professional wrestling, people go there to feel something.” Dragunov didn’t criticize fans for preferring one promotion over another either. As far as he’s concerned, people finding that emotional connection with wrestling is what actually matters. “You know, this is what they want to do. If they do it on one side, that’s okay. If they do it on the other side, that’s okay.” That attitude also ties into how Dragunov approaches his own matches. While wrestling can come in plenty of different forms, he has always viewed what he does as a combination of legitimate-looking combat and art. Dragunov then pointed to some of the wrestlers who helped shape that philosophy. His list stretched across different eras and styles, but they all shared the ability to make what happened inside the ring feel like something more than just a collection of moves. “That’s what all my role models did, like Kobashi, Terry Funk, Roddy Piper, William Regal, Meiko Satomura.” That’s also a big part of why Dragunov believes AEW is the right place for him now. He feels the company is looking for exactly the kind of dramatic, fight-heavy wrestling he’s spent his career trying to create. “And I feel like these values and what I’m standing for, to really be, in my mind, about the most dramatic and beautiful fight, is what AEW is looking for.” Dragunov isn’t trying to turn his arrival in AEW into another WWE-versus-AEW argument. For him, the bigger opportunity is getting to bring his own idea of what wrestling should feel like to a company he believes is actively looking for it. body: El Desperado has been ruled out of the NJPW Super Junior Tag League 2026 due to injury. New Japan Pro-Wrestling announced on Thursday, October 22, that one-half of the current IWGP Junior Heavyweight Tag Team Champions, El Desperado, has been diagnosed with spinal canal stenosis and a hernia. El Desperado and Mistico were originally drawn in Block A. However, with the former having been ruled out, Mistico will now team with NJPW Young Lion Masatora Yasuda. Desperado said his body has reached its limit and apologized to fans. No timeline is currently set for his return. Here’s what he said: “My sincerest apologies, but I will not be appearing at Super Jr. Tag League. I’m currently dealing with spinal canal stenosis and a hernia. My left leg has no strength, and with the pain and pins and needles, I’m currently unable to stand, walk, or even sit upright for long periods of time. From the start of this year I’d noticed some strange sensations in my left glute, and there was some tingling in my legs from around March. At that point I expressed to the company that I was having some symptoms but that I had no issues with strength or anything like that and asked to continue wrestling while staying in contact with the medical and training staff. “For this Super Jr. Tag League, Mistico was scheduled to wrestle with me, and we can’t just send him back with nothing to say for it, so I have chosen (Masatora) Yasuda to replace me. title: Ilja Dragunov Feels Creative Freedom In AEW
raw_title: Former WWE Star Ilja Dragunov On His Experience Since Joining AEW: 'I Feel Freedom'
summary_src: Ilja Dragunov has praised his AEW experience so far, explaining how joining the promotion has given him a sense of freedom.
body: Dragunov, who was let go by WWE earlier this year, debuted in Tony Khan's promotion at the WrestleDream pay-per-view . Following his AEW debut, the former WWE United States Champion spoke to " The Takedown on SI ," saying that his initial impressions of the company are great and that he felt a great sense of freedom there. "It lets my heart beat faster, and I feel like I re-fell in love with professional wrestling in some kind of way. The experience that I've had so far is having people around me that really want to portray everything that is going on in my mind, that really understand what I'm doing," said Dragunov. "They want to enhance what I'm doing and they want to put it into the right light, what I'm doing. And I feel if you can describe it with some word, I feel freedom." He has spoken positively about his AEW stint so far, describing it as a collaborative effort in which he and the AEW creative team have agreed on many creative decisions. Dragunov's debut had a major hurdle as he had to renew his visa , which all came together at the last minute. His decision to leave WWE was down to the TKO-owned promotion failing to offer him a satisfactory contract , prompting him to explore new opportunities. Dragunov has started his AEW career on a positive note, defeating Mike Bailey in the main event of the October 21 episode of " AEW Dynamite ."

title: Shayna Baszler Signs With TNA Wrestling
raw_title: Shayna Baszler Signs With TNA Wrestling
summary_src: Shayna Baszler isn’t just passing through TNA after winning championship gold at Bound For Glory.
body: Speaking to Denise Salcedo on October 22 , Baszler was asked whether she planned on staying with TNA following her championship victory alongside Zoey Serrano. Baszler confirmed the signing and made it clear she expects to be around for a while. “I mean, yeah, that’s what being a champion means, right? And the funny part about it is, we were so confident of the win that, yeah, I signed with TNA knowing we were going to win those titles and that I’d have to be around to put those on the line and beat up anyone that tries to come near them.” Shayna Baszler and Zoey Serrano aren’t planning on playing it safe with the titles either. She wants to defend them against basically anyone willing to step up, whether that’s inside TNA or somewhere else. “So, for the time being, that’s what’s going to happen. You should be seeing lots of broken limbs. We want to defend against everyone all over the place. So, we will carry these into wherever and invite anyone that wants to come in as well.” Baszler also explained why she decided to sign with TNA at this point in her career. She had been spending time coaching and producing at WWE NXT and EVOLVE, and she admitted that helping younger wrestlers develop had become something she genuinely loved. “But, you know, number one, if a friend calls you to help beat someone up, you help them beat someone up and then ask them why after that. That’s a Ronda Rousey thing. So when Zoey calls me, like, okay, yeah, I’ll beat someone up if you need me to help you beat someone up.” The bigger turning point came from Baszler’s Bloodsport match against Natalya. Afterwards, Nattie reminded her that they could still perform at a high level, and Baszler said that made something click for her about how much she still has left. “But I think, honestly, that match I had with Nattie at Bloodsport, she grabbed me afterwards and was like, ‘This is what I want people to know. We can still go.’ And it’s like, yeah, wait a second. Yeah, I can still go. And there’s still no one that can do the things I do the way that I do it.” Baszler isn’t ready to move completely into the coaching side of wrestling just yet. She still feels she has something unique to offer inside the ring, and until she’s satisfied someone else can carry that style forward, the itch to compete isn’t going away. “And I think until I’m satisfied that that banner can be carried, I think I’ll always have this itch to spread the gospel of legitimacy. So I think TNA is the perfect place for me right now.” Baszler and Serrano defeated Allie and Kiera Hogan for the TNA Knockouts World Tag Team Championships at Bound For Glory on October 11. Baszler ultimately choked Allie out to secure the titles, but until now, it wasn’t clear exactly what her long-term status with the company looked like. title: Penta Recalls Stress Before Roman Reigns Bout
raw_title: Penta Recalls Stressful Day Leading Up To Roman Reigns Match
summary_src: Penta was quite stressed out before his match with Roman Reigns. The bout between Penta and Reigns took place on the September 14 edition of WWE Raw. Despite his loss, fans argue that Penta emerged from the match as a new main event player for WWE.
body: Penta was quite stressed out before his match with Roman Reigns. The bout between Penta and Reigns took place on the September 14 edition of WWE Raw. Despite his loss, fans argue that Penta emerged from the match as a new main event player for WWE. In a new interview with Busted Open Radio, Penta recalled the hours leading up to the championship bout. “Now I’m relaxed, I can tell you what happened all day but that day, it was too much stress for me because I have a lot of things in my brain. The first thing is against Roman Reigns, first time ever. Mexico City. My family is there. Hours before that, you saw my arrival shot in the arena with the horse. Two hours before my match, maybe three, problems with the horse. Maybe it’s not here, maybe it’s delayed, maybe something. You need makeup, I need to go the ring, I practice this. Oh, you have an interview. Oh, you have a meet and greet. To be honest, two days later than my match, I started sitting in my garden like, ‘Wow.’ I promise you, two days later because in that moment, everything is on my brain. Hey Penta, you need interview. Oh, Roman is here. Oh, the horse will come. I become crazy in that moment. When I opened my eyes, they were like, ‘You are next.’ Oh shit. Everything was too fast, but in the same moment, I try to enjoy every moment and every interview. The name is Mexico here is a penacho, I use it for my presentation. The guys, ‘Hey, I’m gonna be late.’ Come on. Everything was rushed but at the end of the day, it was perfect.” Continuing on, Penta admitted that he learned a lot from Reigns. “I learned a lot facing Roman Reigns. To be honest, I know now why he is one of the best wrestlers or the best wrestler in the universe. The character, the Shakespeare, every move you can breathe, you can enjoy every move. Bro, it’s different. But I like it, I like that style, I like feeling this moment in the ring when it’s the big dog basically. He looks at me, I look at him, the whole crowd is with me, thank god. Everything was so special and magic.” If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.
summary: Penta felt overwhelmed in the hours leading up to his match against Roman Reigns on the September 14 episode of WWE Raw in Mexico City. In an interview with Busted Open Radio, Penta said he only began to process the experience two days afterward while sitting in his garden.

title: Ronda Rousey Threatened to Quit WWE Over Treatment of Women’s Division

summary_src: Ronda Rousey apparently took her fight for WWE’s women’s division all the way to company headquarters after losing time from one of her pay-per-view matches.
body: Speaking to Denise Salcedo , Baszler pushed back on the idea that Rousey never genuinely cared about professional wrestling. She said there were plenty of things Rousey did behind the scenes that fans — and sometimes even the women in WWE’s locker room — never knew about. “I’ve heard people be like, ‘Ronda didn’t really care about wrestling.’ Like, Ronda, she might hate me telling this story, but there was a time where Ronda had a pay-per-view match and got six minutes cut off of her match because a match before had gone over their time.” Baszler stressed that losing six minutes wasn’t some minor inconvenience. With wrestlers trying to tell an entire story within a limited window, she said even having a single minute taken away can make a huge difference. “And it’s like, to take six minutes from a match is huge. To take one minute from a match, in order to build a story and get emotion involved, it takes time.” According to Baszler, Rousey made it clear during that meeting that money and fame weren’t keeping her in WWE. She wanted to help push women’s wrestling forward, and she was apparently willing to walk away if WWE told her that wasn’t going to happen. “I don’t need to be here to make money. I don’t need to be here to get famous. I’m here to help advance this. And if you’re telling me right now that’s never going to happen, then I’m done. I only want to improve this.” What stood out to Baszler was that Rousey never tried to make the incident public or use it to make herself look good. In fact, she doesn’t even believe most of the women sharing the locker room with Rousey knew what she had done. “And she, you know, no one will ever—she’s not going to tell you that story. She’s not going to tweet about it. She’s not going to go on a thing and talk about it. And nobody’s going to know about the stuff she did like that behind the scenes on her own dime just to argue for the women’s locker room.” “I don’t even think girls in the locker room even knew she did that, you know what I mean? So, just the stuff she would do like that. And then on top of, yeah, like you said, bringing her name and bringing new eyes. There’s many MMA fans that would never have watched professional wrestling because it’s that scary F-word, right? It’s not real. And I think they tuned in just because, ‘Let’s see what happens here.’ And then, much like Ronda, becoming a fan, got sucked into the story.” Whether Rousey ever gets credit for everything she did is another question. Baszler thinks that recognition could come eventually, but she also suggested Rousey was never particularly interested in getting praised for those things in the moment. “So, you know, will she ever get the credit? Maybe years down the road. But I think that’s something Ronda, for her own sanity, I’m glad she doesn’t care to receive the credit in the moment because she did a lot. body: It hasn’t even been a full year since Blake Monroe left NXT. Yet, this past Tuesday’s NXT on CW aired a video of an Evolve talent set to make her debut. The name of this talent really raised eyebrows, as Chantel Monroe is coming to NXT. Now, Blake Monroe reacts to the controversial teaser for Chantel Monroe’s NXT debut. There has been a quicker churn rate for the NXT-WWE pipeline as of late. For instance, Mariah May debuted in NXT as Blake Monroe, and within a year got promoted to SmackDown. These faster-paced call-ups have raised concerns that talents are joining the Main Roster before they are ready. Case in point, Blake Monroe made her SmackDown debut in London back in June. However, she didn’t make her in-ring debut until October. Even then, Blake Monroe’s first WWE match was delayed with many false starts against Giulia. All of that said, WWE still needs to fill the hole growing in the developmental system as NXT stars transition to the Main Roster. One of the lucky names to help fill that gap is Chantel Monroe. The NIL Superstar is expected to make her NXT debut soon, and it’s drawn a lot of criticism from the Internet Wrestling Community. While Blake Monroe has had a turbulent transition from AEW to WWE , she’s starting to settle into a regular role on SmackDown. That said, many things about Blake Monroe’s NXT presentation were stripped away for her WWE run. Fans of Mariah May noted that her mirror entrance was noticeably lacking compared to her NXT days. Perhaps that’s because WWE was saving it for another Monroe? Chantel Monroe’s NXT teaser featured the 26-year-old star looking into a mirror and telling people to pay attention to her. The teaser focused on a lot of close-up shots of Chantel Monroe’s face and makeup. Much of the content was very reminiscent of how Blake Monroe was introduced to the WWE Universe. Understandably, WWE fans took to social media to call out the name and character resemblance. While Chantel Monroe might have had a Next in Line WWE contract, many think she’s next in line to be Blake Monroe. The All-American gymnast signed with WWE in 2022 and started training after her graduation from Auburn in 2023. By 2024, Derrian Gobourne had her first matches at NXT House Shows under her real name. Even with Mariah May under the WWE banner, Derrian Gobourne’s name was changed to Chantel Monroe in 2025. Now, it appears that she will keep the name after her spotlight aired on NXT. title: Penta Feels Power From Money In The Bank Victory
raw_title: Penta Feels Like He Has 'The Fucking Power In His Hands' After Money In The Bank Win
summary_src: Penta is on top of the world. After failing to capture the World Heavyweight Championship from Roman Reigns, Penta was widely expected to return to the midcard scene. Instead, he changed the trajectory of his career by winning the Money In The Bank briefcase just a few weeks later.
body: After failing to capture the World Heavyweight Championship from Roman Reigns, Penta was widely expected to return to the midcard scene. Instead, he changed the trajectory of his career by winning the Money In The Bank briefcase just a few weeks later. Speaking with Busted Open Radio for a new interview , Penta said that he sometimes can’t believe what is happening with his career right now. “Actually, I want to be honest with you. Sometimes, I can’t believe it, what is happening right now. But at the same time, I feel know what is my responsibility now in this business. Every time more [children] come to me, every child uses my t-shirt, my mask, cero miedo, he can say it in Spanish but he tried. When I saw that, it’s like okay, I know now my responsibility with the crowd. I feel great because now my brother started growing up in different kinds of stuff, he is in SmackDown now and I am Raw. But, the time when my brother came to Raw, amazing too.” Continuing on, Penta said that he has the “fucking power in his hands” with the briefcase. “But, as for a briefcase, I actually feel like that. I have the fucking power in my hands basically because at one time, I don’t know where, I don’t know when, but when I feel it in my soul that it is the perfect time for a cash-in, I will. Now, I started thinking something, Roman, you know Sami. I don’t know because it’s my first time but at the same time, I want to do the best, forget the world champions, you know? But for now, I enjoy every presentation with my briefcase, with fire, everything involving about it. I enjoy it.” If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.

title: On the Record: Joe Hendry Speaks On Possibility of Turning Heel in WWE
raw_title: Joe Hendry Addresses Possibility of Turning Heel in WWE
summary_src: Joe Hendry might be one of WWE’s biggest fan-favorites right now, but that’s definitely not how this character was supposed to work. Hendry says he originally created his current persona with the expectation that wrestling fans would absolutely hate him.
body: Speaking with TV Insider , Hendry was asked whether he could eventually show a darker side instead of sticking with the upbeat character that fans have embraced. His answer revealed that the audience already changed his plans once before. “When I was putting together who Joe Hendry is, and I made the music video and all that, it was with the intention that he would be universally hated.” Obviously, things didn’t exactly go according to plan. Instead of rejecting the character, fans latched onto Hendry, his music and everything else surrounding the gimmick: “The opposite happened.” Rather than fighting against that reaction, Hendry allowed the character to go wherever the fans wanted to take it. That’s also why he isn’t locking himself into staying a babyface or eventually turning darker. “So, you know, the audience dictated what happened there, and I think they will continue to dictate that.” That approach has worked out pretty well for Hendry so far, with the character becoming far more popular than he originally intended. The funny part is that one of wrestling’s most naturally likable acts was apparently designed to get exactly the opposite reaction. As for whether fans eventually get a darker Joe Hendry, he’s leaving that decision open rather than forcing a change. If his character takes another unexpected turn, Hendry seems perfectly happy letting the audience decide where things go next. title: Damian Priest Feels Better After 2025 Reduced Schedule
raw_title: Damian Priest Reflects On Reduced Schedule In 2025, ‘I Had To Check Myself A Little Bit’
body: During the back half of 2025, Priest worked a reduced in-ring schedule to help out with some of his nagging injuries. Now, just a year later, he is in a good place both physically and mentally. “Well, we’re never okay. It is what we do, you know. No bitching and moaning, I don’t like overly talking about how my body is because I’m still showing up to do the job. It’s not an excuse. I’m not the only one banged up. So if my opponent’s banged up too, we’re on an even playing field. So I don’t like to rely on that. But, I’m feeling a lot better. I got some procedures done while I never took a day off, you know what I mean? So, I got some stuff done to ease pain and I feel a lot better. I think people can see it visually. I’m training differently, I’m getting back into the shape that I used to be in and it’s all because I feel better. I’m in a better head place too, you know — I got myself down and for somebody who likes to think positively of myself and my career, I started doing the opposite and I had to check myself a little bit. So that came with my health, physically and mentally. I’m in a good place now, man. It is what it is.” Damian Priest told WWE Radio’s Off The Ropes in a new interview . title: Possible Reason Behind Daria Rae’s TNA Television Absence
raw_title: Possible Reason Behind Daria Rae’s TNA Television Absence
summary_src: Daria Rae has been missing from TNA television for more than a month, but that absence is finally about to end. The former Sonya Deville is set to return on the October 22 episode of TNA iMPACT!, and it sounds like she may have been keeping pretty busy while her character was suspended. During a ...
body: During a PWInsider Q&A , Mike Johnson was asked where Rae had disappeared to after TNA wrote her off television. Johnson pointed out that the company already gave fans the storyline explanation, but confirmed she’s now ready to pop back up. “The storyline was she was suspended, but she is slated to return on tonight’s episode, which was pre-taped.” Rae was suspended from her Director of Operations role back in September after things got physical with Indi Hartwell. The two had been butting heads for weeks, with Rae repeatedly blocking Hartwell from getting a shot at the TNA Knockouts World Championship before eventually slapping her. That gave TNA an easy reason to get Rae off television, but apparently she had plenty going on away from wrestling too. Johnson said he knows Rae had several acting commitments and believes that’s what she was working on during her absence. “I know she had a lot of acting commitments, so my belief is she was working on those.” That doesn’t necessarily mean TNA suspended Rae specifically because of those acting commitments, since Johnson made it clear that part is his belief. Either way, the timing worked out pretty nicely, allowing Rae to handle outside projects while her character served the storyline suspension. Things also didn’t exactly stop moving while she was gone. Santino Marella stepped in and gave Hartwell the Knockouts World Championship opportunity Rae had spent so much time trying to keep away from her. Now Rae is walking back into a TNA that kept moving without her, which could make things pretty interesting for the Director of Operations. After more than a month away, fans won’t have to wait much longer to find out what she has to say about everything that happened behind her back. summary_src: Shayna Baszler is officially under contract with TNA Wrestling after debuting for the company at Bound for Glory. The October 11 pay-per-view saw former WWE wrestlers Baszler & Zoey Serrano (Zoey Stark) defeat Allie & Kiera Hogan to become the new Knockouts Tag Team Champions.
body: Shayna Baszler is officially under contract with TNA Wrestling after debuting for the company at Bound for Glory. The October 11 pay-per-view saw former WWE wrestlers Baszler & Zoey Serrano (Zoey Stark) defeat Allie & Kiera Hogan to become the new Knockouts Tag Team Champions. TNA then sent out an announcement today confirming that the promotion has signed Baszler to a contract: Before joining TNA, Baszler, Serrano, and TNA on-screen authority figure Daria Rae (Sonya Deville) were already allies from their time in WWE. Baszler & Serrano’s tag team has been given the name “Apex” in TNA. Baszler told Denise Salcedo that, while she doesn’t feel like her career is anywhere close to the end, she has been thinking about her legacy more often lately. With a background in MMA before bringing that style into her pro wrestling career, Baszler wants her legitimacy to be what people remember. Baszler was released by WWE in May 2025 but has maintained a good relationship with the company, including spending some time helping out backstage in NXT . In addition to signing Baszler, TNA has also added Shotzi Blackheart and Amazing Red to its roster, along with re-signing Director of Authority Santino Marella . Joseph joined F4W during his time at UMass and has now been writing about the industry for nearly a decade. In addition to his work with F4W, Joseph has previously contributed to Sports Illustrated's wrestling coverage. He lives in Massachusetts and is a diehard fan of the Boston sports teams and Liverpool Football Club.
