title: Cody Rhodes Again Dangles Idea of Future Match With The Rock
raw_title: Cody Rhodes Again Dangles Idea of Future Match With The Rock
body: “It’s not that I’m evading that answer,” Rhodes said. “I think personally he has a couple of matches probably left to do.” Rhodes pointed to WrestleMania 40 as a fitting final performance if The Rock decided to leave it there, but he made it clear the decision is not his to make. “That’ll be up to him. That’ll certainly be up to him, if there’s more and what those matches might be,” Rhodes said. He also said he would not turn down the opportunity. “I don’t think any wrestler would ever look you in the eye and tell you they wouldn’t want a match like that,” Rhodes said. “So maybe a match like that does happen. Maybe.” The two have only faced each other in one match. On night one of WrestleMania 40 in April 2024, The Rock teamed with Roman Reigns to beat Rhodes and Seth Rollins. The next night, Rhodes beat Reigns in a Bloodline Rules match to win the Undisputed WWE Universal Championship, in a match that also saw The Rock interfere. The night one tag match remains The Rock’s most recent WWE match. The story began when The Rock slapped Rhodes at the WrestleMania 40 kickoff event in February 2024 and aligned himself with Reigns and The Bloodline. The Rock returned in 2025 and set up the Elimination Chamber angle in which Rhodes turned down his offer, and John Cena turned heel and attacked Rhodes. Rhodes also discussed The Rock during an appearance on Mythical Kitchen’s Last Meals. “That’s the most complicated male relationship I have in my life,” Rhodes said. He noted that the history between the two goes beyond what fans see on television. “Our families have been linked for longer than people see,” Rhodes said, describing it as a “territorial tie” between the families. He then reflected on the WrestleMania 40 storyline. “There’s just a huge amount of reality with what happened at WrestleMania 40,” he said, describing it as The Rock “coming in, him taking my thing away, and me taking it back.” Rhodes also praised The Rock’s Final Boss persona as “one of the best characters” in wrestling. A Cody Rhodes vs. The Rock singles match is the one piece of the WrestleMania 40 story that never got its ending. The Rock was the heel who took the spotlight, and Rhodes overcame him and The Bloodline to finish his story. Fans never got the moment where Rhodes beat The Rock himself, and that is the match that would close the loop. The Rock’s schedule is the biggest obstacle. His film career and business commitments limit how often he can wrestle, and Rhodes is right that it is ultimately his call. But The Rock has not ruled out a return, and Rhodes’ new contract means he will be around for years. That gives both sides plenty of time to find the right WrestleMania for it.

body: NJPW have announced that El Desperado will miss the upcoming Super Jr. Tag League due to injury. The IWGP Junior Heavyweight Tag Team Champion has been diagnosed with spinal canal stenosis and a hernia. El Desperado posted a video on his YouTube channel addressing the injury, describing his symptoms, and his stepping away from the tournament. In it, he announced that Masatora Yasuda would be filling in for him, teaming with Mistico. The transcription of the video from the NJPW website is as follows: My sincerest apologies, but I will not be appearing at Super Jr. Tag League. I’m currently dealing with spinal canal stenosis and a hernia. My left leg has no strength, and with the pain and pins and needles I’m currently unable to stand, walk or even sit upright for long periods of time. From the start of this year I’d noticed some strange sensations in my left glute, and there was some tingling in my legs from around March. At that point I expressed to the company that I was having some symptoms, but that I had no issues with strength or anything like that, and asked to continue wrestling, while staying in contact with the medical and training staff. For this Super Jr. Tag League, Mistico was scheduled to wrestle with me, and we can’t just send him back with nothing to say for it, so I have chosen (Masatora) Yasuda to replace me. Some of you might think ‘with your connections you can come up with a bigger name than a Young Lion,’ but I’d like for you to think of this as a key step to the future of NJPW. And don’t worry about Mistico. Even with his partner like this, he’ll show up for the fans like Mistico always does. I have complete trust in him. So that’s it. I’m off Super Jr. Tag League, and Yasuda is in. Ah, and as for (November 9 Shin Kiba 1st Ring produce event) ‘Gaspe’ Invitational. I can’t move, but my desire to see something truly horrific trumps all that, so we’ll be going ahead as planned. Show up. El Desperado is also scheduled for a big singles match against his partner Mistico at the upcoming CMLL x NJPW event Lucha Kingdom on November 16th, but not statement has been made on whether he will be able to compete in Mexico City. Everyone here at Monthly Puroresu wishes El Desperado a speedy recovery.
summary: NJPW announced that El Desperado will miss the upcoming Super Jr Tag League after being diagnosed with spinal canal stenosis and a hernia. The IWGP Junior Heavyweight Tag Team Champion described losing strength in his left leg along with pain, pins and needles that prevent him from standing, walking or sitting for extended periods. Masatora Yasuda will replace him and team with Mistico.

title: Bayley Drops Bikini Video During WWE Hawaii Tour

summary_src: Bayley is making the most of WWE’s recent trip to Hawaii, and apparently that includes throwing herself off a boat.
body: Bayley posted the clip to Instagram alongside several other photos from her time in Hawaii. She kept the caption pretty simple, using a collection of emojis to sum up everything she got up to during the trip. The video showed Bayley enjoying some downtime on a boat before doing a somersault straight into the water. It wasn’t all ocean adventures either, as her post also included plenty of moments from WWE’s recent live event in Honolulu. Bayley shared photos from the show along with other snapshots of her time on the island, making it pretty clear she squeezed plenty of fun into the trip whenever she wasn’t busy with WWE. Between the wrestling, hiking, drinks, dolphins and boat trip represented in her caption, Hawaii certainly wasn’t all work. This also isn’t the first time Bayley has given fans a look at how she spends her downtime during WWE’s travels. Back in June, she turned heads with a bikini photo from Capri, Italy, while WWE was touring Europe . WWE’s travel schedule can keep its stars pretty busy, but Bayley clearly found time to turn the company’s Honolulu trip into a mini vacation of her own. Between getting in the ring and launching herself off a boat, she certainly didn’t waste the opportunity to enjoy Hawaii while she was there. title: Dispensa Lawsuit Against AEW and Moxley Stays in Michigan
raw_title: Dispensa lawsuit against AEW and Jon Moxley will stay in Michigan where incident occurred
summary_src: Injury case brought by production worker shoved at 2023 AEW Dynamite in Detroit will not be moved to Florida
body: Christopher Dispensa, who worked on AEW’s production team, sued AEW and Moxley (whose legal name is Jonathan Good) in May 2025. He alleges that during a match, Moxley deviated from the plan and shoved him to the floor at the May 10, 2023 show at Little Caesars Arena, allegedly leaving him with injuries that required cervical spine and shoulder surgery. The defendants asked the court to dismiss or put the case on hold so it could be refiled in Florida, where Dispensa lives, where most of his doctors are located, and where AEW is headquartered. Judge Catherine Heise rejected the defendants’ arguments in an order filed on October 5, which followed a hearing on September 17. She wrote that the incident, the likely fact witnesses, and the arena are all in Detroit, and in fact, the courthouse is “within healthy walking distance” of the arena. Medical witnesses who are in Florida can testify remotely, the judge wrote, and moving the case to a Florida court would present the problem of having an out-of-state court apply Michigan law to an injury that happened in Michigan. The judge also found that the defendants waited too long to make the request to move the case. They filed their motion to move the case to Florida on July 7, nearly ten months after AEW answered the complaint in September 2025. The defendants said they would not raise a three-year time-limit statute of limitations defense if the case was allowed to be litigated in Florida. But the judge expressed concern that in that scenario the case might get thrown out regardless. Heise wrote that she “is not confident that a Florida court would honor such an agreement or even an order so stating from a Michigan court.” The order does not rule on the merits of Dispensa’s injury claims, only that the case will continue to be litigated in a Michigan court before Heise. Dispensa’s claims include counts of assault and battery against Moxley, negligence and gross negligence against both Moxley and AEW, and negligent hiring, training, supervision, and retention against AEW. Dispensa has demanded a jury trial. A settlement conference with the court is scheduled for December 22, 2026. The docket shows the parties met for an earlier settlement conference on July 29, 2026, which resulted in those discussions being “held for further settlement.”
summary: A judge ruled that Christopher Dispensa's lawsuit against AEW and Jon Moxley will remain in Michigan. Dispensa claims Moxley went off-script during a 2023 match at Little Caesars Arena in Detroit and shoved him, causing injuries that led to cervical spine and shoulder surgery. The court determined that the incident location, witnesses and arena in Detroit made Michigan the proper venue, noting remote testimony options for Florida-based medical witnesses and that Michigan law would apply to the in-state injury.

llm_long: Christopher Dispensa, a former member of All Elite Wrestling's production team, filed a lawsuit against the promotion and wrestler Jonathan Good in May 2025. The suit claims that Good deviated from the planned sequence during a match at the May 10, 2023 event at Little Caesars Arena in Detroit. Dispensa alleges the deviation resulted in him being shoved to the floor and sustaining injuries that required cervical spine and shoulder surgery.

The defendants requested that the court dismiss the case or pause proceedings to allow it to be refiled in Florida. They cited Dispensa's residence in Florida, the location of most of his doctors there, and the fact that All Elite Wrestling is headquartered in the state. A hearing on the matter took place on September 17.

Judge Catherine Heise denied the request in an order issued on October 5. She determined that the incident occurred in Detroit, where likely fact witnesses and the arena are located. The courthouse is within walking distance of the arena.

The judge noted that medical witnesses based in Florida could provide remote testimony. She also pointed out that transferring the case would require a Florida court to apply Michigan law to an injury that took place in Michigan. Additionally, the defendants waited nearly ten months after All Elite Wrestling answered the complaint in September 2025 before filing their motion on July 7.

The defendants offered not to raise a three-year statute of limitations defense if the case moved to Florida. However, the judge expressed doubt that a Florida court would honor such an agreement or a related order from a Michigan court. The ruling does not address the validity of Dispensa's claims.

Dispensa's lawsuit includes counts of assault and battery against Good, negligence and gross negligence against both Good and All Elite Wrestling, and negligent hiring, training, supervision, and retention against All Elite Wrestling. He has requested a jury trial. A settlement conference is scheduled for December 22, 2026.

title: Meltzer Details WWE's Financial Stakes For Crown Jewel
raw_title: Dave Meltzer Explains Incentives For WWE To Go Through With Crown Jewel Amidst Conflict
summary_src: WWE Crown Jewel is scheduled for November 7 in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, despite the U.S. government advising Americans not to travel to the country.
body: On Wrestling Observer Radio , Bryan Alvarez stated he thinks WWE won't go to Saudi Arabia. He believes the fact that WWE is even considering going is a bad thing. Dave Meltzer agrees that going to Saudi Arabia right now is a terrible idea, but points to why WWE will most likely still go. "There's three shows upcoming, which would be two UFCs and the WWE, their (TKO) profit margin for the quarter would be down between $70 and $90 million which is about a quarter of their profit for the quarter," Meltzer explained. If they don't go, they would also be risking WrestleMania. Meltzer believes those factors are why WWE will proceed with Crown Jewel in Saudi Arabia. A recent tweet from Saudi's General Entertainment Authority director Turki Al-Sheikh seemed directed at WWE and TKO .
summary: Dave Meltzer acknowledged that holding the Crown Jewel event in Saudi Arabia at this time would be a poor decision. He noted that skipping the show along with two upcoming UFC events would reduce TKO's quarterly profit margin by $70 to $90 million, representing roughly one-quarter of their expected profit. Meltzer added that failing to proceed could also jeopardize WrestleMania, making it likely WWE will still go forward with the Saudi Arabia show.

body: "I can confirm it is [for] five years," Meltzer said. "I've seen people speculate it and everything, but I in fact did get it confirmed. It is a five year deal. So yeah, he's signed with WWE." The topic then turned to Lee's brother, AEW's Dralistico, who caused a stir earlier this week when he posted an AI photo of himself in prison, leading many to believe he was looking to leave AEW and possibly join Lee in WWE. Meltzer confirmed earlier reporting by co-host Bryan Alvarez that Dralistico's deal was up in December and that there was some belief in the industry that Dralistico wanted to leave. At the same time, however, Meltzer noted he had received info that suggested that Dralistico's picture had a different intent than the one many interpreted it to have. "I know, from an AEW standpoint, that they [believe that] they [WWE] are going to make him an offer," Meltzer said. "[But] I was told, from people close to him, that the thing with the bars and everything, that's because of the visa issue. It's not because he can't wait to leave, like Fenix."
summary: Dave Meltzer confirmed Dragon Lee signed a five-year contract with WWE. title: Top NXT Star Was Told She Was Too Old Before WWE Signing

body: 0 WWE NXT star Wren Sinclair has opened up about her professional wrestling journey. She revealed being told she was too old for WWE. Before signing, she was even advised to look elsewhere. Speaking to TMZ’s Inside the Ring , Wren Sinclair was asked whether she would still wrestle today. The question focused on what might have happened without WWE. Sinclair initially joked about imagining that alternate timeline. She then opened up about her love for wrestling. She said, “Let’s just not say I didn’t get signed. No, I’m kidding. Yeah. Despite those difficult moments, her passion never completely disappeared. “And I think at the end of the day, I’m not sure because I think I love this so much that it hurts sometimes when it doesn’t love you back. I’m a big proponent of mental health.” “So, depending on the journey that happened after said not being signed, I’m not sure. But I’m glad that I’m here, and I’m going to hold on to this, and I’m just never going to let them fire me.” WWE eventually signed Sinclair in 2023, giving her another opportunity. Now, she is preparing for the biggest match of her career. Sinclair will challenge Kelani Jordan for the NXT Women’s Championship scheduled for NXT Halloween Havoc. summary_src: The Hurt Syndicate’s strange AEW booking has led to plenty of questions, and now there’s another interesting wrinkle to the story. Sean Ross Sapp says there have been situations where members of the group didn’t want to put other wrestlers over.
body: Speaking on The Hump , Sapp was asked what’s actually going on with The Hurt Syndicate and why Bobby Lashley, Shelton Benjamin and MVP haven’t been featured consistently lately. He admitted he doesn’t know the exact reason behind their current booking. However, Sapp then addressed something that’s apparently been talked about regarding the group behind the scenes. While he didn’t say they’ve refused every creative idea thrown their way, he confirmed there have been occasions where they didn’t want to lose to certain opponents. “Listen, I know there’s been a lot of talk about them like not wanting to put people over. There’s definitely been some situations where they haven’t wanted to. That has been a thing.” Sapp didn’t identify which members of The Hurt Syndicate were involved in those situations, who AEW wanted them to put over or whether those disagreements directly caused their recent lack of television time. So there’s still plenty about the situation that isn’t known. The update comes after The Hurt Syndicate’s AEW presence has noticeably cooled off in recent months. Despite Bobby Lashley, Shelton Benjamin and MVP competing at All In in August, the faction hasn’t been anywhere near as consistently featured on Dynamite and Collision since then. Another recent report from Self Made Pro suggested fans shouldn’t expect that to change anytime soon. He claimed the group would appear intermittently on Collision for “random things” rather than returning as a serious weekly act. “They’re gonna show up intermittently on Collision to do random things.” He went even further by arguing that The Hurt Syndicate’s run as a major AEW act has essentially already ended, even if the faction itself hasn’t officially broken up. “I talk about how a lot of people’s runs end way before they actually end, and the Hurt Syndicate’s AEW run has already ended in real terms. So there you go, as in terms of a serious, consistent act.” For a group loaded with veterans like Lashley, Benjamin and MVP, protecting their credibility clearly matters. The bigger question is how AEW finds meaningful opponents and storylines for The Hurt Syndicate if there are certain finishes the group isn’t willing to do. title: TNA Impact Recaps Bound For Glory Title Changes

body: TNA Impact opened its broadcast this week recapping the highlights from their biggest show of the year, Bound For Glory including a number of title changes leading into a new season of storylines going into the fall. The show kicked off with the Hardys, Matt & Jeff, who acted as guest general managers of the show, in honor of their 35th year in the pro wrestling business. The Hardys talked about their own legacy, but then put the shine on other newly crowned champions starting with new X-Division Champion Amazing Redd, followed by new TNA World Champion Leon Slater. The Nemeths were backstage complaining about their match against each other, booked by the Hardys. Breakdown:With the episode of Impact being “booked” by the Hardys, I expected some wacky pairings and match concepts. In this short backstage segment, the Nemeth brothers came at odds when Nic Nemeth assumed his younger brother, Ryan, would take the fall in their match later in the evening. I’m not sure what they are expecting to achieve with this, but perhaps they are moving away from the Nemeths as a tag team. Santino Marella was backstage, enjoying his night off, when he was interrupted by The System. The System demanded a spot on the show, but Santino declared he was on vacation. Bear Bronson drew an issue with Eddie Edwards’ defense of Ricky Sosa. Breakdown: A split of the System may be coming soon and I can get behind that. The TNA Tag Team Champions, Nic & Ryan Nemeth, were booked by The Hardys to face off against each other on Impact this week with a stipulation that if they one intentionally took the fall, the Nemeths would be stripped of the tag titles. After avoiding contact with each other, The Hardys would appear on the entrance ramp to reiterate that the Nemeths would be stripped of the titles if they refused to fight each other. Nic Nemeth would score the victory over Ryan Nemeth shortly thereafter. Nic Nemeth complained that he was not included in the TNA World Title number one contenders ladder match. Breakdown: It was a bit jarring to hear Tom Hannifan talking more glowingly of Nic Nemeth while Matt Rehwoldt put over Ryan Nemeth strongly. The segment was basically for comedy. Expressions demanded the Hardys give AJ Francis a shot at the TNA World Championship. The Hardys countered by giving Francis & Expressions a match against the Hardys. Breakdown: Another segment that was meant for comedy, it did not do much for me. I continue to want more for Francis, but TNA clearly sees him as a comedy figure. Harley Hudson told The Righteous that she wanted to accompany them to the ring for the match against Syx, but they refused to allow her to join them. A match booked by the Hardys as a face-off of two of the Hardys’ recent rivals featured The Righteous and Syx in a table match. Breakdown: The match was not very long but it was decent action while it lasted. The TNA tag team division does seem to be heading in the right direction with the addition of Syx. body: The ‘Mad Dragon’ kicked off his AEW career in a big way by defeating ‘Speedball’ Mike Bailey on the October 21 episode of AEW Dynamite. This match was widely praised by fans, with some considering it to be Dragunov’s best match in quite some time. Speaking with The Takedown on Sports Illustrated , Ilja Dragunov praised AEW for being a company that works for the fans of professional wrestling. “It’s not really much that something is actually changing about the way that I’m working, because I have a lot of confidence of what I did in the past. title: End of an Era: WWE Discussing Plans for Rey Mysterio’s Retirement in 2027
raw_title: WWE Discussing Plans for Rey Mysterio’s Retirement in 2027
summary_src: Rey Mysterio has spent months saying he’s not ready to put a date on retirement, but WWE might already be thinking about his final run. There’s been growing backstage talk that 2027 could finally be the year the legendary luchador calls it a career inside the ring.
body: According to WrestleVotes Radio on Fightful Select , there have been recent “rumblings” within WWE about a major retirement coming next year. The name at the center of those conversations is Mysterio. “According to those that WrestleVotes spoke to, there have been rumblings of a legendary retirement within WWE in 2027, with that talk centering around Rey Mysterio.” Before anyone starts circling a WrestleMania date, nothing is officially locked in yet. The source didn’t know exactly when or where Rey would wrestle his final match, but said the chatter at WWE television lately has pointed toward 2027 being the end of the road. “A source confirmed that they didn’t have any direct knowledge of when or where an official retirement would take place — instead indicating that recent chatter at TV has pointed towards next year marking the end of the road for Rey Mysterio as an active wrestler.” WWE has apparently gone beyond simply wondering when Rey might be finished. The company has reportedly kicked around ideas for how to handle his farewell if he does decide that next year is the right time. “According to the same source, WWE has discussed ideas on how to present his farewell.” Retirement wouldn’t necessarily mean Rey is packing up and disappearing from WWE either. There’s reportedly a feeling that he could stick around and help the next generation once he’s done taking bumps himself. “Much like his counterpart AJ Styles, there’s a feeling among many within WWE that Rey will remain involved once his in-ring days are behind him, as he’ll continue to play a vital role in the development of next-generation talent in WWE and AAA.” “I think I’m just going to wing it and see where this road takes me, you know, because I’m really enjoying the moments right now that I’m living inside the ring, whether as a wrestler or as a GM.” Rey also said he was feeling “really, really good” physically and enjoying a schedule that doesn’t beat him up four or five nights every week anymore. Between wrestling, his GM duties and his involvement with AAA, he sounded pretty happy with where things stood. So this isn’t Rey Mysterio announcing his retirement, and there isn’t a confirmed farewell match sitting on WWE’s calendar. For now, it’s backstage chatter — but WWE apparently thinking about how to send him off makes 2027 a whole lot more interesting. If Rey does decide next year is it, WWE will have plenty of time to make the goodbye count instead of having his career quietly wind down. After everything he’s meant to the company and lucha libre as a whole, there’s no shortage of directions WWE could go if it really is preparing for one last ride. title: Legal Watch: Judge Denies AEW and Jon Moxley’s Request to Move Assault and Battery Lawsuit to Florida
raw_title: Judge Denies AEW and Jon Moxley’s Request to Move Assault and Battery Lawsuit to Florida
summary_src: AEW and Jon Moxley tried to get a former production worker’s lawsuit moved from Michigan to Florida, but the judge wasn’t having it. The case is staying in Detroit, and one of the reasons is pretty simple — that’s where the whole thing allegedly happened.
body: According to POST Wrestling , Wayne County Judge Catherine Heise denied AEW and Moxley’s request in an October 5 order. The ruling came after a September 17 hearing over where Christopher Dispensa’s lawsuit should actually play out. AEW and Moxley had plenty of reasons for wanting Florida. Dispensa lives there, most of the doctors who treated him are there and AEW is headquartered there, so they argued it would make more sense to handle the case in a Florida court. The judge saw things differently. The alleged incident happened during the May 10, 2023 episode of AEW Dynamite at Little Caesars Arena in Detroit, and several potential witnesses are also in the area. Heise even pointed out just how close everything is. The courthouse handling the lawsuit is “within healthy walking distance” of Little Caesars Arena, while any doctors sitting down in Florida can simply testify remotely. Then there’s the timing. AEW and Moxley didn’t file their motion asking to move the case until July 7, nearly 10 months after AEW answered Dispensa’s complaint in September 2025. The defendants tried to deal with another potential headache by saying they wouldn’t use Florida’s three-year statute of limitations as a defense if the case was moved. Heise wasn’t willing to gamble on whether a Florida court would actually go along with that arrangement. She “is not confident that a Florida court would honor such an agreement or even an order so stating from a Michigan court.” Dispensa originally sued AEW and Moxley in May 2025 over an incident that allegedly happened during Moxley’s match against Kenny Omega on Dynamite. Dispensa, who worked on AEW’s production crew, claims Moxley went away from what had been planned and shoved him to the floor. He alleges that the shove left him with serious neck and shoulder injuries that eventually required cervical spine and shoulder surgery. His lawsuit includes assault and battery claims against Moxley, negligence and gross negligence claims against Moxley and AEW, along with negligent hiring, training, supervision and retention claims against the company. This ruling doesn’t mean Dispensa has won any of those claims, and it doesn’t decide whether Moxley or AEW actually did anything wrong. It just means AEW and Moxley didn’t get the change of scenery they wanted, so the legal fight stays in Michigan. There could still be a way for everyone to avoid taking this thing all the way to a jury. Another settlement conference is scheduled for December 22 after the two sides previously met on July 29 and left those discussions “held for further settlement.” For now, AEW and Moxley are stuck fighting this one in Detroit, but the actual allegations at the center of the lawsuit still have to be sorted out. With another settlement meeting coming in December, this case could either find its way toward a deal or move one step closer to a jury hearing the whole story. title: On the Record: Rob Van Dam Says WWE Stars Were Afraid To Speak up Backstage
raw_title: Rob Van Dam Says WWE Stars Were Afraid To Speak up Backstage
body: 0 WWE Hall of Famer Rob Van Dam has discussed backstage culture. He explained why some WWE stars were afraid to speak up. RVD also compared WWE’s environment with AEW’s approach to wrestling. Speaking on his 1 of a Kind with RVD show , Van Dam was asked about potentially appearing in AEW again. The discussion also touched on AEW’s recent growth and roster. Van Dam praised the promotion for establishing itself over time. He said, “They’ve definitely proven themselves, you know. Like, it was so easy when they first came out to be like, “Yeah, well, let’s see how long they stick around.” And I don’t think there’s anything wrong with any of us, you know, that felt that way, because promotions over the years come up all the time. Oh, they got Major League Baseball money. This shit’s for real, and they got this and this, and it never lasts.” He then congratulated AEW and discussed its continued growth. “And those guys, you know, really fill the void, so it’s cool. Congrats to AEW, and they’re just going to keep growing, you know. I always check with the fans and ask what they watch, you know, and a lot of people are watching both products, you know, and I don’t know how much international distribution they have, but obviously they must be on in the places that they’re going to, at least, you know.” Van Dam then explained what he sees as a major difference between WWE and AEW. He suggested AEW gives wrestlers more freedom to express themselves. “So, but yeah, pretty cool. And it still, and I think always will, be coming across as, and I think for valid reasons, the boys being the ones that are kind of running the show more, you know, whereas WWE, you know, was like a lot of people afraid for their job and doing whatever they’re told and sometimes afraid to go against it or say the wrong thing or whatever.” He added that AEW feels different for its performers. “And this seems more like guys that want to be out there expressing themselves with their talent and doing it their way.” RVD previously appeared in AEW, sharing the ring with stars like Swerve Strickland, Jack Perry, the Dark Order, and others. For proof, just go back and revisit his 'Hair vs. Hair' clanger vs. Adrian Adonis from WrestleMania III . It was 6+ minutes of nothingness before Roddy took the win, 'Adorable' lost his locks, and then Adonis was sent packing from the federation. Adrian had retooled his gimmick to become akin to an even more extreme version of Gorgeous George in 1985. Or, perhaps 'Exotic' Adrian Street was more accurate - Adonis practically borrowed Street's entire act, with the key differences being that he had Jimmy Hart as a manager and was in the dizzying world of the WWF during one of its biggest peaks. However, going the effeminate route for cheap heat didn't do much for Adrian. Admittedly, he was pushing the envelope in a company that wasn't exactly known for it whilst trying to sell new-fangled things (for wrestling) like toys, video games and pay-per-views, but people couldn't wait to see the back of the 'Adorable' character by its bitter end. If this was supposed to be some heat-seeking missile that sprinted up the card towards main events, then it flopped. It flopped big style. Piper, for the second year running, was handed a lame duck at 'Mania. He was expected to make the best of a bad situation, but even industry titans like Roddy could never be considered miracle workers .

title: On the Record: Cody Rhodes Breaks Down WWE Future, Addresses Whether Fatigue Has Set In Among Fans
raw_title: Cody Rhodes Discusses WWE Future, Addresses Whether Fatigue Has Set In Among Fans
body: Cody Rhodes opened up about his wrestling future during a recent appearance on INSIGHT with Chris Van Vliet . As noted , The American Nightmare recently signed a new deal with WWE. It’s reportedly a five-year contract. Rhodes had previously said that he’d retire at 40. Now that he’s 41 and just signed a new contract, Chris Van Vliet asked Cody how long he plans to wrestle. He also touched upon the fatigue setting in among fans and explained why he doesn’t want to stick around for too long. Here’s what he said : “I just signed my last contract. I say last contract, but that’s going to go for a while, and if I’m able to do what I’ve been able to do, because I would love this year not to be just one movie, but perhaps two movies, and I’d love to kind of be able to share that at some point, get that going, and be in that. With all that said, my time with WWE could go. I mean, just to give you a real answer here, and not politic around you, probably seven years. Six, seven? I didn’t mean it like that, but yeah, you know that’s a kids’ thing, right? Had to have Carmelo Hayes explain to me what that was, and I still didn’t get it. Yeah, six, seven years. I’d say so. Yeah, and I don’t want to say that in a final sense. I just know that I don’t want to overstay my welcome.” On why he doesn’t want to wrestle after turning 50; touches upon ‘Cody fatigue’ “Well, I definitely don’t want to wrestle into my 50s. No shame to anyone who wrestles in their 50s. I don’t want to overstay my welcome in a sense of this, right? So, I have been given so much from wrestling, and you have to think about my career in its totality. The things that we don’t talk about, the things that I don’t get asked about anymore. You have to think about all that. I have shed so much of my skin for the industry, but I have also been given so, so, so much. I think there’s a point where you have to stop taking. I’m not there, but there’s a point, and I think that’s in that time frame, a point where you just have to stop taking. It’s giving me everything. “I am talking to you today. The first time I talked to you, I was a mid-card talent at WWE, and no shame to anything in the mid-card. Mid-card’s beautiful. I heard Triple H explain the mid-card in a way that changed my perception of it forever. But I was a mid-card talent with a ceiling that was right above my head, and I’m talking to you today as someone who got to play Guile from Street Fighter, created by Capcom, a game that I played growing up as a little kid. Again, be careful what you wish for, but also I don’t know how many moments like this I can take, and I can get hopefully more, hopefully a lot more. But I’ve been so lucky so far and so blessed so far that I think wrestling, I mean, Cody fatigue is already pretty set in.” On whether he genuinely believes that ‘Cody fatigue’ has set in “Well, no, maybe. But I think you can only go so far, and you’re only supposed to go so far.”

title: 5 Iconic WWE October PLE’s — Fall Classics
raw_title: Fall Classics: 5 Iconic WWE October PLE’s
body: October 22, 2026 By Daniel Sinasac WWE , History , Pro Wrestling , WWE Universe October is another month that hasn’t gotten the full love that it deserves. Months that have housed shows like the Royal Rumble, WrestleMania, SummerSlam, and Survivor Series are ones that are marked on any wrestling fan’s calendar. Those shows have a strong foothold in certain months, hyping excitement as they approach. However, that leaves other months to fly under the radar when it comes to epic shows. As the leaves change, WWE fans wait for November to bring Survivor Series, but the previous month is no slouch in the PLE department. October has been home to many iconic shows that don’t get the credit they deserve. As fans look to bigger shows, they sometimes miss the amazing PLEs October has offered. No Mercy 1999 was filled with solid matches, highlighted by a match of the year. Chyna and Jeff Jarrett’s IC Championship match was more fun than it should have been. The Good Housekeeping stipulation hid the obvious deficiencies, and Chyna’s win was an historic moment. The Rock and British Bulldog, and Steve Austin battling Triple H were solid contests. They weren’t tearing the house down, but were engaging matches that kept the fans happy. The solid matches were the appetizer for the main course that was the ladder match between Edge & Christian and The Hardy Boys . It was the first time a tag team ladder match had taken place, and the originality with which it was presented set the tone for everything that came after. It foreshadowed the classic TLC matches that followed. Related Articles Hank and Tank or the Wagner Brothers – Which Team NEEDS a Dusty Rhodes Tag Team Classic Finals Berth? title: Cody Rhodes Believes The Rock Still Has a Couple of WWE Matches Left
raw_title: Cody Rhodes Believes The Rock Still Has a Couple of WWE Matches Left
body: By Jitu Jangir | October 22, 2026 at 7:22 PM IST 3 min read Cody Rhodes believes The Rock still has a few matches left in his wrestling career. During his latest interview with Chris Van Vliet, Rhodes discussed the possibility of facing The Final Boss in a singles match and explained why WrestleMania 40 could also have been a fitting conclusion to The Rock's in-ring career. During his latest appearance on INSIGHT with Chris Van Vliet, Rhodes was asked about the possibility of finally facing The Rock in a singles match. The conversation turned to WWE Elimination Chamber 2024 in Perth, Australia, where Rhodes publicly challenged The Rock to a one-on-one match during an appearance on The Grayson Waller Effect. Despite the challenge and their subsequent rivalry, the two have never faced each other in a singles match. When Van Vliet asked whether WWE had ever planned for that match to happen, Rhodes admitted that he wasn't sure how to answer the question. However, he did share his personal belief that The Rock could still compete in a few more matches before officially ending his wrestling career. “It's not that I'm evading that answer. It's that I don't really know how to answer because I think personally he has a couple of matches probably left to do. I think that personally, but I also know looking at WrestleMania 40, and another guy who he's given all, continues to give all as part of the board, he could easily say that was a great final piece as a performer in a wrestling ring.” “That'll be up to him. That'll certainly be up to him if there's more and what those matches might be. I don't think any wrestler would ever look you in the eye and tell you they wouldn't want a match like that.” The Rock made his in-ring return at WrestleMania 40 in April 2024, teaming with Roman Reigns against Rhodes and Seth Rollins in the main event of Night One. The Rock and Reigns won that match before Rhodes defeated Reigns the following night to capture the Undisputed WWE Universal Championship. Their rivalry continued in 2025 when The Rock returned to WWE television and told Rhodes that he wanted his soul. Rhodes eventually rejected his offer at Elimination Chamber, leading to John Cena's shocking heel turn against The American Nightmare. Despite those developments, Rhodes and The Rock have yet to settle their differences inside the ring. For now, WWE has not announced another match involving The Rock, and Rhodes did not confirm that a singles encounter between them is being planned. Still, Rhodes believes another in-ring appearance is possible, leaving the door open for one of WWE's biggest unresolved rivalries to eventually reach its conclusion. Quotes transcribed by Sacnilk. title: On the Record: Cody Rhodes Says The Undertaker Belongs Among Wrestling's All-Time Greatest Stars
raw_title: Cody Rhodes Says The Undertaker Belongs Among Wrestling's All-Time Greatest Stars
body: During his latest appearance on INSIGHT with Chris Van Vliet, Rhodes turned the tables on the interviewer and asked him to name his personal Mount Rushmore of professional wrestling. Van Vliet selected Stone Cold Steve Austin, The Rock, Hulk Hogan and The Undertaker. Rhodes agreed with The Undertaker's inclusion and explained why he considers The Deadman such an important figure in wrestling history. According to Rhodes, The Undertaker remained a respected and dependable presence during periods when wrestling was extremely popular and when it wasn't receiving the same mainstream attention. “I think Undertaker's a great choice, and I would have put him on my list before. I think he's a great choice because you need a guy like The Undertaker always and forever.” “And when I say that, what I mean is there are times when wrestling is cool as cool gets. We're living in one, right? Then there's times when wrestling is, you just tell that one guy to the side about it, you know, like, ‘Hey, I watch wrestling.’ Right now we're in this wonderful period.” The Undertaker made his WWE debut at Survivor Series in 1990 and went on to become one of the company's most recognizable Superstars. His career stretched across several major periods in WWE history, including the New Generation Era, the Attitude Era, the Ruthless Aggression Era and the modern era. During that time, he became a multiple-time World Champion, built his legendary WrestleMania undefeated streak and developed a reputation as one of WWE's most respected locker room leaders. Rhodes specifically pointed to The Undertaker's ability to carry himself as a leader while continuing to evolve his character and remain interesting to fans. “Undertaker, he floated in all periods, and you need the guy to hang in and lead the room and lead the talk and keep doing things to remain interesting. And again, the way everyone looks at Taker as the sheriff and the guy, right, who was standing there to pass that on to you, and for good reason. That's a great list.” The Undertaker's influence also extended beyond his matches. He became known as a veteran who helped maintain standards backstage, earning the nickname of WWE's locker room sheriff because of the respect he commanded among fellow wrestlers. He also explained that wrestling's biggest names helped build upon the work of previous generations, making it difficult to separate their individual contributions. Rhodes discussed the influence of Hulk Hogan and his own father, Dusty Rhodes, noting how their work helped professional wrestling grow during the 1980s. He also praised the lasting impact Dusty had on younger wrestlers during the final chapter of his career. While Rhodes did not reveal a definitive Mount Rushmore of his own during the conversation, he made it clear that The Undertaker would be a deserving choice. Quotes transcribed by Sacnilk. Adding WWE to its portfolio reflects B/R’s broader strategy to serve fans across the full spectrum of sports and sports culture, particularly around properties that inspire passionate, year-round conversation. Beyond highlights, Bleacher Report will have a ringside presence at select WWE PLEs, with B/R and House of Highlights content teams capturing original storytelling, talent-driven content and behind-the-scenes moments. “WWE fans don’t just watch. They are highly engaged, analyze every detail and debate the sport all week long. That’s exactly the kind of passionate fandom B/R and House of Highlights were built for,” said Bennett Spector, General Manager, Bleacher Report. “This partnership gives us the opportunity to bring fans closer to the biggest moments happening today while also tapping into the incredible history and personalities that have made WWE part of sports culture for generations.” "Bleacher Report has long been at the intersection of sports and culture,” said Alex Varga, EVP, WWE. "Our partnership with B/R reinforces WWE’s commitment to bringing our content to a global audience." WWE coverage will begin rolling out across Bleacher Report and House of Highlights platforms leading into WWE Money in the Bank on Saturday, October 10.

title: WWE’s Potential Dates for John Cena Classic Revealed
raw_title: WWE’s Potential Dates for John Cena Classic Revealed
summary_src: WWE still hasn’t locked down a date for the John Cena Classic, but the calendar is starting to get pretty crowded. Two dates are apparently still in play for December, while another option has now basically been crossed off the list.
body: According to WrestleVotes Radio on Fightful Select , WWE still hasn’t decided whether the John Cena Classic will happen on December 12 or December 19. Cena has already confirmed the event is coming in December, but exactly where it lands remains up in the air. “As for the rumored John Cena Classic — which Cena himself has said will take place in December — a source couldn’t confirm whether the event is more likely to follow WrestlePalooza on December 12 with a stateside event that evening or take place the following weekend on December 19 — which would put it up against AEW Worlds End, as well as AAA Guerra De Titanes later that same evening.” December 12 would make for one seriously loaded day. WWE could hold WrestlePalooza overseas earlier in the day before following it up with the John Cena Classic back in the United States that evening. December 19 would be a very different story. That date would put Cena’s event directly against AEW Worlds End, while AAA Guerra De Titanes is also scheduled for later that night. There is at least one December date that WWE apparently isn’t too interested in. December 5 isn’t considered a likely option because the company doesn’t want to load up its schedule with major events on three straight weekends. “One source from WWE noted that Saturday, December 5 is not likely an option, as the company doesn’t want to present major events on three consecutive weekends. Meanwhile, December 26 is already on the calendar for WWE, as they’re set to host their annual holiday show at Madison Square Garden.” That also leaves December 26 effectively occupied by WWE’s annual holiday show at Madison Square Garden. For now, December 12 and December 19 remain the two dates worth watching. There’s also another interesting piece of the puzzle that has nothing to do with the calendar. Cena apparently still wants fans to have some kind of say in what happens at the event. “Additionally, a source noted that the voting aspect of the event is still something that John Cena would like to see happen. We’re told that several ideas have been floated internally to make that a possibility.” That voting element hasn’t been finalized either, but WWE is kicking around multiple ideas to make Cena’s vision work. Exactly what fans would be voting on wasn’t specified in the latest report. WWE clearly has some decisions to make before the John Cena Classic is ready for primetime. Between potentially creating a massive doubleheader on December 12, jumping into an already packed December 19 and figuring out Cena’s fan-voting idea, there’s still quite a bit left to settle before the event becomes official. title: Where Things Stand With WarGames Match at WWE Survivor Series 2026
raw_title: Where Things Stand With WarGames Match at WWE Survivor Series 2026
summary_src: WWE’s WarGames plans are starting to come into focus, and The Bloodline vs. 946 apparently won’t be stopping at the four-on-four fight fans saw on RAW. The company is planning to go five-on-five this year, which leaves one open spot on each side and two potentially huge reveals still to come.
body: According to WrestleVotes Radio on Fightful Select , the plan as of Monday was to use five-person teams for this year’s WarGames match. That means Roman Reigns, The Usos and Solo Sikoa aren’t quite a complete team just yet. “Amid the rumors following Monday Night Raw and the four-on-four showdown between The Bloodline and 946, a source indicated that as of Monday, the plan is for this year’s WarGames match is to feature teams of five.” WWE has switched between four-on-four and five-on-five versions of WarGames over the years, so there was still some question about which direction the company would take this time. According to the latest update, WWE is sticking with the five-person format it has recently used on the main roster. “Since bringing back the match concept, WWE has utilized different formats, with teams ranging from four to five members on each side. However, it appears that this year’s installment will follow the recent trend on the main roster and feature the traditional five-on-five setup, pitting The Bloodline against The 946.” That suddenly makes the biggest question surrounding this feud pretty obvious — who gets those final two spots? Roman, Jimmy Uso, Jey Uso and Solo already have four places covered for The Bloodline, while Royce Keys, Carmelo Hayes, Bronco Nima and Lucien Price make up the four-man group they’ve been fighting. Jaida Parker has also been heavily involved with 946, including during Monday’s wild closing segment, but the report doesn’t say who WWE has in mind as the fifth competitor for either team. For now, those spots remain wide open. The latest update also adds another piece to what Dave Meltzer reported following RAW. While discussing whether Monday’s huge Bloodline and 946 brawl was setting up WarGames, Meltzer made it clear that was WWE’s direction : “Well, it is.” That’s when Roman’s music hit and San Diego came unglued. Reigns stormed the ring, reunited with his family and helped send 946 packing after dropping Keys with a Superman Punch and Nima with a Spear. Roman standing alongside Solo and The Usos already gave WWE its core WarGames team, but apparently the family still needs one more person before they can walk into the cage. With 946 also needing another competitor, WWE now has two mystery spots it can play with on the road to Survivor Series. Those fifth-member reveals could end up being just as important as the match itself. WWE already has the two sides ready for war, and now it has a couple of open spots that could add another wrinkle to the rivalry before November 28. summary_src: NXT vs. AEW Dynamite is officially back for one night, and WWE apparently isn’t planning to show up quietly. The November 4 episode of NXT is now confirmed to be going head-to-head with AEW Blood & Guts, and WWE has been told to load up the show.
body: Bryan Alvarez of the Wrestling Observer confirmed the Wednesday night showdown after there had previously been some uncertainty about whether NXT would actually make the move. He added that NXT was told to load up the show. “Confirmed that November 4th NXT and AEW are going head-to-head. That’s the Blood and Guts show and NXT was told to load it up.” That last part makes things especially interesting. There’s no word yet on exactly what WWE plans to add to NXT, but being told to “load it up” certainly suggests the company isn’t treating this like an ordinary episode. “I don’t know this 100%. I was told by people who know that CW wants to move NXT to that Wednesday. It probably will be moved because if it’s on Tuesday, it’ll be preempted on far too many stations.” Now that move is confirmed, and WWE couldn’t have landed on a much bigger night for AEW. November 4 is the annual Blood & Guts edition of Dynamite, with AEW already planning two Blood & Guts matches for the show. Meltzer had previously suggested that NXT might need to come out of Halloween Havoc with a major angle to give viewers a reason to tune in that Wednesday. With Alvarez now reporting that NXT has actually been told to load up the episode, it looks like WWE is preparing for a fight once the two shows go head-to-head. There will be even more WWE programming fighting for attention that night too. EVOLVE airs Wednesdays at 8 PM ET on Tubi, while Main Event also occupies the same time slot on Rumble, meaning WWE could have three shows running while Blood & Guts is happening. The schedule change may have started because of election coverage, but November 4 is no longer looking like a simple one-week move for NXT. With WWE reportedly loading up the show and AEW already bringing out Blood & Guts, wrestling fans are getting another full-blown Wednesday night showdown. title: New Rumor Opens Up On WWE is Plotting a Major Send-Off for Another Legend in 2027
raw_title: New Rumor Reveals WWE is Plotting a Major Send-Off for Another Legend in 2027
body: According to people WrestleVotes spoke with , there have been rumblings of a legendary retirement within WWE in 2027, and that talk has centered on Mysterio. A source said they did not have direct knowledge of when or where an official retirement would take place. Instead, the source indicated that recent chatter at TV has pointed toward next year being the end of the road for Mysterio as an active wrestler. The same source said WWE has discussed ideas for how to present his farewell. There is also a feeling among many within the company that Mysterio will stay involved after his in-ring career ends, much like AJ Styles , and that he would continue playing a key role in developing the next generation of talent in WWE and AAA. Styles wrestled his final match at the Royal Rumble in January and has since moved into a role helping younger wrestlers. Mysterio has addressed the idea of retirement himself. In an August interview on WWE’s Raw Recap, he said he had been asking himself whether it was getting close to his time to retire. “I certainly don’t feel like I am,” he said, while adding that he always listens to his body and that the moment “can just pop up one day out of nowhere.” In the same interview, he spoke about his role as AAA’s general manager. “I am enjoying the position of being AAA’s GM and seeing the young rising stars come up in the game,” Mysterio said. The 51-year-old has stayed active on Raw. He beat Big Cass on the October 12 episode and challenged Chad Gable for the Intercontinental Championship twice since August, losing a singles match on the August 17 episode and a triple threat with Dragon Lee on the October 19 episode. He has also worked on AAA programming, teaming with El Grande Americano on the October 3 episode of AAA on FOX. If 2027 is the year, WWE has time to do it right. Mysterio is one of the most important wrestlers of his generation, and his career has connected fans across the United States and Mexico for more than three decades. A farewell run that includes WWE and AAA would reflect that, and it would give fans in both countries a chance to see him one last time. The more important part of this report may be what comes after. Mysterio has already shown how much he cares about the people around him, from helping get Psicosis his surgery to the time he has spent working with younger talent. A role developing wrestlers in WWE and AAA would put that experience to good use, especially with AAA now part of the WWE family. WWE should take the AJ Styles approach and give Mysterio a clear final stretch with a defined ending. He has earned a send-off that matches his place in wrestling history, and announcing it ahead of time would let fans enjoy the final run instead of wondering when it will end.
summary: Per people WrestleVotes spoke with , there have been rumblings of a legendary retirement within WWE in 2027, and that talk has centered on Mysterio. If 2027 is the year, WWE has time to do it right.

title: Cody Rhodes and Randy Orton: A Rivalry Spanning Over a Decade
raw_title: THEN, NOW, FOREVER – Cody Rhodes and Randy Orton: Hubbard’s look at key moments from 2011, 2013, and 2025 with video links
body: One of the current main-event storylines on WWE programming is “The American Nightmare” Cody Rhodes versus “The Viper” Randy Orton. Whether you consider this a continuation of their WrestleMania headlining feud – or perhaps a make-good for the shortcomings and unnecessary detours that derailed that program – Cody and Randy are once again standing face-to-face, man-to-man, on WWE SmackDown. Randy Orton and Cody Rhodes have a relationship that stretches back well over a decade. Cody’s first match on WWE main roster programming was against Orton, and he later became one of Randy’s henchmen alongside Ted DiBiase in the heel group Legacy. After Legacy broke apart, Cody and Randy had a brief feud that is often forgotten. Even before Cody’s departure from WWE, the two found themselves on opposite sides of another storyline, with Orton representing The Authority and Cody standing alongside his brother Goldust and their father, “The American Dream” Dusty Rhodes. That program also marked Dusty’s final major character appearance on professional wrestling television. Since Cody’s return to WWE, he and Randy had largely been portrayed as friends. That friendship came to a dramatic end when Randy viciously attacked Cody, transforming their WrestleMania main-event title match into a personal grudge match. Unfortunately, in the weeks that followed, the feud seemed to lose its way. Or, perhaps more accurately, a hot feud became a dumpster fire. The introduction of Pat McAfee into the program, along with an abundance of meta nonsense, left many wrestling fans frustrated. A lackluster match at WrestleMania did little to remove the sour taste the program had left behind. Now, four months later and following a 100-day absence, Randy has returned to attack Cody, and in many ways, we are right back where we started in January. Hopefully, this time WWE keeps the destination in mind and takes a more straightforward route to get there. Cody and Randy have too much significant history—or should I say Legacy—for this story not to receive a climactic conclusion worthy of their long relationship. In this week’s column, we will explore three matches from the lengthy and interconnected history between Cody Rhodes and Randy Orton. The breakup of Legacy in 2010 and the subsequent feud between its members and Randy Orton ultimately did little for Cody Rhodes – and, frankly, I’m not sure it was supposed to. It’s easy to forget now, but after Legacy broke apart, many fans, and probably WWE Creative, believed Ted DiBiase Jr. was more poised and ready to be elevated up the card than Cody Rhodes. Cody was the tagalong. In the end, however, the feud did little for Cody and even less for DiBiase, as neither man was established as a truly believable threat to Randy Orton. Cody’s first real momentum as a singles star came the following year in his feud with Rey Mysterio. That program involved Mysterio damaging Cody’s face and Cody subsequently wearing a mask. On paper, it sounds bizarre. I
summary: Cody Rhodes and Randy Orton are currently feuding once again on WWE SmackDown in what some view as an extension of their WrestleMania main event program. Their history dates back more than ten years, beginning with Rhodes' first main roster match against Orton, followed by Rhodes joining him in the Legacy faction alongside Ted DiBiase. After Legacy disbanded the pair had a short feud, and later opposed each other in a program featuring The Authority against Rhodes, his brother Goldust and their father Dusty Rhodes, which served as Dusty's last significant on-screen role.

title: WWE Considering Bringing Back Sin Cara Character
raw_title: WWE Considering Bringing Back Sin Cara Character
summary_src: WWE could be getting ready to bring Sin Cara back, but not necessarily the man who previously wore the mask. The company has reportedly started kicking around ideas for resurrecting the character with an entirely new wrestler taking over the role.
body: According to PWInsider , there have been early pitches within WWE centered around bringing the Sin Cara character back. Nothing has been finalized yet, but the concept is officially being discussed. The biggest twist is that WWE apparently isn’t looking at this as a comeback for the previous Sin Cara. If the company actually moves forward with the idea, the current pitch would put somebody new underneath the mask. There’s no word yet on who WWE might have in mind for the role, and the report doesn’t indicate how far along those conversations have gotten. For now, these are simply early pitches, so there’s no guarantee Sin Cara will actually return to television. The timing is pretty interesting considering the previous Sin Cara was just talking about wanting another shot at the character last month. Speaking to TMZ’s Inside the Ring in September, he admitted he would happily return to WWE and put the mask back on if the company ever approached him. “For me, I wouldn’t mind coming back. If they would ask me or we would talk, ‘Hey, you want to portray Sin Cara again?’ I would love to do that definitely again and give it another shot.” He also explained that he’s matured considerably since his original WWE run and believes he would approach things differently today. His first stint ended after he publicly requested his release in November 2019, with WWE eventually granting it the following month. “It’s something that I really think about sometimes in my head. Like, what if this and what if that happen? And in wrestling, anything is possible. You understand that?” Apparently, something involving Sin Cara really could happen again — just potentially without him. WWE owns the character, and if these early pitches eventually turn into actual plans, fans could end up seeing a completely new wrestler trying to make the mask their own. That creates an interesting wrinkle after the former Sin Cara openly talked about wanting another chance just weeks ago. WWE hasn’t committed to bringing the character back yet, but if it does, the bigger story may quickly become who the company trusts to inherit the mask. body: By Jason Powell , ProWrestling.net Editor ( @prowrestlingnet ) Ilja Dragunov vs. Mike Bailey: A good win for Dragunov in a competitive match with Bailey. I probably would have avoided putting this match in the main event spot to avoid making it seem like a former secondary champion in WWE is a bigger deal than everyone else on the show, but saving this for last was probably more about television ratings than anything. Bailey was a good first opponent because he is over with the fans and was a lock to have a good match with Dragunov. Furthermore, the company didn’t have to give away a main event player facing Dragunov on night one. I wouldn’t ask Dragunov to bury his former employer, but AEW should drive home the message that he chose to leave WWE when his contract expired rather than this being a case of AEW picking up a WWE cut casualty. Kyle Fletcher and Kevin Knight vs. AEW World Champion Will Ospreay and Adam Copeland: What is up with Ospreay teaming with babyfaces who are going to challenge him for the AEW World Championship? He’s teamed with Andrade El Idolo a few times since Andrade won the contract that gives him a title shot with seven days’ notice. Ospreay and Copeland were not in the same orbit until Ospreay pinned Copeland to win the Clockwork Carnage match, which Copeland followed by telling Ospreay that he’s coming for his title. Anyway, the match was entertaining and seemed to move Ospreay and Copeland away from one another and into matches with Fletcher and the interfering Kazuchika Okada, respectively. The post-match angle felt contrived, as it conveniently set up the Blood & Guts match, but that’s become the norm for most WarGames-style matches since they became calendar events. As much as I loved the Davis and Doyle squash win over the Bucks, I really could have done without the Bucks coming out to help run off the Callis Family heels just one match later. Nick Wayne and Chris Jericho: A soft Hit for a decent segment. Wayne is in a better place than he was when his feud with Jericho started, and it was good to hear Jericho put him over verbally without calling for a rematch. The follow-up program is crucial for Wayne. It should be all about adding to the momentum he gained from beating Jericho (insert pyro here) in two of their three matches. Orange Cassidy and Jay White vs. Wheeler Yuta and Daniel Garcia: A minor Miss for a match that seemed to happen so they could establish a quick relationship between Cassidy and White before White turned on Cassidy later in the show. By the way, if the Death Riders are so committed to greatness, shouldn’t Jon Moxley put more pressure on Yuta and Garcia to win some meaningful matches?
summary: Ilja Dragunov defeated Mike Bailey in a competitive main event match on AEW Dynamite. The placement was viewed as a ratings decision rather than elevating the newcomer above the rest of the roster. Kyle Fletcher and Kevin Knight faced AEW World Champion Will Ospreay and Adam Copeland in tag team action while the show built toward the upcoming Blood & Guts event.

title: TNA Stars Enter NXT Women’s Battle Royal Amid Rumors of WWE Partnership Crumbling - TWNP-Wrestling News
raw_title: TNA Stars Enter NXT Women’s Battle Royal Amid Rumors of WWE Partnership Crumbling - TWNP-Wrestling News
body: It’s been almost three months since an NXT talent appeared on iMPACT Wrestling television, and almost a year since someone from TNA appeared on NXT on CW. In fact, as we first reported here , WWE and TNA’s relationship seemed to be on the rocks. Less than a week later, WWE claps back by booking TNA talent on next week’s NXT. TNA stars are entering an NXT Women’s Battle Royal to determine the #1 contender to Kelani Jordan’s NXT Championship at Halloween Havoc. After many attempts at capturing the NXT Women’s Championship, Kelani Jordan finally made it to the top. Now, she has to contend with 20 other hungry Superstars. That’s because Robert Stone has booked a women’s battle royal to determine Kelani Jordan’s next challenger. Kelani Jordan made it clear on NXT that her reign wouldn’t feature “open challenges.” She noted Wren Sinclair’s suspension and Kendal Grey’s absence essentially left her without any contenders. This assertion drew the ire of NXT General Manager, Robert Stone. The former Robbie E stated that Kelani Jordan won’t decide the next challenger because a 20-Woman Battle Royal will. Since Kelani Jordan won’t give out open challenges, Robert Stone opened the door for other companies. The NXT GM announced that five brands will be involved in the Women’s Battle Royal. The most shocking of these companies is TNA. As a former TNA star himself, Robert Stone was the perfect person to announce the company’s return to WWE TV. Now, we have word on who some of these talents will be. Halloween Havoc takes place on Halloween night. As this holiday event approaches, WWE is trying to lock down the card. To draw some excitement, NXT is hosting a multi-company Women’s Battle Royal. Here are the competitors who will vie for a chance to challenge Kelani Jordan at Halloween Havoc: This match features many Champions., including the TNA Knockouts and TNA Knockouts Television Champions. So, it seems like WWE is trying to shine a light on the Division, as TNA is struggling to fill the venue for Bound for Glory. Hopefully, this extra attention on CW will help TNA sell more tickets in Tampa. Many believe that while WWE is featuring TNA talent on NXT next week, not much in their deal is changing. WWE is aware they received some bad press last week. They’re also trying to drum up some interest in the Women’s Battle Royal by adding other companies. Creative team members felt adding The Elegance Brand, Indi Hartwell, and Xia Brookeside would increase the buzz in light of the trending news surrounding WWE and TNA’s partnership going south. Interestingly, the last time TNA talent appeared on NXT was during last November’s Gold Rush. At the time, Kelani Jordan was the TNA Knockouts Champion. She defended the Title in a Triple Threat Match against Jordynne Grace and Léi Yǐng Lee. Léi Yǐng Lee defeated Kelani Jordan to become the new TNA Knockouts Champion.

title: Judge Keeps AEW Moxley Lawsuit In Michigan

summary_src: A judge has denied AEW and Jon Moxley's request to move a civil lawsuit to a Florida court. Brandon Thurston of POST Wrestling first reported the news on Thursday, referencing the lawsuit that former production worker Christopher Dispensa filed back in May 2025.
body: A judge has denied AEW and Jon Moxley’s request to move a civil lawsuit to a Florida court. Brandon Thurston of POST Wrestling first reported the news on Thursday, referencing the lawsuit that former production worker Christopher Dispensa filed back in May 2025. As some fans may remember, Dispensa filed the suit alleging negligence, civil assault, and battery over an incident where he was pushed to the floor by Moxley. Thurston’s new report notes that the judge chose to keep the case in Michigan, where the incident occurred in May 2023. Back in July, AEW asked to move the case to Florida because that’s where Dispensa and most of his doctors live. Furthermore, a second settlement conference with the court is set to take place on December 22, 2026. The first conference was held in July of this year. Fightful will update fans when a new update surfaces on the Chris Dispensa’s lawsuit. In the meantime, check out the current lineup for Saturday’s episode of AEW Collision by clicking here.
summary: A judge denied AEW and Jon Moxley's request to transfer former production worker Christopher Dispensa's civil lawsuit from Michigan to Florida. Dispensa filed the suit in May 2025 alleging negligence, civil assault and battery after being pushed to the floor by Moxley during an incident in Michigan in May 2023. A second settlement conference is scheduled for December 22 2026 after the first one took place in July.

title: Injury Update: Injury Rules El Desperado Out of NJPW Super Jr. Tag League 2026, Replacement Set
raw_title: Injury Rules El Desperado Out of NJPW Super Jr. Tag League 2026, Replacement Announced
body: El Desperado has been ruled out of the NJPW Super Junior Tag League 2026 due to injury. New Japan Pro-Wrestling announced on Thursday, October 22, that one-half of the current IWGP Junior Heavyweight Tag Team Champions, El Desperado, has been diagnosed with spinal canal stenosis and a hernia. El Desperado and Mistico were originally drawn in Block A. However, with the former having been ruled out, Mistico will now team with NJPW Young Lion Masatora Yasuda. Desperado said his body has reached its limit and apologized to fans. No timeline is currently set for his return. Here’s what he said: “My sincerest apologies, but I will not be appearing at Super Jr. Tag League. I’m currently dealing with spinal canal stenosis and a hernia. My left leg has no strength, and with the pain and pins and needles, I’m currently unable to stand, walk, or even sit upright for long periods of time. From the start of this year I’d noticed some strange sensations in my left glute, and there was some tingling in my legs from around March. At that point I expressed to the company that I was having some symptoms but that I had no issues with strength or anything like that and asked to continue wrestling while staying in contact with the medical and training staff. “For this Super Jr. Tag League, Mistico was scheduled to wrestle with me, and we can’t just send him back with nothing to say for it, so I have chosen (Masatora) Yasuda to replace me. Some of you might think ‘with your connections you can come up with a bigger name than a Young Lion,’ but I’d like for you to think of this as a key step to the future of NJPW.” -> Mistico & Masatora Yasuda -> Taiji Ishimori & Robbie X -> Yoshinobu Kanemaru & DOUKI -> Ryusuke Taguchi & Kazuma Sumi -> Master Wato & KUUKAI -> KUSHIDA & Nick Wayne -> Robbie Eagles & Kosei Fujita -> YOH & Hyo -> Francesco Akira & Jakob Austin Young -> Titan & Daiki Nagai -> SHO & Dick Togo -> Blake Christian & Lee Johnson The tournament will get underway in Saitama, Japan, on October 24. The top scorers from each Block will battle in the final at NJPW Power Struggle on November 3. El Desperado , NJPW , NJPW Super Junior Tag League , Yash Mittal

body: On Friday, October 23, CMLL will present their Grand Prix de Amazonas main event this year. The 11-on-11 matchup will feature talent from all over the world, including those from the AEW roster. Considering the partnership between the two promotions, it should not be shocking to see All Elite Wrestling having a heavy presence on this major bout coming up in Arena Mexico. Here are six AEW stars to compete in the CMLL Grand Prix de Amazonas 2026. It should be no surprise that Persephone will compete for Team CMLL for the Grand Prix de Amazonas 2026 match. While she has signed a dual contract with both CMLL and AEW, Perse is still the CMLL World Women’s Champion and is the face of the company’s Amazonas division. Holding gold in both promotions as the TBS Champion as well, all eyes should be on Persephone in this match on the October 23 show. On Team World, there will be several stars from the AEW roster competing. Queen Aminata is someone who has been a featured star on AEW TV as of late. After coming up short against Persephone in a TBS Championship four-way at AEW WrestleDream 2026, Aminata might be looking to score a pinfall over Persephone to get another opportunity. Another AEW star who will be part of Team World in the Grand Prix de Amazonas 2026 is Harley Cameron . The former AEW Women’s World Tag Team Champion will look to make her presence felt in this bout. Making her CMLL debut, Cameron can make her mark in this Cibernetico bout on October 23. Someone who has been a force wherever she goes in AEW or elsewhere is Megan Bayne . One half of Divine Dominion will be part of the Team World in the CMLL Grand Prix de Amazonas 2026 match. With her mixture of size, power and agility, Bayne should hold her own and could make it to the very end of this 11-on-11 main event showdown. In 2026, Thunder Rosa became the latest star to sign a dual contract with AEW and CMLL. The former AEW Women’s World Champion will be part of Team CMLL in the Grand Prix de Amazonas 2026 bout. While she is the current Mexican National Women’s Champion, Rosa should have some interesting interactions with both Team CMLL as well as Team World during this contest. Shotzi was scheduled to take part of the CMLL Grand Prix de Amazonas 2026, but she had to be pulled after a passing in her family. In her place, AEW’s Marina Shafir will take her place and look to continue The Death Riders’ presence in CMLL. Wanting a standout performance, Shafir will come in with a chip on her shoulder after not being originally announced for this match and should come in with a fire that no other competitor might have in this match from Arena Mexico. title: Rey Mysterio Rumored To Retire In 2027
raw_title: Backstage News On Potential Upcoming Retirement Of WWE Hall Of Famer Rey Mysterio
summary_src: A new report revealed there is backstage chatter regarding the potential in-ring retirement of WWE Hall of Famer Rey Mysterio.
body: According to WrestleVotes Radio on Fightful Select , there are internal rumblings of Rey Mysterio retiring in 2027. A source told the outlet there is chatter backstage that the legendary luchador could be wrapping up as an active wrestler next year. That source did, however, tell WrestleVotes they had no direct knowledge of when or where Mysterio's potential retirement match could happen. It was not noted if there were plans for him to a have a retirement tour run, like Cena. The source said that WWE creative minds have discussed ideas on how to present Mysterio's farewell to fans, however. The current on-screen AAA general manager is expected to remain a part of the company behind-the-scenes, helping younger talent in both WWE and AAA. The Hall of Famer began his career on the independent scene in 1989. He signed with WCW in 1996 and helped popularize lucha libre in the states, and was pivotal in establishing a cruiserweight division in the promotion. Mysterio joined WWE in 2002, with a hiatus from 2015 to 2018, where he worked elsewhere, including NJPW and Lucha Underground.
summary: Per Fightful Select, internal WWE chatter suggests Rey Mysterio may retire from in-ring competition next year. A source indicated creative has brainstormed ways to present his farewell to fans though no specifics on timing, location or a potential retirement tour are known. The WWE Hall of Famer, currently serving as on-screen AAA general manager, is expected to stay with both companies in a backstage role mentoring young talent.

summary_src: In August 2025, Syko Stu (Stuart Smith) was brutally attacked by Raja Jackson at an independent show. Smith has opened up about the incident for the first time
body: They had shaken hands prior to the in-ring incident and he didn't expect things to escalate the way that they did. After the beer can spot, they decided to make it an angle.
summary: Syko Stu has looked back on the well-known in-ring incident with Raja Jackson. The pair had shaken hands before the situation unfolded and he did not anticipate it escalating. Following a beer can spot the decision was made to turn the moment into an angle.

llm.headline: Syko Stu Reflects On Raja Jackson Altercation
llm.summary: Syko Stu has looked back on the well-known in-ring incident with Raja Jackson. The pair had shaken hands before the situation unfolded and he did not anticipate it escalating. Following a beer can spot the decision was made to turn the moment into an angle.

llm_long: At a KnokX Pro event on August 23 2025, Raja Jackson knocked independent wrestler Syko Stu unconscious during a planned spot that escalated beyond the script.
Raja slammed Stu and then delivered more than 20 unanswered legitimate strikes to his head until independent wrestler Doug Malo intervened and pulled him away.
Syko Stu has limited memory of the incident itself. He recalled Raja filming backstage, which is unusual, and remembered calling a finish that involved one wrestling punch after a beer can spot.

Stu stated he was unconscious from the initial slam and has no recollection of the following events. He woke up in the hospital on Tuesday after being admitted on Saturday and remained in and out of consciousness until then.
During his hospital stay, medical staff would not show him video of the incident or discuss it. Wrestler Rikishi visited him there as he began to recover.

Stu was discharged from the hospital on Thursday. He now participates in word exercises during rehabilitation but continues to experience short-term memory issues such as forgetting things within minutes, repeating actions, and failing to recall names and faces.

title: US Embassy In Riyadh Issues Advisory As WWE Crown Jewel Draws Closer
