body: A security alert has been issued by the US Embassy in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, for US citizens. In the statement, issued on Thursday, October 22, the Riyadh-based Embassy has advised US citizens to take “extreme caution” when using airports in Saudi Arabia. Operations at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh remain suspended, while airports in Dammam and Jeddah are operational with “some delays and cancellations.” “Iranian-supported Houthis have engaged in hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including attacks on civilian airports and other critical infrastructure resulting in civilian casualties and severe travel disruptions. The hostilities have the potential to escalate rapidly beyond that immediate area. U.S. citizens are reminded to follow the guidance of national alerts released by Saudi Arabia’s Civil Defense via cellular broadcast. “U.S. government employees working in Saudi Arabia require special authorization from Chief of Mission to use any airport in Saudi Arabia following recent missile and UAV attacks on airports in the Kingdom. Operations at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh remain suspended. King Abdulaziz International Airport in Jeddah and King Fahd International Airport in Dammam are operational with some delays and cancellations. “U.S. citizens should be aware of potential attacks on airports, airspace closures, flight cancellations, and travel disruptions. Please take extreme caution if you choose to use airports in Saudi Arabia. We recommend checking your flight departure status directly with the airline and with the airport.” Iranian-supported Houthis have engaged in hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including attacks on civilian airports and other critical infrastructure resulting in civilian casualties and severe travel disruptions. title: Cody Rhodes Keeping a List of Wrestlers Who Didn’t Support His Street Fighter Movie
raw_title: Cody Rhodes Keeping a List of Wrestlers Who Didn’t Support His Street Fighter Movie
summary_src: Cody Rhodes is apparently keeping receipts when it comes to which wrestlers supported his new Street Fighter movie. The WWE star admitted he’s been paying close attention to who showed up, who promoted the film and, more importantly, who didn’t.
body: That led Cody into a much broader point about wrestlers supporting each other’s success outside the ring. While wrestlers might say they want to see their peers succeed, Cody believes the real test comes when it’s actually time to show that support. “You could be, but also, Seth—wrestlers always tell each other how much they want each other to do great, but then in those moments, they don’t necessarily support. Seth showed up at the Street Fighter premiere. He’s a real one. He’s a real one. And trust me, I kept track of who showed up, who didn’t, who posted, you know, who didn’t show up.” When asked whether he really had a list of people who didn’t post about Street Fighter, Cody confirmed it without hesitation. He also admitted there was more than a little pettiness involved: “Oh, yeah.” Cody then explained why the lack of support bothered him so much. With three wrestlers involved in Street Fighter, he sees the movie’s success as something that could help move the entire wrestling industry forward rather than simply benefiting him. “Oh, deep pettiness. Deep. Because, I mean, there’s three wrestlers in this movie, and you can’t throw up a, ‘Hey, go see this thing, guys’? What are we doing? We’re trying to move the ball forward.” Cody made it clear that he views the opportunity as something that can benefit everybody in wrestling. At the same time, he jokingly acknowledged that he’s obviously getting a little extra out of the movie doing well. “It’s for everybody. And yeah, is it a little better for me? Sure.” Cody didn’t name any of the wrestlers who landed on the wrong side of his list, so he’s keeping that part to himself for now. Rollins, however, clearly isn’t one of them after making the effort to attend the premiere despite the complicated history between the two WWE stars. title: Parks Highlights Dragunov's Top AEW Matchup Possibilities
raw_title: PARKS’S TAKE: Looking at Ilja Dragunov’s list of standout potential opponents on AEW roster
body: Ilja Dragunov made his AEW last night on Dynamite, defeating “Speedball” Mike Bailey in the show’s main event. The positioning of Dragunov in the last match immediately put him on the map as someone who should be taken seriously by the fans and a threat to the major titles in the company. Even when he was in WWE, Dragunov always seemed like a better fit for AEW. His hard-hitting, aggressive intensity is much closer stylistically to what AEW offers. In that way, Dragunov was a unicorn in WWE, which actually helped make his matches stand out even more. However, it was clear he was unlikely to get above a certain level on Raw or Smackdown. With Dragunov now in AEW, there are a ton of enticing matchups for him. Here are a few that are high on my anticipation list: -Jon Moxley: AEW’s resident hard hitter could meet his match with Dragunov. In fact, Dragunov would even fit in with the motif of the Death Riders should they look to add a new member. -Claudio Castagnoli: These two could just end up trading chops and uppercuts for 15 minutes. I’d be fine with that. -Konosuke Takeshita: Dragunov’s European offense melds well with the Japanese strong style, as does his selling. Takeshita would be able to give as well as he takes. -Nick Wayne: Wayne has recently found his stride as an overconfident, cocky heel who fans will want to see his comeuppance. They’ll also want to see him get bashed around and bruised by the violent Dragunov. -Kyle O’Reilly: This would give Dragunov a little bit of a different work in an opponent who prefers to work holds. Dragunov’s facial reactions have been a strength and he could satisfactorily convey the pain that O’Reilly’s holds bring.
summary: Ilja Dragunov opened his AEW run by beating Mike Bailey in the main event of Dynamite, instantly positioning him as a serious contender for major titles. His intense, hard-hitting style that stood out as unique in WWE now aligns closely with AEW's product. Among the most anticipated future opponents are Jon Moxley, who could even recruit him into the Death Riders, Claudio Castagnoli for a stiff chops-and-uppercuts battle, and Konosuke Takeshita.

title: WWE Live Event Sees Styles Challenge Ambrose for Title
raw_title: 10 YEARS AGO – WWE LIVE EVENT REPORT: AJ Styles vs. Dean Ambrose for WWE Title, plus Ziggler, Kane, Bray Wyatt, Naomi, Alexa Bliss, Usos, Corbin
body: The following is a report originally published here 10 years ago this week… (1) Dolph Ziggler defeated Tyler Breeze to retain the Intercontinental Championship. Dolph scored the pinfall after hitting a Super Kick. Great opening contest with fast-paced action. (2) SmackDown Tag Champion Heath Slater & The Hype Bros (w/Mascot Cowboy Joe) defeated Viktor & The Vaudevillains. Slater pinned Simon Gotch after the “Smash Hit” DDT. This was a entertaining six man tag match. Cowboy Joe is the mascot for the Wyoming Cowboys basketball and football teams. (3) Apollo Crews defeated Curt Hawkins. Crews won with a spin out powerbomb. Solid match up, but afterward Curt Hawkins tells us all we need to face the facts, challenges anyone to come out and face the facts, then “The Demon” Kane’s music hit and he came out to answer the challenge. (4) Kane defeated Curt Hawkins. Kane won via chokeslam in less than 10 seconds. Bray Wyatt cut a promo on the video screen about Randy Orton. (5) Baron Corbin defeated Jack Swagger. Corbin wins via roll up. (6) Randy Orton defeated Bray Wyatt. Orton attempted an RKO, but Wyatt reversed it into a “Sister Abigail.” Then Orton countered into a roll up and Wyatt kicked out, Finally the Viper hit the RKO out of nowhere for the win. Another great match with Orton being really over with the crowd and doing what he does best. Mostly all the fans had their phones lit up as “fire flies” during Wyatts’s entrance. Afterward, Orton circled around, took pictures, and signed autographs for the fans. Styles cut a promo on the video screen about his match with Ambrose later in the night and said he is “the face that runs the place.” (7) Naomi & Natalya defeated Alexa Bliss & Carmella. Naomi pinned Alexa for the win. Towards the end of the match Naomi tried to tag in Natalya, but since Natty is still playing her heel role, she stepped off the apron and walked to the back. Afterwards Naomi danced. (8) American Alpha defeated The Usos. Alpha gets the win with a Grand Amplitude on Jimmy. Solid tag team match. (9) A.J. Styles defeated Dean Ambrose to retain the WWE World Championship. Ambrose almost had the match won, but A.J. hit him with a low blow and Styles Clash for the finish. Great performances by both men as always. The match went about 20 minutes with plenty of action and near falls. Afterwards Styles grabbed the mic and said, “I’m the face that runs the place, the champ that runs the camp, and still the WWE World Champion!” Ambrose then delivered a Dirty Deeds on A.J. to send the crowd home happy. BIGGEST POPS: Orton Ambrose Styles (mixed reaction) Kane Ziggler Wyatt (ring entrance) Hype Bros and Slater Naomi Crews MOST HEEL HEAT: Hawkins Breeze Wyatt (as he taunted the crowd) Usos Styles (mixed reaction) Corbin Vaudevillains and Viktor Natty (when she walked out on Naomi) We still invite live event reports in 2026 to be published here at PWTorch! Send to pwtorch@gmail.com

body: Penta won the men’s Money in the Bank ladder match on Oct. tenth in New Orleans, earning a WWE World Title opportunity. Crown Jewel follows on Nov. seventh in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, where Roman Reigns and Sami Zayn meet in a Champion vs. Champion match . Reigns holds the World Heavyweight Title, and Zayn carries the Undisputed WWE Title. The winner takes the Men’s Crown Jewel Championship. The briefcase gives Penta an opening, and three scenarios follow. Penta took the briefcase after hitting Bron Breakker with a Mexican Destroyer from one ladder onto another. CM Punk, Kevin Owens, Je’Von Evans, and Trick Williams were also in the match. Per WWE.com , the winner earns a world title match at any time within the next year. WWE has not announced either world title as on the line at Crown Jewel. Under the announced terms, Reigns and Zayn will both still be world champions after the match in Riyadh. Edge cashed in at New Year’s Revolution in January 2006. John Cena had retained the WWE Title inside the Elimination Chamber moments earlier. Seth Rollins cashed in at SummerSlam on Aug. second, 2025, right after Punk beat Gunther for the World Heavyweight Title. Penta was one of six men in that year’s ladder match on June seventh in Inglewood, California. A Champion vs. Champion match would leave the Crown Jewel winner in the same spot Punk was in at MetLife Stadium. Reigns has held the World Heavyweight Title since beating Punk at WrestleMania 42 on April 19 in Las Vegas. Penta earned a shot at that belt on the Aug. 31 Raw, defeating Rey Fenix in a brother-versus-brother tournament final. The Tribal Chief retained on the Sept. 14 Raw in Mexico City, catching a springboard attempt with a Superman Punch before hitting a Spear. He had worked over Reigns’ right arm with the Sacrifice earlier in the bout. Zayn congratulated Penta on winning the ladder match during the Oct. 16 SmackDown and pushed for a cash-in on Reigns. Later that night, Fenix fielded a backstage question from Zayn about whether the brothers had spoken since Money in the Bank. Fenix replied that the WWE Champion’s intent was clear, adding that even Penta’s own brother did not know whether the cash-in would target Reigns or Zayn. Penta walked out after the face-to-face between the champions on the Oct. 19 Raw in San Diego. The briefcase went up toward Reigns at ringside. A Crown Jewel cash-in would set up a rematch of the Sept. 14 bout at a premium live event. Penta addressed the timing of a cash-in on the WWE Now Money in the Bank recap, which WWE posted on Oct. tenth. The luchador said: “But not yet. Not too soon.” He added, “Now I decide when. I decide where, and I decide against who.” Rollins won the 2014 contract on June 29 in Boston and held it for nine months. At WrestleMania 31 on March 29, 2015, the cash-in came during the Brock Lesnar vs. Reigns main event. Rollins pinned Reigns to leave Levi’s Stadium with the WWE World Heavyweight Title. title: Cody Rhodes Plans Retirement in Six to Seven Years
raw_title: WWE’s Cody Rhodes gives fresh timeline on retirement after signing ‘last contract’
body: In the next decade, Cody Rhodes will retire from professional wrestling after signing his latest contract with WWE , which will be his "last" one. Speaking to Chris Van Vliet, the "American Nightmare" gave an update on the timeline for his retirement. He previously told Van Vliet that he was going to retire at 40. Rhodes, who is now 41, reinforced that the latest contract he signed will be his "last." However, it will "go for a while." If all goes well, he plans to retire within the next six or seven years. "With all that said, my time with WWE could go probably seven years, six [or] seven [years]," he said, before saying he didn't mean to make a "6-7" joke. He definitely doesn't want to wrestle into his 50s, like legends such as Rey Mysterio are currently doing. Rhodes has been given so much from the industry, but he also knows it's almost his time to "stop taking" from it. It sounds like Rhodes will retire from WWE within the next decade, so fans should buckle up. He is still at the top of the company, but he seems to understand that Father Time is undefeated. Some of his decision to hang it up might depend on his success in Hollywood. After having a small role in the Liam Neeson-led Naked Gun reboot, he starred in the Street Fighter movie alongside his former WWE rival, Roman Reigns. The movie has been a hit so far, grossing over $50 million to date. It topped the domestic box office with its $31.1 million haul during its opening weekend.
summary: Cody Rhodes confirmed to Chris Van Vliet that the new contract he signed with WWE will be his final one. Now 41, he expects to step away from the ring in six or seven years and does not want to wrestle into his 50s. Rhodes acknowledged that the industry has given him much and feels it is nearly time to stop taking from it.

title: Jim Ross returns home after hospital stay
raw_title: Jim Ross back home and “on the mend” after recent hopsital visit
summary_src: Conrad Thompson provided an encouraging update on Jim Ross, who had to be in the hospital "due to low oxygen."
body: Jim Ross is back home after a recent hospital visit earlier this month. The 74-year-old posted on social media on Oct. 12 that he had to be back in the hospital “due to low oxygen.” The event came after his second brain procedure, and he added in his post that he weighed 198 pounds. On the latest episode of “Grilling JR,” co-host Conrad Thompson offered encouraging news about Ross. I finally got an update on the Voice of Wrestling, Mr. Jim Ross. As you all know, J.R. had to do a little outpatient visit recently, and it turns out he got a little bit of a chest cold. He’s got some sort of infection in his chest. They said his oxygen was low, so he spent the night in the hospital, but I’m happy to report that he is home and on the mend. They still haven’t gotten his shunt hooked back up yet, so we’re hoping for that sooner rather than later. Thompson added that Ross was still “under the weather.” He also called back to a quote from Ross, “Hey, man, if it wasn’t for bad luck, I’d have no luck at all,” as a way to show their support for his recovery. Ross has undergone a pair of operations on his brain over the past two months. In August, he had a shunt inserted to address problems he was experiencing regarding his memory and balance. This month, he had a second procedure, which he stated was to address an issue with the shunt. Ross last appeared on an AEW broadcast at Double or Nothing this past May.
summary: Jim Ross was hospitalized earlier this month due to low oxygen levels following his second brain procedure. The 74-year-old spent one night in the hospital after developing a chest infection and cold. Per the latest Grilling JR podcast, Ross is now home and recovering though still under the weather with his shunt yet to be reconnected.

summary_src: WWE has added another young athlete to its developmental system, and this one has already been through the company’s tryout process twice. Former Michigan State track and field athlete Elly Finch has officially signed with WWE and is headed to the NXT Performance Center.
body: According to a report by PWInsider , WWE has signed the 23-year-old Finch to a developmental contract. She participated in WWE tryouts in both January and August 2026 before ultimately landing a deal. “WWE has signed Elly Finch, 23, who took part in January and August 2026 tryouts to a WWE developmental deal, PWInsider.com has confirmed.” Finch will now be part of the incoming class at the WWE Performance Center, where she’ll begin the next stage of her transition into professional wrestling. She comes in with an athletic background that goes well beyond her time competing in track and field. Before getting WWE’s attention, Finch competed as a shot put thrower for Michigan State’s track and field team. She was also a multi-sport athlete long before reaching the college level, including making some history on the football field. Finch became the first girl to play varsity football for Royal Oak High School in Michigan. As part of the school’s graduating class of 2023, she played tackle, left guard and middle linebacker. title: WWE Pitches Revival Of Sin Cara Character
raw_title: Backstage News On Internal WWE Pitch To Revive Defunct Luchador Character
summary_src: Two different backstage reports reveal there has been an internal pitch within WWE creative to revive the defunct luchador character Sin Cara
body: Many will recall that the Sin Cara character was created in 2011 after WWE signed the luchador Mistico. The gimmick would ultimately be portrayed by both Mistico and the luchador Hunico, who took over the gimmick after Mistico was out with injury in mid-2011; upon his return, the two would feud, culminating in a mask vs. mask match where Mistico defeated Hunico. The latter would later don the character again following Mistico's departure in 2014, and continued to portray Sin Cara until he requested and received his release in 2019 . While the character was seen as a strong merchandise mover, the Sin Cara character was largely perceived as a flop , particularly the Mistico incarnation, as the character never moved past the midcard and became well known for botches. For years, Mistico's time as Sin Cara was seen as significantly hindered his career; he has since seen a career resurgence back in CMLL as the promotion's top star, being credited for the promotion's boom period over the last few years. PW Insider is reporting that there have been early pitches based around the idea of resurrecting the Sin Cara character in WWE. False Finish has learned that Myzteziz Jr. was under consideration to resurrect the Sin Cara character pic.twitter.com/IEZiJ4zdKd Now yes, the argument from people in favor of this will be that it was only a favor because Mistico was a bust under the gimmick. He was, but I would argue that was WWE's fault, a result of WWE trying to turn Mistico into something he wasn't instead of playing to his strengths, something that's led to him succeeding in every other company he's worked for. Furthermore, if Sin Cara failing was just a Mistico problem, why did Hunico never get the gimmick over after? Either way it doesn't matter; the character failed, and bringing it back a decade later isn't going to suddenly revitalize it anymore than WWE bringing back the LWO revitalized that concept. I should also point out that it's comical WWE is attempting this when they already have a Mistico knockoff gimmick in house in Myzteziz Jr., and may be pursuing Dralistico, himself a Mistico knockoff! I've already spent too much time on this, so I will again reiterate; this is a silly, stupid, bad idea on WWE's part. And if they knew better, they'd kill this in the crib right now before it goes beyond the pitch stage.
summary: WWE officials have received internal pitches about bringing back the Sin Cara luchador gimmick that was active from 2011 through 2019. The character was originally created for Mistico, then portrayed by Hunico after an injury and later full-time following Mistico's 2014 exit from the company. Hunico continued as Sin Cara until requesting and receiving his release in 2019, with the persona viewed as a merchandise success but an overall in-ring disappointment that never rose above the midcard.

body: A new report has a bit of an update on WWE’s current creative plans for this year’s WarGames match. Monday night’s episode of Raw saw Roman Reigns stand with The Usos and Solo Sikoa to fight back against 946 foursome of Royce Keys, OTM, and Carmelo Hayes. That led to some speculation that this year’s WarGames could be a four-on-four affair rather than the usual five vs. five match. According to WrestleVotes Radio on Fightful Select , that is not the case at least as it currently stands. The outlet cites a source within the company as saying that as of Monday night, the plan was for WarGames to consist of teams of five. Details on who will make up those teams of five are not confirmed. While obviously the plan would seem to be The Bloodline vs. 946, WWE has not made that match official at this time. title: Swerve Strickland Claims Highest In-Ring Level For Black Wrestler
raw_title: AEW's Swerve Strickland: I Perform At 'Highest Level' For A Black Wrestler In History
summary_src: AEW's Swerve Strickland told Billboard that he feels that he performs at the "highest level" you could see in pro wrestling history for a Black star.
body: In a recent interview with Billboard , Strickland spoke about his career as both a professional wrestler, as well as a rapper and hip-hop artist, both professions where he continues to grow and find new successes. He told the outlet that when future generations look back on his path in wrestling, they'll see his in-ring ability took him the farthest out of anything. "Not me being a caricature of hip-hop, and not me being a caricature of a Black wrestler," Strickland said. "I'm being me. My success in pro-wrestling is genuinely because of my ability in the ring. It's not because they're trying to push an agenda, it's because I perform at a really, really high level — probably the highest level you could see of a Black wrestler in the history of the game." Strickland said there were a lot of Black talents who became "household names" in wrestling back in the day, such as Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson and Booker T, but you could rarely say they were the best wrestlers on their respective shows. He said that's due to who they had to compete with, like the Shawn Michaels and the Eddie Guerreros of the wrestling world. He, however, feels like he competes at the highest level with anyone in AEW. "Me and Okada. Me and Kenny [Omega]. Me and [Will] Ospreay. Me and Hangman [Adam Page]," he said. "I have to be pure and genuinely me as possible and get there because of actual ability rather than just co-signs."
summary: AEW star Swerve Strickland told Billboard that his wrestling success stems purely from his in-ring performances rather than any agenda or persona. He stated that future generations will recognize him for performing at the highest level of any Black wrestler in history. Strickland noted past Black stars like The Rock and Booker T became household names but were rarely the best wrestlers on their shows due to the competition they faced.

On Thursday, PWInsider reported that early pitches had been made to revive the character, with a different wrestler taking on the role. Our own Bryan Alvarez later confirmed the news. The character was originally portrayed by Místico, but was first taken over by Hunico after Místico was suspended for 30 days under WWE’s Talent Wellness Program in 2011. This eventually led to a Sin Cara Negro vs. Sin Cara Azul feud that culminated in a Mask vs. Mask match at the October 16, 2011 WWE SmackDown taping in Mexico City. Místico, portraying Sin Cara Azul, won the match and unmasked Hunico, who had been portraying Sin Cara Negro. Místico was eventually released from WWE in 2014, while Hunico resumed portraying Sin Cara in late 2013 and later formed the Lucha Dragons with Kalisto. title: On the Record: Thekla Responds to Criticism Over Her Behavior Around Young Wrestling Fans
raw_title: Thekla Responds to Criticism Over Her Behavior Around Young Wrestling Fans
summary_src: Thekla knows her behavior around some of AEW’s youngest fans probably isn’t going to win her any role model awards, but she doesn’t seem too worried about it.
body: “I did one of my famous dumb bitch quotes. There’s this clip of me saying it on the stage, and there’s like two small children standing right next to me as I’m calling this girl a dumb bitch, and everybody cheering, and those kids just look at me.” The moment quickly took on a life of its own online, especially because of the kids’ reactions. Thekla said people kept pointing out just how funny and inappropriate the whole situation looked, which eventually led Renee Paquette to ask whether Thekla was really “for the children.” “For a long time, people pointed out how hilarious and wrong the whole situation is, and Renee [Paquette] asked me in an interview, I think, you know, jokingly, ‘Is Thekla for the children?’ And I said, ‘Hell yeah, Thekla is for the children. You know, shout out to my toxic toddlers.’ Now it’s becoming a bit.” Apparently, those two kids weren’t exactly traumatized by their encounter with Thekla either. Their father eventually reached out and revealed that both children were actually big fans of hers. That left their dad with one pretty uncomfortable vocabulary lesson to handle. Thekla joked that somebody was eventually going to teach them what the word meant anyway, so it might as well have been “Auntie Thekla.” “We have got to figure out how we explain that to the young ones. I’m sure somebody will, you know, teach them the hard way, anyway, at some point. Let it be Auntie Thekla.” What started as an unintentionally hilarious moment with two young fans has now basically become part of Thekla’s act. Instead of running away from the criticism, she’s leaned straight into it, and her “Toxic Toddlers” now have their own origin story. title: RevPro made decision to not air Leon Slater match on MyAEW broadcast
raw_title: Report: RevPro made decision to not air Leon Slater match on MyAEW broadcast
body: Fans who tuned into RevPro’s 14th Anniversary card on Saturday via MyAEW pay-per-view would’ve noticed a particular match missing from the broadcast. The move to block the match on the service was reportedly made by RevPro, who wanted to avoid any issues which could emerge when a TNA star appears on an AEW-owned service. Dave Meltzer wrote that promoter Andy Quildan said there “were no direct instructions not to air the match on MyAEW, but to avoid problems since it involved a TNA wrestler, he made the call not to put it on MyAEW.” To make up for the match being absent from the lineup, RevPro plans to upload the match onto Youtube for free. Over the past year, numerous instances of wrestling politics have played out on the independent scene, highlighting a tension between TNA and AEW. Over Wrestlemania weekend, Slater was notably pulled from a match against AEW’s Ricochet, cancelling what many had considered a dream match. Around that same time, Nic Nemeth was taken out of a booking against MJF, and Moose was pulled from a Maple Leaf Pro event. The latest move from RevPro shows that TNA’s past actions of pulling talent over proximity to AEW wrestlers might have caused a chilling effect. While no “direct instructions” caused the match to be taken off the air, it’s likely that recent examples of TNA’s issues with AEW have made promoters take extra precautions so as to avoid such conflict.
summary: Per POST Wrestling: the audience who tuned into RevPro’s 14th Anniversary card on Saturday via MyAEW pay-per-view would’ve noticed a particular match missing from the broadcast. title: Drew McIntyre Volunteers to Become New Sin Cara After WWE Revival Report
raw_title: Drew McIntyre Volunteers to Become New Sin Cara After WWE Revival Report
summary_src: Drew McIntyre has apparently found the perfect role for his WWE comeback — Sin Cara. After reports surfaced that WWE has discussed bringing the masked character back with a new wrestler, McIntyre wasted absolutely no time throwing his 285-pound hat into the ring.
body: McIntyre reacted to the Sin Cara report on Twitter by reposting the recent video of himself pulling off a flying arm drag during training. His message was short and pretty hard to misunderstand. The joke couldn’t have been timed much better. Just one day earlier, McIntyre had surprised fans by climbing to the top rope and busting out the high-flying move while continuing to prepare for his eventual WWE return. After landing the flying arm drag, Drew jumped back to his feet and yelled “Olé!” He then joked on Instagram about suddenly adding some lucha libre to his arsenal. Now he’s putting that newfound lucha experience to good use by jokingly volunteering for WWE’s latest idea. According to PWInsider, there have been early pitches within the company to resurrect the Sin Cara character with somebody new underneath the mask. Nothing has been finalized, and there’s currently no word on who WWE might actually have in mind. The report only noted that the idea has been pitched, so McIntyre’s post appears to be him having some fun with the timing rather than any indication he’s seriously being considered for the role. “For me, I wouldn’t mind coming back. If they would ask me or we would talk, ‘Hey, you want to portray Sin Cara again?’ I would love to do that definitely again and give it another shot.” For now, WWE hasn’t even committed to bringing Sin Cara back, let alone revealed who could end up underneath the mask. McIntyre, however, has already made his pitch — and apparently one flying arm drag was all the qualification he needed. McIntyre’s response probably isn’t going to end with him showing up under the Sin Cara mask, but it does make his sudden lucha experiment a whole lot funnier. If nothing else, Drew clearly knows how to have some fun with WWE rumors while he’s preparing to get back in the ring. title: AAA Builds Weakly To Heroes Inmortales PPV
raw_title: Big Vinny V: A Viewer’s Guide to AAA Heroes Inmortales
summary_src: Nearly six weeks have passed since TripleMania 34, but it has been an uneventful six weeks in the world of AAA. They have devoted precious little time to building to Heroes Inmortales, a three-week event that begins this Saturday.
body: Nearly six weeks have passed since TripleMania 34, but it has been an uneventful six weeks in the world of AAA. They have devoted precious little time to building to Heroes Inmortales, a three-week event that begins this Saturday. We don’t even have a full card yet, but here’s a look at what we do know, and which matches are worth your time. Imagine, if you will, that after Roman Reigns defeated CM Punk at WrestleMania this year, both Reigns and Punk decided to take the next month off … which, come to think of it, is more or less what actually happened. But what if, after five weeks of mutual absence, they announced on SmackDown that Reigns and Punk would be doing a rematch a week later. Wouldn’t that be weird? Well, that’s basically what AAA is doing with El Grande Americano and Dominik Mysterio. After they met in the main event of what was theoretically AAA’s biggest show of the year, neither has appeared much on AAA television. Their only appearance: a tag team match on October 3, when Dominik Mysterio & Omos defeated Americano & Rey Mysterio. (They also competed against each other in a trios match on the WWE/AAA Worlds Collide show.) Then last week, out of nowhere, the elder Mysterio announced that his son would be getting his championship rematch this weekend, on seven days’ notice. No, this does not feel like a rematch of the biggest match of the year. In fact, it’s not even the most intriguing match of the night. That honor would go to La Catalina, who will be defending her Reina de Reinas championship on a AAA show for the first time. Her opponents will be former champion Lady Flammer and La Hiedra, who is one-half of the AAA Mixed Tag Team Champions and also Flammer’s stablemate in Las Toxicas. Hiedra spent a lot of time in Flammer’s shadow during the latter’s 1,000-plus-day championship reign. The time seems right for an outright split. Also on Saturday night, Los Perros Del Mal will defend the AAA Trios Championships against Mister Iguana & La Parka & Nino Hamburguesa. It will be a fun match with a lot of action and Los Perros will retain. BANGER ALERT! BANGER ALERT! Rey Fenix’s one-on-one defense of the AAA Cruiserweight Championship against Mini Vikingo should be stellar. The two have met twice before this year, with Fenix successfully defending his championship both times. The first was a singles match that aired in August on AAA TV; the second was a four-way (also including Jack Cartwheel and Nathan Frazer) on the second night of TripleMania in Mexico City. Our own Dave Meltzer gave the first match **** and the second *****1/4. We’re practically guaranteed to see the best match of any given week whenever these two meet. WWE is clearly high on Mini Vikingo, featuring him at Worlds Collide and on NXT, and a title change seems likely. Only one match has been announced for this evening: El Fiscal vs. Abismo Negro Jr. The build for this has been quite odd. Fiscal lost to Taurus on AAA TV last week after Negro interfered. title: On the Record: Sol Ruca Explains Why a Heel Turn Might Never Happen in WWE
raw_title: Sol Ruca Explains Why a Heel Turn Might Never Happen in WWE
summary_src: Sol Ruca has spent her WWE career showing fans her fun-loving side, but she’s definitely curious about what would happen if she went in the complete opposite direction. The NXT star admitted she’d love to experiment with being a heel, even though she’s previously been told it might never happen.
body: Speaking on The Finish , Ruca was asked whether she could eventually turn heel and evolve her character beyond the bubbly babyface fans have gotten to know. Ruca said it’s something she’d absolutely be interested in trying. “I have no idea. I think I would love to be able to try that.” The problem is that apparently some people have a hard time imagining her as the bad guy. Ruca revealed she’s previously been told she probably won’t ever turn heel because her natural personality makes it difficult to picture. “I have been told in the past that I most likely will not be heel ever because of just how I am naturally. I am quite a bubbly and, like, [likable] person.” That doesn’t mean Ruca has completely given up on showing fans a darker side. She believes it might simply take the right person or storyline to finally bring it out of her. “So, I don’t know. I feel like it’s going to take a very special person to really get that side out of me, but I guess we’re just going to have to wait and see.” Ruca didn’t hint that a heel turn is actually being planned, so fans probably shouldn’t expect her personality to suddenly change overnight. Still, she’s clearly open to getting outside her comfort zone if WWE ever gives her the chance. For someone whose personality has apparently been the biggest reason people can’t picture her as a villain, that could actually make the turn even more interesting if WWE eventually pulls the trigger. Ruca just needs to find that “special person” capable of bringing out a side fans haven’t seen before. body: TNA Wrestling has made a unique announcement for its October 13 television taping in Dothan, Alabama. In celebration of Matt & Jeff Hardy entering their 35th year in pro wrestling, TNA is hyping that the duo will have “complete control” of the Impact episode that’s being taped on October 13. The show is set to air on October 15, with The Hardys serving as on-screen matchmakers for the entire broadcast: Matt Hardy responded to the announcement by joking that he’s aiming to win Booker of the Year. This show is happening in the immediate aftermath of Bound for Glory, where Matt & Jeff are set to take on the former Joe Gacy & Dexter Lumis in a falls count anywhere match. The pay-per-view is being held in Tampa, Florida on October 11. Dothan Civic Center is hosting Impact tapings on both October 13-14. For the first night, TNA is encouraging fans to dress up like Matt or Jeff Hardy from any era of their career. There will also be special merchandise on sale to celebrate their 35th year in wrestling. body: September 22, 2026 By Steph Franchomme TNA Wrestling , IMPACT , North America , Pro Wrestling AJ Francis revealed in our interview that being a heel is easier for him, mostly because he’s bigger than most of the TNA roster, and it makes him look more credible when he faces a smaller wrestler. AJ Francis is a wrestler we love to hate. At TNA Lockdown , he defeated Elijah, thanks to EXPRESSIONS. Francis would do anything to win, even if it means lying, cheating, or stealing. Since “The Phenomenal Son” Avery Styles arrived in the iMPACT Zone , he has been on Francis’ radar. He wants to be his first opponent in his first match on TNA Wrestling. Then, Moose and Frankie Kazarian are not exactly okay with that. Could the match happen live this week on TNA iMPACT or live on October 11 at TNA Bound for Glory ? In an interview with Last Word on Sports Pro Wrestling and WorldWide Wrestling , AJ Francis discussed various subjects. This includes his TNA Lockdown match against Elijah, Avery Styles, his Championship goals, his football past, his passion for music, and more. “It was awesome. It felt like history in the moment too. Once the bell rang, one, two, three, I knew that we had put on a masterpiece. Matt Rehwoldt said on commentary, when Elijah was getting in the cage, “This match is going to be a litmus test for the guys in the back for what to expect for the rest of the night.” That’s exactly what it was. It set a standard of what to be expected for the rest of the night. “I love those opportunities to go out there and perform. I say it all the time, putting me on first is dangerous. You might want to save me for later in the show because if you put me on first, it’s going to be a hell of a match to follow. When we’re on top of the cage fighting it out, it’s just one of those crazy moments. You dream of moments like that. The similarities become less obvious once the action begins. WWE performers train for physically demanding, choreographed contests, while boxers must respond to opponents genuinely trying to defeat them. Strength, timing, and confidence can help in both disciplines, but success in one doesn't guarantee success in the other. Several familiar WWE personalities have tested themselves in boxing or related combat sports. Their experiences range from impressive victories to painful reminders that fighting experience matters more than reputation. John Morrison built his wrestling reputation around remarkable athleticism. His acrobatic moves, agility, and impressive physical conditioning helped distinguish him during several WWE runs. In April 2023, Morrison entered a different kind of contest when he faced Harley Morenstein at Creator Clash 2 in Tampa, Florida. The event brought together internet personalities and entertainers for competitive boxing matches. Morrison approached the fight with considerable aggression. He knocked Morenstein through the ropes during the opening round before securing a third-round technical knockout with a powerful right hand. His preparation involved more than relying on wrestling fitness. Morrison later discussed training with experienced fighters, including former UFC heavyweight Josh Barnett, and learning through demanding sparring sessions. The victory brought immediate attention. Morrison even challenged influencer boxer KSI afterward, suggesting an interest in further crossover opportunities. His debut demonstrated that athleticism can transfer successfully when accompanied by appropriate preparation. One victory, however, doesn't establish how someone would perform against an experienced professional boxer. Logan Paul's relationship with boxing began before his WWE career. His fights against fellow internet personality KSI introduced him to competitive combat sports, while a 2021 exhibition against Floyd Mayweather attracted considerable attention. Paul subsequently became a recognizable WWE performer, combining his athletic ability with a talent for attracting audiences. In October 2023, he returned to boxing against mixed martial artist Dillon Danis in Manchester, England. Their heavily publicized encounter ended in the sixth round when Danis was disqualified following illegal grappling attempts. Paul had controlled much of the contest with his jab, but the chaotic ending overshadowed his performance. Security personnel entered the ring as tensions escalated between the fighters and their teams. title: Sin Cara Revival Reportedly Being Pitched in WWE
raw_title: Sin Cara Revival Reportedly Being Pitched in WWE
body: A familiar face, or rather a masked one, might soon be making a comeback in WWE. PWInsider (via Fightful ) reports that early pitches are being made in WWE about potentially reviving Sin Cara. Additionally, PWInsider notes that if WWE moves forward with the idea, a new wrestler will take up the mantle of Sin Cara. Two different wrestlers previously competed under the moniker of Sin Cara in WWE. Luis Ignacio Urive Alvirde, aka Místico, portrayed the role of Sin Cara from 2011 to October 2013. Later, Cinta de Oro, who also wrestled in WWE as Hunico, became the second Sin Cara in WWE. He initially appeared as an impostor version of Sin Cara, Sin Cara Negro, back in 2011. However, Cinta de Oro later became the official version of Sin Cara starting in 2013. He portrayed the character until December 2019, when he was released from the promotion. The wrestler voluntarily requested to be released at the time. WWE has not yet announced a return for the wrestler. However, with WWE’s recent acquisition of Lucha Libre AAA and the surge in popularity of Mexican and luchador stars in WWE, it makes sense that the creative team would contemplate a return of the popular gimmick.

title: Eric Bischoff Makes Surprising Admission About the Real Hulk Hogan
raw_title: Eric Bischoff Makes Surprising Admission About the Real Hulk Hogan
body: During an appearance on the Planet Tyrus podcast , Bischoff discussed how the late WWE legend struggled to separate his wrestling persona from Terry Bollea, the man behind the red-and-yellow gear. For Hogan, being the Hulkster wasn't something he could simply switch off when the cameras stopped rolling. "He was in character all the time," Bischoff said, explaining that Hogan understood what fans expected whenever he stepped outside his home. Whether he was working or running errands, people wanted to meet Hulk Hogan, not Terry Bollea. "He lived it," Bischoff continued. "And, over time, I think he lost sight sometimes of who Terry was and who Hulk was." Bischoff had a front-row seat to Hogan's career, including his blockbuster WCW run and transformation into Hollywood Hogan as the leader of the New World Order. The two remained closely associated long after WCW's collapse, making Bischoff one of the people most familiar with the demands of maintaining wrestling's biggest celebrity persona. But the conversation also turned to the controversies that followed Hogan outside the ring, particularly the leaked recording in which he repeatedly used racial slurs while discussing his daughter Brooke Hogan's relationship with a Black man. The recording became public in 2015, prompting WWE to terminate its relationship with Hogan and remove references to him from its website. WWE reinstated him to the Hall of Fame in 2018. Tyrus, who is Black, defended Hogan's handling of the scandal, arguing that the wrestler eventually accepted responsibility instead of blaming others. "The difference is: he owned it," Tyrus said. "He sincerely apologized, and he owned it. And that to me was the greatest strength of any man!" Tyrus also acknowledged that Hogan had made serious mistakes, but questioned whether anyone could withstand the scrutiny that came with his level of fame. "He wasn't perfect; he didn't always say the right thing," Tyrus said. "Who the f*ck does?" Those comments come as Hogan's personal life continues to receive scrutiny more than a year after his July 2025 death at age 71. His daughter Brooke has been especially outspoken about the difference between the wrestling icon audiences admired and the father she knew. She recently revealed that their relationship fundamentally changed after Hogan had an affair with her friend Christiane Plante, saying she forgave him but never felt he treated her the same way afterward. Brooke also criticized Netflix's four-part documentary Hulk Hogan: Real American , calling it "missing 98 percent of real life" and arguing that it failed to address the family's more difficult history. Bischoff, meanwhile, believes the documentary offered audiences something they rarely got during Hogan's career: glimpses of Terry Bollea without the wrestling character. title: Contract News: 5 Things Cody Rhodes Must Do Before He Finishes His Final WWE Contract
raw_title: 5 Things Cody Rhodes Must Do Before He Finishes His Final WWE Contract
body: Rhodes has already accomplished more than most wrestlers ever do. He won the Royal Rumble in 2023 and 2024, beat Roman Reigns at WrestleMania 40 to win the Undisputed WWE Universal Championship, and has held the WWE Championship multiple times since. He is currently on SmackDown in a feud with Randy Orton, who cost him the WWE Championship match against CM Punk at SummerSlam in August. Even with all of that on his resume, there are still a few things left for him to check off before he calls it a career in WWE. Rhodes and The Rock have only wrestled against each other once, when The Rock teamed with Roman Reigns to beat Rhodes and Seth Rollins on night one of WrestleMania 40. The Rock was also involved in the Bloodline Rules match the next night, and John Cena’s heel turn in February 2025. But Rhodes has never faced him in a singles match. That is something that needs to happen in the next couple of years. Rhodes has held the WWE Championship more than once, but he has never held the World Heavyweight Championship that WWE introduced in 2023. That title is held by Roman Reigns , who is set to face Undisputed WWE Champion Sami Zayn in a champion vs. champion match at Crown Jewel . Winning both of WWE’s top men’s titles would round out his resume, and a world title match against Reigns would bring back one of the biggest rivalries of his career. Rhodes competed in Money in the Bank ladder matches in 2010, 2011, 2012, and 2013 during his first run with WWE but never won the briefcase. Since returning to the company in 2022, he has been in the main event picture and has not needed it. A Money in the Bank win late in his career would be a different look for him. It would give him a reason to chase the title again after losing it, and the cash-in would give WWE a moment that fans would remember. Rhodes has been one of WWE’s top babyfaces since his return at WrestleMania 38 in 2022. He turned down a chance to go to the dark side at Elimination Chamber in 2025, when he refused The Rock’s offer, which led to John Cena turning heel instead. That is exactly why a heel turn would work. Rhodes has spent four years as the hero, and turning on the fans would be the biggest shock WWE could deliver with him. His heel work in Ring of Honor, in NJPW, and during his first WWE run shows he can play the role, and he showed a darker edge on the October 16 episode of SmackDown when he hit Baron Corbin with a punt kick during his feud with Randy Orton. If Rhodes does turn, he should not do it alone. Rhodes led The Nightmare Family in AEW, so he already has experience at the head of a group. Leading his own faction in WWE would give a heel run more weight and would give younger wrestlers a chance to be featured alongside one of the company’s biggest stars. A Rhodes-led group would also give him something different from the one-on-one feuds that have defined his WWE return, and it would set up battles with the established factions on both brands.
summary: Per Sportsnaut: rhodes has already accomplished more than most wrestlers ever do. Even with all of that on his resume, there are still a few things left for him to check off before he calls it a career in WWE.

title: Fan Hospitalized After Tiger Jeet Singh Attack Says He Wishes the Cut Was Deeper
raw_title: Fan Hospitalized After Tiger Jeet Singh Attack Says He Wishes the Cut Was Deeper
summary_src: The wrestling fan who got cracked in the head by Tiger Jeet Singh’s saber apparently isn’t angry about it at all.
body: Speaking to Tokyo Sports after attending the October 21 Strong Style Pro Wrestling event at Korakuen Hall, the fan opened up about the bizarre incident for the first time. He revealed that when he saw Singh charging toward him at the October 17 show, his first reaction wasn’t exactly fear. The longtime wrestling fan admitted he doesn’t even remember the saber actually making contact with his forehead. All he remembers is suddenly feeling the impact and realizing that Tiger Jeet Singh had just nailed him. “I don’t remember being stabbed. Suddenly there was a ‘bang,’ and I thought, ‘I’ve been hit, this is awesome.’” The man, a 38-year-old office worker from Yokohama, has been watching professional wrestling since elementary school. He grew up seeing Singh and Abdullah the Butcher on television and always wanted the chance to experience them in person. “I used to watch Singh and Abdullah the Butcher on TV. I wanted to see them in person, but I never thought I’d actually be attacked.” The attack definitely looked scary in the moment. Singh was making his entrance at Megumi Kudo’s 40th anniversary show when he started swinging his trademark saber through the crowd and caught the fan directly in the forehead. The man was left bleeding and eventually taken to the hospital by ambulance. Thankfully, the injury wasn’t serious, and doctors were able to close the wound with medical staples. Apparently, that’s where the disappointment comes in. Instead of being upset about getting his head busted open, the fan wishes Singh had done enough damage to leave him with a permanent souvenir. “I wish they had cut a little deeper… I’m actually a little shocked.” He isn’t holding a grudge against Singh either. Asked about potentially seeing the wrestling legend again if Singh makes another trip to Japan, the fan made it clear he’d happily be there. That reaction is pretty wild considering what Singh himself said after the incident. Rather than apologizing, the legendary heel blamed the fan for standing in his path when he came charging through the crowd. “It was a mistake for him to be in front of me. It’s his fault. You know that, right? All he had to do was get out of my way.” Tiger Ali Singh backed up his father and pointed out that fans had been warned to be careful during the entrance. The show’s organizer, Megumi Kudo, took a different approach and apologized over what happened. The fan did get another pretty nice surprise out of the ordeal. He’s a huge supporter of Sareee, and after hearing what happened, she sent him a ticket to her December 28 show along with an autographed photo as a get-well gift. “I’m actually kind of happy about it. As long as I’m able to move, I’ll continue to support Sareee.” What initially looked like a nightmare situation apparently turned into one of this fan’s favorite wrestling memories. summary_src: Ilja Dragunov made his debut appearance in AEW over the weekend at the WrestleDream pay-per-view, before winning his first match for the promotion in the main event of this week’s (Oct. 21) episode of Dynamite.
body: Link AEW Cain A. Knight is a hardcore number-cruncher who has analyzed and covered pro wrestling for Cageside Seats since 2014, and followed the sport as a fan going back to the 1980’s. Ilja Dragunov made his debut appearance in AEW over the weekend at the WrestleDream pay-per-view, before winning his first match for the promotion in the main event of this week’s (Oct. 21) episode of Dynamite. I’ve seen quite a few wrestling fans wonder why Dragunov is allowed to keep using his WWE ring name in AEW. title: New U.S. Embassy Security Alert Warns of Airport Threats Ahead of WWE Crown Jewel 2026
raw_title: New U.S. Embassy Security Alert Warns of Airport Threats Ahead of WWE Crown Jewel 2026
body: 0 The U.S. Embassy in Saudi Arabia has issued another security warning amid regional tensions and threats against airports, raising further questions about travel arrangements ahead of WWE Crown Jewel 2026 in Riyadh. The warning comes as WWE prepares for its annual premium live event in Saudi Arabia on November 7. The show is scheduled to take place at Riyadh Season Stadium in the King Abdullah Financial District, with WWE continuing to promote the event despite growing security concerns. The latest advisory follows reports of attacks targeting Saudi airports and warnings about possible flight cancellations, airspace closures, and travel disruptions. The situation has also prompted questions about whether WWE will proceed with Crown Jewel as planned. The October 21 advisory warned that Iran-backed Houthi forces had attacked civilian airports and other critical infrastructure, resulting in casualties and significant travel disruption. It also noted that the conflict could escalate beyond the immediate region. The alert specifically noted that operations at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh remained suspended. King Abdulaziz International Airport in Jeddah and King Fahd International Airport in Dammam were operating, although delays and cancellations were reported. U.S. citizens were advised to exercise extreme caution when using airports in Saudi Arabia and check directly with airlines and airport authorities for updates. Despite the security concerns, WWE has not announced a change to Crown Jewel’s scheduled date or location. The event remains advertised for November 7 in Riyadh, with the promotion continuing its build toward the annual champion-versus-champion matches . According to PWInsider , WWE still plans to proceed with the event and has contingency plans in place, including working with a security firm experienced in the Middle East and North Africa region. llm_long: A federal judge rejected a motion to dismiss a lawsuit against WWE and TKO, Vince McMahon, and Linda McMahon. The case involves seven plaintiffs who allege they were sexually abused as minors in the 1980s and 1990s while working as ring boys for WWE.

The plaintiffs claim abuse by former WWE ring announcer Mel Phillips. One plaintiff also alleges sexual abuse by former executive Pat Patterson, and another alleges sexual harassment by former Vice President of Operations Terry Garvin. All three accused individuals have since passed away.

The suit accuses the McMahons and WWE of negligence for allegedly allowing the abuse to occur and continue. The case was filed under the Maryland Child Victims Act, which removes time limits for lawsuits related to child sexual abuse.

WWE, TKO, and the McMahons argued that the Maryland law violates the 14th Amendment by being unfair or arbitrary, especially given the decades-old allegations and the deaths of the accused. The judge ruled that the defendants failed to demonstrate how the law is arbitrary or irrational in this case.
With the motion to dismiss denied, the lawsuit will proceed to the discovery phase. A teleconference is scheduled for November 17 to establish additional deadlines.

title: Joe Hendry Believes He Can Become Top WWE Draw
raw_title: Joe Hendry: I Know In My Heart I Can Be A Top Draw For WWE
summary_src: Joe Hendry believes he can move the needle for WWE. Hendry became a top star in TNA Wrestling in 2024-25, which led to him signing with WWE and winning the NXT Championship. He has had a consistent presence on WWE TV since joining Raw at the beginning of the year.
body: Hendry became a top star in TNA Wrestling in 2024-25, which led to him signing with WWE and winning the NXT Championship. He has had a consistent presence on WWE TV since joining Raw at the beginning of the year. Speaking to Scott Fishman of TV Insider , Hendry was asked about his hopes for his career. “I’m just always looking to get better at what I do. I know in my heart that I can be a top draw for WWE. I know people have things to say about that, but the truth is I know that I can be a top guy, I know that I can be an asset to the professional wrestling business because I have the metrics to prove it. And those are facts, you know? I had the most viewed clip in all of wrestling in 2024. I wrestled Randy Orton at WrestleMania, which did insane numbers on social media. My WrestleMania shirt was a bestseller. I won the NXT Championship. I have the metrics to prove that I can draw in the professional wrestling business, and my goal is to be somebody who can deliver for the company. I saw in an interview that [WWE President] Nick Khan was asked what WWE is looking for from talent. It is someone that can move the needle for the company immediately or in the near future. I believe that I’m somebody who can do that. I’ve had metrics in the past to prove that I think I can be a top guy for WWE. So I’m looking to acquire the skills to do that as quickly as I can,” he said. Hendry has been making fun of JD McDonagh by using a Funko Pop on recent episodes of Raw. He stars in the company’s first-ever microdrama Agent of Shadows , which premieres on October 23.

title: End of an Era: Former WWE Champion Could Retire in 2027: Report

body: The report did not say when Mysterio plans to retire , but backstage chatter indicates that the former WWE Champion will be calling it an in-ring career next year. Mysterio, the current AAA general manager, is expected to remain with the company in an executive position, while also developing the next generation of WWE stars. While Rey Mysterio is contemplating retirement, his lineage is at the genesis of their budding careers . Mysterios’ son, Dominik, is a former Intercontinental Champion and AAA Mega Champion. His daughter Aalyah has also reported to the WWE Performance Center for training. Dominik Mysterio isn’t satisfied with just being a second-generation star, however, and previously stated that he wants to retire his legendary father. During an appearance on The Ariel Helwani Show , Dirty Dom called it his “birthright” to retire his father, Rey Mysterio. “I’ve been talking about it. I’ve been wanting him to retire. I want him out of here, you know?” he began. “ There’s only room for so many Mysterios in WWE . “There’s one pushing 60, and I think it’s time for him to kick rocks; that’s just how I see it.” “It’s my birthright. I would lose my absolute s**t if it’s not me,” Dominik said of his father’s last match. “I’ve got to take his mask, and I’ve got to take his name.” WWE has not confirmed which city will host Rey Mysterio’s last match, but Dominik Mysterio has the perfect venue in mind. “Auditorio Fausto Gutierrez Moreno, super historical arena down in Tijuana, Mexico,” Dominik said. “I believe my dad has wrestled there, debuted there. My great-uncle and most of my godfathers wrestled there [too].” Regardless of when Rey Mysterio retires, his imprint on pro wrestling will never be forgotten. Mysterio began his career in 1989, beginning on the independent scene. He signed with WCW in 1996, becoming a heralded cruiserweight star and helping popularize lucha libre in America. Mysterio joined WWE in 2002 and boasts one of the most impressive resumes in the promotion’s history. Mysterio, 51, is a former Royal Rumble winner and one of the most revered high-flyers. During his storied career, Mysterio captured the WWE Championship, World Heavyweight Championship, Tag Team Championships and the Cruiserweight Championship. title: Nic Nemeth Wants Final Run Like Peers
raw_title: TNA's Nic Nemeth Ponders Final Run For Him And Other Wrestlers Of His Generation
summary_src: TNA star Nic Nemeth ponders what the road to retirement might look like for himself and other wrestlers of his generation.
body: Last year, John Cena officially retired from in-ring competition. Next year, Adam "Edge" Copeland will do the same. Their former colleague Nic Nemeth, meanwhile, is showing no signs of slowing down. That hasn't stopped him from pondering what his own future road to retirement might look like, though. "I would like to do a cool thing," Nemeth said on "Busted Open Radio." "I would like to do my last show in LA, my last show in Cleveland, my last time fighting for a title, all these different things and go, 'This is my last one.' We'd all like to have a last year run. I don't know how that works. I know it can work out for some people, and a lot of people in our business don't get to call those shots. But when you do and you mean something, hopefully we see more and more of those, because I know we like it." Nemeth, a former collegiate wrestler, kicked off his professional wrestling career under the WWE banner in 2004. At the time, Cena and Copeland were steadily building themselves as major singles stars on WWE's main roster. Other names such as The Miz, Mickie James, and Nemeth himself were working their way up WWE's developmental system. Eventually, Nemeth hopes that all the in-ring performers of his generation, now veterans to the business, receive a moment of recognition before making their own farewells. In his case, "The Showoff" appears to be further away from his. "I love when someone who's done so much, or someone that I've been in the ring with, to get everybody giving them their moment, and enjoy what they did and the sacrifices they made," Nemeth said. "I love that stuff." Nemeth is currently signed to TNA, where he reigns as one-half of the TNA World Tag Team Champions. He lost the TNA World Championship to Leon Slater at Bound For Glory on October 11.

I need to know right now, is this gonna change? Because if it’s not, I don’t need to be here. I don’t need to be here to make money. I don’t need to be here to get famous. I’m here to help advance this. And if you’re telling me right now that’s never gonna happen, then I’m done. I only want to improve this.’ She’s not gonna tell you that story. She’s not gonna tweet about it. She’s not gonna go on a thing and talk about it. body: Coming up is the 2026 CMLL Women’s Grand Prix, and one of the competitors is Alice Crowley. Crowley was interviewed by Fightful’s Luis Pulido and spoke about the opportunity and how it came to be. “I’m so excited; there’s just no other way to put it. I get to wrestle in Arena México, like, that’s awesome and, honestly, I can’t thank everyone enough. Whenever he actually gave me that call and was like, “It’s CMLL; you’re gonna be going to Mexico”, it was just mind-blowing. If it wasn’t for Scott, I would not be here right now, so thank you, Scott, thank you, but yes, that is what I would assume. I don’t know what elseScott did to be able to get the company with this deal; it’s a lot of hard work, and I’m just thankful that I’m the one who gets to be able to represent Maple Leaf in this tournament. body: On Thursday's episode of "TNA Impact" in Brampton , Allie and Hogan laid out an open challenge for their titles. McKenzie and Allie kicked off the action with a lock-up, which the former used as leverage to corner the latter against the ropes. Hogan tossed McKenzie out of the ring, leaving Vipress alone in the ring to eat Allie's codebreaker and Hogan's Face The Music. Allie then pinned Vipress for the win. A recent injury, however, has kept Rosemary sidelined and unable to defend the titles, hence Allie's new alliance with Hogan. title: On the Record: Nic Nemeth Responds to Dave Meltzer's 'Gossipy' Take on WWE Relationship Hurting TNA Wrestling
raw_title: Nic Nemeth Responds to Dave Meltzer's 'Gossipy' Take on WWE Relationship Hurting TNA Wrestling
body: While Vince McMahon was the greatest promoter in wrestling history, there were many things about his business practices that frustrated fans. One of the most prominent was his unwillingness to work with other promotions for much of his nearly 40 years in the business. However, with him out of the picture, the current regime led by Nick Khan and Triple H is open to doing business with competitors. The most notable example of this change in strategy is their ongoing working relationship with TNA, which became official early last year. At first, it seemed like a very good thing for TNA. Via a talent exchange, TNA was able to get its wrestlers on WWE’s highly viewed shows, and WWE stars (mostly from NXT) appeared on episodes of Impact. Several NXT stars even won TNA championships, including Trick Williams , who had a lengthy reign with the brand’s top title. However, some viewers of the sport feel there has been an imbalance that benefits WWE. “ It’s a bad situation ,” Wrestling Observer’s Dave Meltzer claimed this month. “This always happens when you work with WWE historically. The fanbase sees the WWE guys as superior because they are booked as superior, and then when it ends, you have to draw with your inferior guys. TNA’s ticket sales are way down now. It looks like most saw this going in. “That WWE worked with TNA as a way to hurt AEW, the key being to send talent so TNA has better leverage for a TV deal. In that sense, the deal did short-term work out great for TNA, but now they have to struggle with the post-deal period.” In an exclusive conversation with Casino.org , current TNA Champion Nic Nemeth was asked whether he agrees with Meltzer’s take on the WWE-TNA relationship issues. Well, the multi-time WWE titleist doesn’t buy the reporter’s “gossipy” views on the situation. “Meltzer’s kind of story that he’s concocted about this, I don’t really want to get into that, but I think it’s been fruitful for both of us,” the man once known as Dolph Ziggler in WWE said. “It’s really helped us long-term, especially having that name with us. I think physically, I think we lost the battle more than we won the battle when it came to wins and losses with NXT and TNA guys and girls coming back and forth. “It really helped us get that AMC deal and get on a great channel. And they’ve been such incredible partners. I get fired up. I’m watching like Caddyshack or Christmas Vacation with my parents on AMC, and there’s a commercial every time I’m watching; it’s the Hardys, it’s me, it’s TNA. And I’m like, ‘This is incredible!'” he added. “What a great partner that we have. So I can’t really speak for a guy who’s using gossipy kind of algorithms to put something together.” “As someone who’s been behind the scenes for both places. I think it has really, really worked out for us,” Nemeth said.

body: The death is sudden, as he wrestled at AEW's All Out pay-per-view on Saturday night in the greater Chicago area. Satterley challenged Andrade for the AEW National Championship in the evening's opening pay-per-view match, losing the title tilt before later reappearing during the show's main event between Will Ospreay and Jon Moxley. All Elite Wrestling is saddened to announce the passing of Benjamin Satterley, aka Pac. A native of Newcastle upon Tyne, England, Satterley began his wrestling career in 2004 and went on to perform for wrestling organizations all over the world, captivating fans with innovative high-flying moves and incredible in-ring ability. Pac signed with All Elite Wrestling in 2019 and held multiple AEW Championships and competed in some of the most memorable matches in AEW history. Our condolences go out to Satterley's family, friends and fans. Fightful's Sean Ross Sapp reported Monday that Satterley was found dead in a rental car at approximately 4 p.m. ET Sunday afternoon, and that Illinois' Cook County medical examiner's office has ruled out any indications of foul play or trauma. Debuting as a professional wrestler in his native England in 2004, Satterley quickly established himself as one of the most acclaimed high-flying workers of his generation. He competed extensively on the British independent scene before wrestling around the world for promotions including Pro Wrestling Guerrilla, Ring of Honor, New Japan Pro-Wrestling and Dragongate. Satterley's breakout into the sport's mainstream began when he signed with WWE in 2012, performing under the ring name "Neville." Nicknamed "The Man That Gravity Forgot" because of his spectacular aerial offense, Satterley became one of the standout performers of WWE's developmental brand, NXT, before moving to the company's main roster in 2015. During his six years with WWE, Satterley became a two-time WWE Cruiserweight Champion, one-time NXT Champion and two-time NXT Tag Team Champion. After parting ways with the WWE in 2018, Satterley returned to the independent scene and captured another title with Japan's Dragongate before becoming one of AEW's earliest major signings in 2019, performing under the ring name "PAC." Satterley remained with AEW for the next seven years, competing both as a singles wrestler and, more often, as part of several prominent factions. He formed the Death Triangle in 2020 alongside Penta and Rey Fenix before joining Jon Moxley's Death Riders in 2024. During his time in AEW, Satterley became the promotion's inaugural All-Atlantic Champion in 2022 and twice captured its World Trios Championship. His first trios title reign also made him the first wrestler in AEW history to hold two championships simultaneously. Satterley remained an active member of AEW's roster through the final days of his life. In the week before All Out, he defeated Adam Priest and Ace Austin in televised AEW matches. title: TNA Wrestling Officially Signs Shayna Baszler

body: TNA Wrestling has officially announced the signing of former WWE Superstar Shayna Baszler, confirming that the accomplished professional wrestler and mixed martial artist has joined the company’s roster. The signing was first reported by Denise Salcedo of Instinct Culture before TNA confirmed the news in an official press release. Baszler has already made an immediate impact in the promotion, capturing championship gold during her TNA debut at Bound For Glory on October 11, 2026. Teaming with Zoey Serrano under the name The Apex, Baszler defeated the competition to become one-half of the TNA Knockouts World Tag Team Champions. The championship victory marked a successful beginning to Baszler’s TNA career, with the former WWE star securing a title in her first appearance for the promotion. Baszler brings extensive experience to TNA, having established herself as a multi-time champion in both singles and tag team competition throughout her professional wrestling career. Before becoming a prominent figure in professional wrestling, Baszler also enjoyed a lengthy career in mixed martial arts. Her MMA record includes 15 victories, with 13 of those wins coming by submission, highlighting the grappling background that has become a defining element of her in-ring style. Baszler made her professional wrestling debut in 2015 before going on to establish herself as one of the industry’s most recognizable submission specialists. title: Indi Hartwell Retains Knockouts Title On TNA Impact
raw_title: Indi Hartwell Retains KO Title Against Former Champ Xia Brookside On TNA Impact
summary_src: Indi Hartwell retained the Knockouts World Championship in a rematch against Xia Brookside during "TNA Impact."
body: TNA Indi Hartwell defeated Xia Brookside in an impromptu match for her Knockouts World Championship during "TNA Impact." Hartwell defeated Brookside for the title at Bound For Glory earlier this month. She came out during Thursday's show to interrupt Daria Rae in her return and subsequent promo, prompting Rae to book the rematch immediately despite Hartwell not being in ring gear. Brookside then made her entrance to get the match underway, taking advantage relatively quickly by attacking the left arm on the outside of the ring. She brought the action back inside the ring, further targeting the arm on the mat but unable to put the match away. Hartwell fought her way back into the bout and sought for a Full Nelson slam, but due to the damage done to her arm she couldn't complete it. That allowed Brookside to take advantage and go right back to the arm. Brookside looked for the Darkside DDT but Hartwell slipped out from her grasp, connecting with a big boot and the slam for the winning pinfall. After the match, Zoey Serrano and Shayna Baszler entered the ring to ambush Hartwell. Baszler choked the Knockouts World Champion out before posing with her belt, as Rae watched on from the entrance ramp with amusement on her face.
summary: Indi Hartwell defended her TNA Knockouts World Championship against Xia Brookside in an impromptu match on Thursday's episode of TNA Impact. Brookside targeted Hartwell's left arm throughout the bout after interrupting Daria Rae's return promo, which led to the immediate title match. Hartwell overcame the damage to hit a big boot and Full Nelson slam for the pinfall victory.

Brookside went for her Darkside DDT, but Hartwell escaped and hit a big boot followed by a slam to score the winning pinfall. After the match, Zoey Serrano and Shayna Baszler ambushed Hartwell in the ring.

body: Ospreay enters AEW All Out for his first world title defense after completing his decade-long chase with a scintillating win over Kenny Omega at All In London last month . Ospreay defeated Omega at Wembley Stadium to capture the AEW World Championship, then personally sought out Moxley as the first challenger of his reign. Moxley, a four-time AEW World Champion and the current AEW Continental Champion, is the last wrestler to pin Ospreay and he featured heavily in Ospreay's run to the belt. Notably, Saturday pits AEW and WWE head-to-head on the same night in the Chicago market , as WWE and AAA hold Worlds Collide at Allstate Arena in nearby Rosemont. Uncrowned will carry live coverage of both events. AEW All Out takes place this Saturday, Sept. 26, at NOW Arena in Hoffman Estates, Illinois, in the Chicago metropolitan area. The inaugural AEW All Out event took place at the same venue — then known as the Sears Centre Arena — in 2019, and this year's show marks the fifth time in eight years that All Out takes over the building. Saturday's pay-per-view card begins at 8 p.m. ET, while the pre-show begins at 7 p.m. ET. AEW All Out 2026 is available to watch live on pay-per-view in the United States through HBO Max, YouTube, Amazon Prime, PPV.com and Sling. It can be seen internationally through Amazon Prime, PPV.com and MyAEW. With AEW Women's World Champion Mercedes Moné still healing from the broken nose she suffered during her title-winning match at All In, former champions Willow Nightingale and Thekla are instead slated to meet in a high-stakes title eliminator to determine who challenges Moné at AEW WrestleDream on Oct. 17. All Out also features an almost-assuredly bonkers three-way ladder match for the AEW World Tag Team Championship, as Christian Cage and Adam Copeland defend against FTR and The Young Bucks. Five additional title matches are set for the card as well. llm_long: A federal judge rejected a motion to dismiss a lawsuit against WWE and TKO, Vince McMahon, and Linda McMahon. The case involves seven plaintiffs who allege they were sexually abused as minors in the 1980s and 1990s while working as ring boys for WWE.

The plaintiffs claim abuse by former WWE ring announcer Mel Phillips. One plaintiff also alleges sexual abuse by former executive Pat Patterson, and another alleges sexual harassment by former Vice President of Operations Terry Garvin. All three accused individuals have since passed away.

The suit accuses the McMahons and WWE of negligence for allegedly allowing the abuse to occur and continue. The case was filed under the Maryland Child Victims Act, which removes time limits for lawsuits related to child sexual abuse.

WWE, TKO, and the McMahons argued that the Maryland law violates the 14th Amendment by being unfair or arbitrary, especially given the decades-old allegations and the deaths of the accused. The judge ruled that the defendants failed to demonstrate how the law is arbitrary or irrational in this case.
With the motion to dismiss denied, the lawsuit will proceed to the discovery phase. A teleconference is scheduled for November 17 to establish additional deadlines.

body: El Desperado is out of NJPW's Super Jr. Tag League after a diagnosis of spinal canal stenosis and a hernia. Young Lion Masatora Yasuda replaces him as Mistico's partner. El Desperado is out of NJPW’s Super Jr. Tag League, which begins Saturday, October 24, in Kumagaya, Saitama. NJPW announced that he has been diagnosed with spinal canal stenosis and a hernia. Young Lion Masatora Yasuda will replace him as Mistico’s partner, a choice Desperado made himself. In a video released on YouTube, Desperado said: “My left leg has no strength, and with the pain and pins and needles I’m currently unable to stand, walk or even sit upright for long periods of time.” He said he first noticed symptoms at the start of the year and that the pain began around June. He kept wrestling on painkillers. “I said I could still wrestle, but I was taking the issue far too lightly. My body had reached its limits,” he said. On choosing Yasuda, Desperado said: “I want to give Yasuda this opportunity to team alongside a global megastar like Mistico, and to see what he can make of this spot.” Desperado and Mistico had entered the A Block as a debut team.
