body: Link WWE Cain A. Knight is a hardcore number-cruncher who has analyzed and covered pro wrestling for Cageside Seats since 2014, and followed the sport as a fan going back to the 1980’s. In a new interview with Chris Van Vliet , WWE star Cody Rhodes was asked again about his timeline and plan for retiring from WWE. First, here is what the 41-year-old Rhodes said after being reminded that he once said he would retire at 40 years old. “Yeah I did [say that], didn’t I? Told you an old Cody lie, huh?” The American Nightmare talked about the final WWE contract that he recently signed, and guessed that he has six or seven years left in the ring. He certainly won’t be falling on the ground for a living by the time he reaches 50 years old. “I just signed my last contract. I say last contract - that’s gonna go for a while…my time with WWE could go, just to give you a real answer here and not politic around you, probably seven? Seven years? Six, seven? …I definitely don’t want to wrestle into my fifties. No shame to anyone who wrestles into their fifties. I don’t want to overstay my welcome.” Rhodes is grateful that he was able to play Guile in the Street Fighter movie, which is a video game series that he loved to play growing up. Cody talked about how you have to “stop taking” at some point, but it doesn’t like he plans to do that anytime soon. “I have shed so much of my skin for the industry. But I have also been given so, so, so much. I think there’s a point where you have to stop taking. I’m not there, but there’s a point. And I think that’s in that time frame. A point where you just have to stop taking. …I don’t know how many moments like this I can take, and I can get. Hopefully more. Hopefully a lot more. But I’ve been so lucky so far, and so blessed so far.” Rhodes briefly admitted that ‘Cody fatigue’ is a real thing in WWE, before quickly backtracking, and then landing somewhere in the middle. “I mean, Cody fatigue is already pretty set in…Well, no. body: By Jeremy Dick Published Oct 22, 2026, 9:58 PM EDT Jeremy has been a freelance writer and editor since 2014, having contributed to a variety of entertainment websites. It primarily focuses on the rise of boxing legend Muhammad Ali, but it will also feature an appearance from legendary pro wrestling pioneer Gorgeous George. Deadline reports that Chris Jericho plays Gorgeous George in The Greatest . He will first appear in the fourth episode of the eight-episode series, which is set to premiere on Nov. 4 . The real-life Gorgeous George is known for revolutionizing pro wrestling, much in the way Ali did for boxing. He became famous in the 1940s and 1950s, standing out with his flamboyant appearance and arrogant persona. The wrestler, whose real name was George Raymond Wagner, played himself in the 1949 film Alias the Champ . More recently, Adam Demos played Gorgeous George in the 2025 drama Queen of the Ring . In the world of pro wrestling, he inspired countless legends to follow in the decades after his run. That includes names like Ric Flair, Hulk Hogan, and "Superstar" Billy Graham. He is widely regarded as one of the greatest wrestlers of all time, and he was posthumously inducted into the WWE Hall of Fame in 2010. Jericho currently performs for All Elite Wrestling and hosts the popular podcast Talk Is Jericho . His acting work includes appearances in the Terrifier movies, in addition to other films like Dark Match , Jay and Silent Bob Reboot , and MacGruber . The wrestler recently appeared on the TV shows Tracker and Margo's Got oney Troubles. Along with pro wrestling and acting, Jericho also has a music career as the lead singer for the rock band Fozzy. The Greatest is the first authorized scripted series about Muhammad Ali's life, developed in collaboration with the late fighter's estate. Created by Ben Watkins ( Cross ), the series features Jaalen Best as Cassius Clay, also known as Muhammad Ali. The biopic series is a coming-of-age story that chronicles Ali's development as a boxer along with the personal struggles of his life amid his rise. Other stars of the show include Omari Hardwick ( Army of the Dead ), Dana Gourrier ( Django Unchained ), Amin Joseph ( Snowfall ), Michael Ealy ( Barbershop ), and Giovanni Ribisi ( Sneaky Pete ). title: Cedric Alexander Wins X-Division Number One Contender Match
raw_title: Cedric Alexander Becomes Number-One Contender For X-Division Title On TNA Impact
summary_src: After winning Thursday's four-way number one contenders match, Cedric Alexander will face Amazing Red for the X-Division Championship next week on "TNA Impact."
body: TNA Cedric Alexander is one step closer towards reclaiming his lost X-Division Championship after winning a four-way number one contender's match on Thursday's episode of "TNA Impact." He will have the opportunity to face TNA Hall of Famer Amazing Red for his title on next week's show. As most X-Division style matches tend to be, the beginning of it started off lightning fast, as Alexander rocked KC Navarro, Rich Swann, and Fabian Aichner before the commercial break. Coming back from the break, Alexander and Swann joined a temporary alliance with a Doomsday Device on Navarro. Aichner stormed in with a neat moonsault. On the ring apron, Alexander connected an STO on Swann. In a sequence, Navarro, then Aichner (crossbody), flew off the ropes and onto Swann and Alexander on the outside. However, The System's Brian Myers and Bear Bronson came in with a Roster Cut and Side Walk Slam on Aichner, respectively, opening the opportunity for Alexander to connect a moonsault on Aichner for the pinfall victory. Alexander first won the X-Division Championship against the former two-time champion, Leon Slater, in a two-out-of-three falls match on the May 14 edition of "Impact." He'd go on to carry the title for 101 days, dropping it back to Slater at Lockdown this past August. After getting inducted into this year's Hall of Fame at Bound for Glory, Red would go on to secure the title for the fourth time in his career later on in the show in a seven-way scramble match. Next Thursday will mark his first title defense.
summary: Cedric Alexander defeated KC Navarro, Rich Swann and Fabian Aichner in a four-way match on TNA Impact to become the number one contender for the X-Division Championship. He will challenge Amazing Red for the title on next week's episode. The fast-paced bout featured several high-flying spots before Alexander secured the pinfall on Aichner following interference from Brian Myers and Bear Bronson.

Fabian Aichner landed a moonsault during the bout. Alexander delivered an STO to Swann on the ring apron while Navarro and Aichner executed dives from the ropes onto Swann and Alexander on the floor.
Brian Myers and Bear Bronson interfered by hitting a Roster Cut and Sidewalk Slam on Aichner. This allowed Alexander to connect with a moonsault on Aichner to secure the pinfall victory.

title: Shotzi Blackheart Officially Joins TNA Knockouts
raw_title: Shotzi Blackheart Officially Debuts On TNA Impact
summary_src: On Thursday night's episode of "TNA Impact," Shotzi Blackheart made her first appearance as an official Knockout.
body: Earlier this week, TNA confirmed Shotzi Blackheart , a former WWE NXT Women's Tag Team Champion, as the newest member of its Knockouts division. Tonight on "TNA Impact," she then made her official first moves. Coming off their loss at Bound For Glory, the now-former Knockouts Tag Team Champions Allie and Kiera Hogan headed to the ring to address their futures in the company. Allie voiced her wish for a title rematch against Apex. Hogan, however, had no interest in doing so, declaring Allie as the "weakest link" of their team. Cue the arrival of Tasha Steelz, who charged down to attack Allie with Hogan's help. The pair laid in a series of stomps, a leg drop, and a splash, leaving Allie on the receiving end of a two-on-one Fire N' Flava reunion. That changed when Blackheart ran down herself to even the odds. Hogan and Steelz eventually retreated as Allie celebrated her newfound ally. "The Ballsy Badass" has previous experience in TNA, having wrestled for the promotion in 2018 and 2019. Thursday night's appearance marks her first as an official roster member, though. Interestingly, Blackheart's first two in-ring outings in TNA both involved Allie. The first pitted her and Tessa Blanchard against Allie and Hogan. The second saw Blackheart and Allie collide in singles competition. Blackheart departed from WWE in mid-2025 and subsequently signed with MLW, where she went on to the capture the company's women's division title. Due to taping delays, she still reigns as the MLW Women's Featherweight Champion on MLW programming.
summary: TNA confirmed Shotzi Blackheart as the newest member of its Knockouts division earlier this week. title: Shayna Baszler Recalls Ronda Rousey Fighting For WWE Women's Time
raw_title: Shayna Baszler reveals how Ronda Rousey fought for WWE women’s division backstage
summary_src: Shayna Baszler recently dismissed the rumors that Ronda Rousey did not care about wrestling and instead revealed how she fought for the women’s division in WWE.
body: Shayna Baszler recently dismissed the rumors that Ronda Rousey did not care about wrestling and instead revealed how she fought for the women’s division in WWE. In a recent interview with Denice Salcedo, Baszler opened up about how Rousey helped the women’s division flourish in WWE and fought for it. “I’ve heard people be like, ‘Ronda didn’t really care about wrestling.’ She might hate me for telling this story, but there was a time where Ronda had a pay-per-view match and got six minutes cut off of her match because a match before had gone over their time. “And to take six minutes from a match is huge. To take one minute from a match, in order to build a story and get emotion involved, it takes time. “ When that happened, she bought her own ticket and flew herself to headquarters to have a meeting with creative at that time to be like, ‘Guys, this keeps happening. The women keep losing time. I need to know right now, is this going to change? Because if it’s not, I don’t need to be here. I don’t need to be here to make money. I don’t need to be here to get famous ,” Baszler recalled. “ I’m here to help advance this. And if you’re telling me right now that’s never going to happen, then I’m done. I only want to improve this.’ “ She’s not going to tell you that story. She’s not going to tweet about it. She’s not going to go on a thing and talk about it. Nobody’s going to know about the stuff she did like that behind the scenes on her own dime just to argue for the women’s locker room. I don’t even think girls in the locker room knew she did that.” She further revealed how she had a conversation with Rousey about this, and how Rousey had found a hack about making sure their meeting doesn’t get canceled. “I remember her telling me that and I’m like, ‘Why did you buy your own ticket? They would have flown you there to have a meeting.’ “And she’s like, ‘No, because if I buy my own ticket, they can’t cancel the meeting on me because I bought my ticket. So I’m going to make sure.’ It was just the little stuff like that that she thought about. You knew she was serious.” While Shayna Baszler is now a part of TNA Wrestling , Rousey last appeared in AEW before fighting her career’s retirement MMA match against Gina Carano. Baszler shared an incident in which Rousey had six minutes removed from her pay-per-view match after the previous bout ran long. Rousey responded by purchasing her own plane ticket and traveling to headquarters to meet with creative.

During the meeting, Rousey questioned whether the women's matches would continue to lose time. She emphasized that she was participating to help progress women's wrestling rather than for money or fame.

Rousey indicated that if the situation would not change, she would leave the company. Baszler noted that Rousey has not publicly discussed the event or similar actions taken on behalf of the women's locker room.
Baszler added that many in the locker room were likely unaware of these behind-the-scenes efforts by Rousey.

body: Current AEW star Chris Jericho will be appearing on the small screen in an acting role once again, playing a role he is familiar with and of someone many wrestling fans are familiar with as well. Announced by Deadline on Thursday , Jericho will play the legendary Gorgeous George in the upcoming Prime Video series chronicling the life of boxer and mainstream icon Muhammad Ali. The full eight episode series comes out on Wednesday, November 4 with Jericho’s appearance coming in episode four. The two men met in 1961 with Ali taking inspiration from the wrestling star on how to rile up crowds and a style of reciting poems and phrases that caught on in pop culture. “The Greatest features defining moments in Ali’s life and career, both in and out of the ring, that have been well documented, and moments that took place outside the spotlight. The world remembers an icon, but The Greatest is about a man, a husband, a father, a brother and a son.” Jericho has made several appearances on TV outside the wrestling ring this year as he appeared in CBS’ Tracker and Apple TV’s Margo’s Got Money Troubles. He will also make an appearance in the second season of Dexter: Resurrection this fall. title: Jason Hotch Retains TNA International Title
raw_title: Jason Hotch Earns Decisive Win Over Mustafa Ali On TNA Impact
summary_src: Jason Hotch beat Mustafa Ali to retain the International Championship in the main event of "TNA Impact."
body: TNA Jason Hotch defeated Mustafa Ali in a Two Out of Three Falls match to retain the International Championship in the main event of "TNA Impact." Ali went on to score the first fall with a roll-up. He sought to press that advantage but Hotch came back at him to send him to the outside once more, following up with a tope. He brought Ali back into the ring and went to the top rope for a double stomp, but Ali rolled out of the ring again. Hotch gave chase and delivered a moonsault to take him out on the floor, smashing his face against the apron repeatedly. Ali crawled toward the International title belt, followed again by Hotch to prompt the challenger to turn around and strike him with the belt. That caused a disqualification to provide Hotch the equalizing fall. Ali brought Hotch back into the ring and went for the cover for the win, but Hotch kicked out. Ali tried twice more to no avail and began to argue the count with the referee. Hotch ran back at Ali but got sent into the referee instead, allowing Ali to deliver a low-blow before ripping off Hotch's belt and beating him with it. Hotch still managed to fight back into the contest, beating Ali back with the belt before returning to the ring and eventually hitting a GTH for the winning pinfall. Hotch emerged victorious in the Order Four four-way for the title at Bound For Glory, pinning Ali to begin his second reign as International Champion. He had previously held the title after dethroning Ali in June, only to lose it back to him at Lockdown in August. They held two wins apiece in singles action between TNA and Warrior Wrestling prior to Thursday's Two Out of Three Falls match.
summary: Jason Hotch defeated Mustafa Ali in a two-out-of-three-falls match on TNA Impact to keep the International Championship. Ali scored the first fall by roll-up before Hotch evened it via disqualification after Ali used the title belt as a weapon. The bout ended in chaos with Ali delivering a low blow and striking Hotch with his own belt.

title: WWE NXT Ratings Drop Against NBA Opener
raw_title: WWE NXT ratings take hit against NBA opening night
summary_src: The return of the NBA made WWE NXT take a ratings hit this week. This past Tuesday’s show averaged 655,000 viewers on The CW, down 10.5% from the previous week’s 732,000 and their third-lowest audience since August 25.
body: The return of the NBA made WWE NXT take a ratings hit this week. This past Tuesday’s show averaged 655,000 viewers on The CW, down 10.5% from the previous week’s 732,000 and their third-lowest audience since August 25. The episode also averaged a 0.10 rating in the 18-49 demo, down 28.6% from last week. The show went head-to-head with the opening night of the NBA regular season as well as NHL games on various cable networks and streaming services. Featured matches included Cruz Montana vs. Dion Lennox, Dusty Rhodes Tag Team Classic matches, and a show-opening confrontation between Tony D’Angelo and NXT Champion Grayson Waller. As compared to the same week in 2025, overall viewership was up 24.8% with similar competition while the 18-49 rating was up 42.9%. It’s the second straight week the show has been up year-over-year in both categories. Listed below are the last 11 weeks of overall viewership and 18-49 demo ratings for WWE NXT on The CW as well as the 10-week average in both categories. This week’s show was down 1.3% in overall viewers and 16.7% in 18-49 as compared to recent averages. title: Earlier Start Time Set For Final WWE Raw Before Crown Jewel
raw_title: Earlier Start Time Set For Final WWE Raw Before Crown Jewel
body: The first WWE Raw episode of November will take place a little earlier than usual as the company makes plans for Crown Jewel. WrestleVotes Radio On Fightful Select reports that the November 2nd episode of WWE Raw is currently set to air live starting at 6 PM ET/3 PM PT instead of the usual 8 PM ET/5 PM PT. According to the report, the plan is to air Raw live at the earlier time from the Barclays Center in Brooklyn so that they can tape WWE Smackdown on the same night. The episodes will be the final shows before Crown Jewel, and the company is filming the shows on the adjusted schedule to accomodate travel to Saudi Arabia for WWE Crown Jewel. As noted , that week’s WWE TV schedule also has another change in place as WWE NXT will take place on Wednesday, November 4th instead of Tuesday, November 3rd so that it doesn’t go up against election night coverage. That means that NXT will be going head-to-head against the Blood & Guts episode of AEW Dynamite. WWE Crown Jewel is set to take place on November 7th and, as has been noted, is still scheduled to take place in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia despite the US State Department currently at a level three warning about travel to the region.

summary_src: Tonight's "TNA Impact" saw Avery Styles wrestle his first singles match for the promotion, along with the debut of Shotzi Blackheart, and more.
body: TNA Wrestling Tonight's "TNA Impact" brought us a surprise title rematch, an expected title rematch, and Avery Styles' first one-on-one match. Was the show a success? That depends on who you ask, but as always, you can count on Wrestling Inc. to deliver your weekly dose of the good and the bad. If I were Cedric Alexander, I would have invoked my contractual rematch for the TNA X-Division Championship tonight, or even next week. Instead, the ex-titleholder jumped through two matches in which the numbers put him at a great disadvantage. Alexander received his contractual rematch at Bound For Glory, where he and six others competed in a chaotic scramble for the X-Division Title. Unlike Scott Steiner, I know that meant Alexander's odds of winning back the championship were one in seven, or 14%. Had he waited until after BFG (in storyline), however, he could have elevated that number to 50% through a one-on-one against Amazing Red. Alas, that didn't happen, as the seven-way scramble ultimately panned out in Red's favor, making him the new X-Division Champion. On this week's "Impact," Alexander sought to secure another rematch by wrestling in a four-way number one contender's match, which meant his odds increased to 25%. Still not great, though, and like BFG, he didn't have to be pinned or submitted to lose. The System member won in this case to earn himself a one-on-one title shot against Red next week. It should be a solid in-ring performance, too. I can't say that Alexander, a heel, took the most practical or realistic approach to get there, though. TNA Wrestling Shayna Baszler has been a longtime favorite wrestler of mine, and I would be lying if I said I hadn't gotten used to seeing her not being utilized in WWE during her time in the company. With that in mind, it's a really nice change of pace to see TNA using her to her fullest potential by sending her right to the top of the Knockouts Division. I know that Hartwell has just begun her reign as Knockouts World Champion, but she's already had enough singles and tag team matches with Brookside and her feud with Daria Rae is already growing old for me. The Knockouts World Championship picture has largely also been featuring the same players week after week, so it's a nice change of pace to have some fresh blood be infused into it to bring it back to life a little bit. If anyone in the Knockouts Division were to be a double champion (whether it actually comes to fruition or is just an idea to plant into minds of the TNA fans), Baszler would be the perfect pick. Her style makes her feel like a threat to anyone on the TNA roster. Whenever TNA decides to hold the match, Baszler and Hartwell should put on a banger of a match with one another and it will be something that I'm looking forward to seeing. title: TNA Adds Three Specialty Matches to Destination X
raw_title: TNA adds three specialty matches to Destination X
body: Link TNA Manolo Has Pizzazz learned all of life’s lessons from decades of professional wrestling. Manolo has been covering the sport for over ten years on Cageside Seats. TNA is stacking the Destination X PPV by bringing back a variety of specialty gimmick matches. Santino Marella broke the news. Destination X is about taking risks. Ultimate X is one of the riskiest matches in TNA, and there will be two of them on PPV. The women will compete to determine the #1 contender for the Knockouts Championship, and the men will compete to determine the #1 contender for the X-Division Championship. In addition, the World X-Cup returns. There will be two four-way matches with wrestlers from around the world. The winners advance to the final on that same night. TNA generally runs a few Ultimate X matches for the men each year. Cedric Alexander won Ultimate X earlier this year. Ultimate X for the women is more rare. Tasha Steelz won the first women’s Ultimate X in 2022. Gisele Shaw won the second in 2024. This round marks the third time. The last World X-Cup was in 2021. Past formats have varied between tournaments and team competitions. Tournament winners include Chris Sabin, Samoa Joe, Dezmond Xavier, and Ace Austin. title: Sol Ruca Learned to Stand Up For Herself From Becky Lynch
raw_title: Sol Ruca says Becky Lynch taught her to stand up for herself in WWE
summary_src: Sol Ruca recently claimed that WWE veteran Becky Lynch taught her to stand up for herself. During a recent interview with KRON 4, Sol Ruca opened up about what she learned from working with Becky Lynch during their WWE Women’s Intercontinental title feud.
body: Sol Ruca recently claimed that WWE veteran Becky Lynch taught her to stand up for herself. During a recent interview with KRON 4 , Sol Ruca opened up about what she learned from working with Becky Lynch during their WWE Women’s Intercontinental title feud. “ She is one of the greatest of all time for a reason. She is so, so good at what she does. She’s so good at the character work ,” Sol Ruca shared. “ I think I’ve learned a lot from her, especially in the character aspect of it. Seeing how her brain works, seeing how she’s able to take these promos and these segments and really make it her own and really know what people are going to bite on, know what the fans are going to enjoy, and being able to turn nothing into something.” The former WWE Women’s IC Champion also shared that Lynch is really good at questioning WWE’s creative and has taught her to take a stand for herself. “I think she’s really, really good at that. I think she’s really good at questioning creative and really just trying to make everything the best that it can be. “ So I definitely learned to be able to stick up for myself a little bit when I disagree with certain things. I think she’s really good at doing that in a respectful way and being able to perform at the best of her ability and just giving the fans what they wan t,” she finished. Lynch was recently involved in the Women’s World title match at WWE Money in the Bank 2026, while Ruca performed in the Women’s Money in the Bank ladder match in the same PLE. llm_long: Shotzi Blackheart appeared on both MLW Fusion and TNA Impact during the same night on October 22. She first showed up on MLW Fusion where she is involved in a storyline with a Stardom invasion group called H.A.T.E.
In the MLW segment, Shotzi faced off against members of H.A.T.E. including Rina and Lady Frost. Scarlett Bordeaux came to her aid before Zamaya made a surprise run-in to even the odds as her ally.

Later that night on TNA Impact, Shotzi made another surprise appearance. She intervened to rescue Allie after Kiera Hogan turned heel by abandoning her tag partner and reuniting with Tasha Steelz as the team Fire 'n Flava.
Both the MLW Fusion and TNA Impact episodes that aired were taped in advance. Shotzi holds the MLW women's championship in the promotion's television timeline.

title: Billy Gunn Reveals Reason AEW Paired Him With Acclaimed
raw_title: Billy Gunn explains why AEW paired him with The Acclaimed
summary_src: Despite having his sons in AEW, Billy Gunn was paired with The Acclaimed in the promotion. Speaking with Inside The Ropes during his latest UK tour, Gunn was asked about his partnership with Max Caster and Anthony Bowens of The Acclaimed.
body: Despite having his sons in AEW , Billy Gunn was paired with The Acclaimed in the promotion. Speaking with Inside The Ropes during his latest UK tour, Gunn was asked about his partnership with Max Caster and Anthony Bowens of The Acclaimed. Talking about their pairing despite having his own two sons in the promotion, Gunn said, “ They wanted me to kind of just go with The Acclaimed because they were getting [there]. They just needed, like, I still have equity in this business. “ So with me with them, it kind of makes people take notice a little bit. When you put me with them, you have a tendency to watch now instead of just going, ‘Hey, these are just two more wrestlers ,'” Gunn added. He claimed that his presence with them made people look out for The Acclaimed and realize that they were good. Gunn finished by claiming that Acclaimed was not just him, but it was the three of them. “ Because The Acclaimed wasn’t just me. It was all three of us. Everything just kind of fell into place to where we had Max doing the rap and then Anthony would do the hometown, and then he would do the ‘Scissor Me Daddy Ass’ and the place would go nuts.” While Gunn and Bowens are still with AEW, Caster recently parted ways with Khan’s promotion and joined TNA Wrestling. However, things soon took a different turn following his Saudi Arabia rap verses at his TNA Bound for Glory debut. llm_long: Billy Gunn has been part of All Elite Wrestling since 2020. He insisted that his sons Austin and Colten complete their college education before pursuing careers in the promotion.
Gunn stated that he refused to help get his sons hired by AEW until they graduated. He emphasized that his own success in wrestling did not guarantee they would succeed in the same field.

On the day Austin Gunn graduated, he handed his diploma to his father and immediately asked when they could start in wrestling. Gunn had required college graduation as the first condition before any discussion of entering the business.
Colten Gunn also decided to pursue wrestling after having a different career path mapped out until age 60. The choice surprised both Gunn and his wife, given the demanding nature of the profession.

Gunn explained that his frequent absences from home, including 300 days on the road each year early in his career, made him hesitant for his sons to follow the same path. He wanted them to have more stable family lives than he experienced.
Although Gunn trained his sons to a certain point, he required them to seek and complete AEW tryouts on their own. He did not ask for them to be hired simply because they were his children.

title: Shayna Baszler Discusses WWE Coaching After TNA Move
raw_title: Shayna Baszler addresses WWE coaching future following TNA signing
summary_src: A wrestling and MMA veteran, Shayna Baszler recently joined forces with Zoey Serrano in TNA Wrestling. After parting with WWE in 2025, she became more involved with the promotion in a non-wrestling role and was more focused on coaching the young talent.
body: A wrestling and MMA veteran, Shayna Baszler recently joined forces with Zoey Serrano in TNA Wrestling. After parting with WWE in 2025, she became more involved with the promotion in a non-wrestling role and was more focused on coaching the young talent. Recently, speaking with Denice Salcedo , Baszler opened up about her WWE coaching career following her recent TNA signing. “ There’s been some thought because word got out somehow. I’ve been coaching, producing part-time at NXT and Evolve and all that. “That is something that I found that I have fallen in love with, watching these young athletes grow and learn to love pro wrestling ,” she added. Baszler further added that TNA’s her favorite place right now and she still has the liberty to go coach in WWE. “ TNA is the perfect place for me right now. Thankfully, there’s a good relationship so I can still coach when I’m available. I’m obviously not as available as I was, but that door I guess is still there. “ I can coach when I need a cane and have to sit in a chair. Beating people up right now is what I’m able to do right now, and let’s just ride it till the wheels fall off, ” she said. “ Nobody’s told me no ,” Baszler answered when asked if she could coach if she had the time. “To be fair, I did ask people that mattered, ‘Hey, I’m thinking about helping Zoey out. Are there any issues with that? Nobody told me not to do it and that I wouldn’t be welcomed back ,” she added. “ Now again, there’s maybe some discussion to be had about my availability and all that, and we might have to revisit some of that at some point. I’m not someone that’s going to burn bridges either. I’m very thankful to WWE and everything they did for me and the platform they gave me ,” Baszler finished. title: Results Recap: Hall’s WWE Raw Review 7.14.97
raw_title: Hall’s WWE Raw Review 7.14.97
body: Monday Night Raw Date: July 14, 1997 Location: Freeman Coliseum, San Antonio, Texas Attendance: 7,731 Commentators: Vince McMahon, Jim Ross It’s title time as we need some new Tag Team Champions. Steve Austin and Shawn Michaels had held the titles but Michaels was suspended for a backstage fight with Bret Hart. While you get your head around Michaels and Hart not getting along, consider that Austin has to team with someone he picks to face Owen Hart/British Bulldog, who won a tournament. We’re also on the road to Summerslam and Hart is going to need something to do. Let’s get to it. We open with a recap of Canadian Stampede and Bret Hart being a national hero in Canada, but we’re not in Canada tonight are we? Here is the Hart Foundation to get things going. Bret Hart immediately blasts San Antonio (I’m surprised it took that long) and gets to the point: he has a contract that says he gets a WWF Title shot at Summerslam but if he loses, he can never wrestle on American soil again. Bret promises to kill the Undertaker like a dead star and win the title for the fifth time. Owen Hart isn’t worried about facing Steve Austin at Summerslam because Austin is already losing the Tag Team Titles tonight. Then at Summerslam, Austin will have to give Owen a kiss on his…uh, certain area. British Bulldog is ready to beat Ken Shamrock at Summerslam and if he doesn’t, he’ll eat dog food (along with losing the European Title). That leaves us with Brian Pillman, who loves all of the abuse that Dusty Rhodes has given Dustin over the years. At Summerslam, he’ll finish Dustin’s heart for good and if he loses, he’ll wear a dress on Raw. Oh and Jim Neidhart, who doesn’t have a match at Summerslam, will shave his goatee if any of the team loses at Summerslam. If Jim Cornette didn’t come up with most of those ideas, I’ll eat my hat. Do I have a hat? Anyway, this brings out Steve Austin, who is joined by Shamrock, the Patriot, Sid and Shawn Michaels, with the question being which one Austin will pick as his partner tonight. This was basically “here’s most of the Summerslam card” in one segment. The Headbangers are on a golf course, which is some clue for a contest. This is fallout from Lawler attacking Scott a few weeks back and Papa Paduzki wanting revenge. Before the match, Ivan sings as the fans probably have absolutely no idea who he is. Lawler and Christopher jump them to start and send the good guys out to the floor. This lets commentary wonder if Lawler and Christopher are related as Scott is back with a tilt-a-whirl backbreaker to Christopher. Lawler dropkicks Christopher by mistake but Scott gets taken into the wrong corner again. That means a jumping right hand and northern lights suplex have Scott in more trouble. Lawler seems to have Scott done but Christopher asks to finish instead. The Tennessee Jam misses though and Christopher superkicks Lawler by mistake. Ivan comes back in for his wild flailing and the Polish Hammer (ax handle to the chest) finishes Lawle

title: End of an Era: ‘It’s my birthright’- Dominik Mysterio Opens Up On who he wants to retire Rey Mysterio
raw_title: ‘It’s my birthright’- Dominik Mysterio reveals who he wants to retire Rey Mysterio
body: The former Intercontinental Champion also has a specific venue in mind for the potential retirement match, hoping to bring the family rivalry to a historic arena in Mexico. His comments come amid reports that Rey could retire from in-ring competition in 2027, although WWE has not confirmed his plans. Speaking on The Ariel Helwani Show , Dominik explained that he has long wanted his father to step away from wrestling and believes he should be the one to make it happen. He said: “I’ve been talking about it. I’ve been wanting him to retire. I want him out of here, you know? There’s only room for so many Mysterios in WWE. There’s one pushing 60, and I think it’s time for him to kick rocks; that’s just how I see it.” Dominik was even more direct when discussing the prospect of being involved in Rey’s final match. “It’s my birthright. I would lose my absolute s*** if it’s not me,” he said. “I’ve got to take his mask, and I’ve got to take his name.” The 28-year-old also revealed where he would like the match to take place, pointing towards the Auditorio Fausto Gutierrez Moreno in Tijuana, Mexico. “I believe my dad has wrestled there, debuted there. My great-uncle and most of my godfathers wrestled there [too],” Dominik explained. The venue would carry personal significance for the Mysterio family, making it a fitting choice for a potential final chapter in their long-running rivalry. Rey, who began his wrestling career in 1989, remains one of the most respected figures in the sport. He helped popularise lucha libre in the United States during his time in WCW before joining WWE in 2002. The former WWE Champion was inducted into the WWE Hall of Fame in 2023 and was named general manager of AAA in May. Reports have suggested that Rey could retire from active competition in 2027, with the expectation that he would continue working in an executive capacity and help develop younger talent. However, no official retirement date or venue has been announced, leaving Dominik’s dream match dependent on what Rey decides to do next. × Sign in to TalkingPoints Comment, react and follow the stories you care about. body: Chelsea Green already has Liv Morgan waiting for her at Crown Jewel. First, she has to make sure she actually gets there as champion. Green puts the WWE Women’s Championship on the line against Roxanne Perez tonight, and Perez already has proof that she can beat her. Two weeks ago on Raw, Perez defeated Green in a non-title match after interference from Morgan and Raquel Rodriguez. That victory was enough to put Perez in position for the championship match she felt she deserved. Now the stakes are much bigger. Green is supposed to face Women’s World Champion Liv Morgan in the Champion vs. Champion match at Crown Jewel. If Perez takes the WWE Women’s Championship tonight, that entire situation changes just two weeks before the show. The Judgment Day could become important too. Perez won’t necessarily be walking into this alone, and Green has a lot more than one challenger to worry about. A normal match clearly wasn’t enough for Giulia and Blake Monroe. Now there are no normal match rules keeping them under control. Giulia and Monroe meet again tonight in a Street Fight , which feels a lot more appropriate considering how many times their rivalry has already turned into a fight. Alexa Bliss and Tatum Paxley haven’t had much time to enjoy becoming champions. The new WWE Women’s Tag Team Champions make their first defense tonight against Michin and B-Fab. Bliss and Paxley are still a relatively new team, so holding the championships is one thing. Figuring out how to keep them when other teams start coming after them is another. title: On the Record: Nikki Bella Opens Up On Where She Stands on Getting Married Again
raw_title: Nikki Bella Reveals Where She Stands on Getting Married Again
summary_src: Nikki Bella may be single, but getting married apparently isn’t anywhere near the top of her current wish list. The WWE Hall of Famer revealed that finding a husband isn’t even on her vision board right now, although she’s definitely not opposed to having a man — and some good sex — in her life. ...
body: During the October 23 episode of The Nikki & Brie Show , Nikki and Brie Bella spoke with Amanda Hirsch about manifestation and the vision boards they create to represent their goals. The sisters explained that they enjoy getting together with wine, buying magazines and cutting out pictures of things they want to accomplish. When Hirsch asked about the size of their boards, Brie joked that Nikki’s was massive. Nikki explained that she simply has a lot of dreams before pointing out that marriage isn’t currently one of the things she’s trying to manifest. “I got a lot of dreams. She has, I think, yeah, more. Maybe it’s because she has, as far as, like, husband and life. But even though that’s not on my vision board right now…” That doesn’t mean Nikki has completely crossed romance off the board. Later in the conversation, she reconsidered whether there might be room for at least one particular addition. Brie didn’t need much convincing and immediately told her sister exactly what she thought was missing: “Girl, you need a man.” Brie immediately agreed and had a few more suggestions for what her sister should add. “Girl, you need a man. And, like, good sex, and have, like, a good-looking guy and, like, half-naked.” The comments come shortly after Nikki made it clear that being single doesn’t mean she’s desperate to find somebody. During another recent episode of The Nikki & Brie Show, Brie announced that her sister was single and asked their guests whether they had any available friends. Nikki immediately pumped the brakes on Brie trying to shop around for her next boyfriend : “Okay, I’m not, like, for sale.” So while Nikki might be willing to add a good-looking man to that vision board, a wedding apparently isn’t part of the picture right now. She’s got plenty of dreams she’s looking to manifest, and finding another husband isn’t currently one of them. He focuses on delivering reliable coverage across WWE, AEW, and major wrestling promotions.

title: Ari Emanuel Speaks On Possibility of Relocating WWE Crown Jewel Amid Security Concerns
raw_title: Ari Emanuel Addresses Possibility of Relocating WWE Crown Jewel Amid Security Concerns
summary_src: WWE Crown Jewel is still on for Saudi Arabia, at least for now. TKO executive chair and CEO Ari Emanuel says the November 7 show remains set for Riyadh, but the company is monitoring the situation every day and is already looking at where the event could be moved if things get worse. During an ...
body: During an appearance on Fox News , Bret Baier asked Emanuel directly whether Crown Jewel would still happen amid the escalating security situation in Saudi Arabia. Emanuel said nothing has been canceled at this point. “Right now, everything’s still set. This weekend coming up in Abu Dhabi, we have a UFC fight. We have in the middle of November a Frieze art show. So far, so good. Nothing’s been canceled.” That doesn’t mean TKO is simply crossing its fingers and hoping everything works out. When Baier asked whether Emanuel was receiving government briefings and if there was a point where TKO could pull the show, Emanuel revealed that the company has an entire team working on the situation. “Yeah, we have a whole team kind of working on this, and kind of when—and if that doesn’t happen, where we can move it. It’s a daily monitoring.” That last part is especially interesting because it’s the first clear indication that TKO is looking at backup options for Crown Jewel. Emanuel didn’t reveal any potential alternate locations, and he didn’t say that WWE has decided to move the event, only that the company is considering where it could go if Riyadh becomes unworkable. The update comes as travel into Saudi Arabia has become a much bigger concern. The U.S. Embassy in Riyadh issued a security alert on October 22 warning Americans to use “extreme caution” at Saudi airports amid attacks by the Iran-backed Houthis. King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh also remains shut down, according to the latest Embassy alert. Airports in Jeddah and Dammam are still operating, although both have been dealing with delays and cancellations. “Operations at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh remain suspended. King Abdulaziz International Airport in Jeddah and King Fahd International Airport in Dammam are operational with some delays and cancellations.” The Embassy has also warned about the possibility of additional attacks on airports, airspace closures and sudden flight cancellations. U.S. government employees working in Saudi Arabia currently need special authorization to use any airport in the country. Despite all of that, WWE hasn’t pulled the plug on Crown Jewel. Emanuel’s comments make it clear that Riyadh remains Plan A for November 7, but TKO isn’t going into the next two weeks without a Plan B either. For now, Crown Jewel is staying exactly where WWE planned it, but that could change quickly depending on what happens in Saudi Arabia. With TKO checking the situation daily and already looking at possible alternatives, the company appears to be preparing for the possibility that a last-minute move could become necessary. Steve Carrier Steve Carrier is the founder of Ringside News and has been reporting on pro wrestling since 1997. His stories have been featured on TMZ, Forbes, Bleacher Report, and more.
summary: Bret Baier asked Emanuel directly whether Crown Jewel would still happen amid the escalating security situation in Saudi Arabia. Nothing has been canceled at this point. Right now, everything’s still set, Emanuel explained.

title: On the Record: Leon Slater Discusses winning the TNA World Championship, roots in Yorkshire and his thoughts on Destination X
raw_title: Leon Slater talks winning the TNA World Championship, roots in Yorkshire and his thoughts on Destination X
body: Home » Leon Slater talks winning the TNA World Championship, roots in Yorkshire and his thoughts on Destination X The newly crowned TNA World Champion is ready to show a different side of himself in the ring. But as Leon Slater sees it, carrying the title also means carrying the hopes of the people and places that helped him get here. For Leon Slater, the moment the referee’s hand hit the mat for three (against the legendary Nic Nemeth) was almost too big to take in. “I remember hitting the Swanton 450, hearing 1, 2, 3, and just sitting back, like kneeling and just going, ‘Oh my God! Like I can’t believe like what’s just happened,’” he recalled in conversation with Soundsphere’s Dom Smith. “It was relief, it was joy, it was euphoria, it was all of these feelings you could possibly imagine wrapped into one.” At 22, Slater had become TNA’s youngest World Champion. The achievement still feels unreal. He hasn’t even watched the match back: he wants to hold on to the memory as it felt in the moment, rather than let the footage become the version he remembers. “When you watch the footage back, the memory almost becomes like a third-person memory,” he explained. “So, I want to keep this as a first-person memory for as long as possible.” That instinct says something about Slater’s approach. He knows the importance of the milestone, but he doesn’t want the story of winning the title to replace the feeling of having lived it. The win is a new chapter, not a finish line, and the person who once had to believe in his own potential now has to defend his place at the top. Slater has never been short on belief. But for him, confidence has to be earned again and again in the ring. “The last thing that I want to become is someone that is just talk and is no action,” he said. He knows his self-assurance can invite questions: is he confident, or is he cocky? His answer is simple: the work has to back up the words. “I think it’s impossible to call it arrogance when I’m backing it up in the ring on the mic, and as I’ve got this on my shoulder.” There is another kind of pressure attached to the championship. Slater has been supported by family, mentors, peers and fans, and he remembers the people in the business who publicly backed him before he had the world title, and is glad to prove them right. He specifically points to Matt and Jeff Hardy as people who “stuck their neck out” for him. “I can’t let those sacrifices go to waste,” he said. “I don’t want to make those people that have believed in me look stupid.” Rather than shrink from the weight of that responsibility, Slater welcomes it. “Pressure is an absolute privilege,” he said. “I’m glad to be in this position. I welcome the pressure.” That attitude is already shaping how he thinks about his future in TNA. Until now, Slater says, he has usually been the one chasing upward: the underdog, the wrestler climbing the hill. The world title changes the picture. title: Wren Sinclair Praises Total Divas Impact
raw_title: Wren Sinclair explains why WWE Total Divas was important for women’s wrestling
summary_src: Emerged as a revolutionary step in women’s wrestling sports entertainment, WWE’s Wren Sinclair feels that the show was empowering. Speaking on No-Contest Wrestling, Sinclair shared her thoughts on WWE Total Divas and why the show was important for women’s wrestling. “I love Total Divas.
body: Emerged as a revolutionary step in women’s wrestling sports entertainment, WWE’s Wren Sinclair feels that the show was empowering. Speaking on No-Contest Wrestling , Sinclair shared her thoughts on WWE Total Divas and why the show was important for women’s wrestling. “ I love Total Divas. I loved reality TV growing up. I don’t know why. Maybe that’s why I’m kind of confrontational nowadays. I used to watch Total Divas, obviously Keeping Up with the Kardashians, The Bad Girls Club. Avid watcher of that, ” Sinclair said. When further asked what the show meant to her, Sinclair added that it helped highlight the women wrestlers when the television shows did not. “ I feel like it highlighted the women sometimes when the television didn’t. It allowed you to get a grasp of what they actually go through. I know a lot of times in the show, their segments got cut, their promos got cut, etc. So you never really got to learn who they were ,” she said. “ And I feel like that show, it felt like I was in Natty’s house sometimes playing with her cats. It felt like you got to know them. I feel like I know some of them and I haven’t even met them. “ But I feel like it really showed people that they’re people and they’re legitimate professional wrestlers. They’re in this too, even though they don’t have the ball all the time. So I feel like it was empowering.” The first season of WWE Total Divas aired in 2013, and the show ran till 2019. The series gave viewers an insider look into the professional and personal lives of the women WWE wrestlers, including some behind-the-scenes footage. title: Backstage Buzz: Triple H’s Plans for Bobby Roode’s WWE Backstage Future Revealed
raw_title: Triple H’s Plans for Bobby Roode’s WWE Backstage Future Revealed
summary_src: Bobby Roode hasn’t wrestled in years, but WWE apparently has some pretty big plans for him behind the scenes.
body: Speaking with Stephanie McMahon on the October 22 episode of What’s Your Story? , Hayes discussed how his own role in WWE has evolved over the years. That’s when he recalled Triple H approaching him with a pretty blunt reminder about the future. “But yeah, I just made up my mind that this is your new path, and go for it. And I’ll tell you, Trips came up to me one day and he goes, ‘So Michael, you know you’re not gonna be around forever.’” Hayes couldn’t resist having some fun with Triple H’s choice of words: “What does that mean, life or work?” Triple H then explained exactly what he meant. Hayes said Triple H compared his current position to the role the legendary Pat Patterson once held and made it clear that he wanted Roode prepared to eventually follow in Hayes’ footsteps. “You’re our Pat Patterson. I need you to make Bobby Roode Michael.” That apparently got Hayes thinking about the reality that somebody will eventually have to take over responsibilities he’s handled behind the scenes. Judging by his assessment, Roode has already made some serious progress. “And I said, ‘Okay, that’s a really good point, because I’m not gonna be here forever.’ And boy, has he come along.” Stephanie agreed that Roode has a bright future in the role, and Hayes went even further with his praise. He believes Roode can become great at the job, although there’s still one part of working behind the scenes that he wants him to master. “No, I see great things for him. He’s just gotta get out of the stuff where—I don’t know how to really categorize it. This stuff happens in this industry that’s just out of your control, and it’s just gonna happen. And you just gotta kind of let it go and say, ‘Okay.’” Stephanie understood exactly what Hayes meant. She explained that there’s no point burning energy complaining about something that’s going to happen anyway when that energy could be spent figuring out how to make it work. “Yeah, so much energy about bitching about doing it, because you’re going to do it. It’s happening anyways. So save the energy to do it and find a way to do it.” That brought Hayes back to a lesson Vince McMahon once gave him. Instead of explaining why an idea wouldn’t work, Hayes learned that his job was to figure out how to make it work. “I still have problems sometimes. You actually told that story too. You said, ‘Find a way to make it work. Don’t tell me how it doesn’t work.’ That’s what Vince—‘Tell me how you can make it work.’ He said, ‘Michael, I have many people out on the street telling me why it don’t work. I need somebody to tell me how it will work.’” The comments give a lot more context to where Roode stands in WWE these days. His profile was quietly moved into the alumni section of WWE.com in September, but there was never any indication that he’d actually left the company , as he’s continued working as a producer after stepping away from the ring. title: Michael Hayes Confronted Chelsea Green Over Her WWE Character
raw_title: Michael Hayes Confronted Chelsea Green Over Her WWE Character
summary_src: Michael Hayes has found himself in plenty of Chelsea Green drama lately, but apparently he’s also responsible for giving her some pretty important advice. The WWE Hall of Famer revealed that he once pulled Green up over something that was missing from one of her matches — Chelsea Green herself.
body: Speaking with Stephanie McMahon on What’s Your Story? , Hayes explained that one thing he constantly pushes with younger wrestlers is making sure their personalities don’t disappear once the bell rings. Putting together a technically good match is fine, but Hayes wants to actually see the character too. “But, you know, I think pretty much they just told you who went over and, you know, not the details. Right? And are you bringing your character into a match? You know, that’s a theme I go with a lot with kids today. Like, I’ll hear how they’ll run the match. That’s a good match. Where’s your character?” That’s when Hayes brought up Green, and even he seemed to realize that mentioning her name might be dangerous territory these days. “You know, like I did that with Chelsea one time. I always get in trouble when I talk about—” Stephanie immediately knew where this was going. Considering everything that’s happened between Hayes and Green lately, she couldn’t believe he was willingly stepping back into it. Hayes wasn’t about to bury Green this time. Stephanie pointed out that Chelsea is great with her character, and Hayes completely agreed before revealing what he’d actually told her. “She’s fantastic. Yes. But I told her, I said, ‘Chelsea, where was your character?’ I said, ‘I’m not telling you, you can’t wrestle and do good moves.’ Everybody can’t be Chelsea.” Apparently, Chelsea didn’t argue or need the point explained five different ways. Hayes said she immediately understood what he was getting at and gave her plenty of credit for picking it up so quickly. “And she got it right away. She’s very smart. She’s very smart.” Of course, Hayes talking about Chelsea Green is always going to get a little more attention after their WWE Unreal drama. Green wasn’t happy when she first saw footage of Hayes questioning her potential , although she eventually changed her tune and credited his criticism with pushing her to another level. Chelsea may have gotten over it, but her mother definitely had something to say. At SummerSlam, Green’s mom walked right up to Hayes, introduced herself and hit him with a simple “F*** you” over what she’d seen on Unreal , leaving Hayes with a story he immediately went backstage and told everyone. This time, though, Hayes had nothing but praise for Green. His problem wasn’t that she couldn’t wrestle — he just wanted more Chelsea Green in a Chelsea Green match, and apparently she understood exactly what he meant. title: On the Record: Ilja Dragunov Details His Wrestling Influences, Being In AEW With Samoa Joe & More
raw_title: Ilja Dragunov Details His Wrestling Influences, Being In AEW With Samoa Joe & More
body: Ilja Dragunov recently weighed in on his influences as a wrestler and what it’s like to be in AEW with the likes of Samoa Joe. Dragunov debuted on AEW WrestleDream and then won his in-ring debut on Dynamite against Mike Bailey. Dragunov spoke about who influenced him getting into wrestling during his interview with TMZ Inside the Ring. You can see highlights below: “So when I started to do to pursue professional wrestling, I had different influences that made me start. And it wasn’t necessarily the American wrestling-ish style or however you would call it. Like, my role models are [the] Kabashis, Mako Satamuras. Terry Funks, Roddy Pipers. William Regals. And coming from continental Europe, we have our own legends like Axe Dieter, Klaus Karlhoff, René Lazartes. “These are — where I come from, and what people inspired me, professional wrestlers are fighters. And that’s how we entertain. We don’t entertain first and then we are fighters or portraying fighters; we are fighters in the first place.” “Coming over to the States is definitely of course, like a different direction. But this is the beautiful thing about AEW being a place for people who are really expressing this craft. Like, people being there like a Samoa Joe, who was highly influential on me when I didn’t even know how to put on a wristlock. To know that this person is there for instance, just as an example — yeah, it clicks with me and resonates with me. And I feel like, ‘Okay, okay, that feels good.”
summary: Ilja Dragunov recently weighed in on his influences as a wrestler and what it’s like to be in AEW with the likes of Samoa Joe. Dragunov debuted on AEW WrestleDream and then won his in-ring debut on Dynamite against Mike Bailey.

body: AEW commentator Tony Schiavone recently discussed the Clockwork Carnage match from AEW WrestleDream, explaining how he was concerned that the match concept might not work on PPV in practice. Speaking on his What Happened When podcast , Schiavone noted that while he thought the execution of the match worked well live, he was concerned beforehand about it. “I didn’t know what to expect [from the match]. Nobody did, nobody. We’re in the back, we’ve had meetings, we’ve been told what’s going to go on…but we still didn’t know what to expect, and I’m thinking ‘this could really not turn out too good.’ But I thought it was good. I thought it was very good, and I thought there was a lot of drama. “I love matches where guys do a lot of great spots and can work and sell, and all the things that go in to make a good match, but I love the drama. I thought we had a lot of drama at the end of that match, and I thought that (Clockwork Carnage) was very, very good. So I enjoyed it, I don’t know how it was received online, because I don’t look.” Jake Jeremy Jake Jeremy is the Head of Audience Development at F4WOnline, having previously worked as a Combat Sports, Gaming and Pro Wrestling writer, successful Editor in Chief and Sports Coordinator. body: The stadium is obviously still in the early stages of being put together, but the scale of the project is already pretty clear. Crews can be seen working across the huge site as preparations continue with just over two weeks remaining before Crown Jewel. There’s still plenty of work to be done before WWE can actually move in and start setting up its own production. However, the construction activity makes it clear that preparations on the Saudi side haven’t stopped despite the growing security concerns surrounding the event. That’s particularly interesting after TKO executive chair and CEO Ari Emanuel revealed that Crown Jewel remains scheduled for Riyadh while the company monitors the situation daily. Speaking on Fox News, Emanuel said everything remains set for the time being. “Right now, everything’s still set. This weekend coming up in Abu Dhabi, we have a UFC fight. We have in the middle of November a Frieze art show. So far, so good. Nothing’s been canceled.” TKO isn’t operating without a backup plan, though. Emanuel also revealed that a team is monitoring developments and looking at where Crown Jewel could potentially be moved if holding the event in Riyadh becomes impossible. “Yeah, we have a whole team kind of working on this, and kind of when—and if that doesn’t happen, where we can move it. It’s a daily monitoring.” Those precautions come amid serious travel concerns in Saudi Arabia. The U.S. Embassy issued a security alert on October 22 warning Americans to use “extreme caution” at Saudi airports following attacks by the Iran-backed Houthis . King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh also remains suspended according to that alert, while airports in Jeddah and Dammam are operating with delays and cancellations. U.S. government employees working in Saudi Arabia currently require special authorization to use airports in the country. None of that has resulted in WWE announcing any change to Crown Jewel, and the latest footage makes it clear that work in Riyadh isn’t slowing down while TKO weighs its options. The Riyadh Season Stadium still has a long way to go, but crews are already racing to get the massive venue ready for November 7. title: WWE Employees Hated Vince McMahon’s Company-Wide Social Media Mandate
raw_title: WWE Employees Hated Vince McMahon’s Company-Wide Social Media Mandate
summary_src: Vince McMahon apparently didn’t just want WWE employees using social media — he wanted everybody in the company thinking about it.
body: Speaking with Michael Hayes on What’s Your Story? , Stephanie explained that Vince never wanted WWE getting so far ahead of a new trend that audiences couldn’t keep up. His goal was to stay just slightly ahead of everybody else, and Stephanie believes he recognized the importance of social media very early. “He didn’t—he never wanted to be ahead of the curve. He always wanted to be slightly ahead of the curve, but he didn’t wanna be so far ahead that people didn’t understand what was going on. But he just needed to be slightly ahead of the curve. Social media, yeah. I mean, that was—he saw that before anybody else.” At the time, Stephanie was overseeing WWE’s digital and social media operations. After attending a conference, she returned with an idea she’d heard about making social media a small responsibility spread across the entire company. “And I remember, because I was in charge of digital and social at the time, and I had been at a conference and come back and I said, ‘Oh, they said it was really interesting that it wasn’t, you know, a hundred percent of one person’s job. It was one percent of a hundred percent of the people’s jobs.’” Vince apparently heard “one percent” and decided that wasn’t nearly enough. His response was to make social media everybody’s problem in a much bigger way. “And he said, ‘No, it’s a hundred percent of a hundred percent.’” According to Stephanie, things quickly reached the point where every WWE department was expected to explain exactly what it was doing on social media. That mandate didn’t exactly go over well with employees who couldn’t figure out why posting online suddenly had anything to do with their actual jobs. “And it was like everything became about social media, and then all the department heads had to report back what their departments were doing in social media. And people hated it because they had no idea. They were like, ‘Why? What does my job have to do with social media?’” Hayes remembered that period as well and specifically recalled Vince putting Michael Cole in charge of WWE’s social media efforts. “I remember when he put Michael Cole in charge of social media.” Vince’s mandate may have driven people inside WWE crazy at the time, but Stephanie’s story shows just how aggressively he wanted the company to jump onto something once he believed it mattered. What started as her sharing one idea from a conference suddenly turned into every department having to explain its social media strategy. Felix Upton Felix Upton has over 15 years of experience in media and wrestling journalism. His work at Ringside News blends speed, accuracy, and industry insight.
summary: Per Ringside News: speaking with Michael Hayes on What’s Your Story? , Stephanie explained that Vince never wanted WWE getting so far ahead of a new trend that audiences couldn’t keep up. That mandate didn’t exactly go over well with employees who couldn’t figure out why posting online suddenly had anything to do with their actual jobs. And it was like everything became about social media.

title: On the Record: Ilja Dragunov Opens Up On the Legends Who Inspired His Hard-Hitting Style
raw_title: Ilja Dragunov Reveals the Legends Who Inspired His Hard-Hitting Style
body: 0 AEW star Ilja Dragunov has revealed his wrestling inspirations. The former WWE star is known for his hard-hitting style and his matches often feel like real fights inside the ring. Speaking in an interview with TMZ Sports , Dragunov recently discussed his influences and explained how several legends shaped his approach. His inspirations include wrestlers from different wrestling backgrounds. He said, “So when I started to do to pursue professional wrestling, I had different influences that made me start. And it wasn’t necessarily the American wrestling-ish style or however you would call it. Like, my role models are [the] Kabashis, Mako Satamuras. Terry Funks, Roddy Pipers. William Regals. And coming from continental Europe, we have our own legends like Axe Dieter, Klaus Karlhoff, René Lazartes.” He believes wrestling should feel physical and authentic. “These are — where I come from, and what people inspired me, professional wrestlers are fighters. And that’s how we entertain. We don’t entertain first and then we are fighters or portraying fighters; we are fighters in the first place.” He discussed joining AEW and believes AEW allows wrestlers to express their craft. “Coming over to the States is definitely of course, like a different direction. But this is the beautiful thing about AEW being a place for people who are really expressing this craft. Like, people being there like a Samoa Joe, who was highly influential on me when I didn’t even know how to put on a wristlock. To know that this person is there for instance, just as an example — yeah, it clicks with me and resonates with me. And I feel like, ‘Okay, okay, that feels good.'” [H/T: 411mania ] The post Ilja Dragunov Reveals the Legends Who Inspired His Hard-Hitting Style appeared first on Wrestlezone .

title: Way-Too-Early Predictions For WWE WrestleMania 43 Match Card
raw_title: Way-Too-Early Predictions For WWE WrestleMania 43 Match Card
body: Historically, however, it's in the final few months of the year that the company begins building toward the spring spectacle, or at least putting together preliminary plans for what the major matches will be. There has been speculation about the top matches at WrestleMania 43 and whether WWE will bring back familiar faces for the event, which is currently scheduled to take place in Saudi Arabia. However, appearances by legends such as The Rock and "Stone Cold" Steve Austin have not been confirmed. WWE has more than enough star power on its active roster to fill out the two-night weekend and still have a handful of notable names left over. Of course, anything can change creatively between now and then, and there's no telling who could be sidelined with an injury. These are the way-too-early match card predictions for WrestleMania 43. From the moment Oba Femi decisively defeated Brock Lesnar at WrestleMania 42, it was clear he was destined to win a world title sooner rather than later. Realistically, he should have already challenged for and won the World Heavyweight Championship by now (specifically at SummerSlam following his King of the Ring victory that earned him a title shot), but all signs point to WWE holding off on him having his crowning moment at WrestleMania 43. That would explain why Reigns has had a stranglehold on the prestigious prize since 'Mania back in April and will likely continue to reign as champ through the spring spectacle. Femi has repeatedly called out Reigns on post-show panels but has yet to cross paths with him on WWE TV. When they do finally go face-to-face, it will be a massive deal. WWE is attempting to keep Femi busy with random obstacles such as Lesnar and The Vision in the meantime. Expect Femi to win the men's Royal Rumble (the exact match where he made his main roster debut earlier this year) and set his sights on The Tribal Chief from there. That leaves him without an obvious opponent at the event, and the same can be said for all of The Vision. They've been at odds with Oba Femi as of late but are virtually guaranteed to come out on the losing end of that feud. Ideally, Bron Breakker would be in a marquee match at 'Mania next April, especially after missing this past year's installment due to injury (that was where he returned but didn't wrestle), but similar to Keys, there isn't one match that's a "must" for him to have unless he jumps ship to SmackDown or leaves The Vision. WWE has previously used multi-person tag team matches at WrestleMania to get wrestlers without clear storylines onto the card. That could be the case for The Vision and The 946. If built up properly, this could be a fun brawl and a solid showcase for everyone involved. A Street Fight stipulation would make for the most exciting scenario and allow them to go all out. Morgan recently regained the gold at Money in the Bank but has no challengers waiting in the wings. Her rivalries with Stephanie Vaquer and Becky Lynch have been done to deat

title: Ari Emanuel Monitors WWE Crown Jewel Amid Saudi Tensions
raw_title: Ari Emanuel addresses WWE Crown Jewel status amid Saudi Arabia security concerns
summary_src: Ari Emanuel, executive chairman and CEO of TKO Holdings, has addressed the status of WWE Crown Jewel amid growing security concerns in the Middle East. During an interview with Fox News, Emanuel addressed concerns surrounding TKO’s upcoming events including WWE’s Crown Jewel in Riyadh.
body: Ari Emanuel, executive chairman and CEO of TKO Holdings, has addressed the status of WWE Crown Jewel amid growing security concerns in the Middle East. During an interview with Fox News , Emanuel addressed concerns surrounding TKO’s upcoming events including WWE’s Crown Jewel in Riyadh. He indicated that, as of the interview, no events had been cancelled and that the company was closely monitoring developments while considering alternative arrangements if necessary. “Right now, everything is still set. This weekend coming up in Abu Dhabi, we have a UFC fight. We have in the middle of November a Frieze art show. So far so good. Nothing’s been cancelled.” “We have a whole team kind of working on this, and if that doesn’t happen, where we can move it. It’s a daily monitoring.” The uncertainty comes amid heightened regional tensions and security warnings issued by the U.S. State Department for nonessential diplomatic personnel and their families to leave Saudi Arabia. The developments follow reports that King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh had been attacked 20 times during the month, raising further concerns about security and travel disruptions. WWE Crown Jewel 2026 is currently scheduled to take place in Riyadh on November 7. However, a potential backup location in the United States has reportedly been discussed should the security situation force a change of plans. title: Drew McIntyre Teases WWE Return as Sin Cara
raw_title: Drew McIntyre hilariously teases WWE return as popular masked wrestler
body: Currently wrestling as Mistico in AEW and CMLL, the luchador was once known as Sin Cara in WWE. However, throughout Sin Cara's existence in WWE, the masked wrestler gimmick was portrayed by several performers. Recently, PWInsider reported that early pitches had been made to revive the Sin Cara character, although this time with a different wrestler taking on the role. Now absent from in-ring action for several months , former WWE Champion Drew McIntyre reacted to the news on social media and teased his comeback . McIntyre posted a video as a response to the post, where he was seen pulling off some high-flying action, with a caption saying, "I'm ready." The gimmick was originally portrayed by Místico, but was later taken over by Hunico after Místico was suspended for 30 days in 2011. Following Místico's return, it eventually led to a Sin Cara Negro vs. Sin Cara Azul feud that culminated in a Mask vs. Mask match at the Oct. 16, 2011 WWE SmackDown taping in Mexico City. Following Mistico's release in 2014, Hunico became the new Sin Cara, and the character remained a part of WWE until 2019. While McIntyre teased returning as the new masked Sin Cara, it should also be noted that McIntyre is not a stranger to the high-flying Lucha Libre style. "The Scottish Warrior" wrestled a couple of matches in AAA over a decade ago, in 2014 and 2015. McIntyre is currently away from wrestling, busy filming a few big Hollywood projects as well as a microdrama produced by WWE called Agent of Shadows. As of now, there are no confirmed updates on McIntyre's return.
summary: Former WWE Champion Drew McIntyre reacted to PWInsider reports of early pitches to revive the Sin Cara character with a new wrestler. The Scottish star posted a social media video showing himself performing high-flying moves with the caption "I'm ready." The masked luchador gimmick was originally played by Mistico in WWE before being portrayed by multiple performers including Hunico.

llm_long: Drew McIntyre has confirmed he will return to WWE eventually. He described the comeback as something that will be significant for both himself and the fans.
McIntyre has been absent from WWE programming since competing in an unsanctioned match against Jacob Fatu at WrestleMania 42. He has spent the time filming the movies Highlander and The Last Druid.

During an appearance on Going Ringside, the host referenced next year’s Road To Rumble European Tour and inquired about a possible return timeline. McIntyre stated that WWE remains his home while noting that his current focus is on his Hollywood projects.

He pointed out that this six-month break marks the first extended time away from wrestling since he began his professional career at age 15. McIntyre emphasized that the length of the absence will make his eventual return a major event.

title: 51-year-old WWE legend may follow in John Cena, AJ Styles’ footsteps by retiring soon
raw_title: 51-year-old WWE legend may follow in John Cena, AJ Styles’ footsteps by retiring soon
body: Over the last year alone, fans lost Goldberg , AJ Styles , and John Cena to retirement , and now, 51-year-old WWE legend Rey Mysterio may be joining them in 2027. WrestleVotes on Fightful Select reports that there's been "chatter backstage" at WWE about Mysterio possibly retiring in 2027. In turn, the promotion has started laying out plans for his farewell. While he is still a top in-ring performer, it's not surprising that the 51-year-old Mysterio is planning on hanging up the boots and mask soon. He has been wrestling for decades, and he has accomplished everything he can in WWE. WWE is likely planning the perfect final opponent for Mysterio. Gunther would be a great option, considering he was on a tear of retiring legends over the last couple of years. Retiring Mysterio could get him back on track after a year full of feuding with the likes of Danhausen. However, the best option is his son, Dominik Mysterio. Like Gunther, Mysterio has been on a skid over the last year. Retiring his father would give him much-needed legitimacy. The father-son duo has squared off several times previously. Their most notable encounter was at WrestleMania 39, which the elder Mysterio won. They would not have another televised singles match until the July 1, 2024, edition of Monday Night RAW, which Rey Mysterio also won. They have not had another singles match since. The last time that they shared the ring was the Oct. 5, 2026, edition of RAW. Judgment Day's Dominik Mysterio and JD McDonagh defeated the LWO's Rey Mysterio and Dragon Lee. In addition to his work in WWE, Mysterio is the general manager of Lucha Libre AAA Worldwide. He introduced the idea of the AAA tournament to determine Roman Reigns' challenger for the Mexico City episode of RAW in September 2026.

body: Major League Wrestling (MLW) today announced that MLW Saturday Night SuperFight will stream live worldwide on Live Nation’s VEEPS on Saturday, November 7, at 8 p.m. ET from Cicero Stadium in Chicago. Saturday Night SuperFight marks MLW’s return to pay-per-view for the first time in seven years and represents the biggest premium live event on the league’s 2026 calendar. The event arrives amid significant momentum for MLW, following the launch of its flagship weekly series, MLW Fusion , Thursday nights at 8 p.m. ET on Tubi. Saturday Night SuperFight will serve as the culmination of the championship quests, epic rivalries, and escalating conflicts unfolding each week on Fusion , with MLW raising the stakes for a loaded night of must-see title fights and marquee matchups. “MLW is on a roll, and now it’s time to go bigger,” said MLW Founder and CEO Court Bauer. “We’re not coming back to pay-per-view to play it safe. November 7 is where championships will be decided, rivalries will come to a head, and the best fighters in MLW will be expected to deliver on the biggest stage we’ve had in years. Chicago always brings an incredible atmosphere, and we’re giving that crowd — and fans watching around the world — a night of super fights.” “MLW has built a highly engaged global audience, and Saturday Night SuperFight is the kind of must-see moment fans want to experience as it happens,” said Kyle Heller, Co-Founder and Chief Content Officer of VEEPS. “We’re excited to bring MLW’s return to pay-per-view to fans around the world and give them the opportunity to watch the biggest matches, rivalries, and championship moments unfold live.” MLW’s roster features some of the most recognizable and compelling athletes in professional wrestling, including MLW World Heavyweight Champion Killer Kross, Matt Riddle, Místico, Austin Aries, The Good Brothers, CONTRA Unit, and emerging powerhouse ZAMAYA. Matches and championship bouts for Saturday Night SuperFight will be announced in the weeks ahead. MLW and Live Nation’s VEEPS will also collaborate on a collection of limited-edition Saturday Night SuperFight merchandise created exclusively for the event. Additional details about the collection and its availability will be announced soon. MLW Saturday Night SuperFight is executive produced by Court Bauer, Paul Walter Hauser, and Bryan Walsh. Chicago has become one of MLW’s strongest markets, with consecutive sellouts and a passionate fan base that has helped define the league’s success in the city. MLW returns to Cicero Stadium the following night, Sunday, November 8, for an MLW Fusion television taping. Tickets start at $10 and are available at MLWLucha.com.

title: Joe Hendry Comments on Street Fighter Fan Ideas
