title: Ari Emanuel Confirms WWE Crown Jewel Still On In Saudi Arabia
raw_title: TKO's Ari Emanuel Comments On Status Of WWE Crown Jewel In Saudi Arabia
summary_src: WWE Crown Jewel is scheduled to take place in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia on November 7. TKO's Ari Emmanuel appeared on FOX News to discuss the situation.
body: WWE is moving ahead with holding Crown Jewel in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia despite the enormous risks it's taking in doing so. The show is scheduled for November 7 and will take place amidst an ongoing conflict with the Houthis that has recently targeted several airports in Saudi Arabia, resulting in multiple deaths and injuries. The U.S. government recently ordered its diplomats and their families to leave the country as it also advises Americans not to travel to Saudi Arabia. TKO's Ari Emmanuel appeared on Fox News on Thursday to confirm that "everything's all set" with holding the show in Saudi Arabia. UFC has an upcoming show in Abu Dhabi that's still scheduled to take place. "Nothing's been canceled. (...) We have a whole team kind of working on this and if that doesn't happen, where we can move it. It's a daily monitoring," Emmanuel stated. WWE will be taping the "SmackDown" before Crown Jewel on November 2 , following the episode of "Raw" that will air at 6 PM ET. That show will take place at the Barclays Center in New York. On November 9, "Raw" will emanate from Columbia, South Carolina. Two matches have already been announced for Crown Jewel . Dave Meltzer explained that TKO has a financial incentive to hold the show as scheduled in Riyadh. He also said they risk losing WrestleMania 43 in Riyadh if they move Crown Jewel.
summary: TKO's Ari Emanuel stated that everything is set for WWE Crown Jewel on November 7 in Riyadh despite the ongoing regional conflict with the Houthis and recent U.S. government travel warnings. He noted a team is monitoring the situation daily and that nothing has been canceled, with UFC's Abu Dhabi event also proceeding as planned. WWE will tape SmackDown on November 2 at Barclays Center in New York following that night's Raw before heading to Columbia, South Carolina for the November 9 Raw.

llm_long: The US State Department has issued a security alert for Americans in the Middle East, including Saudi Arabia, just weeks before WWE Crown Jewel.
The alert follows an attack on Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport on October 10, after which the airport reopened on Sunday.

title: Comeback Watch: Road Dogg Makes In-Ring Return After 11 Years
raw_title: Road Dogg Makes In-Ring Return After 11 Years
summary_src: Road Dogg actually did it. After more than 11 years without an official match, the WWE Hall of Famer stepped back into the ring at Jeff Jarrett’s All-Star Super Slam on October 22 and officially ended his decade-plus wrestling drought.
body: My World with Jeff Jarrett took to Twitter and confirmed Road Dogg competed at the Hendersonville Pig Fest event while celebrating the show on Twitter the following day. Road Dogg teamed with Jarrett and Jay Lethal for the special anniversary match. “Last night @RealJeffJarrett’s All-Star Super Slam was a SMASH HIT! 💥 Huge thanks to everyone who was part of such a special night at the Hendersonville Pig Fest!” The match saw Road Dogg, Jarrett and Lethal take on QT Marshall, Elijah Drago and Brady Booker. It was part of a show celebrating Jarrett’s 40 years in professional wrestling, but Road Dogg’s return ended up giving fans another pretty big milestone to celebrate. That’s because Road Dogg hadn’t officially wrestled since January 25, 2015. His previous match came at WWE Royal Rumble, where he teamed with Billy Gunn as the New Age Outlaws in a loss to The Ascension. The comeback is even more surprising considering what Billy Gunn said about his longtime tag team partner earlier this year. While discussing the possibility of another New Age Outlaws reunion, Gunn made it sound like Road Dogg’s physical condition meant another match simply wasn’t happening . The event itself featured plenty of other madness, including a Concession Stand Brawl, a Micro Madness Match, a Lucha Libre Showcase and the appropriately named Pigfest 10-Man Gauntlet Battle Boar-Yal. Still, Road Dogg wrestling again after more than a decade away was always going to be one of the night’s biggest surprises. What started as an unexpected comeback announcement is now officially in the books. After 11 years spent working around the wrestling business without competing, Road Dogg finally reset the clock and proved he could still get back inside the ring one more time. title: Penta Discusses Money In The Bank Victory

summary_src: Penta is amazed by the WWE Money in the Bank briefcase win and has explained his plans for his cash-in.
body: WWE WWE's Penta is still in disbelief over winning the men's Money in the Bank match and has explained his plans for the cash-in. The Mexican star has been on a roll in WWE over the last few months, starting with his impressive performance in a match against Roman Reigns before winning the Money in the Bank briefcase . In an interview with " Busted Open ," Penta said he understands the responsibility that comes with holding the briefcase, particularly when it comes to being a role model for young fans. "Sometimes I can't believe what happened. At the same time, I know what is my responsibility now in this business, you know? Because every time more children go to me, every child uses my t-shirt, my mask, say Cero Miedo , can't say in Spanish, but he tries. When I saw that, it's like, 'Okay, I know now my responsibility with the crowd,'" he said. "As for the briefcase, I actually feel like I have the fu**ing power in my hands, basically, because at one time, I don't know where, I don't know when, but when I feel in my soul it's the perfect time for cash in, I will, you know?" The Money in the Bank holder admitted that he hasn't yet decided on whom he would cash in his briefcase, the WWE World Heavyweight Champion Roman Reigns, or the WWE Champion Sami Zayn. He stated that he wants to enjoy his time with the briefcase and the extravagant presentation that comes with it. "So now I start thinking sometimes Roman [Reigns], you know, Sami [Zayn], I don't know. Because it's my first time, but at the same time, I wanna do the best to get the World Championship, you know? But for now, I enjoy every presentation with my briefcase, with fire [pyro], you know, everything involved about it," he added. Penta recently came face-to-face with both champions, Reigns and Zayn, on "Raw" before facing Bron Breakker, whom he defeated to maintain his momentum following his Money in the Bank win.

title: On the Record: Ray Petree
raw_title: Ray Petree | Revisiting the Toni Storm vs. Mariah May ‘Hollywood Ending’
body: In the years since the global COVID-19 pandemic , the word “cinematic” has infiltrated professional wrestling nomenclature. The sentiment, shared by the likes of Roman Reigns and Paul Heyman, implies that professional wrestling can ascend to a higher plane of existence. Professional wrestling isn’t prestige television, nor is it the Marvel Cinematic Universe. It’s an art form unto itself that tells its tales through the catharsis of combat. In their self-styled “Hollywood Ending,” Toni Storm and Mariah May tackled that sentiment. This match was recommended to me by KELSON , from AEW Fan Hub. If you’d like to recommend me a match to me, please email me at [email protected] This match works on two levels: as a standalone match and within its greater context. The context being that this is the end of a trilogy of wars waged over the women’s world championship, cleverly weaving in elements from their 14-month-long saga. It’s also the sixth match in a pay-per-view rife with grudge matches, many of which suffer from the aforementioned imperfect storm: the bloat of “lore” and an inability to exercise brevity. “Hangman” Page could have settled his score with MJF using Christopher Daniels’ Angel’s Wing , but he opted to punctuate the affair with a Buckshot Lariat . Swerve Strickland could have put Ricochet away with a Vertebreaker through the table and the subsequent House Call , but chose to enter a second finishing stretch instead. Kyle Fletcher couldn’t meet his comeuppance with a Spanish Fly from the top of the cage, followed by the Hidden Blade , because Will Ospreay wanted to kill him with the Tiger Driver ‘91 . It’s a classic example of Chekhov’s Gun misfiring. All too often, AEW’s pay-per-view spectacles fail to eliminate what’s inessential. Narrative elements are either totally absent or blatantly overused, bereft of any subtlety. Of all the matches on this show, it’s this no-holds-barred, falls-count anywhere match that improbably finds the common sense that exists somewhere in the middle. May famously betrayed Storm at the top of the entryway, shortly after she won the Owen Hart Foundation Tournament. That’s precisely where this match begins and, ultimately, where it ends. Everything in between carries with it that same keen attention to detail. Storm using the “shoe,” May’s champagne celebration, Storm whipping May with the championship belt… It all feels pertinent. Even when Storm and May steal each other’s finishing maneuvers, it doesn’t feel self-indulgent, because they’ve both quite literally portrayed the other. What they managed to accomplish in fewer than 13 minutes is astonishing, drawing from 14 months’ worth of television in a way that feels organic and purposeful. The only thing this match could be accused of exercising an excess of is blood, which Storm spills profusely. title: Big E Marries Kristen Yim With Stars From Multiple Promotions Attending
raw_title: WWE's Big E Gets Married, With Wrestlers In Attendance
body: Congratulations are in order for WWE's Ettore "Big E" Ewen and Kristen Yim as the happy couple officially married on Wednesday. According to Bryan Alvarez of the Wrestling Observer, wrestlers from WWE, AEW, and TNA were in attendance for the pair's wedding, including Mia Yim, Seth Rollins, Becky Lynch, Kofi, and Austin Creed (formerly Kofi Kingston and Xavier Woods). As seen on his Instagram stories , WWE broadcaster Peter Rosenberg also attended, with the dance floor becoming a hot spot for him and his peers. Big E and Kristen, the sister of WWE star Mia Yim, went on their first date at the premiere of Montez Ford and Bianca Belair's Hulu show "Love & WWE" in early 2024. In the "The Player's Tribune," Big E revealed that he and his now-wife had been communicating via direct message before arranging to hang out at the premiere. It was there that Big E then became truly enamored. "I just felt an energy with Kristen I'd never felt before," Big E wrote. "We were at this premiere with all these beautiful people, all these famous actors and entertainers, and none of them even registered. For me, there was only one other person in the room that night. And what's crazy is, I knew I wanted to see her more after that." After more than a year of dating, Big E and Kristen got engaged in May 2025 , with the former proudly touting that he "couldn't wait" to be the latter's husband. Since sustaining a neck injury in 2022, Big E has taken a giant step back from in-ring competition. He remains signed to WWE as an on-screen host and talent scout, however.

Strickland demanded a rematch after his team lost the titles, and Page agreed that they deserved another opportunity. Swerve then called for the match to happen at Full Gear before trying to turn things considerably more personal. Strickland brought up his violent history with Page and demanded that the Trios Championship rematch be held under Texas Death rules. Page immediately rejected that stipulation because he knew Swerve’s request wasn’t really about the championships. The wrestling story will still be waiting for The New Level when they return, but Big E’s wedding was obviously a night Kingston and Creed weren’t going to miss. After everything the three experienced together during their WWE run, their friendship clearly extends well beyond whichever company logo happens to be on their paycheck. title: Another Major Event in Saudi Arabia Postponed as New Missile Attack Raises WWE Crown Jewel Concerns
raw_title: Another Major Event in Saudi Arabia Postponed as New Missile Attack Raises WWE Crown Jewel Concerns
summary_src: WWE’s Crown Jewel plans in Saudi Arabia are facing even more questions after another major international event in Riyadh was postponed and a ballistic missile targeting the city was intercepted Friday morning.
body: On October 23, Saudi Arabia’s General Authority for Statistics announced that the United Nations World Data Forum and Second Saudi Statistical Forum, scheduled for November 9 through November 12 in Riyadh, have been pushed back to 2027. That’s just two days after WWE is supposed to hold Crown Jewel at Riyadh Season Stadium on November 7. According to Reuters , Saudi officials said the decision was made to ensure international participation and deliver a successful event. They did not specifically blame security concerns for the postponement. This is now the second major international event in Riyadh to get pushed back. Saudi Arabia’s Future Investment Initiative conference, originally scheduled for October 26 through October 29, was also postponed until 2027. And the security situation isn’t getting any better. Early Friday morning, Saudi air defenses intercepted a ballistic missile heading toward Riyadh shortly after 4 a.m. local time. Officials also confirmed another missile was intercepted near Khamis Mushait, along with two drones targeting southern Saudi Arabia. No casualties or damage were reported from the latest interceptions. The developments come just one day after the U.S. Embassy warned Americans to use extreme caution at Saudi airports . The October 22 alert stated that operations at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh remained suspended following attacks on airports and other infrastructure. That creates another problem for WWE, which still has to get its wrestlers, production crew and equipment into Riyadh for Crown Jewel. TKO executive Ari Emanuel addressed the situation during an interview with Fox News earlier this week. Despite the security concerns, he maintained that the company’s upcoming events were still moving forward. “Right now, everything’s still set. This weekend coming up in Abu Dhabi, we have a UFC fight. We have in the middle of November a Frieze art show. So far, so good. Nothing’s been canceled.” Emanuel also confirmed that TKO has people evaluating the situation and looking at possible alternatives in case events can’t take place as scheduled. “Yeah, we have a whole team kind of working on this, and kind of when—and if that doesn’t happen, where we can move it. It’s a daily monitoring.” That’s especially important now that two major events in Riyadh have already been postponed. WWE hasn’t announced any changes to Crown Jewel, but TKO is clearly preparing for the possibility that plans may need to change. For now, Crown Jewel remains scheduled for November 7 at Riyadh Season Stadium. WWE hasn’t announced a postponement or relocation, and there’s no confirmation that the company has decided to move the show. title: Austin Creed Confident In Adapting To AEW Style
raw_title: Austin Creed On Adapting To AEW's Style: 'Kofi And I Are Very Much Chameleons'
summary_src: Austin Creed is confident that he and Kofi can adapt to their new surroundings in AEW, explaining how he did the same during his time in TNA Wrestling.
body: AEW Austin Creed is confident that he and his tag team partner, Kofi, can adjust to their new surroundings in AEW. After spending 16 years in WWE, Creed left the promotion and is now finding his footing in his new home, AEW. Creed and Kofi recently spoke to " Yahoo Sports ," where Creed discussed his past experience adjusting to a new wrestling promotion, citing his stint in TNA Wrestling to make his case. "From my point of view, your boy was born in the [TNA] X-Division. So, I mean, this ain't no thing. We can switch it up as much as we want to," said Creed. "I feel like Kofi and I are very much chameleons in that aspect. As soon as you drop us in an environment, we see what needs to be done and we are able to adapt fairly quickly." Creed had a three-year spell in TNA before joining WWE in 2010, competing several times for the X-Division Championship, which he never won. Later in the interview, Kofi also spoke confidently about how he and his New Level partner can adjust to and fulfill any role they're given in AEW. "We are jacks of all trades, you know, Swiss Army knives. We can do it all and we do it all very, very well," added Kofi. The former WWE Champion spoke glowingly about their time in AEW, saying that their energy has blended well with the promotion's atmosphere. Creed and Kofi have revealed, following their move to AEW, that they had many opportunities away from the wrestling ring too. The two have discussed how their AEW deals provide them with opportunities beyond wrestling, which they are excited about. In the ring, the duo got their AEW careers off to a strong start by winning the Trios Championship, which they unfortunately lost at the WrestleDream pay-per-view.

Creed cited his three years in TNA's X-Division as evidence of his ability to switch styles, describing himself and Kofi as chameleons who adapt to any environment. Kofi echoed the sentiment, calling the pair jacks of all trades and Swiss Army knives who can fulfill any role in their new promotion.

title: Vince McMahon battled WCW's lingering shadow in 2001
raw_title: The Summer of 2001: Vince McMahon’s fight with the ghost of WCW
summary_src: After Rewind-A-Wai covered WWF SummerSlam 2001, John Pollock reflects on the decline of WWF's business and mishandling of the invasion.
body: The summer of 2001 was a confusing time for the World Wrestling Federation, operating off the fumes of its Attitude Era boom with a decline in momentum, while handling the most coveted storyline with its real-life competitor. Ask a fan of this era about the “Invasion storyline,” and you’re likely to be met with a groan, scream, or laundry list of alternative ideas that would have given some resuscitation in its dying days. If there is an underlying theme from the Monday Night War, it was the real-life vitriol possessed by the warring companies, WWF and WCW, making Monday night a firing zone with attacks lobbed back-and-forth, talent being scooped, shoot interviews, and conveying to fans that in a world of make-believe this feud among companies was real. Every fan had their “dream card”, fantasy booking their favorites with the opposition and asking “what if?” It was Marvel fighting DC, Jason vs. Freddy, and Jay-Z vs. Nas. It sounded really simple on paper. The problem was one company buying out the other, and over time, it was so transparent the scars that Vince McMahon wore from that head-to-head era. The man who frequently stated that he loved competition has acted in the opposite way throughout his career, circumventing anything non-WWE in the market space. This is the man who signed Curt Hennig to thwart the XWF, put himself on ECW programming to counter Wrestling Society X, made up with Jim Ross when he was linked to the World of Sport reboot, and used his son-in-law’s sub-brand as the counterattack to shut down AEW in its tracks on Wednesday nights. Taking us back to 2001, Vince McMahon has acquired WCW for a bargain. McMahon had kicked the tires months earlier in hopes of securing WCW as a distressed asset of the Turner empire. Its brand-new relationship with TNN provided the network with exclusive cable rights to WWF and wasn’t going to bend and allow WWF to run a competitor on another broadcaster without a significant fee. It quelled McMahon’s desire to acquire his competitor, but months later, it was a fire sale, and McMahon bought the assets of WCW, including its undervalued tape library, and committed to several years of advertising dollars toward Turner. WCW was a perfect bridge from the Attitude Era to another golden road paved with pay-per-view revenue off the fantasy match-ups and stories they could tell. Yes, many of the major stars had guaranteed deals and had no incentive to break those contracts to go on the road, nor was WWF interested in upsetting its salary structure for those big names. Hulk Hogan, Sting, Bill Goldberg, Kevin Nash, Scott Hall, and even Eric Bischoff would not be around to launch the invasion. The audience didn’t care because the idea of WCW was strong enough that even a diminished army of WCW names was enough to propel its July pay-per-view into the stratosphere and produce one of the largest non-WrestleMania numbers in the company’s history. summary: During the summer of 2001 the WWF was losing steam from its Attitude Era peak while attempting to capitalize on its real-life purchase of rival WCW through the Invasion storyline. Fans often recall the angle with disappointment and point to missed opportunities that could have revived interest. The Monday Night War had featured genuine animosity between the promotions with on-air shots talent raids and shoot promos that made the rivalry feel authentic.

title: End of an Era: Ex-WWE & AEW Star Retires From Wrestling After 24 Years in the Business
raw_title: Ex-WWE & AEW Star Retires From Wrestling After 24 Years in the Business
body: In his retirement message, Gowen revealed the best moment of his career came when he wrestled in front of his family during his AEW appearance. He also opened up about his struggle with drug addiction. Moreover, he explained how he got the chance to rebuild his life and find his love for wrestling again. Gowen shared the news on Facebook on Wednesday. He posted his first-ever promotional picture along with a more recent photo to reminisce on his wrestling journey. The former WWE and AEW star also thanked the promoters who gave him opportunities. He also thanked the fans who supported him throughout his career. "My in-ring career has come to an end. Thank you to every promoter who gave me an opportunity to wrestle. I've had the privilege of performing for every major company over the past 24 years. Special thank you to the fans for not rejecting me. Pro wrestling provided a direction and outlet for a very lost kid. All I ever wanted to be was a professional wrestler and I accomplished that solely because you accepted me not as a sideshow act but as a legitimate pro wrestler. I'm deeply grateful," Gowen wrote. Gowen had several opportunities across different promotions. However, his favorite wrestling memory came during his appearance for AEW in May 2025. He faced Ricochet on the May 14 episode of AEW Dynamite: Beach Break at the NOW Arena in Hoffman Estates, Illinois. Although Gowen lost, the experience meant a lot to him because his wife, children, and parents were there to watch him wrestle. Looking back, Gowen wrote, "The best moment of my career was wrestling for AEW in front of my wife, kids, and parents." Gowen also revealed that he had struggled with drug addiction in the past. It almost destroyed his career. However, he eventually got a chance to turn his life around. "That was the cherry on top after burning my career to the ground as a result of my crippling drug addiction then having the opportunity to not only rebuild my life but my passion then sharing that with the world while enjoying every second of it," he added. Gowen ended his message by thanking God and the people who believed in him. He described himself as "the luckiest guy in the world." Zach Gowen's biggest run in mainstream wrestling came in 2003 and 2004, when he competed for WWE. He became part of a storyline involving Hulk Hogan's Mr. America character, WWE Hall of Famer Roddy Piper, and Sean O'Haire. Gowen also worked behind the scenes more recently. He took on a production role for Maple Leaf Pro Wrestling at its Northern Rising PPV on October 3 in Toronto. He had also wrestled for the promotion in August, defeating Michael Allen Richard Clark. body: TNA One of TNA's recent signees Ricky Sosa will be sitting out of in-ring action for the time being after it was revealed on this week's episode of "TNA Impact" that he's suffered a "severe back injury." As part of its weekly show, "Impact" provides an "injury report" segment that details the rosters' current injuries (both storyline and real) and the expected timeframes of how long they'll be out of action. In last night's segment, TNA announced that the European star obtained his back injury during the number one contenders ladder match for the TNA World Championship on the October 15 edition of "Impact." During the match, Moose powerbombed Sosa out of the ring. Moose attempted to send Sosa crashing through a propped-up ladder, but Sosa's back grazed the ladder before landing on the floor. As of this report, TNA said that Sosa is unable to compete, but did not provide a timeframe of how long he'll be out of in-ring competition. Sosa officially signed with the promotion at Sacrifice this past March. His first big feud under contract was against former talent Eric Young. Sosa scored a major victory over the veteran on the "Countdown to Slammiversary" in June. After he turned his attention towards The System. That rivalry officially ended at Bound for Glory earlier this month with a win over the System's leader, Eddie Edwards.

Sosa, who signed with TNA at Sacrifice this past March and feuded with Eric Young, is currently unable to compete.

llm_long: Ricky Sosa has been sidelined with a severe back injury. The announcement came during the October 22 episode of TNA Wrestling's Thursday Night iMPACT on AMC.
Sosa competed in a ladder match on the October 15 episode of Thursday Night iMPACT. The bout was a main event that offered a future shot at the TNA World Championship.
During the match, Moose executed a powerbomb on Sosa and sent him out of the ring. Sosa's back grazed a propped-up ladder before he landed directly on the floor.
The injury update was part of the TNA Injury Report, which also included notes on Trey Miguel and Jason Hotch. Further details on Sosa's status will be provided when available.

title: WWE to Tape SmackDown Go-Home with Raw in Brooklyn
raw_title: WWE reportedly has a plan for SmackDown the night before Crown Jewel
summary_src: All the attention is on Sat., Nov. 7’s Crown Jewel premium live event, currently scheduled to take place in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.
body: Unlike a couple of their recent go homes for PLEs in the Kingdom (2025’s Night of Champions and this past February’s Royal Rumble ), Crown Jewel 2026’s wasn’t announced for Saudi in advance. Or anywhere else for that matter. Whether that was an intentional move to give WWE some flexibility given the Iran War’s destabilizing impact on the Middle East/North Africa (MENA) region, or it just worked out that way? We don’t know. We are however hearing (from Fightful Select ) that WWE’s set with a plan. That plan is to tape the Crown Jewel go home editions of Raw and SmackDown together at Brooklyn’s Barclays Center on Mon., Nov. 2. That means a pre-taped final push for the event from the blue brand, and an earlier start time for the red one. To not keep the New York crowd there too late for SmackDown ’s taping, Raw will start at 6 p.m. ET. Netflix streams Raw live on Mondays whenever it happens, so the stream will begin two hours early on Nov. 2. Then wherever Crown Jewel ends up happening, the fallout edition of Raw will be at the Bon Secours Wellness Arena in Greenville, South Carolina, streaming live at 8 p.m. ET on Netflix. Got it? title: Major WrestleMania 43 Main Event Rumor Killer Emerges
raw_title: Major WrestleMania 43 Main Event Rumor Killer Emerges
body: "There has been a lot of talk this week that the two main events for WrestleMania in 2027 would be Rhodes vs. Punk on night one and Reigns vs. Femi on night two," Meltzer wrote. "From what we were told, the latter is accurate, but the former is not the current plan." Fightful Select previously said WWE had set Reigns vs. Femi aside for WrestleMania , and some people it spoke with think the bout could close the show. That report also had Rhodes and Punk in prominent spots, and one source floated a second match between them after SummerSlam. WWE has been building toward Reigns vs. Femi since at least June, when it was reported as the fallback if The Rock does not wrestle at WrestleMania 43. Femi called out Reigns on the WrestleMania 42 post-show in April, and he did it again after beating Bronson Reed at Money in the Bank in October. Femi has had a big 2026. He beat Brock Lesnar in the opening match of night two at WrestleMania 42, won the King of the Ring tournament by beating Jey Uso at Night of Champions in June, and beat Lesnar again in a Hell in a Cell match at SummerSlam, though Lesnar beat him at Clash in Italy in May. Reigns won the World Heavyweight Championship from Punk at WrestleMania 42 and is set to face Undisputed WWE Champion Sami Zayn in a champion vs. champion match at Crown Jewel . Rhodes and Punk last met at SummerSlam in August, when Punk kept the Undisputed WWE Championship after a returning Randy Orton interfered. Orton hit Rhodes with an RKO, and Punk followed with the GTS for the win. Punk has since lost the title to Zayn, while Rhodes is now in a feud with Orton on SmackDown. Of the two updates, Reigns vs. Femi carries more weight. WWE has protected the match for most of the year, and it is not hard to see why. Femi has beaten Lesnar twice and won King of the Ring, and a win over Reigns at WrestleMania would go a long way toward making him a top star. Holding the match until next April gives WWE time to build it the right way instead of rushing it onto a smaller show. Rhodes vs. Punk not being the current plan for the night one main event does not rule it out. Meltzer's wording leaves room for things to change, and WrestleMania plans often shift between October and April. But with Rhodes tied up with Orton and Punk no longer champion, a rematch of their SummerSlam match is not the obvious direction it might have seemed a few months ago. That leaves an open question for night one. If The Rock does compete, his match could change the entire card. If not, WWE will need a main event that can stand next to Reigns vs. Femi, and the Rhodes and Orton feud could be one option to watch as the road to Riyadh takes shape. title: In Memoriam: Cause of death revealed for wrestler 'Pac,' who died after AEW competition in Chicago area
raw_title: Cause of death revealed for wrestler 'Pac,' who died after AEW competition in Chicago area
body: A cause of death has been revealed for wrestler Benjamin Satterley, known as "Pac," who dies in Des Plaines after a Hoffman Estates AEW competition. CHICAGO (WLS) -- A cause of death has been revealed for Benjamin Satterley, an English-born wrestler known for high-flying moves that delighted fans worldwide. He died last month after competing at an All Elite Wrestling event in Hoffman Estates, a northern suburb of Chicago, according to the Cook County Medical Examiner. The medical examiner says 40-year-old Satterley died from bronchial asthma. He wrestled Sept. 26 at NOW Arena before his death was reported the next day in nearby Des Plaines. The news shocked fans who watched the English-born wrestler perform the night before, including Jayson Weidman, who attended the event. Inside NOW Arena on Saturday, Satterley competed for All Elite Wrestling under the ring name Pac. The English wrestler, who previously performed in WWE as Adrian Neville, was known for high-flying moves that delighted fans worldwide. "There are wrestlers that can do incredible things, and then there's wrestlers who can do things that you question how it's even humanly possible that they can do what they're doing. Pac was one of those wrestlers," Weidman said. Satterley, who was from Newcastle upon Tyne, began his wrestling career in 2004 and signed in 2019 with All Elite Wrestling, where he held multiple championships. He competed and lost to Andrade El Ídolo on Saturday in Chicago in the AEW National Championship. Weidman said he purchased his seat specifically in hopes of being close to Pac and his group, the Death Riders. "It was such a special moment for me to be able to see him wrestle," Weidman said. He quickly rose to prominence, earning nicknames like "The Super Superman" and "The Man That Gravity Forgot." He began his international journey in 2007 and wrestled under the name of Adrian Neville from 2012 to 2018. After signing with AEW, he became the inaugural AEW International Champion and a two-time AEW World Trios Champion. According to Weidman, Pac wrestled in Saturday's opening match and later returned during the main event. "He looked healthy as can be, and it's unbelievable how less than 24 hours, he could possibly be gone," Weidman said. The Cook County Medical Examiner said Satterley died shortly after 4 p.m. Sunday at 2761 Mannheim Road in Des Plaines. A restaurant employee at that address said Satterley never entered the business. Outside the location, at least one fan left a vase on the sidewalk in tribute to the wrestler. All Elite Wrestling also paid tribute to Satterley on its Facebook page, writing: "The very best of us. title: Chris Jericho Cast As Gorgeous George In Muhammad Ali Series
raw_title: AEW's Chris Jericho To Play Famed Wrestler In Upcoming Streaming Series
summary_src: Even though he lost twice to Nick Wayne, AEW's Chris Jericho continues to add his acting resume and landed an important role in an upcoming series.
body: AEW Chris Jericho is adding to his growing acting resume by playing one of wrestling's most iconic wrestlers. The former AEW Men's World Champion has been cast as Gorgeous George in the forthcoming Muhammed Ali limited series, "The Greatest". The show stars Jaalen Best as the legendary boxer. According to Deadline , who broke the news of Jericho's casting, the Prime Video series "features defining moments in Ali's life and career, both in and out of the ring, that have been well documented, and moments that took place outside the spotlight. The world remembers an icon, but The Greatest is about a man, a husband, a father, a brother and a son." Gorgeous George was a flamboyant, charismatic wrestler who wore fur coats and came to the ring using "Pomp & Circumstance". In the 1940s, he became one of wrestling's first mainstream stars and went by the nicknames "The Beautiful Bicep" and "The Sensation of the Nation". The WWE Hall of Famer influenced many who came after him, including Ali. Jericho will appear in the fourth episode of "The Greatest". He recently appeared in Apple TV's "Margo's Got Money Troubles" and in an episode of CBS' "Trackers". In April, Jericho revealed he'll be in "Dexter: Resurrection" . In November, "Collision" will be live from Jericho's Rock 'N Wrestling Rager at Sea . It will be the first time "Collision" has been live from the cruise and its scheduled for November 7, the same day as WWE Crown Jewel .
summary: AEW's Chris Jericho has been cast to portray the iconic wrestler Gorgeous George in the upcoming Prime Video limited series "The Greatest" about Muhammad Ali. The show, which stars Jaalen Best as Ali, explores both well-known and lesser-seen moments from the boxer's life as a man, husband, father, brother and son. Jericho is set to appear in the fourth episode of the series.

title: Cody Rhodes Targets 2032-2033 WWE Retirement
raw_title: Cody Rhodes On Updated WWE Retirement Timeline: 'I Don't Want To Overstay My Welcome'
summary_src: WWE's Cody Rhodes indicates that he has several more years left to give before retiring from in-ring competition.
body: WWE star Cody Rhodes knows that he's closer to the end of his wrestling career than the beginning. He doesn't intend to hang up his boots for several more years, however. As revealed on "Insight With Chris Van Vliet," Rhodes is eyeing 2032 or 2033 for his official in-ring retirement. "I just signed my last contract ," he said. "I say last contract, but that's going to go for a while, and if I'm able to do what I've been able to do, because I would love this year not to be just one movie, but perhaps two movies, and I'd love to kind of be able to share that at some point, get that going, and be in that. With all that said, my time with WWE could go. I mean, just to give you a real answer here, and not politic around you, probably seven years. Six, seven ...Yeah, six, seven years. I'd say so. I don't want to say that in a final sense. I just know that I don't want to overstay my welcome." Rhodes, 41, made his pro wrestling debut in 2006, the same year in which he inked a developmental deal with WWE. His main roster debut came the following year in a match against Randy Orton, his future mentor in Legacy. Fast forward to 2026, Rhodes is a three-time world champion in the company, currently feuding with Orton on "WWE SmackDown." Orton himself aims to wrestle until at least the age of 50. Based on Rhodes' latest timeline, his respective retirement would put him at either 47 or 48.
summary: Cody Rhodes revealed on Insight With Chris Van Vliet that he signed his last WWE contract and plans to retire in about six or seven years, around 2032 or 2033. The 41-year-old, who debuted in 2006 and signed a developmental deal with WWE that same year, said he does not want to overstay his welcome in the ring. Rhodes also expressed hopes of expanding his acting work beyond one movie this year.

llm_long: Cody Rhodes discussed his future wrestling plans in an interview. He indicated that he recently signed what he considers his last contract with WWE.
Rhodes estimated that his time with the company could last around six or seven more years. He expressed a desire not to overstay his welcome in the industry.
When asked about wrestling into his 50s, Rhodes said he does not want to continue that long. He emphasized his gratitude for what wrestling has provided him throughout his career.

Rhodes reflected on his journey from a mid-card talent with limited opportunities to achieving significant milestones. He mentioned portraying the character Guile from Street Fighter as one example of his accomplishments.

He noted that wrestling has given him a great deal while acknowledging the personal sacrifices made over the years. Rhodes believes there will come a point when it is time to stop taking from the industry.

title: Leon Slater Wants TNA to Bring Back Six-Sided Ring for Destination X
raw_title: Leon Slater Wants TNA to Bring Back Six-Sided Ring for Destination X
summary_src: Leon Slater has one big request for TNA Destination X, and it has nothing to do with who he’s facing. With the event returning as a pay-per-view in November, the TNA World Champion is hoping the company brings back one of the most recognizable parts of its past — the six-sided ring.
body: While speaking on the I Love Wrestling Podcast , Slater was asked about Destination X returning and immediately revealed what he had been hoping for. He made it clear he has no inside information about whether the six-sided ring is actually coming back, but he’d love the chance to finally wrestle inside it. “I was just praying that the six-sided ring would come back, to be real. And I don’t know if it is, I don’t know if it isn’t. But, man, I hope it does, because I’m sure, like you, growing up in TNA, that’s what we loved, right?” Slater is well aware that actually wrestling inside the six-sided ring wasn’t always as fun as it looked on television. Plenty of wrestlers have talked about how much harder the ring was compared to a traditional four-sided setup, but that hasn’t scared him away from wanting the experience. “So, to get the chance to compete in a six-sided ring, as much as people said it sucked back in the day, and it’s, like, way harder, and it hurts way more than a four-sided ring, and that hurts enough, trust me, I would love the chance to be TNA World Champion and wrestle in a TNA six-sided ring.” Destination X is set for November 15 at the Edmonton Expo Centre in Edmonton, Alberta, Canada. The event will be particularly notable because it marks the first Destination X show in nine years, with TNA last holding the event back in 2017. Slater already has plenty to worry about without wondering what shape the ring will be. He’s scheduled to defend the TNA World Championship against Trey Miguel at the show, putting one of TNA’s biggest prizes on the line for Destination X’s comeback. For now, there’s no confirmation that TNA plans to dust off the six-sided ring for the event. Slater is simply hoping the company leans all the way into Destination X nostalgia and gives him the chance to experience something he grew up watching. title: Sean Legacy credits CM Punk for physique transformation
raw_title: WWE NXT wrestler credits CM Punk for inspiring physique change
summary_src: An interaction with CM Punk helped inspire WWE NXT wrestler Sean Legacy to get in shape. During the summer, Punk worked an NXT house show in Virginia and spent some time with the young talent in NXT.
body: An interaction with CM Punk helped inspire WWE NXT wrestler Sean Legacy to get in shape. During the summer, Punk worked an NXT house show in Virginia and spent some time with the young talent in NXT. Legacy was one of the wrestlers that he spoke with, and their conversation about Punk’s diet and workouts motivated Legacy to eat cleaner, push himself harder in workouts, and train more in the ring. Legacy, now at 199 pounds, shared photos showing a noticeable difference in his physique than when he was 217 pounds. WWE produced a behind-the-scenes vlog from Punk’s appearance at the NXT house show, with the video showing some footage of Legacy approaching Punk backstage and praising him for how he’s taken care of his body. Legacy officially joined the NXT roster near the start of 2026 after impressing in the WWE ID program and on WWE Evolve. Punk made the decision to get in better shape during the weeks before WrestleMania 42, and he’s been working with a trainer named Jay Ferruggia who also assists other WWE talent like Chad Gable. Punk, outside of special occasions, has been sticking to a strict meal plan and gym regimen. He sends a mirror selfie to Ferruggia every morning along with his weight and temperature, and Ferruggia responds by telling Punk how much protein, carbs, and fat he should eat that day. While Punk’s muscular physique has led to some fans claiming that it’s because of steroids, Ferruggia denied that and said Punk has fully committed himself to the process of getting in better shape and is not cheating or taking any shortcuts . Legacy dropped from 217 pounds to 199 pounds and shared before-and-after photos of the change. Punk had decided to get in better shape ahead of WrestleMania 42 and has been working with trainer Jay Ferruggia.

title: Peteani analyzes AEW Full Gear build

body: By Frank Peteani , ProWrestling.net Contributor ( @FrankPeteani ) I’m excited to join the ProWrestling.net team as a contributor. For those unfamiliar with my work, I spent nearly eight years contributing to PWTorch.com . My most significant assignment was the VIP podcast Pro Wrestling Then and Now . I also wrote preview articles, most notably for Raw and SmackDown, and briefly covered Dynamite and Rampage—when that was a thing. Here, I’ll examine upcoming AEW pay-per-views from a build perspective, focusing on what unfolds on television and how much interest the shows are generating. I’m “old school” and don’t pay much attention to social media. AEW should give viewers everything they need on Dynamite and Collision. That said, I may occasionally discuss something if I come across it and find it relevant. For now, I plan to publish this column every other week, though I may adjust that around the pay-per-view schedule, family life, and the “shoot” job. “The Brawling Birds” Jamie Hayter and Alex Windsor vs. “Wrathlander” Kris Statlander and Harley Cameron for the AEW Women’s Tag Team Titles: Kris and Harley earned the right to challenge for the titles by defeating “The Sisters of Sin” Julia Hart and Skye Blue and “Divine Dominion” (Megan Bayne and Lena Kross at Collision Grand Slam France. The match was to have taken place at WrestleDream but was cancelled due to an injury to Jamie Hayter. With that said, thus far AEW put out a video on social media (I’m already breaking my rule) with Wrathlander talking about every creature having a predator, with them, of course, being those predators to the birds. This past Wednesday, Renee Paquette was to interview the participants, but the “Sisters of Sin” Thekla, Julia Hart, and Skye Blue, and the Divine Dominion attacked them. We know where this is going, right? They need a women’s Blood & Guts match, so there it is. Back to the tag title match, I’m going to reserve judgment until I see more. I’m also curious who is framed as more likable. Early on, I would suspect that would be Wrathlander since the fans naturally like Harley. “The Young Bucks” Matt Jackson and Nick Jackson vs. Mark Davis and Jake Doyle for the AEW Tag Team Titles: What happened on Dynamite with Davis & Doyle squashing the Bucks in a matter of minutes? I don’t think anyone saw that coming, and quite frankly, it got my attention. It’s something different for AEW. I expected (but didn’t want to see) New Level challenging the Bucks at Full Gear. Why didn’t I want to see it? They lost the AEW Trios Titles, and I hate when champions lose titles and move right to another championship situation. They’re clearly telling a story with the Bucks, given the fact that after their match at WrestleDream, they said (I’m paraphrasing) that they don’t know if they have many of these left. title: Shayna Baszler Reveals Ronda Rousey Threatened To Quit WWE
raw_title: Shayna Baszler Claims Ronda Rousey Threatened To Quit WWE Over Women’s Match Time
body: Skip to content Wrestling News Home » Shayna Baszler Claims Ronda Rousey Threatened To Quit WWE Over Women’s Match Time New TNA star Shayna Baszler says Ronda Rousey once threatened to quit WWE over the promotion cutting time from women’s matches. In a recent interview with Denise Salcedo , Shayna Baszler opened up about joining TNA and her time with WWE. During the conversation, she addressed claims that her friend, MMA legend Ronda Rousey, didn’t care about professional wrestling. Shayna Baszler remembered when WWE cut six minutes from one of Ronda Rousey’s pay-per-view matches. She said Rousey bought her own ticket to fly to the headquarters in Stamford, Connecticut, and threatened to quit if creative continues cutting time from women’s matches. “I’ve heard people be like Ronda didn’t really care about wrestling. She might hate me for telling this story, but there was a time when Ronda had a pay-per-view match and got six minutes cut off because a match before had gone over their time. To take six minutes from a match is huge. In order to build a story and get emotion involved, it takes time,” Shayna Baszler began. “And when that happened, she bought her own ticket and flew herself to headquarters to have a meeting with creative at that time to be like, ‘Guys, this keeps happening. The women keep losing time. I need to know right now. Is this going to change? Because if it’s not, I don’t need to be here. I don’t need to be here to make money. I don’t need to be here to get famous. I’m here to help advance this. And if you’re telling me right now that’s never going to happen, then I’m done. I only want to improve this,'” Baszler continued. “She’s not going to tell you that story. She’s not going to tweet about it. She’s not going to go on a thing and talk about it. And nobody’s going to know about the stuff she did like that behind the scenes, on her own dime, just to argue for the women’s locker room. I don’t even think girls in the locker room even knew she did that,” Baszler went on. “There are many MMA fans that would never have watched professional wrestling because it’s that scary f word, right? It’s not real. And I think they tuned in just because, ‘Let’s see what happens here.’ Will she ever get the credit? Maybe like years down the road. But I think that’s something Ronda, for her own sanity, I’m glad she doesn’t care to receive the credit in the moment because she did a lot. I could tell you a hundred more stories like that,” Baszler added. “I think she knew that (she had the backstage pull to demand more time for the women). That’s why she was able to do stuff like that, and it was just so smart. I remember that story I told you. I remember her telling me that, and I’m like, ‘Why did you buy your own ticket? They would have flown you there to have a meeting.’ She’s like, ‘No, because if I buy my own ticket, they can’t cancel the meeting on me because I bought my ticket, so I’m going to make sure.’ So it was the little stuff like that

title: 5 Greatest Roman Reigns Matches at WWE Crown Jewel — The Crowning Five

body: October 23, 2026 By Nicholas Paul WWE , History , Pro Wrestling , WWE Universe Following this past Monday’s promo segment between World Heavyweight Champion Roman Reigns and WWE Undisputed Champion Sami Zayn , momentum is officially in full gear as the two prepare to face off on November 6 at WWE’s latest PLE, Crown Jewel . Few events match the scale and glamor of WWE Crown Jewel, bringing stadium-level drama to fans worldwide. It’s where champion-versus-champion action takes center stage on a global platform. As this week’s episode of Raw kicked off, the two briefly met in the parking lot. Reigns’ black SUV pulled into the arena garage when another vehicle appeared, revealing Zayn. Reigns’ visible surprise at seeing the SmackDown World Champion on his show transitioned into the live arena, where the two faced off in front of a packed crowd. As the champions made their separate entrances, the mood initially seemed warm and friendly. The segment opened with a hug before Zayn admitted that after capturing the world title, he now fully understands the immense pressure and burden Reigns once spoke of back when Sami served as the “Honorary Uce” in The Bloodline . The World Heavyweight Champion questioned whether Zayn had come to Monday’s show to help deal with 946, led by Royce Keys . However, the Undisputed WWE Champion refused, stating he couldn’t prioritize that business over his responsibilities on SmackDown, causing tensions to quickly flare up. Before leaving the ring, Reigns fired a parting shot at Zayn, suggesting that based on his track record, he might not even remain champion by Crown Jewel – a direct reference to Zayn’s previous world title reign that lasted only nine days . The segment injected just the right amount of heat and tension into a pairing many have questioned might lack the elements of a truly great match and was only scheduled to appease the popularity of both with the Saudi fans . Suddenly, the stakes feel personal. Heading into Crown Jewel, Zayn will be making only his second career appearance at the event, following his 2023 kickoff show victory over JD McDonagh. Meanwhile, Reigns will be stepping into his seventh match at the show. Crown Jewel has essentially served as “The OTC’s” personal kingdom over the last several years. With that decorated history in mind, let’s count down Roman Reigns’ five best matches at the event. Kicking off our list is Roman Reigns’ most recent Crown Jewel bout , and the only one held outside Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. In this rematch with Bronson Reed – following their first encounter at Clash in Paris – expectations for Reed were surprisingly high for a few reasons. First, WWE typically splits the first two bouts of a major feud to make the deciding rubber match feel even bigger. body: By Joseph Ryan Published Oct 23, 2026, 3:18 PM GMT+1 Joe is a writer at GIVEMESPORT with more than a year of experience covering football. His work has appeared across the Football Writers' Association, Dave.Sport, The Non-League Paper, and Football Park. A journalism graduate from the University of Kent, Joe was nominated for both the Football Writers' Association Hugh McIlvanney Young Sports Writer of the Year Award and the Chartered Institute of Journalists Young Sports Writer of the Year Award, recognising his emerging talent in sports journalism. Away from football, Joe is an avid sports fan with a particular passion for hurling, Gaelic football, cycling, and basketball. Sign in to your GiveMeSport account Cody Rhodes has revealed his honest thoughts on whether WWE icon The Rock will ever step foot back in the ring. The 54-year-old wrestler-turned actor last competed at WrestleMania 40, teaming with his cousin, Roman Reigns , to defeat Rhodes and Seth Rollins in the main event of night one of the 2024 extravaganza. The Rock pinned Rhodes in that match to score the victory for his team. Such a finish led most to believe that a singles match between the pair was inevitable, but it has never happened. Their unresolved animosity remains one of wrestling's most tantalising narratives, a feud slowly built on the road to WrestleMania 40 as The Rock stepped off his Hollywood pedestal to block Rhodes from capturing wrestling immortality. While a collision between the pair would be one of the grandest spectacles WWE could conjure, there is no getting away from the fact that The Rock is many years past his physical prime . During a recent appearance on Chris Van Vliet's Insight podcast, Rhodes gave a brutally honest response when he was asked if The Rock would return to action. “It’s not that I’m evading that answer," he began. "It’s that I don’t really know how to answer because I think personally he has a couple of matches probably left to do." The American Nightmare also conceded that The Rock could realistically walk away from the squared circle for good. Having already authored some of the industry’s most indelible moments, his legacy as a Mount Rushmore figure and one of the greatest WWE Superstars in history is securely set in stone. "I think that personally, but I also know looking at WrestleMania 40 and another guy who he’s given all, continues to give all as part of the board. He could easily say that was a great final piece as a performer in a wrestling ring. That’ll be up to him." Ultimately, Rhodes stressed that the decision rests with The Rock himself, rather than WWE or the fans hoping to see him compete again. "That’ll certainly be up to him if there’s more and what those matches might be." Realistically, though, two potential matches stand out above the rest. The first of those is the long-teased clash between The Rock and Roman Reigns , although a meeting between 'The Final Boss' and Rhodes arguably has more storyline build behind it.

body: October 23, 2026 By Josh Prost WWE NXT , Pro Wrestling , WWE , WWE Universe Since Zilla Fatu set foot in NXT, he’s made one thing clear. He may be the son of the late Umaga and part of the legendary Anoa’i wrestling family, but he wants to do things on his terms and not be a part of the nepotism conversation. Meanwhile, being a multi-generational wrestler is something that the members of BirthRight are proud of. Over the past few weeks, BirthRight have been trying to make Zilla join the group. But he’s said no several times, leading to multiple attacks on him. Charlie Dempsey, the son of William Regal, has been the most vocal about that problem. A match between the two men was made for Halloween Havoc after weeks of tension. On the October 20, 2026 episode of NXT, Zilla demanded that the match be a “Spin the Wheel, Make the Deal” match, which means a spinning wheel decides the stipulation. This could be an interesting scenario for both Dempsey and Zilla, as they both want to win the match. One thing that’s been refreshing is the fact that Zilla is unafraid to do things his own way. WWE could’ve stuck him with The Bloodline to bypass NXT completely, but they didn’t do that. He told everyone that he wants to be his own man, which is why BirthRight is angry with him. His first match on the brand was a Fatal Four-Way NXT Championship match won by Grayson Waller at NXT Heatwave. Since then, he’s been beaten down by BirthRight without much resistance. If he doesn’t win, that’ll be very embarrassing for him. Dempsey also has a lot to deal with. Like the rest of the faction, he is sick of BirthRight being beaten and not taken seriously. He’s out to prove that the faction isn’t a joke, which is why beating Zilla means so much to him. A loss would severely damage BirthRight’s credibility. If he loses at Halloween Havoc, it seems like BirthRight’s days as a faction in NXT will be numbered. When someone calls for a “Spin the Wheel, Make the Deal” match, a wheel is brought out with many different stip ulations on it . They are regular stipulations like any other match, but they are all Halloween – themed, adding to the spookiness of the PLE. Halloween Havoc in 2024 had two matches like that. Tony D’Angelo retained the NXT North American Championship against Oba Femi in a Tables, Ladders, and Scares match , while Fallon Henley beat Kelani Jordan to capture the NXT Women’s North American Championship in a Gauntlet match . Zilla and Dempsey won’t know what the stipulation will be until the wheel is spun. They’ll have to modify their game plan based on what the spinner lands on. It could be a n ambulance match, a no-disqualification match, a street fight , among others. Things legal in one match may not be legal in another , creating many challenges . Adapting to the match’s rules will be the key to an exciting match that ends a great feud. title: Hardcore Championship
raw_title: Hardcore Championship - WWE
summary_src: Hardcore Championship WWE
body: Hardcore Championship Retired More Share Options More Share Options Share close facebook x threads email Championships Undisputed WWE Championship 1963 - Present The Hardcore Championship was one of the most unique championships to ever be defended in WWE. It was originally given to Mick Foley, then known as Mankind, by the Chairman, Mr. McMahon. The rules of how to defend the championship even evolved with time, and it was eventually defended under 24/7 rules. That meant that the Hardcore Champion could be pinned at any time of day, any day of the week, as long as a referee was around to make the three-count. The Hardcore Championship found its way around the waists of a very eclectic group of Superstars ranging from the likes of Mankind, Crash Holly, Big Show, Hardcore Holly, Big Boss Man and Kane, among numerous others. title: AEW New Year’s Smash Set for January 1-2 in Georgia
raw_title: AEW New Year’s Smash announced for January 1 & 2 in Georgia
summary_src: The promotion announced on Friday that New Year’s Smash will occur on January 1 & 2 at the Gateway Center Arena in College Park, Georgia.
body: AEW will kick off 2027 with New Year’s Smash over two nights in Georgia. The promotion announced on Friday that New Year’s Smash will occur on January 1 & 2 at the Gateway Center Arena in College Park, Georgia. New Year’s Day lands on a Friday and will see AEW tape an edition of Dynamite followed by a Collision taping the next day. With AEW taping its television, it would allow for any AEW talent traveling to Japan for Wrestle Kingdom 21 on Monday, January 4. Based on recent angles, it would appear several AEW talents would be booked for Wrestle Kingdom, with teases of Kenny Omega, Will Ospreay, MJF, Jon Moxley, and Adam Copeland among them. AEW wraps up its year on December 23 with the Holiday Bash editions of Dynamite and Collision, followed by a nine-day break before the tapings in Georgia.
summary: AEW will open 2027 with New Year’s Smash on January 1 and 2 at the Gateway Center Arena in College Park, Georgia. The promotion will tape Dynamite on the first night followed by a Collision taping the next day. This schedule gives talent time to travel to Japan for Wrestle Kingdom 21 after AEW’s final shows of the year on December 23 and a subsequent nine-day break.

title: Injury Update: Willow Nightingale Provides Latest On Broken Hand Recovery
raw_title: Willow Nightingale Provides Update on Broken Hand Recovery
summary_src: Willow Nightingale’s broken hand is getting better, but she’s not out of the woods just yet. The AEW star has now given fans a fresh update on her recovery and revealed she’s still doing daily treatment to help the injury heal.
body: Nightingale took to her Instagram story and shared a photo of herself behind the wheel with a bone stimulator on her injured hand. She said there’s been progress, although the hand still isn’t completely healed. “It’s better, but not 100% healed. Still using that bone stimulator everyday, even if I have to fit it in while stuck in traffic.” The update comes after Nightingale has continued to appear on AEW television despite the injury. Fightful Select previously reported that AEW planned from the moment she got hurt to keep her involved on television while her hand recovered rather than pulling her from programming completely . The injury hasn’t completely stopped Nightingale from wrestling either. Despite dealing with the broken hand, she went on to face Thekla at AEW All Out last month and even returned to the ring again on the October 6 episode of Collision. That came after Nightingale lost the AEW Women’s World Championship to Mercedes Moné at All In. She passed out in the Statement Maker to end her title reign, and the broken hand only added another obstacle for her in the weeks that followed. For now, Nightingale’s update makes it clear the hand still needs more time, even though she’s seeing improvement. She’s apparently staying committed to the recovery process wherever she can squeeze it in — even if that means getting some treatment done while sitting in traffic. He focuses on delivering reliable coverage across WWE, AEW, and major wrestling promotions.

title: Rey Mysterio eyed for 2027 WWE retirement
raw_title: Update on potential Rey Mysterio WWE retirement | Exclusive
summary_src: Rey Mysterio’s legendary career in the ring could be winding down soon. Even as he entered his 50s, Mysterio was reluctant to put a timeline on retirement given how much he’s enjoying his work and how much better his body has been feeling due to treatment options.
body: Rey Mysterio’s legendary career in the ring could be winding down soon. Even as he entered his 50s, Mysterio was reluctant to put a timeline on retirement given how much he’s enjoying his work and how much better his body has been feeling due to treatment options . But a report emerged from WrestleVotes this week saying there’s “backstage chatter” within WWE regarding a potential Mysterio retirement in 2027. The report said WWE has “started to discuss ideas” on how to present Mysterio’s in-ring farewell. Mysterio, one of the greatest luchadores of all time, was inducted into the Wrestling Observer Hall of Fame in 2010 and WWE Hall of Fame in 2023. When presented with the idea of a WWE Hall of Fame induction, Mysterio made it known at the time that he was not done in the ring yet and was going into the HOF as an active wrestler. Longevity, even while dealing with various injuries over the years, has been one of Mysterio’s strongest attributes. His staying power has allowed him to work in WWE alongside his son Dominik. Mysterio’s daughter Aalyah is now also signed to the WWE Performance Center. It’s likely that the 51-year-old Mysterio will have a visible presence on WWE programming even after he retires. He is already the on-screen general manager of Lucha Libre AAA. We’ve seen John Cena, AJ Styles, and Brock Lesnar all retire over the past year. In addition to Mysterio possibly hanging up his boots, AEW’s Adam Copeland has announced that 2027 will be his last year as an active wrestler . Mysterio had previously been reluctant to set a retirement timeline despite turning 50, citing how much he enjoys performing and how treatment has improved his physical condition. The report notes his Hall of Fame inductions into the Wrestling Observer Hall of Fame in 2010 and WWE Hall of Fame in 2023 as an active competitor, along with his longevity that enabled him to compete alongside son Dominik while daughter Aalyah is now signed to the WWE Performance Center.

title: TKO CEO Says WWE Daily Monitoring Crown Jewel Location
raw_title: TKO CEO: WWE is 'daily monitoring' whether to move Crown Jewel from Saudi Arabia amid deadly attacks
body: Ari Emanuel, the CEO of WWE's parent company — TKO Group Holdings, Inc. — told Fox News on Friday that the combat sports behemoth is "daily monitoring" the situation in Saudi Arabia as the country continues to be attacked by deadly missile and drone strikes lead by Houthi rebels. "Right now, everything is still set [for WWE Crown Jewel]. This weekend coming up in Abu Dhabi, we have a UFC fight. We have, in the middle of November, a Frieze art show. So, so far, so good — nothing's been cancelled." "We have a whole team kind of working on this, and kind of when — and if that doesn't happen, where we can move it. It's a daily monitoring." WWE's decision to push forward with its Crown Jewel event has faced increasing scrutiny as the event draws nearer and fighting in the region continues to escalate. The U.S. State Department on Wednesday ordered non-emergency government employees and their families to leave Saudi Arabia following a series of deadly attacks targeting airports and other infrastructure across the country, which have claimed the lives of at least 20 people and injured at least 370. U.S. State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott confirmed the order Wednesday, stating that "the safety and security of Department personnel and their families remain our highest priority, and we will continue to take all necessary steps to protect and support them." On the same day, the U.S. Embassy in Saudi Arabia additionally issued a security alert warning that the conflict in the country could escalate rapidly. Several other major sporting events in Saudi Arabia have already been postponed due to the attacks, including the Six Kings Slam tennis tournament and Saudi International golf tournament. Despite that, WWE Crown Jewel remains one of two major combat sports still scheduled to take place in Riyadh in the coming weeks. The other, a WBC super middleweight world title fight between star boxer Saul "Canelo" Alvarez and Christian Mbilli on Oct. 31 , has faced significant scrutiny from fans, media and even teams of fighters involved. Noted boxing trainer Robert Garcia, who's readying boxer Lindolfo Delgado for an IBF super lightweight title on the Canelo-Mbilli undercard, has repeatedly voiced fears over his safety and the safety of his team in recent days. For now, WWE Crown Jewel remains scheduled to take place at the Riyadh Season Stadium, headlined by two champion-vs.-champion matches featuring Roman Reigns, Sami Zayn, Liv Morgan and the "SmackDown" women's champion at the time of the event.
summary: Ari Emanuel revealed that TKO Group Holdings is closely tracking the situation in Saudi Arabia amid ongoing Houthi rebel attacks involving missiles and drones. The company has a contingency team preparing potential alternative venues for the Crown Jewel event if needed while continuing with upcoming shows in Abu Dhabi and elsewhere. This comes as the U.S. State Department advised non-emergency personnel to depart Saudi Arabia following strikes that have killed at least 20 people.

title: WWE’s John Cena Classic Could Go Head-To-Head With AEW Worlds End — Report
raw_title: WWE’s John Cena Classic Could Go Head-To-Head With AEW Worlds End — Report
body: 0 A new update suggests WWE’s John Cena Classic might go head-to-head with AEW Worlds End. The former 17-time WWE Champion announced the John Cena Classic during his special appearance at Backlash in May. Earlier reports indicated that the tournament could take place in December to coincide with the first anniversary of the legend’s retirement. Cena himself confirmed later that the tournament will take place in December. However, he didn’t reveal a specific date, though reports noted it could be on December 12, the same day as Wrestlepalooza in Perth, Australia. According to WrestleVotes Radio on Fightful Select , WWE could be looking at two dates for the John Cena Classic. The report noted that a source couldn’t confirm whether the tournament would take place on December 12 in the U.S. after Wrestlepalooza in Perth, Australia. The source also couldn’t confirm whether it would take place the following weekend on December 19. If WWE chooses December 19, the John Cena Classic would go head-to-head with AEW’s Worlds End pay-per-view. AAA’s Guerra De Titanes event also takes place later that same evening. One WWE source noted Saturday, December 5, isn’t a viable option, saying the promotion wouldn’t want to host major events on three consecutive weekends. The post WWE’s John Cena Classic Could Go Head-To-Head With AEW Worlds End — Report appeared first on Wrestlezone .
summary: The former 17-time WWE Champion revealed the John Cena Classic during his special appearance at Backlash in May. Per WrestleVotes Radio on Fightful Select , WWE could be looking at two dates for the John Cena Classic.

title: WWE Crown Jewel Stadium Construction Underway in Saudi Arabia Amid Security Concerns — WATCH
raw_title: WATCH: WWE Crown Jewel Stadium Construction Underway in Saudi Arabia Amid Security Concerns
body: 0 Construction of the Riyadh Season Stadium for WWE Crown Jewel is underway despite regional security worries. The 2026 WWE Crown Jewel Premium Live Event is scheduled for KAFD, Saudi Arabia, on Saturday, November 7, 2026. As they did for Royal Rumble this year, the country’s General Entertainment Authority has begun constructing the Riyadh Season Stadium. This is a temporary outdoor venue for the show. The recent attacks by the Iran-backed Houthi rebel group on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh remain a concern ahead of WWE Crown Jewel. Authorities have instructed U.S. citizens traveling to and from the Middle East to exercise extreme vigilance. Recent reports indicate the promotion plans to proceed as originally planned. body: AEW Former WWE and AEW star Jake Hager suffered a devastating blow to the eye at last month's Power Slap 23 event, one that left him in need of emergency surgery. According to a new report, more operations may be awaiting him in the future now. At Power Slap 23 in Lubbock, Texas, Hager battled independent wrestler Johnny Magna in a slap fight, with the second round proving particularly rough for the former WWE World Heavyweight Champion. Magna landed a hit so powerful that Hager's left eye began bleeding. Hager and his team then demanded that it be ruled the contact as a foul. Instead, the officials awarded Magna the win via referee stoppage, leaving Hager with both a ruptured eye and a loss. Following the gruesome scene, Hager's partner Patricia Blackburn revealed that he underwent an operation on the affected eye. Further details on Hager's condition were unknown at the time due the family wanting to keep the situation private. Hager is no stranger to physical contact, having backgrounds in pro wrestling, mixed martial arts, and now, Power Slap. He initially retired from wrestling in 2025; the former "All-American American" later returned to in-ring action in June 2026 for a pair of shows with World Wrestling Council in Puerto Rico. His aforementioned Power Slap fight marked the third of his career.

body: During the October 23, 2026, episode of the Duke LovesRasslin podcast, Dudley discussed AEW’s handling of former WWE talent and questioned why so many established wrestlers arrive in the promotion with major momentum, only to eventually find themselves sitting on the sidelines. Dudley explained that he’s noticed a pattern with wrestlers who join AEW. They receive plenty of attention when they first arrive, but that excitement doesn’t always translate into consistent television appearances. “The one thing, you know, I’ve noticed with teams or people coming from WWE or just new guys in general to the scene is that, you know, they start off great and hot in the very beginning and then all of a sudden it’s like they’re not used anymore.” That’s when Dudley brought up The Hardy Boyz. Considering everything Matt and Jeff have accomplished throughout their careers, he admitted that he never expected AEW to struggle with finding something for them to do. What made the situation even more surprising was that the brothers personally told him how unhappy they were. “You have so many people that are very good hands that are used one minute and then not used the next. And you know what? The one team that I never thought I would see that happen to and it did. And I spoke to them personally and they were telling me about their frustration were the Hardy Boys.” Dudley went even further, revealing that he had visited AEW on multiple occasions while exploring the possibility of working as a producer. During those visits, he heard wrestlers discussing how they weren’t being used on television and were spending their time backstage instead. “I would have never thought in a million years that they would be put to the side or be the one of the ones that when I went to go a couple of times to, you know, see about being a producer, you know, I was told, you know, by certain people, oh well, you know, we’re not on this week. title: End of an Era: D-Von Dudley Admits He’s Ready to Retire as Constant Travel Takes Its Toll
raw_title: D-Von Dudley Admits He’s Ready to Retire as Constant Travel Takes Its Toll
summary_src: D-Von Dudley has spent decades traveling the world as one of professional wrestling’s biggest names, but the WWE Hall of Famer is getting tired of life on the road.
body: During the October 23, 2026, episode of the D-Von and the Duke podcast , Dudley opened up about his future while discussing the possibility of taking on more acting roles in Hollywood. The conversation started when host Duke Loves Wrestling brought up a hypothetical situation involving Tyler Perry offering Dudley a major role in a big-budget movie. Dudley didn’t hesitate when asked whether he would accept the opportunity. Dudley went on to explain how different Hollywood productions are from the wrestling business. During his WWE career, performers often had to arrange their own rental cars, pay for hotel rooms, and deal with grueling travel schedules. Hollywood productions, on the other hand, have been much more accommodating during his experiences filming commercials. While discussing the possibility of landing roles in major film franchises, Dudley made an admission about his future. That doesn’t mean Dudley has stopped enjoying his interactions with wrestling fans. In fact, he made it clear that meeting people at conventions remains something he genuinely loves. The problem is everything he has to go through just to get there. “I enjoy the Comic Cons. I love talking to the people, interacting with them, you know, but what’s killing me lately is the flights.” Dudley didn’t hold back when describing just how frustrating airline travel has become. The former Dudley Boyz member also revealed that he recently crossed paths with WWE Superstar Damian Priest at an airport. Dudley was returning from Dallas while Priest was coming from Miami, and he decided to ask how WWE talent had been handling the ongoing travel headaches. According to Dudley, Priest told him the situation wasn’t much better for WWE’s current roster. Dudley said Priest acknowledged that things had improved somewhat in recent weeks, but flight problems remained an issue. That conversation only reinforced what Dudley has been experiencing while traveling to conventions and appearances nearly every week. “I’m on the road every week with the ComicCons and appearances and stuff like that. So it’s like okay um am I the only one dealing with this? You know, it it’s hard. It’s really hard. And sometime the traveling is what gets you more than anything.” After decades of working WWE schedules, traveling around the country, and continuing to make public appearances following his in-ring retirement, Dudley clearly isn’t enjoying the airport routine anymore. He hasn’t announced that he’s officially ending his convention appearances, and he certainly isn’t ruling out future entertainment projects. If anything, Dudley sounded enthusiastic about the possibility of trading some of those exhausting airport trips for opportunities in Hollywood. For now, D-Von Dudley is still connecting with fans and remaining active in wrestling through his academy, but his comments make one thing clear: he’s reaching the point where the travel is becoming more trouble than it’s worth. title: Cody Rhodes Hopes Street Fighter Cast Makes Their Way Over To WWE
raw_title: Cody Rhodes Hopes Street Fighter Cast Makes Their Way Over To WWE
summary_src: Cody Rhodes would love to see the cast of Street Fighter come to WWE. With the release of the Street Fighter movie on October 16, Cody Rhodes has been making the rounds with more interviews.
body: Cody Rhodes would love to see the cast of Street Fighter come to WWE. With the release of the Street Fighter movie on October 16, Cody Rhodes has been making the rounds with more interviews. Rhodes played the role of Guile in this film, working with stars such as Andrew Koji, Jason Momoa, Callina Liang, and more. Speaking on The Rich Eisen Show , Rhodes was asked if he went up to Jason Momoa and invited him to WWE. The American Nightmare didn’t give a direct answer, but he did say that he explained to everybody in the production that WWE loves to have celebrity guests. “I think I tried to slowly, with everybody in the production, explain how we’re very open. We love to have guests. We love to try a celebrity moment. We love to promote the things that our boys and girls are in. So throughout the course of the deal, it was fun to explain to a whole different bubble. Whereas I’m in the wrestling bubble, what I do. It’s an open, that’s an open invite. Cause there’s some wrestlers in the cast that may not know they’re wrestlers. Like, Olivier [Richters], the Dutch Giant, who plays Zangief, is seven foot. I think he’s the biggest actor. That’s a no-brainer. Get him out. You don’t have to do anything. People run into you. Maybe one guy slams you. Maybe it’s me. No, there’s a lot of connections. So, I do hope they make their way over and see what I do as the day job, cause there was great synergy with WWE and Street Fighter.” In another interview, Rhodes said that he personally thinks The Rock has a couple of matches left in WWE. Fans can read his full comments here . If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.
