title: TKO CEO Monitors Saudi Situation for WWE Crown Jewel
raw_title: TKO CEO Ari Emanuel gives WWE Crown Jewel update amid deadly attacks in Saudi Arabia
body: Ari Emanuel, the CEO of WWE's parent company — TKO Group Holdings, Inc. — told Fox News on Friday that the combat sports behemoth is "daily monitoring" the situation in Saudi Arabia as the country continues to be attacked by deadly missile and drone strikes lead by Houthi rebels. "Right now, everything is still set [for WWE Crown Jewel]. This weekend coming up in Abu Dhabi, we have a UFC fight. We have, in the middle of November, a Frieze art show. So, so far, so good — nothing's been cancelled." "We have a whole team kind of working on this, and kind of when — and if that doesn't happen, where we can move it. It's a daily monitoring." WWE's decision to push forward with its Crown Jewel event has faced increasing scrutiny as the event draws nearer and fighting in the region continues to escalate. The U.S. State Department on Wednesday ordered non-emergency government employees and their families to leave Saudi Arabia following a series of deadly attacks targeting airports and other infrastructure across the country, which have claimed the lives of at least 20 people and injured at least 370. U.S. State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott confirmed the order Wednesday, stating that "the safety and security of Department personnel and their families remain our highest priority, and we will continue to take all necessary steps to protect and support them." On the same day, the U.S. Embassy in Saudi Arabia additionally issued a security alert warning that the conflict in the country could escalate rapidly. Several other major sporting events in Saudi Arabia have already been postponed due to the attacks, including the Six Kings Slam tennis tournament and Saudi International golf tournament. Despite that, WWE Crown Jewel remains one of two major combat sports still scheduled to take place in Riyadh in the coming weeks. The other, a WBC super middleweight world title fight between star boxer Saul "Canelo" Alvarez and Christian Mbilli on Oct. 31 , has faced significant scrutiny from fans, media and even teams of fighters involved. Noted boxing trainer Robert Garcia, who's readying boxer Lindolfo Delgado for an IBF super lightweight title on the Canelo-Mbilli undercard, has repeatedly voiced fears over his safety and the safety of his team in recent days. For now, WWE Crown Jewel remains scheduled to take place at the Riyadh Season Stadium, headlined by two champion-vs.-champion matches featuring Roman Reigns, Sami Zayn, Liv Morgan and the "SmackDown" women's champion at the time of the event.
summary: TKO Group Holdings CEO Ari Emanuel stated the company is daily monitoring the situation in Saudi Arabia amid ongoing missile and drone attacks by Houthi rebels that have killed at least 20 people. Emanuel confirmed that WWE Crown Jewel remains scheduled as planned while noting upcoming UFC and art events in the region have not been cancelled. He added that a team is prepared with contingency plans if the event needs to be relocated.

title: Bron Breakker cracks up at Solo Sikoa’s antics
raw_title: WWE’s Bron Breakker breaks character thanks to Solo Sikoa’s funny antics
body: It's no secret that WWE Superstar Solo Sikoa has a big personality, and it got The Vision's Bron Breakker to break character during a house show. During a live event in Palm Desert, California, Sikoa teamed up with Oba Femi and LA Knight to take on The Vision's Breakker, Austin Theory, and Bronson Reed. At one point, he had his head slammed into the turnbuckle by Reed. After the second time, he began voluntarily throwing himself head-first into it. If you watch closely, you can see Breakker turn away the first time it happens. When Sikoa throws himself into the corner, you can tell Breakker is amused and smiling. Luckily, the match was able to continue without a hitch. The babyface trio won the six-man tag team match. We'll have to wait and see if WWE runs the match again sometime soon. Currently, Femi is feuding with The Vision. He recently beat Breakker by disqualification at Sunday Night's Main Event in September 2026. A returning Reed, who came back from a bicep injury, interfered in the match. The following month at Money in the Bank, the "Ruler" defeated Reed in a singles match. Meanwhile, Sikoa and Knight have formed a partnership over the last few months. They are in the middle of a heated feud that involves Royce Keys' 946 faction. It might lead to a match at Survivor Series: WarGames next month. Sikoa recently rejoined Roman Reigns' Bloodline. The 946 have been going after the Bloodline, and WarGames may be the only way to settle their differences. Knight is coming off a loss to Reigns at Money in the Bank. He unsuccessfully challenged for the World Heavyweight Championship. This was the second time he lost to Reigns in a PLE singles match after Crown Jewel 2023.

Bron Breakker, part of the opposing team with Austin Theory and Reed, turned away and smiled at the display. The babyface team of Sikoa, Oba Femi and LA Knight defeated Breakker, Theory and Reed in the six-man tag match.

body: Cody Rhodes explains how modern WWE’s executive core made filming Street Fighter easier for him. Street Fighter was released in theaters on October 16, with Cody Rhodes and Roman Reigns playing Guile and Akuma, respectively. Speaking on The Rich Eisen Show , Rhodes talked about filming Street Fighter right after winning the Undisputed WWE Championship at SummerSlam 2025. “I was so lucky, I won the title from John Cena at MetLife for SummerSlam, then went and filmed without doing the, the usual wrestling, put him out, stretcher him out, he’s gone and then big return. It was just… I think the world is all aware of what we’re doing now in terms of, oh, he’s going to film Street Fighter. He doesn’t need to do all that. Modern WWE with its executive core and, you know, Nick Khan and Triple H allowing it to go that way made it very easy, made it very easy. Other guys filled in while I was gone and I was able to come back and get right back into it.” Elsewhere in the interview, Rhodes said he hopes that the cast of Street Fighter would make their way to WWE. title: Match Made: Cody Rhodes-CM Punk WrestleMania 43 Rumor Shot Down: 5 Guesses For Night 1 Main Event, Including Breakker vs. Gunther
raw_title: Cody Rhodes-CM Punk WrestleMania 43 Rumor Shot Down: 5 Guesses For Night 1 Main Event, Including Breakker vs. Gunther
body: Recently, a report suggested a SummerSlam rematch between CM Punk and Cody Rhodes was penciled in as the Night 1 headliner. However, on Friday, Wrestling Observer’s Dave Meltzer claimed Rhodes vs. Punk II actually was not the current pick to main event on Saturday. While Night 2 is still expected to conclude with a matchup between Oba Femi and Roman Reigns, we offer up some early guesses for the first evening’s headliner. The faction 946, led by Royce Keys, is one of the hottest acts on RAW right now. But chances are the group will lose in a rumored War Games match versus The Bloodline. However, that doesn’t mean their push will end. If WWE creative believes in Keys and his crew’s upside, it would not be surprising if they took a chance by moving him to SmackDown and putting him in the Night 1 main event. A perfect hero for him to face off against would be Rhodes, and the night could end with a rare heel leaving with the title belt. With Kevin Owens back and Sami Zayn a heel WWE champion, the two friends have renewed their legendary rivalry. After Zayn had a very short reign in the summer, it seems very possible he holds on to the belt until WrestleMania. The beloved Owens shockingly winning the Royal Rumble and choosing to face Zayn would be entertaining television. Furthermore, finally becoming a world champion again a year after returning from a career-threatening injury would be a top feel-good moment in 2027. After Bron Breakker fell just short in this year’s Money in the Bank match, he will be a popular choice to win the Royal Rumble in January. Choosing to face Reigns in a spear vs. spear matchup would be fun. But he could go in a different direction. It feels like a matter of time before Gunther gets the WWE title on SmackDown. If he were able to get it before WrestleMania 43, a Breakker vs. Gunther clash would be a fresh showcase of two stars that will be main event players for many years to come. Going back to the idea of Gunther getting the WWE title back, it would not be surprising if WWE found a way to get Rhodes into a main event match to face off with the man he had a rivalry with earlier this year. However, with speculation growing about a Rhodes heel turn, what if it came at WrestleMania as he went to new levels to defeat the Austrian? It would be even more interesting if the match was a double turn that created something fans haven’t seen: A babyface Gunther. While it is more likely that Penta will try to use his MITB contract after WrestleMania, maybe he cashes in before, and WWE supercharges his push by putting him in one of the two main events? If they did, he should get the win. But who could be a sacrificial lamb and great opponent that would not be hurt by a loss? Enter Seth Rollins. The Visionary has been MIA since SummerSlam. Making a return soon and working his way into a title match by Mania could happen, and a Penta vs. Rollins match could be dynamite.
summary: Per Sportsnaut: recently, a report suggested a SummerSlam rematch between CM Punk and Cody Rhodes was penciled in as the Night 1 headliner. Punk II actually was not the current pick to main event on Saturday.

title: Results Recap: Hall’s AEW Dynamite Review 10.21.26
raw_title: Hall’s AEW Dynamite Review 10.21.26
body: Dynamite Date: October 21, 2026 Location: Watsco Center, Coral Gables, Florida Commentators: Excalibur, Taz, Tony Schiavone We’re done with WrestleDream and Will Ospreay is still the World Champion, having survived Clockwork Carnage. That probably isn’t the biggest surprise but he was pinned a few times in the match and that very well could set up some challengers for him in the coming weeks. Those coming weeks also include Full Gear so let’s get to it. Non-title. The Family jumps the Bucks to start fast and they’re sent outside, with the Bucks being sent into the steps. A powerbomb sends Nick onto the announcers’ table and another puts him through it. Back in and the double standing clothesline hits Matt and three piledrivers knock him cold. Doyle bearhugs Nick out and it’s a double pin on the Bucks at 2:49. The Bucks had no significant offense here whatsoever and it was a total squash. This would be Kyle Fletcher/Kevin Knight for the Family. Copeland and Knight start things off with Copeland hitting an early clothesline. Knight is right back up to choke in the corner, earning himself a swinging neckbreaker. Ospreay comes in to face Fletcher and it’s already time to slug it out. Fletcher gets knocked down for the standing corkscrew moonsault and it’s back to Copeland. Ospreay’s running hurricanrana is blocked though and a standing Doomsday Device dropkick drops Copeland as we take a break. We come back with Ospreay in trouble and getting kneed in the face. The brainbuster is countered into a Stundog Millionaire but Knight is over to cut off the tag. A Phenomenal Forearm gets Ospreay out of trouble though and it’s back to Copeland to start firing off the clotheslines. Knight gets back up with a springboard clothesline of his own and Fletcher’s Michinoku Driver gets two. Everything breaks down and Fletcher knocks Ospreay off the apron. Cue Kazuchika Okada to distract Copeland, who is fine enough to give Fletcher a Killswitch. The spear hits Knight but Okada gets in a belt shot to Copeland. That and a brainbuster are enough to give Fletcher the pin at 13:22. Rating : B-. This was your standard big time tag match and it was a good way to set up a few things. Copeland has quite a few options for singles matches and it seems like Okada is going to be up next. There is definitely something to be done with Copeland going after the World Title but warming up with Okada isn’t a bad idea either. Okada’s diabolical smile after costing Copeland is great, but he stops to come in and beat on Copeland instead. More of the Family comes in and Ospreay is beaten down as well. Fletcher holds up the World Title and the lights go out. Darby Allin, the returning Steven Borden and a Young Buck run in for the save. Borden: “I’m back. For Blood & Guts.” On one hand, I get the idea, but with the Bucks getting wrecked, Borden having had about five matches, and there only being so much reason for him to hate the Family, this feels like a less than thrilling Blood & Guts tea

title: Ric Flair Rushed to Hospital After Bloody Fall Outside Florida Restaurant Amid Blood Clot Scare
raw_title: Ric Flair Rushed to Hospital After Bloody Fall Outside Florida Restaurant Amid Blood Clot Scare
summary_src: Ric Flair’s health situation just got even more concerning. The WWE Hall of Famer was rushed to a hospital in Florida on Friday, October 23, after suffering a nasty fall that left him bleeding from his face.
body: Flair was at Wagamama in Tampa on Friday morning when the situation unfolded. According to TMZ, the Nature Boy got up from the bar, left his phone and drink behind, and walked across the street before suddenly falling. The fall left Flair with cuts to his head and eye, with significant bleeding around his eye. There are also concerns that the 77-year-old wrestling legend may have suffered a concussion. Emergency medical personnel responded to the scene, where Flair was treated before being loaded into an ambulance and transported to the hospital. A photo obtained by TMZ shows first responders gathered around him following the incident. The latest scare comes at an especially difficult time for Flair, who had already been dealing with another serious medical issue earlier that same day. Just hours before being hospitalized, Flair announced on Twitter that he was canceling his scheduled appearance at Washington State Horror Con in Seattle because doctors had discovered a blood clot in his leg. “Unfortunately, I Am Dealing With A Blood Clot In My Leg, And My Doctors Have Limited My Travel To 3–4 Hours. Seattle Falls Outside That Range, And As Disappointed As I Am, I Have To Put My Health And Recovery First.” Flair wasn’t taking the situation lightly. He specifically warned fans about the dangers associated with blood clots and explained why he was following his doctors’ orders rather than risking additional complications. “Blood Clots Are Extremely Serious And Can Be Life-Threatening. We Have Seen This Recently With Jalen Hurts And The Complications Involving Blood Clots In His Lungs. It Is A Reminder That This Is Not Something To Take Lightly, And I Must Follow Medical Advice.” The Nature Boy also revealed that doctors have already scheduled a procedure to address the affected vein, which could eventually allow him to resume traveling without the current restrictions. “I’m Scheduled To Have A Procedure To Strip The Affected Vein, Which My Doctors Expect Will Allow Me To Be Cleared For More Travel Afterward.” There’s no indication at this point that Flair’s fall was caused by his blood clot, and the full extent of his injuries remains unclear. There’s also no word on whether his hospitalization will affect the upcoming procedure. Flair has dealt with several health setbacks in recent years. In 2025, he revealed that he was battling melanoma and later suffered a torn rotator cuff that forced him to leave an AEW Dynamite taping before appearing on television. The latest incident puts Flair back in the hospital at a time when he was already being told to take precautions with his health. He had been hoping to get his blood clot treated and return to traveling, but Friday’s fall has now added another serious concern to the situation. For now, the biggest question is how he’s doing after being taken away in an ambulance and whether he’ll face any additional complications. Steve Carrier Steve Carrier is the founder of Ringside News and has been reporting
summary: Per Ringside News: flair was at Wagamama in Tampa on Friday morning when the situation unfolded. The fall left Flair with cuts to his head and eye, with significant bleeding around his eye.

He finally dodges a charge from Rubix and dishes out some offense, but Marsciulo is the former WWE wrestler and, by laws of physics, will look awesomer than anyone TNA has. He does hit an awesome dive to the floor onto Spud but gets drilled with a shot from Rubix. Spud tosses Rubix to the floor and steals the cover, but Marsciulo is out at 2 and Spud wastes way too much time screwing around making faces at the fans and allows Marsciulo to get up, hit him with the Jig & Tonic (which also happens to be Rubix's finish) for the win. TNA Impact 10/22/26 - TNA Internationa; Champion Jason Hotch vs. Mustafa Ali - Two Out Of Three Falls. The first fall started with a feeling out process as they each tried to out-think and out-wrestle the other. Ali tossed Hotch out of the ring but the champ stopped himself and returned with a springboard kick, sending Ali off the apron to the floor. Hotch followed to the floor and drilled him with hard chops. They battled on the floor. Hotch slammed him into the ring steps face-first. They battled on the apron, where Ali caught Hotch trying for a move and nailed a German suplex on the apron. Ali controlled the ring for a long time, but wasn't able to secure the pinfall. Ali finally scored it. Hotch battled back in the second fall and hit a dive to the outside. He slammed Ali's face into the apron over and over. Ali grabbed the International title and smacked Hotch with it. The referee called for a DQ. The final fall began. Ali maintained control and whipped Hotch with a belt while the referee was down. Hotch finally blocked it and drilled Ali. He grabbed the belt and began lashing Ali, chasing him to the floor. Ali sent him face-first into the ring post. They battled over a superplex to the floor. Ali was knocked to the floor. Hotch went to dive out but was superkicked as he came down. Ali was caught with a Standing Spanish Fly for a two count. Ali and Hotch began slugging it out. Ali scored with a dropkick to the head. Hotch responded with a boot to the face. Ali nailed a belly to belly and went to the top for a double stomp. Hotch avoided it and hit an overhead suplex into the buckles. Hotch nailed a GTS variation and scored the pin. Your winner and still TNA International Champion, Jason Hotch! Rivera took the tag and did a little mogging (whatever that is) before the face duo sent them mogging to the outside. They regrouped, re-entered the ring, and used nefarious means to take control of the match before they cut to a brief commercial break. [c] Back to the match, The Mog Squad kept Hall isolated in their corner. Rivera took Starboy down with a neckbreaker variation before distracting the referee while Ball thumped on Hall from the ring apron. Ball executed a Three Amigos gut-wrench suplex series on Hall , who fought back and dived for the tag, but was caught. Starboy finally made the hot tag to Jones, who lit the ring on fire as he took down his opponents. After a near fall on Rivera, Jones missed a Froggy Brew splash. Hall broke up a very near fall, then hit an incredible double pele kick. He dropped the denim straps before the face duo landed a series of high dives before executing a simultaneous Froggy Brew and shooting star press for a double pin. (Miller’s Take: This went a little long for an Evolve match, but it was a solid bout. Both teams had equal chances to shine, and the psychology was good. Jones seems to have lost his way a bit since the quiet demise of his Adrenaline Drip team with Jack Cartwheel, but he may have found his path back with this team.) -As if she read my mind, Adriana Rizzo caught the winners at ringside and asked if this was the beginning of a new team. Jones said he sees a dark roast and a denim dragon, then asked the fans if they could dig StarBrew. I’m digging it. -A pretaped promo from Elijah Holyfield saw him warn Braxton Cole and Marcus Mathers that he was going to take them both out in a triple threat match. She showed a little frustration at her inability to put her foe away., but continued with some methodical offense. title: Good Brothers To Defend MLW Tag Titles In Chicago Street Fight
raw_title: Chicago Street Fight For MLW Tag Titles Added To MLW Saturday Night SuperFight
summary_src: A new title match has been added to MLW Saturday Night SuperFight. Major League Wrestling announced that The Good Brothers (Doc Gallows & Karl Anderson) will defend the MLW Tag Team Titles against Glasgow Boys On Top at Saturday Night SuperFight on November 7.
body: A new title match has been added to MLW Saturday Night SuperFight. Major League Wrestling announced that The Good Brothers (Doc Gallows & Karl Anderson) will defend the MLW Tag Team Titles against Glasgow Boys On Top at Saturday Night SuperFight on November 7. After the savage attack that hospitalized CJ Gallows, the Good Brothers are coming to Chicago for vengeance. MLW today announced the Good Brothers will defend the MLW World Tag Team Championship against Glasgow Boys On Top in a Chicago Street Fight at Saturday Night SuperFight, Saturday, November 7, live from a sold-out Cicero Stadium in Chicago and available worldwide exclusively on VEEPS. For months, Glasgow Boys On Top barked about getting a World Tag Team Championship opportunity. Demanding a shot at Doc Gallows and Karl Anderson, the Scots grew increasingly hostile as their pursuit of championship gold became an obsession. Then, GBOT took matters into their own hands in brutal fashion, ruining CJ Gallows’ MLW singles debut and turning a milestone in the teenage rookie’s career into a nightmare for his family. The savage assault on Doc Gallows’ 18-year-old son left CJ hospitalized with a concussion, fractured jaw, damaged teeth and a bruised lung. With his jaw wired shut and doctors monitoring his recovery, CJ faces an uncertain road back to the ring. GBOT’s response? Mocking the young wrestler they put in a hospital bed. Doc Gallows and Karl Anderson cut short an overseas trip to be at CJ’s side. From the hospital, the World Tag Team Champions delivered their answer: Glasgow Boys On Top will get the championship fight they have been demanding — and everything that comes with a Chicago Street Fight. For Gallows, this is a father’s reckoning. For Anderson, it is about standing beside his brother and making GBOT answer for what they did to his family. The champions are putting their titles on the line to get their hands on the men responsible, with no disqualifications to save them when the fight turns ugly. GBOT wanted a title shot badly enough to send a message through the champion’s son. Now, the ruthless Scots have forced open a door that could lead straight to the World Tag Team Championship — if they can survive the fury waiting on the other side. MLW has already levied fines against Glasgow Boys On Top, with contract termination still a possibility. But no fine can settle this score, and no championship victory can erase the image of CJ lying in a hospital bed. In Chicago, the Good Brothers intend to make GBOT feel every bit of it. summary: Major League Wrestling has added a Chicago Street Fight for the MLW World Tag Team Championship to Saturday Night SuperFight on November 7. The Good Brothers will put the titles on the line against Glasgow Boys On Top at the sold-out Cicero Stadium in Chicago. The match stems from Glasgow Boys On Top's brutal attack on CJ Gallows during his MLW singles debut.

title: On the Record: Cody Rhodes Opens Up On His Hollywood Plans After Street Fighter Success
raw_title: Cody Rhodes Reveals His Hollywood Plans After Street Fighter Success
summary_src: Cody Rhodes has officially caught the Hollywood bug, and he’s not planning to stop with Street Fighter. The WWE Superstar wants more movie roles, but anyone thinking he’s getting ready to walk away from wrestling can forget about it.
body: During an October 23 appearance on The Rich Eisen Show , Rhodes opened up about his growing acting career following his role as Guile in Street Fighter and his appearance in The Naked Gun . When asked whether his recent Hollywood experiences had convinced him to pursue more acting opportunities, Rhodes made it clear that he’s interested. However, WWE isn’t going anywhere. “Hard have the bug. Hard, hard have the bug, but also I think it’s probably important to say wrestling is my whole life.” Rhodes isn’t treating wrestling as something he’ll eventually leave behind once Hollywood comes calling. Despite his growing interest in acting, he sees WWE remaining a major part of his career. “It is the day job, right? I don’t think it would ever not be.” That doesn’t mean Rhodes plans to turn down future movie opportunities. When asked whether continuing to work in Hollywood was part of his career trajectory, he confirmed that’s exactly what he wants. He also acknowledged that becoming a better actor means getting more experience in front of the camera. “It’s definitely, it’s my plan. Hopefully it goes according to plan. You know, I don’t, it’s one of those things where if I don’t flex that muscle, if I don’t get reps at it, I’m not going to get any good at this whole thing.” Rhodes also knows he isn’t the first WWE Superstar to make the jump into Hollywood. He specifically credited Dave Bautista, John Cena, and The Rock for opening doors that weren’t always available to professional wrestlers. Thanks to their success, Rhodes believes actors with wrestling backgrounds are getting a much different reception when pursuing film roles. “And action, and that’s a ton of fun, and comedy, that’s an easy place for me to plug into. But because of Dave Batista, John Cena, of course, and The Rock, they’ve made it so that we can walk into a lot of these rooms and they know we have something to offer.” The biggest difference now is that Rhodes doesn’t believe he has to choose between WWE and Hollywood. He pointed out that the wrestling business has changed, allowing stars to take on outside projects without having to abandon their careers in the ring. “It’s definitely going to work in a sense of with wrestling. It’s not like it used to be where, hey, you can only pick one or the other.” Rhodes has already experienced that flexibility firsthand. During the same interview, he credited Triple H and Nick Khan for making it easier to work on Street Fighter while remaining an active WWE Superstar. Instead of creating an elaborate injury angle to explain his absence, WWE simply allowed him to film the movie and return when he was finished. For now, Rhodes appears determined to have the best of both worlds. He’s already sharing the screen with major Hollywood names, and he’s making it clear that more acting opportunities are part of his plans. title: Ric Flair hospitalized after fall outside Tampa restaurant
raw_title: Ric Flair hospitalized after falling outside restaurant
body: Link TMZ Earlier today (Oct. 23), wrestling legend Ric Flair posted his regrets for not being able to fly to Washington state for a scheduled convention appearance this weekend. Shortly after 3 p.m. Eastern, TMZ reported that the 77-year-old Flair was taken to the hospital after falling outside a Tampa, Florida restaurant. “Sources with direct knowledge” told TMZ that the WWE Hall of Famer and AEW employee was “hanging” at the bar Friday morning at Wagamama restaurant “when he got up from the bar, leaving his phone and drink behind and walking across the street”. The outlets sources then saw Flair fall suddenly, injuring his face. We’re told Ric cut his head and eye open during the fall ... and his eye was bleeding extensively. He may also have a concussion. He was ultimately loaded into an ambulance and taken to the hospital. We’ll keep you posted on the Nature Boy’s condition. Our thoughts are with his family. title: Alice Crowley Reflects On ROH Global Wars Canada Bout
raw_title: Alice Crowley Looks Back On Match Against Red Velvet At ROH x MLP Global Wars Canada
summary_src: Alice Crowley looks back on the bout. Back in March 2026, Tony Khan's Ring of Honor and Scott D'Amore's Maple Leaf Pro Wrestling came together to present Global Wars Canada. Crowley faced off with Red Velvet for the ROH Women's World Television Championship at the show.
body: Back in March 2026, Tony Khan’s Ring of Honor and Scott D’Amore’s Maple Leaf Pro Wrestling came together to present Global Wars Canada. Crowley faced off with Red Velvet for the ROH Women’s World Television Championship at the show. She reflected on that match while speaking to Fightful’s Luis Pulido . “That was probably one of the biggest matches I have ever had in my career thus far: that Red Velvet match, and it is probably one of my best matches that I’ve had, and it’s a match that I take pride in for sure. If you guys haven’t watched that match, please go back and watch that match cause it’s really good, but yeah, I was very, very happy to be put in that position and to be put in that position very early on into working with Maple Leaf; that was not very far into- I wanna say it was maybe my second match working for Scott Dore. Before I got put in this title match, it was probably one of the best achievements of my career thus far, for sure, for sure, even though I didn’t win the title, even though that doesn’t matter; it’s just the fact that I was able to be able to have a title match like that on a platform like that.” Crowley will be competing in the 2026 CMLL Women’s Grand Prix.
summary: Alice Crowley spoke to Fightful about her March 2026 match against Red Velvet for the ROH Women’s World Television Championship at the ROH and Maple Leaf Pro Wrestling co-promoted Global Wars Canada event. She called it one of the biggest and best matches of her career so far, expressed pride in the performance, and noted it was only her second match working with Scott D’Amore’s promotion. Crowley encouraged fans to watch the bout and said being placed in that position early on was one of her top career achievements even though she did not win the title.

title: Every WWE Crown Jewel PLE, Ranked By Quality
raw_title: Every WWE Crown Jewel PLE, Ranked By Quality
body: By Andrew Kelly Published Oct 23, 2026, 3:00 PM EDT Andrew Kelly is a pro wrestling writer from The Wirral, England. With bylines on many pro wrestling websites, Andrew has proven himself to be very knowledgeable in the realms of WWE, AEW and more. Andrew is one of TheSportster's Match Reviewers and has covered the best matches of superstars like Cody Rhodes, MJF, Bianca Belair and more. He's also written hundreds of lists and features covering wrestling current events and history. He is also an MA Graduate from the University of Manchester, and a BA Graduate from Liverpool John Moores University, both in Creative Writing. Sign in to your TheSportster account The Crown Jewel PLE first began all the way back in 2018, serving as the second ever event as part of WWE’s partnership with the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. Since then, fans have witnessed seven Crown Jewel shows, most of which taking place in Saudi Arabia and one being hosted in Australia. Over that time, WWE has put forth both some of the all-time worst shows of all time, and some very enjoyable ones. It is interesting to look back across the entire history of WWE’s Crown Jewel PLE to determine the best in history, the weakest of all time, and how everything else stacked up in between. Crown Jewel 2018 is not only the worst in this series of events, but it is a contender for the worst WWE PLE in the entire history of the company. This show featured the infamously awful main event between an aging DX & Brothers Of Destruction, which was a laughably bad showdown which ruined Shawn Michaels’ return to the ring. Not only that, but Shane McMahon also stepped in at the last minute to win the WWE World Cup, being crowned the “Best In The World” in the process. Elsewhere on the card, Braun Strowman’s expected coronation was thwarted as Brock Lesnar beat him in a matter of moments to become the new Universal Champion. The only real highlight was a predictable WWE Title clash between AJ Styles & Samoa Joe, but even this lacked energy and quality. The 2019 Crown Jewel show was plain weird. Two “celebrity attraction” matches made up the biggest draws of the night, as Brock Lesnar & Cain Velasquez rekindled their UFC rivalry in a faux two minute grapple that did not work, and Tyson Fury clashed with Braun Strowman in a plodding big man battle. The rest of the show saw Mansoor get a win over Cesaro, Gallows & Anderson win the Tag Team World Cup, Hulk Hogan & Ric Flair put forth their own respective teams in the latest chapter of their never-ending feud, and Bray Wyatt beat Seth Rollins in a hard-to-watch Universal Title main event. WWE introduced the lackluster Crown Jewel Championship concept in 2024, which saw Cody Rhodes & Liv Morgan win pointless titles. There were some other minor highlights such as Seth Rollins’ fun clash with Bronson Reed and a hot battle between The OG Bloodline and The New Bloodline, but for the most part this show felt pretty bland. It was a solid enough PLE from start to finish,

body: MLW comes to you from a sold-out Chattanooga, Tennessee , with a loaded card headlined by a violent No Holds Barred MLW World Heavyweight Championship fight . Killer Kross puts the richest prize in MLW on the line against Josh Bishop , the new force inside The Skyscrapers. Templario begins his reign as MLW World Middleweight Champion. Lady Frost battles Corinne Joy . Big Damo marches into action with Josef Samael . The 2026 Opera Cup brackets are revealed. And MLW Nation will learn the main event for MLW FIGHTLAND in Charleston. Killer Kross defends the MLW World Heavyweight Championship against Josh Bishop in a No Holds Barred main event from sold-out Chattanooga. Bishop has become a dangerous new piece in The Skyscrapers’ war machine, and the group has made no secret of its championship ambitions. The Skyscrapers have already loomed over the tag team division, but now Bishop gets a direct shot at the biggest belt in Major League Wrestling. For Kross, this is not just a title defense. It is a test of how far The Skyscrapers are willing to go to claim more gold… and how much punishment the champion is willing to absorb to keep his throne. No holds barred means no excuses. No clean lanes. No easy escape. Just the Blood King, a Skyscraper, and the MLW World Heavyweight Championship hanging in the balance. A new reign begins as Templario defends the MLW World Middleweight Championship against rising middleweight player Diego Hill . Fresh off defeating KUSHIDA in Mexico to capture the title, Templario kicks off his reign against one of the most exciting young athletes in MLW. He brings power, precision, and the pride of CMLL into his first defense. But Diego Hill is not entering empty-handed. As the protégé of the legendary Blue Panther , Hill has learned the value of technique, timing, and lucha tradition from one of the sport’s great maestros. Templario wants to establish dominance immediately. Hill wants to turn a major opportunity into a career-changing upset. The middleweight division gets a championship fight with international stakes. Lady Frost takes on Corinne Joy in a women’s division clash loaded with new energy. Frost has already made her arrival felt in MLW, bringing athleticism, confidence, and a cold-blooded edge to every fight. Corinne Joy steps deeper into the spotlight with a massive following behind her and the ambition to turn online buzz into in-ring momentum. Corinne and Jazzy Yang have made it clear they are looking to influence the women’s title picture sooner rather than later. But Lady Frost is not here to be anyone’s stepping stone. This is a chance for one woman to make a statement while the division keeps heating up. Big Damo steps into action with Josef Samael in his corner as he battles Andrew Everett . Damo brings size, power, and blunt-force violence. Josef Samael brings prophecy, manipulation, and the violent doctrine of CONTRA Unit. summary_src: Michael Hayes agrees with the praise of Bobby Roode. Guest appearing on Stephanie McMahon's What's Your Story? podcast was WWE producer Michael Hayes. Hayes shared that Chief Content Officer Paul 'Triple H' Levesque has identified who could replace Hayes in that lead producer role.

Hayes shared that Chief Content Officer Paul ‘Triple H’ Levesque has identified who could replace Hayes in that lead producer role. “But yeah, I just made up my mind that this is your new path and go for it, and I’ll tell you, Trips came up to me one day and he goes, ‘So Michael, you know you’re not gonna be around forever.’ You’re our Pat Patterson. I need you to make Bobby Roode ‘Michael.’” There have been several occasions when those within WWE have praised Roode for his producer work.

title: Tiffany Stratton Injury Update After Money In The Bank Fall
raw_title: Backstage Update On Tiffany Stratton After Rough Landing At WWE Money In The Bank
summary_src: New updates have been released on Tiffany Stratton following her high-risk ladder fall at Money in the Bank earlier this month.
body: WWE Though she's now a two-time WWE Women's Money in the Bank recipient, the high reward came with a very high risk. And now, it remains to be seen what Tiffany Stratton's injury status is after her ladder fall on October 10. In New Orleans, Stratton climbed to the top of a high ladder to execute a high-risk Senton Bomb. However, the ladder jerked violently, causing Stratton to crash short of Charlotte Flair, Lash Legend, and Lola Vice. Instead, she landed on her head and neck when she came down. As of this report, no confirmation was made on if she'll appear at tonight's show at the Toyota Arena in Ontario, California.
summary: Tiffany Stratton executed a high-risk Senton Bomb off a tall ladder during the Women's Money In The Bank match on October 10 but the ladder shifted and she landed awkwardly on her head and neck. The two-time contract winner crashed short of her intended targets Charlotte Flair, Lash Legend and Lola Vice. No word has been given on whether Stratton will appear at tonight's WWE event in Ontario, California.

llm_long: Tiffany Stratton became a two-time WWE Women's Money in the Bank winner. During the match on October 10 in New Orleans she attempted a high-risk Senton Bomb from the top of a tall ladder.
The ladder shifted suddenly as Stratton launched herself. She fell short of her intended targets and landed on her head and neck.
The incident occurred while Charlotte Flair, Lash Legend, and Lola Vice were in the ring area. Stratton has not received medical clearance as of the latest available information.

title: Comeback Watch: MLW returning to PPV with Saturday Night SuperFight
raw_title: MLW returning to PPV with Saturday Night SuperFight
body: MLW is returning to pay-per-view with Saturday Night SuperFight 2026 taking place this November. It was announced today that MLW is partnering with VEEPS (a Live Nation-owned streaming platform) for the PPV, which is set to be held at Cicero Stadium in Cicero, Illinois on November 7. Streaming live on VEEPS, the show has an early-bird pre-order price of $9.99 for the next 48 hours. That rises to $19.99 after the early-bird special, and then $24.99 if you wait to order until the day of the show. MLW and VEEPS first entered into their partnership this May with episodes of MLW Fusion being hosted on the platform. It was noted in the initial announcement that “quarterly premium live PPV supercards” would be coming soon. Fusion now premieres weekly on Tubi every Thursday as part of a recently announced deal , though the show is still available on other platforms like VEEPS and YouTube starting on Saturdays after the initial Thursday airing. “MLW is on a roll, and now it’s time to go bigger,” Bauer said in a statement to The Takedown on SI . “We’re not coming back to pay-per-view to play it safe. November 7 is where championships will be decided, rivalries will come to a head, and the best fighters in MLW will be expected to deliver on the biggest stage we’ve had in years. Chicago always brings an incredible atmosphere, and we’re giving that crowd — and fans watching around the world — a night of super fights.” Bauer, actor/wrestler Paul Walter Hauser, and Bryan Walsh are listed as executive producers of the Saturday Night SuperFight PPV. No matches have been announced yet. The card will include wrestlers from MLW and talent from CMLL. World Heavyweight Champion Killer Kross and new signing Masha Slamovich are among the top names in MLW. It’s noted that Austin Aries, The Good Brothers, Matt Riddle, Mistico, Contra Unit, and Zamaya are also expected to compete at Saturday Night SuperFight. title: Ric Flair Hospitalized Hours After Announcing Blood Clot Diagnosis
raw_title: Ric Flair Hospitalized Hours After Announcing Blood Clot Diagnosis
body: TMZ Sports reported that the WWE icon lost his balance after leaving Wagamama in Tampa and injured his face. The outlet reported that he cut his head and eye open, and was bleeding extensively from his eye. Flair’s bloody fall in Tampa occurred hours after he announced his blood clot diagnosis on social media. Flair canceled a scheduled fan appearance in the Seattle area, saying that doctors advised him to limit travel after discovering a blood clot in his leg. The WWE Hall of Famer shared the news in a post on X , where he apologized to his agent, Steve Solomon, the Washington State Horror Con, Big Event NY, and his fans in Seattle. “Unfortunately, I am dealing with a blood clot in my leg, and my doctors have limited my travel to 3–4 hours. Seattle falls outside that range, and as disappointed as I am, I have to put my health and recovery first,” Flair wrote. Flair referred to Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts as a reason he is approaching the issue with caution. Hurts, 28, will miss the remainder of the 2026 NFL season due to blood clots. “Blood clots are extremely serious and can be life-threatening. We have seen this recently with Jalen Hurts . The complications involving blood clots in his lungs. It is a reminder that this is not something to take lightly. I must follow medical advice,” he wrote. “I’m scheduled to have a procedure to strip the affected vein, which my doctors expect will allow me to be cleared for more travel afterward,” he wrote. “Please know this decision was not made lightly. I am truly sorry for the inconvenience and disappointment. I’m incredibly grateful for your patience, understanding, and continued support,” Flair added. “I look forward to getting healthy and seeing you all down the road.” It is unclear how his fall will impact the timeline of that procedure. This is not the first event Flair has missed due to a blood clot. The Nature Boy missed the Cauliflower Alley Club’s 60th reunion in Las Vegas, where he was honored with the Iron Mike Mazurki Award. Jerry Lawler and Jimmy Hart accepted the award on his behalf. Flair explained his absence via video. “I have a blood clot in my leg. So, I can’t travel the five or six-hour trips that it takes to get there,” he said. Days later, he flew to Philadelphia for a signing. In a social media post, the WWE alum wrote “a little blood clot is not going to keep me from coming to Philly!” Hopefully, the WWE icon makes a speedy recovery from his fall in Florida. title: On the Record: Cody Rhodes Opens Up On Roman Reigns Had Heavy Stunt Involvement in Street Fighter Movie
raw_title: Cody Rhodes Reveals Roman Reigns Had Heavy Stunt Involvement in Street Fighter Movie
summary_src: Roman Reigns wasn’t just showing up to look intimidating in Street Fighter. The WWE Superstar had plenty of stunt work to deal with while playing Akuma, and Cody Rhodes says the movie’s production team made sure neither of them got special treatment just because they’re professional wrestlers.
body: Speaking on The Rich Eisen Show , Rhodes opened up about filming Street Fighter and how different the movie’s fight choreography was from what he’s used to doing in WWE. Rhodes, who plays Guile in the film, explained that stunt coordinator John Valera didn’t assume he already knew everything simply because of his wrestling background. “I’m so glad he didn’t look at me and go, ‘Oh, he’s a wrestler. He’s got it.’ I’m glad he looked at me and said, ‘Oh, he’s a wrestler. Maybe he knows a different way,’ because of how we did this combat.” Rhodes admitted that he needed plenty of help learning how to fight for the camera. While WWE involves physical contact and carefully planned movements, movie fights require a different approach to make everything look convincing on screen. “I needed all the help I could. I’m used to punching a guy on the forehead, getting a little bit of contact, maybe not too much. In this world, a lot of across the frame, a lot of whimsy.” That’s when Rhodes brought up Roman Reigns, revealing that his fellow WWE Superstar had a significant amount of stunt work while portraying Akuma. According to Rhodes, the production didn’t assume Reigns knew everything about movie fighting either. “And Roman Reigns, who’s also in the movie, he was heavily stunt involved in terms of his role as Akuma.” Rhodes explained that the stunt team understood professional wrestling experience didn’t automatically translate into Hollywood fight choreography. Both men had to approach the process differently, and Rhodes said he trained every day to get comfortable with what was required. “They knew to not make the mistake of thinking the wrestlers know what they’re doing. So every day I trained.” Reigns taking on a stunt-heavy role is another example of WWE stars expanding into Hollywood while continuing their wrestling careers. With Rhodes playing Guile and Reigns portraying Akuma, Street Fighter gave both men an opportunity to show what they could do outside the ring. Rhodes made it clear that being a WWE Superstar didn’t mean he could walk onto the set and immediately handle everything. The same production that worked extensively with him also had Reigns involved in demanding stunt sequences for Akuma. Now that the movie has been released, audiences can see the results of that work for themselves. Derek Holloway Derek Holloway is a writer at Ringside News specializing in professional wrestling news, rumors, and results. He focuses on delivering reliable coverage across WWE, AEW, and major wrestling promotions.
summary: Speaking on The Rich Eisen Show , Rhodes opened up about filming Street Fighter and how different the movie’s fight choreography was from what he’s used to doing in WWE. Per Rhodes, the production didn’t assume Reigns knew everything about movie fighting either. And Roman Reigns.
llm_long: The Street Fighter movie topped the North American box office this weekend. The film features Cody Rhodes as Guile, Roman Reigns as Akuma, and NJPW’s Hirooki Goto as E. Honda.

The movie had been projected to earn approximately 70 million dollars worldwide in its opening weekend. It currently holds a 41 percent approval rating from critics on Rotten Tomatoes and a 79 percent approval rating from audiences.
The film has received a 6.3 out of 10 rating on IMDb. Several critics highlighted Cody Rhodes’ performance as Guile.

title: Backstage Buzz: Real Reason WWE Plans to Load Up NXT Against AEW Blood & Guts
raw_title: Real Reason WWE Plans to Load Up NXT Against AEW Blood & Guts
summary_src: WWE apparently got a serious confidence boost the last time NXT went head-to-head with AEW, and now the company wants to turn things up a notch. After beating Dynamite in the ratings, WWE isn’t interested in playing it safe when NXT goes against Blood & Guts on November 4.
body: Speaking on Wrestling Observer Live , Bryan Alvarez revealed that WWE actually wasn’t very confident going into its previous head-to-head battle with AEW Grand Slam France. That’s why fans got what was basically a normal NXT instead of WWE stacking the show with everything it had. “Normal show, like they don’t even care. So then they announced that this will be head-to-head, and I was told they have been told to load it up.” Apparently, WWE wasn’t convinced NXT was going to win that night. Rather than load up the card and potentially still lose, the company decided to just put on its usual show and see where the numbers landed. “Then I was told they gained a lot of confidence from the last time they went head-to-head. So what happened is the reason they didn’t load up NXT — they thought maybe they might not win on Tuesday head-to-head, so they thought, ‘Well, we’ll just do a show.’” AEW wasn’t taking that same approach. Dynamite had a much more loaded lineup, including an Ospreay title match, but WWE still ended up coming out ahead in the ratings. “Dynamite had a loaded-up show, you know, the Ospreay title match. They didn’t have confidence. They thought they were going to lose. Most of us figured NXT was gonna win, but you have to remember, when NXT and AEW went head-to-head and they were both on normal nights for years, Dynamite almost always won.” That win apparently changed the mood in a big way. Alvarez said WWE went from not being sure it could beat AEW to basically having a “we’re gonna crush them” attitude going into the next showdown. “So they didn’t have confidence, and now that they won, it was sort of like, ‘We’re gonna crush them.’ So they will load up against Blood and Guts. They don’t wanna lose again Tuesday night after winning last time.” That certainly makes November 4 a lot more interesting. Dave Meltzer previously reported that Nick Khan allegedly made the call to load up NXT , and now Alvarez is saying WWE’s newfound confidence after the last ratings win is a major reason they’re going harder this time. The funny part is that this whole fight wasn’t even supposed to happen because WWE wanted another Wednesday night war. The CW moved NXT because election coverage on November 3 would have resulted in the show being preempted in too many markets, dropping WWE directly onto AEW’s night in the process. AEW already has two Blood & Guts matches planned, so Dynamite wasn’t exactly going to be a quiet night anyway. Now WWE wants to bring some extra firepower of its own, and after winning the last round, it sounds like the company really doesn’t want to hand AEW the bragging rights back. title: Cody Rhodes Plans To Balance Wrestling And Acting
raw_title: Cody Rhodes Says It's His Plan To Do Both Acting And Wrestling: 'It’s Not Like It Used To Be Where You Can Only Pick One Or The Other'
summary_src: Cody Rhodes wants to keep doing movies while focusing on wrestling. Rhodes played the role of Guile in the Street Fighter movie. He isn’t the only wrestler today to do both movies and work as a wrestler on television.
body: Cody Rhodes wants to keep doing movies while focusing on wrestling. Rhodes played the role of Guile in the Street Fighter movie. He isn’t the only wrestler today to do both movies and work as a wrestler on television. Roman Reigns also worked on the Street Fighter movie alongside Rhodes, and he’s the current World Heavyweight Champion. Stars like The Rock, John Cena and Dave Bautista are other wrestlers who’ve also made a name for themselves in Hollywood. Speaking on The Rich Eisen Show , Rhodes was asked if he has caught the movie bug. “Hard have the bug, but also I think it’s probably important to say wrestling is my whole life that you said day job. It is the day job. I don’t think it would ever not be.” Rhodes then said that it’s his plan to do both wrestling and acting. “It’s my plan. Hopefully it goes according to plan. It’s one of those things where if I don’t flex that muscle, if I don’t get reps at it, I’m not going to get any good at this whole thing. Action, that’s a ton of fun, and comedy, that’s an easy place for me to plug into. It’s not like it used to be where you can only pick one or the other.” Elsewhere in the interview, Rhodes explained how Nick Khan and Triple H made it “very easy” for him to shoot Street Fighter. title: WWE Still Discussing Rock's Praise For Tony Khan
raw_title: Update On Internal WWE Reaction To Rock Praising Tony Khan In PAC Tribute
body: The Rock had kind words for Tony Khan in his PAC tribute video, something that is reportedly still being discussed in WWE. As noted at the start of the month, the WWE star and TKO board member posted a video where he spoke about PAC following the latter’s passing. In the video, he referred to Tony Khan as his friend and said AEW “is growing into this phenomenal wrestling company.” It had been noted that people in WWE weren’t upset about the video, though they were “surprised” by Rock’s comments about Khan and AEW. Meltzer noted that people “have their theories” on the matter, but that it seems likely it’s simply a matter of Rock having love for the industry and wanting to send condolences to the people in AEW, where PAC worked, instead of saying nothing because of the perceived “wrestling war” he isn’t part of. Rock commented on the matter in early October, commenting on an Instagram post about the matter: “you’re right brother, and humanity matters to me. I was born into this business and I’ve seen it all, but when one of our own passes away, I don’t care nor do I see “our competition”, I care about the wrestlers and how it affects them. I’ve been there. To me, humanity matters most.”” In other Rock news, it was noted that while Rock was originally advertised to appear at the WWE tryouts in Hawaii, he did not appear. WWE had stopped advertising him a while before the tryouts and live events that took place on October 16th and 17th.
summary: The Rock referred to Tony Khan as his friend and called AEW a growing phenomenal wrestling company in a tribute video for PAC. Internal WWE reaction has been surprise rather than upset according to reports with people having various theories on why he spoke positively. Dave Meltzer noted it appears to stem from The Rock's love for the business and desire to offer condolences without regard for any wrestling war.

TMZ reported the WWE Hall of Famer fell outside of a restaurant in the Florida city Friday morning. Sources told TMZ Flair suddenly fell and suffered injuries to his face, including a cut to his head. The "Nature Boy" was taken to a local hospital by ambulance. There was no word on why Flair abruptly left the location. Just before 10 a.m., Flair took to X (formerly Twitter) and posted a statement that he was unable to attend Washington State Horror Con in Seattle, due to being unable to travel the distance because of a blood clot. Flair said as disappointed as he was, he had to put "his health and recovery first." He thanked fans for their patience, understanding, and continued support. Flair noted in the post that he is scheduled to have a procedure done on the impacted vein, but did not say when. He told fans that his doctors expected he will be cleared for more travel following the procedure, but it's unclear what impact his recent fall may have on his health. title: WWE Execs Still Upset Over Rock's AEW Praise
raw_title: Report: Some Within WWE Feeling 'Sting' Over The Rock's Comments On Tony Khan
summary_src: According to a new report, there are some within WWE still feeling the "sting" over Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson's comments about AEW and its president, Tony Khan.
body: Following the death of AEW star Pac , real name Benjamin Satterley, WWE star, and member of the TKO board of directors, Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson took to social media to pay tribute to WWE's former Neville . In his Instagram video , Johnson not only expressed condolences for Satterley's family and friends, but also praised AEW and its president Tony Khan, calling the promotion a "phenomenal wrestling company." Meltzer said that while no one is questioning the tribute to Satterley, to some within the company, the "sting still hasn't gone away" regarding The Rock's comments on Khan and AEW. Meltzer also noted that while The Rock was initially briefly advertised for the latest slate of WWE tryouts in Hawaii, a location special to the star after he spent time there growing up, he didn't end up appearing. The Rock hadn't been featured on ads for the tryouts for a while leading up to the event. The veteran wrestling journalist said that he doesn't believe Johnson meant anything other than sending condolences to the AEW locker room and Khan, due to the wrestling industry being a big part of his life. Johnson hasn't addressed the situation further, and AEW did not bring it up his comments during their tribute episode to the late Satterley, " AEW Dynamite: A Tribute to Pac ."
summary: Following the death of AEW wrestler Pac, real name Benjamin Satterley, Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson posted an Instagram tribute that praised AEW and its president Tony Khan as running a phenomenal wrestling company. Per Dave Meltzer, some within WWE remain bothered by those comments despite the sincere condolences for Satterley, who had previously performed in WWE as Neville. The Rock was initially advertised for recent WWE tryouts in Hawaii but ultimately did not appear at the event.

title: Injury Update: AEW Tacked on Injury Time to Dralistico’s Contract Amid Exit Speculation
raw_title: AEW Tacked on Injury Time to Dralistico’s Contract Amid Exit Speculation
summary_src: Dralistico might already be gone from AEW if it wasn’t for one thing — injury time. His contract should have expired by now, but AEW tacked on extra months that will keep him around until December, and WWE could be waiting on the other side.
body: Speaking on Wrestling Observer Live , Bryan Alvarez revealed that Dralistico’s original deal has essentially run its course. The only reason he’s still under contract is because AEW added time for the period he missed due to injury. “I do know that Dralistico’s contract would already have expired, but they tacked on injury time, which takes his contract through December.” That makes his recent “Maybe not for long?” post look even more interesting . Dralistico shared a photo of himself behind bars and handcuffed earlier this month, immediately setting off speculation that he was counting down the days until his AEW deal was finished. AEW hasn’t completely given up on keeping him either. Alvarez said there were talks about a new deal when the injury time was added, but right now there’s a chance that Dralistico could end up heading elsewhere. “Apparently, when they tacked on the injury time, there were discussions of re-signing. So we’ll wait and see, but Dralistico will either go to WWE and team up with his brother or end up under the mask as Sin Cara.” The brother Alvarez is talking about is Dragon Lee, which would obviously give Dralistico a pretty easy connection if WWE comes calling. There’s also been recent talk about WWE possibly dusting off the Sin Cara character with somebody new under the mask , and Alvarez threw that out as another possibility. More importantly, Alvarez doesn’t think WWE is some long-shot option here. He actually put the chances of Dralistico attempting to make the jump at better than 50 percent, although a big offer from AEW could obviously change things pretty quickly. “I would say it’s a better than 50% chance he attempts to go to WWE, but they might throw a million dollars at him, and he might stay. Either way, he’s getting paid.” Dralistico hasn’t wrestled for AEW since the June 6 Collision taping, where he teamed with RUSH and Sammy Guevara in a failed bid for the AEW World Trios Championship. That long absence already had people wondering what was going on before his handcuffed photo added even more fuel to the fire. For now, Dralistico is still an AEW wrestler and there’s no deal with WWE on the table that we know of. But with injury time being the only thing keeping his current contract alive until December, the next couple of months could get very interesting. title: Ex-WWE Writer Calls Vince McMahon a Psychopath
raw_title: Former WWE writer unleashes on ‘psychopath’ Vince McMahon: ‘He was a crazy person’
summary_src: Jimmy Jacobs, who has drawn praise for his tenure as a writer on WWE’s creative team from 2015 to 2017, recently opened up about his time in the company, as well as what it was like working with then-WWE boss Vince McMahon.
body: According to Jacobs, McMahon came off as a “psychopath” who routinely bullied his employees. Jacobs, who later enjoyed stints on the creative teams at TNA and AEW after his time at WWE, is also an active professional wrestler , perhaps best known for his time in Ring of Honor. Currently, he’s doing work with Maple Leaf Pro Wrestling in Canada and coaches at the House of Truth wrestling school in the Detroit area of Michigan. One of his more entertaining contributions while working for WWE’s creative was pitching “ The List of Jericho ,” which helped rejuvenate the run Chris Jericho was on at the time. However, while speaking on the After the Bell podcast, Jacobs indicated that his time at WWE had its share of difficulties, and it started at the top. “He was a crazy person. Vince McMahon was a psychopath,” Jacobs said. “That’s the sort of personality type he is, right? He’s like an overt malignant narcissist — not to use catchphrase words, because I’m not using that hyperbolically. That’s his personality type. “I was around Vince McMahon not very long before I saw, ‘Oh, I wouldn’t trade places with this guy for one second.’ Not for one second. Because for everything he has, he has nothing, because he’s a psychopath. And when you’re a psychopath, you’re incapable of love.” His stinging characterization of his former employer continued with Jacobs saying, “Vince McMahon’s a bully. He’s a maniac. He’s an abuser. All the things that have come out, every story you’ve heard about him, it’s something like true. That’s who he is.” According to Jacobs, McMahon was hard on most people, but he did treat his favorites differently. “The people that I saw Vince treat well: Roman Reigns, Brock Lesnar, The Undertaker, and Blackjack Lanza…But other than the names I listed, at different points, he would bury, be down on, [saying] ‘This guy doesn’t know what he’s doing,’ everybody else.” He concluded his thoughts on McMahon by reiterating that he thinks the former wrestling promoter/executive is legitimately a psychopath. “It’s what it is. There’s a lot of other psychopaths out in the world, but Vince McMahon’s one of them. Because he has that sort of personality type, he’ll take risks. He’ll step on people,” Jacobs said. “He’ll do what it takes to get what he wants, and that’s really what a psychopath ends up being: Somebody that will take anything in reality and use it to get what they want…So you don’t love people, you use people.” What do you think, Cagesiders? summary_src: The WWE Performance Center has a few new additions. Our Bryan Alvarez reports that Gabriela Martinez Asensi, Silvia Likki, Elly Finch, and Tayleigh Robertson all moved to Orlando, Florida in the past week and have signed with WWE.
body: Our Bryan Alvarez reports that Gabriela Martinez Asensi , Silvia Likki , Elly Finch , and Tayleigh Robertson all moved to Orlando, Florida in the past week and have signed with WWE. All four women have a background in athletics as they start their pro wrestling careers at the Performance Center. Martinez Asensi is originally from Spain and touts that she is fluent in Spanish, English, and German. Her background includes playing tennis for the University of Missouri. She is a fitness coach with a large following on social media. Similarly, Likki also comes into WWE with a large social media following of more than 200,000 followers on Instagram. She is from Italy and is a CrossFit athlete. The signing of Finch was first reported by PWInsider this week, with her having participated in track and field for Michigan State University. Robertson is an amateur wrestler and bodybuilder who went to Snow College and Utah Tech. All of these names participated in tryouts before signing with WWE. Joseph Currier Joseph Currier is a graduate of the University of Massachusetts, obtaining a journalism degree in 2016. Joseph joined F4W during his time at UMass and has now been writing about the industry for nearly a decade. In addition to his work with F4W, Joseph has previously contributed to Sports Illustrated's wrestling coverage. He lives in Massachusetts and is a diehard fan of the Boston sports teams and Liverpool Football Club.

Per the Wrestling Observer, all four participated in tryouts prior to signing.

body: October 14 turned out to be an emotional day for many wrestling fans as they learned of Adam "Edge" Copeland's plan to officially retire from in-ring competition in 2027. No definitive time or place has been attached to Copeland's sendoff yet, but according to AEW CEO Tony Khan, the time leading up to it will surely be memorable. "Abosolutely I knew Adam was going to say that 2027 is his last year," Khan said on the AEW WrestleDream media call, referencing Copeland's announcement made on "AEW Dynamite." "I'm very close with Adam. I speak to Adam very regularly, and of course, as the producer of the show, I'm going to talk to him about what he wants to say on the microphone." "... I think he'll have a great run here throughout the next year," Khan continued. "Into 2027, I don't know how much longer exactly Adam will want to go, but I would say this is what he talked to me about, that 2027 was going to be the last year he would want to wrestle. I've accepted that. I think that Adam is somebody that has accomplished so much in wrestling." Copeland, a former world champion in WWE, initially retired from wrestling in 2011 due to spinal stenosis . Nine years later, he made a miraculous return to action as a surprise entrant in the 2020 Men's Royal Rumble, with his neck back to great strength. He went to wrestle for WWE for an additional three years before jumping over to AEW in the fall of 2023. In 2026, "The Rated R Superstar" reunited with his long-time friend Christian Cage, and even enjoyed a reign as AEW Tag Team Champions. Their reign came to a rather bitter end, however, as Cage sustained multiple broken ribs and a collapsed lung. Arthur Cauty/Shutterstock "Christian Cage is recovering from those injuries," Khan said, addressing Cage's ongoing absence from AEW programming. "He's one of the toughest people, but he fought through and had one of the greatest wrestling matches ever. When you know that he hurt himself and he tried to power through, and frankly, shake off the medical team, saying he wasn't hurt and downplay it and say that he could continue. Really, nobody realized until after. Then to be worried about him, somebody that outside of the ring I think we all love and inside of the ring we all love, Adam said it so well, that was something we weren't expecting. " Copeland delivered the news of Cage's status during his aforementioned "Dynamite" promo. The injuries themselves occurred after Cage was thrown into a ladder about five minutes into their AEW Tag Team Championship Ladder Match at All Out on September 26. On the same media call, Khan confirmed that he originally factored Cage into the subsequent pay-per-view, WrestleDream, on October 17. Cage's injuries render him unable to compete right now, though. title: Jimmy Jacobs calls Vince McMahon a psychopath
raw_title: Jimmy Jacobs unleashes on ‘psychopath’ Vince McMahon: ‘He was a crazy person’
body: According to Jacobs, McMahon came off as a “psychopath” who routinely bullied his employees. Jacobs, who later enjoyed stints on the creative teams at TNA and AEW after his time at WWE, is also an active professional wrestler , perhaps best known for his time in Ring of Honor. Currently, he’s doing work with Maple Leaf Pro Wrestling in Canada and coaches at the House of Truth wrestling school in the Detroit area of Michigan. One of his more entertaining contributions while working for WWE’s creative was pitching “ The List of Jericho ,” which helped rejuvenate the run Chris Jericho was on at the time. However, while speaking on the After the Bell podcast, Jacobs indicated that his time at WWE had its share of difficulties, and it started at the top. “He was a crazy person. Vince McMahon was a psychopath,” Jacobs said. “That’s the sort of personality type he is, right? He’s like an overt malignant narcissist — not to use catchphrase words, because I’m not using that hyperbolically. That’s his personality type. “I was around Vince McMahon not very long before I saw, ‘Oh, I wouldn’t trade places with this guy for one second.’ Not for one second. Because for everything he has, he has nothing, because he’s a psychopath. And when you’re a psychopath, you’re incapable of love.” His stinging characterization of his former employer continued with Jacobs saying, “Vince McMahon’s a bully. He’s a maniac. He’s an abuser. All the things that have come out, every story you’ve heard about him, it’s something like true. That’s who he is.” According to Jacobs, McMahon was hard on most people, but he did treat his favorites differently. “The people that I saw Vince treat well: Roman Reigns, Brock Lesnar, The Undertaker, and Blackjack Lanza…But other than the names I listed, at different points, he would bury, be down on, [saying] ‘This guy doesn’t know what he’s doing,’ everybody else.” He concluded his thoughts on McMahon by reiterating that he thinks the former wrestling promoter/executive is legitimately a psychopath. “It’s what it is. There’s a lot of other psychopaths out in the world, but Vince McMahon’s one of them. Because he has that sort of personality type, he’ll take risks. He’ll step on people,” Jacobs said. “He’ll do what it takes to get what he wants, and that’s really what a psychopath ends up being: Somebody that will take anything in reality and use it to get what they want…So you don’t love people, you use people.” What do you think, Cagesiders? title: Sean Legacy Reveals CM Punk Inspired His Physique Transformation

summary_src: Sean Legacy credits CM Punk. Taking to Instagram, WWE NXT talent Sean Legacy shared the story of how a conversation with CM Punk led to him improving his physique. Legacy wrote: "A few months ago, I had a conversation with @cmpunk at a live event about his diet and workouts.
body: Taking to Instagram, WWE NXT talent Sean Legacy shared the story of how a conversation with CM Punk led to him improving his physique. “A few months ago, I had a conversation with @cmpunk at a live event about his diet and workouts. I’ve looked up to him for years, but that conversation hit at a time when I really needed it. It made me want to demand more of myself and follow through. Since then, I’ve been eating cleaner, pushing myself in the gym, doing cardio five/six days a week, and putting in the ring work and conditioning. You can see the difference in these pictures. What you can’t see is how much better I feel mentally. I feel more focused, more confident, and better than I ever felt. I’m sharing this because maybe somebody else needs that same push. I didn’t realize how much of what I was looking for would come from taking better care of myself. Eating better. Moving more. Showing up consistently. Sometimes the things you keep putting off are the things that could change how you feel every day.
summary: WWE NXT wrestler Sean Legacy shared on Instagram how a conversation with CM Punk at a live event motivated him to overhaul his diet and training regimen. He began eating cleaner, hitting the gym harder, doing cardio five or six days a week, and improving his ring conditioning, resulting in visible physical changes and major mental benefits including greater focus and confidence. Legacy said the discussion came at the right time and he hopes sharing his experience might motivate others.

Their discussion focused on Punk's approach to diet and training. Legacy began eating cleaner, intensifying his workouts, and increasing his time training in the ring as a result.
Legacy has since reduced his weight from 217 pounds to 199 pounds. He shared before and after photos that highlight the visible change in his physique.
WWE released a behind-the-scenes vlog from the NXT house show. The video includes footage of Legacy approaching Punk backstage to compliment him on maintaining his body.
Legacy officially joined the NXT roster near the beginning of 2026. He had previously impressed officials through the WWE ID program and appearances on WWE Evolve.

Punk decided to enhance his own conditioning in the weeks leading up to WrestleMania 42. He has followed a strict meal plan and gym routine while working with trainer Jay Ferruggia, who also works with other WWE performers including Chad Gable.

body: One-half of the IWGP Junior Heavyweight Tag Team Champions is not cleared to compete, and has been pulled from New Japan Pro-Wrestling's Super Junior Tag League. NJPW announced on its website on Thursday that El Desperado is injured, and a new competitor will team alongside Mistico as a substitute in his place during the tournament. According to NJPW's statement, El Desperado is suffering from spinal canal stenosis, as well as a hernia, and will be unable to compete in the tournament that kicks off on Saturday. Young Lion Masatora Yasuda will now team with Mistico. El Desperado revealed in his own statement that he is currently able to walk, stand, or even sit upright for long periods of time due to the injury, which is bothering his left leg. The star said he's been having issues with tingling and other odd sensations since March, but the pain began in June and worsened in the last few months. He wanted to continue to wrestle throughout the rest of the year, but his "body has reached its limits," and he apologized to fans. The champion said that NJPW fans should consider the Young Lion's inclusion in the tournament as a "key step to the future of NJPW." Desperado said he wanted to give Yasuda the opportunity to team alongside Mistico, who he called a "global megastar," to see what he can do. He said he has trust in Mistico to pull through and show up for the fans like he always does.
summary: NJPW announced that El Desperado has been forced out of the Super Junior Tag League due to spinal canal stenosis and a hernia. Young Lion Masatora Yasuda will replace him and team with Mistico in the tournament that begins Saturday. El Desperado remains one-half of the IWGP Junior Heavyweight Tag Team Champions.

summary_src: Samantha Irvin is finally about to be free to make her next move, and AEW has already talked about bringing her in. The former WWE ring announcer has spent the last two years dealing with a non-compete agreement after leaving the company, but that restriction is coming to an end this month.
body: According to Fightful Select, Samantha Johnson, better known to WWE fans as Samantha Irvin, is set to become a free agent in October 2026. When she chose to leave WWE two years ago, the company placed an actual non-compete restriction on her. That’s different from the termination periods often described as non-competes when WWE releases talent. AEW has already discussed bringing Johnson into the company in an on-screen role on multiple occasions. However, anyone expecting her to show up on Dynamite the moment she’s free might want to lower their expectations. lt was said that an immediate appearance isn’t planned, and if she does eventually join AEW television, it would likely happen further down the road. There’s certainly no shortage of connections between Johnson and AEW. Her husband, Ricochet, is part of the company’s roster, and she’s been backstage at dozens of AEW events over the past two years. She also has a strong relationship with the promotion, making a future appearance a real possibility. One thing that could make her next move interesting is that Johnson has previously expressed little interest in returning to ring announcing. She became one of WWE’s most recognizable voices before her departure, but that doesn’t mean she’s looking to step back behind a microphone and introduce wrestlers again. That leaves plenty of possibilities for what she might do if she eventually appears on AEW programming. While the company has discussed using her on television, there’s no confirmation of a deal or what kind of role she would take. For now, Johnson is approaching her first real opportunity to explore wrestling-related options since leaving WWE in 2024. AEW clearly hasn’t forgotten about her, but a debut isn’t something fans should expect right away. With her non-compete finally coming to an end, the next decision is hers. title: Willow Nightingale Provides AEW Injury Recovery Update
raw_title: Willow Nightingale gives update on AEW hand injury recovery
summary_src: Willow Nightingale is still working her way back to 100 percent after the hand injury she suffered this summer. On the road to AEW All In 2026, Nightingale’s status for the pay-per-view was complicated by a hand injury. She worked the PPV despite being hurt and has remained in action.
body: Willow Nightingale is still working her way back to 100 percent after the hand injury she suffered this summer. On the road to AEW All In 2026, Nightingale’s status for the pay-per-view was complicated by a hand injury . She worked the PPV despite being hurt and has remained in action. However, she’s done so at less than 100 percent. Nightingale did a Q&A on Instagram today and said she is still using a bone stimulator to help speed up the natural healing process. “It’s better, but not 100% healed,” she responded. “Still using that bone stimulator everyday, even if I have to fit it in while stuck in traffic.” Nightingale had a month-long reign as AEW Women’s World Champion before dropping the title to Mercedes Mone at All In this August. The most recent match that Nightingale took part in was an eight-person tag bout on the Grand Slam France edition this month where The Conglomeration lost to The Death Riders. This week marked the four-year anniversary of Nightingale’s AEW signing being officially announced. She’s become one of the most popular babyfaces in the company and was the first women’s triple crown champion in AEW history, holding the Women’s World Championship, TBS Championship, and Women’s Tag Team titles at different points.
