title: Samantha Irvin Hits Free Agency This Month
raw_title: Backstage News On Former WWE Ring Announcer Samantha Irvin's Impending Free Agency
summary_src: A new report revealed more on the free agency status of former WWE ring announcer Samantha Irvin following her lengthy non-compete clause.
body: Former WWE ring announcer Samantha Irvin, now going by her real name, Samantha Johnson, will soon hit free agency, though she may not be immediately headed to AEW alongside her husband, Ricochet, like many fans may think. Irvin left WWE in October 2024 , but with her departure came a lengthy non-compete clause . According to a new report from Fightful Select , Irvin is a free agent this month. The outlet reported that after leaving WWE, she had an official non-compete clause, compared to the 90-day "termination period" that many stars have after being released from the company, which is not a true non-compete. It was previously reported that her contract allowed her to quit at any time, but if she didn't see out her three-year deal, a two-year non-compete would be imposed. Stars released, or those who do not have their deals renewed, are often paid for their 30-day or 90-day "termination periods," but Irvin was not. Fightful Select confirmed Irvin joining AEW has been discussed, but she won't be jumping on board immediately. After her departure from WWE, Irvin was open about not liking her position as a ring announcer , and said she wanted to be a manager or other on-screen character instead. Irvin has focused mainly on her music career , releasing multiple singles, including the song "Make Me." Plans for a potential AEW career for her, possibly as a manager for Ricochet and The Demand, were not noted in the latest report. The stable are former AEW World Trios Champions, and Ricochet recently competed in the Clockwork Carnage match at AEW WrestleDream, challenging for Will Ospreay's AEW World Championship.
summary: Per Fightful Select, former WWE ring announcer Samantha Irvin, now known as Samantha Johnson, becomes a free agent this month after leaving the company in October 2024. She is subject to a lengthy non-compete clause rather than the standard 90-day termination period given to most released talent. While joining AEW alongside her husband Ricochet has been discussed internally, she will not be appearing with the promotion right away.

title: Alice Crowley Reflects On Early Start In Wrestling
raw_title: Alice Crowley Reflects On Her Career, Speaks About Future Goals
summary_src: Alice Crowley speaks about her career and future goals. Ahead of the start of the CMLL Women's Grand Prix, Fightful's Luis Pulido spoke to participant Alice Crowley.
body: Ahead of the start of the CMLL Women’s Grand Prix, Fightful’s Luis Pulido spoke to participant Alice Crowley. She opened up about her career thus far in wrestling and said the following: “I would say, honestly, I should have probably started a little bit later than what I did because I started at 14, but I, I think it helped me be able to get to, you know, obviously be here and like at 23, not a lot of women can say that you know they’ve done these things at this point in their career. I would say it’s definitely because of the time that I took when I was younger training instead of waiting till I turned 18 or whatever. Most places require you to be, but the place I trained at only required a parent, guardian, or somebody to be present, which I appreciated because my parents would always go with me. I think if I didn’t start that young, I wouldn’t be where I am right now, for sure. It’s genuinely just because of the fact that I have been able to get all of my reps in earlier, way early on, so now that I’m even when I was 20 going on 21 going on into 22 and now 23, I was still, you know, being able to figure that part out.” Adding on to that, Crowley was asked about her future goals in wrestling. “I would say that this is probably one of my goals, I mean, I feel that I can still consider it as one of my goals as it hasn’t happened yet, we still got a few days, but wrestling in Arena México was definitely, of for sure one of my goals, and to be able to say that I’m I’m doing it at 23 is just mind-blowing, it’s still mind-blowing, it’s like still even right now, and wrestling for CMLL just one of the longest running companies in existence, you know, if not the longest running company in existence, you know, it’s just… I’m so grateful, so thankful.”
summary: In an interview with Fightful ahead of the CMLL Women’s Grand Prix, 23-year-old Alice Crowley discussed her wrestling career. She said starting training at age 14, rather than waiting until 18, allowed her to accumulate experience early with parental support at her training facility. Crowley noted that this foundation enabled her to reach significant milestones by her early 20s that few other women have achieved at that stage.

body: They say, “looks aren’t everything,” but physical appearance counts for a lot. Looks play a major role in determining and reinforcing social status. We unconsciously believe attractive individuals to be more intelligent, persuasive, trustworthy, and skilled, even when lacking any objective evidence. In the image-is-reality world of professional wrestling, looks are even more important. The Airport Test is a concept attributed to former WWE head Vince McMahon, though it has long been used by promoters, talent scouts, and wrestling veterans. It is a traditional evaluation of whether a wrestler possesses a larger-than-life presence that naturally turns heads. It poses a simple hypothetical question: If this wrestler walks through a crowded airport in plain civilian clothes, do regular people turn their heads, stop and stare, or ask, “Who is that?” The Airport Test is one way of gauging whether a wrestler possesses “The It Factor”: a combination of physical presence, size, and marketability. Archetypal tough guys like Goldberg, massive behemoths like Andre the Giant and The Undertaker, and hyper-muscular freaks of nature like Brock Lesnar and Batista are classic examples of wrestlers who pass this standard with flying colors. Standing nearly six feet tall with the physical conditioning of a bodybuilder, iconic platinum-blonde hair, natural beauty, and commanding confidence, Cargill is the epitome of a striking look. The fact that she uses a wig takes nothing away from her undeniable star presence. She looks like a Greek goddess and undoubtedly turns heads instantly in public. Onlookers may not know who she is, but they instantly recognize that she is someone important. Cargill may not be a top ring performer, but she certainly looks great on a promotional poster. Oba’s remarkable appearance is the trait that most sets him apart from his peers. One of the most physically imposing stars ever to emerge from NXT onto the main roster, Oba Femi stands roughly 6-4 and is blessed with a massively muscular frame without appearing muscle-bound or slow—reminiscent of Brock Lesnar or Bobby Lashley rather than Hulk Hogan. Oba has a broad, strong jawline and a prominent forehead, giving his face a solid, sculpted look that complements his mighty frame. “The Ruler” maintains an intense, unblinking focus, which projects unshakable confidence. He looks every bit the warrior-king character he portrays, making him the quintessential embodiment of a wrestling champion. Standing 6-3 with superhero proportions, long dark hair, movie-star good looks, and a commanding presence, Reigns naturally draws eyes wherever he goes. It was Reigns’s remarkable look that caused Vince McMahon to push him as WWE’s lead babyface in 2015 despite early fan rejection. Those looks continue to serve Reigns well today, landing him the role of Akuma, the final antagonist in the 2026 “Street Fighter” film. Little acting was required of Reigns for the part; he mostly had to look menacing and threa

The Airport Test, long used by promoters and attributed to Vince McMahon, evaluates if a wrestler has larger-than-life presence that turns heads in civilian clothes at a crowded airport. Oba Femi meets the standard of possessing the It Factor through size, physical presence and marketability, unlike several other rising and fading stars.

body: My final ballot for this year’s Wrestling Observer Hall of Fame is complete. Looking at my final list, what fascinates me the most is that I have overlooked a lot of people over the years who I think are no-brainers now. I’ll get to those I missed, but sorting out all of these names does make me realize that Hall of Fame ballot choices can be quite fluid – some people make it some years, others get left out upon further reflection. Opinions evolve, especially when judging wrestlers who are still on weekly television and are still at their peak. There’s also so much chatter about the Hall of Fame each year, there is always the matter of persuasion. Well, after weeks of analyzing and thinking it over, I’ve come down to my final choices for this year’s ballot. I made the case for these four here . JYD was a big draw in Mid-South and the same for the Von Erichs in Texas, enough to where I think they all deserve in. Pro wrestling history would feel incredibly different without them. And JYD was really close last year! He should get in. I still feel strongly about The Briscoes’ influence on tag team wrestling in the 2010s, and Becky Lynch’s importance in regards to the rise of women’s wrestling in this country can’t be overstated. Jon Moxley has been such an integral part of AEW, he has to be in too. I originally had The Hardy Boyz on my ballot in previous years. I still think they should still be in, as their style and look paved the way for many similar teams in the early-to-mid 2000s like The Young Bucks. The problem here isn’t their eligibility, but the fact that I can only pick six people, and I had to make a tough choice. But there will be future ballots! I am voting for Jeff Jarrett for one reason: TNA. Without a viable second promotion in the wake of WCW’s demise, we wouldn’t have seen the likes of AJ Styles, Samoa Joe, Christopher Daniels, Frankie Kazarian, the Motor City Machine Guns, Amazing Red, Low Ki, and so many others wrestle on a national platform. Granted, many of them were found through ROH first, but TNA was the promotion that brought them to weekly television. There are some caveats that make me think he will struggle. He never became a main event star in WWE, he was WCW Champion at a time when that promotion was in a freefall, and TNA’s story has always been more about survival than success. But he was the one most successful in running a secondary promotion in the mid-2000s that brought attention to the next generation of big stars, and that counts for something. As I mentioned earlier, I have made some big omissions in past ballots, and I am stunned I never thought much about Samoa Joe until now. Upon further reflection, I think he’s a no-brainer, as he has built an incredible legacy for himself. After all, a lot of the early Ring of Honor buzz was because of him and his run as ROH World Champion. title: Comeback Watch: Shotzi Blackheart TNA Wrestling future plans after her return: What's next for the former WWE star in her new home?
raw_title: Shotzi Blackheart TNA Wrestling future plans after her return: What's next for the former WWE star in her new home?
body: On the October 22 edition of TNA Thursday Night IMPACT, Shotzi Blackheart made her official return as the newest signing to the company. Now that the former WWE star has arrived, it should be interesting what she has in store for the fans. From championship gold to unfinished business, there is a ton of potential for Blackheart in TNA Wrestling moving forward. Here are some potential Shotzi Blackheart TNA Wrestling plans after her return. Making her official return to TNA Wrestling on the October 22 IMPACT, Shotzi Blackheart came out to make the save for Allie against Kiera Hogan and Tasha Steelz. Hogan and Allie had been a pairing since Kiera’s return to the company at TNA Lockdown 2026. Winning the TNA Knockouts World Tag Team Championships, it seemed like Kiera was a good friend and partner for Allie until she turned her back on her to reunite Fire N’ Flava with Tasha Steelz. Now that the battle lines are drawn, Shotzi teaming with Allie against Fire N’ Flava feels like the first order of business for “The Ballsy Badass.” Before being betrayed by Kiera Hogan, Allie proclaimed that she wanted the TNA Knockouts World Tag Team Championships back. At TNA Bound For Glory 2026, Shayna Baszler made her debut with the company to team Zoey Serrano to defeat Allie and Kiera Hogan to win the TNA Knockouts World Tag Team Championships. Now known as Apex, Baszler and Serrano are looking to exert their dominance on the Knockouts tag team division. While they will undoubtedly be a tough challenge, Allie and Shotzi Blackheart could make for a unique duo that might have what it takes to dethrone Apex down the line. Shotzi Blackheart is no stranger whatsoever when it comes to tag team action throughout her career. During her time in WWE NXT, Shotzi formed a group with both Gigi Dolin and Tatum Paxley called Chemical X. Since her WWE release, Blackheart has been in the ring as a partner and opponent to Dolin, now known as Priscilla Kelly, on multiple occasions. With Shotzi signing with TNA Wrestling, she may now open the door for PK to join her in the company sooner rather than later. At TNA Bound For Glory 2026, Indi Hartwell defeated Xia Brookside to win the TNA Knockouts World Championship. Then, Hartwell was forced to give Brookside her rematch and defeated her once again on the October 22 TNA Thursday Night IMPACT. With Brookside taken out twice, Indi might have to face new challenges from the Knockouts division. Considering her success since leaving WWE, Shotzi Blackheart feels like someone who could be a more than formidable challenger for the new TNA Knockouts World Champion. title: Results Recap: TNA Bound For Glory 2026 Winners, Live Grades, Reaction and Highlights
raw_title: TNA Bound For Glory 2026 Winners, Live Grades, Reaction and Highlights
body: 01:09 Featured Video 1 Match We Want to See at Crown Jewel 👑 Previous Next TNA Bound For Glory 2026 Winners, Live Grades, Reaction and Highlights Chris Mueller Oct 11, 2026 Welcome to Bleacher Report's coverage of TNA Bound for Glory 2026. Let's take a look at everything that happened at this year's Bound for Glory PPV. The first match of the night saw Sosa take on what the announcers called his biggest opponent to date, Edwards. At just 21 years old, Sosa is in a similar spot to where Slater was when he first joined TNA. If he can keep impressing officials, he will have a long career ahead of him. The pace was quick whenever Sosa was in control, and whenever Edwards took over, it became a little more hard-hitting. This was a decent match, but it felt more like it belonged on TV than on a PPV. This did not have the feel of taking place at the biggest show of the year for TNA. Things picked up in the second half and made it a little more exciting, especially whenever Sosa took to the skies. Sosa ended up taking out Alisha Edwards when she got involved, but that distraction allowed Eddie to gain the upper hand momentarily, but Sosa finished him off with a Headshot for the win. Aichner was out first for this Scramble match that went from six to seven competitors when Amazing Red revealed he would be involved during the TNA Hall of Fame ceremony. The other competitors included BDE, Alexander, Navarro, Swann, Red and the younger Nemeth brother, Ryan. Most of these guys qualify as high-flyers, so we knew we were in for a show, but the inclusion of Nemeth and Aichner gave those guys a base. As expected, this match was fast-paced right out of the gate. There wasn't a single moment when nothing was happening in or outside the ring. Not every spot was memorable, but they all added to the overall entertainment. Swann was one of the standouts, which is not surprising given his skills, but even with seven people all vying for the crowd's attention, it never felt like it was too chaotic to follow what was happening. After several close calls, Red ended up pinning Navarro to become the new X-Division champion. The newly inducted Hall of Famer looked elated when he was handed the belt. Shayna Baszler made her TNA in-ring debut at Bound for Glory when she teamed with Serrano to take on Allie and Hogan for the Knockouts tag titles. Hogan and Allie may have come into this as the champions, but they were also the underdogs in many ways. title: Sheamus Posts Intense Gym Workout
raw_title: Sheamus Shares New Gym Photos, Former WWE Coworkers Respond
summary_src: Former WWE star Sheamus shared new gym photos on Instagram, and many of his former coworkers jumped in his comments to respond.
body: WWE Former WWE star Sheamus, now going by S. Farrelly, may not be immediately jumping back between the ropes following his WWE departure , but he's not skipping any time in the gym. The star took to Instagram on Friday to share some snapshots while training , and a number of his former co-workers took to his comments. Sheamus shared two photos and a video of himself hitting seated shoulder shrugs with 120 pound weights, alongside the caption, "shrug it out." Finn Balor was the first star in his comments, leaving a toilet emoji, seemingly in reference to Sheamus' face while lifting the impressive weight. "Settle down fella," CM Punk commented, alongside a fire emoji. Grayson Waller called the star a "machine," while Bayley left a comment about missing him. Plenty of fans left comments as well, with many saying they hope he ends up in AEW. As of a Fightful Select report on October 1, there had been no discussions between Sheamus and AEW as of that time . The outlet reported that some performers within the company's locker room would like to see Sheamus become "All Elite." The star also recently booked a convention appearance on the same day as AEW Full Gear , but reportedly asked to be able to leave the event early, as he indicated he had a wedding to attend, making wrestling fans suspicious. Sheamus' most recent match came last November. He teamed alongside John Cena and Rey Mysterio to defeat Dominik Mysterio, JD McDonagh, and Balor. His last televised singles match was a Last Time is Now tournament match the same month against Shinsuke Nakamura. After his victory, it was revealed Sheamus had to exit the tournament due to a shoulder injury.

Former coworkers Finn Balor, CM Punk, Grayson Waller and Bayley commented on the post. Per Fightful Select, there had been no talks between Sheamus and AEW as of October 1 though some in the locker room would like to see him join.

body: The MLW World Tag Team Championships will be defended in a Chicago Street fight at MLW Saturday Night SuperFight. MLW announced on Friday that the Good Brothers will defend their championships against Glasgow Boys On Top at the November 7th PPV. The match comes after GBOT attacked CJ Gallows an d then mocked the situation on this week’s show. Gallows, the son of Doc Gallows, was said on the show to be on the hospital with a concussion, fractured jaw, damaged teeth and a bruised lung. “Doc Gallows and Karl Anderson cut short an overseas trip to be at CJ’s side. From the hospital, the World Tag Team Champions delivered their answer: Glasgow Boys On Top will get the championship fight they have been demanding — and everything that comes with a Chicago Street Fight. For Gallows, this is a father’s reckoning. For Anderson, it is about standing beside his brother and making GBOT answer for what they did to his family. The champions are putting their titles on the line to get their hands on the men responsible, with no disqualifications to save them when the fight turns ugly. GBOT wanted a title shot badly enough to send a message through the champion’s son. Now, the ruthless Scots have forced open a door that could lead straight to the World Tag Team Championship — if they can survive the fury waiting on the other side. MLW has already levied fines against Glasgow Boys On Top, with contract termination still a possibility. But no fine can settle this score, and no championship victory can erase the image of CJ lying in a hospital bed. In Chicago, the Good Brothers intend to make GBOT feel every bit of it.”

title: Willow Nightingale Gives Hand Injury Update
raw_title: AEW Star Willow Nightingale Provides Update On Hand Injury
summary_src: Former AEW Women's World Champion Willow Nightingale took to her Instagram stories to provide an update on her hand injury.
body: AEW/Ricky Havlik Former AEW Women's World Champion Willow Nightingale has been battling a hand injury since the end of August , days before she defended, and lost, her championship to Mercedes Mone at AEW All In London 2026 . The star took to her Instagram stories on Friday to address how she's healing, as she hasn't wrestled in a little over two weeks. Replying to a fan question during a Q&A session on her stories, Nightingale revealed her hand is "better," but still not 100 percent healed. She posted the update alongside an image of herself driving using a machine on her left hand. "Still using that bone stimulator every day, even if I have to fit it in while stuck in traffic," Nightingale said. After losing her championship in London, Nightingale battled Thekla at AEW All Out on September 26 in an effort to earn a shot at Mone and the gold at AEW WrestleDream. Thekla defeated Nightingale at the Chicago-area pay-per-view, then went on to lose her title opportunity against "The CEO." The broken hand is the second injury for Nightingale in 2026. In May, she had to forfeit her spot in the 2026 women's Owen Hart Foundation tournament , as well as vacate her TBS Championship, due to a shoulder injury. Nightingale's most recent match, a mixed eight-person tornado tag, took place on October 6, but didn't air until " AEW Collision: Grand Slam Paris " on October 10. She teamed alongside her Conglomeration stablemates Kyle O'Reilly, Orange Cassidy, and Roderick Strong in a loss to the Death Riders' Marina Shafir, Claudio Castagnoli, Daniel Garcia, and Wheeler Yuta.
summary: AEW star Willow Nightingale has been sidelined with a hand injury since late August. In an Instagram Q&A, she revealed her hand is improving but not fully healed and that she continues daily use of a bone stimulator. The injury is her second of 2026 after an earlier issue forced her to forfeit a scheduled appearance in May.

title: Ric Flair Hospitalized After Fall With Head Injuries
raw_title: Legendary wrestler Ric Flair, 77, hospitalized with head injuries hours after revealing blood clot
body: Per the TMZ report, which included photos and video of the 77-year-old wrestler down on the sidewalk being attended to paramedics, Flair suffered a "nasty" fall while walking across the street after leaving Tampa's Wagamama bar and restaurant. TMZ reported that Flair sustained cuts on his head and around his eye, that his eye was "bleeding extensively," and that it is also believed he may have sustained a concussion. The incident occurred just hours after Flair canceled an appearance at a fan convention in Seattle due to a blood clot in his leg. In a social media post Friday, Flair referenced the ongoing situation with Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts, whose season recently ended due to the discovery of blood clots in his lungs , and said he is scheduled to have a procedure to address the issue soon. Unfortunately, I Am Dealing With A Blood Clot In My Leg, And My Doctors Have Limited My Travel To 3–4 Hours. Seattle Falls Outside That Range, And As Disappointed As I Am, I Have To Put My Health And Recovery First. Blood Clots Are Extremely Serious And Can Be Life-Threatening. We Have Seen This Recently With Jalen Hurts And The Complications Involving Blood Clots In His Lungs. It Is A Reminder That This Is Not Something To Take Lightly, And I Must Follow Medical Advice. I'm Scheduled To Have A Procedure To Strip The Affected Vein, Which My Doctors Expect Will Allow Me To Be Cleared For More Travel Afterward. Please Know This Decision Was Not Made Lightly. I Am Truly Sorry For The Inconvenience And Disappointment, And I Am Incredibly Grateful For Your Patience, Understanding, And Continued Support. I Look Forward To Getting Healthy And Seeing You All Down The Road. Thank You For The Love And Support. Flair is a two-time WWE Hall of Famer and widely considered to be one of the greatest talents in pro-wrestling history. Flair's status following his hospitalization Friday is currently uncertain. Uncrowned will continue to update this story as it develops.
summary: Ric Flair, 77, fell while crossing a street in Tampa after leaving a restaurant, suffering cuts to his head and eye along with heavy bleeding and a suspected concussion. The incident happened hours after he canceled a Seattle fan convention appearance due to a blood clot in his leg that limits his travel. Flair had posted on social media about the clot and his upcoming medical procedure, referencing the seriousness of the condition.

title: TKO’s Ari Emanuel Speaks On Possible WWE Crown Jewel Relocation Amid Saudi Arabia Attacks
raw_title: TKO’s Ari Emanuel Addresses Possible WWE Crown Jewel Relocation Amid Saudi Arabia Attacks
body: 0 TKO CEO Ari Emanuel comments on the status of WWE Crown Jewel. The eighth annual WWE Crown Jewel Premium Live Event is scheduled to take place at Riyadh Season Stadium in KAFD, Saudi Arabia, on Saturday, November 7, 2026. However, the recent attacks by the Iran-backed Houthi rebel group on King Khalid International Airport have cast uncertainty over the safety of talent, staff, and fans traveling into the region ahead of the show. The U.S. State Department recently issued a security warning for Americans traveling to or from the Middle East, including Saudi Arabia, to exercise “heightened vigilance.” The U.S. Embassy in Riyadh also instructed American citizens to exercise extreme caution when using airports in Saudi Arabia and check directly with airlines and airport authorities for updates. PWInsider recently reported that WWE still plans to host Crown Jewel in Saudi Arabia and has contingency plans in place, including hiring a security firm experienced in the Middle East and North Africa region. In a recent interview with Fox News to promote his memoir, TKO CEO Ari Emanuel addressed WWE Crown Jewel’s status. He said the event is still set to take place in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, as planned. “Right now, everything is still set. This weekend, coming up in Abu Dhabi, we have a UFC fight. Rey Mysterio then confronted Zayn, expressing uncertainty about his brother Penta's intentions regarding a potential cash-in. title: WWE Remembers "Exotic" Adrian Street
raw_title: WWE Remembers "Exotic" Adrian Street - WWE
body: More Share Options More Share Options Share close facebook x threads email WWE is saddened to learn that Adrian Street has passed away. Born the son of a coal miner in Wales, Street enjoyed a nearly 60-year career that spanned the globe, as his flamboyant style entertained audiences and reimagined what was possible in sports-entertainment. After competing as Kid Tarzan, “Exotic” Adrian Street was introduced to the world in bold fashion, as Street would make his way to the ring adorned in pastels and glitter with his glam-rock entrance music providing the perfect soundtrack. Accompanied by his long-time manager and future wife, Miss Linda, Street worked throughout the UK, Germany, Mexico and Canada before finally settling in the Continental Championship Wrestling promotion in Birmingham, Alabama. Street estimated that he competed in somewhere between 12,000 and 15,000 matches, but his influence stretched well-beyond in-ring competition. Street is credited with designing the gear worn by Mick Foley’s “Dude Love” during his rivalry with “Stone Cold” Steve Austin. Street also starred alongside Ron Perlman in the 1981 film “Quest for Fire” and performed in the band “The Pile Drivers.” WWE extends its condolences to Street’s family, friends, and fans.

title: Comeback Watch: WWE Hall of Famer Makes In-Ring Return After Nearly 12 Years
raw_title: WWE Hall of Famer Makes In-Ring Return After Nearly 12 Years
body: 0 WWE Hall of Famer Road Dogg recently returned to the ring for his first official match in more than 11 years. The former WWE Tag Team Champion competed at Jeff Jarrett’s All-Star Super Slam event in Hendersonville, Tennessee, on October 22. His return was confirmed by the My World with Jeff Jarrett podcast. They shared a post celebrating the success of Jarrett’s event the following day. Road Dogg has remained involved in the wrestling business during his lengthy absence from in-ring competition. He previously worked as a WWE producer and held creative responsibilities. He mainly filled in for a role as co-lead writer for SmackDown, before departing his creative position earlier in 2026. Road Dogg’s participation had been announced ahead of the show. His return to competition ended a break that lasted more than a decade. Road Dogg teamed with Jarrett and Jay Lethal in a six-man tag team match against QT Marshall, Elijah Drago, and Brady Booker. The match took place during an event celebrating Jarrett’s 40 years in professional wrestling as part of Hendersonville Pig Fest. The appearance marked a notable milestone for Road Dogg. He had not wrestled in an official match since January 25, 2015. His last match before Thursday’s return took place at WWE Royal Rumble 2015, where he teamed with Billy Gunn as the New Age Outlaws against The Ascension. Road Dogg was inducted into the WWE Hall of Fame in 2019 as a member of D-Generation X. Beyond his accomplishments as a performer, he spent years contributing to WWE’s production and creative operations. title: Tiffany Stratton Attempts Money in the Bank Cash-In During October 23 WWE SmackDown
raw_title: Tiffany Stratton Attempts Money in the Bank Cash-In During October 23 WWE SmackDown
summary_src: Tiffany Stratton nearly cashed in her Money in the Bank contract on WWE SmackDown, and Liv Morgan was seconds away from being forced to defend her championship. Stratton showed up after Chelsea Green’s title defense against Roxanne Perez and cleared the ring before making her move.
body: The chaos went down on the October 23, 2026 episode of WWE SmackDown , where Chelsea Green defended her WWE Women’s Championship against Roxanne Perez. Green had her hands full throughout the match, especially with Raquel Rodriguez getting involved behind the referee’s back. Raquel pushed Green off the turnbuckles while the referee was checking on Perez, allowing Perez to hit a Shining Wizard for a near fall. IYO SKY eventually came out to confront Raquel, leading to another confrontation at ringside. Despite the interference, Green managed to counter Perez’s Pop Rox and hit UnprettiHER to retain her championship. The trouble wasn’t over for Green. Liv Morgan attacked her immediately after the match, with Raquel joining in. IYO tried to fight them off, but Perez helped turn the numbers back in their favor as the group continued beating down Green and SKY. That’s when Tiffany Stratton’s music hit. Stratton rushed to the ring carrying her Money in the Bank briefcase and went after Perez, Morgan, and Rodriguez. IYO also got involved, hitting Raquel with a missile dropkick as the two women fought back against the attack. Things got even more interesting when Morgan tried using the briefcase against Stratton. IYO stopped her with a strike, allowing Stratton to land a kick of her own. Stratton then handed her briefcase to the referee, appearing ready to officially cash in her Money in the Bank contract. However, she decided to hit Morgan with the briefcase first before going through with the cash-in. That decision cost her the opportunity. While Stratton was discussing the cash-in with the referee, Perez and Rodriguez managed to drag Morgan out of the ring and get her to safety. The match never officially started, meaning Stratton still has her Money in the Bank contract. Stratton made it clear that she’s looking for an opportunity to take Morgan’s Women’s World Championship, but The Judgment Day managed to protect their champion this time. With Morgan also scheduled to face Green at Crown Jewel, Stratton’s involvement could create another problem for both champions. Do you think Tiffany Stratton should have cashed in immediately instead of attacking Liv Morgan with the briefcase first? Let us know what you think in the comments. body: 0 Samantha Irvin could be getting closer to a possible AEW career. According to a new update, the former WWE ring announcer, who now goes by her real name, Samantha Johnson, is set to become a free agent in October 2026 after a non-compete period following her WWE exit. Johnson left WWE in October 2024. However, her departure came with an unusual contract arrangement that set her apart from most WWE stars who leave the company. According to Fightful Select , AEW has discussed bringing Johnson into the company for an on-screen role several times. However, an immediate debut is reportedly not in the plans, and she may not appear on AEW TV anytime soon. Fightful Select reported that Johnson had a non-compete clause in her contract. This was different from the 30-day or 90-day periods often described as non-competes when WWE releases talent or allows their contracts to expire. Those periods usually involve talent receiving pay while their agreements wind down. Johnson’s reported contract allowed her to leave WWE at any time. However, if she quit before completing her three-year deal, she would face a two-year non-compete restriction. Unlike released WWE stars who are typically paid during their termination periods, Johnson reportedly received no payment during this time. With the restriction ending in October 2026, Johnson will soon have more freedom to explore opportunities in pro wrestling again. AEW could be a potential destination for Johnson as her husband, Ricochet, has emerged as a key part of the AEW roster for a few years now. Moreover, she has been backstage at several AEW events earlier. According to Fightful Select, AEW has discussed bringing Johnson into an on-screen role on multiple occasions. However, the latest report did not confirm that she had signed a deal or reveal when she might debut. title: Charlotte Flair Provides Latest On Ric Flair’s Condition After Hospitalization
raw_title: Charlotte Flair Provides Update on Ric Flair’s Condition After Hospitalization
summary_src: Ric Flair’s scary trip to the hospital finally has a positive update, and it came straight from his daughter, Charlotte Flair. After the WWE Hall of Famer was rushed to a Florida hospital following a nasty fall on Friday, October 23, Charlotte confirmed that her father is going to be okay.
body: Later Friday evening, Charlotte addressed her father’s condition on social media after news broke that Flair had been hospitalized in Tampa. Rather than simply telling everyone he was recovering, she shared a funny moment involving her father and a reference to one of wrestling’s most famous rivalries. “Not my dad telling the doctor he fell bc of warrior dropping him on his head…(ps: he’s going to be ok)” Charlotte was referring to The Ultimate Warrior, giving everyone a glimpse of Flair’s sense of humor despite the frightening situation. More importantly, her message offered some much-needed reassurance about his condition. Flair was taken to the hospital Friday morning after falling while walking across the street near Wagamama in Tampa. The 77-year-old suffered cuts to his head and eye, with significant bleeding around his face. Emergency responders treated him at the scene before transporting him to a nearby hospital. The incident came just hours after Flair revealed that he was dealing with a blood clot in his leg . Doctors had already restricted his travel to three or four hours, forcing him to cancel an appearance at Washington State Horror Con in Seattle. He also disclosed plans to undergo a procedure to address the affected vein. There has been no confirmation that the blood clot played any role in Friday’s fall, and Charlotte didn’t provide specific details about his injuries or whether doctors had cleared him to leave the hospital. Still, after everything that happened Friday, Charlotte’s update is the news everyone was hoping to hear. Flair went from announcing a serious medical problem to being taken away in an ambulance on the same day. At least now his daughter says he’s going to be okay, and judging by the story she shared, the Nature Boy hasn’t lost his sense of humor. body: WWE Chelsea Green retained the WWE's Women's Championship against Roxanne Perez on "SmackDown" , despite Judgment Day getting involved. Green backed Perez in the corner and she used the turnbuckle to take her down. Perez worked her arm and rolled her up. Green put her in a body scissors and then took her down again for a pin attempt. Perez sent her to the outside, but Green got in the ring and landed a dropkick and a crossbody. Perez rolled out of the ring and caught a baseball slide attempt. Back in the ring, Perez sent her into the ringpost and stomped on her arm over the rope. After the break, Perez superplexed Green. Green connected with a clothesline, enzuiguri and meteora. Perez blocked the Unprettier and pinned her. Green got pushed off the turnbuckle by Raquel Rodriguez. Perez landed a Shining Wizard. IYO SKY attacked Rodriguez and landed a headscissors. Perez landed a crossbody on SKY. Green reversed Pop Rox into Unprettier for the win. Morgan attacked her after the match. She & Rodriguez double teamed Green. SKY suplexed Morgan. Perez pummeled SKY. Tiffany Stratton returned and cleaned house. SKY landed a dropkick on Rodriguez. Morgan swung Stratton's briefcase, but missed. Stratton considered cashing in, but swung at Morgan with the briefcase instead. Rodriguez & Perez pulled Morgan from the ring before she could finish cashing in.

Despite interference from multiple wrestlers including Raquel Rodriguez, IYO SKY, Liv Morgan and Tiffany Stratton's return, Green reversed Perez's Pop Rox into the Unprettier to score the pinfall victory. Judgment Day members got involved during and after the bout, leading to a chaotic post-match scene.

body: 0 Former AEW Women’s World Champion Willow Nightingale shared a new injury update on her broken hand. Nightingale’s hand injury became a concern in the weeks leading up to AEW All In 2026. Despite the setback, she competed at the PPV but lost the AEW Women’s World title to Mercedes Moné. Her broken hand added another challenge as she moved forward from the defeat. Nightingale shared the update on her Instagram story , posting a photo of herself behind the wheel with the bone stimulator attached to her injured hand. While she is happy with the progress, she mentioned that she still has some healing left to do. “It’s better, but not 100% healed. Still using that bone stimulator everyday, even if I have to fit it in while stuck in traffic,” Nightingale wrote. Her update offers a look at her recovery routine. The injury has not kept her away from AEW TV or the ring completely, as AEW has continued to feature Nightingale on TV while she recovers. Fightful Select previously reported that the promotion wanted to keep her involved in its programming after she suffered the injury. This has allowed Nightingale to remain part of ongoing storylines. She later faced Thekla at AEW All Out last month and returned to action on the October 6 episode of Collision. Her most recent match was an eight-person mixed tornado tag team contest recorded on October 6 and later shown on AEW Collision: Grand Slam Paris on October 10. Nightingale teamed up with her Conglomeration stablemates Kyle O’Reilly, Orange Cassidy, and Roderick Strong. They faced the Death Riders’ Marina Shafir, Claudio Castagnoli, Daniel Garcia, and Wheeler Yuta. The Conglomeration ended up on the losing side. title: Baron Corbin Out Indefinitely After Cody Rhodes’ Brutal Punt Kick on WWE SmackDown
raw_title: Baron Corbin Out Indefinitely After Cody Rhodes’ Brutal Punt Kick on WWE SmackDown
summary_src: Baron Corbin is going to be out of action for a while, and Cody Rhodes is the reason why. The WWE United States Champion took a nasty punt kick to the head last week, and the damage is worse than originally known.
body: Michael Cole delivered the bad news on the October 23, 2026 episode of WWE SmackDown , revealing that Corbin suffered a cervical muscle strain, an orbital bone contusion, and blurred vision. According to WWE’s medical team, Corbin is out indefinitely. This all goes back to last week’s SmackDown, when Corbin ended up in an unplanned match against Cody Rhodes. Randy Orton got involved, but it was Rhodes who delivered the final blow. Cody nailed Corbin with a punt kick to the head, and that’s how the show went off the air. Now Corbin is paying the price, and there’s another problem WWE has to deal with. Corbin is still the United States Champion, which means WWE currently has a titleholder who can’t compete. There’s been no announcement about whether he’ll be stripped of the championship or if WWE will let him hold onto it while he recovers. For now, Corbin is on the shelf with no return date, and the future of the United States Championship is up in the air. Should WWE take the United States Championship off Baron Corbin, or let him keep it until he’s ready to wrestle again? Let us know in the comments. Zayn described himself as the smartest competitor who finds ways to survive, positioning himself as the current WWE Champion. He noted that with eight billion people in the world, only one man holds the title and becomes the target for others.

Rey Mysterio then confronted Zayn, expressing uncertainty about his brother Penta's intentions regarding a potential cash-in. Mysterio emphasized his longstanding friendship with Zayn but warned that disrespect toward his family would create issues, while also mentioning his own problems with Ricky Saints.

title: Liv Morgan Recalls Early WWE Training Advice
raw_title: Liv Morgan On Early Days Of Her WWE Training: 'Shut Up & Keep Your Eyes Open'
summary_src: Liv Morgan learned one important lesson she's kept with her since starting her WWE training.
body: WWE Women's World Champion Liv Morgan continues to be at the forefront of the women's division in WWE, recently defeating Stephanie Vaquer and Becky Lynch in a Triple Threat at Money in the Bank 2026. Although it's her fourth world title reign, Morgan's climb to the top wasn't easy, and while appearing on First We Feast's "Hot Ones," she recalled the key advice that's kept her going since. "Day one, starting [out], it was a lot of, ... 'Shut up and keep your eyes open,' you know?" Morgan recalled about her early days in the WWE system. "We're not even allowed in the ring for 30 days, back in my day when I started. Like, you were not allowed to even set foot in the WWE ring. You had to sit and watch from the sidelines. So I just remember learning to shut the f*** up!" In the past, Morgan reflected on her three-day WWE tryout , admitting how intimidating the physical demands of a wrestler were to her at the time, especially because she lacked an athletic background beyond competitive cheerleading. Despite originally seeing her signing as an achievement on its own, she later learned that she had a long way to go to achieve her dreams, which she eventually did. Now that she's carrying gold again, Morgan will have the eyes of the locker room set on her again, especially WWE Women's Champion Chelsea Green, who she's set to face for the Women's Crown Jewel Championship at the upcoming Night of Champions. At the same time, the current Ms. Money in the Bank, Tiffany Stratton, could potentially cash-in on either of them at any time, making it a hostile environment for any champion right now.

title: Match Made: Randy Orton vs. Cody Rhodes Last Man Standing Match Added to WWE Crown Jewel 2026
raw_title: Randy Orton vs. Cody Rhodes Last Man Standing Match Added to WWE Crown Jewel 2026
summary_src: WWE just added another major match to Crown Jewel, and Cody Rhodes and Randy Orton are going to settle their problems in a Last Man Standing Match. The two have been at each other’s throats for weeks, and now they’ve agreed to face each other in one of WWE’s most brutal stipulations.
body: The announcement came during the October 23, 2026 episode of WWE SmackDown , when Orton came to the ring and started taking shots at Rhodes. Orton actually praised Cody for finally using a punt kick against Baron Corbin last week, saying he never thought Rhodes would have the guts to do something like that. Orton claimed he was proud of Cody because he was the only person who managed to make him snap. However, he also warned that kicking someone like Corbin was one thing, but doing it to Orton would be a completely different story. Orton insisted that Cody would hesitate if he ever had the chance to punt him in the head. That’s when Rhodes had heard enough. Cody came to the ring as Nick Aldis and WWE officials tried to keep the two separated. Rhodes called Orton a coward and reminded him of all the people he had hurt throughout his career, including Triple H, Shawn Michaels, and Cody’s own father, Dusty Rhodes. Rhodes also brought up Orton kicking him in the head, saying that while Orton was nursing his wounds in St. Louis, Cody was the one who walked away with his head held high. Cody then made it clear that he wasn’t afraid of Orton, telling him that the three most dangerous letters he needed to worry about were “I.O.U.” Things nearly got physical when Rhodes removed his jacket, but Aldis stepped in before either man could throw a punch. Orton insisted that just because Cody wanted a fight didn’t mean he would get one. Aldis had another idea. He suggested they settle things at Crown Jewel on November 7. Cody agreed, but he wanted something more than a regular match. He demanded a Last Man Standing Match, leaving Orton to decide whether he was willing to accept those terms. Orton eventually agreed and left Cody with one final warning, telling him to remember that he was the one who asked for this. WWE Crown Jewel takes place on November 7, 2026, in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. <text color=”secondary” inline>WWE’s previously announced champion-versus-champion matches are also listed on its official event page. Orton and Rhodes have made this rivalry personal, and now neither man will be able to win simply by scoring a pinfall or submission. One of them will have to keep the other down for a ten-count. title: Cody Rhodes Challenges Randy Orton To Last Man Standing Match
raw_title: Cody Rhodes To Face Randy Orton In Big Stipulation Match At WWE Crown Jewel
summary_src: Cody Rhodes and Randy Orton will have a rubber match at WWE Crown Jewel on November 7.
body: WWE Randy Orton and Cody Rhodes will meet in a Last Man Standing rubber match at Crown Jewel, after Rhodes made the challenge during "WWE SmackDown." Orton first challenged Rhodes for the WWE Championship at WrestleMania, failing in that bid before meeting Rhodes in a non-title grudge match at Sunday Night's Main Event and getting the equalizing win. Orton revived the punt kick after his initial loss to Rhodes, and though Rhodes looked to do the same to him in their rematch, he hesitated and thus allowed Orton to get the win. Rhodes finally pulled the trigger and followed through on the punt kick last week, though it was not Orton at the receiving end of it, with Baron Corbin instead catching the raw end of things. That preceded their meeting in the ring during Friday's segment. Orton was out first in the segment and said he took pleasure in knowing he had been the one to bring that out of Rhodes. But he still didn't believe he would do it again when in the ring with him again. Rhodes then came out, swiftly followed by General Manager Nick Aldis and officials. Aldis interrupted when Rhodes finally called for a fight on the spot, offering to make the match for Crown Jewel. That's when Rhodes turned around and made the challenge for Last Man Standing, accepted by Orton with the warning that, when all is said and done, he had asked for this.
summary: Cody Rhodes issued a challenge to Randy Orton for a Last Man Standing rubber match at WWE Crown Jewel. The two previously split their pair of encounters this year with Orton winning the non-title rematch at Sunday Night's Main Event after Rhodes hesitated on a punt kick. Rhodes finally delivered the punt kick to Baron Corbin last week on SmackDown before confronting Orton in the ring where the challenge was made and accepted.

body: The rivalry between Cody Rhodes and Randy Orton will continue with a stipulation match at WWE Crown Jewel. WWE has revealed that Rhodes vs. Orton in a Last Man Standing match will take place at the November 7 PLE in Saudi Arabia. The stipulation was proposed by Rhodes during a confrontation on SmackDown tonight, and Orton responded by warning Rhodes to be careful what he wished for. With a history that dates back to Rhodes’ first stint in WWE, Rhodes and Orton have been feuding for much of 2026. They were opponents in one of the main events of WrestleMania 42, where it was Rhodes who got the win. Orton was then victorious when they faced off at Sunday Night’s Main Event in September. Orton has questioned Rhodes’ killer instinct throughout their rivalry. Hesitation cost Rhodes at Sunday Night’s Main Event, but their recent angles have seen Rhodes show a more aggressive side, including taking out Baron Corbin with a punt last week. During their segment tonight, Rhodes was ready to fight Orton right now, but Orton refused to face Rhodes tonight. That led to SmackDown General Manager Nick Aldis booking their match for Crown Jewel. The PLE, at least as of now, is still scheduled to be held in Riyadh despite turmoil in the Middle East. title: New WWE Women’s Tag Team Champions Crowned on October 23 SmackDown
raw_title: New WWE Women’s Tag Team Champions Crowned on October 23 SmackDown
summary_src: Alexa Bliss and Tatum Paxley’s run as WWE Women’s Tag Team Champions is already over. The two walked into SmackDown looking to make their first successful title defense, but Michin and B-Fab had other plans. Thanks to some outside interference, WWE now has new Women’s Tag Team Champions.
body: The title change happened during the October 23, 2026 episode of WWE SmackDown , when Bliss and Paxley defended their championships against Michin and B-Fab. The match started with B-Fab getting aggressive against Bliss, repeatedly shoving her in the face before the two started trading strikes. Paxley eventually tagged in and took control, even hitting a moonsault onto Michin outside the ring. Bliss later got back into the match and went after B-Fab, hitting a DDT and a blockbuster for a near fall. She attempted Sister Abigail, but B-Fab managed to escape before Michin tagged in. Things started falling apart for the champions after Paxley became the legal competitor. She attempted a 450 splash but landed on her feet when Michin moved out of the way. Paxley then tried to hit Cemetery Drive, but Michin managed to grab the ropes to stop the move. That’s when Jade Cargill got involved. Cargill punched Paxley while the referee wasn’t looking, giving Michin the opening she needed. Michin immediately hit a Styles Clash and covered Paxley for the three-count. Just like that, Michin and B-Fab became the new WWE Women’s Tag Team Champions. The result brings Bliss and Paxley’s championship reign to an abrupt end, with the two losing the titles in their first defense. It also raises questions about Jade Cargill’s involvement and why she decided to help Michin and B-Fab steal the victory. Zayn described himself as the smartest competitor who finds ways to survive, positioning himself as the current WWE Champion. He noted that with eight billion people in the world, only one man holds the title and becomes the target for others.

Rey Mysterio then confronted Zayn, expressing uncertainty about his brother Penta's intentions regarding a potential cash-in. Mysterio emphasized his longstanding friendship with Zayn but warned that disrespect toward his family would create issues, while also mentioning his own problems with Ricky Saints.
Zayn responded by urging calm and stating there were no problems between them. He advised focusing on Roman Reigns and reiterated that his issues were only with those showing disrespect.

Trick Williams interrupted the segment and made his way to the ring. Williams addressed Zayn directly, rejecting the idea that he lacks the ability to survive and highlighting his own growth over ten months in the company.

body: Rhodes did the unthinkable on last week's SmackDown after punt-kicking Baron Corbin flush in the head . The WWE Universe was shocked, and for a split second, even his former mentor and arch-rival Orton couldn't believe his eyes. Friday night this week, Orton would come out to address the elephant in the room. What was that? Well, Randy claimed that Cody couldn't do it, but he did it; he pulled the trigger. The "Viper" made it known that he was proud of Rhodes for doing what he did. That said, he knows, and everyone knows, that Cody will "hesitate" when it counts the most: against him. When the opportunity presents itself again, Cody will fall short, and he's going to be back to square one. Cody Rhodes would come out and voice his opinion. Rhodes made it known that he was well aware of how dangerous Randy is. He punted Triple H, Shawn Michaels, and even Cody's father, the late, great "American Dream" Dusty Rhodes. However, every time Orton made a statement, he wouldn't follow through, as Cody pushed the narrative that Orton is a self-sabotaging screw-up. Things got extremely heated as WWE officials surrounded the ring. SmackDown General Manager Nick Aldis tried to break up the impending fight and announced that if they wanted to do it, it wouldn't be tonight. However, it will happen as he sanctions a match at WWE Crown Jewel 2026 . Rhodes would remark that this next bout isn't going to be a normal match. He wants to end it, and he wants it to be a Last Man Standing Match. Orton would agree, setting the stage for the final showdown between Randy Orton and Cody Rhodes.

summary_src: B-Fab and Michin are the new WWE Women's Tag Team Champions after a victory over Tatum Paxley and Alexa Bliss on "WWE SmackDown."
body: WWE Michin and B-Fab are the new WWE Women's Tag Team Champions after defeating Alexa Bliss and Tatum Paxley, thanks to some help from Jade Cargill, on " WWE SmackDown ." Paxley and Bliss reigned for just over two weeks after defeating Fatal Influence for the gold . B-Fab and Bliss started off the match, and B-Fab had a flurry of offense before hitting a sliding clothesline to Bliss. She attempted a quick pin, but Bliss kicked out. She got B-Fab into a hold and backed into her own corner, where Paxley was able to tag in. Paxley took down B-Fab and sent Michin through the ropes before downing her on the outside with a moonsault off the apron. Bliss sent Michin crashing into the mat with a DDT and went to the top and took B-Fab out with a cross body. Paxley hit a kick to the back of Michin's neck and went up top, but had to roll through after a 450 attempt when Michin got out of the way. Michin avoided Paxley's Cemetery Drive by holding on to the rope. title: Match Made: CM Punk vs. Kevin Owens Set for November 6 WWE SmackDown in Brooklyn
raw_title: CM Punk vs. Kevin Owens Announced for November 6 WWE SmackDown in Brooklyn
summary_src: CM Punk and Kevin Owens are finally getting their hands on each other, and WWE has already locked in the date. The two have been blaming each other for their problems involving the Undisputed WWE Championship, and now they’ll get the chance to settle things in the ring.
body: The match was confirmed during the October 23, 2026 episode of WWE SmackDown , when Nick Aldis appeared in a video alongside both men. Aldis announced that Punk and Owens would face each other in two weeks on SmackDown before giving them a chance to speak their minds. Punk immediately made it clear that he didn’t want to be there. He called the entire conversation a waste of his time and blamed Owens for costing him the Undisputed WWE Championship. Owens wasn’t having any of that. He fired back by saying Punk wouldn’t be facing Roman Reigns at Crown Jewel anyway. Owens also argued that he should be the Undisputed WWE Champion right now because of Punk’s actions, not the other way around. Things got personal when Owens brought up Punk’s time away from WWE. Owens said he was perfectly happy ignoring Punk while he was gone and eventually realized that interacting with Punk was what made him miserable in the first place. Punk responded by telling Owens that he didn’t know him. Owens had an answer for that too, saying he knew enough people who had dealt with Punk over the years to know exactly what kind of person he was. The confrontation made it pretty clear that neither man is interested in backing down, especially with both believing the other is responsible for keeping him away from the Undisputed WWE Championship. Now they’ll have the opportunity to do something about it when SmackDown comes to Brooklyn on Friday, November 6, just one day before WWE Crown Jewel. With both men carrying a grudge and blaming each other for their championship problems, this won’t be just another match on SmackDown. Who do you think will come out on top when CM Punk and Kevin Owens finally face each other in Brooklyn? Let us know in the comments. title: End of an Era: ECW Original Angel Medina Officially Retires From Wrestling After Final Match
raw_title: ECW Original Angel Medina Officially Retires From Wrestling After Final Match
summary_src: Another ECW original has officially called it a career. Angel Medina, best known to wrestling fans as Angel of The Baldies, wrestled his final match on October 23, 2026, bringing an end to a career that included some of ECW’s wildest years.
body: Medina officially retired at a FLEX Wrestling event in Elmira, New York, where he faced fellow ECW veteran HC Loc. Medina lost the match, which had another familiar face involved, as longtime Baldies member Tony DeVito served as the special guest referee. That made the farewell a reunion of three men who shared plenty of history during ECW’s original run. Trained by WWE Hall of Famer Johnny Rodz, Medina first made a name for himself in the New York City wrestling scene under the name Spanish Angel. His biggest break came in 1999 when he joined Extreme Championship Wrestling and became part of The Baldies. The group, which included Tony DeVito, Vic Grimes, and Big Vito at different points, became a regular part of ECW television during the promotion’s run on TNN. Medina was primarily paired with DeVito, and The Baldies became known for their violent encounters, including a memorable rivalry with New Jack. When ECW shut down in 2001, Medina continued wrestling and eventually worked for IWA in Puerto Rico. However, he later stepped away from the business as a full-time career and moved into law enforcement in the Kansas area. Although Medina continued making occasional wrestling appearances over the years, he eventually decided it was time to officially close that chapter of his life. His match against HC Loc marked his final appearance as an active wrestler, with DeVito there to help bring things full circle. Medina might not have been one of ECW’s biggest names, but he was part of the promotion during a period that wrestling fans still remember for its chaotic matches and unforgettable rivalries. Now, more than 25 years after his ECW debut, Angel of The Baldies has officially stepped away from the ring on his own terms. title: Comeback Watch: Tiffany Stratton Makes Her SmackDown Return With Title Match Tease
raw_title: Tiffany Stratton Makes Her SmackDown Return With Title Match Tease
body: 0 Tiffany Stratton returned to WWE SmackDown after missing last week’s show following a scary fall at Money in the Bank. The former WWE Women’s Champion helped Chelsea Green and Iyo Sky before teasing a possible cash-in. Stratton had been absent from WWE TV since winning the Women’s MITB Ladder Match earlier this month. It was her second time winning the briefcase, giving her the chance to challenge for a championship whenever she wants. However, her victory came with a concerning moment. During the match, Stratton climbed a tall ladder and attempted a Swanton Bomb onto Charlotte Flair, Lash Legend, and Lola Vice. Unfortunately, the ladder moved, causing her to miss the exact spot and land dangerously on her head and neck. After winning the match, Stratton admitted during a post-show interview that her neck was hurting. She then missed the following episode of SmackDown, where Morgan suggested that Stratton had been injured during the Ladder Match. The October 23 episode of SmackDown featured Chelsea Green defending the WWE Women’s Championship against Roxanne Perez. Perez earned the title match after pinning Green on RAW two weeks earlier. The match took a turn when members of The Judgment Day appeared at ringside to help Perez. However, IYO SKY arrived to help Green retain her championship. The trouble continued after the match, as Liv Morgan, Raquel Rodriguez, and Perez attacked Green and Sky. Morgan caught Green off guard, while SKY tried to fight back against the Judgment Day members. Perez then went after SKY, and the Judgment Day members continued their attack. Just when things looked bad for Green and SKY, Stratton rushed to the ring. Miss MITB 2026 immediately attacked Perez and knocked her out of the ring. She then hit Morgan with a knee and took down Rodriguez with a hurricanrana. This gave SKY an opening to hit a missile dropkick on Rodriguez from the top rope. With the Judgment Day members on the back foot, Stratton thought of using her Money in the Bank contract. The two-time briefcase winner considered cashing in on Morgan and even hit her with the briefcase. However, Rodriguez and Perez pulled Morgan out of the ring before Stratton could officially challenge for the championship. The moment hinted that Morgan could be Stratton’s main target as she looks to become champion. body: 0 WWE SmackDown viewers experienced an apparent audio glitch during the October 23 broadcast on Netflix , prompting confusion and speculation across social media. The interruption occurred just before the WWE Women’s Championship match between Chelsea Green and Roxanne Perez, leaving fans wondering whether the problem was technical or something more. Neither WWE nor Netflix has confirmed the cause behind the incident. However, the timing quickly caught viewers’ attention as Perez made her entrance ahead of the championship contest. The apparent disruption occurred shortly before the commercial break leading into the title match. When the broadcast resumed, Green made her entrance, and the championship bout proceeded as scheduled. The timing sparked immediate questions on X, with several viewers reporting problems with audio. Is it for everyone ??? Or just Netflix #Smackdown” Meanwhile, @straightwrestle expressed frustration about the interruption happening during Perez’s entrance, posting, “Of course the Audio cuts right when Roxanne is coming out… come on mengggggg ?” The incident also fuelled speculation that the disruption might have been intentional, although no evidence has established a connection to a storyline or an upcoming WWE appearance. With no official explanation available, the cause remains unclear. Once the match got underway, Green retained the WWE Women’s Championship against Perez. Raquel Rodriguez attempted to interfere, but IYO SKY intervened, creating further chaos around the contest before Green secured the pinfall with the Killswitch. For now, the audio interruption remains unexplained. While fans are accustomed to reading between the lines of WWE’s storytelling, this time the only confirmed outcome was Green’s successful title defense — not the reason behind the broadcast disruption. body: SmackDown general manager Nick Aldis has granted Trick Williams a shot at the Undisputed WWE Championship against Sami Zayn . Williams vs. Zayn is now official for next week’s SmackDown in Charleston, West Viriginia. The winner of that match will go on to face Roman Reigns at Crown Jewel in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Earlier in the show, Sami Zayn was confronted by Rey Fenix for disrespecting his brother Penta , who is the current holder of the Money in the Bank briefcase. Penta can cash in the MITB on Zayn to become the Undisputed WWE Champion anytime, anywhere in the next year. Just when it looked like Zayn had peace with Fenix, Trick Williams entered the fray and talked his way into the champ’s head. Getty Trick Williams celebrates after defeating Sami Zayn during the United States Championship match during WrestleMania 42 at Allegiant Stadium on April 19, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. Before the bell started for the main event, Ricky Saints attacked Rey Fenix. Sami Zayn and Johnny Gargano then teamed up to beat up Trick Williams before Penta made the save to make it a six-man tag team match. After a back-and-forth between all six superstars, Williams earned momentum for his title shot next week. Getty Sami Zayn reacts during the United States Championship match against Trick Williams during WrestleMania 42 at Allegiant Stadium on April 19, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. body: 0 Cody Rhodes and Randy Orton are set for another showdown at WWE Crown Jewel after their rivalry intensified during the October 23 episode of SmackDown . With both men unwilling to back down, their latest confrontation led to a match announcement that could push their feud to another level. The pair have already traded victories in 2026, but Rhodes’ recent actions have added a more aggressive edge to their rivalry. Now, their next meeting will come under a stipulation that matches the intensity of the feud. Randy Orton opened the segment by praising Rhodes for finally showing a more ruthless side, following his punt kick to Baron Corbin the previous week. However, the Viper remained convinced that Rhodes would hesitate if he had to deliver the same move against him. Cody Rhodes came to the ring and demanded a fight, prompting SmackDown General Manager Nick Aldis to step in and propose a meeting at Crown Jewel. Rhodes then made his preferred stipulation clear. “I don’t think you’re listening to what I’m saying,” Rhodes told Orton. “You want me to wrestle Randy Orton? Okay, I’ll wrestle Randy Orton. But, it’s not just any match. Last Man Standing.” Orton accepted the challenge but warned Rhodes that he would have to live with the consequences of his decision. With the stipulation in place, there will be no disqualifications to end the contest, and the winner must leave his opponent unable to answer the referee’s count. Their rivalry has already featured two major encounters this year. Rhodes defeated Orton at WrestleMania 42, but Orton evened the score in their non-title grudge match at Sunday Night’s Main Event in September. The Viper has repeatedly questioned whether Rhodes has the killer instinct required to beat him. Rhodes’ recent punt kick on Corbin suggests that he is willing to cross lines he previously avoided, setting up another test against his former mentor. Crown Jewel is scheduled for November 7 in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. With the Last Man Standing stipulation now confirmed, Rhodes and Orton will have another chance to settle their differences — this time, the final man standing will have the last word. body: WWE Champion Sami Zayn smacked down United States Champion Trick Williams in a scathing promo last week that acted as an attempt at putting the young upstart in his place. Trick Willy got his chance to really fire back this week. He claimed Zayn doesn’t know anything about having “it,” which is funny because “it” already beat his ass at WrestleMania. That’s true, too. And otherwise, it’s Trick who walks, talks, and acts like a champion, not Sami. It almost felt meta that he was saying all this, even doing it in his own way. Because, yeah, he really does personify what a champion in WWE would typically look like. Sami made clear that if he wanted to, he could absolutely light Trick up on the microphone but he won’t because he’s a good guy. And it’s rich that Williams would talk about “it” when he doesn’t even know what it is. He’s closer to sink or swim than he realizes and he doesn’t actually want to be in there with the shark with sharp teeth. Trick wouldn’t back down. But they wouldn’t agree to a title match. Instead, they had Trick announce he’s getting one next week in a backstage segment. That pretty much tells you how that’s going to go. Meanwhile, Rey Fenix showed up this week to confront Zayn about going a little too hard after Penta, his brother, and what that means. Johnny Gargano is still hanging around the champ, so they did all this to get to a tag team match in the main event. Ricky Saints got involved in the main event, attacking Fenix. Penta showed up as a surprise and suggested making it a six-man tag. Naturally, that’s what happened. Really, it was a way for Trick to score a pinfall win while having Saints be the guy to take the fall, and have both Williams, the challenger next week, and Penta, Mr. Money in the Bank, stare down Zayn to close the show. Trick Willy wrestling for the WWE championship is something I was certain would happen eventually, I just don’t know that I ever saw it happening like this. It’s too much of a placeholder program for my tastes. Oba Femi is being courted as the next major star, and he would never be put in a position like this. I don’t like that WWE is doing it to Trick, while he’s holding a title of his own, no less! But he’s getting valuable experience and another opportunity to continue growing into the major star he can still become. I’ll have to settle for seeing that as the bright side. Chelsea Green had to defend her title against Roxanne Perez of The Judgment Day here, and of course they put together what was a pretty fun match. Green may not be the most polished wrestler but the division is filled with deeply talented workers like Perez who can absolutely do the heavy lifting in a match like this. Intercontinental Champion Raquel Rodriguez tried to interfere but to no avail. Green retained the title, and now looks ahead to her already scheduled showdown against Nikki Bella next week. Given that Bound For Glory is TNA's biggest event of the year, we expected a title match to kick off the main show festivities. The four-way TNA International Championship would have been a solid option, as would have been the seven-way scramble for the TNA X-Division Championship. Instead, the show started with a storyline with not as many teeth sunk into it: Ricky Sosa vs. Eddie Edwards. The match itself was fine. Sosa showed off his high-flying moves. body: WWE Champion Sami Zayn smacked down United States Champion Trick Williams in a scathing promo last week that acted as an attempt at putting the young upstart in his place. Trick Willy got his chance to really fire back this week. He claimed Zayn doesn’t know anything about having “it,” which is funny because “it” already beat his ass at WrestleMania. That’s true, too. And otherwise, it’s Trick who walks, talks, and acts like a champion, not Sami. It almost felt meta that he was saying all this, even doing it in his own way. Because, yeah, he really does personify what a champion in WWE would typically look like. Sami made clear that if he wanted to, he could absolutely light Trick up on the microphone but he won’t because he’s a good guy. And it’s rich that Williams would talk about “it” when he doesn’t even know what it is. He’s closer to sink or swim than he realizes and he doesn’t actually want to be in there with the shark with sharp teeth. Trick wouldn’t back down. But they wouldn’t agree to a title match. Instead, they had Trick announce he’s getting one next week in a backstage segment. That pretty much tells you how that’s going to go. Meanwhile, Rey Fenix showed up this week to confront Zayn about going a little too hard after Penta, his brother, and what that means. Johnny Gargano is still hanging around the champ, so they did all this to get to a tag team match in the main event. Ricky Saints got involved in the main event, attacking Fenix. Penta showed up as a surprise and suggested making it a six-man tag. Naturally, that’s what happened. Really, it was a way for Trick to score a pinfall win while having Saints be the guy to take the fall, and have both Williams, the challenger next week, and Penta, Mr. Money in the Bank, stare down Zayn to close the show. Trick Willy wrestling for the WWE championship is something I was certain would happen eventually, I just don’t know that I ever saw it happening like this. It’s too much of a placeholder program for my tastes. Oba Femi is being courted as the next major star, and he would never be put in a position like this. I don’t like that WWE is doing it to Trick, while he’s holding a title of his own, no less! But he’s getting valuable experience and another opportunity to continue growing into the major star he can still become. I’ll have to settle for seeing that as the bright side. Chelsea Green had to defend her title against Roxanne Perez of The Judgment Day here, and of course they put together what was a pretty fun match. Green may not be the most polished wrestler but the division is filled with deeply talented workers like Perez who can absolutely do the heavy lifting in a match like this. Intercontinental Champion Raquel Rodriguez tried to interfere but to no avail. Green retained the title, and now looks ahead to her already scheduled showdown against Nikki Bella next week. Women’s World Champion Liv Morgan was also in the building supporting her stablemate, and she attacked after
summary: United States Champion Trick Williams responded to WWE Champion Sami Zayn's previous promo by claiming Zayn lacks the intangible quality of a true champion. Williams pointed out that he defeated Zayn at WrestleMania and carries himself like a titleholder. The segment ended with Williams announcing he will challenge for the WWE Championship next week.

title: Samantha Irvin Nears Free Agency With AEW Interest
raw_title: Update on Free Agency Of Samantha Irvin, Interest From AEW
body: Samantha Irvin is set to be a free agent soon, and a new report has an update on the possibility that she will go to AEW. Fightful Select reports that the former WWE ring announcer is finally approaching the end of non-complete clause, which was a condition of her leaving the company early. The site also confirms that, fitting with speculation since she exited WWE, there has been discussion in AEW about potentially bringing Irvin on board. However, the site also notes that it has been “made clear” that it wouldn’t happen as soon as she isa free agent. Any appearance would likely be sometime down the road. Irvin, whose husband Ricochet is part of AEW, has previously said that ring announcing was not her goal, but that she was not done with wrestling. Irvin, real name Samantha Johnson, has been backstage at many AEW events over the last two years is said to have a “great relationship” with the promotion.
summary: Per Fightful Select, Samantha Irvin is nearing the end of her non-compete clause from her early WWE exit. AEW has held discussions about potentially signing the ring announcer, though any move would not occur immediately upon her becoming a free agent. Irvin, whose husband is Ricochet, has been backstage at numerous AEW events over the past two years and maintains a strong relationship with the company.

title: WWE SmackDown 10/23/26: 3 Things We Hated And 3 Things We Loved
raw_title: WWE SmackDown 10/23/2026: 3 Things We Hated And 3 Things We Loved
summary_src: On a night that saw the women's tag titles change hands, here are three things we hated and three things we loved about the 10/23/26 episode of "WWE SmackDown!"
body: WWE Welcome to Wrestling Inc.'s weekly review of "WWE SmackDown," the show that gave us, among other things, new women's tag team champions! The WINC crew actually doesn't have much of an opinion on that, so we won't be covering it here in this column, but we will be talking Chelsea Green's defense against Roxanne Perez , Cody Rhodes and Randy Orton getting their match at Crown Jewel , and more! As always, if you missed the show, you can catch up on all the goings-on Friday night by checking out our "WWE SmackDown" 10/23/26 live blog , which contains all the objective information you could possibly ask for. Here in this space, on the other hand, we deal with the subjective — specifically the WINC crew's opinions about the matches and segments that stood out to us the most on the show. Here are three things we hated and three things we loved about the 10/23/26 episode of "WWE SmackDown!" WWE WWE already has enough moving parts currently going on in their women's division, with the brand crossover of having "Raw" stars Judgment Day and IYO SKY and "SmackDown" stars Chelsea Green and Tiffany Stratton being used or mentioned on both brands because of how close WWE Crown Jewel is and Stratton holding the 2026 Women's Money In The Bank briefcase. With that in mind, they really don't need to introduce fake cash out cash in attempts from Stratton on Liv Morgan and her Women's World Championship. Morgan certainly isn't losing her Women's World Championship before Crown Jewel because of how hard they're going with the advertising for the Women's Crown Jewel Championship match between her and Green. There was no way Stratton would be successful in her cash in attempt even if the referee had gone through with it, and it wasn't needed on top of the already long enough post-match brawl that had broken out between Judgment Day and SKY, Stratton, and Green. The referee also came off looking really bad for taking so long to cash in Stratton's briefcase, and it became really clear it was just a means of giving Perez and Rodriguez more time to be able to pull Morgan out of the ring. It made the cash in even less believable than it already was, and made what should've been viewed as an "exciting moment" into nothing more than WWe trying to hammer home the "unpredictability" that anything could happen on their programming. WWE I was glad a few weeks ago when Blake Monroe and Giulia finally got to have their first match, instead of just brawling backstage and furthering their storyline in social media videos, and I really enjoyed their street fight tonight. As much as I would have liked to see Giulia get the victory to put these women at one win each, "SmackDown" hasn't been on the hottest streak for me lately, so I'll take my enjoyment where I can get it. I didn't really think the street fight stipulation was going to lend itself to setting up another match, either, so Monroe getting the win was fine. This was a fun plunder match, and the women actually got some time
