body: Drew McIntyre recalls meeting Robert Downey Jr as well as Sam Jones in two separate stories of meeting the popular actors. In recent years, McIntyre has become one of several WWE superstars to begin to find his footing in the acting world, working with names such as Russell Crowe and more. While speaking to Sidewalks Entertainment in a new interview, Drew McIntyre was asked about meeting big name actors, with McIntyre recalling meeting Robery Downey Jr and Sam Jones in two separate instances. “Yeah, I don’t really get that excited about that. I’m excited to talk and learn from a lot of people. Like, I remember one time I got an L.A. restaurant. I turned around, get in my car, and Robert Downey Jr. was there, and I was, ‘oh, hey, man, I’m a fan of your work,’ and I started turning away because I know what it’s like when people are kind of up on your business. I realized as I turned away, he wanted to keep talking, but I committed to turning, so I kept turning. I was like, ‘ah, damn it, he wanted to keep talking,’ and now I’ve turned, and we’re both awkwardly waiting for our cars. So I kind of wish I continued that conversation, because I am a fan, but I also know what it’s like when people are up on you and asking too many questions, and somebody really that was exciting to me is usually cult figures. I did a signing once in Knoxville, Tennessee, and Flash Gordon was there, the actor that played him. I can’t remember the name, Sam (Jones), off the top of my head. But I was leaving, and I was like, oh, my brother loves him, and I’m a big fan of Flash Gordon as well, my is brother obsessed. Then I heard my name getting shouty, just “DREW!” a big booming voice and I knew he was right there, and as I turned, it was like a scene from the movie Ted, I just heard the Flash Gordon theme. He was motioning me over and I went over and I did exactly say the Ted line with the teddy bear movie where he says, ‘thanks for saving every one of us,’ he was lovely, signed a picture for my brother, which my brother proudly has on his wall, but I’ve met so many Hollywood actors.” If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.

title: Conrad Thompson Shares Cryptic Update After Ric Flair’s Hospitalization
raw_title: Conrad Thompson Shares Cryptic Update After Ric Flair’s Hospitalization
summary_src: Ric Flair’s health scare has everyone waiting for answers, and now his son-in-law Conrad Thompson has shared a message that could be good news for the WWE Hall of Famer.
body: On October 24, Thompson took to social media with a simple message that appeared to suggest someone close to him had returned home. However, he didn’t specifically identify who he was talking about. The timing is interesting considering Flair was hospitalized Friday morning after falling outside a restaurant in Tampa . The 77-year-old suffered cuts to his head and eye, leaving him bleeding before emergency responders arrived and transported him to the hospital. Later that evening, Flair’s daughter Charlotte gave everyone some reassurance when she revealed that her father was going to be okay. She even shared a joke he made to his doctor about The Ultimate Warrior. “Not my dad telling the doctor he fell bc of warrior dropping him on his head…(ps: he’s going to be ok)” Thompson’s latest post could be another positive development, especially since he’s married to Flair’s daughter Megan. However, there’s one important detail that makes the message difficult to confirm as an update on Flair. Thompson also hosts the Grilling JR podcast with Jim Ross, who recently dealt with his own hospitalization. The 74-year-old WWE Hall of Famer was hospitalized earlier this month after experiencing low oxygen levels. Thompson had already confirmed on the October 22 edition of the podcast that Ross was back home and recovering. That means Thompson’s Saturday message doesn’t definitively establish that Flair has been discharged. Neither Flair nor his family has provided additional details confirming his release from the hospital. Flair’s hospitalization also came just hours after he revealed that he was dealing with a blood clot in his leg . Doctors had restricted his travel and scheduled a procedure to address the issue, although there’s no indication that the blood clot caused his fall. For now, Charlotte’s confirmation that her father is going to be okay remains the clearest update on Flair’s condition. Thompson’s message certainly sounds encouraging, but until someone confirms exactly who he was referring to, it’s too early to say the Nature Boy has officially returned home. After everything that happened Friday, that confirmation would be welcome news. H Jenkins H Jenkins has been breaking pro wrestling news on Ringside News for nearly a decade, with his reports featured by TMZ, Forbes, The Sun, and more.
summary: Thompson took to social media with a simple message that appeared to suggest someone close to him had made a comeback home. The timing is interesting considering Flair was hospitalized Friday morning after falling outside a restaurant in Tampa .

title: The Miz Feared WWE Firing After Talking Smack Clash With Daniel Bryan
raw_title: WWE's The Miz Thought He'd Be Fired After Intense Talking Smack Promo
summary_src: WWE star The Miz explained why he thought he'd be fired after his intense "Talking Smack" promo involving Daniel Bryan back in 2016.
body: WWE's "Talking Smack" ran as a weekly series on the WWE Network for just under a year, and its most famous moment came shortly after the show got underway. In August 2016, then-Intercontinental Champion The Miz went face-to-face with "Talking Smack" co-host Daniel Bryan , in a fiery segment where the then-retired Bryan told Miz he was a coward and didn't like the way he wrestled. Miz perceived it as Bryan thinking less of him for not being an independent scene darling, like Bryan, and went off. During the promo, Miz said that while Bryan called him a coward, Bryan was "the one that doesn't get in the WWE ring again." The shocking line caused Bryan to walk off the set, though Miz thought he was going to get punched, and it also led the "A-Lister" to believe he was going to be in a lot of trouble, something he explained in a video of his greatest moments posted to WWE Vault . "In my head, I'm going, 'What did I just say? What did I just say? Did I just get myself fired?'" Miz explained. "I remember getting a text from Kevin Dunn and Vince and they were like, 'We are popping off of this. This is awesome.' And I'm like, 'Wow. I did it.' The next week, I got to be the start of the show. From then on, that title was made to look like a main event title." Miz explained that he already had a bad night before the heated segment, as he had just been drafted to "WWE SmackDown." When he arrived at the show that night, he found out that he'd just be in a dark match, which he wasn't happy about.
summary: During an August 2016 episode of WWE's Talking Smack, Intercontinental Champion The Miz had an intense exchange with co-host Daniel Bryan. Bryan called Miz a coward for his in-ring style, prompting Miz to fire back that Bryan was the one unwilling to return to a WWE ring. Miz later revealed he immediately worried the heated promo had gotten him fired, though he received positive texts from Kevin Dunn and Vince McMahon.

body: News WWE AEW ROH NJPW INDIE Editorial Results Events Profiles News TNA TNA Tore Up Matt Hardy’s Running Order For Hardys’ 35th Anniversary Show TNA TNA Tore Up Matt Hardy’s Running Order For Hardys’ 35th Anniversary Show by Sap Sinha October 24, 2026 0 336 views ReddIt Facebook Twitter Email Copy URL TRENDING Breaking News – Ric Flair Rushed To The Hospital 0 Sol Ruca Shreds The Internet With These New Bikini Photos, New Boyfriend Revealed? 0 WWE, TNA, and AEW veteran Matt Hardy. (Image credit: TNA Wrestling) Matt Hardy and Jeff Hardy had real creative input on the October 15 episode of TNA iMPACT!, but not everything went the way Matt planned. During a recent edition of his “The Extreme Life of Matt Hardy” podcast, Matt said that he wanted a Tables Match as part of the Hardys’ 35th anniversary show, since the brothers are so closely linked to tables, ladders, and chairs. When he thought about who should fight, he chose two of their most hated rivals, The Righteous and The Sicks, hoping that they would destroy each other and do the Hardys a favor. Matt said that if he had set the running order himself, he would have placed that match right after the opening segment and ahead of Ryan and Nic Nemeth, because a hot match that fans care about works well after an opener. TNA instead put the Nemeth match first and saved the Tables Match for later. However, Matt is not upset about it. He believes that there may have been a production reason, since the Nemeth segment was short and the Tables Match needed more time, which a later spot could give. The Hardys clearly had a say, but TNA still made the final adjustments when putting the final card together. On a potential character change: “It’s gonna be interesting to see what my next character is, especially if Jeff takes a little time off to try and work on his neck a little bit. That may be happening, I guess we’ll see.” On Jeff’s high-risk style: “Well yeah, you know, it’s not necessarily that. Just that nagging, it’s been a year now since he had this bulging disc, which has been bugging him. He’s going to — I think he’s done everything he can do in his power, I think he’s maybe gonna take some time off to get it fixed up and correct it as much as possible.” With his real life brother Jeff, Hardy gained notoriety in WWF’s tag team division during the 2000s due to his participation in TLC matches. ... eWrestlingNews was founded in 1999 and has been covering wrestling news 24/7 ever since. title: On the Record: Indi Hartwell Weighs In On TNA Knockouts World Title Victory At Bound For Glory 2026
raw_title: Indi Hartwell Comments On TNA Knockouts World Title Victory At Bound For Glory 2026
body: Hartwell defeated Xia Brookside to win her first title in TNA Wrestling , a year after missing out on the opportunity at last year's Bound for Glory. In an emotional message following her win, the Aussie star spoke about how glad she was to have won the title after embarrassing herself last year. "First of all, it's crazy what can change in a year. Last year at Bound For Glory, I was going for the title, trying to bring it home, NXT had it. I didn't get the job done, in fact, I feel like I completely humiliated myself, embarrassed myself. My family was right there in the front row. And yeah, I didn't bring it home, but this year finally turned the toy belt into the real thing," she said. The match was refereed by TNA Hall of Famer Mickie James, whom Hartwell idolized, and said that James' presence meant a lot to her. She also spoke about the trials and tribulations she had to go through to reach her goal, making the achievement even more worthwhile. "And the crazy part is that Mickie James was special guest ref, and before the match, I was kind of just going over my own thoughts and understanding how big and how special this is," she said. "To have Mickie there, someone who I used to watch on TNA TV, I used to watch her have crazy matches, and now she's out there refing me. She was there for me to win my first title here in TNA, so, yeah, I'm so grateful. I'm grateful for all the hiccups, all the roller coasters, like all the times I failed, 'cause, I mean, it all led to this, and if I had to do it all over again, I would. I'd go through all the hard sh*t because it's always worth it in the end." Hartwell's win comes three years after her NXT Women's title win, which was cut short after she was called up to the main roster.

title: Michael Hayes Recalls Winning Over Vince McMahon
raw_title: Michael Hayes Says Vince McMahon Used To Hate Him: "I Became One Of His Right-Hand Men, That’s Quite The F*cking Accomplishment"
summary_src: Vince McMahon hated Michael Hayes at one point in time. Guest appearing on the latest episode of Stephanie McMahon's What's Your Story? podcast was WWE producer Michael Hayes.
body: He dove into how he ended up becoming a fixture at WWE despite the rocky start to his relationship with former Chairman Vince McMahon. Hayes remembers Vince saying that he would never have a job at WWE. “I figured I was pretty much done here (after my time with The Hardys) and then I think Vince (McMahon) saw me wandering around when he was doing vignettes and stuff and would start pulling me in, help him out.” Hayes was asked how he won over Vince and said, “I don’t know… This man, he hated me. He hated The Freebirds and swore on everything that was swearable that I would never have a job here. Not only did I get hired back here, I became one of his right-hand men. That’s quite the f*cking accomplishment.” He added, “I got his trust. Because I worked and I outworked everybody, and when he wanted something done, I went and got it done. He didn’t have to ask about it and I would tell him I got it done.” Hayes is 67 years old. He has been part of the company since 1995.
summary: Michael Hayes revealed that Vince McMahon initially hated him and swore he would never work for WWE. Despite the bad start, Hayes began helping with vignettes and eventually became one of McMahon's trusted right-hand men by outworking everyone and delivering without being asked. Hayes, now 67, has been with the company since 1995 after his earlier run with The Hardys.

kind.quote: I became one of his right-hand men. That’s quite the f*cking accomplishment.

title: Kevin Nash Calls Out Critics Over His Friendship With Kane Amid Political Differences
raw_title: Kevin Nash Calls Out Critics Over His Friendship With Kane Amid Political Differences
summary_src: Kevin Nash and Kane may be on completely different sides politically, but Nash isn’t letting that get in the way of their friendship.
body: Kevin Nash addressed the situation on Twitter after his recent political exchanges attracted attention. He pointed out that he and Glenn Jacobs are still friends despite having very different political views. “The amazing piece of information is that @GlennJacobsTN and myself are friends. His political views are his as mine are mine.” Their disagreement over politics apparently hasn’t changed anything between them personally. Nash instead went after the hostility he sees on social media and argued that political differences don’t need to completely divide people. “The hatred on this app is so sad. United we stand divided we fall. Everyone gets one vote. Make it count.” Nash’s comments come after he once again went after Donald Trump on Kliq This, this time while discussing claims he’d seen surrounding Trump’s cryptocurrency venture. Nash made it clear he was repeating someone else’s argument before laying out allegations about who supposedly lost and made money from the cryptocurrency. With the U.S. midterm elections approaching, Nash also encouraged people to use their own vote rather than turning political disagreements into personal hatred. Whatever he and Kane might say about each other’s politics publicly, Nash clearly doesn’t believe it has to become personal. title: Drew McIntyre Calls CM Punk A Piece Of Crap
raw_title: Drew McIntyre Talks WWE 'Beef' With CM Punk: 'He's A Genuine Piece Of Crap'
summary_src: Drew McIntyre says he's had to fake none of his animosity towards 'piece of crap' CM Punk.
body: WWE Ever since the 2024 Men's Royal Rumble when Drew McIntyre injured CM Punk, their onscreen rivalry has just become more and more personal. The hate between McIntyre and Punk led to heated exchanges in a Strap Match and a bloody Hell in a Cell match. According to McIntyre during an interview on Bradley Martin's " RAWTALK PODCAST ," the heat between them is very real. "He's a piece of crap," McIntyre stated plainly. I avoid him whenever I can avoid him." He then emphasized that Punk has had several altercations with fans over the years, using that to prove his rival genuinely isn't a good person. "He tries to play – now he's different, he's better at hiding it now than he used to be, like back in the day everybody couldn't stand him; he was so full of himself," McIntyre recalled, harkening back to Punk's WWE exit and how he believes it was a disrespectful move toward WWE after years of elevating him. Despite his feelings, McIntyre claims he doesn't allow that to get in the way of putting on a good show for fans. "I can be professional. I'm very good at my job. You put us together, you don't have to find the real in it – like, he doesn't like me, I can't stand him, you put us together, it's magic for the audience." WWE Drew McIntyre further claims he could beat CM Punk in a legitimate fight, laughing off 'The Second City Saint's' infamous attempt to establish himself as an MMA fighter post-WWE . "I will crush you! I'm giant and Scottish, do you know how many fights I've been in?" he laughingly asked. "I can't stand him. He's a genuine piece of crap, good at hiding it these days." McIntyre opined that Punk has burned bridges everywhere else and WWE is his last chance to continue wrestling, which is why he plays along with the corporate side of the promotion and is good-natured. "Behind those eyes he's crying, because he wants to be a d**k non-stop; very Charles Manson-like," McIntyre said. "Just talks to the audience, convinces them he's such a good guy, they buy into his BS." All the love Punk continues to get from the audience rubs McIntyre the wrong way, but still admitted that his rival has a legitimate love for pro wrestling unlike some of the other wrestlers who come into the industry today after first establishing prior careers or wanting to use WWE to jump into Hollywood.
summary: Drew McIntyre told Bradley Martin's RAWTALK PODCAST that his dislike for CM Punk is genuine and that he avoids the fellow WWE star whenever possible. McIntyre cited Punk's past fan altercations and what he saw as a disrespectful exit from WWE years ago after the company had elevated him, adding that Punk used to be so full of himself that everybody couldn't stand him. He noted that while the heat is real he remains professional and focuses on delivering good matches for the audience.

kind.quote: He's a piece of crap.

title: Three More Athletes Added to WWE — Report
raw_title: Three More Athletes Added to WWE — Report
body: 0 WWE has expanded its developmental talent pool with three more female athletes reportedly signing contracts and relocating to Orlando, Florida, to begin training at the Performance Center. The latest additions bring experience from different sporting backgrounds, with the company continuing to look beyond established wrestling talent for its next generation of performers. According to Bryan Alvarez of the Wrestling Observer , Gabriela Martinez Asensi, Silvia Likki, and Tayleigh Robertson have all joined WWE after participating in tryouts. Elly Finch was also among the recruits, though PWInsider had already reported on her signing earlier this week. Martinez Asensi arrives from Spain with a background in collegiate tennis, having played for the University of Missouri. She is also a fitness coach with a significant social media following and speaks Spanish, English, and German. Her athletic experience and ability to communicate across three languages give her a varied background as she begins learning professional wrestling. Likki, meanwhile, brings experience from the CrossFit world. The Italian athlete has built an Instagram audience of more than 200,000 followers, and her strength and conditioning background could provide a foundation as she develops her in-ring skills at the Performance Center. Robertson ( Instagram ) offers a different kind of wrestling experience. She has competed in amateur wrestling and bodybuilding and attended Snow College and Utah Tech before making the move into WWE’s developmental system. All three athletes completed WWE tryouts before receiving their contracts. Their backgrounds reflect the variety of sporting experience the company continues to draw upon when recruiting talent for its future roster. Finch, whose signing was previously reported, also joins the group after competing in track and field at Michigan State University. Her addition was confirmed alongside the other recruits in Alvarez’s report. There has been no announcement regarding when any of the new signings might appear on WWE television. Their immediate focus will be training at the Performance Center, where they will work to turn their athletic backgrounds into wrestling skills. For now, the three recruits have taken their first steps toward a WWE career. Their next test will be between the ropes, where athletic credentials must translate into success in the ring. title: Michael Hayes Heartbroken After Split From Hardys

body: In the year 1999, current WWE producer Michael P.S. Hayes served as the manager for The Hardys (Matt Hardy & Jeff Hardy). He cornered them as they won their first WWF Tag Team Championship. Hayes was kicked out of the group in August 1999. While speaking to Stephanie McMahon on the What’s Your Story? podcast , Hayes expressed that his heart was broken when he was split from Matt and Jeff. “Then The Hardys thing didn’t pan out,” Hayes said. “It was funny. Once they dropped the titles, I was specifically told and produced to tell them they’re going back to the starting box and going back to foundation and you’re beginning at the beginning and you would start over and earn it and be a real tyrant, and then Vince (McMahon) goes, ‘God! He can’t be like that to those kids. They should beat him up. Why is he being so mean? Nobody would listen to that. No, get him away from them,’ and then when he told me that, it broke my heart. I was invested and I did what you told me to do…” Matt and Jeff have publicly expressed their appreciation for Hayes. Matt wrote on social media that they will always be grateful to Hayes.
summary: In 1999 Michael P.S. Hayes managed The Hardys and was in their corner when they won their first WWF Tag Team Championship. He was removed from the group in August 1999 after Vince McMahon decided Hayes was too harsh on Matt and Jeff following their title loss. While speaking to Stephanie McMahon on the What’s Your Story? podcast, Hayes said the decision broke his heart because he had become invested in the role.

title: Scotty 2 Hotty Recalls Random Pairing With Brian Christopher
raw_title: Scotty 2 Hotty Details Origins Of Too Cool Tag Team In WWE
summary_src: Scott Garland (AKA Scotty 2 Hotty) recently detailed the origins of Too Cool, including how Rikishi was integrated into the group.
body: WWE Scott "Scotty 2 Hotty" Garland and Brian "Grand Master Sexay" Christopher were a popular mid-card tag team during the Attitude Era, originally debuting as heels before getting over with fans. The two had plenty of memorable moments together, most often with their dance routines alongside other talent. Looking back at his time with the team in an interview on "Insight with Chris Van Vliet," Garland recalled how their pairing came together. "Right before WrestleMania of '98 in Boston, I was sitting home," he said. "I had been home for weeks or months, and they had done nothing with me up to this point. So I'm ready to get released." The veteran was then randomly paired with Christopher to take part in the tag team battle royal that opened up WWE WrestleMania 14. "He was a heel, I was a babyface up to that point; we had wrestled each other a bunch of times, and also we were just thrown into this match as a tag team. It made no sense whatsoever!" he proclaimed. At first, the two didn't have a tag team name, nor were their gimmicks harmonized. Garland bumped into Vince McMahon in catering, and told him about their individual past gimmicks. "I said, 'I don't know if you know this or not,' and I know he didn't know it, 'But a few years ago, on the independents, I wrestled as Scott 'Too Hot' Taylor ... and Brian was 'Too Sexay' Brian Christopher.'" McMahon took the information in, and the following week on television, they became Scott "Too Hot" Taylor and "Too Sexay" Brian Christopher, with their tag team referred to as "Too Much." WWE Garland recalled that they went by "Too Much" for about a year before being rebranded as "Too Cool" by Vince Russo. The choice was made right before Christopher suffered an injury, and upon his return, WWE wanted them to do something similar to The Hardy Boyz, wearing street clothes instead of normal wrestling gear. "'We want you to dress like the kids are dressing in the malls.' That was the only direction we got," he recalled. "They got these baggy jeans in the hip-hop shops. We could wear those in the ring and get knee pads and knee braces and all those good stuff underneath and still be able to wrestle in them." While the two worked well as a tag team, the inclusion of Rikishi led to many memorable moments, such as the three men danced together in the 2000 Royal Rumble before Rikishi eliminated both men. "Rikishi Too Cool didn't start until December [1999]. That iconic moment at the Royal Rumble where the three of us dance together? That was four weeks later," he added. Rikishi's pairing with Too Cool was less than a year according to Garland, but having the legendary Samoan with them was a highlight of his career. As iconic as it would become, Garland didn't originally see the pairing working with Rikishi. "I'm like, 'This doesn't make any sense. He doesn't fit with what Brian and I are doing.' I go, 'I don't see this working,'" he recalled. "But that first night, there was just something — it's one of those thin

title: MVP Diagnosed With a Heart Condition
raw_title: MVP Diagnosed With a Heart Condition
summary_src: MVP just revealed something about his health that fans didn’t know — he has a heart condition. The AEW star opened up about being diagnosed with Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome, a condition that affects the heart’s electrical system.
body: Speaking on Marking Out with MVP and Dwayne Swayze , MVP discussed the recent death of PAC , along with The Butcher and longtime wrestling fan Sign Guy. The conversation turned to heart problems after MVP brought up losing several friends in the business over the years. That’s when he explained why he’d decided to get his own heart checked. MVP then revealed that he has Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome. He learned more about his heart health after undergoing a scan and speaking with his cardiologist, who told him that his results looked good despite the condition. “I got one, and I’m good to go. As a matter of fact, my cardiologist told me, you know, I got the Wolff-Parkinson-White thing, you know, but that’s not fatal. But he said, ‘I don’t know about the rest of you. I don’t know what else you got going on.’” The doctor even managed to get a laugh out of the situation. According to MVP, his cardiologist was confident about his heart but made it clear that anything else going wrong with his body would be somebody else’s problem. “He said, you know, ‘But as far as the heart goes, you’re good. You’re not going to die of a heart attack. You might, you know, whatever else you got going on is a different doctor you got to talk to, but my heart’s good.’” MVP wasn’t sharing his diagnosis just to talk about himself. He had a warning for wrestlers approaching middle age, especially those who spent years drinking, smoking, partying or using performance-enhancing drugs. He urged them to stop assuming they’re healthy simply because they feel fine. “So, I said all that to say this. Man, if you’re—and women pay attention too, but this is primarily for men. If you’re a man and you’re in your 40s, especially if you’ve lived a wrestler’s lifestyle, a bodybuilder’s lifestyle, eating lots of red meat, you know, if you’ve been on the gas and were eating lots of red meat, hard drinking, smoking, partying, go get a CT scan.” He also encouraged people to book an appointment rather than making excuses about the cost. “Book an appointment. It doesn’t cost a lot. It’s really inexpensive. It’s like, I think, less than 100 bucks.” MVP ended his warning by bringing up the people who could be left behind if someone ignores a serious health problem. He said having children and loved ones depending on you should be reason enough to take the issue seriously. “But do yourself a favor, man, for your loved ones, well, for yourself, for your kids, go get a CT scan. Get your heart checked. Make sure that you’re in good shape, because heart disease is a silent killer. You think you’re okay until you’re not.” For MVP, the good news is that his cardiologist has reassured him about his heart health. His newly disclosed condition doesn’t appear to be stopping him from continuing his wrestling career, but he’s not interested in seeing anyone else take unnecessary chances. After losing people he knew in the business, he wants others to get checked while they still have the opportunity. Steve

body: Sam Holloway is the latest name to part ways with WWE’s ID program. Holloway, who was recruited to WWE’s program a little under two years ago, confirmed the news via social media on Monday. Thank you for an incredible two years filled with unforgettable experiences, opportunities, and lessons that will stay with me throughout my career. I’m beyond grateful for this chapter, but even more excited for what’s ahead. Holloway is among a group of prospects who have left the WWE ID program recently. Laynie Luck and Marcus Mathers also exited the system in recent days. Holloway appeared on early episodes of EVOLVE, which relaunched as a weekly WWE series in early 2025. He ended up working 11 matches on the show in total while remaining a highly active name on the North American independent scene. WWE ID is a program which recruits independent wrestlers to the company’s feeder system. Talent signed to WWE ID typically continue to take independent bookings while training at WWE’s Performance Center and making appearances on shows like EVOLVE and NXT.

title: Michael Hayes Recalls Hiding From André The Giant
raw_title: Michael Hayes Recounts André The Giant Agenting Matches
summary_src: Michael Hayes discusses André. The latest episode of Stephanie McMahon's What's Your Story? podcast featured an extensive chat with WWE producer Michael Hayes. As they were going over Hayes' life and pro wrestling career, Hayes brought up that André the Giant agented matches.
body: As they were going over Hayes’ life and pro wrestling career, Hayes brought up that André the Giant agented matches. André held a show in Ohio that The Freebirds (Michael Hayes, Terry Gordy & Buddy Roberts) were scheduled for. Hayes forgot they were booked, so the night before, he drank and took valium. Gordy and Roberts had to carry him into the venue. “We were in Pittsburgh and there was no hotel rooms so Terry (Gordy) slept on the grass by the pool at the Howard Johnson. We got up the next morning and there was a flight to New Haven or something and there was a flight to Atlanta, and it didn’t take long and all of a sudden, we’re changing our flights and here comes André (the Giant), and we hid, all three of us are hiding behind this pillar, like, ‘I hope he don’t see us. Please don’t see us,’” Hayes said about himself, Terry Gordy, and Buddy Roberts. “‘God, I hope he don’t see us.’” Hayes was asked why they were afraid, and he said, “Well, because I’d already got in trouble for showing up when his first time he was an agent.” Hayes was then asked to clarify if he meant to say André the Giant was a match agent, and he replied, “He was an agent. He was running a show in Youngstown, Ohio, and we were staying in Columbus and I thought we were off. So I drank about, I don’t know, 10 or 12 beers, and had taken some valium.” He continued, “We pull up to the school, and I go, ‘What are we doing here?’ Terry goes, ‘We’re going to work.’ ‘Work!?’ I walked in and literally like the cartoon you see, they’re both holding me up and André’s there playing Cribbage or whatever and drinking his wine. ‘He drunk!’ They go, ‘No, he’s not,’ and they let me go. Wham! Faceplant. Really bad.” Hayes added the following about André, “He was very instrumental in talking us up. Him and I were close when he would come to Georgia. I would take him around and stuff, and I blew that.” Hayes has reached 31 consecutive years with WWE. He shared that Chief Content Officer Paul ‘Triple H’ Levesque talked to him about his future, and that can be read about here .

After Hayes partied heavily the night before and needed to be carried into the building, the group later tried to avoid André at an airport by hiding behind a pillar. Hayes explained they were afraid because he had already been in trouble for showing up unprepared the first time André served as agent.

summary_src: The main events of WWE WrestleMania 43 have recently been discussed, but one of them looks more concrete than the other.
body: According to Meltzer, the idea of having Roman Reigns defend the WWE World Heavyweight Championship against Oba Femi on night two of the event is still very much the plan, which was part of the original report from Fightful Select. However, the part that isn't the plan at the moment is to have Cody Rhodes take on CM Punk in the main event of night one, which Fightful didn't outright report as it was only mentioned that Rhodes and Punk would just have major roles to play. Meltzer noted that the bout is not the current direction, though he did say that it would make sense since the two men are the biggest stars on "WWE SmackDown" right now, and have been purposely kept apart since their initial interaction after WWE SummerSlam 2026. Meltzer rounded off by saying that since the show is still just under six months away, these plans are naturally subject to change due to various circumstances like injuries. One thing that is still subject to change is the date of the event itself as nothing has been officially announced by WWE. The weekend of April 10 and 11 has supposedly been penciled in, though WWE is keeping the date under wraps for now , not just because the logistics of the even taking place in Saudi Arabia being more difficult than if it took place in North America, but because it also prevents companies like AEW running a show directly opposite WrestleMania 43.

A Cody Rhodes versus CM Punk match is not currently the intended main event for night one, although both men are the top stars on SmackDown and have been kept apart since their post-SummerSlam 2026 meeting. title: Eric Bischoff Credits DDP's Authenticity For Getting Over In WCW
raw_title: WWE HOFer Eric Bischoff Disagrees With How Diamond Dallas Page Got Over In WCW
summary_src: According to Eric Bischoff, it was a simplification of Dallas Page's onscreen persona that won him over with fans, rather than his finishing move.
body: Iconic finishers can be an important part of what makes a pro wrestler memorable, and sometimes it's the defining element that gets the wrester over with an audience. As the man who popularized the move that would eventually be synonymous with Randy Orton as the RKO , Diamond Dallas Page's Diamond Cutter was set apart on the roster, and to many fans, a huge contributor to his popularity in WCW. However, as stated on "83 Weeks," Eric Bischoff shared his belief that it was something else. "I know, for Page, that finish, in his mind, is what made him; I disagree," Bischoff said. He went on to praise the finisher, stating that there was plenty of spectacle behind it. "It's not what got him over. What got him over was when he became Page Falkinburg; when he allowed himself to go out and be authentic." Bischoff argued that Page was at his best when he started moving away from his larger-than-life gimmick, noting that at the height of his popularity, he was simply being himself and nothing more while his prior gimmicks were not memorable. "Once he started losing all that, then he started getting over, and I think because he was getting over, the Diamond Cutter became more effective as a finish," he further explained. "So it probably feels like the Diamond Cutter was responsible; it was really Page shifting out of the 'I want to be someone else's gimmick' phase, and finally allowing himself to become authentic, because that's what the audience connected with." Before Page, John Laurinaitis used the move in his career, and Orton has stated that it was from Laurinaitis that he borrowed the move and made it his own.
summary: On his "83 Weeks" podcast, WWE Hall of Famer Eric Bischoff disagreed with Diamond Dallas Page's belief that the Diamond Cutter finisher is what made him popular in WCW. Bischoff praised the move but said Page truly connected with fans when he dropped the larger-than-life character and became authentic as Page Falkinburg. Bischoff noted that Page's earlier gimmicks were forgettable and that being himself propelled him to the height of his popularity.

kind.quote: It's not what got him over. What got him over was when he became Page Falkinburg; when he allowed himself to go out and be authentic.

title: On the Record: Conrad Thompson Responds To Roman Reigns Controversy, 'I Just Shared My Personal Wrestling Opinion'
raw_title: Conrad Thompson Responds To Roman Reigns Controversy, 'I Just Shared My Personal Wrestling Opinion'
summary_src: Conrad Thompson just has an opinion. In recent weeks, Thompson has remained in the headlines, with many criticizing him for his opinions about Roman Reigns and his workload. Speaking with Fightful's Sean Ross Sapp for a new interview, Conrad explained himself.
body: In recent weeks, Thompson has remained in the headlines, with many criticizing him for his opinions about Roman Reigns and his workload. Speaking with Fightful’s Sean Ross Sapp for a new interview, Conrad explained himself. Then, he responded to the claim that he talks about Reigns for clicks. “Listen, I slipped it in, my casual opinion—which I’ll admit I do very rarely. I’m normally trying to put myself in the John Stockton position and trying to get the ball to the Karl Malone’s of the world, which would be the Jeff Jarrett’s or the Eric Bischoff’s or whomever. So people listen for their opinions, but Eric and I happened to be doing a SummerSlam review and I said that Seth and Roman had the match of the night, the match of the weekend, but I was ready for something new, and I shared my opinion about Roman that I was ready for something new. Then everyone else started talking about it. That’s what I found so silly is that my opinion is so ridiculous and I’m so irrelevant. Then why the hell is everybody still talking about it? Like even today, my phone was blowing up. People were talking about it on WWE radio. It’s like, that was forever ago. Then when Roman is saying that, he’s doing it for clicks — on Ariel Helwani’s show? On Busted Open? My point was all of my podcasts for the last two months would have had Roman in the thumbnails and we would have been talking about that, but that wasn’t my intent.” Continuing on, Thompson admits that he finds the entire situation amusing. “I never want my opinion to be what everyone’s talking about, but in this particular case, it was my opinion. So when people are telling me I’m wrong, I’m like, ‘I don’t think you can be wrong in your opinion.’ You like some things more than you like other things. That’s where I was with it. But yeah, the bias thing I thought was weird. Like, yes, I’m friendly with Cody, but I’m friendly with a lot of people in the locker room, including my sister-in-law who works there; one of my best friends, who helps run creative. It’s like Eric Bischoff gets talent from TKO every single weekend for Real American Freestyle. I’m Switzerland. I just shared my personal wrestling opinion and people got bent out of shape about it. I found it amusing.” Elsewhere in the interview, Conrad Thompson said that he wants to do podcasts with Paul Heyman and Michael Hayes. Check out his full comments by clicking here .

body: NJPW Super Junior Tag League 2026 kicked off on Saturday with a show in Saitama, Japan. United Empire’s Francesco Akira and Jakob Austin Young defeated House of Torture’s Dick Togo and SHO in the opening tournament match, but there could be some dissension brewing between Akira and Young. Akira appeared to have the match won for his team, but Young made a blind tag, then ran in and covered Togo after Akira had hit him with his Fireball knee strike. HOT’s DOUKI and Yoshinobu Kanemaru defeated the Time Splitters 2.0 team of KUSHIDA and Nick Wayne in the second tournament match. The finish saw Kanemaru use his whisky spray on Wayne before DOUKI rolled KUSHIDA up for the three count while holding the rope. Ichiban Sweet Boys (Kosei Fujita & Robbie Eagles) defeated Unbound Co. (Daiki Nagai & Titan) in the third tournament match on the show after Eagles pinned Nagai after hitting him with Hyperion. Unbound Co.’s Taiji Ishimori and Robbie X defeated Ryusuke Taguchi and Kazuma Sumi in the next match. Robbie X hit X Xpress on Sumi to pick up the win The Swirl (Blake Christian & Lee Johnson) defeated YOH and Hyo in the fifth tournament match. Christian pinned Hyo after Christian and Johnson hit him with Brainrot. Master Wato and KUUKAI defeated Mistico and Masatora Yasuda in the main event. Yasuda is replacing the injured El Desperado in the tournament. Wato pinned Yasuda following an assisted Tsutenkaku German suplex. After the main event, Mistico raised the arm of his partner Yasuda, who had to be helped to the back. After the main event, Wato thanked Mistico for the match and then both him and KUUKAI held the ropes open for him to leave the ring. title: The Rise of Independent Wrestling Promotions in Modern Sports Entertainment

body: DMFirst Veer Game odds uden om ROFUS Jalwa Game Goa Game Raja Game MaanWin The Rise of Independent Wrestling Promotions in Modern Sports Entertainment By Kendall Jenkins on 2026-10-24 08:43:00 Professional wrestling has undergone significant changes as independent promotions attract growing attention from fans, performers, and industry professionals. While major organizations continue to dominate mainstream wrestling, smaller companies are creating opportunities for alternative storytelling, distinctive wrestling styles, and closer connections between performers and audiences. Independent wrestling has existed for decades, but digital platforms and changing viewing habits have made it easier for regional promotions to reach supporters beyond their local communities. Fans can now discover emerging talent, follow independent events, and purchase merchandise directly from organizations that previously depended almost entirely on live attendance. This development has created an increasingly diverse wrestling environment where creativity and entrepreneurial thinking are essential. Running a successful independent promotion requires more than organizing entertaining matches. Financial management, venue coordination, marketing, and audience engagement all contribute to building a sustainable business. Understanding these responsibilities reveals why independent wrestling has become an important part of modern sports entertainment. Behind the excitement of live wrestling is a demanding business operation. Independent promoters must coordinate venues, negotiate performer agreements, arrange insurance, manage ticket sales, and organize promotional campaigns. Unlike major wrestling companies with extensive administrative departments, smaller promotions often rely on limited teams handling several responsibilities simultaneously. Managing equipment and office resources is another part of operating efficiently. Promotions regularly produce contracts, event schedules, merchandise labels, promotional materials, and documentation for performers and venues. As organizations expand or replace their office equipment, they may accumulate unused supplies that still have commercial value. A promotion retiring an older office printer, for example, could recover money from unopened replacement cartridges through www.selltoner.com . Redirecting funds from surplus office inventory toward event production is one practical example of how smaller entertainment businesses can make better use of their existing resources. These operational decisions rarely attract attention from wrestling audiences, but they contribute to financial stability. Promotions that manage their expenses carefully have greater flexibility to invest in production quality, talent development, and memorable live experiences. title: Drew McIntyre Compares WWE Leadership Styles

summary_src: Drew McIntyre believes Triple H has a more realistic take on WWE's creative direction compared to Vince McMahon.
body: Drew McIntyre was one of the first modern examples of a wrestler reinventing themselves after coming up short in WWE. Following his release in 2014, McIntyre returned to the independent scene before making his way back to WWE three years later, where he'd go on to have a dominant run on "NXT" before reaching the top of the main roster. This journey allowed McIntyre to work under both Vince McMahon and Triple H. "[McMahon] saw things a little different, very much the kind of black and white [mentality] — good guy, bad guy, keep things a little simpler," he recalled during an interview on Bradley Martin's "Raw Talk." "You know, [Triple H] is bit more, kind of [seeing] in shades of gray — which, that's the real world." McIntyre then recalled seeing The Bloodline story play out, expressing that it made him excited to tell stories in a similar vein. "In 2022, we really started going from Drew the Big Hero of Covid, the Scottish Warrior, to going down the path of becoming a bad guy," he said. McIntyre then clarified that his character was not a heel in a black-or-white sense, as there's an aspect of his character that's just reacting to fans' opinions of him. "It's been this very fun character arc we've been on for the past four years, because Triple H is very open to making it like real life, and just living in shades of gray," McIntyre explained. He then circled back to McMahon again, explaining what the former WWE Chairman emphasized. "He had a very specific way of how he saw things. Like, keep it like — 'Don't talk about things that happened a month ago, two months ago, certainly not years ago; let's live in the now!'"
summary: Drew McIntyre discussed working under both Vince McMahon and Triple H in WWE. He described McMahon as viewing things in black and white with simpler good guy versus bad guy dynamics while seeing Triple H as operating in shades of gray more reflective of the real world. McIntyre cited the Bloodline storyline as inspiration for his own character shift in 2022 from heroic Scottish Warrior to a more nuanced antagonist.

summary_src: When one pay per view ends, the build for the next begins. body: When one pay per view ends, the build for the next begins. And so, with the dust still settling after Clockwork Carnage and WrestleDream, the focus in AEW now turns to Full Gear next month. Here’s a look at what the card for Full Gear might look like, starting with what we already know, moving on to what sure seems likely, and finishing with some speculation about what the rest of the show might look like. It was announced on Dynamite that both of AEW’s tag team championships would be on the line at Full Gear. Davis & Doyle earned their shot by defeating the champions in dominant fashion in an eliminator match on Dynamite. The team known as Wrathlander got here by defeating the Sisters of Sin and Divine Dominion in a three-way for a title shot at Grand Slam France: Collision. Fletcher pinned Copeland to win a tag team match on Dynamite, then laid out Ospreay with the AEW World Championship belt after the match. Challengers earning title shots by pinning the champion’s partner has become something of a trope in AEW lately, and this seems like another example. In that same segment, Okada distracted Copeland and interfered in the match, leading to Copeland’s defeat at Fletcher’s hands. He also wiped Copeland out after the match. Okada also pinned Copeland during the Clockwork Carnage match at WrestleDream, and Copeland never got his win back—just when he had Okada beat at the end, he was attacked from behind and pinned by Ospreay instead. The Mone-Shafir matchup is easy to explain: Mone was celebrating her win over Thekla on Dynamite and asked who was next, and Shafir came out to confront her. So there you go. Aminata defeated Maya World on Dynamite to win a TBS title shot. The only question is when that match will take place. To be honest, it will probably happen before Full Gear—AEW has a lot of TV time to fill between now and then—but with no other obvious challenger on the horizon, we’ll list this match here for now. As for the trios titles, Strickland challenged Page to a rematch on Dynamite, and Page accepted, but then balked at the idea of a Texas Death match. The stip is the only reason the match has not been rubber stamped yet, and that figures to be sorted out sooner or later. AEW Continental Champion Jon Moxley: With the Bang Bang Gang turning heel on Dynamite and joining the Dogs in a brawl with the Death Riders and Conglomeration, Jay White makes an obvious choice to be Moxley’s next challenger. (Well, his next challenger on PPV—Moxley is sure to defend his title several times on TV between now and then.) AEW National Champion Andrade El Ídolo: Andrade was not on Dynamite, so nothing was done to set up a new challenger. One quick option: Kevin Knight, who suddenly finds himself without a tag team partner, assuming Fletcher does go on to challenge Ospreay. TNT Champion Darby Allin: Allin was on Dynamite, but to promote Blood & Guts, not Full Gear. But in Blood & Guts, one of his opponents will be Wardlow, a three-time former TNT Champion
summary: And so, with the dust still settling after Clockwork Carnage and WrestleDream, the focus in AEW now turns to Full Gear next month. Here’s a look at what the card for Full Gear might look like, starting with what we already know.

summary_src: WWE’s Crown Jewel situation in Saudi Arabia just got another serious development. U.S.
body: According to CBS News , Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton issued the warning in an October 23 memo sent to Secretary of State Marco Rubio. The document, first reported by Axios, warned that Iran has increased its efforts to target American personnel in the Middle East and other countries. Clayton didn’t hold back when describing what U.S. intelligence officials have uncovered. “The lethal plotting efforts by the Iranians against U.S. citizens have reached advanced stages in both the Middle East and certain other countries.” That’s a serious warning with Crown Jewel now just two weeks away. The memo doesn’t identify specific targets, reveal which countries are involved beyond the Middle East, or say whether an attack is imminent. There’s also no indication that WWE, its wrestlers or Crown Jewel are being specifically targeted. Still, the warning comes as the U.S. government is already taking precautions across the region. The State Department ordered non-essential embassy personnel and their families to leave Saudi Arabia earlier this week, while several other diplomatic facilities have reduced staffing. U.S. military officials have also been quietly scaling back their presence at certain locations because of ongoing threats. A U.S. official explained to CBS News that the threats from Iran and the Iranian-backed Houthi movement in Yemen are directly influencing those decisions. “The threat of Houthi attacks and of Iranian terror plots targeting U.S. officials are informing our decisions on staffing adjustments for embassies on RO [Restricted Operations] Status in the region.” That puts another layer of concern on WWE’s upcoming trip. As Ringside News previously covered , the U.S. government had already ordered diplomatic personnel out of Saudi Arabia ahead of Crown Jewel. The situation in Riyadh has also been getting worse. Saudi air defenses intercepted a ballistic missile targeting the capital early Friday morning, while additional missiles and drones were intercepted elsewhere in the country. The U.S. Embassy also warned Americans to use extreme caution at Saudi airports , with operations at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh suspended following attacks on airport infrastructure. WWE isn’t the only organization facing questions about holding a major event in Riyadh. Saudi Arabia has already postponed two international gatherings until 2027, including the United Nations World Data Forum, which had been scheduled for November 9 through November 12. title: Charlotte Flair Gives Positive Update on Ric Flair
raw_title: Charlotte says Ric Flair “is going to be OK” after hospitalization, Conrad Thompson posts “He’s home”
summary_src: Charlotte Flair has provided a positive update on her father after Ric Flair was taken to hospital following a fall in Tampa, Florida.
body: Charlotte Flair has provided a positive update on her father after Ric Flair was taken to hospital following a fall in Tampa, Florida. On Friday night, Charlotte posted on X that the 77-year-old was expected to be OK, while also sharing a joke her father apparently made to his doctor. Not my dad telling the doctor he fell bc of warrior dropping him on his head… The comment referred to The Ultimate Warrior, whom Flair wrestled during the early 1990s. A further potentially positive update came on Saturday from Conrad Thompson. Thompson did not identify the person he was referring to, although the timing of the post points to Flair. He is Ric Flair’s son-in-law, having married Flair’s daughter Megan Fliehr in 2018. TMZ reported on Friday that Flair fell after leaving a Wagamama restaurant in Tampa and suffered cuts to his head and eye. He was attended to by medical personnel before being transported to hospital by ambulance. Earlier that day, Flair had announced that he was dealing with a blood clot in his leg and would be unable to attend the Washington State Horror Con in Seattle. He said doctors had restricted his travel and that he was scheduled to undergo a procedure on the affected vein.
summary: Charlotte Flair shared on social media that her father Ric Flair is expected to be OK after he was hospitalized in Tampa, Florida following a fall that caused cuts to his head and eye. She recounted a joke he made to his doctor referencing a match against The Ultimate Warrior. Conrad Thompson, Flair's son-in-law, later posted that the person in question is home.

title: Injury Update: Ric Flair Shows Off Injured Eye After Hospitalization and Calls Out Reckless Facebook Posts
raw_title: Ric Flair Shows Off Injured Eye After Hospitalization and Calls Out Reckless Facebook Posts
summary_src: Ric Flair is battered, bruised and apparently dealing with some Facebook drama on top of everything else. The WWE Hall of Famer finally broke his silence after a nasty fall sent him to a Florida hospital, sharing a photo of his injured face and promising he’ll be okay. But he also had a bone to ...
body: Flair was rushed to the hospital on October 23 after taking a nasty spill outside a restaurant in Tampa. The 77-year-old suffered cuts around his head and eye, leaving him bleeding before paramedics arrived. Now, a day later, the Nature Boy is letting everyone see the damage for themselves. On October 24, Flair posted an update on Twitter alongside a photo showing him smiling with a bandage covering his right eye. He thanked the doctors at Tampa General Hospital for taking care of him until 4:30 in the morning and made it clear that he’s focused on recovering. “Thank You All For The Messages And Prayers! I Will Get Back To You Each Individually As I Get Stronger. Thank You To All The Tampa General Hospital Staff And Doctors That Put Up With Me Until 4:30am. I Appreciate You All And Thank You For Everything You Did For Me! I Am Focused On My Healing And Recovery Right Now. I Will Be Okay!” That’s the good news. The strange part came immediately afterward, when Flair suddenly turned his attention to his Facebook account. Apparently, some things were posted while he was in the hospital, and Flair wants absolutely nothing to do with them. He revealed that he doesn’t even own his Facebook page anymore and apologized for what he called reckless posting behavior. “And Just So You Know For Those Who Were Asking And Wondering, I Don’t Own My Own Facebook Page Anymore. I Apologize For The Reckless Posting Behavior On My Facebook When I Was In The Hospital. It Was Completely Inappropriate!” Flair didn’t explain what was posted, who controls the page or why the content upset him. But he clearly wasn’t happy about it, especially considering he was dealing with a medical emergency at the time. The whole situation comes at a rough time for Flair. Hours before his fall, he revealed that he had a blood clot in his leg and needed a medical procedure. Doctors had already restricted his travel, forcing him to cancel an upcoming appearance in Seattle. His daughter Charlotte Flair offered some reassurance Friday night, telling everyone her father was going to be okay. She also revealed that he was already joking with his doctor about The Ultimate Warrior dropping him on his head. “Not my dad telling the doctor he fell bc of warrior dropping him on his head…(ps: he’s going to be ok)” Now Flair is speaking for himself, and despite the nasty-looking injury, he seems determined to put the whole ordeal behind him. He’s not giving a timeline for when he’ll be fully recovered, but he’s made two things very clear: he’s going to be okay, and whatever happened on his Facebook page while he was hospitalized didn’t sit well with him. Steve Carrier Steve Carrier is the founder of Ringside News and has been reporting on pro wrestling since 1997. His stories have been featured on TMZ, Forbes, Bleacher Report, and more.
summary: Flair was rushed to the hospital on October 23 after taking a nasty spill outside a restaurant in Tampa. The 77-year-old suffered cuts around his head and eye, leaving him bleeding before paramedics arrived.

title: Master Wato and KUUKAI win NJPW Super Junior Tag League opener
raw_title: Master Wato & KUUKAI win main event as NJPW Super Junior Tag League opens
summary_src: Master Wato & KUUKAI topped the opening night of NJPW’s Super Junior Tag League with a victory over Místico & Masatora Yasuda.
body: Master Wato & KUUKAI topped the opening night of NJPW’s Super Junior Tag League with a victory over Místico & Masatora Yasuda. The 2026 tournament began Saturday at Kumagaya Civic Gymnasium in Saitama, drawing an announced crowd of 1,112. All 12 teams were in action across the two blocks. Yasuda was a late addition to the field after El Desperado withdrew from the tournament because of spinal canal stenosis and a lumbar disc herniation. Desperado personally recommended the Young Lion as his replacement alongside Místico. Yasuda received a main-event opportunity immediately and came close to an upset with a Boston Crab on Wato. However, KUUKAI assisted his partner in setting up a super Tsutenkaku German suplex, with Wato pinning Yasuda after 13:32. AEW’s Blake Christian & Lee Johnson also made a winning start. Competing as The Swirl, they defeated IWGP Junior Heavyweight Champion YOH & Dragongate’s Hyo when Christian pinned Hyo following Brainrot. Nick Wayne had less success in his tournament debut alongside KUSHIDA. House of Torture’s Yoshinobu Kanemaru sprayed Wayne with whisky as KUSHIDA was preparing to attack DOUKI, allowing DOUKI to catch KUSHIDA with a victory roll for the three-count. United Empire’s Francesco Akira & Jakob Austin Young defeated SHO & Dick Togo, although the finish created tension between the partners. Young made a blind tag before covering Togo immediately after Akira had hit the Fireball, with NJPW noting that Akira was unhappy with his partner afterward. Robbie Eagles & Kosei Fujita, Taiji Ishimori & Robbie X and DOUKI & Kanemaru were the other tournament winners, leaving three teams in each block tied on two points. The tournament, whose 12 original teams were announced earlier this month, continues on Sunday at Korakuen Hall. The second night is headlined by the two B Block winners Robbie Eagles & Kosei Fujita and The Swirl. KUSHIDA & Wayne will attempt to get their first points against Místico & Yasuda, while Ishimori & Robbie X meet DOUKI & Kanemaru in another match between opening-night winners. The block winners will advance to the tournament final at Power Struggle in Hiroshima on November 3.
summary: Master Wato and KUUKAI defeated Místico and Masatora Yasuda in the main event to kick off the 2026 NJPW Super Junior Tag League at Kumagaya Civic Gymnasium in Saitama in front of 1,112 fans. title: Kevin Nash Recalls Shawn Michaels Hospital Angle
raw_title: Kevin Nash Remembers WWE's Shawn Michaels Checking Into Hospital To Sell A Storyline
summary_src: Hall of Famer Kevin Nash recalls how well Shawn Michaels did on selling a hospital visit for a WWE storyline.
body: WWE In his prime, Shawn Michaels was never short of being a "Showstopper." Wrestling during some of the most highly watched eras in WWE history, his believability captured fans. WWE Hall of Famer and good friend to Michaels in real life, Kevin Nash, recalls one scenario in which fans actually believed Michaels was hospitalized after his match. Frantic by what they saw, it appears many within the WWE Universe called the hospital where Michaels was staying (storyline wise), seeking information on HBK. "I remember when we did the Shawn Michaels thing, when he took the blow and he went down, and I remember when I pitched it, I said, 'We can't have the commentators talk...We have to have the locker rooms come out, heels and babyfaces, kind of standing to make sure that he's f***ed, and then take him out...' I'm pretty sure we checked him into a Springfield hospital. So, people called. Shawn was in the hospital. So...you can make s*** real. But you can't make s*** half real," Nash said on his "Kliq This" podcast. The quote above comes from a conversation Nash and his co-host Sean Oliver had over the debate of believability in today's wrestling, and how everyone plays a role on how it sells, from the in-ring stars down to the commentators at ringside.
summary: Kevin Nash pitched a detailed angle where Shawn Michaels sold a serious injury after taking a blow in a match. The plan involved both heels and babyfaces coming from the locker room to stand around Michaels before he was taken out on a stretcher. Nash said they checked Michaels into a Springfield hospital as part of the storyline, leading fans to call the facility seeking updates on his condition.

title: Hulk Hogan’s Beachfront Mansion Sells for Nearly $5 Million Below Asking Price
raw_title: Hulk Hogan’s Beachfront Mansion Sells for Nearly $5 Million Below Asking Price
summary_src: Hulk Hogan’s beachfront Florida mansion has officially been sold more than a year after his death. The late WWE legend’s Clearwater property went for $5.9 million, a massive drop from the nearly $11 million asking price it hit the market with earlier this year.
body: According to TMZ , Hogan’s estate has now offloaded the 5,400-square-foot mansion. The property was originally listed for $10.989 million in January, meaning the final sale came in roughly $5 million below that initial asking price. The mansion was more than just another piece of Hogan’s real estate portfolio. He bought the Clearwater Beach property for $3.3 million back in 2012 and spent his final years there before his death on July 24, 2025. The beachfront home features five bedrooms and five-and-a-half bathrooms, along with a massive 1,000-square-foot primary suite. That suite includes a sitting area, Gulf-facing terrace, morning bar, spa-style bathroom and huge walk-in closet. Hogan’s estate also managed to sell another property right next door. His 2,062-square-foot guest cottage, which has three bedrooms and two-and-a-half bathrooms, reportedly went for another $2.8 million. It’s unclear whether the same buyer picked up both properties. If they did, the combined purchases would come to $8.7 million for Hogan’s mansion and neighboring cottage. The mansion first went on the market about six months after Hogan’s death with an asking price just shy of $11 million . His longtime friend Martha Thorn of the Thorn Collection and Coldwell Banker Realty handled the listing. The sale also comes while Hogan’s estate has been dealing with other matters following his death. Celebrity branding firm Carma HoldCo Inc. filed a lawsuit seeking at least $10 million in damages over allegations involving Hogan’s Real American Beer venture, claims that Hogan’s side has disputed. Whatever happens with those separate legal issues, one major piece of Hogan’s estate has now changed hands. The Clearwater mansion where the wrestling icon spent his final years is officially under new ownership, along with his neighboring guest cottage. Felix Upton Felix Upton has over 15 years of experience in media and wrestling journalism. His work at Ringside News blends speed, accuracy, and industry insight.
summary: The property was originally listed for $10.989 million in January, meaning the final sale came in roughly $5 million below that initial asking price. The mansion first went on the market about six months after Hogan’s death with an asking price just shy of $11 million .

title: Match Made: Undertaker vs Kane – WWE Bragging Rights 2010
raw_title: Undertaker vs Kane – WWE Bragging Rights 2010 | WON Flashback
summary_src: October 24 2010 was the date of WWE Bragging Rights that year, and probably the worst match on that card was The Undertaker vs Kane in a Buried Alive match. The match got a 1* in that week’s Wrestling Observer Newsletter, and our own Dave Meltzer was certainly not a fan of the Nexus run […]
body: “Kane beat Undertaker in 16:53 in the Buried Alive match to keep the World title. The match opened with a “We Want Blood” chant which must have thrilled the company on a live show. Fortunately that ended quickly. Mostly brawling in the stands. Crowd was dead in this match as well. Undertaker started throwing chairs in the ring and also threw in the top of the announcers table, which accidentally hit Kane. When Undertaker got in the ring, Kane grabbed a chair and nailed Undertaker in the gut and hit Undertaker with three chair shots to the back. “The one thing I’ve noticed about chair shots to the back is because wrestling has had so many years of chairs to the head, people don’t react to chairs to the back because they expect them to the head. I’m wondering if you just need to put a moratorium on chairs for a little while, so people will react just seeing the chair used as opposed to now where they expect a hard shot to the head and don’t react unless they get it. “More chair shots by Kane and two choke slams. Since there were no pins, Kane had to carry Undertaker to near the entrance area where they had a tombstone and an open grave for someone to be put in. Kane tried to put him in the grave, but Undertaker caught Kane in the gogoplata. Kane started tapping, but no submissions here. Kane then passed out. Undertaker threw him in the grave. He was about to start burying him, but he spotted Paul Bearer. He threw Bearer’s face in the dirt. He was about to choke slam Bearer into the grave when Nexus all attacked him. They all first bumped for Undertaker, until the numbers game became too much. They were beating him down, and Kane emerged from the grave. As they held Undertaker, Kane nailed him with the urn. The Nexus guys started shoveling dirt on him when Kane told them to leave. Kane then did his magic stuff which caused a tractor positioned near the site to drop tons of dirt on Undertaker, and leave him buried alive once again. *’” Jake Jeremy Jake Jeremy is the Head of Audience Development at F4WOnline, having previously worked as a Combat Sports, Gaming and Pro Wrestling writer, successful Editor in Chief and Sports Coordinator. He has more than ten years of experience covering mixed martial arts, pro wrestling, football and gaming across a number of publications, starting at SEScoops in 2012. He previously also worked for PROGRESS Wrestling as Head of Media as well as working on the social channels of the company.
summary: Kane got past Undertaker in 16:53 in the Buried Alive match to keep the World title. Undertaker kicked off throwing chairs in the ring and additionally threw in the top of the announcers table, which accidentally hit Kane.

title: Backstage Buzz: Sheamus's AEW Future Still Unclear Despite Backstage Advocates
raw_title: Sheamus's AEW Future Still Unclear Despite Backstage Advocates
body: By Josh Coulson Published Oct 24, 2026, 1:04 PM EDT Josh studied Journalism and Media and Cultural Studies at the University of the West of England, graduating in the summer of 2014.. Josh is a writer at TheSportster and a lifelong wrestling fan who has been doing news coverage of WWE and AEW for many years. Pro wrestling got its hooks in him at the age of ten and he's been watching ever since. His favorite wrestlers are The Rock and CM Punk, despite the latter doing his level best to make us all dislike him. Sign in to your TheSportster account Sheamus left WWE earlier this year after almost 20 years with the company. The Celtic Warrior is now a free agent, and as is often the case when big stars leave WWE, the wrestling world is expecting him to show up in AEW any day now. The thing is, despite Sheamus's star power, that still seems unlikely to happen. Fightful shared an update on Sheamus's post-WWE status during a Q&A. Apparently, unlike some other departing WWE talent, there is no urgency from AEW to bring the Irishman in. In fact, Sheamus is believed to have had talks with other promotions regarding where he might wrestle next, but it's unclear if one of those promotions is AEW. That doesn't mean Sheamus doesn't have people advocating for him in AEW. The same report notes that Adam Copeland (Edge) and Claudio Castagnoli (Cesaro) have both been lobbying to make Sheamus All Elite. That's to be expected, though, since Castagnoli worked extensively with Sheamus in WWE as The Bar, and Copeland is good friends with Sheamus outside of wrestling. A lack of urgency to make Sheamus a part of the AEW roster now that he's a free agent continues the narrative that there are some in the company who have suggested signing him might not be a good idea . It doesn't sound like anyone has a problem with Sheamus specifically, but some are concerned that the trend of picking up anyone WWE lets go has led to the AEW roster becoming too bloated. There are already a lot of wrestlers in AEW. So many that, despite two shows a week and more PPVs than ever before, there are still a lot of talented competitors who are struggling to get screen time. If Sheamus were to become All Elite, his notoriety would mean he immediately debuts on a big show, gets a spot high on the card, and competes against top wrestlers who can match the star power he brings. That all makes sense. However, it's not like AEW has held off from signing other former WWE Superstars lately. Kofi and Austin Creed were brought in almost as soon as their non-compete clauses expired. Even more recently, Ilja Dragunov made his AEW debut. A combination of AEW's growing roster and Sheamus's age might be what prevents AEW from bringing him in, but even then he's 48, that's only three years older than the recently signed Kofi.
summary: Josh is a writer at TheSportster and a lifelong wrestling fan who has been doing news coverage of WWE and AEW for many years. The thing is, despite Sheamus's star power, that still seems unlikely to happen.

In his tweet, Flair apologized for the fact that his Facebook account continued to post as normal during his hospitalization. Flair does not currently have access to that account amid a legal dispute with a digital talent agency that he says has fraudulently taken control of it. Flair was “bleeding extensively” from his eye after the fall and was taken to the hospital by ambulance. title: Comeback Watch: Drew McIntyre’s WWE Return Status Takes New Turn After Latest Announcement
raw_title: Drew McIntyre’s WWE Return Status Takes New Turn After Latest Announcement
summary_src: Drew McIntyre’s WWE comeback might have to wait a little longer. The Scottish Warrior has been missing from WWE television for six months, and November 7 was looking like a possible date for his return.
body: On October 24, WWE’s official UK account confirmed that McIntyre will appear at Zuffa Boxing 12 on November 7 at the Copper Box Arena in London. He’ll be joined by fellow WWE Superstar Bayley, with VIP meet-and-greet tickets now available for the event. The announcement puts a serious dent in speculation that McIntyre could make his return at Crown Jewel, which is scheduled for the same date at Riyadh Season Stadium. While WWE hasn’t officially ruled him out of the Premium Live Event, having him advertised for an appearance in another country makes a surprise return considerably less likely. McIntyre hasn’t appeared on WWE programming since WrestleMania 42 Night One, where he lost to Jacob Fatu in an Unsanctioned Match. Since then, he’s been busy working on Hollywood projects, including Highlander and The Last Druid . With those filming commitments now wrapped up, questions about his WWE return have only grown. McIntyre also added to the speculation by sharing footage of himself training inside a wrestling ring , but he never provided an official comeback date. McIntyre recently addressed the subject while speaking to Collider about Agent of Shadows . When the conversation turned toward potentially bringing Chase DeMoor into WWE, McIntyre made it clear that he wasn’t ready to discuss his own return. “The wheels are turning. The wheels are turning. Like leave that with me. I mean right now we’re talking today about Hollywood Drew. We’re not worrying about my comeback right now, but the wheels are turning.” Now WWE’s latest announcement gives a better idea of where McIntyre will be on November 7, and it apparently won’t be inside a wrestling ring in Saudi Arabia. Instead, he’ll be meeting fans alongside Bayley at a boxing event in London. Of course, WWE could always change its plans, but McIntyre’s advertised appearance makes Crown Jewel an unlikely destination for his comeback. After six months away, fans are still waiting to see when the Scottish Warrior will finally return to television. At least one thing is clear — WWE has plans for him on November 7, even if those plans don’t involve wrestling. body: In September 2026, Fightful Select reported that the general feeling from those connected to AEW is that the 2027 installment of All In will take place in North America in some form. All Elite Wrestling referee Bryce Remsburg guest appeared on The Certified Mark Show and was asked about the chances of AEW running a show at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. He stated that if AEW were looking for a domestic venue to host All In, Lincoln Financial would be in the conversation. He doesn’t think it’ll happen in 2027, but does believe it’s a possibility in the future. “I will say, the fact they’ve hosted wrestling before, which is WrestleMania, is a positive. I don’t think it’s gonna happen next year… I’m not sure we have demand for a Linc show… But never, ever, ever say never. I’ll say that.” He continued, “There’s no way I could say, ‘No way it’s never happening. Definitely not…’ I’m saying this with actual insider knowledge. It is possible. It’s definitely possible.” The 2026 All In event took place at Wembley Stadium in London, England. The show was headlined by Will Ospreay defeating Kenny Omega to become AEW World Champion.
