title: WWE HOFer JBL Dismisses Long-Standing Rumor Of HBK/Vader Beef
raw_title: WWE HOFer JBL Dismisses Long-Standing Rumor Of HBK/Vader Beef
summary_src: JBL says stories about Shawn Michaels and Vader's bad blood in WWE are overblown.
body: WWE At SummerSlam 1996, Shawn Michaels defended the WWE Championship against Vader, in the main event. The match is often recalled for Michaels breaking character mid-match after Vader wasn't positioned correctly for a spot , and claims that the 'Heartbreak Kid' further complained about Vader backstage to the point where the returning veteran was taken off screen. Despite the online consensus, John 'Bradshaw' Layfield claims that the accusations levied against Michaels for all these years have largely been incorrect. "The part about Shawn not liking to work with Vader because he was stiff? That's a hundred percent not true," he claimed during an episode of " Something To Wrestle ." JBL admitted that Michaels was a bit of a perfectionist about in-ring work at this time, but asserts that HBK actually didn't care about how Vader worked, because he was a tough guy. "Shawn didn't mind contact, so that wasn't an issue," he said. What JBL does think affected Vader's run in WWE was the timing of him coming into the promotion, because by 1996, Vader's body had largely begun to fail him and he had begun to lose confidence in his own ability . "[Vader] gets down there [WWE], and has to be off the gas [steroids], and when that comes, you know he's not as big, he's not as strong, he's not the physically imposing guy, and physically he can't quite do what he did." The veteran further emphasized that the Vader fans saw in WWE wasn't the one fans got used to who competed in Japan or WCW, and Michaels was actually upset because he expected that Vader. "Shawn had all the pressure in the world," JBL added, pointing out that the New Generation Era brought added pressure to big stars. "There was so much pressure on him, on Bret [Hart], and the champions of those days."
summary: The match is often recalled for Michaels breaking character mid-match after Vader wasn't positioned correctly for a spot . That's a hundred percent not true, he claimed during an episode of  Something To Wrestle . JBL admitted that Michaels was a bit of a perfectionist about in-ring work for now.

title: Bryce Remsburg On Lincoln Financial Field Possibly Hosting AEW
raw_title: Bryce Remsburg On Lincoln Financial Field Possibly Hosting AEW
body: In September 2026, Fightful Select reported that the general feeling from those connected to AEW is that the 2027 installment of All In will take place in North America in some form. All Elite Wrestling referee Bryce Remsburg guest appeared on The Certified Mark Show and was asked about the chances of AEW running a show at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. He stated that if AEW were looking for a domestic venue to host All In, Lincoln Financial would be in the conversation. He doesn’t think it’ll happen in 2027, but does believe it’s a possibility in the future. “I will say, the fact they’ve hosted wrestling before, which is WrestleMania, is a positive. That means they know what they’re doing, they know what to do, and I will say Philadelphia has been one of the best (places for) AEW since it started so, if we were looking for a domestic stadium to host All In at, I do think The Linc would be in the conversation. I don’t think it’s gonna happen next year… I’m not sure we have demand for a Linc show… But never, ever, ever say never. I’ll say that.” He continued, “There’s no way I could say, ‘No way it’s never happening. Definitely not…’ I’m saying this with actual insider knowledge. It is possible. It’s definitely possible.” The 2026 All In event took place at Wembley Stadium in London, England. The show was headlined by Will Ospreay defeating Kenny Omega to become AEW World Champion.

body: Ilja Dragunov officially departed WWE in August when his contract expired, and he decided not to renew his deal. Dragunov had been off WWE TV since April when he competed in the Andre The Giant Memorial Battle Royal. He joined AEW after his deal expired, making his debut at AEW WrestleDream. Speaking to Ariel Helwani on The Ariel Helwani Show , Dragunov was asked when he thought of leaving WWE. “After I tore my ACL, I was fortunate to win a championship straight back on my comeback, which was an amazing moment for me that I still cherish. After I dropped the belt, things went into directions where I feel like it could’ve been better and more time to go into a story or something outside of holding a championship. Around April, maybe even a month before that, I was already just thinking about it. It never changed anything about my work because I love what I do and I make every minute count, but we all have feelings and we all want to devote ourselves to this, but I know it’s part of the business. I wouldn’t change that,” he said. Elsewhere during the interview, Dragunov gave more insight into his decision to leave WWE. You can find his full comments here . Dragunov made his AEW in-ring debut on Wednesday’s Dynamite, defeating “Speedball” Mike Bailey. title: Ric Flair’s Facebook Posts Raise Questions After He Claims He No Longer Owns His Page
raw_title: Ric Flair’s Facebook Posts Raise Questions After He Claims He No Longer Owns His Page
summary_src: Ric Flair says he doesn’t own his Facebook page anymore, but something about that explanation isn’t adding up. The WWE Hall of Famer blasted the people behind his account for posting content while he was hospitalized, calling their behavior reckless and inappropriate.
body: On October 24, Flair broke his silence after being hospitalized following a nasty fall in Tampa . He shared a photo of himself with a bandage over his injured right eye and thanked the doctors at Tampa General Hospital for treating him. But his message took an unexpected turn when he started talking about Facebook. “And Just So You Know For Those Who Were Asking And Wondering, I Don’t Own My Own Facebook Page Anymore. I Apologize For The Reckless Posting Behavior On My Facebook When I Was In The Hospital. It Was Completely Inappropriate!” Flair didn’t explain exactly which posts upset him, but a look at his verified Facebook page gives a better idea of what was happening while he was dealing with his medical emergency. The account continued sharing wrestling clips, throwback photos and promotional content throughout the time Flair was hospitalized. One post featured an old clip of Flair with the caption, “Only true champions can carry the gold! WOOOOOO!” Another featured wrestling footage with the caption, “Teamwork Makes The Dream Work! WOOOOOO!” Other posts included a throwback photo of Flair in a pink robe with the caption, “I May Wear Pink, But Stealing Hearts Is My True Signature Move!” Another showed an old photograph of Flair alongside the message, “I’m Just A Humble Nature Boy… With A Little Extra Charm!” There’s nothing particularly unusual about those posts on their own. They’re the kind of nostalgic wrestling content that regularly appears on Flair’s social media accounts. The issue is that they continued going out while Flair was in the hospital with injuries to his face. It’s entirely possible those posts were scheduled in advance and simply continued publishing without anyone stopping them. There’s no confirmation of who actually uploaded the content or whether the person managing the account knew what was happening with Flair at the time. The account also appears to have been professionally managed, with AP Brand Group a possible connection. However, there’s no confirmation that the company was responsible for these particular posts or currently controls Flair’s Facebook presence. But here’s where things get even more confusing. Despite Flair saying he no longer owns his Facebook page, the account also shared the same health update that appeared on his official X and Instagram accounts. That raises an obvious question about how his personal statement ended up on a page he claims is no longer his. Of course, owning a Facebook page and having access to publish content are two different things. Flair could still have some involvement with the account, or whoever manages it could simply be sharing his statements across multiple platforms. The matching post doesn’t prove Flair personally has access, but it does suggest that someone handling the Facebook page is still distributing his official updates. title: Leon Slater Calls TNA World Title Reign Surreal
raw_title: Leon Slater Says TNA World Championship Is 'Finally Beginning To Feel Mine'
summary_src: Leon Slater comments on his TNA World Championship reign. At TNA Bound for Glory, Leon Slater defeated Nic Nemeth and became the youngest TNA World Champion in the company’s history. He accomplished his goal five years earlier than he predicted.
body: At TNA Bound for Glory, Leon Slater defeated Nic Nemeth and became the youngest TNA World Champion in the company’s history. He accomplished his goal five years earlier than he predicted. Speaking on the I Love Wrestling Podcast , Slater commented on his title reign. “It feels very surreal, man. It took a while for it to settle in because I kind of felt like I was carrying Nic Nemeth’s belt around for a while just because I’ve so used to seeing him with it,” Slater said. “Obviously, I still live at home, which is a great balance to have between my professional life and my personal life. So as any other 22-year-old does after he wins a world title, I hopped on GTA with my friends the other day. I was playing my PlayStation, and I had the TNA Championship set up on my TV table, and I was on the party with my friends. I go, ‘You know what I’m looking at right now?’ They go, ‘Oh yeah, we’re driving through Los Santos, whatever.” I go, “No, no, bro. I’m looking at the TNA World Championship.” Like, it’s in my room as I’m playing, and it was just so difficult for me to compute. This is the same room I’ve sat in for the past, you know 10-15 years. It’s the same game I’ve been playing for the past 13 years, and the only difference is I’ve got the actual TNA World Championship on my TV table. So, it’s finally beginning to feel mine. I’m excited for it to take me in a new direction. I’m excited to take it in a new direction as well and make some magic as TNA World Champion.” Slater is currently scheduled to defeat the title against Trey Miguel at TNA Destination X. title: Leon Slater Says Option C Promo Made Him TNA's Top Guy
raw_title: Leon Slater Feels Like His Option C Promo At TNA Lockdown Was The Moment He Became 'The Guy' In TNA
summary_src: Leon Slater comments on his Option C promo at TNA Lockdown. On the show, Leon Slater competed in a Last Man Standing Steel Cage match for the TNA X Division Title. He defeated Cedric Alexander to become the new champion.
body: On the show, Leon Slater competed in a Last Man Standing Steel Cage match for the TNA X Division Title. He defeated Cedric Alexander to become the new champion. Later that night, Slater announced that he’s exercising Option C to go after Nic Nemeth’s TNA World Title. Speaking on the I Love Wrestling Podcast , Slater was asked if the night he enacted Option C was the moment he stamped his spot as a future main eventer in TNA. “Yeah, absolutely. I think it’s rare that we get these pinpoint moments in wrestling. I’m not comparing here but just to use an analogy, the Austin 3:16 promo for example. You can point to that moment and you go, ‘Yeah, that’s when he became who he is.’ I feel like, for me, in my TNA run, the moment of me cashing in Option C was like, ‘Leon’s not the kid anymore. He is the guy now.’ Obviously being able to follow through on that at Bound for Glory just solidified that even further. I think people are going to look back on that Option C promo and that cash in in Chicago and use that as a moment to where I entered the next chapter of my career, which is where I am now.” Later, Slater says that as soon as Carlos Silva handed him the title at Lockdown, he knew that he wanted to go for the TNA World Championship. “I knew, as soon as he [Carlos Silva] handed it to me, I’m not going to lie. It’s not even a thing of like me thinking the X Division is below me now because I don’t think the X Division will ever be below anyone. It is one of the most legendary divisions in all of professional wrestling and it influenced and changed the game more than I can even put into words. But over the course of me having that initial reign, I feel like I did things that I could never even imagine. Whether it was having the title every week for three or four months on NXT television and having it on that platform or having it on SmackDown against Carmelo Hayes or having it walking into John Cena’s final match. You know all of these moments and all of these matches that I’ve managed to have. This is even excluding all the stuff I did in TNA with the championship, my matches with Je’Von [Evans] and Myron [Reed] and Cedric [Alexander] and Rich Swann. I felt like I had such a beautiful run as X Division champion that I just couldn’t see a world where me being as close to–I feel like I’m a very similar person now to when I was holding the X Division. So I think it’d be difficult for me to take that to new heights or different heights as this version of myself. So I feel like it was time to move on from that and move up to the World Heavyweight Title division and see if I could hang there and see if what I thought in my head was true. It turns out it is.” Elsewhere in the interview, Slater commented on his TNA World Title win. Fans can read his full comments here . If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.
summary: Leon Slater defeated Cedric Alexander in a Last Man Standing Steel Cage match to win the TNA X Division Title at Lockdown. He then exercised Option C to challenge for Nic Nemeth's TNA World Title. title: Iran Plots Against Americans Escalate Ahead of Crown Jewel
raw_title: NYT: Iran in ‘advanced stages’ of planning attacks on Americans as Crown Jewel remains set for Riyadh
summary_src: U.S. intelligence officials have warned Secretary of State Marco Rubio that Iranian plans to attack Americans have reached “advanced stages,” according to The New York Times.
body: U.S. intelligence officials have warned Secretary of State Marco Rubio that Iranian plans to attack Americans have reached “advanced stages,” according to The New York Times. In a headline report , the Times said Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton sent Rubio a memo warning of a significant increase in Iranian efforts to target U.S. personnel. The memo stated that intelligence agencies had received information indicating that Iran had “substantially increased efforts to target U.S. personnel.” The lethal plotting efforts by the Iranians against U.S. citizens have reached advanced stages in both the Middle East and certain other countries. U.S. officials told the Times that agencies now assess the threat against Americans in the Middle East and elsewhere to be at its highest level since the war with Iran began in February. The intelligence reportedly includes potential targets outside the Middle East, including in Europe. One official added that Iran’s ambitions to carry out attacks exceeded its ability to do so. The warning adds to security concerns surrounding Saudi Arabia, where WWE is scheduled to stage Crown Jewel in Riyadh on November 7. As reported on Wednesday , nonessential U.S. Embassy personnel and their families have been ordered to leave Saudi Arabia. The Times now reports that the drawdown was directly connected to recent intelligence concerning Iranian attack plans. Despite the security situation, TKO executive chair Ari Emanuel said on Friday that Crown Jewel remained scheduled to proceed. Emanuel said TKO has a team monitoring developments daily and that the company could move an event if circumstances required it. Friday’s edition of WWE SmackDown included multiple promotional spots for Crown Jewel.
summary: U.S. intelligence officials warned Secretary of State Marco Rubio that Iranian efforts to target American personnel have reached advanced stages, according to The New York Times. The memo from Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton notes a substantial increase in lethal plotting in the Middle East, Europe and elsewhere. The threat level against Americans is now assessed at its highest point since the war with Iran began in February, adding to security concerns for the upcoming Crown Jewel event in Riyadh.

title: Injury Update: MVP Shuts Down Rumors The Hurt Syndicate Refused to Put Wrestlers Over in AEW

summary_src: MVP is done hearing that The Hurt Syndicate doesn’t want to put people over in AEW. After weeks of chatter about Bobby Lashley, Shelton Benjamin and MVP supposedly pushing back on creative, MVP jumped on Twitter and basically called the entire story BS.
body: MVP responded on Twitter after an account brought up several rumors surrounding the faction. Those included claims that The Hurt Syndicate had refused to put certain wrestlers over, that MVP was influencing Lashley and Benjamin to say no to ideas, and that he had backstage heat with important members of AEW creative. MVP didn’t dance around any of it. He flat-out denied the claims and even hinted that he may now have an idea where some of the rumors are coming from. “Rumor? Nah man. You are absolutely Wrong!!!! None of this is true. But now I know where this whisper campaign is coming from! 😉” Apparently that wasn’t enough, because MVP then opened Twitter and saw even more talk about The Hurt Syndicate. That’s when he really went off, calling the stories “blatant lies” and demanding to know who was feeding them to people. “So I open up Twitter to see lies being reported about The Hurt Syndicate. BLATANT LIES!!! Who is the source of these lies?” MVP also went directly after the idea that The Hurt Syndicate didn’t want to put other wrestlers over. According to him, they actually wanted to work with younger talent and were even willing to drop the AEW World Tag Team Championships back to Private Party. “To the contrary, we wanted to work with younger talent! We wanted to drop the tag titles BACK to Private Party!!! STOP BELIEVING THE BS!” That Private Party comment certainly gets right to the heart of the controversy. Lashley and Benjamin previously took the AEW World Tag Team Titles from Private Party, and MVP is now saying The Hurt Syndicate wanted to eventually return the favor. All of this comes after Sean Ross Sapp recently addressed the group’s situation on The Hump. While Sapp said he didn’t know why The Hurt Syndicate hasn’t been featured as consistently lately, he claimed there had been situations where members of the group didn’t want to put other wrestlers over . “Listen, I know there’s been a lot of talk about them like not wanting to put people over. There’s definitely been some situations where they haven’t wanted to. That has been a thing.” Sapp didn’t say which members allegedly pushed back, who they supposedly didn’t want to lose to or whether any of it had anything to do with their reduced television presence. Now MVP is pushing back hard against the narrative that The Hurt Syndicate has been difficult when it comes to putting other talent over. Whatever is actually happening with The Hurt Syndicate’s AEW booking, MVP clearly isn’t staying quiet while these stories make the rounds. He’s denying the rumors, saying the group wanted to help younger talent and even claiming they were ready to put the titles back on Private Party. title: Ilja Dragunov Explains Exit From WWE For AEW
raw_title: Ilja Dragunov Reflects On Final Stretch Of WWE Run, Decision To Join AEW
summary_src: Now that he is "All Elite," Ilja Dragunov has reflected on his final year on the WWE roster.
body: AEW/Speedy Ruiz After weeks of rumors and reports, Ilja Dragunov is officially "All Elite." The former WWE Superstar made his AEW debut at the WrestleDream pay-per-view on October 17 , and has already had a successful in-ring debut against "Speedball" Mike Bailey on "AEW Dynamite." His move to AEW comes after a seven year run with WWE that did see the "Mad Dragon" see success, but according to the man himself, could have ended a lot better. Dragunov recently spoke to The Takedown on Sports Illustrated, and admitted that he needed to breathe new air after his return from injury in October of last year. "It has been a very complicated time for me because, you see, I came back from an ACL tear that happened in the most unexciting way possible. I worked myself through rehab and was training very hard, and was very dedicated. I came back, and I won the United States Championship basically on my return, which was an awesome, memorable moment. But then certain times, like after I dropped the belt and I was going through my next performances, I felt like I felt in my gut things are different. And I don't blame anybody. I'm a gentleman and I have way too much respect for the last seven years that I the most of my 20s that I spent with the company. But I felt like it is fine for me and reasonable to ask myself, 'Is there more? Is there a new air I can breathe?'" Dragunov has been open about his departure from WWE since his arrival in AEW, stating that he didn't feel that WWE's renewed contract offer was enough for him to commit his future there, and decided to take his talents elsewhere. It's not yet known the length of his AEW contract, though AEW fans will be hoping he sticks around for many years to come.
summary: Ilja Dragunov made his AEW debut at WrestleDream on October 17 and picked up a win over Mike Bailey on Dynamite. The former WWE star recently told The Takedown on Sports Illustrated that his seven-year run ended on a sour note after he returned from an ACL tear, captured the United States Championship on his first night back, then sensed a shift following the title loss. title: The Rise of Independent Wrestling Promotions in Modern Sports Entertainment

body: DMFirst Veer Game odds uden om ROFUS Jalwa Game Goa Game Raja Game MaanWin The Rise of Independent Wrestling Promotions in Modern Sports Entertainment By Kendall Jenkins on 2026-10-24 08:43:00 Professional wrestling has undergone significant changes as independent promotions attract growing attention from fans, performers, and industry professionals. While major organizations continue to dominate mainstream wrestling, smaller companies are creating opportunities for alternative storytelling, distinctive wrestling styles, and closer connections between performers and audiences. Independent wrestling has existed for decades, but digital platforms and changing viewing habits have made it easier for regional promotions to reach supporters beyond their local communities. Fans can now discover emerging talent, follow independent events, and purchase merchandise directly from organizations that previously depended almost entirely on live attendance. This development has created an increasingly diverse wrestling environment where creativity and entrepreneurial thinking are essential. Running a successful independent promotion requires more than organizing entertaining matches. Financial management, venue coordination, marketing, and audience engagement all contribute to building a sustainable business. Understanding these responsibilities reveals why independent wrestling has become an important part of modern sports entertainment. Behind the excitement of live wrestling is a demanding business operation. Independent promoters must coordinate venues, negotiate performer agreements, arrange insurance, manage ticket sales, and organize promotional campaigns. Unlike major wrestling companies with extensive administrative departments, smaller promotions often rely on limited teams handling several responsibilities simultaneously. Managing equipment and office resources is another part of operating efficiently. Promotions regularly produce contracts, event schedules, merchandise labels, promotional materials, and documentation for performers and venues. As organizations expand or replace their office equipment, they may accumulate unused supplies that still have commercial value. A promotion retiring an older office printer, for example, could recover money from unopened replacement cartridges through www.selltoner.com . Redirecting funds from surplus office inventory toward event production is one practical example of how smaller entertainment businesses can make better use of their existing resources. These operational decisions rarely attract attention from wrestling audiences, but they contribute to financial stability. Promotions that manage their expenses carefully have greater flexibility to invest in production quality, talent development, and memorable live experiences. title: Charlotte Flair Says Vulnerability Boosts Her Strength
raw_title: WWE's Charlotte Flair: 'Being Vulnerable Makes You Powerful'
summary_src: WWE star Charlotte Flair opened up on how embracing vulnerability allowed her to connect with fans better.
body: WWE's Charlotte Flair reflected on how her latest run has allowed her to embrace her vulnerability for a greater connection with fans. Flair spoke to Russell Wilson and Kyle Long for " Set, Hut! " about the pressure that came with being Ric Flair's daughter, her prevalence in the main event picture and the disconnect with fans that came as a result. "Being Ric's kid came with a lot of hate. I have been a bad guy for the last 10 years. I love it. But I tore my knee two years ago. I came back and I had kind of a disconnect with the fans," she explained, going on to say that, as the Charlotte character grew, so did the "armor due to the fans' criticism." "But then I learned while I was gone, being vulnerable is what makes you powerful and resilient and strong," she continued. Flair said that was the goal of her Player's Tribune article , opening up to the audience and separating the "Bada**" that was Charlotte and the real-life Ashley Fliehr behind that character. She said that allowed her to connect with the audience on a different level. "Being able to share that side of me with the audience, from being on top for 10 years. I have won 14 titles, I am synonymous with gold. But I haven't had a title match since in the last year since I lost at WrestleMania. It's like, how is this my best year? Which is crazy to think, but really it's the bond with the fans." She added that when she does turn heel, she's aware that it's going to mean more because she has had the opportunity to share who she really was. But she has learned that it's not her "The Queen" character that made her who she was, rather everything she has gone through in her personal life to get to this point.
summary: WWE star Charlotte Flair discussed the pressure of being Ric Flair's daughter and how it led to a decade as a villain with a disconnect from fans. After tearing her knee two years ago, she realized that embracing vulnerability makes her more powerful and resilient. This approach was the focus of her Player's Tribune article, allowing her to separate her on-screen character from real-life Ashley Fliehr and connect with audiences on a deeper level.

title: Fans Clown AEW Over Kamille’s Birthday Post Amid Her Continued TV Absence
raw_title: Fans Clown AEW Over Kamille’s Birthday Post Amid Her Continued TV Absence
summary_src: AEW tried to wish Kamille a happy birthday, but the post ended up reminding fans of a completely different question — where the hell has she been? The former NWA Women’s Champion has barely been seen on AEW television this year, and fans wasted no time calling the company out over it.
body: AEW posted a birthday message for Kamille on Twitter on October 24 . Instead of simply joining in with birthday wishes, plenty of fans immediately turned the replies into a discussion about her lengthy absence from television. One fan couldn’t understand how Kamille managed to disappear from AEW programming all over again after finally returning earlier this year: “I don’t understand how she disappeared again.” Another fan went directly after Tony Khan and demanded an answer about Kamille’s whereabouts. Some fans were apparently surprised to even be reminded that Kamille remains part of AEW. One questioned whether she was actually still on the company’s roster. Another fan took things a little further and openly mocked the fact that Kamille is still employed by AEW despite barely appearing: “She still works there? LOLOLOLOLOL.” One reply even turned AEW’s birthday message into a joke about how much time Kamille has spent away from television. “Happy birthday. I’m glad you got two years off for your birthday present from AEW. 🤷‍♂️” The reaction comes after Sean Ross Sapp recently confirmed during a Fightful Q&A that Kamille is still under contract with AEW. He also said there hasn’t been a long-term creative plan for her since she was originally removed from television during her storyline with Mercedes Moné. Kamille briefly returned at Dynasty on April 12 , attacking Willow Nightingale backstage before defeating Big Anne on the Zero Hour pre-show. Three days later, she lost to Nightingale in a TBS Championship match on Dynamite and disappeared from AEW television again. According to Sean Ross Sapp, that short comeback was essentially what AEW had planned for her at the time . Kamille was brought back to pick up a quick victory before putting over Nightingale, rather than to begin another extended run. “There was never a long term plan for her after she was taken off TV for the Mercedes angle ever. They brought her back to get a quick win and put over Willow in her challenge. That’s it. There’s never been a long term plan.” Kamille has remained busy with projects outside AEW, but her wrestling appearances have been extremely limited. Her only match since losing to Nightingale came for Diamond Championship Wrestling, with the bout airing in August. AEW’s birthday post certainly got people talking about Kamille again, just probably not in the way the company expected. With her still under contract but nowhere to be found on television, fans clearly haven’t forgotten about her absence. Subhojeet Mukherjee Subhojeet Mukherjee has covered pro wrestling for over 20 years, delivering trusted news and backstage updates to fans around the world.
summary: The latest: AEW posted a birthday message for Kamille on Twitter on October 24 . Instead of simply joining in with birthday wishes, plenty of the audience immediately turned the replies into a discussion about her lengthy absence from television.

title: Billy Gunn Explains Joining The Acclaimed In AEW
raw_title: Billy Gunn Details Thought Process Behind Joining The Acclaimed In AEW
summary_src: Billy Gunn recently shared his thoughts on the reasoning behind his pairing with Anthony Bowens and Max Caster in AEW, explaining what he brought to the group.
body: AEW Billy Gunn's pairing with Max Caster and Anthony Bowens as The Acclaimed might not have made sense on paper , but after the angle started rolling, Gunn leaned heavily into his Attitude Era character and became "Daddy A**" while their stable exploded in popularity amongst AEW fans. Speaking on "Inside the Ropes," Gunn explained the genesis of the group. "I still have equity in this business, so [putting] me with them, it kind of makes people take notice a little bit," Gunn said. The veteran joked that he might come off as arrogant, but he genuinely believes his inclusion legitimized Caster and Bowens. "The Acclaimed wasn't just me — it was all three of us. It was just — everything just kind of fell into place." Gunn fondly recalled their shared entrance, which saw Caster rapping, Bowens calling out the hometown, and him joining them all to "scissor" taunt at the end. Gunn acknowledged that fans were originally confused by the taunt, but the people eventually got it. "I am a parent's worse nightmare. Like, the first half of my career I'm pointing at my crotch, and the second half I'm 'scissoring' people — like a lesbian!" he exclaimed. In recent years, Gunn seems to have heavily drawn back on his in-ring appearances, competing on occasion outside of AEW. His last match for his former promotion took place on "AEW Collision" back in January. Both Caster and Bowens have since parted ways with AEW , with Caster specifically being at the center of controversy after debuting in TNA and being cut loose due to the content of his pre-match rap. Caster then announced his hiatus from wrestling shortly after.
summary: Billy Gunn joined Max Caster and Anthony Bowens to form The Acclaimed in AEW. On Inside the Ropes, Gunn said his presence drew attention due to his equity in the business and helped legitimize the duo as the trio's chemistry developed naturally. He recalled their popular entrance with Caster's rap, Bowens naming the hometown and the group ending with the scissor taunt that fans eventually embraced.

title: Zack Sabre Jr. Refuses To Claim TMDK Leadership
raw_title: Zack Sabre Jr. Would Never Claim To Be Leader Of TMDK, Says It Belongs To Australian Wrestling
summary_src: It is more fulfilling for Zack Sabre Jr. to see people within the group thriving as opposed to being the leader. The T.M.D.K.
body: It is more fulfilling for Zack Sabre Jr. to see people within the group thriving as opposed to being the leader. The T.M.D.K. (The Mighty Don’t Kneel) faction has different branches within the pro wrestling space. It originates in Australia. It started with Shane Haste and Mikey Nicholls, who are scheduled to reunite in Pro Wrestling NOAH on 10/25. The New Japan Pro-Wrestling branch consists of Zack Sabre Jr., Robbie Eagles, Kosei Fujita, Ryohei Oiwa, Bad Dude Tito, and Hartley Jackson. Sabre Jr. was interviewed for CMLL’s Esto es Lucha Podcast and stated that he would never claim to be the leader of the group. “Shane Haste very smartly came up with ‘The Frontman’ because there is no leader. Mikey Nicholls and Shane Haste started T.M.D.K. in 2006, 2007, when the Australian independent wrestling scene was really sort of still trying to create something. I would never claim to be the leader of T.M.D.K., because it would never be mine. T.M.D.K. belongs to Australian wrestling, and as much now, I think with (Ryohei) Oiwa and (Kosei) Fujita, I think something that two Australian wrestlers, Mike and Shane, two people that I spent a lot of time with in the NOAH Dojo and really worked their asses off to make something from nothing in Australia to get to where they got to and now, when I see Fujita and Oiwa with the T.M.D.K. colors and T.M.D.K. flags, winning the biggest tournaments in Japan, that’s much more fulfilling for me rather than claiming to be a leader.”
summary: Zack Sabre Jr. says it is more fulfilling to watch members of TMDK thrive rather than position himself as the group's leader. He credits Shane Haste and Mikey Nicholls with founding TMDK in Australia in 2006 or 2007 and insists the faction belongs to Australian wrestling. The New Japan Pro-Wrestling branch features Sabre Jr., Robbie Eagles, Kosei Fujita, Ryohei Oiwa, Bad Dude Tito and Hartley Jackson, while Haste and Nicholls are set to reunite in Pro Wrestling NOAH on October 25.

title: Ric Flair Hospitalized After Fall in Tampa
raw_title: WWE Legend Ric Flair, 77, Hospitalized After Falling Outside Restaurant While ‘Dealing’ with Blood Clot in His Leg
body: His daughter Charlotte Flair said in a social media post that the WWE legend is "going to be ok" Ric, 77, had canceled a Seattle appearance hours before the fall as doctors limited his travel due to a blood clot in his leg Ric Flair is recovering in the hospital after a fall outside a restaurant in Florida. The retired WWE legend, 77, was injured in a fall outside Wagamama in Tampa on Friday, Oct. 23, TMZ reported. The incident occurred hours after Ric revealed on Instagram that an upcoming appearance was being canceled due to a blood clot in his leg. In photos obtained by TMZ, Ric is seen lying on his back while surrounded by medical staff. He is also pictured being transported into an ambulance. Ric left his phone and drink behind as he walked across the street after visiting the restaurant that morning, per the outlet. He reportedly cut his head in the fall and his eye was "bleeding extensively." Ric's daughter, WWE wrestler Charlotte Flair , shared an update on his condition in a post on X on Saturday, Oct. 24. "Not my dad telling the doctor he fell bc of warrior dropping him on his head … (ps: he's going to be ok)," she wrote. Also on Oct. 24, Ric shared a photo of himself sitting in a chair with a bandage over his eye. "Thank You All For The Messages And Prayers! I Will Get Back To You Each Individually As I Get Stronger," he wrote in the caption of his Instagram post . "Thank You To All The Tampa General Hospital Staff And Doctors That Put Up With Me Until 4:30am. I Appreciate You All And Thank You For Everything You Did For Me! I Am Focused On My Healing And Recovery Right Now. I Will Be Okay," added Ric. The wrestling legend previously shared a lengthy post about his health, hours before he fell. "I want to sincerely apologize to my agent, Steve Solomon … and especially all my fans in Seattle for having to cancel my scheduled appearance," said Ric. "Unfortunately, I am dealing with a blood clot in my leg, and my doctors have limited my travel to 3–4 hours. Seattle falls outside that range, and as disappointed as I am, I have to put my health and recovery first." "Blood clots are extremely serious and can be life-threatening. We have seen this recently with Jalen Hurts and the complications involving blood clots in his lungs," he continued. "It is a reminder that this is not something to take lightly, and I must follow medical advice." Ric said that he is scheduled to undergo a procedure "to strip the affected vein," which will hopefully allow him to travel more and continue with his work commitments. "Please know this decision was not made lightly. I am truly sorry for the inconvenience and disappointment, and I am incredibly grateful for your patience, understanding, and continued support," he concluded. In June 2025, the former wrestling star revealed to PEOPLE he had skin cancer for "the second time in three years." Ric announced in an Instagram post a month later that he was "cancer-free."
summary: The 77-year-old retired WWE star fell outside a Florida restaurant on October 23, cutting his head and causing extensive bleeding around his eye. He had canceled a scheduled appearance in Seattle that same day after doctors restricted his travel due to a blood clot in his leg. His daughter Charlotte Flair later posted on social media that her father is going to be okay.

title: Contract News: AJ Francis’ TNA Contract Coming Up Soon
raw_title: AJ Francis’ TNA Contract Coming Up Soon
summary_src: AJ Francis could be heading into free agency soon, but don’t expect him to leave TNA Wrestling just yet. The former WWE Superstar’s contract is coming up at the end of 2026, and both sides reportedly want to keep their relationship going.
body: According to Sean Ross Sapp of Fightful Select , Francis’ current TNA deal is set to expire toward the end of the year. However, Francis is interested in staying with the company, and TNA wants to keep him around. A new agreement is expected to get done, although nothing has been finalized. That’s a pretty good sign for Francis, who has spent the last three years building his career in TNA after his WWE run came to an end. During his time with the promotion, Francis captured the TNA Digital Media Championship and brought back the Canadian International Heavyweight Championship. He’s also been involved in several major storylines, working with names like Joe Hendry, Mike Santana and Elijah. Francis recently made it clear that he’s happy with how things are going in TNA. During an interview with The Wrestling Classic , he explained why he feels more appreciated by the company than he did during his WWE days. “I felt like I have a home in TNA because they recognize what I bring to the table.” Francis also praised the creative freedom he’s been given, explaining that he’s able to play a bigger role in putting together his storylines. “I’m calling the plays. You know what I’m saying? And they sending me out there first to set the tone.” Before finding success in TNA, Francis competed in WWE as Top Dolla and also made appearances for NWA and MLW. However, his latest run has given him a chance to establish himself as a regular part of TNA programming. For now, there’s no indication that Francis is looking to jump to another promotion. Both sides want to work out a new deal, so unless something changes during negotiations, it looks like he’ll be sticking around. Steve Carrier Steve Carrier is the founder of Ringside News and has been reporting on pro wrestling since 1997. His stories have been featured on TMZ, Forbes, Bleacher Report, and more.
summary: Per Sean Ross Sapp of Fightful Select , Francis’ current TNA deal is slated to expire toward the end of the year. That explained, Francis is interested in staying with the company, and TNA is hoping to keep him around.

title: WWE Legend Ric Flair Gets Promising Health Update After Being Hospitalized
raw_title: WWE Legend Ric Flair Gets Promising Health Update After Being Hospitalized
body: ‘The Nature Boy’s fall came hours after he had shared a health update on social media. Flair, 77, broke his silence and shared a promising health update after being hospitalized yesterday. The WWE Hall of Famer issued a statement on his X account, saying that he will be okay after the fall. Flair posted a photo alongside the statement, which showed his right eye bandaged. He expressed his gratitude to the hospital staff and doctors for taking care of him well into the early morning hours. “Thank you all for the messages and prayers! I will get back to you each individually as I get stronger. Thank you to all the Tampa General Hospital staff and doctors that put up with me until 4:30 a.m. I appreciate you all and thank you for everything you did for me. I am focused on my healing and recovery right now,” Flair wrote on X . “I will be okay! And just so you know, for those who were asking and wondering, I don’t own my own Facebook page anymore. I apologize for the reckless posting behavior on my Facebook when I was in the hospital. It was completely inappropriate!” Flair wrote. Although Flair’s fall was a scary situation, particularly because of his age, it is nice to see that he received a promising health update. Ric Flair was forced to cancel an appearance in Seattle, Washington, because of a blood clot in his leg. The WWE Hall of Famer was told that he had to limit his travel, so he regrettably canceled his appearance. Flair revealed that he will be undergoing a procedure soon to address the issue. He then apologized to fans for the inconvenience, but said that he will be prioritizing his health. “I am truly sorry of the inconvenience and disappointment. I’m incredibly grateful for you patience, understanding, and continued support. I look forward to getting healthy and seeing you all down the road,” Flair wrote on X . Flair’s hospitalization led to fans extending their best wishes to the pro wrestling legend on social media. His daughter, WWE superstar Charlotte Flair took to social media to update fans on her father’s health. While Flair did sustain some injuries from the fall, most noticeably on his eye, Charlotte reassured fans that he will be okay. Charlotte even shared that her father did not lost his sense of humor, saying that late WWE legend Ultimate Warrior was to blame. “Not my dad telling the doctor he fell because of Warrior dropping him on his head. (Ps: He’s going to be ok),” Charlotte Flair wrote on X . Giancarlo Aulino Giancarlo Aulino is sports writer who covers UFC for Heavy.com. title: The Miz Recalls Early Locker Room Backlash After First WWE Tag Title Victory
raw_title: The Miz Recalls Upsetting WWE Locker Room On The Day Of First Tag Title Win
summary_src: Among the many issues between The Miz and the WWE locker room early in his career, the wrestler recalled "ruffling feathers" on the night he won the tag title.
body: The Miz dealt with numerous problems during his early years in the WWE locker, including the infamous stories of him enduring extreme hazing from the veterans at the time , who didn't consider his entry point into the business through "Tough Enough" as legit. Unfortunately, that wasn't the only time he'd worked the locker room up, as he recounted on WWE Vault how the night he first won tag team gold with John Morrison ended with backstage heat. "We used to shoot 'ECW' before 'SmackDown,' and so me and John Morrison went on ECW — I think it was a CM Punk match — and we went on commentary and we just ripped it apart, and people were upset about that," he recalled. "Then we go out on this match, and we end up winning the tag titles, and we upset even more people because we were celebrating while the story was supposed to be with the other tag team." The Miz claimed that he and Morrison were told to celebrate like they "had just won the Superbowl," and considering it was the first time he won gold in WWE, it wasn't hard for him to act excited. However, the locker room took issue with both wrongs taking place on the same night. Despite that, The Miz recalled the tag team being asked to appear on commentary again the next week, meaning the higher-ups were happy with them. "We were ruffling feathers, a lot of feathers," he recalled. "We started a show called 'The Dirt Sheet' that really, really ruffled feathers. ... 'Going into business for yourself' is what I believe the comment was." "The Dirt Sheet" ended up being one of WWE's earliest forays into a web show , becoming so popular that WWE brought it into live television.
summary: The Miz explained on WWE Vault that he and John Morrison drew heat from the locker room on the night they captured their first WWE tag team championships. After cutting loose on commentary during an ECW taping that preceded SmackDown, the duo was instructed to celebrate wildly upon winning the titles, which clashed with the planned focus on the opposing team. This excitement, especially as it marked Miz's initial WWE gold, further upset veterans who already viewed his Tough Enough background skeptically.

title: UFC 336 to feature two championship fights in Toronto, interim welterweight title added
raw_title: UFC 336 to feature two championship fights in Toronto, interim welterweight title added
summary_src: On Saturday’s broadcast from Abu Dhabi, it was confirmed that two title fights will occur on January 30, when UFC 336 takes place in Toronto.
body: Two championship fights are coming to Toronto, with the UFC releasing a pair of announcements for its first major card of 2027. On Saturday’s broadcast from Abu Dhabi, it was confirmed that two title fights will occur on January 30, when UFC 336 takes place in Toronto. The major note is that the latest interim title is being added to the mix, allowing Carlos Prates and Michael Morales to compete for a belt. An interim welterweight title is being introduced due to champion Islam Makhachev being unable to fight in January. A fight between Makhachev and Prates was being targeted for the January 30 event. Announcer Jon Anik told fellow broadcaster Daniel Cormier that he was informed of the news two days ago. Prates (24-7) is 7-1 in the UFC and on a three-fight winning streak with recent stoppages of former champions Jack Della Maddalena and Leon Edwards in his last two fights. He also has the distinction of being awarded a performance of the night bonus for all seven of his wins inside the promotion. Morales (19-0) has an unblemished record with seven wins in the UFC but has not competed since last November when he stopped Sean Brady. In addition, UFC flyweight champion Joshua Van (18-2) will make the third defense of his title when he meets Manel Kape at UFC 336. Van won the title last December when Alexandre Pantoja sustained an arm injury right away in the first round, and Van was declared the winner by TKO. Pantoja received a rematch in September, with Van winning by unanimous decision, and will be a heavy favorite to be named ‘Fighter of the Year’. Kape (23-7) has been victorious in his last four fights, including Brandon Royval and Kyoji Horiguchi by stoppage. The championship fights are the first announcements for UFC 336 as the UFC returns to Toronto for the first time since January 2024. The card in Canada coincides with its pay-per-views moving to a subscription model on Paramount+ in the country, while its preliminary fights will continue to air on Rogers Sportsnet and Fight Pass.
summary: Two championship fights are coming to Toronto, with the UFC releasing a pair of announcements for its first major card of 2027. Officially, two title fights will occur on January 30, when UFC 336 takes place in Toronto.

body: Skadi pinned Megan Bayne at the 1:04:09 mark to win this year’s International Women’s Grand Prix for Team Mexico. This latest International Women’s Grand Prix was a start studded affair with wrestlers coming from AEW, STARDOM, Maple Leaf Pro, MLW, and RevPro coming to Arena Mexico to take on the brightest stars from CMLL. Obviously Bayne will come down as the most dominant in the record books because she was the last to be eliminated, but the other two should be noted. Ever since the International Women’s GP was first introduced in 2021, Team Mexico has been able to beat Team World each time except in 2023 when future Team World member Tessa Blanchard won. title: On the Record: Rob Van Dam Opens Up On Uncomfortable Encounters With Scott Hall and Why Their Relationship Wasn’t Always Positive
raw_title: Rob Van Dam Reveals Uncomfortable Encounters With Scott Hall and Why Their Relationship Wasn’t Always Positive
summary_src: Rob Van Dam isn’t interested in rewriting history just because someone has passed away — and that includes his complicated relationship with WWE Hall of Famer Scott Hall.
body: Speaking on his 1 of a Kind with RVD podcast , Van Dam was discussing why he refuses to pretend every wrestler he encountered throughout his career was a great person. The subject came up while he was defending his continued criticism of Bobby Fulton, explaining that someone’s death doesn’t automatically erase the experiences people had with them. RVD made it clear that he doesn’t believe in changing his stories to make fans feel better about their favorite wrestlers. “After someone passes, unless you made amends with that person, you’re going to have whatever feelings you have about that person based on your experiences with them. And if that don’t change, then it don’t change.” “So, if you want to hear firsthand stories, they’re not always going to be colored the way that you want them to be because that’s not honest and that’s not true. And if you don’t want to hear the stories, then that’s cool, too.” That brought Van Dam back to criticism he received roughly two years earlier after discussing Scott Hall. RVD explained that some fans weren’t happy because his recollections of Hall weren’t particularly flattering. One encounter that stuck with him happened at a For the Love of Wrestling convention in England. Van Dam recalled finding himself at a bar with Hall, who began opening up about personal matters. According to RVD, the conversation quickly became uncomfortable. “It was for the Love of Wrestling, and we were in England, and we ended up at the bar together. And he was just — I was just talking about, you know, like he had this energy reeking off of him, like punishing himself. Like he was, you know, he was in one of those moods.” RVD recalled Hall bringing up the fact that they had never really spent time together drinking despite knowing each other for years. “First he was just like, ‘Robbie, you and I have never sat down together and like had a beer, like in all these years. Like we’ve never.’ And I’m just like, ‘Yeah, how about that, man?'” But Van Dam said there was already some history between them. He remembered an occasion when they were supposed to smoke together, only for Hall to back out after allegedly telling Sean Waltman that RVD was a stooge. “I remember we were gonna go smoking one time, and then he told X-Pac he thought I was a stooge, and so he backed out. And so, you know, I’m thinking about that, you know, like, yeah, stooge. Like if anybody — that’s like Bobby Fulton saying I’m dishonest. You know, like you picked the kind of opposite guy to f*ing label. That’s not even believable.” Things took another turn when Hall started asking RVD whether he knew about his past. Van Dam remembered Hall appearing deeply troubled during the conversation. “Anyway, all I said was, you know, that he was like, ‘Robbie, do you know anything about me? Like, do you know my story? Like what I did?’ And I was just like, ‘Oh God.’ You know, this is just getting really heavy real quick. And I was just like, ‘Yeah, yeah, Scott, I think I do.'”

title: Cody Rhodes Predicts Retirement Sooner Than Later

summary_src: Cody Rhodes has once again commented on his WWE retirement, stating that it'll come sooner than many might realize.
body: Sting's retirement seemed to open the flood gates for many other wrestlers to follow in his footsteps and leave the ring for the last time. In the last year, fans saw John Cena, Brock Lesnar, and AJ Styles retire, while Adam Copeland recently announced that he's gearing up to end his career by the close of 2027. For the likes of Cody Rhodes, retirement might seem too soon considering he's only been back in WWE for four years, but at 41, even "The American Nightmare" knows he's approaching the end. "I'll say it will probably happen sooner than later, and I'm not giving any type of spoiler. Time goes by, time goes by like this [snaps his fingers]," Rhodes said during an interview with " WrestleTalk ." "When my daughter is 11 years old, I'm not going to be falling down for a living anymore." The question was originally asked in context of Cena's retirement, which Rhodes claims taught him a lot in how it was executed and Cena's attitude towards it. "I think one of the things that I really enjoyed about how John did it is the finality he brought to it," he stated. "'I have given you everything, this is all I have, anything else wouldn't be right.' And when John says he will never wrestle again, he really means it." Rhodes also stated that he hopes to be brave enough to take a risk on a rising star to put over on his way out. Looking at the history of the industry, Rhodes believes one of the most impactful things that can happen is when a younger star takes the final steps to becoming the next "face" of a company, and he'd like to go out making that happen.

The 41-year-old WWE star referenced his young daughter, saying he will not be taking bumps for a living when she turns 11. Rhodes cited John Cena's recent retirement as an example he admired for its sense of finality.

Destination X is around the corner on November 15, but that hasn’t stopped the TNA title pictures from running wild before the PPV. One thing we know is that Leon Slater will defend the TNA World Championship against Trey Miguel in the main event of Destination X in Edmonton, Alberta, Canada. Trey earned the shot by winning a ladder match against other contenders. In the Knockouts division, Indi Hartwell won the Knockouts Championship and the Apex won the Knockouts Tag Team Championship at Bound For Glory . Those titleholders collided on Impact (Oct. 22, 2026) thanks to the power play from Daria Rae. The SUIT returned from suspension for slapping Hartwell. Indi was still in Daria’s sights, and she booked the champ into an impromptu contractual rematch against Xia Brookside. Despite wrestling in her street clothes, Hartwell overcame the challenge to prevail via Hurts Donut. In the aftermath, Daria distracted Hartwell so Zoey Serrano and Shayna Baszler could ambush the champ. Baszler choked Hartwell out and stood tall holding the Knockouts Championship over her body. Based on basic storytelling logic in professional wrestling, it seems likely that Baszler will get a shot at Hartwell for the gold. The depth in the Knockouts tag team division is increasing. Kiera Hogan dumped Allie to reunite with Tasha Steelz. Fire ‘n Flava are two-time tag champs in TNA. Shotzi Blackheart made a surprise appearance to save Allie, and it seems like that will be a tag team showdown. The Elegance Brand appears to be on the fritz lately. Plus, M is focused on defending the Knockouts Television Championship against Jada Stone on the next episode of Impact. The Nemeth brothers better keep their heads on a swivel. After winning the Call Your Shot Gauntlet, Frankie Kazarian made it clear that he wants to cash in with Avery Styles for the TNA World Tag Team Championship. Avery picked up momentum by beating Joe Alonzo in his Impact debut . At Bound For Glory, Amazing Red was inducted into the TNA Hall of Fame, and he won the X-Division Championship . The legend’s first challenger was determined in a four-way contender bout. Cedric Alexander earned the shot after the System interfered to set Fabian Aichner on a platter. Alexander landed a moonsault to win. That title bout takes place on the next episode of Impact. Last not not least, the Order 4 saga is officially closed. Jason Hotch put the nail in the coffin to retain the TNA International Championship over Mustafa Ali in 2 out of 3 falls. Ali got the upper hand trading roll-ups to take Fall 1. Ali overzealously hit Hotch with the title belt to give away Fall 2 via disqualification. Hotch dug deep to win Fall 3 on a GTS variation. title: Billy Gunn Recalls Unexpected AEW In-Ring Run
raw_title: Billy Gunn Says He Wrestled Much More Than Expected In AEW
summary_src: When Billy Gunn started with AEW, he expected to mainly be a coach while wrestling a handful of matches each year, but that quickly expanded.
body: AEW Billy Gunn's AEW run saw him going from a backstage coach to accompanying his sons, Austin and Colten, as The Gunn Club. Eventually, he'd take on his "Daddy A**" gimmick alongside The Acclaimed, even winning the AEW World Trios Championships with Max Caster and Anthony Bowens. Detailing his AEW tenure on "Inside The Ropes," Gunn explained that he wasn't expecting to have a career resurgence in his late 50s and early 60s. "Yeah, so my contract, I had 12 dates a year. Like, I really wasn't gonna wrestle, but I told Tony [Khan], 'If you need me to, I'll do some here and here and there,'" he explained. Gunn added that he had two contracts with AEW, one as a talent and the other in a backstage role. "And then, lo and behold, they crack me out and then I'm working both shows. I'm working all the time, about to fall apart," he laughed. When asked about how it felt to go up against talent considerably younger than him, Gunn credited that ability to the fact that he was never out of shape , and asserted that he could always "hang" with the young guys. "No matter what they do, I can still — it's going to hurt a little while — I can go if I need to." The 62 year-old shared his belief that, at his age, he's not supposed to be in the ring anymore, but he loves to work out for his health and was still in shape to perform. "[Working out] also lets me still hang with my kids, and Anthony, and those guys, and when I need to work, I can work," Gunn said.
summary: Billy Gunn signed with AEW expecting to wrestle only about a dozen times per year while also working backstage. Instead he ended up competing frequently on both shows and capturing the AEW World Trios Championship with The Acclaimed as part of his "Daddy Ass" persona. On Inside The Ropes, Gunn said he was surprised by the career resurgence in his late 50s and early 60s but credited staying in shape for his ability to keep up with much younger opponents.

body: McIntyre, who has been out of action since WrestleMania 42, is rumored to be back soon, with " Wrestlevotes on Fightful Select " reporting that fans could see him on "WWE Raw" upon his comeback. The report highlighted that sources in WWE believe that the Scotsman could be of better use on the red brand than on the Friday night show. The outlet added that WWE had intended to bring the former world champion back to television since August and had ideas for him, but ultimately decided to change course. During his absence from WWE television, McIntyre has filmed a few movies, including Russell Crowe's "The Last Druid." A recent report confirmed that the McIntyre's movie commitments have ended , which he appeared to hint at in a social media post featuring a video of him training . McIntyre's last match in WWE came at WrestleMania 42, when he lost to Jacob Fatu in an unsanctioned match. He was a constant fixture on the blue brand since the start of 2025, a run which also saw him win the Undisputed WWE Championship from Cody Rhodes at the start of 2026, which he lost back to "The American Nightmare."

body: Knockout Brothers Recapture IWGP Tag Team Titles, Jeff Cobb Revealed as Mystery Partner for NJPW King of Pro-Wrestling 2026 3 weeks ago Image Credit New Japan Pro-Wrestling Image Credit New Japan Pro-Wrestling On October 6th, NJPW’s first night of Road to King of Pro-Wrestling 2026 took place at the legendary Korakuen Hall, with 1,041 fans in attendance to see the Knockout Brothers challenge the United Empire tandem of Great-O-Khan and HENARE for the IWGP Tag Team Titles. The Knockout Brothers, OSKAR and Yuto-Ice, lost the IWGP Tag Team Titles back in June to HENARE and O-Khan, and earned another shot at the championship by defeating Togi Makabe and Toru Yano last month in a very violent No. 1 contenders match. The title match between UE and the Knockout Brothers took place here in the show’s main event, with the champions coming into the bout with a strict game plan: take out the knee of the giant OSKAR and try to keep Yuto-Ice down long enough to continue their reign with the titles. Streaming now on #njpwworld #njkopw pic.twitter.com/nURVnA8NfM The match was exciting, and all was going to plan for O-Khan and HENARE, until the Knockout Brothers once again affirmed the strength of their Pro-Wrestling High and turned the tide in their favor. title: Leon Slater Hopes For TNA Six-Sided Ring Return
raw_title: Leon Slater Says He Would Love To Compete In TNA's Six-Sided Ring As TNA World Champion
summary_src: Leon Slater says he’d love to compete in a six-sided ring in TNA. When TNA first made its debut, they didn’t use the traditional four-sided ring but rather a six-sided wrestling ring, which was used until 2010. They later brought it back in 2014 but ultimately retired it again in 2018.
body: Leon Slater says he’d love to compete in a six-sided ring in TNA. When TNA first made its debut, they didn’t use the traditional four-sided ring but rather a six-sided wrestling ring, which was used until 2010. They later brought it back in 2014 but ultimately retired it again in 2018. Speaking on the I Love Wrestling Podcast , Leon Slater was asked about his reaction to the announcement of TNA Destination X returning this year. Slater said that he was praying that the six-sided ring would make a comeback again. “I was just praying that the six-sided ring would come back, to be real. I don’t know if it is, I don’t know if it isn’t, but man, I hope it does. Because I’m sure, growing up a TNA fan, that’s what we loved, right? So to get the chance to compete in a six-sided ring, as much as people said it sucked back in the day, it’s like way harder; it hurts way more than a four-sided ring, and that hurts enough. I would love the chance to be TNA World Champion and wrestle in a TNA six-sided ring. Elsewhere in the interview, Slater talked about his Option C promo at TNA Lockdown. Fans can read his full comments here . If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.
summary: Leon Slater expressed his desire to wrestle in TNA's six-sided ring as the TNA World Champion. The British star, a longtime TNA fan, discussed the unique ring on the I Love Wrestling Podcast while reacting to the return of Destination X. He noted the six-sided ring was originally used from TNA's debut until 2010, revived in 2014 and retired again in 2018.

title: Injury Update: Stephanie Vaquer Cleared for WWE In-Ring Return After Ankle Injury
raw_title: Stephanie Vaquer Cleared for WWE In-Ring Return After Ankle Injury
summary_src: Stephanie Vaquer is officially done with the crutches and ready to get back in the ring. After suffering an ankle injury at Money in the Bank, Vaquer has now confirmed she’s cleared to compete — and Becky Lynch is apparently first on her list.
body: WWE posted a video of Vaquer on Twitter , where she delivered the good news herself. Vaquer dramatically tossed her crutches aside before revealing that she’s been cleared and sending a very direct message to Lynch. “Becky, you wanted to know when I’m cleared? See you Monday.” That means Vaquer is set to confront Lynch on the October 26 episode of Monday Night RAW. Whatever Becky has been waiting to say or do, she won’t have to wait much longer now that Vaquer is officially cleared. Vaquer had been dealing with the ankle issue since Money in the Bank , where she lost the Women’s World Championship to Liv Morgan. Fans became concerned after the match when Vaquer was visibly limping, needed help from referee Jessika Carr and eventually sat down on the steel steps before heading backstage. Vaquer later confirmed that she had twisted her ankle during the show . At the time, she played down the severity and said she expected the injury to require only a short period of rest. “I twisted my ankle. It’s not a big deal — just a couple of days of rest.” The injury was legitimate rather than part of a WWE storyline, but there was optimism from the beginning that Vaquer wouldn’t be sidelined for long. She also made it clear that losing her championship bothered her considerably more than the ankle itself. “But more than anything, I’m very disappointed about that match. I would have loved to be able to do this interview with you with the championship here on my shoulder, but I wasn’t able to retain it.” Now the injury question is officially out of the way, and Vaquer already has some unfinished business waiting for her. Her message to Becky makes Monday’s RAW the next stop, and fans won’t have to wait long to find out what happens when the two come face-to-face.
